From 1400 the Freistuhl, the chief seat of the Westphalian Vehmic courts, stood in the city until it was moved to Arnsberg in 1437. In 1444, as the tower of St Reinold's rose above the walls, Dortmund was a self-governing Hanse commonwealth of merchants and brewers whose best days were already slipping away.

The tower, finished in 1454, was hailed as the wonder of Westphalia. After the Anglo-Hanseatic War of 1470–74 Cologne was excluded from the Westphalian quarter and Dortmund took its place as the circle's chief town, and in 1504 the city acquired the last rights over the surrounding County of Dortmund. Lutheran preaching spread gradually from 1523 and a Lutheran church order followed in 1570; in 1543 the city founded its Latin school, one of the oldest schools in Europe. The Thirty Years' War bled the small republic white and reduced it to a farming market town, and in 1661 an earthquake brought down St Reinold's tower, which was rebuilt at once. By 1793 only some 4,500 inhabitants remained. The Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of 1803 ended Dortmund's life as a free imperial city and assigned it as an exclave to the Principality of Orange-Nassau; in 1808 Napoleon made it the prefecture of the Ruhr department in the Grand Duchy of Berg, and in 1815 it passed to the Prussian Province of Westphalia.
zh:
多特蒙德初见于882年的文献，当时称Throtmanni；它依着一座加洛林时代的王家庄园，兴起在横贯威斯特伐利亚的东西古道「海尔路」旁。1016年帝国议会在此召开，1152年腓特烈·巴巴罗萨也在此举行宫廷会议。1232年的大火几乎吞没全城和城市档案，1236年皇帝腓特烈二世重新颁赐特权，首次在文书中称多特蒙德为帝国城市。作为汉萨同盟莱茵－威斯特伐利亚－尼德兰区块的首席城市，本地商人远至英格兰经商；1293年城市取得酿酒权。1339年，由贝尔斯沃特和克莱平两大家族牵头的多特蒙德商人银团甚至收下英格兰王冠，作为爱德华三世欠债的抵押品。1388至1389年的「大多特蒙德仇争」中，城市顶住了马克伯爵与科隆大主教联军长达十八个月的围攻。1400年起，威斯特伐利亚费姆法庭的最高法座「自由座」设在城中，直到1437年迁往阿恩斯贝格。1444年，赖诺尔德教堂的高塔正在城墙内节节升高，多特蒙德是个由商人和酿酒商自治的汉萨城邦，只是它的全盛时光已在悄然流逝。

高塔于1454年落成，被誉为「威斯特伐利亚的奇迹」。1470至1474年英汉战争后，科隆被排挤出威斯特伐利亚区块，多特蒙德接任该区块的首席城市；1504年，城市又取得了对周边多特蒙德伯国的全部权利。路德宗布道自1523年起逐渐传开，1570年颁行路德宗教会规程；1543年创办的市立拉丁语学校，是欧洲最古老的学校之一。三十年战争把这个小小共和国榨得民穷财尽，沦为半城半乡的农耕集镇。1661年一场地震震塌了赖诺尔德教堂的高塔，塔随即重建。到1793年，城中只剩约四千五百名居民。1803年的《帝国代表重要决议》终结了多特蒙德的帝国自由城市身份，把它作为飞地划给奥兰治－拿骚亲王国；1808年，拿破仑将它定为贝格大公国鲁尔省的省会，1815年多特蒙德并入普鲁士的威斯特伐利亚省。

en:
Stuttgart grew from a stud farm founded around 950 by Liudolf, Duke of Swabia, in the Nesenbach valley south of the old Roman town of Cannstatt, and the town's name derives from that Stuotgarten where cavalry horses were bred. It passed to the counts of Württemberg in 1251 with the dowry of Mechthild of Baden, and after the rival imperial city of Esslingen destroyed the family castle on the Württemberg hill in 1311, Count Eberhard I enlarged and fortified Stuttgart as his residence. First documented as a town in 1229, it was the capital of only half of Württemberg in 1444, for the Nürtingen partition of 1442 had split the county between Count Ulrich V at Stuttgart and his brother Ludwig at Urach. Grain, wine and the court sustained the town below the Old Castle.

The two halves were reunited in 1482 under Count Eberhard V, who as Eberhard the Bearded was raised to duke in 1495. Duke Ulrich's seizure of the free city of Reutlingen in 1519 brought the Swabian League down on Württemberg: he was driven into exile and the county passed to the Habsburgs. Peasant bands held Stuttgart for a few days in 1525, and after his restoration with Hessian help in 1534 the Reformation was introduced by Erhard Schnepf. After Nördlingen in 1634 the court fled to Strasbourg, and plague and military billeting halved Stuttgart's 10,000 people before the duke returned in 1638. The court moved to Ludwigsburg in 1718, but Duke Charles Alexander brought it back; on his death in 1737 his financial adviser Joseph Süß Oppenheimer was judicially murdered after a show trial. Under Duke Charles Eugene the New Castle was begun in 1746 and Friedrich Schiller studied medicine at the Karlsschule. In 1803 Stuttgart became capital of the Electorate of Württemberg and in 1806 of the new kingdom.
zh:
斯图加特起源于约950年施瓦本公爵柳道夫在内森巴赫河谷、罗马古城卡恩施塔特以南设立的养马场，地名即由当年繁育战马的「马场」而来。1251年，斯图加特随巴登的梅希蒂尔德的嫁妆归于符腾堡伯爵；1311年，敌对的帝国自由城市埃斯林根摧毁了符腾堡山上的家族祖堡，埃伯哈德一世伯爵便扩建并加固斯图加特，作为自己的驻地。这座1229年已有城市身份明文记载的城镇，在1444年只是半个符腾堡的首府：1442年的尼尔廷根分割把伯国一分为二，分给在斯图加特的乌尔里希五世伯爵和在乌拉赫的弟弟路德维希。谷物、葡萄酒和宫廷维系着旧堡山下的这座城镇。

1482年，两半领地在埃伯哈德五世伯爵治下重新统一，他于1495年被升格为公爵，即「大胡子」埃伯哈德一世。乌尔里希公爵1519年夺取帝国自由城市罗伊特林根，招施瓦本同盟来攻：他被迫流亡，伯国落入哈布斯堡之手。1525年农民武装曾占据斯图加特数日，1534年他借黑森之力复位，随即由埃哈德·施内普夫主持引入宗教改革。1634年内德林根战役后宫廷逃往斯特拉斯堡，瘟疫和军队驻扎使斯图加特的一万人口减半，公爵1638年才返回。1718年宫廷迁往路德维希堡，卡尔·亚历山大公爵又把都城迁回；他1737年死后，财政顾问约瑟夫·聚斯·奥本海默经一场摆样子的审判被冤杀。卡尔·欧根公爵治下，新宫1746年动工，弗里德里希·席勒在卡尔学校攻读医学。1803年斯图加特成为符腾堡选帝侯国首府，1806年成为新生王国的都城。

en:
Ansbach grew up where the brook Onolzbach joins the Rezat, around a Benedictine monastery founded in 748 by the Frankish noble Gumbert. The adjoining settlement was first recorded as a town in 1221, and in 1331 the counts of Oettingen sold it to the Hohenzollern burgrave Frederick IV of Nuremberg; from 1385 it was the chief residence of the Hohenzollern Franconian lands. After Burgrave Frederick became Elector of Brandenburg in 1415, his Franconian possessions kept rulers of their own, and on his death in 1440 Ansbach fell to his son Albert Achilles, who in 1444 held court there in the moated castle built around 1400. The town remained the seat of the Brandenburg-Ansbach margraves, a cadet line of the house that would one day inherit the Prussian crown.

Margrave George the Pious, an early follower of Luther, had the first communion service in German celebrated in Ansbach on 9 April 1525, and Gumbertus Abbey was secularized in 1563. From 1523 to 1603 the Ansbach margraves also held the Silesian duchy of Jägerndorf. The residence was rebuilt in Renaissance style under George Frederick I and given its baroque form by 1738, while a faience works opened in 1710. Caroline of Ansbach, born here in 1683, became queen to George II of Britain. In 1791 the last margrave, Charles Alexander, ceded Ansbach and Bayreuth to Prussia for a life annuity, and Hardenberg's administration pressed hard on the neighbouring imperial knights. Napoleon forced Prussia to surrender Ansbach in the treaty of Schönbrunn in December 1805, and on 1 January 1806 it passed to the new kingdom of Bavaria.
zh:
安斯巴赫坐落于奥诺尔茨巴赫溪汇入雷察特河之处，源自法兰克贵族贡伯特748年创建的本笃会修道院。旁侧的定居点1221年首见记载时已是城镇，1331年厄廷根伯爵把它卖给纽伦堡城堡伯爵、霍亨索伦家族的腓特烈四世，1385年起这里成为霍亨索伦家族法兰克尼亚领地的首要驻地。1415年城堡伯爵腓特烈成为勃兰登堡选帝侯后，其法兰克尼亚领地仍由本支自行统治；1440年他去世后安斯巴赫归儿子阿尔布雷希特·阿喀琉斯，1444年他正在1400年前后建成的水堡中开府治事。这座小城此后一直是勃兰登堡-安斯巴赫藩侯的驻地，这一霍亨索伦旁支日后还将继承普鲁士王位。

虔诚者藩侯格奥尔格早早追随路德，1525年4月9日安斯巴赫举行了首场德语圣餐礼，贡伯特修道院于1563年还俗。1523年至1603年间，安斯巴赫藩侯还领有西里西亚的耶根多夫公国。格奥尔格·腓特烈一世时府邸按文艺复兴风格重建，1738年又完成巴洛克式改造，1710年当地还开设了彩陶工坊。1683年出生于此的安斯巴赫的卡罗琳，后来成为英王乔治二世的王后。1791年末代藩侯卡尔·亚历山大以终身年金为条件把安斯巴赫与拜罗伊特让给普鲁士，哈登贝格主政期间大力兼并周边的帝国骑士领地。1805年12月的申布伦条约中拿破仑迫使普鲁士交出安斯巴赫，1806年1月1日它并入新生的巴伐利亚王国。

en:
The Breisgau is the warm lowland strip between the Upper Rhine and the Black Forest, with Freiburg as its chief town. The Zähringer dukes founded Freiburg in 1120 as a free market settlement, and silver from the Schauinsland mines paid for its minster, begun around 1200, and made the city one of the richest on the Upper Rhine; its Rappenpfennig coin, first struck in 1327, anchored a monetary union with Basel, Colmar and Breisach in 1377. In 1368 the burghers bought themselves free of the counts of Freiburg with a great sum of silver and put themselves under the Habsburgs. In 1444 the Breisgau was the heartland of Further Austria, the Habsburgs' scattered south-western lands, an Alemannic-speaking Catholic country whose silver veins were already running thin.

In 1457 Archduke Albrecht VI founded the university, the Habsburgs' second after Vienna, and in 1498 Maximilian I held an Imperial Diet in Freiburg. The city rejected the Reformation in 1520, but in the Peasants' War of 1525 rebel bands led by Hans Müller occupied it and forced the council into an evangelical brotherhood before the rising was put down; Erasmus of Rotterdam fled reformed Basel for Catholic Freiburg in 1529. During the Thirty Years' War Swedes under Gustav Horn took the city in 1632, and in August 1644 the bloody Battle of Freiburg was fought around it; its people fell from over 10,000 to some 2,000. Louis XIV gained Freiburg by the Peace of Nijmegen in 1679 and set Vauban to fortify it, visiting the works himself in 1681, though Ryswick returned it in 1697. French troops came again in 1713 and 1744, and on the second occasion they gutted the fortifications when they left. Revolutionary France held the city for three months in 1796 until Archduke Charles retook it. The Breisgau was briefly awarded to the Duke of Modena in 1801, then passed to Baden by the Treaty of Pressburg in 1805, a transfer confirmed at Vienna in 1815.
zh:
布赖斯高是莱茵河上游与黑森林之间一片气候温和的低地，以弗赖堡为首府。1120年，策林根公爵在此建起自由市集弗赖堡；绍因斯兰山银矿的收入既资助了1200年前后动工的大教堂，也使城市成为莱茵河上游最富庶的地方之一。1327年弗赖堡开始自铸拉本芬尼银币，1377年又与巴塞尔、科尔马、布赖萨赫结成货币同盟。1368年，市民凑出一笔白银从弗赖堡伯爵手中赎得自由，转投哈布斯堡家族庇护。1444年的布赖斯高是哈布斯堡「前地」——奥地利家族散布在德意志西南的诸领地——的核心，这里讲阿勒曼尼语、信奉天主教，而银矿的矿脉已见枯竭。

1457年，阿尔布雷希特六世大公创办弗赖堡大学，这是哈布斯堡领地内继维也纳之后的第二所大学；1498年，马克西米利安一世在此召开帝国议会。1520年城市拒绝宗教改革，但1525年德意志农民战争期间，汉斯·米勒率领的农民军占领弗赖堡，强迫市议会加入福音兄弟会，起义随后遭到镇压；1529年，鹿特丹的伊拉斯谟从改宗新教的巴塞尔避居仍奉天主教的弗赖堡。三十年战争中，古斯塔夫·霍恩麾下的瑞典军队于1632年入城，1644年8月城郊又爆发惨烈的弗赖堡战役，全城人口从一万有余降到约两千。1679年，路易十四依《奈梅亨和约》取得弗赖堡，命沃邦将其改建为新式要塞，并于1681年亲临工地，1697年《赖斯韦克和约》又把城市归还奥地利。1713年和1744年法军两度攻占，1744年撤离时更拆毁了城防。1796年革命军占领弗赖堡三个月，才被卡尔大公收复。1801年布赖斯高一度被割给摩德纳公爵作为补偿，1805年《普雷斯堡和约》将其划归巴登，1815年维也纳和会予以确认。

en:
The Inntal carries the river Inn through the eastern Alps, and at Innsbruck, 'the bridge over the Inn', the Brenner road crosses on its way from southern Germany into Italy. The Romans kept the station of Veldidena here; the counts of Andechs laid out a market at the crossing, first documented in 1180, and the town passed to the counts of Tyrol in 1248. Their Meinhardiner successors ruled from Castle Tyrol above Meran, until Margaret Maultasch, the last of her line, bequeathed the county to the Habsburg Rudolf IV in 1363. In 1420 Duke Frederick IV of the Empty Pockets moved his residence from Meran to Innsbruck, and the new town outgrew the old capital. In 1444 the valley was the heartland of a Habsburg junior line: Brenner tolls, the salt works at Hall and the fast-swelling silver mines at Schwaz filled its coffers, and the town tower was rising beside the old town hall.

Fire gutted much of upper Hall in 1447, but the town recovered and in 1477 took the Tyrolean mint when it moved from Meran; in 1486 it struck the Guldengroschen, Europe's first large silver coin and ancestor of the thaler. Worked with Fugger capital, Schwaz became one of Europe's great mining towns, home by the sixteenth century to more than 12,000 people, second only to Vienna in the Habsburg lands. Maximilian I often held court at Innsbruck in the 1490s, built the Golden Roof around 1500 and a great arsenal, and in 1511 his Landlibell bound the Tyrolese to military service only for the defence of their own country. The mining towns embraced the Reformation, and in 1525 the peasants of the German Peasants' War rose under Michael Gaismair, only to be crushed within months; after 1562 the Jesuits carried through the Counter-Reformation. The Tyrolean Habsburg line died out in 1665 and the court returned to Vienna, though a university was founded in 1669. A Bavarian invasion was repulsed at the Pontlatzer bridge in 1703. Ceded to Bavaria in 1805, the Tyrol rose in 1809 under Andreas Hofer and won four battles on the Bergisel above Innsbruck before French and Bavarian strength overwhelmed it; Hofer was shot at Mantua in 1810 and the valley returned to Austria in 1814.
zh:
因塔尔是因河横贯东阿尔卑斯的谷地，因斯布鲁克——意为「因河上的桥」——正扼守布伦纳大道自德意志南下意大利的渡口。罗马人曾在此设立韦尔迪德纳军站；安德克斯伯爵在渡口开设的市集于1180年首见记载，1248年城镇归于蒂罗尔伯爵。其后的迈因哈德家族以梅拉诺附近的蒂罗尔城堡为统治中心，直到末代继承人玛格丽特·毛尔塔施于1363年将伯国遗赠给哈布斯堡的鲁道夫四世。1420年，「空口袋」腓特烈四世把府邸从梅拉诺迁至因斯布鲁克，新城就此盖过旧都。1444年的因河谷是哈布斯堡一支幼系领地的核心：布伦纳的过境税、哈尔的盐场和施瓦茨蒸蒸日上的银矿充实着府库，市政塔也正在老市政厅旁筑起。

1447年大火焚毁哈尔上城区大半，但城市很快恢复，1477年蒂罗尔造币厂从梅拉诺迁来此地；1486年哈尔铸出欧洲最早的大型银币古尔登格罗申，即塔勒银币的前身。在富格尔家族的资本经营下，施瓦茨成为欧洲数一数二的矿业城，到16世纪已有一万二千余居民，在哈布斯堡领地内仅次于维也纳。马克西米利安一世在1490年代常驻因斯布鲁克，1500年前后建起金顶屋和大军械库；1511年他颁布《国防规约》，规定蒂罗尔人的军役仅限于保卫本乡。矿区诸镇皈依新教，1525年德意志农民战争中，蒂罗尔农民在米夏埃尔·盖斯迈尔率领下起事，数月即告失败；1562年后耶稣会在此推行反宗教改革，当地重归天主教。1665年蒂罗尔哈布斯堡支系绝嗣，宫廷迁回维也纳，大学仍于1669年创立。1703年，巴伐利亚入侵者在蓬特拉茨桥被击退。1805年蒂罗尔被割让给巴伐利亚，1809年蒂罗尔人在安德烈亚斯·霍费尔领导下起义，在因斯布鲁克近郊的贝吉塞尔四战四胜，最终仍被法、巴联军压倒；霍费尔于1810年在曼图亚就义，因河谷则在1814年回归奥地利。

en:
Baden, the future Baden-Baden, sits on the small river Oos where hot springs rise at the foot of the Black Forest. The Romans knew the baths as Aquae, and after centuries of neglect the medieval margraves brought them back into use: Count Hermann II of the Zähringer, who first styled himself Margrave of Baden in 1112, built Hohenbaden Castle above the springs, and from 1306 the thermal waters were again run as public baths. Lichtenthal Abbey, the margraves' first burial place, was founded in 1245, and the town's collegiate church became their dynastic tomb in 1453. In 1444 Baden was the residence of Margrave Jakob I, a small Swabian, Catholic power on the middle Upper Rhine whose income came from the wine villages of the Black Forest foothills and the bathing guests.

In 1479 Margrave Christoph I moved his court from Hohenbaden to the New Castle in the town, and from 1507 a spa tax was levied on visitors. The margraviate was partitioned in 1535: Baden stayed with the Catholic Bernhardine line, while the junior line at Durlach turned Protestant. The spendthrift Eduard Fortunat was driven out by Baden-Durlach in 1594, but after Tilly won the Battle of Wimpfen on 6 May 1622, Margrave Wilhelm was restored and carried through the Counter-Reformation amid witch trials that took more than a hundred lives in the town. Swedish and other armies passed through in the 1630s and 1640s, and worse came under Louis XIV: in 1689 General Mélac burned Baden and every other Baden town save Gernsbach. Ludwig Wilhelm, the 'Turkish Louis', rebuilt the country but moved his residence to Rastatt in 1705, his widow Sibylla Augusta raising the baroque palaces around it. When the line died out with August Georg in 1771, Karl Friedrich of Baden-Durlach inherited the lands and reunited the margraviate. Revolutionary refugees and the Congress of Rastatt of 1797-99 made the baths fashionable again, and in 1806 Baden became a grand duchy and joined the Confederation of the Rhine; a casino opened in 1811.
zh:
巴登（即后来的巴登-巴登）坐落在奥瑟河畔，黑森林山麓有多处方热泉。罗马人早知此处温泉，称阿奎埃；中世纪的藩侯使温泉重获生机：策林根家族的赫尔曼二世于1112年首次自称巴登藩侯，在温泉上方修建霍亨巴登堡；1306年起热泉再度作为公共浴场经营。1245年建立的利希滕塔尔修道院是藩侯家族最早的墓地，1453年城中的修道院教堂又成为家族陵寝。1444年的巴登是藩侯雅各布一世的驻跸之地，这个信奉天主教的施瓦本小邦位于莱茵河上游中段，收入来自黑森林山麓的葡萄园和入浴的客人。

1479年，藩侯克里斯托夫一世把宫廷从霍亨巴登堡迁入城中的新城堡；1507年起向浴客征收浴税。1535年藩侯国一分为二：巴登留在奉天主教的伯恩哈德支系手中，幼支杜尔拉赫则改宗新教。挥霍无度的爱德华·福图纳特于1594年被杜尔拉赫方面逐出；1622年5月6日蒂利赢得温普芬战役后，藩侯威廉复位，在反宗教改革中推行旧教，同一时期的猎巫在城中夺去上百条性命。1630至1640年代，瑞典等国军队轮番过境；路易十四的战争带来更大的劫难：1689年，梅拉客将军放火烧毁巴登，除格恩斯巴赫外，藩侯国各城无一幸免。有「土耳其人路易」之称的路德维希·威廉重建国家，却在1705年把宫廷迁往拉施塔特，其遗孀西比拉·奥古斯塔在当地建起一批巴洛克宫殿。1771年奥古斯特·格奥尔格去世无嗣，杜尔拉赫的卡尔·弗里德里希继承领地，藩侯国重新统一。法国大革命的流亡者与1797至1799年的拉施塔特和会让温泉再度时髦，1806年巴登成为大公国并加入莱茵邦联，1811年又开设了赌场。

en:
Strasbourg sits on the Ill where that river meets the Rhine, the old Roman Argentoratum. For nine centuries its bishops ruled, until on 8 March 1262 the burghers beat the bishop's army at Hausbergen and made themselves a free city; Charles IV confirmed its rank as a free imperial city in 1358. Ruled by a closed ring of patrician families, the republic grew rich on the Rhine carrying trade. Its minster, rebuilt in Gothic from 1220, was crowned with an openwork spire in 1439, rising 142 metres over the roofs. In the 1430s and 1440s the Mainz goldsmith Gutenberg worked here, experimenting behind closed doors with movable metal type. In 1444 that prosperity looks fragile: the Écorcheur companies, the dreaded Armagnac mercenaries of the Dauphin Louis, are sweeping through Alsace. The Swiss checked them at St. Jakob an der Birs on 26 August, and the peace of Ensisheim on 28 October sent them into winter quarters; they left Alsace only next spring.

Printing became its hallmark: Mentelin, first printer in Alsace, set up his press here and in 1466 produced the first printed German Bible; in 1605 Johann Carolus began the world's first weekly newspaper. Preachers such as Geiler von Kaysersberg and humanists such as Sebastian Brant made it a city of letters. Matthias Zell preached the new doctrines in 1521, Bucer and Capito made the city a Reformation stronghold, its delegates signed the Protestation at Speyer in 1529 and the Tetrapolitan Confession in 1530, and Johannes Sturm opened a Protestant academy in 1538. The Peasants' War lapped at the walls in 1525, when Duke Antoine of Lorraine cut the rebel bands to pieces out at Saverne. Neutral through the Thirty Years' War, the city nonetheless capitulated to Louis XIV on 30 September 1681, in peacetime. Vauban ringed it with bastions, the Edict of Fontainebleau in 1685 drove its Protestants to conversion or exile, and the minster spire remained for more than two centuries the highest building on earth. The young Goethe studied here in the 1770s, and on the night of 25–26 April 1792 Rouget de Lisle wrote his War Song for the Army of the Rhine, soon the Marseillaise. Revolutionary and Napoleonic armies marched through its gates; after 1815 the city stayed French, the kingdom's fortified bridgehead on the Rhine.
zh:
斯特拉斯堡地处伊尔河汇入莱茵河之处，旧城即罗马军营阿让托拉图姆。九百年间主教是这里的主人，直到1262年3月8日，市民在豪斯贝根一役击败主教的军队，赢得自由身；1358年，查理四世正式确认它为帝国自由城市。城市由少数世家望族把持，靠莱茵河转运贸易发家。大教堂自1220年起按哥特风格重建，1439年戴上镂空尖塔，在满城屋顶之上拔起142米。1430至1440年代，美因茨金匠古腾堡正在城中闭门试验金属活字。1444年，这派富庶显得脆弱：令人闻风丧胆的「剥皮者」佣兵团——王太子路易麾下的阿马尼亚克匪兵——正横扫阿尔萨斯。8月26日，瑞士人在比尔斯河畔圣雅克挡住了他们；10月28日恩西赛姆议和，匪兵入营过冬，直到第二年春天才撤出。

印刷术后来成了这座城市的标志：阿尔萨斯第一位印书人门特林在此开业，1466年印出第一部德文圣经；1605年，约翰·卡罗勒斯在这里办起世界上第一份周报。讲道师盖勒·冯·凯泽斯贝格与人文主义者塞巴斯蒂安·布兰特让这里成为文教之城。马蒂亚斯·策尔1521年开始宣讲新教，布塞尔和卡皮托把斯特拉斯堡变成宗教改革重镇，市民代表1529年联署《施派尔抗议书》、1530年签署《四城信纲》，约翰·施图尔姆则在1538年办起新教学园。1525年农民战争漫到城墙脚下，洛林公爵安托万在城外的萨韦尔纳把起义军斩杀殆尽。三十年战争中斯特拉斯堡谨守中立，却仍于1681年9月30日在和平岁月里向路易十四开城投降。沃邦为它环绕棱堡，1685年的《枫丹白露敕令》逼新教徒或改宗或流亡，而大教堂尖塔在此后两百余年里一直是世界最高建筑。1770年代，青年歌德曾在此求学；1792年4月25日深夜至26日凌晨，鲁热·德·利勒谱成《莱茵军团战歌》，不久便以《马赛曲》之名传遍四方。革命与拿破仑的军队在它的城门间往来进出；1815年之后，斯特拉斯堡留在法国，成为王国在莱茵河上设防的桥头堡。

en:
Salzburg lies on the Salzach at the foot of the Alps, on the site of the Roman town of Iuvavum. Saint Rupert refounded it as a bishopric around 696 and it became an archbishopric in 798; its very name comes from the salt barges that paid toll on the river. In 996 the emperor granted market, mint and toll rights, and in 1077 Archbishop Gebhard began the Hohensalzburg fortress on the rock above the town. After the battle of Mühldorf in 1322 the archbishops shook off Bavarian overlordship, and Salzburg entered the fifteenth century as a self-governing prince-archbishopric of the Holy Roman Empire. In 1444 its prince-archbishop ruled a Catholic, Bavarian-speaking city whose salt mines and river tolls made it one of the richest church lands south of the Danube.

In 1525, during the German Peasants' War, miners and peasants besieged Archbishop Matthäus Lang in the Hohensalzburg for three months. The townspeople had leaned Protestant, but the unyielding were expelled by 1590, and Salzburg became a stronghold of the Counter-Reformation. Wolf Dietrich von Raitenau rebuilt the old town in Italian style around 1600, his successors raised the baroque cathedral, and Paris von Lodron kept the little state neutral through the Thirty Years' War while making its capital one of the best-fortified cities in Europe. Archbishop Firmian's edict of 1731 drove more than 20,000 Protestants into exile, most of them to Prussian East Prussia. Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, born here in 1756, served the reforming Archbishop Colloredo before leaving for Vienna in 1781. Secularised as an electorate in 1803, Salzburg passed to Austria in 1805, to the Kingdom of Bavaria in 1810, and by the Treaty of Munich in 1816 back to Austria.
zh:
萨尔茨堡坐落在阿尔卑斯山麓的萨尔察赫河畔，罗马古城尤瓦武姆的故址上。圣鲁佩特于696年前后在此重建主教区，798年升为总主教区；城名就来自河上缴纳通行税的盐船。996年，皇帝颁赐市场、铸币与征税诸权；1077年，格布哈德总主教在城头的岩山上动工修建霍亨萨尔茨堡要塞。1322年米尔多夫战役后，总主教们摆脱了巴伐利亚的宗主权，萨尔茨堡在15世纪成为神圣罗马帝国中自治的大主教领地。1444年统治这座天主教巴伐利亚语城市的是总主教，盐矿和河上关税使它成为多瑙河以南最富庶的教会领地之一。

1525年德意志农民战争期间，矿工和农民把马特豪斯·朗格总主教围困在霍亨萨尔茨堡要塞达三个月。城中居民本已倾向新教，但不肯改宗者到1590年全被驱逐，萨尔茨堡成为反宗教改革的堡垒。1600年前后，沃尔夫·迪特里希·冯·赖特瑙按意大利风格重建老城，继任者建起巴洛克式主教座堂，帕里斯·冯·洛德龙在三十年战争中使这块小邦保持中立，同时把首府修成欧洲设防最坚固的城市之一。1731年，菲尔米安总主教签署驱逐令，两万余名新教徒被迫流亡，多数远徙普鲁士治下的东普鲁士。莫扎特1756年生于萨尔茨堡，曾侍奉主张改革的科洛雷多总主教，1781年前往维也纳。1803年大主教区还俗为选侯国，萨尔茨堡1805年归奥地利，1810年转属巴伐利亚王国，1816年依《慕尼黑条约》重回奥地利。

en:
Heidelberg grew beneath a castle on the Neckar, with the first surviving mention of the town dated to 1196. The Wittelsbach Counts Palatine of the Rhine made it their residence, and the Golden Bull of 1356 confirmed their rank as prince-electors. Rupert I founded the university in 1386, the third in the Holy Roman Empire, and the town was enlarged in 1392 to roughly the extent of the later old town. Rupert III, elected German king in 1400, added the Church of the Holy Spirit as a new focus beside the market. In 1444 Catholic Heidelberg was the capital of the Electoral Palatinate, a riverside seat of court and learning beneath the Königstuhl.

Frederick II permitted the Reformation in 1545 and 1546, but imperial pressure forced a quick return to Catholic worship; Elector Ottheinrich established Protestantism permanently after 1556. Under Frederick III the Palatinate turned to Calvinism, and the Heidelberg Catechism appeared there in 1563. Frederick V accepted the Bohemian crown in 1619 and was defeated at the White Mountain in 1620. Tilly's Catholic League army took Heidelberg on 16 September 1622, beginning Bavarian rule interrupted only by Swedish occupation from 1633 to 1635, while the Bibliotheca Palatina was carried to Rome. The electoral state was restored in 1648, yet French troops sacked Heidelberg in 1688 and again in 1693. The court moved to Mannheim in 1720 under Charles III Philip, though Charles Theodore later built the Old Bridge and completed the Karlstor in 1781. Mediatized to Baden in 1803, Heidelberg kept its reopened university and became an early centre of German Romanticism, where Arnim and Brentano published their folk-song collection between 1806 and 1808.
zh:
海德堡坐落在内卡河畔的城堡山下，现存最早记载见于1196年。维特尔斯巴赫家族的莱茵-普法尔茨伯爵把这里设为驻地，1356年《金玺诏书》确认其选帝侯地位。鲁普雷希特一世于1386年创办大学，是神圣罗马帝国的第三所大学；1392年城市扩建，范围已接近后来的老城。1400年当选德意志国王的鲁普雷希特三世又在市场旁营建圣灵教堂。1444年时，信奉天主教的海德堡是普法尔茨选侯国都城，也是王座山下兼具宫廷与学术气息的内卡河城市。

腓特烈二世在1545至1546年允许宗教改革传入，但皇帝施压后礼拜很快恢复旧制；奥特海因里希1556年之后才最终确立新教信仰。腓特烈三世时期，普法尔茨转向加尔文宗，《海德堡要理问答》于1563年在此问世。腓特烈五世1619年接受波希米亚王位，1620年在白山战役中战败。蒂利率领的天主教同盟军队于1622年9月16日攻占海德堡，此后除1633年至1635年的瑞典占领外长期由巴伐利亚控制，普法尔茨宫廷图书馆也被送往罗马。选侯国虽于1648年恢复，海德堡又在1688年和1693年两度遭法军洗劫。卡尔三世·菲利普1720年把宫廷迁往曼海姆；卡尔·特奥多尔后来修建老桥，并于1781年完成卡尔门。1803年海德堡并入巴登，大学重新振兴，并成为德国浪漫派的早期中心，阿尔尼姆与布伦塔诺于1806年至1808年间在此出版民歌集《少年的魔法号角》。

en:
Mainz began when Drusus founded the Roman camp of Mogontiacum at the Main's mouth in 13/12 BC; it became capital of the province of Germania Superior before Vandals, Alans and Suebi sacked it in the crossing of 406. Under the Franks it rose again: Saint Boniface launched the conversion of the Saxons from Mainz, the see became an archbishopric in 782, and its prelates were archchancellors, prince-electors and primates of Germany. Archbishop Willigis began the great imperial cathedral about 975. Jews called the city Magenza, one of the three ShUM towns where Rabbi Gershom taught and Ashkenazi learning took root, but crusaders slaughtered its Jews in 1096, and about 6,000 died in the pogrom of 1349. In 1244 Archbishop Siegfried III's charter placed the city under a twenty-four-man council; as a free city it hosted the founding of the Rhenish League in 1254. After another expulsion of the Jews in 1438, Mainz in 1444 was a self-governing city beneath its prince-archbishop, while the native Johannes Gutenberg perfected abroad the craft that would make it famous.

Around 1450 Gutenberg set up his press in Mainz, and movable type spread across Europe within a generation. In 1462 Adolf II of Nassau stormed the city in the collegiate feud, stripped its privileges and drove Gutenberg into exile; the restored archbishop Diether von Isenburg founded the university in 1477. The Reformation at first found fertile ground, for Cardinal Albert of Brandenburg held the see, yet the cathedral chapter kept Mainz Catholic, and no Protestant congregation was permitted until 1802. During the Thirty Years' War a Swedish army occupied the city without a fight, until Archbishop Johann Philipp von Schönborn, elected in 1647, guided Mainz to peace and recovery. French troops entered in 1792 and the elector fled; on 18 March 1793 the Jacobins under Georg Forster proclaimed the Republic of Mainz, first on German soil, but an eighteen-week Prussian siege ended it in July. The French returned after Campo Formio in 1797, and from 1800 Mainz, as Mayence, was capital of the French département of Mont-Tonnerre, until the garrison withdrew in 1814; in 1816 it passed to Hesse-Darmstadt as capital of Rhenish Hesse.
zh:
公元前13/12年，德鲁苏斯在美因河注入莱茵河处建起罗马军营莫贡提亚库姆，这里后来成为上日耳曼行省首府，406年被渡过莱茵河的汪达尔人、阿兰人和苏维汇人洗劫。法兰克时代它重新崛起：圣波尼法爵从美因茨出发推动萨克森人皈依，782年美因茨升为大主教区，历任大主教身兼帝国大总理、选侯和德意志首教。威利吉斯大主教约975年动工兴建宏伟的帝国大教堂。犹太人称之为马根察，是舒姆三城之一，拉比格尔肖姆在此讲学，阿什肯纳兹学术在此扎根；但1096年十字军屠杀城中犹太人，1349年的惨案约六千人遇难。1244年齐格弗里德三世颁发特许状，把城市交给二十四人议会；成为自由城市后，美因茨在1254年见证莱茵城市同盟成立。1438年犹太人再遭驱逐；1444年的美因茨在选侯大主教之下自治，本地人古腾堡则在外乡磨炼那门日后将使此城闻名的手艺。

约1450年，古腾堡在美因茨架起印刷机，活字印刷术在一代人的时间里传遍欧洲。1462年，拿骚的阿道夫二世在教堂继承之争中攻破城市、剥夺其特权，古腾堡也被放逐；复任大主教的迪特尔·冯·伊森堡1477年创办大学。宗教改革起初颇有市场：枢机阿尔布雷希特·冯·勃兰登堡正担任大主教，但大教堂议会最终把美因茨留在天主教会内，1802年以前不许成立新教教团。三十年战争中，一支瑞典军队兵不血刃占领此城，直到1647年当选大主教的约翰·菲利普·冯·申博恩引导城市走向议和与复苏。1792年法军入城，选侯出逃；1793年3月18日，福斯特领导的雅各宾派宣布成立美因茨共和国——德意志土地上第一个共和国，但普军围城十八周后于7月将其终结。1797年《坎波福尔米奥和约》后法军卷土重来，1800年起以「马延斯」之名成为法国蒙特托内尔省省会，1814年守军撤离；1816年划归黑森-达姆施塔特，为莱茵黑森首府。

en:
Würzburg straddles a crossing of the Main older than its written records: the Irish missionaries Kilian, Kolonat and Totnan were martyred here about 686, and in 741 Boniface made the settlement a bishop's seat with Burkhard as its first bishop. A stone bridge was thrown across the Main around 1130, and in 1168 Frederick Barbarossa granted the bishops the 'Golden Liberty', after which they ruled a wide swathe of eastern Franconia as prince-bishops and 'dukes in Franconia'; at the imperial diet held here in 1180 Henry the Lion was outlawed and Bavaria was granted to the Wittelsbachs. The Romanesque cathedral was built between 1040 and 1225 and a university opened in 1402, while the citizens' bid to become a free imperial city ended when the bishop's troops routed them at Bergtheim in 1400. In 1444 Würzburg was the compact, firmly governed capital of a clerical state, its steep riverside vineyards yielding the wine for which the city was known.

In the Peasants' War of 1525 rebels stormed the Marienberg fortress in vain, and the sculptor Tilman Riemenschneider, then a town councillor, was imprisoned within it. Bishop Julius Echter von Mespelbrunn (1573-1617) led the Counter-Reformation: he founded the Juliusspital hospital, re-founded the university in 1582 and rebuilt the Marienberg as a Renaissance fortress, while the witch trials he revived reached their height under Bishop Philipp Adolf von Ehrenberg in the 1620s. Swedish troops held Würzburg from 1631 to 1634, and in 1633 Chancellor Oxenstierna briefly bestowed the see on Bernard of Saxe-Weimar as a 'Duchy of Franconia'. The Schönborn bishops then remade the city in baroque splendour, above all with Balthasar Neumann's Residenz, built from 1720 to 1744 and adorned in 1750-53 by Tiepolo's vast staircase fresco. Secularized in 1802 and given to Bavaria, Würzburg became in 1806 the capital of the Grand Duchy of Würzburg under Ferdinand, former grand duke of Tuscany, before returning to Bavaria in 1814.
zh:
维尔茨堡扼守美因河上一处比文字记载更古老的渡口：爱尔兰传教士基利安、科洛纳特和托特南约686年在此殉道，741年波尼法斯在此设立主教座，布尔卡德为首任主教。1130年前后美因河上建起石桥，1168年腓特烈·巴巴罗萨颁赐主教「金自由」特权，此后他们以采邑主教兼「法兰克尼亚公爵」的身份统治东法兰克尼亚的广阔土地；1180年在此召开的帝国会议上，狮子亨利被逐出帝国，巴伐利亚转封给维特尔斯巴赫家族。罗曼式大教堂1040年至1225年建成，大学于1402年创办，市民争取帝国自由市地位的尝试则在1400年被主教军队在贝格泰姆击溃。1444年的维尔茨堡是一个教权邦国紧凑而统治牢固的都城，河畔陡峭的葡萄园出产让这座城市闻名的葡萄酒。

1525年农民战争中，起义者强攻马林贝格要塞不克，时任市议员的雕刻家蒂尔曼·里门施奈德被囚于要塞之中。1573年至1617年在任的尤里乌斯·埃希特·冯·梅斯佩尔布伦主教推行反宗教改革：创办尤利乌斯救济院、1582年重建大学、把马林贝格改建成文艺复兴式要塞；他重启的女巫审判在1620年代菲利普·阿道夫·冯·埃伦贝格主教任内达到顶峰。瑞典军队1631年至1634年占据维尔茨堡，1633年瑞典首相奥克森谢纳一度把教区作为「法兰克尼亚公国」封给萨克森-魏玛的伯恩哈德。此后申博恩家族的主教们以巴洛克气象重塑城市，首推巴尔塔扎·诺伊曼设计的维尔茨堡宫：1720年至1744年建成，1750年至1753年提埃坡罗又为它绘上宏大的楼梯厅穹顶壁画。1802年主教邦被世俗化并划归巴伐利亚，1806年维尔茨堡成为前托斯卡纳大公费迪南德治下维尔茨堡大公国的都城，1814年重新归入巴伐利亚。

en:
Trier was founded by the Romans around 18 BC as Augusta Treverorum, on the Moselle in the land of the Treveri. After 293 it was a residence of the Western Roman emperors, one of the four capitals of the Tetrarchy, when the Porta Nigra, the imperial baths and the great palatial basilica were raised, and its bishopric became the oldest north of the Alps. Sacked in the fifth-century invasions and again by Vikings in 882, the city fell to the Franks and in 925 passed to the East Frankish kingdom. Its archbishops grew into prince-electors, among the seven who chose the emperor, holding a swathe of land from the French border to the Rhine. In 1444 Trier, clustered around its Roman monuments, was the capital of the electoral state named after it and a pilgrimage goal through the relics of Saint Matthias.

The University of Trier opened in 1473, and the Reichstag held here in 1512 definitively fixed the empire's circles. Franz von Sickingen battered the walls in vain during the Knights' War of 1522, and the Reformation won no lasting hold: the Jesuits were called in in 1560, while the witch hunts of 1580–1596 cost hundreds of lives in the city. During the Thirty Years' War Elector Philipp Christoph von Sötern leaned on France; Spanish troops carried him off in 1635 for ten years' captivity, and after his release in 1645 Turenne's French troops retook the city. From the 1630s the electors kept their chief residence at Philippsburg beneath Ehrenbreitstein near Koblenz. French forces took Trier in 1673 and razed the abbeys before its walls, and occupied it again in 1688–1698 and through the War of the Spanish Succession, when its people shrank to some 4,000. French revolutionary armies annexed the city in 1794 and dissolved the archbishopric; in 1815 Trier passed to Prussia, and Karl Marx was born here in 1818.
zh:
特里尔在公元前18年前后由罗马人建于摩泽尔河畔，初名奥古斯塔·特雷维罗伦，意为特雷维里人之地的奥古斯都城。293年后，这里成为西罗马皇帝的驻跸之地，是四帝共治时期的四座都城之一，黑门、皇家浴场和宏伟的宫廷大殿都兴建于此时，当地教区也是阿尔卑斯山以北最古老的主教区。城市在5世纪的蛮族入侵中遭劫，882年又被维京人焚掠，此后落入法兰克人之手，925年并入东法兰克王国。历任大主教权势日隆，跻身神圣罗马帝国的七位选帝侯之列，领有从法兰西边境一直延伸到莱茵河的大片土地。1444年的特里尔环着罗马时代的古迹而立，是同名选帝侯国的都城，圣马提亚的圣骸也吸引着各地朝圣者。

1473年特里尔大学创立，1512年神圣罗马帝国帝国会议在此召开，正式划定帝国行政圈。1522年骑士战争中，弗朗茨·冯·西金根围攻特里尔数日，损兵折将而退；宗教改革始终未能在此立足，耶稣会士于1560年被请入城中，而1580至1596年的猎巫风潮使数百名居民丧命。三十年战争中，选帝侯菲利普·克里斯托夫·冯·瑟特恩借法国为援，1635年被西班牙军队掳走囚禁十年，1645年获释后由蒂雷纳率领法军收复城市。从1630年代起，选帝侯的主要宫廷迁到科布伦茨附近埃伦布赖特施泰因要塞山下的菲利普斯堡。1673年法军攻陷特里尔，拆毁城外诸修道院，1688至1698年及西班牙王位继承战争期间又数度占领，城中人口一度降至约四千。1794年法国革命军吞并特里尔，大主教选帝侯国随之解散；1815年特里尔划归普鲁士，卡尔·马克思于1818年出生于此。

en:
Upper Hesse is the southern Hessian country along the Lahn, a land of wooded ridges and market towns looking to Marburg. The town rose under the landgraves of Thuringia and became a place of pilgrimage after Elizabeth of Thuringia died there in 1231 and was canonized four years later; her great Gothic church was consecrated in 1283. In the Hessian-Thuringian succession war of 1247–1264, Sophie of Brabant secured the landgraviate for her son Henry, and Marburg became a Hessian residence beside Kassel. A partition in 1308 separated Upper from Lower Hesse, but the two parts were reunited in 1311. In 1444 the Catholic landgrave Louis I still ruled the whole territory, moving between Kassel and the castle above the Lahn.

After Louis I died in 1458, Henry III held Upper Hesse from Marburg until his line ended with William III in 1500, when the territory reverted to Lower Hesse. Philip I, born at Marburg in 1504, made the town a centre of the Reformation: he founded its Protestant university in 1527 and brought Luther and Zwingli together for the Marburg Colloquy of 1529. His death in 1567 divided Hesse among four sons, creating Hesse-Marburg. When that line died out in 1604, Lutheran Hesse-Darmstadt and Reformed Hesse-Kassel fought for the inheritance. Tilly took Marburg in 1623, and Landgravine Amalie Elisabeth's siege of 1645–1648 confirmed the Kasseler claim; the Peace of Westphalia left Marburg to Hesse-Kassel and Giessen to Hesse-Darmstadt. In 1807 the castle fortress was dismantled and the town passed into Napoleon's Kingdom of Westphalia.
zh:
上黑森是黑森南部、沿拉恩河展开的丘陵地带，马尔堡是这一带的核心城镇。图林根领地伯爵统治时期，马尔堡开始兴起；图林根的伊丽莎白1231年在此去世，四年后被封圣，使这里成为朝圣地，安放她灵柩的宏伟哥特式教堂于1283年祝圣。1247—1264年的黑森—图林根继承战争中，布拉班特的索菲为儿子海因里希争得领地伯爵之位，马尔堡从此与卡塞尔并列为黑森的两处驻地。1308年的一次分治曾把上黑森与下黑森分开，但两地1311年重新合并。1444年，天主教徒领地伯爵路德维希一世仍统治着整个黑森，在卡塞尔和拉恩河畔的城堡之间往返理政。

路德维希一世1458年去世后，海因里希三世以马尔堡为驻地领有上黑森；这一支至1500年威廉三世去世而绝嗣，土地重归下黑森。1504年生于马尔堡的菲利普一世把此城变成宗教改革中心：他1527年创办新教大学，又在1529年邀请路德与茨温利举行马尔堡会谈。1567年他去世后，黑森由四个儿子瓜分，黑森—马尔堡由此建立。该支1604年绝嗣后，路德宗的黑森—达姆施塔特与归正宗的黑森—卡塞尔为继承遗产长期交战。蒂利1623年攻占马尔堡，领地伯爵夫人阿马莉·伊丽莎白1645—1648年围城，最终确立卡塞尔一方的权利；《威斯特伐利亚和约》把马尔堡划归黑森—卡塞尔，把吉森划归黑森—达姆施塔特。1807年，山上城堡的防御工事被拆毁，马尔堡并入拿破仑建立的威斯特伐利亚王国。

en:
Westfalen here means the wooded Sauerland territory ruled by the archbishop-electors of Cologne, not every later Westphalian land. In 1180, after Henry the Lion's fall, Emperor Frederick Barbarossa granted Archbishop Philip of Heinsberg the south-western Saxon remnant as the Duchy of Westphalia; Cologne parishes and abbeys such as Grafschaft, founded in 1072, had already tied the Lippe and Sauerland country to the see. Purchase of the Arnsberg lands in 1368 joined Cologne's scattered districts. In 1437 knights and towns leagued against arbitrary taxation, and in 1444 Soest, the richest town, rejected Archbishop Dietrich von Moers and submitted to Cleves, beginning the Soest Feud. The Catholic Cologne duchy thus entered the period losing its fertile northern market while upland Arnsberg assumed the role of capital.

The Soest Feud ended in 1449 with Soest under Cleves, while Cologne kept Fredeburg and Bilstein; after the estates' agreement of 1463, the duchy's borders changed little until secularization. The Reformation won only scattered followers until the crisis under Archbishop Gebhard Truchsess and the Cologne War. Archbishop Ernest of Bavaria recovered the territory with Bavarian troops in 1583, and after 1612 Jesuit missions, visitations and new religious houses anchored the Counter-Reformation. The Thirty Years' War brought plundering armies, plague and a long decline in iron mining and hammer works. Arnsberg Castle was destroyed in 1762 during the Seven Years' War, leaving heavy debts. The Cologne cathedral chapter took refuge at Arnsberg in 1794, bringing the Three Kings shrine; Hesse-Darmstadt occupied the duchy in 1802 and the imperial secularization of 1803 confirmed the transfer. The Congress of Vienna awarded the land to Prussia in 1815, and Arnsberg became a Prussian administrative seat after the handover in 1816.
zh:
这里的威斯特法伦指科隆大主教兼选帝侯统治的林地绍尔兰，而不是后世泛指的整个威斯特伐利亚。1180年狮子亨利倒台后，皇帝腓特烈一世把萨克森公国的西南余部封给大主教海因斯贝格的菲利普，设立威斯特伐利亚公国；早在1072年格拉夫沙夫特修道院建立后，科隆的堂区和修院就已把利珀河与绍尔兰乡村同大主教区联结起来。1368年购得阿恩斯贝格领地，使科隆属下分散的辖区连成一片。1437年，骑士和城市因抗税结盟；1444年，最富庶的索斯特拒绝承认大主教迪特里希·冯·默尔斯，转投克莱沃，索斯特之争爆发。这个天主教科隆领地因此在新时期一开始便失去北方肥沃市场，山地中的阿恩斯贝格则承担起首府角色。

索斯特之争于1449年结束，索斯特留在克莱沃手中，科隆则保住弗德堡和比尔施泰因；1463年等级协定后，公国边界直到世俗化前都变化很小。宗教改革起初只赢得零星信徒，但在大主教格布哈特·特鲁赫泽斯任内和科隆战争中再度扩展。1583年，巴伐利亚的恩斯特依靠巴伐利亚军队收复公国；1612年后，耶稣会传教、教务巡查和新修院巩固了反宗教改革。三十年战争带来军队劫掠、瘟疫，也造成铁矿开采和锻造业长期衰退。1762年七年战争期间，阿恩斯贝格城堡被毁，地区背负沉重债务。1794年，科隆主教座堂议会带着三王圣龛退到阿恩斯贝格；黑森—达姆施塔特在1802年占领公国，1803年的帝国世俗化决议确认了这次移交。1815年维也纳会议把这片土地判给普鲁士，1816年实际交接后，阿恩斯贝格成为普鲁士的行政中心。

en:
Nassau was the wooded country between the Taunus and Westerwald, cut by the Lahn and linked by Rhine crossings to Mainz. Nassau Castle became the seat of its counts in 1159 and gave the dynasty its name; Nassau lords acquired the royal estate at Wiesbaden around 1170. In 1255 Walram II and Otto I divided their inheritance, the younger Ottonian line later producing the princes of Orange while the Walramian line kept Weilburg, Idstein and Wiesbaden. Adolf of Nassau ruled as king of Germany from 1292 to 1298 and founded Klarenthal Abbey near Wiesbaden in 1296. The town had hot springs known since Roman Aquae Mattiacorum and received coinage rights in 1329, but Mainz forces destroyed it in 1242 and war with Eppstein brought fresh destruction in 1283. Repeated partitions left the Catholic, Rhenish province of 1444 a patchwork of Nassau counties.

Mining in the Taunus is documented from 1495, when lead, silver, gold and copper were worked in the wooded hills. Wolf Denthener introduced the Lutheran Reformation at Wiesbaden in 1543, and the Old Town Hall was built in 1609-10. After further inheritances Wiesbaden passed to Nassau-Idstein in 1629 and to Nassau-Usingen in 1728; Biebrich Palace became the principal Nassau-Usingen residence in 1744. The Napoleonic settlement of 1806 united the Walramian principalities as the Duchy of Nassau with Wiesbaden as its capital. The Congress of Vienna added the former Orange-Nassau districts in 1815, reuniting most German Nassau lands after centuries of division, and William of Nassau-Weilburg began his rule as duke in 1816.
zh:
拿骚是陶努斯山与韦斯特林山之间的林木之地，兰河穿行其间，经莱茵河渡口与美因茨相连。1159年，拿骚堡成为这一家族伯爵的驻地并赋予其家族名号；约1170年，拿骚领主取得威斯巴登的王室地产。1255年，瓦拉姆二世与奥托一世分割遗产，幼子奥托一支后来诞生了奥兰治亲王，瓦拉姆一支则保有魏尔堡、伊德施泰因和威斯巴登。拿骚的阿道夫1292年至1298年任德意志国王，并于1296年在威斯巴登附近创立克拉伦塔尔修道院。威斯巴登的温泉在罗马时代的阿夸埃马蒂亚科鲁姆已为人所知，1329年又取得铸币权，但城市1242年遭美因茨军队摧毁，1283年与埃普施泰因的冲突再带来破坏。历经多次分封，1444年这个信仰天主教、使用莱茵文化语言的省份成为拿骚诸伯国拼成的棋盘。

陶努斯山的采矿活动有1495年以来的文献记载，林木山丘中出产铅、银、金和铜。1543年，沃尔夫·登特赫纳在威斯巴登引入路德宗宗教改革；旧市政厅建于1609年至1610年。经历更多继承变动后，威斯巴登1629年归入拿骚-伊德施泰因，1728年转入拿骚-乌辛根；1744年，比布里希宫成为拿骚-乌辛根的主要驻地。1806年拿破仑改组德意志，瓦拉姆系诸领地合并为拿骚公国，以威斯巴登为都。1815年维也纳和会把原奥兰治-拿骚地区并入，使多数德意志拿骚领地在数百年分裂后重新合流；1816年，威廉·冯·拿骚-魏尔堡开始以公爵身份统治。

en:
Berg held the right bank of the Rhine between Cologne and the Ruhr, with the Wupper towns behind Düsseldorf at the mouth of the Düssel. Its counts ruled from Schloss Burg above the Wupper from 1133, and Düsseldorf came under Berg in 1186, received ferry rights in 1263, and was granted town rights by Count Adolf of Berg on 14 August 1288 after the victory at Worringen. On 24 May 1380, at Aachen, Wenceslaus raised Margrave William II to ducal rank; William then moved his seat from the inland castle to Düsseldorf, where a residence was documented in 1382 and the court lived from 1386. Adolf of Berg inherited Jülich in 1423, and on his death in 1437 Gerhard II succeeded to the combined Jülich-Berg lands. In 1444 the Catholic, Rhenish duchy drew wealth from Rhine traffic, urban cloth trades and the growing Wupper valley towns.

The Klever Union of 1496 arranged the Jülich-Berg succession: John III of Cleves married Maria of Jülich-Berg in 1510, inherited Jülich, Berg and Ravensberg in 1511, and joined them with Cleves and Mark in 1521. When that united dynasty died out in 1609, Ambrosio Spinola occupied Düsseldorf during the succession dispute, and the Treaty of Xanten in 1614 assigned Berg to Wolfgang William of Palatinate-Neuburg, whose conversion and Jesuit patronage brought the Counter-Reformation. Johann Wilhelm, the popular 'Jan Wellem', kept Düsseldorf as his electoral residence from 1690 and founded its painting gallery around 1705. By then Elberfeld and Barmen were becoming textile centres while Solingen and Remscheid made blades. French troops occupied Düsseldorf in 1795; in 1806 Napoleon made Berg a grand duchy under Joachim Murat, until the settlement of 1815 gave the country to Prussia.
zh:
贝格据有莱茵河右岸、科隆与鲁尔河之间的土地，杜塞尔河汇入莱茵河处的杜塞尔多夫是门户，后方则是伍珀河诸城。1133年起，贝格伯爵以居高临下的伯格城堡为驻地；杜塞尔多夫1186年归入贝格，1263年取得渡河权，并在沃林根战役获胜后，于1288年8月14日由贝格伯爵阿道夫授予城市权。1380年5月24日，文策尔在亚琛把威廉二世提升为公爵；威廉随即把统治中心从内陆城堡迁到莱茵河畔的杜塞尔多夫，当地宫殿1382年见诸文献，宫廷自1386年起常驻。1423年，贝格的阿道夫继承于利希；他1437年去世后，格哈德二世接统合并的于利希-贝格领地。1444年，这个信仰天主教、使用莱茵文化语言的公国靠莱茵河商运、城市呢绒贸易和成长中的伍珀河谷城镇致富。

1496年的《克莱沃联盟》安排了于利希-贝格继承：克莱沃的约翰三世1510年娶于利希-贝格的玛丽亚，1511年继承于利希、贝格和拉文斯贝格，1521年又把这些领地与克莱沃和马克合并。1609年联合王朝绝嗣，安布罗西奥·斯皮诺拉在继承争端中占领杜塞尔多夫；1614年《克桑滕条约》把贝格分给普法尔茨-诺伊堡的沃尔夫冈·威廉，他改宗天主教并庇护耶稣会，推动反宗教改革。受人爱戴的约翰·威廉（「扬·韦勒姆」）1690年起以杜塞尔多夫为选帝侯驻地，并在1705年前后建立绘画陈列馆。此时埃尔伯费尔德和巴门正成为纺织中心，索林根与雷姆沙伊德则以刀剑制造闻名。1795年法军占领杜塞尔多夫；1806年拿破仑把贝格建为若阿尚·缪拉治下的大公国，直到1815年的和约把这片土地划归普鲁士。

en:
Cologne was the Colonia of the Roman Rhine and, from late antiquity, the seat of an archbishopric. In 1164 Archbishop Rainald of Dassel brought the relics of the Three Kings from Milan to its cathedral, drawing pilgrims in their thousands; the present cathedral was begun in 1248 to house them. The city stood where the Rhine crossed the road from Venice to the North Sea, and the staple right of 1259, forcing every passing cargo to be offered to its merchants first, made it one of the richest trading cities north of the Alps, with the Cologne mark the standard weight across wide tracts of the Empire. In 1288 its burghers, fighting beside Count Adolf V of Berg, defeated Archbishop Siegfried at Worringen, after which the prelates kept to Bonn and might enter the city only for religious acts. The patrician council was overthrown without bloodshed in 1396 and replaced by the Verbundbrief, a guild constitution built on twenty-two Gaffeln, and in 1388 the city had opened its university, the fourth in the Empire. In 1444 staunchly Catholic Cologne was among the largest and richest cities of the Empire, a merchant republic in all but name while its archbishop-elector ruled the surrounding lands from Bonn.

Emperor Frederick III confirmed Cologne's imperial immediacy in 1475, and the city held fast to the old faith when the Reformation divided Germany, though work on the cathedral was halted around 1560. In 1582 Archbishop Gebhard Truchsess von Waldburg married a Protestant canoness and proclaimed parity of the confessions, refusing to surrender his electorate under the ecclesiastical reservation; excommunicated and replaced by Ernest of Bavaria, he unleashed the Cologne War of 1583–88, which sacked Bonn, Neuss and Deutz but never breached the walls of Cologne. During the Thirty Years' War the city bought off passing armies, sold arms to the Catholic powers and emerged unscathed. In 1709 Eau de Cologne was first distilled there. French revolutionary troops entered the undefended city without a fight on 6 October 1794; under the Treaty of Lunéville of 1801 the left bank passed to France, Cologne became an arrondissement of the department of the Roer, and in 1798 the French closed its medieval university. In 1815 the Congress of Vienna assigned Cologne to Prussia.
zh:
科隆本是罗马人在莱茵河畔建立的殖民城，自古典时代晚期起便是大主教驻地。1164年，大主教赖纳尔德·冯·达瑟尔把三王圣骸从米兰带回科隆，引来数以千计的朝圣者；现存的大教堂于1248年动工，正是为安放圣骸而建。科隆地处莱茵河与威尼斯至北海商路的交会处，1259年取得的堆栈权规定途经货物须先向本地商人发卖，使它成为阿尔卑斯山以北最富庶的商业城市之一，「科隆马克」衡制通行帝国大片地区。1288年，科隆市民联合贝格伯爵阿道夫五世在沃林根击败大主教齐格弗里德，此后大主教避居波恩，非因宗教事务不得入城。1396年，贵族议会被和平推翻，取而代之的是《联合书》——一部以二十二个行会「加弗尔」为基础的等级宪法；1388年，科隆还创办了帝国境内第四所大学。1444年的科隆坚守天主教，是帝国最大、最富庶的城市之一，实质上是个商人共和国，而大主教选帝侯只能在波恩统治周边领地。

1475年，皇帝腓特烈三世正式确认科隆的帝国直辖地位。宗教改革分裂德意志之际，科隆坚守旧信仰，大教堂工程却在1560年前后停工。1582年，大主教格布哈德·特鲁赫泽斯·冯·瓦尔德堡与一名新教修女结婚，宣布两教平等，又拒绝援引「教士保留条款」辞去选帝侯之位；他被教皇开除教籍，巴伐利亚的恩斯特被选为继任者，莱茵兰由此陷入1583至1588年的科隆战争，波恩、诺伊斯和多伊茨遭兵燹劫掠，而科隆城垣始终未破。三十年战争中，科隆用金钱打发过境军队，向天主教列强贩卖军火，竟得安然无恙。1709年，「古龙水」首次在此蒸馏问世。1794年10月6日，法国革命军队兵不血刃进入不设防的科隆；依1801年《吕内维尔和约》，莱茵河左岸并入法国，科隆成为鲁尔省的一个专区，1798年法国人又关闭了它的中世纪大学。1815年，维也纳会议把科隆划归普鲁士。

en:
Münster began as Mimigernaford, a small Saxon settlement at a ford of the Aa. In 793 the Frisian missionary Liudger founded a monastery there—monasterium, which gave the town its name—and in 805 he became its first bishop, with the first cathedral standing by 850. Chartered in 1170, it ringed itself with walls some four kilometres long and became the largest city in Westphalia by area. Government rested with the hereditary patrician families known as the Erbmänner, who alone sat on the council until 1458 and represented the city at Hansetage. The linen trade of the Prinzipalmarkt made Münster a Hanseatic power from the mid-fourteenth century and, after 1494, the leading Westphalian city of the League. In 1444 the prince-bishopric was held by Heinrich von Moers, who also administered Osnabrück, while his self-assured capital guarded its liberties against him.

After Heinrich's death the Diocesan Feud of 1450–1457 set Walram von Moers against Erich von Hoya and left neither side a victor. The Reformation entered with the preacher Bernd Rothmann, and when the radical Anabaptists around Jan van Leiden won the council election of 23 February 1534 they seized the town, abolished infant baptism and, in September 1534, proclaimed the kingdom of Zion with Jan as its king. On 24 June 1535, after more than a year of siege and starvation, the troops of Bishop Franz von Waldeck stormed the city; its Anabaptist leaders were tortured to death and their bodies hung from the tower of St. Lamberti in three iron baskets, as a warning. Münster stayed Catholic, and from 1643 to 1648 its town hall housed the Catholic side of the Westphalian peace congress; the peace of 24 October 1648 ended both the Thirty Years' War and the Eighty Years' War. When the burghers sought the status of a free imperial city, Bishop Christoph Bernhard von Galen retook Münster in 1661 after an eight-month siege and stripped it of its privileges. The university opened in 1780, in the years when Johann Conrad Schlaun was raising the vast baroque Schloss. Prussian troops occupied the city in 1802; French-backed rule followed through the Grand Duchy of Berg from 1808 and direct annexation from 1811, until Prussian and Russian troops returned in November 1813. From 1815 Münster was the capital of the Prussian province of Westphalia.
zh:
明斯特的前身是阿河渡口旁的萨克森小聚落米米杰纳福德。793年，弗里斯兰传教士柳德格在此建起修道院（monasterium），城市由此得名；805年他成为首任主教，到850年前后第一座主教座堂已经落成。1170年明斯特获得城市权，筑起长约四公里的城墙，成为威斯特伐利亚面积最大的城市。市政长期由被称为「世袭家族」的城市贵族把持，1458年以前只有他们能进入市议会，并代表城市出席汉萨议会。亲王市场上那些山墙商馆里成交的亚麻布，使明斯特从14世纪中叶起成为汉萨重镇，1494年起更成为同盟在威斯特伐利亚的领衔城市。1444年，主教之位由身兼奥斯纳布吕克行政官的海因里希·冯·默尔斯占据，而他这座自负的都城处处防范，维护着自己的自由。

海因里希死后，1450年至1457年的主教继承争端使瓦尔拉姆·冯·默尔斯与埃里希·冯·霍亚兵戎相见，两败俱伤。宗教改革随传教士贝恩特·罗特曼而来；1534年2月23日，莱顿的约翰周围的激进再洗礼派在议会选举中获胜，随即控制全城、废除婴儿洗礼，并于1534年9月建立锡安王国，约翰自立为王。经过一年多的围困与饥饿，主教弗朗茨·冯·瓦尔德克的军队于1535年6月24日破城；再洗礼派首领被酷刑处死，尸体装入三只铁篮悬挂在圣兰贝蒂教堂塔楼示众。明斯特此后恪守天主教，1643年至1648年，市政厅承办威斯特伐利亚和会的天主教一方；1648年10月24日签署的和约同时结束了三十年战争和八十年战争。市民谋求帝国自由城市地位，主教克里斯托夫·伯恩哈德·冯·加伦遂经八个月围城于1661年攻克明斯特，褫夺其特权。大学于1780年创立，同期约翰·康拉德·施劳恩主持修建了宏伟的巴洛克宫殿。1802年，布吕歇尔率普鲁士军队占领城市；此后法国势力先后以贝格大公国（1808年起）和直接吞并（1811年起）的形式统治此地，1813年11月普鲁士与俄国军队卷土重来。1815年起，明斯特成为普鲁士威斯特伐利亚省的省会。

en:
Calais faces the white cliffs of Dover across the narrowest strait of the Channel, just thirty-four kilometres of water from England. It began as a fishing village on a low island amid the marshes, chartered in 1181 by the Count of Boulogne, and owed its fame to its harbour. Edward III of England besieged it for eleven months after Crécy and took it in 1347; six leading citizens came out barefoot with ropes around their necks to surrender, and Queen Philippa begged their lives. The French inhabitants were expelled and replaced by English settlers, and the Treaty of Brétigny in 1360 confirmed the town and its small 'Pale' of Guînes and Marck in English hands. Made a staple port in 1363, Calais grew rich on wool, tin, lead and cloth, 'the brightest jewel in the English crown', its customs sometimes yielding a third of the English crown's revenue; of its 12,000 people more than five thousand lived by the wool trade. A Burgundian army under Philip the Good failed to storm it in 1436, and in 1444 Calais is the last English foothold in France, a costly garrison town guarding the shortest sea crossing.

Henry VIII came to Calais in 1532, when the town had stabling for some two thousand horses, but the English reign there was nearly done. On 8 January 1558, after two hundred and ten years, the Duke of Guise surprised the forts and sluices and retook the town for Henry II; Queen Mary of England is said to have declared that 'Calais' would be found lying in her heart after her death, and Elizabeth I renounced the English claim only in the Treaty of Troyes of 1564. War returned before the century ended: on 24 April 1596 Archduke Albert of Austria seized Calais for Spain from the Netherlands, and the Treaty of Vervins gave it back to France in May 1598; another Spanish coup was beaten off in 1657. Through the following decades it remained a haunt of privateers and smugglers while Dunkirk and Boulogne drew off its trade, and in 1805 Napoleon quartered part of his Army of England and its invasion flotilla in the harbour.
zh:
加莱隔着英吉利海峡最窄的水道与多佛尔的白崖相望，距英格兰仅三十四公里。它原是沼泽中一座低矮沙洲岛上的渔村，1181年由布洛涅伯爵授予城市特许状，全凭港口成就声名。克雷西会战后，英格兰国王爱德华三世围城十一个月，于1347年拿下加莱；六名市民领袖赤足、颈系绳索出城请死，经王后菲莉帕求情才保住性命。城中的法兰西居民被逐走，换成英格兰移民；1360年的《布勒丁尼条约》确认加莱连同圭讷、马尔克一带的「加莱帕莱」归英格兰所有。1363年加莱被定为大宗土产贸易港，靠羊毛、锡、铅和布匹致富，被誉为「英格兰王冠上最亮的宝石」，关税有时占到英格兰王室岁入的三分之一；全城一万两千居民中，五千多人靠羊毛贸易为生。勃艮第公爵好人腓力1436年强攻不克。1444年的加莱是英格兰在法兰西的最后立足点，一座耗费巨大的驻军城镇，守着这条最短的跨海通道。

亨利八世1532年亲临加莱，当时城中厩舍可容约两千匹马，但英格兰在此的统治已近尾声。1558年1月8日，吉斯公爵突袭要塞和水闸，为亨利二世收复加莱，结束了二百一十年的英格兰占领；据说英格兰女王玛丽曾悲叹，死后剖开她的胸膛，会看到「加莱」刻在她心上，伊丽莎白一世直到1564年的《特鲁瓦条约》才正式放弃对加莱的主权。世纪末战火重燃：1596年4月24日，奥地利的阿尔布雷希特大公从尼德兰出兵替西班牙夺下加莱，1598年5月的《韦尔万条约》又把它归还法国；1657年西班牙人的另一次偷袭被击退。此后数十年间，这里始终是私掠船和走私者出没之地，贸易渐渐被敦刻尔克和布洛涅分走。1805年，拿破仑的征英大军及入侵舰队曾有一部分驻扎在加莱港。

en:
Artois takes its name from the Atrebates, the Gallic tribe whose capital Nemetocenna became Arras. Absorbed for a time by Flanders, it passed to the French crown in 1180 as the dowry of Isabelle of Hainaut, wife of Philip Augustus, and became a county again in 1237 for Robert, the king's grandson; inheritance brought it to the dukes of Burgundy in 1384. Arras had grown rich earlier than the Flemish cloth towns: by the eleventh century it led the wool trade of the north, and its tapestries were so prized that arrazzi in Italian and 'arras' in English came to mean any hanging of the kind; wealthy merchants patronised trouvères such as Adam de la Halle and Jean Bodel, and the city may have held some 35,000 people at its peak. In 1435 the Congress of Arras, meeting in the city, reconciled Charles VII with Duke Philip the Good and drew Burgundy out of its English alliance. In 1444 Artois is a province of the Burgundian Netherlands, Arras a cloth city whose trade is drifting north to Bruges and Ghent.

When Charles the Bold was killed in 1477 Louis XI's troops seized Arras; after the city revolted the king stormed it, razed its walls, expelled the burgher families and renamed the town Franchise. The Peace of Arras of 1482 and the Treaty of Senlis of 1493 left Artois with the Habsburgs, and the wars of Francis I against Charles V drained its textile towns until by 1525 barely a hundred merchants remained in Arras. The province stayed Catholic through the Dutch revolt: the Union of Arras of January 1579 bound the loyal southern provinces to Philip II and was answered within weeks by the Union of Utrecht. On 9 August 1640, after a two-month siege, the armies of Louis XIII and Richelieu stormed Arras, d'Artagnan serving in the royal guards; Turenne relieved a Spanish counter-siege in 1654, the Treaty of the Pyrenees of 1659 confirmed Artois as a French province, and Vauban soon girded its towns with new fortresses. Robespierre, born at Arras in 1758, went to Versailles in 1789 as a deputy of Artois, and the Terror under Joseph Le Bon sent roughly four hundred of its citizens to the guillotine in 1793–94.
zh:
阿图瓦得名于高卢部落阿特雷巴特人，他们的首府内梅托肯纳后来成为阿拉斯。这里本是被佛兰德吞并的封建伯国，1180年随埃诺的伊莎贝尔嫁给腓力·奥古斯特的嫁妆归入法兰西王室，1237年又封给国王之孙罗贝尔、重建为伯国；1384年因继承转入勃艮第公爵之手。阿拉斯的致富早于佛兰德诸城：11世纪时它已是北方羊毛贸易之首，出产的挂毯极负盛名，意大利语的arrazzi和英语的arras都成了挂毯的代名词；富有的商人资助了亚当·德·阿尔、让·博代尔等行吟诗人，城市极盛时人口约有三万五千。1435年，阿拉斯会议在此召开，促成查理七世与勃艮第公爵好人腓力和解，使勃艮第退出与英格兰的同盟。1444年的阿图瓦是勃艮第尼德兰的一个省份，阿拉斯虽是呢绒名城，贸易的重心却正流向北方的布鲁日和根特。

1477年大胆查理战死，遗产之争把全省拖入战火：路易十一的军队当年5月占领阿拉斯，城市再度反叛后，国王强攻得手，拆毁城墙，逐走市民家族，还把城市改名为「弗朗什兹」。1482年的《阿拉斯和约》和1493年的《桑利斯条约》最终把阿图瓦留给了哈布斯堡家族；弗朗索瓦一世与查理五世之间的战争耗尽了这里的呢绒城镇，到1525年阿拉斯只剩下约一百名商人。尼德兰起义期间全省坚守天主教：1579年1月的阿拉斯同盟把效忠西班牙的南方各省绑在腓力二世旗下，几周后乌得勒支同盟便针锋相对地成立。1640年8月9日，路易十三和黎塞留的大军围城两个月后攻陷阿拉斯，达达尼昂此时正在王家卫队中服役；1654年蒂雷纳为城市解了西班牙人的反扑之围，1659年的《比利牛斯条约》确认阿图瓦成为法国行省，沃邦不久又为各城筑起新式要塞。1758年生于阿拉斯的罗伯斯庇尔1789年作为阿图瓦的代表前往凡尔赛；1793至1794年约瑟夫·勒邦主持的恐怖统治把约四百名市民送上了断头台。

en:
Amiens began as Samarobriva, the 'bridge over the Somme' of the Ambiani, one of the chief tribes of Gaul; the Romans called the town Ambianum. Vikings plundered it in 859 and again in 881–882, when they used it as a base before burning it, but by the twelfth century it was a self-governing commune, its sworn charter recognised by Louis VI in 1113, and Philip Augustus attached it to the French crown in 1185. Its merchants grew rich on woollen cloth and on woad, the blue dye called waide in Picard, a 'blue gold' which helped pay for the cathedral begun in 1220, the largest of all Gothic churches. Kings made its choir a stage: in 1264 Louis IX issued there his Mise of Amiens between Henry III and his barons, in 1329 Edward III of England knelt in the cathedral to do homage to Philip VI, and in 1385 Charles VI married Isabeau of Bavaria in the city. The Hundred Years' War brought Crécy in 1346 and Agincourt in 1415 on Picard ground, and the Treaty of Arras of 1435 handed Amiens to Burgundy. In 1444 Picardy is a Burgundian march on the Somme, its cloth trade shaken by war and Flemish competition.

Louis XI brought the city back to the crown in 1477 and confirmed its communal liberties, after which Amiens found new life in the light worsteds of the sayetterie; the king licensed two yearly fairs, and its merchants shipped cloth as far as Portugal, Italy and the Antilles. The city stood with the Catholic League in the Wars of Religion and opened its gates to Henry IV only in August 1594. On 11 March 1597 a Spanish force from Doullens took the town by a trick, scattering a cartload of walnuts at the gate to rush the guards; Henry IV returned with an army and retook Amiens on 25 September, after a six-month siege. Through the eighteenth century the city lived on its velvet manufacture, and in March 1790 it became the capital of the new department of the Somme. In its town hall, on 25 March 1802, France and Britain signed the Peace of Amiens, which briefly brought the wars of the Revolution to an end.
zh:
亚眠最初是高卢大族安比亚尼人的撒马罗布里瓦，意为「索姆河上的桥」，罗马人称之为安比亚努姆。维京人859年、881—882年两度袭城，第二次还把这里占为据点后付之一炬；但到12世纪，它已是自治的城市公社，1113年宣誓的公社特许状得到路易六世承认，1185年腓力·奥古斯特把它并入王室领地。市民靠呢绒和一种蓝色染料——皮卡第方言称waide的菘蓝——致富，这种「蓝色黄金」为1220年动工的大教堂提供了部分营建费用，那是哥特式教堂中规模最大的一座。国王们把这里的祭坛当作舞台：1264年路易九世在此作出裁断亨利三世与其贵族之争的《亚眠判决》，1329年英格兰国王爱德华三世在大教堂向腓力六世行臣服礼，1385年查理六世在此迎娶巴伐利亚的伊莎博。百年战争中，1346年克雷西、1415年阿赞库尔两场大战都在皮卡第的土地上进行，1435年的《阿拉斯条约》把亚眠割给了勃艮第。1444年的皮卡第是勃艮第治下索姆河畔的边省，呢绒贸易饱受战火和佛兰德竞争的打击。

1477年路易十一把城市收归王室，确认其公社自由；此后亚眠靠一种轻薄毛料sayetterie重振生计，国王批准每年开设两次集市，商人把布匹一直卖到葡萄牙、意大利和安的列斯群岛。宗教战争中，城市站在天主教同盟一边，直到1594年8月才向亨利四世打开城门。1597年3月11日，一支来自杜朗的西班牙军队用诡计夺城——在城门口掀翻一车核桃，趁乱制服守卫；亨利四世率大军回攻，围城六个月，于9月25日复克亚眠。整个18世纪，城市以丝绒织造为业，1790年3月成为新设索姆省的省会。1802年3月25日，法国与英国在亚眠市政厅签订《亚眠和约》，革命战争一度就此终结。

en:
Bruges grew up on the little river Reie, where a ninth-century Flemish stronghold guarded the coastal crossing. It became the capital of the counts of Flanders in 1089 and was walled after its city charter of 1128, and English wool made it the greatest of the Flemish cloth towns. A storm in 1134 opened the sea arm called the Zwin, carrying ocean-going ships to the outports of Damme and Sluys; in 1277 the first Genoese fleet sailed in, opening the trades of the Mediterranean, and Hanseatic, Castilian and Portuguese merchants took their own houses here. The merchants' meeting house by the inn of the Van der Beurze family gave the world the word 'bourse'. In May 1302 the guildsmen killed the French garrison in the Bruges Matins and went on to the Battle of the Golden Spurs. By about 1350 perhaps 46,000 people lived inside the walls. In 1444 the city is at its zenith: Philip the Good of Burgundy keeps his court here, he founded the Order of the Golden Fleece at Bruges in 1430, and Jan van Eyck and the painters of the Flemish school work for its merchants and churches.

In 1473 William Caxton, working at Bruges with Colard Mansion, produced the first book printed in English. The golden age lasted only a generation longer. After Mary of Burgundy died in 1482 the city defied her widower Maximilian of Austria and even held him prisoner in the Craenenburg house in 1488; once free he turned the dynasty away from Bruges, while the Zwin silted and trade slipped to Antwerp. In the 1570s Bruges became a centre of Calvinism and briefly held a Protestant government in 1578, but in 1584 the duke of Parma retook it for Spain, and it remained a quiet Catholic city of the Spanish Netherlands through the seventeenth century, living by its lace; Charles II of England kept his exiled court here in the 1650s. The Peace of Utrecht in 1713 transferred it with the rest of the Spanish Netherlands to Austria. French armies overran it during the War of the Austrian Succession, until the Peace of Aachen returned it in 1748, and in 1794 Revolutionary France annexed the city. In 1815 Bruges became part of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.
zh:
布鲁日发端于赖厄河畔的一座九世纪佛兰德要塞，扼守沿海商路的渡口。1089年它成为佛兰德伯爵的驻地，1128年获城市特许状后筑起城墙；英格兰羊毛把它造就成佛兰德诸呢绒城中最大的一个。1134年的一场风暴冲出名为「兹温」的海湾，海船可直达外港达默和斯勒伊斯；1277年第一支热那亚船队驶入，地中海贸易由此打开，汉萨、卡斯蒂利亚和葡萄牙商人纷纷在此设立商馆。范·德尔·伯尔斯家族客栈前的广场是商人固定聚首之处，「交易所」（bourse）一词便来源于此。1302年5月，行会市民发动「布鲁日晨祷」，尽杀法军戍卒，随后投身金马刺之战。到1350年前后，城内人口约有四万六千。1444年的布鲁日正值鼎盛：勃艮第公爵腓力三世（「好人腓力」）在此设宫廷，并于1430年在布鲁日创立金羊毛骑士团；扬·凡·艾克等佛兰德画派大师为这里的商人和教堂作画。

1473年，威廉·卡克斯顿在布鲁日与科拉尔·芒西翁合作，印出了第一本英文书籍。但这座城市的黄金时代只延续了一代人。1482年勃艮第的玛丽去世后，布鲁日起而对抗她的丈夫奥地利的马克西米利安，1488年甚至把他囚禁在集市广场的克拉南堡客栈；马克西米利安脱身之后便把王朝宫廷迁出布鲁日，兹温水道又日渐淤塞，贸易重心随之让给安特卫普。1570年代，布鲁日成为加尔文宗的一个中心，1578年一度建立新教政权，但1584年帕尔马公爵为西班牙收复此城，整个17世纪它都是西属尼德兰一座安静的天主教城市，以蕾丝织造维持生计；1650年代，英格兰的查理二世曾把流亡朝廷设在这里。1713年《乌得勒支和约》把它连同西属尼德兰其余部分划给奥地利。奥地利王位继承战争期间法军曾占领此城，至1748年《亚琛和约》后归还；1794年它在革命战争中被法国吞并。1815年，布鲁日并入尼德兰联合王国。

en:
Hainaut, named after the Haine, was a French-speaking frontier county of the Holy Roman Empire. Mons grew up around the 7th-century oratory of Waltrude and the counts' castle, succeeding Valenciennes as capital of the county in 1295; its walls and market served a cloth-working countryside. West on the Scheldt, Tournai was older still, a Roman crossing that became a free city directly under the French Crown after 1187 and grew rich on English wool, tapestry and painters such as Robert Campin and Rogier van der Weyden. Philip the Good acquired Hainaut from the Bavarian inheritance in 1433, so in 1444 Mons was a Catholic Walloon town of the Burgundian Netherlands, while Tournai remained under the French Crown.

Mary of Burgundy's marriage to Maximilian in 1477 carried Hainaut to the Habsburgs. Henry VIII took Tournai in 1513, the city returned to France in 1519, and Charles V acquired it in 1521, four years after he had sworn at Mons as Count of Hainaut. Iconoclastic unrest reached Hainaut in 1566; Louis of Nassau seized Mons on 24 May 1572, but the Duke of Alba retook it on 21 September. Hainaut joined the Catholic, loyalist Union of Arras in 1579, whereas Calvinist Tournai, called the Geneva of the North, fell to Alessandro Farnese in 1581 after the defence led by Christine de Lalaing. Louis XIV's wars detached southern Hainaut in 1659 and 1678; French troops took Mons in 1691 and Tournai in 1668 and 1745, while the Treaty of Utrecht assigned northern Hainaut to Austria in 1713. Tournai porcelain manufacture began in 1750. After Jemappes in 1792, a brief Austrian restoration and Fleurus in 1794, France made Mons capital of the Jemappes department; the Mons-Condé canal, begun in 1800, carried Borinage coal toward France. In 1815 Hainaut passed to the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.
zh:
埃诺以埃讷河得名，是神圣罗马帝国境内讲法语的边境伯国。蒙斯围绕圣瓦德鲁7世纪建立的祈祷所和伯爵城堡发展，1295年继瓦朗谢讷之后成为伯国首府，城墙与市集服务着周边织布乡村。西边斯海尔德河畔的图尔奈更为古老，原为罗马渡口，1187年后成为直属法兰西王冠的自由城市；英格兰羊毛、挂毯作坊以及罗伯特·康平、罗希尔·范德魏登等画家使其富庶。「好人」腓力三世1433年从巴伐利亚继承权中取得埃诺，因此1444年的蒙斯已是勃艮第尼德兰的天主教瓦隆城镇，图尔奈却仍在法兰西王冠治下。

1477年勃艮第的玛丽嫁给马克西米利安后，埃诺转入哈布斯堡。亨利八世1513年攻占图尔奈，该城1519年归还法国，1521年又落入查理五世之手；四年前，查理曾在蒙斯以埃诺伯爵身份宣誓。1566年圣像破坏运动波及埃诺，路易·冯·拿骚1572年5月24日袭取蒙斯，阿尔瓦公爵在9月21日将其夺回。1579年埃诺加入忠于西班牙的天主教阿拉斯同盟；有「北方日内瓦」之称、信奉加尔文派的图尔奈，则在1581年被亚历山德罗·法尔内塞征服，克里斯蒂娜·德·拉兰曾主持守城。路易十四的战争在1659年和1678年割走南埃诺，法军1691年攻陷蒙斯，又在1668年和1745年攻占图尔奈；1713年乌得勒支和约把北埃诺交给奥地利。图尔奈瓷器制造业始于1750年。1792年热马普战役后法国一度入城，经历奥地利短暂恢复和1794年弗勒吕斯战役后，法国把蒙斯设为热马普省省会；1800年动工的蒙斯—孔代运河把博里纳日煤炭运往法国。1815年，埃诺并入尼德兰联合王国。

en:
Brussels grew up on the Senne, where a fortified crossing commanded the road between Bruges and Ghent and Cologne; its cloth trade paid for the first walls in the early 13th century and a second circuit in 1356–1383. North-east along the Dyle, Mechelen received city rights from John II of Brabant in 1303 and challenged Antwerp in wool, salt and cloth. When Philip the Good inherited Brabant in 1430, Brussels became one of the capitals of the Burgundian Netherlands, its Coudenberg palace set above a Flemish Catholic city of merchants and guilds. In 1444 Brussels and Mechelen were wealthy cloth towns at the heart of Philip's assembled inheritance.

After Charles the Bold's death in 1477, Mary of Burgundy's marriage to Maximilian of Austria tied the towns to the Habsburgs. Mechelen's high court, briefly set up by Charles in 1473, was restored as the Great Council in 1504; Margaret of Austria held her regency there from 1507 and raised the future Charles V, who was declared of age at Coudenberg in 1515 and abdicated there in 1555. Mechelen became an archdiocese in 1559, but revolt and war followed: Spanish troops sacked it in 1572, English garrison troops in 1580, and Brussels, Calvinist from 1577, fell to Spain after a siege in 1585. French bombardment in August 1695 destroyed about a third of Brussels, including the Grand-Place, whose guild houses were rapidly rebuilt. The War of the Spanish Succession transferred the southern Netherlands to Austria in 1713; French troops occupied Brussels in 1746–1749. The short-lived United Belgian States were proclaimed there in 1790, French armies annexed the region in 1795 and made Brussels capital of the Dyle department, and in 1815 Waterloo, just south of the city, ended Napoleonic rule.
zh:
布鲁塞尔兴起于塞讷河畔的设防渡口，控制布鲁日、根特通往科隆的商路；布匹贸易促成13世纪初第一道城墙和1356—1383年第二道城墙。东北方的梅赫伦位于代勒河畔，1303年从布拉班特公爵约翰二世手中获得城市权，在羊毛、盐和布匹贸易上与安特卫普争锋。1430年「好人」腓力三世继承布拉班特后，布鲁塞尔成为勃艮第尼德兰的都城之一，库登山城堡俯瞰这座佛兰德天主教商业与行会城市。1444年，布鲁塞尔和梅赫伦都是腓力聚合领地中富庶的布业城镇。

1477年大胆的查理死后，勃艮第的玛丽嫁给马克西米利安，两地随之卷入哈布斯堡霸业。梅赫伦高等法院1473年由大胆的查理设立，1504年作为梅赫伦大议会恢复；奥地利的玛格丽特1507年起在此摄政并抚养后来的查理五世。查理1515年在库登山宣告亲政，1555年又在此退位。梅赫伦1559年升为总教区，但叛乱与战争随即席卷：西班牙军队1572年洗劫该城，英格兰驻军1580年再度劫掠；布鲁塞尔1577年起建立加尔文派政权，1585年在围城中降于西班牙。1695年8月，法军炮轰布鲁塞尔，约三分之一城区包括大广场被毁，行会宅邸随后迅速重建。西班牙王位继承战争后，南尼德兰1713年转归奥地利，法军1746—1749年占领布鲁塞尔。1790年，短命的比利时合众国在此宣告成立；法军1795年兼并此地，设代勒省并以布鲁塞尔为省会。1815年，城南的滑铁卢结束了拿破仑统治。

en:
Liège grew up where the Ourthe joins the Meuse. In 985 Bishop Notger received secular lordship over the County of Huy, making his see an ecclesiastical state of the Holy Roman Empire; its schools were called the Athens of the North, and after 1345 the city's thirty-two guilds gave its citizens an unusually direct share in government. Namur stood higher upstream at the confluence of the Sambre and Meuse, where a rocky spur had carried the counts' castle since the 10th century; Philip the Good bought the County of Namur in 1421. In 1444 Liège was therefore an independent Catholic Walloon prince-bishopric, while Namur belonged to the Burgundian Netherlands, their roads and fortresses commanding the Meuse crossings.

In 1456 Philip the Good forced John of Heinsberg from the see and installed his nephew Louis de Bourbon. Liège revolted in 1465, 1467 and 1468, losing at Montenaken and Brustem; in October 1468 the six hundred Franchimontois failed to surprise Charles the Bold and Louis XI, and Charles sacked and burned the city. Mary of Burgundy renounced her rights over Liège in March 1477, and France and Maximilian recognized its neutrality in 1492. Érard de La Marck rebuilt the episcopal palace early in the next century, while Namur became a bishop's see in 1559. During the Eighty Years' War the principality protected the military corridor known as the Spanish Road. Louis XIV took Namur in 1692 and Vauban rebuilt its citadel, but William III recovered the town in 1695; the Treaty of Utrecht placed it under Austria in 1713. The Liège Revolution of 1789 created a republic until imperial troops restored the bishop in 1791. French forces entered in 1792, secured the region after Fleurus and Sprimont in 1794, and annexed the prince-bishopric in 1795, when St Lambert's Cathedral was destroyed. In 1815 the Meuse lands passed to the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.
zh:
列日兴起于乌尔特河注入默兹河之处。985年，主教诺特格尔受封于伊伯国的世俗统治权，使这个主教区成为神圣罗马帝国的教会邦国；列日的学校曾有「北方雅典」之名，1345年后城中三十二个行会更让市民获得低地罕见的直接参政权。那慕尔位于桑布尔河与默兹河交汇处，自10世纪起，岩角上的城堡就拱卫着同名伯国；「好人」腓力三世1421年买下那慕尔伯国。因此在1444年，列日是独立的天主教瓦隆亲王主教区，那慕尔则属于勃艮第尼德兰，两地道路和要塞控制着默兹河渡口。

1456年，腓力三世迫使海因斯贝格的约翰去职，安插外甥路易·德·波旁。列日人在1465年、1467年和1468年三次起兵，先后在蒙特纳肯和布吕斯泰姆战败；1468年10月，六百名弗朗希蒙人试图夜袭大胆的查理与路易十一的营地失败，列日随即遭洗劫焚毁。1477年3月，勃艮第的玛丽放弃对主教区的权利，法国和马克西米利安又在1492年承认其中立。16世纪初，埃拉尔·德·拉马克重建亲王府；那慕尔则在1559年成为主教驻地。八十年战争期间，亲王主教区拱卫着被称为「西班牙之路」的军事走廊。1692年路易十四攻占那慕尔，沃邦改造其城堡，威廉三世1695年夺回该城；1713年乌得勒支和约把它交给奥地利。1789年列日革命建立共和国，1791年被帝国军队颠覆。法军1792年一度进入，1794年弗勒吕斯和斯普里蒙战役后控制全区，1795年兼并亲王主教区，圣朗贝尔大教堂也被毁。1815年，这些默兹河流域土地并入尼德兰联合王国。

en:
Luxembourg grew around a castle on the Bock, a sandstone spur above the Alzette. In 963 Count Siegfried of the Ardennes acquired the little castellum of Lucilinburhuc from St Maximin's Abbey in Trier and built his fortress there, and a market town took shape below it. Countess Ermesinde granted the town its charter in 1244, and in 1354 Charles IV raised Luxembourg to a duchy. The house gave the Empire Henry VII, its first Luxemburger emperor, and John the Blind, king of Bohemia, who founded the town's great annual fair in 1340 and fell at Crécy six years later. Burgundian troops under Philip the Good took the city in 1443, so that in 1444 the duchy enters the age as the south-eastern stronghold of the Burgundian Netherlands, its cliffs already ringed with walls and towers.

On Charles the Bold's death in 1477 Luxembourg passed with the Burgundian inheritance to the Habsburgs. Francis I's troops overran the duchy twice in 1542, but Charles V retook it each time. In 1554 lightning struck a Franciscan convent whose attic was stored with gunpowder, and much of the upper town burned. The Spanish began the casemates in 1644, tunnelling 23 kilometres of galleries through the rock. The Treaty of the Pyrenees in 1659 stripped away Thionville and Montmédy, and in 1684 Vauban besieged and took the fortress, then rebuilt its works; France handed it back in 1697, and from 1714 it was Austrian. A republican army needed seven months to force its surrender on 6 June 1795, earning it the name 'Gibraltar of the North'. Luxembourg became the chief town of the French département des Forêts, and a peasant revolt flared across the countryside in 1798. In 1815 the Congress of Vienna made Luxembourg a grand duchy in personal union with the Netherlands, with a Prussian garrison in the fortress.
zh:
卢森堡城围绕博克岩上的城堡兴起，那块砂岩岬角俯瞰阿尔泽特河。963年，阿登伯爵齐格弗里德从特里尔的圣马克西米努斯修道院换得卢西林堡小寨，在岩顶筑起要塞，城下逐渐形成集市城镇。1244年女伯爵埃尔梅辛德授予城市特许状，1354年查理四世把卢森堡升为公国。卢森堡家族走出了神圣罗马皇帝亨利七世，还有波希米亚国王盲人约翰——他1340年为城市设立一年一度的大集市，六年后战死于克雷西。1443年好人菲利普的勃艮第军队攻占该城，因此到1444年，这座峭壁上早已城墙塔楼环列的公国，成为勃艮第尼德兰东南端的堡垒。

1477年大胆查理死后，卢森堡随勃艮第遗产转入哈布斯堡家族手中。1542年弗朗索瓦一世的军队两度攻陷公国，都被查理五世夺回。1554年雷电击中一座方济各会修道院，阁楼里储存的火药被引爆，上城大半焚毁。西班牙人1644年开始在岩壁中开凿坑道，建成23公里长的炮台地道。1659年《比利牛斯条约》割走蒂永维尔和蒙梅迪；1684年沃邦围攻并拿下要塞，随后重修工事，法国于1697年将其归还，1714年起归奥地利。1795年6月6日，共和国军队围城七个月才迫其投降，要塞由此得到「北方的直布罗陀」之称。卢森堡成为法国森林省的省会，1798年乡间还爆发了农民起义。1815年维也纳会议把卢森堡升为与荷兰君合的大公国，要塞中驻扎普鲁士军队。

en:
Breda grew up at the meeting of the Mark and Aa rivers, its name referring to the broad Aa. It first appears in a charter of 1125 and received its own municipal charter in 1252, after which brick walls and gates protected the town. In 1350 John III of Brabant sold the high lordship to John II of Polanen, and in 1403 Johanna of Polanen's marriage to Engelbert I of Nassau carried Breda into the House of Nassau. Their son John IV succeeded in 1442. In 1444, therefore, Breda was a fortified Catholic trading town in Brabant, locally governed as a Nassau lordship and already used as a residence by the family that would shape its later court.

Henry III of Nassau strengthened the works in 1534, the same year a great fire left only about 150 houses and the Grote Kerk standing. In July 1581 Spanish troops under Claudius van Barlaymont took the town during the Eighty Years' War, and more than 500 citizens died in the ensuing sack. In March 1590 Maurice of Nassau recovered Breda when sixty-eight picked men hid aboard Adriaen van Bergen's peat boat and seized a gate. Ambrogio Spinola's Spanish army then besieged the fortress for eleven months and received its surrender on 2 June 1625, a scene later painted by Diego Velázquez. Frederick Henry retook Breda between 21 July and 11 October 1637, and the Treaty of Münster assigned it to the Dutch Republic in 1648. Charles II issued his Declaration of Breda there in 1660, the Treaty of Breda ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War in 1667, and British and French negotiators met at the Congress of Breda in 1746–1748. French revolutionary forces captured the town in 1795.
zh:
布雷达兴起于马克河与阿河交汇处，地名意为宽阔的阿河。它最早见于1125年的一份特许状，1252年获得城市特许状，随后建起砖墙和城门。1350年，布拉班特公爵约翰三世把这片高级领地卖给波拉嫩的约翰二世；1403年，波拉嫩的约翰娜嫁给拿骚的恩格尔贝特一世，布雷达随之归入拿骚家族，其子约翰四世于1442年继位。因此在1444年，布雷达是布拉班特境内一座设防的天主教商业城镇，由拿骚家族作为领地统治，并已成为这一家族的驻地，日后的宫廷正由此发展。

1534年，拿骚的亨利三世加固城防；同年大火过后，全城只剩约一百五十栋房屋和大教堂还立着。八十年战争期间，克劳狄乌斯·范·巴莱蒙率领西班牙军队在1581年7月攻占城镇，随后的洗劫导致五百多名市民死亡。1590年3月，拿骚的莫里斯靠阿德里安·范·贝尔根的泥炭船计谋夺回布雷达：六十八名精兵藏在船中泥炭下面，入城后控制了城门。后来安布罗焦·斯皮诺拉率西班牙大军围城十一个月，于1625年6月2日受降，这个场面后由迭戈·委拉斯开兹绘成名画。腓特烈·亨德里克在1637年7月21日至10月11日间再次攻取布雷达，1648年《明斯特条约》将其划归尼德兰共和国。查理二世1660年在此发布《布雷达宣言》，1667年《布雷达条约》结束第二次英荷战争，英法则于1746—1748年召开布雷达会议。法国革命军队在1795年攻占布雷达。

en:
Zeeland is the chain of islands and peninsulas at the mouths of the Scheldt and Meuse. Flemish abbeys organized dikes and polders from the eleventh century; Middelburg received city rights in 1217, Zierikzee in 1248, and Vlissingen in 1315. Their people burned salt-impregnated peat to make sea salt, fished herring, and carried goods between England, Flanders and the Baltic. The County of Zeeland took shape in 1323, and in 1432 Philip the Good added it to his Burgundian Low Countries. In 1444 the Catholic, Dutch-speaking island towns were thus bound to the Burgundian state, prosperous from salt and shipping yet always dependent on dikes, tides and safe roadsteads.

Charles V forbade digging salt peat in 1515 because it weakened sea defences, after which Zierikzee and other towns refined imported raw salt. On 6 April 1572 Vlissingen drove out its pro-Spanish garrison without waiting for the Sea Beggars, while Middelburg held for Spain until a rebel siege ended in 1574. Zeeland joined the Union of Utrecht and became one of the seven United Provinces; from 1602 Middelburg's VOC chamber oversaw a quarter of the company's operations, while Vlissingen served as a major naval roadstead. In 1809 a British army landed on Walcheren and bombarded Vlissingen, but disease frustrated the move against Antwerp and the expedition withdrew. After French rule ended, Zeeland entered the United Kingdom of the Netherlands as a province in 1815.
zh:
泽兰是斯海尔德河与默兹河河口一带由岛屿和半岛组成的地区。11世纪起，佛兰德修道院组织修筑堤坝、围垦土地；米德尔堡1217年获得城市权，济里克泽1248年获得城市权，弗利辛恩则在1315年获得城市权。居民焚烧含盐泥炭制取海盐，捕捞鲱鱼，并在英格兰、佛兰德和波罗的海之间转运货物。泽兰伯国1323年成形，1432年被好人菲利普并入勃艮第尼德兰。因此在1444年，这些信奉天主教、操荷兰语的岛城归勃艮第政权统治，靠盐业和航运致富，却始终离不开堤坝、潮汐和安全锚地。

1515年，查理五世因挖取含盐泥炭会削弱海防而下令禁止，济里克泽等城转而精炼进口原盐。1572年4月6日，弗利辛恩不等海上乞丐支援便自行驱逐亲西班牙驻军；米德尔堡则为西班牙坚守，直到1574年被起义军长期围困后攻克。泽兰加入乌得勒支同盟，成为尼德兰七省之一；1602年后，米德尔堡的东印度公司泽兰商会掌管公司四分之一业务，弗利辛恩则是重要海军锚地。1809年，英军在瓦尔赫伦岛登陆并炮轰弗利辛恩，但疫病使进军安特卫普的计划失败，远征最终撤退。法国统治结束后，泽兰于1815年成为尼德兰联合王国的一个省。

en:
Amsterdam began as a fishing settlement at a dam in the Amstel, which the All Saints' Flood of 1170 threw open to the waters of the Zuiderzee. A dam was built there between 1264 and 1275, and in 1275 Count Floris V of Holland freed its people from tolls throughout the county; city rights followed shortly after 1300. The Miracle of the Host in 1345 made the young city a place of pilgrimage, but its future lay on the water. Its ships traded with the Hanseatic towns, and after the herring buss appeared in 1415 the fleet grew rich on cured herring and opened a direct Baltic trade in grain and timber, cutting out the Hanseatic middlemen. In 1444 Amsterdam belongs to the county of Holland, held since 1433 by the duke of Burgundy. It is still far smaller than the cloth cities of Flanders, yet it is already the staple market of northern Europe for bulk cargo, a town built, as the saying went, on herring bones.

In 1578, late among the towns of Holland, the Catholic town government was turned out in the Alteratie and Amsterdam joined the revolt against Spain. The fall of Antwerp in 1585 poured in Flemish merchants and printers together with Sephardic Jews, and the city entered its Golden Age. In 1602 its chamber of the new East India Company began trading its own shares, making Amsterdam the world's first stock exchange, and the Bank of Amsterdam opened in 1609. The concentric canal belt of merchants' houses and warehouses rose for a population that passed 100,000 in 1622 and 200,000 by the end of the seventeenth century, when Amsterdam was among the greatest cities in Europe. The Rampjaar of 1672 nearly destroyed all this, as French armies overran the border provinces and the republican regime of the De Witts gave way to William III as stadtholder. In 1787 a Prussian army marched in to restore the prince of Orange against the Patriot movement, and in the winter of 1795 French troops crossed the frozen rivers and the Batavian Republic was proclaimed. Louis Bonaparte made Amsterdam his capital in 1808 under the Kingdom of Holland, and from 1815 it was the capital of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands, by then a city of some 140,000 people.
zh:
阿姆斯特丹发端于阿姆斯特尔河上一座水坝旁的渔村。1170年的诸圣节洪水使艾河拓宽，此地由此通向须得海。水坝建于1264年至1275年间，1275年荷兰伯爵弗洛里斯五世下诏，免除「阿姆斯特尔水坝」居民在伯国境内的通行税；1300年之后不久，这里获得城市权利。1345年的圣体神迹使这座新城成为朝圣地，但它真正的前途在水上。14世纪起，阿姆斯特丹的船只已与汉萨诸城通商；1415年腌鲱鱼渔船问世后，船队靠腌制鲱鱼致富，并开辟了直通波罗的海的谷物木材航运，把汉萨中间商甩在一旁。1444年的阿姆斯特丹属于荷兰伯国，自1433年起由勃艮第公爵领有；它的规模还远不及佛兰德的呢绒诸城，却已是北欧大宗商品的集散中心，正所谓一座「建在鲱鱼骨头上的城市」。

1578年，在荷兰诸城中行动偏晚的阿姆斯特丹发生「改弦更张」，天主教市政府被推翻，城市加入反抗西班牙的起义。1585年安特卫普陷落后，佛兰德商人、印刷工匠和塞法迪犹太人大批涌入，城市由此步入黄金时代。1602年，新成立的东印度公司阿姆斯特丹分会开始买卖本公司股票，阿姆斯特丹因此成为世界上第一个股票交易所；阿姆斯特丹银行1609年开业。城市又开凿出一圈同心运河带，两岸建起商宅与仓库，人口1622年超过十万，到17世纪末突破二十万，跻身欧洲最大城市之列。1672年的「灾难年」险些断送这一切：法军横扫边境诸省，德·维特的共和政权倒台，威廉三世出任执政。1787年，普鲁士军队入城，帮助奥兰治亲王恢复了执政的权位；1795年的严冬里，法军越过封冻的界河，巴达维亚共和国宣告成立。1808年，路易·波拿巴在荷兰王国治下定都阿姆斯特丹；1815年起它成为尼德兰联合王国的首都，当时人口约十四万。

en:
Utrecht grew up at a Rhine ford where the Romans built the fort of Traiectum. Around 700 Willibrord used the old stronghold as a base for converting Frisia, and in 1024 the bishops became princes of the Holy Roman Empire. The town received city rights in 1122, built canalside wharves, and became a major northern market, with St Martin's Cathedral rising at its centre; the nave begun in 1420 was left unfinished as funds ran out. In 1444 Utrecht was still the Catholic, Dutch-speaking capital of a church state and the largest city of the northern Low Countries, yet the Utrecht Schism had set rival episcopal claimants and urban factions against one another since 1423.

In 1528 Charles V took the bishops' secular power, ended the prince-bishopric, and made the territory the Lordship of Utrecht, guarded by the new Vredenburg fortress. On 23 January 1579 northern provinces and towns concluded the Union of Utrecht in the city against Philip II, and the new Protestant state abolished the bishopric in 1580. Utrecht University was founded on 26 March 1636. French forces occupied the city during the disaster year of 1672; after their withdrawal a storm in 1674 brought down the unfinished cathedral nave. In 1713 the Peace of Utrecht, ending the War of the Spanish Succession, was negotiated and signed there. Louis Napoleon briefly made Utrecht capital of the Kingdom of Holland in 1808, and after 1813 the university recovered its standing as the city entered the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.
zh:
乌得勒支兴起于莱茵河的一处渡口，罗马人曾在此修建特拉耶克图姆要塞。约700年，威利布罗德以这座旧要塞为基地向弗里斯兰传教；1024年，乌得勒支主教成为神圣罗马帝国诸侯。城市1122年获得城市权，沿运河修建码头，发展成北方重要商埠，圣马丁大教堂也在城中心拔地而起；1420年开工的中殿到1444年仍因财力不足未能完工。此时乌得勒支是一个教会政权的天主教荷兰语首府，也是尼德兰北部最大城市，但自1423年起，乌得勒支分裂已使主教位的竞争者和城市派系彼此对立。

1528年，查理五世收走主教世俗权力，终结采邑主教区，把这片领地改为乌得勒支领地，并由新建的弗雷登堡要塞驻军控制。1579年1月23日，北方诸省和城市在此缔结乌得勒支同盟，共同对抗腓力二世；1580年，新教政权废除主教区。1636年3月26日，乌得勒支大学创立。1672年灾难年中，法军占领城市；撤军后，1674年的一场风暴又吹塌大教堂未完工的中殿。1713年，结束西班牙王位继承战争的《乌得勒支和约》在此谈判并签署。1808年，路易·拿破仑曾短暂以乌得勒支为荷兰王国首都；1813年后大学恢复地位，城市也随之加入尼德兰联合王国。

en:
Guelders is the river country of the Waal, IJssel and Maas, where lords of Wassenberg built a county about 1096, added Zutphen by marriage in 1127 and were raised to dukes of the Holy Roman Empire in 1339. The duchy was gathered in four quarters around Zutphen, the Veluwe, Nijmegen and Roermond, and eighteen of its towns, among them Arnhem, Nijmegen and Zutphen, belonged to the Hanseatic League. Nijmegen, old already in Roman days and pledged to Guelders for an unrepaid loan in 1247, traded up the Rhine; the Limbourg brothers, painters of the duke of Berry's book of hours, were born there. After the Wassenberg and Jülich lines ran out, Arnold of Egmond was recognised as duke in 1423. In 1444 his duchy is one of the great principalities of the Low Countries, rich on river tolls and the cloth trade of Zutphen, and already pressed by the expanding power of Burgundy.

Arnold's son Adolf rebelled and shut his father up in the castle of Buren in 1465. Charles the Bold of Burgundy intervened, restored Arnold in 1471 and bought the succession for 300,000 Rhenish florins, so that at Arnold's death in 1473 Guelders passed to Burgundy. Freed after Charles fell at Nancy in 1477, Adolf died the same year besieging Tournai, and Maximilian of Austria took the duchy. In 1492 the towns ransomed Adolf's son Charles of Egmond, who for nearly half a century held Charles V at bay in the Guelders Wars with French backing; when he died in 1538 his heir William of Jülich-Cleves could not keep the inheritance and ceded it by the Treaty of Venlo in 1543. In the Dutch Revolt the three northern quarters joined the Union of Utrecht in 1579 and became Gelderland in the United Provinces, while the country was fought over around Zutphen, where Sir Philip Sidney was mortally wounded in 1586 and Maurice of Orange retook the town in 1591. French armies flooded across Guelders in 1672, and the peace ending that war was signed at Nijmegen in 1678. In 1795 French revolutionary armies incorporated the country, splitting it between the departments of Roer and Meuse-Inferieure; in 1815 it became the province of Gelderland in the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.
zh:
海尔雷地处瓦尔河、艾瑟尔河与马斯河之间的河网之地。瓦森贝格的领主约1096年在此建立伯国，1127年通过联姻取得聚特芬，1339年获神圣罗马帝国擢升为公爵。公国由四个分区组成，分别以聚特芬、费吕沃、奈梅亨和鲁尔蒙德为中心，境内共有十八座汉萨城市，阿纳姆、奈梅亨、聚特芬皆在其中。奈梅亨在罗马时代便已兴起，1247年因一笔从未偿还的借款被抵押给海尔雷，从此沿莱茵河经商；为贝里公爵绘制《时序祈祷书》的林堡兄弟就出生在这座城里。瓦森贝格和于利希两系绝嗣后，埃赫蒙德的阿诺尔德于1423年被拥立为公爵。1444年的海尔雷是低地的大诸侯之一，靠河上税卡和聚特芬的呢绒贸易致富，同时已感受到勃艮第扩张的压力。

阿诺尔德之子阿道夫起兵反叛，1465年把父亲囚禁在比伦城堡。勃艮第公爵「大胆的查理」出兵干预，1471年扶阿诺尔德复位，并以三十万莱茵盾买下继承权，所以1473年阿诺尔德一死，海尔雷便落入勃艮第之手。1477年查理战死于南锡，阿道夫获释，却在同年围攻图尔奈时丧命，奥地利的马克西米利安随即接管公国。1492年，各城出资赎回阿道夫之子查理·范·埃赫蒙德，他在法国支持下同查理五世的海尔雷战争周旋了近半个世纪；1538年他去世，继承人于利希-克莱沃的威廉守不住这份遗产，于1543年依《芬洛条约》把公国割让给皇帝。荷兰起义期间，北方三个分区1579年加入乌得勒支同盟，成为联省共和国的海尔德兰特省；聚特芬一带战事反复，菲利普·锡德尼1586年在此受致命伤，奥兰治的莫里斯1591年收复该城。1672年法军横扫海尔雷，而结束那场战争的和约1678年在奈梅亨签订。1795年，法兰西共和国的军队兼并此地，分置鲁尔和下默兹两省；1815年，它成为尼德兰联合王国的海尔德兰省。

en:
Friesland is a low country of terps, drained pastures and Wadden Sea channels between the Zuider Zee and the Lauwers. Its cattle and dairy produce supported merchant towns, while the customs of Frisian freedom left local justice in the hands of rural communities and wealthy headmen rather than a feudal prince. Leeuwarden had grown up on terps beside the Middelzee; after the waterway silted, the settlements of Oldehove, Nijehove and Hoek were united on 21 January 1435, though the exact date of its city rights is lost. Harlingen, chartered in 1234, remained the fishing and shipping outlet. In 1444 the Catholic, Frisian-speaking land was formally without a lord, but its Vetkopers and Schieringers were turning private disputes into fortified factional war.
