贝贾亚古称萨尔代，坐落在朱尔朱拉山下的海湾旁，群山是卡比尔柏柏尔人的家园。1067年，哈马德王朝埃米尔纳绥尔把都城从班尼·哈马德堡迁到这座渔港，它由此成为西地中海最富庶的港口之一。比萨、热那亚和加泰罗尼亚商人从这里运走蜂蜡（法语的「蜡烛」一词bougie便来源于此）、皮革、明矾和铁，还有从比斯克拉与姆西拉由陆路贩来的羊毛和棉花；斐波那契少年时正是在此学会了阿拉伯数字。阿尔摩哈德王朝之后，贝贾亚转入哈夫斯王朝之手，15世纪大部分时间由哈夫斯王族的一支以近乎独立的「布日王国」统治，仍不断接纳逃离收复失地运动的安达卢西亚难民。1444年的贝贾亚是卡比尔海岸的首城，奉突尼斯为宗主，随着葡萄牙人开辟远洋航路，贸易已开始走下坡。

1510年，佩德罗·纳瓦罗为西班牙攻陷贝贾亚，末代苏丹阿卜杜勒·阿齐兹出逃；其弟阿布·巴克尔在君士坦丁自称苏丹，1512年反攻失败，海盗奥鲁奇·巴巴罗萨在围城战中失去一条手臂。在城后的群山里，艾哈迈德·乌勒·卡迪建立了卡比尔人的库库王国，在伊瑟尔击败海雷丁·巴巴罗萨，并于1520年至1527年间占据阿尔及尔；与之争雄的阿伊特·阿巴斯家族则据守自己的卡拉堡。1555年，贝勒贝伊萨拉赫·拉伊斯在库库战士协助下终于收复此城，贝贾亚从此成为阿尔及尔摄政国的港口，隶属君士坦丁贝伊领，主要靠船坞和内陆的木材、蜂蜡维持；1671年一支英国舰队为制止海盗劫掠炮轰了该城。土耳其人始终未能征服卡比尔群山：库库在17世纪初衰落，阿伊特·阿巴斯则一直保有卡拉堡。

en:
Constantine stands on a rocky plateau all but severed from the land by the gorge of the Rhumel, a natural fortress in the high plains of the eastern Maghreb. As Cirta it was the capital of the Numidian kings and the main base from which Metellus and Marius campaigned against Jugurtha; destroyed in 311, it was rebuilt in 313 by Constantine the Great, who gave it his name. After the Arab conquest it passed with Ifriqiya through the Aghlabid, Fatimid, Zirid, Hammadid and Almohad empires before coming to the Hafsids, who entrusted this restive city to princes of their own house and repeatedly had to reconquer it. In 1444, under the strong sultan Abu 'Amr 'Uthman in Tunis, Constantine is the inland market of a grain-growing country, its Hammadid Great Mosque already centuries old.

Its dependence on Tunis ended in the 1530s, and in 1535 the city passed to the Ottomans, becoming the seat of the Beylik of the East, the largest and richest of the three provinces of the Regency of Algiers. Rival marabout families, the Abd al-Mu'min and the Lefgoun, made the next century turbulent. Stability and prosperity returned in the eighteenth century under a line of energetic beys, above all Salah Bey, who ruled from 1771 to 1792: he sent his cavalry against the Spanish army besieging Algiers in 1775 and on campaigns against Tunis, and adorned the city with mosques, madrasas and the restored Roman bridge of El Kantara. Deposed by the dey of Algiers in 1792, he was followed by seventeen beys in thirty-four years; a Tunisian army besieged the city in 1807 without taking it. Grain, wool and leather from the eastern plains remained the sources of its wealth.
zh:
君士坦丁雄踞鲁梅尔河峡谷几乎切断的岩石台地上，是马格里布东部高原上的天然要塞。古时此地称基尔塔，曾是努米底亚诸王的都城，梅特鲁斯与马略讨伐朱古达时即以它为主要据点；城市311年被毁，313年由君士坦丁大帝重建并以其名命名。阿拉伯征服之后，它随易弗里基叶先后经历艾格莱卜、法蒂玛、齐里、哈马德和阿尔摩哈德诸王朝，最后归入哈夫斯王朝；哈夫斯君主常把这座难治之城交给本族王公，又屡屡被迫重新征服它。1444年，在突尼斯强人苏丹阿布·阿慕尔·奥斯曼治下，君士坦丁是谷产区的内陆商埠，城中哈马德时代的大清真寺已有数百年历史。

16世纪30年代，君士坦丁与突尼斯的宗属关系终结，1535年转入奥斯曼人之手，成为东方贝伊领的首府——这是阿尔及尔摄政国三个贝伊领中最大、最富庶的一个。此后一个世纪，阿卜杜勒·慕敏与莱夫昆两大家族纷争不断。进入18世纪，接连几位有为的贝伊带来稳定与繁荣，其中最著名的是1771年至1792年在位的萨拉赫贝伊：他派骑兵参加1775年击退围攻阿尔及尔的西班牙军队之役，也东征突尼斯，并在城内修建清真寺和伊斯兰学校、修复罗马时代的坎塔拉桥。1792年他被阿尔及尔代伊罢免，此后34年间换了17任贝伊；1807年突尼斯军队围城不克。东部平原的谷物、羊毛和皮革，始终是此地财富的来源。

en:
Tunis stands behind the Lake of Tunis, with La Goulette linking its medina and kasbah to the Mediterranean. After the Arab conquest of 698, the Zaytuna Mosque grew at the city's heart. The Almohads made Tunis the capital of Ifriqiya in 1159, and in 1229 Abu Zakariya founded Hafsid rule there. Walls enclosed the medina, kasbah and new suburbs, while Muslim and Jewish refugees from al-Andalus strengthened trade, crafts and scholarship. In 1444 the city, with roughly 100,000 people, was the wealthy Sunni capital of Abu 'Amr 'Uthman, who had begun his long reign in 1435; its souks and harbor connected Saharan caravans with merchants from Italy and Catalonia.

'Uthman extended Hafsid overlordship as far as Tripolitania in 1458, but later succession struggles drew in Spain and the Ottomans. Hayreddin Barbarossa took Tunis in 1534, Charles V restored the Hafsids as tributaries in 1535, and Uluç Ali seized the city in 1569 before a Spanish army returned in 1573. The Ottoman conquest of August 1574 ended Hafsid rule. A pasha, janissaries, deys and then increasingly independent beys governed the regency; after the 1591 janissary revolt, privateering, ransom traffic and legitimate trade filled the port. Husayn ibn Ali founded the Husainid dynasty in 1705. Algerian troops intervened in 1756, yet the dynasty survived. Under Hammouda Pasha, ruling from 1782 to 1813, Tunis prospered, an Algerian invasion was repulsed in 1807, and the last janissary rising was crushed in 1811. By 1821 the city was the seat of a virtually autonomous beylical government.
zh:
突尼斯城坐落于突尼斯湖后方，靠拉古莱特港把麦地那、卡斯巴与地中海连接起来。698年阿拉伯人征服后，宰图纳清真寺在城中心发展起来。穆瓦希德王朝1159年以突尼斯为伊弗里基叶首府；1229年，阿布·扎卡里亚在此建立哈夫斯王朝。城墙环绕麦地那、卡斯巴和新兴郊区，来自安达卢斯的穆斯林与犹太难民也增强了贸易、手工业和学术。1444年，这座约有十万人口的城市是阿布·阿慕尔·奥斯曼统治下富庶的逊尼派都城；他在1435年开始漫长统治，城中集市和港口把撒哈拉商队与意大利、加泰罗尼亚商人联系在一起。

乌斯曼1458年把哈夫斯宗主权扩张到的黎波里塔尼亚，但此后的继承纷争把西班牙和奥斯曼帝国引入突尼斯。海雷丁·巴巴罗萨1534年攻占突尼斯，查理五世1535年恢复向西班牙称臣的哈夫斯王朝；乌鲁吉·阿里1569年夺城，西班牙军队又在1573年返回。1574年8月，奥斯曼最终征服突尼斯，结束哈夫斯统治。帕夏、禁卫军、戴伊和日益独立的贝伊相继主持这个行省；1591年禁卫军叛乱后，私掠、赎金交易与合法贸易共同填满港口。侯赛因·伊本·阿里1705年建立侯赛因王朝。阿尔及利亚军队1756年武力干预，但王朝仍然存续。哈穆达帕夏1782年至1813年统治期间，突尼斯贸易繁荣，1807年击退阿尔及利亚入侵，1811年镇压最后一次禁卫军起事。到1821年，这里已成为一个几乎自治的贝伊政权所在地。

en:
The Gharb is an Atlantic plain of about 6,000 square kilometres, crossed by the Sebou River and enclosed by the coast and the pre-Rif hills. Berber tribes, including the Barghawata confederacy, once held the country; after the Almohad conquest Yaqub al-Mansur settled Riyah Arabs of the Banu Hilal there, and their mounted tribes served the Makhzen while the plain supplied Fez and the Ghomara mountains with grain, livestock and horses. At its southwestern edge stood Rabat, on the Bou Regreg opposite Salé. Abd al-Mu'min built its kasbah in 1150 or 1151, and Yaqub al-Mansur later planned the fortified Ribat al-Fath, beginning the Hassan Mosque in 1184, but the imperial city was unfinished at his death in 1199. Under the Marinids, Salé outshone the southern bank. In 1444 Rabat was therefore a quiet fortified settlement guarding a rich grain plain, with much of the region's trade passing through Salé.

Leo Africanus found only about a hundred inhabited houses at Rabat in 1515. Revival followed the Spanish expulsion of the Moriscos in 1609, when refugees from Hornachos and Andalusia occupied the kasbah and settled beneath it. Their New Salé joined Old Salé across the river to form the autonomous Republic of Bou Regreg in 1627, whose Salé Rovers preyed on Atlantic merchant shipping. Al-Rashid conquered the estuary for the Alawi dynasty in 1666. After 1672 Moulay Ismail enlarged the Kasbah of the Udayas, placed loyal Udaya tribesmen there and strengthened central rule over the surrounding tribes. Muhammad III later made Rabat an imperial residence, and Moulay Slimane added mosques, a Jewish quarter and extended walls after 1792. By 1821 the corsair republic had long gone, but the Gharb still fed the Makhzen and Rabat was steadily becoming a royal city.
zh:
盖尔卜是一片面积约6000平方公里的大西洋平原，塞布河穿流其间，海岸与里夫山前缘丘陵构成它的边界。柏柏尔部族，包括巴尔加瓦塔联盟，曾据有此地；穆瓦希德王朝征服后，雅各布·曼苏尔把巴努希拉尔中的里亚赫阿拉伯部落安置到平原上。这些骑马部族为马赫曾服役，平原则向非斯和戈马拉山区供应谷物、牲畜与马匹。平原西南边缘、布赖格赖格河畔是与塞拉隔河相对的拉巴特。阿卜杜勒·慕敏在1150或1151年修建城堡，雅各布·曼苏尔后来规划设防的「胜利里巴特」，并于1184年动工修建哈桑清真寺，但这座帝都在他1199年去世时仍未完工。马林王朝时期，对岸的塞拉比南岸更繁荣。因此1444年的拉巴特只是一座守卫肥沃粮田的寂静要塞，地区贸易多经塞拉往来。

1515年，利奥·阿非利加努斯发现拉巴特只有约一百栋有人居住的房屋。1609年西班牙驱逐摩里斯科人后，局势为之一变：来自奥尔纳乔斯和安达卢斯的难民占据城堡，并在堡下定居。他们的「新塞拉」与对岸的「旧塞拉」在1627年组成自治的布赖格赖格共和国，「塞拉海盗」从此在大西洋劫掠商船。1666年，拉希德为阿拉维王朝征服河口。1672年以后，穆莱·伊斯梅尔扩建乌达雅堡，安置忠诚的乌达雅部众，并加强对周围部族的中央控制。穆罕默德三世后来把拉巴特作为帝国驻跸地之一；穆莱·苏莱曼在1792年以后增建清真寺、犹太区并扩展城墙。到1821年，海盗共和国早已不复存在，但盖尔卜仍供养着马赫曾，拉巴特也正稳步成为一座皇家城市。

en:
Fez was founded in 789 by Idris I on the banks of the Oued Fes, and in 809 his son Idris II laid out a second settlement on the opposite bank and moved the Idrisid capital here from Volubilis. The Qarawiyyin mosque, founded by Fatima al-Fihri in 859, grew into the foremost seat of Maliki learning in the Maghreb, while the Chouara tannery made the city's name for leather. In 1069–70 the Almoravid Yusuf ibn Tashfin joined the two towns within one circuit of walls; the Almohads stormed Fez in 1145, and the ramparts were rebuilt by 1204. Under the Marinids, who made the city their capital in 1250, Fez entered its golden age: Abu Yusuf Ya'qub founded Fes Jdid in 1276, and seven madrasas went up between 1271 and 1357 around the Qarawiyyin. In 1444 Fez is the capital of Marinid Morocco, its souks and dye-pits feeding the cloth and leather trade across the Maghreb, though the sultan's authority is already overshadowed by his Wattasid viziers.

In 1465 a Fez mob killed Sultan Abd al-Haqq II, the last Marinid, and an Idrisid sharif was proclaimed in his place until the Wattasids took power in 1472. Sephardic refugees from Spain and Portugal swelled the Mellah after 1492. The Saadis of Marrakesh seized Fez in January 1549, lost it briefly to an Ottoman-backed Wattasid restoration in 1554, and checked an Ottoman invasion at Wadi al-Laban in 1558; keeping their court in Marrakesh, they ringed Fez with forts such as the Borj Nord of 1582. After Ahmad al-Mansur died in 1603, rival princes fought over Fez and Marrakesh until 1627, and the Dila'iyya Sufis held the city from 1641. Moulay Rashid, founder of the 'Alawi dynasty, took Fez in 1666, built the Kasbah Cherarda and the Cherratine Madrasa of 1670, and made it his capital. Moulay Isma'il preferred Meknes and taxed Fez heavily, and after his death in 1727 the city spent decades at odds with the Udaya garrison and the crown. Stability returned under Muhammad ibn Abdallah between 1757 and 1790, and in 1821 Fez remains Morocco's political and scholarly capital, its ulama kingmakers at the 'Alawi court.
zh:
非斯由伊德里斯一世于789年在非斯河畔建立；809年其子伊德里斯二世在对岸另筑一城，并把伊德里斯王朝的都城从瓦卢比利斯迁来。859年法蒂玛·菲赫里倡建的卡拉维因清真寺，后来成为马格里布首屈一指的马立克学派学府，舒阿拉制革坊也让非斯皮革闻名于世。1069至1070年，穆拉比特王朝的优素福·本·塔什芬把两岸两镇合筑于一道城墙之内；1145年穆瓦希德王朝攻破非斯，城墙到1204年重修完成。马林王朝1250年定都于此，非斯进入黄金时代：阿布·优素福·叶尔孤白1276年兴建新非斯，1271至1357年间卡拉维因周围又陆续建起七座伊斯兰学院。1444年的非斯是马林摩洛哥的都城，集市和染坊支撑着遍及马格里布的布匹与皮革贸易，只是苏丹的权势已被瓦塔斯族维齐尔盖过。

1465年，非斯民众杀死末代马林苏丹阿卜杜勒·哈克二世，一位伊德里斯谢里夫被拥立继位，直到1472年瓦塔斯王朝掌权。1492年后，来自西班牙和葡萄牙的塞法迪犹太难民大量涌入梅拉区。以马拉喀什为根基的萨阿德王朝1549年1月攻占非斯，1554年该城一度被奥斯曼支持的瓦塔斯复辟夺回，1558年摩洛哥又在瓦迪拉班挡住奥斯曼入侵；萨阿德苏丹仍以马拉喀什为宫廷所在，并在非斯周围大修堡垒，1582年建成的北堡便是其一。艾哈迈德·曼苏尔1603年死后，争位的诸王子在非斯与马拉喀什之间混战至1627年，迪拉苏菲教团又自1641年起占据该城。阿拉维王朝的开创者穆莱·拉希德1666年攻取非斯，建起谢拉达堡和1670年的谢拉廷学院，再次定都于此；穆莱·伊斯梅尔却偏爱梅克内斯，对非斯课以重税，1727年他死后，非斯又与乌达亚驻军和朝廷对抗数十年。1757至1790年穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉在位期间局势重归安定，到1821年，非斯仍是摩洛哥的政治与学术之都，城中乌理玛的向背足以左右阿拉维宫廷。

en:
Marrakesh was founded in 1062 by Abu Bakr ibn Umar as the capital of the Almoravids, on a plain below the High Atlas. Ali ibn Yusuf ringed it with red earthen walls in 1122–23, giving the future 'Red City' its name. The Almohads under Abd al-Mu'min sacked it in 1147 and then gave it its greatest monuments, from the Kutubiyya Mosque of 1184–99 to the Kasbah and the Menara and Agdal gardens, while Averroes taught at its court. The Marinids took Marrakesh in 1269 and moved the capital to Fez, and after the death of Abu Inan in 1358 the Hintata Berbers made the city a virtually independent emirate. In 1444 Marrakesh therefore answers to its own Hintata emir rather than to the Marinid sultan in Fez, while its Jemaa el-Fnaa square and souks still draw caravans carrying gold and slaves across the Sahara.

In 1515 the people of Marrakesh and their Saadi allies drove off a Portuguese assault. Ahmad al-Araj, son of the Saadi leader, entered the city in 1521 by marrying the Hintata emir's daughter, and in 1524–25 he seized the Kasbah after having his father-in-law killed; the Treaty of Tadla in 1527 divided Morocco between Saadis and Wattasids. As the Saadian capital, Marrakesh entered a new golden age: Sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib built the Ben Youssef Madrasa, the Mouassine Mosque and the Saadian Tombs and laid out the Mellah in 1558. Victory at the Battle of the Three Kings in 1578 brought Ahmad al-Mansur to power; he raised the El Badi Palace with Italian marble, paid for by the sugar of the Haouz and Sous and by gold flowing in after the conquest of Songhai in 1591. His death in 1603 opened years of civil war, Fez and Marrakesh passing between rival princes until 1627; the last Saadian sultan was killed in 1659, and Moulay Rashid conquered the city for the 'Alawis in 1668. Moulay Ismail favoured Meknes and in 1696 stripped El Badi of its materials, though under him the pilgrimage of the Seven Saints made Marrakesh a Sufi holy city. Sidi Muhammad ibn Abdallah rebuilt the Royal Palace and much of the medina between 1757 and 1790; in 1821 Marrakesh remains a seat of 'Alawi power and Sahara commerce.
zh:
马拉喀什由阿布·伯克尔·本·奥马尔于1062年在大阿特拉斯山脚下的空旷平原上建立，作为穆拉比特王朝的都城。阿里·本·优素福1122至1123年绕城建起红色夯土城墙，这座日后的「红城」由此得名。1147年阿卜杜勒·穆明率穆瓦希德人攻破并洗劫该城，此后又为它留下最恢宏的建筑：1184至1199年的库图比亚清真寺、王宫城堡以及梅纳拉花园与阿格达尔花园，伊本·鲁世德也曾在其宫廷讲学。马林王朝1269年攻占马拉喀什后把都城迁往非斯；1358年阿布·伊南死后，欣塔塔柏柏尔人把这座城市变成近乎独立的酋长国。因此1444年的马拉喀什听命于自己的欣塔塔埃米尔，而不是非斯的马林苏丹，杰马夫纳广场和集市上仍穿梭着贩运黄金与奴隶的撒哈拉商队。

1515年，马拉喀什人与萨阿德盟军击退了葡萄牙人的进攻。萨阿德领袖之子艾哈迈德·阿拉吉1521年借迎娶欣塔塔埃米尔之女入城，又在1524至1525年杀死岳父、夺取城堡；1527年的《塔德莱条约》以乌姆赖比阿河为界，把摩洛哥分归萨阿德与瓦塔斯两家。成为萨阿德都城后，马拉喀什步入新的黄金时代：阿卜杜拉·加利布苏丹修建本·优素福学院、穆瓦辛清真寺和萨阿德王陵，1558年又划定梅拉区。1578年三王之战的胜利把艾哈迈德·曼苏尔送上王位，他以意大利大理石修建巴迪宫，财源来自豪兹和苏斯的蔗糖，以及1591年征服桑海后流入的黄金。1603年他死后内战连年，非斯与马拉喀什在争位王公之间反复易手，直到1627年；末代萨阿德苏丹1659年被杀，穆莱·拉希德1668年为阿拉维王朝征服该城。穆莱·伊斯梅尔偏爱梅克内斯，1696年拆走巴迪宫的建材运往新都，但在他治下，「七圣」朝觐让马拉喀什成为苏菲圣城。西迪·穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉1757至1790年间重建王宫和大片老城，继位纷争平息之后，到1821年马拉喀什仍是阿拉维王朝的一方权力中心和撒哈拉贸易重镇。

en:
Abda is the Atlantic coast behind Safi, or Asfi, the harbour that had served Marrakesh since the Almohads made it their port in the twelfth century; al-Idrisi already described it as a busy harbour. Its hinterland was the country of the Abda, an Arab tribal confederation largely of Ma'qil descent, pasturing south of the Doukkala. In 1444, with the Marinid sultanate in Fez dissolving, local caïds and tribal sheikhs held the town and its countryside, while Safi's roadstead carried Marrakesh's overseas trade.

The Portuguese seized Safi in 1488 and built it up behind the sea castle of Ksar el-Bahr, making it a fortress of the Portuguese Crown in 1508. In 1516 the Abda and Gharbiya tribes rose and cut the roads into the city, and on 16 February 1518 they killed the Portuguese-backed governor Yahya ibn Ta'foufat in a tribal tent. As the Saadian sharifs advanced, John III evacuated Safi and Azemmour in 1541. The town recovered as Marrakesh's safest harbour: in 1751 the Danes held its trade monopoly, and under Sultan Mohammed III the Abda caïd Abd al-Rahman al-Abdi helped raise the kasbah and great mosque, until the new port of Mogador drew European commerce south after 1765. In May 1815 the Abda rose against the sultan's governor and besieged Safi.
zh:
阿卜达位于萨菲背后的大西洋沿岸，萨菲阿拉伯语称阿斯菲。12世纪穆瓦希德王朝把它辟为马拉喀什的外港，伊德里西的地理书中已称这里商船云集。港口腹地是阿卜达人的牧地，他们是以马基勒人后裔为主的阿拉伯部落联盟，游牧于杜卡拉以南。1444年，非斯的马林王朝苏丹权柄瓦解，萨菲城和周围乡野由当地卡伊德与部落谢赫把持，海港承担着马拉喀什的海外贸易。

1488年，葡萄牙人夺取萨菲，依托海边的海上城堡设防，1508年将其设为葡萄牙王室要塞。1516年，阿卜达人与加尔比亚人起事，切断通往萨菲的道路；1518年2月16日，他们在一顶部落帐篷中杀死了亲葡萄牙的总督叶海亚·伊本·塔富法特。随着萨阿德圣裔势力北进，若昂三世于1541年撤出萨菲和艾宰穆尔。此后萨菲作为马拉喀什最安全的海港复苏：1751年丹麦人取得这里的贸易垄断权；穆罕默德三世时期，阿卜达卡伊德阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·阿卜迪主持修建了城堡与大清真寺。1765年穆罕默德三世在南方另建摩加多尔（索维拉），欧洲贸易随之南移，萨菲渐趋冷落。1815年5月，阿卜达人起兵反抗苏丹任命的总督，围攻萨菲城。

en:
Tafilalt is the great oasis of south-eastern Morocco, a long string of walled ksour along the Wadi Ziz at the northern edge of the Sahara. There the Midrarids founded Sijilmasa in the eighth century, and for six hundred years it was the northern terminus of the western trans-Saharan road, where gold from the lands of the Niger was minted into dinars and caravans dealt in salt, cloth and slaves. Ibn Battuta, passing through in 1352 on his way to Mali, praised its fine dates and handsome buildings. In the fifteenth century the gold trade slipped away to the Portuguese sea route and to the rising city of Marrakesh, and in 1444 the oasis villages largely governed their own affairs, though caravans still came north from the Niger bend.

Early in the sixteenth century Leo Africanus found Sijilmasa in ruins, its people scattered among outlying villages, though its high walls and waterwheels still stood. In 1606 the Saadian sultan Zidan Abu Maali took refuge in the oasis, raised an army on its gold and recovered Marrakesh. In 1631, when Abu Hassun of the Sous occupied the Tafilalt, its inhabitants turned to a local sharifian family that had come from Yanbu and proclaimed its head Mawlay al-Sharif their sultan; his sons expelled the occupiers in 1640 and held off the Dila'iyya Berbers. One son, Mawlay al-Rashid, was proclaimed sultan in 1664, took Fez in 1666 and Marrakesh in 1668, carrying the Alaouite dynasty from this oasis to the throne of Morocco. Moulay Ismail later had Sijilmasa rebuilt, but in 1818 the Aït Atta nomads sacked it, and only ruined gateways remained at the site.
zh:
塔菲拉勒特是摩洛哥东南部的大绿洲，沿济兹河分布着一长串设防的城堡村，地处撒哈拉北缘。8世纪时，米德拉尔王朝在此建起西吉勒马萨；此后六百年间，它是跨撒哈拉西路的北方终点，尼日尔河一带运来的黄金在此铸成第纳尔，商队则买卖盐、布匹和奴隶。1352年，伊本·白图泰在前往马里途中经过此城，称赞这里椰枣甘美、建筑壮丽。15世纪，黄金贸易随葡萄牙人开辟海路和马拉喀什崛起而流失；1444年，绿洲诸村大多自行其是，而商队仍从尼日尔河湾北上到此。

16世纪初，利奥·阿非利加努斯见到西吉勒马萨已成废墟，居民散居郊外村落，唯有高墙和水车犹存。1606年，萨阿德苏丹齐丹·阿布·马阿利避居绿洲，靠当地出产的黄金募军，随后收复马拉喀什。1631年，苏斯的阿布·哈松占领塔菲拉勒特，当地人转而投奔一支来自延布的圣裔家族，拥立族长穆莱·谢里夫为苏丹；他的儿子们于1640年逐出占领者，又挡住了迪拉叶柏柏尔人。其中一子穆莱·拉希德于1664年称苏丹，1666年取非斯、1668年下马拉喀什，把阿拉维王朝从这座绿洲送上摩洛哥王座。穆莱·伊斯梅尔后来下令重建西吉勒马萨，但1818年艾特阿塔游牧部落洗劫了此城，遗址上只剩残破的城门。

en:
Ifni is a small Atlantic landing on Morocco's Sous coast, its hinterland climbing from shoreline hills toward the edge of the Sahara. In 1444 the people here were Shilha Berbers of the Aït Baâmrane, a Sous tribal confederation grouped around Sidi Ifni. Its clans kept animals, sold fish and hides to European seamen, and acted as intermediaries between northern Morocco and trans-Saharan traffic, while the coast remained largely in tribal hands during the breakup of Marinid rule.

In 1476 Castilian-Canarian forces established a fortified fishing and trading post, Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequeña, later associated with the bay of Ifni although its exact ruins remain disputed. Local raids and the rising Saadian movement made the outpost untenable, and Saadi forces took it in 1524, ending the Castilian presence. The Aït Baâmrane then retained their fishing anchorages, coastal markets, and contacts with the Saharan caravan routes.
zh:
伊夫尼是摩洛哥苏斯海岸一处小型大西洋登陆地，腹地从沿岸丘陵伸向撒哈拉边缘。1444年住在这里的是阿伊特·巴阿姆兰联盟的什卢赫柏柏尔人，各氏族以西迪伊夫尼一带为中心。他们放牧牲畜，向欧洲船员出售鱼和皮革，也在摩洛哥北部与跨撒哈拉商路之间充当中介；马林王朝统治瓦解之际，海岸大体仍掌握在地方部落手中。

1476年，来自卡斯蒂利亚和加那利群岛的武装设立了设防的小型渔业贸易站圣克鲁斯-德拉马尔佩克尼亚，后世把它与伊夫尼海湾联系起来，但其确切遗址仍有争议。地方袭扰和兴起的萨阿德运动使据点难以维持，1524年萨阿德军队将其夺取，卡斯蒂利亚人的存在就此终结。此后阿伊特·巴阿姆兰人仍掌握着渔港锚地、沿岸市集以及与撒哈拉商路的联系。

en:
The Sus is the irrigated plain of the Sous River, enclosed between the High Atlas and the Anti-Atlas and looking west toward Agadir and the Atlantic. It is Shilha Berber country, thick with argan trees and crossed by routes linking the Sahara to the sea; sugar had been grown and exported here since at least the eleventh century. Taroudant, described by Arab geographers as the capital of Sus, was its inland market, where Jewish caravan merchants and Berber clans exchanged desert and lowland goods. In 1444 Fez's hold on the south was loose, leaving the city, villages and tribal confederations largely to arrange their own affairs.

After the Portuguese occupied Agadir in 1505, resistance in the Sus gave the Sharifian family of the Saadis their opening. In 1510 Muhammad al-Qa'im was recognized at Tidsi near Taroudant as leader of the Sous tribes and Sufi groups; his son Ahmad al-Araj governed the Sus from 1513, while another son, Muhammad al-Shaykh, forced Agadir's Portuguese garrison to surrender on 12 March 1541. The death of Ahmad al-Mansur in 1603 broke Saadian unity. In 1613 Sidi Ali Bou Dmia took over the zawiya of Illigh and built the principality of Tazeroualt, dominating Sus, the Draa and the gold routes; his men held Sijilmasa from 1631 until Alawi pressure drove them out in 1640. Bou Dmia died in 1659, and Tazeroualt's independent power narrowed as Moulay Rashid's Alawis reunited Morocco after taking Marrakesh in 1668. In 1760 Sultan Mohammed bin Abdallah closed Agadir to commerce and favored Essaouira, stripping Taroudant of its chief outlet and beginning its decline.
zh:
苏斯是苏斯河灌溉的平原，夹在大阿特拉斯山与小阿特拉斯山之间，西经阿加迪尔通向大西洋。这里是什卢赫柏柏尔人的乡土，遍布阿甘树，也是撒哈拉与海岸之间商路的要冲；至迟从11世纪起，当地已种植并出口蔗糖。塔鲁丹特被阿拉伯地理学家称为苏斯的首府，是内陆市场，犹太商队商人和柏柏尔氏族在此交换沙漠与低地货物。1444年，非斯对南方的控制已经松弛，城市、村庄和部落联盟大体自行维持秩序。

1505年葡萄牙人占领阿加迪尔后，苏斯的抵抗给圣裔萨阿德家族打开了局面。1510年，穆罕默德·卡伊姆在塔鲁丹特附近的提德西被苏斯各部落和苏菲团体承认为领袖；其子艾哈迈德·阿拉吉自1513年起掌管苏斯，另一个儿子穆罕默德·谢赫则于1541年3月12日迫使阿加迪尔的葡萄牙守军投降。1603年艾哈迈德·曼苏尔去世后，萨阿德政权陷入分裂。1613年，西迪·阿里·布·德米亚接掌伊利格扎维利亚，建立塔扎鲁瓦特埃米尔国，控制苏斯、德拉河谷与黄金商路；他的军队1631年夺取西吉勒马萨，1640年在阿拉维家族压力下退出。布·德米亚于1659年去世，塔扎鲁瓦特的独立势力随之收缩；穆莱·拉希德1668年攻占马拉喀什、重新统一摩洛哥后，苏斯也被纳入阿拉维政权。1760年，苏丹穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉关闭阿加迪尔商港、扶植索维拉，塔鲁丹特失去主要出海口并走向衰落。

en:
Figuig is a Berber palm-grove on the wadi Zouzfana, cupped in the Ksour mountains where the Atlas fall away into the Sahara. Its springs feed the dates, and seven walled ksour — Zenaga, Loudaghir and their fellows — line the wadi, each Zenata or Sanhaja community keeping its own laws and customs. The Almohads raised Ksar el-Aïn beside the springs, and the oasis later passed to the Marinids before their rise in Morocco. In 1444 the ksour managed their own affairs within the orbit of Tlemcen, and the caravans between Sijilmasa and Tlemcen watered at its wells.

In the 15th century Sidi Abdel Jabbar and his son Mohammed taught algebra and Islamic theology in a school famed along the Saharan frontier, and another son, Ibrahim el-Figuigui, composed the hunting treatise Rawdat al-Soulwan. The Saadians brought the oasis into the Moroccan realm in 1549 under Mohammed al-Shaykh, and Ahmad al-Mansur tightened his grip as his quarrel with the Ottomans grew; near the end of the 16th century the ksour called in a troop from Algiers against raiders from Tafilalt and ran their own affairs thereafter. Under the Alaouites Moulay Ismail settled the makhzen tribe of the Ouled Jaber at Figuig, whose feud with the Zenaga over the Tzadert springs ran bloodily from about 1770 into the 1820s. Moulay Slimane restored the tribe briefly in 1805, during his southern campaigns of 1805 to 1808.
zh:
菲吉格是济兹法纳干河畔的柏柏尔椰枣绿洲，坐落在库苏尔群山环抱之中，阿特拉斯山在这里没入撒哈拉。泉水滋养着椰枣林，泽纳加、卢达吉尔等七座带围墙的堡村沿河排开，泽纳塔和桑哈贾人的每个聚落各守自己的法律与风俗。穆瓦希德王朝曾在泉水旁筑起艾因堡，绿洲后来又在马林王朝崛起之前落入其手。1444年的七座堡村自行管理事务，处在特莱姆森的势力范围内，往来锡吉勒马萨与特莱姆森之间的商队在此取水补给。

15世纪，西迪·阿卜杜勒·贾巴尔和儿子穆罕默德在一所闻名撒哈拉边缘的学堂里教授代数学和伊斯兰神学，另一个儿子易卜拉欣·菲吉吉写下了狩猎著作《慰藉之园》。1549年，萨阿德王朝的穆罕默德·谢赫把绿洲纳入摩洛哥版图，艾哈迈德·曼苏尔又因与奥斯曼人交恶而加强了对这里的控制。16世纪末，各堡村请来一支阿尔及尔军队抵御来自塔菲拉勒特的袭掠者，此后长期自行其是。阿拉维王朝的穆莱·伊斯梅尔把马赫曾部落奥拉德·贾贝尔安置在菲吉格，他们与泽纳加人为争夺扎德尔特泉源世代仇杀，流血冲突从1770年前后一直延续到19世纪20年代。穆莱·苏莱曼于1805年短暂恢复该部落的地位，时当他1805至1808年的南征。

en:
Laghouat is an oasis on the Wadi Mzee, where the Amour Range of the Saharan Atlas falls away into the desert and the caravan road from Algiers drops towards Touggourt. In the fourteenth century Ibn Khaldun found here a walled ksar held by the Laghouat-ksel, a branch of the Maghraoua Berbers; in 1368 the fugitive Zayyanid sultan Abu Hammu II rallied his partisans at its gates before taking refuge in the M'zab. Two clans, the Berber Ouled Serghine and the Arab Ahlaf, divided the town and its palm gardens between them. In 1444 Laghouat owns no master: its walls and its stubborn refusal of tribute had long earned it the name of a 'rebel city'.

The marabout Sidi Hadj Aissa, later the town's patron saint, settled in the oasis in 1698. In 1708 the Marrakesh sultan Moulay Abdelmalek camped before its walls and imposed a tribute the Laghouatis never paid, and in 1727 the town formally acknowledged the suzerainty of the Regency of Algiers without mending its ways: the Bey of Titteri was defeated beneath its walls in 1741, and in 1785 the Bey of Oran led a punitive expedition to force payment of the annual tax. Caravans continued to water at its wells and its weavers sold rugs across the Sahara.
zh:
艾格瓦特是姆济干河畔的绿洲，地处撒哈拉阿特拉斯山脉的阿穆尔山没入沙漠之处，也是从阿尔及尔通向图古尔特的商路下坡入漠的驿站。14世纪时，伊本·赫勒敦记载这里有一座围墙堡寨，属马格拉瓦柏柏尔人的支派艾格瓦特-克塞尔；1368年，被非斯的马林苏丹逐出的扎扬王朝苏丹阿布·哈穆二世曾在寨门前召集部众，随后退入姆扎卜。寨内的椰枣园分为两族所有：柏柏尔裔的奥拉德·塞尔金和阿拉伯裔的阿赫拉夫。1444年的艾格瓦特不承认任何宗主，凭围墙和一再拒贡，早有「叛城」之名。

1698年，后来成为该城守护圣徒的马拉布特西迪·哈吉·伊萨在此定居。1708年，马拉喀什苏丹穆莱·阿卜杜勒-马利克在城外扎营，强定贡赋，艾格瓦特人却始终不缴；1727年，该城正式承认阿尔及尔摄政国的宗主权，但旧习不改：1741年提特里贝伊大军围攻，反被击退；1785年奥兰贝伊又为追讨年税发动惩罚性远征。商队依旧来此水井补给，织工把地毯卖到撒哈拉各地。

en:
Biskra, the Roman Vescera, is the queen of the Ziban oases, standing at the gate of the Sahara where the road from Béjaïa and Constantine descends towards Touggourt. The Arab conqueror Uqba ibn Nafi was killed nearby in 683, and his tomb at Sidi Okba became one of the great sanctuaries of the Maghreb. In the fourteenth century Biskra was the true capital of the Zab under the Béni Mozni, a practically independent principality that made alliances by turns with Béjaïa, Tlemcen and Fez and even received ambassadors from Mali, while the Lawata Berbers of the oases gathered the Hafsid tax at the head of a thousand horsemen. In 1444 the walled oasis still orders its own affairs, rich from its dates and from the wool of desert flocks; the Arab nomad confederation of the Dawaouida would overrun the Zab only later in the century.

Turkish expeditions under Hassan Agha in 1542 and Salah Raïs in 1552 finally placed a garrison and a fort in Biskra, and the Beylik of the East ruled its Saharan approaches through the town, granting the chief Ali Bou Akkaz the title of Sheikh el-Arab. Through the Ottoman centuries two families, the Bouakkaz and the Bengana, disputed mastery of the Ziban. In 1680 plague carried off some 7,000 of the inhabitants and the old town was abandoned for seven new ksour built within the palm grove; Biskri porters and water-carriers became familiar figures in the streets of Algiers. Caravans continued to pass north with dates and wool and south with manufactured goods.
zh:
比斯克拉古称维斯塞拉，是济班绿洲群之首，位于撒哈拉的门户，贝贾亚和君士坦丁南下图古尔特的道路由此入漠。阿拉伯征服者欧格白·伊本·纳菲683年战死在附近，他在西迪·奥克巴的墓地成为马格里布最受尊崇的圣迹之一。14世纪时，比斯克拉是贝尼·穆兹尼家族治下扎布的真正首府，一个事实独立的公国，先后与贝贾亚、特莱姆森和非斯结盟，甚至接待过马里的使节；绿洲的莱瓦塔柏柏尔人则率上千骑兵替哈夫斯王朝收税。1444年的比斯克拉仍是一座自行其是的围墙绿洲，靠椰枣和漠地羊群的羊毛致富；阿拉伯游牧联盟达瓦维达要到该世纪后期才席卷扎布。

1542年哈桑·阿加和1552年萨拉赫·拉伊斯的两次土耳其远征，终于在比斯克拉设下驻军与堡垒；东方贝伊领通过此城控制撒哈拉方向，授予首领阿里·布·阿卡斯「阿拉伯长老」之号。整个奥斯曼时期，布阿卡斯与本加纳两大家族争夺着济班的权力。1680年瘟疫夺去约7000人的生命，旧城被弃，人们在椰枣林内另建了七座堡寨；比斯克拉来的脚夫和运水人也成了阿尔及尔街头常见的身影。商队依旧北运椰枣和羊毛、南贩手工制成品。

en:
Gafsa, the Roman Capsa, lies at a spring-fed oasis in the broken hills north of the Chott el-Djerid, where the roads from Tunis, the Maghreb and the land of the blacks converge. Arab armies took it at the end of the seventh century, the great mosque was raised under the Aghlabids, and after the Hilalian collapse the local Banu al-Rand dynasty made the town its capital from 1053 until the Almohads overthrew it; a later revolt ended when Caliph al-Mansur stormed Gafsa in 1187. Al-Idrisi saw a walled city of crowded markets set among date palms, its fields growing henna and cotton, its Berber townsfolk still speaking a Latin tongue that lingered here into the 1200s. In 1444 its fifteenth-century kasbah commanded the northern gateway to the Djerid oases, under the loose authority of the Hafsid sultans of Tunis.

In 1551 Ottoman Turkish armies pushing into the Hafsid south laid siege to Gafsa, which held out for five years until it was reduced in 1556. A Turkish governor with an Ottoman garrison then kept the oasis for the regency of Tunis, and Turkish families were settled in the town to secure its taxes and the caravan road. Under the Husaynid beys who ruled Tunis from 1705, command of Gafsa passed to chiefs drawn from its own notables. Its dates and the salt gathered from the chotts continued to supply the trans-Saharan caravan trade long after.
zh:
加夫萨古称卡普萨，坐落于杰里德盐沼以北丘陵间一处泉水滋养的绿洲，是突尼斯、马格里布与黑非洲道路交会之地。7世纪末阿拉伯军队攻取此城，阿格拉布王朝时期建起大清真寺；希拉勒部落入侵、中央政权崩溃后，本地王朝于1053年起以加夫萨为都，直到被穆瓦希德王朝推翻，后来的一次反叛又在1187年招致哈里发曼苏尔发兵破城。伊德里斯笔下的加夫萨城墙环绕、市集喧闹，四周椰枣成林，田间种植指甲花与棉花，城中柏柏尔居民仍说拉丁语，这种语言在此一直存留到13世纪。1444年，15世纪建起的城堡扼守着杰里德绿洲群的北大门，只在名义上臣属于突尼斯的哈夫斯王朝苏丹。

1551年，攻入哈夫斯王朝南部的奥斯曼土耳其军队围攻加夫萨，城寨坚守五年，1556年才被制服。此后一名土耳其长官率领奥斯曼驻军替突尼斯行省镇守这处绿洲，又迁来土耳其人家族定居，以保障赋税与商路。1705年起统治突尼斯的侯赛因王朝把加夫萨的指挥权交给本地望族首领。此后很久，这里的椰枣和盐沼出产的盐仍供应着跨撒哈拉商队贸易。

en:
The arid hills of the Dahar and Matmata rise above the Jeffara plain in Tunisia's far south-east, where springs give the land its Berber name, Tiṭṭawin. Exposed between sea and desert, its Amazigh villagers perched their settlements on hilltops as ksour: walled citadels of stacked vaulted granary cells, or ghorfas, guarding stores and families against raiding parties. The oldest houses at Chenini go back to the twelfth century, and Douiret and its neighbours served as caravan stages on the track from Gabès south to Ghadames. In 1444 the land owed allegiance to the Hafsid sultan in Tunis, but power lay with the tribes and their fortified granaries rather than with governors.

The Hafsid kingdom crumbled in the early sixteenth century, and after the Ottoman conquest of Tunis in 1574 the south-east became the desert flank of the new regency. In the course of that century the Berber tribes of the Jeffara, the Akkara, Ouderna and Touazine among them, drew together as the Ouerghemma confederation, a semi-independent alliance that policed the desert road and the Tripolitanian frontier as makhzen warriors of the bey of Tunis. Its long feud with the Arab Nawaiel tribe of Tripolitania ran through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the age in which Ksar Ouled Soltane was raised above its valley, its earliest granaries dated to 1699. Grain, dates and livestock remained the wealth locked behind the ksar walls.
zh:
突尼斯最东南，达哈尔山与迈特马泰山耸峙在杰法拉平原之上，柏柏尔语地名Tiṭṭawin意为「泉眼」，得自山间的泉水。夹在海洋与沙漠之间，阿马齐格村民把村落修在山顶，建成一座座堡寨式储粮城（ksar）：层层拱顶粮窖（ghorfa）围合成堡，护着存粮和家小，以防匪帮劫掠。舍尼尼最古老的屋舍可追溯到12世纪，杜伊雷特等村庄则是加贝斯南往古达米斯商道上的驿站。1444年，这片土地名义上臣服于突尼斯城的哈夫斯苏丹，但实权操在部落和他们的堡寨手中，而非君主派来的官吏。

哈夫斯王国在16世纪初瓦解，1574年奥斯曼征服突尼斯后，东南山区成为新摄政国的沙漠侧翼。16世纪间，杰法拉的柏柏尔部落——阿卡拉、乌代尔纳、图阿津等——结成瓦尔加马联盟；这个近乎独立的部落同盟作为突尼斯贝伊的马赫赞武装，巡守沙漠大道和的黎波里塔尼亚边境。联盟与的黎波里塔尼亚阿拉伯部落纳瓦伊勒的长期仇杀贯穿17、18世纪；乌立德·苏丹堡也正是在这一时期耸立于山谷之上，其最早的粮窖断代为1699年。谷物、椰枣和牲畜，始终是锁在堡寨高墙之内的财富。

en:
Tripoli stands on a rocky point of the North African coast, where a natural bay looks across at Sicily. It was Oea, the only survivor of the three cities of Roman Tripolitania, alongside Sabratha and Leptis Magna. After the Arab conquest it was ruled in turn by dynasties based in Kairouan and Cairo, then by the Almohads, before passing to the Hafsids of Tunis. Around 1324 Thabit ibn Ammar of the Huwwara Berbers made the city autonomous under loose Hafsid overlordship; the Genoese seized it in 1354 and the Banu Thabit retook it in 1369, until a Hafsid army restored direct rule in 1401. In 1444 Tripoli was the principal port of the Hafsid east, its quays handling cloth and the gold, ivory and slaves that caravans brought north from Fezzan.

In 1510 a Spanish army under Pedro Navarro stormed the city after a bitter defence, and in 1530 Charles V granted it, with Malta, to the Knights of St John, who rebuilt the walls and the Red Castle. In 1551 the Ottoman admirals Sinan Pasha and Turgut Reis took Tripoli after a siege; Turgut, its first pasha, adorned the city and was buried there in 1565 in the Sidi Darghut Mosque he had founded. It became a corsair regency whose janissaries soon reduced the pasha to a figurehead, and Christian squadrons cruised off its walls; the French bombarded it into terms in 1686. In 1711 a janissary officer, Ahmed Karamanli, killed the Ottoman governor and founded a hereditary dynasty that ruled Tripolitania in near-independence, living by privateering and tribute. The wars with the young United States followed: in 1803 the frigate Philadelphia was taken in the harbour, though Stephen Decatur slipped in and burned her the next year, and in 1815 an American squadron forced the pasha to make peace.
zh:
的黎波里位于北非海岸一处突出的岩石岬角，天然海湾与西西里岛隔海相望。它古称奥伊阿，是罗马时代的黎波里塔尼亚三城中唯一存续者，与塞卜拉泰、大莱普提斯并称。阿拉伯征服后，城市先后由凯鲁万和开罗的王朝统治，继而归属穆瓦希德王朝，后来转入突尼斯的哈夫斯王朝治下。1324年前后，霍瓦拉柏柏尔人萨比特·本·阿马尔让城市在哈夫斯宗主权下自立；1354年热那亚人攻陷此城，巴努·萨比特家族于1369年将其收复，1401年哈夫斯大军攻入，恢复直接统治。1444年的的黎波里是哈夫斯东部的首要港口，码头吞吐布匹，以及商队从费赞北运的黄金、象牙和奴隶。

1510年，佩德罗·纳瓦罗率领的西班牙军队经苦战攻陷城市；1530年，查理五世把它连同马耳他一起封给圣约翰骑士团，骑士们重修城墙和红堡。1551年，奥斯曼海军统帅锡南帕夏和图尔古特·雷斯围城得手；首任帕夏图尔古特大力营建城市，1565年去世后葬在他所修建的西迪·达尔古特清真寺。的黎波里由此成为海盗摄政之国，禁卫军很快把帕夏架空成虚君，基督教各国舰队轮番巡弋城外，1686年法国人以炮火迫使它议和。1711年，禁卫军军官艾哈迈德·卡拉曼利杀死奥斯曼总督，建立世袭的卡拉曼利王朝，以近乎独立的地位统治的黎波里塔尼亚，靠海上劫掠和朝贡为生。随后便是与新生的美国的战争：1803年护卫舰「费城号」在港内被俘，斯蒂芬·迪凯特次年潜入港内将其烧毁；1815年，一支美国舰队迫使帕夏缔和。

en:
The old city of Surt stood on the Gulf of Sidra, a walled town a bow-shot from the sea when Ibn Hawqal passed through in 947; its Berber inhabitants grew dates, kept goats and camels and exported alum. After the Hilalians overran the region it shrank, and by the 13th century Ibn Sa'id saw only a fort where some Arabs dwelt; soon afterwards Surt was abandoned, its ruins at al-Mudayna half-buried in sand. In 1444 the coast between Tripoli and Benghazi was a stretch of Bedouin wells, cisterns and fishing beaches without a town, under the loose lordship of Fezzan.

When the traveller al-Ayyashi crossed it in 1662 the region obeyed Abd al-Rahman al-Jabali, styled 'master of his own soul'. Early in the 18th century the Awlad Suleiman and their Mahamid allies drove out the al-Jabali, who fled to Egypt's Fayyum, and for decades fought the Ottoman governors of Tripoli over the coastal pastures.
zh:
古城苏尔特坐落在苏尔特湾畔，伊本·豪盖勒947年路过时，它还是一座距海一箭之地的有墙城镇，柏柏尔居民种椰枣、放山羊和骆驼，并出口明矾。希拉尔部落涌入后城市衰落，13世纪伊本·赛义德见到的只剩一座还住着阿拉伯人的堡垒，此后苏尔特便遭废弃，遗址米迪奈半埋在沙中。1444年，的黎波里与班加西之间这段海岸只有贝都因人的水井、蓄水池和渔村，没有城镇，松散地处在南方费赞的治下。

1662年旅行家阿亚希经过时，这一地区听命于自称「自己灵魂的主人」的阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·贾巴利。18世纪初，奥拉德·苏莱曼部落联合马哈米德人赶走贾巴利家族，后者逃往埃及的法尤姆；此后数十年间，他们为争夺沿海牧场，与的黎波里的奥斯曼总督反复交战。

en:
The harbour below the Green Mountains grew up near a Greek colonial town planted beside a lagoon; in the third century BC that settlement was moved and refounded as Berenice. After the third century AD it outstripped Cyrene and Barca as the centre of the Pentapolis, but by the Arab conquest of 643 it had shrunk to a small town among ruins. The wider country became known in Arabic as Barqa and was drawn into Egypt's political orbit. After the migrations of the Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym in 1051-1052, Arab Bedouins dominated its pastures while the old port cities declined. In 1444 the Mamluk sultan in Cairo claimed suzerainty, but real power rested with Bedouin confederations; a small anchorage on this coast served Genoese merchants exchanging metalwork and cloth for the interior's livestock and pastoral products.

The Ottomans took Benghazi in 1578 and administered it through the rulers of Tripoli. In 1711 the Karamanli dynasty turned Tripoli into the centre of an autonomous regency, and Benghazi remained under that dynasty's authority in 1821. Greek and Italian sponge fishermen worked its coastal waters, while merchants continued to trade with tribesmen from the Cyrenaican plateau. The town stayed modest, overshadowed by Tripoli, valuable chiefly as a harbour for the livestock, hides and other products brought down from Bedouin pastures.
zh:
绿山北麓的这座海港，起于希腊人在一处澙湖边建立的殖民城市；公元前3世纪，旧城迁址，另建为贝列尼凯。公元3世纪以后，它超过昔兰尼和巴尔卡，成为五城地区的中心，但到643年阿拉伯人征服时，已衰败成废墟间的小镇。周围地区在阿拉伯语中称巴尔卡，政治上逐渐被纳入埃及的势力范围。1051至1052年巴努希拉尔、巴努苏莱姆等部落迁入后，阿拉伯贝都因人掌控了牧场，古老港口城市进一步衰落。1444年，开罗的马穆鲁克苏丹虽保有宗主权，实际权力却在贝都因部落联盟手中；海岸边的小锚地供热那亚商人往来，用金属器和布匹交换内地的牲畜和牧产品。

奥斯曼人1578年夺取班加西，通过的黎波里统治者进行管理。1711年，卡拉曼利王朝以的黎波里为中心建立自治政权，到1821年时班加西仍处在该王朝治下。希腊和意大利海绵渔民在附近海域作业，商人则继续同昔兰尼加高原的部落交易。这座城镇始终不大，声势远逊于的黎波里，价值主要在于它是贝都因牧场的牲畜、兽皮和其他物产外运的港口。

en:
Derna occupies a rare break in the dry coast between the Green Mountain and the Mediterranean, where Wadi Derna carries fresh water from mountain springs toward a small anchorage. Its ancient predecessor Darnis was a Greek and Roman port on the edge of the Libyan Pentapolis and later a Christian bishopric, but the medieval settlement was much diminished. The Mamluks of Cairo had extended their suzerainty over Barqa by the late thirteenth century, though tribal shaykhs and caravan routes usually mattered more than distant officials. In 1444 Derna was therefore a modest watering place and livestock market, useful to coastal traders, herdsmen and Bedouin moving between Egypt and Tripolitania.

In 1493 refugees from Islamic Spain resettled the old site and gave the port a new lease of life. Under Ottoman rule Derna at first answered to the pasha of Tripoli, and after Ahmed Karamanli seized power in 1711 it passed into the hereditary Karamanli regency. Mahmud Karamanli restored the Old Mosque in 1772, roofing it with small cupolas suited to a region short of timber. A French squadron under Admiral Gantheaume landed there in June 1800 hoping to send reinforcements overland to Napoleon in Egypt, but the local garrison refused it passage. During the First Barbary War William Eaton led a small mixed force across the desert from Alexandria and captured Derna in 1805, the first American battlefield victory on foreign soil.
zh:
德尔纳位于干燥海岸上一处难得的缺口，绿山与地中海在此相接，德尔纳河把山泉中的淡水引向一座小锚地。古城达尔尼斯曾是利比亚五城边缘的希腊与罗马港口，后来成为基督教主教驻地，但中世纪时已大为衰落。开罗的马穆鲁克人到13世纪末已把宗主权扩展到巴尔卡，不过真正左右日常的通常是部落谢赫和商路，而非远方官员。1444年的德尔纳因此只是一处小型补水地和牲畜市场，为沿海商人、牧民以及往来埃及与的黎波里塔尼亚的贝都因人服务。

1493年，来自伊斯兰西班牙的难民在古址上重新定居，使港口恢复生机。奥斯曼统治初期，德尔纳隶属于的黎波里帕夏；1711年艾哈迈德·卡拉曼利夺权后，它又归入世袭的卡拉曼利摄政政权。1772年，马哈茂德·卡拉曼利重修旧清真寺，以适应当地缺乏木材的环境，用许多小穹窿作顶。1800年6月，冈托姆海军少将率法国分舰队在此登陆，希望经陆路向埃及的拿破仑派出援军，却被当地驻军拒绝通行。第一次巴巴里战争期间，威廉·伊顿率领一支小规模混合部队从亚历山大穿越沙漠，于1805年攻占德尔纳，这是美军首次在外国土地上取得战场胜利。

en:
Alexandria was founded on the Mediterranean coast in 331 BC by Alexander the Great and became the capital of Ptolemaic and Roman Egypt. After the Arab conquests, government moved to Fustat, later absorbed by Cairo, but Alexandria kept its role as Egypt's chief port and naval base. Spices, incense, pearls, ivory and Indian woods came up the Red Sea to Aydhab, crossed by caravan to the Nile at Qus, and were shipped to Alexandria for Venetian, Genoese, Catalan and Provençal merchants, whose consuls and walled funduqs had existed there since the twelfth century. A crusader force sacked the city in October 1365, and repeated earthquakes left the Pharos lighthouse unusable by 1349. In 1444 a Mamluk emir and the sultan's customs officer governed a wealthy but strategically exposed spice port, politically overshadowed by Cairo.

In 1480 Sultan Qaytbay built a fortress on the lighthouse's foundations to guard the harbour. Within a generation, Vasco da Gama's voyage of 1498 opened an Atlantic route to India, drawing spices away from Alexandria and weakening Mamluk revenues. After the Battle of Ridaniya in 1517 the city passed to the Ottomans, and for much of the next three centuries it was overshadowed by Rosetta and suffered from a failing Nile waterway. Napoleon's troops took Alexandria on 2 July 1798; a British victory outside the city on 21 March 1801 was followed by the French surrender on 2 September. Muhammad Ali began rebuilding soon after 1810, and the Mahmoudiyah Canal, completed in 1820, restored fresh water and Nile traffic to the harbour, setting Alexandria on the road to renewed prosperity by 1821.
zh:
亚历山大公元前331年由亚历山大大帝建在地中海岸，后成为托勒密埃及和罗马埃及的首都。阿拉伯征服后，统治中心迁往福斯塔特，也就是后来开罗的一部分，但亚历山大仍是埃及首要海港和海军基地。香料、乳香、珍珠、象牙和印度木材先沿红海北上阿伊扎布，再由商队运到尼罗河畔的库斯，最后从水路送到亚历山大，交给威尼斯、热那亚、加泰罗尼亚和普罗旺斯商人；早在12世纪，这些商人已在此设有领事和带围墙的商馆。1365年10月，一支十字军洗劫城市，接连的地震又使法罗斯灯塔到1349年已无法进入。1444年，马穆鲁克埃米尔和苏丹的海关官共同管辖这座富庶却暴露在外的香料港，政治声势则笼罩在开罗之下。

1480年，盖特拜苏丹在灯塔旧址上修筑要塞，拱卫港湾。但不到一代人后，1498年瓦斯科·达·伽马开通通往印度的大西洋航路，香料不再大量经过亚历山大，马穆鲁克的岁入随之削弱。1517年里达尼叶战役后，城市转入奥斯曼人之手；此后三个世纪里，尼罗河支流水运衰败，亚历山大多半时间反被罗塞塔盖过。拿破仑的军队1798年7月2日夺取亚历山大，1801年3月21日英军在城外获胜，法军于9月2日投降。穆罕默德·阿里1810年后着手重建，1820年马哈茂迪耶运河完工，恢复了通往港口的淡水和尼罗河航运，使亚历山大在1821年走上复兴之路。

en:
The Fayyum is a Nile-fed desert basin rather than a spring-water oasis. Near al-Lahun the Bahr Yussef leaves the Nile valley, branches through the fields, and finally drains into Lake Qarun. Its market town stood on ancient Crocodilopolis, later Arsinoe, and around 1245 Ibn al-Nabulusi carried out one of the most detailed provincial surveys to survive from the medieval Arab world. East across the Nile valley, Beni Suef was known in the Middle Ages for linen. In 1444 the towns and villages of the Fayyum and Beni Suef were provincial possessions of the Burji Mamluks, governed through Cairo and tied to its grain and textile markets.

In 1517 Selim I's Ottoman army overthrew the Mamluk sultanate, but the new regime kept Mamluk emirs in provincial offices; the first Ottoman land survey of Egypt followed in 1527. Mamluk beys gradually recovered much local power during the following centuries. French forces took Cairo in 1798 and held Egypt until the British-Ottoman victory of 1801. Muhammad Ali seized power in 1805, and under his rule Beni Suef became the chief town of the second province of Upper Egypt, while Fayyum produce continued to move along the Bahr Yussef toward Cairo.
zh:
法尤姆不是依赖泉水的普通绿洲，而是由尼罗河引水滋养的沙漠盆地。优素福河在拉洪附近离开尼罗河谷，在田间分出支渠，最后注入加龙湖。河畔的法尤姆城位于古城鳄鱼城（后称阿尔西诺伊）旧址；1245年前后，伊本·纳布卢西在此完成了中世纪阿拉伯世界保存下来最详尽的地方地籍调查之一。东面尼罗河畔的贝尼苏韦夫，在中世纪以亚麻织造闻名。1444年，法尤姆和贝尼苏韦夫的村镇都是布尔吉马穆鲁克的地方辖地，由开罗统辖，同开罗的粮食与织物市场相连。

1517年，塞利姆一世的奥斯曼军队攻灭马穆鲁克苏丹国，但新政权仍保留马穆鲁克埃米尔担任地方官职；1527年，奥斯曼当局又对埃及进行了第一次土地普查。此后几个世纪里，马穆鲁克贝伊逐步重新掌握许多地方权力。1798年法军攻占开罗，并控制埃及至1801年英国—奥斯曼联军获胜为止。穆罕默德·阿里1805年掌权后，贝尼苏韦夫成为上埃及第二省的首邑；法尤姆的农产品则继续沿优素福河运往开罗。

en: Qus stands on the east bank of the Nile between Qena and Luxor, the Nile terminus for desert roads leading toward the Red Sea. After a new route opened in the 13th century, it replaced Qift as Upper Egypt's chief mart for goods from Arabia, Africa and India, drew pilgrim caravans, and housed troops, markets and madrasas serving the Sa'id. By the late 14th century trade was moving toward Girga, Qena and other routes, yet in 1444 Qus remained a Mamluk garrison and river town. The Ottoman conquest of 1517 tied it to the Egyptian eyalet, while Mamluk beys kept much provincial power; after the French occupation of 1798-1801, Muhammad Ali's rise from 1805 brought Upper Egypt under a stronger Cairo government.
zh: 古斯位于尼罗河东岸、基纳与卢克索之间，是通往红海的沙漠商道在尼罗河上的端点。13世纪新商路开通后，它取代吉夫特，成为上埃及交换阿拉伯、非洲和印度货物的主要市场，又有驻军、市集和伊斯兰学校，并接待前往麦加的商队。到14世纪末，商路转向吉尔贾和基纳等地，古斯声势渐衰，但1444年仍是马穆鲁克治下的驻军河港。1517年奥斯曼征服埃及后，这里隶属埃及省，地方实权仍多由马穆鲁克贝伊掌握；1798—1801年法国占领结束后，穆罕默德·阿里在1805年崛起，上埃及重新被开罗政府强力整合。

en:
Cairo grew up beside the Nile at the head of the Delta, where the Arab garrison town of Fustat was founded in 641 and the Fatimid caliphs laid out al-Qahira in 969, making it their capital four years later. Saladin began the Citadel in 1176, and under the Mamluks the city became the seat of a sultanate, a centre of scholarship around al-Azhar and a meeting point for spices from the Indian Ocean, Mediterranean merchants and Meccan pilgrims. The Black Death reached it in 1348 and returned repeatedly for generations, killing about 200,000 people in its worst waves. By 1444, Cairo held perhaps 150,000 to 300,000 people. Its Burji Mamluk sultan still ruled from the Citadel over a city whose bazaars and caravanserais had recovered partly through migrants from the Egyptian countryside.

Qaytbay, sultan from 1468 to 1496, was the last great Mamluk builder of the period, raising and restoring mosques and mausolea across the city. Cairo's commerce then lost much of the spice trade after Vasco da Gama opened the sea route around the Cape of Good Hope in 1497-1499. Sultan Selim I defeated al-Ghuri at Marj Dabiq in 1516 and conquered Egypt in 1517, reducing Cairo to the chief city of an Ottoman province while leaving Mamluk households considerable local power. The city remained an emporium for Yemeni coffee and Indian textiles and a provisioning centre for the hajj, with al-Azhar setting the tone of Sunni religious learning. Napoleon arrived in Cairo in 1798, but an Ottoman and British siege forced the French garrison to surrender on 22 June 1801. Rival Ottoman, Albanian and Mamluk factions fought on until Muhammad Ali, an Albanian commander, was recognized as viceroy in 1805 and made the Citadel the centre of a new Egyptian government.
zh:
开罗兴起于尼罗河畔、三角洲顶端。阿拉伯人641年在此建立驻军城镇福斯塔特，法蒂玛王朝969年规划新城「胜利之城」开罗，并在四年后定都于此。萨拉丁1176年开始修建城堡；马穆鲁克时期，这里既是苏丹国的权力中心，也是以爱资哈尔为核心的学术胜地，印度洋香料、地中海商人和麦加朝觐者在此交汇。黑死病1348年传入，此后反复流行，最严重的几波夺去约二十万人的生命。到1444年，开罗人口约在十五万至三十万之间。布尔吉系马穆鲁克苏丹仍在城堡发号施令，城里的市集和商队旅馆则依靠埃及乡村移民部分恢复了元气。

1468年至1496年在位的盖特拜是这一时期最后一位大兴土木的马穆鲁克苏丹，在开罗修建和整修了许多清真寺与陵墓。1497至1499年瓦斯科·达·伽马开辟绕好望角航路后，开罗商业失去了香料贸易的大宗收入。1516年，塞利姆一世在达比克草原击败苏丹古里，次年征服埃及，开罗降为奥斯曼一省的首要城市，但马穆鲁克家族仍保有相当大的地方权力。此后城市继续转运也门咖啡和印度织物，为朝觐队伍提供补给，爱资哈尔则主导着逊尼派宗教学术。拿破仑1798年进入开罗，奥斯曼与英国军队围城，法军于1801年6月22日投降。奥斯曼人、阿尔巴尼亚人和马穆鲁克各派继续相争，直到阿尔巴尼亚裔将领穆罕默德·阿里1805年被承认为总督，并以城堡为中心建立新的埃及政权。

en:
Rosetta, known in Arabic as Rashid, commands the Nile mouth that came to bear the same name. The medieval town grew around an Abbasid fort built on the site of Bolbitine in the 850s. Nearby Fuwwah and Alexandria overshadowed it under the Fatimids and Mamluks, although its wheat and barley lands, palm groves and fisheries gave the mouth real value. Louis IX briefly took Rashid in 1249 during the Seventh Crusade, and Baybars built a fortress there in 1262. Ships for the Mamluk campaign against Cyprus sailed from the town in 1426. Hospitaller galleys from Rhodes raided it in 1439 and carried off cattle and goods, a strong garrison was posted in 1451, and Qaytbay renewed the towers, castle and town wall in 1479. In 1444, Rashid was therefore a fortified Mamluk frontier town, guarding Nile grain traffic more than rivalling Alexandria as an emporium.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1517, neglect of the Alexandria canal made Rashid the convenient entrance for Mediterranean ships heading to Fuwwah, Desuq and Cairo. The town entered its economic golden age and reached its greatest extent in 1777, with about 15,000 inhabitants when Napoleon's expedition reached Egypt in 1798. French soldiers found the Rosetta Stone at nearby Fort Julien in 1799, and on 19 September 1807 the British Fraser expedition was defeated outside Rashid. The Mahmoudiyah Canal, completed in 1820, turned Nile traffic back towards Alexandria. By 1821 Rosetta's age as Cairo's preferred maritime gateway was already drawing to a close.
zh:
罗塞塔在阿拉伯语中称拉希德，扼守后来同名的尼罗河河口。中世纪城镇围绕850年代阿拔斯哈里发穆泰瓦基勒下令在博尔比廷旧址修建的要塞发展。法蒂玛和马穆鲁克时期，邻近的福沃与亚历山大遮蔽了它的光芒，但这里的小麦、大麦、椰枣和渔场仍使河口颇具价值。1249年，路易九世在第七次十字军期间短暂占领拉希德，拜巴尔斯1262年又在此修筑堡垒。1426年，马穆鲁克进攻塞浦路斯的舰队从此地出发。1439年，罗得岛医院骑士团的桨帆船来袭，掠走牲畜和货物；1451年苏丹贾格马克派驻重兵，1479年盖特拜又整修塔楼、城堡和城墙。因此在1444年，拉希德是一座设防的马穆鲁克边疆城镇，主要护卫尼罗河谷物运输，而不是与亚历山大一争高下的商港。

1517年奥斯曼征服埃及后，亚历山大运河失修，拉希德反而成为地中海船只前往福沃、德苏克和开罗的便捷门户，进入经济黄金时代，并在1777年达到最大规模；1798年拿破仑远征军到达埃及时，城中约有一万五千人。1799年，法国士兵在附近的朱利安要塞发现罗塞塔石碑。1807年9月19日，英国弗雷泽远征在拉希德城外战败。1820年马哈茂迪耶运河完工，尼罗河航运重新转向亚历山大。到1821年，罗塞塔作为开罗首选海上门户的时代已接近尾声。

en:
Damietta (Dumyat) stands on the eastern branch of the Nile, fifteen kilometres from the Mediterranean, on a narrow strip between the river and Lake Manzala. It was Tamiathis in antiquity, and rose to importance as the old Canopic mouth of the Nile silted up and the port of Tinnis was abandoned in the twelfth century, leaving it one of Egypt's two chief sea gates alongside Alexandria. Crusaders twice made it their target: the Fifth Crusade took the city in November 1219 after a cruel siege and held it until al-Kamil drove them out in 1221, and Louis IX of France landed there on 4 June 1249 at the head of the Seventh Crusade, only to be captured at al-Mansura and ransom himself by giving Damietta back in May 1250. The Mamluks rebuilt the ruined town, and under Sultan al-Ashraf Barsbay it became the seat of a provincial deputy. In 1444 it was a busy Mamluk port, shipping the grain and rice of the Delta to Cairo and the wider Mediterranean.

After the Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517 Damietta kept its place among the busiest harbours of the Delta: in 1783 nearly five hundred ships entered or left the port, and its customs takings of 1786–1798 were surpassed only by those of Cairo and Alexandria. On 16 August 1732 a small squadron of the Order of Malta seized an Ottoman convoy off its coast and freed the Christian slaves aboard. French troops occupied the city during Bonaparte's invasion of 1798, and with the French evacuation of 1801 it returned to Ottoman rule. Under Muhammad Ali, who seized power in 1805, Damietta held some 30,000 people and served as the great warehouse of Egyptian rice; canals were dug, bridges raised and a weaving mill opened, but the Mahmudiyya Canal, completed in 1820, soon drew the Delta's trade toward Alexandria.
zh:
达米埃塔（杜姆亚特）位于尼罗河三角洲东支杜姆亚特河上，北距地中海十五公里，城在河道与曼宰莱湖之间的狭长地带上。其古称塔米阿提斯，随着古卡诺皮克河口淤塞、邻近的提尼斯港在12世纪废弃，它崛起为埃及与亚历山大并列的两大海上门户之一。十字军曾两度以此为目标：第五次十字军经惨烈围城于1219年11月攻占此城，直到1221年被卡米勒逐出；法兰西国王路易九世率第七次十字军于1249年6月4日在此登陆，却在曼苏拉兵败被俘，最终以交还达米埃塔赎身，1250年5月城归埃及。马穆鲁克人重建了残破的城市，阿什拉夫·巴尔斯拜苏丹在位时这里成为行省副王的驻地。1444年的达米埃塔是马穆鲁克王朝繁忙的港口，将三角洲出产的谷物和稻米运往开罗和更广阔的地中海。

1517年奥斯曼征服埃及后，达米埃塔仍是三角洲最繁忙的港口之一：1783年进出港船只近五百艘，1786至1798年的关税收入仅次于开罗和亚历山大。1732年8月16日，一支马耳他骑士团的小舰队在达米埃塔外海截获奥斯曼护航船队，放走了船上的基督教奴隶。1798年拿破仑入侵埃及时法军占领该城，1801年法军撤离后重归奥斯曼统治。穆罕默德·阿里1805年掌权时，达米埃塔约有三万居民，是埃及稻米的大货仓，任内开凿运河、架设桥梁、开设纺织厂，但1820年马哈茂德运河通航后，三角洲的贸易很快被引向亚历山大。

en:
Gaza stands on the last rise before the Sinai desert, the gateway where the coast road between Egypt and Syria leaves the Nile lands. The Mamluks made it the seat of the Mamlakat Ghazzah in 1277, a governorship running up the coast from Rafah to beyond Caesarea, and Emir Sanjar al-Jawli filled it with mosques, colleges, caravanserais and baths after 1311. The Great Mosque, once a crusader cathedral, was rebuilt by Baybars with a great manuscript library; a few years after the plague of 1348 and the rare flood of 1352, Ibn Battuta in 1355 found the city large and populous and many-mosqued. Caravans between the Nile and Damascus paid tolls at its gates, and the townsmen prided themselves as keepers of the birthplace of al-Shafi'i, founder of the Shafi'i school of law. In 1444 Gaza was a provincial capital of the Mamluk sultanate, Sunni and Arabic-speaking, its Jewish community restored after the crusading centuries.

In 1481 a Jewish traveller from Volterra still counted fifty or sixty Jewish households in an unwalled town four miles about, rich in fruit and wine. The Ottoman army arrived in 1516 after Marj Dabiq, and Gaza became chief town of a sanjak in the province of Damascus. Its Ridwan governors gave the city its last Ottoman golden age: Ahmad ibn Ridwan worked with the jurist Khayr al-Din al-Ramli, while under Husayn Pasha peace was made with the Bedouin and Gaza served, men said, as the virtual capital of Palestine, its Great Mosque restored and six new mosques raised. After Musa Pasha the family was removed from office, and with Bedouin pressure growing about half the district's villages were abandoned in the seventeenth century; only around 1800 did settlement begin to spread again across the coastal plain.
zh:
加沙坐落在西奈沙漠前最后一处高地上，是埃及通往叙利亚的沿海大道离开尼罗河流域后的门户。1277年，马穆鲁克以加沙为加沙省的治所，辖区沿海岸从拉法一直延伸到凯撒里亚以北；1311年后，埃米尔桑贾尔·乔利在这里广修清真寺、学院、商栈和浴场。大清真寺的前身是十字军的主教座堂，后由拜巴尔重建，并附设一座宏大的写本图书馆。1348年的瘟疫和1352年罕见的洪水过去没几年，伊本·白图泰1355年见到的加沙仍然城大民稠、清真寺林立。往返尼罗河与大马士革的商队在城门口缴纳商税，加沙人也以沙斐仪法学派创始人沙斐仪的诞生地为荣。1444年的加沙是马穆鲁克苏丹国的省城，居民讲阿拉伯语、信奉逊尼派，十字军时代后回归的犹太社群也已恢复。

1481年，一位来自沃尔泰拉的犹太旅人仍在这座没有城墙、周长约四英里的城里数出五六十户犹太人家，城中瓜果和葡萄酒丰饶。1516年达比克草原战役后，奥斯曼大军抵达，加沙成为大马士革省下辖一个桑贾克的首邑。里德万家族的历任总督给了这座城市在奥斯曼时代最后的黄金岁月：艾哈迈德·伊本·里德万与法学家海鲁丁·拉姆利合作，侯赛因帕夏治下与贝都因人修好，时人都说加沙实际上是巴勒斯坦的都城——大清真寺得到修缮，还新建了六座清真寺。穆萨帕夏之后里德万家族被罢免，随着贝都因压力日增，17世纪全地区约有一半村落废弃；直到1800年前后，沿海平原上的定居点才重新多了起来。

en:
The arid mountains of southern Sinai stand between the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba, the desert bridge between Africa and Asia. Bedouin Arabs held the wells and pastures, guided caravans, and carried local trade between the interior and the coast; Arabic tradition calls the peninsula the land of turquoise. On the Gulf of Suez shore, At Tur had grown up in the thirteenth century near an old Christian settlement and was valued for its springs. Inland, below Jabal Musa, the fortified Orthodox monastery of Saint Catherine had stood since its construction under Justinian I in 527–565. In 1444 Cairo's Mamluk sultans ruled the country, but beyond the roads and the port their authority rested on arrangements with the Bedouin.

As Mamluk power weakened, Bedouin raiders captured and sacked Saint Catherine's in 1505; the sultan demanded restitution but could not restore order in the mountains. The Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517 placed Sinai under Selim I and the governors of Ottoman Egypt. During the Red Sea war against Muslim shipping, Estêvão da Gama's Portuguese armada attacked At Tur in 1541 while moving against Suez, drove out its Ottoman garrison, and sacked the port. The Portuguese failed to take Suez and withdrew, leaving Sinai a remote Ottoman frontier where the monastery, the caravan wells, and Bedouin tribal power remained the fixed facts of life.
zh:
南西奈的干旱山脉横亘在苏伊士湾与亚喀巴湾之间，构成非洲和亚洲之间的沙漠陆桥。贝都因阿拉伯人掌握水井和牧场，为商队引路，也在内地与海岸之间转运货物；阿拉伯传统称西奈为绿松石之地。苏伊士湾畔的图尔（At Tur）于13世纪在一处古老基督教聚落附近兴起，城中泉水十分珍贵。内地摩西山下，设防的希腊正教会圣凯瑟琳修道院自查士丁尼一世527—565年在位时建成后便屹立于此。1444年，开罗的马穆鲁克苏丹统治着这片土地，但在道路和港口之外，其权威主要依赖与贝都因部落维持的安排。

马穆鲁克势力衰落时，贝都因袭掠者于1505年攻占并洗劫了圣凯瑟琳修道院；苏丹要求归还财物，却无力在山中恢复秩序。1517年奥斯曼征服埃及，西奈归入塞利姆一世和奥斯曼埃及总督治下。1541年，在争夺红海航运的战争中，埃斯特旺·达伽马率领葡萄牙舰队进攻苏伊士途中袭击图尔，逐走奥斯曼守军并劫掠港口。葡萄牙人未能夺取苏伊士，最终撤退；西奈仍是遥远的奥斯曼边地，修道院、商队水井和贝都因部落势力始终是这里生活的固定现实。

en:
Gran Canaria is a steep volcanic island in the Canaries. Its Canario people, probably related to the Berbers of North Africa, farmed and herded along its barrancos under native rulers called guanartemes. Jean de Béthencourt's early-fifteenth-century invasion failed, though his chronicle helped fix the name Gran Canaria, and later European raids brought slaves and plunder rather than lasting rule. In 1444 the island was still independent: Castile and Portugal coveted its anchorage and farmland, but Las Palmas did not yet exist and the sugar economy had not been planted.

On 24 June 1478 Juan Rejón landed for Castile and founded the fortified camp of Real de Las Palmas beside the Guiniguada ravine. The war lasted five years: Doramas fell at Arucas, Tenesor Semidán, guanarteme of Gáldar, was captured and baptized as Fernando Guanarteme, and resistance ended near Ansite on 29 April 1483. Portuguese settlers then built the first sugar mills, while Genoese, Flemish and Aragonese merchants tied the island to Atlantic trade. The diocese moved to Las Palmas in 1485, Columbus anchored there on his first voyage in 1492, Drake was repulsed in 1595, and a Dutch army under Pieter van der Does sacked and burned the city in 1599 before island militias drove it out.
zh:
大加那利是加那利群岛中一座地势崎岖的火山岛。岛上的卡纳里奥人可能与北非柏柏尔人有亲缘关系，沿沟壑耕作放牧，由称为瓜纳特梅的本地首领统治。15世纪初，让·德·贝当古的征服失败，但他的编年史使「大加那利」之名流传下来；此后欧洲人的袭击只带来奴隶和劫掠，并未建立长久统治。1444年的岛屿仍保持独立，卡斯蒂利亚和葡萄牙都觊觎它的锚地与农田，但拉斯帕尔马斯尚未建立，糖业经济也还没有出现。

1478年6月24日，胡安·雷洪代表卡斯蒂利亚登陆，在吉尼瓜达溪口建立设防营地皇家拉斯帕尔马斯。战争持续五年：多马拉斯在阿鲁卡斯战死，加尔达尔首领特内索尔·塞米丹被俘后受洗，改名费尔南多·瓜纳特梅并协助征服者，抵抗最终于1483年4月29日在安塞特附近结束。葡萄牙移民随后建起最早的糖厂，热那亚、佛兰德和阿拉贡商人把岛屿纳入大西洋贸易。1485年教区迁至拉斯帕尔马斯，1492年哥伦布首航美洲途中曾在此停泊；1595年德雷克的进攻被击退，1599年彼得·范·德·多斯率领荷兰军队焚掠城市，最后仍被岛民民兵逐出。

en:
The Azores are nine volcanic islands spread across the North Atlantic, with no confirmed population before the Portuguese voyages. Diogo de Silves found the eastern islands in 1427, and a royal charter of 2 July 1439 authorized Prince Henry to settle seven islands where sheep had already been put ashore. Under Captain Gonçalo Velho, families from Alentejo, the Algarve and Estremadura began colonizing Santa Maria that year. In 1444 settlement was extending to São Miguel, while Flores and Corvo would not be reached until 1452. The new colonists lived from fish, wheat, livestock, timber, woad and orchil, and the Crown divided the islands into hereditary donatary captaincies.

Flemish settlers became numerous after Joss van Hurtere received Faial in 1468, and for years northern maps called the central islands the Flemish Islands. Angra, on Terceira, became an episcopal see in 1534. During the Portuguese succession crisis the Azores acclaimed António, Prior of Crato, and repulsed a Castilian attack at Salga, but Álvaro de Bazán defeated the Franco-Portuguese fleet off Vila Franca on 26 July 1582 and conquered Terceira in 1583, sacking Angra. English raiders struck in 1589 and returned without success in 1598. After the 1640 restoration, local militias blockaded the Spanish fortress on Monte Brasil until its surrender on 4 March 1642. In 1766 the Pombaline government replaced the old captaincies with a Captaincy General seated at Angra.
zh:
亚速尔群岛是散布在北大西洋上的九座火山岛，葡萄牙人到来前没有已确认的常住居民。迪奥戈·西尔韦斯于1427年发现东部诸岛；1439年7月2日的王家特许状授权恩里克王子在七座已放养绵羊的岛屿上殖民。受封首领贡萨洛·维利乌当年带领来自阿连特茹、阿尔加维和埃什特雷马杜拉的家庭开始定居圣玛丽亚岛。1444年，殖民活动正扩展到圣米格尔岛，而弗洛雷斯岛和科尔武岛要到1452年才被抵达。早期移民以鱼类、小麦、畜牧、木材、菘蓝和石蕊苔为生，葡萄牙王室则把各岛划为世袭的受封首领辖区。

1468年约斯·范·许尔特受封法亚尔岛后，佛兰德移民大量到来，北方地图曾长期把中部诸岛称为佛兰德群岛。1534年，特塞拉岛上的英雄港成为主教驻地。葡萄牙王位继承危机期间，亚速尔拥戴克拉图修道长安东尼奥，并在萨尔加击退卡斯蒂利亚军；但阿尔瓦罗·德·巴桑于1582年7月26日在维拉弗兰卡外海击败法葡舰队，又在1583年征服特塞拉岛，洗劫英雄港。英格兰劫掠者1589年来袭，1598年再次进攻却未成功。1640年葡萄牙复国后，本地民兵围困巴西山的西班牙要塞，迫其于1642年3月4日投降。1766年，蓬巴尔政府废除旧有受封首领辖区，改设驻英雄港的亚速尔总都督府。

en:
Madeira is a wooded volcanic island with the smaller, drier Porto Santo nearby. The islands had no permanent population when João Gonçalves Zarco and Tristão Vaz Teixeira found Porto Santo in 1418; with Bartolomeu Perestrelo they reached Madeira at Machico in 1419. Ordered colonization began around 1425, bringing families from the Algarve and northern Portugal, former prisoners and lesser nobles to clear the laurel forest, cut water channels called levadas and sow wheat. Machico became the first formally invested captaincy in 1440. In 1444 the young colony still lived chiefly from grain, fish and timber, while Funchal remained a modest south-coast anchorage.

Zarco received the Funchal captaincy in 1450. Sugar cane, Sicilian technicians, Genoese capital, water-driven mills and the levadas then turned Madeira into Europe's leading sugar supplier by 1490, drawing Flemish merchants and enslaved labourers from the Canaries and African coasts. Funchal became a bishopric in 1514 and a mandatory Atlantic port of call. Competition from Brazil and São Tomé weakened sugar in the late sixteenth century, and vineyards gradually took its place; English merchants came to dominate the fortified wine trade. Barbary corsairs carried off more than 1,800 islanders in 1617, and British forces garrisoned Madeira in 1801-1802 and again from 1807 to 1814.
zh:
马德拉是一座林木茂密的火山岛，旁边是较小而干燥的圣港岛。若昂·贡萨尔维斯·扎尔科和特里斯唐·瓦斯·特谢拉于1418年发现圣港岛时，岛上并无常住人口；次年，两人与巴尔托洛梅乌·佩雷斯特雷洛在马希库一带抵达马德拉岛。1425年前后，奉王命开展的殖民把阿尔加维、葡萄牙北部的家庭、获释囚犯和低级贵族带来此地，他们砍伐月桂林，开凿名为列瓦达的引水渠，种植小麦。1440年，马希库成为第一个正式授封的首领辖区。1444年的年轻殖民地仍主要依靠谷物、渔获和木材，丰沙尔还只是南岸一处不大的锚地。

扎尔科于1450年受封丰沙尔首领辖区。此后，甘蔗、西西里技师、热那亚资本、水力磨坊和列瓦达水渠共同改变了马德拉；到1490年，这里已成为欧洲最重要的糖料供应地，吸引佛兰德商人前来，也使用来自加那利群岛和非洲沿岸的奴隶劳动力。丰沙尔1514年成为主教驻地，也是大西洋航线上的必经停靠港。16世纪后期，来自巴西和圣多美等地的竞争削弱了糖业，葡萄园逐渐取代甘蔗田，英国商人后来主导了加强葡萄酒贸易。1617年，巴巴里海盗从岛上掳走一千八百多人；1801年至1802年，以及1807年至1814年，英国军队曾两度驻防马德拉。

en:
Orkney is a cluster of some seventy islands ten miles off Caithness, where the North Sea meets the Atlantic. Harald Fairhair of Norway made them a Norwegian earldom in 875, and for six centuries the islands belonged to the Nordic world: Norn was the speech of farm and fishing boat, the bishop answered to Nidaros, and the Orkneyinga saga recorded the feuds of its earls. At Kirkwall, Earl Rognvald began St Magnus Cathedral in 1137 to honour his uncle Magnus, killed in 1115. In 1444 the earldom was held of the Norwegian crown by William Sinclair, a baron who held estates in Lothian as well; the fertile islands grew grain and salted the teeming herring of their fishing grounds, while their ultimate lord was the Kalmar king reigning in Copenhagen.

In 1468 Christian I pledged Orkney and Shetland as security for the dowry of his daughter Margaret, bride of James III; the money was never paid, William Sinclair yielded the earldom for Scottish estates, and on 20 February 1472 the Scottish parliament annexed the islands. Kirkwall became a royal burgh in 1486. The Stewarts then ruled the islands as feudal lords: Robert Stewart, illegitimate son of James V, was made earl in 1581, and his son Patrick's tyrannies ended with his execution for treason in 1615, when the islands reverted to the crown. In March 1650 the Marquess of Montrose gathered his last small army in Orkney before crossing to Sutherland, where defeat at Carbisdale on 27 April delivered him to the scaffold. Dutch and Scottish boats had long swept the herring grounds, and from the 1670s Orcadians made up the bulk of the Hudson's Bay Company's servants in Canada. The islands were stoutly Jacobite: after 1715 fugitives were smuggled through them to Sweden, and in 1746 Orkney was the last corner of Britain to submit, holding out until 24 May. By 1800 kelp burned for soda ash had become the islands' second trade beside fish.
zh:
奥克尼是凯斯内斯以北十英里、北海与大西洋交汇处七十余座岛屿组成的群岛。875年挪威国王「金发」哈拉尔将群岛设为挪威伯国，此后六百年这里属于北欧世界：农田和渔船上讲的是诺恩语，主教听命于尼达罗斯，《奥克尼萨迦》记下了历代伯爵的仇杀。1137年，伯爵罗格瓦尔德在柯克沃尔动工修建圣马格努斯大教堂，以纪念1115年遇害的叔父马格努斯。1444年时，伯国由威廉·辛克莱从挪威王冠处领有，这位男爵在洛锡安也拥有地产；肥沃的岛屿种植谷物，人们把渔场里密布的鲱鱼腌制成货，群岛的最高君主则是坐镇哥本哈根的卡尔马联盟国王。

1468年，克里斯蒂安一世把奥克尼和设得兰抵押出去，作为女儿玛格丽特嫁给苏格兰国王詹姆斯三世的嫁妆担保；这笔钱始终未付，威廉·辛克莱交出伯国、换取苏格兰本土的地产，1472年2月20日苏格兰议会正式吞并群岛，柯克沃尔则于1486年成为皇家自治镇。此后斯图亚特家族以封建领主身份统治群岛：詹姆斯五世的私生子罗伯特·斯图亚特1581年受封伯爵，其子帕特里克的暴政以1615年以叛国罪被处决、群岛收归王冠告终。1650年3月，蒙特罗斯侯爵在奥克尼集结起他最后一支小小的军队，渡海前往萨瑟兰，4月27日在卡比兹代尔战败，随即被送上断头台。荷兰和苏格兰的渔船长期在群岛渔场作业，1670年代起，奥克尼人又占了哈德逊湾公司在加拿大雇员的大多数。群岛对詹姆斯党忠心耿耿：1715年叛乱失败后，逃亡者经此被秘密送往瑞典；1746年奥克尼更是不列颠最后归顺的角落，一直坚持到5月24日。到1800年前后，烧制海带制取纯碱已成为群岛仅次于渔业的第二大产业。

en:
Reykjavík's bay on Faxaflói was settled, according to the Book of Settlements, when the Norwegian chieftain Ingólfr Arnarson made his homestead there in 874; hot springs gave the place its name of Smoky Bay. No town followed for centuries. Iceland came under the Norwegian Crown by the Old Covenant of 1262-1264, and in 1444 it formed part of the Kalmar Union under the Danish-Norwegian Crown. Catholic Icelandic families around the bay lived from sheep pastures, fishing and stockfish, while English merchants largely controlled the valuable stockfish trade from the 1430s to the 1470s.

Plague returned to Iceland in 1494-1495, and the Reformation reached the island by force when Jón Arason, its last Catholic bishop, was beheaded in 1550. From 1602 the Danish-Norwegian Crown confined Icelandic commerce to licensed trading posts and fixed prices, a monopoly that lasted until the end of 1787. In 1752 Frederik V granted the Reykjavík estate to Skúli Magnússon's Innréttingar, whose wool houses gave the little settlement its first regular industry. In 1786 Reykjavík received a trading charter as the monopoly was being dismantled, marking the birth of the future capital.
zh:
据《定居书》记载，挪威首领英戈尔夫·阿尔纳松于874年在法赫萨湾的雷克雅未克湾建立农庄，附近温泉喷出的蒸汽使这里得名「冒烟的海湾」。此后数百年间，城镇并未出现。冰岛依据1262年至1264年的《旧约》归入挪威王权，1444年时已是丹麦-挪威王权治下卡尔马联盟的一部分。海湾周边信奉天主教的冰岛家庭以牧羊、捕鱼和风干鱼为生，1430年代至1470年代，价值不菲的风干鱼贸易大体掌握在英格兰商人手中。

1494年至1495年，瘟疫再度袭击冰岛。1550年，冰岛最后一任天主教主教约恩·阿拉松被斩首，宗教改革以强力推行。1602年起，丹麦-挪威王权把冰岛商业限制在特许贸易站并实行定价，这一垄断一直延续到1787年底。1752年，弗雷德里克五世把雷克雅未克庄园交给斯库利·马格努松主持的革新会，其毛纺织作坊为这个小居民点带来第一项稳定产业。1786年，随着垄断被拆除，雷克雅未克获得贸易特许状，这座未来首都由此诞生。

en:
Akureyri lies at the head of Eyjafjörður, one of Iceland's longest fjords, where fertile river lowlands meet a sheltered, ice-free harbour. The Norse settler Helgi the Slim took land in the district during the ninth century, but no town grew on the later town site. In 1444 the shore was a string of Catholic Icelandic farms and fishing stations belonging to the Norwegian realm within the Kalmar Union. Much of the north's medieval commerce passed through Gásir, about eleven kilometres north of modern Akureyri, where stockfish and farm produce were exchanged with visiting merchants.

The name Akureyri first appears in court records in 1562, after the Reformation had ended Catholic jurisdiction in Iceland. During the seventeenth century Danish traders using the royal commercial monopoly pitched seasonal camps on the Pollurinn spit, drawn by the harbour and productive hinterland. A permanent settlement was not established until 1778. In 1786 Christian VII granted Akureyri a municipal charter together with five other Icelandic communities, but the new town had only twelve inhabitants and long remained a modest northern outlet rather than a second Reykjavík.
zh:
阿克雷里位于冰岛最长峡湾之一埃亚峡湾的尽头，肥沃的河谷低地与避风不冻港在此相接。诺斯移民「瘦子」赫尔吉在9世纪占下这一带土地，但后来的城址当时并未形成城镇。1444年，海岸上只有一串信奉天主教的冰岛农庄和捕鱼站，属于卡尔马联盟中的挪威王国。北部中世纪贸易多经过今阿克雷里以北约11公里的Gásir，外来商人在此交换风干鱼和农牧产品。

宗教改革结束冰岛的天主教管辖权之后，阿克雷里之名首次见于1562年的法庭记录。17世纪，获得王室商业垄断权的丹麦商人看中这里的港湾和富饶腹地，在波卢林沙洲设立季节性营地。永久性居民点直到1778年才出现。1786年，克里斯蒂安七世与另外五个冰岛聚居地一同授予阿克雷里市镇特许状，但这座新镇只有十二名居民，在1821年以前始终只是北部一个小规模贸易口岸，而不是第二个雷克雅未克。

en:
Tyrone takes its name from Tír Eoghain, the 'land of Eoghan', the core lordship of the Cenél nEógain and the O'Neills. From Dungannon, where the O'Neills held a castle on Castle Hill, their chiefs dominated mid-Ulster, while their kings were inaugurated at Tullyhogue Fort. The older kingdom had once reached toward Lough Foyle, but in 1444 it remained a Catholic Gaelic power beyond the English Pale, its politics shaped by rivalry with the O'Donnells and by the loyalty of lesser Ulster chiefs.

Tudor pressure turned the lordship into repeated war. Shane O'Neill routed the Earl of Sussex's army in 1561 and had himself inaugurated as The Ó Néill at Tullyhogue, only to be defeated and killed in 1567. Hugh O'Neill led the Nine Years' War and burned Dungannon Castle in 1602 as Lord Mountjoy's forces closed in. After Hugh fled in the Flight of the Earls in 1607, the Crown confiscated O'Neill land and planted it with English and Scottish Protestants; Dungannon passed to Sir Arthur Chichester. A royal school was chartered in 1608 and opened in the town in 1636. Sir Phelim O'Neill seized Dungannon in 1641, and it changed hands during the Confederate Wars. James II visited its Jacobite garrison in 1689, and in 1782 the town hosted the Volunteer convention demanding Irish legislative independence.
zh:
蒂龙其名来自蒂尔·欧文（Tír Eoghain），意为「欧文之地」，是欧文后裔与奥尼尔家族的核心领地。奥尼尔首领以邓甘嫩城堡丘上的城堡为驻地，控制阿尔斯特中部，首领则在塔利霍格堡举行即位仪式。古老王国的势力曾北抵福伊尔湾；1444年，它仍是英格兰佩尔之外的天主教盖尔强权，政治深受与奥唐奈家族的竞争和小部族忠贰的影响。

都铎王朝的压力把这片领地拖入连年战争。肖恩·奥尼尔1561年击溃萨塞克斯伯爵的军队，并在塔利霍格堡即位为「奥尼尔」，但1567年战败被杀。休·奥尼尔领导九年战争，1602年芒乔伊勋爵的王军逼近时烧毁邓甘嫩城堡。1607年休在「伯爵逃亡」中离开爱尔兰后，王室没收奥尼尔家族土地，安排英格兰和苏格兰新教徒移居，邓甘嫩被授予阿瑟·奇切斯特爵士。皇家学校1608年获敕许，1636年在城中开办。费利姆·奥尼尔爵士1641年夺取邓甘嫩，联盟战争期间城镇又数次易手。1689年詹姆斯二世曾到访驻守此地的詹姆斯党军队；1782年，城中召开志愿兵会议，要求爱尔兰议会拥有独立立法权。

en:
The Pale (Irish An Pháil) was the English crown's fortified coastland around Dublin, the port where the Liffey meets Dublin Bay. Dublin began as a Viking base in 841, but after the Anglo-Norman takeover of 1171 it became the seat of the Lordship of Ireland; John ordered Dublin Castle built in 1204, and from 1297 the Parliament of Ireland had its main seat there. Edward Bruce's raids, the Black Death of 1348 and the Gaelic revival steadily shrank English authority. In 1444 Dublin was a walled Catholic merchant town of perhaps 5,000 to 10,000 people, while the countryside loyal to the crown formed a small embattled enclave guarded by ditches and marcher lords.

In 1454 workmen were levied to dig trenches on the border; in 1494 Edward Poynings's parliament used the name 'English Pale' for the first recorded time. The Fitzgerald earls of Kildare dominated this marcher world, and Dublin was used in 1487 to proclaim the Yorkist pretender Lambert Simnel. The revolt of Silken Thomas Fitzgerald in 1534–1535, including his siege of Dublin Castle, broke their power and turned Dublin into the main base of the Tudor conquest. Elizabeth I founded Trinity College in 1592 as a Protestant university. Plague in 1649–1651 killed nearly half the city, yet the wool and linen trade restored its fortunes; by 1700 more than 50,000 people lived there. George Frideric Handel's Messiah was first performed in 1742, the Wide Streets Commission began remodelling the city in 1757, and the Guinness brewery opened in 1759. The Acts of Union in 1800 closed the era of the Irish Parliament in Dublin.
zh:
佩尔（爱尔兰语An Pháil）是英格兰王室在都柏林周围设防的沿海地带，港口都柏林位于利菲河注入都柏林湾处。都柏林841年由维京人建立据点，1171年盎格鲁-诺曼人接管后成为爱尔兰领地的统治中心；约翰王1204年下令修建都柏林堡，1297年起爱尔兰议会主要在此召开。爱德华·布鲁斯的袭扰、1348年黑死病和盖尔文化复兴不断压缩英格兰势力。1444年的都柏林是一座有城墙的天主教商业城镇，人口约五千至一万；效忠于王室的乡野则是靠壕沟和边疆领主守卫的狭小飞地。

1454年，官府征发民夫在边界挖掘壕沟；1494年，爱德华·波伊宁斯召开的议会首次在文献中使用「英格兰佩尔」一名。基尔代尔的菲茨杰拉德伯爵家族长期主导这片边防地带，1487年约克家族觊觎者兰伯特·西姆内尔便是在都柏林被拥立为王。绰号「绸衣托马斯」的托马斯·菲茨杰拉德在1534—1535年叛乱并围攻都柏林堡，家族权势由此崩解，都柏林转而成为都铎征服爱尔兰的主要基地。伊丽莎白一世1592年创立新教大学都柏林三一学院。1649—1651年的瘟疫使近半居民丧生，但羊毛和亚麻贸易让城市恢复，1700年人口已超过五万。1742年，格奥尔格·弗里德里希·亨德尔的《弥赛亚》首演；1757年宽街委员会开始改造街道，1759年健力士酒厂创办。1800年《联合法案》结束了爱尔兰议会在都柏林的时代。

en:
This part of Leinster is the southeastern coast around Wexford, where the Slaney enters Wexford Harbour. Vikings raided from 819 and settled the town by the late ninth century; its Norse community remained largely independent until May 1169, when Diarmait Mac Murchada and Robert Fitz-Stephen besieged Wexford at the opening of the Anglo-Norman invasion. The town received its first charter in 1318, while the MacMurrough-Kavanaghs recovered much of the inland north. Art Óg MacMurrough-Kavanagh dominated the region's Gaelic and Anglo-Norman lords and faced Richard II in the campaigns of 1394–1395. In 1444 Catholic Wexford was an Old English walled port, but its cattle-raising hinterland and the Ferns lowlands were still strongly Gaelic.

Between 1536 and 1541 Henry VIII's government dissolved the local monasteries, including Dunbrody and Tintern. County Wexford supported the rebellion of 1641 and Confederate Ireland, and Wexford sheltered privateers who raided Parliamentarian shipping. Cromwell's army took and sacked the town in 1649, confiscating Irish and Old English lands for its soldiers; after the Boyne, James II sailed from Duncannon into exile. In 1798 the county became the rebellion's heart. United Irishmen took Enniscorthy and Wexford, but their camp on Vinegar Hill and their attack on New Ross ended in defeat, with massacres and reprisals on both sides.
zh:
伦斯特的这一部分是韦克斯福德周围的东南海岸，斯拉尼河在此注入韦克斯福德港。维京人819年起前来劫掠，到9世纪末已在城中定居；这里的诺斯社群长期保持很大独立性，直到1169年5月，迪亚马特·麦克穆尔查达与罗伯特·菲茨斯蒂芬在盎格鲁-诺曼入侵开端时围攻韦克斯福德。城镇1318年获得第一份特许状，麦克穆尔罗-卡瓦纳家族则收复了北部内陆的大片土地。阿特·奥格·麦克穆尔查达·卡瓦纳压过本地盖尔和盎格鲁-诺曼领主，并在1394—1395年对抗理查二世的征伐。1444年，信奉天主教的韦克斯福德是一座旧英格兰人聚居的设防港口，但其畜牧腹地和费恩斯低地仍有浓厚的盖尔色彩。

1536—1541年间，亨利八世政府解散当地修道院，邓布罗迪和廷滕两所修道院也在其中。韦克斯福德郡支持1641年叛乱和爱尔兰邦联，韦克斯福德还为袭击议会派航运的私掠船提供庇护。克伦威尔的军队1649年攻占并洗劫这座城镇，随后没收爱尔兰人和旧英格兰人的土地，分给麾下士兵；博因河战役后，詹姆斯二世从邓坎农启航流亡。1798年，该郡成为叛乱中心。联合爱尔兰人攻占恩尼斯科西和韦克斯福德，但他们在维尼格山的营地和对纽罗斯的进攻最终失败，双方都出现屠杀与报复。

en:
Limerick guards the head of the Shannon Estuary, its medieval core on King's Island, ringed by the Shannon and the Abbey River. Norse longships first raided up the Shannon in 812, and by 922 a Viking settlement had taken root on the island, growing into a sea-kingdom that rivalled Dublin until Brian Boru broke its Norse kings and made Limerick his capital. The Normans came in 1173; Domnall Mór Ua Briain burned the town rather than surrender it, but Prince John's men took it in 1195, and the charter of 1197 installed a mayor and a merchant council. King John's Castle rose on the island around 1200, beside St Mary's Cathedral, with English Town within the walls and Irish Town on the south bank. In 1444 Limerick was a self-governing merchant city, nominally the Crown's westernmost outpost but long cut off from the Pale, trading with the Gaelic lords around it while the O'Briens of Thomond held the Clare bank of the Shannon.

In 1642 the Catholic Confederates seized King John's Castle, and in 1651 Henry Ireton's Cromwellian army starved and bombarded the city into surrender after famine and plague had killed some 5,000 of its people. Limerick withstood William of Orange's siege in 1690, when Patrick Sarsfield's cavalry destroyed the Williamite siege train, but the second siege forced its surrender, and the Treaty of Limerick was signed on 3 October 1691 on a stone by Thomond Bridge. Sarsfield sailed for France with some 19,000 men, the first great Flight of the Wild Geese; the treaty's guarantees to Catholics were then discarded and the Penal Laws followed. In the eighteenth century the port grew rich shipping the beef, butter and grain of the Golden Vale to Britain and America, and the Georgian terraces of Newtown Pery gave the city a new centre, until the Act of Union of 1800 ended its protected trade.
zh:
利默里克扼守香农河口湾的湾头，中世纪老城位于香农河与阿比河环绕的王岛上。诺斯长船812年首次溯香农河而上前来劫掠，到922年，维京人已在岛上定居，发展成一个与都柏林分庭抗礼的海上王国，直到布赖恩·博鲁攻灭这里的诺斯国王，以利默里克为都。诺曼人1173年到来，多姆纳尔·莫尔·奥布赖恩宁肯焚城也不投降，但约翰王子的部下仍于1195年攻占此地，1197年的特许状设立了市长和商人议会。1200年前后，约翰王城堡在岛上建成，与圣马利亚大教堂相望，城墙内是「英格兰镇」，南岸是「爱尔兰镇」。1444年的利默里克是一座自治的商人城市：名义上是英王治下最西的据点，实则早已和英格兰人实际控制的佩尔地区隔绝，与周围的盖尔领主通商往来；香农河对岸的克莱尔一带则在托蒙德的奥布赖恩家族手中。

1642年，天主教联盟军夺取约翰王城堡；1651年，亨利·艾尔顿麾下的克伦威尔军队以围困和炮轰迫使城市投降，此前饥荒和瘟疫已夺去约五千人的性命。1690年，利默里克顶住了奥兰治的威廉的围攻，帕特里克·萨斯菲尔德的骑兵还摧毁了围城军的辎重火炮；但1691年的第二次围攻以投降告终，1691年10月3日，双方在托蒙德桥旁的一块石头上签署《利默里克条约》。萨斯菲尔德率约一万九千人扬帆赴法，是为第一次「野雁大出走」；条约给予天主教徒的保证旋即被废弃，随之而来的是《刑法》。18世纪，利默里克港把黄金谷出产的牛肉、黄油和粮食运往英国和美洲，因商致富，佩里新城的乔治式排屋为城市添了新的中心，直到1800年《联合法案》终结了它受保护的贸易地位。

en:
Galway, the only medieval city of Connacht, sits where the Corrib runs out of Lough Corrib into the Atlantic. In 1124 Tairrdelbach Ua Conchobair, King of Connacht and High King of Ireland, raised a fort at the river mouth to anchor his fleet. Richard Mór de Burgh took it in 1232, and under the de Burghs the trading town grew behind walls; a murage charter of 1396 licensed its merchants to fortify themselves against the Gaelic lords and their own Burke cousins alike. By 1444 Galway was ruled by the clique of English-descended merchant families later called the Fourteen Tribes, shipping wine and salt between Spain, France and the western isles, while its nominal overlords, the Clanricard Burkes, held the plains and castles of the east of the county.

In December 1484 a royal charter freed the town from the Clanricard Burkes and put the collegiate church of St Nicholas under the townsmen's wardenship; Christopher Columbus had called there in 1477 on a voyage to the far north. On 19 August 1504 the Lord Deputy Kildare defeated Ulick Fionn Burke, sixth Clanricarde, at Knockdoe. The townsmen went over to the Catholic Confederates in 1642 and held out through a nine-month Parliamentarian siege before surrendering in 1652, when plague and the Cromwellian transplantation to Connacht emptied much of the town. After the Jacobite army was destroyed at Aughrim on 12 July 1691, Galway capitulated under the Articles of Galway without a siege. The Penal Laws then shut its Catholic merchants out of the corporation, the harbour fell into decay, and in 1755 the Lisbon earthquake sent a wave over the Spanish Arch; by then brandy smuggled through gaps in the old walls was one of the port's steadiest trades.
zh:
戈尔韦是康诺特唯一的中世纪城市，坐落在科里布河从科里布湖注入大西洋的河口。1124年，康诺特国王、爱尔兰至高王泰尔德巴赫·奥康却拜尔在河口修筑要塞，作为舰队的锚地。1232年，理查德·莫尔·德·伯格攻占要塞；在德·伯格家族治下，商贸城镇在城墙内成长，1396年的筑墙特许状授权商人自行设防，既防盖尔领主，也防与自己同宗的伯克族人。到1444年，戈尔韦由后来被称为「十四部族」的一批英格兰裔商人家族把持，把葡萄酒和盐贩往西班牙、法国和西海诸岛；名义上的宗主克兰里卡德伯克家族，则占据着郡东部的平原与城堡。

1484年12月，王室特许状使城镇摆脱克兰里卡德伯克家族的控制，圣尼各老协同教堂也划归市民自己的教务长管辖；哥伦布1477年远航北方途中曾在此停留。1504年8月19日，爱尔兰总督基尔代尔伯爵在诺克多击败第六代克兰里卡德尤利克·菲恩·伯克。1642年，市民倒向天主教联盟，坚守了议会军九个月的围攻，终在1652年投降；瘟疫加上克伦威尔政权向康诺特的强制移民，使城镇大半空虚。1691年7月12日詹姆斯党军队在奥赫里姆被歼灭后，戈尔韦依《戈尔韦条款》不战而降。此后《刑法》把信奉天主教的商人排挤出市政机构，港口日渐荒废，1755年里斯本大地震引发的巨浪还冲毁了西班牙拱门一带；到这时，穿过旧墙缺口走私白兰地，已成了这座港口最稳定的生意之一。

en:
Aleppo crowns a low hill on the Quweiq River, where the caravan road from Mesopotamia and Persia comes down to the Mediterranean. It was already ancient when the Arabs took it in 637; the Hamdanid prince Sayf al-Dawla made it his capital in 944, and under the Zengid Nur al-Din and the Ayyubids it vied with Damascus. The Mongols sacked it in 1260, Tamerlane's army stormed it in 1400 and raised a tower said to hold 20,000 skulls outside the walls, and the city took a generation to recover. Under the Mamluks it was the seat of a great viceroyalty: its covered markets handled the silk of Iran and the spices of India, and in 1420 its Christian brokers laid out the al-Jdayde quarter outside the walls to deal with foreign merchants. In 1444, with a Mamluk governor in the citadel, Aleppo was once more the busiest caravan city in Syria, though still rebuilding after Timur's ruin.

On 24 August 1516 Selim I's Ottoman army destroyed the Mamluks at Marj Dabiq, a day's march north of the city, where Aleppo's governor Khai'r Bey had secretly gone over to the sultan; the town then opened its gates without a fight. It became the seat of the Aleppo Eyalet and by the mid-sixteenth century had overtaken Damascus as the empire's principal silk market. Venetian, French, English and Dutch consulates opened in 1548, 1562, 1583 and 1613, Sinan's Khusruwiyah Mosque was completed in 1547, and the great khans and covered souks took their present form. The city's wealth made it a rebel's prize: in 1606 the Kurdish governor Ali Janbulad ruled all Syria from Aleppo until Kuyucu Murad Pasha crushed his musketeers in the Amik Valley in October 1607, and in February 1659 the celali rebel Abaza Hasan Pasha was murdered in Aleppo after being lured there with a false pardon. In the eighteenth century the Persian wars choked the silk caravans, while the city was torn by the feud of its Janissaries with the ashraf, the Prophet's descendants; after a fresh rising in 1804 the governor Jelal al-Din Pasha trapped and slaughtered the Janissary commanders in 1813. By 1821 the caravan age was fading, but Aleppo, close to 400,000 strong, remained one of the greatest cities of the Ottoman East.
zh:
阿勒颇雄踞于库韦克河畔的一座低丘之上，是美索不达米亚和波斯的商路通向地中海的门户。阿拉伯人637年攻取它时，它已是一座古城；944年，哈姆丹王公赛义夫·道莱以此为都，后来在赞吉王朝的努尔丁和阿尤布王朝治下，它一度与大马士革争辉。蒙古人1260年洗劫此城，帖木儿的军队1400年再破城墙，据说在城外堆起以两万颗头颅筑成的京观，城市花了一代人时间才恢复元气。马穆鲁克时期，阿勒颇是一方大总督区的治所：有顶集市吞吐着伊朗生丝和印度香料，1420年，城中的基督徒掮客在城墙外辟建朱代达区，专与外国商人交易。1444年，城堡中坐镇着马穆鲁克总督，阿勒颇重新成为叙利亚最繁忙的商队之城，只是帖木儿留下的创伤尚未完全平复。

1516年8月24日，塞利姆一世的奥斯曼军队在城北一日路程的达比克草原击溃马穆鲁克——阿勒颇总督哈伊尔贝伊早已暗中倒向苏丹——城市随即不战开门。阿勒颇成为阿勒颇行省省会，到16世纪中叶已取代大马士革，成为帝国首要的生丝市场。威尼斯、法国、英国、荷兰分别于1548、1562、1583、1613年在此设立领事馆，锡南设计的胡斯鲁维耶清真寺1547年落成，一座座巨大的商队客栈和有顶集市也在这一时期形成今日的格局。财富使它成为叛党觊觎的大奖：1606年，库尔德族总督阿里·詹布拉德据阿勒颇自立，一度号令整个叙利亚，直到掘井者穆拉德帕夏1607年10月在阿米克谷地歼灭其火枪手；1659年2月，杰拉里叛党阿巴扎·哈桑帕夏被一纸虚假赦免诱入城中杀害。18世纪，对波斯的战争使生丝商队断绝，城中又陷入禁卫军与圣裔两派的世仇，巷战不断；1804年新一轮起事后，总督哲拉尔丁帕夏于1813年设伏，将禁卫军头目一网打尽、尽数诛杀。到1821年，商队时代已近尾声，但拥有近四十万人口的阿勒颇，仍是奥斯曼东方最伟大的城市之一。

en:
Tripoli takes its name from a Phoenician 'triple city' whose three quarters belonged to Tyre, Sidon and Arwad. Arab armies took it in 635, and under the Fatimids it was a nearly independent port famed for its Dar al-Ilm, a library to rival Baghdad's. The Crusaders under Raymond of Saint-Gilles entered it in 1109 after a long siege and put that library to the torch, and for 180 years it was the capital of the County of Tripoli, a silk-weaving town of perhaps four thousand looms, busy with sugar and citrus and guarded upcountry by the Hospitallers' Krak des Chevaliers. In 1289 Sultan Qalawun stormed it for the Mamluks, destroyed the old harbour town and rebuilt four kilometres inland beneath the Crusader citadel. The new city ranked third among the Mamluk provinces of Syria, after Aleppo and Damascus: its amirs raised the Mansouri Great Mosque in 1294 and a score of madrasas, while merchants shipped sugar, soap, olive oil, grain and velvet to Europe. Unwalled but ringed with watchtowers such as the Lion Tower, in 1444 Tripoli was a rich Mamluk viceroyalty of perhaps 30,000 people.

After the Mamluk defeat at Marj Dabiq the city passed to Selim I's Ottomans in 1516, and Suleiman the Magnificent later restored its citadel. In 1579 Tripoli became the seat of its own eyalet under Yusuf Sayfa, its first pasha, who long fought the Druze emir Fakhr al-Din II for the hill country and briefly submitted to the rebel Ali Janbulad at the Krak des Chevaliers in 1606, before the revolt was crushed the following year. Until 1612 Tripoli served as the port of Aleppo; in that year a great flood swept through its mosques. Khan al-Saboun was built about the same time, and Hammam al-Jadid followed in 1740. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries French merchants kept the leading factories here, loading grain, cotton, silk and soap for Marseille, and the city remained one of the busiest ports of Ottoman Syria.
zh:
的黎波里之名来自腓尼基人的「三联城」，三个城区分属推罗、西顿和阿尔瓦德。635年阿拉伯军队攻占该城，法蒂玛时代它是近乎独立的港口，以堪与巴格达比肩的「知识之宫」图书馆闻名。雷蒙·德·圣吉尔率领的十字军经长期围城于1109年入城，纵火焚毁这座图书馆；此后180年间它是十字军的黎波里伯国首府，丝织业发达，织机多达四千张，蔗糖和柑橘贸易繁忙，内陆有医院骑士团的骑士堡为屏障。1289年苏丹盖拉温为马穆鲁克攻克该城，摧毁旧港城，在十字军城堡下四公里处的内陆另建新城。新城在马穆鲁克叙利亚诸省中位列第三，仅次于阿勒颇和大马士革：埃米尔们1294年建起曼苏尔大清真寺和二十来所经文学院，商人把蔗糖、肥皂、橄榄油、谷物和丝绒运往欧洲。城市不设城墙，而以狮子塔等瞭望塔环绕；1444年的的黎波里是富庶的马穆鲁克总督治所，人口约有三万。
