en: The upper Sekong winds south through Attapeu, the remote southeastern march of the Lan Xang kingdom. Its old name Idkabue means 'buffalo dung', from the wild herds that pastured its forest clearings; Lao Theung villages held the highlands, and ivory, cardamom and wax moved down the river to the Mekong. In 1444 this was a thin, animist frontier governed through local chiefs rather than a walled town. The muang was formally founded in 1560, under King Setthathirat of Lan Xang. When the kingdom broke apart, Attapeu emerged as one of the three small Lao principalities of the lower Mekong's left bank, alongside Bassac and Stung Treng. In 1777 Taksin of Siam's army overran the south with little fighting, and from 1778 Attapeu followed Champasak as a tributary of Bangkok.
zh: 塞公河上游蜿蜒穿过阿速坡，这里是澜沧王国东南边陲。旧称Idkabue，意为「牛粪」，得名于在林间空地吃草的野牛群；老听人村寨据守高地，象牙、豆蔻和蜂蜡顺河南下运往湄公河。1444年时这里还是人烟稀少的泛灵信仰边陲，靠当地头人治理，并无筑城的市镇。阿速坡城于1560年澜沧国王赛塔提拉在位时正式设立。澜沧分裂后，阿速坡崛起为湄公河下游左岸三个佬人小邦之一，与巴塞、上丁并立。1777年，暹罗达信的军队几乎未遇激战便席卷南部，1778年起阿速坡同占巴塞一样向曼谷称臣纳贡。

en:
Angkor—Yasodharapura, the 'capital city'—spread across the plain north of the Tonlé Sap, where Jayavarman II founded the Khmer Empire in 802 and Yasovarman laid out the first great city around 889. Suryavarman II raised Angkor Wat in the early twelfth century, and Jayavarman VII later girdled Angkor Thom with walls and built the Bayon. By the time the Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan visited in 1296, Theravada Buddhism had displaced the old Hindu cults. Monsoon failures, silted reservoirs and pressure from Ayutthaya then sapped the city: it first submitted to Siam in 1351, and a Khmer revolt brought the Siamese sack of 1431. King Ponhea Yat abandoned Yasodharapura, moving first to Basan and then to Chaktomuk, the future Phnom Penh. In 1444 Angkor was a thinned, partly forested capital whose people had largely followed the court south, though Buddhist monks still kept Angkor Wat and its ponds in use.

Angkor was never wholly deserted. Around 1560, so the Portuguese historian Diogo do Couto reported, a Khmer king came upon the ruins while hunting elephants and planned to move his court back, and inscriptions show the crown repairing temples between 1577 and 1578. The Capuchin friar António da Madalena visited in 1586, and Japanese Buddhist pilgrims kept coming; one of them, Ukondayu Kazufusa, celebrated the Khmer New Year at Angkor Wat in 1632. During the Siamese–Cambodian war of 1591–1594 an Ayutthayan column campaigned against Siem Reap and Kampong Svay. In 1795 the new Bangkok dynasty placed the northwest, including Siem Reap, under its own governor at Battambang, and the 'Inner Cambodian' provinces were ruled from Siam. In the dynastic war of 1811–1813 Siamese armies marched out of Battambang against King Ang Chan, who returned in 1813 behind Vietnamese bayonets; by 1821 Angkor answered to Bangkok.
zh:
吴哥，即耶输陀罗补罗，高棉语意为「首都」，铺展在洞里萨湖北岸的平原上。802年阇耶跋摩二世在此建立高棉帝国，约889年耶输跋摩一世建起第一座大城；12世纪初苏利耶跋摩二世筑起吴哥窟，12世纪末阇耶跋摩七世又修建了吴哥通王城和巴戎寺。1296年中国使节周达观到访时，上座部佛教已取代旧有的印度教信仰。此后季风失常、水库淤塞，加上阿瑜陀耶的逼迫，城市日渐凋敝：1351年首次臣属于暹罗，高棉人反叛后，暹罗军队在1431年洗劫吴哥。国王博涅亚弃守耶输陀罗补罗，先后迁都巴山（斯雷桑托）和四臂湾，即后来的金边。1444年的吴哥人口流散、部分城区没入丛林，只有佛教僧侣仍维持着吴哥窟的香火和水池。

吴哥从未被彻底遗弃。据葡萄牙史家迪尤哥·都古托记载，约在1560年，一位高棉国王猎象时重见废墟，曾打算把宫廷迁回；碑铭也显示1577至1578年间王室出资修缮了部分寺庙。方济各会修士安东尼奥·达·马格达莱纳1586年前来寻访，日本佛教朝圣者也络绎于途，其中名唤Ukondayu Kazufusa者于1632年在吴哥窟庆祝了高棉新年。1591至1594年暹罗—柬埔寨战争期间，一支阿瑜陀耶军队进攻了暹粒和磅斯外一带。1795年，曼谷新王朝把包括暹粒在内的西北各省交给驻马德望的亲暹长官治理，这片被称为「内柬埔寨」的土地从此由暹罗管辖。1811至1813年的王室内乱中，暹罗军队出兵马德望攻打国王安赞二世，安赞1813年靠越南军队护送才得以复国；到1821年，吴哥已听命于曼谷。

en:
Known to the Chinese commanderies as Cửu Chân, this coast took the name Thanh Hóa in 1029, when the Lý court turned the old Ái Châu march into a prefecture. In 1397 the minister Hồ Quý Ly raised the great stone citadel of Tây Đô at Vĩnh Lộc and moved the Trần court south from Thăng Long, but the Ming conquered his short-lived dynasty in 1407 and ruled the country as Jiaozhi. The hill country never accepted it: in 1418 Lê Lợi raised his standard at Lam Sơn, took Nghệ An in 1424 and drove the Ming out by 1427. As Lê Thái Tổ he built at Lam Sơn the western capital of Lam Kinh, its palace and ancestral temple facing the Chu River. In 1444, early in the Later Lê dynasty, Thanh Hóa was the imperial homeland, its clans supplying the court at Đông Kinh with generals, consorts and soldiers.

In 1466–1469 Lê Thánh Tông recast the provinces and Thanh Hóa became the Thanh Hoa thừa tuyên, four prefectures reaching into the Sầm uplands. After Mạc Đăng Dung seized the throne in 1527, the restoration came from Thanh Hóa lineages: in 1533 Nguyễn Kim of Gia Miêu raised the Lê banner in the Ai Lao hills, and after his murder in 1545 his son-in-law Trịnh Kiểm of Biện Thượng led the southern court from its camp at Vạn Lại until Trịnh armies retook Đông Kinh in 1592. Sent to govern distant Thuận Hóa in 1558, Kim's son Nguyễn Hoàng built the southern domain whose heirs fought the Trịnh–Nguyễn wars of 1627–1672; the Trịnh drew their crack regiments solely from Thanh Hóa and Nghệ An. When the Tây Sơn fleet came north in 1786 the Trịnh governor of Thanh Hóa fled without a fight. In 1788 the last Lê emperor called in a Qing army; Nguyễn Huệ marched up the mandarin road through Thanh Hóa and destroyed it at Ngọc Hồi–Đống Đa in the first month of 1789. His dynasty fell in 1802 to Nguyễn Phúc Ánh of the Gia Miêu line, who reigned as Gia Long.
zh:
清化在汉唐郡县时代称九真，1029年李朝改爱州为清化府，「清化」之名由此始。1397年，权臣胡季牦在永禄修筑巨石城垒西都，把陈朝朝廷从升龙南迁，但其胡朝国祚短促，1407年明军南下灭胡，将安南置为交趾。山区始终不服：1418年黎利在蓝山举兵，1424年采纳阮只之计攻取乂安为根本，转战数年，至1427年迫使明军依东关之誓撤出。黎利称帝后在故乡蓝山营建西京蓝京，宫城与太庙面向朱江。1444年正值后黎初年，清化是王朝的龙兴之地，朝中的将帅、后妃与精兵多出此地。

1466至1469年黎圣宗重定版图，清化改为清化承宣，领四府，辖境伸入山间的岑州。1527年莫登庸篡位后，勤王之举正起自清化望族：1533年嘉苗的阮淦在哀牢山中奉立黎庄宗；1545年阮淦遇刺，其婿、汴上的郑检继领南朝，设行营于万赖，至1592年郑军终于收复东京。1558年，阮淦之子阮潢受命出镇遥远的顺化，开创阮氏基业，两家后人于1627至1672年间连兵相争，是为郑阮纷争；郑氏的精锐「优兵」也只从清化、乂安两籍签取。1786年西山军沿海北上，清化镇官不战而逃。1788年末，末代黎帝乞来清军入关，西山帝阮惠自乂安兼程北上、取道清化，于1789年正月在玉洄—栋山大破清军。1802年，嘉苗阮氏的后人阮福映攻灭西山，是为嘉隆帝。

en:
Sikhottabong guarded a middle Mekong reach below the limestone ridges of Khammouane. Its riverside crossing, later called Thakhek, was also known during Lan Xang times as Muang Kabong and Lakhon. Fa Ngum's army passed through Thakhek and Kham Muang in the 1350s, drawing the old mueang into Lan Xang's network. The riverside That Sikhottabong preserved the memory of the older Sikhottabong kingdom and was said to have been built by King Nanthasene. In 1444, after a generation of royal assassinations at Luang Prabang, it remained a Lao mueang of Lan Xang; narrow floodplains grew rice, while the Mekong carried ivory, benzoin and lac from the interior.

During Đại Việt's White Elephant War of 1478–1479, a Vietnamese column pushed south toward Vientiane and the Lan Xang court fled down the Mekong. In 1539 Photisarath made a pilgrimage to Sikhottabong, and the shrine was restored under Setthathirath after the royal capital moved downriver to Vientiane in 1560. The mueang remained a regional trading power, sending highland goods downstream toward the Khone Falls. When Lan Xang split in 1707, Sikhottabong passed to the Kingdom of Vientiane; Burmese overlordship in the 1760s gave way to Siamese suzerainty after Vientiane fell in 1779. In 1804 Anouvong inherited that tributary throne, and in 1821 the Mekong crossing at Thakhek still belonged to his Vientiane kingdom.
zh:
西科达邦扼守甘蒙石灰岩山岭下方的一段湄公河中游河道。河畔渡口后来称他曲，澜沧时期也叫Muang Kabong和Lakhon。14世纪50年代，法昂的军队经他曲和甘蒙北上，把这座旧孟纳入澜沧的勐邦网络。河畔的西科达邦佛塔保存着更古老的西科达邦王国记忆，相传由南塔森王（Nanthasene）修建。1444年，在琅勃拉邦经历约一代弑立纷争之后，这里仍是澜沧治下的佬人孟邦；狭窄河漫滩种植稻米，湄公河则把内陆的象牙、安息香和紫胶运往下游。

1478—1479年的白象战争中，一支大越军队向南逼近万象，澜沧王廷沿湄公河南逃。1539年，波迪萨拉到西科达邦朝圣；1560年赛塔提拉把王都迁往湄公河下游的万象后，这座佛塔也得到修葺。西科达邦仍是区域贸易重镇，高地货物从此顺流运往孔瀑布一带。澜沧1707年分裂后，西科达邦归属万象王国；18世纪60年代它受缅甸宗主权支配，1779年万象陷落后又改受暹罗宗主权。1804年，阿努冯继承这个藩属王位；到1821年，他曲的湄公河渡口仍属于他的万象王国。

en:
Khorat guards the western edge of the Khorat Plateau, where the Lam Takhong runs toward the Mun on the road from the Ayutthaya lowlands to the Lao and Khmer interior. The old town at Sema was the chief place of Srijanasa, a Dvaravati kingdom whose 9th-century inscriptions praise its kings in Sanskrit and Khmer, and farther east the Khmer raised Phimai: a stone Buddhist temple of Suryavarman I's day and a walled stage on the highway from Angkor, which Jayavarman VII linked to the capital with seventeen rest houses. As Khmer power ebbed, King Borommarachathirat II of Ayutthaya campaigned against Phimai and Phanom Rung in 1431. In 1444 the Ayutthayan border post here was Mueang Korakha on the Lam Takhong, a fortified town facing Lan Xang and the Khmer kings of Lovek, whose Khmer-speaking villagers wove silk for trade.

King Borommatrailokkanat ranked Khorat among the eight great provincial cities under a hereditary governor. Cambodian troops sacked it in 1570, and Naresuan later made it a second-class city. In 1674 King Narai abandoned old Korakha for a new walled town on the present site, laid out with bastions by the French engineer De la Mare and named Nakhon Ratchasima, with Chaiyaphum, Phimai, Buriram and Nang Rong among its dependencies. After Narai died in 1688 his governor held out against King Phetracha until 1690, and in 1698 a headman named Bun Kwang seized the town and withstood a three-year siege. When Ayutthaya fell in 1767, Prince Thepphiphit ruled these parts from Phimai until Taksin's generals, the brothers Thong Duang and Bunma, crushed him in 1768. As Rama I, Thong Duang made Khorat a first-class stronghold watching the Lao kingdoms of Vientiane and Champasak.
zh:
呵叻镇守着呵叻高原的西缘，南空河在此一带流向蒙河，正是从阿瑜陀耶平原通往老挝、高棉内陆的大道门户。社玛古城曾是陀罗钵地时期斯里阇那沙国的首邑，9世纪的碑铭以梵文与高棉文称颂其王；其东的披迈有苏利耶跋摩一世时代的石砌佛寺，也是吴哥大道上有城墙围护的驿镇，阇耶跋摩七世在首都到披迈的沿途设了十七处宿馆。高棉势力衰退后，阿瑜陀耶王三披耶于1431年征讨披迈与帕侬蓝。1444年，南空河畔的呵功目拉城（Mueang Korakha）是阿瑜陀耶在此的边防重镇，与澜沧及洛韦的高棉诸王相望，说高棉话的乡民以织绸贩卖为生。

戴莱洛迦纳王把呵叻列为八大府城之一，城主世袭。1570年高棉军队攻破此城，纳黎萱后来将它定为二级城。1674年，那莱王放弃旧呵功目拉城，在今址另建新城，由法国工程师德拉马尔（De la Mare）按棱堡形制修筑城墙，赐名那空叻差是玛，猜也蓬、披迈、武里南、娘隆皆为其属城。那莱王1688年去世后，他任命的城主抗拒碧罗阇王，坚守到1690年；1698年，名叫文宽（Bun Kwang）的乡民率众夺城，苦守三年才被攻灭。1767年阿瑜陀耶陷落后，王子贴披披以披迈为据点割据一方，1768年被郑昭麾下的通銮、汶玛兄弟讨平；通銮日后成为拉玛一世，把呵叻升为一等要塞，监视万象与占巴塞等老挝人属国。

en:
Đông Kinh stands at the heart of the Red River delta. In 1010 Lý Thái Tổ fixed the capital of Đại Việt on the old citadel site of Đại La and named it Thăng Long, the 'ascending dragon'. After the Ming conquest in the early fifteenth century the city knew two decades of rule as Đông Quan, until the Lam Sơn insurgent Lê Lợi drove the Ming out and in 1428 renamed it Đông Kinh, the 'eastern capital', from which Europeans took the name Tonkin. In 1444 it is again the seat of the Lê court, though the emperor Lê Nhân Tông is a small boy and his mother, Queen Dowager Tuyên Từ, rules as regent; junks crowd the wharves, and downstream at Bát Tràng the kilns fire the bowls and plates carried out by the tribute and trade fleets.

In 1459 the young emperor was murdered in a palace coup, and in 1460 Lê Thánh Tông seized the throne; his Hồng Đức reign was the high noon of the restored Lê, when Confucian scholars replaced the old warrior lords, laws and exams were remade, and the armies overran the Cham lands. In 1527 the strongman Mạc Đăng Dung usurped Đông Kinh and founded the Mạc dynasty, and the Trịnh clan won the city back only in 1592; the last Mạc held Cao Bằng until 1677. Thereafter the Lê emperors reigned while the Trịnh lords ruled, fighting long, inconclusive wars with the Nguyễn lords of the south; European envoys put the city's population at about 100,000. In 1788 the last Lê emperor, Chiêu Thống, called in a Chinese Qing army, which entered Đông Kinh; the Tây Sơn leader Nguyễn Huệ destroyed it at Ngọc Hồi and Đống Đa outside the walls early in 1789, among the proudest victories in Vietnamese history. In 1802 the Gia Long emperor, Nguyễn Ánh, took Thăng Long, moved the capital to Huế, and reduced the old city to a fortified northern gateway of the Nguyễn empire.
zh:
东京地处红河三角洲腹地。1010年，李太祖在旧大罗城的位置上定都大越，号称升龙，取「龙飞升」之意。15世纪初明军征服大越后，该城以「东关」之名受明朝直辖约二十年，直到蓝山起义的黎利驱逐明军，于1428年改名东京——欧洲人由此把这里叫作「东京」（Tonkin）。1444年，这里再度是黎氏朝廷所在，不过皇帝黎仁宗尚在幼年，由母亲宣慈皇太后摄政；码头上商船云集，下游钵场社的窑火烧出瓷碗瓷盘，随贡船与商船出海。

1459年幼帝在宫廷政变中遇害，1460年黎圣宗夺权登基，洪德年间成为中兴黎朝的盛世：儒臣取代旧勋贵，律令与科举为之一新，大军南下攻占占城之地。1527年，权臣莫登庸篡据东京，建立莫朝，郑氏直到1592年才收复此城，莫氏余部退守高平，一直撑到1677年。此后黎皇在位、郑主当政，自东京发号施令，与南方的阮主长年交战而无果；欧洲使节估计城中人口约有十万。1788年，末代黎帝昭统引来清朝大军，清军进驻东京；西山军首领阮惠于1789年初在城外玉洄、栋多大破清军，是越南战史上最著名的大捷之一。1802年，嘉隆帝阮映攻下升龙，把国都迁往顺化，旧城被改造为阮朝镇守北方的城塞。

en:
Vientiane, the 'walled city of sandalwood', sits on a Mekong bend where the river enters its widest rice plain. Once the Khmer trading town of Chanthaburi, it became the chief southern city when Fa Ngum founded Lan Xang, the 'million elephants', in 1354, rich on floodplain rice and river trade. The royal court still lay far upstream at Muang Sua, the future Luang Prabang, and the preceding forty years were court slaughter: seven kings were killed between 1428 and 1438 at the bidding of Queen Nang Keo Phimpha, 'the Cruel', herself drowned as a naga offering in 1438. Vientiane revolted in 1440 and was subdued from the capital. In 1444 it stands as the granary and southern stronghold of a shaken kingdom.

In 1478 Lê Thánh Tông of Đại Việt, affronted by the white-elephant affair – a request for a hair answered, in legend, with a box of dung – invaded; the Lan Xang army was broken, Luang Prabang taken, and old King Chakkaphat fled down the Mekong to Vientiane, where his son Thaen Kham rallied the provinces and destroyed the Vietnamese column. In 1560 Setthathirath moved the capital from Luang Prabang to Vientiane, raising new walls, a teak palace, the Haw Phra Kaew for the Emerald Buddha, and rebuilding the golden That Luang stupa. Twice he emptied the city and wore out Bayinnaung's Burmese armies with guerrilla war, but after he vanished campaigning against the Khmers in 1571, Vientiane fell in 1574 and its king and heir were carried off to Pegu; war followed until Nokeo Koumane, back from Burma, reunited the kingdom in the 1590s. Under Sourigna Vongsa (1637–94) came a long golden peace: laws were codified, monks and merchants filled the city, and in 1641 the Dutchman van Wuysthoff arrived up the Mekong from Longvek. His death in 1694 opened a succession struggle; in 1707 Vientiane became a separate kingdom, Luang Prabang split away, and Champasak followed in 1713. After a Burmese interlude, Phraya Chakri's Siamese army sacked Vientiane in 1779 and carried the Emerald Buddha to Thonburi; the city then ruled as a Siamese dependency. In 1821 King Anouvong, installed by Siam in 1804, reigns over a loyal-seeming Vientiane.
zh:
万象意为「檀香木城」，坐落在湄公河的一处大湾上：河水由此涌入最宽阔的稻米平原。它本是高棉人的商埠占塔布里；1354年法昂建立澜沧王国——意为「百万大象」——之后，这里成为王国南方的首要城邑，凭平原上的稻米与河上贸易而富庶。那时国王的朝廷还远在湄公河上游的芒斯瓦，即后来的琅勃拉邦；此前四十年间宫廷喋血：1428至1438年有七位国王相继遇害，幕后都是人称「残忍者」的王后南胶披发，她本人也于1438年被沉入湄公河，献祭水神。万象自己曾在1440年起兵反叛，被国都发兵镇压。1444年的万象，是一个惊魂未定的王国的粮仓与南疆首镇。

战火烧到这片平原是在1478年：大越的黎圣宗因白象受辱——传说他求取象毛，却收到一盒象粪——大举来攻，澜沧军溃败，琅勃拉邦失守，老国王乍加帕沿湄公河南逃到万象；其子坦坎在南方诸城纠集兵力，全歼来犯的越军。1560年赛塔提拉把国都从琅勃拉邦迁至万象，筑起新城墙、巨大的柚木王宫和供奉玉佛的玉佛寺，又重修了金色的塔銮。他两次坚壁清野，以游击战争拖垮勃印曩的缅甸大军；但1571年他在征讨高棉途中失踪，万象于1574年陷落，国王与王储被掳往勃固。占领与内战接踵而至，直到从缅甸归来的诺胶古曼在1590年代重新统一王国。苏里亚旺萨（1637—1694年在位）时迎来漫长的黄金太平：律令重修，僧侣与商人充满城中，1641年荷兰人范·维斯霍夫从洛韦溯湄公河到访。1694年他一死，继承之争撕裂澜沧：1707年万象自成一国，琅勃拉邦分立，占巴塞也于1713年独立。经过一段缅甸臣属时期，披耶却克里率暹罗军队于1779年洗劫万象，把玉佛带回吞武里，万象从此作为暹罗属国存续。1821年，1804年由暹罗扶立的阿努王，正统治着这座看似恭顺的都城。

en:
Luang Prabang lies on the Mekong at the mouth of the Nam Khan, on the site of Muang Sua, a river town also called Xieng Dong Xieng Thong. It was a Khmer dependency from 1185 and regained its freedom as Khmer power collapsed. In 1353 Fa Ngum, returning from the Khmer court with an army, made the town the capital of Lan Xang, the 'Land of a Million Elephants', and in 1359 the Khmer king sent him the Phra Bang, a Buddha image that became the kingdom's palladium. In 1444 Xieng Thong was still the royal capital and a trading town on the upper Mekong, but the court had passed through a generation of short-lived kings overshadowed by the queen mother Maha Devi, and the outlying muang were drifting away; Vientiane had risen in revolt in 1440. Theravada Buddhism shared the town with the older spirit cults of the countryside.

In 1478 Emperor Lê Thánh Tông of Đại Việt opened the White Elephant War, and in 1479 his armies sacked and burned Xieng Thong. The city recovered under King Visoun (1500–1520), who built Wat Visoun in 1513 and had the chronicles and Jataka tales set in writing. In 1560 King Setthathirath moved the capital to Vientiane, taking the Phra Bang and the Emerald Buddha with him; Xieng Thong was renamed Luang Prabang, and Wat Xieng Thong was built for the old capital. Burmese armies under Bayinnaung took Vientiane in 1574, and Luang Prabang lived under Burmese overlordship until 1591, when Nokeo Koumane, home after sixteen years at Pegu, reunited the kingdom and cast off Burmese rule. Under Sourigna Vongsa (1637–1694) Lan Xang knew its longest peace and the city grew rich on Mekong trade. After his death his grandson Kingkitsarat seized Luang Prabang, and in 1707 Lan Xang split in two, leaving the city capital of the separate Kingdom of Luang Prabang. A Burmese army conquered it in March 1765 and carried off hostages, and in 1778 King Surinyavong II joined a Siamese campaign against Vientiane and accepted Bangkok's suzerainty. Anurutha, crowned under Siamese eyes in 1792, was restored in 1796 after detention in Bangkok and raised the great Wat Mai monastery; when he died in 1819 his kingdom was a quiet tributary of the Chakri dynasty.
zh:
琅勃拉邦位于湄公河与南康河交汇处，其地古称勐苏瓦，又叫川东川铜。1185年起，这里受吴哥阇耶跋摩七世治下的高棉宗主权管辖，高棉势力衰落之后重获自由。1353年，从高棉宫廷借兵归来的法昂以此地为都建立澜沧王国，意为「百万大象之地」；1359年，高棉国王送来勃拉邦金佛，成为王国的镇国之宝。1444年的川铜仍是澜沧王都和湄公河上游的商埠，但此前数十年王位更迭频繁，王太后玛哈黛维长期干政，外藩离心，万象已于1440年举兵反叛。城里上座部佛教与乡间古老的精灵崇拜并行。

1478年，大越黎圣宗发动「白象之战」，越军于1479年攻陷并焚毁川铜。城市在维苏王（1500—1520年在位）治下恢复，他于1513年修建维苏寺，并将编年史和《本生经》故事形诸文字。1560年，赛塔提拉王迁都万象，带走勃拉邦佛与玉佛；川铜改名琅勃拉邦，并建通寺为旧都增辉。1574年，勃印曩的缅军攻陷万象，琅勃拉邦处在缅甸统治之下，直到1591年，在勃固为质十六年的诺胶·古曼回到此地，重新统一王国、摆脱缅甸。苏里亚旺萨（1637—1694年在位）时期，澜沧享受了最长的和平，琅勃拉邦因湄公河贸易而富庶。他死后，王孙景吉萨占据琅勃拉邦，1707年澜沧一分为二，该城成为独立的琅勃拉邦王国都城。1765年3月缅军征服此城、掳走人质；1778年，国王苏林亚翁二世加入暹罗征讨万象的战事，接受曼谷宗主权，年年进贡金银花。阿努鲁塔1792年在暹罗人注视下即位，一度被掳往曼谷，1796年才获释回国，主持修建了宏伟的迈寺；他1819年去世时，琅勃拉邦仍是却克里王朝治下安静的属邦。

en:
The limestone valleys that later became Cao Bằng were known to the Vietnamese courts as Quảng Nguyên, a border country of Tày and Nùng villages rather than a tightly governed lowland province. In 1039 Emperor Lý Thái Tông drove out Nùng Trí Cao and brought the area into Đại Việt. Under the later Trần and Lê dynasties, local Tày lords kept much of their authority; rebellions in the 1430s showed how fragile the throne's hold remained. In 1444 the newly established Lê dynasty treated Cao Bằng as a strategic gateway towards Guangxi, where mountain valleys and passes controlled frontier defence and exchange.

The highlands became a refuge for a fallen dynasty after Mạc Đăng Dung seized the Lê throne in 1527. When the Lê-Trịnh army recovered the capital in 1592, Mạc claimants withdrew into these mountains and maintained a court for three reigns at Bản Phủ. Between February and August 1677 a Lê-Trịnh campaign fought through Cao Bằng, destroyed the last Mạc forces and ended the long Lê-Mạc war. The highland passes then returned to the Vietnamese realm.
zh:
后来成为高平的石灰岩谷地位于红河三角洲以北，越南朝廷称这一带为广源，是岱依人与侬人村寨组成的边地，而非低地那样严密统辖的省份。1039年，李太宗逐走侬智高，把该地纳入大越。陈朝和后黎时期，当地岱依贵族仍保有很大权势；1430年代的叛乱说明朝廷控制并不稳固。1444年，建立不久的后黎朝把高平视为通往广西的战略门户，山间谷地与隘口关系着边境防务和往来。

1527年莫登庸篡夺黎朝皇位后，这片高地成了亡国政权的退路。1592年黎郑军队收复都城，莫氏余部退入山区，在本府城维持了三代朝廷。1677年2月至8月，黎郑军队在高平连续作战，消灭莫氏最后的武力，结束漫长的黎莫战争，高原各隘口也重归大越。

en:
Kutaraja stands at the north-western tip of Sumatra, where the Aceh River meets the sea. Before it became a royal capital, this coast was Lamuri or Lambri, known to Arab geographers from the ninth century and to Chinese sailors as Nanwuli. By the early fifteenth century its ruler and more than a thousand households were Muslim. Ships waited out the winter monsoon there before sailing to Sri Lanka and India, while the hinterland supplied sappanwood, lakawood, white rattan, ivory and camphor. A tsunami damaged the port in 1394, and Samudera-Pasai overshadowed the older harbours. In 1444 Lamuri's Muslim ruler still held a small Acehnese trading port at the entrance to the Strait of Malacca.

During the 1520s Sultan Ali Mughayat Syah built Aceh Darussalam on the old Lamuri shore and conquered Pasai, making the harbour his capital, Kutaraja, the City of the King. Pepper and firearms drew the court into the rivalry over Malacca; Alauddin al-Kahar, who died in 1571, attacked Johor and Portuguese Malacca with Ottoman gunners and ships. Cornelis de Houtman's Dutch fleet reached the roadstead in 1599, and James Lancaster brought a letter from Elizabeth I in 1602. Under Iskandar Muda, sultan from 1607, Kutaraja presided over Aceh's greatest power and a court of trade and Islamic learning. The 1629 assault on Malacca destroyed much of his fleet, although Aceh took Kedah in the same year. The crown later weakened in favour of territorial chiefs, but about 1819 Sultan Jauhar al-Alam used his Penang contact Koh Lay Huan to help put down a chiefs' revolt.
zh:
哥打拉贾位于苏门答腊西北角、亚齐河入海处。在成为王都以前，这片海岸是南浡里（Lamuri，亦称Lambri），阿拉伯地理学家9世纪已有记载，中国水手则称之为南浡里。15世纪初，当地统治者和一千多户居民都已是穆斯林。商船在此等候冬季季风，再驶往斯里兰卡和印度，腹地输出苏方木、降真香、白藤、象牙和樟脑。1394年的海啸破坏港口，邻近的苏木都剌－巴赛又使这些老港相形失色。1444年，南浡里的穆斯林统治者仍据有马六甲海峡入口处一座不大的亚齐人商港。

1520年代，苏丹阿里·穆加亚特·沙阿在南浡里旧岸建立亚齐达鲁萨兰，征服巴赛，并把港口建为王都哥打拉贾，意为「王城」。胡椒与火器把宫廷卷入马六甲霸权之争；1571年去世的阿拉丁·卡哈尔曾在奥斯曼炮手和战船支援下进攻柔佛与葡属马六甲。1599年，科尔内利斯·德·霍特曼的荷兰船队抵达锚地；1602年，詹姆斯·兰开斯特带来伊丽莎白一世的书信。1607年即位的伊斯坎达尔·穆达在位时，哥打拉贾号令亚齐的鼎盛疆域，宫廷也是贸易与伊斯兰学术中心。1629年进攻马六甲使亚齐舰队大部覆灭，但亚齐同年仍攻取吉打。此后王权渐弱，地方首领坐大；约1819年，苏丹乔哈尔·阿拉姆仍借助槟城的辜礼欢平定首领叛乱。

en:
The lowlands of Riau run from the eastern slopes of the Barisan range to mangrove-lined channels facing the Strait of Malacca. Boats sailing between the strait and the Sumatran interior exchanged forest and sea products at rivers such as the Siak; the Buddhist ruin of Muara Takus recalls older Srivijayan links. By the fifteenth century Islam and Malay court culture had spread from Malacca to Siak, Rokan and neighboring river mouths. In 1444 these were small Muslim Malay port-polities, tied to Malacca's commerce and overlordship rather than governed as a single inland realm.

After Malacca fell to the Portuguese in 1511, a Portuguese expedition traced the Siak River in 1514, while the rulers of Johor claimed the coast as their own. Their authority was contested in 1723, when Raja Kecil founded the Siak Sultanate at Buantan after losing the Johor succession. Siak grew into a strong naval power, controlling Rupat and shipping lanes off eastern Sumatra; in 1759 Sultan Abdul Jalil Muzaffar Shah destroyed a Dutch garrison and attacked the VOC post at the mouth of the Siak, killing 65 of its 72 men. The court moved to Senapelan under Sultan Muhammad Ali in 1780-1782, the settlement that became Pekanbaru. Under Sultan Ali Abdul Jalil Syaifuddin, who died in 1810, Siak was at the height of its power.
zh:
廖内低地从巴里桑山脉东坡延伸到马六甲海峡沿岸的红树林水道。商船往来海峡与苏门答腊内陆，在锡亚河等河口交换林产和海产；穆阿拉塔库斯佛寺遗址仍显示这里曾与三佛齐相连。到15世纪，伊斯兰教和马来宫廷文化已从马六甲传到锡亚、罗干及相邻河口。1444年，这里是若干穆斯林马来港口政权，依附马六甲的贸易与霸权，并非由一个统一的内陆王国统治。

1511年马六甲落入葡萄牙人之手后，一支葡萄牙远征队在1514年沿锡亚河探查，柔佛统治者则宣称这片海岸归其所有。1723年，拉惹·基希尔争夺柔佛王位失败后在布安坦建立锡亚苏丹国，柔佛的权威受到挑战。锡亚随后成为强大的海上政权，控制鲁帕岛和苏门答腊东部航道；1759年，苏丹阿卜杜勒·贾利勒·穆扎法尔·沙消灭一支荷兰驻军，并袭击荷兰东印度公司在锡亚河口的据点，72人中65人被杀。1780年至1782年苏丹穆罕默德·阿里在位时，宫廷迁至森纳佩兰，该地后来发展为北干巴鲁。到1810年去世的苏丹阿里·阿卜杜勒·贾利勒·赛义夫丁时期，锡亚正处在权势顶峰。

en:
The Batak lands rise from Sumatra's western coastal strip into volcanic highlands and the basin of Lake Toba. Their inhabitants were not a single state but related Toba, Karo, Pakpak-Dairi, Simalungun, Angkola and Mandailing communities, organized under rajas and exogamous marga clans. They farmed wet and dry rice, followed a Hindu-tinged ancestor cult, and carried camphor, benzoin, resin and hardwoods down to trading ports. Barus, also called Fansur, was the richest outlet; Tamil merchants left an inscription there in 1088, and Tomé Pires's early sixteenth-century Suma Oriental called it a very rich kingdom. In 1444 the highlands were still ruled by Batak chiefs while Barus controlled the coast and the incense trade.

From the sixteenth century Aceh expanded pepper production across northern Sumatra and imported Batak rice in exchange, drawing the highlands more tightly into the coastal economy. Aceh absorbed Barus around the middle of the century and stationed a panglima there; the Malay poet Hamzah Fansuri may have been born or raised in the port in this period. In 1668 the Dutch East India Company drove out the Acehnese governor, but coastal overlordship did not immediately reach the mountain villages. The Batak kept their clans, script and priestly rituals, and in 1821 most of the interior still lay under its own rajas.
zh:
巴塔克之地从苏门答腊西部沿海低地抬升，延伸入火山高地和多巴湖盆地。这里的居民并非统一国家，而是彼此关联的托巴、卡罗、帕克帕克-代里、西马隆贡、昂科拉和曼代林社群，由拉阇和外婚的马尔嘎氏族组织。他们种植水稻与旱稻，奉行带有印度教色彩的祖先崇拜，并把樟脑、安息香、树脂和硬木背到贸易港口。又称凡苏尔的巴鲁斯是最富庶的出海口，泰米尔商人1088年在那里留下碑文；托梅·皮莱资在16世纪初的《东方诸国记》中也称其为非常富庶的王国。1444年，高地仍由巴塔克首领统治，巴鲁斯则控制海岸和熏香贸易。

16世纪起，亚齐在苏门答腊北部扩大胡椒生产，并用沿海产品换取巴塔克稻米，使高地更深地卷入海岸经济。约在16世纪中叶，亚齐吞并巴鲁斯并派驻庞利马；马来诗人哈姆扎·凡苏里可能就在这一时期出生或成长于该港。1668年，荷兰东印度公司赶走亚齐任命的长官，但沿海的宗主权并未立刻深入山地村落。巴塔克人保留了氏族、文字和祭司仪式，到1821年，大部分内陆仍处在本地拉阇治下。

en:
The Siak River winds through the mangrove coast of eastern Sumatra to the Strait of Malacca, and its villages grew rich floating the interior's gold, pepper, rattan and forest produce downriver, where island merchants bartered Chinese porcelain and Indian cloth. Malays settling the lower reaches mingled with Minangkabau drifting down from the highlands, and Islam came with the trade. In 1444 Siak was a small Malay river-port, its harbour busy but its court overshadowed by the far greater marts across the strait; within a generation it would be drawn into Malacca's empire.

Sultan Mansur Shah of Malacca vassalised Siak during his reign of 1459–1477, and after Malacca fell to the Portuguese in 1511 the river passed with its other Sumatran dependencies into Johor's orbit. In 1718 Raja Kecil, a chief raised among the Minangkabau who claimed the murdered Sultan of Johor as his father, captured Johor itself; driven out by the Bugis, he withdrew up the Siak River and in 1723 founded his capital at Buantan, the Sultanate of Siak Sri Indrapura. From there he and his heirs commanded the carrying trade between the strait and Sumatra's interior and made Siak a sea power feared along the whole east coast. The second sultan, once installed with Dutch help, had the VOC garrison in Siak annihilated in 1759 and stormed the company's guardpost at Pulau Contong, killing sixty-five of its seventy-two men. In 1780 the court moved upstream to Senapelan, the 'new market' later called Pekanbaru. Under the seventh sultan, the Arab-born Sharif Ali, who died in 1810, Siak reached its peak, its sway reaching the island of Rupat, until Deli on the northern coast broke away in 1814.
zh:
锡亚河穿过苏门答腊岛东岸的红树林注入马六甲海峡，河畔村落把内地的黄金、胡椒、藤条和林产顺流运下，与岛上来船交换中国瓷器和印度布匹，由此致富。定居下游的马来人与从高地顺流而来的米南佳保人杂处，伊斯兰教也随商路传到这里。1444年的锡亚还是一个小小的马来河港，码头虽忙，宫廷却笼罩在海峡对岸那些大商埠的阴影之下；不出一代人，它便被纳入马六甲的帝国。

1459至1477年在位的马六甲苏丹满速沙将锡亚收为藩属；1511年马六甲落入葡萄牙人之手后，这条河又随其他苏门答腊属地转入柔佛的势力范围。1718年，在米南佳保人中间长大、自称遇害柔佛苏丹遗腹子的拉惹·克齐尔（意为「小王」）一度攻陷柔佛本土，被布吉斯人逐出后退回锡亚河上游，于1723年在布安坦建都，是为锡亚斯里因陀罗补罗苏丹国。他和后继者据此扼守海峡与苏门答腊内地之间的转运贸易，把锡亚建成整个东岸都畏惧的海上强权。第二位苏丹曾借荷兰东印度公司之力登位，却在1759年下令全歼驻锡亚的荷兰守军，并攻破公司在孔通岛的哨所，七十二名守兵被杀六十五人。1780年，宫廷迁往河上游的森纳佩兰，即后来得名「新集市」的北干巴鲁。第七位苏丹、阿拉伯裔的谢里夫·阿里于1810年去世，在他治下锡亚臻于鼎盛，势力远及鲁帕岛；1814年，北岸的日里脱离独立。

en:
Bengkulu is the surf-beaten coast of southwestern Sumatra, where small rivermouth chiefdoms such as Sungai Serut, Selebar and Sungai Lemau met the villages of the Barisan foothills. Srivijaya had once drawn these landing places into its maritime trade, but no later empire ruled them directly, and in 1444 authority rested with local chiefs and highland Rejang communities. Pepper, gold, rattan and beeswax moved down to the shore, where Malay, Javanese and Chinese traders exchanged cloth, metalware and ceramics. The coast was therefore wealthy enough to attract outside courts, but too divided to form a single Bengkulu kingdom.

Portuguese visitors reached the coast before Dutch ships appeared in 1596. As pepper exports grew, Selebar came within Banten's commercial orbit, while the Minangkabau rulers of Inderapura extended their influence southward along the shore. After the Dutch East India Company shut the English out of Banten, the English East India Company founded a pepper station and garrison at Bencoolen in 1685. Fort Marlborough was raised between 1713 and 1719 under Governor Joseph Collett, but the unhealthy coast and uncertain pepper supplies made the settlement a financial disappointment. It remained a small British foothold on an otherwise Dutch-dominated Sumatra, and when Stamford Raffles became its lieutenant-governor in 1818 he began reforms, including measures against slavery, that were still underway in 1821.
zh:
明古鲁位于苏门答腊西南岸，常年受印度洋拍岸浪冲击。双溪塞鲁特、斯莱巴尔、双溪莱马等河口小酋邦，与巴里桑山麓的村社在此相接。室利佛逝曾把这些停泊点纳入海上贸易网络，但后来的帝国并未直接统治此地；1444年时，权力仍掌握在本地首领和拉让山地社群手中。胡椒、黄金、藤条和蜂蜡从内陆运到海边，马来、爪哇和中国商人用布匹、金属器和陶瓷交换。这片海岸因此富庶到足以吸引外来王权，却又处于分裂之中，没有形成统一的明古鲁王国。

葡萄牙人先到访此地，荷兰船只随后在1596年出现。随着胡椒出口扩大，斯莱巴尔进入万丹的商业势力范围，因德拉普拉的米南佳保统治者也把影响力沿海南伸。荷兰东印度公司把英国人排挤出万丹后，英国东印度公司于1685年在本库伦设立胡椒商站和驻军。1713年至1719年间，总督约瑟夫·科利特主持修建马尔伯勒堡，但沿海气候恶劣、胡椒供应不稳，使这个据点始终难以盈利。在荷兰势力控制苏门答腊大部分地区的格局下，它只是英国占据的一小块立足地；1818年斯坦福德·莱佛士出任副总督后推行改革，包括限制奴隶制，这些措施到1821年仍在展开。

en:
Palembang straddles the Musi River in southern Sumatra, the old heart of Srivijaya. From the seventh century its river anchorage drew Chinese and Indian merchants waiting for the monsoon to turn, and Yijing found more than a thousand Buddhist monks and scholars maintained in the kingdom. Javanese pressure later broke Srivijayan power: Parameswara fled Palembang, the port came under Majapahit influence, and Chen Zuyi's pirates made the Strait of Malacca unsafe. In 1407 Zheng He's fleet destroyed Chen's fleet at Palembang, killed 5,000 of his men and installed the Muslim chieftain Shi Jinqing. By 1444 Shi's descendants held a small Old Port polity under loose Ming recognition and Majapahit overlordship, far removed from the old Srivijayan capital.

Around 1513 Portuguese accounts described Palembang as tied to Java's Demak and involved in campaigns against Portuguese Malacca. A Demak noble later founded the Kuto Gawang court on the Musi, and Islam became dominant as the river port grew into a pepper emporium. The Dutch East India Company set up a trading post in 1619 and secured the pepper monopoly in 1642. In 1659 its forces burned Kuto Gawang, while Susuhunan Abdurrahman proclaimed the Palembang Sultanate and moved his court. Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin I built the Great Mosque between 1738 and 1748, and Sultan Muhammad Bahauddin raised the fortified Kuto Besak, completed in 1797. The British deposed Mahmud Badaruddin II in 1812 and placed Najamuddin on the throne, but a Dutch expedition seized Najamuddin in 1818. In 1821 Dutch troops returned, established a garrison and brought the river court under direct military control.
zh:
巴邻旁（中国史籍称旧港）横跨苏门答腊南部的穆西河，曾是三佛齐的核心。7世纪起，河港吸引中国和印度商人等候季风转向；义净到此求法时，王廷供养的佛僧与学者超过千人。爪哇势力后来击碎三佛齐政权，拜里米苏拉逃离巴邻旁，港口转入满者伯夷影响之下，陈祖义等海盗又使马六甲海峡商旅不安。1407年，郑和舰队在巴邻旁击破陈祖义船队，杀五千人，并立穆斯林首领施进卿。到1444年，施进卿的子孙统辖旧港小政权，既得到明朝松散承认，又服属满者伯夷，与当年的三佛齐帝都已不可同日而语。

约1513年的葡萄牙记载称，巴邻旁已依附爪哇的淡目，并参与对葡属马六甲的军事行动。此后一名淡目贵族在穆西河畔建立库托加旺宫廷，伊斯兰教逐渐占据主导，河港也发展为胡椒商埠。荷兰东印度公司1619年设立商馆，1642年取得胡椒贸易垄断权。1659年，公司军队焚毁库托加旺，苏苏胡南·阿卜杜勒拉赫曼同年宣布建立巴邻旁苏丹国并迁移王庭。马哈茂德·巴达鲁丁一世在1738—1748年修建大清真寺；穆罕默德·巴哈乌丁修建设防的库托贝萨克王宫，工程于1797年完工。1812年，英国人废黜马哈茂德·巴达鲁丁二世，改立纳扎穆丁；荷兰远征军1818年俘获纳扎穆丁。1821年，荷军重返巴邻旁、设立驻军，以武力直接控制这座河畔王庭。

en:
Tulangbewang takes its name from the Tulang Bawang, the broad river that carries the produce of north-eastern Lampung to the sea through mangrove swamps. A polity here is probably named in Chinese records as early as the fifth century, when Pohuang sent missions to the Song court, and the Buddhist pilgrim Yijing heard of the country during his stay at Palembang in the 680s; its river chiefs later came under Srivijaya's sway. The Lampung people lived in small settlements strung along the navigable rivers, growing pepper in forest clearings, and Tome Pires, writing at Malacca soon after 1511, listed Tulang Bawang among the Sekampung lands that traded with Sunda. In 1444 its pepper moves downriver under loose Hindu chiefs who look to Palembang as overlord, an ill-defined frontier rather than a kingdom.

Islam and Banten's overlordship came in the later sixteenth century: by local account Banten's rule began in 1568, spread less by conquest than by its grip on the pepper market, as the sultan's agents channelled all Tulang Bawang pepper through Banten. From 1619 foreigners might buy it only at the sultan's court, and Sultan Ageng Tirtayasa made the monopoly absolute during his reign of 1651 to 1683. When he was deposed in April 1682 his son Sultan Haji, with Dutch help, granted the VOC the monopoly of Lampung's spice trade; a Company fleet reached Tanjung Tiram that August but found the local chiefs less obedient than the treaty assumed, and Tulang Bawang pepper long continued to leave by older routes. Banten's loose dominion lasted until 1808, when Governor Daendels brought Lampung under direct rule from Batavia, though Menggala, the pepper port up the Tulang Bawang River, remained the district's busiest market. In 1821 the pepper boats still tie up there, their cargoes now traded on Dutch terms.
zh:
图朗巴旺得名于图朗巴旺河，这条大河穿过红树林沼泽，把楠榜东北部的物产送往大海。早在5世纪，中国史籍中的「婆皇」遣使南朝，可能就是这里的政权；7世纪80年代，佛教僧人义净在巴邻旁停留时也曾听说该国，河畔的首领们后来臣服于室利佛逝。楠榜人散居在可通航的河流两岸，于林间空地种植胡椒；1511年后不久，托梅·皮莱士在马六甲写成的《东方诸国记》把图朗巴旺列入与巽他通商的塞坎蓬诸地。1444年的图朗巴旺由松散的印度教首领治理，名义上尊巴邻旁为宗主，胡椒顺河而下——这里与其说是王国，不如说是一片疆界模糊的边地。

16世纪后期，伊斯兰教与万丹的宗主权一同到来：按当地记载，万丹的统治始于1568年，主要靠掌控胡椒市场而非武力征服，苏丹的代理人把图朗巴旺的胡椒尽数引向万丹。1619年起，外商只能在苏丹王廷购买胡椒；苏丹阿庚·蒂尔塔雅沙（1651—1683年在位）更把垄断推向极致。1682年4月阿庚被废，其子苏丹哈只借荷兰人之力登位，于同年8月27日立约，把楠榜香料贸易的垄断权让予东印度公司；公司舰队当月驶抵丹戎提朗，却发现当地首领远不似条约设想的那样恭顺，图朗巴旺的胡椒很长时间里仍循旧路出海。万丹松散的统治维持到1808年，丹德尔斯总督才把楠榜置于巴达维亚直接治下，而图朗巴旺河畔的胡椒港孟加拉，依旧是全区最繁忙的市集。1821年，运椒的船只仍在那里停靠，只是货易要按荷兰人的规矩来做。

en:
Banten occupied a sheltered harbour at the mouth of the Banten River, where shipping from the Sunda Strait could move into western Java. In the fifteenth century it was a pepper port of the Hindu Sundanese kingdom of Sunda; its older political settlement lay upstream at Banten Girang. Chinese records already praised Sunda pepper, and early sixteenth-century Portuguese accounts numbered Banten among the realm's chief harbours. In 1444 the port was thus a Sundanese, Hindu and mercantile edge of the kingdom, open to traffic between Java and Sumatra, but not yet the seat of an Islamic court.

Around 1526, as Demak and Cirebon expanded along Java's northwest coast, Maulana Hasanuddin secured Banten Bay and transformed the river mouth into a Muslim royal stronghold; his fortified palace at Surasowan is dated to 1552, the year his rule as first sultan is conventionally reckoned to begin. Pepper from Lampung and the Sundanese highlands made the new capital wealthy, and on 27 June 1596 Cornelis de Houtman brought the first Dutch fleet there. James Lancaster opened a permanent English factory in 1602, the Dutch followed in 1603, and Banten became one of the cosmopolitan pepper marts of the Indies. Rivalry with Batavia, founded after Jan Pieterszoon Coen took Jayakarta in 1619, brought blockades and war. Sultan Ageng Tirtayasa maintained open trade with many nations, but Dutch intervention in his 1682 quarrel with Sultan Haji gave the Company a pepper monopoly, Fort Speelwijk and dominance over the court. Herman Willem Daendels destroyed the palace and declared Banten absorbed in 1808; in 1813 Stamford Raffles ended the sultanate.
zh:
万丹位于万丹河口的避风港，船只可经巽他海峡驶入爪哇西部。15世纪时，这里是印度教巽他人的巽他王国胡椒港；较早的统治中心在上游的万丹吉朗。中国记载已称赞巽他胡椒，16世纪初的葡萄牙记载也把万丹列为该国主要港口之一。因此1444年时，万丹仍是巽他王国信奉印度教的巽他商人海滨前哨，通行爪哇与苏门答腊之间的航路，却还不是后来的伊斯兰宫廷所在地。

1526年前后，淡目与井里汶的势力沿爪哇西北海岸扩张，莫拉纳·哈桑丁控制万丹湾，把河口改造成伊斯兰王城；1552年，他在苏拉索旺修建设防王宫，这一年也通常被视为他以初代万丹苏丹身份统治的开端。楠榜和巽他高地的胡椒使新都富足。1596年6月27日，科尔内利斯·德·霍特曼率领第一支荷兰船队抵达。1602年，詹姆斯·兰开斯特开设英国常设商馆，荷兰商馆也于次年设立，万丹由此成为东印度最国际化的胡椒市场之一。荷兰总督库恩1619年夺取雅加达并建立巴达维亚后，两港对抗带来封锁与战争。苏丹阿庚·蒂尔塔雅萨允许各国自由贸易，但1682年他与苏丹哈吉父子争位，荷兰出兵支持哈吉，由此取得胡椒垄断权、斯皮尔韦克要塞和对宫廷的支配地位。1808年，赫尔曼·威廉·达恩德尔斯摧毁王宫并宣布吞并万丹；1813年，斯坦福·莱佛士废除苏丹，万丹苏丹国告终。

en:
Kawali, near modern Ciamis, was the eastern capital of the Hindu Sundanese kingdom during its Galuh period. An older Galuh center had stood farther southeast at Karang Kamulyan on the Citanduy, and Kawali inscriptions show a settled royal town before the long reign of Niskala Wastu Kancana; the Carita Parahyangan calls its walled and moated palace Surawisesa. Indonesian sources date the Kawali era from 1333 to 1482. In 1444 Niskala Wastu Kancana, ruler from 1371 to 1475, still reigned over the forested Sundanese hinterland between Galunggung, Kuningan and old Galuh, far from the Muslim ports beginning to form on Java's northern coast.

In 1482 Sri Baduga Maharaja reunited Sunda and Galuh and moved the center of government to Pakuan Pajajaran. After the late-sixteenth-century collapse before Banten, a Galuh polity centered on Panaekan reemerged, only to be conquered by Panembahan Senopati of Mataram in 1595. The Galuh lord Adipati Panaekan became a Mataram wedana and was killed in 1625 during a dispute over an attack on Batavia. By the agreements of October 1677 and 5 October 1705, Galuh passed under the Dutch East India Company, which ruled through a regent under the Priangan system. Coffee cultivation began around Kawali in 1720. The regent Wiradikusuma moved Galuh's seat to Ciamis in 1815, and in 1819 Raden Adipati Adikusuma became the last regent installed before the close of this period.
zh:
卡瓦利在今尖米士附近，是印度教巽他王国加卢时期的东部都城。更早的加卢中心位于东南方芝塔杜伊河畔的卡朗卡穆利扬，卡瓦利铭文显示，在尼斯卡拉·瓦士徒·坎卡纳漫长统治之前，这里已是人口聚居的王城；《帕拉扬扬书》称其带城墙与壕沟的王宫为苏拉维西沙。印尼文资料把卡瓦利时代系于1333年至1482年。1444年，1371年至1475年在位的尼斯卡拉·瓦士徒·坎卡纳仍统治着加隆贡、库宁岸和旧加卢之间林木茂密的巽他内陆，爪哇北岸此时才刚开始形成穆斯林港口。

1482年，史力·巴度贾·马哈拉扎重新统一巽他与加卢，并把统治中心迁往帕匡·帕查查兰。16世纪末巽他—加卢在万丹压力下崩溃后，以帕奈坎为中心的加卢政权复兴，却在1595年被马打兰的帕能巴罕·森纳帕提征服。加卢领主阿迪帕蒂·帕奈坎成为马打兰的维达纳，1625年在是否进攻巴达维亚的争执中被杀。根据1677年10月和1705年10月5日的协议，加卢转入荷兰东印度公司治下，公司通过帕拉阳安制度和一名摄政实行间接统治。1720年前后，卡瓦利一带开始种植咖啡。摄政维拉迪库苏马1815年把加卢治所迁至尖米士，1819年拉登·阿迪帕蒂·阿迪库苏马成为这一时期结束前就任的最后一位摄政。

en:
The southern plains of Central Java — Banyumas, Bagelen and the rice lands of Kedu — stretch from Mount Slamet to the Indian Ocean, drenched by the monsoon and long one of Java's granaries. This was the heartland of the old Hindu kingdom of Mataram, whose ninth-century rulers raised Borobudur on the Kedu Plain, and its villages still acknowledged Majapahit as their overlord. In 1444, however, Majapahit's writ ran little beyond eastern Java: Muslim merchant cities were growing up beyond the northern hills, while the rice-growing interior kept its Hindu-Javanese customs under local lords who paid little more than tribute.

When a new Mataram arose at nearby Kotagede late in the sixteenth century, the fighting men of Bagelen became the picked troops of its founder, Sutawijaya. Soon after his accession in 1613 Sultan Agung built a timber palace at Karta, five kilometres south of Kotagede, and ruled there at Mataram's zenith: Surabaya fell to him in 1625, and the great armies of the 1628 and 1629 expeditions against Dutch Batavia marched out across this plain. Fire gutted the wooden court in 1634, and after Agung's death in 1645 his son Amangkurat I moved in 1647 to a grander brick palace at nearby Plered. There, in 1677, Trunajaya's Madurese and north-coast rebels sacked the court and carried off at least 300,000 Spanish reals; Amangkurat died in flight near Tegal, and the court moved to Kartasura in 1680. The old Karta was briefly rebuilt as Kartasekar in 1719, only to collapse the following year. After the Chinese war of 1741–1743 Mataram's domains were reduced to Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen, and the treaty of Giyanti in 1755 assigned the ruined old heartland, Karta and Plered among them, to the new Sultanate of Yogyakarta.
zh:
中爪哇南部的平原——万由马士、巴格伦和葛都的稻作地带——从斯莱梅特山绵延到印度洋，季风雨丰沛，自古是爪哇的粮仓之一。这里曾是印度教马打兰古国的腹地，9世纪的君主在葛都平原建起婆罗浮屠，而此时各村落仍尊满者伯夷为宗主。但1444年时，满者伯夷的号令已几乎不出东爪哇：北山之外，穆斯林商人城邦正在兴起；种稻的内陆仍守着印度教—爪哇旧俗，由地方领主统治，对中央不过进献贡物而已。

16世纪末，新的马打兰在邻近的哥打格德兴起，巴格伦的武士成了开国君主苏托维佐约的精锐。1613年苏丹阿贡即位后不久，在哥打格德以南五公里的卡尔塔营建木构王宫，并在那里统治马打兰的鼎盛时代：1625年泗水陷落，1628、1629年两度远征荷属巴达维亚的大军都从这片平原出发。1634年木宫毁于大火；阿贡1645年去世后，其子阿莽古拉特一世于1647年迁入附近普莱雷德更宏大的砖砌王宫。1677年，杜鲁诺佐约率领的马都拉与北海岸叛军攻陷并洗劫普莱雷德，掠走至少三十万西班牙里亚尔银币，阿莽古拉特一世逃亡途中死于直葛附近，宫廷随后于1680年迁往卡尔塔苏拉。旧卡尔塔宫1719年被改建为卡尔塔塞卡尔宫，次年便告坍塌。1741至1743年的华人战争后，马打兰疆土只剩梭罗、日惹、葛都和巴格伦；1755年《吉安蒂条约》把卡尔塔、普莱雷德等废墟王都所在的旧畿辅划给新立的日惹苏丹国。

en:
Blambangan fills the easternmost spur of Java, the forested Oosthoek whose coast points across a narrow strait to Bali. The eastern salient was granted to the Madurese prince Arya Wiraraja in 1295 and grew into a rival court to Majapahit; after the Regreg war of 1404–1406 its princes went their own way. In 1444 the land was, in all but name, a separate Hindu Javanese kingdom, drawing its wealth from the north-coast port of Panarukan and from cotton and rice, with Bali lying close across the water.

Tomé Pires heard in the 1510s that the 'heathen' Blambangan was the strongest Javanese realm east of Surabaya, its ships using the ports of Panarukan, Muncar and Puger. Demak's eastward drive cost it Pasuruan in 1545, and in 1598 Pasuruan's armies stormed in and wiped out the royal house, after which the Balinese stepped in as overlords until Sultan Agung of Mataram took Panarukan in 1639. The kingdom revived under Tawang Alun II, who cleared the forest of Sudiamara in 1665 to found his new capital of Macan Putih; when he died in 1691 the VOC recorded that 271 of his 400 wives burned themselves on his pyre. A Buleleng expedition in 1697 drew Bali deeper into its affairs. The end came under the Company's own flag: Blambangan rose in the puputan at Kabakaba in 1767 and the Wilis war of 1768, and after Prince Jagapati's last stand at Bayu failed in 1772 the VOC annexed the realm to Besuki, seating its regent at Banyuwangi beside Fort Utrecht. So perished the last Hindu kingdom of Java.
zh:
布兰邦岸地处爪哇最东端的海岬，林木茂密的「东角」隔着一道狭窄海峡与巴厘相望。1295年，这片东境被封给马都拉亲王阿里亚·维拉罗阇，日后发展成与满者伯夷分庭抗礼的王廷；1404—1406年的雷格雷克战争之后，东境王公便自行其是。1444年时，这里实际上已是一个独立的爪哇印度教王国，财富得自北岸港口帕纳鲁坎以及棉花与稻米，巴厘岛就在海峡对岸不远处。

1510年代，托梅·皮莱资听说「异教的」布兰邦岸是泗水以东最强盛的爪哇国家，海船出入帕纳鲁坎、蒙扎尔和普格尔诸港。淡目东扩使它在1545年失去帕苏鲁安；1598年帕苏鲁安军队攻入，屠灭王室，巴厘人随即成为宗主，直到1639年马打蓝苏丹阿贡攻占帕纳鲁坎。王国在塔旺·阿仑二世治下复兴，他于1665年开辟苏迪亚马拉丛林，营建新都马坎普蒂；1691年他去世时，荷兰东印度公司的档案记载，他的四百名妻妾中有271人登上火葬堆自焚殉葬。1697年布勒冷出兵，使巴厘更深地介入布兰邦岸事务。终局在公司自己的旗帜下到来：1767年卡巴卡巴的普普坦起事、1768年维利斯战争相继爆发，查加帕蒂亲王在巴尤的最后抵抗于1772年失败后，荷兰东印度公司将该国并入贝苏基管区，任命的甫伯驻在外南梦的乌得勒支堡旁。爪哇最后的印度教王国就此灭亡。

en:
Surabaya commands the northeastern corner of Java, where the Brantas delta opens onto the Madura Strait and the Java Sea. It began as the estuary port linked to Janggala, one of the Javanese realms formed after Airlangga divided his kingdom in 1045, and by the fourteenth century it served Majapahit alongside Tuban and Gresik. The Chinese observer Ma Huan, visiting with Zheng He's fleet in 1413, called the port Sulumayi and noted fresh water flowing out at its river mouth. In 1444 Surabaya was still a Majapahit port on the route between Malacca and the Spice Islands, but the Hindu-Buddhist empire's power was contracting while Java's northern coastal towns grew wealthy from trade.

In the late fifteenth century Sunan Ampel established the Muslim settlement of Ampel in what is now northern Surabaya, and Tomé Pires found a Muslim lord ruling there in 1513, probably still as a Majapahit vassal. The duchy resisted Demak before submitting in 1530, then became independent after Sultan Trenggana died in 1546. War with Mataram began in 1614; Surabaya's allies were defeated near Pajang in 1616, the city came under siege in 1620 and it surrendered in 1625 after Sultan Agung's forces cut the Brantas. Mataram handed Surabaya to the Dutch East India Company in 1743. The Dutch made the natural harbor their main eastern Javanese naval base and a center of the sugar, tobacco and coffee trades; by the early nineteenth century it was the seat of the Surabaya Residency.
zh:
苏腊巴亚（泗水）扼守爪哇岛东北角，位于布兰塔斯河三角洲注入马都拉海峡和爪哇海的位置。它早期是与重迦卢相连的河口港，重迦卢是1045年爱尔朗卡分割王国后形成的爪哇政权之一；到14世纪，苏腊巴亚与图班、锦石同为满者伯夷效力。1413年随郑和船队到访的马欢称此港为苏鲁马益，并注意到河口有淡水流出。1444年的苏腊巴亚仍是满者伯夷的港口，地当马六甲通往香料群岛的航路，但这个印度教—佛教帝国的势力正在收缩，爪哇北岸城镇则靠贸易日益富庶。

15世纪末，苏南·安佩尔在今苏腊巴亚北部建立穆斯林聚居地安佩尔；1513年托梅·皮莱士已见到一位穆斯林统治者主政，当时他可能仍是满者伯夷附庸。苏腊巴亚公国抵抗淡目，1530年臣服，1546年苏丹特伦加纳死后重获独立。它与马打兰的战争始于1614年，1616年盟军在帕章附近战败，城市1620年遭到围攻，1625年阿贡苏丹的军队切断布兰塔斯河后迫降苏腊巴亚。1743年，马打兰将苏腊巴亚移交荷兰东印度公司。荷兰人把这个天然港湾建设成他们在东爪哇的主要海军基地，以及蔗糖、烟草和咖啡贸易中心；到19世纪初，这里已成为苏腊巴亚管区的治所。

en:
Demak began as Glagah Wangi, a marshy north-coast fief on the channel between Java and Muria Island. Muslim Chinese, Arab, Malay and Javanese trading communities had taken root in northern ports after the early Ming voyages, but in 1444 Demak still belonged to the Hindu-Buddhist Majapahit court at Trowulan. Rice, spices and shipping toward Malacca and the Maluku Islands gave the small harbour importance beyond its size. It was thus a Javanese, formally Hindu port on an increasingly Islamic coast, poised between a fading inland empire and the coming north-coast sultanates.

Later Javanese tradition credits Raden Patah with founding Demak, building its Grand Mosque and gathering teachers later remembered among the Wali Songo. As Majapahit collapsed in the late fifteenth century, Demak became Java's first Muslim state and brought Semarang, Jepara, Tuban and Gresik under its leadership. Pati Unus led fleets of about a hundred ships against Portuguese Malacca in 1513 and 375 ships in 1521, falling in the second expedition. In 1527 Fatahillah's Demak and Cirebon forces took Sunda Kelapa and renamed it Jayakarta. Trenggana was killed campaigning against Panarukan in 1546, and Sunan Prawoto was murdered the next year by supporters of Arya Penangsang. The succession struggle ended when Joko Tingkir defeated Penangsang and, in 1554, moved the court and royal regalia to Pajang, founding the Pajang Sultanate and reducing Demak to a vassal. Around the end of the century it passed into Mataram's orbit, while the old channel to Muria slowly silted and the former rice port lost its maritime primacy.
zh:
淡目原称格拉旺伊，是爪哇北岸、爪哇与穆里亚岛之间水道旁的一片沼泽封邑。15世纪初郑和下西洋后，穆斯林华商、阿拉伯人、马来人和爪哇人贸易社群已在北方港口扎根，但1444年的淡目仍臣属特洛武兰的印度教—佛教满者伯夷宫廷。稻米、香料以及通往马六甲和马鲁古的航运，使这座小港拥有超出其规模的重要性。它因此是一座爪哇人居住、名义上仍奉印度教的港口，却坐落在日益伊斯兰化的海岸上，处在内陆帝国衰亡与北岸苏丹国兴起之间。

晚期爪哇传统把淡目的建国归于拉登·帕塔：他修建淡目大清真寺，聚集后来被称为「九圣」的伊斯兰教师。15世纪末满者伯夷瓦解之际，淡目成为爪哇第一个伊斯兰政权，并领导三宝垄、哲帕拉、图班和锦石等北岸港口。帕提·乌努斯1513年率约100艘船、1521年又率375艘船两度攻打葡萄牙占据的马六甲，并在第二次远征中身亡。1527年，法塔希拉率领淡目与井里汶军队夺取巽他格拉巴，将其改名为雅加达。特伦加纳1546年征讨帕纳鲁坎时被杀，普拉沃托次年又被阿利亚·帕南桑的支持者刺杀。继承之争最后由佐科·廷基尔胜出，他于1554年把宫廷和王室圣器迁往巴让，建立巴让苏丹国，淡目降为属邦。约16世纪末，淡目又落入马打兰势力范围；通往穆里亚的旧水道逐渐淤塞，这座旧日米港也失去海上优势。

en:
Kalapa, better remembered as Sunda Kelapa, stood on the Ciliwung estuary on Java's northwest coast. From the thirteenth to the sixteenth century it was the chief seaport of the Hindu Sundanese kingdom of Sunda, linked by river and road to Pakuan Pajajaran, the capital about sixty kilometres inland. Pepper drew ships from Sumatra, Malacca and the Javanese north coast, and Tomé Pires's Suma Oriental of 1512–1515 called Kalapa the realm's most important trading harbour. In 1444 it was therefore a wealthy Hindu Sundanese gateway to the Java Sea, controlled from Pakuan and exposed to the expansion of Muslim ports to the east.

On 21 August 1522 the Sundanese court agreed to let Portugal build a fortress at Kalapa in return for support against Demak and Cirebon. The fortress never rose: on 22 June 1527 Demak forces overran and burned the port, renamed it Jayakarta, and it subsequently passed under Banten. Early in the following century English and Dutch traders competed for the harbour, and in May 1619 Jan Pieterszoon Coen's Dutch East India Company force stormed Jayakarta and built Batavia on its ruins. Canals, wharves, warehouses and a castle made the walled town the Company's Asian headquarters, but sediment and disease-ridden waterways also gave old Batavia a deadly reputation. Anti-Chinese violence in 1740 killed large numbers of Chinese residents, and a Chinese quarter was designated in 1741. By the early nineteenth century much of the elite had moved to healthier southern quarters, while the old harbour remained the crowded mouth through which Java's products were shipped out.
zh:
噶喇吧（即巽他格拉巴）位于爪哇西北海岸的芝利翁河口。13至16世纪，这里是印度教巽他王国的主要海港，通过河运和道路连接约60公里内陆的都城帕库安帕查查兰。胡椒吸引苏门答腊、马六甲和爪哇北岸的船只，托梅·皮莱资在1512至1515年写成的《东方诸国记》中，称它为巽他最重要的贸易港。1444年时，噶喇吧已是富庶的印度教巽他海港，是巽他王国通向爪哇海的门户，也直接面对东方伊斯兰港口的扩张。

1522年8月21日，巽他宫廷同意葡萄牙在噶喇吧修筑要塞，以换取对抗淡目和井里汶的援助。要塞尚未建成，淡目军队便在1527年6月22日攻陷并焚毁港口，将其改名为雅加达，后来这里归属万丹。17世纪初，英国与荷兰商人争夺该港；1619年5月，扬·彼得松·库恩率领荷兰东印度公司军队攻占雅加达，在废墟上建立巴达维亚。城墙、运河、码头、仓库和城堡使这里成为荷兰东印度公司在亚洲的总部，但泥沙淤积和疫病流行也让旧巴达维亚声名不佳。1740年的排华暴力使大量华人罹难，1741年当局划定华人街区。到19世纪初，许多上层居民已迁往南部更有益健康的街区，旧港则仍是爪哇物产外运的拥挤河口。

en:
Bali lies in the narrow sea lane between Java and Lombok, its rice plains watered by the old subak irrigation system and governed from Hindu courts. Majapahit troops sent by Gajah Mada campaigned on the island in 1342 and defeated the Balinese ruler at Bedulu in 1343, after which Sri Aji Kresna Kepakisan was installed at Samprangan, in the country later centred on Gianyar. His brother Dalem Ketut founded the nearby court of Gelgel. In 1444 that Hindu dynasty still linked Bali to the fading Majapahit world, while wet-rice villages, temples and local weaving supported the island's commerce.

A Portuguese fleet sailing to the Moluccas sighted northern Bali in 1512, and a 1585 expedition sent from Malacca to found a post was wrecked on the Bukit reefs. During the 16th century Gelgel reached its height under Dalem Baturenggong, who welcomed the Javanese sage Nirartha and made his influence felt over Lombok, western Sumbawa and Blambangan. Cornelis de Houtman reached Bali in 1597, and a VOC trading post attempted in 1620 failed because the island offered rice rather than the spices sought in Batavia. In 1639 Gelgel backed Blambangan against Mataram. Internal conflicts after 1651 weakened Gelgel, and a new paramount seat was set up at Klungkung in 1686 as the island split into competing kingdoms. Gianyar itself became a royal seat on 19 April 1771, under Ida Dewa Manggis Sakti.
zh:
巴厘位于爪哇与龙目岛之间的狭窄海路上，稻田由古老的苏巴克灌溉系统滋养，岛上政权以印度教宫廷为中心。加查·马达派出的满者伯夷军队1342年征伐巴厘，1343年在贝杜卢击败巴厘统治者，随后把室利·阿吉·克雷斯纳·克帕基西安置在后来以吉安雅为中心的桑普兰甘；其弟达伦·克图特又在附近建立格尔格尔宫廷。1444年，这个印度教王朝仍把巴厘与日渐衰微的满者伯夷世界联系在一起，水稻村落、神庙和本地织物支撑着岛上贸易。

1512年，一支前往摩鹿加的葡萄牙舰队望见巴厘北岸；1585年，马六甲派人前来建立商馆，船队却在布吉礁盘失事。16世纪，格尔格尔在达伦·巴图伦贡治下达到鼎盛，他接待来自爪哇的贤者尼拉尔塔，势力遍及龙目、松巴哇西部和布兰班甘。科内利斯·德·霍特曼1597年抵达巴厘，荷兰东印度公司1620年尝试开设商馆却告失败，因为这里输出稻米而非巴达维亚渴求的香料。1639年，格尔格尔支持布兰班甘对抗马打兰。1651年后的内乱削弱格尔格尔，新的共主王庭1686年设在克隆孔，巴厘随之分裂为彼此争战的诸王国。1771年4月19日，伊达·德瓦·芒吉斯·萨克蒂在吉安雅建立王庭。

en:
The west of Sumbawa, called Samawa by its own people, is a land of grassy plains and horses, ringed by the harbours of the Java and Flores Seas. In the fourteenth century its small river kingdoms, Sumbawa itself and the vassal lands of Taliwang, Seran and Jereweh, were counted among the dependencies of Majapahit in Java, and Javanese and Makassar shipping already carried away the island's honey, sandalwood and sappanwood, the tree that yields red dye. In 1444 the rajas of Samawa still kept their old cults, touched only lightly by Hinduism, while Majapahit's power ebbed across the water.

Between 1450 and 1540 Muslim merchants from Java and Palembang, and preachers such as Sunan Prapen, brought Islam to the coast, and the Balinese kingdom of Gelgel held part of western Sumbawa for a time. In the seventeenth century the kingdom accepted the protection of Gowa in Makassar, whose agents deposed its last Hindu-leaning ruler, Mas Goa, in 1673. The Dutch East India Company arrived that same year, and on 12 June 1674 Sumbawa emerged as an independent sultanate under Harunnurrasyid I, called Mas Bantan in the local chronicle and a son of a Banjarmasin prince, surrendering its claims to Selaparang in Lombok in exchange for Dutch protection. His son Jalaluddin I made war on Selaparang in 1723; after Kaharuddin I (1732-1758) his queen I Sugiratu ruled as sultana until she was deposed in 1761, while the Dutch hold tightened year by year. In 1815 ash from Tambora, erupting in the east of the island, blotted out the sun over Sumbawa and brought famine and sickness.
zh:
松巴哇岛西部，本地人称作萨马瓦，是一片草原起伏、出产马匹的土地，港口环抱着爪哇海与弗洛勒斯海。14世纪时，这里的河畔小邦——松巴哇本邦及附庸之地塔利旺、瑟兰和哲雷韦——被算作爪哇满者伯夷的藩属，爪哇和望加锡的商船早在此收购蜂蜜、檀香，以及可制取红色染料的苏木。1444年，萨马瓦的拉惹们仍守着旧有信仰，印度教只留下很浅的痕迹，而满者伯夷的威势正在海对岸消退。

1450至1540年间，来自爪哇和巨港的穆斯林商人以及苏南·普拉彭等传教士把伊斯兰教带到海岸，巴厘的格尔格尔王国也曾一度占据松巴哇西部的一部分。17世纪，王国接受望加锡戈阿的保护，1673年戈阿人废黜了仍倾向印度教的君主马斯·果阿。同年荷兰东印度公司到来；1674年6月12日，松巴哇成为独立苏丹国，初代苏丹哈伦拉希德一世在本地编年史中称马斯·班坦，是马辰王子之子，他以放弃对龙目塞拉帕朗的权利换取荷兰保护。其子贾拉鲁丁一世1723年出兵攻打塞拉帕朗；卡哈鲁丁一世（1732—1758年在位）之后，王后伊·苏吉拉图以苏丹娜称制，1761年被废，荷兰人的控制逐年收紧。1815年，岛东侧坦博拉火山喷发，火山灰遮蔽了松巴哇的天空，饥荒与疫病随之而来。

en:
Flores is a long volcanic island in the Lesser Sunda chain between Sumbawa and Timor. Its own peoples knew it as Nusa Nipa, 'snake island'; the name Flores, from the Portuguese cabo de flores or 'cape of flowers', arrived only with European sailors. Manggarai, Ngada, Ende, Sikka and Lamaholot communities, each speaking its own Austronesian language, lived in small hill chiefdoms bound by ancestor cults and megalithic rites, and sailed to the markets that linked Timor, Sulawesi and Java. In 1444 the island had no foreign ruler and no foreign faith, though the sandalwood shipping between Timor and Malacca already used its anchorages.

In 1520 the Portuguese opened a transit post at Lamakera on nearby Solor, on the route between Malacca and the Moluccas, and Dominican friars built a palm-timber fortress there in 1562; Javanese Muslims burned it the following year and it was rebuilt in stronger materials. Quarrels between traders and friars drove the traders to Larantuka on Flores' eastern tip before 1600, and when the Dutch seized Solor in 1613 the Dominicans followed. Larantuka became the centre of the Timor sandalwood trade, and refugees from the fall of Malacca in 1641 and the Dutch attack on Makassar in 1660 swelled its mixed settlement into the Larantuqueiros, or Topasses, the 'black Portuguese', whose da Costa and de Hornay families made and unmade the local rajas. When royal officials sent from Lisbon tried to assert control in 1769, the Larantuqueiros drove them off, and as the sandalwood trade faded they turned to their own estates; in 1821 the rajas of Flores still answered to the families of Larantuka, and no foreign flag flew over the island's interior.
zh:
弗洛勒斯是小巽他群岛中的一座狭长火山岛，位于松巴哇与帝汶之间。岛民本称此岛为努萨尼帕（Nusa Nipa），意为「蛇岛」；「弗洛勒斯」得自葡萄牙语cabo de flores，即「花之角」，是欧洲水手到来后才有的名字。芒加莱、恩加达、恩德、锡卡、拉马霍洛特等族群各说自己的南岛语，生活在以祖先崇拜和巨石仪式维系的山间小邦中，并乘船往来于连接帝汶、苏拉威西与爪哇的商路。1444年时，岛上既无外来统治者，也无外来宗教，只是帝汶通往马六甲的檀香木商船已会在岛上的锚地停靠。

1520年，葡萄牙人在邻近的索洛岛东岸拉马凯拉设立中转据点，扼守马六甲与摩鹿加之间的航道；1562年多明我会修士在当地筑起一座棕榈木要塞，次年被爪哇穆斯林烧毁，后又以更坚固的材料重建。商人与修士相争，商人在1600年前迁居弗洛勒斯东端的拉兰图卡；1613年荷兰人攻占索洛，修士们也随之而来。拉兰图卡成为帝汶檀香木贸易的中心，1641年马六甲陷落、1660年荷兰人进攻望加锡后，两批葡萄牙难民涌入，与当地人融合成拉兰图卡人，即托帕塞人，又称「黑葡萄牙人」；达科斯塔与德奥奈两大家族凭此废立各地拉惹。1769年，里斯本派来宣示主权的王室官员被他们赶走；檀香木贸易衰落后，拉兰图卡人转而经营自己的庄园，到1821年，弗洛勒斯的拉惹们仍听命于拉兰图卡的两大家族，岛上内陆没有任何一面外邦旗帜。

en:
Sumba lies south of Flores across the Sumba Strait, a dry, grassy island whose people kept the Marapu ancestor cult and buried their dead beneath great megalithic tombs. Javanese chronicles numbered it among the lands claimed by Majapahit, but no outside power actually ruled the island: in 1444 its villages were governed by their own clan lords among the sandalwood forests of the interior.

European ships first came in 1522, when the Portuguese reached Sumba in search of its sandalwood, and from the 1600s skippers of the Dutch East India Company followed; European geographers took to calling it the Sandalwood Island. Neither company nor sultanate conquered the island, however, and through 1821 its lords remained independent, bargaining with every fleet that anchored off the northern beaches while the megalithic tombs and Marapu rites continued as before.
zh:
松巴与弗洛勒斯岛隔着松巴海峡相望，岛上气候干燥、草原广布；岛民信奉马拉普祖先崇拜，把死者葬在巨石墓下。爪哇史书把它算进满者伯夷声言的属岛，但从无外来政权真正统治此岛：1444年，各村落由自己的氏族长老治理，内陆遍布檀香林。

1522年，为檀香而来的葡萄牙人成为最早到来的欧洲人；1600年代起，荷兰东印度公司的船只继至，欧洲制图者干脆把这里称作「檀香岛」。但无论公司还是苏丹国都没有征服松巴，直到1821年，岛上的长老们依旧自立，同每一支停泊在北部海滩的船队讨价还价，巨石营造与马拉普祭仪也照旧延续。

en:
West Timor is the drier western half of the sandalwood island, and its Kupang Bay was the finest natural anchorage in the whole Lesser Sunda chain. The Atoin Meto and their neighbours — Helong, Tetum, Kemak and Bunak — lived in scores of small kingdoms; their ritual centre was Wehale, whose lord at Laran spoke for the whole island, and Sonba'i rose in the west after his model. For centuries Malay, Javanese and Chinese junks came to load white sandalwood from the inland hills, with beeswax beside it. In 1444 the rajas still answered to no foreign power, and the first Portuguese ships were two generations away.

António de Abreu sighted Timor around 1512 while searching for the Spice Islands. Dominican friars began work on the north coast in 1556, and in 1641 they baptised the royal family of Ambeno at Lifau, which became the first Portuguese settlement on the island; the Larantuqueiros, the mestiço Topasses of Flores and Solor, had established themselves there the year before. When Francisco Fernandes overran Sonba'i and Wehale in 1642, the Topass Hornay and Costa clans became the real power behind the sandalwood trade. The Dutch raised their first fort near Kupang in 1640, destroyed the Portuguese post there in 1653, stormed its fortress in 1656 and only secured the bay in 1688, binding five small 'loyal ally' rajas to the VOC while malaria emptied their own garrison. At Penfui in 1749 the Topass host was routed and Capitão-Mor Gaspar da Costa killed; in 1756 Paravicini accepted the submission of forty-eight local rulers, and in 1769 the Topasses drove the Portuguese governor himself from Lifau to Dili, fixing European power at opposite ends of the island. British troops held Kupang from 1811 to 1816, and when Dutch rule returned, the inland kingdom of Amanuban was still fighting column after column to a standstill.
zh:
西帝汶是檀香木之岛较干燥的西半，古邦湾是整条小巽他群岛最好的天然锚地。阿托尼梅托人及邻族赫龙、德顿、克马克、布纳克人生活在数十个小王国中；全岛的礼仪中心是韦哈莱，其君主在拉兰号令全岛，西部的松巴伊王国便是仿效它而兴。数百年来，马来、爪哇和中国的商船前来装运内陆丘陵出产的白檀与蜂蜡。1444年时，各位拉惹仍不臣服于任何外来强权，葡萄牙人的船还要两代人之后才会出现。

约1512年，安东尼奥·德·阿布雷乌在寻找香料群岛时望见帝汶。1556年多明我会修士开始在北岸传教，1641年在利福为安贝诺王室施洗，利福由此成为岛上第一个葡萄牙人定居点；而来自弗洛勒斯和索洛的混血族群——托帕塞人（即拉兰图卡人）——此前一年已在那里落脚。1642年弗朗西斯科·费尔南德斯连克松巴伊和韦哈莱后，托帕塞人的奥尔奈与科斯塔两大家族成了檀香木贸易背后真正的主人。荷兰人1640年在古邦附近建起第一座要塞，1653年摧毁葡萄牙人的商站，1656年强攻其堡垒，最终于1688年控制古邦湾，以条约绑定五个「忠盟」小邦，而疟疾不断清空他们自己的驻军。1749年彭富伊一役，托帕塞大军溃败，首领加斯帕尔·达科斯塔战死；1756年，帕拉维奇尼接受四十八位地方君主归附；1769年，托帕塞人又把葡属总督本人从利福逐往帝力，欧洲人的势力就此固定在岛的两端。1811至1816年古邦为英军占据，荷兰人重新接管时，内陆的阿马努班王国仍让一支支远征军无功而返。

en:
The heart of this province was the sheltered Brunei River estuary on Borneo's northwest coast, where South China Sea shipping met riverine routes into the island. Chinese and Arab records knew the trading polity there as Po-ni. In 1365 the Javanese Nagarakretagama counted Brunei among Majapahit's tributaries, bound to send camphor, and a Sulu attack in 1369 looted the capital and left it weaker. During the fifteenth century Brunei broke from Majapahit and became a Sunni Muslim sultanate. In 1444, therefore, its river capital was an independent Bornean Muslim port, sustained by camphor, spices and commerce between Borneo, the Philippines and China.

Brunei's maritime power reached its height under Sultan Bolkiah, who ruled from 1485 to 1528 and claimed suzerainty over much of coastal Borneo and the Sulu Islands. Survivors of the Magellan expedition visited the wealthy port in 1521. In March 1578 a Spanish expedition sailed from Manila, and on 16 April its troops, helped by dissident Bruneian nobles, captured the capital; cholera or dysentery forced them to withdraw on 26 June after seventy-two days. The court survived, but succession rivalries did not. Malay sources date the Bruneian Civil War to 1665–1673, when Abdul Hakkul Mubin killed Sultan Muhammad Ali and proclaimed himself ruler, only to be opposed by Muhyiddin and finally killed on Cermin Island. The long war weakened the outer empire, while the old capital on the Brunei River remained an independent sultan's seat as the eighteenth century closed.
zh:
这一省的核心是婆罗洲西北岸隐蔽的文莱河口，南海航运与深入岛内的河路在此交会。中国和阿拉伯记载称当地贸易政权为渤泥。1365年，爪哇的《爪哇史颂》把文莱前身列为满者伯夷属国，须纳樟脑；1369年苏禄人攻陷劫掠都城，使其实力受损。15世纪，文莱摆脱满者伯夷，成为逊尼派苏丹国。因此1444年时，文莱河口都城已是独立的婆罗洲穆斯林港口，依靠樟脑、香料以及婆罗洲、菲律宾与中国之间的贸易维持繁荣。

苏丹博尔基亚1485—1528年在位时，文莱的海上势力达到顶峰，据称统辖婆罗洲大部分沿海地区和苏禄群岛。1521年，麦哲伦船队的幸存者到访这座富庶港口。1578年3月，西班牙远征军从马尼拉出发，在异议贵族协助下于4月16日攻占都城；但霍乱或痢疾流行，军队72天后便于6月26日撤回马尼拉。文莱宫廷幸存下来，继承之争却未平息。马来文资料将文莱内战系于1665—1673年：阿卜杜勒·哈库勒·穆宾杀死苏丹穆罕默德·阿里并自立，穆希丁起而对抗，最终在镜岛将其击杀。长期战争削弱了外围帝国，而直到18世纪末，文莱河畔的旧都仍是独立苏丹的宫廷所在地。

en:
Api-Api faces Gaya Bay on the northwest coast of Borneo, beneath Mount Kinabalu and sheltered by Gaya Island. Kadazan-Dusun, Bajau and other coastal peoples fished the bay and traded forest and sea produce through Bruneian ports; the country around present Kota Kinabalu was under Bruneian influence from the 15th century. In 1444 the anchorage thus belonged to the Sultanate of Brunei, a Muslim maritime power whose merchants handled spices, camphor, wax, rattan and pearls gathered along the Bornean shore.

Brunei's power reached its height under Sultan Bolkiah, who reigned from 1485 to 1524 and made his court known across Borneo and the southern Philippines; Antonio Pigafetta visited it during the 1521 Magellan expedition. A Dutch map of Borneo labelled the Gaya Bay settlement Api Api in 1657. During the Bruneian civil war of 1665 to 1673, Sultan Abdul Hakkul Mubin made a strong base at Kinarut, south of the bay, with Bajau and Dusun support, while his rival Muhyiddin sought Sulu help and promised Kimanis as a reward. Farther north, Alexander Dalrymple obtained Sulu permission for an East India Company station on Balambangan in 1761. The factory opened in December 1773, was sacked in February 1775, was briefly restored in 1803 and was abandoned in 1805, leaving Api-Api itself to its Bruneian coastal trade.
zh:
亚庇位于婆罗洲西北岸的加雅湾，前有加雅岛遮蔽，后倚京那峇鲁山。卡达山-杜顺人、巴瑶人和其他沿海族群在湾中捕鱼，并通过文莱港口交易山林与海产；今哥打京那峇鲁一带自15世纪起受文莱影响。1444年，这个锚地属于文莱苏丹国；这个穆斯林海上强权的商人经营婆罗洲沿岸汇集的香料、樟脑、蜂蜡、藤条和珍珠。

文莱在苏丹博尔基亚1485年至1524年统治期间达到鼎盛，权势遍及婆罗洲与菲律宾南部；1521年麦哲伦船队航行时，安东尼奥·皮加费塔曾到访其宫廷。1657年的一幅婆罗洲荷兰地图已把加雅湾聚落标为Api Api。1665年至1673年的文莱内战中，苏丹阿都·哈库·穆宾在海湾以南的京那律建立据点，得到巴瑶人和杜顺人支持；其竞争者穆希丁则向苏禄求援，并许诺以金马尼士为酬。更北的巴兰邦安岛方面，亚历山大·达尔林普尔1761年取得苏禄许可，为东印度公司设立据点。商站1773年12月开张，1775年2月遭洗劫，1803年短暂恢复，1805年废弃，亚庇本地仍维持着文莱体系下的沿海贸易。

en:
The Mahakam delta and riverine lands below its forested interior were the old territory called Kutai, home to river-dwelling Kutai communities related to the Dayak peoples of the basin. Around the 4th century, a Hindu court upstream at Muara Kaman left seven stone yupa pillars bearing brahmanic rites and Indianized political ideas. A newer coastal power, Kutai Kartanegara, arose at Kutai Lama near the river mouth in 1300 under Aji Batara Agung Dewa Sakti and adopted Hindu-Javanese titles. In 1444 its court commanded the estuarine fisheries and traffic between the Mahakam interior and the sea, while the older Martapura realm still centred on Muara Kaman.

Muslim traders and teachers gained influence along the coast during the 16th century, and in 1575 Aji Raja Mahkota Mulia Alam made Islam the religion of the court. In 1635 Kutai Kartanegara defeated Martapura, annexed the old Hindu kingdom and joined its name to Martapura. The royal centre then shifted down the lower Mahakam for defence and trade: Jaitan Layar and Tepian Batu gave way to Jembayan in 1732, and Tenggarong became the capital in 1782. From these river landings, Kutai's rulers exchanged fish, forest produce and sea goods while drawing upstream communities into the sultanate.
zh:
马哈坎河三角洲及其密林下游的河畔土地，古称古泰，居住着与流域达雅克各族有亲缘关系的古泰人。约4世纪时，上游穆阿拉卡曼一带出现印度教王权，留下七根记载婆罗门仪礼的Yupa石柱，显示印度化的政治观念已传入此地。较晚的滨海政权古泰卡塔内加拉于1300年在河口附近的古泰拉马兴起，开国者为阿吉·巴塔拉·阿贡·德瓦·萨克蒂，宫廷采用印度教—爪哇式尊号。1444年，这个政权控制着河口渔业以及马哈坎内陆与海洋之间的往来，而更古老的马尔塔普拉王权仍以穆阿拉卡曼为中心。

16世纪，穆斯林商人和传道者在沿海逐渐扩大影响；1575年，阿吉·拉贾·马科塔·穆利亚·阿拉姆定伊斯兰教为宫廷宗教。1635年，古泰卡塔内加拉击败马尔塔普拉，吞并这个古老印度教王国，并将国名与马尔塔普拉相连。为兼顾防御与贸易，王都随后在马哈坎下游迁移：贾伊坦拉亚尔和特皮安巴图之后，1732年迁至占巴延，1782年又定都登加龙。统治者以这些河畔泊地交换鱼类、林产和海货，也把上游社群逐渐纳入苏丹国势力范围。

en:
Banjar lies at the wet southern edge of Borneo, where the Barito and Martapura rivers meet the Java Sea through a maze of tidal channels. Its river port, Banjarmasin, was known to foreign sailors long before any sultan: around 1325 the Italian friar Odoric of Pordenone called there and left a description of sago eaters and blowpipe hunters under the name 'Thalamasin', and the Chinese traveller Wang Dayuan listed the place as 'Pa-nan-pa-hsi' in 1349. Real power sat upriver at Negara, seat of the Hindu kings of Negara Daha, heirs of the old Negara Dipa kingdom founded under Majapahit influence, while the port itself was held by a local chief, Patih Masih. In 1444 the Banjar lowlands were Hindu, and their praus carried rice and forest produce to Java and the Malay ports.

Civil war among the Daha royals drove Raden Samudra down to the Barito mouth, where he built a new town; on 24 September 1526 he took the title Sultan Surianshah and made Banjar an Islamic sultanate, at first tributary to Demak and independent from the 1540s. Pepper made its fortune: under Sultan Mustain Billah (1595-1642) Banjarmasin traded from Malacca and Brunei to Gowa and the Moluccas, a Dutch assault on the port failed in 1633, and the VOC was driven out altogether in 1638. The Dutch returned as kingmakers in the civil war of 1663-1679, when their candidate Tahlilullah took Banjarmasin in 1679. A Bugis invasion led by the pretender Prince Amir was beaten back with VOC help in 1757; Amir was exiled to Ceylon in 1787 and Banjar became a Dutch protectorate. During the British occupation of Java the East India Company made its own treaty with the sultan in 1812, but an agreement of January 1817 confirmed the port's return to the Netherlands.
zh:
班贾尔位于婆罗洲湿润的南缘，巴里托河与马塔普拉河在潮水纵横的河网中汇入爪哇海。这里的河港马辰（Banjarmasin）早在苏丹国建立之前就为外国水手所知：1325年前后，意大利修士鄂多立克曾在此停靠，把一个以西米粉和吹箭猎人闻名的地方记作「Thalamasin」；1349年，中国旅行家汪大渊在《岛夷志略》中把此地记作「巴南巴西」。真正的权柄在上游的尼加拉（Negara），那是印度教王国尼加拉·达哈的都城，其前身是受满者伯夷影响建立的尼加拉·迪帕，港口本身则由地方首领帕提赫·马西（Patih Masih）执掌。1444年的班贾尔低地信奉印度教，当地船队把稻米和林产品运往爪哇和马来港口。

达哈王室的内战把拉登·沙穆德拉（Raden Samudra）赶到巴里托河口，他在那里建起新城；1526年9月24日，他称苏丹·苏利安沙（Surianshah），把班贾尔变为伊斯兰苏丹国，起初向淡目称臣，1540年代起独立。胡椒造就了它的富庶：在苏丹慕斯泰因·比拉（Mustain Billah，1595—1642年在位）治下，马辰的商路西起满剌加和文莱，东抵戈瓦和马鲁古；1633年荷兰人攻打马辰失利，1638年荷兰东印度公司更被尽数逐出。1663至1679年的内战中，荷兰人以拥立新君的姿态卷土重来，他们支持的塔赫利卢拉（Tahlilullah）于1679年攻占马辰。1757年，觊觎王位的阿米尔王子（Pangeran Amir）率布吉人来攻，被荷兰东印度公司出兵击退；阿米尔于1787年被流放锡兰，班贾尔沦为荷兰的保护国。英国占领爪哇期间，东印度公司于1812年与苏丹另订条约，但1817年1月的协议最终确认马辰交还荷兰。

en:
Sambas occupies the north-western coast of Borneo around the lower Sambas River, where coastal Malays had long mingled with Dayak farming and seafaring peoples. A kingdom called Sambas was already named in the fourteenth-century Javanese poem Negarakertagama, but its fifteenth-century king Tan Unggal was overthrown by his own people for his cruelty, and for decades the river districts lived under no raja at all. In 1444 the coast subsisted on fishing and the exchange of forest produce, its villages welcoming traders who sailed the South China Sea route between Java, Melaka and China.

In 1530 more than five hundred Hindu nobles of fallen Majapahit, descendants of King Wikramawardhana, settled upriver at Kota Lama and founded the Hindu Panembahan Sambas. In 1609 its ruler Ratu Sapudak made the land's first trade agreement with the Dutch, and in 1631 his son-in-law Raden Sulaiman, son of Sultan Tengah of Sarawak, took the throne as Sultan Muhammad Shafiuddin I, the first Muslim ruler of Sambas. His sultanate prospered on the upriver goldfields and the traffic of the Borneo straits. By the early nineteenth century Sambas was also a lair of sea-raiders led by the sultan's son Pangeran Anom; British expeditions out of Java were repulsed in 1812 but took the town in 1813. The Dutch replaced them in 1819 and thereafter intervened in every succession.
zh:
三发位于婆罗洲西北海岸的三发河下游，沿海马来人与务农、航海的达雅克人早在此杂居。以「三发」为名的王国在14世纪爪哇史诗《爪哇史颂》中已有记载，但15世纪的国王丹·翁加尔因残暴被民众推翻，此后数十年河口各地再无君主。1444年的三发以捕鱼和林产物交易为生，各村迎送着往来于爪哇、满剌加与中国之间南海航道上的商人。

1530年，五百余名仍信印度教的满者伯夷遗民——国王威克拉玛瓦尔达纳的后裔——在三发河上游的哥打拉马定居，建立印度教的三发潘嫩巴汉王国。1609年，统治者拉杜·萨普达克与荷兰人达成当地首次通商协议；1631年，他的女婿、砂拉越苏丹登加之子拉登·苏莱曼即位，称苏丹穆罕默德·沙菲乌丁一世，成为三发第一位穆斯林统治者。苏丹国靠上游金矿和婆罗洲海峡的航运致富。到19世纪初，三发又成为海寇巢穴，首领是苏丹之子邦格兰·阿诺姆；英国从爪哇派出的远征军1812年被击退，1813年攻占三发城。荷兰人于1819年接防，此后频频干预三发的王位继承。

en:
Makassar commands the south-western tip of Sulawesi, the last landfall before the Spice Islands for ships out of Java and the Malay world. The Majapahit eulogy Nagarakretagama already counted it a tributary in 1365. Its Makassarese inhabitants were rice-growers and sailors ruled by chiefs whose line became the kings of Gowa, until a succession quarrel split the land between Gowa and the river kingdom of Tallo, and the two spent generations at war. In 1444 the people still kept their old animist rites, Malukan cloves and nutmeg mostly travelled in Malay and Javanese bottoms, the great free port of later fame did not yet exist, and Gowa was only the strongest of several bickering little states at the peninsula's end.

Reunification came under King Tunipalangga (r. 1512–1546), who built the twin realm of Gowa-Tallo and its harbour at Sombaopu; Malay merchants fleeing Portuguese Malacca arrived after 1511, and the Portuguese themselves came by the 1540s, using the port as their base for the Maluku trade. On 22 September 1605 the ruler accepted Islam at the hands of three ulama from Minangkabau and took the name Sultan Alauddin, the first official Friday prayer following on 9 November 1607; the Islamic wars launched in 1608 had brought the Bugis lands, Bone included, to submission by 1611. Makassar kept its port open to all—English factors in 1613, Danes in 1618, and after Malacca fell in 1641 the Portuguese made it their greatest base east of India. The chancellor Karaeng Pattingalloang, who read Portuguese, Spanish and Latin and plied the Jesuit Alexandre de Rhodes with questions of astronomy, embodied that open age. Sultan Hasanuddin's defiance ended when Cornelis Speelman's VOC fleet, seconded by the Bugis prince Arung Palakka, extorted the Bungaya treaty of 18 November 1667 and stormed Sombaopu on 12 June 1669; the Dutch rebuilt the northern fort as Fort Rotterdam, around which the modern city grew, and in the eighteenth century Makassarese proas sailed as far as the Australian coast gathering trepang, while sandalwood, pearls and rattan changed hands at the quays.
zh:
望加锡地处苏拉威西岛西南端，是船只从爪哇和马来世界驶往香料群岛前的最后一个停泊之地。满者伯夷的颂诗《爪哇史颂》在1365年已把望加锡列为藩属。望加锡人世代种稻航海，首领的后裔成为戈瓦诸王；后来一场继位纷争把土地分成戈瓦与河口王国塔洛克，两国世代攻战。1444年时，这里的人们仍守着古老的泛灵仪式，摩鹿加的丁香和豆蔻大多还由马来人和爪哇人的商船转运，日后闻名的自由港尚未出现，戈瓦不过是半岛南端几个相争小国中最强的一个。

统一在国王图尼帕朗加（1512—1546年在位）手中完成，他建立戈瓦—塔洛克二元王国，并在松巴乌普营建港口；1511年后逃离葡属马六甲的马来商人到此落脚，葡萄牙人也不晚于1540年代以此为经营摩鹿加贸易的基地。1605年9月22日，国王在三位米南佳保乌理玛的劝导下皈依伊斯兰教，改称苏丹阿劳丁，第一次官方聚礼于1607年11月9日举行；1608年发动的「伊斯兰战争」，到1611年已使包括波尼在内的布吉人诸邦臣服。望加锡向所有来客开放港口：英国人1613年、丹麦人1618年先后开设商馆，1641年马六甲陷落后这里更成为葡萄牙人在印度以东最大的据点。宰相卡朗·帕廷加洛昂能读葡萄牙文、西班牙文和拉丁文书籍，还曾向耶稣会士罗历山反复请教天文历算，正是那个开放时代的写照。苏丹哈桑丁的抵抗，最终被科内利斯·斯皮尔曼统率的荷兰东印度公司舰队粉碎——布吉王子阿隆·帕拉卡从旁相助，1667年11月18日《邦加亚条约》签订，1669年6月12日松巴乌普陷落；荷兰人把北岸要塞扩建为鹿特丹堡，今日城市即在其周围成长。进入18世纪，望加锡人的帆船远航至澳大利亚海岸采集海参，檀香、珍珠和藤条也在码头集散。

en:
Kolaka faces the Gulf of Bone beneath the forested Mekongga highlands. Its inhabitants were Tolaki speakers of the Mekongga branch; their rulers held the title bokeo, with their early center at Bende and later at Wundulako. Bugis settlers had begun occupying Luwu's coastal margins around 1300, trading iron tools and weapons for hill and sea produce, and the fourteenth-century Nagarakretagama already named Luwu among Sulawesi's powers. In 1444 the Kolaka shore therefore lay under Luwu's loose overlordship, where Mekongga chiefs governed the interior and the datu at Malangke upheld exchange across the gulf.

The earliest named Luwu ruler, Bataraguru, appears in a mid-fifteenth-century peace treaty with Bone; Dewaraja later attacked Wajo and Sidenreng in campaigns around 1495-1520 without restoring Luwu's old primacy. On 4 or 5 February 1605 La Patiwareq became the first major South Sulawesi ruler to accept Islam, ruling as Sultan Muhammad Wali Mu'z'hir al-din. Around 1620 the court abandoned Malangke for Palopo on the shore facing Kolaka, drawing the Mekongga coast into Muslim shipping networks while leaving the highland valleys largely under their own chiefs.
zh:
科拉卡位于波尼湾东岸，后方是森林覆盖的梅孔加山地。居民属托拉基人的梅孔加支系，首领称博凯奥，早期中心在本德，后来迁至温杜拉科。约1300年起，布吉斯定居者开始进入鲁乌沿海边缘，以铁制工具和武器交换山林与海产；14世纪的《爪哇史颂》也已把鲁乌列为苏拉威西的强权之一。1444年，科拉卡沿岸处在鲁乌松散的宗主权下：梅孔加首领治理内陆，马朗凯的达图则维持波尼湾两岸的贸易。

可考的最早鲁乌君主巴塔拉古鲁，出现在15世纪中叶与波尼的和约中；德瓦拉查约在1495年至1520年间进攻瓦乔和西登伦，却未能恢复鲁乌旧日的优势。1605年2月4日或5日，拉·帕蒂瓦雷克成为南苏拉威西第一位接受伊斯兰教的主要统治者，称苏丹穆罕默德·瓦利·穆扎希尔·丁。约1620年，宫廷放弃马朗凯，迁至与科拉卡隔海相望的帕洛波，把梅孔加海岸带入穆斯林航运网络，而高地河谷仍大体由本地首领掌握。

en:
At the narrow waist of Sulawesi, the Poso River carries the water of the long mountain lake of Poso into the Gulf of Tomini. Its banks and the surrounding hills are the country of the Pamona, Bare'e-speaking Toraja villagers who farmed the highland valleys and fished lake and shore while honouring the ancestral spirits of Lamoa. They lived under a scattering of small domains—Poso, Napu, Mori, Tojo—ruled by local chiefs and councils of elders, and their coast was pulled into the trade of greater neighbours: the Bugis kingdom of Luwu to the south, which smelted the interior's iron ore at Malangke, Sigi beyond the western mountains, and Ternate, whose sway reached across the gulf to the eastern islands. In 1444 no town yet stood at the river mouth, and the traders who beached their craft there were Bugis and Ternatans, not Europeans.

Later the Islamic kingdom of Parigi, founded about 1515 on the gulf's northern shore, brought much of the Tomini coast under its hand. On 4 February 1605 the Datu of Luwu became the first ruler in South Sulawesi to accept Islam, and after his court moved from Malangke to Palopo around 1620, Muslim merchants and teachers followed the trade route into the southern Poso lands, where the kingdom of the Pamona had taken shape in the course of the seventeenth century. The inland Toraja kept to Lamoa, however, and through 1821 the country remained a remote fringe of small chiefdoms, with no European fort or factory on its shores.
zh:
在苏拉威西岛的蜂腰地带，波索河把狭长的波索湖之水送入托米尼湾。河两岸与周围山地是帕莫纳人的家园——这支操巴雷埃语的托拉查人在高地山谷务农，在湖中与近海捕鱼，信奉名为拉莫阿的祖灵信仰。他们分处波索、纳普、莫里、托约等众多小邦，由酋长和长老议事会统领，沿海则被强邻的贸易牵动：南方的布吉斯王国卢雾在马来诺冶炼产自内陆的铁矿，西山之外有锡吉，特尔纳特的势力则越过海湾波及东侧群岛。1444年的河口还没有城镇，在此泊岸的是布吉斯和特尔纳特商人，而不是欧洲人。

此后，约1515年在托米尼湾北岸建立的伊斯兰王国帕里吉逐渐把海湾大半海岸收入掌中。1605年2月4日，卢雾的达图成为南苏拉威西第一位皈依伊斯兰教的统治者；约1620年王都从马来诺迁往帕洛波后，穆斯林商人和教师沿商路进入波索地方南部，而帕莫纳人的王国也已于17世纪在这一带形成。但内陆的托拉查人仍信奉拉莫阿；直到1821年，这片地方仍是一众小酋长国的偏远边陲，海岸上没有一座欧洲人的要塞或商馆。

en:
At the far tip of the Minahasa peninsula, Manado looks out over a bay ringed by volcanic peaks and set with islands, among them Bunaken and old Manado Tua. Behind the shore lived the Minahasa, a congeries of independent hill districts (walak)—Tombulu, Tonsea, Tontemboan, Tondano and others—warrior villagers who spoke nine related languages and kept the rites of their ancestors; the coastal hamlet of Wenang was their oldest settlement on the bay. The Sultans of Ternate across the sea exacted tribute and carried the faith of Islam along the sea road, and Bugis, Malay and Chinese skippers called at the bay on their voyages to and from the clove islands, yet the hill peoples held to their old gods. In 1444 Manado was still only such a roadstead, known to Ternatan and Bugis seamen and unknown in Europe.

A Portuguese ship first coasted the peninsula in 1523, when Simão d'Abreu sighted Manado Tua, and by mid-century the Portuguese kept a factory at Wenang. Spaniards sailing from Manila seized the fort at Amurang in the 1550s and raised one of their own at Manado; a mestizo community grew there, and in 1630 Muntu Untu, the son of a Spanish mestizo, was acknowledged as the first king of Manado. Spain later yielded its claims to Portugal, whereupon the Minahasan chiefs Supit, Pa'at and Lontoh turned to the VOC: the Company's Fort Amsterdam was built in 1658 and the last Portuguese were expelled a few years later. On 10 January 1679 Robertus Padtbrugge, the Dutch governor of Maluku, signed an alliance with twenty-three walak chiefs against Bolaang Mongondow, binding Minahasa to the Dutch for generations. The districts rose in the Tondano War of 1808 rather than furnish levies for Java, and in June 1810 the British warship Dover captured Manado, holding it until Dutch rule returned in 1817.
zh:
在米纳哈萨半岛的最北端，万鸦老朝向被火山群峰环抱的海湾，布纳肯和古万鸦老等岛屿浮在海面。岸后的内陆是米纳哈萨人的家园——通布卢、通西、通滕博安、通达诺等各自独立的山地区域（瓦拉克），村民尚武，操九种互有关联的语言，恪守祖先的祭仪；海边的韦南村是他们在湾畔最古老的定居点。海那边的特尔纳特苏丹向这里索取贡赋，也把伊斯兰教随商路带来；布吉斯、马来和中国的商船在往返摩鹿加香料群岛的途中在此停泊，山地各部却仍守着自己的神明。1444年的万鸦老只是这样一处锚地，闻名于特尔纳特和布吉斯水手之间，欧洲人还一无所知。

1523年，葡萄牙水手西芒·德·阿布雷乌望见万鸦老岛，成为第一个看见这座半岛的欧洲人；到16世纪中叶，葡萄牙人已在韦南设有商馆。来自马尼拉的西班牙人在1550年代夺取阿穆朗的要塞，又在万鸦老自建堡垒，当地逐渐形成混血社群；1630年，西班牙混血儿之子蒙图·温图被承认为第一位万鸦老国王。后来西班牙把在半岛的权益让给葡萄牙，米纳哈萨酋长苏皮特、帕阿特和隆托转而联络荷兰东印度公司：公司的阿姆斯特丹堡于1658年建成，最后一批葡萄牙人几年后被逐走。1679年1月10日，驻摩鹿加的荷兰总督罗伯特斯·帕德特布鲁赫与二十三位瓦拉克首领缔约结盟，共同对抗博拉翁蒙贡多，米纳哈萨由此与荷兰人捆绑了数代人之久。1808年各部拒绝为爪哇提供兵丁，爆发通达诺战争；1810年6月，英国战舰多佛号攻占万鸦老，直到1817年荷兰人才恢复统治。

en:
Buru lies between the Banda and Seram seas, the third largest of the Moluccan islands. Its mountainous, forested interior is ringed by coastal plains where Buru clans grew rice, sago and, above all, cloves. In 1365 the Old Javanese eulogy Nagarakretagama counted the island, under the name Hutan Kadali, among the lands subordinate to Majapahit, though no Javanese rule ever reached its villages. In 1444 Buru was still governed by local clan heads; merchants from Java, Sulawesi and the Malay world called for its cloves, but no outside power held the island.

In the 16th century the sultans of Ternate and the Portuguese both laid claim to Buru without occupying it, while Makassar traders raised fortifications and forced the islanders to expand their clove gardens. A Dutch East India Company expedition drove the Makassar out in 1648 and burned more than three thousand clove trees rather than leave them to rivals. In 1658 the Company built a fort on Kayeli Bay, held by 24 soldiers and four cannon, and forcibly relocated about 2,000 islanders, including much of the tribal nobility, into thirteen villages around it to work the new plantations. The mixed Kayeli community beside the fort supplied the rajas through whom the Company ruled the island until its charter lapsed in 1799 and Buru passed to the Dutch crown.
zh:
布鲁岛地处班达海与塞兰海之间，是摩鹿加群岛第三大岛。岛上内陆山林密布，沿海平原上的布鲁人诸部种植水稻、西谷，最重要的物产则是丁香。1365年的古爪哇颂诗《爪哇史颂》将该岛以「Hutan Kadali」之名列为满者伯夷的附属之地，但爪哇人的势力从未真正触及岛上的村落。1444年的布鲁仍由本地氏族首领治理，爪哇、苏拉威西和马来世界的商人前来收购丁香，却没有任何外来政权据有此岛。

16世纪，特尔纳特苏丹与葡萄牙人都宣称对布鲁拥有主权，却都不曾占领该岛；望加锡商人则在岛上修筑工事，强迫岛民扩大丁香种植。1648年，荷兰东印度公司的远征队逐走望加锡人，并烧毁三千余株丁香树，以免其落入竞争者之手。1658年，公司在卡耶利湾修筑要塞，驻兵24人、配炮4门，又把包括大部氏族贵族在内的约两千名岛民强行迁入要塞周围的十三个村庄，为新辟的种植园劳作。要塞旁形成的混血卡耶利人共同体世代出任拉贾，公司便通过他们统治布鲁，直到1799年特许状到期、岛屿转归荷兰国家管辖。

en:
Ambon is a small, fertile island off the south coast of Seram, where two mountainous peninsulas, Hitu and Leitimor, clasp a broad sheltered bay. Its cloves drew Malay and Javanese merchants to a mosaic of village realms, and in 1444 the islanders still followed the old beliefs; the northern villages turned to Islam only with the rise of the kingdom of Hitu around 1470. No foreign lord ruled Ambon then, but its harbor was already known to sailors from Malacca to the spice markets of Java.

The Portuguese landed in 1512 and opened a factory in 1521, yet Muslim Hitu harried them for decades and they held Ambon securely only after raising a stone fort in the 1570s. In February 1605 Steven van der Hagen took that fort for the Dutch East India Company without a shot, and Ambon served as the Company's eastern headquarters until Batavia was founded in 1619. An English factory at Cambello became the Amboyna massacre of 1623; Cromwell extracted a heavy indemnity in 1654, and John Dryden staged the story in London in 1673. The island's own clove wars lasted longer: Kakiali of Hitu was killed by a traitor in 1643, his successor Telukabesi died when the rock fastness of Kapahaha was stormed in July 1646, and the Great Ambon War, aided by Makassarese fighters, was crushed only in 1656.
