The Company then made Ambon the center of its clove monopoly, destroying the trees on other islands. British squadrons seized the island in 1796 and again in 1810, returning it to the Dutch in 1802 and 1814, and in 1821 Ambon remained the Moluccas' clove capital under Fort Victoria.
zh:
安汶是斯兰岛南岸外一座肥沃小岛，希图与莱蒂莫尔两个多山半岛环抱着宽阔的避风海湾。岛上出产的丁香把马来和爪哇商人引到林立的村邦；1444年时岛民仍信奉旧俗，直到约1470年希图王国兴起，北岸诸村才改宗伊斯兰教。此时没有任何外来君主统治安汶，但它的港湾已为从马六甲到爪哇香料市场的水手所熟知。

葡萄牙人1512年登岛，1521年设立商馆，但穆斯林的希图数十年间不断袭扰，直到1570年代筑起石砌要塞后才稳固据有该岛。1605年2月，史蒂文·范德哈根兵不血刃地为荷兰东印度公司夺下这座要塞，安汶此后成为公司在东方的总部，直到1619年巴达维亚建立。英国人在坎贝洛开设的商馆酿成1623年的「安汶大屠杀」，克伦威尔1654年为此索取巨额赔款，约翰·德莱顿又于1673年在伦敦把此事搬上舞台。岛上的丁香战争持续更久：希图的卡卡亚利1643年被叛徒杀害，其继任者特卢卡贝西据守的绝壁要塞卡帕哈于1646年7月被攻陷；有可望加锡战士相助的「大安汶战争」也到1656年才被镇压。公司随后把安汶作为丁香专卖的中心，在其他岛屿铲除丁香树。英国舰队1796年、1810年两度攻占安汶，又先后于1802年和1814年归还荷兰；1821年时，维多利亚要塞拱卫下的安汶仍是摩鹿加的丁香之都。

en:
Seram, called Nusa Ina, the Mother Island, by central Moluccans, is the largest island of the Moluccas, a rugged mountain mass across a narrow strait from Ambon. Its interior peoples lived by the sago palm and the forest in autonomous clan societies, while coastal villages traded with Ternatan merchants for the spices of the smaller islands. In 1444 no sultan yet ruled in Ternate, whose court would accept Islam only after 1465, and Seram's clans kept the old beliefs, loosely drawn into the trade networks of the spice islands.

The ships of António de Abreu and Francisco Serrão first charted its southern coast for Europeans in 1512, and Portuguese missionaries followed later in the century. Ternate ruled its western districts, the Hoamoal peninsula, through noble chiefs until the Great Ambon War of 1651 to 1656 ended their power and left Seram under nominal Dutch control, while the sultans of Tidore held suzerainty in the east from 1700 to 1768. In 1780 Prince Nuku of Tidore raised his standard against the Dutch and made Seram a principal base of a thirty years' rebellion, uniting islanders from the Moluccas to New Guinea and, with British East India Company backing, briefly ruling as sultan in Tidore. After his death in 1805 the movement collapsed, and by 1821 Seram was back under the Dutch flag, its mountain interior still unconquered.
zh:
塞兰岛被中摩鹿加人称作「努萨·伊纳」，意为母岛，是摩鹿加群岛最大的岛屿，与安汶隔一道狭窄海峡相望，全岛山岭崎岖。内陆居民以西谷椰和山林为生，结成自治的氏族社会，沿海村落则与特尔纳特商人交易，换取更小岛屿上出产的香料。1444年时特尔纳特还没有苏丹——其宫廷要到1465年以后才接受伊斯兰教，塞兰诸部仍守旧俗，只是被松散地卷入香料群岛的贸易网络。

1512年，安东尼奥·德·阿布雷乌与弗朗西斯科·塞朗的船只首次为欧洲人测绘了塞兰南海岸，葡萄牙传教士随后在该世纪晚些时候登岛。特尔纳特通过贵族首领统治西部的霍阿莫阿尔半岛，直到1651至1656年的大安汶战争终结了他们的权势，塞兰从此处于荷兰的名义控制之下；1700至1768年，蒂多雷苏丹在岛的东部保有宗主权。1780年，蒂多雷王子努库举旗反荷，以塞兰为主要基地进行了长达三十年的战争，把从摩鹿加到新几内亚的岛民联合起来，并借助英国东印度公司的支持一度在蒂多雷称苏丹。他1805年死后运动瓦解，到1821年塞兰重归荷兰旗下，内陆山区却始终未被征服。

en:
Halmahera, called Jilolo on early European maps, is the largest of the Moluccas, mountainous and overshadowed by the clove isles Ternate and Tidore off its west coast. On its western shore stood Jailolo, one of the four kingdoms of Maloko Kie Raha, whose ruler, the Jika ma-kolano or Lord of the Bay, held pride of place after the four kings met on Moti in the 1320s. Ternate later overtook it: under Komalo Pulo, who reigned from 1377 to 1432, it seized villages on Halmahera and the precedence with them. Its forest interior belonged to animist peoples under a Raja Papua, a lord with access to highland gold. In 1444 Jailolo still kept the old rites, for Islam came only late in the century; its cloves grew wild, and the island chiefly fed the spice marts with sago.

Late in the fifteenth century the preacher Mahadum converted King Yusuf. The first Portuguese reached Ternate in 1512, and after their fortress rose there in 1522-23 Jailolo leaned instead on the Spaniards posted on Tidore. Tristao de Atayde sacked the royal center in 1533, but the regent Katarabumi seized the throne around 1536 and made its stone fort the scourge of every European; he devised a script for the local language and held out until March 1551, when Bernaldim de Sousa and Sultan Hairun of Ternate starved him out. Katarabumi took poison the next year, and Jailolo became a Ternatan vassal paying tribute of sago. Its last prince, Doa, fell at sea against Tidore in 1613, and a later Raja Jailolo was taken off Buru and drowned by the Dutch in 1656. The title revived only in 1804, when Sultan Nuku of Tidore raised Muhammad Arif Bila to it; when the Dutch retook Tidore in 1806 he perished in the Halmahera forest. His brother Hajuddin, proclaimed sultan in 1818 or 1819, led raiding fleets no Dutch expedition of 1819-20 could catch.
zh:
哈马黑拉在早期欧洲地图上称作吉洛洛，是摩鹿加群岛中最大的岛屿，山林密布，西海岸外两座小小的香料之岛特尔纳特和蒂多雷反倒更令外人瞩目。岛西岸立着贾伊洛洛，是「摩鹿加四山」（Maloko Kie Raha）四大王国之一；14世纪20年代四王在莫蒂岛会盟后，贾伊洛洛君主的王号「吉卡马科拉诺」（意为「海湾之主」）位列四王之先。后来特尔纳特后来居上：1377年至1432年在位的科马洛·普洛夺取了哈马黑拉的村庄，也夺走了首席地位。丛林腹地属于信奉泛灵的各部族，由一位「巴布亚拉惹」统辖，这位首领能大量取得高地黄金。1444年的贾伊洛洛宫廷仍守旧礼，伊斯兰要到本世纪末才传入；岛上的丁香只是林间野生，哈马黑拉主要以西谷米供应香料市场。

15世纪末，传教士马哈德姆使国王优素福皈依。1512年，首批葡萄牙人抵达特尔纳特；1522至1523年葡萄牙人在岛上筑起要塞后，贾伊洛洛反而倚仗驻扎蒂多雷的西班牙人。1533年，葡萄牙船长特里斯唐·德·阿泰德洗劫王城，但约1536年篡位的摄政卡塔拉布米把石堡变成所有欧洲人的劲敌，他为当地语言创制文字，坚守到1551年3月，才被贝尔纳丁·德·索萨与特尔纳特苏丹哈伦以长期围困耗尽粮草。卡塔拉布米次年服毒而死，贾伊洛洛沦为特尔纳特附庸，以进贡西谷米为务。末位有名可考的王公多阿1613年在与蒂多雷的海战中阵亡，后来的一位「贾伊洛洛拉惹」1656年在布鲁岛外被荷兰人擒获、抛入海中。王号直到1804年才复兴，蒂多雷苏丹努库拥立穆罕默德·阿里夫·比拉复位；荷兰军队1806年夺回蒂多雷，阿里夫·比拉在哈马黑拉山林中殒命。其弟哈朱丁于1818或1819年被拥立为苏丹，率领袭掠船队纵横海上，1819至1820年的荷兰历次远征都没能将他抓获。

en:
Beneath the volcano Gamalama, Ternate's cloves made its kolano one of the richest rulers in the Moluccas. Villages founded by migrants from Halmahera had been united under one king in 1257, and in the 1400s Ternate subdued the Sula Islands and Seram, shipping cloves to China and Java in an endless duel with Tidore across the water. Javanese and Chinese merchants had their own quarters by the shore, and the Moti Agreement of about 1322 had regularized the spice trade among the islands. In 1444 Kolano Marhum still kept the old Moluccan rites, though Muslim traders were already at his court; his son Zainal Abidin would be the first sultan.

Zainal Abidin ruled from 1486 to 1500, took the title sultan and made Islamic law the basis of government. Shipwrecked off Seram, the Portuguese Francisco Serrão was brought to Ternate in 1512 by Sultan Bayan Sirrullah, who allowed Kastela fort to be built from 1522. The alliance turned to feud: the Portuguese deposed Sultan Tabariji in 1535 and murdered Sultan Hairun in 1570, after which Sultan Baabullah took Kastela in 1575 and carried Ternatean power to its height over Ambon, the Bandas and parts of Mindanao. A Spanish fleet conquered the island in 1606 and exiled its sultan to Manila; the Dutch built Fort Malayo in 1607, and the island was split between the two powers until Spain left in 1663. Sultans Hamzah and Mandar Syah ceded lands to the VOC in return for aid, and Ternate became a Dutch client; the British held it from 1810 until its return to the Netherlands in 1817.
zh:
在加马拉马火山脚下，特尔纳特出产的丁香使其科兰诺成为摩鹿加最富有的统治者之一。1257年，来自哈马黑拉的移民建立的诸村已统一于一位君王；15世纪里特尔纳特征服苏拉群岛和斯兰岛，把丁香销往中国和爪哇，与一水之隔的蒂多雷争斗不休。爪哇和中国商人在岸边各有聚居区，约1322年的《莫蒂协议》还曾规范诸岛之间的香料贸易。1444年，科兰诺马尔胡姆仍奉行摩鹿加旧礼，尽管宫廷里已有穆斯林商人；他的儿子扎伊纳尔·阿比丁日后将成为第一位苏丹。

扎伊纳尔·阿比丁1486年至1500年在位，改称苏丹，以伊斯兰教法为治国之本。1512年，在斯兰岛外海沉船的葡萄牙人弗朗西斯科·塞朗被巴彦·西鲁拉苏丹接到特尔纳特，1522年起苏丹允许葡萄牙人修建卡斯特拉堡。同盟很快反目：1535年葡萄牙人废黜塔巴里吉苏丹，1570年又谋杀海伦苏丹，巴布乌拉苏丹遂于1575年夺取卡斯特拉堡，特尔纳特的势力臻于鼎盛，远及安汶、班达群岛和棉兰老部分地区。1606年西班牙舰队征服该岛，把苏丹流放马尼拉；1607年荷兰人修建马来尤堡，全岛自此由两大势力分据，直到1663年西班牙撤离。哈姆扎与曼达尔·夏以土地换取荷兰东印度公司的援助，特尔纳特沦为荷兰附庸；1810年至1817年英国一度占据，随后交还荷兰。

en:
Tidore rises from the sea in a single volcanic cone, and its cloves drew the same Malay and Chinese prahus that enriched its rival Ternate, an hour's sail to the north. Its kolano, the King of the Mountain, ruled southern Halmahera, Buru and the islands off the Papuan coast, and married his daughters to Ternate's sultans. In 1444 the court still kept the old Moluccan cults; the elite turned to Islam only in the 1460s and 1470s, when the ninth king Ciri Leliatu took the Muslim name Jamaluddin under the Arab preacher Syekh Mansur.

Survivors of Magellan's expedition reached Tidore in November 1521, and Sultan al-Mansur loaded their ships with cloves and took Spain as his ally against the Portuguese of Ternate. A Spanish-Tidore army conquered Ternate in 1606 and Madrid kept several forts on the island until its withdrawal in 1663. Left without its patron, Tidore stayed largely independent under Sultan Saifuddin (r. 1657–1689), who spent Dutch payments for cloves on gifts binding the outer islands to his court. The VOC's extirpatie destroyed spice trees outside its licensed plots and impoverished the island, and a treaty of 1780 reduced Tidore to a Dutch vassal. Prince Nuku fled that same year and waged a generation of guerrilla war with Papuan and Halmaheran followers and British arms; he took Tidore in 1797 and helped the British storm Ternate in 1801, but after his death in 1805 the Dutch returned and reoccupied the Moluccas in 1817.
zh:
蒂多雷是一座拔海而起的锥形火山岛，岛上的丁香把马来和中国快船吸引而来，也养肥了北面仅一小时航程的劲敌特尔纳特。它的科兰诺号称「山之王」，统治南哈马黑拉、布鲁和巴布亚沿岸诸岛，并把公主嫁给特尔纳特的苏丹们。1444年的宫廷仍奉行摩鹿加旧俗；直到1460至1470年代，在阿拉伯传教师谢赫·曼苏尔感召下，第九代王西里·莱利亚图取了穆斯林名字贾马卢丁，伊斯兰教才在统治层立足。

1521年11月，麦哲伦远征队的幸存者抵达蒂多雷，曼苏尔苏丹用丁香装满他们的船，并与西班牙结盟对抗盘踞特尔纳特的葡萄牙人。1606年西班牙与蒂多雷联军攻克特尔纳特，此后西班牙在岛上设有数座要塞，直到1663年撤军。失去靠山的蒂多雷在赛夫丁苏丹（1657—1689年在位）治下仍大体保持独立，他用荷兰人收购丁香的货款笼络外岛首领。荷兰东印度公司推行除树政策，毁掉特许种植区之外的香料树，使蒂多雷日益穷困，1780年的条约更把它降为荷兰附庸。同年王子努库出逃，率巴布亚和哈马黑拉部众、凭英国军火打了二十余年游击战，1797年攻占蒂多雷，1801年助英军拿下特尔纳特；1805年他一死，荷兰人卷土重来，于1817年重新占领摩鹿加。

en:
The Sulu islands lie across the busiest seaways of the Sulu Sea, home to the Tausug, whose port of Jolo grew on the trade between China, Borneo and the Moluccas. Arab missionaries brought Islam in the late 14th century, and Karim ul-Makhdum is said to have raised the first mosque in the Philippines on Simunul in 1380; early in the 15th century Sharif ul-Hashim founded the sultanate at Buansa, near Jolo. In 1417 Paduka Pahala, East King of Sulu, sailed to the Yongle Emperor's court together with the West King and the Cave King, but he fell ill and died on his way home and was buried at Dezhou in Shandong, where his younger sons and their following stayed; Sulu sent no more tribute missions after 1424. In 1444 Jolo, enriched by the traffic of the Sulu Sea and its pearl beds, remained an independent Sunni sultanate ruled by his line.

Later in the 15th century Sulu came under Bruneian overlordship and only regained its freedom in 1578, when Spain was already conquering the Philippines to the north. In 1658 Brunei granted the sultan lands along the northeast coast of Borneo in return for help in its civil war, the root of Sulu's later claim to Sabah. From Zamboanga Spain warred on the sultanate for centuries, while Tausug and Iranun fleets swept the Visayas in their lanong warships, bringing thousands of captives to Jolo's slave market. Sulu yielded Palawan to Spain in 1705. Between 1726 and 1733 it revived its old trade with China and sent tribute to the Qing court. In 1761 Alexander Dalrymple of the East India Company made a treaty at Jolo and opened a factory on Balambangan, though the English abandoned the island in 1805; Basilan passed to Spain the following year.
zh:
苏禄群岛横亘苏禄海最繁忙的航道上，岛上的陶苏格人以霍洛为港，经营中国、婆罗洲与摩鹿加之间的贸易。14世纪末，阿拉伯传教士把伊斯兰教带到这里，据说卡里姆·马克敦1380年在锡穆努尔岛建起菲律宾的第一座清真寺；15世纪初，谢里夫·哈希姆在霍洛附近的布安萨建立苏丹国。1417年，苏禄东王巴都葛·叭哈喇与西王麻哈喇·葛麻·丁、峒王巴都葛·叭喇卜一同晋见明成祖，归国途中东王病逝，安葬于山东德州，他的次子、三子及随从从此留居当地；1424年以后苏禄不再遣使入贡。1444年的霍洛凭苏禄海的商路和珠池之利，仍是一个独立的逊尼派苏丹国，由东王的后裔统治。

15世纪后期，苏禄一度受文莱控制，直到1578年才重新独立，此时西班牙已在北面的菲律宾展开征服。1658年，文莱为酬答苏禄助平内战，把婆罗洲东北沿岸一带割让给苏禄，这便是后来沙巴之争的由来。西班牙人以三宝颜为前沿，与苏丹国交战数百年；陶苏格人和伊拉农人则乘兰农（lanong）战船袭掠米沙鄢，把数以千计的俘虏送到霍洛的奴隶市场。1705年，苏禄把巴拉望让给西班牙；1726年至1733年又恢复对华通商，向清廷遣使入贡。1761年，英国东印度公司的亚历山大·达尔林普尔在霍洛缔约，在巴兰邦岸岛设立商站，但英国人1805年放弃了该岛；次年，巴西兰落入西班牙之手。

en:
The Cotabato basin is the floodplain of the Pulangi, the great river of Mindanao, whose delta channels run through mangrove and rice land to Illana Bay. In 1444 Maguindanaon and Iranun fishermen and traders lived along these banks, with the Teduray in the nearby hills, all keeping their ancestral cults; Malay and Chinese junks already called there for wax and forest produce, while the river chiefs looked across the water to Muslim Brunei and Johor. No sultan yet ruled the valley — Islam came only with the next generation.

It arrived with Sharif Kabungsuwan of Johor, who married local princesses and in 1515 founded the Sultanate of Maguindanao with its first seat at Tubok. A Spanish expedition of 1579 failed, and in 1596 Esteban Rodríguez de Figueroa, holder of the right to conquer Mindanao, was beaten at Buayan and killed in an ambush. The sultanate reached its height under Muhammad Dipatuan Kudarat (r. c. 1619–1671), whose allied raiders reached the Visayas; Governor Corcuera stormed his river capital of Lamitan in 1637, but Kudarat escaped to the hills and recovered all he had lost after the Spanish withdrawal of 1663. In 1705 the sultan ceded Palawan to Spain, and in 1711 he moved his seat to Tamontaka. The rebuilding of Fort Pilar at Zamboanga in 1719 began a long decline, marked by civil war in the 1730s and rival courts at Buayan and Cotabato.
zh:
哥打巴托盆地是棉兰老大河普兰吉河的冲积平原，三角洲上的河汊穿过红树林与稻田，注入伊拉纳湾。1444年，马京达瑙人和伊拉农人在河畔渔猎贸易，特杜赖人居住在附近山地，都奉行祖先旧俗；马来和中国帆船已来此收购蜂蜡和山林物产，河畔诸首领则与穆斯林的文莱、柔佛隔海相望。那时河谷里还没有苏丹，伊斯兰要等到下一代才随传教者到来。

1515年，来自柔佛的谢里夫·卡本苏安娶了当地首领之女，创立马京达瑙苏丹国，最初定都图博。1579年西班牙远征队无功而返；1596年，获封棉兰老征服权的埃斯特万·罗德里格斯·德·菲格罗阿在布亚延兵败，又死于伏击。苏丹国在穆罕默德·迪帕图安·库达拉特（约1619—1671年在位）治下达到鼎盛，盟友的袭掠远达米沙鄢；1637年总督科尔奎拉攻破他在河畔的都城拉米坦，库达拉特却逃入山中，并在1663年西班牙撤军后收复全部失地。1705年苏丹把巴拉望割让给西班牙，1711年迁都塔蒙塔卡。1719年西班牙人在三宝颜重建皮拉尔堡，苏丹国由此步入长期衰落，1730年代陷入内战，布亚延与哥打巴托两庭相争。

en:
Lanao is the country of Lake Lanao, the great lake at the heart of Mindanao, whose waters drain north through the Agus river. The Maranao — 'people of the lake' — built their tall-roofed torogan houses along its shores, grew rice in the surrounding plains, cast brass and traded with the Maguindanaon of the Pulangi. In 1444 they still followed the old animist ways celebrated in the Darangen, a sung epic older than the 14th century; no Muslim preacher had yet reached the lake, and no sultan ruled its chiefs.

Islam arrived through the Maguindanao valley: Sharif Makaalang, the Maranao son of Sharif Kabungsuwan, brought the new faith and the sultan's title into Lanao. The bond broke in 1616, when Datu Kudarat seized power in Maguindanao against the old rotation between the two lands, and the lords of Bayabao, Masiu, Unayan and Balo-i met at Taraka to form the four Confederate States of Lanao — still sailing and fighting beside Maguindanao against Spain. On 4 April 1639 Governor Corcuera sent Francisco de Atienza and the missionary Agustín de San Pedro against the lake with Boholano troops, and a garrison planted in 1640 was stormed and destroyed by the Maranao; no Spaniard returned for 250 years. The lakeside settlement of Dansalan, at the northern end of the lake, was first recorded by the Spanish in 1689.
zh:
拉瑙是棉兰老腹地拉瑙湖一带的国度，湖水经阿古斯河北泄入海。马拉瑙人——意为「湖畔之民」——沿湖岸建起高脊飞檐的托罗甘大宅，在周围平原种植稻米、铸造黄铜，并与普兰吉河流域的马京达瑙人通商。1444年，他们仍奉行《达兰根》史诗所吟唱的古老泛灵信仰，这部口传长诗早于14世纪；那时没有穆斯林传教师涉足湖区，也没有苏丹统辖诸首领。

伊斯兰经马京达瑙河谷传来：谢里夫·卡本苏安的马拉瑙人之子谢里夫·马卡朗把新信仰和苏丹称号带上拉瑙。两地处的纽带于1616年断裂，达图·库达拉特打破拉瑙与马京达瑙之间旧有的轮替惯例夺取苏丹之位，巴亚包、马西乌、乌纳扬和巴洛伊四邦的首领遂在塔腊卡集会，结成拉瑙四邦同盟，不过对西班牙作战时仍与马京达瑙联兵。1639年4月4日，总督科尔奎拉派弗朗西斯科·德·阿蒂恩萨和传教士阿古斯丁·德·圣佩德罗率保和兵进犯湖区；1640年设立的要塞旋即被马拉瑙人攻陷摧毁，此后二百五十年间再无西班牙人在此立足。湖北端的湖畔聚落丹沙兰最早于1689年为西班牙人记载。

en:
Samar is the third-largest island of the Philippines and the eastern edge of the Visayas, a wet, jungle-cloaked land facing the open Pacific. Its Waray people lived in coastal chiefdoms such as Laoang, Palapag and Sulat, whose datus wore gold earrings and chains and were rowed by collared oarsmen; early Spaniards heard the island called Ibabao or Tandaya, and Pigafetta wrote it down as Zamal. It lay a little off the main China–Maluku sea lane, trading on a smaller scale in gold and beeswax. In 1444 Samar knew no sultan and no foreign master, only its rival datus and the rites of the anito.

On 16 March 1521 Magellan's fleet, sailing from the Marianas, made Samar the first Philippine land it sighted, and the next day the crews landed at Homonhon to take water; Pigafetta named the archipelago San Lázaro. In 1543 the Villalobos expedition called here and gave Samar and Leyte the name Filipinas, after the prince who became Philip II, a name that later spread to the whole colony. Spanish rule only really arrived in 1596 with the first missions, and Samar was long administered from Cebu. On 1 June 1649 the Waray leader Agustín Sumuroy killed the friar at Palapag and raised a revolt against the forced-labor levy; the rising ran across the Visayas and into Mindanao before it was put down in 1650, and its survivors founded new villages in the mountains. Samar was joined to Leyte in 1735 with Carigara as capital and separated again in 1768; in 1821 it remained a poor, storm-beaten province of friar parishes and scattered coastal towns.
zh:
萨马是菲律宾第三大岛，也是米沙鄢的最东缘，一座湿润的丛林之岛直面开阔的太平洋。岛上的瓦瑞人分属拉旺、帕拉帕格、苏拉特等沿海达图领地，首领耳戴金环、身挂金链，出行由颈戴金圈的桨手划船；早期西班牙人听到此岛叫伊巴奥或坦达亚，皮加费塔则记作扎马尔。萨马稍稍偏离中国到摩鹿加的主航道，只以金、蜂蜡一类山货做较小规模的贸易。1444年的萨马既无苏丹，也无外来宗主，只有相互争雄的达图和阿尼托祖灵祭祀。

1521年3月16日，从马里亚纳群岛驶来的麦哲伦船队把萨马作为望见的第一块菲律宾土地，次日船员在霍蒙洪岛登陆取水，皮加费塔将这片群岛命名为圣拉扎罗。1543年，维拉洛沃斯的探险队到此，以后来成为腓力二世的王子之名，把萨马和莱特称作「菲律宾」，这个名字日后才扩及整个殖民地。西班牙人的实际统治迟至1596年随首批传教士到来，萨马长期由宿务管辖。1649年6月1日，瓦瑞人首领阿古斯丁·苏莫罗伊在帕拉帕格杀死修士，率众反抗强征服役，起义席卷米沙鄢并蔓延到棉兰老，直到1650年才被镇压，幸存者退入山区另建新村。1735年萨马与莱特合并，以卡里加拉为首府，1768年又重新分设；1821年时，它仍是个贫穷、常遭风暴的省份，散布着修士教区和沿海小镇。

en:
Southern Palawan faces the Sulu Sea, with Balabac guarding the island-studded passage toward Borneo. Tagbanwa, Palaw'an and Batak communities lived in the interior, while Islamized Molbog farmers and fishermen held the far south and Malay-speaking traders linked the coast with Borneo and Sulu. By the fifteenth century the older orbit of Ma-i had given way to Brunei's maritime empire, though Sulu datus exercised much of the immediate power along the shore. In 1444 the island grew rice, coconuts and sugarcane and could provision passing vessels, but Brunei's authority rested lightly on the interior forests.

In 1521 the survivors of Magellan's expedition reached the island they called Pulaoan. A local datu sealed friendship with a blood compact and supplied the ships with rice cooked in bamboo, wine, bananas, livestock and sugarcane. Spanish power moved south only slowly: Recollect missions met Muslim resistance in the seventeenth century, and the Sultan of Brunei ceded southern Palawan to Spain in 1749. A Spanish expedition reached Balabac in 1753, intending to secure the channel against Sulu raiders, but fever killed 116 men and left another 200 sick. The south remained a fortified frontier, and an 1818 census recorded 4,486 native families and 29 Spanish-Filipino families on Paragua under the Calamianes jurisdiction.
zh:
南巴拉望面朝苏禄海，巴拉巴克扼守着通往婆罗洲的岛群航道。塔格巴努阿人、巴拉望人和巴塔克人居住在内陆，伊斯兰化的莫尔博格农人、渔民住在岛的最南端，操马来语的商人则把海岸同婆罗洲和苏禄连接起来。到15世纪，旧日麻逸贸易圈已让位于文莱的海上势力，但沿岸近边权力多由苏禄达图掌握。1444年时，岛上种植稻米、椰子和甘蔗，也能为过往船只补给，可文莱的权威对内陆森林仍很稀薄。

1521年，麦哲伦船队的幸存者抵达他们称作普劳安的岛屿。当地达图以歃血为盟缔结盟谊，并用竹筒饭、酒、香蕉、牲畜和甘蔗补给船队。西班牙势力向南推进缓慢：17世纪的雷科莱传教团遭到穆斯林社群抵抗，文莱苏丹又在1749年把南巴拉望割让给西班牙。1753年，一支西班牙远征队进抵巴拉巴克，试图控制航道、防备苏禄袭掠者，但热病夺去116人的生命，另有200人病倒。南部始终是设防边疆；1818年的人口调查记载，归卡拉棉管辖的帕拉瓜岛有4486户本地家庭和29户西班牙—菲律宾家庭。

en:
Maynila stood on the south bank of the Pasig delta, facing Manila Bay, a fortified Tagalog bayan of wooden palisades, while the separate polity of Tondo held the north bank. Together the two towns dominated the Chinese junk trade, taking porcelain and silk from Fujian junks and redistributing them through the archipelago. In 1444 it was still a pagan town ruled by its own datus, though its chiefs already kept ties with Brunei. Around 1500 Bruneian princes married into the ruling house and the elite turned Muslim, making Maynila the northernmost reach of Islam in the Philippines; by the 1570s Rajah Matanda and his nephew Rajah Sulayman held a cosmopolitan port whose ramparts carried lantaka bronze guns cast by the local smith Panday Piray.

In 1570 Martin de Goiti stormed Maynila and left it in ashes. Miguel Lopez de Legazpi returned with his whole force in 1571, and on 24 June proclaimed a Spanish city of Manila on the ruins; Sulayman's last charge had been broken at Bangkusay channel on 3 June. Within the new walls rose Intramuros, and from 1571 to 1815 the Manila galleons carried Chinese porcelain and silk across the Pacific to Acapulco. Limahong's 62 warships failed to take the city in 1574, after which the Chinese merchants were confined to their own quarter, the Parian. Manila was formally decreed capital of the Philippines in 1595. During the Seven Years' War a British expedition captured the city in October 1762, accepted Archbishop Rojo's surrender on 30 October and held it until 1764, while Simon de Anda kept the countryside loyal to Spain. The last galleon sailed in 1815, ending the trade on which Manila had grown great.
zh:
梅尼拉位于巴石河三角洲南岸，面向马尼拉湾，是一座木栅环绕的他加禄城镇，北岸则是另一个政体汤都（Tondo）。两地把持中国帆船贸易，收购福建商船载来的瓷器和丝绸，再分销到群岛各处。1444年的梅尼拉还是由本地达图统治的泛灵信仰城镇，但首领已与文莱素有往来。1500年前后，文莱王室与统治家族联姻，上层改宗伊斯兰教，梅尼拉由此成为伊斯兰教在菲律宾传播的最北端；到1570年代，拉者·马塔达和侄子拉者·苏莱曼统治着这座五方杂处的港市，城墙上架着本地铁匠潘代·皮雷（Panday Piray）铸造的青铜旋炮（lantaka）。

1570年，马丁·德·戈伊蒂攻陷梅尼拉，将其付之一炬。1571年，米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮率全军重返，6月24日在旧城废墟上宣布建立西班牙城市马尼拉，而苏莱曼的最后一次冲锋已于6月3日在邦库赛（Bangkusay）海峡被击退。新城墙内筑起王城（Intramuros），1571年至1815年间，马尼拉大帆船把中国瓷器和丝绸横渡太平洋运往阿卡普尔科。1574年林凤率六十二艘战船来攻，未能得手，此后华人商人被安置到专门的街区「涧内」（Parian）。1595年，马尼拉被正式定为菲律宾的首府。七年战争期间，英国远征军1762年10月攻占马尼拉，10月30日接受大主教罗霍的投降，一直占领到1764年，西蒙·德·安达则在乡间坚持效忠西班牙。1815年最后一艘大帆船起航，马尼拉赖以兴盛的旧商路就此终结。

en:
The narrow coastal plain trapped between the Cordillera mountains and the South China Sea was Samtoy, the land of the Ilocanos: a string of trading towns set where the highlands meet the shore. Junks from Fujian unloaded porcelain and silk at Vigan, Japanese merchants kept a settlement at Agoo, and the markets moved Cordillera gold, beeswax, cotton and heavy burnáy stoneware jars along a coast the monsoons linked to China, Japan and the Spice Islands. In 1444 the Ilocanos still governed themselves under their own datus, their wealth drawn from the China trade and from the gold trails winding over the mountains behind them.

Juan de Salcedo, Legazpi's grandson, sailed north with eighty men in May 1572 and on 13 June founded Villa Fernandina at Vigan, the town that became the seat of the diocese of Nueva Segovia; Augustinian friars followed in 1574 to begin the conversion of the coast. Spanish taxes and monopolies bred repeated revolts. Pedro Almazán rose in Ilocos Norte in 1661, and during the British occupation of Manila Diego Silang seized Vigan with British backing and proclaimed an Ilocano state, until he was assassinated on 28 May 1763; his wife Gabriela carried on the rising until she was captured and hanged on 20 September 1763. On 16 September 1807 the cane-wine makers of Piddig rose against the basi monopoly and marched on Vigan, only to be cut down at the Bantaoay River on 28 September; in 1818 Madrid divided the province into Ilocos Norte and Ilocos Sur.
zh:
夹在中科迪勒拉山与南海之间的狭长海岸平原，是伊洛卡诺人的萨姆托伊故地，一连串背山面海的贸易城镇。福建来的帆船在维甘卸下瓷器和丝绸，日本商人在阿戈设有聚居地，市场上流转着中科迪勒拉山的黄金、蜂蜡、棉布和布尔奈粗陶大瓮，季风把这条海岸与中国、日本和香料群岛连在一起。1444年，伊洛卡诺人仍在自己的达图治下，财富来自对华贸易和身后山间的运金小道。

1572年5月，黎牙实比的外孙胡安·德·萨尔塞多率八十人北上，6月13日在维甘建立费尔南迪纳镇，日后成为新塞哥维亚主教区驻地；1574年奥斯定会修士随之而来，开始在海岸传教。西班牙人的赋税和专卖激起接连反抗：1661年佩德罗·阿尔马桑在北伊罗戈举事；英军占领马尼拉期间，迭戈·西朗借英军支持夺取维甘，宣布建立伊洛卡诺人的国家，1763年5月28日遇刺身亡，其妻加芙列拉继续领导起义，直到1763年9月20日被处绞刑。1807年9月16日，皮迪格的酿酒者为反抗巴锡甘蔗酒专卖起事，向维甘进军，9月28日在班陶伊河畔遭截杀，死者数百；1818年，马德里朝廷将伊罗戈分为北伊罗戈与南伊罗戈两省。

en:
Cagayan is the long river valley of northern Luzon, walled between the Cordillera and the Sierra Madre and opening north through marshlands to the Babuyan Channel. Ibanag, Itawes, Gaddang and their kin lived in villages strung along the river and its tributaries, farming and fishing, while the older Atta hunter-gatherers kept to the hills; at Lal-lo and Gattaran their shell mounds record centuries of river life. The valley had long stood on the Maritime Jade Road, and junks from China, Japan and the Indies put in at the river mouth, trading porcelain and metalware for gold, beeswax and forest produce. In 1444 the Cagayanes answered only to their own datus.

Juan de Salcedo first traced this coast on 29 June 1572, and in 1581 Captain Juan Pablo de Carrión entered the valley with a hundred soldiers and settler families, sent from Manila to conquer the country and plant missions. The sharpest fighting came on the north coast, where in 1582 Carrión's small force stormed the riverside stronghold of the Japanese wokou lord Tay Fusa and drove his pirates from Luzon. He founded Nueva Segovia at Lal-lo, garrisoned by Spaniards and soldiers levied in Mexico, and a royal decree of 1583 organised the whole valley as La Provincia de Cagayan, with Ibanag made its common tongue. The see created in 1595 was entrusted to the Dominicans and transferred to Vigan in 1758. By the later eighteenth century tobacco plantations were drawing Ilocano settlers up the valley, and the census of 1818 counted at old Nueva Segovia 975 native and 513 Spanish-Filipino families.
zh:
卡加延是吕宋北部的长河谷，西倚中科迪勒拉山、东靠马德雷山，北端穿过沼泽地带通向巴布延海峡。伊巴纳格人、伊塔韦人、加丹人及其亲族的村落沿干流和支流分布，农耕渔捞；更古老的阿塔采猎者则退守山地，他们在拉洛和加塔兰留下的贝丘，记录着千百年的河畔生活。河谷早就在海上玉石之路的路线上，中国、日本和南洋的帆船驶入河口，用瓷器和金属器换取黄金、蜂蜡和山林物产。1444年，卡加延人只听命于自己的达图。

1572年6月29日，胡安·德·萨尔塞多首次巡航这段海岸；1581年，胡安·巴勃罗·卡里昂奉马尼拉之命，率百名士兵和移民家属进入河谷，征服此地并设立传教区。最激烈的战斗发生在北海岸：1582年，卡里昂的小部队强攻日本倭寇首领泰·富萨设在河畔的据点，把海盗逐出吕宋。他在拉洛建立新塞哥维亚，由西班牙人和从墨西哥征募的士兵驻守；1583年的王室敕令把整条河谷编为卡加延省，并以伊巴纳格语为通用语。1595年设立的主教区于1596年交由多明我会，1758年主教座迁往维甘。到18世纪后期，烟草种植园把伊洛卡诺移民不断引入河谷；1818年的户口册载，旧新塞哥维亚有975户本地家庭和513户西菲家庭。

en:
The Lingga Islands are a scattered equatorial group between Sumatra and the southern approaches to the Strait of Malacca. Daik, on Lingga Island, lies beneath the three peaks of Mount Daik, while fishing grounds and sheltered anchorages sustained Malay boats from many small islands. In 1444 this was a quiet fishing outpost on the sea lanes running from Jambi toward Melaka, valued for fish, fresh water and safe anchorage rather than for a great court or fortress.

Later in the fifteenth century, Melaka's chief minister Tun Perak brought the Riau Islands into the Malaccan sphere, and after Melaka fell to the Portuguese in 1511 Lingga passed into the maritime empire of Johor. Its importance came suddenly in 1788, when Sultan Mahmud Shah III left Bintan for Daik with some 2,000 followers to escape Dutch control. Houses and roads were built, and tin from Singkep joined gambier and spices in trade with British ships. Mahmud died on Lingga in 1812. The succession dispute between Tengku Hussein and Tengku Abdul Rahman gave the Dutch their opening; in 1818 they stationed a garrison in Riau and required their consent for future royal appointments.
zh:
林加群岛是散落在苏门答腊东岸与马六甲海峡南口之间的一组赤道岛屿。林加岛上的岱克坐落在三峰并立的岱克山下，渔场和避风水泊供养着各小岛上的马来船户。1444年，这里只是占碑通往马六甲航道上一处安静的渔业据点，价值在鱼类、淡水和避风港，而非宏大的宫廷或要塞。

15世纪后期，马六甲宰相敦霹雳将廖内群岛纳入马六甲势力范围；1511年马六甲落入葡萄牙人之手后，林加转归柔佛的海上帝国。1788年，其地位骤然上升：苏丹马哈茂德·沙阿三世为摆脱荷兰控制，率约两千名随从从民丹迁至岱克，营建房屋与道路，新及岛的锡也与甘密、香料一起登上英国商船。1812年，马哈茂德在林加去世，东姑胡先与东姑阿都拉曼之间爆发继承之争，荷兰人趁机介入，于1818年在廖内驻扎军队，并规定此后苏丹继位须经荷兰同意。

en:
Sipsong Panna, 'twelve rice-plain districts', is the land of the Tai Lü on the upper Mekong, here called the Lancang; its capital Chiang Hung, the 'city of dawn' that later became Jinghong, straddles the river. Around 1180 the chieftain Paya Chueang unified the neighbouring mueang and founded a kingdom whose sway once reached Kengtung and Chiang Saen. The Mongols reached the valley in the 1290s, and in 1296 the Yuan installed the Cheli native office under the Dao ruling line. In 1382 the chao phaendin Dao Kan submitted to the Ming, who two years later recognised him as pacification commissioner of Cheli, a title his descendants kept for centuries. In 1444 this Theravada Buddhist land of wet rice and forest tea gardens lived under loose Ming overlordship, while just to the north Wang Ji's imperial armies were marching on Mong Mao in the second Luchuan campaign.

In the 1560s Bayinnaung's Burmese conquered Lanna and reduced Chiang Hung to a joint tributary of Burma and the Ming, each new ruler installed at a ceremony attended by both; in 1570 the local chao phaendin codified the domain as twelve banna. The Qing tightened their hold in 1729, detaching the six banna east of the Mekong into the new Pu'er Prefecture, through which the hill tea long grown by Tai Lü and Bulang villagers was carried north to fame as Pu'er tea. Sipsong Panna then became a battleground of the Qing-Konbaung war of 1765-1769, and the fighting emptied many villages; around the turn of the 19th century Siamese and Lanna armies serving Rama I and Kawila raided Chiang Hung to carry its people south. The Tai Lü court at Jinghong nevertheless survived to the end of the period as a Qing tusi.
zh:
西双版纳，傣语意为「十二千田」，是傣仂人在澜沧江（湄公河上游）沿岸居住的坝子之地，首府景洪傣语意为「黎明之城」，跨江而立。1180年前后，首领叭真（帕雅真）统一各勐，建立景陇金殿国，势力一度远达景栋、清盛。13世纪90年代蒙古军进入滇南，1296年元朝设彻里军民总管府，以刀氏为世袭总管。1382年召片领刀坎归附明朝，两年后受封为车里军民宣慰使，子孙世袭此职数百年。1444年，这个种稻植茶、信奉上座部佛教的地方处在明朝松散的土司统辖之下，而北面王骥二征麓川的大军正在征讨孟卯。

16世纪60年代，缅甸东吁王朝莽应龙攻灭兰纳，景洪沦为缅甸与明朝共同的朝贡之地，新召片领即位须由两方使者共同主持仪式；1570年，第二十四世召片领召应勐将三十多个勐整编为十二个版纳。清朝于1729年强化控制，把澜沧江以东六个版纳划归新设的普洱府，傣仂、布朗村民世代种植的山茶经普洱府北运，成就了普洱茶的名声。1765年至1769年，西双版纳成为清缅战争的战场，许多村落为之一空；18世纪末19世纪初，拉玛一世和清迈王迦威罗派暹罗、兰纳军队劫掠景洪，把人口掳往南方。尽管如此，景洪的傣仂土司朝廷仍作为清朝土司存续到本时期之末。

en:
Dali lies between the Cangshan range and Erhai Lake, the heart of the Bai country. In 738, with Tang support, Piluoge united the six zhao around the lake and founded Nanzhao, whose capital was moved to Yangjumie on the site of old Dali in 779. Tang armies sent against Nanzhao between 750 and 754 were defeated, but the Cangshan oath of 794 restored peaceful relations. Duan Siping founded the Dali kingdom at Yangjumie in 937; its Bai-ruled court traded horses with the Song and preserved its independence south of the Dadu River. Kublai's Mongol army conquered Dali in 1253, after which the Duan family served as hereditary governors under the Yuan. Ming forces under Lan Yu and Mu Ying took the city in 1382, carried the last Duan governor to Nanjing, changed Dali Route into Dali Prefecture and built the walled city still known as Dali Old Town. In 1444 it was therefore a Bai-speaking prefectural seat, Buddhist market town and caravan gateway on the Yunnan tea routes.

For most of the Ming period Dali remained a frontier prefecture rather than an independent royal capital. Horse caravans carried tea, salt and silk along the Tea Horse Road toward Tibet, while the Bonan Road ran west from Xiaguan through Yangbi and Yongping to Baoshan and the routes beyond the Yunnan border; Dali marble was another famous cargo. In 1659, as Qing armies pushed into Yunnan, the prefecture passed from Southern Ming resistance to Qing rule, and the new dynasty retained the Ming prefectural structure. Through the eighteenth century the old walled town continued to serve as an administrative and caravan centre for the Bai people beside Erhai.
zh:
大理位于苍山与洱海之间，是白族地区的中心。738年，蒙舍诏首领皮罗阁在唐朝支持下统一洱海六诏，建立南诏；779年，南诏王把都城迁到羊苴咩城，也就是后来的大理旧城。750年至754年，唐朝三次出兵南诏都被击败，794年南诏王异牟寻又与唐使在苍山会盟，恢复和好。937年，段思平在羊苴咩城建立大理国；这个以白族贵族为核心的政权与宋朝市易马匹，长期据有大渡河以南的土地。1253年，忽必烈率领的蒙古军攻灭大理，段氏随后在元朝治下出任世袭大理总管。1382年，蓝玉、沐英率领的明军攻占大理，末代段氏被执送南京，明朝改大理路为大理府，并修筑后世所称的大理古城。1444年的大理，因此是白语居民聚集的府城、佛教市镇，也是云南茶路上的马帮门户。

明代大部分时间里，大理不再是独立王都，而是西南边地的府治。马帮沿茶马古道把茶、盐和丝织品运往西藏；博南古道则从下关向西，经漾濞、永平抵达保山，再接通往云南边外的道路，大理所产大理石也是路上名货。1659年清军攻入云南，大理府从南明抵抗势力转入清朝之手，清代沿袭明代府制。整个18世纪，这座洱海旁的城垣仍作为白族地区的行政中心和马帮商镇继续运转。

en:
This province centres on Kunming, north of Dian Lake. The Dian kingdom arose around the lake before Han armies incorporated the region as Yizhou Commandery in 109 BC. In 765 Nanzhao built Tuodong, later called Shanchan, as its eastern city. Mongol forces took Shanchan in 1254, and in 1276 the Yunnan Branch Secretariat was established with its capital at Zhongqing, making Kunming rather than Dali the political centre of Yunnan. In 1381 the Hongwu Emperor sent Fu Youde, Lan Yu and Mu Ying with a large army to destroy the Yuan Prince of Liang's regime; in 1382 Zhongqing became Yunnan Prefecture and a brick walled city was built, after which Mu Ying and his heirs garrisoned the southwest while Han migrants settled around military farms. In 1444 the court launched Wang Ji's second campaign against the Luchuan tusi, drawing Yunnan's guards and native chiefs into a frontier war fought beyond the prefecture's western approaches.

Wang Ji's third campaign of 1449 broke Luchuan power but tied down Ming resources for years. The Ming collapse later brought the Yongli Emperor of the Southern Ming to Kunming, which briefly served as his Dian capital. Wu Sangui's Qing army entered Yunnan in 1659, the Yongli Emperor fled to Burma, and in 1662 Wu had him strangled in Kunming before enlarging his own princely palace there. When the court moved to reduce the feudatories in 1673, Wu raised his rebellion from Kunming; Qing troops did not recover the city until 1681, when his grandson Wu Shifan killed himself. Under the high Qing, Yunnan became a crucial copper province: in 1725 its mints had forty-seven operating furnaces, and from 1726 Ortai's reforms made Yunnan cash coins profitable enough to export to other provinces while Yunnan copper supplied mints across the empire. By the early nineteenth century Kunming was again a fortified provincial capital, copper market and caravan gateway to Southeast Asia.
zh:
这片地区以滇池以北的昆明为中心。滇国曾在湖畔兴起，公元前109年汉军将其地并入益州郡。765年，南诏王阁罗凤派其子凤伽异修筑拓东城，后来改称鄯阐城，又称东都。1254年蒙古军攻取鄯阐；1276年元朝设立云南行中书省，以中庆为省会，昆明从此取代大理成为云南的政治中心。1381年，明太祖派傅友德、蓝玉、沐英率大军攻灭元梁王政权，次年改中庆路为云南府并修筑砖城，设六门。此后沐英及其后裔世代镇守云南，汉族移民也随卫所和屯田陆续进入。1444年，明廷命王骥发动第二次征讨麓川土司之役，云南卫所和各土司都被卷入这场府城以西的边疆战争。

1449年王骥第三次出征，最终压下麓川势力，也使明军多年陷在西南边务之中。明末，南明永历帝入滇，昆明一度称滇都，成为抗清中心。1659年吴三桂率清军入滇，永历帝逃往缅甸；1662年，吴三桂将永历帝绞杀于昆明，并在五华山、翠湖一带扩建平西王府。1673年朝廷议撤藩，吴三桂在昆明起兵反清；直到1681年清军攻破昆明，其孙吴世璠自杀，三藩之乱才告结束。清代盛期，云南成为举足轻重的铜产区：1725年云南铸钱局已有47座开工熔炉，1726年鄂尔泰整顿铸务后，云南制钱不仅供给本省，还可销往外省，滇铜也支撑着全国许多钱局。到19世纪初，昆明已重新成为墙垣坚固的云南省会、滇铜集散地，以及通往东南亚的马帮门户。

en:
Guangnan lies in the karst hills of south-eastern Yunnan, on old routes toward Guangxi and the Annamese frontier. Under the Song the country belonged to the Temo circuit, and in 1275 the Yuan established the Guangnan West Route Pacification Office, with its seat where the Guangnan prefectural town later stood. The Ming replaced it with Guangnan Prefecture in 1382. The Nong clan, traditionally held to descend from Nong Zhigao, kept native authority under the new dynasty, serving as native assistant prefects. In 1444 Guangnan was thus a Ming border prefecture ruled through Zhuang native lords rather than a county directly administered by interior-style officials.

When the Southern Ming collapsed, the Yongli emperor's wandering court passed through these hills. Princess Anhua, his sister, was left in the region and, according to local tradition, died of grief after the emperor was killed; one account places her at Gerong near Guangnan, where villagers raised her tomb and the Imperial Aunt Temple and maintained an annual rite called Receiving the Imperial Aunt. The Qing brought Guangnan Prefecture under regular appointed officials in 1661. Former Vimo territory was attached to it in 1669, and in 1736 Baoning County was established as the prefectural seat in the same walled town.
zh:
广南地处云南东南的喀斯特山地，扼守通往广西和安南边境的山路。宋代这里属特磨道，元至元十二年（1275年）设广南西路宣抚司，治所即后来的广南府城。明洪武十五年（1382年）改置广南府。侬氏土司相传为侬智高后裔，元代领有宣抚司，明代降为土同知。1444年的广南是明朝边府，朝廷通过壮族侬氏世袭土官治理，而不是像内地州县那样直接派官治民。

南明覆灭前后，永历帝流亡朝廷曾往来于这片山地。安化郡主是永历帝之姐，途中被留在这一带；相传永历帝被杀后，她因悲痛而逝。其留居地有富州皈朝、广南革农村两说，广南革农村的乡民为她建墓和皇姑庙，岁岁举行「接皇姑」祭祀。清顺治十八年（1661年），广南府改设流官。康熙八年（1669年），原维摩州北部并入广南府。乾隆元年（1736年），清廷置宝宁县为广南府附郭县，府县同治于这座边地山城。

en:
Lingyun lies in the forested mountains of northwestern Guangxi, where Zhuang settlements watched the routes leading toward Yunnan and Guizhou. The Song created Sicheng Subprefecture in 1053 after the defeat of Nong Zhigao, with its seat southwest of the present town. Under the Ming the native administration moved to Gukandong, later Sicheng town, and became a directly subordinate subprefecture under Guangxi's provincial government. In 1409 Cen Zicheng, son of the Sicheng native officer Cen Shanzhong, was placed over the newly established Shanglin Chief's Office. In 1444, therefore, this remote hill country was still ruled through a Cen Zhuang native official under Ming overlordship, whose imperial titles counted for more than the court's day-to-day reach.

During the Chenghua reign Sicheng's native officer Cen Bao attacked Shanglin and forced its administration to flee westward into Guangnan. In 1490 Cen Ying occupied eighteen fortified places in Shanglin and Zhenning in Guizhou before withdrawing. The Qing raised Sicheng to a native prefecture in 1658 and reorganized it as a military and civilian prefecture three years later under Si'en. Direct official rule came only in 1727 with the replacement of native chieftains by appointed magistrates. Xilong Subprefecture and Xilin County were attached to Sicheng in 1730, and in 1740 Lingyun County was created at the prefectural seat, fixing the town's later name.
zh:
凌云地处广西西北的群山之间，壮族村寨扼守着通往云南、贵州的山路。北宋皇祐五年（1053年）平定侬智高后，朝廷设泗城州，最初治所在今凌云西南。明代，泗城州治迁往古磡峒，也就是后来的凌云县城泗城镇，并成为直隶广西承宣布政使司的土州。永乐七年（1409年），泗城土官岑善忠之子岑子成受命管辖新设的上林长官司。因此到1444年，这片偏远山地仍由岑氏壮族土司在明朝名号下世袭治理，朝廷的影响力多停留在封授与名义上。

成化年间，泗城土官岑豹出兵攻打上林长官司，迫使司署西迁广南。弘治三年（1490年），土官知州岑应一度占据上林和贵州镇宁一带的十八座城，随后退回。清顺治十五年（1658年），泗城州升为土府，十八年改为军民府，隶属思恩府。雍正五年（1727年）改土归流，朝廷委派的流官才真正接管此地。雍正八年（1730年），西隆州和西林县划归泗城府；乾隆五年（1740年），府城所在地增设凌云县，县城名称也由此确定。

en:
Commanding a bend of the Xi River above the Pearl River delta, Zhaoqing began as Gaoyao, a Han dynasty county, and became Duanzhou under the Sui in 589. The Song prince Zhao Ji held it as his fief before taking the throne as Emperor Huizong, and in 1118 he bestowed on his old residence the name Zhaoqing, 'the beginning of good fortune'. Stone from the Duanxi gorges had been carved into the prized Duan inkstones since the early Tang, and under the Song they were sent to court as tribute. In 1444 Zhaoqing was the walled seat of Zhaoqing Prefecture in Ming Guangdong, a Cantonese, Confucian town where the river trade from Guangzhou met the hills of the Two Guangs.

In 1564 the supreme commander of Liangguang moved his seat from Wuzhou to Zhaoqing, which for the next 182 years served as the political centre of Guangdong and Guangxi. In 1583 the Jesuits Michele Ruggieri and Matteo Ricci were permitted to settle in the city, building the first Jesuit house and church on the Chinese mainland, and in 1584 Ricci produced the first world map in Chinese, until a new viceroy expelled him to Shaozhou in 1589. As the Ming collapsed, the Prince of Gui was enthroned at Zhaoqing in 1646 as the Yongli Emperor, and the city served off and on as his Southern Ming capital until Qing armies took it in 1650. The viceroy moved to Guangzhou in 1746, leaving Zhaoqing a quiet prefectural seat above the river gorges.
zh:
肇庆控扼西江在珠江三角洲上游的一处江湾，汉代为高要县，隋开皇九年（589年）置端州。端王赵佶曾以端州为封地，他后来即位为宋徽宗，重和元年（1118年）把这座潜邸之地赐名「肇庆」，意为吉庆之始。自唐初起，端溪山涧的石材便用来雕琢名贵的端砚，宋代端砚被列为贡品。1444年的肇庆是明朝广东肇庆府的治所，城墙临江，广州上行的商船与两广山区的货物在此交汇，是操粤语、尊孔儒的粤西重镇。

嘉靖四十三年（1564年），两广总督把驻地从梧州移到肇庆，此后182年间肇庆是广东、广西两省的军政中心。1583年，耶稣会士罗明坚、利玛窦获准在此定居，建起中国大陆第一座耶稣会住院与教堂；1584年利玛窦在这里绘成第一幅中文世界地图，直到1589年新任总督把他逐往韶州。明末天下崩解，桂王朱由榔于1646年在肇庆称帝，是为永历帝，肇庆几度成为南明行在，1650年终被清军攻占。1746年（乾隆十一年）两广总督移驻广州，肇庆仍为府城，守着西江上的羚羊峡。

en:
Facing the Leizhou peninsula across the narrow Qiongzhou Strait, Qiongshan and its port Haikou form the northern gateway of Hainan. Han armies set up the Zhuya commandery on the island in 110 BC; the Tang established Qiongshan county in 627, and from Tang times on the prefecture seated here was called Qiongzhou. Song and Yuan rulers used Hainan as a place of exile, while settlers from Fujian brought their Min speech to the northern coast. In 1444 this was the seat of Qiongzhou Prefecture, the Ming dynasty's administrative centre for the whole island, and the Haikou garrison – walled in 1395 – guarded the crossing through which tropical hardwoods, incense, betel nut and island sugar were shipped to the mainland; Li peoples held the wooded highlands of the interior.

Qiongshan produced two of the most revered officials of the Ming. Qiu Jun (1421–1495), a poor island boy who rose to be Minister of Revenue and a grand secretary, left a vast body of writing, above all the Supplement to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, a grand compendium of statecraft. Hai Rui (1514–1587), born in the same prefectural city, earned the name 'Hai the Clear Sky' as an incorruptible magistrate and censor; a memorial denouncing the Jiajing Emperor's neglect of rule had him condemned in the imperial prison, and he was freed only after the emperor's death. On 13 July 1605 a magnitude-7.5 earthquake struck Qiongshan: the northern shore subsided into the strait and seventy-two villages vanished beneath the waves, the 'undersea villages' unique in China's earthquake history.
zh:
琼山与它的外港海口隔琼州海峡与雷州半岛相望，是海南岛的北门。公元前110年，汉军在岛上设立珠崖郡；唐贞观元年（627年）置琼山县，唐代以来设治于此的州郡便称琼州。宋元两代长期把海南作为流放官员之地，福建沿海的移民则陆续登岸，把闽地乡音带到岛北。1444年的琼山是明朝琼州府治所、全岛的行政中心；1395年（洪武二十七年）筑城的海口所在海峡边把守渡口，岛上的热带硬木、香料、槟榔和蔗糖由此渡海北上，黎族则居住在林木幽深的内陆山地。

琼山走出了明代最受敬重的两位名臣。丘濬（1421—1495）由岛上孤学的童子位至户部尚书、武英殿大学士，一生著述宏富，所撰《大学衍义补》是明代经世之学的巨著。海瑞（1514—1587）也生于琼山府城，以清廉刚直得号「海青天」；他上章痛斥嘉靖帝怠政，被下诏狱论死，直到新君即位才获释。1605年7月13日，琼山发生7.5级大地震，北岸陆地沉陷入海，七十二个村庄没入波涛，成为中国地震史上独有的「海底村庄」。

en:
Canton, the Chinese Guangzhou, grew at the head of the Pearl River estuary around the old city of Panyu, which became a provincial capital under the Han and the seat of Guang Prefecture in 226. By Tang times it was China's greatest seaport: a maritime trade office was set up in 661 and Arab and Persian merchants crowded the foreign quarter until their pirates sacked the city in 758; in 879 Huang Chao's rebel army slaughtered much of that community. The Southern Han made it their capital from 917 to 971, and under the Song and Yuan the port traded with fifty and more countries. The early Ming reversed this with the sea bans: the maritime trade offices were closed in 1384, and only tribute embassies might lawfully trade, leaving Canton the one port still open to most foreigners. In 1380 the marquis Zhu Liangzu rebuilt the walls across Yuexiu Hill and raised the five-storey Zhenhai Tower above them. In 1444 the city was still the rich emporium of the south, handling Southeast Asian spices and incense under the eye of Ming officials.

The Portuguese reached it in 1516-1517, but were defeated at Tunmen in 1521 and Xicao Bay in 1522; only the accord of 1554 regularized their trade, and from 1557 they warehoused goods at nearby Macau. When the sea ban was lifted in 1567 the port surged again, and by the Wanli reign the merchant houses of the Thirteen Hongs handled foreign commerce. The Ming-Qing transition struck hard: the Shaowu Emperor was enthroned at Canton in December 1646 and executed when Li Chengdong stormed the city the next month, and on 24 November 1650 Shang Kexi's Qing army broke in and killed tens of thousands in the sack remembered as the Gengyin calamity. Canton then became the fief of the Shang princes until the Three Feudatories revolt, in which the Zhenhai Tower burned; it was rebuilt in 1687. After Taiwan fell in 1683 the European East India companies returned - British, Dutch, French, Danish and Swedish - and in 1757 the Qianlong Emperor confined all European trade to Canton. For two generations the Cohong merchants made it the world's emporium of tea and porcelain; the first American ship, the Empress of China, reached the roadstead in 1784.
zh:
广州（英文称Canton）位于珠江口内，城基是秦汉时的番禺。汉代番禺成为岭南都会，公元226年成为广州治所，城市由此得名。唐代广州已是中国第一大港：661年唐廷在此设市舶使，阿拉伯、波斯商人聚居蕃坊，直到758年大食、波斯海盗洗劫城池；879年黄巢军攻破广州，蕃商惨遭屠戮。917年至971年这里是南汉国都兴王府，宋、元两代重开市舶司，与广州通商的国家有五十余国。明初一反宋元旧制实行海禁，1384年罢撤市舶机构，只准朝贡使团合法贸易，广州成为对大多数国家唯一开放的港口。1380年永嘉侯朱亮祖扩建城墙、跨越秀山筑城，并在城头建起五层镇海楼。1444年的广州仍是岭南最富庶的港城，在明朝官员的管束下吞吐南洋的香料与熏香。

葡萄牙人在1516年至1517年间首抵广州，却在1521年屯门海战和次年西草湾之战中被明军击退；直到1554年双方议定通商，葡人从1557年起得以在邻近的澳门屯放货物。1567年隆庆开关后港口重新繁盛，万历年间代理外商贸易的「十三行」已经出现。明清易代给广州重创：1646年12月绍武帝在此仓促登基，次年初李成栋破城，绍武被俘遇害；1650年11月24日尚可喜的清军攻陷广州，大肆屠城，史称庚寅之劫，广州此后成为平南王尚氏的封藩，直到三藩之乱中尚之信败亡——镇海楼也毁于这场战乱，1687年重修。1683年台湾平定后，英国、荷兰、法国、丹麦、瑞典的东印度公司船只相继到来，1757年乾隆帝下令西洋商船只准在广州一口通商，十三行垄断了中西贸易，使广州成为全世界的茶叶和瓷器集散地；1784年，第一艘美国商船「中国皇后号」驶抵黄埔。

en:
Macau, then called Haojing, the Oyster Mirror bay, was a scatter of fishing coves on the south-eastern tip of the Xiangshan peninsula, joined to the mainland only by the narrow Lotus Stem sandbar. Part of Xiangshan County since the Southern Song, its Tanka boat-dwellers and Hakka villagers lived by fishing and salt. The early Ming sea bans kept the coast otherwise empty of shipping, and in 1444 there was no town here, only an anchorage where the tides ran between the islands later called Taipa.

After their defeat at Tunmen in 1521 the Portuguese felt their way along the estuary until 1553, when, pleading the need to dry storm-soaked goods, they bribed the coast intendant Wang Bai for leave to land; in 1557 the Ming posted a guard officer over the settlement and accepted an annual rent, fixed from 1571 at five hundred taels of silver. They named the place Macau after A-Ma Gao, the bay of the sea goddess Mazu. It became the first European town on Chinese soil: the diocese was erected in 1576, the municipal council in 1583, and the Jesuit College of St Paul, founded in 1594, was the first Western college in the Far East, training missionaries for China and Japan while the carracks carried Chinese silk to Nagasaki and Manila and the population rose from some 5,000 in 1563 to 20,000 by 1580. The Monte fort was built from 1617 to 1626, and in June 1622 a Dutch fleet of seventeen ships under Reijersen was beaten back from its beaches. Japan's closure in 1639 and the loss of Malacca in 1641 broke that trade. Under the early Qing sea bans foreign commerce was all but confined to Macau, and in 1685 the new Guangzhou customs took the anchorage under its charge; a Qing subprefect was stationed there in 1744, and after 1757 every European ship had to report at Macau before proceeding to Canton. In the later eighteenth century the peninsula lived on as the gateway of the Canton trade, increasingly as the staging point for the opium carried up to Whampoa.
zh:
澳门旧称濠镜澳，是香山县东南端一串傍海的渔村，半岛与大陆之间只靠一道名叫莲花茎的狭长沙堤相连。南宋以来此地属香山县，居民以蜑家和客家人为主，靠捕鱼、煮盐过活。明初厉行海禁，沿岸几无商船停泊，1444年时这里还没有城镇，只有一处潮汐往来的避风锚地，隔着十字门水域望见日后被称作氹仔的岛屿。

1521年屯门海战失利后，葡萄牙人沿着珠江口一路摸索落脚点。1553年，他们以晾晒被水浸湿的货物为由贿赂广东海道副使汪柏，获准在澳门半岛登岸暂住；1557年明朝设守澳官衙门加以管理，葡人每年缴纳白银五百两，这笔钱在1571年正式转为地租，他们又从当地海神妈祖的海湾得名「Macau」。澳门成为中国土地上第一座欧洲人城镇：1576年天主教教区成立，1583年议事会设立，1594年耶稣会创办圣保禄学院——远东第一所西式大学，为前往中国、日本传教培养教士；大帆船把中国丝绸运往长崎和马尼拉，半岛人口也从1563年的约五千增至1580年的两万。1617年至1626年耶稣会在山上筑起大炮台，1622年6月荷兰提督雷尔生率十七艘战船来攻，被炮台火力击退。好景不长：1639年日本锁国、1641年马六甲落入荷兰之手，旧日转口贸易一落千丈。清初海禁中对外贸易几乎只留澳门一处，1685年清廷设立粤海关，澳门关口归其管辖；1744年清廷专设澳门海防军民同知管束华夷，1757年一口通商后，所有欧洲商船更必须先到澳门报备，才能上驶广州。18世纪后期，这座小半岛作为广州贸易的外港延续下来，也日渐成为鸦片运往黄埔的中转地。

en:
Fuzhou commands the lower Min River, where river traffic from Fujian's inland valleys meets the sea. A walled settlement called Ye served as the capital of Minyue after Wuzhu was enfeoffed there in 202 BC; the Tang renamed the city Fuzhou in 725, and Wang Shenzhi later made it the capital of the Min kingdom. Under the Ming, walls were rebuilt in 1371, and Fuzhou remained the chief administrative city of Fujian. Its Changle anchorage supplied Zheng He's Indian Ocean voyages of 1405–1433, and local yards were famed for the broad ocean-going fu ships. In 1444 Fuzhou was therefore a Ming provincial capital with skilled sailors and close ties to Ryukyu, though private sea trade was hemmed in by maritime prohibitions.

In 1474 Fuzhou became the seat of the Fujian maritime trade office and received Ryukyu missions at the Rouyuan Hostel; the Ming also assigned it the licensed trade with the Philippines, sometimes sharing it with Quanzhou. During the Jiajing reign, pirate raids struck the prefecture repeatedly, and Qi Jiguang twice brought troops into Fujian to suppress the wokou. At the end of 1624 Giulio Aleni brought Catholic teaching to the city. In 1645 the Prince of Tang, Zhu Yujian, was enthroned there as the Longwu emperor and renamed Fuzhou Tianxing Fu, but Qing forces took it in 1646. Geng Jingzhong rebelled from Fuzhou in 1674–1676, and the coastal evacuation disrupted shoreline communities until the policy ended in 1684. Trade with Ryukyu and Japan then supported the city's growth through the eighteenth century.
zh:
福州扼守闽江下游，是福建内陆河谷通往海洋的门户。公元前202年无诸受封闽越王，以冶城为都；唐代在725年改置福州，王审知后来又以此为闽国都城。明代1371年重修城垣，福州长期是福建的行政中心。所辖长乐的太平港为1405年至1433年郑和下西洋船队的停泊和补给基地，当地船场也以适于远洋的福船闻名。因此到1444年，福州既是明朝的福建省城，聚居着熟悉琉球与南洋航路的水手，民间海上贸易又受到海禁约束。

1474年，福州成为福建市舶司驻地，琉球使团被安置在柔远驿；明朝还把对菲律宾的特许贸易交予福州，有时由泉州分沾。嘉靖年间倭寇多次寇掠福州府，戚继光两度率兵入闽平倭。1624年底，艾儒略将天主教传入福州。1645年，唐王朱聿键在福州称帝，建立隆武政权，升福州为天兴府，但清军在1646年攻占此地。1674年至1676年，耿精忠据福州起兵反清；清初迁界又使沿海社会遭到破坏，直到1684年政策结束。此后与琉球和日本的贸易支撑福州在18世纪继续发展。

en:
Ganzhou commands the upper Gan River, where the Zhang and Gong streams meet before flowing north through Poyang Lake to the Yangtze. A Han county was placed here in 201 CE, but Chinese settlement long clung to the river valleys; an earthen wall was raised in 349 and faced with brick in the Jiayou reign of the Northern Song. Known as Qianzhou from 589, the city took its present name in 1153, by when refugees from the fall of Kaifeng in 1126 had long been swelling the southern Jiangxi hills. West of the city the Meiling road, cut through the Dayu ranges in 716 for the Tang minister Zhang Jiuling, linked the Gan valley with the Beijiang and Guangzhou. In 1444 Ganzhou was the seat of a Ming prefecture, a staging town on the river-and-mountain road to Canton, set in a rice-rich hill country of Hakka speakers later called the cradle of the Hakka.

In 1495 the Ming created the grand coordinator of Nan-Gan, a special command over the lawless marches of Jiangxi, Guangdong, Fujian and Huguang. Its most famous holder, Wang Yangming, arrived in 1517, stormed the bandit strongholds at Hengshui and Tonggang in the Dayu mountains, and had Chongyi county founded to settle the pacified country; he died on a boat at Nan'an in 1529. By then the Meiling road was among China's busiest: in the late Ming 25,000 to 50,000 kilograms of silver crossed the pass each year, paying for Jingdezhen porcelain carried from the Gan to Canton, where Portuguese and Dutch ships loaded it for Europe, and in 1567 the pass's thirtieth-duty alone came to 43,000 taels. When the Ming collapsed, Ganzhou held for the Longwu emperor and was renamed Zhongcheng, the loyal prefecture, before it fell to the Qing in 1646. Hakka lineages in the hills built walled wei manors for defence, the Guanxi New Wei near Longnan being begun in 1798. In 1793 the Macartney embassy travelled the old post road south over the pass on its way to Canton.
zh:
赣州当赣江上游，章、贡二水在此汇合，北经鄱阳湖入长江。汉高祖时（前201年）已在此设县，但中原编户长期只局限在河谷之间；349年始筑土城，北宋嘉祐年间起以砖石包砌。589年置虔州，1153年改名赣州——1126年靖康之变后北人南迁，赣南山间的人口已渐稠密。城西南的大庾岭路为唐相张九龄于716年开凿，沿梅岭越过南岭，把赣江与广东北江、广州连成一条通道。1444年的赣州是明朝赣州府治、赣江—大庾岭通往广州商路上的中转重镇，周围稻作丰足的丘陵是客家人的主要聚居地，后世称之为「客家摇篮」。

1495年，明朝特设南赣巡抚，弹压江西、广东、福建、湖广四省交界的山区。最有名的一任是王阳明：他1517年到任，攻破大庾岭横水、桶冈诸寨，随即奏设崇义县安插新民，1529年病逝于南安府舟中。此时梅岭道已是天下最繁忙的商路之一：晚明每年约有2.5万至5万公斤白银从广州经梅关北运，换取景德镇瓷器；瓷器由赣江翻越大庾岭抵广州，再由葡萄牙、荷兰商船运往欧洲，1567年梅关按三十税一征得的关税即有4.3万两。明亡之际，赣州为南明隆武朝廷坚守，改名忠诚府，1646年被清军攻破。山间的客家大族筑起围屋自保，龙南的关西新围1798年动工。1793年，马戛尔尼使团沿这条旧驿道逾岭南下，前往广州。

en:
Changsha lies on the lower Xiang River, whose boats carried the produce of the Dongting basin toward the Yangtze. The Qin and Han made it a commandery and then a kingdom, and early in the tenth century Ma Yin made the city the capital of Southern Chu. In 976 the Yuelu Academy was founded at the foot of Yuelu Hill; the lectures of Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi later made it a center of Hunan learning. The Song-Yuan conquest devastated Tanzhou, but in 1372 the Ming renamed the city Changsha Prefecture under Huguang, improved its river trade and planted imperial princely courts in the city. In 1444 Changsha was a busy prefectural seat dealing in tea and the grain of the surrounding lake plain, while the Yuelu Academy, ruined in the Mongol wars, still awaited its late-fifteenth-century revival.

By the late Ming, Changsha was counted among China's four great tea markets, and the young Wang Fuzhi studied at Yuelu before the dynastic collapse. In 1664 the Qing made Changsha the seat of the Huguang Right administration, preparing its future as the capital of Hunan. Wu Sangui's rebellion began in December 1673, and in 1674 his generals poured into Hunan; the provincial governor Lu Zhen abandoned Changsha, which then remained under rebel power for several years. Qing forces recovered Liuyang and Pingjiang in 1677, secured the Xiangtan naval command, and in early 1679 retook Yuezhou, Changde, Hengzhou and Changsha. Hunan became a separate provincial administration under the Yongzheng Emperor in 1723–1724. During the following century Changsha's riverfront grew into one of China's great rice markets, as Huai salt arrived from the lower Yangtze and Hunan rice was freighted back in its place.
zh:
长沙位于湘江下游，湘江船队把洞庭湖区的物产运往长江。秦汉时这里先后为长沙郡、长沙国，10世纪初马殷又以长沙为南楚都城。976年，岳麓书院在岳麓山下创立，朱熹与张栻的会讲后来使这里成为湖湘学术中心。宋元易代使潭州遭到重创，但明代在1372年改置长沙府，隶属湖广，整治河道通商，并在城中安置藩王。1444年的长沙已是繁忙的府城，经营茶叶和周围湖平原告饶的粮食；岳麓书院在蒙元战乱中毁坏，还要到15世纪后期才在明代复兴。

到明代后期，长沙已被列为中国四大茶市之一，青年王夫之也曾在岳麓书院求学。1664年，清朝以长沙为湖广右布政使驻地，为其后来成为湖南省会奠定基础。1673年12月吴三桂起兵，1674年其部将攻入湖南，湖南巡抚卢震放弃长沙，城池此后数年间处于吴军势力之下。1677年，清军收复浏阳、平江，争取湘潭吴军水师主将归附；1679年初，又连克岳州、常德、衡州和长沙。1723年至1724年，湖南在雍正初政下成为独立省级行政区，长沙定为省治。此后一个世纪里，长沙沿江街市发展为中国重要米市，淮盐自长江下游而来，湖南稻米又随回程船流通各地。

en:
Wuling, the country around modern Changde, lies where the Yuan and Li rivers leave the Wuling Mountains for the marshes of Dongting - 'the throat of Sichuan and Guizhou', as the old tag has it. The Ming kept Changde Prefecture here, seated at Wuling city, and the mountain trade from Guizhou passed down the Yuan River to the Yangtze. Beyond the plain the Wuling ranges were governed by native chieftains, above all the Peng lords of Yongshun and Baojing, whose Tujia followers held the hills. In 1444 the prefectural city lived by this traffic between the river world and the tribal mountains.

In 1508 an imperial prince was planted here when Zhu Youshu, the Prince of Rong, took up his fief at Changde. The hills' soldiery won their moment of fame in 1555, when the young Yongshun chieftain Peng Yinan led 3,000 Tujia troops to the coast and helped destroy a pirate host at the battle of Wangjiangjing. Wuling itself produced Yang Sichang, the grand secretary commanding the late-Ming anti-rebel campaigns, who died in 1641 after Zhang Xianzhong killed the Prince of Xiang. When Zhang's army swept Hunan in 1643, the last Prince of Rong fled with his mother up the Yuan to Chenxi and was never heard of again. Wu Sangui's rebels overran the country in 1674, and the Peng chieftains sent troops against them, fighting at the Chenlong Pass; between 1727 and 1729 the Yongzheng court ended the eight-century-old chieftaincies and set up Yongshun and Baojing counties under regular officials.
zh:
武陵即今常德一带，是沅、澧二水出武陵山脉、注入洞庭湖沼地的地方，旧有「川黔咽喉」之称。明代在此设常德府，治武陵县，贵州方向的山货顺沅水而下，经此通往长江。平原以西的群山由土官管辖，以永顺、保靖的彭氏土司势力最大，其土民多为土家族。1444年的常德城，就夹在这条水道与土官山地之间，靠中转贸易为生。

1508年荣王朱祐枢就藩常德，这里成为亲王封国。山地土兵在1555年名动一时：年轻的永顺宣慰使彭翼南率三千土兵奉调东南，在王江泾之战中会同各路狼兵土兵大破倭寇。武陵本地走出了督师镇压民变的阁臣杨嗣昌，1641年张献忠焚杀襄王后，他忧悸而死。1643年张献忠席卷湖南，末代荣王朱慈炤奉母沿沅水逃到辰溪，不知所终。1674年吴三桂叛军据有湖南，彭氏土司出兵助清，参加了攻克辰龙关的战斗；1727年至1729年雍正改土归流，彭氏八百年的土司统治告终，其地设永顺、保靖各县，由流官治理。

en:
Zhenyuan guards a walled town on the old road from Hunan into the Yunnan-Guizhou plateau, country originally held by Dong and Miao peoples. The Southern Song set up the Zhenyuan Border Stream Defense Commission there; the Yuan reorganized it as the Zhenyuan Military and Civilian Prefecture and placed Anyi County at its seat. Ming forces built both civilian and garrison offices in the Hongwu reign, and Zhenyuan Prefecture was restored in 1413. In 1438 the nearby Zhenyuan and Shibing native chief commissions were placed under it. In 1444, prefecture and garrison shared the same town, which served as a military gateway into the Miao hills.

After the prefecture was briefly reduced to a subprefecture in 1491 and then restored, Zhenyuan County was established under it in 1498. During Wu Sangui's revolt in 1673, Gan Wenkun, governor-general of Yun-Gui, failed to hold Guiyang and fell back on Zhenyuan, where he was besieged and killed. The Qing later kept a regional military commander stationed in the prefectural town. When Shi Liudeng launched the great Miao rising in north-eastern Guizhou in 1795, Miao communities in Zhenyuan's Forty-eight Streams took up arms, and armies from seven provinces were mobilized before the rising was broken.
zh:
镇远扼守从湖南进入云贵高原的古道，是一座依山临江的军事城镇，本地原有侗族、苗族聚居。南宋始设镇远沿边溪洞招讨使司，元代改为镇远军民府，并在府城设安夷县。明洪武年间，朝廷在此同时布设民政衙门和军卫，永乐十一年（1413年）复置镇远府，正统三年（1438年）又将近旁的镇远、施秉长官司划归府属。1444年的镇远府、卫同城，是明军进入苗疆的门户。

弘治四年（1491年）镇远府一度降为镇远州，随后恢复；弘治十一年（1498年）改设镇远县，隶属镇远府。1673年吴三桂起兵反叛，云贵总督甘文焜在贵阳不能据守，退至镇远后被围身亡。清代仍以镇远府为黔东重镇，派总兵驻守。1795年石柳邓在黔东北发动苗民起事，镇远四十八溪地方的苗民纷纷响应；清廷从七省调集大军围剿，才将这场起事镇压下去。

en:
Guiyang lies in a mountain basin on the Nanming River, at the centre of Guizhou. The Tang established Juzhou there in 621, and under the Yuan the town was called Shunyuan; in 1292 the Eight Fan and Shunyuan pacification headquarters and military marshals' office was placed within its walls. When Guizhou became a province in 1413, the provincial administration commission was seated in this city, then still called Guizhou. Military guards and civilian offices shared the town, while the surrounding hills remained under Yi, Miao and Bouyei chiefs. In 1444 Guiyang was thus a Ming provincial capital barely thirty years old, a garrison outpost on the routes into Shui-Xi and the Miao country rather than an old interior metropolis.

In 1568 the Ming moved Chengfan Prefecture into the city, and in 1569 renamed it Guiyang Prefecture, giving the town the name it has kept. Xingui County was attached to it in 1586, and in 1597 Jiang Dongzhi, governor of Guizhou, built Jiaxiu Pavilion on the Aoji reef in the Nanming River, its name invoking literary success. The prefecture became the Guiyang Military and Civilian Prefecture in 1601. In the second month of 1622, the Yi rising led by She Chongming and An Bangyan reached Guiyang and some 100,000 rebels besieged the city for more than ten months; when Wang Sanshan's relief army arrived in spring 1623, famine had devastated the inhabitants. The Qing stationed the governor of Guizhou here in 1659, moved the Yun-Gui governor-general to Guiyang in 1666, and in 1687 set up Guizhu County on the lands of the Guizhou guards and changed the military prefecture back to Guiyang Prefecture.
zh:
贵阳地处贵州中部的南明河山间盆地。唐武德四年（621年）置矩州，元代称顺元城；至元二十九年（1292年），八番顺元宣慰司都元帅府设于城中。永乐十一年（1413年），贵州等处承宣布政使司设在当时仍称贵州城的贵阳，贵州成为明朝第十三个行省。卫所与民政衙门同城而治，周围山地则分属彝族、苗族和布依族土司。1444年的贵阳是设立仅三十余年的明代行省会城，也是一座扼守水西与苗疆通道的军镇，而不是历史悠久的内地大都市。

隆庆二年（1568年），程番府移入贵州城；次年改称贵阳府，贵阳由此成为行政名称。万历十四年（1586年）设新贵县，万历二十六年（1597年）贵州巡抚江东之在南明河鳌矶石上筑堤建甲秀楼，取「科甲挺秀」之意。万历二十九年（1601年），贵阳府升为贵阳军民府。天启二年（1622年）二月，奢崇明、安邦彦领导的彝族起事波及贵阳，十万叛军围城逾十月；天启三年（1623年）春王三善率援军解围时，城中已因饥荒残破。清顺治十六年（1659年）设贵州巡抚，驻贵阳军民府；康熙五年（1666年）移云贵总督驻贵阳；康熙二十六年（1687年）以贵州卫、贵州前卫地置贵筑县，并改贵阳军民府为贵阳府。

en:
The Wumeng country occupies the Wumeng Mountains at the meeting of Yunnan, Guizhou and Sichuan, above the gorges of the Jinsha and Niulan rivers. The old Five-Foot Road through these hills linked the Sichuan basin with Yunnan, and under the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms the area was the Wumeng tribe's land. The Yuan created Wumeng Route in 1278. In 1381 Fu Youde, Lan Yu and Mu Ying led the Ming army into northeastern Yunnan, and the next year the dynasty established the Wumeng Military-Civilian Prefecture under Sichuan. In 1444 Wumeng remained a Yi tusi chiefship on the Ming frontier, governed through hereditary rulers rather than ordinary county officials.

Direct Qing rule came only in the 1720s. Ortai, the official directing the southwestern tusi reforms, transferred Wumeng to Yunnan in 1727 and began replacing hereditary chiefs with appointed officials. Exactions by garrison commander Liu Qiyuan helped provoke a rising under Lu Wanfu, in which Liu and several local officials were killed; Ortai suppressed it with troops from Yunnan, Guizhou and Sichuan. In 1728 the Qing set up En'an and Yongshan counties, and in 1731 Wumeng Prefecture was renamed Zhaotong, with its seat moved to En'an, the future core of Zhaotong city.
zh:
乌蒙地处乌蒙山区，位于云南、贵州、四川三地交会处，金沙江与牛栏江在群山中切出深峡。汉代开凿的五尺道经过这里，把四川盆地与云南连接起来；南诏、大理时期，这里是乌蒙部之地。元朝于1278年置乌蒙路。1381年，傅友德、蓝玉、沐英率明军进入滇东北，次年设立乌蒙军民府，改隶四川。1444年的乌蒙仍是明朝边地上的彝族土司，由世袭首领治理，而非普通州县官吏。

清朝的直接统治到1720年代才到来。主持西南改土归流的鄂尔泰于1727年将乌蒙府划归云南，随后以流官取代世袭土司。总兵刘起元的贪暴激起禄万福叛乱，刘起元和数名地方官被杀；鄂尔泰调集云南、贵州、四川三省兵力将其镇压。1728年，清廷设恩安县和永善县；1731年改乌蒙府为昭通府，府治移驻恩安，即后来的昭通城。

en:
Shigatse, long known in Tibetan as Samdrubtsé, stands where the Nyang River meets the Yarlung Tsangpo, on the road from Lhasa into western Tsang. The old settlement of Nyangmé took urban shape under Sakya rule in the eleventh century, and early Phagmodrupa rulers built it up in the fourteenth century as Samdrubtsé dzong. By 1444 the Rinpungpa, formerly Phagmodrupa governors in the Rinpung valley, had become the real power in Tsang. Their lord Norbu Zangpo balanced between the fading Phagmodrupa court and the region's Sakya and Gelug monasteries.

In 1447 Gendun Drup, a disciple of Tsongkhapa later counted as the First Dalai Lama, founded Tashi Lhunpo below the town's Sun Hill with support from local nobles. Norbu Zangpo did not block the work, and the monastery grew into the first major Gelug house in Tsang. The Shigatse governor's revolt of 1565 broke Rinpungpa power and opened the Tsangpa period; in 1618 the Tsangpa made the town their capital after defeating Gelug forces and bringing most of Ü-Tsang under their rule. In 1642 Güshi Khan's Mongol army took Shigatse and ended Tsangpa rule, then granted wide lands around the town to the Fourth Panchen Lama, Lobsang Chökyi Gyaltsen, making Tashi Lhunpo the Panchen Lamas' seat. The Kangxi Emperor recognized the Fifth Panchen Lama as Panchen Erdeni in 1713. A dispute over the Sixth Panchen Lama's estate after his death in Beijing in 1780 helped draw Gorkha armies into Tsang; they sacked Tashi Lhunpo in 1791 and returned the plunder after surrendering the next year.
zh:
日喀则旧称溪卡桑珠孜，简称桑珠孜，位于年楚河与雅鲁藏布江汇流处，扼守从拉萨进入后藏西部的道路。11世纪萨迦王朝时期，年麦一带已有城镇雏形；14世纪初，帕木竹巴在此建城，称溪卡桑珠孜。到1444年，原任帕竹臣属的仁蚌巴已成为后藏实际统治者，诺布桑波借帕竹内乱扩张权力，在萨迦、格鲁各派寺院与衰弱的帕竹宫廷之间维持自己的势力。

1447年，宗喀巴弟子根敦珠巴——后来被追认为一世达赖喇嘛——在当地贵族资助下，于日光山南麓创建扎什伦布寺；诺布桑波没有阻止工程，这座格鲁派在后藏的第一座大寺历时十二年建成。1565年，日喀则宗本起兵反对仁蚌巴，开启藏巴汗时期；1618年，藏巴汗在击败格鲁派联军后以日喀则为都，控制卫藏大部。1642年，固始汗的蒙古军队攻下日喀则，终结藏巴汗政权，并把日喀则周围大片土地划归四世班禅罗桑曲结，扎什伦布寺从此成为历代班禅驻锡地。1713年，康熙帝册封五世班禅为班禅额尔德尼。1780年六世班禅在北京圆寂后，遗产纠纷成为廓尔喀侵藏的诱因之一；廓尔喀军队1791年洗劫扎什伦布寺，次年请降并归还财物。

en:
Lhasa stands on the banks of the Lhasa River in a high valley of the Tibetan plateau. Songtsen Gampo moved his capital here in the seventh century and built the Jokhang to house the Jowo image brought by his Chinese bride, and pilgrims have circled that temple ever since; after the fall of the Tibetan kings the city became a religious shrine without a throne, ruled from elsewhere. The fifteenth century brought new life: Tsongkhapa founded Ganden in 1409, and his disciples built Drepung in 1416 and Sera in 1419, so that Lhasa was girdled by the three great Gelug monasteries. In 1444 the city still owed allegiance to the Phagmodrupa gongma at Nedong, Drakpa Jungne, though his house had never recovered from the strife of 1434 and the Rinpung lords were rising in Tsang; Lhasa itself was a town of pilgrims, monks and the Jokhang rather than a seat of government.

In 1642 the Qoshot Güshi Khan overthrew the Tsangpa dynasty and handed power to the Fifth Dalai Lama, who moved his Ganden Phodrang administration to Lhasa; work on the Potala began on Red Hill in 1645, the White Palace was finished in 1648 and the Red Palace in 1690–1694, and the Barkhor around the Jokhang became a market thronged with Mongol, Chinese, Kashmiri and Nepali merchants. The Jesuit Ippolito Desideri saw it in 1716, when musk, gold and yak tails left for tea, turquoise and coral. In 1717 the Dzungars sacked the city and killed Lhazang Khan, but a Qing army expelled them in 1720 and installed the Seventh Dalai Lama, and ambans were stationed at Lhasa. The riot of 11 November 1750 left both ambans dead, and the Qianlong Emperor answered it in 1751 by establishing the Kashag council. After the Gurkha war the Twenty-Nine Articles of 1793 placed the garrison and the Golden Urn for reincarnations under amban supervision. In 1821 Lhasa was the fixed capital of the Dalai Lamas under Qing protection.
zh:
拉萨坐落在青藏高原一处高峻的河谷中，拉萨河畔。7世纪时松赞干布迁都于此，为迎娶文成公主所携的觉卧佛像修建大昭寺，从此转经的信众绕寺不绝；吐蕃王权崩溃之后，这里成了没有王座的圣地，政权中心一直在别处。15世纪它重获生机：宗喀巴1409年创建甘丹寺，弟子们又于1416年、1419年建起哲蚌寺和色拉寺，拉萨由此被格鲁派三大寺环绕。1444年，城市仍在名义上臣服于乃东的帕木竹巴贡玛札巴迥乃，但这一家族自1434年内乱后元气大伤，仁蚌巴的首领正在后藏崛起；此时的拉萨与其说是政都，不如说是香客、僧人与大昭寺的城市。

1642年，和硕特的固始汗推翻藏巴汗王朝，把权力交给第五世达赖喇嘛，达赖喇嘛将甘丹颇章政权移驻拉萨；1645年红山上开始重建布达拉宫，白宫1648年落成，红宫1690至1694年建成，大昭寺周围的八廓街也成为蒙古、汉地、克什米尔和尼泊尔商人云集的市场。耶稣会士德西德里1716年到此，见到麝香、黄金和牛尾在此换走茶叶、绿松石和珊瑚。1717年准噶尔人洗劫拉萨、杀死拉藏汗，1720年清军将其逐出，册立第七世达赖喇嘛，并在拉萨设置驻藏大臣。1750年11月11日的暴乱中两名大臣被杀，乾隆帝遂于1751年设立噶厦。廓尔喀之役后，1793年的《钦定藏内善后章程二十九条》把驻军与认定转世的金瓶掣签置于驻藏大臣监督之下。1821年的拉萨，已是清朝庇护下达赖喇嘛们稳固的都城。

en:
Dartsedo, recorded in Chinese as Dajianlu or Tachienlu, is wedged into a steep valley over 8,000 feet high, where the road from Chengdu enters the Tibetan country of Kham. It was the seat of the kings of Chakla, called Chala in Chinese records, whose line the Yuan confirmed as native chieftains. In 1407 the local chief Ngawang Gyaltsen submitted to the Ming and received from the Yongle Emperor a bronze seal as Pacification Commissioner of Changhexi, Yutong and Ningyuan. Porters and caravans carried brick tea up the mountain trails from Ya'an and Chengdu to exchange here for Tibetan wool, horses and medicinal herbs. In 1444 the small walled town was already the busiest market on the Sino-Tibetan frontier, the chief mart of the tea-and-horse trade.

During the Tianqi reign of 1621–1627 the armies of Lijiang swept through much of Kham but were driven back from Chakla, and in 1643 the kingdom submitted to the rising Qing. In 1700 the Lhasa-appointed commissioner at Dartsedo, leaning on Khoshut Mongol power, murdered the Chakla king and seized the town; on 28 January 1701 a Qing army stormed Dartsedo and restored the tusi under imperial supervision. In 1725 the Qing reorganised the Kham frontier and removed Chakla from Lhasa's rule, and in 1730 they established the Dajianlu subprefecture. On 1 June 1786 an earthquake of magnitude 7.75 levelled the town, so that, in the Sichuan governor's report, not one merlon of its walls was left standing, while a landslide dammed the Dadu River and its later burst devastated the valley below. The tea market was rebuilt and remained the town's livelihood.
zh:
打箭炉，藏语称达折多，夹在海拔八千多英尺的深山峡谷中，是成都方向的道路进入康地藏区的门户。这里是察拉（Chakla，汉文史书作明正土司）王国的治所，元代便册封当地首领为土官。1407年（永乐五年），长河西土酋阿旺坚参内附，受封长河西鱼通宁远宣慰使，获赐铜印。背夫和马帮把雅州、成都的砖茶沿山路背来，在此换取藏地的羊毛、马匹和药材。1444年的打箭炉已是汉藏边地上最热闹的市集，茶马互市的首要商埠。

天启年间（1621—1627年），丽江土司的军队横扫康区大部，却在察拉被击退；1643年（崇祯十六年），明正土司归附新兴的清朝。1700年（康熙三十九年），驻打箭炉营官昌侧集烈借和硕特蒙古之势攻杀土司蛇蜡喳吧、占据地方，1701年1月28日清军攻破打箭炉，在朝廷监督下恢复土司统治。1725年清朝整顿康区边务，将察拉划出拉萨管辖，1730年（雍正八年）置打箭炉厅。1786年6月1日发生7.75级大地震，全城尽毁，四川总督的奏报称城垣全行倒塌、不存一雉；山崩又壅塞大渡河，日后坝溃，下游河谷漂没甚众。茶市事后重建，依旧是这座小城的生计所系。

en:
Chengdu sits on the irrigated Chengdu Plain, whose wealth was secured after Li Bing built the Dujiangyan waterworks in the third century BC. Qin conquered Shu in 316 BC, and Zhang Yi laid out a walled city five years later. Under the Han a brocade office supervised the district's most famous tribute, giving Chengdu the name Brocade City. It was capital of Shu Han, then of the Former Shu and Later Shu kingdoms, and under the Tang was ranked with Yangzhou as one of the richest cities in China. Song Chengdu saw the early jiaozi paper money in 1021 and supplied large quantities of Shu brocade to the court. Mongol armies twice sacked the city before the Yuan made it the seat of Sichuan. Ming Yuzhen's Xia regime seized the basin in 1363 from its capital at Chongqing, and after the Ming conquest of 1371 Chengdu became Sichuan's provincial seat; Zhu Chun, the Prince of Shu, was enfeoffed there with a new palace. In 1444 it was thus the political and mercantile centre of the southwest, rich in silk and grain.

In 1621 the Yi leader She Chongming rebelled while Ming forces were occupied with the Later Jin, killed the provincial governor Xu Keqiu, and besieged Chengdu for 102 days. A greater catastrophe followed when Zhang Xianzhong's army entered Chengdu in 1644 and he proclaimed the Great Western kingdom, calling the city Xijing. In 1646 Chengdu was burned in the fighting and became badly depopulated; for years Qing provincial administration was sheltered at Langzhou, while the Three Feudatories' revolt of 1673 carried renewed war into Sichuan. The Qing then promoted the migration known as filling Sichuan from Huguang, settled soldiers and farmers on abandoned land, and returned the provincial government to Chengdu with a governor-general and Chengdu general. By the eighteenth century it again produced grain, silk and tobacco, and Chengdu recovered as the chief city of southwest China.
zh:
成都位于都江堰灌溉的成都平原。公元前256年李冰主持修建都江堰，使这片平原获得持久丰饶。公元前316年秦灭蜀，五年后张仪按咸阳规制筑起成都城。汉代设锦官管理蜀锦，成都因此又称「锦官城」。它先后做过蜀汉、前蜀和后蜀的都城；唐代商贸繁盛，时称「扬一益二」，地位可与扬州比肩。宋代成都在1021年出现早期纸币「交子」，蜀锦也大量上供朝廷。蒙古军两次攻破成都后，元朝在此设立四川等处行中书省。1363年明玉珍建立大夏、据有四川，但以重庆为都；1371年明军平定大夏后，成都成为四川承宣布政使司治所，明太祖第十一子朱椿受封蜀王，并在旧子城一带新建蜀王府。1444年的成都既是四川省会和藩王驻地，也是西南依托丝、粮而兴的商业中心。

1621年，奢崇明趁明朝与后金交战起兵反明，杀死巡抚徐可求，并从十月起围攻成都102天。更大的灾难在明末到来：1644年张献忠率军攻入成都，自立为帝，建立大西，改成都为西京。1646年，成都在战火中被焚毁，人口凋敝；清朝的四川布政使司一度迁往保宁府阆中，1673年三藩之乱又把战火烧回四川。此后清廷推行「湖广填四川」，招募兵民垦殖弃地，并将省会迁回成都，另设四川总督与成都将军驻防。到18世纪，成都平原重新出产粮食、生丝和烟草，成都也恢复为中国西南首要都会。

en:
Chongqing commands the meeting of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers. The ancient Ba people had centres at Zhi, Jiangzhou and Dianjiang in this region, and after Qin conquered Ba in 316 BC Zhang Yi stationed troops at Jiangzhou and built a fortress beside the Chaotianmen crossing. The Sui renamed the town Yu Prefecture in 581, the source of Chongqing's abbreviation Yu. In 1189 the newly enthroned Emperor Guangzong promoted Gong Prefecture to Chongqing Fu, the double celebration that gave the city its name. When Mongol forces took Chengdu in 1261, the Song prefect Peng Daya enlarged Chongzhou's walls down to the Jialing, fixing the outline later inherited by the Ming and Qing city. Ming Yuzhen entered Sichuan through the Wu Gorge and made Chongqing the capital of his Daxia kingdom in 1363; his young son Ming Sheng surrendered to the Ming in 1371. In that same year the Chongqing guard commander Dai Ding rebuilt the walls with seventeen gates, nine open and eight closed. In 1444 the city was a heavily garrisoned river hub linking Sichuan with the middle Yangtze.

In 1621 the Yongning tusi leader She Chongming rebelled and made Chongqing the capital of his short-lived Daliang regime before his forces besieged Chengdu for 102 days; he was not finally killed until 1629. Zhang Xianzhong's army captured Chongqing in 1644 amid the Ming collapse, and war, massacre and flight emptied much of eastern Sichuan. Qing conquest was followed by the further fighting of the Three Feudatories' revolt after 1673, after which the state-sponsored migration known as filling Sichuan from Huguang brought farmers, boatmen and merchants back to the river city. During the Ming and Qing, Ciqikou on the lower Jialing was a busy porcelain wharf and market town. By the early nineteenth century Chongqing was again the chief transshipment point between Sichuan's basin and the Yangtze gorges, though it had not yet been opened as a treaty port.
zh:
重庆扼守长江与嘉陵江交汇处。古代巴国曾在这一带的枳、江州、垫江建都；公元前316年秦灭巴后，张仪屯兵江州，在朝天门一带筑城，这是史籍所见重庆建城之始。581年隋代因嘉陵江古称渝水而改楚州为渝州，重庆简称「渝」由此而来。1189年，宋光宗由恭王入继皇位，取「双重喜庆」之意升恭州为重庆府。1261年蒙古军攻破成都后，南宋重庆知府彭大雅拓修城垣，北抵嘉陵江，西至临江门、通远门一线，奠定了明清重庆城的基本轮廓。明玉珍后来率天完红巾军由巫峡入蜀，1363年在重庆称帝，建立大夏；其子明昇于1371年向明朝投降。同年，重庆卫指挥使戴鼎修筑城垣，设九开八闭共十七座城门。1444年的重庆，已是连接四川盆地与长江中游的重兵河港。

1621年，永宁宣抚使奢崇明起兵反明，在重庆建立短暂的大梁政权，随后发兵围攻成都102天；战事持续多年，他本人到1629年才败死。1644年明朝崩溃之际，张献忠军攻占重庆，战乱、屠杀和逃亡使川东大片地区人口凋敝。清朝取得四川后，1673年三藩之乱又把战火烧回这一带；战后清廷推行「湖广填四川」，招募农民、船工和商人重新充实江城。明清时期，嘉陵江下游的磁器口既是瓷器产地，也是繁忙的码头市镇。到19世纪初，重庆再度成为四川盆地与长江三峡之间最重要的货物转运港，只是此时尚未开为通商口岸。

en:
Yichang, the Ming subprefecture of Yiling, sits at the mouth of the Xiling Gorge, where the Yangtze leaves the last of the Three Gorges for the Jianghan plain. Boats to and from Sichuan were hauled through its whirlpools by trackers and changed crews at its wharves, making the town the gate between the river's upper and middle reaches. The Ming made Yiling a subprefecture under Jingzhou in 1376. In 1444 it was a small walled town of boatmen, porters and fishermen, overshadowed by its prosperous downstream neighbour Jingzhou.

The Ming-Qing wars made a fortress of its western hills. Ming loyalists of the Kuidong camps held the Sichuan-Hubei border mountains, and Li Laiheng entrenched himself on Maolu Mountain above Xingshan. A Qing army of 200,000 moved against them in 1662; by 1664 only Li held out, and when the siege exhausted his supplies he slew the envoy sent to recruit him, saw his old mother to safety, and burned himself to death with his wife and children, the last Ming force on the mainland perishing with him. The Qing changed Yiling's written name in 1648 and, after bringing the native chieftaincies of the western hills under regular rule in 1735, raised the town to Yichang Prefecture, with newly founded Hefeng placed under it. White Lotus sects rose in these same border hills in 1796, and the nine-year war of 1796-1804 scorched the gorges before it was put down.
zh:
宜昌即明代的夷陵州，地处西陵峡口，长江在此出三峡最后一峡、进入江汉平原。出入四川的船只须由纤夫拉过险滩，在此更换舟夫，夷陵因此扼守长江上游与中游之间的门户。1376年明朝在此设夷陵州，隶属荆州府。1444年的夷陵只是一座船夫、脚夫和渔夫聚居的小城，声势远不及下游富庶的荆州。

明清易代之际，夷陵以西的群山成了坚守之地。号称夔东十三家的明军余部据守川鄂边境山地，李来亨在兴山茅麓山筑寨相持。1662年清廷发兵二十万围剿，至1664年只剩李来亨一部；寨中粮尽，他处死前来招降的清使，遣走老母，与妻子全家举火自焚，南明在大陆的最后一支武装随之覆灭。1648年清廷改夷陵为彝陵；1735年西山改土归流、废容美土司设鹤峰州，升彝陵州为宜昌府。1796年白莲教在川鄂边境山区起事，历时九年的川楚教乱殃及三峡一带，至1804年才告平定。

en:
Wuchang and Hanyang face each other where the Han River enters the Yangtze. Hanyang was already a river port under the Han, walls were raised there in 206 and at Wuchang in 223, when the Yellow Crane Tower was built on the southern bank. Tang poets made that tower and the Yangtze crossing famous across China. Under the Yuan, Wuchang became the administrative seat of Huguang. In 1370 the Ming created the Chu princedom for Zhu Zhen, the Hongwu Emperor's sixth son, and his princely court joined the provincial offices in the city. In 1444 Wuchang was thus the political center of Huguang, while older Hanyang faced it across the Yangtze; the marshy ground that would become Hankou had not yet grown into a great market town.

During the Chenghua reign the Han shifted to a course north of Guishan, creating a sheltered anchorage from which Hankou rapidly grew. A local inspection office and five wards were established under the Jiajing emperor; the town had 1,281 houses in 1525 and 1,395 households by 1545. Under Wanli it became the chief transshipment point for Huguang tribute grain and Huai salt, which moved up the Yangtze and was redistributed through Hunan and Hubei. In 1635 a long dyke was built to protect Hankou's riverfront streets. In 1643 Zhang Xianzhong took Hanyang and Wuchang; Chu Prince Zhu Huakui was drowned in the Yangtze, and Zhang proclaimed himself King of the Great West before carrying his regime into Sichuan. Qing rule then opened Hankou's greatest age: a rice merchants' guild was founded in 1678, and merchants from Shanxi, Shaanxi, Huizhou and Jiangxi dealt in salt, rice, timber, cloth and medicines. By the eighteenth century Hankou was ranked among China's four great market towns, the commercial heart of the three cities.
zh:
武昌与汉阳隔长江相望，地处汉水入长江之处。汉阳在汉代已是沿江港口，206年筑城；武昌城垣起于223年，同年长江南岸建起黄鹤楼。唐代诗人的题咏使黄鹤楼和这处长江渡口闻名全国。元代，武昌成为湖广地区的行政中心。1370年，明太祖封第六子朱桢为楚王，楚王府与湖广布政使司同驻武昌，城池随之扩建。因此到1444年，武昌已是湖广的政治中枢，历史更久的汉阳隔江相辅；后来称为汉口的低洼江岸尚未发展成大商镇。

明成化年间，汉水改从龟山以北入江，在北岸形成风浪较小的停泊地，汉口由此迅速兴起。嘉靖年间设汉口巡检司和五坊；1525年镇上有房屋1281间，到1545年已有居民1395户。万历年间，汉口成为湖广漕粮与淮盐的转运枢纽，物资沿长江汇集，再分销湖南、湖北各地。1635年，当地修筑长堤保护沿江街市。1643年，张献忠攻破汉阳和武昌，楚王朱华奎被沉入长江，张献忠自称「大西王」，随后把势力带往四川。入清以后，汉口进入全盛：1678年米业公所建立，山西、陕西、徽州和江西商人在此经营盐、米、木材、棉布和药材。到18世纪，汉口已位列中国四大名镇，成为武汉三镇的商业心脏。

en:
Nanchang sits on the Gan River at the edge of the Poyang Lake plain, the natural hub of Jiangxi. Under the Han it became the seat of Yuzhang Commandery; as Hongzhou in Tang times it headed the Jiangxi circuit, famed for its shipyards and paper and for the Tengwang Pavilion, built in 653 and immortalised by Wang Bo's preface of 675. The Yuan made it capital of Jiangxi province. Zhu Yuanzhang's forces took the city in 1362, and after his defeat of Chen Youliang in the Poyang campaigns it became Nanchang Prefecture; in 1368 he feasted his commanders at the pavilion. In 1444 it was the seat of the Jiangxi provincial government and of Zhu Quan, the scholarly Prince of Ning, while the river road south carried Jiangxi paper and porcelain toward Canton.

In 1519 Zhu Chenhao, the fourth Prince of Ning, raised rebellion from his Nanchang mansion, but the Nangan grand coordinator Wang Shouren crushed it in forty-three days and the prince was taken on Poyang Lake; the Tengwang Pavilion burned in the fighting and was rebuilt in 1526. The Jesuit Matteo Ricci sojourned in Nanchang while seeking leave to enter Beijing, and under the Wanli emperor imperial clansmen were settled here until the imperial house made up a quarter of the city's people. In 1648, in the Ming-Qing wars, a Qing siege again put the pavilion to the torch; it was rebuilt in 1654, burned and restored again and again through the Kangxi reign, and rebuilt once more in 1789 under the Qianlong emperor.
zh:
南昌位于赣江下游、鄱阳湖平原之畔，是江西的枢纽。汉代在此设豫章郡治，唐代称洪州，为江南西道治所，造船、造纸之业兴盛；653年所建的滕王阁，因675年王勃一篇《滕王阁序》名扬天下。元代以南昌为江西行省省会。1362年朱元璋攻取南昌，在击败陈友谅的鄱阳湖水战后改置南昌府，1368年他在滕王阁大宴群臣。1444年的南昌是江西布政使司治所，也是宁王朱权的藩府所在，这位寄情道教、琴茶与戏曲的亲王就封于此，溯赣江通往岭南的商路则把江西纸张、瓷器运往广州。

1519年，第四代宁王朱宸濠在南昌起兵反叛，南赣巡抚王守仁仅用四十三日便将其平定，朱宸濠在鄱阳湖中被俘，滕王阁也毁于兵火，1526年重建。耶稣会士利玛窦北上谋求进入北京途中曾留居南昌；万历年间大批宗室被安置于此，朱氏宗亲一度占城中人口的四分之一。1648年明清易代之际，清军围攻南昌，滕王阁再付一炬，1654年由巡抚蔡士英主持重建，康熙年间屡毁屡修，1789年乾隆年间又一次重建。

en:
Qiantang, the core of later Hangzhou, was brought under Qin county administration in 222 BC. In 589 the Sui made it the seat of Hang Prefecture and linked the city to the Grand Canal, whose southern terminus met the Qiantang River and Hangzhou Bay. It was capital of the Wuyue kingdom and then, as Lin'an, became the effective Southern Song capital from 1138 until the Mongols entered the city in 1276. Northern refugees, officials and merchants enlarged it into a great market for silk, paper, printed books, porcelain and ships, while West Lake was shaped by the causeways of Bai Juyi and Su Shi. Zhu Yuanzhang captured Hangzhou in 1366, and the Ming made it the administrative centre of Zhejiang. In 1444, two years after a drought dried West Lake, the city was still the wealthy Wu-speaking terminus of the canal trade.

Wokou raiders struck Hangzhou Bay repeatedly between 1553 and 1558, at times pressing close to the city, whose publishers and silk merchants remained active through the late Ming. Qing forces took Hangzhou in May 1645, and in 1650 a walled Manchu banner garrison was built in the western city. Under the Qing the Hangzhou weaving bureau joined those of Suzhou and Jiangning as one of the three great imperial silk centres of Jiangnan. The Kangxi Emperor first visited West Lake in 1689 and wrote plaques for its Ten Scenes in 1699; the Qianlong Emperor followed with six southern tours between 1751 and 1784, his poems helping to make Longjing tea a court favourite. In 1782 a copy of the Siku Quanshu was placed in the Wenyuan Pavilion on Gushan, and in 1797 Ruan Yuan's dredging of West Lake formed Ruangong Islet.
zh:
杭州的核心是秦代在公元前222年设置的钱唐县。589年，隋代改设杭州并修筑城垣，随后江南运河通达此处，使它位居大运河最南端、钱塘江与杭州湾之间。五代时它是吴越国都；南宋时改称临安，1138年起成为实际都城，直到1276年元军入城。北方移民、官员和商人汇聚于此，使杭州成为丝绸、纸张、印书、陶瓷和造船业的大市场，白居易、苏轼主持的西湖堤工也奠定了湖城相依的面貌。1366年朱元璋攻取杭州，明代以杭州府为浙江行政中心。1444年的杭州，虽在两年前刚经历西湖干涸的大旱，仍是运河贸易南端最富庶的吴语城市。

1553年至1558年，倭寇反复袭扰杭州湾，有时兵锋直逼杭州，但晚明的书坊和丝商仍十分活跃。1645年5月清军进入杭州，1650年又在城西筑起墙垣环绕的八旗驻防城。清代杭州织造局与苏州、江宁并列，成为江南三大官办丝织中心之一。康熙帝1689年初游西湖，1699年为西湖十景题字立碑；乾隆帝1751年至1784年间六次南巡，他咏龙井茶田的诗篇也使龙井茶叶受到宫廷推崇。1782年，《四库全书》一部入藏孤山文澜阁；1797年，阮元主持疏浚西湖，以葑泥堆成阮公墩。

en:
