In 1444 it was a guard town of soldier-farmers on the edge of the Jurchen hills, a northern outpost of the Liaodong garrisons.

In 1621 the Later Jin took Shenyang in the Shen-Liao campaign, and in the third month of 1625 Nurhaci moved his capital here from Dongjing at Liaoyang. Work began at once on the Great Administration Hall and the Ten Kings Pavilions, the core of the surviving Mukden Palace; from 1631 Hong Taiji spent five years rebuilding city and palace on a grid plan. In 1634 he named the city Shengjing, 'the Rising Capital', Mukden in Manchu, and in 1636 he took the imperial title there and proclaimed the Qing dynasty. After the court moved to Beijing in 1644 Shengjing remained the Qing secondary capital, with the Fuling and Zhaoling tombs of Nurhaci and Hong Taiji east and north of the city, and in 1657 Fengtian Prefecture was set up within it. The Kangxi and Qianlong emperors stayed at the old palace on their eastern tours, and in 1780 Qianlong added its western quarter, including the Wensuge Library built to house a copy of the Siku Quanshu.
zh:
沈阳位于浑河（旧称沈水）北岸，依「水北为阳」得名，地处辽东丘陵与辽河平原相接之处。辽、金两朝在此置沈州，元代设沈阳等路，「沈阳」之名始见。1386年，明朝改沈阳路为沈阳中卫，隶辽东都司；1388年闵忠就任沈阳中卫城指挥使，次年奏准改建城防，把元代夯土城墙包砌砖石，四门对十字街，引浑河水为两道护城河。1444年，沈阳是军户屯种的卫城，直面东面的女真山林，为辽东各卫的北缘前哨。

1621年，后金在沈辽之战中攻占沈阳；天命十年（1625年）三月，努尔哈赤把都城从辽阳东京城迁来，同年动工修建现存的大政殿与十王亭，是为沈阳故宫的开端。1631年起，皇太极用五年时间按井字街格局改建城池与皇宫；1634年赐沈阳名「天眷盛京」，满语称Mukden，1636年又在此去汗号称帝，改国号为清。1644年清廷迁都北京，盛京作为陪都留存，努尔哈赤的福陵与皇太极的昭陵在城东、城北相守；1657年，城内仿顺天府之制设奉天府。康熙帝、乾隆帝东巡祭祖皆驻跸故宫，1780年乾隆增建西路，包括嘉荫堂戏台和为庋藏《四库全书》而建的文溯阁。

en:
Aigun stood on the middle Amur, where the river leaves the Xing'an and bends towards the sea. During the Yongle reign a Ming fort garrisoned this bank for some twenty years to guard the water route down to Nurgan, but after the court's withdrawal the shore reverted to the Duchers, a Jurchen-speaking people who grew grain, pastured horses and trapped sable for the fur trade. In 1444 their stockaded villages dotted both banks, answerable to no Chinese official and only loosely tied to the rival Jurchen chiefs upstream.

Russian Cossacks reached the Amur in the 1650s and built the fort of Albazin upstream; after Yerofey Khabarov's raids the Qing evacuated the Duchers to the Sungari and the Hurka. In 1683 Sabsu raised a garrison at the Daur village of Aigun, which became the first seat of the military governor of Heilongjiang, and Qing troops fed by crops planted along the river forced Albazin to surrender in June 1685, then blockaded it into submission a second time in 1686. That same year the town was rebuilt on the southern bank as Sahaliyan Ula Hoton, 'Black River City'. The governor's seat moved to Mergen in 1690 and later to Qiqihar, but a deputy lieutenant-general kept Aigun as the base of the Amur river fleet. When Jesuit surveyors sent by the Kangxi Emperor mapped the frontier in 1709, they found a well-defended town ringed by provision villages.
zh:
瑷珲位于黑龙江中游，江流穿过兴安岭后自此折向远方的海口。永乐年间，明朝为保障通往奴儿干的水路，曾在这一带设堡驻军约二十年；朝廷撤守之后，江岸重归久切尔人——一支操女真语的部族，种谷养马，猎貂取皮。1444年，他们的城寨散布两岸，不受流官管辖，只与上游互争雄长的女真酋长保持松散的联系。

17世纪50年代，俄国哥萨克进抵黑龙江，在上游筑起雅克萨堡；哈巴罗夫焚掠之后，清廷把久切尔人南迁松花江与牡丹江流域。1683年，萨布素在达斡尔人的瑷珲村筑城屯兵，这里成为新设黑龙江将军的第一个驻所；大军就食于沿江开垦的屯田，于1685年6月迫使雅克萨投降，1686年又以长期围困再度将其攻克。同年，城址迁至黑龙江南岸重修，满语称萨哈连乌拉霍通，意为「黑龙江城」。1690年将军衙署移驻墨尔根，后来再迁齐齐哈尔，瑷珲仍留副都统一员，并作为黑龙江水师营的基地。1709年，康熙派往测绘皇舆的耶稣会士雷孝思等抵达此地，见到的是一座守备严整、四围村落粮饷充足的江城。

en:
Tuwan is the rolling grass and woodland between the Nen and the upper Hulan, where the Xing'an forests give way to the Songhua plain. Ming writers called the Jurchen clans of these parts the 'river Jurchen': they herded horses and cattle, scratched scattered fields of grain and trapped sable, trading ponies and pelts beyond the Kaiyuan border. The loose-reign guards scattered across the Amur country lapsed with the Nurgan command, and in 1444 the clans answered only to their own headmen. On the Nen to the west, the Khorchin Mongols, defeated by the Oirats, had arrived only six years before, and their shadow already lay over the pasture.

By the mid-1500s the Sibe clans of the plain were Khorchin tributaries. Sibe horsemen rode in the nine-tribe coalition that Nurhaci routed at Gure in 1593, and over the following decades the Khorchin themselves submitted to the Later Jin. In 1692 the Kangxi Emperor redeemed the Sibe, Gūwalca and Daur from the Khorchin for silver, enrolled them in the upper three banners and posted them to Qiqihar, Boduna and Girin Ula; from 1699 tens of thousands of banner soldiers with their families were moved south to Mukden and the capital. The grassland they left was closed to settlement, its remaining Solon and Daur hunters placed under the Butha command set up in the Kangxi reign and bound to a yearly tribute of sable, and early in the 19th century it remained an empty pasture and hunting reserve.
zh:
托温在嫩江与呼兰河上游之间，是小兴安岭林地向松嫩平原过渡的丘陵草原。明初把这一带的女真部落称作「江夷」：他们牧放马牛，零星开垦谷田，入山猎貂，把马匹和皮张拿到开原边外互市。明朝散置在黑龙江流域的羁縻卫所随奴儿干都司一同废弛，1444年的各部只听本部首领约束。西边嫩江流域，被瓦剌击败的科尔沁蒙古六年前刚刚迁来，阴影已经压上这片牧场。

到16世纪中叶，草原上的锡伯诸部都成了科尔沁的属部。1593年，锡伯骑兵随九部联军进犯建州，在古勒山被努尔哈赤击溃；此后数十年间，科尔沁自身也陆续归附后金。1692年，康熙皇帝以银两代科尔沁赎出锡伯、卦尔察和达斡尔人，编入上三旗，分驻齐齐哈尔、伯都讷和吉林乌拉；1699年起，数万旗兵家口又分批南迁盛京和京师。他们空出的草原长期封禁，留在山里的索伦、达斡尔猎户归康熙年间设立的布特哈总管衙门管辖，岁岁纳貂；直到19世纪初，这里仍是人烟稀少的牧场与围场。

en:
Bohori, the Boli of Chinese records, lies among the lowlands and channels where the Ussuri joins the Amur. Tungusic villagers fished the rivers and hunted the riverine forest; in the fifteenth century Ming records placed the Bahulu Guard here under the Nurgan military administration. In 1444 there was still no walled town at the confluence. Jurchen and Oroch bands lived by fishing, hunting and exchanging furs along a frontier that Ming garrisons touched only lightly.

Qing records register Bohori as a village station, or gashan, in 1643. Eight years later Yerofey Khabarov's Cossacks sailed down the Amur and in September 1651 built the fortified winter camp of Achansk in this river stretch. Local Achan and Ducher people attacked it that October, and Manchu cavalry under Haise assaulted the camp in March 1652; Khabarov withstood the day-long battle but destroyed the fort when the ice broke and withdrew. The 1689 Treaty of Nerchinsk checked the Russian advance. French Jesuits surveying the Ussuri and Amur in 1709 found Nanai fishing villages, known to the Qing as the Fish-skin Tartars, and Bohori remained a loosely administered Qing frontier under the Sanxing commandant until after 1821.
zh:
伯力在中国记载中又作勃利，位于乌苏里江汇入黑龙江处的低地与河汊之间。通古斯人的村落长期在江中捕鱼、在河畔森林狩猎；15世纪，明朝在此设巴忽鲁卫，隶属于奴儿干都指挥使司。1444年时，两江汇流处还没有城墙环绕的城镇，女真和鄂罗奇人群以捕鱼、狩猎和毛皮交换为生；明朝卫所对这片边疆的控制十分薄弱。

清朝记载在1643年把伯力记作一处噶珊，即村落站所。八年后，叶罗费·哈巴罗夫率领哥萨克沿黑龙江而下，于1651年9月在这一段河道修建了阿钱斯克冬营。当地阿钱人和久切尔人在当年10月发起进攻，海色率领的满洲骑兵又于1652年3月攻打营寨；哈巴罗夫坚守一整天，却在开春冰解后毁掉营寨撤走。1689年《尼布楚条约》遏止了俄国东进。1709年，沿乌苏里江和黑龙江测绘的法国耶稣会士见到那乃人的渔村，清朝称他们为「鱼皮鞑子」；直到1821年以后，伯力仍是三姓副都统辖下管辖松散的清朝江河前沿。

en:
Girin, the Manchu Girin Ula shortened to mean 'along the river', straddles the Songhua where the grain-growing river plain meets the forested Changbai foothills. A Buyeo royal town stood at the foot of Dongtuan Hill in the early centuries, until Xianbei forces took it in 346, and Goguryeo fortresses later crowned Longtan Hill above the river. In 1409 the Ming built a shipyard on this bank, launching vessels that carried troops, grain and gifts to the Nurgan command far downstream; by 1444 the yard and river road lay in the country of the Haixi Jurchen, whose clans sold sable, ginseng and river pearls at the Kaiyuan border market, and whose Ula, 'the river', was the strongest power on the middle Songhua.

Buyan took the title of beile in 1561 and built Ula city at the present Wula Street; under his grandsons Mantai and Bujantai the kingdom dominated the trade road from the Amur to Kaiyuan. Bujantai was captured fighting Nurhaci at Gure in 1593 and lost the Eastern Sea clans after the rout at Wujieyan in 1607. In the first month of 1613 Nurhaci marched thirty thousand men down the Songhua, stormed the capital and ended Ula, and Bujantai fled to Yehe. The Qing turned the old Ula city into its Buthai Ula tribute station, formally constituted in 1657, whose twenty-two game hills and sixty-four pearl rivers supplied the court with Eastern pearls, sturgeon, sable and ginseng. A new naval yard was laid out on the river in 1661; the wooden walled town rose in 1673, and in 1676 the Ningguta general moved his seat there, making Girin the second city of the Manchu north-east after Mukden. The Kangxi emperor inspected the fleet in 1682 and in 1685 shortened the city's name to Girin.
zh:
「吉林」是满语吉林乌拉的简称，意为「沿江」，城在松花江岸，上接长白山林，下连宜于农耕的松花江平原。扶余前期的王城秽城就坐落在东团山麓，346年被鲜卑慕容皝派军攻破，高句丽后来又在龙潭山筑起山城戍守。1409年，明朝在今吉林城区设造船基地，所造船只沿松花江、黑龙江运送官兵粮草和赏赐贡品，维系辽东都司与奴儿干都司之间的联络。到1444年，船厂与这条水路已处在海西女真的地界，诸部以紫貂、人参、东珠在开原关市交易，以「江」为名的乌拉是松花江中游最强的势力。

1561年，布颜称贝勒，在乌拉河畔扩建乌拉城，建立乌拉国；传到满泰、布占泰兄弟时，乌拉控制了黑龙江至开原的贡市商路。1593年，布占泰参加九部联军攻打建州，在古勒山兵败被俘；1607年又在乌碣岩大败，丧失对东海诸部的控制。1613年正月，努尔哈赤率三万大军沿江而下，攻破乌拉都城，布占泰逃奔叶赫，立国五十一年的乌拉灭亡。清朝把乌拉旧城改为采捕贡品的打牲乌拉总管衙门，1657年正式设立，辖22处贡山、64处采珠河口，东珠、鲟鳇、貂皮、人参源源不断送入内务府。1661年，清廷又在松花江边设厂造船、建立水师营；1673年宁古塔副都统安珠瑚修筑吉林木城，1676年宁古塔将军巴海移驻于此，吉林由此成为清朝统辖松花江、乌苏里江、黑龙江流域的重镇，地位仅次于盛京。康熙帝1682年东巡吉林、检阅水师，1685年奉旨将吉林乌拉简称定为「吉林」。

en:
Ilan Hala, Manchu for 'three clans', was known to the Chinese as Sanxing and stood where the Mudan River, then often called the Hurka, enters the Sungari. Under the Ming it was, together with Ninguta up the valley, one of the two important centres of the Jianzhou Jurchens in the Hurka country. In 1444 Jurchen headmen controlled the river crossing, where fisheries, forest products and tribute furs from the lower Sungari met rather than a Chinese county magistrate.

The Qing turned that informal importance into a permanent garrison. In 1714 Sanxing was walled and given a colonel's office. In December 1731 the court established a deputy lieutenant-general there, and Aisin Gioro Qishihwu took up the post the following March. Under the Jilin general, his command stretched along the middle and lower Sungari and Amur, across the Ussuri basin and to Sakhalin. Sanxing therefore served as the Qing military gateway to the lower Amur, and retained that frontier role through 1821.
zh:
依兰哈喇是满语「三姓」之意，汉文史籍称三姓，位于当时多称忽尔哈河的牡丹江汇入松花江处。明代时，它与河谷上游的宁古塔同为忽尔哈河流域建州女真的两个重要中心。1444年，女真首领掌握着这处河口要地；这里汇聚的是下游松花江的渔产、山林物产和贡貂，而不是中原式知县直接治理的县城。

清朝把这种自然形成的重要地位变成固定军镇。1714年，三姓筑城并设立协领衙门。1731年12月，清廷增设三姓副都统镇守地方，爱新觉罗·七十五于次年3月到任。该职隶属吉林将军，辖区沿松花江、黑龙江中下游延伸，涵盖乌苏里江流域和库页岛。三姓由此成为清朝通向黑龙江下游的军事门户，并在1821年以前始终保持这一前沿职能。

en:
Hamheung, the old Goryeo town of Hamju, sits on the coastal plain where the Seongcheon River reaches the East Korea Bay. It returned to Goryeo rule in 1356 after a century under Yuan frontier administration. After Yi Bang-won's coup in 1400, King Yi Seong-gye retired here and refused to receive the new court's envoys, giving rise to the Korean phrase for a messenger who never returns. In 1416 the town was raised to Hamheung-bu and became the seat of Hamgil-do, the northeastern frontier province consolidated under King Sejong against Jurchen raiders. In 1444 it was thus a royal provincial centre on a recently secured coast.

The province was renamed Hamgyeong in 1468, but unrest brought demotion for Hamheung in 1469 and moved the governor's seat to Yeongheung; both the city's standing and the provincial capital returned in 1509. During the Japanese invasion of 1592, Katō Kiyomasa's division pushed through to Hamheung, while Jeong Mun-bu raised a Righteous Army in northern Hamgyeong and retook the province around Gyeongseong and Gilju before the Japanese withdrew south early in 1593. Qing forces raided Hamgyeong during their 1636-1637 invasion, and after King Injo's surrender the frontier remained part of a Joseon kingdom bound to the Qing as a tributary.
zh:
咸兴古称咸州，位于城川江注入东朝鲜湾的沿海平原。这一带在元朝的边疆行政体系下达约百年，1356年才由高丽收复。1400年李芳远发动政变后，太上王李成桂退居咸兴，拒绝接纳新朝廷派来的使者，后来朝鲜语便用「咸兴差使」比喻一去不回的人。1416年，咸州升为咸兴府，成为咸吉道监营所在地；朝鲜世宗继续经营东北边疆，防备女真人袭扰。到1444年，这里已是新近巩固的东海沿岸上的一道王朝治所。

1468年，咸吉道改称咸镜道；1469年地方变乱后，咸兴被降级，监营移往永兴。1509年，咸兴恢复府级地位，监营也迁回此地，咸镜道之名随之稳定下来。1592年壬辰战争爆发，加藤清正所部北上攻占咸兴；郑文孚则在咸镜道北部组织义兵，在镜城、吉州一带作战并收复道内各地，日军最终于1593年初南撤。1636年至1637年清军入侵时攻掠咸镜道，仁祖投降后，这片边疆继续属于向清朝称臣纳贡的朝鲜王朝。

en:
Hwangju stands on the western Korean road between Hanyang and Pyongyang, near the lower Taedong River and the Yellow Sea coast. Under Goguryeo it was called Tonghol; after Silla took the area it became Chwiseong, and early Goryeo renamed it Hwangju, establishing Hwangju-mok in 983. It passed under Yuan control late in the thirteenth century before King Gongmin restored it to Goryeo. In 1417 its name was joined with that of Haeju to form Hwanghae Province, whose governor resided at Haeju. In 1444 Hwangju was thus a walled Confucian administrative town, guarding the western coastal road and nearby fishing waters.

Under King Sejo, who reigned from 1455 to 1468, a garrison was placed at Hwangju and its regional military duties were enlarged. In 1624, during Yi Gwal's rebellion, rebel troops routed royal forces under Chong Chung-sin and Nam I-hung at Hwangju-singyo before pushing on toward Kaesong. During the Later Jin invasion of 1627, reports from the front announced that Pyongyang had fallen and Hwangju had collapsed, while the Manchu vanguard reached the town; raiders also swept Hwangju and Haeju before the April peace established brotherly relations between Joseon and Later Jin. Through the remaining Joseon centuries, Hwangju kept its place as a Hwanghae garrison and administrative town.
zh:
黄州位于朝鲜西海岸汉阳通往平壤的大道旁，靠近大同江下游和黄海沿岸。高句丽时这里称冬忽，新罗攻取后改称取城郡；高丽初年改名黄州，并于983年设置黄州牧。13世纪末，黄州一度归入元朝控制，恭愍王时才由高丽收复。1417年，黄州与海州的首字合称为黄海道，道内监营则设在海州。因此1444年的黄州是朝鲜一座有城墙的儒教行政城邑，扼守西海岸通道和附近渔场。

1455年至1468年在位的世祖年间，黄州设镇，地方军务随之加重。1624年李适之乱时，叛军在黄州新橋击败郑忠信、南以兴所部官军，随后向开城推进。1627年后金入侵时，前方奏报称平壤陷落、黄州已溃，后金前锋抵达黄州；在四月和议达成、朝鲜与后金结为兄弟之国前，后金游骑还袭掠黄州、海州一带。此后直至1821年，黄州始终是黄海道的驻防与行政城邑。

en:
Wonju occupies a broad basin of the upper Namhan River, with Chiak Mountain rising to its south, in the Yeongseo country west of the Taebaek range. It was contested ground in the Three Kingdoms era: Goguryeo established Pyeongwon-gun here in 469, and after Silla secured the region it made Bukwon one of its five secondary capitals in 678, renaming it Bukwongyeong in 757. As Silla collapsed, the rebel Yang Gil used the country as his base. Goryeo's King Taejo gave the town its present name in 940, for its wide-open plains. When the Mongol rebel Qadan's army raided into Goryeo in 1291, the local scholar Won Ch'ung-gap and the men of Wonju routed the invaders, and in 1308 the town was raised to a mok. In 1395 King Taejo merged the Gangneung and Gyoju circuits into Gangwon Province and planted the governor's office, the Gangwon Gamyeong, at Wonju. Thus in 1444 Wonju is the administrative heart of Gangwon, where the governor conducts provincial business from his hall, the Seonhwadang.

The Imjin War reached Wonju in the eighth month of 1592, when its magistrate Kim Chegap, an aged former pupil of Yi Hwang, evacuated the civilians into the hill fortress of Yeongwon and held it against a full Japanese assault until the walls were carried. He was cut down together with his wife and second son, and was later enshrined in the town's Chungnyeolsa. In 1594 Queen Inyeol, the future queen of King Injo and mother of King Hyojong, was born in Wonju. The Later Jin invasion of 1627 and the Qing invasion of 1636–1637 ended with Choson submitting to the Manchus, and the Gangwon Gamyeong now governed the province under a new suzerain. Successive governors kept their seat at Wonju for the rest of the period, overseeing more than two dozen mok, gun and hyeon scattered across the mountains.
zh:
原州地处南汉江上游的宽阔盆地，雉岳山耸立于其南，属太白山脉以西的岭西地方。三国时代这里是列强角逐之地：高句丽于469年设平原郡；新罗取得这一带后，于678年将北原列为五小京之一，757年改称北原京。新罗末年天下大乱，叛军首领梁吉以原州为根基扩张势力。高丽太祖940年因其地开阔、田野平广而得名原州。1291年蒙古叛王合丹的军队窜入高丽，乡贡进士元冲甲率原州军民击溃入侵者，1308年原州升为牧。1395年，太祖合并江陵、交州两道置江原道，把观察使衙门江原监营设在原州。因此1444年的原州是江原道的行政中枢，观察使在宣化堂总理全道事务。

1592年农历八月，壬辰倭乱波及原州：牧使金悌甲是李滉晚年的弟子，时年近七旬，他先将百姓撤入领愿山城，随后率军死守，抵挡日军全力进攻，直至城破，与夫人李氏、次子一同殉节，后奉安于原州忠烈祠。1594年，仁祖的王妃、孝宗生母仁烈王后韩氏出生于原州。1627年后金入侵、1636至1637年清军入侵，最终朝鲜臣服于满洲，江原监营在新的宗主权下继续治理全道。此后历任观察使均驻原州，管辖散布于群山之中的二十余个牧、郡、县。

en:
Hanseong, the city later called Seoul, stands on the Han River ringed by granite hills. It held the Baekje capital of Wiryeseong and Goryeo's Southern Capital before Yi Seong-gye made it the seat of his new Joseon dynasty in 1394; named Hanseongbu the next year, it was laid out around the new Gyeongbokgung palace and the Jongmyo shrine, with a fortress wall climbing the surrounding ridges, and held perhaps a hundred thousand people by the early fifteenth century. In 1444 King Sejong rules here over a Confucian capital of officials, scholars and the licensed shops of Jongno. His Hall of Worthies had just completed the native alphabet in December 1443, and Choe Manri's memorial of protest in February 1444 was still fresh; the Hunminjeongeum was formally proclaimed in 1446.

Fire gutted much of Gyeongbokgung in 1553, and the rebuilt palace burned again when the Japanese seized Hanseong on 11 June 1592 after the court fled north; the occupiers withdrew only in May 1593. Gyeongbokgung then stood in ruins for more than two and a half centuries, while Changdeokgung, restored by 1610, became the working palace. In 1623 the Injo coup deposed Gwanghaegun there, and in 1636 the court fled the Manchus to Namhansanseong, submitting early the next year. The crew of the Dutch ship Sperwer, wrecked off Jeju in 1653, were brought to Hanseong and attached to the Military Training Agency through the long-settled castaway Jan Jansz Weltevree, until hardship scattered them south in 1659. In 1762 Yeongjo ordered Crown Prince Sado confined in a rice chest, where he starved to death. Catholic learning from Beijing also found readers here: after Yi Seung-hun returned baptized in 1784 a house church met at Myeongryebang, and in the persecution of 1801 its leaders were beheaded outside Seosomun.
zh:
汉城，即后来的首尔，坐落于汉江之畔，四周环绕着花岗岩山岭。这里曾是百济慰礼城所在、高丽的南京；1394年李成桂定都于此，次年定名汉城府，以新建的景福宫和宗庙为核心，沿山脊修筑城墙，15世纪初人口约有十万。1444年的汉城是世宗治下的儒教都城，官署、书册与钟路的特许市廛并立。集贤殿学者刚于1443年12月制成本国文字训民正音，崔万里1444年2月上疏反对一事犹在眼前，新文字最终于1446年正式颁布。

1553年景福宫大火，多数殿阁焚毁；复建不久，1592年6月11日日军在朝廷北逃后占领汉城，三大宫尽数被毁，日军直到1593年5月才南撤。景福宫此后荒废二百七十余年，光海君在1609至1610年重建昌德宫，这里从此成为历代国王处理政务的正宫。1623年，仁祖反正的军队在昌德宫废黜光海君；1636年清军入侵，王室退入南汉山城，次年出降。1653年，荷兰船「斯佩尔韦号」在济州近海失事，船员哈梅尔一行被押到汉城，经早年归化朝鲜的朴渊介绍编入训练都监，直到1659年因生计艰难被分散安置到南方。1762年，英祖下令将世子李愃关进米柜，最终饿死。来自北京的天主教义也在这里找到读者：李承薰1784年受洗归国后，明礼坊出现了家庭教会，1801年辛酉迫害中，教会首领被押到西小门外处死。

en:
Sangju lies in the western hills of Gyeongsang, where roads from the Han River valley run toward the old Silla heartland around Gyeongju. Silla made the fortress one of its provincial ju, and in 983 Goryeo established Sangju-mok. In 1408 the Joseon court moved the Gyeongsang governor's seat to the town. Thus, in 1444 Sangju was an administrative stronghold of Confucian Joseon, set among farmlands whose rice, silk and dried persimmons gave the district its local reputation.

Sejo established a military post at Sangju in 1457. During the Japanese invasion of 1592, after Busan and Dongnae had fallen, Konishi Yukinaga's army advanced on the town; the Korean commander Yi Il gathered troops there but was defeated, opening the route north toward Chungju. The Gyeongsang governor's seat was moved to Daegu in 1601. Sangju then remained a provincial mok town and inland market, its roads and periodic trade still drawing the rice, silk and persimmons of the surrounding countryside.
zh:
尚州位于庆尚西部丘陵，控制着从汉江谷地通往庆州一带新罗旧地的道路。新罗曾在此设州筑城，高丽于983年置尚州牧。1408年，朝鲜朝廷把庆尚道监营移到这里。因此1444年的尚州是儒教朝鲜的一处行政要镇，周围乡村出产的米、丝绸和柿饼使这一带颇有声名。

1457年，朝鲜世祖在尚州设镇。1592年壬辰倭乱期间，釜山和东莱陷落后，小西行长率领日军进逼尚州；朝鲜将领李镒在此募兵迎战却告败北，日军由此打开北上忠州的道路。1601年，庆尚监营移往大邱。此后尚州仍是一道内陆地路上的牧镇和集市，周边所产米、丝绸与柿饼继续沿道路汇集于此。

en:
Jeonju began as Wansan, a market town of Baekje in the fertile Honam plain. Silla made it a provincial seat in 685 and renamed it Jeonju in 757. In 892 the rebel general Gyeon Hwon chose the city as the capital of his Later Baekje kingdom, and it remained so until the state fell to Goryeo in 936. The town walls went up in 1388. Under the new Joseon dynasty it gained singular prestige: the ruling Jeonju Yi clan hailed from here, so in 1410 King Taejong built Gyeonggijeon to house King Taejo's portrait, and in 1439 an archive was established to keep a copy of the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty. In 1444 Jeonju was the capital of Jeolla Province and the seat of its governor, the chief city of Korea's rice-rich southwest.

During the Japanese invasion of 1592, General Kwon Yul with roughly a thousand men held the Ichi pass on 14 August, turning back some fifteen thousand troops under Kobayakawa Takakage and keeping the road to Jeonju closed. The city did not hold in the second invasion: after Namwon fell on 26 September 1597 the court forces withdrew, and the Japanese occupied Jeonju until their pull-back the following year. Back under Joseon rule, the city kept its role as the administrative and scholarly centre of Honam, its hyanggyo academy and provincial governor's hall drawing scholars and degree candidates from across the southwest.
zh:
全州古称完山，本是百济在肥沃的湖南平原上的一处集镇。685年新罗在此设州，757年改名为全州。892年，叛将甄萱以这里为都建立后百济，直到936年后百济为高丽所灭。1388年，全州筑起包括丰南门在内的州城。新立的朝鲜王朝给予此地特殊的尊崇：统治国家的全州李氏便发祥于此，太宗于1410年建庆基殿供奉太祖御真，1439年又在全州设实录阁，珍藏一部《朝鲜王朝实录》。1444年的全州是全罗道的首府和监营所在地，也是朝鲜米粮丰足的西南地区的首要城市。

1592年壬辰倭乱中，权栗将军率约千人在8月14日据守梨峙，击退小早川隆景麾下约一万五千人的军队，保住了通往全州的道路。但第二次入侵时全州未能幸免：1597年9月26日南原陷落后，官军撤走，日军进占全州，直到次年撤退。重归朝鲜统治后，全州继续承担湖南行政与学术中心的角色，乡校与监营吸引着西南各地的儒生和应举士子。

en:
Sakam was the Siraya country behind the Tayouan sandbar, where the future city of Tainan took shape. Its villages were closely tied to the Sinkan community and stood along the shallow Taikang inlet that separated their fields from the anchorage outside. The people farmed the coastal plain, hunted deer and managed their own village affairs without a larger island ruler. In 1444 Sakam was therefore an indigenous landing place and hunting ground rather than a Chinese walled town, its settlements facing a lagoon that later traders and colonizers would enter.

The Dutch East India Company changed that in 1624 by founding Fort Zeelandia on Tayouan as its China and Japan trade base. On 20 January 1625 Governor Marten Sonck bought a tract at Sakam from the Sinkan people for fifteen pieces of flowered cloth and laid out the Provintia settlement. After the 1635-36 pacification of neighbouring Siraya villages, the company encouraged Chinese farmers to grow rice and sugar. The Guo Huaiyi rising of 1652 was crushed with Sinkan help, and Fort Provintia was built at Sakam the next year.

In 1661 Zheng Chenggong sailed through the Luerhmen channel, took Provintia and besieged Zeelandia until its surrender on 1 February 1662. Sakam became the centre of his Ming-loyalist Kingdom of Tungning; the first Confucian temple on Taiwan was built there in 1665. After the Qing conquest of 1683, Taiwan Prefecture was established in 1684 with its seat at the growing Taiwan-fu near old Sakam. During the Lin Shuangwen rebellion of 1787-1788, much of the island rose around the prefecture, which remained a Qing stronghold until Fuk'anggan's campaign restored control.
zh:
赤崁（Sakam）是大员沙洲内侧的西拉雅地域，后世台南便在此成形。这里的村社与新港社关系密切，村田和外海锚地之间隔着水浅的台江内海。居民耕种滨海平原、猎鹿，并按村社自行管理事务，岛上并无更高的统一政权。1444年的赤崁还不是汉人城垣，而是原住民的登陆地与猎场；村社面向的潟湖，后来将把商人和殖民者引入此地。

1624年，荷兰东印度公司在大员建立热兰遮城，作为对中国、日本贸易的据点，改变了这里的命运。1625年1月20日，首任台湾长官宋克以十五匹花布向新港人购得赤崁一带土地，开辟普罗民遮市街。1635至1636年征服邻近西拉雅村社后，公司招来汉人农民种植稻米和甘蔗。1652年郭怀一领导的汉人起事被荷兰人联合新港等社镇压，次年荷兰人在赤崁修筑普罗民遮城。

1661年，郑成功率军从鹿耳门水道进入台江内海，先取普罗民遮城，再长期围困热兰遮城，迫使荷军于1662年2月1日投降。赤崁成为明郑反清基地的中心，1665年台湾第一座孔庙在此建成。1683年清军攻占台湾后，1684年设置台湾府，府城就在旧赤崁附近发展起来。1787至1788年林爽文抗清期间，台湾大片地区卷入战事，台湾府城始终是清军固守的据点，直到福康安率军渡台平定局势。

en:
Known in older Chinese records as Shule, Kashgar is the oasis where northern, central and southern Silk Road routes meet below the Pamirs. The Karakhanids made it an early centre of Turkic Islam after Satuq Bughra Khan's conversion in the tenth century; it later passed through the Qara Khitai and Genghisid realms into the Chagatai ulus. After the city fell to Timur's armies, the Eastern Chagatai khanate recovered it only in 1432. In 1444 Kashgar was a Muslim merchant city rebuilding after decades of war, its bazaars drawing caravans between the Tarim Basin, Ferghana and the Pamir passes, while Dughlat emirs held much local power.

After 1466 local wars brought Kashgar firmly under the Dughlat emirs. In 1514 Sultan Said Khan defeated Mirza Abu Bakr, founded the Yarkand khanate, and used Kashgar as his capital before moving his court to Yarkand. Rival White Mountain and Black Mountain khoja networks later divided the cities of Altishahr. In 1680 the White Mountain leader Apak Khoja called in Galdan's Dzungar army, reducing the Yarkand khanate to a dependent state, and direct Dzungar rule followed under Tsewang Rabtan. Qing armies took Kashgar in 1759 after suppressing the revolt of Burhan-ud-din and Khoja Jahan, stationing a garrison and an imperial councillor there. Through 1821 it remained a guarded Qing frontier city on the Pamir trade roads, with Kokand and exiled khojas beyond the mountains.
zh:
喀什噶尔在汉文古籍中称疏勒，是帕米尔高原脚下、丝绸之路北中南三道汇合的绿洲。10世纪萨图克·博格拉汗皈依伊斯兰教后，喀喇汗王朝把这里经营成突厥语世界较早的伊斯兰中心；此后它先后经历西辽和成吉思汗系政权，归入察合台兀鲁思。帖木儿的军队攻陷该城后，东察合台汗国直到1432年才将其收复。1444年的喀什噶尔是一座在数十年战火后重建的穆斯林商业城，巴扎吸引往来塔里木盆地、费尔干纳和帕米尔山口的商队，地方实权则多掌握在杜格拉特埃米尔手中。

1466年后，长期战乱使喀什噶尔成为杜格拉特氏族的属地。1514年，萨亦德汗击败埃米尔阿布·伯克尔，建立叶尔羌汗国，并在迁都叶尔羌前以喀什噶尔为都。后来，白山派与黑山派和卓势力分裂了回疆诸城。1680年，白山派首领阿帕克和卓引来噶尔丹的准噶尔军队，使叶尔羌汗国沦为附庸，策妄阿拉布坦时期又转为准噶尔直接统治。1759年，清军在平定大小和卓之乱后进驻喀什噶尔，设城驻军并派遣参赞大臣。到1821年，这里始终是清朝扼守帕米尔商路的边疆要城，山外则有浩罕和流亡和卓窥伺。

en:
Chanderi lies on the border of Malwa and Bundelkhand, ringed by hills, lakes and forest south-west of the Betwa River. Balban took it for Delhi in 1251; Koli weavers settled there from the 1300s gave the town its name for fine cotton and silk, and Jain merchants built a cluster of temples. Sultan Mahmud Khalji I of Malwa captured it in 1438 after a siege of several months, so in 1444 Chanderi is a recent acquisition of the Malwa Sultanate. In 1445 the sultan, passing through after his victory over the Jaunpur army at Kalpi, ordered the seven-storey Koshak Mahal, a Mandu-style palace of which only three floors were ever finished.

After Rana Sanga of Mewar crushed Mahmud II at Gagron in 1519, his protege Medini Rai made Chanderi the capital of a Rajput kingdom, until Babur stormed the fort in January 1528 and the defenders' women perished in jauhar. Puran Mal retook it in 1529, but the conquests of Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1531–1532, Humayun's campaign of 1535 and Sher Shah's takeover in 1542 made it a Sur frontier post. When Akbar's armies overthrew Baz Bahadur, Chanderi was annexed with the rest of Malwa in 1562 and became a sarkar of the Malwa subah. The Bundelas took the town in 1586 and held it under Ram Sab, a son of Raja Madhukar of Orchha; Devi Singh Bundela was made its governor in 1646, and his line kept it until 1811, when Jean Baptiste Filose seized it for Daulat Rao Scindia of Gwalior. Through every change of ruler the town's handlooms carried on weaving the sheer cloth that gave Chanderi its lasting fame.
zh:
钱德里坐落在摩腊婆与本德尔肯德的交界处、贝特瓦河西南，四周丘陵、湖泊与森林环抱。巴尔班1251年为德里攻取此地；14世纪起在此定居的科利族织工让这座城以精细棉布和丝绸闻名，耆那教商人也建起成群的庙宇。摩腊婆苏丹马哈茂德·卡尔吉一世1438年围攻数月后将其占领，因此1444年的钱德里还是摩腊婆苏丹国新到手的边城。1445年，苏丹在卡尔皮击败江布尔军队后途经此地，下令修建七层的科沙克宫；这座曼杜风格的宫殿最终只建成三层。

1519年梅瓦尔的拉纳·桑加在加格龙击溃马哈茂德二世后，他扶持的梅迪尼·拉伊把钱德里定为一个拉杰普特王国的都城；1528年1月巴布尔强攻此堡，守军女眷行乔哈尔自焚而死。普兰·马尔1529年收复钱德里，但古吉拉特的巴哈杜尔·沙1531至1532年的征服、胡马雍1535年的远征和舍尔沙1542年的夺取，使它成为苏尔王朝的边防要地。阿克巴的大军推翻巴兹·巴哈杜尔后，钱德里于1562年随摩腊婆全境并入莫卧儿，成为摩腊婆苏巴下辖的一个萨卡尔。本德拉人1586年夺取此城，由奥尔查王公马杜卡尔之子拉姆·萨卜据守；1646年德维·辛格·本德拉被任命为城主，其家族一直保有此地，直到1811年让-巴蒂斯特·菲洛斯为瓜廖尔的道拉特·拉奥·辛迪亚将其攻占。城头王旗几番更迭，城里的手工织机却始终不辍，织出钱德里赖以传世的轻薄织物。

en:
Cumaná lies at the entrance to the Gulf of Cariaco, where the Manzanares River meets the Caribbean, and in the tongue of its first inhabitants the name was said to mean 'union of sea and river'. In 1444 this coast belonged to the Cumanagoto and Chaima, whose forebears had come from the Orinoco basin, and pearl beds lay off the island of Cubagua.

From 1500 Spanish pearl fishers from Nueva Cádiz on Cubagua drew fresh water at the river mouth, and friars sent by Pedro de Córdoba began a peaceful mission. On 3 October 1515 Cumanagoto under the cacique Maragüey, avenging Spanish slave raids, destroyed the convent and killed the friars. Gonzalo de Ocampo answered with punitive raids and a fort he named Nueva Toledo; Bartolomé de las Casas arrived in 1521 to settle the land peacefully but left after quarrels with Ocampo. The Dominican Francisco de Montesinos refounded the town as Nueva Córdoba on 1 February 1562, and in 1569 Diego Fernández de Serpa, first governor of New Andalusia, renamed it Cumaná as his capital. By 1741 the city had 4,263 inhabitants. Antonio José de Sucre was born here, and on 15 July 1811 the city declared independence.
zh:
库马纳位于卡里亚科湾湾口、曼萨纳雷斯河注入加勒比海的地方，据说这个名字在最早的居民的语言里意为「海与河的交汇」。1444年，这片海岸属于库马纳戈托人和柴马人，他们的祖先来自奥里诺科河流域，近海的库瓦瓜岛一带蕴藏着珍珠。

1500年起，在库瓦瓜岛新加的斯采珠的西班牙人来河口取淡水，佩德罗·德科尔多瓦派来的修士也在此开始和平传教。1515年10月3日，库马纳戈托人在酋长马拉圭伊率领下报复西班牙人的猎奴袭击，捣毁修院，杀死修士。冈萨洛·德奥坎波随即出兵讨伐，修起一座要塞，命名为新托莱多；1521年巴托洛梅·德拉斯卡萨斯来到这里，想和平拓殖，却因与奥坎波不和而离去。多明我会修士弗朗西斯科·德蒙特西诺斯于1562年2月1日重建城镇，称新科尔多瓦；1569年，新安达卢西亚首任总督迭戈·费尔南德斯·德塞尔帕将其改名库马纳，定为首府。到1741年，城中有居民4263人。安东尼奥·何塞·德苏克雷生于此地，1811年7月15日，库马纳宣布独立。

en:
At Angostura — the 'narrows' deep inland from the Orinoco's delta — the great river contracts from a broad floodplain to a rocky gap barely 800 metres wide, the natural crossing between its lower banks. This is the old country of the Caribs: river villages fished and planted cassava, canoe-borne trade moved between the coast and the interior, and no war party could pass the strait unseen. In 1444 the Spaniards were still no more than a rumour from the Caribbean islands, and the crossing belonged entirely to the peoples of the river.

On 1 August 1498, on his third voyage, Columbus sighted the freshening mouths of the Orinoco. The first Spanish town on the lower river, Santo Tomé de Guayana, was planted in 1576 near the Caroní confluence and destroyed by Dutch raiders three years later. Antonio de Berrío refounded it in 1595, and in 1617 an English expedition under Walter Raleigh sacked the place, his son Wat dying in the assault; Raleigh was beheaded in England the next year. Fernando de Berrío rebuilt it in 1620, but English and Dutch raiders burned it in 1629 and the Dutch again in 1637. Only on 22 May 1764 did Joaquín Moreno de Mendoza settle the town for good at the narrows, as Santo Tomás de la Nueva Guayana de la Angostura del Orinoco — Angostura, capital of Guayana Province. Humboldt passed through in 1800. In the wars of independence Manuel Piar's patriots defeated the royalists at San Félix, on the Chirica tableland, on 11 April 1817; the garrison abandoned Angostura that July, and the town became the republic's provisional capital. On 15 February 1819 Bolívar opened the Congress of Angostura there, which proclaimed Gran Colombia before the year ended and sat on until 1821.
zh:
安戈斯图拉意为「狭口」，地处奥里诺科河三角洲深处，浩荡的河面在此从开阔的泛滥平原收束为仅800米宽的岩石水道，是下游两岸的天然渡口。这里本是加勒比人的故土：河畔村落以捕鱼和种植木薯为生，独木舟商队往来于海岸与内陆之间，任何武装队伍都无法悄悄通过狭口。1444年，西班牙人还只是来自加勒比海岛的传闻，这座渡口完全掌握在河畔原住民手中。

1498年8月1日，哥伦布在第三次航行中望见了奥里诺科河淡水奔涌的河口。1576年，西班牙人在下游卡罗尼河汇流处建起第一座城镇圣托梅·德·圭亚那，三年后即被荷兰袭掠者摧毁。安东尼奥·德·贝里奥1595年重建此城；1617年沃尔特·雷利率领的英国远征队将其洗劫，雷利之子瓦特在攻城中丧命，雷利本人次年在英格兰被斩首。费尔南多·德·贝里奥1620年再度建城，但英荷袭掠者1629年、荷兰人1637年两次将其焚毁。直到1764年5月22日，华金·莫雷诺·德·门多萨才在狭口定下永久城址，命名为「奥里诺科河狭口的新圭亚那圣托马斯」，简称安戈斯图拉，成为圭亚那省首府。1800年洪堡曾途经此地。独立战争中，1817年4月11日，曼努埃尔·皮亚尔率领的爱国军在奇里卡台地的圣费利克斯击败保王军；守军于当年7月弃城，安戈斯图拉成为共和国的临时首都。1819年2月15日，玻利瓦尔在此召开安戈斯图拉议会，议会于年底宣布成立大哥伦比亚，会期一直持续到1821年。

en:
The Essequibo rises in the Acarai Mountains and runs 1,014 kilometres through forest and savanna to the Atlantic, the largest river between the Orinoco and the Amazon. In 1444 its lower banks, islands and swampy shore were Lokono country, the mainland Arawak people. Arawakan-speaking villagers farmed, fished and travelled by canoe, exchanging river and coastal produce while no European fort yet commanded the mouth.

European ships reached the estuary in 1498, and in 1596 Lawrence Kemys pushed upstream on Walter Raleigh's Guiana venture in search of the fabled Lake Parime. In 1616 Zeelanders under Joost van der Hooge founded the Dutch colony and began Fort Kyk-Over-Al on the Mazaruni, a side channel, using the post for trade with the indigenous population and for plantations where enslaved Africans grew cotton, indigo and cacao. The British seized Essequibo in 1665 and the French plundered it before Zeeland forces returned in 1667. British planters arrived after 1740, and by 1800 Essequibo and Demerara together contained about 380 sugarcane plantations. British privateers took the colony in 1781, the French held it from 1782 to 1783, and the Dutch then returned. A British occupation begun in 1796 was briefly interrupted in 1802 and 1803; Essequibo was merged with Demerara in 1812 and confirmed to Britain by the Treaty of London in 1814.
zh:
埃塞奎博河发源于阿卡拉伊山脉，穿过森林与稀树草原，奔流1014公里注入大西洋，是奥里诺科河与亚马孙河之间最大的河流。1444年，河下游两岸、岛屿与沼泽海岸是洛科诺人的土地，他们是大陆上的阿拉瓦克人。说阿拉瓦克语系语言的村民务农、捕鱼，乘独木舟往来，交换河上与沿海物产；当时河口还没有欧洲堡垒控制。

欧洲船只1498年到达河口。1596年，劳伦斯·凯米斯随沃尔特·雷利的圭亚那远征溯河而上，寻找传说中的帕里梅湖。1616年，约斯特·范德霍赫率领泽兰人建立荷兰殖民地，在支河马扎鲁尼河畔动工修建凯克-奥弗阿尔堡，以此同原住民贸易，并经营种植园；被奴役的非洲人在那里种植棉花、靛蓝和可可。1665年英军夺取埃塞奎博，随后法兰西人劫掠此地，泽兰军队1667年返回。1740年后英国种植园主到来，到1800年，埃塞奎博与德梅拉拉共有约380处甘蔗种植园。1781年英国私掠者占领殖民地，法兰西人1782年至1783年占据，随后荷兰恢复统治。1796年开始的英国占领曾在1802年至1803年短暂中断；1812年埃塞奎博与德梅拉拉合并，1814年《伦敦条约》确认其归属英国。

en:
The Demerara River runs 346 kilometres from the central Guiana rain forest to a shallow Atlantic estuary. Its Lokono name, immenary or dumaruni, meant the river of letter wood. In 1444 Lokono communities moved along its banks and tidal creeks, fishing, planting and using the waterway as a road between forest, savanna and coast. No European fort, sugar works or permanent plantation yet stood on the shore.

Demerara is first mentioned as a trading post in 1691, and on 18 October 1745 the Dutch West India Company made it a separate colony on an uncolonized part of the Essequibo claim, enjoining settlers to keep peace with the Amerindians and respect their freedom and lands. Andries Pieterse became the first planter; within six months 18 large sugar plantations and 50 smaller holdings had been laid out. Laurens Storm van 's Gravesande at first governed from Fort Zeelandia, and in 1755 the administration moved to Borsselen Island while the lower guard post grew into Stabroek. Enslaved Africans carried the labour behind this boom. When Cuffy's Berbice revolt began on 23 February 1763, van 's Gravesande allied with Lokono, Kalina, Warao and Akawaio fighters, prevented the rising from entering Demerara and sent 50 soldiers east. By 1780 nearly 200 plantations lined the river. British forces took it without fighting in 1781, French forces in 1782, and the 1783 Treaty of Paris returned Demerara to the Dutch. A West Demerara slave revolt was crushed in 1795; the British seized the colony in 1796, restored it under the 1802 Peace of Amiens, retook it in 1803, and received formal cession in 1814.
zh:
德梅拉拉河从圭亚那中部雨林向北流淌346公里，注入水浅的大西洋河口。它的洛科诺语名称 immenary 或 dumaruni 意为「蛇纹木之河」。1444年，洛科诺人沿河岸和潮汐溪汊活动，以捕鱼、耕作为生，并把这条水道当作往来森林、稀树草原与海岸的通路。此时岸边还没有欧洲堡垒、制糖工场或永久种植园。

德梅拉拉最早在1691年作为贸易站被提及；1745年10月18日，荷兰西印度公司将其设在埃塞奎博属地内尚未殖民的区域，另立为殖民地，并要求定居者与印第安人和平相处，尊重他们的自由和土地。安德里斯·彼得瑟成为第一个种植园主；六个月内，当地已开辟18座大型甘蔗种植园和50处较小农庄。劳伦斯·斯托姆·范·斯赫拉夫桑德起初从泽兰迪亚堡治理此地，1755年行政中心迁往博瑟伦岛，河口附近的哨站则发展为斯塔布鲁克。被奴役的非洲人承担了这场繁荣背后的劳动。1763年2月23日，科菲领导的伯比斯起义爆发，范·斯赫拉夫桑德与洛科诺、卡利纳、瓦劳和阿卡瓦约战士结盟，阻止起义蔓延到德梅拉拉，同时派出50名士兵东援。到1780年，河两岸已有近200座种植园。英军1781年兵不血刃占领德梅拉拉，法军1782年又将其夺取，1783年《巴黎条约》把它归还荷兰。1795年，西德梅拉拉的奴隶起义被镇压；英军1796年夺取殖民地，1802年依《亚眠和约》归还，1803年再度占领，并于1814年正式获得割让。

en:
Paramaribo lies on the west bank of the Suriname River, about ten kilometres from the Atlantic. In 1444 this low coast was a country of creeks, mangroves and raised village mounds. Lokono (Arawak) communities grew cassava on the higher ground, fished the river mouth and traded along the shore, while Kalina (Carib) groups also moved between the coast and savanna. The earliest Dutch records called an indigenous village near the river mouth Parmurbo, from which the later town took its name. No European power yet held the Guianas, and the canoe routes into the interior belonged to their indigenous users.

In 1613 Nicolaes Baliestel and Dirck Claeszoon van Sanen set up a Dutch trading post at Parmurbo; French and English traders also tried posts nearby. In 1650 settlers sent by Francis Willoughby, governor of Barbados, founded the English colony of Surinam, and in 1651 they strengthened the post as Fort Willoughby. During the Second Anglo-Dutch War a Zeeland squadron under Abraham Crijnssen sailed up the Suriname River and took the fort after a three-hour fight. The Treaty of Breda in 1667 confirmed Dutch control; the stronghold was renamed Fort Zeelandia and Paramaribo became the colony's chief town. The Society of Suriname, chartered in 1683, organized river plantations where enslaved Africans produced sugar, coffee, cocoa and cotton. Many escaped into rainforest Maroon communities, and eighteenth-century wars and treaties forced the colonial authorities to recognize inland Maroon territory and trading rights. British forces occupied Suriname from 1799 to 1802 and again from 1804 to 1816. In January 1821 a fire destroyed more than 400 buildings in the wooden town.
zh:
帕拉马里博位于苏里南河西岸，距大西洋约十公里。1444年，这片低海岸河汊纵横、红树林密布，村落建在堆高的土岗上。洛科诺（阿拉瓦克）人在高地种植木薯，在河口捕鱼并沿岸交易；卡利纳（加勒比）人也往来于海岸与草原之间。最早的荷兰文献把河口附近的原住民村落称作帕尔穆尔博，后来的城市便由此得名。此时还没有欧洲强国占领圭亚那，通向内陆的独木舟水路仍掌握在原住民手中。

1613年，两名荷兰商人在帕尔穆尔博设立贸易站，法国和英国商人也先后在附近建立据点。1650年，巴巴多斯总督弗朗西斯·威洛比派来的移民建立英国殖民地苏里南，1651年又把贸易站加固为威洛比堡。第二次英荷战争中，亚伯拉罕·克莱因森率领泽兰舰队沿苏里南河而上，经三小时战斗夺取要塞。1667年《布雷达和约》确认荷兰的控制权，堡垒改名泽兰迪亚堡，帕拉马里博成为殖民地首城。1683年获许成立的苏里南协会经营沿河种植园，奴役非洲人种植甘蔗、咖啡、可可和棉花。许多人逃入雨林形成马龙社群，18世纪的战争与和约迫使殖民当局承认马龙人的内陆领地和贸易权。英军在1799—1802年、1804—1816年两度占领苏里南。1821年1月，这座木结构城市发生大火，400多栋建筑被毁。

en:
Cayenne occupies an island at the shared mouth of the Cayenne and Montsinéry rivers, behind a mangrove coast. In 1444 Arawak and Palikur groups fished the beaches and creek mouths, while Kali'na (Galibi) communities held much of the shore and nearby islands. They grew cassava and moved by dugout along the coast; a hill above the river would later be named after the Galibi chief Cépérou. No European settlement yet interrupted that canoe-borne world.

Christopher Columbus's fleet sailed along the Guianese coast on 5 August 1498, but Spain never occupied Cayenne. In 1643 Charles Poncet de Brétigny brought 400 French settlers, bought a hill from the Galibis, named it Mont Cépérou and built Fort Cépérou. His introduction of slavery and harsh treatment of indigenous people helped provoke revolt, and by 1648 only 25 French settlers remained. Dutch traders occupied the ruins and, from 1660, developed sugar works around Fort Nassau. In May 1664 Joseph-Antoine Le Febvre de La Barre and Alexandre de Prouville de Tracy took the colony for France. An English force from Suriname sacked Cayenne in August 1667, though the Treaty of Breda returned it to French rule. A Dutch fleet under Jacob Binckes captured the town in March 1676, only for Jean d'Estrées to retake it on the night of 21 December. The surrounding plantations then expanded with enslaved African labour, producing sugar, indigo, cotton and spices. The French Convention abolished slavery in 1794 and the decree was proclaimed in Guiana on 14 June; Napoleon restored it in December 1802. An Anglo-Portuguese force took Cayenne in 1809 and administered it from Brazil until the last occupiers withdrew in 1817.
zh:
卡宴地处卡宴河与蒙特西内里河共同河口的岛屿，前方是红树林海岸。1444年，阿拉瓦克人和帕利库尔人在滩涂与河口捕鱼，卡利纳（加利比）人则据有大片海岸和近岸岛屿。他们种植木薯，乘独木舟沿岸往来；河畔一座高地后来以加利比首领塞佩鲁命名。此时还没有欧洲人定居，这里仍是独木舟串联的世界。

1498年8月5日，克里斯托弗·哥伦布的船队沿圭亚那海岸航行，但西班牙从未占领卡宴。1643年，夏尔·庞塞·德·布雷蒂尼率400名法国移民前来，从加利比人手中买下一座高地，命名为塞佩鲁山并修建塞佩鲁堡。他引入奴隶制，又严酷对待原住民，终于引发反抗，到1648年只剩25名法国移民。荷兰商人随后占据废墟，1660年起在拿骚堡一带经营制糖设施。1664年5月，约瑟夫-安托万·勒费夫尔·德·拉巴尔与亚历山大·德·普鲁维尔·德·特拉西为法国夺取殖民地。1667年8月，一支来自苏里南的英军洗劫卡宴，但《布雷达和约》仍将此地归还法国。1676年3月，雅各布·宾克斯率荷兰舰队攻占卡宴，让·德斯特雷则在12月21日夜收复。此后，周围种植园依靠非洲奴隶劳动扩张，出产蔗糖、靛蓝、棉花和香料。法国国民公会1794年废除奴隶制，法令于6月14日在圭亚那公布；拿破仑又在1802年12月恢复奴隶制。1809年，英葡联军攻占卡宴并由巴西的葡萄牙当局管理，最后一批占领军直到1817年才撤离。

en:
The mangrove coast and seasonally flooded plains of Amapá lie on the north side of the Amazon delta. In 1444 the country behind the shore was held by Arawak- and Carib-speaking peoples, among them the Tucuju, Waiãpi, Palikur and Maracá-Cunani, who farmed raised earth plots, fished and managed groves of bacaba palms. The rivers and channels gave access to the Amazon mouth, but there was no European town or permanent garrison here.

Vicente Yáñez Pinzón sighted this coast in February 1500. During the early seventeenth-century struggle for the delta, Portuguese expeditions from Pará destroyed English and Dutch posts, including the Dutch forts at Muturu and Nassau; in 1637 the Crown granted the Captaincy of Cabo do Norte. French claims survived the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht. A Portuguese military post was set up in 1738, São José de Macapá was founded on 4 February 1758, and work on its riverside fortress ran from 1764 to its inauguration on 19 March 1782. In 1808-1809 Luso-Brazilian and British forces used the area as a base against Cayenne.
zh:
阿马帕的红树林海岸与季节性泛滥平原位于亚马孙三角洲北岸。1444年，海岸后方的土地由阿拉瓦克语和加勒比语诸族群掌握，包括图库鲁人、瓦亚皮人、帕利库尔人和马拉卡-库纳尼人；他们垒起圆形土台耕作、捕鱼，并经营巴卡巴棕榈林。河汊通向亚马孙河口，但此时欧洲人的城镇和常驻要塞尚未出现。

1500年2月，维森特·亚涅斯·平松望见这片海岸。17世纪初争夺三角洲时，来自帕拉的葡萄牙远征军摧毁英国与荷兰据点，其中包括荷兰的穆图鲁和拿骚要塞；1637年，葡萄牙王室封授北角都督辖区。1713年《乌得勒支和约》签订后，法国仍未放弃声索。葡萄牙1738年设立军站，圣若泽·德·马卡帕于1758年2月4日建立；河畔要塞1764年动工，1782年3月19日启用。1808至1809年，葡属巴西与英国军队以此地为基地进攻卡宴。

en:
Guajará Bay, where the Guamá River enters the Pará channel beside Marajó Island, was Tupinambá and Pacajá country in 1444. The Tupinambá knew the broad water as Guaçu Paraná, and their canoes used the igarapés and flooded forests to move between fishing grounds, gardens and camp sites on the edge of the Amazon. No European fort yet commanded the gateway between the great river and the Atlantic, although Marajoara exchange networks had long given the bay value beyond a simple anchorage.

In 1615 Francisco Caldeira Castelo Branco was sent from Portuguese Brazil to check French, Dutch and English trade up the Amazon. On 12 January 1616 he founded Feliz Lusitânia on the bay and raised the straw-roofed wooden Forte do Presépio, the nucleus of Belém. The Tupinambá rose under Guaimiaba and took the fort in January 1619; their attacks paused only for the chief's funeral before resistance continued into 1621. The Portuguese established the Haver-o-Peso customs post in 1625, taxing European goods and Amazonian forest produce, and Bento Maciel Parente strengthened the fort after his 1639 campaign against the Tapajós. The settlement, named Santa Maria de Belém do Grão-Pará, received city status in 1655. Sugar gave way to cattle, then rice, cotton and coffee in the eighteenth century, and in 1772 Belém became the capital of the separate State of Grão-Pará and Rio Negro, brought under the Brazilian colonial administration only in 1775.
zh:
瓜雅拉湾位于瓜马河注入帕拉河道、邻近马拉若岛的地方，1444年时是图皮南巴人与帕卡雅人的土地。图皮南巴人把这片宽阔水域称为瓜苏巴拉纳，他们的独木舟穿行于溪流和泛滥林间，往来亚马逊边缘的渔场、园圃和营地。此时还没有欧洲要塞控制这条大河通往大西洋的门户，但马拉若人的交换网络早已使这里不只是普通锚地。

1615年，弗朗西斯科·卡尔代拉·卡斯特洛·布兰科奉葡属巴西之命北上，阻止法国人、荷兰人和英国人沿亚马逊河贸易。1616年1月12日，他在瓜雅拉湾建立幸福卢西塔尼亚定居点，并竖起茅草顶的木堡普雷塞皮奥堡，这就是贝伦的雏形。图皮南巴人在首领瓜伊米阿巴率领下起事，于1619年1月攻占堡垒；只是为首领举行葬礼才暂停攻势，抵抗一直延续到1621年。1625年，葡萄牙人设立阿韦罗佩索税馆，对欧洲货物和亚马逊林产品征税；1639年本托·马西埃尔·帕伦特征讨塔帕若斯人后又加固堡垒。定居点得名圣玛利亚·德·贝伦·杜格劳帕拉，1655年获得城市地位。17世纪末以后，蔗糖先后让位于养牛以及稻米、棉花和咖啡种植；1772年，贝伦成为独立的格劳帕拉与里奥内格罗国首府，1775年才并入巴西殖民行政体系。

en:
The coast later called Maranhão is cut by the mouths of the Mearim, Pindaré and Itapecuru, whose waters meet the Atlantic around the island the Tupi knew as Upaon-Açu. In 1444 the island and shore held Tupi-speaking communities, among them Guajajara, Urubu and the people later called Tupinambá, while Jê-speaking Timbira and Sakamekra groups occupied the inland forests and savannahs. They farmed, fished and moved between the rivers and seasonally flooded lands, and no European power yet controlled the coast.

Vicente Yáñez Pinzón sighted the coast in 1500, and from 1535 the Portuguese crown included it in the Maranhão grants, though lasting colonization began with French traders. Jacques Riffault left men on Upaon-Açu in 1594, and in 1612 Daniel de La Touche and François de Razilly founded Saint-Louis as the centre of Equinoctial France. Portuguese forces from Pernambuco took it in 1615 and renamed it São Luís. In 1621 the town became capital of the separate Estado do Maranhão e Grão-Pará, a base for missions and expansion toward the Amazon, before the Dutch West India Company held it from 1641 to 1644. Disputes over Indian enslavement and the Maranhão Trading Company helped bring the Beckman revolt in 1684. In the late eighteenth century cotton and enslaved African labour transformed the lowlands, sharply raising exports before the colonial boom faltered after 1800.
zh:
后来被称为马拉尼昂的海岸，被梅阿林河、平达雷河和伊塔佩库鲁河的河口切开，河水在图皮人称作乌帕翁阿苏的岛屿周围注入大西洋。1444年，岛上与岸边居住着图皮语族群，包括瓜雅雅拉人、乌鲁布人和后来所称的图皮南巴人；廷比拉人和萨卡梅克拉人等热依语族群则占据内陆林地与草原。他们农耕、渔猎，随河流与季节性泛滥地迁徙，此时还没有任何欧洲势力控制这片海岸。

比森特·亚涅斯·平松于1500年望见这片海岸，葡萄牙王室自1535年起把它列入马拉尼昂封赐，但永久殖民始于法国商人。雅克·里福约1594年把部分人员留在乌帕翁阿苏岛；1612年，达尼埃尔·德·拉图什与弗朗索瓦·德·拉齐利建立圣路易，作为「赤道法兰西」的中心。葡萄牙军队1615年从伯南布哥赶来夺取该地，改名圣路易斯。1621年，圣路易斯成为独立的马拉尼昂与大帕拉国首府，也是传教和向亚马逊内陆扩张的基地；荷兰西印度公司又在1641年至1644年占据此岛。印第安人奴役问题和马拉尼昂贸易公司的盘剥引发1684年的贝克曼叛乱。18世纪末，棉花与被奴役非洲劳工改变了低地经济，出口迅速增长，但这场殖民繁荣在1800年后趋于衰退。

en:
Crato lies below the Chapada do Araripe, where springs and the valleys of the Granjeiro and Jaguaribe-Mirim rivers make a humid brejo in the dry northeastern interior. In 1444 the country was held by Kariri, Aquijiró, Guariú, Xocó and Quipapaú villages. Their fields and hunting grounds were linked by river valleys, and the reliable water and richer soil gave this district a value rare in the surrounding sertão.

In the seventeenth century, expeditions moving up the Jaguaribe-Mirim were accompanied by clergy who gathered Kariri communities into settled villages. The Capuchin Carlos Maria de Ferrara later organized the Mission of Miranda, also called the Mission of the New Kariris, on the Itaitera River; sugar cane, manioc and grain grew well in its moist lands. A church dedicated to Our Lady of Penha was begun in 1745, the parish was created in 1762, and on 21 June 1764 the settlement was installed as the Vila Real do Crato. When the Pernambucan Revolution of 1817 reached Ceará, the subdeacon José Martiniano de Alencar proclaimed independence from the pulpit on 3 May. Royalist landowners crushed the one-day rising and sent the rebels to prisons in Fortaleza and Salvador.
zh:
克拉图位于阿拉里皮崖壁北麓，格朗热罗河与雅瓜里比-米林河的谷地和泉水在干旱的东北内陆形成湿润的山麓湿地。1444年，卡里里人、阿基罗人、瓜里乌人、绍科人和基帕帕乌人的村社居住在这片土地。河谷连接着他们的农田与猎场，稳定水源和较肥沃土壤使这里在周围干旱高原中格外珍贵。

17世纪，沿雅瓜里比-米林河深入内地的远征队有教士同行，把卡里里诸村聚为定居村落。嘉布遣会士卡洛·玛丽亚·德·费拉拉后来在伊泰拉河组织米兰达传教村，又称新卡里里传教村；湿润土地上种植甘蔗、木薯和谷物。1745年，供奉佩尼亚圣母的教堂开工，教区于1762年设立，1764年6月21日聚落正式安装为克拉图皇家城镇。1817年伯南布哥革命传到塞阿拉时，副执事若泽·马蒂尼亚诺·德·阿伦卡于5月3日在讲坛上宣布独立；保王派地主镇压了这场仅持续一天的起事，并把起事者押往福塔莱萨和萨尔瓦多的监狱。

en:
In 1444 the dunes, river mouths and dry sertão of Ceará were Indigenous country. Potiguara and Tabajara groups, together with Tremembé, Kariri, Anacés and other peoples, controlled the coast, wet valleys and inland highlands. No European fort had yet been raised, although the beaches would soon become meeting places for Tupi-speaking villagers and the French traders who came for brazilwood.

The Portuguese planned settlement as early as 1534, but the first attempts failed. In 1603 Pero Coelho de Sousa built Fort São Tiago near the Ceará River, only to abandon it within a year during a drought. Martim Soares Moreno raised Fort São Sebastião on the same coast in 1612 and, after returning in 1618, anchored Portuguese power through an alliance with the Potiguara. Dutch forces and their Indigenous allies took the post in 1637; the garrison was destroyed in an Indian attack in 1644. Matias Beck arrived in 1649 and built Fort Schoonenborch on the Pajeú, and when the Portuguese took it in 1654 they renamed it Fortaleza de Nossa Senhora da Assunção, the nucleus of future Fortaleza. Ceará became subordinate to Pernambuco in 1680, while cattle ranches, hides, dried beef and cotton linked its sertão to the coast. In 1799 it became a separate captaincy.
zh:
1444年，塞阿拉的沙丘、河口和干旱内陆仍是原住民的土地。波蒂瓜拉人、塔巴雅拉人、特雷门贝人、卡里里人、阿纳塞人及其他族群控制着海岸、湿润山谷和内陆高地。欧洲人尚未在此修筑堡垒，但到下个世纪，海滩便会成为图皮语村人与前来寻求红木的法兰西商人交易结盟的场所。

葡萄牙人早在1534年就计划向塞阿拉移民，最初的尝试却接连失败。1603年，佩罗·科埃略·德·索萨在塞阿拉河口附近筑起圣迪亚哥堡，仅仅一年后便因旱灾撤离。1612年，马蒂姆·苏亚雷斯·莫雷诺在同一海岸修建圣塞巴斯蒂昂堡；1618年他返回后，凭借与波蒂瓜拉人的盟约确立了葡萄牙势力。1637年，荷兰军队及其原住民盟友攻占据点，1644年原住民又袭击荷兰守军，堡垒随之被毁。1649年，马蒂亚斯·贝克到来，在帕热乌河畔修建斯霍嫩博赫堡；1654年葡萄牙人夺取该堡，改名为圣母升天堡，这便是后来福塔莱萨的雏形。塞阿拉于1680年改隶伯南布哥，牧牛场、皮革、肉干和棉花逐渐把干旱内陆与海岸连接起来。1799年，它成为独立的都督辖区。

en:
Oeiras lies in the valley of the Canindé, a seasonal river of the southern Piauí sertão, where caatinga scrub gives way to cerrado and the carnaúba wax palm raises its fronds above the watercourses. In 1444 the land belonged to the Indian bands of the sertão, who hunted and planted along the streams and knew nothing of European herds or boundaries. Two centuries later it was cattle that brought the Portuguese into this country.

From the mid-seventeenth century ranchers pushed inland from the sugar coast, and the Portuguese Domingos Afonso Mafrense opened the valley with his fazendas; the Fazenda Cabrobó, on the Riacho Mocha, was settled in the 1670s and grew into the Vila da Mocha. Two Jesuits built a chapel there in 1697, and when Mafrense died in 1711 he left his estates to the Society of Jesus. John V made the place a vila in 1712, and in 1718, when Piauí was detached from the captaincy of Maranhão, the king named Vila da Mocha its capital. A Jesuit seminary, the first secondary school of the region, opened in 1749; the first governor, João Pereira Caldas, arrived in 1759, and in 1761 the town was raised to a city as Oeiras, honouring the Count of Oeiras, soon to be the Marquis of Pombal. In 1821 it was still the capital of Piauí, a quiet cattle town gathered about its parish church.
zh:
奥埃拉斯地处皮奥伊南部荒原的卡宁德河谷，卡宁德河是一条季节河；两岸是卡廷加灌丛向塞拉多草原过渡的地带，水道旁矗立着巴西蜡棕榈。1444年，这片土地属于荒原上的印第安人群体，他们沿溪游猎、垦地种粮，还不知道欧洲人的畜群和界碑。两百年后，正是牛群把葡萄牙人带进了这个地方。

从17世纪中叶起，牧人从种甘蔗的海岸向内陆推进，葡萄牙人多明戈斯·阿方索·马弗伦塞凭借多处牧场开辟了这片谷地；他在莫沙溪畔的卡布罗博牧场约建于1670年代，后来发展成莫沙镇。1697年，两名耶稣会士在那里建了一座小教堂；1711年马弗伦塞去世，把产业留给了耶稣会。若昂五世1712年将此地升为镇，1718年皮奥伊从马拉尼昂都督辖区分出，国王指定莫沙镇为首府。1749年耶稣会神学院开学，这是当地第一所教授文法与人文学科的中学；首任都督若昂·佩雷拉·卡尔达斯1759年到任，1761年莫沙镇升格为市并改名奥埃拉斯，向奥埃拉斯伯爵、也就是后来的蓬巴尔侯爵致敬。1821年时，它仍是皮奥伊的首府，一座围着教区教堂的安静牧城。

en:
Rio Grande is the elbow of South America around the Potengi River, whose wide mouth gave the Captaincy of Rio Grande its name. In 1444 Potiguara villages of the Tupi family held the dunes, mangroves and anchorage, while Cariri and Tarairiu peoples lived farther inland toward Seridó and the Chapada do Apodi. Coastal peoples exchanged fish, manioc flour and brazilwood along canoe routes, and no European power yet held a permanent fort.

Spanish expeditions reconnoitred the coast around 1500. In August 1501 the Portuguese voyage of Amerigo Vespucci and Gaspar de Lemos erected a possession marker at Touros and called the Potengi the Rio Grande. The Crown included the district in the 1534 captaincy grants, but the 1535 expedition sent for the donatary João de Barros under Aires da Cunha collapsed after heavy losses. French corsairs therefore kept trading brazilwood with the Potiguara. A Portuguese squadron entered the Potengi on Christmas Day 1597; the Barra fortress was begun on 6 January 1598 and completed on 24 June, and Natal was founded at the same anchorage on 25 December 1599. Sugar and cattle spread from the new town. A Dutch attack failed in 1631, but in December 1633 the garrison fell; the fort became Castle Keulen and Natal became New Amsterdam. The Cunhaú and Uruaçu massacres of 1645 sharpened the Catholic and Calvinist conflict, and Portuguese reconquest ended Dutch rule in 1654, after which cattle ranchers pushed inland. In 1817 André de Albuquerque Maranhão seized Natal on 29 March, but his provisional junta fell on 25 April; wounded and imprisoned in the Reis Magos fortress, he died the next day.
zh:
里奥格兰德位于南美洲的东北转角，环绕波滕吉河一带；这条河宽阔的河口后来赋予里奥格兰德都督区名称。1444年，图皮语系的波蒂瓜拉人村社占据沙丘、红树林和锚地，卡里里人与塔赖里乌人则住在更深入内陆的塞里多和阿波迪高地方向。沿海居民沿独木舟航路交换鱼、木薯粉和巴西木，此时还没有任何欧洲势力建立常驻要塞。

1500年前后，西班牙远征队已侦察过这段海岸。1501年8月，亚美利哥·韦斯普奇与加斯帕尔·德莱莫斯的葡萄牙航行在托鲁斯立起占领标柱，并把波滕吉河命名为里奥格兰德。王室1534年将这一地区划入都督封授，但1535年受封者若昂·德·巴罗斯派艾雷斯·达·库尼亚率领的远征队损失惨重、终归失败，法国私商因此继续同波蒂瓜拉人交易巴西木。1597年圣诞节，一支葡萄牙舰队进入波滕吉河口；河口要塞于1598年1月6日动工、6月24日完工，纳塔尔则于1599年12月25日在同一锚地建立，甘蔗种植和牧牛业随后从新城向外扩展。荷兰1631年的进攻失败，但1633年12月攻克守军，把要塞改称克伊伦堡，纳塔尔改称新阿姆斯特丹。1645年的库尼亚乌与乌鲁阿苏屠杀激化了天主教和加尔文宗冲突，葡萄牙再征服于1654年终结荷兰统治，牧牛人随后向内陆推进。1817年，安德烈·德·阿尔伯克基·马拉尼昂于3月29日夺取纳塔尔，但他的临时执政会在4月25日倒台；他受伤后被关入三王堡，次日死去。

en:
The Paraíba do Norte river reaches the sea between Rio Grande and Pernambuco, at the easternmost bulge of Brazil; the cape of Ponta do Seixas nearby is the easternmost point of the American mainland. In 1444 its estuary and the wooded plain behind it belonged to the Potiguara, a Tupi people whose villages grew manioc and fished the shore, while Kiriri and Ariú bands held the dry rising ground toward the Borborema Plateau. Their forests were thick with brazilwood, and within two generations French traders were anchoring in the Bay of Traição to load it.

In 1534 the coast was granted as the Captaincy of Itamaracá, named after the island off its shore, but the Portuguese barely occupied it. In 1574 Potiguara warriors, urged on by the French, wiped out the Tracunhaém sugar mill and its people, opening the Potiguara War and moving the crown to create the Royal Captaincy of Paraíba. With Tabajara allies the colonists broke resistance and in 1585 founded Filipeia de Nossa Senhora das Neves, the first royal city of Brazil under the Habsburg kings; sugar mills spread beneath the Santa Catarina fort raised at Cabedelo in 1589. A Dutch assault was repulsed in 1632, but in 1634 a fleet returned, taking the forts and the abandoned city on Christmas Eve and holding it until the Portuguese reconquest of 1654. From the 1670s bandeirantes pushed upriver into the sertão, and in 1755 Paraíba was annexed to Pernambuco, recovering its separate captaincy in 1799.
zh:
帕拉伊巴河北河在里奥格兰德与伯南布哥之间入海，地处巴西最东端的凸出部，附近的塞沙斯角是美洲大陆的最东点。1444年，河口及其后方林木葱郁的平原属于图皮人的一支波蒂瓜拉人，他们的村落种植木薯、在海岸捕鱼；基里里人和阿里乌人则据有通往博尔博雷马高原的干旱台地。林中盛产巴西木，不出两代，法国商船便已驶入特赖桑湾装运木材。

1534年，这片海岸被封给以近海岛屿命名的伊塔马拉卡都督辖区，但葡萄牙人几乎没有实际占据。1574年，波蒂瓜拉战士在法国人鼓动下血洗特拉库尼亚恩糖坊，波蒂瓜拉战争由此爆发，葡萄牙王室随即设立帕拉伊巴皇家都督辖区。殖民者在塔巴雅拉人协助下平定抵抗，1585年建立「降雪圣母菲利佩亚」，这是哈布斯堡诸君治下巴西的第一座王城；1589年在卡贝德卢修筑圣卡塔琳娜要塞，一座座糖坊在其庇护下扩展开来。1632年荷兰人的进攻被击退，但1634年荷兰舰队卷土重来，于圣诞前夜夺取各要塞和被弃守的城市，占据直到1654年被葡萄牙收复。1670年代起，旗兵沿河向内陆旱源推进；1755年帕拉伊巴被并入伯南布哥，1799年恢复为独立都督辖区。

en:
By 1444 the coast that would be called Pernambuco was a chain of Tupi-speaking villages between the Atlantic and a rainforested escarpment, its red massapê soil shaded by brazilwood groves. The Caeté and their neighbours planted manioc in common fields, fished the reef-guarded inlet that later became Recife, and raided one another for captives taken in ritual warfare. No European had yet charted the shore, but its dyewood was soon to carry them across the Atlantic.

Vicente Yáñez Pinzón made the first recorded European landing in Brazil at Cape Santo Agostinho on 26 January 1500, but the Treaty of Tordesillas left the shore to Portugal, whose ships followed from 1501. Pero Lopes de Sousa stormed a French post run by Bertrand d'Ornesan in 1532, and in 1534 the crown granted the Captaincy of Pernambuco to Duarte Coelho, who took possession in 1535; Olinda became a town in 1537. Sugar made Pernambuco the richest of Brazil's captaincies and by 1600 the greatest sugar region on earth, yet in 1595 James Lancaster sacked its port of Recife in the richest English privateering coup of the age. A Dutch fleet of 7,000 men took Olinda and Recife in February 1630, and from 1637 Count Johan Maurits laid out canal-cut Mauritsstad, patronised the painters Frans Post and Albert Eckhout, and allowed the New World's first synagogue. Planters rose in 1645, won Guararapes in 1648 and 1649, and retook Recife in January 1654.

The Portuguese shopkeepers of Recife, called mascates, grew rich on the Olinda planters' debts, and the feud became the Mascate War of 1710-11, fought in the port's streets. In 1817 masonic plots and the cost of the Rio court kindled the Pernambucan Revolution of 6 March, whose republic fell to royal troops who executed its leaders; Alagoas was split off in reprisal. In 1821 the Beberibe convention drove the Portuguese garrison from Pernambuco, opening the road to Brazilian independence.
zh:
1444年，后来被称作伯南布哥的海岸还是一连串图皮语村落，夹在大西洋与雨林覆盖的崖地之间，红色的马萨佩沃土掩映在巴西木林中。卡埃特人及邻近诸族在公田种植木薯，在后来形成累西腓、有礁石护卫的海湾捕鱼，并互相征伐、掳人用于仪式之战。此时还没有欧洲人测绘过这段海岸，但这里的染料木很快就要把他们引过大西洋。

1500年1月26日，西班牙人比森特·亚涅斯·平松在圣阿戈斯蒂纽角留下欧洲人在巴西有据可考的首次登陆；《托尔德西里亚斯条约》使西班牙无法据为己有，葡萄牙船只从1501年起接踵而至。1532年，佩罗·洛佩斯·德·索萨攻破贝特朗·多尔讷桑开设的法国商站；1534年，王室把伯南布哥都督辖区封给杜阿尔特·科埃略，他1535年到任，奥林达于1537年设镇。蔗糖使伯南布哥成为巴西最富庶的都督辖区，到1600年前后已是世界最大的蔗糖产区；然而1595年，詹姆斯·兰开斯特洗劫外港累西腓，成就了当时英国收益最丰的一次私掠远征。1630年2月，七千人的荷兰舰队攻占奥林达与累西腓；1637年起，约翰·毛里茨伯爵营建运河纵横的毛里茨城，资助画家弗兰斯·波斯特和阿尔贝特·埃克豪特，还容许新大陆第一座犹太会堂设立。种植园主1645年起兵，1648和1649年两度赢得瓜拉拉佩斯战役，1654年1月光复累西腓。

累西腓的葡萄牙店主被蔑称为「马斯卡特」，他们靠奥林达种植园主的债务发家，双方仇怨演变为1710至1711年的马斯卡特战争，港中巷战不断。1817年，共济会密谋和供养里约宫廷的开支点燃3月6日的伯南布哥革命，革命者宣布的共和终被王军扑灭、领袖处死，阿拉戈斯也作为报复被划出。1821年，贝贝里布协议将葡萄牙驻军逐走，为巴西独立铺平了道路。

en:
The province of Bahia takes its name from the Bay of All Saints, which the Tupinambá who fished its mangrove-fringed waters knew as Kirimurê, the 'great inland sea'. In 1444 its shores and the surrounding Recôncavo are Tupinambá country. They had spread north along the coast centuries earlier, clearing fields of manioc around villages of thatched longhouses and paddling the bay in dugout canoes; each village was independent and feuds between them were constant. They knew nothing of Europeans, and Europeans knew nothing of the greatest bay on the Brazilian shore.

On All Saints' Day, 1 November 1501, a Portuguese expedition under Gaspar de Lemos, with Amerigo Vespucci aboard, entered the bay and named it. In 1509 a castaway, Diogo Álvares, whom the Tupinambá called Caramuru, settled among them. The crown granted the captaincy of Bahia in 1534 to Francisco Pereira Coutinho, whose settlement the Tupinambá overran in the mid-1540s; Coutinho himself was killed in a shipwreck in 1547. On 29 March 1549 Tomé de Sousa laid out Salvador on the bluff above the bay as the first capital of Brazil, bringing Jesuits in his company, and the first Brazilian bishopric was erected there in 1551. Sugar engenhos spread across the Recôncavo, and Salvador became one of the busiest ports of the African slave trade in the New World. A Dutch West India Company fleet under Jacob Willekens and Piet Hein stormed and sacked the city on 10 May 1624, but a great Luso-Spanish armada under Fadrique de Toledo retook it on 1 May 1625, and John Maurice of Nassau-Siegen besieged it in vain in 1638. The colonial capital moved to Rio de Janeiro in 1763. On 28 January 1808 the regent John, newly landed at Salvador, signed the decree opening Brazil's ports to friendly nations before sailing on to Rio.
zh:
巴伊亚省得名于万圣湾，在湾畔红树林间捕鱼的图皮南巴人把这片水域称为基里穆雷，意为「巨大的内海」。1444年时，海湾两岸和四周的雷孔卡沃平原都是图皮南巴人的土地。他们在数百年前沿海岸北迁至此，在茅草长屋组成的村落周围开辟木薯田，划着独木舟穿行湾上；各村彼此独立，相互仇杀不断。此时他们不知欧洲人为何人，欧洲人也不知道巴西海岸藏着这样一座大海湾。

1501年11月1日诸圣节，加斯帕尔·德·莱莫斯率领、亚美利哥·韦斯普奇随行的葡萄牙探险队驶入海湾，并以节日为其命名。1509年，遇海难的葡萄牙人迪奥戈·阿尔瓦雷斯流落此间，被图皮南巴人称作「卡拉穆鲁」。1534年，王室将巴伊亚都督辖区封给弗朗西斯科·佩雷拉·科蒂尼奥，他建立的定居点在1540年代中期被图皮南巴人攻破，他本人也于1547年因船只失事身亡。1549年3月29日，托梅·德·索萨在俯瞰海湾的高崖上营建萨尔瓦多，作为葡属巴西的第一个首府，随行的还有耶稣会士；1551年，巴西第一个主教区在此设立。此后甘蔗种植园和榨糖作坊遍布雷孔卡沃，萨尔瓦多成为新大陆贩运非洲黑奴最繁忙的港口之一。1624年5月10日，雅各布·威廉肯斯与皮特·海恩率领荷兰西印度公司舰队攻陷并洗劫城市，但法德里克·德·托莱多率领的庞大西葡联合舰队于1625年5月1日将其收复，拿骚-锡根的约翰·莫里斯1638年又围城不克。1763年，殖民地首府迁往里约热内卢。1808年1月28日，刚在萨尔瓦多登岸的葡萄牙摄政若昂在此签署敕令，向友好国家开放巴西港口，随后启程前往里约。

en:
The island-dotted coast around the Bay of Ilhéus, where the Cachoeira and Almada rivers meet the Atlantic, was held by the Tupiniquim in 1444. Tupi-speaking peoples moving from the Amazon had displaced older Tapuia groups centuries earlier, and the Tupiniquim combined coastal fishing and hunting with gardens in the Atlantic Forest. Their villages controlled the sheltered anchorages later called São Jorge dos Ilhéus, before any Portuguese settlement had been planted on this shore.

On 26 June 1534 John III granted the fifty-league coast as the hereditary Captaincy of Ilhéus to Jorge de Figueiredo Correia, a royal scribe who stayed in Portugal and sent Francisco Romero to occupy it. Romero settled first on Tinharé in 1535 and soon moved his seat to the Bay of Ilhéus, where sugar became the first export crop and the Engenho de Santana received a land grant in 1537. After Figueiredo's death in 1551, Aimoré raids and the Guerra dos Ilhéus of 1559 weakened the town; Mem de Sá broke Tupiniquim resistance with Tupinambá allies at Cururupe. A French raid was beaten off in 1595, and the little Santo Antônio fort was rebuilt in stone and lime in 1611. The eighteenth century brought poverty and shrinking sugar works, but Amazonian cacao spread along the southern Bahian rivers, and by the end of the century the Itaípe canal carried cacao canoes from the Almada to Ilhéus's modest port.
zh:
1444年，伊列乌斯湾一带岛礁散布，卡舒埃拉河与阿尔马达河在此注入大西洋，沿岸属于图皮尼金人。数个世纪前，来自亚马逊方向的图皮语族群把较早的塔普亚族群挤入内陆；图皮尼金人在大西洋林地开辟园圃，也在近海渔猎。他们的村落控制着后来被称为圣若热-杜斯-伊列乌斯的避风锚地，此时葡萄牙人尚未在这段海岸建立定居点。

1534年6月26日，若昂三世把这段五十里格长的海岸作为世系都督府授予王室书记官若热·德·菲格雷多·科雷亚。受封者留在葡萄牙，派弗朗西斯科·罗梅罗前来占守。罗梅罗1535年先驻蒂尼亚雷岛，不久把治所迁到伊列乌斯湾；甘蔗成为最早的出口作物，圣安娜糖坊在1537年获得授地。1551年菲格雷多死后，艾莫雷人的袭击和1559年开始的伊列乌斯战争使城镇衰落，梅姆·德·萨借助图皮南巴盟军在库鲁鲁佩粉碎图皮尼金人的抵抗。1595年法国人来袭被击退，圣安多尼小堡于1611年改用石灰和石块重建。18世纪这里只剩凋敝的糖坊和贫困渔村，但来自亚马逊的可可沿巴伊亚南部河流传播，到世纪末，伊塔伊皮运河已把阿尔马达河上载运可可的独木舟引向伊列乌斯的小港。

en:
The Goias uplands fill the basin between the upper Tocantins and the Araguaia, a sweep of cerrado savanna threaded by riverine forest. On the middle Araguaia the river divides around the Ilha do Bananal, twenty thousand square kilometres of seasonally flooded island where the riverine Karajá and Javaé kept their villages; Xavante and Xerente bands of the Jê family roamed the grasslands between the two rivers, while the Goiá, who gave the whole region their name, lived by the Rio Vermelho to the south. These nations planted maize and manioc, hunted and fished, and in 1444 no European had yet entered their part of the interior.

Jesuits first met the Karajá on the Araguaia in 1658, and the sertanista José Pinto Fonseca surveyed and named the Bananal on 26 July 1773, calling it the Ilha Sant'Ana. The upheaval came from the south, where Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva struck gold in 1725 and Vila Boa rose from 1727, becoming the centre of a new Captaincy of Goiás in 1748. The northern sertão stayed unconquered: Portugal answered its raids with 'pacification' columns, and Tristão da Cunha's campaigns of 1794-1798 broke the Xavante villages, settling survivors in supervised aldeamentos. In 1812 a presidio, Santa Maria, was raised on the lower Araguaia to guard a chartered river-trade company, and on 11 February 1813 allied Xavante, Xerente and Karajá stormed it and drove the garrison downstream.
zh:
戈亚斯高地位于托坎廷斯河上游与阿拉瓜亚河之间，是一片河林交错的塞拉多稀树草原。阿拉瓜亚河中游分岔，环抱约两万平方公里、随季节涨水的巴纳纳尔岛，滨水而居的卡拉雅人和雅瓦埃人在岛上立村；沙万特人与谢伦特人同属热依语族群，游猎于两河之间的草原，后来整个地区得名所自的戈亚人，则住在南方的红河一带。这些部族种植玉米和木薯，兼事渔猎；1444年，还没有欧洲人进入这片内陆。

1658年，耶稣会士最早在阿拉瓜亚河畔与卡拉雅人接触；1773年7月26日，内陆探险家若泽·平托·丰塞卡踏勘并命名巴纳纳尔岛，当时称之为圣安娜岛。变局来自南方：巴托洛梅乌·布埃诺·达席尔瓦1725年发现黄金，博阿镇1727年兴起，1748年成为新设戈亚斯都督府的中心。北部腹地始终未被征服：葡萄牙人以「绥靖」纵队回应袭扰，1794至1798年特里斯坦·达库尼亚的征讨打散了沙万特人的村落，幸存者被编入受监管的村屯。1812年，葡方在阿拉瓜亚河下游修建圣马利亚要塞，为一家特许河运公司护航；1813年2月11日，沙万特人、谢伦特人和卡拉雅人联手攻破要塞，把残军逐向下游。

en:
Diamantina lies in the cold upper ridges of the Serra do Espinhaço, where streams feed both the Jequitinhonha and São Francisco systems. In 1444 there was no Portuguese town or mining camp here; Macro-Jê and other indigenous peoples moved through the valleys, hunted and planted along the watercourses, and knew the quartz ridges long before any European reached the Serro Frio highlands.

Gold seekers entering from the Serro settlements founded Arraial do Tejuco in 1713, when a chapel to Saint Anthony was raised on the slopes of Serra da Lapa. Diamonds found while prospecting for gold were worked clandestinely until the crown officially recognized the mines in 1729, some accounts naming Bernardo da Fonseca Lobo as their discoverer. Portugal created the Diamond District and Intendency of Diamonds in 1734, leased extraction to contractors from 1740, and in 1771 the Marquês of Pombal brought the fields under direct royal administration. Enslaved Africans sustained the lavras, while the freedwoman Chica da Silva shared the household of diamond contractor João Fernandes de Oliveira. Kept subordinate to Serro for easier control, Tejuco became a parish and municipal district only in 1819.
zh:
迪亚曼蒂纳位于埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉寒冷的上部山脊，溪流分别注入热基蒂尼奥尼亚河与圣弗朗西斯科河水系。1444年时，这里还没有葡萄牙人的城镇或采矿营地；大热依语系及其他印第安族群在山谷间往来，沿水道狩猎和耕作，早在欧洲人抵达塞鲁弗里乌高地之前就熟悉这些石英岩山脊。

18世纪初，从塞鲁聚居点进入内地的淘金者被金矿吸引，1713年在拉帕山山坡建起供奉圣安多尼的小堂，特茹科村（Arraial do Tejuco）由此形成。淘金时发现的钻石一度被秘密开采，直到1729年葡萄牙王室才正式承认这些矿藏，部分文献把发现者记为贝尔纳多·达丰塞卡·洛博。1734年，葡萄牙设立钻石区和钻石监督署，1740年起把开采包租给承包商，1771年又由蓬巴尔侯爵将矿区收归王室直接管理。被奴役的非洲人支撑着矿场劳动，获得自由的奇卡·达席尔瓦则与钻石承包商若昂·费尔南德斯·德·奥利维拉共同生活。特茹科长期受塞鲁管辖以便控制，直到1819年才成为堂区和市政辖区。

en:
Porto Seguro lies on the forested coast of southern Bahia, around the mouth of the Buranhém River. Around the year 1000 Tupi-speaking peoples moving down from the Amazon drove the older Tapuia, Jê-speaking hunters, into the interior; by the fifteenth century Tupiniquim villagers farmed manioc on these beaches and fished from dugout canoes, while their Tapuia enemies kept the woods behind the Monte Pascoal hills. The harbor itself was called Nhoesembé. In 1444 no sail from Europe had yet been seen here.

On 22 April 1500 Pedro Álvares Cabral's fleet, bound for India, sighted the hump of Monte Pascoal; the Portuguese first landed the next day and on 24 April anchored in the sheltered roadstead, which Cabral named Porto Seguro, the 'safe harbor'. Two days later Frei Henrique de Coimbra said the first Mass on Brazilian soil at Coroa Vermelha, and the scribe Pero Vaz de Caminha sent the king his famous letter describing the land. Gonçalo Coelho raised a small fort there in 1504, and in 1534 the captaincy of fifty leagues of coast went to Pero do Campo Tourinho, who founded the town and its church of Our Lady of Pena in 1535; brazilwood and sugar worked by enslaved Indians and Africans made its early fortune. The Jesuits built a church and college on the upper town in 1551, and in 1559 the captaincy was sold to the Duke of Aveiro. The fort was strengthened in the seventeenth century, and in 1761 the old captaincy was incorporated into that of Bahia.
zh:
塞古罗港位于巴伊亚南部林木繁茂的海岸，坐落在布拉年河口一带。约公元1000年，自亚马逊方向南迁的图皮语民族把先居于此的塔普亚人——操热语的狩猎部落——逐入内陆；到15世纪，图皮尼金人在这片海滩上种植木薯、划独木舟捕鱼，他们的塔普亚仇敌则据有蒙特帕斯科阿尔丘陵后方的丛林。这座港湾当时名叫尼奥恩森贝。1444年时，欧洲人的船帆还从未在这里出现过。

1500年4月22日，开往印度的佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔舰队望见了蒙特帕斯科阿尔的山影；葡萄牙人次日首次登岸，4月24日在避风的锚地停泊，卡布拉尔将其命名为塞古罗港，意为「安全港」。两天后，恩里克·德·科英布拉神父在科罗阿韦梅利亚举行了巴西土地上的第一场弥撒，书记员佩罗·瓦兹·德·卡米尼亚则向国王发出了那封描述这片土地的著名书信。1504年贡萨洛·科埃略在此建起一座小要塞，1534年这段五十里格海岸的都督辖区封给佩罗·多·坎波·图里尼奥，他于1535年建城并修造仁慈圣母教堂；巴西红木和由印第安与非洲黑奴耕作的蔗糖构成此地早期的财富。耶稣会1551年在高城修建教堂和学院，1559年都督辖区被卖给阿威罗公爵。17世纪要塞得到加固，1761年，这片老牌辖区被并入巴伊亚都督辖区。

en:
The sheltered Bay of Vitória and the Atlantic Forest slopes behind it had no Portuguese town in 1444. Tupinambá and Temiminó villages occupied much of the coast, while Aimoré and Goitacá peoples of the Jê family moved through the forests, the Doce valley and the southern sertão. Their fishing grounds, gardens and trails linked the islands of the bay with inland hunting country, but this was not a single state waiting to receive a European name.

A Portuguese expedition carrying Amerigo Vespucci surveyed the coast in 1501. In June 1534 John III granted fifty leagues between the Mucuri and Itapemirim rivers to Vasco Fernandes Coutinho, who landed at the Prainha anchorage, where Vila Velha later took root, on 23 May 1535, Whit Sunday, and named his settlement Vila do Espírito Santo. Indigenous resistance, French and Dutch intruders and rebellious grant-holders made the early captaincy insecure. Around 1549 Duarte de Lemos founded Vila Nova on Santo Antônio Island in the Bay of Vitória; the seat moved there for protection and, after a Portuguese victory on 8 September 1551, the town was renamed Vitória. Mem de Sá sent troops under his son Fernão, while Jesuits led by José de Anchieta began missionary work. Raiders under Thomas Cavendish in 1592 and Piet Heyn in 1625 were beaten off, with Maria Ortiz prominent in the defence against the Dutch. Small gold finds made by Antônio Rodrigues Arzão near Castelo in 1692 opened routes toward the Minas hinterland. The captaincy reverted to the crown and passed under Bahia in 1718, was restored under Bahian oversight in 1800, gained full autonomy in 1810 and became a province in 1821.
zh:
1444年，避风的维多利亚湾和湾后大西洋林地的山坡上还没有葡萄牙城镇。图皮南巴人与特米米诺人的村落占据海岸大部分地方，艾莫雷人和戈伊塔卡人等热依语族群则活动于林地、多西河谷和南部内陆。渔场、园圃和小路把湾中岛屿与内陆猎地连接起来，但这里并不是一个等待获得欧洲名称的统一国家。

1501年，一支载有亚美利哥·韦斯普奇的葡萄牙探险队勘测了这段海岸。1534年6月，若昂三世把穆库里河到伊塔佩米林河之间的五十里格海岸授予瓦斯科·费尔南德斯·科蒂尼奥。1535年5月23日五旬节，他在后来发展为维拉韦利亚的普拉伊尼亚锚地登陆，把定居点命名为圣埃斯皮里图镇。原住民的抵抗、法国与荷兰船只的侵入以及受封者内部反叛，使早期都督府很不安全。约1549年，杜阿尔特·德·莱莫斯在维多利亚湾的圣安多尼岛建立新镇，治所为求安全迁往那里；1551年9月8日葡萄牙人取胜后，该镇改名维多利亚。梅姆·德·萨派儿子费尔南率军增援，若泽·德·安谢塔等耶稣会士也开始传教。1592年托马斯·卡文迪什和1625年皮特·海因率领的袭击先后被击退，玛丽亚·奥尔蒂斯在抵御荷兰人时尤为突出。1692年，安东尼奥·罗德里格斯·阿藏在卡斯特卢附近发现少量金矿，打开了通往米纳斯内陆的道路。1718年，都督府收归王室并划归巴伊亚管辖；1800年恢复建制但仍受巴伊亚节制，1810年取得完全自治，1821年升为省。

en:
Between the mountains and the sea east of Guanabara lay a flat, waterlogged country of lagoons, sandspits and the Paraíba do Sul floodplain. Tupinambá fishing villages ringed the Araruama lagoon, where the Indians evaporated salt and called the cape Gecay; west of them roamed the Goitacá, a non-Tupi people of the Campos plains who lived by hunting and fishing and had a name for keeping outsiders at arm's length, while Puri bands held the forests further upriver. In 1444 this shore was still a world of lagoon fishermen and Goitacá hunters, with no European settlement anywhere along it.

A Portuguese expedition under Gaspar de Lemos, sailing with Amerigo Vespucci, sighted the low cape in 1501 and named it São Tomé for Saint Thomas. In 1503 a surviving party of the third Portuguese reconnaissance voyage, under Vespucci, built a brazilwood factory guarded by 24 men on the Araruama bar, which Tupinambá warriors destroyed in 1526. The crown granted the coast to Pero de Góis; he landed in 1538 and in 1539 founded Vila da Rainha on the Campos plain, planting sugarcane brought from São Vicente, only for Goitacá and Puri attacks to leave the captaincy abandoned. The French filled the void, raising a stone fort on the same island in 1556 to load brazilwood, and were not dislodged until the Guerra de Cabo Frio of 1575, when the Rio de Janeiro governor Antônio Salema led combined levies from Guanabara, São Vicente and Espírito Santo against the French–Tamoio alliance. The Goitacá were ground down by slave raids and a smallpox epidemic spread among them by the colonists. On 29 May 1677 the Vila de São Salvador de Campos was raised on the Paraíba plains, a country the crown finally pacified by buying the captaincy in 1752; its salt pans, the whaling stations at Búzios and its sugar mills supplied Rio de Janeiro and the gold camps of Minas Gerais.
zh:
在瓜纳巴拉以东，群山与大海之间横亘着一片低平多水的土地：潟湖、沙嘴和南帕拉伊巴河的冲积平原。图皮南巴人的渔村环抱着阿拉鲁阿马潟湖，他们在那里晒盐，把海角称作格凯；在他们以西的坎波斯平原上游荡着戈伊塔卡人——一支非图皮语族的族群，以渔猎为生，素来拒斥外人；更上游的森林里则住着普里人。1444年，这条海岸还是潟湖渔民和戈伊塔卡猎人的世界，沿岸没有任何欧洲人的据点。

1501年，加斯帕尔·德·莱莫斯率领、亚美利哥·韦斯普奇随行的葡萄牙考察队望见这座低矮的海角，以圣多默之名将其命名为圣多美。1503年，葡萄牙第三次海岸考察队的残部在韦斯普奇率领下，在阿拉鲁阿马沙洲建起一座由24人守卫的巴西木贸易站，1526年被图皮南巴战士摧毁。王室把这段海岸封给佩罗·德·戈伊斯；他1538年登陆，次年在坎波斯平原建立维拉达赖尼亚，种下从圣维森特带来的甘蔗，却因戈伊塔卡人和普里人的进攻而使领地沦为废墟。法国人乘虚而入，1556年在同一座岛上修筑石堡装运巴西木，直到1575年的卡布弗里乌战争才被逐出：里约热内卢长官安东尼奥·萨莱马调集瓜纳巴拉、圣维森特和圣埃斯皮里图的联军，击破了法国与塔莫伊人的同盟。戈伊塔卡人则在奴隶猎捕和殖民者有意散播的天花中消亡。1677年5月29日，圣萨尔瓦多-迪坎波斯镇在帕拉伊巴平原设立，王室1752年买下这块领地后地方才告平定；当地的盐田、布齐奥斯的捕鲸站和蔗糖作坊，供应着里约热内卢与米纳斯吉拉斯的淘金营地。

en:
Guanabara, the great coastal bay, was ringed by the villages of the Tamoio, a Tupinambá confederation who farmed manioc on its islands and fished its calm waters. At its mouth rose the granite cone of the Sugarloaf, and behind the shore stood the forested wall of the Serra do Mar. In 1444 the bay had neither a European name nor a European settlement; it belonged entirely to the Tamoio, and the first Portuguese ships would enter it only in 1502.

On 1 January 1502 a Portuguese expedition led by Gaspar de Lemos, with Amerigo Vespucci aboard, mistook the bay for a river mouth and named it Rio de Janeiro, the January River. In 1555 the French admiral Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon landed 500 colonists on an island in the bay and built Fort Coligny, the heart of his France Antarctique, in alliance with the Tamoio. Governor Mem de Sá stormed the fort in 1560, and his nephew Estácio de Sá founded São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro on 1 March 1565; on 20 January 1567 a Portuguese army broke the French and Tamoio outside the town, and Estácio died of his wounds a month later. Sugar and the African slave trade then built the city, which in September 1711 paid a heavy ransom to the French squadron of René Duguay-Trouin. Once gold and diamonds were found in Minas Gerais, Rio became the outlet for that wealth to the Atlantic, and on 27 January 1763 it replaced Salvador as capital of the colony. Fleeing Napoleon, the Portuguese court of Queen Maria I and the Prince Regent John arrived in 1808, founding the Royal Library and the Botanical Garden and licensing Brazil's first newspaper, the Gazeta do Rio de Janeiro. In 1815 Rio became capital of the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves, and so it remained when the court sailed back to Lisbon in 1821.
zh:
瓜纳巴拉这座大海湾四周，是塔莫伊人的村落——这是一个图皮南巴人联盟，在湾中岛屿上种植木薯，在平静的水面捕鱼。湾口矗立着糖面包山的花岗岩奇峰，岸后是森林覆盖、如高墙般的马尔山。1444年，这座海湾既没有欧洲名字，也没有欧洲人的据点，它完全属于塔莫伊人；葡萄牙船只第一次驶入湾内，要等到1502年。

1502年1月1日，加斯帕尔·德·莱莫斯率领的葡萄牙考察队（亚美利哥·韦斯普奇随行）把海湾误认作河口，取名里约热内卢，即「一月之河」。1555年，法国海军将领尼古拉·迪朗·德·维尔加尼翁率500名殖民者在湾中一座岛上登陆，筑起科利尼堡，与塔莫伊人结盟，以此作为「南极法兰西」的核心据点。巴西总督梅姆·德·萨1560年攻陷该堡；其侄埃斯塔西奥·德·萨于1565年3月1日建立圣塞巴斯蒂昂-杜里约热内卢。1567年1月20日，葡军在城外击溃法国人与塔莫伊人的联军，埃斯塔西奥一个月后伤重而死。此后蔗糖和非洲奴隶贸易撑起了城市；1711年9月，勒内·迪盖-特鲁安的法国舰队袭占港湾，里约被迫支付巨额赎金。随着米纳斯吉拉斯发现黄金和钻石，里约成为这批财富通往大西洋的门户，1763年1月27日取代萨尔瓦多成为殖民地首府。1808年，为躲避拿破仑兵锋，玛丽亚一世女王与摄政若昂的葡萄牙宫廷抵达里约，开办皇家图书馆和植物园，并准许出版巴西第一份报纸《里约热内卢报》。1815年，里约成为葡萄牙、巴西与阿尔加维联合王国的首都；1821年王室启程返回里斯本时，它仍是巴西的都城。

en:
Between Guanabara and the island of São Vicente the Serra do Mar runs almost into the sea, leaving a narrow shore of steep green islands, deep channels and Tupinambá villages. The Bertioga channel, held between Santo Amaro island and the mainland, gave sheltered anchorage to the canoes that plied the coast, while the rivers behind Ubatuba and Caraguatatuba were the only doors through the mountains to the plateau. In 1444 this coast belonged to the Tupinambá alone, and no European keel yet lay at permanent anchor in its bays.

The Lemos expedition, with Amerigo Vespucci, charted these shores in 1502, and in 1534 John III created the hereditary captaincy of Santo Amaro for Pero Lopes de Sousa, a strip running from the Juqueriquerê river at Caraguatatuba to Bertioga. Martim Afonso de Sousa had already raised a watchtower at Bertioga in 1531; Diogo de Braga replaced it with a palisade in 1547, which the Tupinambá stormed and burned in 1551. In 1560 the crown built the Forte de São Tiago there, later called São João, the first royal fortification in Brazil, which crossed its fire with the Forte de São Filipe across the channel to cover the approaches to the port of Santos. A whale-oil works at the mouth of the channel and Jesuit missions among the Indians were almost the only colonial enterprises: lacking resources or a road to the plateau, Santo Amaro never prospered, and from the 1620s it shared its lord with the captaincy of São Vicente. On 3 November 1709 the crown bought both captaincies and folded them into the new captaincy of São Paulo e Minas de Ouro.
zh:
在瓜纳巴拉与圣维森特岛之间，马尔山几乎直逼入海，只留下一道狭窄的海岸，遍布陡绿的岛屿、深水水道和图皮南巴人的村落。圣阿马鲁岛与大陆夹峙的贝尔蒂奥加水道，为沿海往来的独木舟提供了避风锚地；乌巴图巴和卡拉瓜塔图巴背后的河流，则是穿越群山、通往高原仅有的门户。1444年，这段海岸完全属于图皮南巴人，还没有欧洲船只会长期停泊在它的海湾里。

韦斯普奇随行的莱莫斯考察队1502年测绘了这段海岸；1534年，若昂三世设立世袭的圣阿马鲁领，封给佩罗·洛佩斯·德·索萨，其地北起卡拉瓜塔图巴的茹克里凯雷河，南至贝尔蒂奥加。马丁·阿方索·德·索萨1531年已在贝尔蒂奥加建起一座瞭望塔；1547年迪奥戈·德·布拉加将其改建成木栅寨，1551年被图皮南巴人攻破焚毁。1560年，王室在原址修建圣雅各要塞（后称圣若昂要塞），这是巴西第一座王家防御工事，与水道对岸的圣腓力要塞炮火交叉，拱卫桑托斯港的入口。水道口的鲸油作坊和在印第安人中传教的耶稣会，几乎是这里仅有的殖民事业：既无值钱物产，也没有通往高原的道路，圣阿马鲁始终未能兴盛，1620年代起便与圣维森特领同封一主。1709年11月3日，王室买下两块领地，将其并入新设的圣保罗与黄金米纳斯领。

en:
The wooded highlands around the Sabará River and the Rio das Velhas were Macro-Jê country long before the Portuguese called the wider region Minas Gerais. Xakriabá, Puri and other related peoples used its river crossings, hunting grounds and village lands, linked by inland trails rather than by the markets of the Brazilian coast. In 1444 there was no European town, royal tax house or gold camp here; the rivers and hills remained under the Indigenous peoples whose world the Paulista expeditions would only enter more than two centuries later.

Fernão Dias Pais's expedition entered the Rio das Velhas backcountry in the 1670s, and Manuel de Borba Gato's camps at Sumidouro and Roça Grande endured after gold was found in the streams. By about 1700 the Arraial da Barra do Sabará was a crowded supply and mining centre on the Estrada Real. The rush also pitted Paulista pioneers against Portuguese and Brazilian newcomers: in the War of the Emboabas of 1707–1709, Sabará was one of the contested mining districts, and the outsiders' victory together with royal intervention broke the Paulistas' exclusive claims. In 1711 the riverside settlements were united as Vila Real de Nossa Senhora da Conceição do Sabará, which became a judicial district seat in 1714. A royal gold office and smelter collected the crown's fifth, churches and fountains multiplied in the wealthy eighteenth century, and the Municipal Theatre opened in 1819.
zh:
早在葡萄牙人把这片广大地区称作米纳斯吉拉斯以前，萨巴拉河与旧河（Rio das Velhas）一带的林木高地就是大热依语族各民族的土地。沙克里亚巴人、普里人及相关族群使用这里的渡口、猎场和村地，彼此以内陆小路相连，并不依附巴西海岸的市场。1444年时，这里还没有欧洲人的城镇、王室税馆或淘金营地，河流与群山仍掌握在原住民手中；要到两百多年后，圣保罗远征队才会进入他们的世界。

17世纪70年代，费尔南·迪亚斯·派斯的远征队进入旧河内陆，曼努埃尔·德·博尔巴·加托在苏米多鲁和罗萨格兰德设立的营地，在河川发现黄金后延续下来。约1700年时，萨巴拉的巴拉营地已是皇家大道上人员稠密的补给与采金中心。淘金潮也使圣保罗拓殖者同葡萄牙本土及巴西其他地区新来者对立；1707—1709年的恩博阿巴斯战争中，萨巴拉是争夺中的采矿区之一，外来者获胜并促成王室介入，打破了圣保罗人的独占主张。1711年，河畔各聚居点合并为萨巴拉圣母受孕皇家镇，1714年成为司法辖区驻地。皇家金务署和熔铸厂征收五分之一金税，繁荣的18世纪建起大量教堂与喷泉，市立剧院则于1819年落成。

en:
Off this coast lay a sheltered island anchorage, separated from the mainland by a narrow tidal channel, while beyond the wall of the Serra do Mar stretched the Piratininga plateau, a country of open grasslands and Atlantic forest. Tupiniquim and Tupinambá groups held the shore, and the nomadic Guaianá roamed the plateau above. In 1444 the island had no Portuguese name, and the escarpment behind it was crossed only by Indian trails.

Gaspar de Lemos's expedition sighted the island on 22 January 1502 and named it for Saint Vincent. Sent to assert Portuguese rule against French smugglers, Martim Afonso de Sousa founded the vila of São Vicente early in 1532, the first formally constituted town in Portuguese America, whose councilmen were elected on 22 August 1532; around 1534 one of the colony's first sugar mills, the Engenho dos Erasmos, began grinding cane on the island. About 1536 a band of Spaniards from the Plate under Ruy Garcia de Mosquera entrenched themselves at Iguape, routed the settlers and sacked São Vicente, and were not driven south until about 1537. High on the plateau the Jesuits Manuel da Nóbrega and José de Anchieta said their first mass at the College of São Paulo de Piratininga on 25 January 1554; settlers moved from João Ramalho's Santo André made a town of it in 1560, and Tupiniquim allies under the chief Tibiriçá beat off the Tamoio siege of 9 July 1562. For the next century the paulistas lived by the great bandeira raids, hunting Indian slaves and opening the sertão. On 22 March 1681 the Marquês de Cascais moved the captaincy's seat from São Vicente to São Paulo; after bandeirantes struck gold in Minas Gerais and the War of the Emboabas followed, the crown bought the São Vicente and Santo Amaro captaincies on 3 November 1709 and made them the captaincy of São Paulo e Minas de Ouro.
