São Paulo became a city on 11 July 1711, and in the later eighteenth century its sugar went down the new Calçada do Lorena to the port of Santos.
zh:
这段海岸外有一座宜于避风的岛屿，与大陆隔着一条狭窄的潮汐水道；岛后马尔山如墙，山那边是皮拉蒂宁加高原，遍布疏林草原与大西洋森林。图皮尼基姆人和图皮南巴人据守海岸，逐猎为生的瓜亚纳人游荡在高处的高原上。1444年，这座岛还没有葡萄牙名字，身后的陡崖上只有印第安人的小径。

1502年1月22日，加斯帕尔·德·莱莫斯的考察队望见该岛，以圣维森特之名为它命名。为对抗法国走私者、宣示葡萄牙主权，马丁·阿方索·德·索萨于1532年初在岛上建立圣维森特镇——这是葡属美洲第一个正式建制的城镇，1532年8月22日选出了镇议会；约1534年，岛上的埃拉斯莫斯糖坊开工榨蔗，是殖民地最早的糖坊之一。约1536年，鲁伊·加西亚·德·莫斯基拉率领一群来自拉普拉塔的西班牙人在伊瓜佩筑垒据守，击败居民并洗劫圣维森特，到约1537年才被逐往南方。在高原之上，耶稣会士曼努埃尔·达·诺布雷加和若泽·德·安谢塔于1554年1月25日在圣保罗德皮拉蒂宁加学苑举行首场弥撒；1560年，若昂·拉马略所建圣安德雷镇的居民奉总督梅姆·德·萨之命迁入学苑周边，城镇初具规模，1562年7月9日酋长蒂比里萨率领图皮尼基姆盟军击退了塔莫伊人的围攻。此后一个世纪里，高原上的「圣保罗人」以深入内陆的旗队为生：猎捕印第安奴隶，开辟腹地荒原。1681年3月22日，卡斯卡伊斯侯爵将领地治所从圣维森特迁至圣保罗；旗队在米纳斯吉拉斯发现黄金、又引发恩博阿巴战争之后，王室于1709年11月3日买下圣维森特和圣阿马鲁两块领地，改建为圣保罗与黄金米纳斯领。1711年7月11日圣保罗正式设市；18世纪后期，当地蔗糖沿新建的洛雷纳石道运往桑托斯港。

en:
Ortelsburg lies among the forests and lakes of southern Masuria, the old Galindian wilderness that the Teutonic Order called the Wilderness. Between 1350 and 1360 Ortolf von Trier, Komtur of Elbing, raised a wooden border fort on the isthmus between two lakes, and on 24 September 1360 he settled Masovian beekeepers beside it; their hamlet of Beutnerdorf, later Bartna Strona, gave the fort its name of Ortulfsburg, in time Ortelsburg. Kęstutis's Lithuanians burned the wooden fort in 1370, and it was rebuilt in stone. Standing on the trade road from Warsaw to Königsberg, it served the Order as a frontier strongpoint against Lithuania and Masovia, and Polish troops occupied it after Grunwald in 1410. In 1444 it was still a small garrison post of the Order's state, with a Polish-speaking hamlet at its gates.

In 1454 the town was incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland with the Prussian Confederation, but it changed hands repeatedly during the Thirteen Years' War and the Second Peace of Thorn in 1466 left it with the Teutonic Order as a Polish fief. In 1525 it passed to the new Duchy of Prussia; the townsfolk were nearly all Polish-speaking Masurians, and in 1538 only five burghers knew no Polish. The old fort decayed until Duke George Frederick turned it into a hunting lodge from 1580, and the craftsmen drawn to the works founded the town of Ortelsburg beside it in 1581. A quarrel over beer-brewing rights with neighbouring Passenheim ended in an armed clash and, on 23 March 1616, in a charter of town rights from Elector John Sigismund. In 1629 Elector George William met King Władysław IV Vasa here to prepare the truce that ended the Polish-Swedish war of 1626 to 1629. Plague struck in 1656, when Tatar raiders also swept through the south, and fires and the plague of 1709 to 1711 checked the town again. From 1744 a Prussian jäger corps garrisoned Ortelsburg and won fame as scouts and sharpshooters. In the winter of 1806 Frederick William III and Queen Louise took refuge there before the French; on 1 December the king issued the Ortelsburg Publicandum on army reform, and French troops occupied and sacked the town on the last day of that year.
zh:
奥特尔斯堡地处马祖里南部的林湖之间，原是古普鲁士加林迪亚人的荒野，条顿骑士团称之为「荒原」。1350至1360年间，埃尔宾长官奥特洛夫·冯·特里尔在两湖之间的陆颈上筑起一座木制边防堡；1360年9月24日，他把马佐夫舍的养蜂人安置在堡旁，他们的「养蜂人村」（后来的巴尔特纳斯特罗纳）使城堡得名奥特卢夫斯堡，日后讹转为奥特尔斯堡。1370年，科斯图提斯率领立陶宛人烧毁木堡，骑士团随即以石头重建。城堡坐落在华沙通往柯尼斯堡的商路上，是骑士团防备立陶宛和马佐夫舍的边境据点，1410年格伦瓦德战役后曾被波兰军队占领。1444年时，它仍是骑士团国家里一座小小的驻军要塞，城门外是一个说波兰语的村落。

1454年，它随普鲁士联盟并入波兰王国，但十三年战争中数度易手，1466年第二次《托伦和约》把它留在条顿骑士团手中，作为波兰的封邑。1525年它转入新立的普鲁士公国；镇上居民几乎全是说波兰语的马祖里人，1538年时只有五名市民不懂波兰语。旧堡日渐倾颓，直到格奥尔格·弗里德里希公爵从1580年起把它改建为狩猎行宫，被工程吸引来的工匠于1581年在堡旁建起奥特尔斯堡镇。后来因啤酒酿造权与邻镇帕森海姆相争，竟酿成一场武装冲突，最终选帝侯约翰·西吉斯蒙德于1616年3月23日颁状授予城市权。1629年，选帝侯格奥尔格·威廉与波兰国王瓦迪斯瓦夫四世·瓦萨在此会晤，筹备结束1626至1629年波瑞战争的停战协定。1656年瘟疫袭来，同年鞑靼劫掠者又横扫南方；此后火灾和1709至1711年的瘟疫一再挫阻城镇的发展。1744年起，一支普鲁士猎兵部队驻防奥特尔斯堡，以侦察和精准射击闻名。1806年冬，弗里德里希·威廉三世与路易丝王后为躲避法军来到这里；国王于12月1日颁布关于军队改革的《奥特尔斯堡公告》，法军则在当年最后一天占领并洗劫了城镇。

en:
Guayrá was the forested plateau bounded by the Paraná River to the west, the Iguazu to the south and the Tietê to the north, cut by the Paranapanema, Tibagi, Ivaí and Piquiri and shaded by vast Paraná pine woods. In 1444 Kaingang bands still held much of the hunting country, but Avá-Guarani villagers were already the strongest agricultural power, clearing riverside fields and contesting paths through the forest; Tupi lands began beyond the Tietê. The indigenous Peabiru road crossed the southern edge toward Santa Catarina and Asunción, yet no Spanish town or mission stood in Guayrá itself.

Aleixo García crossed the region in 1522, and Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca followed its southern route to Asunción in 1542. Spanish settlement began with Ontiveros in 1554; Ruy Díaz de Melgarejo founded Ciudad Real del Guayrá in 1556 and Villa Rica del Espíritu Santo in 1570. Jesuits Manuel Ortega and Tomás Fields worked at Villa Rica in 1588, and after a royal order of 1608, José Cataldino and Simón Mazeta founded the Loreto and San Ignacio reductions from 1610, followed by more than a dozen mission towns along the Paranapanema, Tibagi, Ivaí and Piquiri. In 1628 Antônio Raposo Tavares and Manuel Preto built a fort on the Tibagi, opening the great bandeirante offensive. From late 1631 Antonio Ruiz de Montoya led roughly 12,000 surviving Guaranis downriver on 700 rafts; only about 4,000 reached safety and refounded the missions in 1632. Ciudad Real held out until it was destroyed in 1638, ending Spanish rule. The Treaty of Madrid assigned Guayrá to Portugal in 1750, and in 1821 it remained a sparsely governed São Paulo forest frontier rather than a revived mission province.
zh:
瓜伊拉是一片森林高原，西界巴拉那河，南界伊瓜苏河，北界铁特河，巴拉那帕内马河、蒂巴日河、伊瓦伊河和皮基里河穿行其间，广阔的巴拉那松林覆盖大地。1444年时，卡因冈游群仍据有大片猎场，但阿瓦-瓜拉尼村民已是最强的农耕势力，他们在河畔开垦田地，并争夺穿越森林的道路；铁特河以北则进入图皮人的地域。原住民的佩阿比鲁路从南缘通往圣卡塔琳娜和亚松森，但瓜伊拉境内还没有西班牙城镇或传教站。

1522年，阿莱霍·加西亚穿过此地；1542年，阿尔瓦尔·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡沿其南路前往亚松森。西班牙人1554年建立翁蒂韦罗斯，鲁伊·迪亚斯·德·梅尔加雷霍随后于1556年建立皇家瓜伊拉城，1570年又建立圣灵比亚里卡。耶稣会士曼努埃尔·奥尔特加和托马斯·菲尔兹1588年在比亚里卡传教；1608年王室下令后，何塞·卡尔塔尔迪诺与西蒙·马塞塔从1610年起建立洛雷托和圣伊格纳西奥归化区，此后又在巴拉那帕内马河、蒂巴日河、伊瓦伊河和皮基里河流域设立十多个传教镇。1628年，安东尼奥·拉波索·塔瓦雷斯和曼努埃尔·普雷托在蒂巴日河畔筑堡，揭开旗队大攻势的序幕。1631年底，安东尼奥·鲁伊斯·德·蒙托亚率领约一万二千名幸存瓜拉尼人乘七百只木筏顺河撤离，最终只有约四千人抵达安全地带，并于1632年重建传教区。皇家瓜伊拉城坚守至1638年被毁，西班牙统治至此终结。1750年《马德里条约》把瓜伊拉划归葡萄牙；到1821年，这里仍是归圣保罗管辖、人烟稀少的森林边地，而非复兴的传教区。

en:
Beyond the Serra do Mar, more than nine hundred metres above the Atlantic, the Curitiba plateau mixed open grasslands with forests of the umbrella-shaped Paraná pine. The northern woods were the country of the Kaingang and Xoclengue, Jê-speaking hunters, while Guarani peoples, the Mbyá and Nhandeva, farmed and hunted to the south around the headwaters of the Iguaçu; Curitiba itself is a Tupi name for the abundance of pine nuts. In 1444 only native trails crossed these cold green campos, and the Portuguese on the coast knew nothing of them.

Bandeirantes from São Vicente climbed up from Paranaguá in the mid-seventeenth century, panning for gold along the old Caminho de Queretiba, and in 1649 Eleodoro Ébanos Pereira led the first official mining expedition. Around 1661 a thatched chapel to Our Lady of Light gave its name to the little settlement of Nossa Senhora da Luz dos Pinhais, where Gabriel de Lara erected the pillory in 1668; on 29 March 1693 the capitão-povoador Mateus Martins Leme raised it to a vila and held its first council election. The gold gave out within a generation and the miners drifted to Minas Gerais, but in 1720–21 the royal judge Rafael Pires Pardinho renamed the vila Curitiba and issued rules, even then, requiring leave to cut trees along the rivers. After 1730 the great cattle road from the Rio Grande do Sul by way of Sorocaba to the mines of Minas Gerais turned Curitiba's campos into breeding and wintering grounds for the tropeiros' herds, and in 1812 the town became seat of the new comarca of Curitiba and Paranaguá.
zh:
越过马尔山，在大西洋上方九百多米的高处，库里蒂巴高原上交错着开阔草甸与长满伞状巴拉那松的森林。北部林地是操热语的卡因冈人和肖克伦人的猎场，南方伊瓜苏河源一带则住着务农兼狩猎的瓜拉尼人——姆比亚人和南德瓦人；「库里蒂巴」本身是图皮语地名，意为多松籽之地。1444年，只有土著小道穿行在这片清冷的绿色草原上，海岸上的葡萄牙人对这里还一无所知。

17世纪中叶，圣维森特的旗队从巴拉那瓜翻山而来，沿古老的克雷蒂巴路淘金；1649年，埃莱奥多罗·埃巴诺斯·佩雷拉率领了第一支官方采矿队。1661年前后，一座供奉光明圣母的茅草小堂催生了「松林光明圣母」小村，加布里埃尔·德·拉腊1668年在此立起镇柱；1693年3月29日，殖民统领马特乌斯·马丁斯·莱梅将其升为镇，并举行首次镇议会选举。黄金不到一代人便告采尽，矿工纷纷转往米纳斯吉拉斯。1720至1721年，王室法官拉斐尔·皮雷斯·帕尔迪尼奥将镇名改为库里蒂巴，并颁布规定，即使在当时也已要求砍伐河岸林木须经许可。1730年后，从南里约格兰德经索罗卡巴通往米纳斯吉拉斯矿区的赶牛大道，使库里蒂巴草原成为赶骡人马群的繁育和越冬之地；1812年，此镇成为新设的库里蒂巴-巴拉那瓜司法区治所。

en:
Braslaw occupies a narrow isthmus between the lakes Dryvyaty and Navyata, the site of an early fortified settlement guarding the approaches from the Baltic lake country. From its first mention in 1065 it was a border castle of the Principality of Polotsk. It passed to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania early in the fourteenth century and became one of the strongholds watching the uneasy frontier with the Livonian Order. In the civil war of 1434-1435 Prince Švitrigaila gathered his supporters here, joined by Livonian knights and Tatar cavalry, before his ruin in the campaign that ended at Wiłkomierz. In 1444 Braslaw was a Lithuanian frontier castle whose Ruthenian-speaking Orthodox townsfolk grazed cattle around the lakes.

On 8 October 1500 Grand Duke Alexander Jagiellon, staying in the castle, granted the town a charter of incomplete Magdeburg law. From 1506 the castle and estate belonged to his widow Helena, daughter of Ivan III of Moscow; she settled at Braslaw, founded an Orthodox convent on Castle Hill and died there in 1513. The Habsburg envoy Herberstein passed through in 1517 and wondered at the vast lake beside the town. It remained a small backwater under the Polish-Lithuanian union, receiving its Eye of Providence coat of arms from Stanisław August in 1792 and briefly giving its name to a voivodeship in 1793-1795, after which the Third Partition assigned it to Russia. In 1812 Marshal Ney kept his headquarters here for nine days during the French invasion, before Russian partisans retook the town that autumn.
zh:
布拉斯拉夫坐落在德里维亚特湖与纳维亚塔湖之间的狭窄地峡上，早在1065年的记载中就是波洛茨克公国的边境城堡，扼守波罗的海湖区方向的通道。14世纪初它并入立陶宛大公国，成为监视对立的立窝尼亚骑士团边境的要塞之一。1434至1435年内战期间，斯维特里盖拉亲王在此集结部众，与立窝尼亚骑士和鞑靼骑兵会师，随后在1435年的决战中惨败。1444年的布拉斯拉夫是立陶宛的边塞城堡，说罗塞尼亚语的东正教徒镇民环湖放牧为生。

1500年10月8日，驻跸城堡的亚历山大·雅盖隆契克大公赐予这座城镇不完整的马格德堡法特许状。1506年起，城堡与领地归属他的遗孀、莫斯科的叶莲娜（伊凡三世之女）；她定居布拉斯拉夫，在城堡山上修建东正教女修院，1513年在此去世。1517年，哈布斯堡使节赫伯斯坦路过此地，为城边浩瀚的湖泊惊叹。在波兰与立陶宛联合的体制下，这里始终是偏僻小镇：1792年斯坦尼斯瓦夫·奥古斯特赐下「上帝之眼」纹章，1793至1795年间一度设有以它命名的省，第三次瓜分后划归俄国。1812年法军入侵时，内伊元帅曾在此设置司令部九天，同年秋天俄国游击队收复该镇。

en:
Vitebsk grew up at the mouth of the Vitba where it joins the Western Dvina, on the river road between the Baltic and Black seas. First recorded in 1021, it became the seat of its own principality in 1101, and in 1321 it entered the Grand Duchy of Lithuania by inheritance, when Algirdas married Maria, daughter of its last prince; stone Upper and Lower Castles stood by 1351. In 1441 Vitebsk was counted among the fifteen largest cities of the grand duchy. In 1444 it was a major Orthodox Ruthenian trading town, whose merchants carried goods between the Dvina and the Dnieper basins.

Early in the sixteenth century it became the seat of Vitebsk Voivodeship, and in 1597 it received Magdeburg law and a coat of arms. The quarrel over the Union of Brest reached the town on 12 November 1623, when Orthodox burghers killed Josaphat Kuntsevych, the Uniate archbishop of Polotsk; the crown punished Vitebsk by withdrawing its Magdeburg rights, restored only in 1644. A Russian-Cossack army took the town by siege in 1654 during the Thirteen Years' War, though the Truce of Andrusovo returned it in 1667, and the Jesuit collegium ran a school theatre from 1641. In 1772, under the First Partition, Vitebsk passed to Russia, becoming the seat of a province in 1772 and of Vitebsk Governorate in 1802; by the later eighteenth century it was the second-largest town of the Belarusian lands after Mogilev. Fighting on the Luchosa river outside Vitebsk on 26-27 July 1812 delayed Napoleon for two days before the French occupied the town.
zh:
维捷布斯克兴起于维季巴河注入西德维纳河的河口，地处波罗的海与黑海之间的水路上。它1021年首见记载，1101年成为独立公国的都城；1321年，阿尔吉尔达斯娶末位维捷布斯克公爵之女玛丽亚，以继承方式将此地并入立陶宛大公国，到1351年已建起石砌的上堡与下堡。1441年，维捷布斯克名列大公国十五座最大城市。1444年时，它是一座重要的东正教鲁塞尼亚商镇，商人在西德维纳河与第聂伯河流域之间转运货物。

16世纪初，这里成为维捷布斯克省的治所，1597年获得马格德堡法和城徽。围绕布列斯特联合的争端在1623年11月12日殃及此城：东正教徒市民杀死了波洛茨克的东仪派大主教约萨法特·昆采维奇；王室褫夺维捷布斯克的马格德堡法作为惩罚，直到1644年才恢复。十三年战争中，俄-哥萨克联军于1654年围攻夺取此城，1667年安德鲁索沃停战协定又把它归还；1641年起，耶稣会学院在此办有校园剧场。1772年第一次瓜分波兰后，维捷布斯克并入俄罗斯，1772年成为省治，1802年改为维捷布斯克省省会；到18世纪后期，它是白俄罗斯土地上仅次于莫吉廖夫的第二大城。1812年7月26至27日，维捷布斯克城外卢乔萨河上的战斗把拿破仑阻滞了两天，随后法军占领该城。

en:
The lands around the future Paysandú lie on the east bank of the Uruguay River, where open pastures meet wooded stream valleys. In 1444 there was no Spanish town here. Charrúa, Chaná and Minuane bands moved with the seasons: summer brought them to the river to fish and gather shellfish, while winter camps inland hunted deer and rheas with bolas and bows. The river crossings and grazing grounds were shared country, not a fixed frontier.

Spanish and Portuguese rivalry reached the Banda Oriental long before a permanent town took shape. A Jesuit map by José Quiroga Méndez marked Paysandú in 1749, and colonial documents called the crossing the Paso de Paisandú in 1754; the First Treaty of San Ildefonso placed this southern part of the eastern bank under Spain in 1777. The landing became a river port and saladero, where cattle were turned into tasajo and hides for trade. A parish was created in 1805 and Benito Chain laid out the town in 1810. José Artigas crossed here in 1811 to lead the Oriental revolution, and in 1815 his headquarters briefly made small Paysandú the provisional capital of the Orientals.
zh:
未来派桑杜周围的土地位于乌拉圭河东岸，开阔牧场与林木溪谷相接。1444年时这里还没有西班牙城镇。查鲁亚、查纳和米努安人的游群随季节迁徙：夏天到河边捕鱼、采集贝类，冬天在内地扎营，用流星锤和弓箭猎鹿和美洲鸵。渡口与草场是共同使用的土地，而不是固定边界。

早在固定城镇成形前，西班牙与葡萄牙的争夺已经延伸到东部海岸。何塞·基罗加·门德斯的耶稣会地图1749年已标出派桑杜，殖民地文献1754年把这处渡口称为Paso de Paisandú；1777年《第一次圣伊尔德方索条约》将东岸南段划归西班牙。这个登陆点后来成为河港和腌肉场，牛只被加工成肉干和皮革出售。1805年这里设立教区，1810年贝尼托·查因规划城镇。何塞·阿蒂加斯1811年由此渡河，领导东岸革命；1815年，他的总司令部一度使小小的派桑杜成为东岸人的临时首都。

en:
The eastern part of the Banda Oriental is a land of Atlantic dunes, coastal lagoons and open grasslands, with the Cerro de San Miguel rising south of Laguna Merín. In 1444 it was Guenoa country, a people colonial sources group with the Charrúa. There were no stone forts or fixed imperial frontiers; bands followed game across the plains and used the lagoons, shore and stream valleys according to the season.

European cattle later multiplied as feral herds, and by the eighteenth century their hides drew smugglers and slaughter crews to the eastern grasslands. A Spanish fieldwork stood on the Cerro de San Miguel in 1734; Portuguese forces occupied it three years later and began the stone fort on 17 October 1737, a work attributed to Brigadier José da Silva Paes. Its hundred-man garrison watched Spanish movements, and the Treaty of Madrid in 1750 allowed Portugal to keep and strengthen the Castillos Grande line. Pedro de Cevallos took San Miguel in April 1763 after the Portuguese had begun the nearby Fortaleza de Santa Teresa the previous October. Bernardo Lecocq strengthened the works in 1775, the Treaty of San Ildefonso confirmed Spanish possession in 1777, and repairs in 1797 kept the bastion ready for war.
zh:
东岸东部是一片由大西洋沙丘、沿海潟湖和开阔草原组成的土地，圣米格尔山耸立在梅林潟湖以南。1444年时，这里是格诺阿人的土地，殖民地文献把格诺阿人归入查鲁亚人群体。当时还没有石堡或固定的帝国边界；游群在草原上追逐猎物，并按季节利用潟湖、海岸和溪谷。

欧洲牛只后来在平原上野化繁殖，到18世纪，牛皮把走私者和屠宰队吸引到东部草原。1734年，圣米格尔山上已有一座西班牙野战工事；三年后葡萄牙军队将其占领，并于1737年10月17日开始修建石堡，工程通常归于准将何塞·达席尔瓦·派斯。百名驻军负责监视西班牙军队的动向，1750年的《马德里条约》允许葡萄牙保留并加固大卡斯蒂略斯防线。佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯于1763年4月夺取圣米格尔；此前一个10月，葡萄牙人已开始在附近修建圣特蕾莎要塞。贝尔纳多·勒科克1775年加固工事，1777年《圣伊尔德方索条约》确认西班牙占有该地，1797年的修缮使这座棱堡继续处于战备状态。

en: Al-Junaynah, called El Geneina or the 'little garden' in Arabic, is a watered basin and caravan crossing on the Darfur-Wadai frontier, surrounded by the Masalit homeland of Dar Masalit. In 1444 its farmers and herders lived under the fringe of Tunjur power, which had grown out of the old Daju lands and linked Darfur with Ouaddaï. In 1635 Abd al-Karim overthrew the Tunjur king Daud, founded Wadai's Kolak dynasty at Wara, and sealed alliances with Masalit and Dajo families. After Muhammad Sabun took power in 1804, Wadai fitted out royal caravans for the route through Ennedi and Kufra to Benghazi, drawing livestock, ivory, and captives from this western borderland into trans-Saharan commerce.
zh: 朱奈纳（Al-Junaynah，阿拉伯语意为「小花园」）是达尔富尔与瓦达伊边界上一处有水的盆地和商队通道，周围是马萨利特人的家园达尔马萨利特。1444年，此地的农民和牧人处在通朱尔势力边缘；通朱尔人在旧达朱土地上崛起，把达尔富尔与瓦达伊边地连成一片。1635年，阿卜杜勒·卡里姆推翻通朱尔国王达乌德，在瓦拉建立瓦达伊的科拉克王朝，并以联姻笼络马萨利特和达朱家族。1804年穆罕默德·萨本掌权后，瓦达伊组织王室商队，取道恩内迪和库夫拉前往班加西，使这片西部边地的牲畜、象牙和人口被卷入跨撒哈拉贸易。

en:
The land beside the Paraguay River that would become Asunción belonged in 1444 to Guarani-speaking Cario communities. Their villages, fields, and river crossings occupied the bay where Spanish ships later anchored; Guaraní alliance-making and kinship would do as much as Spanish conquest to shape the province. For nearly another century the region remained outside the Atlantic world being opened by European voyagers.

Juan de Salazar y Espinosa raised the fort of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción on 15 August 1537, and Domingo Martínez de Irala's cabildo of 16 September 1541 turned it into a city. Refugees from the abandoned first Buenos Aires soon made it the base from which expeditions refounded Buenos Aires and founded towns across the Río de la Plata basin. The 1603 Synod of Asunción directed Guaraní-language evangelization, while the governorship seated here passed from the Viceroyalty of Peru to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776 and became the Intendency of Paraguay in 1782. José de Antequera y Castro's comunero revolt, crushed in 1731, was an early criollo challenge to viceregal authority. On 14–15 May 1811 Asunción overthrew Governor Bernardo de Velasco, and from 1813 Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia gave the new republic its isolationist rule.
zh:
1444年，后来成为亚松森的巴拉圭河畔土地属于讲瓜拉尼语的卡里奥人社群。他们的村落、农田和渡口占据着日后西班牙船只停泊的河湾；瓜拉尼人的结盟与亲属制度日后同西班牙征服一起塑造了这个省份。此后近一百年间，这片地区仍处在欧洲航海者正在打开的大西洋世界之外。

1537年8月15日，胡安·德·萨拉查·伊·埃斯皮诺萨建起圣母升天堡；1541年9月16日，多明戈·马丁内斯·德·伊拉拉设立市政会，把要塞升格为城市。第一次布宜诺斯艾利斯被弃守后，逃难者来到这里，使亚松森成为远征队再建布宜诺斯艾利斯、并在拉普拉塔河流域建立诸城的基地。1603年的亚松森主教会议规定以瓜拉尼语传教。驻节于此的巴拉圭督辖区原属秘鲁总督辖区，1776年划入拉普拉塔总督辖区，1782年改为巴拉圭监政区。何塞·德·安特克拉·伊·卡斯特罗领导的公社社员起义于1731年被镇压，是土生白人挑战总督权威的先声。1811年5月14日至15日，亚松森推翻总督贝纳尔多·德·贝拉斯科；1813年起，加斯帕尔·罗德里格斯·德·弗朗西亚把新生共和国带入孤立主义统治。

en:
The wooded banks and crossings north of Asunción had no Spanish town in 1444. Guarani-speaking villagers lived east of the Paraguay River, while Mbayá bands ranged the northern Chaco across and upstream; the Guarani gave these feared raiders the name Mbayá, and Spaniards later grouped them with the Guaycurú. The river was therefore a frontier rather than a fixed border, linking peoples who would meet as enemies and allies after European ships entered the basin.

Colonial settlement came late and under arms. Bandeirantes pushed in from the east, and after acquiring horses Mbayá bands raided Spanish holdings and Guarani villages. Jesuits founded Belén as a mission among the Mbayá in 1760, and Governor Agustín Fernando de Pinedo planted Villa Real de la Concepción in 1773 as a military town guarding the Portuguese frontier. The garrison settlement kept that role for forty years until a cabildo was created in 1812. In 1813 José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia established the penal colony of Tevego in this northern territory, using frontier settlement to secure the young republic's border.
zh:
1444年，亚松森以北林木覆盖的巴拉圭河畔还没有西班牙城镇。讲瓜拉尼语的村社生活在河东，姆巴亚人则在对岸和上游的北查科活动；瓜拉尼人赋予这些可怕袭掠者的名字便是姆巴亚，西班牙人后来把他们归入瓜伊库鲁人。与其说巴拉圭河是固定边界，不如说是一条边疆通道；欧洲船只进入流域后，两岸居民将在战和之间相遇。

殖民定居来得很晚，而且从一开始就带着军事性质。巴西的班德拉捕奴队从东方压入，姆巴亚人获得马匹后又袭击西班牙据点和瓜拉尼村社。1760年，耶稣会在姆巴亚人中建立贝伦传教村；1773年，总督阿古斯丁·费尔南多·德·皮内多设立王家康塞普西翁镇，把它当作守卫葡萄牙边境的军镇。此后四十年间它一直承担驻军职能，1812年设立市政会后才转为民政居民点。1813年，何塞·加斯帕尔·罗德里格斯·德·弗朗西亚在这片北部领地建立特韦戈流放地，以定居和管控来巩固新生共和国的北疆。

en:
At the bend where the Paraná turns south, some fifty kilometres below its meeting with the Paraguay, seven rocky points jut into the river and throw up fast currents, the siete corrientes that give the place its Spanish name; the Guarani know it as Taragüí. In 1444 this was Guarani country. Large communal villages, the tekoá, lined the Paraná and the Uruguay, where people grew maize and manioc and fished the river, raiding their old enemies the Charrúa away to the south-east, while Kaingang bands held the woods to the east. No European had yet reached the bend; the first ships, Sebastian Cabot's, only entered the Paraná in 1527 and went on to the Paraguay.

On 3 April 1588 the adelantado Juan Torres de Vera y Aragón, with Alonso de Vera y Aragón and Hernandarias, founded a way-station on the flood-free high bank between Asunción and Buenos Aires: Ciudad de Vera de las Siete Corrientes, settled first by 148 colonists from Asunción and Concepción de Buena Esperanza on the Bermejo. Itatí, Santa Lucía and Santa Ana de los Guácaras were laid out the same year as Indian towns, and a royal cedula of 30 January 1609 opened the north-east to the Jesuit reductions. The town stayed small, about forty vecinos in the 1620s, yet its shipyards built for the whole viceroyalty and its hides went downriver to market. Correntino comuneros rose against Governor Zabala in 1732 and again under Ceballos thirty years later. The Cazadores Correntinos militia helped defend Buenos Aires during the English invasions of 1806 and 1807, and in 1810 the cabildo joined the May Revolution as Belgrano's little army passed through on its way to Paraguay. An open cabildo in 1814 recognized Artigas as Protector of the Free Peoples, and from 1818 to 1819 the province was governed by his Guarani lieutenant Andrés Guazurarí, known as Andresito.
zh:
巴拉那河在这里折向南流，下游约五十公里便是它与巴拉圭河的交汇处；河岸七道石岬伸入江中，激起股股急流——西班牙语「七股急流」（Siete Corrientes）由此得名，瓜拉尼语则称此地为塔拉圭（Taragüí）。1444年，这里还是瓜拉尼人的土地。巴拉那河与乌拉圭河畔分布着瓜拉尼人的大型村社tekoá，村民种玉米、木薯，下河捕鱼，不时与东南方的宿敌查鲁亚人交战；东边丛林里则住着卡因冈人。此时还没有任何欧洲人到过这道河湾，直到1527年，塞瓦斯蒂安·卡博特的船队才驶入巴拉那河，并继续上溯到巴拉圭河。

1588年4月3日，殖民督办胡安·托雷斯·德·贝拉-亚拉贡在阿隆索·德·贝拉-亚拉贡与埃尔南达里亚斯协助下，在不受洪水威胁的高岸建起亚松森与布宜诺斯艾利斯之间的驿站——「七急流的贝拉城」（Ciudad de Vera de las Siete Corrientes），最早的148名居民来自亚松森和贝尔梅霍河畔的布埃纳埃斯佩兰萨。同年，伊塔蒂、圣卢西亚和圣安娜-德洛斯瓜卡拉斯作为印第安人村镇设立；1609年1月30日的国王敕令又为耶稣会在东北方建立传教区打开大门。城镇长期很小，1620年代只有约四十户市民，它的造船厂却为整个拉普拉塔总督辖区造船，兽皮也顺河运往市场。1732年，科连特斯的公社派起事反对总督萨瓦拉，约三十年后塞瓦约斯任内又起波澜。1806至1807年英国入侵拉普拉塔时，「科连特斯猎兵」民团参加了保卫布宜诺斯艾利斯的战斗；1810年市议会响应五月革命，贝尔格拉诺的小股部队经此出征巴拉圭。1814年，开放市政会承认阿蒂加斯为「自由人民保护者」；1818至1819年，执掌省政的是阿蒂加斯的瓜拉尼人副将安德列斯·瓜苏拉利，人称「小安德列斯」。

en:
The Río de la Plata is the vast freshwater estuary where the Paraná and Uruguay rivers pour into the Atlantic, backed on its southern shore by the flat, unbroken grassland of the pampas. In 1444 no city stood on its banks. Charrúa bands ranged the northern shore and the open pampas, while Querandí hunters held the country around the future Buenos Aires. They were wanderers without masters, living on the guanaco and the rhea, running game down on foot and hobbling it with the boleadora, pitching skin tents wherever the hunting was good. The Inca world ended far to the north among the Andes, and as yet no European ship had entered the great river.

In 1516 Juan Díaz de Solís became the first European to sail into the estuary, and was killed on its Uruguayan shore by Charrúa warriors. Pedro de Mendoza founded Puerto de Nuestra Señora del Buen Ayre on 2 February 1536, but famine and Querandí attacks drove the settlers out, and at the end of June 1541 the Spaniards themselves burned and abandoned the post. A permanent town rose only on 11 June 1580, when Juan de Garay came down the Paraná from Asunción with some three hundred settlers, many of them Guaraní families, and laid out the Ciudad de la Trinidad above its anchorage. For two centuries the Crown forced its trade through Lima and Seville, so the porteños grew rich instead on smuggled cloth and the hides of feral cattle; their capture of the Portuguese Colonia del Sacramento in 1680 showed their growing strength. In 1776 Buenos Aires became capital of the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. British troops seized the city in 1806 only to be thrown out by Santiago de Liniers, who repelled a second invasion in 1807. On 25 May 1810 a junta in the cabildo deposed Viceroy Cisneros, opening the war that ended Spanish rule.
zh:
拉普拉塔河是巴拉那河与乌拉圭河汇入大西洋形成的宽阔淡水河口，南岸连着平坦无垠的潘帕斯草原。1444年，河岸边还没有一座城市：查鲁亚人的游群活动在北岸和开阔草原上，克兰迪猎人则占据着日后布宜诺斯艾利斯一带的土地。他们是不受任何人统治的游动猎手，以原驼和美洲鸵为生，徒步追逐猎物，用流星索将其绊倒，在猎物丰足处支起兽皮帐篷。印加人的世界远在北方的安第斯群山间便到了尽头，此时也还没有欧洲船只驶入这条大河。

1516年，胡安·迪亚斯·德·索利斯成为第一个驶入河口的欧洲人，却在今日乌拉圭一侧的岸上被查鲁亚武士杀死。1536年2月2日，佩德罗·德·门多萨建立了「善风圣母港」，但饥荒与克兰迪人的袭击逼走了殖民者，1541年6月底，西班牙人自己烧毁并放弃了据点。永久的城市直到1580年6月11日才出现：胡安·德·加赖从亚松森顺巴拉那河而下，带着约三百名移民（其中多为瓜拉尼人家族），在锚地旁的高地上建起「三一城」。此后两百年间，王室强迫贸易绕道利马和塞维利亚，港口人转而靠走私布匹和剥取野牛皮致富；1680年他们攻下葡萄牙人建立的萨克拉门托殖民地，声势日盛。1776年，布宜诺斯艾利斯成为新设拉普拉塔总督辖区的首府。1806年英军一度占领该城，圣地亚哥·德·利尼耶斯将其逐出，又于1807年击退第二次入侵。1810年5月25日，市政会议成立执政委员会，废黜总督西斯内罗斯，终结西班牙统治的战争由此展开。

en:
The Tandilia and Ventana hills rise from the grass plains between the Salado River and the Atlantic, the southern edge of the country the Spaniards called the Pampas. In 1444 their glens, and the empty coast beyond, were roamed by small bands of Serranos, northern Tehuelche groups the Jesuit Thomas Falkner later counted among the Het and the Spaniards knew as Puelches. They were nomadic hunters of guanaco and rhea, armed with the bolas, living in leather tents, moving with their quarry and constantly at war with the Pampas bands to the north. No European ship had yet touched this shore, and the plains belonged entirely to them.

In 1520 Magellan's fleet sailed past this coast. Horses and feral cattle from the Spanish settlements on the Río de la Plata gradually changed the hunt, and the hill country became the stronghold of the Serrano cacique Cangapol, called 'the Brave': after the treaties at Sierra de la Ventana in 1742, Governor Salcedo's envoys recognized his people at Tandil and Sierra Chica, fixed the Río Saladillo as the frontier and licensed the 'poncho fair' at Tandil. In 1746 the Jesuits José Cardiel and Thomas Falkner opened the mission of Nuestra Señora del Pilar by the coastal lagoons, abandoned in 1751. About 1770 a Spanish expedition crossed the Tandil range, and in 1782 the cacique Lorenzo Calpisqui, whose sway ran between the Tandil and Ventana hills, made peace in Buenos Aires and was acknowledged 'principal cacique of all the Pampas', renewing it in 1790. In 1821 no Spanish town yet stood on these hills.
zh:
坦迪利亚山与本塔纳山矗立在萨拉多河与大西洋之间的草原上，这里是西班牙人所称潘帕斯草原的南缘。1444年，群山的山谷和更南方荒无人烟的海岸由塞拉诺人的小股游群往来游猎——他们是北特维尔切人的一支，耶稣会士托马斯·福克纳后来把他们归入海特人，西班牙人则称之为普埃尔切人。他们是追逐羊驼和美洲鸵的游猎部族，以投石索为武器，住兽皮帐篷，随猎物迁徙，并不断与北方的潘帕斯诸部交战。此时还没有欧洲船只靠过这段海岸，整片草原都属于他们。

1520年，麦哲伦的船队从这段海岸外驶过。来自拉普拉塔河畔殖民点的马匹和野化牛群逐渐改变了这里的狩猎生活，山区后来成为塞拉诺酋长坎加波尔（人称「勇者」）的根据地：1742年本塔纳山和约之后，萨尔塞多总督的使者承认他的部众驻牧于坦迪尔和奇卡山，以萨拉迪约河为界，并准许在坦迪尔举办「篷乔集市」。1746年，耶稣会士何塞·卡迭尔与托马斯·福克纳在滨海潟湖畔建立皮拉尔圣母传教所，1751年即告废弃。约1770年，一支西班牙探险队越过坦迪尔山地。1782年，势力横亘坦迪尔山与本塔纳山之间的酋长洛伦索·卡尔皮斯基在布宜诺斯艾利斯议和，被承认为「全潘帕斯大酋长」，并于1790年重申和约。到1821年，这些山间还没有一座西班牙人的城镇。

en: The low, salt-white shores around Bahía Blanca mark the southern edge of the Pampas. In 1444 mobile Gününa küna bands, called Puelche by Mapuche-speakers, and related northern Patagonian groups moved through this coast; they hunted guanaco and rhea with bows and bolas, camped in skin tents by streams and estuaries, and lived in small family bands under elders. Ferdinand Magellan's fleet sighted the bay in 1520 while searching for a strait to the Pacific, yet European ships long remained visitors. Epidemics in the late eighteenth century greatly reduced the Gününa küna, with survivors merging into Mapuche and Tehuelche communities; in 1805 the Spanish crown ordered a formal survey of this poorly mapped coast.
zh: 布兰卡港周围低矮、盐色发白的海岸是潘帕斯草原的南缘。1444年，被马普切语称为普埃尔切人的居努纳·库纳人群体，以及相近的北巴塔哥尼亚人群，在这一带迁徙活动；他们猎取原驼和美洲鸵，使用弓箭与投石索，在溪流和河口旁支起兽皮帐篷，以长者率领的小型家族群为单位生活。1520年，斐迪南·麦哲伦的船队在寻找通往太平洋的海峡时望见这座海湾，但欧洲船只在很长时间里仍只是沿岸过客。18世纪末的疫病使居努纳·库纳人口大减，幸存者融入马普切人和特维尔切人；1805年，西班牙王室下令正式勘测这条仍缺少精确地图的海岸。

en:
Puerto Deseado occupies one of Patagonia's finest natural harbors, a narrow, roughly twenty-mile ria where the Deseado River meets the Atlantic. The dry hills and shoreline were not empty in 1444: Aónikenk Tehuelche bands camped on the coast during winter for fish, shellfish and seals, then followed guanaco and rhea toward the open steppe and uplands in summer. They moved with the seasons rather than building a town, and the deep inlet was a reliable landing place long before European ships arrived.

In March 1520 the Magellan-Elcano expedition, driven in by a storm, entered the inlet and named it Bahía de los Trabajos Forzosos. Thomas Cavendish returned on 17 December 1586 aboard the Desire, called the anchorage Port Desire, and remained ten days under Tehuelche arrow fire; the headland at the mouth became Punta Cavendish. John Narborough claimed the coast for England in 1670, but his expedition failed to occupy it. A Spanish camp placed by Antonio de Viedma in April 1780 lasted only seven months. In 1789 the Real Compañía Marítima tried a permanent fishing station, adding a chapel, hospital, fields, salting works and the Todos los Santos and San Carlos forts. Whales were scarce, sea lions could not sustain the enterprise, supply costs and desertions mounted, and the company withdrew in 1803; the last soldiers left in 1807.
zh:
德塞阿多港坐落在巴塔哥尼亚最好的天然港湾之一，德塞阿多河注入大西洋时形成一条近32公里长的狭窄河口湾。1444年，干旱丘陵与海岸并非无人之地：阿奥尼肯克·特维尔切人群冬季在岸边扎营，捕鱼、拾贝、捕猎海豹，夏季再跟随原驼和美洲鸵前往开阔草原与高地。他们按季节迁徙，不建城镇；早在欧洲船只到来前，这条深水湾就已是可靠的登陆地。

1520年3月，麦哲伦—埃尔卡诺探险队被风暴吹入海湾，将其命名为「苦役湾」。1586年12月17日，托马斯·卡文迪什乘「欲望号」再来，把锚地命名为欲望港，并在特维尔切人的箭雨下停留十日；湾口的岬角后来称卡文迪什角。1670年，约翰·纳伯勒虽为英格兰宣称这片海岸，却未能占领。1780年4月，安东尼奥·德·别德马设立的西属营地仅维持七个月。1789年，皇家海事公司尝试建立常设渔业站，增设小堂、医院、农田、腌渔场以及诸圣堡和圣卡洛斯堡。由于鲸鱼稀少、海狮产业不足以维持，再加上补给昂贵和人口逃亡，公司于1803年撤出，最后的士兵也在1807年离开。

en:
Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego lies beyond the Strait of Magellan, a wind-scoured island of treeless northern steppe and broken southern coasts. By 1444 its northern plains and center were the country of the Selk'nam, or Ona, land nomads who hunted guanaco and gathered along the shore; the related Haush held the southeastern Mitre Peninsula, while canoe-going Yahgan and Kawesqar used the colder channels. The Selk'nam called the island Karukinka, 'our land,' and kept constant fires against the southern cold rather than building towns.

On 21 August 1520 the Magellan-Elcano expedition saw those fires from the sea and first called the coast Land of Smoke, a name Charles I of Spain changed to Land of Fire. On 1 November the ships found the All Saints' Strait, soon called the Strait of Magellan, and spent nineteen days tracing the island's northern shore. Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa made the first recorded face-to-face contact with Selk'nam there in 1580. Dutch voyagers under Jacob le Maire and Willem Schouten opened the route around Cape Horn in January 1616, and the Nodal brothers circumnavigated the archipelago in 1619. The first European shelter on the island was only a castaway camp: after the Purísima Concepción was wrecked in 1765, 193 survivors spent three months at Puerto Consolación before building a vessel and reaching Buenos Aires. James Cook surveyed the northeast coast and met Haush people at Buen Suceso Bay in 1769, but no lasting European settlement followed before 1821.
zh:
火地岛隔麦哲伦海峡与大陆相望，北部是寒风掠过的无树草原，南部海岸曲折。到1444年，岛北平原和中部已是塞尔克南人（又称奥纳人）的土地；他们是陆地游牧者，捕猎原驼并在海岸采集，亲缘相近的豪什人占据东南米特雷半岛，驾独木舟的雅甘人和卡韦斯卡尔人则往来于更寒冷的水道。塞尔克南人称此岛为卡鲁金卡，意为「我们的土地」；他们不建城镇，而靠常燃不熄的火堆抵御南方严寒。

1520年8月21日，麦哲伦—埃尔卡诺探险队从海上看见这些火堆，最初把海岸称为烟地，西班牙国王卡洛斯一世后来改名为火地。11月1日，船队发现诸圣海峡，也就是后来的麦哲伦海峡，并花十九天沿岛屿北岸航行。1580年，佩德罗·萨米恩托·德·甘博阿与塞尔克南人留下最早的面对面接触记录。1616年1月，雅各布·勒梅尔和威廉·斯豪滕率领的荷兰船队打开绕过合恩角的航路；1619年，诺达尔兄弟环绕火地群岛航行。欧洲人在岛上的第一处居留地只是海难营地：1765年「至圣受孕号」失事后，193名幸存者在安慰港停留三个月，造出一艘船并回到布宜诺斯艾利斯。1769年，詹姆斯·库克测绘东北海岸，并在好运湾与豪什人接触；但直到1821年以前，这类航行都没有带来持久的欧洲人定居点。

en:
Kawésqar country is a drowned maze of islands, channels and fjords along western Patagonia, reaching from the Gulf of Penas south to the Strait of Magellan and including Wellington, Santa Inés and Desolación islands and the shores of the Brunswick Peninsula. The people knew themselves as Kawésqar; Alacaluf was a later outsider's name, taken from the Yahgan language. In 1444 families moved through the maze by canoe, gathering shellfish and hunting seals and sea lions in the frigid water. Sea-lion oil and close capes protected them from rain and cold, while no town, road or outside chiefdom bound the channels.

Magellan's fleet entered the Strait of Magellan in 1520, but the first recorded encounter with people likely to be Kawésqar came on 22 April 1526, when García Jofre de Loaísa's Spanish expedition sighted them on the southern shore near the western end of the passage. The strait gave European ships a route between the Atlantic and Pacific, yet the side channels and islands long remained Kawésqar waters. From the late eighteenth century, British and North American whalers and sealers began visiting in growing numbers. Trade, occasional abductions and introduced diseases weakened the nomadic camps, but in 1821 canoes still dominated most of the wet archipelago.
zh:
卡韦斯卡尔之地是巴塔哥尼亚西部一片被海水淹没般的岛屿、海峡与峡湾迷宫，北起佩尼亚斯湾，南至麦哲伦海峡，包括惠灵顿岛、圣伊内斯岛、德索拉西翁岛以及不伦瑞克半岛沿岸。住在这里的人自称卡韦斯卡尔；「阿拉卡卢夫」是后来外来者借雅甘语使用的他称。1444年，各家族乘独木舟穿行于水道之间，在冰冷海水中采集贝类、捕猎海豹和海狮。海狮油脂和贴身斗篷帮助他们抵御雨水与严寒；这里没有城镇、道路，也不受外来首领统治。

麦哲伦的舰队1520年驶入麦哲伦海峡，但首次有记录地遇见可能是卡韦斯卡尔人的欧洲人，是1526年4月22日加西亚·霍弗雷·德·洛艾萨率领的西班牙探险队，他们在海峡西端附近的南岸望见了这些居民。海峡为欧洲船只提供了连接大西洋与太平洋的航路，但支离的旁侧水道和岛屿长期仍是卡韦斯卡尔人的水域。18世纪末起，英国和北美捕鲸船、猎海豹船开始大量到访。贸易、偶发的掳掠以及外来疾病削弱了游牧营地，但到1821年，独木舟仍支配着这片湿润群岛的大部分水道。

en:
Between the cold rivers running toward the Pacific and the forests facing Chiloé, Huillimapu is the southern land of the Huilliche, the southern branch of the Mapuche. The Pitrén farming and pottery tradition had spread through these clearings between about 300 and 1200; by the fifteenth century Cunco groups held the coast and wooded foothills, while Huilliche communities in the eastern plains grew potatoes, maize, quinoa and beans and took fish and shellfish from sea inlets. In 1444 no Spanish road or town crossed the territory, and local chiefs held its valleys, fishing grounds and forest trails.

Juan Bautista Pastene explored the Valdivia estuary in 1544, and in 1558 García Hurtado de Mendoza founded San Mateo de Osorno in the Rahue and Damas lowlands. Gold washings, crops and trade with Chile and Peru made the town a rich southern outpost, but the general rising after Curalaba overwhelmed it. Osorno was besieged and destroyed in 1604, and most surviving settlers withdrew toward Chiloé. For generations Huillimapu remained a closed frontier, marked by slave raids from Chiloé and rumours of the lost City of the Caesars. A peace treaty was concluded on the Bueno River in 1789; after a Spanish expedition and renewed fighting in 1792, the Parliament of Las Canoas in 1793 opened the country to the Crown and permitted the re-establishment of Osorno, with haciendas spreading from 1795.
zh:
维利马普位于通向太平洋的冷水河流与面向奇洛埃的森林之间，是马普切人南支维利切人的南方土地。约300年至1200年间，从事农耕和制陶的皮特伦传统已扩展到这些林间空地；到15世纪，库恩科诸部占据海岸与林木山麓，东部平原上的维利切社群种植马铃薯、玉米、藜麦和豆类，并在海湾捕捞鱼类和贝类。1444年时，西班牙人的道路和城镇都尚未进入这片土地，各部首领掌握着谷地、渔场和林中通道。

胡安·包蒂斯塔·帕斯特内1544年探查瓦尔迪维亚河口，1558年，加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨在拉韦河与达马斯河之间的低地建立圣马特奥·德·奥索尔诺。淘金、作物和同智利、秘鲁的贸易使它成为富庶的南方前哨，但库拉拉巴战役后的全面起义将其吞没。奥索尔诺遭围困后于1604年被毁，幸存居民大多退往奇洛埃。此后数代人时间里，维利马普一直是封闭边疆，伴随来自奇洛埃的捕奴袭击，以及关于失落的恺撒之城的传闻。1789年，双方在布埃诺河畔缔结和约；1792年西班牙远征和战事再起后，1793年的拉斯卡诺阿斯议会向西班牙王室开放此地，并允许重建奥索尔诺，大庄园从1795年起扩展。

en:
Pehuenmapu is the high country of the Pehuenche, whose camps moved between winter valleys and summer stands of pehuén, the monkey-puzzle tree. On the eastern side of the Andes their country ran from the Diamante River south to Lake Aluminé; trails through the Pehuenche and neighboring passes linked those headwaters with the Chilean slopes. Families gathered pine nuts between March and May, hunted guanaco and kept no permanent towns. In 1444 local chiefs controlled the routes independently, before Spanish soldiers or missionaries reached the upper Neuquén.

Jerónimo de Bibar recorded Pehuenche groups in 1550, and later Spanish chronicles placed them on both sides of the cordillera. Raiders from the mountains crossed the Pehuenche Pass into Maule and Cuyo in 1657, opening a direct route toward southern Mendoza; Pehuenche and Huilliche fighters sacked San Luis in 1712. They joined Cangapol's plains confederation in 1740, whose raid crossed the Luján district and reached Magdalena near the Río de la Plata. A general rising under Lebián and Pilmigerenantu in 1769 brought raids against Mendoza, and in 1770 a displaced band settled by the Malargüe River and attacked the new Fort San Carlos. The Parliament of Negrete restored peace with Chile in February 1771, while the eastern valleys and passes remained under indigenous leaders. By then Mapudungun had become the common Pehuenche language.
zh:
佩温马普是佩温切人的山地，各营地在冬季山谷与夏季佩温杉林之间迁移。安第斯山东坡的领地北起迪亚曼特河，南至阿卢米内湖；穿过佩温切山口及邻近山口的小路，把这些河源地带同智利坡地连接起来。各家在3月至5月采集松子，猎取原驼，没有永久性城镇。1444年，各地酋长独立控制山路，西班牙士兵或传教士尚未深入内乌肯河上游。

1550年，赫罗尼莫·德·比瓦尔记录下佩温切诸部，后来的西班牙编年史又把他们记载在安第斯山两坡。1657年，山地战士经佩温切山口进入马乌莱和库约，打开了通往门多萨南部的直接路线；1712年，佩温切人与维利切人联手洗劫圣路易斯。1740年，他们加入坎加波尔组织的草原联盟，突袭军越过卢洪一带，进抵拉普拉塔河畔的马格达莱纳。1769年，莱维安和皮尔米赫雷南图领导全面起事，对门多萨发动突袭；1770年，一支被迫迁徙的群体在马拉圭河畔落脚，并攻打新建的圣卡洛斯堡。1771年2月，内格雷特议会恢复了他们与智利之间的和平，但东部山谷和山口仍掌握在原住民首领手中。到这时，马普敦贡语已成为佩温切人的共同语言。

en:
The lower Río Negro, where the river crosses dry steppe to reach the Atlantic, was in 1444 a hunting ground and crossing place of the Chechehet, one of the nomadic Het groups of the southern Pampas. They moved between the Colorado and Negro rivers in search of guanaco, rhea and deer, used boleadoras, gathered wild seeds and camped near fresh water. No Spanish fort stood there yet; the camps beyond the river also bordered the worlds of the Puelche and Tehuelche peoples.

Francisco de Viedma y Narváez formally established the Establecimiento del Río Negro on 22 April 1779, choosing the south bank for a fort and colonists. A flood on 13 July swept away the first huts, so the survivors moved to the left bank that became Carmen de Patagones; colonists began arriving by sea from October, many from Galicia, and the isolated post survived through a small garrison, subsistence farms and trade with surrounding native peoples. After the May Revolution of 1810 the Buenos Aires junta took the fort, but royalist prisoners seized it in April 1812 and held it for Montevideo until 23 December 1814, when it passed to the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata.
zh:
内格罗河下游穿过干旱草原注入大西洋，1444年时是切切赫特人的狩猎地和往来通道；他们是南部潘帕斯草原上的海特人游牧群体之一。切切赫特人在科罗拉多河与内格罗河之间追踪原驼、美洲鸵和鹿，使用投石索，采集野生种子，并在淡水旁扎营。此时河口还没有西班牙堡垒，河外的营地也毗邻普埃尔切人与特维尔切人的世界。

1779年4月22日，弗朗西斯科·德·别德马-纳瓦埃斯正式建立「内格罗河定居点」，最初选在河南岸修筑要塞并安置移民。7月13日的洪水冲毁了最初的棚屋，幸存者遂迁到后来形成卡门-德帕塔戈内斯的左岸；移民从10月起由海路陆续抵达，其中多为加利西亚人。这个孤立据点依靠一支小规模驻军、自给农业和与周边原住民的贸易维持。1810年五月革命后，布宜诺斯艾利斯执政委员会接管要塞，但保王派囚犯在1812年4月夺占此地并替蒙得维的亚据守，直到1814年12月23日才归入拉普拉塔联合省。

en:
Picunmapu was the central Chilean country of the Picunches, Mapudungun-speaking 'people of the north.' Their hamlets and farming lands were spread through the valleys from the Aconcagua to the Biobío; communities irrigated their fields, worked stone and metal, and made pottery. The strongest southern groups, called Promaucaes by the Incas, lived between the Maipo and Maule. In 1444 the Inca frontier had not yet crossed the Choapa valley, and these villages followed their own lonkos rather than Cuzco.

Late in the fifteenth century, armies sent by Túpac Inca Yupanqui pushed into the region. The Promaucaes and neighboring allies met them at the Maule in an indecisive battle; the Incas fortified the hilltop Pucará La Muralla, their southernmost known outpost, but did not master the valley. Pedro de Valdivia's invasion later met three years of resistance. In 1544, after burning their own villages and fields, the Promaucaes withdrew south toward the Maule groups, who refused to receive them, and Spanish grain estates took over their irrigation channels. Encomienda labor and resettlement in pueblos de indios steadily dissolved Picunche identity. Many Promaucaes nevertheless joined Lautaro in 1554, marching with his army until the Spanish destroyed his camp at Peteroa in 1557.
zh:
皮昆马普是智利中部皮昆切人的土地，「皮昆切」在马普切语中意为「北方的人」。他们的村落和农田散布在阿空加瓜河至比奥比奥河之间的诸河谷中，各社区引水灌田，加工石器、金属并制作陶器。南方最强的诸部居于马伊波河与马乌莱河之间，印加人称他们为普罗马乌卡人。1444年，印加疆界尚未越过乔阿帕河谷，这些村落听从本地酋长，而不是库斯科的君主。

15世纪后期，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基派遣的军队推入这一地区。普罗马乌卡人与邻近盟友在马乌莱河迎战，战局未分胜负；印加人在山上修筑拉穆拉亚堡，这是已知最南的印加前哨，却未能征服河谷。后来佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚的入侵遭到三年抵抗。1544年，普罗马乌卡人焚毁自己的村庄和田地后南撤到马乌莱诸部之地，却又遭到当地人拒绝，西班牙人的谷物庄园随即接管了他们的灌渠。委托监护制下的劳役和迁入印第安人村镇逐渐消解了皮昆切人的身份。尽管如此，仍有许多普罗马乌卡人在1554年加入劳塔罗的军队，直到1557年西班牙人攻破其佩特罗阿营地。

en:
Angoche occupies a cluster of low islands set in mangrove creeks where the African coast bends toward Mozambique. Muslim merchants had lived and traded there since the late first millennium, and by 1444 the town was the southernmost of the Swahili sister-cities that looked to Kilwa, a free emporium beyond the reach of any European power. Dhows took aboard ivory, ambergris and gold brought from the Zambezi fairs and the lands of the Maravi, and the town's straw mats and hats were famous all along the shore. The mainland behind it belonged to the Makua, whose caravans fed its market.

Around 1485 refugees from the dynastic wars of Kilwa, led by Xosa, seized the old community and made it a sultanate of their own, and Vasco da Gama sighted its islands in 1498. For decades Angoche defied the Portuguese, but the rise of Zambezi factories and Maravi tolls on inland caravans wore it down; by the end of the sixteenth century it kept a Portuguese factor and a resident priest, until the priest was murdered in 1627. What trade remained was leased out in 1709. When Francisco Moraes Pereira visited in 1752, the sultan had just been restored with Portuguese help after a raid by an ex-slave and his bandits, and the town was being rebuilt on a new site after quarrels with the Makua on the mainland. In the later 1700s demand from the Mascarene plantations swelled the traffic in ivory and slaves, and by 1821 Angoche was stirring back to life as an independent emporium.
zh:
安戈谢坐落在非洲海岸折向莫桑比克处的一组低矮岛群上，四周环着红树林水道。穆斯林商人自公元第一个千年晚期便在此居住贸易；1444年时，它是拥戴基尔瓦的斯瓦希里姊妹诸城最南端的一座，也是任何欧洲势力都够不着的自由商港。独桅帆船在这里装上来自赞比西集市和马拉维之地的象牙、龙涎香与黄金，本地编织的草席和草帽更是沿岸闻名。身后的大陆属于马库阿人，他们的商队为岛上市场供货。

1485年前后，基尔瓦王朝混战中的一批流亡者在肖萨率领下夺取这个旧社群，建立自己的苏丹国；1498年达·伽马看到了它的岛群。安戈谢与葡萄牙对抗了数十年，但赞比西河商站的兴起和马拉维人对内陆商队的抽税使它日渐衰微；到16世纪末，岛上驻有葡萄牙商馆代表和一名神父，1627年神父被杀。残余的贸易在1709年被包租出去。1752年弗朗西斯科·莫赖斯·佩雷拉到访时，苏丹国刚在葡萄牙帮助下从一名叛奴匪帮的洗劫后复国，城镇也因与大陆上马库阿人的冲突放弃旧址，迁到新址重建。18世纪后期，马斯克林群岛种植园的需求使象牙和奴隶贸易膨胀；到1821年，安戈谢正重新成为一座不受管束的独立商港。

en:
The well-watered coastal hills of northern Natal, falling from the Nkandla heights toward the Indian Ocean, had been settled for centuries before 1444 by Nguni cattle-herders and growers of sorghum and millet, living in scattered homesteads under their own chiefs. Among the northern Nguni clans were the Mthethwa, 'the rulers', who had made the country south of Delagoa Bay their home by the late seventeenth century. In 1444 this was a world of royal herds, ancestral spirits and the forges of iron-smiths, untouched by Europeans, although ivory already moved north along the coast toward the trading stations on Delagoa Bay.

During the eighteenth century the Mthethwa built a paramountcy uniting some thirty northern Nguni chiefdoms. Under Dingiswayo, born Godongwana, who came to power after long exile, they traded ivory for Portuguese firearms through Delagoa Bay, the first Nguni power to do so, and organised young men into age-set regiments. Around 1811 the small Zulu clan under Senzangakhona joined the confederation; his son Shaka, who had grown up among the Mthethwa, became a favoured commander. In 1817 Dingiswayo was captured and killed by Zwide of the Ndwandwe, and leadership passed to Shaka, who turned the confederate regiments into the army of the Zulu kingdom. He withstood Zwide at Gqokli Hill in 1818 and broke the Ndwandwe alliance on the Mhlatuze River in 1820, leaving the old Mthethwa country the heartland of an empire stretching from the Pongola to the Tugela.
zh:
纳塔尔北部水草丰美的滨海丘陵，从恩卡德拉高地缓缓伸向印度洋，早在1444年之前数百年便住着恩古尼牧人和农人。他们牧放牛群，种植高粱与谷子，在各部首领治下以分散的家园聚族而居。姆泰特瓦人——族名意为「统治者」——便是北部恩古尼诸部之一，到17世纪末已在德拉戈阿湾以南站稳脚跟。1444年的这里是王有牛群、祖先神灵和铁匠炉火的世界，尚无欧洲人踏足，不过沿海岸北运的象牙已经流向德拉戈阿湾的贸易站。

18世纪，姆泰特瓦建成一个统合约三十个北部恩古尼部族的盟主政权。丁吉斯瓦约本名戈东瓦纳，长年流亡后归国掌权；他在位时经德拉戈阿湾以象牙换取葡萄牙火器，是最早这样做的恩古尼政权，又把青年按年龄编为兵团。约1811年，辛赞格科纳率领的弱小祖鲁部族加入联盟；他的儿子恰卡在姆泰特瓦人中间长大，成为深受器重的将领。1817年，丁吉斯瓦约被恩德旺堆首领兹维德俘杀，领导权落入恰卡之手，他把联盟的兵团改造成祖鲁王国的军队。1818年恰卡在戈克利山挡住兹维德，1820年又在姆拉图泽河畔粉碎恩德旺堆联盟，旧日的姆泰特瓦故土就此成为一个北起蓬戈拉河、南抵图盖拉河的帝国的心脏。

en:
Chaco Austral is the southern sweep of the Gran Chaco, a country of dry thorn forest and palm savanna crossed by the Salado, Dulce and Bermejo river corridors. In 1444 its interior belonged to mobile Guaycuru-speaking nations, who hunted with bows, fished, gathered honey and carob, and moved between seasonal camps. Along the south-western floodplains, the Tonocoté lived in palisaded villages, watered maize, quinoa, beans and squash with annual floods, herded llamas and rheas, and made large funerary urns. Farming edge and nomadic forest together formed the southern Chaco.

Túpac Yupanqui's later Inca expedition failed to master the thickets. Alejo García crossed the Chaco in 1524, and Juan de Ayolas was killed there in 1540, but Spanish power took root only around the south-western river towns. El Barco, first planted by Juan Núñez de Prado in 1550, was moved repeatedly before Francisco de Aguirre established Santiago del Estero in 1553; the see of Tucumán was created there in 1561. Farther east, Concepción de Nuestra Señora, founded in 1585, was abandoned under attack in 1632, and the later Jesuit mission of San Fernando del Río Negro also failed. Santiago passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776 and supported the May Revolution in 1810, although an earthquake wrecked its cathedral in 1817. In 1821 the Toba, Wichí, Mocoví and other Chaco nations still held the interior beyond the creole frontier.
zh:
南查科是大查科南部的广袤地带，干旱刺林与棕榈草原相连，萨拉多河、杜尔塞河和贝尔梅霍河形成通向内地的走廊。1444年，内陆仍属于流动的瓜伊库鲁语诸族；他们用弓狩猎、捕鱼，采集蜂蜜和角豆，在季节性营地间迁徙。西南河泛地上，托诺科特人住在有栅栏的村落里，利用每年河水泛滥灌溉玉米、藜麦、菜豆和南瓜，牧养羊驼和美洲鸵，并制作大型葬瓮。农耕边缘与游猎森林共同构成南查科。

图帕克·尤潘基后来派出的印加远征军也未能征服这片密林。1524年，阿莱霍·加西亚穿越大查科；1540年，胡安·德·阿约拉斯在此被杀。西班牙势力只能在西南河流城镇立足：胡安·努涅斯·德·普拉多1550年首建埃尔巴科，聚落后几经迁移，弗朗西斯科·德·阿吉雷最终于1553年建立圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗；1561年，图库曼主教区设在那里。更东面，1585年建立的康塞普西翁-德努埃斯特拉-塞尼奥拉在原住民攻击下于1632年废弃，后来圣费尔南多-德尔里奥内格罗的耶稣会传教区也未能持久。1776年，圣地亚哥划归拉普拉塔总督辖区，1810年支持五月革命；1817年，地震摧毁了当地大教堂。到1821年，托巴人、维奇人、莫科维人和其他查科族群仍控制着克里奥尔人边疆以外的内陆。

en:
The mountain valleys and puna crossings of Catamarca were held in 1444 by Pazioca peoples whom the Spanish later called Diaguitas. Capayán groups occupied the southern valleys, Olongastas the southeast, and Atacameño-speaking communities the high northwest; irrigated villages, llama herds and stone settlements were linked by mountain tracks. Inca armies had not yet crossed from the northwest, so these señoríos still faced one another rather than an imperial governor.

Diego de Almagro's expedition crossed the valleys in 1536, and Francisco de Aguirre's San Pedro Mártir of 1554 did not survive. In June 1558 Juan Pérez de Zurita founded Londres de la Nueva Inglaterra in the Quimivil valley, naming it for Mary Tudor of England; it was moved in 1561, abandoned during a Diaguita revolt in 1562, and repeatedly refounded as San Juan Bautista. The great Calchaquí rising of 1630 destroyed that settlement, with Juan Chalimín among its leaders, and a fifth foundation followed at Pomán in 1633. Only on 5 July 1683 did Fernando de Mendoza y Mate de Luna establish the lasting town of San Fernando del Valle de Catamarca, following a royal order of 1679. After the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata was formed in 1776, Catamarca became a subintendency under Salta. In 1821 it claimed provincial autonomy and chose Nicolás Avellaneda y Tula as its first governor.
zh:
1444年，卡塔马卡的山谷与普纳渡口掌握在帕西奥卡人手中，西班牙人后来把他们统称为迪亚吉塔人。卡帕扬人占据南部谷地，奥隆加斯塔人在东南，阿塔卡马语社群在西北高地；灌溉村社、大羊驼群和石砌聚落由山路相连。印加军队此时尚未从西北进入，这些地方首领各自为政，面前还没有帝国总督。

1536年，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的远征穿过这些谷地；1554年弗朗西斯科·德·阿吉雷建立的圣佩德罗殉道者镇未能维持。1558年6月，胡安·佩雷斯·德·苏里塔在基米维尔谷建立新英格兰的伦敦镇，以英格兰的玛丽·都铎命名。该镇1561年迁移，1562年在迪亚吉塔人起义中被弃，后来又以圣胡安·包蒂斯塔之名多次重建。1630年卡尔查基人大起义摧毁聚落，胡安·查利明是领导者之一；1633年，第五次建城在波曼进行。直到1683年7月5日，费尔南多·德·门多萨·伊·马特·德·卢纳才依照1679年王令建立持久的圣费尔南多-德尔巴列-德卡塔马卡。1776年拉普拉塔总督辖区成立后，卡塔马卡成为萨尔塔监政区下辖的副监政区。1821年，它宣布实行省自治，并选举尼古拉斯·阿韦利亚内达·伊·图拉为首任省长。

en:
The Copiapó River cuts a narrow oasis through the Atacama Desert, its meadows and fields supporting the Copayapu people, later grouped with the Diaguita. By the fifteenth century they lived in compact farming and herding villages, built hilltop pucarás, worked copper and other metals, and made black-on-red pottery decorated with stylized llamas. In 1444 the valley was still outside the Inca world: its lords drew strength from local oasis exchange rather than from Cuzco, and the road network of the Tawantinsuyu had not yet reached the river.

Around 1470 Inca power annexed Copayapu, settled mitma families from the Elqui and Huasco valleys in the middle and upper basin, and promoted sun and huaca worship; Viña del Cerro became a Diaguita-Inca metallurgical centre. Diego de Almagro crossed the Andes and reached the valley on 21 March 1536, and Pedro de Valdivia took possession there on 26 October 1540, naming it the Valley of Possession. Long administered as part of Coquimbo, the settlement was formally founded as San Francisco de la Selva de Copiapó by Governor José Manso de Velasco on 8 December 1744, and in 1786 it became the Partido of Copiapó.
zh:
科皮亚波河在阿塔卡马沙漠中切出一道狭窄绿洲，河畔草地和田地供养着科帕亚普人，后世常把他们归入迪亚吉塔诸族。到15世纪，这里已有聚居的农牧村落、山巅堡垒、铜与其他金属作坊，还出产以风格化羊驼纹装饰的黑彩红陶。1444年的科皮亚波河谷仍在印加世界之外：各部首领依靠绿洲间的往来壮大，库斯科的势力和塔万廷苏约大道都还没有抵达这条河。

约1470年，印加势力吞并科帕亚普，把来自埃尔基和瓦斯科河谷的米蒂马移民安置在流域中上游，并推广太阳神与瓦卡崇拜；比尼亚德尔塞罗成为迪亚吉塔—印加风格的冶金中心。1536年3月21日，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗越过安第斯山抵达河谷；1540年10月26日，佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚在此宣布取得智利，将其命名为「领有谷」。此地长期归科金博辖区管辖，直到1744年12月8日，总督何塞·曼索·德·贝拉斯科才正式建立圣弗朗西斯科·德拉塞尔瓦·德·科皮亚波；1786年，这里改设为科皮亚波区。

en:
Iquique, its Aymara name Iki Iki suggesting a place of rest or dreams, faces the Pacific below the rainless Tarapacá desert. In 1444 the shore belonged to Camanchaco fishermen, called Changos by Spaniards, who launched sea-lion-hide rafts, gathered shellfish and salted fish. Inland Colla farmers in the ravines and oases traded with the highland Aymara world and the lords of Chucuito; no strong coastal town yet dominated a land whose wealth moved on exchanges between sea, desert and altiplano.

Later in the fifteenth century the Incas annexed Tarapacá, and on Cerro Esmeralda their capacocha ritual left two young victims and offerings of gold, silver, Spondylus shell, textiles and pottery, dated between 1475 and 1499. Spanish rule from 1539 attached the coast to the Viceroyalty of Peru, and the encomiendas of San Lorenzo de Tarapacá and Pica organized indigenous labour. Iquique long remained a guano and fish landing place, while eighteenth-century silver from Huantajaya and Santa Rosa went chiefly overland to Arica. San Lorenzo became the jurisdiction's seat in 1768, a customs house followed at Iquique in 1788, and documents of 1811 already record the first saltpetre shipments. When Peru proclaimed independence on 28 July 1821, the small port remained part of the Peruvian south.
zh:
伊基克的艾马拉语原名「伊基伊基」，意为休息或入梦之地，面朝太平洋，背后是终年少雨的塔拉帕卡沙漠。1444年时，海岸属于卡曼查科渔民，西班牙人后来称他们为昌戈人；他们驾着海狮皮皮筏出海，采集贝类、腌制鱼货。沟谷和绿洲里的科利亚农人则同高原艾马拉世界及丘基托领主贸易。这里还没有强势的海岸城镇，海岸、沙漠与高原之间的物资交换，才是这片土地的命脉。

15世纪后期，印加吞并塔拉帕卡；在埃斯梅拉达山上，卡帕科查祭祀留下两名年轻牺牲者，以及金器、银器、海菊蛤、织物和陶器等供品，测年在1475年至1499年间。1539年起，西班牙把这片海岸并入秘鲁总督辖区，以塔拉帕卡的圣洛伦索和皮卡两个委托监护制辖区组织原住民劳役。伊基克长期只是装运鸟粪和鱼货的小码头，18世纪万塔哈亚与圣罗莎的白银主要经陆路运往阿里卡。1768年，圣洛伦索成为治所；1788年，伊基克设立海关，1811年的文献已记载最早一批硝石外运。1821年7月28日秘鲁宣布独立时，这座小港仍是秘鲁南部的一部分。

en:
Jujuy is a fertile high valley where the Xibi Xibi joins the Río Grande, at the southern mouth of the 155-kilometre Humahuaca canyon, the natural road from the plains to the Altiplano. In 1444 it was Diaguita country: the Jujuí and Omaguaca herders of the valley, kin to the Calchaquí of the western mountains, grew maize on its flats, drove llama trains up the canyon and held its pucará fortresses against rivals, while Inca power was pushing south along the same road. The Spaniards met them early: in late 1535 a foraging party of Almagro's Chile expedition was killed here and an eighty-man force had to storm a local pucará.

Gregorio de Castañeda founded the town of Nieva on the Xibi Xibi on 20 August 1561, but the cacique Juan Calchaquí destroyed it in the rising of 1563; a second settlement, San Francisco, planted by Pedro de Zárate on 13 October 1575, was burned seven months later. On 19 April 1593, the Monday after Easter, Francisco de Argañaraz y Murguía at last founded San Salvador de Velazco with forty soldiers, and the town throve as the staging post on the mule road from Tucumán to the silver mines of Potosí. It formed part of the Viceroyalty of Peru until 1776, when it passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, and on 3 March 1781 Gregorio de Zegada repulsed a Chaco war party in the Zapla hills. From 1810 Jujuy stood on the main front of the independence war. Manuel Belgrano took command of the Northern Army there on 19 May 1812, and at dawn on 23 August 1812, leaving nothing to the royalist advance, the entire population left the town with him for Tucumán in the scorched-earth march remembered as the Jujuy Exodus.
zh:
胡胡伊是希比希比河汇入格兰德河处的肥沃高谷，位于全长155公里的乌马瓦卡峡谷南口——这条峡谷是从平原通往高原的天然道路。1444年时这里是迪亚吉塔人的土地：河谷中的胡胡伊人与奥马瓦卡牧人和西山的查尔查奇人同源，他们在滩地上种植玉米，沿峡谷驱赶驼队，据守一座座普卡拉堡垒抵御邻族，而印加势力正沿着同一条道路向南进逼。西班牙人很早就与他们遭遇：1535年末，阿尔马格罗智利远征队的一支搜粮小队在此被杀，一支八十人的部队强攻才拿下当地的一座普卡拉。

1561年8月20日，格雷戈里奥·德·卡斯塔涅达在希比希比河畔建立涅瓦城，但酋长胡安·查尔查奇在1563年的起义中将它摧毁；1575年10月13日，佩德罗·德·萨拉特建立第二个定居点圣弗朗西斯科，仅七个月后便被焚为平地。1593年4月19日，即复活节后的星期一，弗朗西斯科·德·阿加尼亚拉斯·伊·穆尔吉亚率四十名士兵终于建成圣萨尔瓦多·德·贝拉斯科，这座城镇作为从图库曼通往波托西银矿的骡马道上的补给驿站而繁荣。1776年之前它隶属秘鲁总督辖区，此后划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区；1781年3月3日，格雷戈里奥·德·塞加达在萨普拉丘陵击退了来自查科的部落武装。1810年起，胡胡伊始终处在独立战争的最前线。1812年5月19日，曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺在此接掌北方军；1812年8月23日黎明，为不给推进的保王军留下任何物资，全城居民随他撤离城镇、迁往图库曼，这场坚壁清野的行军史称「胡胡伊大出走」。

en:
Potosí is a cold, high basin of the Charcas, lying more than 4,000 metres up in the Andes beneath Sumaq Urqu, the mountain later called Cerro Rico. Aymara-speaking farmers and llama herders knew its metallic veins, treated the peak as a sacred huaca, and linked the plateau with older Andean caravan routes. In 1444 there was no Spanish mining city here, only the settlements, pastures and shrines of the Charca world; the mountain's silver had not yet become the prize of an Atlantic empire.

The Spanish conquest of Peru transformed the basin. In 1545, the indigenous prospector Diego Huallpa is traditionally credited with revealing its rich silver ores, and the Villa Imperial de Potosí was founded around the same rush. Andean guayra furnaces first smelted the richest native silver, but by 1565 those easily worked ores were declining; mercury amalgamation opened the lower-grade veins, and a pan amalgamation method developed at Potosí in 1609 helped prolong the boom. Spanish sources credit Cerro Rico with about 80 percent of the silver mined worldwide in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The metal went by llama and mule train to the Pacific, then to Panama and Spain, while other shipments reached Buenos Aires or crossed the Pacific from Acapulco in the Manila trade. That wealth also rested on Andean mit'a labour, which Spanish authorities turned into a colonial mining levy. When the Upper Peruvian independence war began in 1809, Potosí's mines and mint remained a strategic prize still contested in 1821.
zh:
波托西是查卡人寒冷的高原盆地，坐落在安第斯山脉海拔四千多米处，脚下是后来被称为里科山的苏马克乌尔库山。说艾马拉语的农民和骆马牧民早已知道山中矿脉，把峰顶视为神圣的瓦卡，并让这片高原与安第斯古老的商队道路相连。1444年时这里还没有西班牙人的矿业城市，只有查卡世界的聚落、牧场和神殿；山中白银也尚未成为大西洋帝国争夺的财富。

西班牙征服秘鲁改变了这个盆地。1545年，传统说法把富银矿的发现归于印第安探矿者迭戈·瓦尔帕，波托西皇家城也在这场淘金热中建立。安第斯的「瓦伊拉」炉最初熔炼最富的自然银，但到1565年，易于处理的矿石已经减少；水银混汞法使低品位矿脉得以开采，1609年又在波托西发展出碾盘混汞法，延长了繁荣。西班牙文资料称，16至17世纪里科山出产的白银约占世界银产量的80%。白银由骆马和骡队运往太平洋，再经巴拿马运往西班牙，也有货物运抵布宜诺斯艾利斯，或从阿卡普尔科横跨太平洋进入马尼拉贸易。这笔财富也建立在安第斯米塔劳役之上，西班牙当局将其改造成殖民矿山劳役。1809年上秘鲁独立战争爆发后，波托西的矿山和造币厂仍是战略要地，到1821年仍在争夺之中。

en:
Arica lies where the Azapa and Lluta valleys open to the Pacific beside a steep coastal headland, the Morro. After Tiwanaku's influence faded, its farmers, herders and Camanchaco fishermen formed the interconnected Arica culture, while Aymara lordships from the altiplano planted colonies in the upper valleys to exchange llamas, maize, fish and shellfish across different altitudes. In 1444 this coast and its desert roads were an Aymara frontier on the edge of the Inca world; within a generation it was folded into Collasuyo and resettled with mitma communities.

The discovery of Potosí in 1545 drew Spanish traffic toward the natural roadstead, though Arica's great growth came only in the 1560s, when Huancavelica mercury and Potosí silver began moving through its warehouses and mule trains. Probably in 1584 the settlement was formally titled San Marcos de Arica. Its treasure fleets drew Francis Drake, Thomas Cavendish, Richard Hawkins, Bartholomew Sharp and William Dampier, and earthquakes repeatedly tested the exposed port. When Peru's independence was proclaimed on 28 July 1821, Arica left Spanish rule as one of the southernmost ports tied to the trade of Arequipa and Upper Peru.
zh:
阿理卡位于阿萨帕谷与柳塔谷入海处，陡峭的海岬「莫罗」俯瞰太平洋。蒂亚瓦纳科影响衰退后，当地农人、牧人和卡曼查科渔民共同构成彼此依存的阿里卡文化；来自高原的艾马拉领主则在上游谷地设立移民点，在不同海拔之间交换羊驼、玉米、鱼和贝类。1444年，这片海岸和沙漠道路已是印加世界边缘的艾马拉边疆；不到一代人后，它被并入科利亚苏约，并有米蒂马移民被安置到此。

1545年波托西银矿被发现，把西班牙商路引向这个天然锚地；但阿理卡的真正起飞是在16世纪60年代后，万卡韦利卡的汞和波托西的白银开始经由这里的仓库与骡队转运。约1584年，定居点正式获得「圣马科斯·德·阿理卡」的城市头衔。宝船也引来弗朗西斯·德雷克、托马斯·卡文迪什、理查德·霍金斯、巴塞洛缪·夏普和威廉·丹皮尔等袭掠者，地震则一再考验这座暴露在海湾边的港口。1821年7月28日秘鲁宣布独立时，阿理卡作为连接阿雷基帕与上秘鲁贸易的南端港口之一，结束了西班牙统治。

en:
Oruro is a mineral-bearing stretch of the central Altiplano, around the cold Uru Uru heights. After the decline of Tiwanaku, Uru communities and small Aymara towns shared the plateau; the Aymara kingdoms brought many Uru groups under their power, and Inca rule later reached the district from Paria. In 1444 there was still no Spanish town here, only scattered pastures and settlements within the Pacajes highland world, with Caracara remembered as the province's principal local place. Its copper- and silver-bearing rocks were known locally, but they had not yet been drawn into a transatlantic mining economy.

Spanish explorers first entered the Paria district in 1535, and for decades prospectors searched the Uru Uru range for precious metals. Lorenzo de Aldana received the Paria encomienda in 1565 and revived silver workings, while Diego Alemán made the first recorded mining claim in the range in 1568. The town itself was founded on 1 November 1606, after Francisco Medrano and other Spaniards found rich silver at San Cristóbal; Manuel de Castro del Castillo established it as the Real Villa de San Felipe de Austria. By 1618 twenty ore-processing mills served the surrounding mines, and a 1678 census recorded 75,920 inhabitants, making Oruro the second-largest city of Upper Peru before silver mining stagnated after 1680. In 1739 Juan Vélez de Córdova issued an early protest against Spanish abuses, and on 10 February 1781 Sebastián Pagador, Jacinto Rodríguez de Herrera and their allies launched the Oruro revolt, which royalists suppressed by 1783. The revolutions at Chuquisaca and La Paz in 1809 opened the wider independence war; Oruro rose under Tomás Barrón on 6 October 1810 and remained a contested mining centre as the war passed 1821.
zh:
奥鲁罗位于安第斯高原中部，是环绕寒冷的乌鲁乌鲁高地、富含矿藏的一片地带。蒂亚瓦纳科衰落之后，乌鲁人的群落和小型艾马拉城镇共同生活在高原上；艾马拉诸王国将许多乌鲁群体置于统治之下，后来印加又从帕里亚把权力伸入这一地区。1444年时这里还没有西班牙城镇，只有帕卡赫斯高原世界中分散的牧场和聚落，卡拉卡拉则是该省留名的主要本地地点。当地人知道含铜和含银的岩石，但这些矿脉尚未被卷入跨大西洋矿业经济。

西班牙探险者在1535年首次进入帕里亚地区，此后数十年间，探矿者一直在乌鲁乌鲁山脉寻找贵金属。洛伦索·德·阿尔达纳于1565年获得帕里亚监护权并恢复银矿开采，迭戈·阿莱曼则在1568年提出了这片山脉中有记载的第一份矿权申请。城镇本身建立于1606年11月1日；此前弗朗西斯科·梅德拉诺等西班牙人在圣克里斯托瓦尔发现富银矿，曼努埃尔·德·卡斯特罗·德尔·卡斯蒂略随后将其建为「奥地利圣费利佩皇家城」。到1618年，周边矿山已有二十座选矿场；1678年的人口普查记录了75,920名居民，使奥鲁罗成为上秘鲁第二大城市，但银矿在1680年后陷入停滞。1739年，胡安·贝莱斯·德·科尔多瓦发表了早期抗议西班牙弊政的文告；1781年2月10日，塞巴斯蒂安·帕加多尔、哈辛托·罗德里格斯·德·埃雷拉等人发动奥鲁罗起义，到1783年被保王党镇压。1809年丘基萨卡和拉巴斯的革命开启更大范围的独立战争；奥鲁罗于1810年10月6日在托马斯·巴龙领导下起兵，并在战争延续到1821年以后仍是各方争夺的矿业中心。

en:
Mbwila, Ambuíla to the Portuguese, was a small Mbundu state in the rugged hills at the headwaters of the Lukala River, where a pass through the mountains linked Kongo with Ndongo. Its rulers bore the title Ndembu, and the Portuguese called the whole hill country the Dembos. The capital sat on the heights above the valley, almost unassailable, so that Kongo and Ndongo both claimed the land but neither truly governed it, and the caravans through the Lukala gap carried the trade of both kingdoms. In 1444 Mbwila was the remote southern march of the Kongo crown, its villages growing grain and answering to their own hill lords.

The Portuguese, settled at Luanda from 1575, first forced an act of vassalage on Mbwila in 1619–20, but its rulers switched allegiance between Angola, Ndongo and Kongo as armies moved through the pass: they backed Queen Njinga during the wars of 1627–1630 and joined her again when the Dutch seized Luanda in 1641. After a Portuguese army retook Luanda in 1648, Lisbon ceded its claims on Mbwila to Kongo in exchange for a mining concession, until a succession quarrel brought an Angolan army through the gap. At the battle of Mbwila on 29 October 1665 King António I of Kongo was defeated and killed, and his realm collapsed into decades of civil war. Further Portuguese campaigns in 1692–1693 won no more than a nominal vassalage, and in 1758 Lisbon built a fort at Encoge to stop the slave trade slipping through the Lukala pass to Dutch, French and English ships on the coast.
zh:
姆布维拉（葡萄牙人称为安布伊拉）是卢卡拉河源头山区的一个姆本杜人小国，山间隘口连接着刚果与恩东戈。当地统治者称「恩登布」，葡萄牙人遂把整片山地叫作登博斯。首府雄踞河谷上方的高地，几乎无懈可击，刚果与恩东戈都宣称对它拥有主权，却都无法真正统治；穿过卢卡拉隘口的商队往来于两个王国之间。1444年的姆布维拉是刚果王权遥远的南疆，村落种植谷物，听命于各自的山酋。

1575年据有罗安达的葡萄牙人于1619至1620年首次迫使姆布维拉称臣，但它的统治者总在安哥拉、恩东戈和刚果之间见风使舵：1627至1630年恩津加女王作战时它站在女王一边，1641年荷兰人夺取罗安达后它再次投奔恩津加。1648年葡萄牙军队夺回罗安达后，以一项采矿特许权为交换把对姆布维拉的主张让给刚果，直到一场继承之争把安哥拉军队引入隘口。1665年10月29日，刚果国王安东尼奥一世在姆布维拉战役中兵败被杀，他的王国随后陷入数十年内战。1692至1693年葡萄牙再度出兵，也只换来名义上的臣服；1758年，为阻止奴隶贸易经卢卡拉隘口流向海岸上的荷、法、英商船，里斯本在恩科热修筑要塞。

en:
North of the Pilcomayo and west of the Paraguay, the Chaco Boreal was in 1444 a spread of dry forest, palm savanna and seasonal floodplain without cities or an imperial frontier. Chiquito and Chané communities lived near its western openings, Ayoreo and Yshyr or Chamacoco groups moved through the interior, and Mbayá-Caduveo and Qom bands used the riverine approaches. Many peoples moved with game and water; tracks linking the Paraguay, Pantanal and Andean foothills mattered more than any fixed border.

Europeans first crossed these lands from the Paraguay basin in the early sixteenth century: Alejo García, Domingo Martínez de Irala and Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca all passed through or along the Chaco while seeking routes toward the Andes. A lasting Spanish wedge appeared only on 26 February 1561, when Ñuflo de Chaves, marching from Asunción, founded Santa Cruz de la Sierra on the edge of the Chiquitos country. Indigenous resistance and the hardships of the plains forced the town westward before the end of the century, while Guaycurú and Mbayá horsemen long denied Spain control of the open Chaco. On the north-western frontier Jesuits gathered Chiquito groups into reductions from 1691, founding eleven mission towns by 1760; the Jesuits' expulsion in 1767 broke that system apart. At the western edge, Santa Cruz rose against Spanish rule on 24 September 1810, yet in 1821 most of the Chaco Boreal still answered to its own nations rather than to the new republics.
zh:
1444年，北查科是皮科马约河以北、巴拉圭河以西的干旱林、棕榈稀树草原与季节性洪泛地带，没有城市，也没有帝国边界。奇基托人和查内人住在靠近西部山口的地带，阿约雷奥人和伊希尔人（查马科科人）散布内陆，姆巴亚—卡杜韦奥人与科姆人则在通向河流的路上活动。许多人群随猎物和水源迁徙；连接巴拉圭河、潘塔纳尔与安第斯山麓的小径，比任何固定边界都重要。

16世纪初，欧洲人最先从巴拉圭河流域穿过这里：阿莱霍·加西亚、多明戈·马丁内斯·德·伊拉拉和阿尔瓦尔·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡，都曾在寻找通往安第斯的道路时经过查科或其边缘。1561年2月26日，从亚松森出兵的纽弗洛·德·查韦斯在奇基托斯边缘建立圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉，西班牙人才打下一根持久的楔子。原住民的抵抗和平原上的艰困迫使该城在16世纪结束前西迁，瓜伊库鲁与姆巴亚骑兵则长期使西班牙无法控制开阔查科。在西北边疆，耶稣会从1691年起把奇基托人集入传教村，到1760年共建立十一座传教镇；1767年耶稣会被逐，这套体系随之瓦解。西陲的圣克鲁斯于1810年9月24日起事反对西班牙统治，但到1821年，北查科大部分土地仍听命于本地族群，而不是新生的共和国。

en:
Chiquitos is the tropical savanna between the Amazon and the Gran Chaco. In 1444 it was not a single realm; Piñoco, Tao, Manasi and other peoples moved among its rivers and gallery forests, cultivating maize and manioc, hunting and making pottery. The humid yungas on the eastern Andean slopes kept Inca power at a distance, and the villages remained organized by their own kinship and languages. Spaniards later grouped these varied grassland peoples together as Chiquitos.

Spanish contact began with the founding of the old Santa Cruz de la Sierra in 1559, but colonial control long remained weak. In 1637 Brazilian bandeirantes crossed the Paraguay River and raided toward the future San José de Chiquitos, beginning decades of slave-trading pressure. Jesuit work began making inroads in 1690, and in 1691 José de Arce founded San Francisco Xavier, the first reduction; by 1760 eleven mission towns had gathered many local groups around cattle herds, weaving, church music and the Chiquitano language. The Jesuits were expelled in 1767, and Franciscans and secular authorities took over their towns; Chiquitos was attached to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1778. By 1821 many missions had declined, with some families withdrawing to small camps while others labored on ranches and farms.
zh:
奇基托斯是亚马孙与大查科之间的热带稀树草原。1444年，这里并不是一个统一政权，皮尼奥卡、陶、马纳西等族群在河流与林带间迁徙，种植玉米和木薯、狩猎并制作陶器。安第斯山东麓湿润的云加林带使印加势力难以直达，各村落仍依照自身的血缘关系和语言组合生活。后来的西班牙人把这些不同的草原居民统称为奇基托斯。

1559年西班牙人建立最早的圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉后，与这里的接触开始，但殖民控制长期薄弱。1637年，巴西旗兵渡过巴拉圭河，袭扰至后来的圣何塞-德奇基托斯附近，开启了数十年的奴隶掳掠压力。耶稣会传教自1690年开始取得进展，1691年，何塞·德·阿尔塞建立第一座归化传教镇圣弗朗西斯科·哈维尔；到1760年，已有十一座传教镇把许多当地族群聚合在牛群、织布、教会音乐和奇基塔诺语周围。1767年耶稣会被逐，方济各会和世俗当局接管传教镇；1778年，奇基托斯划归拉普拉塔总督辖区。到1821年，许多传教镇已经衰落，一些家庭退入较小营地，另一些人则在牧场和农庄劳作。

en:
The temperate valleys later named Cochabamba, from the Quechua Quchapampa or 'lake plain', lie between the cold Altiplano and the eastern lowlands. In 1444 Inca rule had not yet reached them: Quta, Chui, Sipi-Sipi, Sura and neighboring communities farmed the lower and central valleys, herded llamas on higher ground and maintained a multi-ethnic local order. Their maize lands made the valleys a prize for the highland empires forming to the west.

Inca armies conquered Cochabamba in the late 1400s. Huayna Capac turned the valleys into state maize lands, brought in some 14,000 mitmaq farmers and stored harvests in 2,400 hillside qollqas for the army and highland administrative centers. In 1542 Garci Ruiz de Orellana became the first Spaniard to hold land in the valley. Viceroy Francisco de Toledo ordered the founding of Villa Real de Oropesa in 1571, and the town was re-established around its present plaza in 1574. During Potosí's silver boom it supplied the mines with grain, food and timber, and in 1786 Charles III renamed it Villa de Cochabamba. On 27 May 1812, during the independence wars, Cochabamba's women defended the Coronilla hill against José Manuel de Goyeneche's royalists, making the town a symbol of resistance.
zh:
后来得名科恰班巴的温凉谷地，名称来自克丘亚语Quchapampa，意为「湖原」，位于寒冷高原与东部低地之间。1444年，印加统治尚未到达这里：库塔、丘伊、西佩西佩、苏拉及邻近社群在下谷地和中谷地耕作，在高处牧养羊驼，维系着多族群的地方秩序。谷地的玉米田也使它成为西方高原政权觊觎的富庶之地。

15世纪末，印加军队征服科恰班巴诸谷。瓦伊纳·卡帕克把这里划为国家玉米产区，迁入约一万四千名米特马克农民，并在山坡上设置二千四百座科尔卡仓库，把收成供给军队和高原行政中心。1542年，加西·鲁伊斯·德·奥雷利亚纳成为最早在谷地置产的西班牙人。1571年，总督弗朗西斯科·德·托莱多下令建立奥罗佩萨皇家镇；1574年，城镇在日后的城市广场一带再度建立。波托西银山繁荣时期，科恰班巴为矿区供应粮食和木材；1786年，卡洛斯三世将其改名为科恰班巴镇。1812年5月27日独立战争期间，科恰班巴妇女在科罗尼利亚山抗击何塞·曼努埃尔·德·戈耶内切率领的保王军，使这座城镇成为抵抗象征。

en:
Chuquiabo, the Aymara Chuqiyapu, is a deep, green valley cut through the cold Altiplano by the Choqueyapu River, its terraced fields dropping toward the coca lands of the yungas beneath the snow peak of Illimani. Aymara-speaking Colla farmers had long worked it before 1444, washing gold from its streams and carrying cloth and metals along the road linking the Titicaca basin with the eastern lowlands, while the older ruins of Tiwanaku stood out on the nearby plain. In 1444 it was still Colla country under its own lords, as Inca armies out of Cuzco pressed into the Collao. Spanish horsemen first crossed the valley in 1535 with Almagro's march on Chile.

On 20 October 1548 Captain Alonso de Mendoza, acting for President Pedro de la Gasca, founded Nuestra Señora de La Paz at the native village of Laja; three days later the town was moved into the Chuquiago valley. Its name celebrated the peace imposed after Gonzalo Pizarro's rebellion was put down, and its task was to guard the silver road from Potosí to Lima. La Paz passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776. In 1781 the Aymara leader Túpac Katari raised the highland peoples and blockaded the city for six months before he was captured and killed. On 16 July 1809 Pedro Domingo Murillo proclaimed a junta in La Paz, the first open cry of independence in Spanish South America; royalist troops retook the city and hanged him on 29 January 1810.
zh:
丘基亚博，艾马拉语称丘基亚普，是乔克亚普河在寒冷高原上切出的深翠河谷，层层梯田沿雪山伊伊马尼峰下的山势，朝盛产古柯的云加低地铺展。1444年之前很久，说艾马拉语的科拉农人已在此耕作，从溪流中淘金，沿着连通的的喀喀湖盆地与东部低地的道路贩运布匹和金属，更古老的蒂亚瓦纳科遗址就矗立在附近的平原上。1444年时这里仍是科拉人的土地，由本族首领统治，而库斯科的印加大军正向科利亚奥高原步步进逼。1535年，西班牙骑兵随阿尔马格罗远征智利首次穿过这道河谷。

1548年10月20日，阿隆索·德·门多萨舰长受命于检审庭主席佩德罗·德拉加斯卡，在土著村落拉哈建立「和平圣母城」；三天后城址迁入丘基亚博河谷。城名纪念贡萨洛·皮萨罗叛乱平定后的和平，职责则是守护波托西通往利马的白银商路。1776年，拉巴斯划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区。1781年，艾马拉人领袖图帕克·卡塔里号召高原各部起事，围城达六个月之久，最终兵败被俘处死。1809年7月16日，佩德罗·多明戈·穆里略在拉巴斯宣布成立执政委员会，这是西属南美洲第一声公开的独立呐喊；保王军队重占城市，于1810年1月29日将他绞死。

en:
Moxos, more commonly rendered Mojos in Spanish sources, is the seasonally flooded Beni savanna crossed by headwaters of the Mamoré and Madeira. In 1444 Arawak-speaking Moxo communities and neighbouring peoples such as the Itonama, Cayuvava, Canichana, Tacana and Movima lived among rivers, lakes and gallery forest. Their villages relied on fishing, hunting and cultivation on raised ground, connected by an ancient landscape of artificial mounds, ponds, canals and drainage works that turned annual floods into harvests. The wet lowlands remained beyond Inca control, their communities governed by local chiefs and guided by spirits of forest and water.

A Spanish expedition under Pedro de Candía probed the region from Lima in 1538, but the lowlands long resisted incorporation. The Jesuits Pedro Marbán and Cipriano Barace began sustained evangelization from Santa Cruz de la Sierra in 1675, and Nuestra Señora de Loreto, founded in April 1682, opened the formal Moxos missions. Barace established Trinidad on the Mamoré in 1686; San Pedro de Moxos followed in 1697 and became the mission capital in 1700. The reducciones gathered many distinct peoples into Catholic towns with church music and crafts, shaping the broader Mojeño identity. When the Jesuit expulsion reached Moxos in 1768, fifteen mission villages passed to secular clergy; a royal corregidor was appointed in 1772, and from 1776 the territory belonged to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata.
zh:
莫克索斯在西班牙文资料中常写作Mojos，即中文通行所称的莫霍斯平原，是马莫雷河与马代拉河上游贯穿的季节性洪泛贝尼草原。1444年，操阿拉瓦克语的莫克索斯诸社群，以及伊托纳马、卡尤瓦瓦、卡尼查纳、塔卡纳、莫维马等邻族，生活在河流、湖泊与林带之间。他们的村落以渔猎和高地耕作为生，四周分布着古老的人工土丘、池塘、沟渠和排水系统，把一年一度的洪水转化为收成。这片湿润低地不在印加控制之下，各村由本地首领治理，并遵从森林与水之灵的指引。

1538年，佩德罗·德·坎迪亚率领的西班牙远征队曾从利马试探进入此地，但低地长期没有被纳入殖民统治。1675年，耶稣会士佩德罗·马尔万和西普里亚诺·巴拉塞从圣克鲁斯德拉谢拉开始持续传教；1682年4月建立的洛雷托圣母传教站，标志着莫克索斯传教区正式开端。巴拉塞于1686年在马莫雷河畔建立特立尼达，圣佩德罗德莫克索斯则建于1697年，并在1700年成为传教区中心。这些归化村镇把许多不同族群汇聚到拥有教堂音乐和手工业的天主教城镇中，也塑造了更宽泛的莫赫尼奥认同。1768年驱逐耶稣会的命令抵达莫克索斯时，十五个传教村镇转交世俗神职人员；1772年王室委派行政官，1776年起这片领土划入新设立的拉普拉塔总督辖区。

en:
The Puno highlands lie along the north-western shore of Lake Titicaca, around Hatuncolla and Lake Umayo. After Tiwanaku's decline, Colla chiefs raised fortified pukaras on the hills and built the tower-like chullpa tombs of Sillustani for their nobles. Herds of llamas and alpacas grazed the cold plain, potatoes and quinoa grew in high fields, and lake routes and gold-bearing eastern lands gave the chiefs their wealth. In 1444 Hatuncolla was the capital of the Colla ruler Chuchi Capac, yet its settlements were only loosely joined, pressed by the rival Lupaqa and by the fast-growing power of Pachacuti.

The Colla–Inca War of 1445–1450 ended in conquest by Pachacuti and incorporated the country into the Tawantinsuyu as part of Qullasuyu. Francisco Pizarro granted its lands in encomienda in 1535, a Spanish tambo was recorded at Puno in 1543, and a parish for the local population was built in 1563. On 1 May 1657 José de Salcedo discovered the rich Laykakota silver lode, around which San Luis de Alba and the Salcedo brothers' fortune grew. In 1668 the Viceroy Count of Lemos established the Spanish town of San Carlos de Puno as capital of Paucarcolla, on the road between Arequipa, Cuzco, La Paz and Potosí. The Crown created the intendancy of Puno in 1784, and a royal order raised the town to city rank on 14 October 1805.
zh:
普诺高原位于的的喀喀湖西北岸，环绕哈通科拉和乌马约湖。蒂亚瓦纳科衰落之后，科拉首领在山丘上筑起名为普卡拉的堡垒，并在西路斯塔尼为贵族修建塔状的楚尔帕墓。大羊驼和羊驼群在寒冷平原放牧，马铃薯和藜麦生长在高地上，湖上通路与东方产金的土地为首领带来财富。1444年，哈通科拉是科拉统治者楚奇·卡帕克的都城，但各聚落只是松散联合，又受到敌对的卢帕卡人和帕查库特克迅速扩张势力的压迫。

1445—1450年的科拉—印加战争以帕查库特克获胜告终，此地被并入塔万廷苏尤，成为科利亚苏尤的一部分。弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗1535年把这里的土地作为监护征赋地授予；1543年，普诺已有一处西班牙驿站被记录在案，1563年又为当地居民建立教区。1657年5月1日，何塞·德·萨尔塞多发现富饶的莱卡科塔银脉，圣路易斯·德·阿尔瓦矿区和萨尔塞多兄弟的财富由此兴起。1668年，莱莫斯伯爵总督设立西班牙城镇圣卡洛斯·德·普诺，作为保卡科利亚的首府，地处阿雷基帕、库斯科、拉巴斯和波托西之间的道路上。1784年，西班牙王室设立普诺监督管区；1805年10月14日，王室命令把普诺提升为城市。

en:
The Chili Valley runs from the Andean foothills toward Peru's arid southern coast. Yarabaya and Chimba communities, together with Collagua and Cabana villages, dug irrigation canals along its river terraces and kept routes open to the sea. Inca expansion under Pachacuti did not produce a single city here; instead the valley became a southwestern frontier watched over by mitma settlers. In 1444 the hamlets that later became Yanahuara, Cayma and Characato were therefore a string of farming settlements on the edge of Tawantinsuyu, growing grain in the desert and linked to the coastal road toward Camaná.

On 15 August 1540 Juan de la Torre and Garcí Manuel de Carbajal, acting for Francisco Pizarro, moved the settlement of Villa Hermosa de Camaná into the Chili Valley and refounded it as Arequipa; Charles V granted it city status in 1541. Its wheat, maize, wine and brandy fed the mining circuits of Caylloma and Potosí. On 19 February 1600 people in Arequipa witnessed the great eruption of Huaynaputina, which darkened the region with ash, buried fields and killed perhaps 1,000 to 1,500 people. The Catholic see was authorized in 1612, and white sillar churches and monasteries gave the town its lasting appearance. In 1784 the Crown made Arequipa the seat of an intendancy. During the Cuzco revolt of 1814, Mateo Pumacahua and Vicente Angulo took the city on 12 November, but royalists under Juan Ramírez de Orozco recovered it on 9 December. When Peru's independence was proclaimed in 1821, Arequipa remained under royalist control.
zh:
奇利河谷从安第斯山麓伸向秘鲁干旱的南海岸。亚拉瓦亚人和钦巴人同科利亚瓜、卡瓦纳人的村落一起，沿河阶修筑灌渠，并保持着通往海边的道路。印加人在帕查库特克时期扩张至此，并未建立单一城市，而是把这片谷地交由米特马屯垦者戍守，作为帝国西南边境。1444年，后来发展为亚纳瓦拉、凯马和查拉卡托的那些村落，因此是印加边缘上一串农耕聚落；它们在荒漠中出产谷物，并与通往卡马纳的沿海道路相连。

1540年8月15日，胡安·德·拉·托雷和加西·曼努埃尔·德·卡瓦哈尔奉弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗之命，把卡马纳的美丽镇迁入奇利河谷并重建为阿雷基帕；1541年，查理五世授予它城市地位。当地的小麦、玉米、葡萄酒和白兰地供应卡伊约马与波托西的矿业圈。1600年2月19日，阿雷基帕人亲眼看见瓦伊纳普蒂纳火山大喷发；火山灰遮暗天空，田地被掩埋，约有一千至一千五百人丧生。1612年，教廷批准设立阿雷基帕教区，白色凝灰岩建造的教堂和修道院后来塑造了城市面貌。1784年，西班牙王室以阿雷基帕为监督区治所。1814年库斯科起义期间，马特奥·普马卡瓦和比森特·安古洛于11月12日攻占该城，胡安·拉米雷斯·德·奥罗斯科率领保王军在12月9日将其收复。1821年秘鲁宣布独立时，阿雷基帕仍在保王派手中。

en:
Nazca is a group of narrow, river-watered valleys cut through Peru's southern desert between the Andes and the Pacific. Earlier Paracas and Nasca societies built puquios, stone-lined filtration galleries and underground canals that carried groundwater to fields in the Aja, Ingenio and Grande valleys, while coastal settlements supplied fish. Inca expansion began to reach this coast around 1438, and regional history attributes the annexation to Pachacuti, whose officials tied the valleys to Cusco by roads and drew on their harvests. In 1444 Nazca was therefore a recently incorporated Inca coastal frontier, valued for irrigated farming, fishing and the desert road running south toward Arequipa.

Colonial chronicles place the Spanish founding of Santiago de la Nasca on 28 October 1548, when Alonso de Mendoza acted on behalf of Pedro de la Gasca; another tradition places the formal foundation in 1591 under Viceroy García Hurtado de Mendoza. Vineyards soon became the valleys' wealth, above all in the Ingenio Valley, where Jesuit estates owned by the colleges of Cuzco and Lima produced wine and grape brandy in large ceramic jars with the labour of enslaved Africans. After Charles III expelled the Jesuits in 1767, the Crown confiscated these properties. On 14 October 1820, during San Martín's coastal campaign, 250 patriots under Manuel Rojas Argerich surprised Colonel Manuel Quimper's royalist detachment in Nazca; the town swore independence two days later. Its formal town government was established on 29 August 1821.
zh:
纳斯卡是安第斯山与太平洋之间、秘鲁南部荒漠中一组由河流滋养的狭窄谷地。更早的帕拉卡斯和纳斯卡社会修建了普基奥斯，即以石砌渗水廊道和地下暗渠把地下水引入阿哈、因赫尼奥和格兰德河谷农田的系统，沿海聚落则提供鱼类。印加扩张约在1438年开始抵达这段海岸；地区史把这些谷地并入帝国归于帕查库特克，他的官员用道路把谷地连接到库斯科，并征调当地农产品。1444年的纳斯卡因此是印加刚纳入版图不久的沿海边地，价值在灌溉农业、渔业，以及南通阿雷基帕的荒漠道路。

殖民地编年史多把圣地亚哥·德·拉纳斯卡的西班牙建城时间定在1548年10月28日，由阿隆索·德·门多萨代表佩德罗·德·拉·加斯卡完成；另一种传统则称正式建城是在1591年总督加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨任内。葡萄园很快成为诸谷地的财富，尤以因赫尼奥河谷为盛；库斯科和利马耶稣会学院拥有的庄园使用非洲奴隶劳动，把葡萄酒和葡萄白兰地装入大型陶瓮。1767年卡洛斯三世驱逐耶稣会后，这些产业被王室没收。1820年10月14日，圣马丁沿海战役期间，曼努埃尔·罗哈斯·阿尔赫里奇率250名独立派士兵在纳斯卡突袭曼努埃尔·金佩尔上校的保王分队；两天后，城镇宣誓独立。1821年8月29日，纳斯卡正式建立镇政机构。

en:
Abancay occupies a warm grain-growing valley on the eastern Andean slope, beneath Mount Ampay and north of the Pachachaca River. Long before the Spanish conquest it held Quechua agricultural villages, while the Pachachaca marked the border country with the Chancas beyond. Its native name was connected with the amancay, a white mountain flower. In 1444 this made Abancay a sensitive Cuzco frontier, crossed by routes between the highland capital, the southern mountains and the roads to the coast.

On 12 July 1537 those roads brought the conquistadors' civil war to the valley. Alonso de Alvarado, sent by Francisco Pizarro toward Cuzco, held the Abancay bridge and ford against Diego de Almagro's lieutenant Rodrigo Orgóñez; Pedro de Lerma's desertion let the Almagrists overwhelm and capture Alvarado, opening the struggle that ended with Almagro's defeat at Las Salinas in April 1538. The Spanish formally founded Villa de Santiago de los Reyes de Amancay on 3 November 1574. Early encomiendas planted sugar cane for aguardiente, and mule trains made the town a freight link between the coast and the southeastern Andes. In 1781 Micaela Bastidas, born into one of the area's muleteer families, joined Túpac Amaru II's rising against Spanish rule.
zh:
阿班凯坐落在安第斯山东坡温暖的谷物河谷，位于安佩伊山下、帕查查卡河以北。西班牙征服以前很久，这里已有克丘亚人的农业村落，帕查查卡河一线则是与更远的昌卡人相邻的边地。本地名称与「阿曼凯」这种白色山花有关。1444年的阿班凯因此是库斯科敏感的前沿，连接高原都城、南部山地和通往沿海道路的商路都从这里经过。

1537年7月12日，征服者之间的内战随这些道路打到河谷。阿隆索·德·阿尔瓦拉多奉弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗之命驰援库斯科，扼守阿班凯桥和渡口，迎战迭戈·阿尔马格罗的部将罗德里戈·奥戈涅斯；佩德罗·德·莱尔马临阵倒戈，使阿尔马格罗一方击溃并俘虏阿尔瓦拉多。这场冲突开启的争斗，最终以1538年4月阿尔马格罗在萨利纳斯战败告终。1574年11月3日，西班牙人正式建立「阿曼凯的圣地亚哥·德·洛斯雷耶斯镇」。早期监护地种植甘蔗酿造烧酒，骡队则使该镇成为沿海与安第斯东南部之间的货运枢纽。1781年，出身当地骡夫家庭的米卡埃拉·巴斯蒂达斯参与了图帕克·阿马鲁二世反抗西班牙统治的起义。

en:
Cuzco lies high in a valley of the eastern Andes, the navel of the Inca world. The Killke people raised the first walls of the Sacsayhuamán citadel above it around 1100, and after 1438 the Sapa Inca Pachacuti turned the old town into the capital of Tawantinsuyu, laying it out in the shape of a puma with the great plaza of Haucaypata at its breast. Roads ran from its quarters toward every suyu of the empire, while the Coricancha, the temple of the Sun, was sheathed in gold. In 1444 Pachacuti and his son Túpac Yupanqui were carrying Inca arms from Quito toward the Maule, and Cuzco was the richest and holiest city of the Andes.

Atahualpa's generals had only just seized the city in the civil war when, on 15 November 1533, Pizarro's Spaniards entered and stripped its palaces; on 23 March 1534 Almagro refounded it in the Spanish fashion around the same plaza. In May 1536 Manco Inca rose, burned the city and besieged its garrison for ten months before withdrawing to Vilcabamba, whose last Inca, Túpac Amaru I, was beheaded in the plaza in 1572. The conquerors' own feud was settled on 6 April 1538 at Las Salinas outside Cuzco, where the Pizarro brothers defeated Almagro, who was executed in the city that July.
