Europeans first documented these bands in November 1528, when survivors of Pánfilo de Narváez's expedition were cast ashore on Isla de Malhado near Galveston; Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca's account became the earliest ethnohistorical record. After La Salle crossed the upper Atakapa country in 1686–1687, a Spanish search party on the Calcasieu in April 1687 recovered Nicolás de Vargas, a castaway Mexican boy adopted by an Atakapa family, while Enrique Barroto logged their deerskin dress and tattoos. Permanent French pressure followed the founding of Louisiana in 1699. French traders entered the Attakapas country, and after Louisiana passed to Spain in 1762, Acadians led by Joseph Broussard were settled there in 1765. The 1766 census counted 409 inhabitants in the Attakapas region, and Eastern Atakapa families joined the cattle trade and registered brands at Poste des Attakapas. After the Louisiana Purchase of 1803, American officials organized Attakapas Parish in 1805, the year John Sibley estimated only about fifty Atakapa men remained in Louisiana while planters acquired communal lands along the Mermentau and Vermilion.
zh:
伊沙克意为「人」，邻族和后来的欧洲人称他们为阿塔卡帕。他们的沼泽草原与河湖水乡从加尔维斯顿湾、特里尼蒂河向东延伸至卡尔克苏河、梅门托河和弗米利恩河。1444年，阿科基萨、比戴、卡尔克苏等亲缘群体各自生活在这些流域，使用一种孤立语言。他们捕鱼、猎取小动物、采集根茎和浆果，并把干鱼、鲨鱼牙、兽皮和盐沿湾岸商路输往卡多、奇蒂马查和卡兰卡瓦邻人那里。鹿皮衣、纹身和便于迁移的营地，适应了潮汐、水道与河口交错的海岸。

欧洲人最早在1528年11月留下关于这些群体的记载，当时潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯远征的幸存者被冲上加尔维斯顿附近的「厄运岛」，阿尔瓦·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡的记述成为最早的民族史资料。拉萨尔1686至1687年穿过阿塔卡帕北部后，一支西班牙搜索队1687年4月在卡尔克苏河找回被阿塔卡帕家庭收养的墨西哥漂流男孩尼古拉斯·德·巴尔加斯，恩里克·巴罗托的航海日志还记录了鹿皮衣与纹身。法国1699年建立路易斯安那后，长期殖民压力随之而来。法国商人进入阿塔卡帕地区；路易斯安那1762年转交西班牙后，约瑟夫·布鲁萨尔率领的阿卡迪亚人在1765年被安置到此。1766年人口普查显示阿塔卡帕地区有409名居民，东阿塔卡帕群体也参与牛群贸易并在阿塔卡帕驿站登记牲畜烙印。1803年路易斯安那购地后，美国官员在1805年设立阿塔卡帕堂区；同年约翰·西布利估计路易斯安那的阿塔卡帕男子只剩约五十人，而种植园主正在取得梅门托河与弗米利恩河沿岸的共有土地。

en:
Nawunena, the “Southern People,” was the southernmost Arapaho division, with its own Nawathinehena speech. Their later country lay on the dry High Plains, where short grass climbs toward the Rocky Mountain front. In 1444 this was still a pre-horse bison land. Pedestrian Apache hunters moved with dog travois, pitched hide lodges, dried meat into jerky and pemmican, and traded across the plains in sign language. The Arapaho themselves were then far to the northeast, farming and hunting with the people who would become the Gros Ventre around the Red River valley.

In 1541 Francisco Vázquez de Coronado's army crossed the southern High Plains in search of Quivira and met Querecho Apaches on the Llano Estacado, leaving the first European description of dog-drawn travois and bison-hide lodges. Early in the eighteenth century Ojibwe pressure pushed the Arapaho and Gros Ventre toward the upper Missouri; there the peoples separated, and Arapaho bands moved south into Wyoming and Colorado as they adopted horse nomadism. They allied with the Cheyenne, raided and traded across the bison plains, and by the late eighteenth century the divisions south of the Gros Ventre had consolidated as Arapaho. About 1800 the southern camps began to form the Nawunena, and by 1821 they were part of a wide horse-and-fur network stretching from the Platte toward the Arkansas River.
zh:
Nawunena意为「南方人」，是阿拉帕霍人最南的一支，曾使用自己的Nawathinehena方言。他们后来的家园位于干旱的高地平原，短草草原一路抬升，通向落基山东麓。1444年，这里仍是前马匹时代的野牛之地。步行的阿帕奇猎人靠狗拉橇迁移，搭起兽皮营帐，把肉制成肉干和肉糜饼，并通过手势语在平原上交易。那时阿拉帕霍人还远在东北方，与后来成为格罗斯文特人的族群一起在雷德河谷农耕和狩猎。

1541年，弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多的军队为寻找基维拉穿越南部高地平原，在拉诺埃斯塔卡多遇到Querecho阿帕奇人，留下欧洲人对狗拉橇和野牛皮营帐的最早描述。18世纪初，欧及布威人的压力把阿拉帕霍人与格罗斯文特人推向密苏里河上游；两族在途中分离，阿拉帕霍诸支接受骑马游牧，南下进入怀俄明和科罗拉多。他们与夏延人结盟，在野牛草原上袭掠和贸易；到18世纪末，格罗斯文特人以南的各支已整合为阿拉帕霍人。约1800年，南方营地开始形成Nawunena；到1821年，他们已成为从普拉特河延伸至阿肯色河的庞大马匹与皮草网络的一部分。

en:
Tokinahyup is a sweep of shortgrass plains between the Arkansas River and the smaller streams of southern Kansas. In 1444 its valley camps and buffalo hunts belonged to the wider Caddoan world of the Pawnee and Wichita. Families planted corn, beans and squash in river-bottom fields and joined communal hunts on foot, living in grass or earth lodges when the bands gathered along the watercourses.

The first Europeans drew near in 1541, when Coronado followed the Arkansas into Quivira and found farming villages rather than gold. Horses reached the southern plains later in the seventeenth century, strengthening Apache and Comanche riders and drawing French trade westward. La Salle's Mississippi claim of 1682 included this country as Louisiana; it passed from France to Spain in 1762, returned to France, and was sold to the United States in 1803. During those years the Kiowa and their Naisha Apache allies were moving south toward these hunting grounds, but in 1821 the prairie itself remained Native ground.
zh:
托基纳休普是阿肯色河与堪萨斯南部诸溪之间的一片短草平原。1444年，河畔营地和野牛猎场属于波尼人与威奇托人所在的卡多语世界。各家族在河谷低地种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，并结成队伍徒步围猎野牛；各部群在水道旁聚集时，住在草屋或土屋之中。

1541年，科罗纳多沿阿肯色河进入基维拉，第一批欧洲人由此逼近此地，但他见到的只是农耕村落，并没有黄金。17世纪后期，马匹传入南部平原，阿帕奇和科曼奇骑手的势力增强，也把法国贸易引向西方。拉萨尔1682年宣称密西西比河流域后，这里被划入路易斯安那；1762年由法国转交西班牙，后来归还法国，1803年又被售予美国。那些年间，基奥瓦人与纳伊沙阿帕奇盟友正南下趋近这片猎场，但到1821年，草原本身仍是原住民的土地。

en:
Naisha preserves Ná'ishą, the later Plains Apache name for their people, while the camp name Jicarilla recalls the basket-making Eastern Apache bands who also ranged across the grassland between the Canadian and Arkansas rivers. In 1444 its short-grass pastures and cottonwood bottoms were crossed on foot by Southern Athabaskan bison hunters using dog travois. They dried meat and hides, knew the seasonal watercourses, and exchanged plains products with farming villages before horses or Europeans reached the Southern Plains.

Coronado's expedition knew the Canadian as the Río Cicuyé in 1541 while pushing toward Quivira, and Juan de Oñate followed the same river east in 1601. Horses spread after the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, and mounted Comanche bands pressed the Apache through the following century. The Ná'ishą, closely allied with the Kiowa, lived around the upper Missouri early in the 1700s and did not make this part of the Southern Plains their principal range until around 1800. In 1821 the grassland remained Indian country, claimed only from a distance by newly independent Mexico.
zh:
纳伊沙保留了平原阿帕奇人后来的自称Ná'ishą；首府名希卡里亚，则令人想起也会在加拿大河与阿肯色河之间草原活动的制篮东阿帕奇群体。1444年，短草牧场和三角叶杨河谷由南阿萨巴斯卡野牛猎人步行往来，他们用狗拖拉沃伊橇，晒制肉干、加工兽皮，熟悉季节性水道，并在马匹和欧洲人到达南部平原以前，同务农村落交换草原物产。

1541年，科罗纳多远征基维拉时把加拿大河称作「西库耶河」；1601年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特又沿这条河东下。1680年普韦布洛起义后马匹扩散，在接下来的一个世纪里，骑马的科曼奇群体不断压迫阿帕奇人。纳伊沙人与基奥瓦人关系密切，18世纪初住在密苏里河上游，约1800年才把南部平原这一带作为主要活动范围。1821年，这里仍是印第安人的土地，只被独立之初的墨西哥远远宣称管辖。

en:
Kitkit'ish preserves Kitikiti'sh, the name the Wichita gave themselves. Their towns belonged to the Great Bend farming world along the Arkansas and Walnut rivers, where fertile bottoms were planted with maize, beans, squash and sunflowers while bison hunts crossed the surrounding prairie. In 1444 the Wichita lived in round, grass-thatched lodges with granaries close by, tattooed straight marks around their eyes, and had never seen horses or Europeans.

Members of Coronado's expedition reached the Arkansas on 29 June 1541 and entered the Wichita province they called Quivira, finding about twenty-five farming villages, some with as many as two hundred houses, but no gold. Juan de Oñate visited the great Walnut River settlement of Etzanoa in 1601 and counted more than twelve hundred houses among the people he called Rayados, or 'striped ones'. Disease and pressure from Apache and Osage raiders weakened these towns in the following century; Quivira was abandoned early in the 1700s, and by 1757 the Wichita had moved their main villages south to the Red River. The Louisiana Purchase carried the region to the United States in 1803, and the Adams-Onís Treaty, in force in 1821, made the Arkansas a formal frontier with Mexico.
zh:
基特基蒂什保存了威奇塔人的自称Kitikiti'sh。他们的村镇属于阿肯色河与沃尔纳特河沿岸的大弯农业圈：肥沃河滩种着玉米、豆类、南瓜和向日葵，男人则到周围草原猎野牛。1444年的威奇塔人住在草顶圆屋中，屋旁就是谷仓；他们在眼周纹出直线，既没有见过马，也没有见过欧洲人。

1541年6月29日，科罗纳多远征队抵达阿肯色河，进入他们称作基维拉的威奇塔地区，见到约二十五座务农村镇，有些村镇多至两百座房屋，却没有黄金。1601年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特到访沃尔纳特河畔的大定居点埃特萨诺阿，在他称为「雷亚多人」（意为「纹线之人」）的居民中数出一千二百多座房屋。此后一个世纪，疫病以及阿帕奇人、奥塞奇人的袭扰削弱了这些村镇；基维拉在18世纪初被废弃，到1757年威奇塔人已把主要村镇南移到雷德河。1803年路易斯安那购地使这片地区在名义上转归美国，1821年生效的《亚当斯-奥尼斯条约》又把阿肯色河定为同墨西哥之间的正式边界。

en:
The Chitimacha, whose name means 'people who live on the Grand River', held the Atchafalaya Basin, the maze of swamps, bayous and lakes between the Mississippi and the Gulf. Their unfortified villages, some five hundred strong, stood on ground so tangled that no enemy could reach them. The women grew many varieties of corn, beans and squash while the men took deer, turkey, alligator and fish; dugouts hollowed from single cypress logs, some carrying fifty men, linked the villages, and surplus grain was carried north to middlemen such as the Avoyel in exchange for the flint their delta lacked. Nobles and commoners even spoke different dialects, and their tongue was a language isolate. In 1444 the four Chitimacha bands were the undisputed masters of one of the richest estuaries in North America.

European diseases reached them long before Europeans did: historians put the four bands at some 20,000 around 1500 but at only about 4,000 in 1650. Direct French contact came at the end of the century, and in 1707 the Louisiana French opened a long war against them; the Chitimacha were driven from their Bayou Lafourche villages and many captives sold into slavery. In 1730 the French at New Orleans turned on the Chawasha band and all but destroyed it, and its survivors joined the Chitimacha, who later also absorbed remnants of the Taensa and some Houma. After the British took Acadia, Acadian exiles began settling the basin in the 1760s; Chitimacha families married among these Cajun newcomers and turned Catholic, a small people holding on along Bayou Teche.
zh:
奇蒂马查人的名字意为「住在大河上的人」，他们占据着阿查法拉亚盆地——密西西比河与墨西哥湾之间由沼泽、河汊和湖泊织成的迷宫。他们的村落不设栅栏，大的足有五百人，周边水道泥泞难行，外敌根本无法靠近。妇女栽种多种玉米、菜豆和南瓜，男子猎鹿、捕野火鸡和短吻鳄、下河捕鱼；整根柏木剜成的独木舟可载五十人，把各村彼此相连，多余的谷物向北经阿沃耶尔人这样的中转商，换回三角洲所缺的燧石。贵族与平民甚至各说不同的方言，而他们的语言是一门孤立语言。1444年时，奇蒂马查人的四个族群仍是这片北美最丰饶河口的无可争议的主人。

欧洲人带来的疫病比欧洲人本人先到：据史学家估计，1500年前后四族合计约有两万人，到1650年只剩下约四千。与法国人的直接接触迟至17世纪末，1707年，路易斯安那的法国人对他们发动了一场旷日持久的战争，奇蒂马查人被逐出拉福什河汊的村落，许多俘虏被卖为奴隶。1730年，新奥尔良的法国人又转而剿灭查瓦沙部族，幸存者并入奇蒂马查；此后他们又接纳了坦萨人的残余和部分霍马人。英国夺取阿卡迪亚后，阿卡迪亚流亡者从1760年代起迁入盆地，他们就是后来的卡津人；奇蒂马查人与这些新来者通婚并改宗天主教，作为一个小小的民族在泰什河汊一带坚持了下来。

en:
The Kadohadacho were the northern cluster of the three Caddo confederacies. Caddoan villages and ceremonial mound centres had emerged in the Piney Woods and Red River bottomlands by around 1000, and the communities later recorded around the Great Bend planted maize, beans and squash, gathered pecans, and traded bows and pottery. In 1444 their country lay beyond European reach, linked to neighbouring Caddo, Hasinai and Natchitoches towns by language, ceremony and exchange.

The de Soto expedition met Kadohadacho travellers in 1542, without entering the Red River villages. In 1687 the Kadohadacho sheltered survivors of La Salle's French venture and thereafter traded with French Louisiana. Chickasaw raiders struck the villages early in the eighteenth century, killing or enslaving many people and driving survivors toward the Nasoni and Natchitoches. By the late eighteenth century the remaining Kadohadacho had left the Great Bend for their kinsmen's country around Natchitoches.
zh:
卡多哈达乔是卡多三大联盟中位置最北的一支。约1000年时，卡多语族群的村落和祭祀土墩中心已在松林地带与红河低地形成；后来记载中居于红河大弯一带的社群种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，采集山核桃，并用弓和陶器交易。1444年，欧洲人尚未到达这里，卡多哈达乔通过语言、仪式和交换，与邻近的卡多、哈西奈和纳基托什城镇相连。

1542年，德索托远征队遇到卡多哈达乔游群，但没有进入红河沿岸的村落。1687年，卡多哈达乔收留了拉萨尔法国远征的幸存者，此后与法属路易斯安那贸易。18世纪初，奇克索袭击者攻打这些村庄，杀死或掳走许多居民，幸存者逃往纳索尼和纳基托什。到18世纪后期，余下的卡多哈达乔人已离开红河大弯，前往纳基托什一带投奔亲族。

en:
Anilco was the Mississippian river province recorded by Spanish chroniclers on the lower Arkansas, near its confluence with the Mississippi. The Menard–Hodges site, the strongest archaeological candidate for its chief town, had been occupied since the Baytown period of 300–700 and contained two large platform mounds and several house mounds. In 1444 its farmers drew maize from the Arkansas bottomlands, while its plaza and mounds tied the district to the wider Mississippian world of Casqui and Pacaha.

The de Soto expedition entered the region in 1541. In May 1542, as de Soto lay dying nearby, his men sacked Anilco, fearing it would ally with Quigualtam down the Mississippi. When Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet passed in 1673, the French knew the river villages as Akansea, and the Menard locality later held the Quapaw village of Osotouy. Henri de Tonti founded Arkansas Post nearby in the summer of 1686 to exchange French goods for furs. John Law's plantation scheme failed, Chickasaw raiders under Payamataha attacked in 1749, and the post passed to Spain in 1763 before James Colbert's British and Chickasaw force raided it in 1783. It became American in 1803 and was the first capital of Arkansas Territory from 1819 to 1821.
zh:
阿尼尔科是西班牙编年史所记阿肯色河下游、临近密西西比河汇流处的一个密西西比文化地区。梅纳德—霍奇斯遗址是其主要城邑最有力的考古候选地，早在300年至700年的贝敦时期已有人居住，遗址内有两座大型台墩和若干住宅土墩。1444年，这里的农人在阿肯色河低地种植玉米，广场与土墩也把该地区同卡斯奎、帕卡哈等更大的密西西比文化世界连接起来。

1541年，德索托远征队进入这一地区。1542年5月德索托在附近病死前，部下因担心阿尼尔科会同密西西比河下游的基瓜尔坦结盟而洗劫该地。1673年雅克·马凯特和路易·若利埃经过时，法国人已把河畔诸村称为阿肯色；梅纳德一带后来有夸帕人的奥索图伊村。1686年夏，亨利·德·通蒂在附近设立阿肯色站，用法国货物交换毛皮。约翰·劳的种植园开发失败后，帕亚马塔哈率领的奇克索袭击者又在1749年来攻；站点于1763年转归西班牙，1783年遭詹姆斯·科尔伯特所率英国与奇克索部队突袭。它在1803年归入美国，1819年至1821年成为阿肯色领地的第一个首府。

en:
Yscani is an early spelling of Iscani, a Caddoan Wichita group later often identified with the Waco. The province lies on the prairie-and-oak edge where the southern plains meet the Cross Timbers, around the Salt Fork of the Arkansas. In 1444 hunters followed bison and deer through grassland broken by walnut and bur-oak groves, moving on foot with dog travois before horses reached the region, while related Wichita towns to the north kept maize, bean and squash fields.

The Teyas whom Coronado met on the plains to the west in 1541 may have been ancestors of the Escanjaques and Iscani. In 1601 Juan de Oñate followed the Canadian River eastward, then crossed to the Salt Fork and found an Escanjaque camp of more than five thousand people in six hundred round lodges, some twenty-seven metres across and covered with dressed bison hides. Oñate says they planted no crops and lived by the bison hunt. They reported the Rayado town of Etzanoa about twenty kilometres away and guided the Spaniards north, seeking allies against their enemies, but fought Oñate on his return. Later records call the related Wichita band the Iscani or Yscani; Iscani warriors stood with the Taovaya and Comanche at the Twin Villages in 1759, and the smallpox of 1777–78 further weakened the Wichita towns. The Louisiana Purchase nominally transferred the region to the United States in 1803, yet in 1821 no European town had been planted on this oak-fringed prairie.
zh:
阿斯卡尼（Yscani）是伊斯卡尼（Iscani）的早期拼法，这是一支说卡多语族语言的威奇塔群体，后来常被比定为韦科人。本省位于南部平原与十字林交会的草原—橡树林缘，环绕阿肯色河的索尔特支流。1444年，猎人们随着野牛和鹿群穿行在间有胡桃林与大果栎林的草原上；在马匹传入以前，他们步行迁移，用狗拖拉沃伊橇，北方的威奇塔亲族村镇则种植玉米、豆类和南瓜。

1541年，科罗纳多在西方草原遇到的特亚人，可能就是埃斯坎哈克人和伊斯卡尼人的先祖。1601年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特沿加拿大河东进，再转至索尔特支流，发现一座有五千多人、六百座圆屋的埃斯坎哈克营地；有些圆屋直径达二十七米，覆以鞣制野牛皮。奥尼亚特记载他们不种庄稼，以猎野牛为生。他们说雷亚多人大镇埃特萨诺阿在约二十公里外，并引导西班牙人北行，想拉拢其对付仇敌，但在奥尼亚特返程时又与之交战。后来的文献把这支与威奇塔有关的群体称为伊斯卡尼或阿斯卡尼；1759年，伊斯卡尼战士同塔韦哈什人和科曼奇人并肩作战于双子村，1777年至1778年的天花又进一步削弱了威奇塔诸镇。1803年路易斯安那购地使这片地区在名义上转归美国，但到1821年，这片橡树林环绕的草原上仍未建立欧洲人的城镇。

en:
Casqui was a Mississippian paramount polity along the St. Francis and Tyronza rivers. Its likely chief town, the Parkin site at their confluence, was a 17-acre palisaded village with a river-fed moat, one large substructure mound and six smaller mounds around a plaza. Around it lay about twenty-one Parkin-phase villages, set among maize fields, fish-rich waters and pecan groves. In 1444 rivalry with Pacaha and other neighbouring phases kept the people behind timber walls, while the chief's hold on the waterways controlled travel and exchange.

The Hernando de Soto expedition reached Casqui in 1541. The chief came more than a mile to meet it, and the Spaniards baptized several villagers before raising a tall wooden cross on the principal mound. When the expedition moved on to Pacaha, Casqui's men sacked their old enemy's town; de Soto then threatened retaliation until the spoils were returned and the two chiefs ate together and made peace. Spanish beads, bells and musket balls recovered at Parkin confirm the encounter. The palisaded village was abandoned around 1650, and by the 1670s the river country was held by Quapaw-speakers, leaving Casqui known chiefly through the Spanish journals.
zh:
卡斯基是圣弗朗西斯河与蒂龙扎河一带的密西西比文化酋邦。其主邑最可能是两河汇流处的帕金遗址：一座17英亩、以木栅和河水壕沟环绕的村镇，中央广场旁有一座大台墩和六座较小土墩。周边约有21个帕金阶段村落，散布在玉米田、富产鱼类的水道和山核桃林之间。1444年，由于同帕卡哈等邻近群体长期敌对，人们栖身于木墙之后；帕金主邑据守水路，也使酋长能够控制通行和交换。

1541年，德索托远征队抵达卡斯基。酋长走出一英里多迎接，西班牙人为几名村民施洗，并在主土墩上竖起高大木十字架。远征队随后前往帕卡哈，卡斯基人趁机洗劫这座旧敌的城镇；德索托威胁报复，卡斯基人才归还战利品，两名酋长随后共餐议和。帕金出土的西班牙玻璃珠、铃铛和火枪弹印证了这次相遇。这座木栅村镇约在1650年废弃，到1670年代，河谷已由使用夸帕语的人群占据，卡斯基之名主要保存在西班牙人的行记中。

en:
Kanza is the prairie of the Kansas River, which winds through a broad valley on its way to the Missouri. In 1444 Caddoan-speaking Pawnee bands planted corn, beans and squash on its bottoms and hunted buffalo on the surrounding grasslands, gathering in villages of earth and grass lodges. The river gave access from the Missouri to the bison plains.

Coronado's Quivira expedition crossed central Kansas to the southwest in 1541, but sustained European contact came with the French. The Dhegiha Kanza had moved up the Missouri during the early or middle seventeenth century, and Marquette's 1673 map is the first certain record. Bourgmont visited a Kanza village in 1724, and in 1744 the French built Fort de Cavagnial on the Missouri to secure high-grade furs; its garrison withdrew about 1764 after Louisiana passed to Spain. By the 1790s the principal Kanza village lay on the Kansas River near the mouth of the Big Blue. After the Louisiana Purchase of 1803, Lewis and Clark saw the old French ruins and estimated about 1,500 Kanza, their numbers reduced by wars with neighbors. The valley remained their farming and hunting country in 1821.
zh:
坎扎是堪萨斯河流经的草原，宽阔河谷一路通向密苏里河。1444年，说卡多语的波尼群体在低地种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，到周围草原猎捕野牛，并在土屋与草屋村落中聚集。堪萨斯河把密苏里河水道与野牛草原连接起来。

1541年，科罗纳多的基维拉远征经过西南方的堪萨斯中部；持续的欧洲接触要等到法国人才开始。德吉哈人的坎扎支系在17世纪早中期沿密苏里河上迁，1673年的马凯特地图是第一份可靠记载。1724年，布格蒙探访了坎扎村落；1744年，法国人在密苏里河修建卡瓦尼亚勒堡，以获取优质毛皮，路易斯安那转归西班牙后，驻军约于1764年撤离。到1790年代，坎扎主村位于堪萨斯河近大布鲁河口一带。1803年路易斯安那购地后，刘易斯与克拉克见到法国旧堡遗迹，并估计坎扎人约有1500人，人口已因与邻部交战而减少；到1821年，这片河谷仍是他们耕作与狩猎之地。

en:
The Osage River winds through the wooded northern Ozarks, and here the Pahatsi — the 'Upland Forest' band of the Osage, who call themselves the Wazhazhe, 'Children of the Middle Waters' — kept their permanent villages on open hilltops above the bottoms; the French would later call them the Great Osage. Women raised corn, beans and squash by the lodges, men hunted deer in the oak forest and twice a year struck out after buffalo on the western plains, on foot, for the horse was still unknown in 1444. Clans split into Sky People and Earth People, and the force of Wakonda ran through every animal and stream. No European neighbour existed then; the world turned on kinship, ceremony and the blood feud.

The first European trace is the map made by Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet in 1673, which places the Osage on the river that now bears their name. Horses had reached them by 1690, and trade and war with the French drew them into Louisiana: Claude-Charles Du Tisné led the first official French expedition to the Great Osage villages in 1719, and in 1725 Osage chiefs were presented to Louis XV at Versailles and hunted with him in the royal forest. Allied with France, the Osage harried the Illiniwek and by 1750 had defeated the Caddoan villages to the south, holding sway between the Missouri and the Red rivers. In 1795 the Chouteau brothers of St Louis, trading under a Spanish licence, built Fort Carondelet inside the Great Osage village. Smallpox swept the bands in 1801–2, killing perhaps 2,000 Osage, and Lewis and Clark in 1804 found the Great Osage on the Osage River, the whole nation then numbering about 5,500. The treaty made at Fort Osage in 1808 ceded their Missouri lands, and the Treaty of St Louis in 1818 stripped away more of the old grounds, opening the long retreat towards Kansas.
zh:
奥塞奇河蜿蜒穿过林木葱郁的欧扎克北部山区，帕哈齐人——奥塞奇（自称瓦扎热，意为「中游之水的儿女」）的「山林」一支——把永久村落建在河滩之上开阔的山顶，法国人后来称他们为大奥塞奇。女人们在屋舍旁种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，男人在橡树林中猎鹿，每年两度徒步西征大平原围猎野牛，因为1444年时马还没有传入。氏族分作「天人」与「地人」两个半偶族，瓦孔达的力量穿行于每一头走兽、每一道溪流之间。那时他们没有欧洲邻居，世界靠亲属、仪典和血仇维系。

欧洲人留下的最早痕迹，是1673年雅克·马凯特与路易·若利埃绘制的地图，图上把奥塞奇人标在这条后来以他们命名的河畔。到1690年，马已传入；与法国人的贸易和战争把他们卷入路易斯安那：1719年，克洛德-夏尔·迪蒂内率第一支法国官方远征队到访大奥塞奇诸村；1725年，奥塞奇首领们在凡尔赛觐见路易十五，并随他在王室森林行猎。与法国结盟后，他们攻伐伊利诺伊人，到1750年又击败南方的卡多语村落，称雄于密苏里河与红河之间。1795年，圣路易斯的舒托兄弟凭西班牙当局的贸易特许，把卡龙德莱特堡直接修进了大奥塞奇人的村子。1801至1802年天花横扫各支，约两千名奥塞奇人病死；1804年刘易斯与克拉克发现大奥塞奇人居于奥塞奇河畔，整个民族当时约有五千五百人。1808年在奥塞奇堡签订的条约割走了他们在密苏里的土地，1818年的《圣路易斯条约》又削去大片故地，开启了迁往堪萨斯的漫长过程。

en:
The Tamaroa were an Algonquian-speaking band of the Illiniwek confederacy, holding the key stretch of the upper Mississippi on both banks around the mouths of the Illinois and Missouri rivers. Perhaps 3,000 strong, they lived in mat-covered lodges, raised corn, beans and squash on the floodplain and hunted bison on the prairies. Their chief village, Tamaroa, stood on the east bank beside the grass-grown mounds of a far older, long-abandoned town. In 1444 the great confluence was a native crossroads, where Illinois bands met Siouan peoples and parties from the lower Mississippi, and no European had yet reached it.

Louis Jolliet and Jacques Marquette passed the confluence in 1673, and in 1682 La Salle counted about 600 lodges at Tamaroa. In 1696 Father Pinet founded the Mission of the Holy Family beside the village, drawing the Cahokia band to settle with them; disease and liquor soon cut the two groups to ninety dwellings. In 1703 the Tamaroa joined the Kaskaskia at the mouth of the Kaskaskia River, where a French town grew into a wheat and fur centre of the Illinois Country. Chickasaw and Shawnee raids thinned them further, and after France ceded the east bank in 1763 the Ottawa leader Pontiac was killed near Cahokia in 1769. Jean-Baptiste de Coigne, born of a Tamaroa mother and a French trader, led a Kaskaskia, Tamaroa and Cahokia alliance that aided George Rogers Clark in 1778 and later visited Thomas Jefferson in Virginia. In 1803 the surviving Tamaroa were counted among the Kaskaskia, and five of their leaders signed the Treaty of Edwardsville in 1818, ceding half of Illinois.
zh:
塔马罗厄人是伊利尼韦克联盟中说阿尔冈昆语的一支，据有密西西比河上游最要紧的一段河身——伊利诺伊河与密苏里河两个河口之间的两岸。他们约有三千人，住在草席覆顶的棚屋里，在河漫滩种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，又到草原猎捕野牛。主村塔马罗厄位于东岸，挨着一座早已废弃的古城留下的、长满野草的土丘。1444年，大河交汇处是原住民的通衢，伊利尼各支在此与说苏语的族群、密西西比河下游来的队伍往来，欧洲人尚未到此。

1673年，路易·乔利埃特与雅克·马凯特驶过两河交汇之处；1682年，拉萨尔在塔马罗厄数到约六百座棚屋。1696年，皮内神父在村旁建立圣家传教站，引来卡霍基亚一支同住，疫病和烈酒很快把两支人削减到只剩九十处住所。1703年，塔马罗厄人在卡斯卡基亚河口并入卡斯卡基亚人，一座同名法国城镇在那里成长为伊利诺伊地区小麦与皮货的中心。奇克索人和肖尼人的袭扰使他们进一步凋零；1763年法国割让密西西比河以东土地后，渥太华首领庞蒂亚克于1769年在卡霍基亚附近被杀。让-巴蒂斯特·德·夸涅的母亲是塔马罗厄人、父亲是法国商人，他统领卡斯卡基亚、塔马罗厄与卡霍基亚联盟，1778年协助乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克，后来还曾前往弗吉尼亚面见托马斯·杰斐逊。1803年，幸存的塔马罗厄人被计入卡斯卡基亚人；1818年，他们的五名首领在《爱德华兹维尔条约》上签字，割让了伊利诺伊的一半土地。

en:
The Platte bottomlands here are the heart of Pawnee country, home of the Tsawi – the Chaui, 'People in the Middle', whom French traders called the Grand Pawnee and who took precedence among the four Pawnee bands. Their villages were clusters of dome-shaped earth lodges on the river terraces; the women raised corn, beans and squash in the bottom fields, and each summer the whole community marched out on foot behind the priests of the sacred bundles for the buffalo hunt. In 1444 neither horses nor Europeans had yet reached the Platte, and the Chaui world ran from the Skidi villages on the Loup to the Kitkehahki villages on the Republican.

The first Europeans to draw near were Spaniards: in 1541 Coronado's entrada reached Quivira on the Arkansas and was met at its edge by the people of Harahey, likely Pawnee kin. In August 1720 the Skidi villages on the Loup destroyed the Villasur expedition, killing Villasur, 45 other Spaniards and 11 Pueblo auxiliaries. Around 1770 the Chaui led the southern bands north from the Arkansas and settled the Platte, their main village standing where Central City later rose; a brief war with the Skidi ended in the latter's defeat and their acceptance of the Chaui chiefs as heads of the nation. Smallpox swept the Pawnee villages from about 1760, shrinking the Skidi from eight large villages in 1725 to one by 1800. In 1806 the rival expeditions of Melgares and Pike came to win the Pawnees' allegiance, and in 1818 the Grand Pawnee signed their first treaty with the United States at St Louis.
zh:
这里是普拉特河沿岸的波尼人腹地，察维（Chaui，意为「中间人」）人的家园；法国商人称他们为「大波尼」，在波尼四大支派中地位最高。他们的村落是河阶地上一簇簇圆顶土屋，妇女在河谷农田里种玉米、豆子和南瓜，每年夏天全村在圣束祭司的带领下徒步出动，围猎野牛。1444年时，马和欧洲人都还没有到过普拉特河，察维人的世界北起卢普河畔的斯基迪村落，南到共和河畔的基特克哈基村落。

最早逼近这里的欧洲人是西班牙人：1541年，科罗纳多的远征队抵达阿肯色河畔的基维拉，在其边缘受到哈拉埃人的迎接，他们大概是波尼人的亲族。1720年8月，卢普河畔的斯基迪村落歼灭了比利亚苏尔远征队，比利亚苏尔及其麾下四十五名西班牙人、十一名普韦布洛辅兵被杀。1770年前后，察维人率领南部各支派从阿肯色河北上，定居普拉特河，主村就在后来森特勒尔城的所在；随后他们与斯基迪人进行了一场短暂的战争，斯基迪人战败，承认察维酋长为全波尼之首。约1760年起天花反复扫过各村落，斯基迪人从1725年的八个大村减到1800年只剩一个。1806年，梅尔加雷斯和派克各率远征队先后来此，争相争取波尼人；1818年，「大波尼」在圣路易斯与美国签订了第一个条约。

en:
The province name recalls Niutachi, the name the Missouri gave themselves, 'people of the river mouth'. They spoke a Chiwere Siouan tongue and in the fifteenth century lived in permanent villages along the lower Missouri, chiefly near where the Grand River joins it and where it itself enters the Mississippi. Farmers and bison hunters, they held the gateway to a river whose course no outsider yet knew, linking the prairie nations to the towns of the Illinois; Sauk and Meskwaki raiders from the upper Mississippi already troubled them. In 1444 their villages still commanded both river mouths.

Jacques Marquette made French contact with the Missouri in 1673, opening a fur trade that brought guns, goods and epidemics. Étienne de Bourgmont, who had married a chief's daughter, built Fort Orleans on the Missouri in 1723 as a trade and alliance post, only for it to be abandoned in 1726. In 1730 a Sauk and Meskwaki attack killed hundreds and all but destroyed the people; most survivors joined the Otoe and others the Osage and Kansa. After 1763 the west bank passed to Spain, and in 1803 the lower Missouri country came to the United States with the Louisiana Purchase, by which time the Missouri survived only as a small band living among the Otoe.
zh:
省名「纽阿奇」得自密苏里人的自称「Niutachi」，意为「河口之人」。他们说奇维雷语支的苏语，15世纪时在密苏里河下游定居，主要聚居于格兰德河汇流处以及密苏里河注入密西西比河的河口一带。他们既耕作也猎捕野牛，扼守着一条外人尚不知其流向的大河门户，把草原诸族与伊利尼人的村镇连接起来；来自密西西比河上游的索克人与梅斯夸基人已不时来犯。1444年，他们的村落仍据有这两处河口。

1673年，雅克·马凯特与密苏里人首次接触，由此打开的毛皮贸易带来了火枪、货物，也带来了疫病。曾娶一位密苏里首领之女为妻的艾蒂安·德·布尔蒙于1723年在密苏里河畔修建奥尔良堡，作为贸易与结盟的据点，堡垒却在1726年即遭废弃。1730年，索克人与梅斯夸基人的进攻杀死数百人，几乎将这个部族消灭；幸存者大多投奔奥托埃人，其余加入奥塞奇人与坎扎人。1763年后河西岸归于西班牙；1803年，密苏里河下游地区随路易斯安那购地转入美国之手，此时密苏里人已只是寄居奥托埃人之中的一小支。

en:
Omaha takes its name from a Missouri River crossing above the mouth of the Platte, where wooded bottomlands met the open buffalo plains. In 1444 the country was part of the Central Plains world of Caddoan-speaking villagers related to the Pawnee: families raised maize, beans and squash, lived in earth lodges, and left the valleys for communal hunts. The Omaha, Dhegihan Siouan people whose name means 'upstream', still lived far to the east; their migration would not reach the upper Missouri until the late seventeenth century.

Pierre-Charles Le Sueur first reported the Omaha from French reports in 1700, describing a village of about 400 dwellings and 4,000 people near the Big Sioux River. Guillaume Delisle mapped them along the upper Missouri in 1718, and by about 1734 the Omaha had a village west of the river on Bow Creek. Around 1770 they became the first documented equestrian people on the Northern Plains, and Chief Blackbird's Tonwantonga controlled access to the fur trade near present Homer. A smallpox epidemic about 1800 killed roughly a third of the Omaha, including Blackbird; Lewis and Clark met Otoe and Missouria leaders nearby in 1804, and Fort Lisa opened as a fur post in 1812.
zh:
奥马哈得名于普拉特河口以北的密苏里河渡口，林木覆盖的河畔低地在这里接上开阔的野牛平原。1444年时，这片地方属于中央平原上与波尼人相近的卡多语村民世界：人们种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，住在土屋中，并按季节离开河谷集体狩猎。名为「上游之人」的奥马哈人属于德吉哈语支苏语族群，当时仍远在东方，直到17世纪末才迁到密苏里河上游。

1700年，皮埃尔·夏尔·勒苏尔根据法方报告首次记载奥马哈人，称他们在大苏河附近有一座约四百座住所、四千居民的村庄。1718年纪尧姆·德利尔把他们标在密苏里河上游；约1734年，奥马哈人在密苏里河以西的鲍溪建立村庄。约1770年，他们成为北平原最早有记载采用马背文化的族群，黑鸟酋长的「大村」托恩万通加位于今荷马附近，控制着毛皮贸易通道。约1800年的天花夺去约三分之一奥马哈人的生命，黑鸟也在其中；1804年刘易斯和克拉克在附近会见奥托人与密苏里人首领，1812年利萨堡作为毛皮贸易站设立。

en: The Wahpetunwan, or Leaf Village, were one of the four Eastern Dakota bands of the Seven Council Fires. In 1444 their people lived by northern lakes and the woodland-prairie edge, gathering wild rice, fishing from canoes, hunting deer, and joining seasonal buffalo hunts on the plains. Radisson and Groseilliers made the first recorded French meeting with the Dakota in 1659–60, and Daniel Greysolon, sieur du Lhut, traded here and mediated a Dakota-Ojibwe peace in 1679. That peace did not last: warfare after 1736 drove Dakota bands from Leech Lake and Mille Lacs toward the upper Minnesota and Red River prairies, where horses and the fur trade were reshaping camp life by 1800.
zh: 沃珀顿（Wahpetunwan，意为「叶村」）是七营联盟东达科他四支之一。1444年，这支达科他人生活在北方湖群与森林草原的交界地带，采集野米、划独木舟捕鱼、猎鹿，并按季节到平原捕猎野牛。1659至1660年，拉迪松与格罗塞耶完成了有记载的法国人与达科他人的首次接触；1679年，法国商人迪吕在此贸易，并促成达科他人与奥吉布瓦人和谈。和平未能持久，1736年后的战争迫使达科他群体离开利奇湖、米拉湖一带，迁往明尼苏达河上游与雷德河草原；到1800年前后，马匹和毛皮贸易已经在改变营地生活。

en:
In 1444 the prairies and wooded valleys drained by the Iowa River belonged to the late Oneota world. Farmers chose light soils near water, raised corn, beans and squash, hunted bison and deer, and stored harvests in underground pits. The Chiwere-speaking Báxoje, whom the French later called Ioway, were moving from the upper Mississippi toward the eastern plains, and their bark- or earth-covered villages would give this river country the name used by Europeans.

European knowledge reached the region on 17 June 1673, when Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet met Illinois parties on the nearby Mississippi; La Salle claimed the whole valley for France in 1682, and in 1684 Nicolas Perrot led French peacemaking among the upper Mississippi nations. By the late seventeenth century the Báxoje were established in Iowa, perhaps 1,000 to 1,500 strong and the dominant local people. Horses reached them through plains networks in the 1720s, while Sioux pressure in the 1760s pushed their villages westward. French and later British fur traders brought metal goods and marriage ties, but after the Louisiana Purchase of 1803 American competition, warfare and smallpox reduced the Báxoje to about 800 people by 1804; disputes over bison-hunting grounds brought an Omaha attack in 1814.
zh:
1444年，艾奥瓦河滋养的草原与林木河谷属于晚期奥内奥塔文化圈。农人在近水的松软土地上种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎捕野牛与鹿，并把收获贮藏在地下窖穴中。操奇维雷语的巴霍杰人后来被法国人称作艾奥瓦人，此时正从密西西比河上游向东部平原移动；他们覆有树皮或泥土的村落，后来使这片河地有了欧洲人使用的名称。

1673年6月17日，雅克·马凯特与路易·乔利埃特在附近的密西西比河畔接触伊利诺伊人，欧洲人由此知道这片地区；1682年，拉萨尔代表法国宣布整个河谷为法国所有，1684年尼古拉·佩罗又在上密西西比诸族之间进行调停。到17世纪后期，巴霍杰人已在艾奥瓦定居，人口约一千至一千五百，是当地最强的族群。1720年代，马匹经平原族群网络传到他们这里；1760年代，苏人的压力又迫使村落西迁。法国及后来的英国皮货商带来金属器物和通婚关系，但1803年路易斯安那购地后，美国竞争、战事与天花使巴霍杰人到1804年只剩约八百人；围绕野牛猎场的争端又在1814年招致奥马哈人袭击。

en: The Ithanktunwanna, or Yanktonai, meaning 'Little Village at the End', were Western Dakota rather than Lakota. In 1444 their pedestrian bison hunters moved between Mni Wakan, the sacred lake later mistranslated as Devils Lake, and the headwaters of the Sheyenne and James rivers; Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara parties also visited the lake. Horses extended their hunting and trade range during the eighteenth century, and in 1794 French trader Jean Trudeau named the James River Rivière aux Jacques. The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 and the 49th-parallel settlement of 1818 changed the imperial frontier, while Yanktonai warriors led by Red Thunder and the young Wanata joined the British in the War of 1812; Wanata fought at Fort Meigs in 1813. Yanktonai camps still held the country in 1821.
zh: 扬克托奈（Ithanktunwanna，意为「尽头处的小村庄」）是西达科他群体，而不是拉科他。1444年，徒步猎牛的扬克托奈人随季节往来于米尼瓦坎（意为「灵水」，后来被误译为魔鬼湖）与夏延河、詹姆斯河上游之间，曼丹人、希达察人和阿里卡拉人也会来到湖畔。18世纪马匹传入后，他们的狩猎和贸易范围大为扩展；1794年，法国商人让·特鲁多把詹姆斯河命名为Rivière aux Jacques。1803年路易斯安那易手、1818年北纬49度边界划定，帝国边疆随之改变；1812年战争中，雷德桑德与年轻首领瓦纳塔率扬克托奈战士加入英国一方，瓦纳塔于1813年参加莫米堡围城。到1821年，这片土地仍由扬克托奈营地掌握。

en: Ihanktonwan is the Dakota name of the Yankton, 'People of the End Village', recalling a time when they lived at the end of Spirit Lake near Mille Lacs in the Minnesota woods. Wars with musket-armed Ojibwe in the 17th and 18th centuries drove the Dakota south and west; in the 18th century the Yankton were recorded along the Blue Earth River, and they kept the sacred Pipestone Quarry for the Seven Council Fires of the Sioux. On a bluff above the Missouri the La Vérendrye brothers secretly buried a lead plate claiming the land for France in 1743, and in late August 1804 Lewis and Clark held council with the Yankton at Calumet Bluff.
zh: 伊汉克顿万是扬克顿人的达科他语自称，意为「村落尽头的人」，源于他们当年住在明尼苏达林区米勒拉克斯湖附近灵湖尽头的往事。17、18世纪，手持火枪的奥吉布瓦人步步进逼，把达科他人赶向南方和西方；18世纪的记载中，扬克顿人住在蓝土河一带，并为苏族的「七议火」看守神圣的烟斗石采石场。1743年，拉韦朗德里兄弟在密苏里河畔的崖上暗中埋下一块铅板，宣布此地归属法国；1804年8月下旬，刘易斯与克拉克在卡卢梅特崖与扬克顿人举行会谈。

en: The Sisithunwan, or Sisseton, perhaps meaning 'Fishing Grounds Village', were one of the four Eastern Dakota bands. In 1444 their camps followed fish, wild-rice beds and deer coverts along the upper Minnesota River, then moved west through the Traverse Gap toward buffalo plains between Big Stone Lake and Lake Traverse. French trade entered the river system around 1700, when Pierre-Charles Le Sueur ascended the Minnesota and built Fort L'Huillier on the Blue Earth. Eighteenth-century wars with the Ojibwe pushed Sisseton camps farther west, where horses and beaver pelts linked them to plains commerce; the 1818 Anglo-American convention fixed the imperial border at the 49th parallel, but Dakota camps still held the lake country in 1821.
zh: 锡塞顿（Sisithunwan，名字可能意为「渔场村」）是东达科他四支之一。1444年，他们的营地随明尼苏达河上游的鱼群、野米地和鹿群林地迁徙，再穿过特拉弗斯隘口，前往比格斯通湖与特拉弗斯湖之间的野牛草原。约1700年，法国毛皮贸易进入这一水系，皮埃尔-夏尔·勒叙厄尔沿明尼苏达河上行，在蓝土河畔修建利利耶堡。18世纪与奥吉布瓦人的战争把锡塞顿营地进一步向西挤压，马匹和河狸皮也把他们卷入草原商路；1818年英美公约把帝国边界定在北纬49度，但到1821年，湖沼地带仍掌握在达科他营地手中。

en: The Nueta, better known as the Mandan, had by the 1400s consolidated in fortified earth-lodge villages along the upper Missouri and Heart River. In 1444 women tended corn, bean and squash fields, and the plaza villages bartered surplus grain for bison meat, hides and distant goods. Pierre Gaultier de La Vérendrye became the first known European visitor in 1738, finding nine prosperous palisaded villages on the Heart. Horses arrived in the mid-eighteenth century and widened the plains trade, but smallpox in 1781 reduced the Mandan from thirteen clans to seven and drove survivors to consolidate northward with the Hidatsa. Lewis and Clark wintered at Fort Mandan in 1804–05 and took Chief Sheheke to Washington; Sheheke was killed in fighting with the Hidatsa in 1812. The reduced villages still anchored upper Missouri trade in 1821.
zh: 努埃塔人（Nueta，更常见的称呼是曼丹人）到15世纪已在密苏里河上游与哈特河一带结成设防的土屋村落。1444年，妇女种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，广场周围的村落用余粮交换野牛肉、皮革和远方货物。1738年，皮埃尔·戈尔捷·德·拉韦朗德里成为已知第一位到访的欧洲人，见到哈特河畔九座繁荣的栅栏村庄。18世纪中叶马匹传入，扩大了草原贸易；1781年天花传到北部平原，曼丹氏族由十三个减为七个，幸存者向北收缩并与希达察人合并聚居。刘易斯与克拉克1804至1805年在曼丹堡过冬，并带首领谢赫克前往华盛顿；谢赫克后来在1812年与希达察人的战斗中被杀。到1821年，规模大减的村落仍是密苏里河上游的贸易支点。

en:
Makoua covers the cold fir woods and maze of lakes behind Minnesota's north shore, from Onamanii-zaaga'iganiing, later called Lake Vermilion, to Gichi-onigaming, the Great Carrying Place on Lake Superior. Its portages linked the Superior watershed with Rainy Lake and the fur rivers running toward Hudson Bay, while wild-rice beds, fish runs, moose yards and bear woods sustained seasonal camps. In 1444 Eastern Dakota parties still controlled much of the interior, Cree travelers used the northern waters, and Anishinaabe families from the Superior shore knew the eastern carries. The country's wealth lay in beaver, otter and birchbark canoes rather than towns.

French trade entered after Médard Chouart des Groseilliers's western voyage of 1654-1656, and in 1659 he and Radisson reached the far end of Lake Superior. Daniel Greysolon du Lhut reached the western end of the lake in autumn 1679 and made peace there between Saulteur and Dakota parties. In 1729 the Cree guide Auchagah drew for La Vérendrye a map of the Grand Portage route, which became the gateway to the northwestern fur country and, under British rule, a North West Company depot. Although the Treaty of Paris placed it in the United States in 1783, British traders stayed until 1802-1803, when they removed to Fort William. Meanwhile Lake Superior Ojibwe bands, later grouped as the Bois Forte, pressed into the woods from the 1730s, gradually displacing the Eastern Dakota.
zh:
马夸是明尼苏达北岸后方的寒温带冷杉林地与湖网，从奥吉布瓦语称 Onamanii-zaaga'iganiing 的维尔米利翁湖，一直延伸到苏必利尔畔的 Gichi-onigaming，即大波蒂奇。这里的陆路转运把苏必利尔流域与雷尼湖、通向哈得孙湾的毛皮河网连接起来，野米床、鱼汛、驼鹿场和熊林则供养着季节性营地。1444年，东达科他猎人仍控制大片内陆，克里旅人使用北部水道，来自苏必利尔岸的阿尼什纳比人熟悉东部搬运道。此地的财富是河狸、水獭和桦皮独木舟，而不是城镇。

1654—1656年，梅达尔·舒阿尔·德·格罗塞耶西行后，法国贸易进入西大湖；1659年，他与拉迪松抵达苏必利尔湖西端。1679年秋，达尼埃尔·格雷索隆·迪吕也到达湖西，并在当地促成索尔托人与达科他人和解。1729年，克里向导奥查加为拉韦朗德里绘出大波蒂奇路线图，这条通道由此成为西北毛皮之地的门户，英国统治时期又是西北公司的补给站。1783年《巴黎条约》将其划入美国，但英国商人留到1802—1803年才迁往威廉堡。与此同时，后来归入布瓦福特人的苏必利尔奥吉布瓦诸部从1730年代起深入林地，逐渐排挤东达科他人。

en:
Baawitigon is a spelling of Baawitigong, the place of the rapids where the St. Marys River carries Lake Superior into Lake Huron. South of the crossing, the land takes in the forests of Michigan's eastern Upper Peninsula and trails reaching west toward the Menominee River and Noquet country. The rapids yielded sturgeon in spring and whitefish in autumn; an Ojibwe fishing camp of perhaps 150 to 200 people could swell into a much larger Algonquian gathering during the runs. Inland families gathered wild rice and blueberries, hunted moose, and trapped beaver. In 1444 Baawitigong was a fishery, portage and meeting place, not a European-style town.

Étienne Brûlé became the first European known to see the rapids around 1620. In 1641 Isaac Jogues and Charles Raymbault found many Ojibwe there, and French priests named the crossing Sault Sainte-Marie. Claude Dablon and Jacques Marquette founded the Jesuit mission on the south bank in 1668, the oldest permanent European settlement in Michigan. At the same rapids in 1671, Saint-Lusson staged the ceremony that claimed the Lake Superior country for Louis XIV before representatives of fourteen Indigenous nations. Louis Le Gardeur de Repentigny received a seigneury there in 1751 and built a small French post. Britain acquired the strait in 1763; although the Treaty of Paris assigned the south bank to the United States in 1783, British forces did not leave until 1797. A joint boundary commission fixed the river frontier in 1817, by which time the fur trade had bound Ojibwe, French, Métis and Scottish families around the rapids.
zh:
巴维蒂冈是 Baawitigong 的转写，意为「急流之地」，即圣玛丽斯河把苏必利尔湖送入休伦湖的水道。渡口以南，是密歇根上半岛东部林地，小径向西通往梅诺米尼河与诺奎特人的地方。急流春季出鲟鱼、秋季出白鱼；一座约有150至200人的奥吉布瓦渔村，在鱼汛期间会扩大成阿尔冈昆诸族的更大集会。内陆居民采集野米和蓝莓，猎驼鹿，捕河狸。1444年的巴维蒂冈是渔场、搬运道和会盟地，而不是欧洲式城镇。

约1620年，艾蒂安·布吕莱成为已知最早见到这处急流的欧洲人。1641年，依撒格·饶格与夏尔·兰博在此见到许多奥吉布瓦人，法国神父把渡口命名为苏圣玛丽。1668年，克洛德·达布隆和雅克·马凯特在南岸建立耶稣会传教站，这是密歇根最早的欧洲人永久定居点。1671年，圣吕松又在急流前举行仪式，当着十四个原住民民族代表的面，宣布苏必利尔地区归属路易十四。1751年，路易·勒加德尔·德·勒庞蒂尼获得这里的领地并建起一座法国小据点。1763年，英国取得这条水道；1783年《巴黎条约》虽把南岸划给美国，英军却直到1797年才撤离。1817年，联合边界委员会确定沿河边界，此时毛皮贸易已把奥吉布瓦、法裔、梅蒂和苏格兰家庭联结在急流周围。

en:
The Osaakiiwaki are the Sauk, an Algonquian people; Osaakiiwaki is the Ojibwe name the French wrote as Sac, 'people of the outlet'. Their principal town stood at the mouth of the Fox River, where it opens into Green Bay. The Sauk planted maize, beans and squash, hunted big game through the summer and split into winter trapping camps, while clans named for the bear, beaver, eagle and wolf ordered the village. Closest of their allies were the Meskwaki, the Fox, up the same river. In 1444 no European had yet entered Green Bay, and the Sauk traded and feuded with the Ho-Chunk, Menominee and Dakota around them.

French priests and traders reached the bay in the 1660s, founding the mission of Saint-François-Xavier in 1671, and for half a century the Sauk kept the peace with New France even while the Fox fought it. That ended in 1733, when the Sauk sheltered Fox survivors of the second Fox War and French reprisals drove both peoples out of the bay; the Sauk moved to the Mississippi and later built Saukenuk at the mouth of the Rock River. They stayed allied to the French and then the British, fighting beside the redcoats in the War of 1812.
zh:
奥萨基瓦基人即索克人，属阿尔冈昆族群；Osaakiiwaki是奥吉布瓦人对他们的称呼，意为「水口之人」，法国人拼作Sac。他们的主镇坐落在福克斯河注入格林贝的河口。索克人种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，夏季结队猎捕大兽，冬天分散成设陷阱的捕猎营地；熊、河狸、鹰、狼等图腾氏族维系着村落的秩序。同河上游的梅斯克瓦基人（即福克斯人）是他们最亲近的盟友。1444年，欧洲人尚未进入格林贝，索克人与周边的霍春克人、梅诺米尼人、达科他人贸易往来，也彼此争战。

法国神父和商人在1660年代抵达格林贝，1671年建起圣方济各·沙勿略传教站；此后半个世纪里，尽管福克斯人屡与法国交战，索克人始终与新法兰西相安无事。1733年，索克人收留第二次福克斯战争中幸存的梅斯克瓦基人，招致法国报复，两族被迫一同离开格林贝，迁到密西西比河一带，后来在罗克河口建起索克努克。他们先后维系与法国和英国的同盟，1812年战争中还曾为英军而战。

en:
The province named Meskwaki covers the lower Wisconsin corridor where the Wisconsin meets the Mississippi beneath wooded bluffs. In 1444 it is Oneota country, its Chiwere-speaking villages farming corn, beans and squash, gathering wild rice, fishing the rivers and hunting deer and bison. Sauk, Ho-Chunk, Ioway and Illinois neighbours share or contest the surrounding prairies. The Fox-Wisconsin route, linking Green Bay by portage to the Mississippi, gives the river crossings their lasting value in the fur trade.

Jacques Marquette and Louis Joliet reached the prairie in June 1673, the first known French expedition through the crossing; they found a Meskwaki band led by Alim, and his name gave the place its French designation, Prairie du Chien. Nicolas Perrot established a trading post there in 1685, and on 8 May 1689 he formally claimed the Fox, Wisconsin and Mississippi waters for France. Control of the Fox River made the Meskwaki gatekeepers of the route, bringing the Fox Wars: French accounts date the first war from 1712 to the peace of 1716, and renewed war from 1728 to its military end in 1733. A royal decree of 1728 called for the people's destruction, and on 9 September 1730 about 900 Meskwaki attempting to break eastward were killed or captured by French and allied warriors; the survivors joined the Sauk. Prairie du Chien passed to Britain in 1763 and, despite the 1783 treaty, remained a British frontier post until the War of 1812. The British captured Fort Shelby in July 1814 and withdrew after 1815; the Americans built Fort Crawford in 1816, securing the fur-trade crossing.
zh:
梅斯夸基省覆盖威斯康星河下游走廊，河水在林木崖壁下汇入密西西比河。1444年，这里是奥内奥塔人的土地：说奇维雷语的村落种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，采集野米，在河中捕鱼，并猎鹿和野牛。索克人、霍春克人、艾奥瓦人和伊利尼人在周围草原上往来、联姻或争地。福克斯—威斯康星水道经短途陆运连接格林贝与密西西比河，使这些渡口在毛皮贸易中长期具有价值。

1673年6月，雅克·马凯特与路易·若利埃抵达这片草原，成为已知最早穿过这一渡口的法国探险队；他们遇到由阿利姆率领的梅斯夸基游群，阿利姆之名后来被法方理解为「狗」，此地遂称普雷里德欣。尼古拉·佩罗1685年在此设立贸易站，1689年5月8日又正式代表法国宣告占有福克斯河、威斯康星河与密西西比河水域。控制福克斯河使梅斯夸基人成为这条通道的守门人，也引发福克斯战争：法文记载将第一次战争定于1712年至1716年议和，1728年战火重燃，至1733年军事结束。1728年法王甚至下令消灭梅斯夸基人；1730年9月9日，约九百名试图向东突围的梅斯夸基人被法国及其原住民盟军杀死或俘获，幸存者投奔索克人。普雷里德欣1763年转入英国之手，尽管1783年条约已将它划归美国，直到1812年战争期间它仍是英国边疆据点。1814年7月英军攻占谢尔比堡，1815年后撤离；美军1816年修建克劳福德堡，守住了这个毛皮贸易渡口。

en:
The Ho-Chunk are a Chiwere-speaking Siouan people of the Green Bay country, their lands running from Lake Winnebago up the Fox and Wisconsin rivers and south to the Rock. Neighboring Algonquians called them Winnebago, 'people of the fetid water', and the French rendered this as les Puants; they call themselves Hoocągra. Successors to the effigy-mound builders and the Oneota culture, they lived in bark-and-mat villages under twelve clans, growing maize and wild rice, sugaring the maples and taking sturgeon from Lake Winnebago. In 1444 they were the dominant power between Lake Michigan and the Mississippi.

Jean Nicolet came ashore at Red Banks in 1634, feasted by the Ho-Chunk at a gathering he put at 5,000 warriors. Within a generation the people were nearly broken: a lake storm drowned hundreds of hunters, European fevers swept the villages, and Illinois raiders killed many more, so that by the 1660s barely 500 remained. The Beaver Wars then poured Algonquian refugees through their country. French traders came back in the late 1650s, and the Fox Wars of 1712–1733 made the Green Bay villages a theatre of French campaigning. Peace let the Ho-Chunk recover inland, from 700 people in 1736 to over 2,900 by 1806, though smallpox returned in 1757–58.
zh:
霍春克人是说奇维雷语支苏语的民族，世居格林贝一带，乡土从温内贝戈湖沿福克斯河、威斯康星河延伸，南抵罗克河。邻近的阿尔冈昆人称之为温内巴戈，意为「浊水之民」，法国人译作「臭人」（les Puants）；他们自称Hoocągra。他们是象形丘营造者与奥内奥塔文化的后裔，住在树皮和草席搭成的村落里，分十二个氏族，种植玉米和野米，熬煮枫糖，在温内贝戈湖捕捞鲟鱼。1444年时，他们是密歇根湖与密西西比河之间最强盛的势力。

1634年，让·尼科莱在红岸登岸，霍春克人设宴款待，尼科莱称聚集的武士有五千之众。但仅仅一代人之后，这个民族便几近覆灭：一场湖上风涛溺死数百名猎人，欧洲传来的热病席卷各村，伊利诺伊袭击者又杀死许多人，到1660年代幸存者只剩五百左右。海狸战争随后又把大批阿尔冈昆难民推入他们的乡土。法国商人1650年代末重返此地，1712至1733年的福克斯战争使格林贝沿岸村落沦为法国用兵之地。和平之后霍春克人内迁恢复，人口从1736年的七百回升到1806年的两千九以上，只是天花又在1757至1758年卷土重来。

en:
Peewareewa is the Peoria country along the central Illinois River, where the river broadens into Peoria Lake, called Pimiteoui by the French. The Peoria, whose self-name was peewaareewa, were one of the Algonquian-speaking peoples of the Illinois Confederation. In 1444 their seasonal villages occupied wooded bottomlands and adjoining prairie, cornfields stood near the lodges, and hunting parties crossed the grasslands for bison while the river linked them to neighboring Illini bands.

French exploration reached the Illinois country in 1673. In January 1680 La Salle and Henri de Tonti built Fort Crèvecoeur on the east bank near Pimiteoui, but on 16 April 1680 the garrison mutinied and destroyed it as Iroquois war parties pressed into the valley. Tonti established Fort St Louis du Pimiteoui nearby in 1691, and the post became a fur-trade center. War and epidemic disease reduced the Illinois from about 10,500 at intensive European contact to fewer than 500 within a century. After France ceded its lands east of the Mississippi in 1763, many Peoria withdrew west of the river. Americans built Fort Clark at Peoria Lake in September 1813, and the 1818 Treaty of Edwardsville ceded Peoria lands in Illinois to the United States.
zh:
佩瓦雷瓦是伊利诺伊河中游的皮奥里亚人土地，河道在此展宽为皮奥里亚湖，法国人称之为皮米特威。皮奥里亚人自称peewaareewa，是说阿尔冈昆语的伊利尼联盟成员之一。1444年，他们的季节性村落设在林木繁茂的河漫滩与相邻草原上，屋舍附近有玉米田，猎队穿过草原猎捕野牛，伊利诺伊河则把他们与邻近的伊利尼群体连在一起。

法国探险在1673年抵达伊利尼地区。1680年1月，拉萨尔和亨利·德·通蒂在皮米特威附近东岸修建克雷夫科尔堡，但易洛魁战队进逼河谷时，守军于1680年4月16日哗变并摧毁堡垒。1691年，通蒂在附近建立圣路易·德·皮米特威堡，这里成为毛皮贸易据点。战争和疫病使伊利尼人从欧洲人密集接触初期约一万零五百人，在一个世纪内减至不足五百。1763年法国割让密西西比河以东土地后，许多皮奥里亚人撤往河西。1813年9月，美国人在皮奥里亚湖修建克拉克堡；1818年的《爱德华兹维尔条约》把伊利诺伊境内的皮奥里亚土地割让给美国。

en:
Kaskankaham covers the lower Kaskaskia River country near the Mississippi, where oak woods and tallgrass prairie meet fertile alluvial bottoms. The people whose name it bears, the Kaskaskia or Kaaskaaskia, were one of the Algonquian-speaking bands of the Illinois Confederation. In 1444 the river valleys were Illini planting and hunting range; corn, beans and squash grew in rich soil, bison hunts crossed the prairies, and dugout canoes carried pelts and dried food along the Mississippi system.

Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet met the Kaskaskia at the Grand Village on the upper Illinois River in 1673. A French mission and fur post grew there in 1675, but Iroquois pressure scattered the village; around 1691 its people began moving south, and in 1703 the Jesuit mission of the Immaculate Conception became the nucleus of Kaskaskia on the Mississippi. The mixed French-Illinois settlement held about 2,200 people in 1707. French farms shipped wheat, corn and flour to New Orleans, voyageurs opened fur and lead routes west, Fort de Chartres was built nearby in 1719, and Louis XV sent a church bell in 1741. After the cession of 1763 many French and Illinois families crossed into Spanish-held Missouri. An American force under George Rogers Clark seized Kaskaskia on 4 July 1778; the town became capital of Illinois Territory in 1809 and the first state capital in 1818–1819.
zh:
卡斯坎卡哈姆是卡斯卡斯基亚河下游临近密西西比河的土地，橡树林与高草草原在此接上肥沃的冲积低地。省名所指的卡斯卡斯基亚人在迈阿密—伊利尼语中作Kaaskaaskia，是说阿尔冈昆语的伊利尼联盟一支。1444年，这些河谷属于伊利尼人的种植和游猎范围；玉米、豆类和南瓜生长在沃土上，野牛猎队穿过草原，独木舟则沿密西西比水系运送毛皮和干粮。

1673年，雅克·马凯特和路易·若利埃在伊利诺伊河上游的大村遇到卡斯卡斯基亚人。1675年，法国传教站和毛皮据点在那里发展起来，但易洛魁人的压力使村落离散；约1691年，居民开始南移，1703年，圣母无原罪耶稣会传教站成为密西西比河畔卡斯卡斯基亚的核心。1707年，这座法兰西—伊利尼混血聚落约有二千二百人。法国农场把小麦、玉米和面粉运往新奥尔良，船工向西开辟毛皮和铅矿商路；沙特尔堡于1719年在附近建成，路易十五又在1741年送来教堂钟。1763年割地后，许多法国和伊利尼家庭渡河西迁，进入西班牙控制的密苏里。1778年7月4日，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克率领的美军夺取卡斯卡斯基亚；这座城镇1809年成为伊利诺伊领地首府，1818—1819年担任伊利诺伊州第一个首府。

en:
Cahokia lies on the east side of the Mississippi, where bottomland lakes and woods meet tallgrass prairie in the fertile floodplain later called the American Bottom. The great earthworks north of the colonial village had formed the core of a Mississippian town at its peak in the thirteenth century and stood abandoned long before Europeans reached the river. In 1444 Illini bands used this same country, planting corn, beans and squash in alluvial soil, hunting deer and bison, and fishing the sloughs; the Cahokia, Kahokiaki in Miami-Illinois, were one of the clans later met by the French.

In late 1696 Father Pinet and the Quebec Seminary of Foreign Missions founded the Holy Family mission among the Cahokia and Tamaroa, building a log church on the Mississippi bank. Cahokia became a major market for furs and Indian goods and grew to roughly 3,000 people, while French habitants planted wheat across the lowlands toward Kaskaskia. After France ceded the east bank in 1763, many Catholic families crossed to Ste Genevieve and the new settlement of St Louis. The Odawa leader Pontiac was killed in or near Cahokia on 20 April 1769. George Rogers Clark established a court there in 1778, 105 Cahokia household heads pledged loyalty to the Continental Congress, and after 1787 the old French courthouse served the Northwest Territory's vast St. Clair County.
zh:
卡霍基亚位于密西西比河东岸，河迹湖与林地在此接上高草草原，这片肥沃泛滥平原后来被称为阿梅里肯洼地。殖民村以北的巨大土丘曾是13世纪达到鼎盛的密西西比文化城镇核心，欧洲人抵达河流之前早已荒废。1444年，伊利尼群体仍在这片土地上往来，在冲积土中种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎鹿与野牛，并在牛轭湖和沼泽捕鱼；卡霍基亚人在迈阿密—伊利尼语中作Kahokiaki，是后来法国人遇到的氏族之一。

1696年末，皮内神父与魁北克外方传教会神学院在卡霍基亚人和塔马罗亚人中建立圣家堂传教站，并在密西西比河畔修建木构教堂。卡霍基亚随后成为毛皮和印第安货物的重要市场，人口增至约三千，法国定居者则在通往卡斯卡斯基亚的低地上种植小麦。1763年法国割让河东土地后，许多天主教家庭渡河西往圣热纳维耶夫和新建的圣路易斯。1769年4月20日，奥达瓦人领袖庞蒂亚克在卡霍基亚或其附近被杀。1778年，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克在此设立法庭，一百零五名卡霍基亚户主向大陆会议宣誓效忠；1787年后，古老的法国法院又为西北领地辖境广阔的圣克莱尔县服务。

en:
The high Chickasaw Bluffs above the Mississippi once held Mississippian villages whose people raised mounds on the ground later named Chucalissa, 'abandoned house' in the Chickasaw language. By the fifteenth century those villages had emptied, and the country west of the Tennessee River had become hunting ground for the Chickasaw, whose towns lay to the south in the upper Yazoo and Tombigbee valleys. In 1444 the bluffs carried no town or fort; Chickasaw parties camped there on the hunt and crossed the great river by canoe, and no European flag had yet been seen on its banks.

Hernando de Soto's Spaniards, after wintering among the Chickasaw in 1540–41, crossed the Mississippi near these bluffs in May 1541, the first Europeans to reach them. In late February 1682 La Salle's canoe expedition threw up a stockade, Fort Prudhomme, while searching for a lost hunter — the first French structure in Tennessee, occupied for only ten days, though La Salle himself lay ill there for forty on his way back upriver. In 1739 Bienville led more than 3,000 French, African and Indian troops to the fourth bluff and built Fort Assumption there on 15 August; disease, desertion and drink broke the army, which abandoned the post on 31 March 1740 and left the Chickasaw in possession. They held the bluffs until the Treaty of Tuscaloosa of 19 October 1818, when Andrew Jackson and Isaac Shelby bought all Chickasaw land east of the Mississippi. Memphis was laid out on the fourth bluff on 22 May 1819 by Jackson, John Overton and James Winchester.
zh:
密西西比河畔高耸的奇克索崖上，曾有密西西比文化的村落，村民在后来被称作丘卡利萨的地方垒筑土丘——这个名字在奇克索语中意为「废弃的房屋」。到15世纪，这些村落已经荒废，田纳西河以西的土地成了奇克索人的猎场，他们的村镇在南边的亚祖河与汤比格比河上游。1444年的崖上没有城镇也没有要塞，只有奇克索猎手在此宿营、乘独木舟渡过大河，欧洲人的旗帜还没有出现在河岸边。

1540至1541年冬，埃尔南多·德·索托率领的西班牙人在奇克索人那里过冬后，于1541年5月在这一带渡过密西西比河，成为最早到达此地的欧洲人。1682年2月底，拉萨尔的独木舟探险队为寻找一名走失的猎人，仓促筑起一座栅栏堡——普鲁多姆堡，这是法国人在田纳西修建的第一处建筑，只使用了十天；拉萨尔返航途中还曾在此养病四十天。1739年，边维尔率三千多名法军、黑人士兵和印第安盟军来到第四道崖，于8月15日建成圣母升天堡；疾病、逃亡和酗酒击垮了这支军队，1740年3月31日法军弃堡而去，奇克索人仍是这片土地的主人。直到1818年10月19日签订《塔斯卡卢萨条约》，安德鲁·杰克逊与艾萨克·谢尔比买下密西西比河以东的全部奇克索土地。1819年5月22日，杰克逊、约翰·奥弗顿和詹姆斯·温彻斯特在第四道崖上规划兴建孟菲斯。

en:
The black-soil hills of northeast Mississippi were the homeland of the Chickasaw, a Muskogean-speaking people whose maize fields and scattered towns lay along the upper Yazoo and Pearl River valleys. They had left the Tombigbee country in the fifteenth century, when the old Moundville chiefdom collapsed. In 1444 no single king ruled them: their towns answered to matrilineal clans and two moieties, and their warriors already had a name for fierceness that the first European visitors would record with dread.

Hernando de Soto's Spaniards wintered in a Chickasaw town in 1540-41, in the heart of the Chickasaw country. When de Soto demanded two hundred bearers, the Chickasaw burned his camp in a night attack and nearly destroyed the expedition before it broke away to the Mississippi River. Traders from Carolina reached them after 1670, bartering guns for captives taken in raids on the Choctaw, until the French armed the Choctaw in answer. Louisiana's armies fared no better: on 26 May 1736 Bienville's French and Choctaw force was bloodily repulsed from the palisaded town of Ackia, and the Chickasaw kept their hills until France ceded its claims east of the Mississippi in 1763. The 1786 Treaty of Hopewell fixed their first boundary with the United States, and in 1821 the Chickasaw still ruled the country of their birth.
zh:
密西西比州东北部的黑土丘陵是奇克索人的家园，在亚祖河与珍珠河上游的谷地间，散布着他们的玉米田和一座座城镇。15世纪，古老的蒙德维尔酋邦瓦解，他们离开汤比格比河谷迁来此地。1444年的奇克索人没有共主，各城镇由母系氏族和两个半族按血缘统辖；他们的战士早已以悍勇闻名，最早到来的欧洲访客也将这份悍勇记入史料。

1540至1541年冬，埃尔南多·德·索托的西班牙队伍在奇克索腹地的一座城镇过冬。德·索托强征两百名挑夫，奇克索人趁夜火攻营地，几乎将这支远征队彻底消灭，残部只得脱身逃往密西西比河。1670年后，卡罗来纳的英国商人深入此地，用火枪交换奇克索人袭击乔克托人掳来的俘虏，法国随后以武装乔克托人回应。路易斯安那殖民当局的大军同样讨不到便宜：1736年5月26日，比安维尔率领的法国-乔克托联军攻打栅栏坚固的阿基亚（Ackia）村，被血腥击退；直到1763年法国放弃密西西比河以东的领地，奇克索人始终守住了自己的丘陵。1786年的《霍普韦尔条约》首次划定他们与美国的边界，到1821年，奇克索人仍是这片生息之地的主人。

en:
Central Mississippi, from the upper Pearl River to the Chickasawhay, is the country of the Choctaw, who call themselves Chahta. In 1444 its prairies and creek bottoms held dozens of farming towns of late Plaquemine stock, their maize fields watched over from the old sacred mound of Nanih Waiya. No emperor ruled here: towns and matrilineal clans managed their own affairs, and disputes were as often fought out in a brutal stickball game, the 'little brother of war', as with weapons. Within two centuries these villages had coalesced into one nation in three great divisions, the western Okla Falaya, the eastern Okla Tannap and the southern Okla Hannali.

Hernando de Soto crossed the region's northern edge in 1540-41 without recording the Choctaw name, which first appears in French records after Iberville made the first documented contact in 1699. French guns helped the Choctaw answer Chickasaw slave raids; their warriors helped crush the Natchez rising in 1730 and marched with Bienville against Ackia in 1736. Trade rivalry between Britain and France then split the nation in a civil war from 1747 to 1750, which left the pro-French faction on top. The Treaty of Hopewell in 1786 fixed their first boundary with the United States, and under Pushmataha Choctaw warriors fought with the Americans at New Orleans in 1815. The treaties of Fort Adams in 1801 and Doak's Stand in 1820 opened millions of acres to planters, leaving the Choctaw of 1821 surrounded on every side.
zh:
密西西比腹地——从珍珠河上游到奇克索海河（Chickasawhay）——是乔克托人的家园，他们自称查塔。1444年，在这片草原与河谷低地上，散布着数十座普拉克明文化（Plaquemine）传统的农耕城镇，玉米田由古老的圣丘纳尼怀亚（Nanih Waiya）俯看着。这里没有君王：城镇与母系氏族各自为政，争端常以激烈的棍球赛——「战争的小兄弟」——代替刀兵。此后两百年间，这些村镇凝聚为一个民族，分作三大部：西部的 Okla Falaya、东部的 Okla Tannap 和南部的 Okla Hannali。

1540至1541年，德·索托从这片地区的北缘经过，却没有记下乔克托之名；这个名字最早见于法国记载——1699年，伊贝维尔与他们首次有了可考的接触。法国提供的火器让乔克托人得以回击奇克索人的掳掠；1730年，他们出兵协助法国人镇压纳奇兹起事，1736年又随比安维尔攻打阿基亚。随后，英法之间的贸易争夺使乔克托社会在1747至1750年内战分裂，亲法一派最终占了上风。1786年的《霍普韦尔条约》首次划定他们与美国的边界；在普什马塔哈率领下，乔克托战士于1815年在新奥尔良与美军并肩作战。1801年的《亚当斯堡条约》和1820年的《多克斯坦德条约》（Doak's Stand）把数百万英亩土地让给种植园主，到1821年，乔克托人的家园已四面受困。

en:
This stretch of the lower Mississippi above the delta takes its recorded name from the Bayagoula, whose river village stood near the Bayou Goula of present Iberville Parish. Burial mounds on the parish ground mark earlier Indigenous societies along the same banks. In 1444 the river, canoes, maize fields and hunting grounds belonged to a world of neighboring Bayagoula, Houma, Mugulasha and Quinipissa settlements; no European fort or mission had yet been built there.

La Salle entered the lower river in 1682 and claimed Louisiana for France, but direct contact came only in 1699, when Iberville met the Bayagoula sharing a village with the Mugulasha and Quinipissa. The Houma attacked that winter, and in the spring of 1700 the Bayagoula destroyed their village-mates. Raids by Taensa and Tunica in 1706 and smallpox by 1721 broke the surviving community; about forty warriors were counted in 1715, and by 1739 the remnant lived between the Houma and Acolapissa and was being absorbed. The river country later passed from France to Spain in 1763 and became part of the Louisiana Purchase in 1803.
zh:
密西西比河三角洲以上的这一段河地，其见载名称来自巴尤古拉人；他们的河畔村落靠近今伊贝维尔堂区境内的贝尤古拉。堂区内留存的墓葬丘，说明更早的原住民社会也曾生活在同一片河岸。1444年，河流、独木舟、玉米田和猎场都属于巴尤古拉、霍马、穆古拉沙与基尼皮萨等相邻村落构成的世界；这里还没有欧洲人的要塞或传教站。

拉萨尔1682年进入密西西比河下游，代表法国宣布占有路易斯安那，但直接接触要到1699年才到来：伊贝维尔在那里见到巴尤古拉人同穆古拉沙人、基尼皮萨人共居一村。霍马人在那年冬天发动袭击，1700年春，巴尤古拉人又消灭了同村的伙伴。1706年坦萨人与图尼卡人的袭击，以及到1721年已蔓延的天花，摧垮了幸存社群；1715年他们尚有约四十名战士，到1739年，残余部众已住在霍马人与阿科拉皮萨人之间并逐渐被吸收。这片河地后来在1763年由法国转入西班牙之手，1803年成为路易斯安那购地的一部分。

en:
At the head of Mobile Bay, the Mobile River meets sheltered water leading into the Gulf of Mexico. In 1444 this was the country of Mobile and Tohomé towns, whose canoes linked river villages, fishing grounds, maize fields and coastal exchange networks; their speech later supplied much of Mobilian Jargon, the trade language used across the central Gulf Coast. No European post yet stood on the bay.

Álvarez de Pineda's Spanish expedition mapped the Gulf shore in 1519, but lasting contact began when Iberville entered Mobile Bay on 31 January 1699. In 1702 Iberville and Bienville founded La Mobile and Fort Louis twenty-seven miles up the river, capital of French Louisiana until 1711. A Catholic parish followed in 1703, and the Pélican's 1704 call brought yellow fever as well as some of the colony's first African slaves. Around 1709 the Mobile and Tohomé received leave to settle near the fort; floods and disease then pushed the town down to the bay in 1711. Work on brick Fort Condé began in 1723. Britain took Mobile in 1763 and renamed the post Fort Charlotte, Bernardo de Gálvez captured it after a siege in 1780, and United States forces under James Wilkinson occupied it in 1813.
zh:
莫比尔河在莫比尔湾顶端注入这片通向墨西哥湾的隐蔽水域。1444年，这里是莫比尔人与托霍梅人的土地，独木舟连接着河畔村落、渔场、玉米田和海岸交换网络；他们的语言后来构成莫比尔行话的主要基础，这种贸易通语曾通行于墨西哥湾中部沿岸。此时湾畔还没有欧洲人的据点。

阿尔瓦雷斯·德·皮内达的西班牙远征队1519年测绘了这段墨西哥湾海岸，但持久接触要到1699年1月31日伊贝维尔驶入莫比尔湾才开始。1702年，伊贝维尔与边维尔兄弟在河上游二十七英里处建立拉莫比尔和圣路易堡，这里作为法属路易斯安那首府直至1711年。1703年天主教堂区设立，1704年「鹈鹕号」到来，也带来黄热病和殖民地最早的一批非洲奴隶。约1709年，莫比尔人与托霍梅人获准在要塞附近定居；洪水和疾病随后迫使城镇在1711年下移到湾畔。砖砌康德堡1723年动工。1763年英国取得莫比尔并将要塞改名夏洛特堡；贝尔纳多·德·加尔维斯1780年围城后将其攻占，1813年詹姆斯·威尔金森率领美军占领此地。

en:
Sheltered by Santa Rosa Island, Pensacola Bay offered one of the deepest harbors on the northern Gulf Coast. In 1444 its shores and inland waters were Muskogean country, lived over by the people later called Pensacola; dugout canoes linked their villages to fishing grounds, trade paths and the mound-centered ceremonial world of Bottle Creek. Creek visitors from the north were part of that wider network, but no European fortress yet commanded the bay.

Spanish expeditions reached the water in 1528 and 1539, the latter naming it the Bay of Ochuse. On 15 August 1559 Tristán de Luna landed from Veracruz with about 1,500 people and eleven ships to found Santa María de Ochuse, but a hurricane on 19 September sank six ships and destroyed most supplies; the survivors abandoned the post in 1561. Spain returned permanently in 1698, building Presidio Santa María de Galve. Bienville's French force seized Pensacola in May 1719, and it reverted to Spain before new presidios were opened on Santa Rosa Island in 1722 and the mainland in 1754. Britain took Florida in 1763 and made Pensacola capital of West Florida. Bernardo de Gálvez besieged it from 9 March to 10 May 1781 with nearly 8,000 troops, and Spain received it formally in 1783. Andrew Jackson captured the town in November 1814 and again in 1818; in 1821 the last Spanish garrison gave way to United States rule.
zh:
圣罗莎岛环抱的彭萨科拉湾，是墨西哥湾北岸最优良的深水港湾之一。1444年，湾岸与内水都是穆斯科格语人群的土地，住在这里的人后来被称为彭萨科拉人；独木舟把他们的村落同渔场、贸易小路以及以土丘为中心的博特尔克里克礼仪世界连接起来。北方来的克里克访客也属于这个更广的交往网络，但此时还没有欧洲要塞控制海湾。

西班牙远征队先后在1528年和1539年抵达这片水域，后一次将其记为奥丘塞湾。1559年8月15日，特里斯坦·德·卢纳率约一千五百人、分乘十一艘船从韦拉克鲁斯登陆，建立圣玛丽亚·德·奥丘塞；但9月19日的飓风击沉六艘船、毁掉大部分物资，幸存者最终在1561年放弃据点。1698年西班牙人重返并长期驻守，修建圣玛丽亚·德·加尔韦要塞。边维尔率领的法军1719年5月夺取彭萨科拉，此后此地又归还西班牙，1722年在圣罗莎岛、1754年在大陆另设要塞城镇。1763年英国取得佛罗里达，把彭萨科拉定为西佛罗里达首府。1781年3月9日至5月10日，贝尔纳多·德·加尔维斯率近八千军队围城，1783年西班牙正式获得此地。安德鲁·杰克逊1814年11月攻占城镇，1818年再次进占；1821年，最后的西班牙驻军让位于美国统治。

en:
The middle Alabama winds through cane bottoms and fertile red bluffs between the fall-line hills and the coastal plain. In towns such as Tawasa and Atagi ('pure water') lived the people later called the Tawasa, Muskogean-speaking villagers who grew maize and beans in the long aftermath of the mound-building chiefdoms whose earthworks still stood up and down the valley. They were close to the Alibamu on the upper river and to the Choctaw in the west, bound by trade and kinship rather than by any single chief. In 1444 these towns went their own way, and no European was yet within a thousand miles of the Alabama.

Hernando de Soto's army crossed the valley in 1540, and the palisaded town of Mabila fell to him nearby on 18 October after a day's slaughter. In 1560 the starving colonists of Tristán de Luna, who had landed at Pensacola the year before, occupied the abandoned river town of Nanipacana not far downstream before the expedition collapsed. Around 1707 the Tawasa were raided and carried off into the slave trade; one captive, Lamhatty, reached Virginia, where the sixty-word list taken from him became the only record of the Tawasa tongue, seemingly akin to the distant Timucua. Survivors sheltered with the French at Mobile after 1702, and about sixty of them joined the Alibamu beside Fort Toulouse, raised in 1717 at the forks of the Coosa and Tallapoosa; in time they were absorbed into the Creek Confederacy. Their descendants fought with the Red Sticks in the Creek War of 1813–14, and Andrew Jackson's victory at Horseshoe Bend and the Treaty of Fort Jackson in August 1814 opened the Alabama valley to American settlement.
zh:
中亚拉巴马河蜿蜒穿过河蔗密布的滩地与肥沃的红色崖岸，介于瀑布线丘陵和沿海平原之间。塔瓦萨、阿塔吉（Atagi，意为「清水」）等城镇就坐落于此，居民后来被称为塔瓦萨人。他们是操穆斯科格语的村民，在筑丘酋邦衰落之后的漫长岁月里种植玉米和豆类，河谷上下仍可见到先人的土筑工程。他们与上游的阿拉巴马人、西边的乔克托人关系密切，靠贸易和姻亲往来相连，却不奉共同的首领。1444年，这些城镇各自为政，欧洲人距亚拉巴马河尚有千里之遥。

1540年，埃尔南多·德·索托的军队穿过这片河谷，10月18日，栅寨环绕的马比拉在附近经一天血战之后被他攻陷。1559年特里斯坦·德·卢纳率殖民队在彭萨科拉登陆，1560年，饥饿的殖民者占据了下游不远处已遭遗弃的河畔城镇纳尼帕卡纳，但远征最终瓦解。约1707年，塔瓦萨人遭袭掠，被掳入奴隶贸易；俘虏之一拉姆哈蒂辗转到达弗吉尼亚，人们据他的口述记下60个词，成为塔瓦萨语唯一的记录——这种语言似乎与遥远的蒂穆夸语相近。幸存者在1702年法国人建立的莫比尔避难，约60人在1717年建于库萨河与塔拉普萨河交汇处的图卢兹堡旁投奔阿拉巴马人，最终并入克里克联盟。他们的后裔在1813至1814年的克里克战争中加入「红棍」一方；安德鲁·杰克逊在马蹄湾取胜，1814年8月的杰克逊堡条约把亚拉巴马河谷开放给美国人定居。

en:
Coweta stands on the lower Chattahoochee, among river-bottom fields of maize, beans and squash beneath the long fall line of the river. In 1444 the valley was held by the farming towns of a South Appalachian Mississippian chiefdom, with platform mounds and plazas and Hitchiti-speaking villagers, the communities from which Coweta and its neighbour Tuskegee would grow. The towns were autonomous, linked by kinship and by the old trade that carried shell and copper through the Southeast; the Spaniards had not yet come, and the English were still beyond the mountains.

The de Soto expedition of 1540 passed to the east, and the epidemics it set loose broke the old chiefdom; the valley's towns shrank and reshaped themselves. In 1685 they welcomed the English trader Henry Woodward, and after Spanish retaliation most of them moved east in 1690 to the Ochese Creek post on the Ocmulgee, where English muskets and the deerskin trade made them the Ochese Creeks. They raided the Florida missions in 1704, joined the Yamasee War in 1715, and then fell back to the Chattahoochee as the Lower Creeks. In May 1718 Brims, mico of Coweta, summoned British, French and Spanish agents to his town and declared Creek neutrality, playing the three empires off one another until his death in 1733; his half-sister Mary Musgrove became James Oglethorpe's interpreter when Georgia was founded in 1733, and Savannah shipped up to 50,000 deerskins a year by the 1750s. The American Revolution split the towns, and in 1790 Alexander McGillivray signed the Treaty of New York with Washington. In the Red Stick War of 1813-14 the Lower Creeks under William McIntosh fought with Andrew Jackson, whose victory at Horseshoe Bend on 27 March 1814 was sealed by the Treaty of Fort Jackson, ceding 22 million acres; in 1821 McIntosh set his name to the first Treaty of Indian Springs, opening the first Lower Creek lands to the cotton frontier.
zh:
考维塔地处查特胡奇河下游，河滨滩地里玉米、豆类和南瓜连绵，上游不远便是河流的瀑布线。1444年，河谷里散布着南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化的农耕城邦，筑有高台墩和广场，居民操希奇蒂语，考维塔和邻近的塔斯克吉就是从这些社群发展出来的。各镇各自为政，靠亲缘和东南古商道联系，商道上流通着贝壳与铜器；此时西班牙人尚未来到，英国人也还远在大山以东。

1540年德索托远征从东边经过，随之而来的疫病瓦解了旧邦国，河谷城邦人口锐减、重新组合。1685年他们接纳了英国商人亨利·伍德沃德，遭西班牙报复后，多数城镇于1690年东迁到奥克马尔吉河畔的奥切塞溪商栈，靠英军火枪和鹿皮贸易被称为奥切塞克里克人。1704年他们随英军劫掠佛罗里达布道所，1715年又参加雅马西战争，战后退回查特胡奇河，成为下克里克人。1718年5月，考维塔酋长布里姆把英、法、西三国代表召到镇上，宣布克里克中立，在三大帝国间左右逢源，直至1733年去世；他的异母妹玛丽·马斯格罗夫在1733年佐治亚建立时为奥格尔索普担任翻译，到1750年代萨凡纳每年输出多达五万张鹿皮。美国独立战争使诸镇分裂，1790年麦吉利夫雷与华盛顿签订《纽约条约》。1813至1814年的红棍战争中，麦金托什率领的下克里克人随安德鲁·杰克逊作战；1814年3月27日杰克逊在蹄铁湾取胜，8月9日的《杰克逊堡条约》割让2200万英亩土地；1821年麦金托什签署第一个《印第安斯普林斯条约》，首批下克里克土地向棉花种植边疆开放。

en:
The Ais, or Ays, lived on the sheltered islands and mainland shore of the long lagoon the Spanish called the River of Ais, now the Indian River, their land running from Cape Canaveral south to the St. Lucie Inlet. Fish, turtle and shellfish teemed in the brackish water and palm berries and cocoplums ripened along its banks, so that the Ais sowed no crops yet wanted for little. Theirs was a chiefdom of towns, each led by its own cacique under a paramount chief at the town of Ais. In 1444 no European had yet touched this coast, and the lagoon towns traded little even with other Florida peoples.

Juan Ponce de León sailed along this shore in 1513. By the 1550s the Ais were allied with Carlos, the powerful king of the Calusa, to whom their chief Oathchaqua had given his daughter. In November 1565 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés, fresh from founding St. Augustine, visited the Ais town and received its chief's oath to Philip II; the presidio he left behind was abandoned within months amid hunger and bloodshed, and a formal peace followed in 1570. Governor Méndez de Canço reported in 1597 that the Ais chief could field more warriors than any chief in Florida, and in 1605 the soldier Álvaro Mexía mapped the lagoon and agreed a ransom for shipwrecked sailors. Jonathan Dickinson, shipwrecked with his party in 1696, left the fullest account of Ais life; friars sent in 1699 made no converts. After 1700 Carolinian slavers and their Indian allies raided the coast; some 88 'coast Indians' were removed to the northern missions in 1726 and only 52 remained by 1728. In 1763 the last of the Ais sailed for Cuba with the Spaniards and the Calusa.
zh:
艾斯人（Ais，又作Ays）住在一条狭长潟湖的障壁岛与大陆沿岸，西班牙人把这片水域称作「艾斯河」，即今印第安河；其地北起卡纳维拉尔角，南至圣露西入海口。潟湖里鱼、龟和贝类繁庶，岸边棕榈浆果与可可李成熟，艾斯人不事农耕却衣食丰足。他们的社会是由多个村镇组成的酋邦，各镇自有首领，统属于坐镇艾斯镇的大酋。1444年，还没有欧洲人到过这片海岸，潟湖诸镇与佛罗里达其他族群也很少往来。

1513年，胡安·庞塞·德莱昂的船队沿这一带海岸南下。16世纪50年代，艾斯人已与势力强盛的卡卢萨王卡洛斯结盟，大酋奥阿奇夸把女儿嫁给他。1565年11月，刚建立圣奥古斯丁的佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯造访艾斯镇，大酋向腓力二世宣誓效忠；留守的要塞却因缺粮和流血冲突数月后即告废弃，双方1570年正式议和。1597年，门德斯·德·坎索总督奏称艾斯首领能调集的武士冠于佛罗里达诸部；1605年，士兵阿尔瓦罗·梅希亚在艾斯人协助下测绘潟湖，并定下赎救失事船员的约定。1696年随船遇险的乔纳森·迪金森留下了关于艾斯生活最详尽的记载，1699年派来的修士则未赢得一名信徒。1700年后，卡罗来纳的奴隶贩子及其印第安盟友不断洗劫海岸：1726年约88名「沿海印第安人」被迁往北方传教站，1728年仅剩52人。1763年，最后的艾斯人随西班牙人和卡卢萨人登船前往古巴。

en:
The lands between the Suwannee and Santa Fe rivers were held in 1444 by the Northern Utina, the Timucua-speaking people whose dialect the Spanish later called Timucua proper. Their scattered villages belonged to small chiefdoms linked by language, marriage, and the Suwannee Valley ceramic tradition; maize fields, river crossings, and a principal settlement perhaps near Fig Springs gave the country its centers. Across the Suwannee lived the closely related Yustaga, while raids and shifting alliances separated the Northern Utina from other Florida chiefdoms.

In 1539 Hernando de Soto marched through this region, seized Chief Aguacaleycuen, and after a clash near Napituca put many Timucua to death. Franciscan missions entered the chiefdom in 1597, and San Martín de Timucua, likely at Fig Springs, became the leading station among missions founded between 1608 and 1616. The Northern Utina joined the Timucua Rebellion of 1656; Spanish forces then burned their towns and moved survivors along the road from St. Augustine to Apalachee. Creek and Yamasee raids, epidemics, and Carolinian slave raids further reduced the province. The remaining Timucua were withdrawn toward St. Augustine and, when Spain ceded Florida in 1763, left for Cuba with the Spanish.
zh:
1444年，萨旺尼河与圣菲河之间的土地由北乌蒂纳人占据，他们是蒂穆夸语人群的一支，西班牙人后来把他们的方言称为「正宗蒂穆夸语」。分散的村落分属各个小酋邦，依靠共同语言、联姻和萨旺尼河谷陶器传统联系在一起；玉米地、渡口，以及菲格泉附近可能存在的主要村镇，构成这片土地的中心。萨旺尼河对岸是关系密切的尤斯塔加人，而袭击与不断变化的同盟，又使北乌蒂纳人与佛罗里达其他酋邦保持距离。

1539年，埃尔南多·德·索托率军穿过这里，俘获酋长阿瓜卡莱昆，并在纳皮图卡附近的冲突后处死许多蒂穆夸人。1597年，方济各会传教站进入这一酋邦；可能位于菲格泉的圣马丁·德·蒂穆夸，是1608年至1616年间建立的各传教站中最重要的一处。北乌蒂纳人参加1656年的蒂穆夸叛乱，事后西班牙军队焚毁村镇，把幸存者迁往圣奥古斯丁通往阿巴拉契的道路沿线。克里克人与亚马西人的袭击、疫病以及卡罗来纳奴隶劫掠使教区人口继续锐减。残余的蒂穆夸人被撤往圣奥古斯丁附近，1763年西班牙割让佛罗里达后又随西班牙人前往古巴。

en:
In 1444 Apalachee was a densely settled Muskogean-speaking country between the Aucilla and Ochlockonee rivers, opening onto Apalachee Bay. Farming villages lived under powerful regional chiefs in a Mississippian world of mound ceremonialism and long-distance trade reaching toward the Great Lakes. Anhaica was the principal town, and the province's stored grain, copper ornaments, and strict hierarchy made it one of the strongest chiefdoms in Florida. The peoples to the east along the Aucilla were Timucuan speakers, and alliances and raids shifted with every generation.

Pánfilo de Narváez entered Apalachee on 15 June 1528 and met fierce resistance before fleeing to the coast. Hernando de Soto seized Anhaica eleven years later and wintered there in 1539 and 1540 despite ambushes and raids on his horses. Franciscan missionaries began work around 1600, and in 1656 San Luis de Talimali became the western capital of Spanish Florida, linking Apalachee farms and ranches to St. Augustine. From the 1670s, Apalachicola, Yamasee, and other Creek raiders carried captives to Carolina, and in 1704 Colonel James Moore led fifty colonists and about a thousand Creek warriors through the missions. Moore carried off roughly 1,300 surrendered Apalachee and another thousand enslaved people; the Spanish burned San Luis and abandoned the province. Survivors fled toward Pensacola, Mobile, and the Carolinas, with only a small band returning near St. Marks in 1718.
zh:
1444年的阿巴拉契是一片人口稠密的穆斯科格语地区，位于奥西拉河与奥洛克洛尼河之间，通向阿巴拉契湾。务农村落受强有力的地区酋长统辖，属于有土墩仪式和远途贸易的密西西比社会，贸易联系远达五大湖方向。安海卡是主要城镇，储存的谷物、铜饰和森严等级使阿巴拉契成为佛罗里达最强盛的酋邦之一。奥西拉河以东是蒂穆夸语人群，各代人之间的同盟与侵袭不断变化。

1528年6月15日，潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯进入阿巴拉契，遭到猛烈抵抗，最后逃向海岸。十一年后，埃尔南多·德·索托夺取安海卡，并在当地人伏击和射杀马匹的袭扰中于1539年至1540年在此过冬。约1600年，方济各会传教士开始传教；1656年，圣路易斯·德·塔利马利成为西属佛罗里达的西部首府，把阿巴拉契的农庄和牧场与圣奥古斯丁连接起来。1670年代起，阿巴拉奇科拉人、亚马西人和其他克里克袭掠者把俘虏带往卡罗来纳。1704年，詹姆斯·摩尔上校率领五十名殖民者和约一千名克里克战士横扫各传教站，带走约一千三百名投降的阿巴拉契人，另有一千人被掳为奴；西班牙人焚毁圣路易斯并放弃教区。幸存者逃往彭萨科拉、莫比尔和南北卡罗来纳，只有一小群人在1718年回到圣马可斯附近。

en:
In 1444 Guale was a string of towns and island settlements among Georgia's tidal waterways and Sea Islands, including Sapelo and St. Catherines and the lower Altamaha and Ogeechee rivers. Chiefs called micos ruled with town councils and matrilineal lineages; plazas, platform mounds, shell deposits, and ceramics place the country in the Savannah and Irene phases of coastal Mississippian life. Families raised maize and beans, hunted on the mainland, and took fish and shellfish from the estuaries, while island and river towns exchanged food, shells, and marriage alliances.

Jean Ribault's French expedition met the Guale in 1562, when Chief Oade supplied maize and beans to the Charlesfort settlement on Parris Island. Jesuits arrived in the 1560s, and Franciscans were working in at least five principal towns by 1595. In September 1597 five friars were killed; the older story centered on Juanillo's revolt against the suppression of polygyny, while later accounts also stress rivalries among Guale chiefs. Governor Gonzalo Méndez de Canzo burned towns and crops, and in 1601 Domingo of Asao killed Don Francisco and Juanillo. Missions returned early in the new century, six being listed in 1655, among them Santa Catalina de Guale, San Joseph de Sapala, and Santo Domingo de Talaje. Forced labor, epidemics, Westo raids, and piracy then weakened the province, and Spain withdrew all six coastal missions in 1684. Many Guale joined the emerging Yamasee, forming most of the Upper Towns, and became entangled in slave raids armed through the Scottish settlement of Stuarts Town. James Moore overran the remaining settlements in 1702; after the Yamasee War of 1715 the survivors scattered, leaving too few Guale to resist James Oglethorpe's founding of Georgia in 1733.
zh:
1444年，瓜莱是佐治亚潮汐水道与海岛上的一串村镇，分布在萨佩洛岛、圣凯瑟琳斯岛以及阿尔塔马哈河、奥吉奇河下游一带。称为mico的酋长依靠镇议会和母系氏族行使权力；广场、土墩、贝壳堆积和陶器表明，这里属于沿海密西西比社会的萨凡纳阶段与艾琳阶段。居民种植玉米和豆类，在大陆狩猎，也在河口捕捞鱼虾和贝类，海岛与河畔村镇之间交换食物、贝壳并互通婚姻。

1562年，让·里博率领的法国探险队遇到瓜莱人，酋长奥阿德向帕里斯岛上的查尔斯堡供应玉米和豆类。耶稣会士在1560年代首先到来，到1595年方济各会已在至少五个主要村镇传教。1597年9月，五名修士被杀；传统叙述把事件核心归于胡安尼略反抗多妻制被禁，后来的解释也强调瓜莱酋长之间的权力争斗。总督贡萨洛·门德斯·德·坎索出兵焚毁村镇和作物，1601年阿萨奥的多明戈杀死唐·弗朗西斯科和胡安尼略。传教站在17世纪初恢复，1655年已有六座，包括圣卡塔利娜·德·瓜莱、圣何塞·德·萨帕拉和圣多明各·德·塔拉赫。劳役征调、疫病、韦斯托人袭掠和海盗随后削弱教区，1684年西班牙撤出全部六座海岸传教站。许多瓜莱人加入正在形成的亚马西人，并在亚马西上镇中占多数，又因苏格兰斯图尔特镇提供火器而卷入奴隶袭掠。1702年，詹姆斯·摩尔摧毁残余定居点；1715年亚马西战争后幸存者四散，到1733年詹姆斯·奥格尔索普建立佐治亚时，瓜莱人已无力阻挡。

en:
The fall-line hills and creek-cut valleys of the lower Chattahoochee are the country of the Lower Creek towns, Muskogean-speaking villagers of the South Appalachian Mississippian world. Maize fields climbed the river terraces below platform mounds that carried temples and the houses of chiefs, and the towns governed their own affairs in the long peace after the old mound centers broke up. Kasihta, which the Spanish would write as Casista, ranked with Coweta as the oldest and foremost of the Chattahoochee towns, a 'white' or peace town where councils were held and blood could not be spilled. In 1444 its people traded along the ridge paths with neighbours near and far and had never met a European.

Franciscans and soldiers first reached the Chattahoochee towns from Apalachee in 1638, and by the 1670s their deerskins were going by way of Florida to Havana, even as English traders from Charleston appeared at Coweta. Slave raids and imperial rivalry soon pulled most of the towns east to the Ocmulgee, where Carolina knew them as the Ochese. Kasihta and Coweta people were counted among the Yamasee, the armed confederation that raided for slaves on Carolina's behalf until debt and abuse drove it to revolt on 15 April 1715, opening the Yamasee War. Defeat scattered the Yamasee, and the towns returned to the Chattahoochee as the Lower Towns of the Creek confederacy. For a century Kasihta shared in the deerskin trade with Carolina and Georgia, a peace town that sheltered refugees as smaller peoples folded into the Creek world. The American Revolution and the treaties that followed bit into the town lands, and when the Creek civil war of 1813–14 ended in Andrew Jackson's victory the defeated nation was forced to cede its Georgia country; by 1821 the old Kasihta lands lay open to American settlement.
zh:
查特胡奇河下游的瀑布线丘陵与溪谷纵横之地，是下克里克诸镇的家园。这些讲穆斯科格语的村镇属于南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化圈，玉米地沿河畔台地拾级而上，平顶土丘上矗立着神庙和酋长的居所；古老的土丘中心瓦解后，诸镇在漫长岁月里各自治理内部事务。卡西塔——西班牙人写作Casista——与考维塔并列为查特胡奇河畔最古老、最首要的城镇，是一座「白镇」，即讲和议事、禁止流血的和平镇。1444年的卡西塔人沿山脊商路与远近邻族贸易，还从未见过欧洲人。

方济各会修士和士兵1638年从阿巴拉奇首次抵达查特胡奇诸镇；到1670年代，这里的鹿皮已经佛罗里达远销哈瓦那，与此同时，来自查尔斯顿的英国商人也出现在考维塔。贩奴袭扰和列强争夺很快把大多数城镇向东引向奥克马尔吉河，卡罗来纳人把他们称作奥切斯人。卡西塔人和考维塔人也被计入亚马西联盟——这个武装联盟替卡罗来纳掳掠人口为奴，直到债务盘剥和种种凌虐把他们逼反：1715年4月15日，亚马西战争爆发。战败使亚马西人四散，诸镇重返查特胡奇河，组成克里克联盟的下镇。此后一个世纪里，卡西塔参与对卡罗来纳和佐治亚的鹿皮贸易，作为和平镇收容难民，看着较小的族群陆续并入克里克世界。美国独立战争及随后的条约不断蚕食城镇土地；1813至1814年克里克内战以安德鲁·杰克逊的胜利告终，战败的联盟被迫割让佐治亚故土，到1821年，古老的卡西塔土地已向美国拓殖者敞开。

en:
The mountain-fringed valleys of the upper Coosa were the heart of Coosa, the greatest of the South Appalachian paramount chiefdoms. Its capital on the Coosawattee, a town of plazas and three platform mounds, headed eight villages of perhaps a few thousand people, while its mico drew tribute from subject chiefdoms strung four hundred miles along the Appalachians, as far north as Chiaha on the French Broad, where maize, bean, squash and tobacco fields overlooked the river. In 1444 Coosa stood at the height of its power, its merchants and war parties known from the Tennessee to the Alabama piedmont.

Hernando de Soto entered the chiefdom in the summer of 1540, his chroniclers spelling its name Coça and remarking on the fertile gardens and abundance of food rather than any single city. Tristán de Luna came in 1560 and Juan Pardo in 1566–68, building Fort San Pedro beside Chiaha; when the inland forts rose in 1568 Pardo's garrisons were killed and Spain gave up the interior. Old World diseases proved more destructive than soldiers: by 1600 the Coosa heartland was largely abandoned, and the survivors withdrew into fortified villages down the Coosa River in Alabama, while Cherokee warriors from the mountains made themselves masters of the empty northern valleys. The name of Coosa lived on as one of the four mother towns of the Creek confederacy among the Upper Towns, deep in the deerskin trade of the eighteenth century. The Creek civil war of 1813–14 ended in Andrew Jackson's victory over the Upper Towns, and the forced cessions that followed stripped the old Coosa country of its self-rule.
zh:
群山环抱的上库萨河谷，是南阿巴拉契亚诸最高酋邦中最强大的库萨的腹地。其首府坐落库萨瓦蒂河畔，镇中有广场和三座平顶土丘，统辖着八座村落、约数千人口；大酋长（mico）向沿阿巴拉契亚山脉绵延四百英里的臣属酋邦索取贡赋，势力最北抵达弗伦奇布罗德河畔的奇亚哈——那里的玉米、豆类、南瓜和烟田俯瞰着河面。1444年正值库萨鼎盛之时，它的商队和战队闻名于从田纳西到亚拉巴马皮德蒙特的广阔地带。

1540年夏，埃尔南多·德索托进入库萨，随行记事把它的名字拼作Coça，他们记下的不是某一座雄城，而是遍地肥沃田园、粮食丰足的一串村镇。特里斯坦·德·卢纳1560年、胡安·帕尔多1566至1568年先后来到，帕尔多还在奇亚哈旁修建圣佩德罗堡；1568年内陆各堡据点的西班牙驻军尽被歼灭，西班牙从此放弃内陆。旧大陆带来的疫病比军队更具毁灭性：到1600年，库萨腹地已大半荒废，幸存者退入亚拉巴马境内库萨河下游筑有防御工事的村落，山里的切罗基战士则成了空旷北方谷地的主人。「库萨」之名延续下来，成为克里克联盟四大母镇之一，位列上镇之中，深度参与18世纪的鹿皮贸易。1813至1814年的克里克内战以安德鲁·杰克逊击败上镇告终，随后的强迫割地终结了古老库萨故土的自治。

en:
Issati covers the Santee country, where the Santee River gathers piedmont streams such as the Congaree and Wateree and crosses the South Carolina coastal plain to the Atlantic. The Santee were a small Catawban-speaking people whose villages, burial mounds and hunting grounds followed the middle river. In 1444 their paths and canoe routes linked them with the Winyah, Congaree and Catawba, while Spanish ships had not yet explored the river mouth.

A Spanish party led by Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón reached this coast in 1526, and Francisco Fernández de Écija, sent from St Augustine in 1605 and 1609, documented Santee villages on the river. English settlement at Charles Town in 1670 soon drew the Santee into colonial diplomacy and trade. John Lawson found their settlements extending for miles along the Santee in 1700, and Santee warriors served with John Barnwell in the Tuscarora War of 1711-12. They joined the Yamasee War against the colonists in 1715; a census shortly before the rising counted two villages and forty-three men, and in late 1716 English forces with Etiwan and Cusabo allies captured the river villages and sold many of the men into West Indian slavery.
