During the Revolution the British stockaded Fort Watson on the Santee as a link between Charleston and the interior, but Francis Marion and Henry Lee besieged it from 15 to 23 April 1781 and used a rough sharpshooter's tower to force its surrender. The Santee Canal, chartered in 1786 and opened in 1800, ran twenty-two miles to the Cooper River, opening a shallow inland route between the upcountry and Charleston.
zh:
伊萨蒂是桑蒂人的土地，桑蒂河汇集资河、沃特里河等皮德蒙特河流，穿过南卡罗来纳沿海平原注入大西洋。桑蒂人是人口不多的卡塔万语族群，村落、墓冢和猎场沿河中游分布。1444年时，他们的小路和独木舟航线把自己与温亚人、康加里人和卡托巴人联系起来，西班牙船只也尚未探入河口。

1526年，卢卡斯·巴斯克斯·德·艾永率领的西班牙队伍到达这段海岸；1605年和1609年，圣奥古斯丁派出的弗朗西斯科·费尔南德斯·德·埃西哈两次记录了河畔的桑蒂村落。1670年英国人建立查尔斯镇，桑蒂人很快被卷入殖民外交与贸易。1700年，约翰·劳森看到桑蒂人的聚落在沿河数英里间延展；1711至1712年，桑蒂战士随约翰·巴恩韦尔参加图斯卡罗拉战争。1715年他们在亚马西战争中转攻殖民者，战前一次人口调查记载当地有两座村落、四十三名男子；1716年底，英军联合埃蒂万人和库萨博人袭取河畔村落，许多男子被贩往西印度群岛为奴。独立战争期间，英军在桑蒂河畔修筑沃森堡，作为查尔斯顿与内陆之间的联络据点；1781年4月15日至23日，弗朗西斯·马里昂和亨利·李围攻该堡，以简陋的狙击手高台压制守军，迫使英军投降。桑蒂运河1786年获准修建、1800年通航，长二十二英里，连通库珀河，为内陆与查尔斯顿之间打开了一条浅水内河航路。

en:
The rolling Piedmont of the Wateree and Catawba rivers is the homeland of the Iswa, 'people of the river' — Ye Iswąˀ, the name later rendered as Catawba. In the fifteenth century its mound towns answered to the mico of Cofitachequi, the paramount chief seated at Talimeco on the Wateree, where a temple crowning the greatest earthen mound kept the bones of rulers and stores of freshwater pearls. Long wars with Ocute in Georgia had emptied the Savannah, Saluda and Broad basins into a wide no-man's-land, leaving Cofitachequi in 1444 the strongest power between the mountains and the coast, its reach extending up toward the North Carolina piedmont.

Spanish ships raiding the coast in 1521 carried off tales of a pearl-rich ruler, Datha, and in 1540 Hernando de Soto crossed the empty buffer into Cofitachequi. A woman, the Lady of Cofitachequi, met him borne on a litter; the Spaniards took her hostage while hunting gold, but she escaped. Juan Pardo found the chiefdom much weakened in 1566–68, calling its town Canosi, and his forts were burned within two years. Slave raids by the Westo and Occaneechi savaged the region through the 1600s, though Henry Woodward still met an 'emperor' said to command a thousand bowmen in 1670, who even visited Charleston. The old chiefdom was abandoned soon after; in 1701 John Lawson found only Congaree hamlets, and the survivors merged into the Catawba confederacy. As the Catawba the river people became the Piedmont's leading tribe, allied with Carolina against the Seneca and Shawnee, until smallpox epidemics in 1738 and 1759 — the second killing nearly half the nation — broke their power. Chief King Hagler was killed by Shawnee raiders in 1763, when South Carolina also confirmed the Catawba a 144,000-acre reservation on the river. They supported the American revolutionaries, withdrawing to Virginia when British troops marched through in 1780 and returning after Guilford Court House in 1781.
zh:
沃特里河与卡托巴河流经的起伏皮德蒙特，是伊斯瓦人的家园——Iswa 意为「河上人」，Ye Iswąˀ 后来被英国人写作卡托巴。15世纪时，这一带的土丘城镇都听命于科菲塔切基的大酋长（mico）；其首府塔利梅科位于沃特里河畔，最大的土丘顶上建有神庙，供奉历代统治者的遗骨和淡水珍珠储藏。与佐治亚奥库特的长期战争使萨凡纳河、萨卢达河和布罗德河流域沦为大片无人地带，到1444年，科菲塔切基已是山地与海岸之间最强的势力，影响一直向北伸向北卡罗来纳皮德蒙特。

1521年劫掠海岸的西班牙船带走了一位坐拥珍珠的君主达塔的传闻；1540年春，埃尔南多·德索托穿过那片空旷缓冲地，开进科菲塔切基。一位被称为「科菲塔切基女主」的女性乘肩舆接见了他，西班牙人在搜寻黄金期间将她扣为人质，但她最终逃脱。胡安·帕尔多1566至1568年再到时，酋邦已大为衰弱，他把其城镇称作卡诺西；他修建的西班牙要塞两年内全被烧毁。整个17世纪，韦斯托人和奥卡尼奇人的贩奴袭扰使这一地区人口凋敝，不过亨利·伍德沃德1670年仍见到一位据称能调动上千弓箭手的「皇帝」，此人还在1670年和1672年两度访问查尔斯顿。此后不久这座老酋邦便遭废弃；1701年约翰·劳森路经此地，只见到康加里人的小村落，幸存者陆续并入卡托巴联盟。以卡托巴之名，河上居民成为皮德蒙特最强大的部族，与卡罗来纳结盟对抗塞内卡人和肖尼人，直到1738年和1759年两度天花流行——后一次夺去近半数族人的生命——才瓦解其势力。1763年，首领哈格勒王被肖尼袭扰者杀害，同年南卡罗来纳为卡托巴人确认了横跨卡托巴河、面积14.4万英亩的保留地。独立战争中他们支持美方；1780年英军过境时卡托巴人暂避弗吉尼亚，1781年吉尔福德县府战役后才返回家园。

en:
The gorges and tablelands of the upper Cumberland were, in 1444, a meeting-ground of peoples. The Yuchi — Tsoyaha, 'children of the sun', as they called themselves in a language with no known kin — held the Tennessee valley to the south and ranged across these headwaters, planting corn in the river bottoms, while Shawnee hunters from the Ohio country knew the Cumberland as Wasioto. The hills carried deer and elk herds, and no European had yet crossed the ridges to the east.

Hernando de Soto's men heard of these people as the Uchi when they passed through the Tennessee valley in 1541. The first English reach over the mountains came in 1671, when Thomas Batts and Robert Fallam, sent from Fort Henry by Abraham Wood, crossed the divide to the western rivers. By then the old country was emptying: in the 1670s Iroquois war parties, claiming the Ohio valley for the fur trade, drove the Shawnee out of Kentucky, and in 1714 the Cherokee destroyed the Yuchi town of Chestowee, pushing the survivors south toward the Savannah and Chattahoochee. For two generations the upper Cumberland was left to passing hunters, until March 1775, when the Cherokee at Sycamore Shoals sold the Kentucky and Cumberland country to Richard Henderson's Transylvania Company. Daniel Boone blazed the Wilderness Road through Cumberland Gap, and by the end of the century settlers' stations had taken root along the upper river.
zh:
1444年，坎伯兰河上游的峡谷与台原是几支人群交会之地。尤奇人按他们那种与任何语言都不亲缘的语言自称「措亚哈」，意为「太阳之子」；他们据有南方的田纳西河谷，游猎范围遍及这一带河源，并在河谷低地种植玉米，来自俄亥俄方向的肖尼猎人则把坎伯兰河称作瓦西奥托。山林里奔走著鹿和麋鹿，东面的山脊之外还不曾有欧洲人翻越而来。

1541年，埃尔南多·德·索托的队伍穿过田纳西河谷时，已听说这些人，记作「乌奇」（Uchi）。欧洲人最早翻越山脉是在1671年：亚伯拉罕·伍德从亨利堡派出托马斯·巴茨和罗伯特·法勒姆，首次越过阿巴拉契亚分水岭抵达西向的河水。此时这片故地正在变空——1670年代，易洛魁武装为毛皮贸易宣称俄亥俄河谷为猎场，把肖尼人逐出肯塔基；1714年切罗基人又摧毁尤奇城镇切斯托维，幸存者向南退往萨凡纳河与查特胡奇河一带。此后两代人的时间里，坎伯兰河上游只剩往来的猎手，直到1775年3月，切罗基人在锡卡莫尔浅滩将肯塔基与坎伯兰的土地卖给理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚公司。丹尼尔·布恩开辟了穿过坎伯兰峡的荒野之路，到18世纪末，移民的据点已在上游河畔扎下根。

en:
The Chiaha were a Mississippian chiefdom of the lower French Broad River valley in East Tennessee, one of the Dallas-phase farming peoples whose raised-house villages had dotted the Appalachian valleys since about 1300. Beneath the towns lay fields of maize, beans, squash and tobacco, and the chiefdom stood at the northern edge of Coosa's sphere of influence. In 1444 its principal village remained the centre of the river valley's maize lands, and no European had yet crossed the mountains.

Hernando de Soto's entrada reached Chiaha in 1540 and rested several days at its principal village. Juan Pardo followed in 1567, and his men built Fort San Pedro nearby, one of a chain of garrisons reaching west from Joara. In 1568 the inland peoples rose, burned the forts and killed the garrisons; all but one of Pardo's soldiers died, and Spain never again attempted the interior. European diseases then emptied and rearranged these chiefdoms, so that when the Virginians James Needham and Gabriel Arthur crossed the mountains in 1673 seeking the Tomahittans, the French Broad valley was already passing under Cherokee sway.
zh:
奇亚哈人是东田纳西弗伦奇布罗德河下游谷地的密西西比文化酋邦，属达拉斯期农耕人群：自约1300年起，他们的高脚屋村落散布在阿巴拉契亚的河谷间，镇外是玉米、豆类、南瓜和烟草田，其酋邦地处库萨势力范围的北缘。1444年，奇亚哈的主镇仍是这片河谷玉米地的中心，此时还没有欧洲人翻山而来。

1540年，埃尔南多·德·索托的远征队抵达奇亚哈，在主镇休整数日。1567年胡安·帕尔多接踵而至，部下在附近建起圣佩德罗堡，它是从乔阿拉向西延伸的一连串要塞之一。1568年，内陆各族群起事，焚毁要塞、杀死驻军，帕尔多的士兵仅一人生还，西班牙人从此再未尝试深入内陆。欧洲人带来的疫病使各酋邦人口锐减、聚落重组，到1673年弗吉尼亚人詹姆斯·尼达姆与加布里埃尔·阿瑟为寻找托马希坦人翻山到来时，弗伦奇布罗德河谷已渐入切罗基人的势力范围。

en:
Joara, founded around AD 1000 in the upper Catawba valley at the foot of the Blue Ridge, was the largest Mississippian town in what is now North Carolina. Its earthen mound rose above a prosperous river centre whose people traded copper and salt through the hills, one of three chiefdoms—with Cofitachequi and Guatari—that held the Carolina Piedmont in turn. In 1444 the chiefdom still ruled the fertile upper Catawba bottoms near present Morganton, its granaries and towns untouched by Europeans.

De Soto's chroniclers recorded Joara in 1540. In January 1567 Juan Pardo wintered there, named the town Cuenca and built Fort San Juan, the first European settlement in the North Carolina interior, linking it to five more forts reaching west to Chiaha. In 1568 the townspeople burned the fort, and across the six forts all but one of Pardo's 120 soldiers were killed; Spain never returned to the interior. Disease emptied the upper Catawba soon after: neighbours still knew the place as Hoada in 1605, after which all mention ceases. Its survivors, the Sara or Cheraw, drifted east to the Yadkin and Dan and were absorbed into the Catawba Nation between 1726 and 1739. English, Scots-Irish and German farmers settled the abandoned valley in the later eighteenth century.
zh:
乔阿拉约于公元1000年兴起于蓝岭山麓的卡托巴河上游，是日后北卡罗来纳境内最大的密西西比文化城镇。土筑墩台矗立在这座繁华的河贸中心，居民以铜和盐同山地各部交易；它与科菲塔切基、瓜塔里并称卡罗来纳皮德蒙特三大酋邦，权势在三者间轮替。1444年，乔阿拉仍统治着今摩根顿附近肥沃的卡托巴河上游滩地，粮仓和市镇尚未遭欧洲人染指。

1540年，德·索托的书记官记下了乔阿拉。1567年1月，胡安·帕尔多在此过冬，把镇子命名为昆卡，建起圣胡安堡——欧洲人在北卡罗来纳内陆的第一个定居点，又以五座要塞向西连到奇亚哈。1568年，镇民焚毁圣胡安堡，六座要塞的一百二十名驻军仅一人生还，西班牙人从此再未踏入这片内陆。疫病很快使卡托巴河上游人口凋零：1605年邻族仍以「霍阿达」之名提到此地，此后记载断绝；余部即萨拉人（又称切罗人）向东退入亚德金河与丹河流域，于1726至1739年间并入卡托巴联盟。18世纪后期，英格兰、苏格兰-爱尔兰和德意志农户迁入这片废弃的河谷。

en:
The pinewoods and river bottoms between the North Carolina coast and the Piedmont are the country of the Tuscarora, whose name Skarù·ręˀ means 'hemp gatherers', after one of the three tribes of their Iroquoian confederacy. Their large towns stood on the Roanoke, Tar, Neuse and Pamlico, rivers that carried dugout canoes from inland villages down to the coastal sounds, and seven matrilineal clans, among them Bear, Beaver, Turtle and Wolf, bound the towns together. The wild hemp they gathered supplied fibre, cord and medicine. In 1444 these were populous, self-ruling towns, linked by language and kin to the Iroquois far to the north but untouched as yet by any European.

By 1700 English colonists were pushing up the rivers from the coast, raiding villages for the slave trade and bringing diseases that thinned the towns. In September 1711 the southern chief Hancock, joined by the Pamlico, Coree and other neighbouring peoples, launched a coordinated assault on the settlements, opening the Tuscarora War. South Carolina militia under John Barnwell stormed his fort on the Neuse in 1712 and Hancock was captured and executed; in 1713 the stronghold of Neoheroka fell, with about 900 killed or taken. Tom Blount, the northern chief who had held aloof, made a treaty in June 1718 securing his followers a 56,000-acre tract on the Roanoke, chartered in 1722 as the Indian Woods reservation. Other bands moved north to the Iroquois, who admitted the Tuscarora as their sixth nation the same year. Cessions and sickness shrank Indian Woods to 104 people by 1767, and in 1804 the last band left for New York.
zh:
北卡罗来纳海岸与皮德蒙特之间的松林和河滨低地，是塔斯卡洛拉人的家园。族名Skarù·ręˀ意为「采麻者」，原是其易洛魁语三族联盟中一支的称呼。他们的大镇坐落在洛亚诺克河、塔尔河、纽斯河和帕姆利科河畔，独木舟顺流而下，可从内陆村落直达海岸潟湖；熊、河狸、龟、狼等七个母系氏族把各镇联结在一起，采来的野麻用来搓绳、织布和制药。1444年的塔斯卡洛拉各镇人烟稠密、自主其政，语言和亲缘虽与遥远北方的易洛魁人相通，欧洲人的足迹却尚未到此。

1700年前后，英国殖民者从海岸沿河道不断深入，掳掠村民贩卖为奴，带来的疫病也使各镇人口锐减。1711年9月，南支首领汉考克联合帕姆利科人、科里人等邻族，对殖民点发动协同进攻，塔斯卡罗拉战争爆发。1712年，约翰·巴恩韦尔率领的南卡罗来纳民兵攻破他在纽斯河畔的堡垒，汉考克被俘处死；1713年内奥赫罗卡堡陷落，约九百人战死或被俘。保持中立的北支首领汤姆·布朗特于1718年6月缔约，为部下争得洛亚诺克河畔5.6万英亩土地，1722年正式划为印第安伍兹保留地。另一些人北上投奔易洛魁联盟，同年被接纳为第六族。此后土地不断割让、疫病流行，到1767年保留地上只剩104人；1804年，最后一支塔斯卡洛拉人离开北卡罗来纳，迁往纽约。

en:
The sheltered waters of the Pamlico River and Pamlico Sound, guarded from the Atlantic by the long line of the Outer Banks, were the country of the Pamlico, a Carolina Algonquian people whom Raleigh's men recorded in 1585 as the Pomoui. They planted corn and beans in riverside fields and drew shad and herring from the sound, sharing its inlets and shoals with the Croatan, Machapunga and Secotan, their kin in language and trade. In 1444 no European sail had yet crossed this horizon; the inlets later charted as Wococon and Hatteras were known only to the canoe men who fished them.

English ships of the Roanoke voyages began calling here in 1585, but settlement waited until the 1690s, when English farmers and French Huguenots took up the Pamlico River. Bath, chartered on 8 March 1705, was the first town in North Carolina and prospered on naval stores, furs and tobacco. A smallpox 'great mortality' of 1696 shattered the Pamlico, and by 1710 John Lawson found them living in one small village of perhaps fifteen fighting men. On 22 September 1711 the southern Tuscarora, with the Pamlico and other allies, struck Bath, New Bern and the plantations along the Neuse and Trent rivers, opening the Tuscarora War; Lawson was among the killed and more than a hundred settlers died in the New Bern raids. The pirate Blackbeard took the king's pardon at Bath in 1718, only to be hunted down and killed by Lieutenant Robert Maynard at Ocracoke Inlet on 22 November 1718. Rebuilt New Bern became the colony's capital in 1770 and held the seat until 1792.
zh:
帕姆利科河与帕姆利科湾水面平静，外滩群岛如长堤横在外面，挡住大西洋的风浪。这里是帕姆利科人的土地，他们操卡罗来纳阿尔冈昆语，雷利的手下1585年把他们记作「波莫伊」。他们在河畔田地里种玉米和豆子，在湾中捕捞西鲱和鲱鱼，与语言相通、贸易往来的克罗阿坦人、马查邦加人和塞科坦人共用各处水口和浅滩。1444年，欧洲人的船帆还没有出现在海平线上；后来被标作沃科康和哈特勒斯的水道口，那时只有打鱼的独木舟船夫知晓。

1585年起，罗阿诺克远航的英国船只开始在此停靠，但真正的殖民要等到1690年代——英格兰农户和法国胡格诺教徒陆续迁居帕姆利科河畔。1705年3月8日获许建城的巴斯是北卡罗来纳第一座城镇，靠柏油松脂、毛皮和烟草兴旺起来。1696年一场被称为「大死亡」的天花重创帕姆利科人，到1710年，约翰·劳森发现他们只剩一个小村子，能作战的人不过十五名上下。1711年9月22日，南部图斯卡罗拉人联合帕姆利科等盟邦袭击巴斯、新伯尔尼以及纽斯河、特伦特河沿岸的种植园，图斯卡罗拉战争爆发；劳森也在遇害者之列，新伯尔尼一带有一百多名殖民者被杀。海盗黑胡子1718年在巴斯接受国王赦免，却在同年11月22日于奥克拉科克水口被罗伯特·梅纳德中尉追上击毙。战后重建的新伯尔尼1770年成为殖民地首府，一直延续到1792年。

en:
The Pennyrile is a rolling karst tableland between the lower Cumberland and the Green, its limestone split by sinkholes, springs and river caves. In 1444 it was the southern ground of the Shawnee, whose bark-covered houses and cornfields stood in the bottoms and whose hunters followed deer and bison to the salt licks; the lower Cumberland would later appear on French maps as the Rivière des Chaouanons, the River of the Shawnee. No European had yet set eyes on the Green or the Cumberland.

In the 1670s Iroquois raids waged for the fur trade drove the Shawnee out of Kentucky, leaving the tableland to passing Cherokee and Chickasaw hunting parties, and by the 1680s French canoes on the Mississippi had marked the Cumberland's mouth as the Shawnee River. In 1750 Thomas Walker crossed the mountains to the south-east and gave the Cumberland its name. Long hunters followed him: in 1766 James Smith's party traced the Cumberland all the way down to the Ohio through this country, and in 1769 Kasper Mansker, Isaac Bledsoe and Uriah Stone returned to mark its licks and trails. The Treaty of Sycamore Shoals in 1775 brought the tableland within Richard Henderson's Transylvania purchase, and settlers' stations began to take root. In 1797 tradition places a hunter named Houchin chasing a wounded bear into a vast cave mouth on the Green; Valentine Simon registered the land in 1798 and worked its saltpeter, and in July 1812 Charles Wilkins and Hyman Gratz bought the cave and mined calcium nitrate there on an industrial scale with seventy slaves, feeding the gunpowder mills of the War of 1812.
zh:
彭尼罗尔是坎伯兰河下游与格林河之间一片起伏的喀斯特台原，石灰岩上遍布落水洞、泉眼和溶洞。1444年，这里是肖尼人南部的活动之地：他们树皮为顶的房屋和玉米地坐落在河谷低地，猎手追逐鹿和野牛前往盐渍地；下游的坎伯兰河后来在法国人的地图上被标作「肖尼人之河」。此时格林河与坎伯兰河还不曾被欧洲人看见。

1670年代，为毛皮贸易而来的易洛魁袭掠把肖尼人逐出肯塔基，台原上只剩切罗基和奇克索的猎手往来；到1680年代，密西西比河上的法国独木舟已把坎伯兰河口记作肖尼人之河。1750年，托马斯·沃克在东南方向翻山而过，为坎伯兰河命名。随后而来的是「长猎人」：1766年詹姆斯·史密斯的队伍沿坎伯兰河一直探到俄亥俄河口，1769年卡斯珀·曼斯克、艾萨克·布莱德索和尤赖亚·斯通又来到这里，记下沿途的盐渍地和小径。1775年的锡卡莫尔浅滩条约把台原纳入理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚购置，移民据点开始扎下根。1797年，据传一个姓霍钦的猎人追一头受伤的熊，追到了格林河畔一个巨大的洞口；1798年瓦伦丁·西蒙登记这块土地并开采硝石，1812年7月查尔斯·威尔金斯和海曼·格拉茨买下洞穴，驱使七十名奴隶大规模开采硝酸钙，为1812年战争的火药厂供料。

en:
Kentahke is the flat western end of Kentucky, where prairie-like barrens and Green River bottoms slope toward the Ohio and Mississippi. From about 1000 Mississippian farmers built mound towns in this country; Wickliffe, occupied until about 1350, had two large platform mounds around a plaza, a hereditary chief, maize stores and trade links reaching Wisconsin, North Carolina and the Gulf of Mexico. As those Angel-phase chiefdoms declined and reorganized, the land was not emptied. In 1444 Native hunters, farmers and traders still knew its trails, cane flats and river landings, though no European had mapped the country later glossed as “at the field” or “on the prairie.”

By the sixteenth century the Algonquian-speaking Kispoko controlled much of the interior. The Beaver Wars of 1640–1680 displaced Mascouten and Kispoko groups, with Kispoko survivors merging into the Shawnee; epidemics and fur-trade wars explain why later travelers found few large towns rather than the country having always been only a hunting ground. Thomas Walker and Christopher Gist surveyed Kentucky in 1750 and 1751, and the 1768 Treaty of Fort Stanwix opened the floodgate of colonial claims. In 1780 George Rogers Clark built Fort Jefferson near the Ohio's mouth without Chickasaw consent; Chickasaw resistance forced its abandonment in June 1781. Veterans took claims along the Green River after the Revolution, and Kentucky became a state in 1792, but the western tip remained Chickasaw land until Andrew Jackson and Isaac Shelby signed the Treaty of Tuscaloosa on 19 October 1818. The United States promised $300,000 over fifteen years, and by 1821 surveyors and settlers were entering the purchased plains.
zh:
肯塔基是肯塔基西部的平坦边地，草原般的贫瘠地与格林河河洲朝俄亥俄河和密西西比河方向倾斜。约1000年起，密西西比文化农民在此建立土墩城镇。威克利夫遗址延续至约1350年，广场周围有两座大型台墩，城镇由世袭首领统治，存有玉米，并与威斯康星、北卡罗来纳和墨西哥湾等地贸易。安吉尔阶段诸邦衰落重组后，这片土地并未空无一人。1444年，原住民猎人、农民和商人仍熟悉这里的小路、藤丛平地和河边登陆点；欧洲人尚未测绘这片后来被解释为「在原野上」「在草地上」的土地。

16世纪时，说阿尔冈昆语的基斯波科人控制着内陆大部。1640年至1680年的海狸战争迫使莫斯科腾人和基斯波科人迁徙，幸存的基斯波科人并入肖尼人。后来旅人少见大镇，是疫病和毛皮战争造成的结果，并非这里从来只是猎场。托马斯·沃克与克里斯托弗·吉斯特分别在1750年、1751年测量肯塔基，1768年《斯坦威克斯堡条约》更打开了殖民索地的闸门。1780年，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克未获奇克索人同意，便在俄亥俄河口附近修建杰斐逊堡；奇克索人的抵抗迫使守军于1781年6月弃堡。独立战争后，退伍军人沿格林河领取土地，肯塔基本身在1792年建州，但西端仍属奇克索人，直到安德鲁·杰克逊与艾萨克·谢尔比在1818年10月19日签订《塔斯卡卢萨条约》。美国承诺在十五年内支付三十万美元，到1821年，测量员和定居者已开始进入这片购得的平原。

en:
Ouasioto was an older name for the forested Cumberland ridge country on the eastern edge of Kentucky. The Shawnee called the river winding out of these mountains Wasioto, and hunters followed its valleys and the high gap where Kentucky, Virginia and Tennessee meet. In 1444 there was no European town or frontier here; the ridges were a country of game, furs and native trails, linked to the Chisca and Yuchi peoples later met by Spanish expeditions near the upper Tennessee.

Abraham Wood's Virginia traders left the earliest written report of the Cumberland Gap in the 1670s. Thomas Walker explored the pass in 1750 and gave the Cumberland name to the river and mountains. In March 1775 Richard Henderson's Transylvania Company purchased Cherokee lands beyond the mountains and sent Daniel Boone to mark the Wilderness Road through the gap. Boone's trace opened southeastern Kentucky to packhorse settlers, while Cherokee raids during the wars of 1776–1794 made the route a war path as well. After the Treaty of Tellico Blockhouse in 1794, the road was improved for wagons in 1796, by which time tens of thousands of migrants were crossing into Kentucky.
zh:
奥瓦西奥托是肯塔基东部森林茂密的坎伯兰山岭一带的旧称。肖尼人把从群山中流出的大河叫作瓦西奥托，猎人们沿河谷穿行，并利用肯塔基、弗吉尼亚和田纳西交界处的高山隘口往来。1444年时，这里还没有欧洲人的城镇或边界，山岭间是猎物、毛皮和原住民小路交织之地，与后来西班牙人在田纳西河上游遇到的奇斯卡人和尤奇人联系在一起。

17世纪70年代，亚伯拉罕·伍德派出的弗吉尼亚商人留下了关于坎伯兰峡的最早文字记录。1750年，托马斯·沃克探查这个隘口，并把坎伯兰之名带给河流与群山。1775年3月，理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚公司购买山外的切罗基土地，派丹尼尔·布恩标出穿过隘口的荒野之路。布恩开辟的小径让驮马移民得以进入肯塔基东南部；1776年至1794年的切罗基战争中，这条路也成了行军和袭掠之路。1794年《特利科堡条约》后，道路于1796年拓宽到可通行马车，此时已有数以万计的移民翻山进入肯塔基。

en:
Waayaahtanwa is the middle Wabash country of the Wea, whose Miami-Illinois name means the people of Waayaahtanonki, the 'place of the whirlpool'. In 1444 their bark-covered lodges and cornfields occupied wooded bottoms between present Terre Haute and Logansport, above the later town of Ouiatenon near Lafayette. The river carried canoes toward the Ohio and the Mississippi, while trails linked them with the Miami, Piankeshaw, Pepikokia and Illini. They were then wholly beyond the reach of French traders or missionaries.

The Wea first appear in written records in 1673. After the disruptions of the Beaver Wars, French firearms and trade helped Miami-speaking bands reoccupy the Wabash, and in 1717 François Picote de Beletre built Fort Ouiatenon as a fur post and barrier against English expansion. Wea villages faced the French settlement, and by the mid-eighteenth century Ouiatenon was the hub of five Wea and two Kickapoo villages. Wea, Kickapoo and Mascouten warriors seized the post without bloodshed on 1 June 1763 during Pontiac's War. American militia under Charles Scott burned Ouiatenon in June 1791, and the Wea made peace in the 1795 Treaty of Greenville. On 7 November 1811 William Henry Harrison destroyed Prophetstown on the nearby Tippecanoe, breaking Tecumseh's confederacy; the 1818 Treaty of St Mary's ceded most Wea lands, and in 1820 the band agreed to leave the Wabash for Missouri and Arkansas.
zh:
瓦亚坦瓦是韦阿人在沃巴什河中游的土地；他们的迈阿密—伊利尼语自称Waayaahtanwa，来自waayaahtanonki，意为「漩涡之地的人」。1444年，他们覆着树皮的屋舍和玉米田分布在今特雷霍特至洛根斯波特之间林木繁茂的河漫滩，下临后来乌亚塔农（Ouiatenon）和拉斐特所在的河段。沃巴什河的独木舟可通向俄亥俄河与密西西比河，陆路则把他们与迈阿密人、皮安克肖人、佩皮科基亚人和伊利尼人相连。那时法国商人和传教士还完全没有到过这里。

韦阿人最早在1673年出现于文字记载。海狸战争造成流徙后，法国火器与贸易帮助说迈阿密语的各支重回沃巴什河；1717年，弗朗索瓦·皮科特·德·贝莱特尔在此修建乌亚塔农堡，作为毛皮贸易站和阻挡英国扩张的据点。韦阿村落与法国聚落隔河相对，到18世纪中叶，乌亚塔农已成为五个韦阿村落和两个基卡普村落的中心。1763年6月1日，韦阿、基卡普和马斯库滕战士在庞蒂亚克战争中兵不血刃夺取据点。1791年6月，查尔斯·斯科特率领的美国民团焚毁乌亚塔农，韦阿人随后在1795年《格林维尔条约》中和谈。1811年11月7日，威廉·亨利·哈里森在附近的蒂珀卡努摧毁先知镇，瓦解特库姆塞联盟；1818年《圣玛丽斯条约》割让大部分韦阿土地，1820年这支人同意离开沃巴什，迁往密苏里和阿肯色。

en:
In the fifteenth century the rivers at the head of the Maumee were Atchakangouen country. This Miami band, later called the Crane band, planted maize in the bottomlands, hunted beaver and deer in the woods, and kept a short portage from the Maumee to the Little River. That carry linked Lake Erie with the Wabash and the Mississippi. Kekionga, their principal village, stood where the Saint Joseph and Saint Marys join to form the Maumee, on the edge of the Great Black Swamp. In 1444 Europeans had not yet entered the country, and furs, food, and shell ornaments moved along older Miami trade paths.

French missionaries first found Miami bands around western Lake Michigan in the mid-seventeenth century, after the Beaver Wars had driven them west from Indiana. French firearms and trade helped the Atchakangouen return to the Maumee about 1700, and Jean-Baptiste Bissot de Vincennes established a post and fort at Kekionga in 1704. Smallpox emptied the village for a year in 1733. In 1749 the pro-British chief Memeskia, called La Demoiselle, broke away to found Pickawillany; the French rebuilt Fort Miamis in 1752 and their Native allies destroyed the rival town. Kekionga joined Pontiac's rising in 1763, accepting British posts by 1765. In 1780 Little Turtle destroyed Augustin de La Balme's raiders near the village. His Western Confederacy defeated Josiah Harmar in 1790 and Arthur St. Clair in 1791, but Anthony Wayne's victory at Fallen Timbers in 1794 opened the way to Fort Wayne. The Treaty of Greenville in 1795 took the portage, while the Maumee and Saint Mary's treaties of 1817 and 1818 ceded the country around the fort and south of the Wabash to the United States.
zh:
15世纪时，莫米河源头一带的河汊是阿恰坎戈恩人的土地。这个迈阿密支派后来被称为鹤部，在河畔低地种植玉米，在林中猎取河狸与鹿，并控制着从莫米河到利特尔河的短途陆运。这条水陆联运道把伊利湖、沃巴什河与密西西比河连接起来。他们的主要村落凯基翁加位于圣约瑟夫河与圣玛丽斯河汇成莫米河之处，紧邻大黑沼泽边缘。1444年时欧洲人尚未进入此地，毛皮、粮食和贝饰仍沿着迈阿密人更古老的商路往来。

17世纪中叶，法国传教士最初在密歇根湖西岸见到迈阿密诸部；此前海狸战争已把他们从印第安纳驱向西方。约1700年，依靠法国火器与贸易，阿恰坎戈恩人回到莫米河流域，让—巴蒂斯特·比索·德·万塞讷于1704年在凯基翁加设立贸易站和堡垒。1733年，天花使村民撤离村落一年。1749年，亲英的首领梅梅斯基亚（人称拉·德穆瓦泽勒）另立皮卡维兰尼；法国人1752年重建迈阿密堡，其原住民盟友随即摧毁这座竞争村镇。凯基翁加1763年参加庞蒂亚克起义，到1765年接受英国商站。1780年，「小乌龟」在村落附近击溃奥古斯丁·德·拉尔姆的袭击队。他的西部联盟1790年击败乔赛亚·哈马尔、1791年击败阿瑟·圣克莱尔，但安东尼·韦恩1794年在福伦廷伯斯获胜，为韦恩堡打开道路。1795年《格林维尔条约》夺走陆运道，1817年和1818年的《莫米条约》与《圣玛丽斯条约》又把堡垒周围及沃巴什河以南土地割让给美国。

en:
The lower Michigan peninsula stretches between Lake Michigan and Lake Huron, its southern prairies and oak openings cut by rivers running west to the lake. In 1444 this is Algonquian country, and the Bodéwadmi — the Potawatomi, 'keepers of the fire' and youngest brother of the Council of Three Fires with the Ojibwe and Odawa — hold its southwestern reaches, with Mascouten and Miami neighbours beyond. Their bands live in bark-mat lodges, raising maize, beans and squash in river-bottom fields, spearing fish through winter ice, gathering wild rice and maple sugar as the seasons turn, and taking beaver and deer in the woods. Furs and the native trails that cross the peninsula give the land its place in the wider lake world.

French records first mention the Bodéwadmi in southwestern Michigan, but the Beaver Wars drove them west to Green Bay before Iroquois and Neutral raiders; in 1659 the coureurs de bois des Groseilliers and Radisson passed through the upper lakes on their way to Lake Superior. La Salle built Fort Miami at the mouth of the St. Joseph River in November 1679, and after Claude Allouez's mission of the 1680s a permanent Fort St. Joseph rose there in 1691, anchoring the southern Lake Michigan fur trade among Potawatomi and Miami villages. With the Great Peace of 1701 the bands drifted back east: Cadillac founded Detroit that same year, and Potawatomi villages gathered beneath its walls and along the St. Joseph. Faithful allies of France through the colonial wars, they turned on the incoming British garrisons during Pontiac's rising of 1763 and seized Fort St. Joseph, taking every frontier post in the region save Detroit.
zh:
密歇根下半岛伸处于密歇根湖与休伦湖之间，南部草原与橡树林间有一条条向西入湖的河流。1444年，这里是阿尔冈昆人的土地：博德瓦德米人——波塔瓦托米人，意为「守火者」，在与奥吉布瓦人、奥达瓦人结成的「三火议会」中排行幼弟——据有半岛西南部，东北与马斯库滕人、迈阿密人为邻。他们住在树皮席小屋组成的村落，在河畔低地种玉米、豆类和南瓜，冬季凿冰叉鱼，按季节采集野米、熬制枫糖，在林中猎取河狸与鹿。毛皮和纵贯半岛的古道，使这片土地在大湖族群的交往网络中占有一席之地。

法国文献最早提到博德瓦德米人时，他们住在密歇根西南部；河狸战争中，为躲避易洛魁人与中立联盟的攻掠，他们西撤到格林贝一带，1659年德·格罗塞耶与拉迪松即经上游大湖前往苏必利尔湖。1679年11月，拉萨尔在圣约瑟夫河口修筑迈阿密堡；1680年代阿卢埃神父在此传教，1691年永久性的圣约瑟夫堡正式设立，成为密歇根湖南部毛皮贸易的支柱，堡周是波塔瓦托米人与迈阿密人的村庄。1701年《蒙特利尔大和约》后，各部陆续东归；同年卡迪亚克建立底特律，波塔瓦托米人的村庄聚到城墙脚下与圣约瑟夫河畔。在历次殖民地战争中他们始终与法国结盟，1763年趁庞蒂亚克起兵转而攻打新来的英国驻军，攻克圣约瑟夫堡，湖区一带的边疆据点除底特律外尽数落入其手。

en:
Michigami takes its name from the Anishinaabe word for the great lake at its western edge, but this province is the river country behind that shore: forest and oak openings drained west by the Grand River, called Owashtanong by the Odawa and later La Grande Rivière by the French. In 1444 its trails belong to the Anishinaabe lake world, where Bodéwadmi (Potawatomi) bands and Mascouten neighbours move between hunting camps and river-bottom fields. They raise maize, beans and squash, take sturgeon and whitefish, gather wild rice and maple sugar, and trap beaver for a fur trade that still reaches Europeans only through distant Native middlemen.

The Beaver Wars of the mid-seventeenth century scattered the peninsula's villages, and by the late 1600s Odawa bands had settled the Grand River rapids and the later sites of Grand Rapids, Lowell and Lyons. French voyageurs followed the lake-and-river route, yet the valley remained Indigenous fur country long after France ceded Michigan to Britain in 1763 and Britain withdrew from the lower lake posts in 1796. In 1806 Joseph and Madeline La Framboise opened the first trading post in West Michigan near the mouth of the Thornapple; after Joseph was killed that autumn, Madeline, whose mother was Odawa, maintained and expanded the business. By 1810 Chief Noonday's village at the rapids held about 500 Odawa. He fought beside Tecumseh at the Thames in 1813, and in 1821 the Odawa, Ojibwe and Potawatomi signed the Treaty of Chicago, ceding Michigan lands south of the Grand River to the United States.
zh:
密歇加米得名于阿尼什纳比语中对西边大湖的称呼；这个省份写的却是湖岸背后的河乡：林地与橡树草原之间，格兰德河向西汇水入湖。奥达瓦人称它奥瓦什塔农，法国人后来称它「大河」。1444年，这里的陆路属于阿尼什纳比人的大湖世界，波塔瓦托米游群与马斯库滕邻人往来于猎营和河畔田地之间。他们种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，捕捞鲟鱼和白鱼，按季节采集野米、熬制枫糖，并猎捕河狸；此时毛皮还要经过远方的原住民中介，才能抵达欧洲人手中。

17世纪中叶的河狸战争打散了下半岛村落；到17世纪末，奥达瓦游群已在格兰德河急流一带，以及后来大急流城、洛厄尔和莱昂的位置建立村庄。法国船夫沿着湖河航路而来，但即使法国在1763年把密歇根割让给英国、英国又于1796年撤出下游湖堡，河谷仍长期由原住民掌控毛皮贸易。1806年，约瑟夫与马德琳·拉弗朗布瓦兹在山楂河注入格兰德河处附近设立西密歇根最早的贸易站；同年秋天约瑟夫遇害后，母亲为奥达瓦人的马德琳继续经营并扩展生意。到1810年，诺戴酋长在急流边的村庄约有五百名奥达瓦人。1813年，他随特库姆塞参加泰晤士河战役；1821年，奥达瓦人、奥吉布瓦人和波塔瓦托米人签订《芝加哥条约》，把密歇根领地内格兰德河以南的土地割让给美国。

en:
In the fifteenth century Hotaawathipi was the northwestern Ohio country between the Maumee and Sandusky rivers, where oak ridges and prairie islands rose out of the Great Black Swamp and the waters drained north to Lake Erie. Miami-speaking bands used the higher ground for camps and maize fields, taking fish, waterfowl, beaver and deer from marsh and forest. River trails linked them with Kekionga to the west, Lake Erie to the north, and Shawnee country farther south. In 1444 no European fort or mission stood there; the region remained an Indigenous world of village councils, hunting grounds and old exchange paths.

During the Beaver Wars, Iroquois raiding turned much of the Ohio Country into a contested fur ground, and Miami bands returned only with French support around 1700. In 1738 a Wyandot band from Detroit moved to Sandusky Bay; Nicholas Orontony's followers founded Junundat about 1740 and welcomed British traders. The English post built there in 1745 was the first European fort in the Ohio Country, but it and the village were soon abandoned. Reoccupied in the 1750s, the Sandusky towns sided with France in the French and Indian War and rose with Pontiac in May 1763, when Wyandots seized Fort Sandusky. The village was burned in reprisal and the people moved up the Sandusky River. Upper Sandusky became their principal town, and Native delegates met there in September 1783 to organize the confederacy that fought the Northwest Indian War. Anthony Wayne's victory at Fallen Timbers in 1794 and the Treaty of Greenville in 1795 opened the country to American forts and settlement, while the Treaty of Fort Meigs in 1817 confined the Wyandot to a reservation around Upper Sandusky.
zh:
15世纪时，霍塔瓦西皮是俄亥俄西北部莫米河与桑达斯基河之间的土地，橡树林高岗和草原岛屿从大黑沼泽中隆起，河水向北注入伊利湖。操迈阿密语的群体在较高处设立营地、种植玉米，从沼泽与森林中获取鱼、水禽、河狸和鹿。河路把他们同西边的凯基翁加、北边的伊利湖以及更南方的肖尼人地区连接起来。1444年时这里还没有欧洲人的堡垒或传教站，仍是村落议事会、猎场和古老交换道路构成的原住民世界。

河狸战争期间，易洛魁人的袭掠使俄亥俄地区大部分成为各方争夺的毛皮猎场，迈阿密诸部直到约1700年才在法国支持下返回。1738年，一支怀安多特人从底特律迁往桑达斯基湾；尼古拉·奥龙托尼的追随者约1740年建立Junundat村，并接纳英国商人。英国人1745年在那里设立的商站是俄亥俄地区第一座欧洲人堡垒，但商站和村落不久都被放弃。18世纪50年代村落重新有人居住，桑达斯基诸镇在法国—印第安人战争中支持法国，又在1763年5月随庞蒂亚克起事，怀安多特人袭取桑达斯基堡。村落随后被报复焚毁，居民沿桑达斯基河上迁。上桑达斯基成为他们的主要村镇，1783年9月，原住民代表在那里集会，筹组后来投身西北印第安战争的联盟。安东尼·韦恩1794年在福伦廷伯斯获胜，1795年《格林维尔条约》为美国堡垒和定居者打开这一地区；1817年《梅格斯堡条约》又把怀安多特人限制在上桑达斯基周围的保留地内。

en:
Kentaientonga was the western Erie country around Presque Isle Bay, where a sandy peninsula almost enclosed one of the finest anchorages on Lake Erie. These Iroquoian villagers, whom French sources would call the Cat Nation, lived in palisaded towns and raised maize, beans and squash on the Erie Plain, while hunting deer and beaver in the woods behind the shore. Trails ran south from the bay toward the Allegheny portages and the Ohio headwaters. In 1444 Europeans had not seen the peninsula, and the fur rivalries of the next century still lay ahead.

War with the Haudenosaunee began in 1653; in 1654 about 1,800 Iroquois warriors destroyed Rique, the largest Erie town near modern Erie, and by 1656 the Erie had ceased to be a separate people, most survivors being adopted into Seneca communities. French soldiers returned to the shore in summer 1753, building Fort Presque Isle at the northern end of the Venango Path, the first post in their Ohio Country chain. They burned it after losing Fort Niagara in 1759; the British rebuilt it, only to lose it on 19 June 1763, when about 250 Ottawas, Ojibwas, Wyandots and Senecas overwhelmed the garrison during Pontiac's War. Pennsylvania bought the Erie Triangle in 1792, Americans laid out Erie and built a new blockhouse in 1795, and in 1813 Oliver Hazard Perry used the sheltered bay to prepare the squadron that won the Battle of Lake Erie.
zh:
肯泰恩通加是普雷斯克岛湾周围的伊利人西部土地，沙质半岛几乎围住伊利湖上最好的锚地之一。这些说易洛魁语的村民后来被法国文献称为「猫族」，住在栅栏村镇中，在伊利平原种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，也在湖岸后方林地猎鹿与河狸。小径从湖湾南通向阿勒格尼水陆联运道和俄亥俄河源。1444年时欧洲人尚未见过这座半岛，下一个世纪的毛皮争夺也还未到来。

与豪德诺索尼的战争始于1653年；1654年，约一千八百名易洛魁战士摧毁了今伊利附近最大的伊利人村镇Rique，到1656年伊利人已不再是独立族群，多数幸存者被塞内卡社群接纳。1753年夏，法军回到这片湖岸，在韦南戈通道北端修建普雷斯克岛堡，这是他们俄亥俄堡垒链的第一座据点。1759年失去尼亚加拉堡后，法军烧毁该堡；英军将其重建，却又在1763年6月19日失去它，庞蒂亚克战争中约二百五十名渥太华、奥吉布瓦、怀安多特和塞内卡战士围攻堡垒，守军出降后大多被杀。宾夕法尼亚1792年购得伊利三角地，美国人1795年规划伊利镇并修建新木堡；1813年，奥利弗·哈泽德·佩里利用这个受庇护的湖湾装备舰队，最终赢得伊利湖战役。

en:
Ohiyo names the upper Ohio's passage through wooded hills where western Pennsylvania gives way to the Virginia frontier. In 1444 this was late Fort Ancient country, a river world that historical memory would connect with the Shawnee. Bark-covered villages and maize fields occupied fertile bottoms; canoes carried shell, tobacco, furs and people between the Mississippi system and trails climbing toward the Alleghenies, while hunters took deer and turkey in the hills. No European had yet mapped the river that the Seneca would call Ohi:yo', the Good River.

Virginian parties brought back the first reports of the valley in the trans-Appalachian expeditions of 1671 and 1673–74, and Arnout Viele traveled from the Allegheny to Shawnee towns on the Ohio in 1692–93. Gaspard-Joseph Chaussegros de Léry made the first French river survey in 1729; in 1749 Céloron de Blainville buried a lead plate at Wheeling Creek to proclaim France's claim. After Britain won the Ohio Country, the 1768 Treaty of Fort Stanwix made the Ohio the southern boundary of Native territory, but Virginia frontiersmen kept crossing. Ebenezer Zane settled the Wheeling bottom in 1769, and Fort Fincastle, soon renamed Fort Henry, was built in June 1774 during Dunmore's War. Shawnee, Wyandot and Mingo fighters besieged it in 1777 and returned with British support in 1782, when Betty Zane carried powder from her family's blockhouse to save the garrison. The river became the Northwest Territory's southern edge in 1787, and in 1818 the National Road reached Wheeling, tying the Ohio landing to the Potomac.
zh:
俄亥俄（Ohiyo）指上俄亥俄河穿过林木丘陵的一段，即西宾夕法尼亚转入弗吉尼亚边疆之地。1444年，这里属于晚期堡古文化圈，是历史记忆常与肖尼人联系起来的河上世界。树皮屋村落和玉米地占据肥沃河洲，独木舟转运贝壳、烟草、毛皮和人员，把密西西比水系与通向阿勒格尼山脉的小路连接起来，猎人则在丘陵间猎鹿与火鸡。欧洲人尚未测绘这条后来被塞内卡人称为Ohi:yo'（「好河」）的大河。

弗吉尼亚探险队在1671年、1673年至1674年的跨阿巴拉契亚行动中最早传回河谷消息；1692年至1693年，阿尔瑙特·维勒从阿勒格尼河进入俄亥俄河畔的肖尼村镇。加斯帕尔—约瑟夫·肖斯格罗·德·莱里1729年完成法国人的首次河道测绘；1749年，塞洛隆·德·布兰维尔在惠灵溪口埋下铅牌，宣告法国的领属。英国赢得俄亥俄地区后，1768年《斯坦威克斯堡条约》把俄亥俄河定为原住民领地南界，但弗吉尼亚边疆居民仍不断渡河。埃比尼泽·赞恩1769年在惠灵河洲定居；1774年6月邓莫尔战争期间，芬卡斯尔堡建成，不久改名亨利堡。肖尼、怀安多特和明戈战士1777年围攻此堡，1782年又与英军一道再来；贝蒂·赞恩从家族木屋取回火药，使守军支撑下来。1787年，俄亥俄河成为西北领地南界；1818年国家公路通到惠灵，把这个河港与波托马克河连接起来。

en:
The Monacan country is the rolling Virginia piedmont between the falls of the James River and the Blue Ridge Mountains. Its Siouan-speaking people planted corn and beans on the river bottoms, handled the copper that moved along the upland trails, and raised earthen burial mounds above their towns. Their capital Rassawek stood where the Rivanna joins the James, while Mowhemencho guarded the eastern approaches above the falls. Beyond the falls the Algonquian Powhatan were their sworn enemies, and the Monacan held the upland with their kinsmen and allies the Manahoac. In 1444 no European had yet entered their country.

In November 1608 Christopher Newport led forty Jamestown men up the James to the towns of Massinacak and Mowhemencho and carried off a headman to guide them. John Lederer, visiting the same two towns in 1670, found a nation of only about thirty bowmen, already carrying muskets. Their leader Surenough signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation in 1677 after Bacon's Rebellion, and by 1702 the last Monacan had drifted away; Virginia granted their old fields to Huguenot refugees, who founded Manakin town from 1700. The survivors merged with the Nahyssan and Saponi, and as Tutelo-Saponi they were adopted by the Cayuga of the Iroquois in 1753. In 1784 Thomas Jefferson excavated one of their ancient burial mounds on the Rivanna and described it in his Notes on the State of Virginia.
zh:
莫纳坎人的家园在詹姆斯河瀑布线与蓝岭山脉之间起伏的弗吉尼亚皮德蒙特丘陵。这支操苏语的部族在河滩种植玉米和豆类，经营沿山麓小路流通的铜料，并在村镇旁堆起泥土坟丘。首镇拉萨韦克坐落在里瓦纳河汇入詹姆斯河之处，莫赫门乔则扼守瀑布上游的东部门户。瀑布以东说阿尔冈昆语的波瓦坦联盟是世仇，莫纳坎人与北方的亲族盟友马纳霍克人共守这片山地。1444年，还没有任何欧洲人踏入他们的土地。

1608年11月，克里斯托弗·纽波特率领四十名詹姆斯敦移民溯詹姆斯河而上，到达马西纳卡克和莫赫门乔两镇，并掳走一名头人充当向导。1670年约翰·莱德勒重访这两镇时，发现整个部族只剩约三十名弓箭手，而且已经持有火枪。首领萨雷诺夫在1677年培根叛乱后签署了《中种植园条约》，到1702年最后的莫纳坎人已离散而去；弗吉尼亚殖民当局把他们的旧地拨给胡格诺派难民，后者自1700年起建起马金镇。幸存者并入纳赫桑人与萨波尼人，以「图特洛－萨波尼」之名在1753年被易洛魁联盟的卡尤加人接纳。1784年，托马斯·杰斐逊在里瓦纳河畔发掘了他们的一座古坟丘，并写入《弗吉尼亚纪事》。

en:
The Chesepian, whose Algonquian name meant 'the country on a great river', lived where the Elizabeth River meets the Chesapeake Bay, in what is now southern Hampton Roads. Their Late Woodland culture rested on the bay's fish and oysters, with cornfields beyond the marshes, and their town of Skicoak was described to early English visitors as the greatest settlement of the region. In 1444 no European sail had entered the bay, and the Chesepian lived independently, outside the chiefdoms taking shape on the James River.

Philip Amadas, exploring the bay from Roanoke in the winter of 1585-86, found Skicoak a plainer place than native report had promised. Before the English founded Jamestown in 1607, Powhatan destroyed the tribe after his priests warned that a nation rising from the Chesapeake would dissolve his empire; perhaps 350 Chesepian remained in 1607, possibly joined by survivors of the Lost Colony, and by 1669 they existed no longer as a tribe. Planters bought the Elizabeth River shore for tobacco, the House of Burgesses established Norfolk town in 1680, and it was incorporated in 1705. The Battle of Great Bridge in December 1775 drove Governor Dunmore out of the district; his fleet bombarded Norfolk on 1 January 1776, and two weeks later the patriots burned the remaining houses, leaving only the walls of St Paul's Church.
zh:
切萨皮克人的阿尔冈昆语族名意为「大河之畔的地方」，他们住在伊丽莎白河注入切萨皮克湾之处，即今汉普顿锚地南部。他们的晚期林地文化以湾中的鱼蚝为生，沼泽之外广种玉米；村镇斯基科阿克曾被邻人形容为这一带最大的城邑。1444年，欧洲船帆尚未进入海湾，切萨皮克人自成一方，不在詹姆斯河流域正在成形的酋长联盟之内。

1585至1586年冬，菲利普·阿马达斯从罗阿诺克北上探湾，发现斯基科阿克其实远比传闻中平常。1607年英国人建立詹姆斯敦之前，波瓦坦因祭司警告「切萨皮克湾将兴起一个瓦解其帝国的民族」，发兵灭掉了该部；1607年切萨皮克人仅剩约三百五十人，其中或许还收留了「失落殖民地」的幸存者，到1669年他们已不再作为部落存在。种植园主为种植烟草买下伊丽莎白河岸，弗吉尼亚议会1680年设立诺福克镇，1705年建市。1775年12月的大桥战役把总督邓莫尔逐出此地；1776年1月1日他的舰队炮轰诺福克，两周后爱国者又焚毁残存屋舍，唯有圣保罗教堂的四壁留存。

en:
The Kanawha is formed by the confluence of the New and Gauley rivers and winds about 97 miles northwest through the wooded Allegheny Plateau to the Ohio. Early hunters left fluted points in its valley, Adena communities raised earthen mounds there, and later Fort Ancient farmers occupied bottomland villages including Buffalo and Marmet. In 1444 the river was still a Native corridor of fields, hunting camps and canoe travel, far beyond the recorded knowledge of Europeans.

During the seventeenth century, Haudenosaunee raids from what is now New York dispersed or subjugated Fort Ancient, Wyandot and Conoy-Kanawha communities, and the Haudenosaunee, Lenape and Shawnee came to use the valley chiefly as a hunting ground. In 1671 Abraham Wood sent the Batts and Fallam party into the upper watershed, the first recorded English exploration of the New River. Virginia surveyors were already marking tracts along the Coal River in April 1774, and on 10 October that year Andrew Lewis's militia met Cornstalk's Shawnee and Mingo warriors at the Kanawha's mouth in the Battle of Point Pleasant. Cornstalk withdrew after a hard-fought day, and late-eighteenth-century Virginia land grants near the mouth brought permanent settlement up the valley.
zh:
卡诺瓦河由纽河与高利河汇流而成，在林木覆盖的阿勒格尼高原间向西北蜿蜒约97英里，最终注入俄亥俄河。远古猎人曾在河谷留下克洛维斯尖状器，阿德纳文化社群在此堆筑土墩，后来的古堡文化农民则居住在布法罗、马梅特等河漫滩村落。1444年时，这条河仍是原住民往来耕作、狩猎和乘独木舟穿行的通道，完全不为欧洲人所知。

17世纪，来自今纽约一带的易洛魁军队侵袭并驱散或征服了古堡文化、休伦和科诺伊—卡诺瓦社群，此后易洛魁、莱纳佩与肖尼人主要把这片河谷用作猎场。1671年，亚伯拉罕·伍德派出巴茨和法伦姆小队进入上游流域，这是英文资料中对纽河最早的探险记录。1774年4月，弗吉尼亚测量员已在科尔河沿岸划分土地；同年10月10日，安德鲁·刘易斯率领的民兵在卡诺瓦河口与科恩斯托克率领的肖尼、明戈战士交战，史称波因特普莱森特战役。科恩斯托克在激战后撤退，18世纪末弗吉尼亚在河口附近授地，永久定居点随即沿河谷发展起来。

en:
The broad tidewater peninsulas between the James, York and Rappahannock are Tsenacommacah, the thickly settled country of the Virginia Algonquians. Bark-covered longhouse towns stood beside maize fields renewed by the river floods, and dugout canoes carried fish, oysters and surplus corn through the Chesapeake's inlets; each town obeyed its own weroance or weroansqua. One upstream town at the falls of the James was called Powhatan, a name the English would later give both to its people and to the chief who ruled them. In 1444 these were independent, rivalrous villages, with no sign yet of the paramountcy built in the late 1500s, and no European had yet settled the bay.

That empire was the work of Wahunsenacawh, who inherited six tribes and by 1607 held more than thirty between the bay and the falls, ruling from Werowocomoco on the York over some 14,000 to 21,000 people. In 1607 the English built Jamestown on his doorstep, and after parleys and corn trade their hunger for tobacco land brought fourteen years of war. John Smith, captured on the Chickahominy in December 1607, was carried before the mamanatowick in the episode his memoirs later tied to Pocahontas. Wahunsenacawh died in 1618, and in March 1622 his brother Opechancanough's warriors fell on the outlying plantations, killing hundreds of settlers; the reprisals destroyed half the confederacy's towns. His last rising, in 1644, ended in 1646 when the aged chief was captured and shot by his guard; the treaty of that year dissolved the confederacy and confined the survivors beyond the York and Blackwater, on some of Virginia's first reservations. A law of 1665 made their chiefs appointees of the governor, and the Treaty of Albany in 1684 marked the confederacy's end. By 1821 only the Pamunkey and Mattaponi still held reservation lands first set aside in the 1600s.
zh:
詹姆斯河、约克河与拉帕汉诺克河之间开阔的潮汐水半岛，是弗吉尼亚阿冈昆人村落密布的家园塞纳科马卡。覆以树皮的长屋城镇旁是借河水泛滥保持肥力的玉米地，独木舟载着鱼、牡蛎和余粮穿行于切萨皮克湾的水汊之间；每座城镇各有自己的首领，男称维罗安斯，女称维罗安斯夸。詹姆斯河瀑布附近一座上游城镇名叫波瓦坦，后来英国人把这个名字同时给了它的居民和统治他们的大酋长。1444年的这些村落彼此独立、时有纷争，16世纪末才建立的最高酋邦此时尚无踪影，海湾边也还没有欧洲人落脚。

这个酋邦是瓦洪苏纳科一手缔造的：他从母亲手中继承六个部落，到1607年已统辖海湾与瀑布线之间的三十多个部族，以约克河畔的韦罗沃科莫科为都，治下约有14,000至21,000人。1607年，英国人就在他眼皮底下建起詹姆斯敦，几番交涉和玉米交易之后，对烟草种植用地的贪欲引发了长达十四年的战争。约翰·史密斯1607年12月在奇克哈莫尼河畔被俘，被带到大酋长面前——他后来在回忆录里把这段经历与宝嘉康蒂联系在一起。瓦洪苏纳科1618年去世；1622年3月，其弟奥普查纳卡诺的战士突袭外围种植园，杀死数百名殖民者，报复行动又摧毁了联盟半数城镇。1644年他发动最后一次起义，1646年这位年迈酋长被俘，遭看守士兵枪杀；同年的条约解散了联盟，幸存者被限制在约克河与布莱克沃特河之外，住进弗吉尼亚最早的一批保留地。1665年的法律规定各部首领改由总督任命，1684年的奥尔巴尼条约标志着联盟彻底终结。到1821年，只剩帕蒙基人和马塔波尼人仍守着17世纪划出的保留地。

en:
Piscataway is the lower Potomac country of southern Maryland, where tidal creeks and marshes meet the western shore of Chesapeake Bay. Its Algonquian-speaking people raised maize, beans, and squash in the river bottoms, fished the shallows, and drew together under hereditary chiefs as pressure from the Susquehannock and other northern peoples increased. The tayac's principal town was Moyaone, on Accokeek Creek above the Potomac. Neighbouring Iroquoians called these people Conoy. In 1444 the Piscataway still controlled the creek mouths, fields, and canoe routes that later colonizers called Piscataway land.

John Smith visited the upper Potomac in 1608 and recorded the people as Moyaons, after their ruler's town. On 25 March 1634 the English ships Ark and Dove reached St Clement's Island; Leonard Calvert's settlers bought ground from the Yaocomico and founded St Mary's, beginning the Catholic Calvert family's Maryland colony. English friendship soon became land pressure: by 1668 western-shore Algonquian communities were confined to two reservations, and after 1680 Piscataway families took shelter at Zekiah Swamp, crossed into Virginia in 1697, and lived on Conoy Island in the Potomac from 1699. During the eighteenth century Maryland extinguished the remaining reservations as tobacco plantations spread along the river.
zh:
皮斯卡塔韦位于马里兰南部的波托马克河下游，感潮河溪与沼泽在此通向切萨皮克湾西岸。说阿尔冈昆语的居民在河滨低地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在浅水捕鱼；随着萨斯奎汉诺克人和北方其他群体压力增大，各村落逐渐团结在世袭首领之下。最高首领塔亚克的主要城镇莫亚翁位于波托马克河畔的阿科基克溪。邻近的易洛魁语族群称他们为科诺伊。1444年时，皮斯卡塔韦人仍控制着后来被殖民者称作皮斯卡塔韦之地的河口、田地和独木舟水路。

约翰·史密斯1608年进入波托马克河上游，根据其首领城镇把这些人记为莫亚翁人。1634年3月25日，英国船只「方舟号」和「鸽子号」抵达圣克莱门特岛；伦纳德·卡尔弗特率领的移民从约科米科人手中购地，建立圣玛丽斯，开启卡尔弗特家族信奉天主教的马里兰殖民地。英国式友谊很快变成土地压力：到1668年，西岸阿尔冈昆社群已被限制在两块保留地内；1680年后，皮斯卡塔韦家族避入泽基亚沼泽，1697年渡波托马克河进入弗吉尼亚，1699年起居住在河中的科诺伊岛。18世纪，随着烟草种植园沿河扩展，马里兰取消了剩余保留地。

en:
The upper Allegheny and French Creek wind through a wooded plateau that formed the southern country of the Erielhonan, the Erie, whom the French called the Cat Nation. These Iroquoian villagers farmed maize, beans and squash around palisaded towns while hunting beaver and deer in the creek bottoms; trails and short portages linked their watershed to Lake Erie. In 1444 Europeans had not entered the valleys, and Erie communities still controlled the furs, crossings and hunting grounds between the lake plain and the Ohio headwaters.

Epidemics and the competition for beaver pelts drew the Erie into the Beaver Wars, and by the mid-1650s they had ceased to be an independent polity; survivors were absorbed into Haudenosaunee communities, after which Shawnee and Iroquois parties contested the Allegheny valley. In 1753 the French occupied Scottish trader John Fraser's post at Venango, a Lenape town at the mouth of French Creek, and secured the Venango route from Lake Erie. Fort Le Boeuf guarded the portage when George Washington reached it that December with Virginia's demand for withdrawal, and Fort Machault was built at Venango in 1754. The French burned both posts in August 1759 after losing Fort Niagara. The British rebuilt the Venango post as Fort Venango in 1760, but it was burned during Pontiac's Rebellion in 1763.
zh:
上阿勒格尼河与弗伦奇溪蜿蜒穿过林木覆盖的高原，这里是伊利霍南人，即伊利人的南部土地，法国人称他们为「猫族」。这些说易洛魁语的村民在栅栏村镇周围种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，也在溪谷猎取河狸与鹿；小径和短途水陆联运把他们的流域与伊利湖连接起来。1444年时，欧洲人尚未进入这些河谷，伊利人仍控制着湖滨平原与俄亥俄河源之间的毛皮、渡口和猎场。

流行病与河狸皮竞争把伊利人卷入海狸战争，到1650年代中期，他们已不再是独立政治实体；幸存者多被豪德诺索尼（即易洛魁）社群吸收，此后肖尼人与易洛魁人又反复争夺阿勒格尼河谷。1753年，法军占领苏格兰商人约翰·弗雷泽在弗伦奇河口莱纳佩村镇韦南戈的商栈，控制了从伊利湖南下的韦南戈通道。同年12月乔治·华盛顿抵达守卫水陆联运线的勒伯夫堡，递交弗吉尼亚要求法军撤退的信函；马绍尔堡则于1754年在韦南戈建成。1759年8月，法军在失去尼亚加拉堡后烧毁两座要塞。英军1760年将韦南戈据点重建为韦南戈堡，但它又在1763年庞蒂亚克战争中被焚毁。

en:
Conestoga is the Susquehanna lowland around the later Conestoga River, where wooded ridges open into fertile flats above Chesapeake Bay. In 1444 this was Susquehannock country in the broad sense, although the Iroquoian-speaking people then lived chiefly in palisaded hamlets on the North Branch, in present northern Pennsylvania and southern New York. Their longhouse communities raised corn, beans and squash, fished the river and used canoe routes through the valley; the southward move that brought fortified towns to the lower Susquehanna came during the next century.

John Smith met Susquehannock warriors near the river mouth in 1608 and described fortified towns able to send out hundreds of men. From the 1620s the Susquehannock exchanged beaver pelts for cloth, kettles, axes and, by the 1630s, muskets with Virginian, Dutch and Swedish traders. War with Maryland ended only with a treaty in 1652. Disease and raids then broke their power: after abandoning their Susquehanna town in the 1670s, they suffered a Maryland and Virginia siege in 1675 and the survivors scattered or joined the Iroquois. A remnant returned with Seneca families in the late 1680s and founded Conestoga Town. William Penn's government treated with them in 1701, and Conestoga Manor was surveyed for their use in 1718, but settler encroachment reduced both land and people. By December 1763 only twenty Conestoga remained; Paxton Boys vigilantes killed six at their village on 14 December and slaughtered the fourteen sheltered in Lancaster on 27 December. Settler farms and a small village laid out as Conestoga Centre in 1805 later took their place along the river.
zh:
科内斯托加是萨斯奎哈纳河下游低地，位于后来的科内斯托加河一带，林木覆被的山脊在此展成切萨皮克湾上方的肥沃平地。1444年，广义上这里属于萨斯奎汉诺克人的地域，但这些操易洛魁语的人当时主要住在北支沿岸设有栅栏的村落，也就是今宾州北部与纽约州南部一带。他们的长屋社群种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在河中捕鱼，并利用河谷独木舟路线往来；要到下一个世纪，他们才南迁并在萨斯奎哈纳河下游建立设防城镇。

1608年，约翰·史密斯在河口附近见到萨斯奎汉诺克战士，并记载他们的设防城镇能出动数百人。1620年代起，萨斯奎汉诺克人用河狸皮同弗吉尼亚、荷兰和瑞典商人交换布匹、铜锅、斧头，并在1630年代开始换得火枪。他们与马里兰的战争直到1652年缔约才告结束。随后疫病和突袭削弱了他们的力量：1670年代放弃萨斯奎哈纳河畔城镇后，他们又在1675年遭到马里兰与弗吉尼亚民兵围攻，幸存者四散，或加入易洛魁人。1680年代末，一批遗民同塞内卡家庭返回，建立科内斯托加镇。威廉·佩恩政府于1701年同他们缔约，1718年又勘定供他们使用的科内斯托加庄园，但移民侵夺使土地和人口不断缩减。到1763年12月，科内斯托加人只剩二十名；帕克斯顿帮治安队员于12月14日在村里杀死六人，又于12月27日在兰开斯特杀害受庇护的十四人。此后，移民农场和1805年规划的小村科内斯托加森特沿河岸取代了旧聚落。

en:
Sakimauchheening is the Lenape council ground later written Shackamaxon, on the west bank of the Delaware, called Lënapei Sipu, near its meeting with the Schuylkill. Lenape villages lined the deep river, fished its estuary and used the Great Minquas Path to carry furs toward Susquehannock country; canoes could come up from Delaware Bay to the chiefs' meeting place. In 1444 the councils, crossings and fur traffic at the future Philadelphia riverside remained entirely in Lenape hands, with no European claim on the valley.

Henry Hudson entered the Delaware valley in 1609, and the Dutch later built Fort Beversreede near the Schuylkill mouth to guard the fur route. New Sweden was founded on the lower Delaware in 1638 and contested the trade until Peter Stuyvesant conquered it in 1655; England took the river from the Dutch in 1664. In 1682 Tamanend met William Penn at Shackamaxon to make peace, and Penn laid out Philadelphia between the Delaware and Schuylkill as the capital of his Quaker colony. Its wharves made it a leading colonial port, while the Walking Purchase of 1737 displaced Lenape communities up the Delaware as settlement spread. Independence was declared at Philadelphia on 4 July 1776. After winning at Brandywine on 11 September 1777, William Howe's army entered the city on 26 September and wintered there while Washington's army suffered at Valley Forge; the British evacuated in 1778. The United States Constitution was drafted here in 1787, and Philadelphia served as the republic's temporary capital from 1790 to 1800.
zh:
萨基毛切宁是莱纳佩酋长议事地，殖民者后来写作沙卡马克逊，位于莱纳佩语称作莱纳佩西普的特拉华河与斯库尔基尔河汇流一带。莱纳佩村落依深水河岸而居，在河口捕鱼，并沿大米因夸斯小道把毛皮运往萨斯奎汉诺克人的地方；独木舟可从特拉华湾直达酋长会盟之地。1444年，后来费城所在河岸的议事会、渡口和毛皮贸易仍完全掌握在莱纳佩人手中，欧洲人尚未对河谷提出任何主权要求。

1609年，亨利·哈德孙驶入特拉华河谷，荷兰人后来在斯库尔基尔河口附近修建贝弗斯雷德堡，守护毛皮商路。1638年，瑞典在下游特拉华河畔建立新瑞典并争夺贸易，直到1655年被彼得·施托伊弗桑特征服，英格兰又于1664年从荷兰手中夺取这条河。1682年，塔曼恩德在沙卡马克逊与威廉·佩恩缔和，佩恩随后在特拉华河与斯库尔基尔河之间规划费城，作为贵格会殖民地的首府。码头使费城成为殖民地大港，1737年的《步行购地》又迫使特拉华河上游的莱纳佩社群迁离，英裔定居点随之扩展。1776年7月4日，《独立宣言》在费城通过。1777年9月11日布兰迪万战役获胜后，威廉·豪所部于9月26日入城并在此过冬，华盛顿的军队则在福吉谷苦守；英军于1778年撤离。1787年，美国宪法在这里起草，1790年至1800年费城又成为共和国的临时首都。

en:
The low western shore of Delaware Bay, from the sand-spit of Cape Henlopen to the falls above the future Wilmington, was Unami Lenape country when our period opens. Bands of the Turtle, Turkey and Wolf clans kept villages along the bay and the Christina and Brandywine creeks, raising maize, beans and squash on the coastal plain, netting fish in the shallows and hunting inland, while their Algonquian kin the Nanticoke held the creeks farther south. They called the broad river Lenapewihittuk, and in 1444 no European had yet entered its bay.

Henry Hudson's Half Moon nosed into the bay in 1609. In 1631 the Dutch planted Zwaanendael near Cape Henlopen, the first European settlement in what is now Delaware, and within a year all thirty-two settlers were killed in a quarrel over a Dutch West India Company signboard. Peter Minuit founded New Sweden at Fort Christina in 1638; Peter Stuyvesant built Fort Casimir at New Castle in 1651 and overran the Swedes in 1655, only for an English fleet to take the bay in 1664. In 1682 the Duke of York granted these 'Lower Counties on the Delaware' to William Penn, and from 1704 they kept their own assembly at New Castle. Caesar Rodney's midnight ride to Philadelphia carried Delaware's vote for independence in July 1776, and the skirmish at Cooch's Bridge in 1777 was the only fighting on Delaware soil. On 7 December 1787 Delaware became the first state to ratify the federal Constitution.
zh:
特拉华湾西岸的低地，从亨洛彭角的沙嘴到日后威明顿以北的瀑布线，在本时期开始时是乌纳米特拉华人的土地。龟氏、火鸡氏和狼氏氏族的群体在湾岸及克里斯蒂娜溪、布兰迪万溪畔建立村落，在沿海平原种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在浅滩捕鱼、入内陆狩猎；更南边的河湾则属于他们阿尔冈昆语的亲族南蒂科克人。他们把这条宽阔的大河称为莱纳佩希图克，1444年时还没有欧洲人进入过这片海湾。

1609年，亨利·哈得孙的「半月号」探入湾中。1631年，荷兰人在亨洛彭角附近建立兹瓦南代尔——今特拉华境内第一个欧洲人定居点，不出一年，因一面荷兰西印度公司徽章招牌引起的冲突，三十二名殖民者全数被杀。1638年，彼得·米纽伊特在克里斯蒂娜堡建起新瑞典；1651年彼得·施托伊弗桑特在纽卡斯尔修筑卡西米尔堡，1655年攻灭瑞典殖民地，而1664年一支英国舰队又夺取了海湾。1682年，约克公爵把这片「特拉华下游三县」授予威廉·佩恩，1704年起三县在纽卡斯尔自开议会。1776年7月，西泽·罗德尼星夜驰赴费城，为特拉华投下赞成独立的一票；1777年的库奇桥前哨战是这片土地上唯一的战斗。1787年12月7日，特拉华成为第一个批准联邦宪法的州。

en:
Onodowaga, the Seneca name for the Great Hill People, belonged to the westernmost Iroquoian nation south of Lake Ontario. In 1444 its palisaded towns stood between the Genesee River and Canandaigua Lake, with longhouses set among fields of corn, beans and squash and hunting camps reaching toward the Allegheny. The rivers and the Seneca Trail linked the villages to fur-bearing forests and western raiding paths, making this country the western doorway of the Iroquoian world long before Europeans saw it.

Dutch and later English trade drew the Seneca deeper into the Beaver Wars, and captives taken in mourning raids replaced relatives lost after a smallpox epidemic in 1635. Ganondagan, their principal town, had about 150 longhouses when English visitors reached it in 1677; Jesuits had opened the mission of St. Jacques there in 1668, but rising tension with New France forced them out in 1684. In July 1687 the Marquis de Denonville's French and allied army marched from Irondequoit, burned Seneca towns and destroyed their stores. Most Seneca fought for Britain during the American Revolution, and in 1779 John Sullivan's scorched-earth campaign drove thousands of Haudenosaunee toward Fort Niagara. The 1784 Treaty of Fort Stanwix opened the old country to cession; the Seneca sold lands east of the Genesee in 1788, received peace guarantees in the 1794 Treaty of Canandaigua, and in 1797 sold their western New York lands while retaining reservations.
zh:
Onodowaga是塞尼卡人的自称，意为「大丘之人」；他们是安大略湖以南位置最西的易洛魁语族群。1444年，塞尼卡人的栅栏村镇分布在杰纳西河与卡南代瓜湖之间，长屋周围种着玉米、菜豆和南瓜，狩猎营地一直延伸向阿勒格尼方向。河流与塞尼卡小径把各村镇同产毛皮的森林、西侧的征战道路连接起来，使这片土地在欧洲人到来很久以前就是易洛魁世界的西部门户。

与荷兰人、后来的英国人通商后，塞尼卡人更深地卷入海狸战争；1635年天花疫后，他们以「哀悼战争」中掳来的俘虏补入失去的族人。塞尼卡首要村镇加农达甘在1677年已有约一百五十座长屋。耶稣会士1668年在那里建立圣雅克传教站，但与新法兰西的紧张关系在1684年迫使传教士离开。1687年7月，德农维尔侯爵率领法军及原住民盟军从伊龙德夸湾进军，焚毁塞尼卡村镇并破坏储粮。美国独立战争中，多数塞尼卡人站在英国一方；1779年，约翰·沙利文的焦土远征把数千名豪德诺索尼人逼向尼亚加拉堡。1784年的斯坦威克斯堡条约开启了故土割让，塞尼卡人1788年出售杰纳西河以东土地，1794年通过《卡南代瓜条约》获得和平保障，又在1797年出售纽约西部土地，只保留若干保留地。

en:
Gayogohono, the People of the Great Swamp, was the Cayuga country around Cayuga Lake in the Finger Lakes, between Onondaga to the east and Seneca to the west. In 1444 elm-bark longhouses stood beside fields of corn, beans and squash, while the long lake carried canoes through fishing waters rich in salmon and eels. Marshland, oak plains and deer herds gave the towns their name and their food; forest trails linked them to neighboring Iroquoian nations and to the fur country south of the lakes.

In 1656 Cayuga chief Saonchiogwa invited Jesuits Joseph Chaumonot and René Ménard from Onondaga, and their mission of St. Joseph was founded near Goiogouen, the village later called Cayuga Castle. Étienne de Carheil and Pierre Raffeix later served there; in 1671 Raffeix described the plains between the lakes as rich in fish, deer and salt springs. In 1753 the Cayuga took in Tutelo and Saponi refugees, who built Coreorgonel near the southern inlet of Cayuga Lake. During the American Revolution Cayuga allegiances were divided, though most bands who went to war joined the British frontier raids. Sullivan and Clinton's 1779 campaign destroyed Goiogouen on 23 September with its fifteen large longhouses and cornfields, burned Chonodote the next day, and also destroyed Coreorgonel. Survivors fled to other Haudenosaunee towns, the Seneca country or Upper Canada; on 11 November 1794 the Cayuga joined the Treaty of Canandaigua, which recognized Haudenosaunee sovereignty even after the loss of most of the lake country.
zh:
Gayogohono意为「大沼泽之人」，是卡尤加人在五指湖之一卡尤加湖周围的乡土，东接奥农多加，西连塞尼卡。1444年，榆树皮覆盖的长屋坐落于玉米、菜豆和南瓜田边；狭长的湖泊让独木舟穿行于盛产鲑鱼、鳗鲡的渔场之间。沼泽、橡树林平原和鹿群既解释了族名，也供养着村镇；林间小路把卡尤加人同邻近易洛魁族群、湖泊以南的毛皮产地连接起来。

1656年，卡尤加首领Saonchiogwa从奥农多加邀来耶稣会士约瑟夫·肖莫诺和勒内·梅纳尔，圣约瑟传教站在后来被称为「卡尤加堡」的Goiogouen附近建立。艾蒂安·德·卡埃尔和皮埃尔·拉费后来在此传教；1671年，拉费称两湖之间的平原鱼群、鹿群和盐泉都很丰饶。1753年，卡尤加人收留了自弗吉尼亚北迁来投的图特洛人和萨波尼人，后者在卡尤加湖南口附近建立Coreorgonel。美国独立战争时，卡尤加人立场不一，但参战的多数队伍加入了英国支持的边境袭掠。1779年，沙利文与克林顿远征在9月23日摧毁拥有十五座大长屋和大片玉米田的Goiogouen，次日焚毁Chonodote，Coreorgonel也被破坏。幸存者逃往其他豪德诺索尼村镇、塞尼卡地方或上加拿大；1794年11月11日，卡尤加人加入《卡南代瓜条约》，虽然湖乡大部已经丧失，条约仍承认豪德诺索尼诸族的主权。

en:
Onondagaono, the People of the Hills, took its name from the ridges above Onondaga Lake and Onondaga Creek. In 1444 its bark longhouses stood among cornfields and fishing waters, with paths crossing between the eastern and western Iroquoian nations. Brine springs rose near the lake, and its outlet led through the Seneca and Oswego rivers toward Lake Ontario, giving the hill towns fish, waterfowl, furs and a place on the northern canoe routes. This central country would later keep the council fire of the Haudenosaunee.

Around 1600 the principal Onondaga town stood near Cazenovia, from 1609 to 1615 near Pompey, and in 1640 it moved toward Manlius. The Jesuit Simon Le Moyne visited in 1654 and learned of the salt springs; in 1656 the French built Sainte-Marie de Gannentaha on Onondaga Lake, but the fortified mission was abandoned in 1658. The principal town moved to Onondaga Creek in 1720 and remained the meeting place of the Grand Council. The Onondaga tried neutrality at the opening of the American Revolution, but on 20 April 1779 Colonel Goose Van Schaick led 558 Continental troops from Fort Stanwix against their settlements, burning about fifty houses and winter stores. Most Onondaga then joined the British, and after the war many followed Joseph Brant to Upper Canada. The Treaty of Canandaigua acknowledged Onondaga land rights in 1794, while settlers around the lake began boiling its brine into salt.
zh:
Onondagaono意为「山丘之人」，得名于奥农多加湖与奥农多加溪上方的丘陵。1444年，这里的榆树皮长屋坐落在玉米田和渔场之间，小路把东部与西部的易洛魁语各族连接起来。湖畔有盐水泉，湖水出口经塞尼卡河、奥斯威戈河通向安大略湖，使这些丘陵村镇获得鱼、水禽、毛皮，并处在北方独木舟商路上。后来，正是在这片居中的土地上燃起了豪德诺索尼联盟的议事火塘。

1600年前后，奥农多加主城在卡泽诺维亚附近，1609年至1615年间位于庞培一带，1640年迁往曼利厄斯附近。耶稣会士西蒙·勒穆瓦纳1654年到访并得知湖畔盐泉；1656年，法兰西人在奥农多加湖畔建立圣玛丽·德·甘嫩塔哈传教据点，但这座设防传教站1658年即遭放弃。主城1720年迁往奥农多加溪畔，并继续作为大议事会集会地。美国独立战争爆发时，奥农多加人曾试图中立，但1779年4月20日，古斯·范·沙伊克上校率领五百五十八名大陆军从斯坦威克斯堡出击，焚毁约五十座房屋和过冬储粮。多数奥农多加人随后加入英国一方，战后许多人随约瑟夫·布兰特前往上加拿大。1794年的《卡南代瓜条约》承认奥农多加人的土地权利；与此同时，湖畔定居者开始煎煮盐水制盐。

en:
Onyo'taaka is the Oneida country around Oneida Lake and the streams that lead toward Lake Ontario, lying between Mohawk lands to the east and Onondaga lands to the west. The Onʌyoteˀa·ká, the People of the Standing Stone, were one of the five nations of the Haudenosaunee, dwelling in bark-covered longhouse towns and farming maize, beans, and squash while fishing and hunting across the lake plain. Their trails met at the Oneida Carry, a short passage between the Mohawk River and the Wood Creek–Oneida Lake waterway. In 1444 this was still a world untouched by European traders; its value lay in cornfields, fishing places, furs, and the Oneida seat between the eastern and western doors of the longhouse.

Dutch and French trade goods reached Iroquoia in the seventeenth century, drawing Oneida hunters into the fur trade and the Beaver Wars. In the early colonial period the nation held roughly six million acres of central New York. Samuel Kirkland began missionary and school work among the Oneida in 1764, and many allied with the American revolutionaries; their warriors fought at Oriskany on 6 August 1777 after the Haudenosaunee had split into British and Patriot factions. In 1780 Joseph Brant's Loyalist and Mohawk volunteers destroyed Kanonwalohale, the principal pro-American Oneida village. The treaties of Fort Stanwix in 1784 and Canandaigua in 1794 were followed by relentless land cessions, while the Oneida Carry was canalized between 1792 and 1803 to carry more commerce toward Oneida Lake. By 1821 settler New York pressed closely around a reduced Oneida homeland.
zh:
奥尼约塔卡是奥奈达人围绕奥奈达湖及通向安大略湖诸水道的家园，东接莫霍克人之地，西连奥农达加人之地。自称Onʌyoteˀa·ká的奥奈达人意为「立石之人」，是豪德诺索尼五族之一；他们住在树皮覆盖的长屋村镇，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，也在湖原上渔猎。各条小路在奥奈达陆运道汇合，那里是莫霍克河与伍德溪—奥奈达湖水路之间的短途通道。1444年，欧洲商人尚未进入这里，此地的重要性来自玉米田、渔场、毛皮，以及奥奈达人在长屋东门与西门之间的位置。

17世纪，荷兰和法国商货进入易洛魁地区，奥奈达猎人被卷入毛皮贸易和海狸战争。殖民时代早期，奥奈达人在纽约中部保有约六百万英亩土地。塞缪尔·柯克兰1764年开始在奥奈达人中传教和办学，许多人随后与美国革命者结盟；豪德诺索尼联盟分裂为亲英与亲美两派后，奥奈达战士在1777年8月6日参加奥里斯卡尼战役。1780年，约瑟夫·布兰特率领的效忠派与莫霍克志愿军摧毁了亲美奥奈达人的主村卡农瓦洛黑尔。1784年《斯坦维克斯堡条约》和1794年《卡南代瓜条约》之后，土地割让仍接踵而至；1792年至1803年，奥奈达陆运道被改建为运河，更多商货得以运往奥奈达湖。到1821年，纽约定居者已紧紧逼近大幅缩小的奥奈达家园。

en:
The land between the lower Delaware and the sea, from the falls where Trenton now stands down to the dunes of Cape May, was the heart of the Unami-speaking Lenape; they called the country Scheyichbi. Turtle, Turkey and Wolf clans kept shifting villages on the tidewater creeks, tending maize fields, harvesting fish and shellfish from the bay and hunting the pine woods of the interior. In 1444 these bands answered to no outside power, and the only ships they knew were dugout canoes.

Henry Hudson charted this coast in 1609. The Dutch built Fort Nassau, a beaver-trading factorij, near present Gloucester City in 1626, and in 1643 Governor Printz of New Sweden raised Fort Nya Elfsborg on the Salem River, soon abandoned to the mosquitoes that earned it the nickname Fort Mosquito and burned when the Dutch moved against the Swedes in 1651; New Sweden itself fell to Stuyvesant in 1655, and the whole river passed to England in 1664. Quakers bought West Jersey in 1674, planted Salem in 1675 and Burlington in 1677, while East and West Jersey ran as separate proprietorships until the crown reunited them in 1702. In 1758 the colony set aside Brotherton in the Pine Barrens, its first reservation for the remaining Lenape; most of them accepted an Oneida invitation and left for New Stockbridge in 1801. Washington crossed the Delaware to strike Trenton on 26 December 1776 and won again at Princeton on 3 January 1777, while the hard-fought draw at Monmouth in June 1778 earned New Jersey its name of the Crossroads of the Revolution. On 18 December 1787 it became the third state to ratify the Constitution.
zh:
特拉华下游与大海之间的这片土地，从今日特伦顿所在的瀑布地带一直延伸到梅角的沙丘，是操乌纳米语的特拉华人的腹地，他们把这片乡土称作斯海奇比。龟氏、火鸡氏和狼氏氏族在潮汐溪畔迁徙设村，耕种玉米地，从海湾捕捞鱼贝，在内陆的松林里狩猎。1444年，这些群体不受任何外来政权管辖，他们所知的船只是挖空树干做成的独木舟。

1609年，亨利·哈得孙测绘了这段海岸。1626年，荷兰人在今格洛斯特城附近修筑做海狸皮贸易的商站拿骚堡；1643年，新瑞典总督普林茨在塞勒姆河畔建起新埃尔夫斯堡，这座堡垒很快因蚊虫肆虐被弃，得了「蚊子堡」的绰号，1651年荷兰人对瑞典人动手时又被烧毁。新瑞典本身于1655年被施托伊弗桑特征服，整条河在1664年落入英国之手。贵格会1674年买下西泽西，1675年建立塞勒姆、1677年建立伯灵顿；东泽西与西泽西作为两个业主殖民地分治，直到1702年被英王重新合并。1758年，殖民地在松林荒地里为留下的特拉华人辟出布拉泽顿保留地——这是英属北美第一个印第安人保留地；1801年，大多数人接受奥奈达人的邀请迁往新斯托克布里奇。1776年12月26日，华盛顿渡过特拉华河奇袭特伦顿，1777年1月3日又在普林斯顿获胜；1778年6月的蒙茅斯之战打成惨烈的平手，新泽西由此得到「独立战争的十字路口」之名。1787年12月18日，它成为第三个批准宪法的州。

en:
The west bank of the upper Hudson, above the mouth of Catskill Creek, was the country of the Mechkentowoon, one of the five tribes of the Mahican confederacy. Their longhouse towns stood on the river flats, where women grew maize, beans and squash and men took shad, sturgeon and beaver. Villages at the head of tidewater drew furs from the northern forests, and the carrying places between the Hudson and Connecticut rivers were in Mahican hands. In 1444 no European had yet entered the river; their rivals were the Mohawk, easternmost of the Iroquois, whose towns lay up the Mohawk River to the west.

In September 1609 Henry Hudson traded for furs at Mahican villages just below the site of Albany. Dutch merchants built Fort Nassau on Castle Island in 1614 and replaced it with Fort Orange in 1624. Rivalry over the trade brought war with the Mohawk: in 1626 a Dutch party marching to aid the Mahicans was ambushed near the fort and its commander killed, and by 1629 the Mohawk held the west bank and many Mahicans had crossed the Hudson. The English took New Netherland in 1664, lost it to a Dutch fleet in 1673 and recovered it by treaty in 1674, when Fort Orange was named Albany. In 1755 the British built Fort William Henry at the south end of Lake George; it fell to Montcalm in 1757 and its surrendered garrison was massacred. Burgoyne's army surrendered at Saratoga in October 1777, and in 1778 the Americans fortified West Point and stretched a great iron chain across the Hudson.
zh:
卡茨基尔溪口以上的哈得孙河上游西岸，是莫希干联盟五部之一马奇坎托文（Mechkentowoon）部的土地。他们的长屋村镇坐落在河畔滩地，妇女种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，男子捕捞西鲱、鲟鱼，猎取河狸；潮水尽头的村镇汇集北方森林的毛皮，哈得孙河与康涅狄格河之间的陆运道也在莫希干人掌握之中。1444年时还没有欧洲人进入这条河；他们的劲敌是西边莫霍克河谷的莫霍克人，即易洛魁诸部最东的一支。

1609年9月，亨利·哈德逊在今奥尔巴尼以南的莫希干村镇以货物换取毛皮。荷兰商人1614年在卡斯尔岛修建拿骚堡，1624年另建奥兰治堡取而代之。毛皮之争演变为与莫霍克人的战争：1626年，一支出堡援助莫希干人的荷兰队伍在要塞附近遇伏，指挥官战死；到1629年莫霍克人已占据西岸，许多莫希干人东渡哈得孙河。1664年英国人夺取新尼德兰，1673年被荷兰舰队收复，1674年依条约再度归英，奥兰治堡改名奥尔巴尼。1755年，英军在乔治湖南端修建威廉·亨利堡；该堡1757年陷于蒙卡尔姆之手，投降的守军随后遭到屠杀。1777年10月伯戈因所部英军在萨拉托加投降；1778年美军在西点筑垒，并在哈得孙河上横亘巨大的铁链。

en:
Kanien'kehaka, the Mohawk country, follows the Mohawk River through the fertile valley between the Adirondack and Catskill highlands, from the Oneida border in the west to the Hudson-Mohawk fork in the east. The Kanien'kehá:ka, People of the Flint Place, were the easternmost of the five Haudenosaunee nations and keepers of the Eastern Door. In 1444 their bark-covered longhouse towns stood above maize fields on the river flats, and hunting and war trails ran north toward the St. Lawrence and east toward Mahican country. Furs, corn, and command of the natural road from the Hudson into Iroquoia gave this valley its strategic weight.

Contact with Europeans began in 1609, when Samuel de Champlain joined a Wendat war party and his firearms struck down Mohawk chiefs near Ticonderoga. The Dutch built Fort Nassau near the Hudson-Mohawk fork in 1614, and after the Mohawks pushed back the Mohicans in 1628 they gained direct access to the European fur trade. Alexandre de Prouville de Tracy's French expedition burned Mohawk towns and food stores in 1666; the peace opened the country to Jesuit missionaries, and converts settled on the St. Lawrence. William Johnson built Fort Johnson about 1749 and moved to Johnson Hall in 1763, making the valley a center of British-Indigenous diplomacy. Most Mohawks supported Britain during the American Revolution, and in October 1780 forces under John Johnson, John Butler, and Joseph Brant burned through the Schoharie and lower Mohawk valleys. Defeat brought dispossession in New York, while the Haldimand Proclamation of 25 October 1784 granted Mohawk refugees land on the Grand River in Canada. By 1821 the old valley was largely a landscape of settler farms and mills.
zh:
卡尼恩凯哈卡是莫霍克人的家园，沿莫霍克河展开，处在阿迪朗达克山地与卡茨基尔山地之间的肥沃河谷中，西接奥奈达边界，东抵哈得孙河与莫霍克河交汇处。Kanien'kehá:ka意为「燧石之地的人」，莫霍克人是豪德诺索尼五族中最东的一族，负责守护联盟东门。1444年，他们以树皮覆盖的长屋村镇矗立在河畔玉米田旁，狩猎和征战小路向北通往圣劳伦斯河，向东伸入莫希干人之地。毛皮、玉米以及对哈得孙河通往易洛魁内陆天然通道的控制，使这座河谷举足轻重。

与欧洲人的接触始于1609年，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰随一支温达特战队行动，在泰孔德罗加附近用火器击杀莫霍克首领。荷兰人1614年在哈得孙河与莫霍克河交汇处附近修建拿骚堡；1628年莫霍克人击退莫希干人后，得以直接进入欧洲毛皮贸易。1666年，亚历山大·德·普鲁维尔·德·特拉西率领法军焚毁莫霍克村镇和粮仓，议和后耶稣会传教士进入此地，皈依者逐渐迁往圣劳伦斯河畔。威廉·约翰逊约1749年修建约翰逊堡，1763年迁入约翰逊厅，使这座河谷成为英国与原住民外交的中心。美国独立战争中，多数莫霍克人支持英国；1780年10月，约翰·约翰逊、约翰·巴特勒和约瑟夫·布兰特率领的部队焚毁斯科哈里和莫霍克河下游谷地。战败导致他们在纽约失去土地，1784年10月25日的《哈尔迪曼德公告》将加拿大格兰德河畔的土地授予莫霍克难民。到1821年，旧日河谷已大多变成定居者的农场和磨坊。

en:
Manhattan is a long island in the Hudson estuary, sheltered by the waters that form New York Harbor. It was part of Lenapehoking, and Lenape-speaking Munsee and Wappinger bands kept villages, fishing stations and maize fields there; their main island trail ran from the northern woods toward the southern landing place later followed by Broadway. In 1444 the harbor knew bark canoes rather than European ships. No foreign fort stood on the shore, and the island's value to its inhabitants lay in fish, shellfish, planted ground and easy passage between the coast and the Hudson valley.

After Henry Hudson visited in 1609, Dutch traders saw that the anchorage could secure the Hudson River beaver trade. A Dutch post was planted on Governors Island in 1624, Fort Amsterdam was begun on southern Manhattan in 1625, and Peter Stuyvesant, appointed director-general in 1647, granted New Amsterdam city rights on 2 February 1653. Four English frigates entered the harbor in 1664 and took the town without a fight, renaming it New York for the Duke of York. The Dutch briefly recovered it as New Orange in 1673, but returned it to England in 1674. During the American Revolutionary War, the Continental Army lost the Battle of Fort Washington on 16 November 1776; fire and British occupation followed until 25 November 1783. New York served as the capital of the United States from 1785 to 1790, and by 1810 it had overtaken Philadelphia as the country's largest city. The Commissioners' Plan of 1811 laid its famous street grid over the island.
zh:
曼哈顿是哈德逊河口的一座长岛，受纽约港水域环抱。它原属莱纳佩人的莱纳佩霍京，操莱纳佩语的芒西人和瓦平格尔人各支在这里设有村落、渔场和玉米地；岛上的主要步道从北部林地通往南端渡口，后来的百老汇大道大体沿此线延伸。1444年，港中往来的还只是树皮独木舟，欧洲船舰尚未出现。岸上没有外来堡垒，居民倚重的是鱼、贝类、耕地以及海岸与哈德逊河谷之间便利的水路。

1609年亨利·哈德逊到访后，荷兰商人意识到这个锚地可以控制哈德逊河的河狸皮贸易。1624年，荷兰人在总督岛设立贸易站；1625年，曼哈顿南端开始修建阿姆斯特丹堡。1647年出任总干事的彼得·斯泰弗森特于1653年2月2日授予新阿姆斯特丹城市权利。1664年，四艘英国护卫舰驶入港中，兵不血刃夺取城镇，并按约克公爵的封号改称纽约。荷兰人1673年一度收复，改名新奥兰治，但在1674年又将它交还英国。美国独立战争期间，大陆军在1776年11月16日的华盛顿堡战役后失去曼哈顿；随后火灾与英国占领一直持续到1783年11月25日。1785年至1790年，纽约是美国首都；到1810年，它已超过费城成为美国最大城市，1811年的《专员计划》为全岛划定了著名的方格街道。

en:
Nipmuc is Nippenet, the freshwater-pond country of central Massachusetts, a rolling inland network of ponds, streams, maize fields, hunting grounds, and trails between the Massachusett coast, Wampanoag and Narragansett country, the Connecticut valley, and the Mahican lands. The Nipmuc were not a single centralized chiefdom but related village bands speaking an Eastern Algonquian language, living in movable wetus and moving between farmland, fishing places, and hunting camps. In 1444 their furs, food, and paths gave them a place among stronger neighboring nations, while the inland ponds and forests remained entirely their own world.

Recorded contact came in 1630, when Nipmuc people carried maize to hungry Boston colonists. The fur and metal trade was followed by epidemics, debt, and land sales. John Eliot began preaching in Massachusett in 1646, Hassanamesit was made a praying town in 1647, and Eliot's Indian Bible appeared in 1663. When King Philip's War began in 1675, many Nipmuc joined Metacom; they struck Brookfield, Sudbury, Bloody Brook, and Lancaster, where the 10 February 1676 raid led by Monoco and Sagamore Sam captured Mary Rowlandson for eleven weeks. Christian Nipmuc were also suspected by the colonists: hundreds from praying towns were interned on Deer Island in the winter of 1675–1676, and many died of cold and hunger. Survivors were killed, sold to the West Indies, exiled, or absorbed into Abenaki, Mahican, and Stockbridge communities. Families who regrouped around Hassanamesit and Chaubunagungamaug saw Hassanamesit shrink from 7,500 to 500 acres by 1727 and Chaubunagungamaug from 200 to 26 acres in 1797. By 1821 their old country had become the towns and farms of central Massachusetts, with small Nipmuc communities holding only fragments of Nippenet.
zh:
尼普马克即尼佩内特，意为「淡水塘之地」，位于马萨诸塞中部，是一片起伏内陆中的池塘、溪流、玉米田、猎场与小路网络，连接马萨诸特海岸、万帕诺亚格和纳拉甘西特之地、康涅狄格河谷以及莫希干人地区。尼普马克人并非一个高度集权的酋邦，而是彼此关联的村社群体，使用东阿尔冈昆语，住在可迁移的wetus中，随农地、渔场和猎营轮换生活。1444年，他们的毛皮、粮食和小路使其在周边更强的各部族之间保有位置，而内陆池塘与森林仍完全属于他们自己的世界。

有记载的接触发生在1630年，尼普马克人把玉米运给断粮的波士顿殖民者。毛皮与金属器贸易之后，疫病、债务和土地出售接踵而至。约翰·艾略特1646年开始用马萨诸特语传教，Hassanamesit在1647年被设为祈祷镇，他的印第安语《圣经》于1663年问世。1675年菲利普国王战争爆发后，许多尼普马克人加入梅塔卡姆一方，袭击布鲁克菲尔德、萨德伯里、血溪和兰开斯特；在1676年2月10日的兰开斯特袭击中，莫诺科和萨加莫尔·萨姆的部队俘虏玛丽·罗兰森达十一周。信奉基督教的尼普马克人也遭到殖民者猜疑，数百名祈祷镇居民在1675年至1676年冬被囚禁于迪尔岛，许多人死于寒冷和饥饿。幸存者或被杀、被卖到西印度群岛、被迫流亡，或并入阿贝纳基、莫希干和斯托克布里奇社群。重新聚集在Hassanamesit和Chaubunagungamaug周围的家族，则眼见Hassanamesit到1727年从7500英亩缩至500英亩，Chaubunagungamaug也在1797年从200英亩缩至26英亩。到1821年，他们的故土已成为马萨诸塞中部的城镇与农场，尼普马克小社群只保有尼佩内特的零星残土。

en:
Narraganset is the bay country west of Narragansett Bay, from the Providence River toward the Pawcatuck, a shore of salt ponds, tidal inlets, cleared fields and oak woods. In 1444 its Algonquian-speaking people wintered in bark-covered longhouses, moved to coastal camps in summer, farmed and hunted inland, and paddled large dugouts between fishing grounds and neighboring communities. Their sachems drew authority from the western inlets and points of the bay, a country already linked by canoe, trail and exchange before any European ship entered those waters.

Giovanni da Verrazzano visited the bay in 1524 while sailing for France, and Adriaen Block charted it during his 1614 Dutch voyage. The epidemics of 1616-1619 devastated coastal peoples farther south but largely spared the Narragansetts, leaving them unusually strong when English settlement reached their territory in 1635. In 1636 Roger Williams, exiled from Massachusetts Bay, acquired land from sachems Canonicus and Miantonomo and founded Providence Plantations; he learned their language and published A Key into the Language of America in 1643. The Narragansetts joined the English against the Pequots in 1637, but the brutality at Mystic turned them against the alliance. During King Philip's War their neutrality did not spare them: on 19 December 1675 colonial forces stormed their palisaded Great Swamp fort and killed hundreds of non-combatants. The Narragansetts burned Providence on 27 March 1676 before Canonchet was captured and the nation broken; survivors were enslaved or merged with Eastern Niantic communities. In the 1740s the Narragansett Indian Church became a center of conversion, and after King Tom became sachem in 1746 much of the remaining land passed to colonial buyers.
zh:
纳拉甘西特是纳拉甘西特湾西岸的乡土，从普罗维登斯河一直延伸向波卡塔克河，沿岸遍布咸水塘、潮汐湾、开垦地和橡树林。1444年，说阿尔冈昆语的纳拉甘西特人冬季住在树皮覆盖的长屋，夏季迁往海岸营地，在内地农耕狩猎，也划着大型独木舟往来于渔场和邻近社群之间。酋长的权威来自海湾西侧的水口与岬角；在欧洲船只驶入这些水域之前，独木舟、小径和交换网络已把这片土地连成一体。

1524年，为法国效力的乔瓦尼·达·韦拉扎诺到访海湾；1614年，阿德里安·布洛克在荷兰航行中测绘了这里。1616至1619年的疫病重创更南方的沿海族群，却基本没有波及纳拉甘西特人，所以1635年英格兰拓殖抵达时，他们仍相当强盛。1636年，被马萨诸塞湾放逐的罗杰·威廉姆斯从酋长卡诺尼库斯和米安托诺莫手中取得土地，建立普罗维登斯种植园；他学习纳拉甘西特语，并在1643年出版《美洲语言钥匙》。1637年，纳拉甘西特人与英格兰人联手进攻佩科特人，但米斯蒂克屠寨的残酷使他们疏远这一同盟。菲利普王战争期间，中立并未保护他们：1675年12月19日，殖民地军队强攻大沼泽中的木栅要塞，数百名非战斗人员遇害。纳拉甘西特人于1676年3月27日焚毁普罗维登斯，随后卡农切特酋长被俘，族群力量瓦解；幸存者或被卖为奴隶，或并入东尼安蒂克社群。1740年代，纳拉甘西特印第安教会成为传教中心；1746年汤姆酋长继任后，大部分剩余土地转入殖民地买主手中。

en:
The shores of Massachusetts Bay, between the Charles and Neponset rivers beneath the wooded Great Blue Hill, take their name from the Massachusett, the 'people of the great hill'. Their villages stood on the bay's inlets and harbor islands; under sachems they raised maize, beans and squash, took herring and shellfish at their weirs, and spoke Massachusett, an Eastern Algonquian tongue understood along much of the neighboring coast. In 1444 this was among the more thickly settled shorelands of the northeast, its paths and planting grounds long established, and no European had yet been seen there.

European ships began to appear after 1600: Bartholomew Gosnold cruised the coast in 1602, Samuel de Champlain anchored in the harbor in 1605 and traded with its sachems, and John Smith mapped the bay as part of New England in 1614. Then in 1616–19 the 'Great Dying', an epidemic now often identified as leptospirosis spread by shipboard rats, emptied village after village, and smallpox returned in 1633. A short-lived fishing station on Cape Ann, founded in 1623, moved to Naumkeag, soon renamed Salem, in 1626. The Massachusetts Bay Colony received its royal charter in 1629, and in September 1630 John Winthrop's Puritans crossed from Charlestown to the nearly deserted Shawmut Peninsula and named their town Boston. Harvard College was founded nearby in 1636, the first press in English North America began work at Cambridge in 1638, and John Eliot's Massachusett translation of the Bible was printed there in 1663, after many converts had settled in Christian 'praying towns'. King Philip's War of 1675–76 shattered those communities, and in 1692 the Salem witch trials shook the colony's north shore. Boston then became the storm center of quarrel with the crown: the Boston Massacre in 1770, the Tea Party in 1773, and in 1775–76 the Battle of Bunker Hill and the siege that ended only when the British evacuated the town.
zh:
马萨诸塞湾的海岸位于查尔斯河与内邦西特河之间，林木葱郁的大蓝山俯瞰其上，地名来自马萨诸塞人，意为「大山之人」。他们的村落散布在海湾水湾和港中诸岛，在酋长带领下种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，在鱼堰捕捞鲱鱼、采挖贝类，所说的马萨诸塞语属东阿尔冈昆语，邻近海岸的许多族群都能听懂。1444年时，这里是北美东北海岸人烟较稠密的地方之一，小径和玉米田由来已久，欧洲人尚未出现。

1600年以后，欧洲船只陆续到来：巴塞洛缪·戈斯诺尔德1602年沿海航行，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1605年在港中停泊并与当地酋长交易，约翰·史密斯1614年测绘海湾，把这里标作新英格兰的一部分。1616至1619年的「大死亡」（今人多认为是船上老鼠传播的钩端螺旋体病）使一座座村庄为之一空，1633年天花又至。安角上1623年建立的渔业据点未能持久，1626年迁往瑙姆基格，不久改名塞勒姆。马萨诸塞湾殖民地1629年获得王室特许状；1630年9月，约翰·温思罗普率领清教徒从查尔斯敦渡过海湾，登上几乎荒无人烟的肖马特半岛，将新城命名为波士顿。1636年哈佛学院在附近创立，1638年英属北美的第一台印刷机在坎布里奇开工，1663年印出约翰·艾略特翻译的马萨诸塞语《圣经》；此前许多皈依者已迁入基督徒的「祈祷镇」。1675至1676年的菲利普国王战争摧毁了这些社区，1692年塞勒姆审巫案震动殖民地北岸。此后波士顿成为与王室争端的风暴中心：1770年的波士顿惨案、1773年的倾茶事件，以及1775至1776年的邦克山战役与围城战，最终以英军撤离波士顿告终。

en:
Mahican is the name given here to an Algonquian borderland stretching from the upper Hudson and Lake George country toward the Green Mountains and the upper Connecticut River. Pocumtuk, later Deerfield, was a major Pocomtuc village on rich river intervales, where maize, beans, and squash were grown and the Connecticut supplied fish and water routes. In 1444 Abenaki trails crossed the northern woods, Mohawk war paths entered from the west, and Mahican hunters ranged toward Lake Champlain. Pine timber, furs, river crossings, and the meetings of these nations gave the region its importance before any European town had been planted.

Samuel de Champlain reached Lake Champlain in 1609, opening the valley to French rivalry with the Mohawk and New England. English purchasers obtained Pocumtuc land in the 1660s, and Deerfield was laid out in 1670. During King Philip's War the Pocomtuc victory at Bloody Brook in September 1675 was answered by the settler attack at Peskeompskut in May 1676; many survivors fled to Schaghticoke and later joined Abenaki communities. On 29 February 1704, French, Abenaki, Mohawk, and Pocomtuc raiders under Jean-Baptiste Hertel de Rouville burned much of Deerfield and carried 112 captives toward Montreal. Farther north, Benning Wentworth issued the New Hampshire Grants between 1749 and 1764. Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys, formed in 1770, resisted New York's claims and captured Fort Ticonderoga on 10 May 1775. Delegates of the grants proclaimed the independent Vermont Republic on 15 January 1777; after the Hubbardton and Bennington campaigns of that year, it entered the United States as the fourteenth state on 4 March 1791.
zh:
莫希干是这片阿尔冈昆边地的名称，地域从上哈得孙河与乔治湖一带延伸到绿山和康涅狄格河上游。波康塔克（Pocumtuk）即后来的迪尔菲尔德，是波康塔克人在肥沃河滨低地上的重要村镇；人们种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，也依靠康涅狄格河捕鱼和通行。1444年，阿贝纳基人的小路穿过北方林地，莫霍克人的战道从西面伸入，莫希干猎人则活动到尚普兰湖一带。在欧洲人建立任何城镇之前，松木、毛皮、河流渡口以及各部族的会集便已赋予此地重要性。

1609年，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰到达尚普兰湖，使这座河谷卷入法国人与莫霍克人及新英格兰的争夺。英国购地者在1660年代取得波康塔克土地，迪尔菲尔德于1670年划建。菲利普国王战争期间，波康塔克人1675年9月在血溪取胜，1676年5月定居者又袭击佩斯基奥姆普斯库特；许多幸存者逃到斯卡蒂科克，后来加入阿贝纳基社群。1704年2月29日，让-巴蒂斯特·埃尔泰尔·德·鲁维尔率领法国人、阿贝纳基人、莫霍克人和波康塔克人焚毁大半个迪尔菲尔德，并将112名俘虏带往蒙特利尔。更北面，本宁·温特沃思在1749年至1764年间发放新罕布什尔授地。伊桑·艾伦的绿山男孩1770年组成，抵抗纽约的土地要求，并于1775年5月10日夺取泰孔德罗加堡。授地居民代表在1777年1月15日宣布成立独立的佛蒙特共和国；经历同年哈巴顿和本宁顿战役后，它于1791年3月4日作为美国第十四个州加入联邦。

en:
At Amoskeag the Merrimack narrows and drops fifty feet over ledges in a quarter of a mile, and its Pennacook name, Namoskeag, means 'good fishing place'. Sturgeon, salmon and alewife ran the rapids in such numbers that the Pennacook strung great nets across the river and kept their largest settlements on the high bluffs above, where bands of the loose Pennacook alliance gathered seasonally to fish and take council. The valley also led west toward the Mohawk and north toward the Mi'kmaq, whose raids were long known there. In 1444 the falls were one of the busy centers of the Merrimack country, its camps and weirs older than memory.

The great epidemic of 1616–19 thinned the Pennacook villages, and the bashaba Passaconaway chose peace with the English rather than war. Wonalancet, his son and successor, tried to hold neutrality in King Philip's War of 1675–76, but Pennacook bands were drawn in anyway; afterwards some were sold into slavery and others fled north to the Abenaki or west to Schaghticoke. Massachusetts had already granted Dunstable on the lower Merrimack in 1673. In 1719 Scots-Irish families out of Ulster settled Nutfield, chartered as Londonderry in 1722, and John Goffe settled beside Cohas Brook at Amoskeag the same year; the township, granted as Tyngstown in 1727, was voided when New Hampshire separated from Massachusetts in 1741 and rechartered as Derryfield in 1751. John Stark, brought at the age of eight to his family's homestead at the falls, served in Rogers' Rangers against the French and led New Hampshire troops at Bunker Hill in 1775 and to victory at Bennington on 16 August 1777. In 1807 Samuel Blodget built a canal and locks around the falls; Derryfield was renamed Manchester in 1810, and the first Amoskeag cotton mills rose on the water power he had opened.
zh:
