阿莫斯凯格一带，梅里马克河在约四分之一英里内收窄、从岩壁间跌落五十英尺；佩纳库克语称此地为纳莫斯凯格，意为「好渔场」。鲟鱼、鲑鱼和灰西鲱成群涌上急流，佩纳库克人在河面张起大网捕鱼，最大的几处村落就建在俯瞰瀑布的高崖上，佩纳库克联盟的各支族群按季到此聚集，捕鱼议事。河谷向西通向莫霍克人的地界，向北则是米克马克人的地盘，这两处的袭扰由来已久。1444年时，这片瀑布是梅里马克地区最热闹的中心之一，营地和鱼堰古老得无人能说清其来历。

1616至1619年的大瘟疫使佩纳库克诸村人口锐减，大酋长帕萨科纳韦选择与英人讲和而非开战。他的继任者、儿子沃纳兰塞特在1675至1676年的菲利普国王战争中力图保持中立，佩纳库克人的队伍却仍被卷入；战后一些人被卖为奴，另一些人向北投奔阿布纳基人，或向西逃入斯凯蒂科克。此前马萨诸塞已于1673年在梅里马克下游授予邓斯特布尔镇地。1719年，来自阿尔斯特的苏格兰裔爱尔兰人在附近的纳特菲尔德落脚，1722年获特许为伦敦德里；同年约翰·戈夫在阿莫斯凯格的科哈斯溪畔定居。这片镇区1727年曾被授予为廷斯敦，1741年新罕布什尔与马萨诸塞分治时授地作废，1751年重新设治为德里菲尔德。八岁便随家迁居瀑布边的约翰·斯塔克曾在罗杰斯游骑兵中对法作战，1775年率新罕布什尔部队奔赴邦克山，1777年8月16日又取得本宁顿大捷。1807年，塞缪尔·布洛杰特绕瀑布修成运河船闸；1810年德里菲尔德改名曼彻斯特，最早的阿莫斯凯格棉纺厂也借他开通的水力在瀑布边兴起。

en:
Penapawsket is the country of the Pαnawάhpskewi, the Penobscot, around the broad estuary where the Penobscot River meets Penobscot Bay. Their name means 'the people of where the white rocks extend out'. Seasonal villages and camps followed moose, caribou, beaver, fish runs and shellfish beds between the northern woods and the cold coast, while birchbark canoes linked river, islands and bay. In 1444 no European trading post had yet been built there, and Penobscot bands controlled the furs, fish, canoe routes and deep-water anchorages of this severe-winter Wabanaki shore east of the Kennebec.

George Weymouth explored Penobscot Bay in 1605 and carried five Abenaki people to England. A French post opened at Majabigwaduce, later Castine, in 1613, and Charles de la Tour built Fort Pentagouët there in 1625. Plymouth forces seized it in 1628, the French retook it in 1635, and Robert Sedgwick's New England troops sacked it in 1654. After 1667 Jean-Vincent de Saint-Castin made the post a French-Abenaki trade and diplomacy centre by marrying the daughter of sachem Modockawando. The Dutch took it in 1674, Saint-Castin recovered it in 1676, and after Edmund Andros plundered it in 1688 he led an Abenaki raid on Pemaquid in August 1689; Benjamin Church destroyed the settlement in 1692. The Penobscot lost their main French protector after Quebec fell in 1759. In 1779, although the Penobscot supported the Patriots, Britain built Fort George at Majabigwaduce. Massachusetts forces besieged it from 25 July until George Collier's relief on 13 August, losing all 44 ships of the expedition. Land cessions from 1794 increasingly confined the Penobscot toward Indian Island.
zh:
佩那保斯凯特是佩纳瓦普斯凯维人，即佩诺布斯科特人的土地，环绕佩诺布斯科特河注入佩诺布斯科特湾的宽阔河口。他们的族名意为「白色岩石向外伸出之地的人」。季节性村落和营地随北方森林与寒冷海岸之间的驼鹿、驯鹿、河狸、鱼群和贝场迁移，桦皮独木舟则把河流、岛屿与海湾连成一路。1444年，欧洲商栈尚未在此建立，佩诺布斯科特诸群体仍控制着肯纳贝克河以东、严冬漫长的瓦巴纳基海岸上的毛皮、鱼获、独木舟水道和深水锚地。

1605年，乔治·韦茅斯探查佩诺布斯科特湾，并把五名阿布纳基人带往英格兰。1613年，法国人在后来卡斯廷所在的马贾比瓜杜斯设立贸易站，夏尔·德·拉图尔又于1625年修建彭塔古埃堡。普利茅斯武装1628年夺取该堡，法军1635年收复，罗伯特·塞奇威克率领的新英格兰部队则在1654年洗劫此地。1667年后，让-樊尚·德·圣卡斯坦迎娶酋长莫多达卡万多之女，把据点变成法国与阿布纳基人的贸易和外交中心。荷兰人1674年占堡，圣卡斯坦1676年将其夺回；埃德蒙·安德罗斯1688年劫掠后，他又在1689年8月率阿布纳基战队袭击佩马奎德。1692年，本杰明·彻奇摧毁这一定居点。1759年魁北克陷落后，佩诺布斯科特人失去法国这一主要后盾。1779年，尽管佩诺布斯科特人支持爱国者，英军仍在马贾比瓜杜斯修建乔治堡；马萨诸塞军队从7月25日起围攻，乔治·科利尔8月13日率援军到达，远征军44艘船全部损失。1794年起的土地割让，使佩诺布斯科特人日益被限制到印第安岛一带。

en:
The rugged inlets around Nootka Sound, Mowichat to the Nuu-chah-nulth, were the Pacific coast of related Wakashan-speaking nations. Each nation had its own hereditary chief, and the Mowachaht kept Yuquot on Friendly Cove as a harbour village facing the open ocean. In 1444 the sound was unknown to European charts and remained entirely within the alliances, rivalries and sea routes of the peoples of western Vancouver Island.

Juan Pérez's Santiago anchored off the sound on 8 August 1774, though the Spanish did not land; Nuu-chah-nulth canoes came out to trade. James Cook reached Yuquot in March 1778, and his misunderstanding of the local word nuutkaa fixed 'Nootka' on European maps. James Hanna's iron-for-furs voyage in August 1785 opened the maritime fur trade there. When Esteban José Martínez occupied Friendly Cove in 1789, he built Santa Cruz de Nuca and Fort San Miguel and seized British ships, bringing Spain and Britain close to war; the Nootka Conventions of 1790 to 1794 settled the crisis and left Maquinna's Mowachaht still central to trade and diplomacy at Yuquot. In March 1803, after quarrels with traders, Maquinna captured the Boston and kept two of its crew, including John R. Jewitt, for nearly three years.
zh:
努特卡湾（努查努阿特语称莫维查特）周围岛礁错落的海岸，是努查努尔斯人（Nuu-chah-nulth，中文资料常作努查努阿特人）的太平洋家园；这些彼此关联、操瓦卡什语的族群各有世袭首领。莫瓦查特人在友谊湾的尤阔特保有一座面向大洋的港湾村落。1444年，欧洲海图上还没有这片海峡，温哥华岛西岸的联盟、争端与海上往来完全属于当地诸族。

1774年8月8日，胡安·佩雷斯的「圣地亚哥号」在湾外停泊，西班牙人没有上岸，努查努阿特人则划独木舟前来交易。1778年3月，詹姆斯·库克抵达尤阔特，却把当地语义为「绕行」的nuutkaa误作地名，使「努特卡」留在欧洲地图上。1785年8月，詹姆斯·哈纳以铁货交换毛皮，开启了这里的海上毛皮贸易。1789年，埃斯特万·何塞·马丁内斯占领友谊湾，建起圣克鲁斯·德·努卡和圣米格尔堡，并扣押英国船只，几乎使西班牙与英国开战；1790至1794年的《努特卡公约》化解危机，马金纳的莫瓦查特人仍是尤阔特贸易与外交的核心。1803年3月，在与商人接连发生冲突后，马金纳夺取「波士顿号」，留下包括约翰·R·朱伊特在内的两名船员近三年。

en:
Howe Sound is a fjord-like arm of the Strait of Georgia, whose Squamish name means 'paddling north'. At its head the Squamish River joins the sea, while the Cheakamus, Mamquam and Elaho valleys lead into the mountains. Squamish villages and camps were spread through the sound and its islands, together with places used by the Shishalh, and salmon runs supplied much of the winter food stored at the river mouths. In 1444 this was Coast Salish country, ordered by Squamish families and waterways, with no European ship yet in the sound.

Smallpox reached the coast before direct European contact, and the epidemic of the 1770s devastated many Squamish camps and villages. José María Narváez observed the sound in 1791 and named it Boca del Carmelo; George Vancouver entered it in 1792 and renamed it after Earl Howe. The first recorded Squamish meetings with Vancouver's and Narváez's expeditions took place in these same years around the adjacent inlets, and another smallpox epidemic struck in 1800-01. Through 1821 no European fort or permanent settlement stood at the head of Howe Sound, which remained a network of Squamish villages, camps, fishing places and river routes.
zh:
豪湾是乔治亚海峡一条峡湾般的支海，斯阔米什语中的含义为「向北划行」。湾头有斯阔米什河入海，Cheakamus河、Mamquam河和Elaho河则通向群山。斯阔米什人的村落与营地遍布海湾和岛群，Shishalh人也使用这里的多处地方；鲑鱼洄游为河口各村提供了大量冬季储粮。1444年，这里仍是沿海萨利什人的土地，由斯阔米什人的家族与水路关系维系，欧洲船只尚未进入海湾。

天花在欧洲人直接接触之前已传到海岸，1770年代的疫病摧毁了许多斯阔米什营地和村落。1791年，何塞·玛丽亚·纳瓦埃斯观察到豪湾，将其命名为Boca del Carmelo；1792年乔治·温哥华驶入湾内，又以豪伯爵之名称之为豪湾。斯阔米什人与温哥华、纳瓦埃斯船队最早有记载的接触，也发生在这两年间邻近各处海湾；1800至1801年，天花再度袭来。到1821年，豪湾湾头仍没有欧洲要塞或永久定居点，依旧是斯阔米什人的村落、营地、捕鱼地与河路网络。

en:
'Kwakiutl' originally meant one Kwak'wala-speaking community whose village of Tsaxis later became Fort Rupert on Beaver Harbour, near the northern tip of Vancouver Island. Around it lay the wider Kwakwaka'wakw country, stretching through Queen Charlotte Strait, Johnstone Strait and the Discovery Islands. Fishing was the base of life, supplemented by hunting, wild berries, weaving and carved woodwork. Rank and wealth were shown not by hoarding but by lavish distribution at potlatches. In 1444 the villages followed their own chiefs and seasonal rounds, linked by related dialects and canoe routes.

On 5 August 1786, a British fur-trading expedition reached Goletas Channel; the commander of Experiment named the opening Queen Charlotte's Sound. George Vancouver's expedition made the first documented European contact with the Kwakwaka'wakw in 1792, while British ships surveyed the maze of island channels. The coastal fur trade brought new goods and pressures, but through 1821 Tsaxis had not become a European fort or town; the Hudson's Bay Company post later built there still lay in the future. Village life remained in Kwakiutl and neighbouring hands, with rank and wealth still expressed through ceremony and potlatch gifts.
zh:
「夸扣特尔」本指一个说Kwak'wala语的社群，其村址Tsaxis后来成为温哥华岛北端附近Beaver Harbour的鲁珀特堡。其周边是更广阔的夸夸嘉夸诸族之地，穿过夏洛特皇后海峡、约翰斯通海峡和发现群岛。渔业是生计基础，辅以狩猎、采集野果野莓、编织和木雕。地位与财富不靠囤积显现，而在夸富宴上以丰厚馈赠展示。1444年，这些村落仍按各自首领和季节节律生活，由相近方言与独木舟水路联系。

1786年8月5日，一支英国毛皮贸易探险队到达Goletas Channel；Experiment号的指挥官将前方水道命名为Queen Charlotte's Sound。1792年，乔治·温哥华的船队测绘这片岛群交错的海峡时，与夸夸嘉夸人发生欧洲人最早有记载的接触。沿海毛皮贸易带来新货物和新压力，但到1821年，Tsaxis仍未成为欧洲人的要塞或城镇，后来的哈德逊湾公司商站尚未出现。村落仍由夸扣特尔及邻近诸族掌握，地位与财富继续通过仪式和夸富宴馈赠来表达。

en:
The Tsimshian, whose name Ts'msyen means 'inside the Skeena River', hold the foggy islands and inlets where the lower Skeena meets Hecate Strait. Their oral history recalls earlier homes on the upper Skeena, but chiefly houses had moved down to the coast by the fifteenth century. In 1444 families wintered in villages around Prince Rupert Harbour and Metlakatla, then followed the salmon to summer stations along the lower river. Matrilineal clans and hereditary chiefs controlled names, fishing grounds and ceremonial privileges, while canoes linked the harbour with neighbouring nations.

European ships did not break that seasonal round for more than three centuries. In 1787 the British captains Charles Duncan and James Colnett reached Gitxaala on the outer coast, perhaps the first Tsimshian village recorded as visited by Europeans, although Russian traders may have met northern groups earlier. The coastal fur trade then reached the Skeena estuary, bringing new goods and rival shipping into Hecate Strait. Through 1821, however, Tsimshian chiefs still controlled the winter villages, salmon fisheries and canoe passages of their own coast.
zh:
钦西安人自称Ts'msyen，意为「斯基纳河内」，居住在斯基纳河下游注入赫卡特海峡一带的雾中岛屿与峡湾。口传历史说他们早先住在斯基纳河上游，但到15世纪，各世袭首领家族已迁居海岸。1444年，各部族在鲁珀特港和梅特拉卡特拉一带的村落过冬，鲑鱼洄游时再前往下游河滨的夏季渔场。社会按母系氏族划分，世袭首领掌管名号、渔场和仪式特权；独木舟航线把港湾与邻近各族连接起来。

此后三个多世纪里，欧洲船只并未改变这套随季节转徙的生活。1787年，英国船长查尔斯·邓肯和詹姆斯·科尔内特抵达外海的Gitxaala，这可能是欧洲人到访钦西安村落的最早记录，不过俄国毛皮商也许更早接触过北部群体。海上毛皮贸易随后延伸到斯基纳河口，把新货物和彼此竞争的船只带进赫卡特海峡。但直到1821年，钦西安首领仍控制着本族海岸上的冬村、鲑鱼渔场和独木舟航道。

en: The forested islands, fjords and Taku River mouth of the central Alaska Panhandle are Tlingit country. In 1444 its people lived in plank-house winter villages facing the water, then moved to seasonal salmon, herring and sea-otter camps. Matrilineal clans and moieties governed inheritance, while large canoes carried dried fish, furs, hides and cedar goods to Athabascan-speaking peoples inland. Russian explorers made the first recorded European contact with the Tlingit in 1741, and Spanish ships followed in 1775. The sea-otter trade then drew foreign vessels along the coast, but the Taku kept their place as middlemen on the river and entered 1821 without a permanent European fort in their homeland.
zh: 阿拉斯加狭地中部林木密布的岛屿、峡湾和塔库河口，是特林吉特人的土地。1444年时，人们住在面向水面的木板长屋冬村，再按季节前往鲑鱼、鲱鱼和海獭营地。世系与财产沿母系氏族传承，大型独木舟把鱼干、毛皮、兽皮和雪松制品运往内陆，与说阿萨巴斯卡语的族群交易。俄国探险者在1741年留下欧洲人与特林吉特人接触的最早记录，西班牙船只则在1775年到来。此后海獭贸易把外国帆船引到海岸，但塔库人仍守着河道上的中介地位；到1821年，他们的家园还没有出现欧洲人的永久要塞。

en:
Yakutat Bay opens between the Gulf of Alaska and glacier-cut mountains at the northern end of the Alaska Panhandle. Its Tlingit name, Yaakwdáat, means the place where canoes rest. Before European ships reached the coast, Eyak-speaking people from the Copper River country lived here, and incoming Tlingit families gradually absorbed them; by 1444 Yakutat was one of several Tlingit and mixed Tlingit-Eyak settlements drawing salmon, seals and sea otters from the bay.

Jean-François de La Pérouse visited the bay in 1786, and Alessandro Malaspina and José de Bustamante followed in 1791. In 1795 the Shelikhov-Golikov Company, managed by Alexander Baranov, founded New Russia, also called Slavorossiya, to trade for sea-otter pelts. When the colonists cut off nearby fishing grounds, a Tlingit war party attacked and destroyed the post in 1805, keeping Yakutat free of a permanent Russian settlement through 1821.
zh:
亚库塔特湾位于阿拉斯加狭地北端，处在阿拉斯加湾与冰川切割的群山之间。特林吉特语称 Yaakwdáat，意为独木舟停泊之地。欧洲船只到来前，来自铜河地区、说埃亚克语的渔人住在此地，后来迁入的特林吉特家族逐渐与他们融合；到1444年，亚库塔特已是若干特林吉特及特林吉特—埃亚克混合聚落之一，人们从湾中获取鲑鱼、海豹和海獭。

拉彼鲁兹在1786年到访此湾，马拉斯皮纳与何塞·德·布斯塔曼特于1791年相继前来。1795年，由亚历山大·巴拉诺夫管理的舍利霍夫—戈利科夫公司建立「新俄罗斯」，又称斯拉沃罗西亚，用以收购海獭皮。殖民者阻断附近渔场后，特林吉特战团在1805年攻毁据点；直到1821年，亚库塔特都没有俄国人的永久定居点。

en:
The Kenai Peninsula (Dena'ina Yaghanen, 'the good land') juts into the Gulf of Alaska between Cook Inlet and Prince William Sound. Dena'ina Athabascans, the only Alaskan Athabaskan people who made their home on salt water, lived in settled villages along the inlet and the Kenai River, taking king salmon from the river and seals and beluga from its tides; Chugach Alutiiq villages held the foggy Pacific coast. In 1444 its people traded and warred with their inlet and island neighbours, and no European ship had yet entered their waters.

Europeans came only in 1778, when James Cook sailed into the inlet and, with William Bligh charting its arms, found mudflats instead of the Northwest Passage; George Vancouver named Cook Inlet for him in 1794. In the late 1780s the Lebedev-Lastochkin company built the stockaded Fort Nikolaevskaia at the mouth of the Kenai River, the first Russian post on the Alaskan mainland, and its sea-otter crews nearly stripped the inlet. In 1797 the Dena'ina stormed the fort and the company's camps, and more than a hundred died on both sides; after 1799 the post passed to the Russian-American Company.
zh:
基奈半岛（德内因语称亚加嫩，意为「好地方」）伸入阿拉斯加湾，夹在库克湾与威廉王子湾之间。德内因阿塔帕斯克人是唯一在海边定居的阿拉斯加阿塔帕斯克族群，在库克湾沿岸和基奈河畔聚村而居，捕捞基奈河的王鲑，在潮水中猎取海豹和白鲸；多雾的太平洋沿岸则是楚加奇阿留特克人的村落。1444年时，他们与海湾和岛屿上的邻族贸易、争战，还没有一艘欧洲船驶入过这片水域。

欧洲人直到1778年才到来：詹姆斯·库克驶入海湾，威廉·布莱测绘两处分汊，发现尽头是泥滩而非西北航道；乔治·温哥华1794年将此湾以库克命名。1780年代末，列别杰夫-拉斯托奇金公司在基奈河口建起木栅围护的尼古拉堡，这是俄罗斯人在阿拉斯加大陆上的第一个据点，猎取海獭的船队几乎将湾内海獭捕尽。1797年，德内因人攻打堡垒和公司营地，双方共有一百多人丧生；1799年后该据点归入俄美公司。

en:
The Aleutian Islands stretch some twelve hundred miles from the Alaskan Peninsula almost to Kamchatka, a wind-scoured volcanic chain between the Pacific and the Bering Sea. Their people, the Unangan or Aleuts—'the original people'—lived in semi-subterranean houses in coastal villages and took nearly everything from the water: they built the swift skin-covered baidarka and hunted sea otters, seals and whales far out in the ocean. In 1444 the eastern islands were the most populous; the Unangan traded along the chain, warred with rival islands, and had never seen an outsider from beyond the fog.

Vitus Bering and Alexei Chirikov sighted the islands in 1741, and Bering died on the island later named for him; the sea-otter furs carried home by his survivors brought Siberian promyshlenniki within years, the first wintering at Attu in 1745. Hostages and the fur tribute turned Unangan men into forced hunters, and in 1763–65 the Fox Islanders burned four Russian ships; Stepan Glotov's punitive campaign killed thousands in reprisal. In 1778 James Cook fixed the islands on the map from Unalaska, trading charts there with the Russian navigator Gerasim Izmailov. The Russian-American Company then ruled the chain and Orthodox monks arrived in the 1790s. Within a generation, disease and the fur trade had cut a people once perhaps 25,000 strong to a fraction of that number.
zh:
阿留申群岛自阿拉斯加半岛向西绵延约一千九百公里，直逼堪察加，是太平洋与白令海之间一条狂风不断的火山岛链。岛上的乌南甘人（即阿留申人，族名意为「原住民」）在海岸村落里居住半地穴式房屋，几乎一切取之于海：他们造出轻快的兽皮小艇「拜达卡」，远出外海猎捕海獭、海豹和鲸。1444年时东端诸岛人口最密，乌南甘人沿岛链贸易，也与敌对岛屿争战，还从未见过雾霭之外来的外人。

1741年，白令和奇里科夫望见了这片群岛，白令本人死在后来以他命名的岛上；幸存者带回的海獭皮几年内就引来西伯利亚的猎皮人，他们1745年首次在阿图岛过冬。人质制度和毛皮贡赋把乌南甘男子变成被迫出猎的猎手，1763至1765年福克斯群岛的岛民焚毁四艘俄国船，斯捷潘·格洛托夫的讨伐队随即屠杀数千人报复。1778年，詹姆斯·库克在乌纳拉斯卡与俄国航海者格拉西姆·伊兹梅洛夫交换海图，把群岛准确地标在地图上。此后群岛归俄美公司统辖，东正教修士在1790年代到来。短短一代人的时间里，疾病和毛皮贸易就把一度约两万五千的人口削减到只剩零头。

en:
The bays, rivers and interior caribou grounds of northern and central Newfoundland were Beothuk country in 1444. Their camps were concentrated around Notre Dame and Bonavista bays, though family bands moved with the seasons between sealing coasts, salmon rivers and winter hunting grounds. They built conical bark-covered mamateeks, painted bodies and possessions with red ochre each spring, and drove migrating caribou behind long fences of brush. Each band of a few dozen kin managed its own route through a land still untouched by European settlement.

After John Cabot's 1497 voyage, Portuguese, French and English fishing ships increasingly used Newfoundland's shores, and Humphrey Gilbert claimed the island for England in 1583. At Cuper's Cove, Governor John Guy sought trade rather than flight: on 6 November 1612 his party shared a meal and gifts with Beothuk in Trinity Bay. That opening did not last. Seasonal fishing stations crowded the coast, and the Beothuk withdrew toward the Exploits River and its lakes. David Buchan's attempted friendship mission upriver in January 1811 ended with two marines dead. On 1 March 1819 John Peyton Jr.'s armed party seized a Beothuk woman and killed her husband, the band's leader; she died of tuberculosis on 8 January 1820, by which time only about thirty-one Beothuk were said to remain.
zh:
1444年，纽芬兰岛北部和中部的海湾、河流与内陆驯鹿场仍是贝奥图克人的土地。他们的营地集中在圣母湾和博纳维斯塔湾一带，各个家族群随季节在海豹海岸、鲑鱼河流与冬季猎场之间迁徙。他们搭建锥形桦皮屋，每年春天用赭红涂染身体和器物，还会设置长长的灌木栅栏，把迁徙中的驯鹿驱向猎手。每个数十人的亲族群都沿着自己的路线，在尚无欧洲人定居的土地上轮转。

约翰·卡博特1497年航行之后，葡萄牙、法国和英国渔船越来越多地使用纽芬兰海岸；汉弗莱·吉尔伯特1583年代表英格兰宣称占有此岛。在卡珀斯湾，总督约翰·盖伊试图建立贸易而非迫使对方逃离：1612年11月6日，他的队伍在三一湾与一群贝奥图克人共餐并交换礼物。这次接触未能延续。季节性渔场逐渐挤满海岸，贝奥图克人退向埃克斯普洛伊茨河及上游湖泊。1811年1月，戴维·巴肯沿河而上的友好尝试以两名海军士兵死亡告终。1819年3月1日，小约翰·佩顿的武装队伍掳走一名贝奥图克妇女，并杀死她的丈夫、也就是该群首领；她于1820年1月8日死于肺结核，当时据说只剩约三十一名贝奥图克人。

en:
Taqamkuk, later the Mi'kmaq name for Newfoundland, fits the island's broken southern shore: foggy headlands, island shelters, salmon rivers and grounds where seals, seabirds and caribou supported seasonal camps. In 1444 the island itself was Beothuk country, while the Cabot Strait coast also lay open to hunting and fishing parties crossing from the lands to the west. No European station yet ruled these bays, though the Great Banks beyond them were already among the richest cod waters in the North Atlantic.

John Cabot's 1497 voyage opened the coast to Breton, Norman, Portuguese and English fishermen; English sources place Mi'kmaq villages at St. George's Bay and Placentia by 1594. During the seventeenth century Mi'kmaq boat crews crossed the Cabot Strait to hunt along the south coast as far east as Placentia Bay, exchanging furs and provisions in French harbours. France's colonial claims ended with the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713, although French fishermen retained seasonal shore rights. In the 1760s, after the British conquest of Acadia, Chief Jeannot Pequidalouet led families from Cape Breton toward permanent camps at St. George's Bay and Bay d'Espoir; James Cook encountered a Mi'kmaq band there in May 1767. By 1818 a British visitor found another settled band at Flat Bay, holding land through loyalty to the Crown.
zh:
塔卡姆库克后来成为米克马克语中对纽芬兰的称呼，用来称呼岛南破碎的海岸十分贴切：雾中岬角、可供避浪的岛屿、鲑鱼河流，以及能以海豹、海鸟和驯鹿维持季节性营地的渔场和猎场。1444年，这座岛本身仍是贝奥图克人的土地，而卡伯特海峡沿岸也向西方各地渡海而来的狩猎和捕鱼队伍敞开。当时还没有欧洲人的据点统治这些海湾，但外侧的大浅滩已是北大西洋最丰饶的鳕鱼场之一。

约翰·卡博特1497年的航行把这片海岸带入布列塔尼、诺曼、葡萄牙和英格兰渔民的活动范围；英文资料称，到1594年圣乔治湾和普拉森西亚已有米克马克村庄。17世纪，米克马克人驾船渡过卡伯特海峡，沿南海岸狩猎，最东可达普拉森西亚湾，并在法国渔港用毛皮和给养交易。1713年《乌得勒支条约》结束了法国对纽芬兰的殖民主张，但法国渔民仍保留季节性上岸权。1760年代阿卡迪亚被英国征服后，首领让诺·佩基达卢埃（Jeannot Pequidalouet）率族人从布雷顿角岛迁来，在圣乔治湾和希望湾一带形成永久营地；詹姆斯·库克1767年5月就在圣乔治湾遇到一群米克马克人。到1818年，英国来访者已在弗拉特湾见到另一支定居族群，他们因效忠英国王室而获得土地。

en:
Onamagag is the Mi'kmaq land of Unama'ki, the rugged island later called Cape Breton, where Atlantic headlands meet the Gulf of St Lawrence. The Bras d'Or lake and ice-free harbours suited a people who moved with the fishing, sealing and hunting seasons rather than ploughing the thin soil. Family bands and district chiefs formed part of the wider Mi'kma'ki country. In 1444 the island had no European settlement; its shores and canoe routes belonged to Mi'kmaq fishermen and hunters, while European voyages into these waters still lay in the future.

John Cabot's 1497 voyage was later credited with reaching the island, though contemporary records cannot distinguish Cape Breton from Newfoundland. By the 1520s Mi'kmaq parties were trading with European fishing crews, and around 1521-22 João Álvares Fagundes planted a short-lived Portuguese fishing settlement, possibly near Ingonish. A Scottish post at Baleine in 1629 was soon destroyed by the French, who then founded small posts at Englishtown and St. Peter's. After the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713, France made the island its colony of Île Royale, moved settlers from Plaisance there, and raised Louisbourg to guard the Gulf of St Lawrence and the Grand Banks fishery; its lighthouse was built in 1734. New England troops with a British fleet took Louisbourg in 1745, and the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle returned it in 1748. British forces captured the fortress again in 1758, and the Treaty of Paris transferred Île Royale to Britain in 1763.
zh:
奥纳马加格是米克马克人所说的乌纳马基，即后来的布雷顿角岛；崎岖岛屿处在大西洋岬角与圣劳伦斯湾之间。布拉多尔湖和不冻港湾适合随渔汛、海豹猎季和狩猎季迁徙的生活，却不适合耕作贫瘠土地。岛上的家族群和地区酋长，属于更广的米克马克基世界的一部分。1444年时，这里没有欧洲人定居点，海岸与独木舟航路都属于米克马克渔人和猎人，欧洲船只尚未驶入这片水域。

约翰·卡伯特1497年的航行后来被认为可能到过此岛，但同时代记载无法区分布雷顿角与纽芬兰。到1520年代，米克马克人已同欧洲渔民交易；1521年至1522年前后，若昂·阿尔瓦雷斯·法贡德斯在此建立过一个短暂的葡萄牙渔业定居点，位置可能在英戈尼什附近。1629年苏格兰人在贝莱讷设立的据点很快被法国人摧毁，法国人随后在英吉利敦和圣彼得斯建立小据点。1713年《乌得勒支和约》后，法国把此岛建为皇家岛殖民地，把普莱桑斯移民迁来，并修筑路易斯堡以拱卫圣劳伦斯湾入口和大浅滩渔场；岛上灯塔建于1734年。新英格兰军队在英国舰队协助下于1745年攻克路易斯堡，1748年《亚琛和约》又将其归还法国。1758年英军再次占领要塞，1763年《巴黎和约》把皇家岛割让给英国。

en:
Epekwitk, ‘cradled on the waves’, lies low and red-soiled in the Gulf of St. Lawrence, cut off from the mainland by a narrow strait. The Mi'kmaq knew it also as Minegoo, and their shell middens and campsites mark shores where families took mackerel, herring, lobster and seal before moving inland to hunt moose and caribou. The island made up the Epekwitk half of the Mi'kma'ki district Epekwitk aq Piktuk, ruled by community saqamaq, a women's council and wampum keepers under the Grand Council, and its people sat with the Wolastoqiyik, Passamaquoddy and Abenaki in the Wabanaki confederacy. In 1444 no European keel had yet entered the gulf, and the island belonged wholly to its seasonal round.

In late June 1534 Jacques Cartier, coasting westward on his first voyage, became the first known European to sight its shores, and in 1604 France claimed it with the rest of Acadia as Île Saint-Jean, a claim the Mi'kmaq never acknowledged. France kept the island after Utrecht in 1713, and in 1720 Port-la-Joye became the seat of government, receiving Acadian settlers and a French garrison. A New England force out of captured Louisbourg burned the post in 1745, only to be driven to its boats by Acadian militia and Mi'kmaq fighters, who overwhelmed its garrison near the York River in 1746. Refugees from the expulsions in Nova Scotia swelled the population to nearly five thousand, but after Louisbourg fell again, Colonel Andrew Rollo landed five hundred men in August 1758, built Fort Amherst above Port-la-Joye and deported most of the population; the sinking of the transports Violet, Duke William and Ruby alone drowned more than eight hundred. Ceded outright in 1763 and surveyed into sixty-seven lots granted by an absentee-landlord lottery in 1767, the island became the separate colony of St. John's Island in 1769, with the new town of Charlottetown as its capital; in 1798 it was renamed Prince Edward Island, for the Duke of Kent.
zh:
埃佩奎特克意为「浪涛摇荡的摇篮」，低伏在圣劳伦斯湾中，红土遍布，与大陆仅隔一道狭窄海峡。米克马克人又称它米尼古；沿岸贝丘和营地遗址表明，他们的氏族曾在此捕捞鲭鱼、鲱鱼、龙虾和海豹，再转入内陆猎取驼鹿和驯鹿。本岛与大陆上的皮克图共同构成米克马克基七区之一的「埃佩奎特克-皮克图」，由各村酋长、妇女议事会和贝壳串珠保管人在大议事会统辖下治理，岛民并与沃拉斯托基伊克人、帕萨马科迪人、阿布纳基人同属瓦巴纳基联盟。1444年，还没有任何欧洲船底驶入过这片海湾，全岛完全按他们的季节节律而存在。

1534年6月底，雅克·卡蒂亚在第一次航行中沿海岸西行，成为有记载最早望见此岛的欧洲人；1604年，法国将它与阿卡迪亚其余土地一并宣称占有，命名为圣让岛，但米克马克人从未承认这一主权。1713年《乌得勒支和约》后法国保住了该岛，1720年在拉乔伊港设治，迁来阿卡迪亚移民并驻扎法军。1745年，一支新英格兰军队从攻陷的路易斯堡出击，焚毁拉乔伊港，却被阿卡迪亚民兵和米克马克战士赶回船上；1746年，他们又在约克河附近全歼这支驻军。新斯科舍驱逐行动中的难民使岛上人口增至近五千人，但路易斯堡再度陷落后，安德鲁·罗洛上校于1758年8月率五百人登陆，在拉乔伊港上方修建阿默斯特堡，并将大部分居民驱逐出境；仅维奥莱特号、威廉公爵号和鲁比号三艘运输船沉没，就有八百多人溺亡。1763年该岛被正式割让给英国，经测绘分为67块份地，1767年以抽签方式授予身在英国的外地业主；1769年它成为独立的圣约翰岛殖民地，以新建的夏洛特敦为首府，1798年为纪念肯特公爵改名为爱德华王子岛。

en:
Segepenegatic is the Mi'kmaq district of Sipekne'katik, the wooded centre of peninsular Nova Scotia between the Bay of Fundy approaches and the deep harbour later called Halifax. Its name means a place rich in wapato, the water plant whose tubers grew in the wet ground of the Shubenacadie river country. Mi'kmaq families summered on the sheltered waters of the harbour and moved inland for winter hunting, while district chiefs took part in the councils of Mi'kma'ki. In 1444 this was a country of seasonal camps and canoe portages, with no Acadian farms or British blockhouses.

France planted its wider Acadian colony on Saint Croix Island in 1604 and moved the settlement to Port-Royal in 1605, but European power long remained concentrated on the coasts. Louis-Pierre Thury opened Mission Sainte-Anne on the Shubenacadie in 1699; Antoine Gaulin gave it a permanent station during Dummer's War in 1722-25. Port-Royal fell to a British siege in 1710, and the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 assigned peninsular Acadia to Britain without ending Mi'kmaq and French influence at Shubenacadie. Jean-Louis Le Loutre arrived in 1738, and the mission served as both chapel and military base in the border wars. The disease-ruined Duc d'Anville expedition sheltered in the harbour in 1746, its commander dying before the projected counterattack collapsed. British settlers founded Halifax in 1749, and during Father Le Loutre's War Mi'kmaq warriors used Shubenacadie as a base for raids on Halifax and Dartmouth. British forces destroyed Mission Sainte-Anne in October 1755, as the Acadian deportation began. The Halifax Naval Yard was established in 1759 and supported British operations through the American Revolution and the War of 1812.
zh:
塞格佩内加蒂克是米克马克人的锡佩克内卡蒂克地区，位于新斯科舍半岛中部林地，一边通向芬迪湾，一边连接后来哈利法克斯所在的深水港。地名意为瓦帕托水生块茎丰生之地，这种植物的球茎生长在舒贝纳卡迪河流域的湿地中。米克马克家族夏季在港湾避风水域捕鱼，冬季转入内陆狩猎，地区酋长则参加米克马克基的议事会。1444年，这里只有季节性营地和独木舟搬运道，还没有阿卡迪亚农庄或英国人的堡垒。

1604年，法国在圣十字岛建立范围更广的阿卡迪亚殖民地，次年把定居点迁至皇家港，但欧洲势力长期集中在沿海。路易-皮埃尔·蒂里1699年在舒贝纳卡迪河畔开设圣安妮传教站；安托万·戈兰在1722年至1725年的达默战争期间把它建成常驻站点。皇家港于1710年在英军围攻下降落，1713年《乌得勒支和约》把阿卡迪亚半岛部分划归英国，却没有终结米克马克人和法国在舒贝纳卡迪的影响。让-路易·勒卢特尔1738年来到这里，传教站在此后的边境战争中兼具礼拜场所和军事据点的作用。1746年，疫病横行的昂维尔公爵远征队在港湾避泊，主帅病死，计划中的反攻也告失败。1749年，英国移民建立哈利法克斯；勒卢特尔神父战争期间，米克马克战士以舒贝纳卡迪为基地袭击哈利法克斯和达特茅斯。1755年10月阿卡迪亚大驱逐开始时，英军摧毁圣安妮传教站。哈利法克斯海军船坞于1759年设立，并在美国独立战争和1812年战争中支援英国军事行动。

en:
The Petkootkweak, or Petitcodiac, winds through wooded ridges to Shepody Bay at the head of the Bay of Fundy, bending almost at a right angle where Moncton now stands. Before its tide raced one of the great bores of the Fundy shore, a wall of brown water rushing in with a noise like a storm: the Mi'kmaq called the river Petkootkweak, ‘the river that bends like a bow’, and Wolastoqey speakers heard in its name the sound of thunder. The valley belonged to Siknikt, ‘the drainage place’, the south-eastern district of Mi'kma'ki, whose villages kept their own saqamaq under the Grand Council of the Wabanaki confederacy. Families wintered at the headwaters, where a carry led over to the Shubenacadie, and took salmon, sturgeon and waterfowl from the river and its marshes; their kinsmen the Wolastoqiyik held the Saint John to the west. In 1444 no European had yet settled the bay.

In 1604 the expedition of Dugua de Mons, with Champlain aboard, entered the Bay of Fundy but passed the river mouth, and Acadians from Port-Royal were the first to settle: in 1698 Pierre Thibodeau founded Chipoudie on Shepody Bay and Guillaume Blanchard opened Petitcoudiac, which with Memramcook made up the Trois-Rivières; by 1733 dyked marsh farms had climbed the river to Le Coude, the elbow bend. Utrecht in 1713 left the region under the British flag, its people the ‘neutral French’ who would not swear an unconditional oath. After Fort Beauséjour fell in June 1755, Major Joseph Frye led two hundred men to burn the Trois-Rivières, but on 4 September Charles Deschamps de Boishébert's Acadians and Mi'kmaq struck his column at Village-des-Blanchard, leaving twenty-three of his men casualties for one of their own and driving the expedition out. Some seven hundred villagers were evacuated up the gulf to the Miramichi, where famine swept the refugee camps in 1756–1758. British expeditions returned to the river in 1758, their boats harried by Joseph Broussard's partisans, and the last holdouts surrendered at Fort Cumberland in November 1759. In 1766 eight families of Pennsylvania Germans, among them Heinrich Stief, settled the deserted elbow as ‘The Bend’, the seed of the later Moncton.
zh:
佩特库特奎阿克河（法国人写作 Petitcoudiac，后作 Petitcodiac）穿过林木覆盖的丘陵，注入芬迪湾湾头的希波迪湾，在今蒙克顿附近折出一个近乎直角的大弯。河口的涌潮是芬迪湾畔最壮观的潮景之一，一道黄褐色的水墙轰然逆河而上，声如雷鸣：米克马克人称之为佩特库特奎阿克，意为「弯如弓弦的河」，而在沃拉斯托基伊克语里，这个名字的意思正是雷鸣之声。河谷属于米克马克基东南的希格尼克特区——「排水之地」，各村由酋长在瓦巴纳基联盟大议事会下自行治理。氏族在河源地带过冬，那里有一条联运道通往舒贝纳卡迪；人们在河中与沼泽间捕捞鲑鱼、鲟鱼，猎取水鸟，西边圣约翰河上住着同族的沃拉斯托基伊克人。1444年，湾畔还没有欧洲人定居。

1604年，迪瓜·德·蒙斯的探险队（尚普兰随行）驶入芬迪湾，却从河口外驶过；最先来此定居的是从罗亚尔港迁来的阿卡迪亚人：1698年，皮埃尔·蒂博多在希波迪湾畔建立希波迪村，纪尧姆·布朗沙尔开辟佩蒂特库迪亚克，二者与梅拉姆库克合称「三河」；到1733年，靠海塘围垦的沼泽农庄已沿河上溯到河弯处的勒库德。1713年《乌得勒支和约》后此地归英国所有，而居民是不肯无条件宣誓效忠的「中立法兰西人」。1755年6月博塞茹尔堡陷落后，约瑟夫·弗莱少校率两百人前去焚毁三河，但在9月4日，夏尔·德尚·德·布瓦埃贝尔率领的阿卡迪亚人与米克马克人在布朗沙尔村突袭其纵队，以己方一人的代价造成英军23人伤亡，将其逐出。约七百名村民沿湾岸撤往米拉米希，1756至1758年间饥荒席卷难民营。1758年英军再度溯河进剿，船队不断遭到约瑟夫·布鲁萨尔游击队的袭扰；最后的抵抗者于1759年11月在坎伯兰堡投降。1766年，八户宾夕法尼亚德意志移民（其中有海因里希·施蒂夫一家）在荒废的河弯处定居，称此地为「弯镇」，即后来蒙克顿的雏形。

en:
Gespegeogag, 'the end of the land' in Mi'kmaq, is the wooded finger of the Gaspé Peninsula, where the Appalachian hills run out into the Gulf of St. Lawrence around Gaspé Bay. In 1444 it was Mi'kmaq country: family bands summered on the bay and its offshore islands, fishing mackerel and salmon and taking seal and walrus, then moved inland after moose and caribou, their bark camps following the season. No European had yet charted the bay; the first sail came ninety years later.

On 24 July 1534 Jacques Cartier raised a ten-metre cross bearing the arms of Francis I on the shore of Gaspé Bay and carried off the two sons of Stadaconan chief Donnacona, the first French taking of possession in what would become Canada. For more than a century Europeans came only for the fishing season, drying cod on the beaches, until Pierre Denys de la Ronde set up the first permanent fishing post in 1676. Around 1740 the whole peninsula held only about five hundred settlers, and in 1750 the seigneurie of Pabos was its richest fishery. In September 1758, after Louisbourg fell, Wolfe and Hardy burned Gaspé, Grande-Rivière and Pabos, destroyed some two hundred fishing vessels and shipped the fishermen back to France. The coast passed to Britain with the conquest of 1760; Acadians fleeing the expulsions and, after 1784, Loyalists settled its coves, and by the early nineteenth century Jersey merchant houses ran most of the cod trade.
zh:
盖斯佩盖奥加格在米克马克语里意为「陆地的尽头」，是加斯佩半岛林木覆盖的尖端：阿巴拉契亚丘陵在此伸入圣劳伦斯湾，环抱出加斯佩湾。1444年时这里是米克马克人的土地：各家族群夏天在海湾和海岛上捕捞鲭鱼、鲑鱼，猎取海豹和海象，入冬转入内陆追逐驼鹿和驯鹿，树皮帐篷随季节搬移。此时还没有欧洲人测绘过这个海湾，第一面船帆要到九十年后才出现。

1534年7月24日，雅克·卡蒂亚在加斯佩湾岸边竖起一面十米高、刻有弗朗索瓦一世纹章的十字架，又带走斯塔达科纳酋长多纳科纳的两个儿子——这是法国在未来的加拿大第一次宣示占有。此后一个多世纪里，欧洲人只在渔季前来、在海滩上晾晒鳕鱼，直到1676年皮埃尔·德尼·德·拉龙德建立第一个常住渔业据点。1740年前后，整个半岛只有约五百名定居者；1750年，帕博领地是此地最大的渔场。1758年9月，路易堡陷落后，沃尔夫和哈代焚毁加斯佩、格朗德里维耶尔和帕博，毁掉约两百艘渔船，把渔民遣送回法国。1760年征服之后，海岸归入英国；逃避大流放的阿卡迪亚人、以及1784年之后到来的效忠派在各个小湾安家，到19世纪初，鳕鱼贸易大半落入泽西岛商号之手。

en:
Onguhiara takes its name from Onguiaahra, the Neutral community on the strait between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario. In 1444 the Niagara Peninsula belonged to the Attiwandaron, later called Neutrals because they could trade with both the Wendat and the Haudenosaunee. Their Iroquoian villages kept maize fields in the fertile lowland and deer hunt in the surrounding woods, while furs and dressed deerskins moved through the river corridor. The Niagara linked two Great Lakes, but its falls forced travellers onto a portage, giving Onguiaahra value out of proportion to its size.

The French interpreter Étienne Brûlé crossed Attiwandaron country around 1615, and the Récollet Joseph de La Roche Daillon wintered with a Neutral chief in 1626-1627; Jesuits later listed Onguioaahra on the Niagara among their villages. Epidemics and then the Beaver Wars broke that power, and in 1651 Haudenosaunee attacks dispersed the Neutral confederacy. La Salle built Fort Conti at the river mouth in 1678, where Louis Hennepin saw the falls; the Marquis de Denonville raised a short-lived second fort in 1687. Louis-Thomas Chabert de Joncaire obtained Seneca consent for a trading post in 1720, and the machicolated stone house begun in 1726 became the core of Fort Niagara, which Pierre Pouchot surrendered to Sir William Johnson in July 1759. During the American Revolution the fort was a British, Loyalist and Seneca base. Butlersburg on the west bank began in 1781, became Newark and in 1792 served as the first capital of Upper Canada, before John Graves Simcoe moved the government to York in 1797; Fort George was built nearby in the 1790s. Isaac Brock was killed at Queenston Heights on 13 October 1812 while repelling an American crossing. American troops took Fort George in May 1813 and burned Niagara on their retreat that December, and British forces stormed Fort Niagara on 19 December. The town was rebuilt after the peace.
zh:
昂古希亚拉得名于Onguiaahra，即住在伊利湖与安大略湖之间水道旁的中立人聚落。1444年，尼亚加拉半岛属于阿蒂万达伦人，他们后来被法兰西传教士称为「中立人」，因为能够同时与温达特人和豪德诺索尼人贸易。这些说易洛魁语的村民在肥沃低地种植玉米，在周围林地猎鹿，毛皮和鞣制鹿皮沿河流走廊流通。尼亚加拉河连通两大湖，瀑布却迫使旅人改行陆路转运，使昂古希亚拉的重要性远超其聚落规模。

法兰西译员艾蒂安·布吕莱约在1615年穿过阿蒂万达伦人的地域；1626年至1627年冬，重整派修士约瑟夫·德·拉罗什·达永在一位中立人首领处过冬，后来的耶稣会士把尼亚加拉河畔的Onguioaahra列入其村落。疫病与随后的海狸战争摧毁了这一势力，1651年，豪德诺索尼人的进攻使中立联盟溃散。1678年，拉萨尔在河口兴建孔蒂堡，路易·亨内平在此见到瀑布；1687年，德农维尔侯爵又修建了一座短命的要塞。1720年，路易-托马·沙贝尔·德·容凯尔取得塞内卡人同意设立商站；1726年动工的石造雉堞楼成为尼亚加拉堡的核心，皮埃尔·普绍最终于1759年7月把它交给威廉·约翰逊爵士。美国独立战争期间，这座堡垒是英军、效忠派与塞内卡人的基地。西岸的巴特勒斯堡始于1781年，后改称纽瓦克，1792年成为上加拿大第一个首府，约翰·格雷夫斯·西姆科因该地距边界过近，于1797年把政府迁往约克；乔治堡则于1790年代建在附近。1812年10月13日，艾萨克·布洛克在昆士顿高地击退美军渡河时阵亡。1813年5月美军攻占乔治堡，12月撤退时焚毁尼亚加拉，英军随即在12月19日强袭尼亚加拉堡。战争结束后，城镇在河畔重建。

en:
Attignawantan was the country of the Bear People, the largest nation of the Wendat confederacy, on the wooded peninsula between Matchedash Bay and Nottawasaga Bay. Wendat farmers had moved north from Lake Ontario by the late thirteenth century; their bark-covered longhouse villages were ringed with palisades, and fields of maize, beans and squash opened beyond the hunt paths. In the fifteenth century the Bear People joined their Cord neighbours to the southeast in the first Wendat league. By 1444, their country was already a settled western core of Wendake, connected to Algonquin fur routes leading toward Lake Nipissing and the Ottawa River.

Étienne Brûlé probably reached this country before 1615, and that summer Samuel de Champlain and the Récollet Joseph Le Caron were at Carhagouha, where Le Caron said the first recorded Catholic mass in Wendake. The Bear village of Ossossané was a principal Wendat settlement from 1632 to 1636, and Jean de Brébeuf saw its Feast of the Dead there in 1636. Jesuits had begun work among the Wendat in 1626 and built the fortified mission of Sainte-Marie near the Bear village of Quieunonascaranas in 1639; the Bear nation then had thirteen villages. Epidemics from 1634 to 1640 killed much of the population, and Haudenosaunee raids destroyed Saint-Ignace and Saint-Louis in March 1649. Sainte-Marie was burned and abandoned, while survivors starved on Christian Island before fleeing toward Quebec in 1650. Ojibwe families later used the emptied shore; after a fur post opened on Matchedash Bay in the late 1770s, British treaties of 1785, 1798 and 1815 opened the way for Penetanguishene Road and its garrison.
zh:
阿蒂格纳万坦是温达特（休伦）联盟中人口最多的熊族之地，位于马奇特达什湾与诺塔瓦萨加湾之间的林木半岛。温达特农人在13世纪后期已从安大略湖北迁，树皮长屋村落外筑木栅，猎路之后是玉米、菜豆和南瓜田。15世纪时，熊族与东南邻的绳族结成温达特最早的联盟。到1444年，这里已是温达克西部定居密集的核心，并同通往尼皮辛湖和渥太华河的阿尔冈昆毛皮商路相连。

艾蒂安·布吕莱可能在1615年以前抵达此地；同年夏天，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰和重整奥斯定会传教士约瑟夫·勒卡龙来到Carhagouha，勒卡龙在那里主持了温达克有记载的第一场天主教弥撒。熊族村落Ossossané在1632年至1636年间是温达特的主要村落之一，让·德·布雷伯夫1636年在此目睹亡者之宴。耶稣会士1626年开始向温达特传教，1639年在熊族村落Quieunonascaranas附近修建设防的圣玛丽传教站；当时熊族共有十三座村落。1634年至1640年的疫病夺去大量人口，1649年3月，豪德诺索尼人的袭击摧毁圣伊尼亚斯和圣路易。圣玛丽被焚毁放弃，幸存者在克里斯蒂安岛挨饿，1650年逃往魁北克方向。后来阿尔冈昆人的奥吉布瓦家族使用这片空出的湖岸；1770年代末马奇特达什湾开设毛皮站后，英国在1785年、1798年和1815年的条约为佩内唐吉申道路和驻军据点打开了通路。

en:
Attigneenongnahac was the country of the Cord People, one of the oldest Wendat nations, on the well-drained rises of Mount St. Louis Ridge between the Sturgeon and Coldwater rivers. Wendat farmers built palisaded longhouse villages here and planted maize, beans and squash on the lighter upland soils. In the fifteenth century the Cord People joined the neighbouring Bear People to form the first league within Wendake. In 1444 their ridge was therefore the southeastern agricultural core of the emerging Huron confederacy, with tracks leading west to Bear towns, east toward Rock country and south toward other Iroquoian peoples.

By the time Samuel de Champlain travelled through Wendake in 1615, the Cord People were one of its four nations, and in 1640 their territory contained three principal villages. Jesuit missionaries passed through these fields in the 1630s, but the epidemics of 1634 to 1640 weakened the villages before the Haudenosaunee invasion of the spring of 1649. More than 300 Wendat survivors reached Quebec under Father Paul Ragueneau in the summer of 1650. Of the groups there, the Cord People alone refused to leave the protection of Fort Saint-Louis the following spring, becoming part of the Huron community that later took root at Lorette. Their old ridge was left largely empty; Ojibwe families later travelled through it, and the British treaties of 1798 and 1815 opened the district around Penetanguishene and Lake Simcoe.
zh:
阿蒂格内农纳哈克是绳族之地。绳族是温达特最古老的族群之一，住在斯特金河与科尔德沃特河之间、排水良好的圣路易斯岭高地上。温达特农人在此筑起木栅环绕的长屋村，在较轻的高地土壤中种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜。15世纪时，绳族与相邻的熊族结成温达克最早的联盟。因此到1444年，这片山岭已是形成中的休伦联盟东南面的农业核心，小路向西通往熊族村落，向东通往岩族之地，向南则连接其他易洛魁语族群。

塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1615年穿行温达克时，绳族已是联盟四大族群之一；到1640年，其境内有三座主要村落。1630年代，耶稣会传教士经过这些农田，但1634年至1640年的疫病先削弱了村落，1649年春豪德诺索尼人又大举入侵。1650年夏，三百多名温达特幸存者在保罗·拉格诺神父带领下抵达魁北克。在当地各族群中，唯有绳族在第二年春天不愿离开圣路易堡的保护，后来成为定居于洛雷特的休伦社群的一部分。他们原来的山岭大体荒弃，后来奥吉布瓦家族在此往来；1798年和1815年的英国条约使佩内唐吉申与锡姆科湖周围地区向殖民开拓开放。

en:
Maisouna covered the lower valley of the river later called the Saint-Maurice, where islands split the current into three channels before it entered the St. Lawrence and the French later built Trois-Rivières. In 1444 no European post stood there. Laurentian peoples lived in semi-sedentary riverside communities, cultivating maize, beans and squash around longhouse villages, while Algonquian-speaking hunters used the forests and river crossings; later French regional histories place the Maisouna between Stadacona and Hochelaga.

Jacques Cartier stopped at the site on 12 October 1535, named the river the Fouez, and planted a cross on Île Saint-Quentin. The Laurentian settlements had vanished before French traders returned around 1600. Laviolette founded the permanent post of Trois-Rivières on 4 July 1634, and it became a fur market between Quebec and Montreal, exposed to Mohawk raids; in June 1641 about 350 Mohawk warriors came there seeking firearms. The town became seat of a regional government in 1665, Ursuline nuns opened a school in 1697, and the Great Peace of Montreal ended the long raiding wars on 4 August 1701. Work at the Forges Saint-Maurice began in 1730, Trois-Rivières passed to Britain in 1760, and a Continental Army invasion force was defeated outside the town on 8 June 1776.
zh:
迈索纳位于后来得名圣莫里斯河的下游，河水流经岛屿时分作三道水口，再注入圣劳伦斯河，法国人后来便在这处要冲建立三河城。1444年时，欧洲人尚未在此设立据点。劳伦提亚人在河畔半定居，围绕长屋村落种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，阿尔冈昆语猎人则穿行于森林和渡口之间；后来的法语地方史把迈索纳人置于斯塔达科纳与奥谢拉加之间。

1535年10月12日，雅克·卡蒂埃途经此地，把这条河命名为富瓦河，并在圣康坦岛竖起十字架。等到法国商人在1600年前后重返时，劳伦提亚人的聚落已经消失。1634年7月4日，拉维奥莱特建立永久据点三河城，使这里成为魁北克与蒙特利尔之间的毛皮市场，也长期暴露在莫霍克人的袭掠之下；1641年6月，约三百五十名莫霍克战士前来索要火枪。1665年，三河城成为地方政府驻地；1697年，乌尔苏拉会修女在此开办学校；1701年8月4日，《蒙特利尔大和平》结束了漫长的袭掠战争。圣莫里斯锻铁厂于1730年开炉，三河城在1760年随新法兰西转入英国之手；1776年6月8日，一支大陆军进攻部队在城外战败。

en:
Lake Nipissing is a broad, shallow water between the Ottawa River and Georgian Bay, reaching Lake Huron through the French River. The Nipissing, an Anishinaabe people of Ojibwe and Algonquin kin, kept their villages on its shores and islands, took sturgeon from its shoals and passed on the furs of the northern forests along the canoe corridor that ran by the Mattawa River to the Ottawa and the St Lawrence; later French visitors, struck by their seers, would call them the 'Sorcerers'. In 1444 the lake country belonged to these middlemen of the northern trade and no European had yet entered it.

Étienne Brûlé, travelling with Huron bands, was the first European to reach the lake about 1610, and Samuel de Champlain followed in 1615 on his way to Huronia; Jean Nicolet kept a cabin and trading house there from the mid-1620s until 1633. The Jesuit Claude Pijart spent nine years among the Nipissing and gathered a small Christian flock, but in 1649–50 the Iroquois overran the country and the Nipissing fled with the Amikwa to distant Lake Nipigon, where Claude Allouez found them in 1667. By 1671 they were back on their own lake. Voyageurs then made it a link on the Montreal fur route, and around 1780 the North West Company raised Fort La Ronde on its shores; the post passed to the Hudson's Bay Company with the merger of 1821.
zh:
尼皮辛湖是一片宽阔水浅的湖泊，地处渥太华河与乔治亚湾之间，湖水经弗伦奇河注入休伦湖。尼皮辛人是兼有奥吉布瓦与阿尔冈昆渊源的阿尼什纳贝人，村落散布在湖岸与岛上，在浅滩捕捞鲟鱼，并沿马塔瓦河—渥太华河—圣劳伦斯河的独木舟走廊转销北方森林的毛皮；后来的法国人震慑于他们的先知，称他们为「巫师」。1444年，这片湖区属于这些北方贸易的中间人，欧洲人尚未涉足。

1610年前后，随休伦人队伍游历的艾蒂安·布吕莱成为第一个见到此湖的欧洲人；1615年，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰在前往休伦尼亚途中经过此地，让·尼科莱则在1620年代中期至1633年住在湖畔，设有木屋与贸易站。耶稣会士克洛德·皮雅尔在尼皮辛人中传教九年，聚集起一小群信徒，但1649—1650年易洛魁人攻入此地，尼皮辛人随阿米克瓦人远逃至尼皮贡湖，克洛德·阿卢埃1667年在那里找到了他们；到1671年，他们已回到故乡的湖边。此后船夫们把这里当作通往蒙特利尔毛皮商路的一站，1780年前后西北公司在湖畔建起拉龙德堡；1821年公司合并，这座贸易站归入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
The Weskarini, the Wàwàckeciriniwak or 'people of the deer', were the Algonquin band the French called La Petite Nation, the Little Nation, to distinguish them from the Kichesipirini of the upper Ottawa. Their country ran along the north bank of the Ottawa and up the Lièvre, Rouge and Petite-Nation rivers, whose name remembers them. They lived by the seasonal hunt, fishing and gathering, their beaver pelts feeding the trade networks of the Ottawa valley, and they held the forested mountain the French named Mont Tremblant as Manitonga Soutana, the mountain of the spirits. In 1444 these Laurentian valleys belonged to the Weskarini alone, and no European canoe had yet entered them.

Champlain met Ouescharini bands on his way up the Ottawa in 1613, and they became French allies, trading at the mouths of the Gatineau, Saint-Maurice and Dumoine and wintering with their Huron friends. The Beaver Wars undid them: when the Iroquois struck in 1654, the main band was cut to pieces and survivors fled toward Trois-Rivières, where the Jesuits sheltered only those who accepted baptism. By the later seventeenth century the Weskarini ceased to appear as a people, their kin merged into other Algonquin communities, and their valleys were left to passing fur brigades. On 16 May 1674 the French West India Company granted the empty country as the seigneury of La Petite-Nation, the westernmost in New France, to Bishop François de Laval; he planned an Algonquin mission there, then thought better of it and gave the seigneury to the Séminaire de Québec in 1680. Joseph Papineau bought it in 1801 and 1803, set a sawmill on the river and brought in New England lumbermen, and in 1817 the estate passed to his son Louis-Joseph.
zh:
韦斯卡里尼人自称瓦瓦克齐里尼瓦克，意为「鹿族」，是阿尔冈昆人的一支；法国人称他们为「小民族」（La Petite Nation），以区别于渥太华河上游的「大民族」基奇西皮里尼人。他们的家园沿渥太华河北岸展开，深入 lièvre 河、鲁日河和因他们得名的小民族河上游。他们按季节狩猎、捕鱼、采集为生，所产海狸皮进入渥太华河谷的贸易网络；那座被法国人叫作蒙特朗布朗的山林，在他们心中是神灵之山马尼通加·苏塔纳。1444年时，这些劳伦琴山谷只属于韦斯卡里尼人，还没有欧洲人的独木舟驶入。

1613年，尚普兰溯渥太华河而上时遇见了韦斯卡里尼人；他们后来成为法国盟友，在加蒂诺河、圣莫里斯河和迪穆万河口贸易，并与交好的休伦人一同过冬。海狸战争葬送了他们：1654年易洛魁人来袭，主体队伍被击溃，幸存者逃向三河市，而耶稣会只收留接受洗礼的人。到17世纪后期，韦斯卡里尼作为一个族群不再见于记载，余部并入其他阿尔冈昆社群，山谷只剩过往的毛皮商队。1674年5月16日，法国西印度公司把这片人烟稀少的土地封为主教方济各·德·拉瓦尔的「小民族领地」，那是新法兰西最西端的领地；他原想在此为阿尔冈昆人设传教站，后来作罢，1680年将领地赠予魁北克神学院。约瑟夫·帕皮诺1801年和1803年分两次买下领地，在河上建起锯木厂，招来新英格兰伐木工人；1817年，产业传到他的儿子路易-约瑟夫手中。

en:
The island beneath Mount Royal lies where the Ottawa River meets the St. Lawrence, just short of the Lachine Rapids that give the place its Iroquoian name, Osheaga, the 'big rapids'. In 1444 it is Laurentian country: St. Lawrence Iroquoians tend fields of maize, beans and squash around stockaded villages of bark-covered longhouses and fish one of the river's richest fisheries. Hochelaga, girdled by its wooden palisade near the mountain, is the greatest of these towns, and the rapids at its gate mark the head of sea navigation, where inland canoe brigades meet ocean-going vessels.

Jacques Cartier, sailing upstream in search of a route to China, landed on 2 October 1535 and was led through Hochelaga the next day; he named the hill above the village Mount Royal. When he returned in 1541 the town was already gone, and by the end of the century warfare and dispersal had emptied the valley of its Iroquoians; in 1603 Champlain found only an abandoned hunting ground. In 1611 he cleared a fur-trade station, Place Royale, below the rapids, and on 17 May 1642 Maisonneuve's company of the Société Notre-Dame founded Ville-Marie, where Jeanne Mance opened the Hôtel-Dieu. Beset by Iroquois raids — the settlement of Lachine was destroyed in 1689 — the town grew into the hub of the western fur trade and the launching point for Jolliet, La Salle and the Vérendryes. The Great Peace of Montreal brought 1,300 Indigenous delegates to the town in August 1701, but after the fall of Quebec, Vaudreuil surrendered it to Amherst without a fight on 8 September 1760.
zh:
皇家山下的岛屿坐落在渥太华河注入圣劳伦斯河之处，上游便是拉欣急流——「奥谢阿加」这个易洛魁语地名意为「大急流」。1444年时，这里是劳伦提亚人的土地：圣劳伦斯易洛魁人在木栅环绕、树皮长屋组成的村庄周围种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，又在河上经营全流域最丰饶的渔场。奥什拉加是这些村镇中最大的一座，木栅圈起的村子依皇家山而立；村前的急流是海船航道的尽头，内陆独木舟商队与海船在此交接货物。

1535年10月2日，为寻找通往中国水道而溯河上行的雅克·卡蒂埃登岛，次日被迎入奥什拉加，并把村旁的山丘命名为皇家山。1541年他重返此地时，村庄已不复存在；到16世纪末，战乱与流徙使河谷中的易洛魁人散失殆尽，1603年尚普兰见到的只是一片荒废的猎场。1611年，他在急流脚下辟出名为「皇家广场」的毛皮贸易站；1642年5月17日，迈松纳夫率领蒙特利尔圣母使团的人马建立维尔马利，让娜·芒斯在此办起主宫医院。小镇顶住了易洛魁人的反复袭扰——1689年拉欣村即遭其摧毁——日后成为西部毛皮贸易的枢纽，若利埃、拉萨尔、拉韦朗德里等探险家都由此深入大陆。1701年8月，1300名原住民代表会聚于此，缔结《蒙特利尔大和约》；魁北克陷落后，沃德勒伊于1760年9月8日不战而降，城市归入英国之手。

en:
At the narrows where the St. Lawrence squeezes between Cape Diamant and the heights opposite — Kebec, 'where the river narrows', in Algonquin — stood Stadacona, a St. Lawrence Iroquoian town on the Saint-Charles River. Its people lived in bark longhouses above fields of maize, beans and squash and took fish and eel from the great river; their word kanata, a village, would become Canada. In 1444 the river belonged to such towns, and no European sail had yet entered the gulf.

That ended in September 1535, when Jacques Cartier wintered beside the town: scurvy killed a quarter of his men until the Stadaconans showed him annedda, a white-cedar brew that cured the rest. In May 1536 he carried off chief Donnacona and his two sons; none ever returned. In August 1541 he came back with five ships and raised Charlesbourg-Royal on the Cap-Rouge, France's first settlement in North America, but sickness and hostility drove the last colonists out in June 1543. When Champlain passed the narrows, Stadacona had vanished, wasted by war, disease and the cooling climate, and only Innu and Algonquin bands still came to fish eel. On 3 July 1608 Champlain built his Habitation below Cape Diamant, the seed of Quebec. The Kirkes took it in July 1629, the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye restored it in 1632, and Champlain died there in 1635.

From 1663 Quebec was the capital of royal New France, seat of a bishopric from 1674. Frontenac drove off Phips's invasion in 1690, and Walker's great fleet was wrecked in the river fogs in 1711 before reaching the town. In 1759 Wolfe's men climbed the heights and on 13 September beat Montcalm on the Plains of Abraham, where both generals fell; the city surrendered five days later. Lévis retook it at Sainte-Foy in April 1760 but could not hold it, and France ceded Canada in 1763. The Quebec Act of 1774 let the French keep faith and laws, so the American assault on New Year's Eve 1775 died in the snow with Montgomery; the siege ended in May 1776. In 1791 Quebec became capital of Lower Canada, and by the early nineteenth century it was North America's third-largest port, busy with timber ships.
zh:
圣劳伦斯河在钻石角与对岸高地之间骤然收窄——阿尔冈昆语称这里为 Kébec，意即「河流变窄之处」。北岸圣夏尔河畔坐落着圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的城镇斯塔达科纳，居民住树皮长屋，屋前是玉米、菜豆和南瓜田，又在大河里捕鱼和鳗鱼；他们表示村庄的词 kanata 日后演成了「加拿大」。1444年时，大河仍属于这样的村镇，还没有欧洲船帆驶入海湾。

这一切在1535年9月终结：雅克·卡蒂亚在城边过冬，坏血病夺走他四分之一的人手，直到斯塔达科纳人教他用白雪杉熬制 annedda 汤剂，其余人才被治愈。1536年5月他带走酋长多纳科纳和他的两个儿子，三人再无一人归来。1541年8月，他率五艘船重返故地，在卡普魯日筑起法国在北美的第一个定居点「皇家夏尔堡」，但疾病和敌意使最后一批殖民者在1543年6月撤离。等尚普兰经过窄峡时，斯塔达科纳已经消失——一般认为毁于战争、疫病和气候转冷，只有因努和阿尔冈昆游群还来此捕鳗。1608年7月3日，尚普兰在钻石角下建起「居所」，这便是魁北克的起点。1629年7月柯克兄弟夺城，1632年《圣日耳曼昂莱条约》将其归还，尚普兰1635年在此去世。

1663年起，魁北克成为王家新法兰西的首府，1674年起设主教区。1690年，弗龙特纳克击退菲普斯的入侵；1711年，沃克的大舰队还没抵达城市，就在河上浓雾中覆没。1759年，沃尔夫的部队攀上峭壁，9月13日在亚伯拉罕平原击败蒙卡尔姆，两位将领双双殒命，城市于五天后投降。莱维1760年4月在圣福瓦夺回城市却无力守住，1763年法国割让加拿大。1774年《魁北克法案》保住了法裔的信仰与法律，所以1775年新年前夜美军的强攻和蒙哥马利一起死在雪里，围城延续到1776年5月。1791年魁北克成为下加拿大首府，到19世纪初已是北美第三大港，满是运木材的船只。

en:
Toutouskak is the bay the French called Tadoussac, where the Saguenay fjord's black water meets the St. Lawrence estuary. In 1444 it was summer country of the Innu, whom the French would name the Montagnais: they camped on the shore to hunt seal and meet the canoes that came down the Saguenay with furs. When Jacques Cartier stopped there in 1535 he found Innu sealing parties, and by the end of the century Basque whalers flensed their catch on the beach while more than a thousand Innu, Algonquin and Etchemin gathered each summer to barter beaver pelts with the European ships, the busiest fur rendezvous in North America by 1600.

In 1600 Pierre de Chauvin and François Gravé Du Pont, holding Henri IV's monopoly, built a trading house at the mouth of the Saguenay; sixteen men wintered and only five survived, yet Tadoussac became France's first enduring settlement in North America. At a solemn summer feast in 1603 Gravé and Champlain made alliance with the Innu, Algonquin and Etchemin. In 1608 Basque captains answered Gravé's monopoly claims with cannon fire and wounded him before Champlain negotiated a truce. Franciscan Recollet friars opened a mission in 1615, and for thirty years Tadoussac was the only seaport on the St. Lawrence; settlers whaled out of the bay from 1632, and a new mission chapel was raised in 1747. The post joined the royal King's Posts in 1720, kept trading after the British conquest, was leased to the North West Company in 1802, and passed to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821.
zh:
塔杜萨克位于萨格奈峡湾深色的江水与圣劳伦斯河口湾交汇处。1444年，这里是因努人——法国人后来称他们为蒙塔涅人——的夏日之地：他们在岸边扎营捕猎海豹，并接应从萨格奈河载着毛皮顺流而下的独木舟。1535年卡蒂亚途经此地，见到的正是捕猎海豹的因努人。到16世纪末，巴斯克捕鲸人在海滩上解剖鲸尸、熬炼鲸油，每年夏天还有上千名因努人、阿尔冈昆人和埃切明人聚集于此，用河狸皮与欧洲商船交易；到1600年，这里已是北美最繁忙的毛皮会市。

1600年，持有亨利四世垄断权的皮埃尔·德·肖万与弗朗索瓦·格拉韦·迪蓬在萨格奈河口建起贸易屋；十六人留下过冬，仅五人生还，而塔杜萨克却就此成为法国在北美第一个延续下来的定居点。1603年夏天，迪蓬与尚普兰在一场隆重的宴会上同因努人、阿尔冈昆人和埃切明人结盟。1608年，巴斯克船长们以炮火回应迪蓬的垄断要求、将他击伤，最后由尚普兰谈成休战。1615年方济各重整派修士开设传教点；此后三十年塔杜萨克是圣劳伦斯河上唯一的海港，1632年起定居者从湾口出航捕鲸，1747年又建起一座新的传教小教堂。商站1720年并入王室直辖的国王据点，英国征服后贸易不辍，1802年租给西北公司，1821年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
The wide bay the Innu called Uashat, 'the great bay', is guarded by seven islands and by the mouths of the Moisie and Sainte-Marguerite rivers. It was the summer ground of two Montagnais bands, the Chisedec — a Mi'kmaq name for the Moisie — and the Oumamiwek west of the Sainte-Marguerite. Families came down from inland hunting grounds to spear salmon, hunt seal and whale and meet in trade, then turned back upriver to winter on caribou in the country they called Nitassinan. By the early 1500s Basque whalers were sailing in each season, yet in 1444 the coast had no European settlement and the year still followed the old round.

Jacques Cartier entered the bay on 18 August 1535 and set down the seven islands as the Ysles Rondes, finding Basque fishermen there before him. In 1603 Champlain anchored off the river he called Saincte Marguerite. On 7 June 1651 the Jesuit Jean de Quen said the first mass and opened the Ange-Gardien mission. François Bissot set up the Sept-Îles fur post in 1661, trading from about 1676 within the king's reserved Domaine du roy, and Louis Jolliet opened another at the Moisie mouth in 1679. The Innu signed the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. In August 1711 Admiral Walker's expedition against Quebec, groping through fog, lost eight ships and more than 900 men on the Île-aux-Œufs reefs west of the bay, and the point facing the reefs was named Pointe-aux-Anglais. British raiders destroyed the post more than once until it was rebuilt in 1761; the North West Company held it from 1802, and it passed to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821.
zh:
因努人称作 Uashat（意即「大海湾」）的宽阔海湾被七座岛屿环护，穆瓦西河与圣玛格丽特河分别从东西两侧在此入海。湾畔夏天是两支蒙塔涅人的聚地：切斯迪克人（Chisedec 本是米克马克人对穆瓦西河的旧称），以及圣玛格丽特河以西的奥马米韦克人。各家从内陆猎场赶来叉鲑鱼、捕海豹和鲸、彼此交易，入冬再溯河返回他们称作尼塔希南的故地，靠驯鹿过冬。到16世纪初，巴斯克捕鲸船已年年到此，但1444年时沿岸还没有欧洲人定居，岁月仍按古老的节律轮转。

1535年8月18日，雅克·卡蒂亚驶入海湾，把七岛记作 Ysles Rondes，发现已有巴斯克渔人先他而至。1603年，尚普兰在他称作 Saincte Marguerite 的河外抛锚。1651年6月7日，耶稣会士让·德康做了第一场弥撒，并创立守护天使传教所。1661年，弗朗索瓦·比索在国王保留的王家领地内建起七岛毛皮站，约1676年起营业；路易·若列又于1679年在穆瓦西河口另设一站。1701年，因努人签署《蒙特利尔大和约》。1711年8月，沃克海军上将远征魁北克的舰队在雾中摸路，八艘船在湾西的蛋岛礁群失事，九百多人丧生，正对礁群的海角遂得名「英格兰角」。殖民战争中贸易站几度被英军摧毁，1761年重建；该站自1802年归西北公司经营，1821年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Chisedec was the name later given to the Innu band around Uashat, the great bay that became Sept-Îles, and Mishta-shipu, the Moisie River. The river cuts south through spruce and birch country to the Gulf of St Lawrence and is one of eastern North America's richest salmon waters. In 1444 its people, whom the French would later call Montagnais, moved between coast and boreal interior in portable skin tents. They took salmon and marine mammals in season and followed caribou and moose through Nitassinan, their homeland, while no European mission or trading post yet stood on the bay.

When Jacques Cartier sailed past the islands in 1535, he found Basque fishermen already coming annually for cod and whales, and recorded them as the Ysles Rondes. The fish and fur trades drew the French to settle at the anchorage. Jean de Quen founded the L'Ange-Gardien mission there in 1650, a fur post was operating by 1658, and Louis Jolliet established another in 1679. Chisedec hunters were thus tied to New France's commerce and its wars with the English and Haudenosaunee. After Britain took Canada in 1763, the North West Company took over the Sept-Îles post in 1802; in 1821, the year of its merger with the Hudson's Bay Company, the bay became a Hudson's Bay post.
zh:
切斯迪克是后来文献对一支因努人群的称呼，其活动中心是Uashat大湾与Mishta-shipu大河；前者日后成为七岛，后者即穆瓦西河。穆瓦西河穿过云杉和桦木林地，南入圣劳伦斯湾，是北美东部鲑鱼最丰沛的河流之一。1444年，这些后来被法国人称作蒙塔格奈人的居民带着可搬运的兽皮帐篷，在海岸与北方森林内陆间往返：渔季捕捞鲑鱼和海兽，狩猎季则在故土Nitassinan内追逐驯鹿与驼鹿。那时海湾边还没有欧洲传教站或贸易栈。

1535年雅克·卡蒂埃驶过群岛时，已有巴斯克渔民年年到此捕鳕和捕鲸；他把这群岛屿记作Ysles Rondes。渔业和毛皮贸易随后吸引法国人来到这个锚地。1650年，让·德·康在此创立「守护天使」传教站；1658年当地已有毛皮贸易栈，路易·若列又于1679年另设一处。切斯迪克猎人由此被卷入新法兰西的商业网络，以及它同英格兰人和易洛魁联盟的战争。1763年英国夺取加拿大后，西北公司于1802年接掌七岛贸易站；1821年西北公司与哈德逊湾公司合并，海湾边的据点也转入哈德逊湾公司名下。

en:
The Qikirmiut province takes its name from the Qikirtamiut, the Inuit islanders of the Belcher Islands. The archipelago's roughly 1,500 treeless islands lie in southeastern Hudson Bay, off the eastern shore of the bay. Dorset communities used them between 500 BCE and 1000 CE, and Thule hunters arrived between 1200 and 1500. In 1444 their Inuit descendants moved by kayak and umiak among islands and sea ice, taking seals, walrus, Arctic char, eiders and caribou; no European fort or boundary had yet entered these waters.

Henry Hudson sighted the archipelago in 1610. The successful fur voyage of 1668 prepared Charles II's 1670 charter, which folded the islands into the Hudson's Bay Company's Rupert's Land. Anglo-French rivalry then swept the bay: Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville defeated the Royal Navy in 1697, and the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht confirmed British rights, though forts and fighting centred on the busier southern routes. No permanent European post was built on the Belchers before 1821, so the islanders continued their seasonal rounds on ice and open water.
zh:
基蒂克美奥特（Qikirmiut）得名自Qikirtamiut，即贝尔彻群岛的因纽特岛民。约一千五百个无树岛屿散布在哈得孙湾东南部的湾口，临近哈得孙湾东岸。多塞特人在公元前500年至公元1000年间使用这些岛屿，1200年至1500年间，图勒猎手来到这里。1444年，他们的因纽特后裔乘皮艇和木架皮舟往来于岛屿与浮冰之间，猎捕海豹、海象、北极红点鲑、欧绒鸭和驯鹿；欧洲人的要塞和边界此时尚未进入这片水域。

亨利·哈德逊于1610年望见这座群岛。1668年英国商船在哈得孙湾成功进行毛皮贸易，为查理二世1670年颁发特许状铺平道路，群岛也被划入哈得孙湾公司的鲁伯特地。英法争夺随后席卷海湾：皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德·伊贝维尔1697年击败英国皇家海军舰队，1713年《乌得勒支和约》确认英国的权利，但要塞和战事主要集中在更繁忙的南方航路。直到1821年以前，贝尔彻群岛仍未建立欧洲人常设商站，岛民继续依季节在冰面和开阔水域间往来营生。

en:
Cisasipi is a spelling of Cisâsîpî, Chisasibi, 'Great River', the East Cree country around the mouth of the La Grande on the rocky eastern shore of James Bay. At European contact, the peoples on both shores were Cree, and for centuries families moved nomadically between coast and interior, fishing, hunting and trapping along rivers that froze through the long winter. In 1444 no Atlantic ship had yet entered James Bay, and the riverside camps lived on fish, game and furs taken for their own use.

Henry Hudson entered James Bay in 1610, and the successful fur voyage of 1668, followed by Charles II's 1670 charter, opened the shore to the Hudson's Bay Company. Because French and independent traders could reach this East Main overland from the Saint Lawrence, the Company long found it harder to control than posts farther west. In 1803 it built Fort George on Fort George Island at the mouth of the Great River. The post drew Cree hunters into a regular fur trade, but in 1821 most families still kept their seasonal round rather than a permanent village.
zh:
奇萨西比（Cisasipi）是克里语Cisâsîpî的游戏拼写，即奇萨西比，意为「大河」，指东克里人在詹姆斯湾岩石东岸、拉格朗德河口一带的土地。欧洲人到来时，海湾两岸的居民都是克里人；许多世纪以来，家族在海岸与内陆间迁徙，沿河流捕鱼、狩猎和设陷阱，度过漫长的冰封冬季。1444年，尚无来自大西洋的船只进入詹姆斯湾，河畔营地以鱼、猎物和自用毛皮为生。

亨利·哈德逊于1610年驶入詹姆斯湾；1668年毛皮航行成功后，查理二世1670年颁发特许状，哈得孙湾公司由此进入这片海岸。由于法国商人和独立商人可从圣劳伦斯方向由陆路抵达东岸，公司长期难以像控制更西的商站那样控制这里。1803年，公司在大河口的乔治堡岛设立乔治堡。商站把克里猎手纳入固定的毛皮贸易，但到1821年，多数家族仍按季节迁徙，尚未形成永久村落。

en:
Iyiyiw is a spelling of iiyiyuu, the East Cree or Eeyou self-designation, meaning 'human being'. This taiga-and-lake country southeast of James Bay is part of Eeyou Istchee, its routes running by the Eastmain and Rupert rivers toward Lake Mistassini. In 1444 it had neither town nor fixed border: Eeyou families summered by the lakes, then moved to inland hunting and trapping grounds for caribou, beaver, marten, fish and waterfowl. Mistassini means 'big rock' in Cree or Innu, and Cree and Innu travellers already knew the portage chain from the Saguenay to the Rupert.

Henry Hudson reached James Bay in 1610, opening the Eeyou coast to Europeans. In 1663 Guillaume Couture's party, guided by Indigenous travellers, took forty-four canoes up the Saguenay to Lake Mistassini and on toward the Rupert. In 1671 Jean Talon sent the Jesuit Charles Albanel with Paul Denys de Saint-Simon; they wintered among the Mistassini, baptised about a hundred adults and as many children, and reached James Bay on 28 June 1672. In 1674 the English seized Albanel on the Rupert, a sign of the Anglo-French struggle for the fur route. Lakeside trading posts moved several times before the Hudson's Bay Company fixed the post at present Mistissini in 1821.
zh:
伊伊尤（Iyiyiw）是东克里人自称iiyiyuu（Eeyou）的游戏拼写，意为「人」。这片詹姆斯湾东南的泰加林与湖沼地带属于东克里祖地埃尤乌伊斯特奇，通路沿东梅因河和鲁珀特河伸向米斯塔西尼湖。1444年，这里既无城镇也无固定边界：东克里家族在湖畔度夏，入秋后转入内陆猎场和陷阱地，获取驯鹿、河狸、貂、鱼和水鸟。米斯塔西尼在克里语或因努语中意为「大岩石」，克里人与因努旅行者早已知道从萨格奈河到鲁珀特河的水陆联运路线。

亨利·哈德逊于1610年到达詹姆斯湾，欧洲人由此打开东克里海岸的门户。1663年，纪尧姆·库蒂尔一行在原住民向导带领下，乘四十四艘独木舟上溯萨格奈河，抵达米斯塔西尼湖，再继续前往鲁珀特河。1671年，让·塔隆派遣耶稣会士夏尔·阿尔巴内尔与保罗·德尼·德·圣西蒙北上；他们在米斯塔西尼人中过冬，为约一百名成人和同样数目的儿童施洗，并于1672年6月28日到达詹姆斯湾。1674年，英国人在鲁珀特河拘押阿尔巴内尔，显示法英对毛皮通道的争夺。湖畔商站此后多次迁移，哈得孙湾公司最终于1821年把商站设在今米斯塔西尼的位置。

en:
At Baawitigong, the 'place of the rapids', the waters of Lake Superior race down the St. Marys River into Lake Huron. The Ojibwe kept a permanent village beside the white water, taking sturgeon in spring and whitefish in autumn, when thousands gathered from the surrounding Anishinaabe nations to fish and trade; the Odawa and Potawatomi came too, and the catfish-named Marameg belonged to the same country. In 1444 the Sault was one of the great meeting-places of the upper lakes, and its people knew nothing as yet of Europeans.

Étienne Brûlé, travelling with Huron guides, was the first European to see the rapids in 1623 according to French reckoning, and the French named them the Sault de Gaston after the brother of Louis XIII. In 1668 Claude Dablon and Jacques Marquette founded a Jesuit mission there and renamed the place Sault Sainte-Marie, and on 4 June 1671 Saint-Lusson, before chiefs of fourteen nations, proclaimed the whole Lake Superior country for France. In 1736 Louis Denys de La Ronde opened a shipyard at Pointe-aux-Pins on the north shore, launching the first decked vessel onto Lake Superior to search for copper. The country passed to Britain in 1763; around 1790 the North West Company built a post and in 1798 the first lock past the rapids. On 20 July 1814 an American raid burned the company depot and the lock, but the British held the Sault.
zh:
在巴维蒂冈——奥吉布瓦语意为「瀑布之地」，苏必利尔湖的湖水经圣玛丽斯河急泻入休伦湖。奥吉布瓦人在激流边设有定居村落，春天捕捞鲟鱼，秋天捕捞白鱼；每到白鱼季，阿尼什纳贝各族数千人到此捕鱼交易，奥达瓦人和波塔瓦托米人也会前来，以鲶鱼为名的马拉梅格人就生活在这片地方。1444年，圣玛丽瀑布是五大湖上游最大的聚会地之一，居民还不知欧洲人为何物。

据法国方面记载，1623年艾蒂安·布吕莱在休伦向导带领下成为第一个见到这处急流的欧洲人，法国人随后以路易十三之弟加斯东之名称之为加斯东瀑布。1668年，克洛德·达布隆与雅克·马凯特在此建立耶稣会传教站，将此地改名为圣玛丽瀑布；1671年6月4日，圣吕松在十四个部族的首领面前宣布整个苏必利尔湖地区归属法国。1736年，路易·德尼·德·拉龙德在北岸的潘角开设船坞，造出第一艘驶入苏必利尔湖的甲板船，用以寻访铜矿。1763年，此地随新法兰西转入英国之手；1790年前后西北公司在此设站，1798年又修成绕过急流的第一座船闸。1814年7月20日，美军的一支突击队焚毁了公司货栈和船闸，但圣玛丽瀑布仍在英国人手中。

en:
Shallow, island-dotted Lake Abitibi and the river draining it northwest toward the Moose River and James Bay form a canoe country between the Ottawa valley and Hudson Bay. The Algonquian-speaking Abitibi people gathered at Pointe Abitibi in summer and dispersed through the surrounding forests and waterways in winter, taking fish, moose, and caribou. French sources explain their name as the people of the dark-water lake. In 1444 no European fort or boundary had reached this cold forest belt, and the shoreline camps and portages remained in Indigenous hands.

From the mid-17th century French missionaries and fur travellers learned the route. In 1686 Pierre de Troyes led a French expedition through the lake on its way to seize English Hudson's Bay posts on James Bay and built a post on the shore; it became a fur station on the Montreal-James Bay canoe route. After Britain acquired Canada in 1763, independent traders and the North West Company competed on the lake. The Hudson's Bay Company opened Abitibi House in 1794 but found it unprofitable against its rivals and abandoned it in 1811. When the two companies merged in 1821, the remaining lake post passed into the Hudson's Bay Company system.
zh:
水浅、岛群散布的阿比蒂比湖，与向西北汇入穆斯河、通向詹姆斯湾的阿比蒂比河，构成渥太华河谷与哈得孙湾之间的独木舟通道。阿尔冈昆语的阿比蒂比人在阿比蒂比角聚集度夏，冬季分散到周围森林和水道，捕鱼并猎取驼鹿与驯鹿。法文资料把他们的自称解释为「深色湖水之人」。1444年，欧洲人的堡垒和疆界尚未进入这片寒冷林带，湖岸营地与搬运路线仍由原住民自主使用。

17世纪中期以后，法国传教士和毛皮旅人逐渐知道这条路线。1686年，皮埃尔·德·特鲁瓦率领法国远征队经阿比蒂比湖前往詹姆斯湾，夺取英格兰人的哈得孙湾商站，并在湖畔设立据点；这里后来成为蒙特利尔至詹姆斯湾独木舟路线上的毛皮商站。英国1763年取得加拿大后，独立商人和西北公司相继在湖畔竞争。哈得孙湾公司1794年开设阿比蒂比屋，却因竞争无利可图，于1811年放弃。1821年两家公司合并，湖畔剩余商站并入哈得孙湾公司的贸易体系。

en:
Mosoni is a form of Môsonî, the Moose Cree or Ililiw country around the mouth of the Moose River on James Bay. In 1444 the Moose Cree kept an annual round rather than a fixed town: summer canoe parties fished and gathered berries, autumn camps hunted geese and ducks along the bay shore, families moved inland for winter game and fur traps, and spring hunts met the birds flying north. The broad Moose River linked the winter forest to the estuary, but no European had yet entered the bay.

Henry Hudson sailed into James Bay in 1610, and the Jesuit Relations of 1671 already located Moose Cree on the bay and river. Pierre-Esprit Radisson reconnoitred the area in the winter of 1670-71, and in 1673 the Hudson's Bay Company governor Charles Bayly founded Moose Fort. Cree traders brought pelts, provisions and labour to the post. In March 1686 the Chevalier de Troyes led thirty French soldiers, seventy Canadian volunteers and Indigenous guides more than 800 miles in eighty-two days from Montreal by the Ottawa, Abitibi and Moose rivers; Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville helped storm the sleeping garrison. Renamed Fort St Louis, it was retaken and burned by the English in 1696, confirmed to Britain in 1713 and rebuilt in 1730. After a fire in 1735 it took seven years to rebuild. The 1821 merger with the North West Company removed the rivalry, the post expanded beyond its palisade as Moose Factory and became the Company's principal James Bay base.
zh:
莫索尼（Mosoni）是克里语Môsonî的游戏拼写，指驼鹿克里人（Ililiw）在詹姆斯湾麋河口一带的土地。1444年，驼鹿克里人没有固定城镇，而是遵循年复一年的迁徙周期：夏季乘独木舟捕鱼、采集浆果，秋季在湾岸猎捕雁鸭，冬季举家迁入内陆猎取大型猎物和毛皮兽，春季再趁水鸟北返狩猎。宽阔的麋河把冬季森林与河口相连，欧洲人此时尚未进入海湾。

亨利·哈德逊于1610年驶入詹姆斯湾，1671年的《耶稣会报道》已在湾岸和麋河畔提到驼鹿克里人。皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松于1670年至1671年冬侦察这一带；1673年，哈得孙湾公司总督查尔斯·贝利设立麋河堡。克里商人把毛皮、食物和劳力带到商站。1686年3月，德·特鲁瓦骑士率领三十名法国士兵、七十名加拿大志愿兵和原住民向导，从蒙特利尔出发，经渥太华河、阿比蒂比河和麋河行军八十二天、八百多英里，皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德·伊贝维尔随军突袭睡梦中的守军。法军将其改名圣路易堡，英军1696年夺回后焚毁，1713年《乌得勒支和约》确认英国主权，商站又于1730年重建。1735年火灾后，重建历时七年。1821年哈得孙湾公司与西北公司合并，竞争随之消失，商站越过栅栏扩展为驼鹿工厂，成为公司在詹姆斯湾的主要基地。

en:
Attawapiskat takes its name from the Swampy Cree, or Mushkegowuk, name for a people of the divided rocks. Their country followed the Attawapiskat River from inland lakes to Akimiski Strait on James Bay, opposite Akimiski Island. In 1444 the river mouth was a spring and summer gathering place where bands came for the fishing; in winter families dispersed to the coast, inland woods and the island, trapping, hunting and gathering roots, berries and nuts. No European post stood on the river; canoe, toboggan and seasonal trails joined the camps.

Henry Hudson's 1610 voyage opened James Bay to Europeans, but Attawapiskat long felt the fur trade only through posts farther south. A French overland force captured the Hudson's Bay Company's bay forts in 1686, and Jesuits made only brief contacts while the French held Fort Albany. An English four-ship fleet retook Albany in 1693, and the post became the nearest fixed point in a commercial fur economy that drew Cree hunters and trappers southward; Company influence still reached this river only weakly in the early nineteenth century. In 1814 George Budge built a wintering Hudson's Bay post on Attawapiskat Lake, abandoned in 1817, reopened in 1820 and given up in 1821. At the end of the period the mouth remained chiefly a seasonal Mushkegowuk camp.
zh:
阿塔瓦皮斯基特（Attawapiskat）出自沼泽克里人（Mushkegowuk）的名称，法文资料释为「岩石分隔之地的人」。他们的土地沿阿塔瓦皮斯基特河，从内陆湖沼延伸到詹姆斯湾的阿基米斯基海峡，与阿基米斯基岛相望。1444年，河口是各群体春季和夏季聚集捕鱼的地方；入冬后，家族分散到海岸、内陆林地或岛上设陷阱、狩猎，采集根块、浆果和坚果。河上没有欧洲商站，独木舟、平底雪橇和季节小径连接着各处营地。

亨利·哈德逊1610年的航行使欧洲人得见詹姆斯湾，但阿塔瓦皮斯基特长期只通过更南方的商站感受毛皮贸易。1686年，法国陆上远征军夺取哈得孙湾公司的湾岸要塞；法军控制奥尔巴尼堡期间，耶稣会士只与这一地区有过短暂接触。1693年，一支由四艘船组成的英国舰队夺回奥尔巴尼堡，这里成为最近的固定商站，把克里猎手和陷阱猎人引入商业毛皮经济；但直到19世纪初，公司势力对阿塔瓦皮斯基特河仍很薄弱。1814年，乔治·巴奇在阿塔瓦皮斯基特湖设立哈得孙湾公司冬站，1817年废弃，1820年重开又于1821年放弃。游戏时代结束时，河口仍主要是沼泽克里人的季节性营地。

en:
The Nelson and Hayes rivers break the swampy south-western shore of Hudson Bay, draining the Saskatchewan and Red River countries into the ice through a maze of tidal flats and muskeg. The people of the coast call themselves Mushkegowuk, 'people of the muskeg' — the western Swampy Cree — who summered on the bay fishing and hunting goose in the marshes, and wintered inland at the caribou hunt, their bark canoes the only masters of that river network. In 1444 no European had entered their waters, and the furs of the interior moved along their canoe roads without passing a single foreign post.

English ships followed soon after the bay was found. Thomas Button reached the Nelson in 1612, buried his sailing master Robert Nelson at its mouth, wintered at Port Nelson and claimed the coast as New Wales. The Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Nelson there in 1684, its first headquarters, and then York Factory on the handier Hayes. Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville failed to take the post in 1690, captured it in 1694 and renamed it Fort Bourbon, lost it back to the English in 1695, and retook it on 13 September 1697 after sinking the Hampshire in the bay's greatest sea fight; France held it until Utrecht, and the Company returned in 1714. Henry Kelsey had already set out from York in June 1690 to pioneer the inland fur route, and for the rest of the period the coastal Mushkegowuk — the Company's 'Homeguard Cree' — provisioned the ships and manned the trade that drew the Saskatchewan country down to the bay.
zh:
纳尔逊河与海斯河在哈得孙湾西南岸切开泥泞的低地，把萨斯喀彻温河、雷德河流域的来水，经由潮滩与泥炭沼组成的迷宫送入冰海。沿岸居民自称穆什凯戈人（Mushkegowuk），意为「泥炭沼之人」，即西部沼泽克里人：他们夏天到海湾捕鱼、在沼泽猎雁，冬天退回内陆猎驯鹿，树皮独木舟是纵横这方水网唯一的主人。1444年，还没有欧洲人进入这片水面，内陆的毛皮沿他们的独木舟之路流动，不经过任何外人的商栈。

海湾被发现后，英国船很快循迹而来。托马斯·巴顿1612年驶抵纳尔逊河，把领航员罗伯特·纳尔逊安葬在河口，随后在纳尔逊港过冬，并宣布这片海岸为新威尔士。哈得孙湾公司1684年在河口建起尼尔森堡——公司的第一个总部——随后又在更便于航行的海斯河上设立约克堡。皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·迪贝维尔1690年攻城受挫，1694年攻陷该堡并改名波旁堡，1695年又被英军夺回；1697年9月13日，他在哈得孙湾规模最大的海战中击沉「汉普郡」号，再次拿下要塞。法国一直占据此地，直到《乌得勒支和约》签订，公司1714年才返回。早在1690年6月，亨利·凯尔西已从约克堡出发，开辟通往内陆的毛皮之路；此后整个年代里，沿海的穆什凯戈人——公司所称的「卫堡克里人」——为船队提供给养，支撑起把萨斯喀彻温腹地引向海湾的贸易。

en:
West of Hudson Bay the forest ends and the Barren Lands begin: treeless tundra cut by the Kazan River and strewn with lakes, swept each year by the great caribou migration. The Ahiarmiut — the Ihalmiut, 'people from beyond' — hunted that herd along the inland rivers, while other Inuit wintered on the coast taking seal, walrus and beluga; Chipewyan Dene, caribou-eaters from the taiga edge, likewise ranged east to the bay shore. In 1444 this was a country measured by the caribou walk, where no ship had yet watered.

In 1619 the Dane Jens Munk brought two ships into the Churchill River; winter and scurvy killed all but three of his 64 men. The Hudson's Bay Company built the Churchill River Post in 1717 and raised the stone Prince of Wales Fort there between 1731 and 1741, drawing the Chipewyan into trade after their peace with the Cree of 1715-16. Through that century, as the caribou failed, the Dene drew south and Kivallirmiut bands took to wintering inland year-round. Samuel Hearne set out from Churchill in 1769 with Chipewyan guides under Matonabbee, crossed the Kazan and Dubawnt barrens to the Coppermine, and on 17 July 1771 watched his Dene companions massacre an Inuit camp at Bloody Falls. In 1782 the French admiral La Pérouse accepted the surrender of the great stone fort without a shot.
zh:
哈得孙湾以西，森林走到尽头，便是「不毛之地」：没有树木的苔原被卡赞河切开，湖泊星罗棋布，驯鹿群的年度大迁徙年复一年扫过旷野。阿希亚尔米尤特人——自称伊哈尔米乌特，意为「来自远方之人」——沿内陆河流追逐鹿群；另一些因纽特人则在海岸过冬，捕猎海豹、海象和白鲸；来自泰加林边缘、以驯鹿为食的奇佩瓦恩迪纳人，也向东活动到湾岸。1444年的这片土地以驯鹿的脚步丈量，还没有一条船在这里补过淡水。

1619年，丹麦人延斯·蒙克率两艘船驶入丘吉尔河；寒冬与坏血病夺去64名船员中61人的性命，只有3人驾船返国。哈得孙湾公司1717年建起丘吉尔河商栈，又在1731至1741年间筑成石砌的威尔士亲王堡；1715至1716年奇佩瓦恩人与克里人议和后，他们开始成批前来贸易。同一世纪里，驯鹿减少，迪纳人逐渐南撤，基瓦利尔米乌特（驯鹿因纽特人）转为终年在内陆生活。1769年，塞缪尔·赫恩从丘吉尔堡出发，由马顿纳比率领的奇佩瓦恩人做向导，越过卡赞河与迪邦特湖一带的荒原，抵达科珀曼河；1771年7月17日，同行的迪纳人在血腥瀑布突袭一处因纽特营地，大开杀戒，赫恩只能在一旁看着。1782年，法国海军将领拉佩鲁斯兵不血刃，接受了这座巨大石堡的投降。

en:
Rainy Lake, Gojiji-zaaga'igan to the Ojibwe after its many inlets and Tekamamiouen to the Cree for the rain that sweeps it, drains westward by the Rainy River into the Lake of the Woods and the Winnipeg River, the canoe road from Lake Superior into the far interior. Its people, the Gojijiwininiwag, were Saulteaux of the Monsoni country, living on fish and the wild rice of its bays and trading along that road; the Cree dwelt to their west and the Sioux to the south, and war with the southerners was never far off. In 1444 the lake was still entirely their own.

In 1688 Jacques de Noyon became the first European to reach Rainy Lake and threw up a temporary post, and a fort Robutel de La Noue built there in 1717 was abandoned before long under Sioux pressure. In 1731 Christopher Dufrost de La Jemeraye, pushing ahead of his uncle La Vérendrye, raised Fort Saint-Pierre at the lake's outlet, the first French post west of Lake Superior; a Cree chief named La Colle gave the French his aid against the Sioux, though war with them came anyway in 1741. The fort served the western trade until 1758, and between 1775 and 1787 the North West Company built Fort Lac la Pluie on the same ground. The Hudson's Bay Company set up Lac la Pluie House there in 1818, three years before the two companies were joined.
zh:
雷尼湖在奥吉布瓦语中称戈吉吉湖，因湖岸多湾而得名；克里人则称之为特卡马米温，意即「雨总是下个不停」。湖水向西经雷尼河注入伍兹湖与温尼伯河，这条水路正是从苏必利尔湖通往西部内陆的独木舟干道。湖畔居民是戈吉吉维尼尼瓦格人，即蒙索尼一带的索尔托人，以捕鱼和采食湖湾中生长的野稻为生，并沿这条商路贸易；他们西边住着克里人，南边住着苏人，与南方邻居的战事从未真正远去。1444年，这座湖还完全属于他们自己。

1688年，雅克·德努永成为第一个到达雷尼湖的欧洲人，并搭起一座临时驿站；1717年罗比泰尔·德拉努在那里修建的堡垒，不久便因苏人的威胁而废弃。1731年，克里斯托夫·迪弗罗·德拉热默赖赶在舅父拉韦朗德里之前，在湖的出口处建起圣皮埃尔堡，这是苏必利尔湖以西第一座法国驿站；克里人首领拉科勒帮助法国人对付苏人，但对苏战争还是在1741年爆发。堡垒维持西部贸易直到1758年；1775至1787年间，西北公司在同一地点建起雨湖堡，1818年哈德逊湾公司又在此设立雨湖商馆，三年后两家公司合二为一。

en:
The Red River comes down out of the plains to Lake Winnipeg, and at its meeting with the Assiniboine lies the Forks, a canoe crossroads and trading ground used by First Nations for thousands of years. The great lake to the north was winipīhk, 'muddy water', in Western Cree. Before contact, corn grew in fields along the Red, and the waterways linked the bison hunters of the plains with the fishing and trapping camps of the forests; Cree, Anishinaabe, Assiniboine and Dakota all met here. In 1444 no European had ever seen the lake, and the Forks was an indigenous crossroads where only furs, hides and dried meat changed hands between nations.

Henry Kelsey of the Hudson's Bay Company may have been the first European to sight Lake Winnipeg in 1690. In 1738 the French under La Vérendrye built Fort Rouge at the Forks, their first post on the Red River. British traders took over after 1763: the North West Company raised Fort Gibraltar in 1809, and in 1812 the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Douglas while Lord Selkirk's Scottish settlers founded the Red River Colony beside it. On 19 June 1816 the rivalry over the pemmican trade came to bloodshed at Seven Oaks, where Cuthbert Grant's Métis killed Governor Robert Semple and twenty of his men for the loss of one Métis. The two companies merged in 1821, ending their long feud at the Forks.
zh:
雷德河自草原北流入温尼伯湖，在与阿西尼博因河交汇处形成「福克斯」河汊，是原住民使用了数千年的独木舟枢纽和贸易地。北边的大湖在西克里语中称温尼皮赫克，意为「浑水」。与欧洲人接触之前，雷德河沿岸已种有玉米，水网把草原上的野牛猎人与林间捕鱼设阱的营地连成一片，克里人、奥吉布瓦人、阿西尼博因人和达科他人都在此往来。1444年时还没有任何欧洲人见过这座湖，河汊完全是原住民的通衢，往来的只有各族之间的毛皮、兽皮和肉干。

1690年，哈德逊湾公司的亨利·凯尔西可能是第一个望见温尼伯湖的欧洲人。1738年，拉韦朗德里麾下的法国人在河汊建起鲁日堡，这是他们在雷德河上的第一座商栈。1763年后英国商人接手：西北公司1809年筑起直布罗陀堡；1812年，哈德逊湾公司建起道格拉斯堡，塞尔扣克伯爵的苏格兰移民同时在旁建立雷德河殖民地。1816年6月19日，争夺肉糜饼贸易的冲突在七株橡树流血收场，卡斯伯特·格兰特率领的梅蒂人击杀总督罗伯特·森普尔及其部下二十人，梅蒂一方仅死一人。1821年两公司合并，河汊上的长期争斗随之结束。

en:
Lake Winnipeg — wīnipēk, 'muddy water', in Cree — is a vast, shallow remnant of glacial Lake Agassiz, and its eastern shore rises into the Atikaki, 'caribou country' in Anishinaabe: granite ridges and black spruce where the Bloodvein, Berens and Poplar rivers come down out of the Shield. Cree bands netted whitefish and sturgeon on the lake and hunted moose and caribou in the woods; Anishinaabe peoples lived to the south-east and Assiniboine on the prairie edge. In 1444 the lake's long sand beaches were empty of Europeans.

Henry Kelsey, travelling out from York Factory, is thought to have been the first European to sight the lake in 1690. In 1733 a son of La Vérendrye came within twenty miles of it before ice stopped him; the French reached the lake in 1734, mapped it as Ouinipigon and raised Fort Maurepas on its southern shore, and the lake's furs began to slide toward Montreal instead of the bay. Traders first descended the Berens from the Severn country in 1767, and the Hudson's Bay Company put a post at the Berens River mouth in 1814, one stop on the canoe highway that then linked York Factory with the Red River through the lake.
zh:
温尼伯湖——克里语名 wīnipēk，意为「浑水」——是冰川时代阿加西斯湖残留的一片广阔浅湖；湖东岸地势隆起，便是阿蒂卡基（Atikaki），阿尼什纳比语意为「驯鹿之地」：花岗岩脊与黑云杉林间，布拉德维恩河、贝伦河、波普勒河从加拿大地盾奔流而下。克里人部落在湖上捕捞白鱼和鲟鱼，在林中猎驼鹿与驯鹿；东南方住着阿尼什纳比人，草原边缘则是阿西尼博因人。1444年，长长的湖滩上还没有一个欧洲人。

一般认为，1690年从约克堡方向而来的亨利·凯尔西，是最早见到此湖的欧洲人。1733年，拉韦朗德里的一个儿子前进到距湖仅二十英里处，被浮冰挡住；法国人1734年抵达大湖，把它记作 Ouinipigon，并在湖南岸建起莫勒帕堡，湖中的毛皮也随之改向蒙特利尔，而不再流向海湾。1767年，商人首次从塞文河地方顺贝伦河而下；1814年，哈得孙湾公司在贝伦河口设立商栈——这条湖路把约克堡与雷德河连在一起，贝伦河口正是途中一站。

en:
Lake Manitoba runs from the edge of the plains into the boreal woods, its two basins pinched together at the Narrows, where wind and water over the shallow strait made a sound heard as the voice of the Great Spirit — manitou-wapow in Cree, manidoobaa in Ojibwe, the straits of Manitou from which Manitoba takes its name. Assiniboine and Cree camps lined its shores, taking fish and waterfowl from the reed beds and meeting the bison hunters of the grassland to the south. Through the Narrows, linked by short portages, a canoe road ran between the Assiniboine River and the great lake to the north. In 1444 only those nations knew the waterway; no European had yet mapped a league of it.

La Vérendrye's French parties reached the lake in the mid-1730s, calling it Lac des Prairies and canoeing through it from Fort La Reine on their way to the Saskatchewan, and it became a link in the fur route to Hudson Bay. In 1767 French fur traders built a second Fort Dauphin on the north shore of neighbouring Dauphin Lake, and after the wars the Hudson's Bay Company and the North West Company both ran posts on that lake, vying for the lake-country furs until their merger in 1821 ended the rivalry there.
zh:
马尼托巴湖从草原边缘伸入北方针叶林，两座湖盆在最窄处收束为大窄口：风浪穿过浅水海峡，声若大神的低语——克里语称马尼图瓦波，奥吉布瓦语称马尼多巴，意为「大神的海峡」，马尼托巴一名即出于此。湖岸散布着阿西尼博因人和克里人的营地，他们在芦苇荡中捕鱼、猎取水禽，与南边草原上的野牛猎人相会。穿过大窄口、经几段短途陆运，独木舟可在阿西尼博因河与北方大湖之间往来。1444年时，只有这些部族认得这条水道，欧洲人尚未绘出它的一里水程。

1730年代中期，拉韦朗德里的法国队伍抵达此湖，称之为草原湖，从拉雷讷堡出发经此划向萨斯喀彻温河，马尼托巴湖由此成为通往哈得孙湾皮毛商路的一环。1767年，法国毛皮商人在邻近的多芬湖北岸建起第二座多芬堡；战乱之后，哈德逊湾公司与西北公司都在多芬湖畔经营商栈，争夺湖间地带的毛皮，直至1821年两公司合并，湖上的相争才告结束。

en:
West of Lake Winnipeg the Saskatchewan River breaks out of the boreal forest into a chain of broad lakes, Cedar Lake and Lake Winnipegosis, before running through Grand Rapids into open water. Swampy Cree bands have gathered here for thousands of years; at the wooded narrows of the Saskatchewan, Opaskwayak in their language, families met each summer to fish, harvest and keep the rites of the Midewiwin. The river was also a highway, and most of the furs taken in the west and northwest came down it by canoe. In 1444 the lake chain and the narrows was the country of the woods Cree, while the grassland to the south was Assiniboine ground.

Henry Kelsey came this way between 1690 and 1692, the first European on the Saskatchewan. In 1741–42 the La Vérendryes built Fort Dauphin on Lake Winnipegosis, Fort Bourbon near the river's outflow and Fort Paskoya on Cedar Lake, later moved upstream to The Pas — posts meant to turn the canoe brigades away from Hudson Bay. Anthony Henday visited Paskoya in 1754 and dismissed the post as a hogsty, and as New France collapsed the French burned and abandoned the chain in 1758–59. Independent winterers and then the North West Company reopened the old sites, which the Hudson's Bay Company eventually took over.
zh:
温尼伯湖以西，萨斯喀彻温河钻出北方针叶林，注入锡达湖、温尼伯戈西斯湖这一串宽阔湖泊，再经大急流进入开阔水面。沼泽克里人的支系在此聚居易数千年：萨斯喀彻温河林木丛生的窄口，克里语称奥帕斯夸亚克，各家族每年夏天到此捕鱼、采集、举行米德维温仪式。这条河又是一条通衢，西部和西北部出产的毛皮大半顺河由独木舟运出。1444年时，湖链与窄口是林地克里人的家园，南边的草原则是阿西尼博因人的地界。

1690年至1692年间，亨利·凯尔西经此前往野牛草原，是第一个抵达萨斯喀彻温河的欧洲人。1741至1742年，拉韦朗德里父子在温尼伯戈西斯湖畔建起多芬堡、在河口附近建起波旁堡，又在锡达湖畔建起帕斯科亚堡（后来上移至帕斯），意在把独木舟商队从哈得孙湾引开。1754年安东尼·亨迪到访帕斯科亚堡，把这座商栈贬为猪圈；新法兰西崩溃之际，法国人于1758至1759年焚毁并放弃了这一串堡垒。此后先是个体冬猎者、继而西北公司重开旧址，最终由哈德逊湾公司接管。

en:
Satsuma lay along the Satsuma Peninsula and the East China Sea coast of southern Kyushu, the western half of the later Kagoshima mainland. The court province was split from Hyuga after a Satsuma-Hayato rising in 702, and its ancient provincial seat stood near Satsumasendai. From the Kamakura period the Shimazu held office as military governors; by the late 1300s their Kagoshima base at Shimizu Castle looked over a sheltered inlet south of Sakurajima. In 1444 Satsuma was thus a Shimazu land of coastal villages, mountain valleys and seaborne traffic, its ancient provincial administration overshadowed by the warrior power at Kagoshima.

Francis Xavier landed at Gionnosu near Kagoshima on 15 August 1549, beginning Christian mission in Japan; the faith was later suppressed with exceptional severity after the Tokugawa bans. Under Shimazu Takahisa and Yoshihisa, Satsuma forces united Satsuma, Osumi and Hyuga, and defeated the Ryuzoji and Otomo houses until Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Kyushu campaign of 1587 forced them back to their home core. They joined the western army at Sekigahara in 1600 but kept their lands, and in 1601 Shimazu Iehisa established Kagoshima Castle as the seat of Satsuma Domain. A three-month expedition in 1609 captured Shuri and King Sho Nei in Ryukyu; the Amami and Tokara islands were annexed, while Ryukyuan tribute and Chinese goods flowed through Kagoshima even after the maritime prohibitions of the 1630s. Sengan-en was laid out for Shimazu Mitsuhisa in 1658, and in 1821 Satsuma remained one of the greatest outer domains under the Tokugawa order.
zh:
