萨摩位于九州南部的萨摩半岛和东海沿岸，相当于后来鹿儿岛本土的西半部。702年萨摩隼人叛乱后，该地从日向国分置为令制国，古国府靠近萨摩川内。镰仓以来，岛津氏担任守护；到14世纪后期，鹿儿岛的清水城成为其据点，隔海湾眺望樱岛。1444年的萨摩是岛津治下由海岸村落、山谷与海路组成的土地，古老国衙已让位于鹿儿岛的武家势力。

1549年8月15日，方济各·沙勿略在鹿儿岛附近的祇园之洲登陆，基督教由此初传日本；德川幕府禁教后，萨摩对基督教的镇压尤为严酷。岛津贵久、义久在位时，岛津军统一萨摩、大隅、日向三州，又击败龙造寺氏和大友氏，直到1587年丰臣秀吉发动九州征伐，才将他们压回旧领核心。1600年关原之战时岛津加入西军，却保全了本领；1601年岛津家久筑鹿儿岛城，作为萨摩藩厅。1609年，萨摩出兵三个月后攻陷琉球首都首里并俘虏尚宁王，奄美和吐噶喇群岛被并入藩域；即使日本在1630年代后厉行海禁，琉球的朝贡关系与中国货物仍经鹿儿岛流通。1658年岛津光久开辟仙岩园；到1821年，萨摩仍是德川秩序下最强大的外样藩之一。

en:
Cheongju began as Sangdang, a Baekje district guarded by the mountain fortress of Sangdang Sanseong. Unified Silla made it Seowon, one of its five secondary capitals, in 685, and Goryeo renamed the town Cheongju in 940 and raised it to a provincial mok in 983. Its lasting claim to fame came in 1377, when monks at Heungdeok Temple printed the Jikji, a collection of Zen patriarchs' teachings, with movable metal type—the oldest surviving book so printed, decades before Gutenberg. Under the Joseon the Buddhist town became a Confucian county of Chungcheong Province, sitting on the rich grain lands of the Musimcheon valley and astride the road from Hanyang to the southwestern provinces. In 1444 Cheongju was a quiet prefectural town beneath its old fortress.

The Japanese invasion put the town at war in 1592: the scholar-official Cho Hon raised a righteous army at Okcheon and joined the monk Yeonggyu's warrior monks to storm and retake Cheongju, the first combined victory of civilians and monk-soldiers in the war; both commanders fell in the later fighting at Geumsan. The town saw battle again on 15 March 1728, when Yi In-jwa's Soron rebels seized Cheongju Castle at the opening of the Musin Rebellion against King Yeongjo; the royal army retook it within weeks and the rising collapsed. Cheongju otherwise lived out the Joseon centuries as a market and county seat of the central grain country.
zh:
清州古称上党，百济时已在此设县，并有上党山城扼守要冲。统一新罗于685年在此设西原小京，是五小京之一；940年高丽改名为清州，983年升为清州牧。此地最负盛名的事发生在1377年：兴德寺的僧众用金属活字印出了《直指心体要节》，这是现存最古老的金属活字印本，比古腾堡还早数十年。进入朝鲜时代，这座佛风浓厚的城镇变为忠清道的一处儒家化县治，坐落于无心川流域的丰饶谷地上，又扼守汉阳通往西南诸道的大路。1444年的清州，是座古城墙下安静的州治小镇。

1592年壬辰倭乱把这座城镇卷入战火：文臣赵宪在玉川举起义兵，与灵圭率领的僧兵合力攻复清州城，这是开战后义兵与僧兵首次联手告捷，两位主将后来都在同年的金山之战中战死。1728年3月15日，战火再度降临：少论派李麟佐起兵反对英祖，在戊申乱（李麟佐之乱）爆发之际袭取清州城，但官军数周内便将城夺回，叛乱旋即失败。除此之外，清州在朝鲜时代一直是中部谷仓地带的一处县治和集镇。

en:
Bungo occupied eastern Kyushu, from the Kunisaki Peninsula and the Funai coast to the mountain valleys bordering Hyuga and Higo. The province was formed when old Toyo was divided in 701, and its provincial centre lay near modern Oita. In 1185 Minamoto no Yoritomo sent the Otomo east from the Kanto region as shugo to subdue pro-Taira warriors in Kyushu. The clan kept Bungo through the Kamakura and Muromachi centuries, enlarged its power by marriage, war and trade, and in 1444 ruled from Funai over a timbered, deeply indented coast, while local gentry and shrine and temple estates preserved much autonomy.

Bungo's age of maritime fortune came under Otomo Sorin. He received Francis Xavier in 1551, opened trade with the Portuguese, Ming China, the Ryukyus and Cambodia, and made Funai a centre of Jesuit activity; European records called him the King of Bungo, and the Tensho embassy sent by Kyushu Christian lords sailed for Rome in 1582. At his height Sorin dominated six provinces, but defeat by the Shimazu at the Mimikawa in 1578 broke Otomo power. Shimazu armies overran much of Bungo in 1586, including Funai, until Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Kyushu campaign restored Sorin's son Yoshimune the next year. Otomo rule did not long survive the Korean wars, and under the Tokugawa Bungo was divided between shogunal lands and the small domains of Funai, Kitsuki, Usuki and Saeki.
zh:
丰后位于九州东部，从国东半岛和府内海岸延伸到毗邻日向、肥后的山地河谷。701年，旧丰国被分为丰前与丰后，丰后的国府就在今大分附近。1185年，源赖朝为压制九州的亲平氏武士，把出身东国的大友氏派任守护。大友氏历经镰仓和室町时代保有丰后，通过婚姻、战事与贸易扩张势力；1444年，他们以府内为本据，统治这片森林密布、海岸曲折的土地，而国人豪族与寺社庄园仍保有很大自治。

丰后的海上机运在大友宗麟时代达到顶峰。他在1551年接纳方济各·沙勿略，开展与葡萄牙、明朝、琉球和柬埔寨的贸易，使府内成为耶稣会活动中心；欧洲文献称他为「丰后之王」，九州基督教大名派遣的天正遣欧使节也于1582年启程前往罗马。宗麟最盛时控制六国，但1578年在耳川之战中败于岛津氏，大友霸权由此崩塌。1586年，岛津军攻占丰后大片土地并拿下府内，直到次年丰臣秀吉发动九州征伐，才恢复宗麟之子大友义统的领国。大友氏的统治在朝鲜之役后未能久存；德川时代的丰后由幕府直领和府内、杵筑、臼杵、佐伯等小藩分割治理。

en:
Okinawa is the chief island of the Ryukyu chain, lying between the East China Sea and the Pacific about 640 kilometres south of Kyushu. After 1314 its gusuku lords coalesced into Hokuzan, Chuzan and Nanzan; Chuzan held Shuri and the neighbouring port of Naha, while Ming investiture and the Fujianese families sent in 1392 tied its court to Chinese shipping. In 1429 Sho Hashi united the three realms, made Shuri Castle the royal seat, and turned Naha into the harbour of a tributary kingdom linking China, Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia. In 1444, only fifteen years after that unification, Okinawa was the prosperous centre of Ryukyu: its nobles used Chinese-style court forms, noro priestesses maintained island rites, and junks carried silver, swords, ceramics, spices, sappanwood and sugar through Naha.

Ryukyu conquered Amami Oshima in 1447 and campaigned against Kikai Island in 1466; the First Sho line ended when Sho En founded the Second Sho dynasty in 1469. Under Sho Shin, who reigned from 1478 to 1526, the kingdom brought the Sakishima Islands under its control, centralized the lords and priestesses, and reached its greatest age, though Portuguese competition and piracy weakened Naha's trade by the late 1500s. In 1609 Satsuma invaded, captured Shuri and King Sho Nei after hard fighting, and imposed the Fifteen Articles. The Amami Islands were ceded, diplomacy and commerce came under supervision, and Ryukyu kept its throne as a tributary of both China and Satsuma; that ambiguous position let Chinese goods continue toward Kagoshima under the Tokugawa maritime bans. Naha's Tsuboya potters established their distinctive enameled Ryukyuan ware in 1682. The British captain Basil Hall visited and described Okinawa in 1816, and in 1821 the Shuri court still managed the island's internal affairs under Satsuma's oversight.
zh:
冲绳是琉球群岛的主岛，横亘在东海与太平洋之间，北距九州约640公里。1314年后，岛上的按司势力形成北山、中山、南山三个政权；中山据守首里，邻近那霸港。明朝册封以及1392年福建三十六姓的到来，使首里宫廷与中国航船紧密相连。1429年，尚巴志统合三山，以首里城为王都，把那霸建设成连接中国、日本、朝鲜和东南亚的朝贡贸易港。1444年，距统一仅十五年，冲绳已是琉球的繁盛中心：贵族采用中国式宫廷制度，祝女维持岛上祭祀，帆船载着白银、刀剑、瓷器、香料、苏木和糖出入那霸。

琉球1447年攻取奄美大岛，1466年出兵喜界岛；1469年尚圆建立第二尚氏，第一尚氏王统结束。尚真1478年至1526年在位期间，琉球将先岛群岛纳入势力，整合豪族与祝女制度，进入全盛；到16世纪末，葡萄牙人的竞争和海盗活动削弱了那霸贸易。1609年，萨摩军队入侵，激战后攻陷首里、俘获尚宁王，随后颁布《掟十五条》。奄美群岛被割让，外交和贸易受到监管，琉球则保留王位，形成同时向中国与萨摩朝贡的两属局面。德川海禁之下，这种暧昧地位使中国货物仍可借由琉球流向鹿儿岛。1682年，那霸壶屋工匠确立了独具冲绳特色的釉彩琉球陶器。1816年，英国船长巴兹尔·霍尔到访并记录冲绳；1821年，首里宫廷仍在萨摩监督下管理岛上内政。

en:
Ha Tinh is the narrow coastal shelf where the Hong Linh hills meet the Gulf of Tonkin, its living divided among rice fields, fishing inlets and the road linking Thanh Hoa to Hue. Ming armies conquered Dai Viet in 1407, but the Thanh-Nghe uplands never accepted the occupation: in 1418 Le Loi raised his banner at Lam Son just to the north, and in 1424, on a lieutenant's advice, the rebels marched south through this coast to seize Nghe An and turn it into the springboard for the victories that drove the Ming out in 1427. In 1444 the district belongs to the restored Later Le dynasty, a southern march of soldier-settlers, salt-makers and fishing villages.

The Mac usurpation of 1527 made Thanh-Nghe the base of the Le restoration, and in 1558 Nguyen Hoang led the men of Thanh-Nghe south through here to hold Thuan Hoa, founding the Nguyen lordship. For the next century Ha Tinh lay on the Trinh side of the Trinh–Nguyen wars, its coast road crowded with armies and supply fleets. In 1774 Trinh Sam sent Hoang Ngu Phuc with 30,000 men down the coast to storm the Nguyen capital Phu Xuan, and the Tay Son wars soon swept the same road back and forth. This was the home country of the poet Nguyen Du, born at Tien Dien in 1766, who lived through the fall of the Le and then served the Nguyen; he led the embassy to the Qing in 1813–14 and wrote the 3,254-line nom poem The Tale of Kieu from a Chinese novel before his death in 1820.
zh:
河静是洪岭余脉直逼北部湾的一道狭长海岸，生计分在稻田、渔港和连接清化与顺化的官道之间。1407年明军征服大虞，清乂山区却始终不肯臣服：1418年黎利在北面的蓝山举兵，1424年又纳部下之计率义军沿这条海岸南下夺取乂安，以此为跳板连战连捷，1427年逼退明军。1444年时，这片滨海之地属于复国的后黎朝，是军屯、盐灶和渔村散布的南陲。

1527年莫登庸篡位，清乂成为后黎复辟派的根基；1558年阮潢率清乂子弟经此南下镇守顺化，开阮主基业。此后百余年，河静处在郑阮纷争的郑氏一侧，沿海大道上大军与粮船往来不断。1774年，郑森派黄五福率兵三万沿海南下，攻克阮都富春；不久西山战事又在这条路上来回席卷。这里也是诗人阮攸的故土，他1766年生于仙田，身经后黎覆亡与西山战乱，终出仕阮朝，1813至1814年出使清朝，并据中国小说《金云翘传》写成3254句的喃字长诗《传翘》，1820年病故。

en:
Suō faces the Seto Inland Sea at the south-western tip of Honshu, its sheltered harbours looking toward Kyushu and Korea. The ancient provincial capital stood at Hōfu, whose Tamanooya Shrine was named the province's ichinomiya. The Hōjō held the shugo post in the Kamakura age, and under the Muromachi shogunate the province passed to the Ōuchi, who moved their seat to the new town of Yamaguchi in 1360. The clan grew rich on the tally trade with Ming China and with Korea, exchanging copper, sulphur and swords for silk and porcelain. In 1444 Ōuchi Norihiro ruled from Yamaguchi, laid out in the manner of Kyoto and already a magnet for monks, scholars and merchants drawn by its lords' trade wealth.

Norihiro's son Masahiro led the western host through the Ōnin War from 1467, and his grandson Yoshioki restored the deposed shogun Ashikaga Yoshitane at Kyoto in 1508. Under Yoshitaka, who succeeded in 1528, Yamaguchi reached its height: the painter Sesshū worked under Ōuchi patronage, the clan overawed the rival Hosokawa mission at Ningbo in 1523 and came to monopolize the Ming trade, and Francis Xavier was received at Yamaguchi in 1550 and 1551, winning leave to preach Christianity. In 1551 the general Sue Harukata rebelled and Yoshitaka took his own life; Mōri Motonari destroyed Sue at Itsukushima in 1555 and completed the conquest of Suō in 1557. After Sekigahara in 1600 the Mōri were reduced to Suō and Nagato and built their capital at Hagi, while Yamaguchi remained a posting town on the road to the port of Mitajiri. The Kikkawa, kinsmen of the Mōri, held Iwakuni and in 1673 raised the five-arched Kintai Bridge over the Nishiki River.
zh:
周防位于本州西端、面朝濑户内海，良港朝向九州与朝鲜。律令时代的国衙在防府，一之宫玉祖神社也坐落于此。镰仓时代北条氏担任守护，进入室町时代后，周防归于大内氏；1360年大内弘世把本据迁到新建的山口。大内氏靠对明朝和朝鲜的勘合贸易致富，以铜、硫磺和刀剑换回丝绸与瓷器。1444年的周防由大内教弘统治，以京都为样板营建的山口，凭借主家的贸易财富，吸引着僧侣、学者和商人前来。

教弘之子政弘自1467年起统率应仁之乱的西军，其孙义兴又于1508年拥戴被废的将军足利义稙重返京都。1528年继位的义隆治下，山口迎来鼎盛：画僧雪舟在此作画，大内氏1523年在宁波压过竞争的细川使团，逐步独占对明贸易；方济各·沙勿略也于1550、1551年两度在山口谒见义隆，获准传教。1551年重臣陶晴贤谋反，义隆自尽；毛利元就1555年在严岛奇袭攻灭陶晴贤，1557年平定周防。1600年关原合战后，毛利氏被减封至周防、长门两国，把居城设在萩；山口则作为通往三田尻港的萩往还中继町继续存在。毛利一门吉川氏领有岩国，1673年在锦川上建起五拱的锦带桥。

en:
Izumo faces the Sea of Japan on the San'indo coast of western Honshu, its plains watered by rivers running down from the Chūgoku mountains. It was the sacred land of the Izumo Taisha, the great shrine of the god Ōkuninushi, and kept a priestly standing after the Yamato court brought it under its rule. The medieval shugo — Sasaki, Yamana and finally Kyōgoku — rarely resided in the province, and government fell to their deputies the Amago, entrenched at Gassan Toda Castle above the coast. Its streams carried iron sand, and tatara furnaces smelted it into steel for the weapons trade. In 1444 the Kyōgoku lived in distant Ōmi while the Amago ruled from Gassan Toda, the shrine and the iron furnaces giving Izumo its name for piety and steel.

Expelled for seizing manors in 1484, Amago Tsunehisa retook Gassan Toda by surprise in 1486 and built the clan into Sengoku lords commanding Izumo, Hōki and the iron trade. A combined Ōuchi–Mōri army was beaten off in 1543, and in 1552 Amago Haruhisa was named shugo of eight San'in and Sanyō provinces; his sudden death in 1560 opened the way for Mōri Motonari, whose blockade starved Gassan Toda into surrender in 1566, when Amago Yoshihisa was led captive to Aki. The loyal retainer Yamanaka Yukimori raised restoration armies from 1569, only to be crushed in 1570. After Sekigahara, Horio Tadauji received Izumo and Oki at 240,000 koku in 1600, and his father Yoshiharu built Matsue Castle between the lakes in 1607–1611, moving the seat from the mountain fastness to a new castle town. Kyōgoku Tadataka followed briefly from 1634, and in 1638 Matsudaira Naomasa held Matsue at 186,000 koku, his line ruling until the nineteenth century.
zh:
出云位于本州西部山阴道的日本海沿岸，平野由中国山地流下的诸河灌溉。这里是祭祀大国主的出云大社所在的圣地，并入大和朝廷后仍保有神国地位。中世的守护佐佐木氏、山名氏乃至最后的京极氏很少在国，政务落入守护代尼子氏之手，其据点是临海山丘上的月山富田城。出云的河川盛产铁砂，踏鞴炉将其炼成钢铁，支撑兵器之利。1444年，京极氏远居近江，尼子氏据月山富田城统治出云，大社与铁炉让这片土地以信仰和产铁闻名。

1484年，尼子经久因侵吞庄园被逐，1486年又以奇袭夺回月山富田城，此后扩张为制霸出云、伯耆、掌控制铁之利的战国大名。1543年大内与毛利联军来攻被击退，1552年尼子晴久获任山阴、山阳八国守护；1560年晴久暴卒，毛利元就乘机围攻月山富田城，围城经年，城中粮尽，1566年开城，尼子义久被押往安艺。忠臣山中幸盛自1569年起兵谋求复兴尼子家，1570年兵败。关原之战后的1600年，堀尾忠氏受封出云、隐岐二十四万石，其父堀尾吉晴于1607至1611年在湖水之间修筑松江城，把居城从山上旧城迁到新城下町。1634年京极忠高短暂入封，1638年松平直政以十八万六千石入主松江，其家族一直统治到19世纪。

en:
Harima, also called Banshū, faces the Seto Inland Sea on the San'yō road between the capital region and Kyūshū, its well-watered coastal plain growing rice for the western sea lanes. The province was formed in the seventh century, and its gazetteer of 713, the Harima no Kuni Fudoki, is one of only five provincial Fudoki to survive. The Akamatsu, shugo governors of Harima, first fortified Himeyama hill above the port of Himeji in 1333, and Akamatsu Sadanori rebuilt the fort as Himeyama Castle in 1346. In 1441 Akamatsu Mitsusuke murdered the shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori at a banquet in Kyoto; Yamana Sōzen's punitive army overran the province, and Mitsusuke and his son took their own lives at Shōyama Castle. In 1444 Harima has but recently been granted to the Yamana, whose new rule is far from settled.

The Akamatsu were restored in 1458, and when the Ōnin War began in 1467 Akamatsu Masanori sided with Hosokawa Katsumoto and recovered Harima from the weakened Yamana. In the Sengoku breakup that followed, the Kuroda held Himeji for the Kodera lords, Kuroda Yoshitaka becoming castellan in 1567. After Toyotomi Hideyoshi opened his Chūgoku campaign in 1577, Bessho Nagaharu of Miki held out for the Mōri through the two-year 'starvation siege' of 1578–1580, while Kuroda yielded Himeji to Hideyoshi, who raised a three-storey keep in 1581 and made the White Heron Castle his base for the conquest of the west. After Sekigahara in 1600 Tokugawa Ieyasu granted Himeji to his son-in-law Ikeda Terumasa, who rebuilt it between 1601 and 1609 into the great eighty-three-building castle of the early Tokugawa age; Honda Tadamasa added further towers in 1617–1618, among them the Dressing Tower built for Princess Sen. Harima was then divided among small domains including Akō, where in 1703 the forty-seven rōnin were ordered to die after avenging their lord Asano Naganori.
zh:
播磨别称播州，地处山阳道要冲，南临濑户内海，是畿内通往九州的必经之地，沿海平原水渠纵横，稻米沿西部海路外运。播磨国在7世纪设立，713年奉命编纂的《播磨国风土记》是仅存的五国风土记之一。世代担任播磨守护的赤松氏1333年在姬路港背后的姬山筑起城砦，赤松贞范又于1346年将其改建为姬山城。1441年，赤松满祐在京都的宴会上刺杀幕府将军足利义教，史称嘉吉之乱；山名宗全率讨伐军攻入播磨，满祐父子最终在城山城自尽。1444年的播磨封给山名氏未久，新主人的统治远未稳固。

赤松氏于1458年获许再兴，1467年应仁之乱爆发，赤松政则加入细川胜元一方，趁山名氏衰弱夺回播磨。此后战国乱世，播磨群雄分立，黑田氏作为小寺氏的家臣驻守姬路，黑田孝高（官兵卫、如水）1567年出任城代。1577年丰臣秀吉发动中国征伐，据守三木城的别所长治呼应毛利氏，在1578至1580年长达两年的「三木干杀」围困中粮尽城陷；黑田孝高随即将姬路让给秀吉，秀吉1581年建起三层天守，把这座「白鹭城」经营成平定西国的大本营。1600年关原之战后，德川家康把姬路封给女婿池田辉政，辉政在1601至1609年间大举改建，筑起江户初年八十三座建筑相连的宏伟城郭；本多忠政又在1617至1618年增建角楼，包括为千姬修建的化妆楼。此后播磨被分为姬路、赤穗等多个小藩，1703年，赤穗四十七士为报主君浅野长矩之仇，被勒令切腹自尽。

en:
Kyoto grew from Heian-kyo, the Chinese-style capital laid out in Yamashiro Province after Emperor Kanmu moved his court there in 794. Even after military rulers arose, the city remained Japan's imperial centre; the Ashikaga shoguns also kept their government in the Muromachi district, where their Flower Palace gave the age its name. By the 1440s, however, shogunal authority was shaky after Ashikaga Yoshinori was murdered in the 1441 Kakitsu Incident. Aristocratic Kamigyo and merchant Shimogyo still revolved around the court, temples and markets. In 1444 Kyoto was therefore the ceremonial heart of Japan, but a capital whose warrior government no longer overawed the provinces.

The strain became open war in 1467, when Onin factions fought through Kyoto until 1477, burning much of Kamigyo and turning mansions and temple grounds into fortifications. Oda Nobunaga entered the city in 1568 with Ashikaga Yoshiaki and overthrew him in 1573, ending the Muromachi shogunate. Toyotomi Hideyoshi then replanned the streets, gathered temples into Teramachi, and in 1591 raised the Odoi earthworks around the city. After Tokugawa Ieyasu established his shogunate at Edo in 1603, Kyoto kept the imperial palace and Nijo Castle, and remained one of Japan's three great cities alongside Edo and Osaka through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
zh:
京都起源于平安京。794年，桓武天皇把朝廷迁到山城国的这片盆地，按中国都城形制营建新京。后来武家掌权后，京都仍是日本朝廷所在；足利将军也把政权设在室町，其「花之御所」更为这个时代得名。到1440年代，足利义教在1441年嘉吉之乱中被杀，幕府权威已经动摇。以上京为中心的公家社寺与下京的商业市区仍围绕朝廷运转，因此1444年的京都仍是日本的礼仪中心，却也是一座武家政权已难以镇服诸国的都城。

1467年，紧张局势演变为应仁之乱，各派武士在京都巷战至1477年，上京大片焚毁，公家宅邸和寺社境内也变成堡垒。1568年，织田信长奉足利义昭上洛，又在1573年驱逐义昭，室町幕府就此终结。此后丰臣秀吉重新划分町区，把诸寺集中到寺町一带，并于1591年在城市周围修筑御土居。1603年德川家康在江户开设幕府后，京都仍保有京都御所和二条城，并在整个十七、十八世纪与江户、大坂并称三都。

en:
Settsu, the 'port province' facing the Seto Inland Sea at the mouth of the Yodo, was where Japan's western sea lanes met the river road to Kyoto. Its harbour of Naniwa served as capital under Emperor Kotoku after the court moved there in 645, and the Naniwa Palace was completed in 652; Shitennō-ji had been founded there in 593, and Sumiyoshi Taisha became the province's chief shrine. Taira no Kiyomori developed the anchorage of Ōwada no Tomari, later Hyōgo, and briefly moved the court to nearby Fukuhara in 1180. Rebuilt by the monk Chōgen in the Kamakura period, Hyōgo grew into Japan's foremost harbour and the base of the Muromachi trade with Ming China. In 1444 the shugo post was held by the Hosokawa, the house of the shogun's deputies, though rival deputies and local lords shared much of the province.

In 1496 Rennyo, the aged leader of the Jōdo Shinshū, built a retreat on the long slope called Ōsaka, around which rose the fortified temple-town of Ishiyama Hongan-ji; after the burning of the Yamashina Hongan-ji in 1532 it became the sect's headquarters. The Miyoshi, former deputies of the Hosokawa, had come to rule Settsu when Oda Nobunaga's demands brought on the Ishiyama war: from 1570 to 1580 the Hongan-ji withstood siege and blockade until imperial mediation secured its surrender. Toyotomi Hideyoshi began Ōsaka Castle on the site in 1583, and the castle town became the seat of his national hegemony. After his death the Tokugawa destroyed the Toyotomi in the winter and summer campaigns of 1614–1615 and rebuilt Ōsaka as a shogunal city. It became the 'kitchen of the realm', ringed by daimyō warehouses, and from 1697 the Dōjima rice market set the nation's rice price, its futures trading officially licensed in 1730.
zh:
摄津地处淀川入海口、面向濑户内海，是日本通往西海的航路与通往京都的水路交汇之地，古来便有「津国」之称。难波津一带在645年孝德天皇迁都后成为都城，难波宫于652年落成；更早的593年，圣德太子在此建四天王寺，住吉大社则是摄津的一之宫。平清盛看中大轮田泊（后来的兵库津），修筑人工岛经岛作为避风锚地，并于1180年短暂迁都附近的福原。镰仓时代僧人重源再修此港，兵库津发展为日本第一大港，室町时代更成为日明贸易的基地。1444年的摄津，守护职出自担任管领的细川氏，但国内还分封着分郡守护和地方豪族。

1496年，净土真宗法主莲如在名为「大坂」的长坡建坊，周围形成寺内町环绕的石山本愿寺；1532年山科本愿寺被焚后，这里成为本愿寺的本山。出身细川家臣的三好氏此时已取而代之号令摄津，织田信长的征用要求最终引发石山合战：1570年至1580年，本愿寺凭坚城与海路死守，最后靠朝廷调解才开城退出。丰臣秀吉1583年在原址动工修建大坂城，城下町成为他号令天下的居城。秀吉死后，德川家在1614至1615年的大坂冬之阵、夏之阵中攻灭丰臣氏，随即将大坂重建为幕府直辖城。江户时代的大坂是「天下的台所」，诸大名的藏屋敷林立；1697年堂岛米市场迁来后决定全国米价，1730年其账合米（期货）交易更获幕府公许。

en:
Indrapura, modern Đồng Dương, was raised as the capital of Champa around 875 by the Buddhist king Indravarman II, whose Bhrgu dynasty ruled from it for a century and built the great Mahayana temple complex of Lasmindra Lokesvara; nearby stood the shrine valley of Mỹ Sơn and the sea roadstead that later became Hội An. Power moved south to Vijaya in the 12th century, yet Indrapura remained the gateway of northern Champa. In 1402 the Hồ dynasty of Đại Việt forced King Indravarman VI to cede Chiêm Động, organised as the Thăng and Hoa prefectures covering present Thăng Bình, Tam Kỳ, Quế Sơn and Duy Xuyên; the Cham recovered the land in 1407 when the Ming overthrew the Hồ. By 1444 the frontier with the restored Lê dynasty ran along this coast, and in May that year King Maha Vijaya's attack on Hóa Châu opened a war that would bring Vietnamese armies past Indrapura to Vijaya.

In 1446 the expedition of Trịnh Khả and Lê Thụ captured Vijaya and led Maha Vijaya captive to Thăng Long, though the Cham retook the city the next year. The final blow came under Lê Thánh Tông, whose navy forced the Đại Áp and Tiểu Áp sea gates off present Tam Kỳ before sacking Vijaya on 2 March 1471; Amaravati and Vijaya were annexed as the Quảng Nam province, with a Thăng Hoa garrison, and the old capital country came under Vietnamese administration. In 1558 Nguyễn Hoàng entered Thuận Hóa and from 1559 governed Quảng Nam as well, drawing settlers and soldiers from the north, and under his successors the old Cham roadstead at Hội An became one of the richest ports of Southeast Asia: Japanese red-seal ships, Chinese junks and Portuguese and Dutch traders exchanged silk, porcelain and aloewood there through the 17th and 18th centuries. The late wars of the century swept over Quảng Nam after the Tây Sơn rising began at Quy Nhơn in 1771, and Hội An's foreign trade scattered in the campaigning. With the Nguyễn reunification of 1802 the land of Indrapura became part of the new dynasty's Quảng Nam domain.
zh:
因陀罗补罗即今东阳，约875年由崇佛的占婆王因陀罗跋摩二世建为都城，他所开创的Bhrgu王朝在此统治约一个世纪，并营建了宏伟的大乘寺院群Lasmindra Lokesvara；不远处便是美山圣谷和日后长成会安的海港。12世纪占婆的权力中心南移阇盘，但因陀罗补罗仍是北占婆的门户。1402年，大越胡朝逼迫占王因陀罗跋摩六世割让占洞，置为升、华二州，即今升平、三岐、桂山、维川之地；1407年明朝灭胡，占婆乘机收复故土。到1444年，复国的后黎朝与占婆沿这段海岸对峙，当年五月摩诃贲该王攻打化州，战端由此开启，越军日后正是经过因陀罗补罗直取阇盘。

1446年，郑可、黎受的远征军攻陷阇盘，把摩诃贲该俘回升龙，但占人次年便收复了都城。最后的打击来自黎圣宗：其水军攻破今三岐近海的大压门、小压门，于1471年3月2日攻陷阇盘；阿摩罗伐底与阇盘被吞并改设广南承宣，驻军升华卫，旧都之地就此纳入越南版图。1558年阮潢入镇顺化，1559年起兼领广南，招徕北方流民军户；在其后继者治下，占婆古港会安成为东南亚最富庶的商港之一，整个17至18世纪，日本朱印船、中国帆船以及葡萄牙、荷兰商人在此交易丝绸、瓷器和沉香。1771年西山起义在归仁爆发后，广南在连绵内战中饱受兵祸，会安的外商贸易随之星散。1802年阮朝重新统一，因陀罗补罗故地成为王朝广南辖地的一部分。

en:
Echizen lay on the Sea of Japan coast between Kyoto and the northern highway, covering the fertile Fukui basin. After old Koshi was split in 701 and Kaga was separated in 823, it became the only great province of the Hokurikudo, with its provincial headquarters and guardian shrine around Fuchu, the Takefu district. Paper making began in the Imadate valleys in the Kamakura period, and a paper guild was organized at Otaki during the Muromachi period; Echizen rice and coastal traffic also made the province valuable. In 1444 the Shiba still held the title of provincial governor, but local military houses, above all the Asakura of Ichijodani, kept the real armed power.

In 1471 Asakura Toshikage displaced the Shiba and fortified Ichijodani. Refugees from the Onin War brought court nobles, priests, scholars and performers from Kyoto, and the valley became a cultural town of more than 10,000 people at its height. Asakura Yoshikage's resistance to Oda Nobunaga ended with defeat at Anegawa in 1570 and the burning of Ichijodani in 1573. After the Echizen Ikko uprising of 1574, Nobunaga subdued the province and entrusted it to Shibata Katsuie at Kita-no-sho. In 1601 Tokugawa Ieyasu gave Echizen to his son Yuki Hideyasu, who rebuilt Fukui Castle and founded the Matsudaira domain. Its officials controlled Echizen paper as a domain monopoly; in 1665 Echizen hosho paper received the privileged mark honoring it as the finest paper in the land.
zh:
越前位于日本海沿岸，扼守京都通往北方的北陆道，坐拥肥沃的福井盆地。701年旧越国分裂、823年加贺分立后，越前成为北陆道唯一的大国，国衙和总社都在武生一带的府中。镰仓时代，今立诸谷开始造纸，室町时代又在大泷村设立纸座；越前米与日本海沿岸交通也使此国十分富庶。1444年，斯波氏仍保有守护头衔，但真正掌握武力的是国内武家，尤其是以一乘谷为据点的朝仓氏。

1471年，朝仓敏景（亦称孝景）取代斯波氏，把一乘谷建成坚固据点。应仁之乱中，避乱的公家、僧侣、学者和艺人从京都前来，使这条山谷发展为极盛时人口逾万的文化町，号称「北之京」。朝仓义景对抗织田信长，先于1570年在姊川战败，1573年一乘谷又被焚毁。1574年越前一向一揆爆发，织田信长次年平定越前，把它交给以北之庄为本据的柴田胜家。1601年，德川家康将越前封给儿子结城秀康，秀康重修福井城，开创松平氏福井藩。藩方把越前和纸纳入专卖统制；1665年，越前奉书获准使用「御上天下一」印，享有天下第一纸的荣誉。

en:
Echigo stretched along the Sea of Japan from the Kubiki plain into the northern river valleys, corresponding to most of later Niigata Prefecture. It began as a Yamato border province facing Emishi lands, and in 702 it received the fertile districts of Kubiki, Koshi, Uonuma and Kanbara. The provincial office was placed at Naoetsu in 706, followed by the provincial temple in 741; the port itself is documented under the name To in 762. The Hojo of Kamakura once ruled Echigo directly, and under the Muromachi shogunate the Uesugi held the governorship. In 1444 their Nagao deputies managed much of the Kubiki heartland, while local warrior houses and the grain-rich inland valleys kept considerable autonomy.

That deputy house overturned the old order in 1507, when Nagao Tamekage attacked Governor Uesugi Fusayoshi and installed Uesugi Sadazane as a puppet. Nagao Kagetora inherited Kasugayama in 1548, took the Uesugi name as Kenshin, and used the mountain fortress as his base for the 1561 Kawanakajima campaign against Takeda Shingen. After Kenshin's death in 1578, the Otate succession war ended with Uesugi Kagekatsu in control. Hideyoshi transferred Kagekatsu to Aizu in 1598; Hori Hideharu took Kasugayama, but the coastal Fukushima Castle replaced it as the administrative seat in 1607. Under the Tokugawa, Echigo was divided among Takada, Nagaoka, Shibata and other domains; Matsudaira Tadateru built Takada Castle before his removal in 1616, while Niigata grew rich in the coastal kitamaebune trade.
zh:
越后位于日本海沿岸，从颈城平原延伸到北方河谷，辖境大体相当于后来的新潟县本州部分。它最初是大和政权面向虾夷之地的边境国，702年领有肥沃的颈城、古志、鱼沼、蒲原四郡。706年，国衙设在直江津，741年又建立国分寺；762年的文书中已以「都宇」记载这座港口。镰仓时代北条氏曾直接统治越后，室町幕府时期则由上杉氏担任守护。1444年，上杉氏的守护代长尾氏实际管理颈城腹地，地方武家与盛产谷物的内陆诸谷仍保有相当自主权。

1507年，守护代家推翻旧秩序：长尾为景袭击守护上杉房能，另立上杉定实为傀儡。1548年，长尾景虎继承春日山城，后来改名上杉谦信，并以这座山城为基地，在1561年的川中岛之战中对阵武田信玄。1578年谦信死后，御馆之乱以养子上杉景胜掌权告终。1598年，丰臣秀吉把上杉景胜转封会津，堀秀治入主春日山；1607年，沿海的福岛城取代春日山成为行政中心，春日山遂废。江户时代，越后被分为高田、长冈、新发田等藩，松平忠辉曾修建高田城，后于1616年被除封；新潟则因北前船沿海贸易日益繁荣。

en:
The Yamagata and Yonezawa basins make up the southern half of Dewa, walled off from the Pacific by the Ōu Mountains and watered by the Mogami River. In 1356 Shiba Kaneyori entered the valley as the shogunate's Ushū tandai and raised Yamagata Castle around 1360; his descendants took their name from the land and became the Mogami clan. In 1444 the Mogami, a cadet branch of the Shiba, ruled the region from Yamagata, but their hold was loosening as the blood ties binding their retainer families frayed.

In 1514 Mogami Yoshisada lost to Date Tanemune, and for a generation the clan bowed to the Date until Mogami Yoshimori won back his freedom during the Date civil war of 1542. Under Yoshimori's son Mogami Yoshiaki the north had a new power: Hideyoshi confirmed him at some 200,000 koku after the 1590 Odawara campaign, and in 1600 he withstood a full Uesugi invasion while Ieyasu won at Sekigahara, emerging with 570,000 koku, the fifth-largest fief outside the Tokugawa domains. Yoshiaki rebuilt Yamagata Castle and its castle town and tamed the Mogami River for navigation and irrigation; after he died in 1614 succession quarrels tore at the house, and in 1622 the shogunate confiscated the fief, which then passed through the Torii, Hoshina and other families and ended with the Mizuno on 50,000 koku. In the southern basin the Uesugi, defeated at Sekigahara, were settled at Yonezawa with 300,000 koku, cut to 150,000 in 1664 and nearly bankrupt when Uesugi Harunori took power; his long reforms of austerity and new industries restored the domain and carried it through the Tenmei famine of 1781–1789.
zh:
山形与米泽两处盆地构成出羽国的南半，奥羽山脉将其与太平洋隔开，最上川横贯其间。1356年，斯波兼赖以幕府羽州探题的身份进入山形盆地，约1360年筑起山形城；其后代以地名为氏，改称最上氏。1444年，斯波一族的旁支最上氏据山形统治此地，但随着维系一门与家臣的血缘纽带松弛，他们对领地的掌控也在动摇。

1514年最上义定为伊达稙宗所败，此后一代人的时间臣服于伊达氏，直到最上义守趁1542年伊达内讧的天文之乱恢复独立。义守之子最上义光时代，最上成为北国的一大势力：1590年小田原出阵后，丰臣秀吉承认他约二十万石的领地；1600年关原之战时，他顶住上杉大军的全面进攻，战后领有五十七万石，成为德川家领地之外的第五大藩。义光改建山形城与城下町，又整治最上川以利航运与灌溉；他1614年去世后继嗣纷争不断，1622年领地被幕府没收，此后山形先后转封鸟居、保科等家，最终为五万石的水野氏。南边的米泽盆地安置了关原战败的上杉氏，封地三十万石，1664年削为十五万石；到上杉治宪（鹰山）主持藩政时藩国已濒临破产，他以俭约和兴产的长期改革重振米泽，使其度过了1781至1789年的天明大饥荒。

en:
The Pacific seaboard and the inland Aizu basin together formed the southern marches of Mutsu Province. In 1189 Minamoto no Yoritomo rewarded Isa Tomomune for his part in the Genpei War with the Date district, and the Date clan he founded grew into one of the great warrior houses of the north, siding with the Southern Court through Kitabatake Akiie in the Nanboku-chō wars. Deep in the western hills the Ashina clan held the Aizu basin around Kurokawa, styling themselves its governors. In 1444 the Date ruled the eastern lowlands and the Ashina the basin behind the mountains, and the two houses watched one another across the passes.

In 1589 Date Masamune broke Ashina power at the Battle of Suriagehara and made Kurokawa his base, but after the Odawara campaign of 1590 Hideyoshi stripped Aizu from him for breaking his peace edict and enfeoffed Gamō Ujisato, who renamed Kurokawa Wakamatsu and laid out its castle town beneath a seven-storey keep. When Ujisato died in 1595 his house fell from favour, and in 1598 Uesugi Kagekatsu moved in from Echigo with 1,200,000 koku; the warlike preparations of his minister Naoe Kanetsugu gave Ieyasu the pretext for the Aizu expedition of 1600, and after Sekigahara the Uesugi were gone. The Gamō returned and then the Katō, until Katō Akinari was attainted in 1643 and the fief passed to Hoshina Masayuki, half-brother of Shōgun Iemitsu and guardian to the child Ietsuna, whose Aizu-Matsudaira line held Wakamatsu thenceforth. Masamune, moved off his ancestral lands, took up Iwadeyama Castle and built Sendai; the Date entered the Edo order with some 620,000 koku, the third-largest domain in Japan, though even they came to succession bloodshed in the Date Disturbance of 1671.
zh:
太平洋沿岸与深藏内陆的会津盆地，共同构成陆奥国的南境。1189年，源赖朝将伊达郡封给在源平合战中立功的伊佐朝宗；他开创的伊达氏成长为北国的大武士家族之一，南北朝纷争中还通过北畠显家效忠于南朝。西部群山之中，芦名氏以黑川为据点领有会津盆地，自称会津守护。1444年，伊达氏统治东部低地，芦名氏保有群山环抱的盆地，两家隔着山口彼此戒备。

1589年，伊达政宗在摺上原之战击灭芦名氏，把黑川作为新据点；但1590年小田原征伐后，秀吉以违背总无事令为由收回会津，封给蒲生氏乡。氏乡把黑川改名若松，筑起七层天守，规划城下町，奠定了日后会津若松的基础。1595年氏乡去世后蒲生家失势，1598年上杉景胜以一百二十万石从越后入封；家老直江兼续主持的军备扩张给了家康1600年会津征伐的口实，关原战后上杉氏撤出会津。其后蒲生氏一度回归，又转封加藤氏；1643年加藤明成遭改易，会津封给三代将军家光的异母弟、幼主家纲的后见人保科正之，其会津松平家从此世代领有若松。伊达政宗则离开祖传之地，先入岩出山城，继而营建仙台；伊达氏以约六十二万石位列江户幕府第三大藩，即便如此仍在1671年的伊达骚动中卷入继嗣流血纷争。

en:
Hitachi faced the Pacific on the eastern side of Kanto and covered most of what later became Ibaraki. Its seventh-century provincial capital and temple stood near Ishioka, while Kashima Shrine drew warriors and travellers to the coastal lowlands. The Satake, based at Ota Castle, served the Ashikaga shogunate as provincial governors, but their hold was incomplete. In 1427 the Edo family seized Baba Castle, the stronghold that later became Mito, and often defied the Satake. Thus in 1444 the province was a patchwork of Satake retainers and local warrior houses, whose estates rose from fishing shores and the lower Naka River valley toward the wooded northern hills.

The Satake backed Toyotomi Hideyoshi at Odawara in 1590 while the Edo held out for the Hojo, and Satake Yoshishige and Yoshinobu were confirmed over Hitachi, assessed at 540,000 koku. Baba Castle fell in 1594, was rebuilt as Mito Castle, and became the Satake seat in place of Ota. After Yoshinobu's ambiguous conduct at Sekigahara, Tokugawa Ieyasu transferred him in 1602 from Hitachi to the much smaller Kubota domain in Dewa. In 1609 Tokugawa Yorifusa, Ieyasu's eleventh son, entered Mito with 250,000 koku and founded the Mito Tokugawa house, one of the three chief Tokugawa branches. Under Tokugawa Mitsukuni, who became lord in 1661, the Shokokan compiled the Dai Nihon-shi; the annals and biographies were presented to the shogunate in 1720, giving Mito its lasting name for historical scholarship.
zh:
常陆位于关东东部，临太平洋，辖境大体相当于后来茨城县的大部分。7世纪设立令制国后，国衙和国分寺建在石冈附近，鹿岛神宫则吸引武士与旅人来到沿海低地。以太田城为本据的佐竹氏奉室町幕府之命担任常陆守护，却未能完全控制全国。1427年，江户氏夺取后来成为水户城的马场城，并屡次与佐竹氏对抗。因此1444年的常陆是佐竹家臣与各地武家领地交错的局面，庄园从渔业海岸和那珂川下游谷地一直延伸到北面的山林丘陵。

1590年小田原征伐时，佐竹义重、佐竹义宣父子投靠丰臣秀吉，江户氏则支持后北条氏；佐竹氏遂获得本领54万石的常陆一国。1594年马场城陷落，被改建为水户城并取代太田成为佐竹氏本据。关原之战后，德川家康追究佐竹义宣的暧昧态度，于1602年把他从常陆转封到出羽小得多的久保田藩。1609年，家康第十一子德川赖房以25万石进入水户，开创德川御三家之一的水户德川家。1661年继任藩主的德川光圀设彰考馆编纂《大日本史》，本纪与列传于1720年上呈幕府，水户也以史学传统闻名。

en:
Musashi, the largest province of the Kantō, is the plain between the Chichibu hills and Edo Bay, crossed by the Arakawa and the Tone. Its ancient capital stood at Fuchū and its ichinomiya was the Hikawa Shrine; native copper found at Chichibu in 708 gave the court its Wadō era name and supplied Japan's first coinage. Under the Kamakura shoguns the province was the heartland of the eastern warriors, the Musashi shichitō. In the Muromachi age it was governed by the Uesugi, the Kantō kanrei, from strongholds such as Kawagoe, while fishing boats and traders used the harbours of Shinagawa and Asakusa on the bay. In 1444 the Uesugi had just crushed the Kamakura kubo in the Eikyō war, but the Kantō was far from settled and Edo itself was still a small fortified homestead.

In 1457 the Ogigayatsu-Uesugi had their steward Ōta Dōkan fortify both Kawagoe and Edo, linking them with a military road. The Later Hōjō of Odawara seized Edo in 1524, and in the night battle of Kawagoe in 1546 Hōjō Ujiyasu overwhelmed the besieging Uesugi armies, making himself master of the Kantō. Toyotomi Hideyoshi destroyed the Hōjō at Odawara in 1590 and moved Tokugawa Ieyasu to the east; Ieyasu entered Edo that August and built it into his capital, and from 1603 it was the seat of his shogunate. The Tamagawa aqueduct reached the city in 1653, the Meireki fire swept it in 1657, and by the early eighteenth century Edo held over a million people. Kawagoe, seat of Musashi's greatest domain and the shogunate's northern guard, fed the city by river barge and became known as 'little Edo', famed for its sweet potatoes.
zh:
武藏是关东最大的令制国，地处秩父山地与江户湾之间的平原，荒川、利根川流贯其间。古代国府在府中，一之宫为冰川神社；708年秩父发现自然铜，朝廷因此改元「和铜」，并以这批铜铸造日本最早的钱币和同开珎。镰仓时代，这里是东国武士的大本营，武藏七党的族人随源氏起家。室町时代，担任关东管领的上杉氏以川越等据点统治此国，江户湾边的品川凑、浅草凑则是渔船和商船往来之处。1444年，上杉氏刚在永享之乱中压服镰仓公方，但关东远未安定，江户还只是一座小小的武士馆。

1457年，扇谷上杉氏命家宰太田道灌、道真父子修筑河越城与江户城，并用军路把两城连为一线。1524年，小田原的后北条氏夺取江户城；1546年河越夜战，北条氏康以奇袭击溃围城的两上杉大军，就此成为关东之主。1590年丰臣秀吉攻灭小田原北条氏，把德川家康转封关东；家康同年8月入主江户，将其营建为居城，1603年更在此开设幕府。1653年玉川上水通水，1657年明历大火焚毁大半市区，到18世纪初江户人口已逾百万。川越是武藏最大藩川越藩的城下町、幕府的北方屏障，靠新河岸川舟运为江户供给物资，被称为「小江户」，川越芋尤为有名。

en:
Kai, later abbreviated Kōshū, filled the mountain-girt Kōfu Basin of central Honshū, with Mount Fuji standing on its border with Suruga and Sagami. One of the provinces created by the Taihō Code, it was ranked a 'superior country' and counted among the Tōkaidō provinces even though the highway itself passed it by. In the Heian period the Kai Genji, a branch of the Minamoto, spread through the basin, and their Takeda line held the shugo post through the Kamakura and Muromachi ages. But when Takeda Nobumitsu perished in the Uesugi Zenshū rebellion of 1416–17, the province lost its shugo, and by 1444 the deputy Atobe clan and local landowners had divided Kai among themselves, leaving the Takeda lord little more than his title. The steep pastures bred sturdy horses, while the basin floor, laced by the Fuefuki and Kamanashi rivers, flooded as often as it yielded rice.

The Takeda restored themselves later in the century, and in 1519 Takeda Nobutora built his Tsutsujigasaki residence in the middle of the basin, founding the castle town of Kōfu. His son Harunobu, better known as Shingen, drove him out in 1541 and made Kai the arsenal of a war state: gold from the Kurokawa mines, first mentioned in writing in 1498, was struck into Kōshū coin, while dikes and diversion works along the Kamanashi protected the flooded fields. From Kōfu he conquered Shinano, fought Uesugi Kenshin in the five Kawanakajima battles of 1553–64, and invaded Suruga in 1568, before dying on campaign in Mikawa in 1573. His son Katsuyori was broken at Nagashino in 1575, and in 1582 the Takeda were destroyed by Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu. After Nobunaga's death Kai was contested between Ieyasu and the Go-Hōjō in the Tenshō-Jingo disturbance, and after the fall of Odawara in 1590 Hideyoshi stationed loyalist daimyō there to watch Ieyasu's Kantō. Under the Tokugawa, the Kōshū Kaidō linked Kōfu with Edo; Kōfu Domain passed through Tokugawa kinsmen and, from 1705 to 1724, the Yanagisawa family, after which most of Kai was kept as direct shogunal land.
zh:
甲斐（简称甲州）是本州中部群山环抱中的甲府盆地，东南与骏河、相模交界处耸立着富士山。它是《大宝律令》设定的令制国之一，定为上国，虽不在东海道干线沿线，仍被划入东海道诸国。平安时代，源氏支流甲斐源氏进入盆地，其嫡流武田氏在镰仓、室町时代历任守护。1416至1417年的上杉禅秀之乱中，守护武田信满败亡，甲斐陷入守护不在的局面；到1444年，守护代迹部氏与各地国人割据盆地，武田氏徒有守护之名。山间牧场出产良马，而笛吹川、釜无川纵横的盆底虽能种稻，却也水患不断。

15世纪后期武田氏重新振作，1519年武田信虎在盆地中央筑起踯躅崎馆，开创了甲府城下町。1541年，其子晴信（即信玄）将他放逐，把甲斐变成战争机器的腹地：黑川金山的黄金——现存最早记载见于1498年的《王代记》——被铸成甲州金，釜无川沿岸的堤防与分洪工程则护住了良田。他以甲府为基地征服信浓，1553至1564年间与上杉谦信五度鏖战川中岛，1568年攻入骏河，最终于1573年在三河军中病亡。其子胜赖1575年惨败于长篠，1582年武田氏被织田信长与德川家康攻灭。信长死后，德川与后北条为争夺武田旧领爆发天正壬午之乱；1590年小田原落城后，秀吉把丰臣系大名安置在甲斐，监视坐拥关东的家康。江户时代，甲州街道把甲府与江户相连；甲府藩先后由德川一族及谱代大名执掌，柳泽氏在1705至1724年领有此地，此后甲斐大部分土地收为幕府直辖的天领。

en:
Owari is a small province on the Ise Bay plain, watered by the lower Kiso and crossed by the Tokaido highway linking Kyoto with the east. Its black soil raised heavy rice crops, and the ancient Atsuta Shrine, keeper of the imperial sword Kusanagi, drew pilgrims along the same road. Kiyosu Castle was raised in 1405 for the Shiba, the warrior house that ruled the province as military governors, but day-to-day power had passed to their deputies, the Oda. In 1444 Owari was therefore a rich and populous farming country of the eastern seaboard, governed from Kiyosu by the Oda in their lords' name.

The Onin War split the Oda into rival Kiyosu and Iwakura houses. Oda Nobuhide seized Nagoya Castle from an Imagawa garrison in 1532, and his son Nobunaga was born there in 1534; Nobunaga took Kiyosu in 1555, overthrew Iwakura in 1559, and on 12 June 1560 destroyed the invading army of Imagawa Yoshimoto at Okehazama, the first blow in his march across Japan. After Nobunaga's death in 1582 his generals divided the succession at the Kiyosu conference, and in 1584 the fields of Komaki and Nagakute saw the stand-off between Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu. When Oda Nobukatsu refused a transfer after the fall of the Hojo in 1590, Hideyoshi split the province among his generals, Fukushima Masanori taking the largest share. After Sekigahara the domain went to Ieyasu's fourth son, Matsudaira Tadayoshi, and in 1607 to his ninth son, Tokugawa Yoshinao, whose Owari Tokugawa house, rated at some 620,000 koku, stood first of the three collateral branches that could supply a shogun. Nagoya Castle, built from 1610 on the site of the old Oda fort, became the seat of a flourishing castle town, fed by the Seto kilns whose pottery made Owari known nationwide.
zh:
尾张是伊势湾沿岸平原上的小国，木曾川下游润泽其地，连接京都与东国的东海道纵贯而过。这里土地肥沃，稻米丰产；古老的热田神宫供奉着三种神器之一的草薙剑，参拜客沿东海道络绎而来。1405年，出任守护的斯波氏修筑清洲城，但实权逐渐落入守护代织田氏之手。1444年的尾张已是东海道上富庶人众的农业之国，由织田氏在清洲代主治国。

应仁之乱中，织田氏分裂为清洲、岩仓两家相争。织田信秀1532年从今川家守军手中夺取那古野城，其子信长于1534年出生在那里；信长1555年取得清洲，1559年攻灭岩仓家，又在1560年6月12日的桶狭间之战中大破来犯的今川义元，迈出了争夺天下的第一步。1582年信长死后，诸将在清洲会议上分割家业；1584年，小牧、长久手一带成为丰臣秀吉与德川家康对峙的战场。1590年后北条氏灭亡，织田信雄拒绝转封，秀吉便把尾张分封给麾下诸将，福岛正则所得最多。关原之战后，尾张先封给家康四子松平忠吉，1607年由九子德川义直继承；他开创的尾张德川家石高约六十二万石，在可继承将军之位的御三家中居首。1610年起在织田旧城址上修筑的名古屋城，成为繁荣的城下町中心，濑户窑场出产的陶器也让尾张名闻全国。

en:
Kamikawa is the broad northern interior of Ezo, from the forested basin of the upper Ishikari—the Ainu Peni Unguri Kotan, 'the village of the upstream people', from which its name comes—north to Sōya, where the island narrows to a strait opposite Sakhalin. Ainu villages dotted the Ishikari and Teshio valleys and the Sea of Okhotsk coast, living on salmon, deer and sea mammals, and the shore still held shell mounds left by the older Okhotsk fishing culture. In 1444 no Japanese lord ruled here: furs crossed the Sōya Strait to Sakhalin and the continent, while rice and iron were bartered up from the Japanese settlements on the Oshima Peninsula far to the south.

In 1603 the Matsumae domain placed a station at Sōya, its furthest trading post, with charge over Sōya and Sakhalin alike. From the 1680s Santan merchants, Ulch and Nivkh from the lower Amur, brought Qing official robes and silk brocades to Sōya through Sakhalin Ainu hands; the so-called Ezo brocades passed on through Matsumae and were prized in Edo and Osaka. In 1787 the French navigator Lapérouse surveyed the strait off Cape Sōya that now bears his name. As Russian ships probed the Kurils, the shogunate took East Ezo under direct rule in 1799 and the west, including Sōya, in 1807. In 1809 Matsuda Denjūrō settled the Ainu's accumulated Santan debts, while Mamiya Rinzō crossed the strait to explore the Amur. Through the whole Edo period the mountainous Kamikawa interior remained Ainu hunting ground.
zh:
上川是虾夷地北部的广阔内陆，南起阿伊努语称「佩尼温古里科坦」（意为上游人之村，上川由此得名）的石狩川上游森林盆地，北抵与桦太隔海相望的宗谷。阿伊努人的村落散布在石狩川、天盐川流域和鄂霍次克海沿岸，以捕鲑、猎鹿和猎取海兽为生，海岸上还留着更早的鄂霍次克渔猎文化的贝冢。1444年时没有任何和人领主统治这里：毛皮经宗谷海峡流向桦太与大陆，稻米和铁器则从南方渡岛半岛的和人聚落辗转换来。

1603年，松前藩在宗谷设置其最北端的番所，统管宗谷与桦太。1680年代起，来自黑龙江下游的山丹人——乌尔奇人和尼夫赫人——借桦太阿伊努人之手，把清朝官服和织锦带到宗谷，所谓「虾夷锦」再经松前转销，在江户和大坂备受珍视。1787年，法国航海家拉彼鲁兹测量了宗谷岬外的海峡，这道海峡后来便以他的名字命名。随着俄罗斯船只在千岛一带活动，江户幕府于1799年将东虾夷地收归直辖，1807年又接管包括宗谷在内的西虾夷地。1809年，松田传十郎清理阿伊努人积欠山丹商人的债务，间宫林藏则渡过海峡探查黑龙江下游。整个江户时代，上川的深山内陆始终是阿伊努人的渔猎之地。

en:
The Kurils are a chain of volcanoes and fog banks running some 1,300 kilometres from the tip of Ezo to Kamchatka. By the fifteenth century Ainu had spread through the islands: Kuril Ainu lived on the wind-scoured northern isles of Shumshu and Paramushir, while Menashi Ainu from eastern Ezo crossed to Kunashir and Iturup in the south. They hunted sea otter and seal, took salmon in the rivers, and had traded among themselves for centuries, so that Japanese iron and cloth moved north from island to island and furs moved back toward Ezo. In 1444 the archipelago belonged to no state, bound together by Ainu canoe routes reaching south to Ezo and north to Kamchatka.

The first Europeans came in 1643, when the Dutch expedition of Maarten Gerritsz Vries landed and met Ainu on Urup; the shogunate's own Shōhō map of 1644 already showed thirty-nine islands northeast of Cape Nosappu. In 1711 Cossacks crossing from Kamchatka landed on Shumshu, and in 1713 they fought their way onto Paramushir and imposed the fur tribute called yasak, pressing south island by island for sea-otter pelts. From the other direction the Matsumae domain opened its Kunashir trading post in 1754, covering Kunashir, Iturup and Urup. A Russian party under Ivan Cherny occupied Urup in 1766 and worked the Ainu hard; in 1772 the islanders rose, killed twenty-one Russians and drove the rest to Kamchatka. Mogami Tokunai surveyed Iturup and Urup for the shogunate in 1786, and in 1798 Kondō Jūzō raised a 'Great Japan' marker on Iturup; the next year the Kurils, as part of East Ezo, came under direct shogunal rule. Khvostov's Russians raided Iturup in 1806, and in 1811 Captain Golovnin was seized on Kunashir and held prisoner at Matsumae until 1813.
zh:
千岛是一串火山与雾之岛，从虾夷地东北端绵延约一千三百公里直到勘察加。到15世纪，阿伊努人已散布列岛：千岛阿伊努人居于占守、幌筵等风高浪急的北海岛屿，道东的目梨阿伊努人则渡海来到南方的国后、择捉。他们猎海獭和海豹、在河中捕鲑，彼此间已有数百年贸易：和人的铁器、布匹一岛岛向北流转，毛皮则南销虾夷。1444年的千岛不属于任何政权，维系全列岛的是阿伊努人的独木舟航路，南接虾夷，北连勘察加。

最早到来的欧洲人是荷兰人：1643年，马滕·赫里特松·弗里斯的探险队在得抚岛登陆并与阿伊努人接触；江户幕府1644年的正保国绘图上，已在纳沙布岬东北绘出三十九座岛屿。1711年，哥萨克从勘察加渡海登陆占守岛，1713年又以武力镇压幌筵岛的阿伊努人，课以毛皮贡赋（雅萨克），随后为猎取海獭皮逐岛南下。另一方向，松前藩1754年开设国后场所，统辖国后、择捉、得抚三岛。1766年，伊万·乔尔内一伙俄人进占得抚岛，苛役阿伊努人猎獭；1772年岛民起事，杀死二十一名俄人，将余者逐回勘察加。1786年，最上德内奉幕府之命调查择捉、得抚；1798年近藤重藏在择捉岛立下「大日本惠登吕府」标柱，次年千岛随东虾夷地收归幕府直辖。1806年，赫沃斯托夫率俄船袭掠择捉与桦太；1811年，俄舰舰长戈洛夫宁在国后岛被扣，囚于松前，直到1813年才获释。

en:
Enchiw lies on Sakhalin, the long, fog-bound island between the Sea of Okhotsk and the Strait of Tartary. In 1444 its southern shore was Ainu country, while Nivkh fishers and hunters used the northern coasts and moved between the island and the Amur estuary; both peoples lived from salmon, sea mammals, forest game and furs. The Yuan had subdued the island's Ainu by 1308 and taken tribute at mainland posts, and the Ming later gave Sakhalin headmen hereditary titles through the Nurgan commission. Yet that commission had faded by the mid-1430s, so Ming silk and ranks reached the island only loosely while clan elders controlled the villages and fishing grounds.

Japanese vessels from Matsumae reached southern Sakhalin in 1635, and a Matsumae explorer wintered on the island in 1636 before sailing to Taraika the next spring. The Dutch mariner Martin de Vries charted Cape Aniva and Cape Patience in 1643 without realizing that the land was one island, and a Japanese settlement was founded at Otomari in 1679. After the 1689 Treaty of Nerchinsk, Qing officers entered the Amur estuary and reimposed a fur tribute; the 1732 register counted six clans, eighteen village units and 148 tribute households on Sakhalin. In 1787 Jean-Francois de La Perouse mapped much of the Strait of Tartary and recorded the local name Tchoka. Ivan Kruzenshtern surveyed much of the coast in 1805, and Japanese expeditions proved Sakhalin was an island in 1808.
zh:
恩奇乌位于狭长多雾的萨哈林岛，地处鄂霍次克海与鞑靼海峡之间。1444年，岛的南岸是阿伊努人的土地，尼夫赫渔猎民则利用北部海岸，并在岛屿与黑龙江口之间往来；他们以鲑鱼、海兽、山林猎物和毛皮为生。元朝到1308年已降服岛上阿伊努人，并在大陆站点收受贡物；明朝后来通过奴儿干机构授予萨哈林族长世袭职衔。但该机构到1430年代中期已经衰微，明朝的丝绸和官衔只能松散地抵达此岛，村落与渔场仍由氏族长老掌控。

1635年，松前的日本船只到达萨哈林南部，一名松前探险者1636年在岛上过冬，次年航至塔拉伊卡。1643年，荷兰水手马丁·德·弗里斯测绘阿尼瓦角和捷尔佩尼耶角，却未察觉这片土地是一座岛屿；1679年，日本人在大泊建立定居点。1689年《尼布楚条约》后，清朝官员进入黑龙江口，重新推行毛皮朝贡；1732年的册籍登记了岛上6个氏族、18个村单位和148户贡民。1787年，让-弗朗索瓦·德·拉彼鲁兹测绘鞑靼海峡大部，并记下当地名称「乔卡」。1805年，伊万·克鲁森施滕考察了大部分海岸；1808年，日本探险队证实萨哈林是一座岛屿。

en:
The rivers and sheltered bays of southern Kamchatka were Itelmen country in 1444. Villages moved with the salmon runs, and boats also put out for seals, whales and sea birds along the Pacific coast; Ainu settlements reached the southern tip, while Koryak lands began toward the north. The Kamchatka River linked fishing camps through the peninsula's long volcanic valley, but no outside ruler yet collected tribute there.

Russian Cossacks entered from the Arctic side rather than the stormy Pacific. Vladimir Atlasov left Anadyrsk in January 1697 with about 120 men, crossed the Koryak Range and built the Verkhnekamchatsk ostrog on the upper Kamchatka. Nizhnekamchatsk followed in 1700 and Bolsheretsk in 1703, yet rebellion and Cossack mutiny continued; Atlasov himself was killed at Nizhnekamchatsk in 1711. During the 1740s Vitus Bering's expedition founded Petropavlovsk on Avacha Bay and Orthodox baptism spread among the Itelmens. Stepan Krasheninnikov published his detailed description of Kamchatka in 1755, and organized resistance ended the next year. The smallpox epidemic of 1768–1769 reduced the native population by about 65 percent, to roughly 2,600 people, opening the way for Russian settlement and the mixed Kamchadal community recorded by the early nineteenth century.
zh:
1444年的南堪察加河湾与河谷是伊捷尔缅人的土地。村落在鲑鱼洄游季节迁移营地，船只也从太平洋海岸出海猎捕海豹、鲸和海鸟；阿伊努人的聚落延伸到半岛南端，北面则进入科里亚克人的活动范围。堪察加河把火山长谷中的渔营串连起来，但此时还没有外来统治者到这里征收贡赋。

俄国哥萨克没有从风浪险恶的太平洋直接登岸，而是从北极一侧进入。1697年1月，弗拉基米尔·阿特拉索夫率约120人离开阿纳德尔堡，越过科里亚克山脉，在堪察加河上游建立上堪察加茨克堡。下堪察加茨克和博利舍列茨克分别建于1700年和1703年，但当地反抗与哥萨克哗变仍持续不断，阿特拉索夫本人也于1711年在下堪察加茨克被杀。1740年代，维图斯·白令的探险队在阿瓦恰湾建立彼得罗巴甫洛夫斯克，东正教洗礼也在伊捷尔缅人中传播。斯捷潘·克拉舍宁尼科夫于1755年出版详尽的堪察加记述，有组织的抵抗在次年结束。1768—1769年的天花使当地人口减少约65%，只剩约2600人，为俄国移民和19世纪初已见记载的堪察加人混血社会铺平了道路。

en:
The Penzhina River winds 713 kilometres through tundra and low mountains to a narrow arm of the Sea of Okhotsk, where tides can rise nearly thirteen metres. In 1444 its banks and coast were Koryak country: settled coastal villages fished for salmon and hunted seals, while reindeer herders moved inland between seasonal pastures. Chukchi camps lay farther toward the Anadyr, but no Cossack tribute route had yet crossed this stormy, ice-bound threshold to Kamchatka.

Mikhail Stadukhin's men saw the western Kamchatkan coast from Penzhina Bay in 1651 and clashed with Koryaks on the Gizhiga the next year. During 1696–1697 Vladimir Atlasov led sixty Russians and sixty Yukaghirs against the Penzhina Koryaks and took furs from Aklan and two other fortified camps. The Penzhinsky ostrog, raised in the autumn of 1709, became a target in the hard frontier wars of 1708–1715 and again in the great Koryak rising of 1745–1757; another Aklansk fort, built at the Oklan mouth in 1742–1743, was destroyed in 1746. Armed resistance ended by the later 1750s, though a new town of Aklansk founded in 1786 lasted only until 1804. War and the smallpox epidemic of 1769–1770 helped reduce the Koryaks from roughly 10,000–11,000 at the end of the seventeenth century to about 4,800 by 1800.
zh:
品仁纳河蜿蜒713公里，穿过苔原与低山，注入鄂霍次克海一道狭窄海湾，湾内潮差可达近13米。1444年时，河岸与海滨都是科里亚克人的土地：定居沿岸的村落捕捞鲑鱼、猎捕海豹，内陆的养鹿人则随季节在牧场间迁徙。楚科奇人的营地更靠近阿纳德尔河方向，此时还没有哥萨克的贡赋路线越过这片通往堪察加、冰雪封阻的狂暴门户。

1651年，米哈伊尔·斯塔杜欣的队伍从品仁纳湾望见堪察加西海岸，次年又在吉日加河与科里亚克人交战。1696—1697年，弗拉基米尔·阿特拉索夫率领60名俄国人和60名尤卡吉尔人进攻品仁纳的科里亚克人，从阿克兰和另外两处设防营地收取毛皮贡赋。1709年秋建立的品仁纳堡，在1708—1715年严酷的边境战争中成为攻击目标，又在1745—1757年科里亚克人大起义中遭围攻；1742—1743年在奥克兰河口修建的另一座阿克兰斯克堡于1746年被毁。武装抵抗到1750年代后期结束，而1786年新设的阿克兰斯克城只维持到1804年。战争和1769—1770年的天花，使科里亚克人从17世纪末约1万至1.1万人降至1800年的约4800人。

en:
The middle Kolyma is a wide, forested reach of the great river that drains northeast Siberia into the Arctic. Its Yukaghir inhabitants called themselves odul or vadul, 'the mighty'. They spent the short summers fishing and driving wild reindeer into the water, and the long winters trapping sable and travelling by dog sled across the snow. Clans gathered in spring under elders and shamans, and in 1444 no Russian had yet seen the Kolyma; the nearest horse-keeping strangers were the Yakuts far to the southwest on the Lena.

In 1644 Cossacks under Mikhail Stadukhin and Dmitry Zyryan, pushing east from the Indigirka, raised a fort on the left bank at the head of sea-going navigation, one of three Kolyma forts a few days' sled journey apart. Spring fairs of Yukaghir hunters and Yakutsk merchants later gave it the name Yarmanka. Sable tribute and the overland route to the Indigirka long made it the Russians' chief station on the river. It gained town status and its present name, Srednekolymsk, in 1775. In 1786 and 1787 Joseph Billings's north-east expedition built two vessels, the Yasashka and the Palas, upriver at Verkhnekolymsk for its survey of the Arctic coast.
zh:
科雷马河是西伯利亚东北部注入北冰洋的大河，本省所在的中游两岸是茂密的泰加林。住在这里的尤卡吉尔人自称奥杜尔（瓦杜尔），意为「强者」。他们在短暂的夏季捕鱼，把野鹿赶进河中围猎，漫长的冬季则猎捕紫貂，乘狗拉雪橇在雪原上游走。各氏族在长老和萨满主持下于春天聚首。1444年时还没有俄国人见过科雷马河，离这里最近的外来者是远在西南面勒拿河上养马的雅库特人。

1644年，米哈伊尔·斯塔杜欣和德米特里·济良率领哥萨克从因迪吉尔卡河东进，在海船通航河段顶端的左岸建起寨堡，这是科雷马河上三座相距数日雪橇路程的寨堡之一。尤卡吉尔猎人与雅库茨克商人每年春季在此赶集，集市后来给这里带来「亚尔曼卡」的名字。中游的紫貂实物税和通往因迪吉尔卡的陆路，使它长期成为俄国人在科雷马河上的首要据点。1775年，寨堡设镇并定名中科雷姆斯克。1786至1787年，约瑟夫·比林斯的东北探险队在上游的上科雷姆斯克建造「亚萨什卡号」和「帕拉斯号」两艘船，用于勘测北冰洋海岸。

en:
The Omolon winds 1,114 kilometres out of the Kolyma Range to join the Kolyma above its delta, the great river's largest tributary; its Yukaghir name means 'river of the Omol clan'. Along its lower course and on the Kolyma tundra lived the Omolontsy, Omoki and Chuvantsy, tundra Yukaghirs who chased wild reindeer on foot and by dog sled, took the autumn fish runs and trapped Arctic fox. To their east ranged the Chukchi. In 1444 the whole country knew no master but its own clans.

In 1644 Mikhail Stadukhin and Dmitry Zyryan founded the Nizhnekolymsk winter post on an island in the lower river, and a winter or two later Semyon Dezhnyov and thirteen Cossacks beat off an assault by the Omoki chief Olay, who died in hand-to-hand fighting. The first summer fair opened in 1647, with Yakutsk bread resold at many times its price; from this river mouth Dezhnyov sailed east in 1648 around the Chukchi cape. Chukchi raids burned the post again and again, their last siege falling in 1710. In 1662 Yukaghirs on the upper Omolon killed the Cossack Ivan Kamchaty, after whom Kamchatka is popularly named. A smallpox epidemic in the 1680s thinned the clans, and the Nizhnekolymsk fair ceased by the end of the century.
zh:
奥莫隆河从科雷马山原蜿蜒1114公里而出，在三角洲上游汇入科雷马河，是后者最大的支流；尤卡吉尔语里，它的名字意为「奥莫尔氏族之河」。下游沿岸和科雷马冻土带上住着奥莫隆人、奥莫克人和楚万人等冻原尤卡吉尔人：他们步行或驱狗拉雪橇追逐野鹿，秋季捕捞洄游的鱼群，冬季设陷阱诱捕北极狐。他们东面是楚克奇人的游猎之地。1444年，这片土地除了自己的氏族之外不知有主人。

1644年，米哈伊尔·斯塔杜欣和德米特里·济良在下游的一座岛上建起下科雷姆斯克冬营。一两年后的冬天，谢苗·杰日尼奥夫率十三名哥萨克击退奥莫克首领奥莱的进攻，奥莱本人在肉搏中战死。1647年，第一届夏季集市开张，雅库茨克贩来的粮食在这里以数倍的价格转手；1648年，杰日尼奥夫正是从这个河口扬帆东进，绕过楚科奇角。此后楚克奇人屡屡来袭，寨堡几度被焚，最后一次围攻发生在1710年。1662年，奥莫隆河上游的尤卡吉尔人杀死哥萨克伊万·卡梅恰特——据说堪察加的名字就来自他。1680年代的天花使各氏族人口锐减，下科雷姆斯克集市也在17世纪末停办。

en:
The Karalveyem runs through cold forest-tundra north of the upper Anadyr, near the watersheds that drain toward the Kolyma. In 1444 its hunting grounds belonged to the Khodynts, a Yukaghir group whose speech was close to the Chuvan dialect. Small mobile bands pursued wild reindeer, fished the shallow northern rivers and kept sled dogs; the furs of the northern forest sustained a country without towns or forts. Chukchi power was rising to the northeast, while Koryak lands lay toward the south.

Russian entry into the region followed Semyon Dezhnev and Fedot Popov, who sailed from the Kolyma in 1648 and reached the Anadyr. Dezhnev built winter quarters there in 1649, and Anadyrsk was fortified in 1660; its hostages and fur tribute drew the upper-Anadyr Yukagirs into a long frontier war. Yukagirs besieged Anadyrsk without success in 1697, the year Vladimir Atlasov left it for Kamchatka. Smallpox in 1669 and 1690, Chukchi raids and decades of fighting eroded Yukagir power. At the turn of the eighteenth century Russian records counted about 480 Khodynts, roughly 120 able-bodied men, living chiefly by hunting wild reindeer. Orthodox baptism spread during the 1700s, and the Khodynts were absorbed into the Chuvans.
zh:
哈拉尔维冶姆河流经上阿纳德尔以北的寒冷森林苔原，靠近流向科雷马河的分水地带。1444年，这片猎场属于霍京人——使用接近楚凡方言语言的一支尤卡吉尔人。小规模游动群体追捕野鹿、在北方浅河捕鱼并饲养雪橇犬；北方林地的毛皮支撑着这片没有城镇和堡垒的土地。楚科奇势力正在东北方兴起，南方则是科里亚克人的地盘。

俄国势力进入这一地区，始于谢苗·杰日尼奥夫与费多特·波波夫。他们1648年从科雷马河出海，抵达阿纳德尔河。杰日尼奥夫于1649年在当地修建冬营，阿纳德尔堡则于1660年设立；人质与毛皮贡赋把上阿纳德尔的尤卡吉尔人卷入长期边境战争。1697年，即弗拉基米尔·阿特拉索夫从阿纳德尔堡出征堪察加的同一年，尤卡吉尔人围攻该堡但未能攻下。1669年和1690年的天花、楚科奇人的袭击以及数十年战争削弱了尤卡吉尔人的力量。18世纪之交，俄国记载霍京人约有480人，其中成年劳力约120人，主要以猎野鹿为生。18世纪间东正教洗礼逐渐传播，霍京人后来并入楚凡人。

en:
Verkhoyansk is the upper Yana country beyond the Verkhoyansk Range, a cold expanse of larch forest and tundra where the river lies frozen for much of the year. Yukaghir clans of the Yana hunted wild reindeer and elk, fished under the midnight sun and buried their dead with their heads turned south towards the sun. In 1444 they bartered with reindeer Tungus and, distantly, with the Yakut herdsmen settling the Lena; no Russian stockade yet stood east of that river.

Russians first met Yukaghirs on the Yana in 1634 or 1635, when Cossack parties under Ivan Rebrov and Ilya Perfilyev gathered furs and hostages. In 1638 the pathfinder Posnik Ivanov founded the Verkhoyansky winter post on the upper river, one of the first Russian forts in this far north-eastern land, whose sable tribute was carried the long sled road to Yakutsk. The post was moved to the left bank of the Yana in 1775 to ease tax gathering. In the reform of 1803 Zashiversk lost its uyezd, and the offices were transferred here in 1804; town status followed in 1817.
zh:
上扬斯克是维尔霍扬斯克山脉以东、亚纳河上游的一片土地，严寒的落叶松林与冻原上，河流一年里大半时间封冻。亚纳河的尤卡吉尔氏族猎野鹿、捕驼鹿，在极昼下捕鱼，安葬死者时令其头朝南、朝向太阳。1444年，他们与养鹿的通古斯人为邻，又同远在勒拿河上落脚的雅库特牧人有所往来；此时勒拿河以东还没有一座俄国人的寨堡。

1634或1635年，伊万·列布罗夫、伊利亚·佩尔菲利耶夫的哥萨克队伍在亚纳河上第一次遇见尤卡吉尔人，向他们征收毛皮并带走人质。1638年，探险家波斯尼克·伊万诺夫在亚纳河上游建起维尔霍扬斯克冬营，这是俄国人在这片东北极寒之地上最早的据点之一，征收的紫貂税经漫长的雪橇路运往雅库茨克。1775年，为便于征税，据点迁至亚纳河左岸。1803年的行政改革裁撤了扎希维尔斯克县，县署各机构于1804年并入维尔霍扬斯克；1817年，这里正式设镇。

en: The Suntar Khayata is a wall of glacier-capped peaks running 450 kilometres between the Indigirka and the Sea of Okhotsk, its highest summit, Mus-Khaya, rising to 2,959 metres. The range is a triple watershed: its snows feed the Indigirka, the Aldan-Lena system and the rivers of the Pacific coast. In 1444 only small bands of Yukaghirs and reindeer Tungus knew its passes, hunting sable and wild reindeer in the high larch valleys. After the Russians built Zashiversk beyond its northern edge in 1639, fur parties crossed the range, and Tungus from the upper Indigirka and even the Okhotsk seaboard brought tribute sables over it to the Indigirka fort; no fort or town was ever raised in the high country itself.
zh: 孙塔尔哈亚塔是一道雪峰连绵的山脉，横亘在因迪吉尔卡河流域与鄂霍次克海之间，绵延450公里，最高峰穆斯哈亚峰海拔2959米。它是一座三重分水岭：冰雪融水分别注入因迪吉尔卡河、阿尔丹河—勒拿河水系和太平洋沿岸诸河。1444年时，只有尤卡吉尔人和养鹿通古斯人的小队伍认得山间通道，在高处的落叶松谷地里猎紫貂、逐野鹿。1639年俄国人在山脉北缘之外建起扎希维尔斯克后，征收毛皮的队伍开始翻山往来，因迪吉尔卡河上游乃至鄂霍次克海岸的通古斯人也带着贡貂越过山岭前往那座寨堡；但在这整个年代里，山地本身始终没有建起要塞或城镇。

en: Gizhiga takes its name from the river that runs into Gizhiga Bay on the Sea of Okhotsk, by the neck of Kamchatka: a tundra coast of the Koryaks. Russians reached the river in 1651, by sea under Mikhail Stadukhin and overland from the upper Kolyma under Ivan Baranov. After Koryak hostility closed the land route from Okhotsk to Kamchatka in 1743, the Gizhiga fortress was built upriver in 1752, and its Cossacks married Even and Koryak women. Once the Anadyrsk fort was abandoned in 1771, Gizhiga became the main stronghold of the northeast, with 229 soldiers. Made a district town in 1782, it lost its offices in 1805 but still had about 700 people in 1818, living on fish and Okhotsk grain.
zh: 吉日加得名于吉日加河，这条河注入鄂霍次克海的吉日加湾，靠近堪察加半岛根部，沿岸是科里亚克人的苔原。1651年俄国人来到吉日加河，米哈伊尔·斯塔杜欣走海路，伊万·巴拉诺夫一队从科雷马河上游走陆路。1743年科里亚克人的敌对切断了从鄂霍次克到堪察加的陆路，1752年俄国在河上游修筑了吉日加要塞，守军中的哥萨克多娶埃文人和科里亚克人为妻。1771年阿纳德尔斯克堡撤废后，吉日加成为东北地区最大的要塞，驻军229人。1782年吉日加升为县城，1805年县署撤销，但到1818年仍有约七百人，靠捕鱼和鄂霍次克运来的粮食过活。

en:
East of the middle Lena the Aldan gathers mountain rivers — the Tompo, the Tyry, the Eastern Khandyga — in a cold forest country ringed by the Verkhoyansk Range and the Suntar-Khayata. Into its lower valleys Sakha clans pushed upriver from the Lena during the great migration of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, when their Turkic-speaking ancestors left the Baikal country under Mongol pressure; they kept the Yakut cattle and horses, fished and worked iron, while the high pastures belonged to the Even reindeer nomads they call Lamuts. No khan or prince ruled here: in 1444 the taiga knew only the toyons' camps, the log balagans and the old rites of Tengri.

Cossacks reached the Lena in the 1620s and built the Yakutsk ostrog in 1632; six years later Posnik Ivanov founded a wintering post beyond the ranges at Verkhoyansk, and yasak parties crossed the upper Aldan in pursuit of sable. The Sakha clans rose in 1634 and 1636 and most widely in 1642, and voivode Golovin broke them with executions and burned settlements; between 1642 and 1682 smallpox and the new fevers, on top of the tribute hunts, cut the Yakut people by an estimated seventy per cent. When the Khangalas toyon Djennik's last rising collapsed near Yakutsk in 1682, fugitive Sakha fled east through these uplands to the Indigirka and Kolyma. In the eighteenth century the survivors paid fur tribute and were baptised but kept the old shrines, and the reindeer Evens still crossed the high passes while the Yakutsk authorities counted them in the rolls of a distant volost.
zh:
勒拿河中游以东，阿尔丹河汇拢了托姆波河、特雷伊河、东汉德格河等山溪，形成一片寒冷的林原，四周被维尔霍扬斯克山脉与孙塔尔-哈亚塔山脉环抱。14至15世纪的大迁徙中，萨哈氏族顺着河道从勒拿河向上游推进，进入这里较低的谷地——他们讲突厥语的祖先在蒙古压力下离开贝加尔湖故地；萨哈人牧养雅库特牛和雅库特马，捕鱼、冶铁，而高山牧场上是被他们称为拉穆特人的埃文驯鹿游猎部落。这里没有汗王或王公：1444年的泰加林里只有酋长的营地、圆木搭的巴拉甘木屋和古老的腾格里祭仪。

哥萨克在1620年代进抵勒拿河，1632年筑起雅库茨克寨堡；六年后，波斯尼克·伊万诺夫在山外的上扬斯克设立过冬营地，征收毛皮贡的队伍随即越过阿尔丹河上游追索紫貂。萨哈诸氏族先后在1634年、1636年起事，1642年的反抗规模最大，督军戈洛温以处决和焚村将其镇压；1642至1682年间，天花和新来的疫病加上毛皮征敛，使雅库特人口估计减少了约七成。1682年，坎加拉斯酋长真尼克最后的起义在雅库茨克附近失败，幸存的萨哈人向东穿过这片山地，逃往因迪吉尔卡河和科雷马河。到18世纪，留下的人缴纳毛皮贡、受洗入教，却仍保存着旧有神龛；牧鹿的埃文人依旧翻越高山口迁徙，雅库茨克的官府只能在遥远的乡册上清点他们。

en:
At the mouths of the Okhota and Kukhtuy, the shore of the Lam Sea, later called the Sea of Okhotsk, joined fish-rich water, taiga and open coast. In 1444 there was no town here. Lamut clans, the people later called Evens, moved with reindeer between the forest and the shore, while settled coastal families lived in earth-and-log dugouts and stored frozen fish. Their Tungusic language, fishing and reindeer herds set the rhythm of a coast the Russian advance across Siberia had not yet reached.

Russian Cossacks reached this sea at the Ulya River in 1639. Semyon Shelkovnikov's men built winter quarters at Okhotsk in 1647 after fighting local clans, and Ivan Afanasyev raised the Kosoy Ostrozhok fort there by 1649. In 1716 Kozma Sokolov completed the Vostok at Okhotsk and sailed her to Kamchatka. The settlement received port status in 1731, became a base for Vitus Bering's Pacific expeditions, and then handled sea-otter furs from the Aleutian Islands. After the Russian-American Company was founded in 1799, Okhotsk linked the Siberian hinterland with Russian America. Ice, floods and a shallow harbor bar made the port a difficult one, and in 1815 the town was moved to a new spit at the river mouth.
zh:
鄂霍特河与库赫图伊河在后来所称的鄂霍茨克海畔入海，河口一带连接着多鱼的水面、泰加林和开阔海岸。1444年这里还没有城镇：拉穆特人，即后来的鄂温人，赶着驯鹿在森林与海岸间迁徙；定居的沿海家族住在木骨半地穴房屋中，储藏冻鱼。他们的通古斯语、渔猎生活和驯鹿群，决定着这片尚未被俄国横扫西伯利亚之势波及的海岸节奏。

1639年，俄国哥萨克在乌利亚河口抵达这片海。1647年，谢苗·舍尔科夫尼科夫的队伍在与当地氏族交战后，于鄂霍茨克建立冬营；到1649年，伊万·阿法纳西耶夫又在此筑起斜堡。1716年，科济马·索科洛夫在鄂霍茨克造成「东方号」，并驾船驶往堪察加。1731年，这里正式取得港口地位，随后成为维他斯·白令太平洋探险的基地，也经手阿留申群岛的海獭皮。1799年俄美公司成立后，鄂霍茨克把西伯利亚腹地与俄属美洲连接起来。浮冰、洪水和浅水沙洲使港口条件十分艰难，1815年城镇被迁到河口的一处新沙嘴。

en:
The Taui River drains into wide Taui Bay on the Lam coast, the northwestern Sea of Okhotsk. In 1444 no fort stood at its mouth. Tungus clans of the northern Even world moved between river, forest and shore, living by reindeer, fishing, trapping and the sable hunt. Their camps and trails gave access to one of the richest fur coasts of northeast Asia, although no outside administration yet collected tribute there.

Ivan Moskvitin's Cossacks learned of the Taui in 1639, and a party explored north to the bay the following year. In 1653 Mikhail Stadukhin, travelling west from Anadyr by ski and sled after wintering on the Gizhiga and Yama rivers, reached the mouth and built the first Tauisk ostrog on the right bank. He remained for about four years, collecting fur tribute and hunting sables. The post later served the difficult coastal route between Okhotsk and Kamchatka. The scholar Jacob Lindenau reached it from Okhotsk in January 1743, and in 1783 it was placed in the Okhotsk district. Late in the eighteenth century the small settlement was moved about forty kilometres east toward the Yana River, nearer its later site.
zh:
陶伊河注入开阔的陶伊湾，这里是鄂霍茨克海西北岸的拉姆海岸。1444年河口还没有堡寨；北方埃文世界的通古斯氏族在河流、森林与海岸间迁徙，以驯鹿、捕鱼、设陷阱和猎紫貂为生。他们的营地与小路通向东北亚最丰饶的毛皮海岸之一，但那时还没有外来政权在此征收贡赋。

伊万·莫斯克维京的哥萨克在1639年得知陶伊河，次年又派人北上探查陶伊湾。1653年，米哈伊尔·斯塔杜欣从阿纳德尔乘滑雪板和雪橇西行，在吉日加河与亚马河一带越冬后抵达河口，在右岸建起第一座陶伊斯克堡寨。他在此停留约四年，征收毛皮贡并猎取紫貂。这座据点后来服务于鄂霍茨克与堪察加之间艰险的海岸通道。1743年1月，学者雅各布·林德瑙从鄂霍茨克抵达这里；1783年，陶伊斯克被划入鄂霍茨克县，18世纪末又向东迁移约40公里，靠近亚纳河和后来的位置。

en:
The Yakut, or Sakha, took shape on the middle Lena after Turkic-speaking cattle herders from around Lake Baikal settled among Evenk and Yukaghir clans. Sites of the Kulun-Atakh culture show their horse-and-cattle economy spreading through the grassy river valleys from the 13th to the 16th centuries. Hunting, fishing, smithing and river trade sustained scattered clans, whose log winter dwellings and birch-bark summer tents were built for a far colder land than the steppe. In 1444 the Yakut clans followed their own chiefs and observed Turkic sky-cult traditions mixed with northern spirit beliefs; no Russian fort yet stood on the Lena.

Russian Cossacks exploring the Lena reached this area in 1623, and Pyotr Beketov founded Lensky Ostrog in 1632 with a garrison of thirty Cossacks. Yakut forces besieged it in 1634, and Russian chronicles later recorded seven risings between 1633 and 1684 against fur tribute and fortified rule. The stockade became seat of the Yakutsk Voivodeship in 1638, then moved in 1642-1643 to the riverside site that became Yakutsk, from which expeditions toward the Arctic and Pacific were supplied. Yakut envoys reached Tsar Feodor III in Moscow in 1676. Peasant settlers introduced ploughland, Orthodox parishes expanded, the stone Trinity Cathedral was completed in 1728, and many Yakuts were baptized in the later 18th century. After Peter I brought the region into Siberian government, a Yakutsk oblast formed in 1784 became a separate administration in 1805.
zh:
雅库特人又称萨哈人。贝加尔湖一带的突厥语牧人迁入勒拿河中游后，与埃文基、尤卡吉尔等氏族交融，逐渐形成这一族群。库伦—阿塔赫文化遗址显示，13至16世纪间，养马牧牛的经济已扩展到这片寒冷的宜牧河谷；渔猎、锻铁和河上贸易维系着分散的氏族，冬季木屋与夏季桦皮帐都适应了远比草原严酷的气候。1444年，各雅库特氏族仍由本族首领统领，保持着融合突厥天神信仰与北方神灵观念的传统信仰，勒拿河上还没有俄国堡寨。

探查勒拿河的俄国哥萨克于1623年抵达这一带。1632年，彼得·别克托夫设立连斯克堡，最初驻军只有三十名哥萨克。雅库特人1634年围攻堡寨；俄文编年史记载，1633至1684年间当地为反抗毛皮贡赋和堡寨统治共发动七次起事。1638年，堡寨成为雅库茨克督军辖区中心，1642至1643年迁到后来的雅库茨克城址，并为前往北冰洋和太平洋的探险队伍提供补给。1676年，雅库特使节在莫斯科觐见沙皇费奥多尔三世。俄国农民带来耕地，东正教教区逐渐扩展，石造圣三一大教堂1728年完工，许多雅库特人在18世纪后半叶受洗。彼得一世将此地并入西伯利亚行政体系后，雅库茨克州于1784年设立，1805年成为独立行政单位。

en:
The Maya comes down from the Dzhugdzhur highlands through deep taiga to join the Aldan, and for ages its valley was a hunters' corridor between the Lena country and the Sea of Okhotsk, which the Tungus call Lam. Even reindeer bands, the Lamuts, and their Evenki kin ranged the woods, while Sakha cattle-keepers grazed the lower Aldan meadows; the sable was thick and the winters pitiless. In 1444 this was roadless fur country of scattered log balagans and birch-bark urasas along nomad trails, owing tribute to no one.

On 28 June 1638 a Tomsk Cossack detachment under Dmitry Kopylov built the Butalsky ostrog on the Aldan, a hundred kilometres above the Maya's mouth, and sent Ivan Moskvitin with thirty men up the Maya, across the Dzhugdzhur by the Nudyma portage and down the Ulya: in 1639 he became the first Russian to look on the Pacific. From the 1650s the Maya and Yudoma line carried the Yakutsk–Okhotsk route; in 1680 Tungus raiders killed a party escorting the sable treasury on the Yudoma, and the Yudoma Cross later marked where roughly two hundred travellers perished in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Made a postal highway in 1731–1733, with stations from 1735, the track wore out thousands of horses — nearly eight thousand died along it in 1818–1819 alone — while furs and supplies moved between Yakutsk and Okhotsk.
zh:
玛雅河从朱格朱尔山地的密林深谷中流出，汇入阿尔丹河；很久以来，它的河谷就是勒拿河流域与鄂霍茨克海（通古斯人称为拉穆海）之间猎人往来的走廊。牧鹿的埃文部落拉穆特人和他们的埃文基亲族在林中游走，萨哈牧人则在阿尔丹河下游草甸放牧；这里紫貂繁盛，冬天酷寒难耐。1444年，这里还是没有道路的毛皮之地，游牧小径旁散落着圆木的巴拉甘和桦皮的乌拉萨，不向任何人纳贡。

1638年6月28日，德米特里·科佩洛夫率领的托木斯克哥萨克队伍在阿尔丹河畔、玛雅河口上游一百公里处筑起布塔利斯基寨堡，随后派伊万·莫斯科维京带三十人溯玛雅河而上，经努德马连水陆翻越朱格朱尔山，再沿乌利亚河而下：1639年，他成为第一个望见太平洋的俄国人。从1650年代起，玛雅河—尤多马河水线承担起雅库茨克—鄂霍茨克通道；1680年，通古斯人在尤多马河畔袭杀了押送紫貂官银的队伍，后来的尤多马十字标记着十七至十八世纪约两百名旅人丧命之处。通道在1731至1733年被辟为驿道，1735年起设立驿站；无数马匹累死途中，仅1818和1819两年就死去近八千匹，而毛皮与给养就这样在雅库茨克与鄂霍茨克之间往返转运。

en:
The Jugjur, or Dzhugdzhur, runs for about 700 kilometres along the northwestern shore of the Sea of Okhotsk and divides the Aldan river basin from the short streams falling into the sea. Its Evenki name means a great bulge. Reindeer-herding Evenki clans knew the high passes, moving between taiga hunting grounds, sable forests and the coast. Ivan Moskvitin's Cossacks crossed from the Maya to the Ulya in 1639 and wintered beside the sea, yet in 1444 the range had no Russian fort and remained a world of indigenous trails and portages.

Vasily Poyarkov used Moskvitin's old Ulya huts in 1646 after his Amur journey. From Ulya tributaries, the Lama and Alachak portages reached the Mati and then the Maya, carrying traffic through these mountains toward the Aldan, Lena and Yakutsk. After Okhotsk became Russia's Pacific port, sable and sea-otter furs went inland while grain and shipbuilding supplies were dragged toward the coast. Vitus Bering's eighteenth-century expeditions increased that traffic, but the steep climbs, swamps and short summer season kept the Jugjur crossing one of the costliest links on the Okhotsk route through 1821.
zh:
朱格朱尔山脉沿鄂霍茨克海西北岸延伸约700公里，分隔阿尔丹河流域与短促入海的河流。其鄂温克语名称意为巨大的隆起。牧养驯鹿的鄂温克氏族熟悉高山山口，在泰加林猎场、紫貂森林和海岸之间往返。1639年，伊万·莫斯克维京的哥萨克从马亚河越岭到达乌利亚河，并在海边越冬；但到1444年，山中仍没有俄国堡寨，依旧是原住民小径和联运道路的世界。

1646年，瓦西里·波亚尔科夫在阿穆尔之行后使用了莫斯克维京留在乌利亚河的旧棚屋。拉马联运道和阿拉恰克联运道从乌利亚河支沟通向马季河，再转入马亚河，使人货能穿过这些山岭前往阿尔丹河、勒拿河和雅库茨克。鄂霍茨克成为俄国太平洋港口后，紫貂皮和海獭皮经此运往内陆，粮食与造船物资则被拖向海岸。维他斯·白令在18世纪的探险增加了这条路的运输量，但陡坡、沼泽和短暂夏季，使朱格朱尔山口直到1821年仍是鄂霍茨克路线上最昂贵的路段之一。

en:
Miyoo Gasan covers the forested ridges and storm-bound shore beyond the lower Amur, where Nivkh families followed a hard seasonal round. In 1444 they took salmon from the rivers, seals and other sea mammals from offshore waters, and elk, deer and fur animals in the taiga. Dogs pulled their sledges, shamanic rites centred on the spirits of sea and forest, and the winter bear festival bound camps and clans together. Sable and fox skins moved south through neighbouring peoples, but the country itself was ruled from no distant capital.

Vasily Poyarkov's Amur expedition brought the first Russian written report in 1643, using the Tungus name Gilyak for the Nivkh. On the Uda, a Russian post begun in 1679 gained a winter hut in 1681, the nucleus of Udsk ostrog. Stepan Krasheninnikov later recorded that six Tungus clans paid 85 sables and 12 fox skins there each year. Ten farming families transferred to the post in 1735 could not ripen grain in the cold soil, so fish and furs remained the country's wealth. A scientific expedition visited Udsk in 1806 to collect plants and describe the little-known coast.
zh:
庙街位于阿穆尔河下游以远的森林山岭与风浪严寒的海岸之间，尼夫赫人在此依季节轮换谋生。1444年时，他们在河汊捕捞鲑鱼，在近岸猎捕海豹等海兽，又在泰加林中猎取驼鹿、鹿和毛皮兽。狗为他们拉雪橇，萨满仪式围绕海洋与森林的神灵展开，冬季的熊节把各个营地和氏族联系在一起。紫貂和狐皮经邻人输往南方，但这片土地并不受远方都城统治。

瓦西里·波亚尔科夫的阿穆尔探险队在1643年留下俄国人最早的文字记载，并用通古斯人的称呼把尼夫赫人称为「基利亚克人」。在乌第河上，俄国据点始于1679年，1681年又建起冬营，成为乌第堡的雏形。斯捷潘·克拉舍宁尼科夫后来记载，六个通古斯氏族每年在此缴纳85张紫貂皮和12张狐皮。1735年迁来的十户农耕人家无法让谷物在寒地成熟，渔产和毛皮因此始终是此地的财富。1806年，一支科学考察队到访乌第堡，采集植物并记录这条尚少为人知的海岸。

en:
Haiilanboo lies where the Zeya River meets the Amur, among forested ridges and river meadows on the northern fur route. In 1444 the country was traversed by Solon Evenki hunters, who took furs from the taiga and carried them toward Manchurian and Mongol markets. On the richer Amur bottomlands, Daur and Ducher communities kept horses, cattle and pigs and sowed rye, wheat and millet. There was no great fortress here, only camp sites, ferry crossings and tracks through the forest.

The first Russian force to reach the Amur basin was Vasily Poyarkov's, which entered the Zeya country in 1643; its exactions met with Daur resistance. Yerofey Khabarov found a fortified Ducher town near the Zeya's mouth in 1652. From 1654 the Qing moved the Amur farming population away from the Cossack raiding grounds, but in 1673 they reoccupied the site as Old Aigun and used it in the 1683-1685 campaigns against Albazin. The 1689 Treaty of Nerchinsk recognized Qing sovereignty over this stretch of the Amur, leaving Haiilanboo a quiet river crossing and fur country on the imperial frontier.
zh:
海兰泡位于结雅河汇入黑龙江处，林地与江畔草场夹着这条北方毛皮通路。1444年前后，索伦鄂温克猎人在这一带游猎，从泰加林取得毛皮，再输往满洲和蒙古市场；黑龙江畔较肥沃的滩地上，达斡尔人和杜切尔人饲养马、牛、猪，种植黑麦、小麦和糜子。此时这里没有大型要塞，主要是营地、渡口和穿过森林的小路。

1643年，瓦西里·波雅尔科夫率领首批进入黑龙江流域的俄国队伍抵达结雅河流域，因强征物资与达斡尔人发生冲突。1652年，叶罗费·哈巴罗夫在结雅河口附近见到杜切尔人的设防土城。1654年起，清朝把黑龙江沿岸务农人口迁离哥萨克袭扰之地；1673年又在原址设立旧瑷珲，并在1683年至1685年对阿尔巴津的战事中将其作为基地。1689年《尼布楚条约》确认清朝领有这一段黑龙江两岸，海兰泡由此成为帝国边境内一处平静渡口和毛皮之地。

en:
Tyr commands a stretch of the lower Amur where the river draws near the Amgun and the road to the sea opens between forested banks. The Yuan kept a military post and shrine on Tyr Cliff in the 1260s. The Ming eunuch Yishiha later sailed here with great fleets, founded Yongning Temple to Guanyin in 1413, and after a later mission found it ruined rebuilt the temple in 1433–1434. His Chinese, Mongolian and Jurchen stele recorded a loose Nurgan allegiance. That commission was abandoned in 1434, so in 1444 the cliff and fishing grounds were again Nivkh country, with a Buddhist monument standing above the river.

In the autumn of 1644 Vasily Poyarkov's Cossacks reached the Gilyak lands at the Amur mouth after fighting their way downriver. They wintered among hostile camps, built boats, and returned north along the Sea of Okhotsk coast, carrying to Yakutsk the first detailed Russian reports of the river's fur wealth. The Treaty of Nerchinsk in 1689 did not turn Tyr into a settled border town; Nivkh clans instead moved furs, fish and news between Russian outposts, Manchu authorities and Sakhalin peoples. The temple later burned and was not rebuilt, though its cliff remained a landmark for every party passing up or down the Amur.
zh:
提尔控扼阿穆尔河下游一段，河道在森林夹岸间接近阿姆贡河，也打开了通往河口的道路。元朝在1260年代于特林崖设置军事据点和祠庙。后来明朝宦官亦失哈率大船队航行至此，1413年建造供奉观音的永宁寺；最后一次出使时见寺院已毁，又于1433—1434年重修。寺前的汉、蒙古、女真文碑刻记录的是奴儿干各部松散的臣属关系。奴儿干都司到1434年已经废弃，因此1444年时，崖下河道与渔场重归尼夫赫人的天地，只有一座佛教碑刻矗立在河畔。

1644年秋，瓦西里·波亚尔科夫率领哥萨克一路转战南下，抵达阿穆尔河口的基利亚克人之地。他们在充满敌意的营地间越冬、造船，随后沿鄂霍次克海岸北返，把关于这条大河毛皮财富的第一批详细俄文报告带回雅库茨克。1689年《尼布楚条约》之后，提尔并未变成固定的边界城镇；尼夫赫氏族反而在俄国据点、清朝官府和库页岛诸族之间转运毛皮、渔产与消息。寺院后来毁于火灾，再未重建，但特林崖仍是往来阿穆尔河上下各方都能辨认的标志。

en:
The Aldan is a great right-hand tributary of the Lena in eastern Siberia, and the Uchur joins it from the forested Stanovoy highlands after 812 kilometres of rapids and mountain valleys; its Evenki name refers to a whirling wind. By the 15th century Yakut clans spreading from the Lena and the Baikal direction shared the wider basin with Evenki hunters and reindeer herders whose trails linked the Aldan, Maya and Uchur portages. In 1444 there was no town or Russian post here, only riverside winter camps and taiga hunting trails, with the waterways frozen for much of the year.

In 1637 Ivan Moskvitin's Cossack party built Butalsky Ostrozhok on the Aldan. In spring 1639 he led thirty-nine Tomsk and Krasnoyarsk servicemen up the Aldan and Maya, crossed to the Ulya, and reached the Sea of Okhotsk that August. He returned by the same river-and-mountain passage to Yakutsk in 1641 with sable tribute and reports from the Pacific shore. The Aldan thus became part of the Russian river road to Okhotsk, carrying Cossacks and fur hunters from Yakutsk toward the Pacific while yasak obligations drew the Evenki and Yakut interior into the Siberian fur trade.
zh:
阿尔丹河是东西伯利亚勒拿河的重要右岸支流，乌丘尔河从森林密布的斯塔诺夫山地流出，穿过812公里急流峡谷后汇入阿尔丹；乌丘尔是埃文基语地名，意为旋风。到15世纪，从勒拿河与贝加尔湖方向扩散的雅库特氏族，已与埃文基猎人和牧鹿人共享这片盆地，后者的山道连接着阿尔丹河、玛雅河和乌丘尔河的转运路线。1444年，这里没有城镇，也没有俄国据点，只有河畔冬营和泰加林猎道，河道一年中长时间封冻。

1637年，伊万·莫斯科维京的哥萨克队伍在阿尔丹河修筑布塔尔斯克小堡。1639年春，他率三十九名托木斯克和克拉斯诺亚尔斯克军役人员溯阿尔丹河与玛雅河而上，越过分水岭抵达乌利亚河，同年8月到达鄂霍次克海岸。1641年，他经同一条山河水道回到雅库茨克，上缴紫貂贡并报告太平洋沿岸的情形。阿尔丹河由此成为俄国通往鄂霍次克的河路的一部分，哥萨克和毛皮猎人从雅库茨克走向太平洋，毛皮贡赋也把埃文基人与雅库特人的内陆山林纳入西伯利亚贸易。

en:
The Stanovoy, known in Chinese as the Outer Khingan, is a mountain chain about 700 kilometres long from the middle Olyokma to the headwaters of the Uchur. It joins the Stanovoy Highlands in the west to the Dzhugdzhur in the east and divides the Arctic-bound Lena system from the rivers flowing toward the Amur and the Pacific. Evenki clans knew these linked ranges as Dzhugdzhur, the 'backbone of the Earth,' crossing frozen valleys with reindeer and hunting in the sable forests. In 1444 no Cossack had yet crossed from the Lena world into the Amur basin; the high country was an indigenous hunting frontier, not a fixed imperial border.

Vasily Poyarkov, sent from Yakutsk in 1643 by Governor Pyotr Golovin, became the first recorded Russian to cross the range. His Daurian expedition returned in 1646, probably following frozen riverbeds up the Nuyam and down the Mulmuga toward the Zeya. In January 1650 Yerofey Khabarov reached the Tungir headwaters and found the lower Tungir portage through the Olyokminsky Stanovik; it became the decisive route between Yakutsk and the Amur. Cossack fur demands and Qing frontier power then met at the watershed. The 1689 Treaty of Nerchinsk made the Outer Khingan the Russo-Qing boundary, and the sable-rich passes remained that cold frontier in 1821.
zh:
斯塔诺夫山脉（即外兴安岭）西起奥廖克马河中游，东至乌丘尔河源，绵延约700公里，西接斯塔诺夫高地，东连朱格朱尔山脉，分隔注入北冰洋的勒拿水系与流向阿穆尔河和太平洋的河流。鄂温克氏族把这组相连山岭称为朱格朱尔，即「大地的脊梁」，赶着驯鹿穿越冰封河谷，在紫貂林中狩猎。1444年，还没有哥萨克从勒拿河流域越入阿穆尔河流域；高山地带是原住民的游猎边疆，而不是帝国划定的边界。

1643年，奉雅库茨克督军彼得·戈洛温之命出发的瓦西里·波亚尔科夫，成为有记载第一名越过山脉的俄国人。他前往达斡里亚的探险队于1646年返回，可能沿冰封河床溯努亚姆河而上，再顺穆利穆加河通向结雅河。1650年1月，叶罗费·哈巴罗夫抵达通吉尔河源，找到穿过奥廖克明斯基斯塔诺维克的低矮通吉尔联运道；这条路线后来成为雅库茨克与阿穆尔地区之间的关键通道。哥萨克的毛皮索求与清朝的边疆势力随即在分水岭相遇。1689年《尼布楚条约》把外兴安岭定为俄国与清朝的界山，到1821年，这些盛产紫貂的寒冷山口仍是那条边境。

en:
Hinggan is the wooded spine of the Greater Khingan, the high taiga lying between the Nonni River and the upper Amur, where winter locks the forests for half the year. In 1444 its people were the Solon, Evenki-speaking bands whom the Ming loosely counted among the Wild Jurchens: they herded reindeer, followed the sable hunt, moved their camps with the seasons and kept the old shaman's rites, answering to no khan or emperor beyond their own clan chiefs.

Their first test came from the south. Bombogor, the Solon chief born at Yaksa on the Amur, united the Solon and Daur against Hong Taiji, but Qing columns drove as far as the Huma River in 1639, took Yaksa and three other stockades in May 1640, and seized Bombogor himself that August as he fled toward the Mongols; he was executed at Mukden and his people entered the Eight Banners. Even as they submitted, strangers came from the north: in June 1643 Vasily Poyarkov left Yakutsk with 133 men and reached the Zeya, the first Russians seen in the Amur lands. Under the Kangxi emperor the Khingan hunters were organized into the Butha, the Hunt banners, whose sable pelts went as tribute and whose companies became some of the toughest soldiers of the Qing; Solon banners marched to garrison Xinjiang in 1763, and the Solon general Hailancha won his fame in the Qianlong emperor's wars.
zh:
兴安即大兴安岭林木茂密的山脊，横在嫩江与黑龙江上游之间，一年里有半年寒冬锁着林海。1444年，这里的主人是索伦人——讲鄂温克语的游猎部众，明朝笼统归入野人女真；他们牧养驯鹿、猎捕紫貂，营地随季节迁徙，奉行古老的萨满仪式，除了自己的氏族首领，不臣服于任何汗王。

最初的考验来自南方：出生于黑龙江边雅克萨的索伦酋长博木博果尔联合索伦与达斡尔对抗皇太极。1639年清军深入到呼玛河，1640年5月攻克雅克萨等四座城寨，同年8月博木博果尔在逃往蒙古途中被截获，押赴盛京处死，部众编入八旗。南方的征服刚定，北方的陌生人已到：1643年6月，波雅尔科夫率133人从雅库茨克出发，抵达结雅河，成为出现在黑龙江流域的第一批俄国人。康熙年间，兴安岭的猎人被编为布特哈八旗（「布特哈」为满语渔猎之意），紫貂皮充作贡物，索伦兵以善战成为清军劲旅，1763年索伦八旗远戍新疆，索伦名将海兰察则在乾隆朝的征战中屡立战功。

en:
Mukhtuya lay along the upper Lena, taking its game name from the Evenk camp of Mukhtuy, meaning 'great water', and stretching toward the Ilim and Kuta rivers. In 1444 Tungus hunters and reindeer herders moved through this taiga by canoe and reindeer trail, using the low portages where the Angara system came close to the Lena. No Russian fort or ploughland stood here yet, but the watersheds already marked a natural passage between the Yenisei and Lena basins.

Russian Cossacks reached the Ilim in summer 1627. In 1630 Ivan Galkin opened the Lena portage from the Ilim to the Kuta and built winter quarters that grew into Ilimsky Ostrog, which became the seat of a separate voivodeship in 1649. Yerofey Khabarov was among the earliest settlers, starting ploughland and salt works on the Lena around 1639; three years later he sold the treasury as much as 1,000 poods of grain and 3,000 poods of salt. By the end of the century the district had about 300 villages and more than 15,000 desyatinas under plough, and in the early 1700s it sent up to 25,000 poods of market grain down the Lena. Ilimsk provisioned Vitus Bering's first Kamchatka expedition in 1726 and his second expedition of 1734-1742, when Mukhtuya served as a Lena postal station. Alexander Radishchev spent his Ilimsk exile here from 1792 to 1796.
zh:
穆赫图亚位于勒拿河上游，名称来自埃文基人的穆赫图伊营地，意为「大水」；这片泰加林还向西连接伊利姆河与库塔河。1444年，通古斯猎人和牧鹿人乘独木舟、沿鹿道穿行林中，利用安加拉水系与勒拿河相距最近处的低矮分水岭转运。这里还没有俄国堡寨和耕地，但这些水道之间的缺口已构成叶尼塞河流域通往勒拿河流域的天然通道。

1627年夏，俄国哥萨克首次抵达伊利姆河。1630年，伊万·加尔金探明从伊利姆河通往库塔河的勒拿连水陆路，并设立冬营，后来发展为伊利姆斯克堡；1649年，这里成为独立督军辖区的中心。叶罗费·哈巴罗夫是最早的定居者之一，约1639年在勒拿河畔开垦耕地、经营盐场，三年后已能向官府出售多达一千普特粮食和三千普特盐。到17世纪末，这一地区约有三百个村庄，垦地超过一万五千俄亩；18世纪初，每年沿勒拿河外运的商品粮多达二万五千普特。1726年，伊利姆斯克为维图斯·白令的第一次堪察加探险筹备物资，1734至1742年又为第二次探险提供补给，穆赫图亚则成为这条路线上的勒拿河驿站。1792至1796年，亚历山大·拉季谢夫被流放于此。

en:
Kirenga is the taiga river valley running north from the Baikal Mountains to its meeting with the Lena. Its name is Evenki, and in 1444 small Tungus clans moved through the forests and river terraces by reindeer, hunting, fishing, and paying deference only when stronger Mongol parties reached the Baikal country. Buryat herds and camps were concentrated closer to Lake Baikal, leaving this cold northern valley a thin frontier of trails rather than towns.

In 1630 a Cossack band under Vasily Bugor founded the Nikolsky pogost at the mouth of the Kirenga, securing one of the early routes between the Yenisei and Lena systems. Yerofey Khabarov built a mill above the mouth in 1641, the settlement was enclosed as the Ust-Kirensky ostrog in 1665, and in 1775 it received town status as Ust-Kirensk, later called Kirensk. As Russian power consolidated, Evenki hunters were brought into the fur-tribute system and furs moved down the Lena.
zh:
