该世纪末，阿拉伯首领阿卜杜拉·詹马推翻阿洛迪亚，定都盖里（Qarri），1504年阿马拉·敦卡斯率领的丰吉人在阿尔巴吉附近将其击败；此后阿卜杜拉布人以「曼吉拉克」之衔担任北方副王，统治布塔纳，向麦加与乍得湖之间的商队征收关税。谢赫阿吉卜·卡富塔1576年击退奥斯曼入侵，兵锋远达阿斯旺，随后以伊斯兰圣战为名举兵对抗森纳尔，1611至1612年被苏丹阿德兰一世杀于卡尔科季；他的儿子获赦返回盖里，旷野平原则由舒克里亚阿拉伯人以武力称雄。18世纪中叶，谢赫阿卜杜拉三世把宫廷南迁至哈勒法耶特穆鲁克，盖里这个自身没有多少贸易的税卡就此荒废。末代谢赫纳西尔于1821年向土埃军队不战而降。

en:
East of the Atbara the steppe climbs to the Taka hills, where the Gash river spreads its seasonal flood over the pastures around what is now Kassala. This was the inland country of the Beja, Cushitic-speaking herdsmen who had grazed camels and cattle between the Nile and the Red Sea since antiquity, and who by the fifteenth century, through intermarriage with incoming Arab tribes, were Muslims, if stubbornly independent ones. In 1444 the Beja clans owned no prince, moving between wells under their own sheikhs and selling their herds at Suakin on the coast; a Mamluk expedition had already marched through the Taka in pursuit of Arab raiders in 1317.

After the Funj founded their sultanate in 1504 the Taka entered the loose orbit of Sennar, whose power at its peak ran east to the Red Sea and levied camels from the Beja clans; the Ottomans took Suakin in 1526, and in the 1530s the slaving armies of Ahmad Gragn swept west from the Ethiopian highlands as far as the Taka hills before turning back. In the seventeenth century Beja clans pushed south after fresh grazing, and the Hadendoa emerged in the eighteenth as the dominant tribe of eastern Sudan, forever feuding with the Bisharin. As Sennar tore itself apart in civil wars the Taka slipped free under its own sheikhs after 1791, and when the Turco-Egyptian army conquered Sennar in 1821 its rule stopped at the Nile and the Gezira; the Beja kept their wells and pastures.
zh:
阿特巴拉河以东，草原渐次抬升为塔卡丘陵，加什河的季节性洪水在今卡萨拉一带漫过牧场。这是贝扎人的内地家园：操库希特语的牧民自古在尼罗河与红海之间放牧骆驼和牛群，到15世纪经与迁入的阿拉伯部落通婚，已成为穆斯林，却始终桀骜不驯。1444年的贝扎各部不奉君王，随各自的谢赫辗转于水井之间，把牲畜赶到红海之滨的萨瓦金出售；早在1317年，一支马穆鲁克远征军追击阿拉伯劫匪时就曾穿过塔卡。

1504年丰吉苏丹国建立后，塔卡进入森纳尔的松散势力范围，丰吉鼎盛时势力东抵红海，向贝扎各部征取骆驼；奥斯曼人于1526年夺取萨瓦金，1530年代艾哈迈德·格兰的掠奴大军从埃塞俄比亚高原向西扫荡，兵锋远及塔卡丘陵方才折返。17世纪，贝扎部落向南开拓新牧场，哈登多亚人到18世纪已成为苏丹东部的主导部落，与比夏林人争斗不休。塞纳尔在内战中四分五裂，1791年以后塔卡便在本族谢赫治下脱离控制；1821年土埃军队攻灭森纳尔，其统治止于尼罗河和杰济拉，贝扎人得以保有自己的水井和牧场。

en:
The highland country around Aksum and Debarwa was the old Christian core of the Ethiopian world. Aksum had once linked Red Sea commerce with the interior as capital of the Aksumite kingdom; after the court moved south it remained a shrine city, its Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion restored under Dawit I in 1406 and the site of Zara Yaqob's coronation in 1436. North of the city, above the Mereb River, Debarwa held the palaces of the Bahr Negash, governor of Medri Bahri and overseer of routes climbing inland from Massawa. In 1444, under Emperor Zara Yaqob, Tigrinya-speaking lords, priests, farmers, and merchants shared grain villages and church lands on the northern edge of a united Solomonid Ethiopia.

Francisco Alvares, visiting in the 1520s, found Aksum full of ancient stone thrones and stelae, while Debarwa kept a crowded Thursday market and the governor's fortress-house. In 1535 Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi's forces overran the district, burned Aksum, and destroyed the old church; Cristovao da Gama's Portuguese passed through a depopulated Debarwa during the rainy season of 1542. Ottoman troops seized Massawa in 1557 and built a fort at Debarwa, and the rebellious Bahr Negash Yeshaq leaned on them against Emperor Menas after 1561. Emperor Sarsa Dengel took Debarwa in 1576, destroyed the Ottoman fort, and rebuilt Aksum's church in 1580. Oromo raiders burned the church in 1611, Fasilides restored it in 1655, and it survived the rebel burning of the town in 1678 to serve Iyasu I's coronation in 1693. Charles-Jacques Poncet found Debarwa still called the capital of Tigray around 1700, though Adwa was overtaking it; amid later fragmentation Aksum fell to the rulers of Tigray, and Wolde Selassie granted lands to its church in 1794.
zh:
阿克苏姆与德巴尔瓦周围的高地，是埃塞俄比亚世界古老的基督教核心。阿克苏姆曾作为阿克苏姆王国都城，连接红海商路与内陆；王廷南移后，它仍以圣城身份延续。1406年，达维特一世修复锡安圣母教堂，1436年扎拉·雅各布又在此加冕。城市以北、马雷布河上方的德巴尔瓦，是梅德里·巴赫里总督的驻地，掌管从马萨瓦通向高原的道路。1444年，在扎拉·雅各布皇帝治下，这里是所罗门王朝统一埃塞俄比亚的北缘：操提格雷尼亚语的贵族、祭司、农民和商人围绕谷物村落与教会土地生活。

1520年代，弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯到访时，阿克苏姆仍可见古代石座与方尖碑，德巴尔瓦则有热闹的周四集市和堡垒般的总督宅邸。1535年，艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的军队席卷此地，焚毁阿克苏姆并拆毁旧教堂；1542年雨季，克里斯托旺·达·伽马率领的葡萄牙军经过德巴尔瓦，见到居民因战乱逃散。奥斯曼军队1557年夺取马萨瓦，并在德巴尔瓦筑垒；1561年后，反叛的总督伊沙克又借奥斯曼人对抗米纳斯皇帝。萨尔萨·丹格尔皇帝1576年攻克德巴尔瓦、摧毁奥斯曼堡垒，1580年重建阿克苏姆教堂。1611年奥罗莫袭击者烧毁教堂，法西利德斯于1655年重修；1678年叛军焚毁城镇而教堂幸存，并在1693年用于伊亚苏一世加冕。1700年前后，夏尔-雅克·蓬塞仍称德巴尔瓦为提格雷首府，但阿杜瓦已逐渐超过它。帝国权威分裂后，阿克苏姆转入提格雷统治者之手；沃尔德·塞拉西于1794年向当地教堂赐地。

en:
Dunqula, Old Dongola, rises from the east bank of the Nile facing the mouth of the Wadi Howar, once the capital of the Christian kings of Makuria. Its granite-columned cathedral and royal throne hall made it the chief city of Nubia for nine centuries; then Arab raids emptied the streets, the throne hall itself became a mosque in 1317, and the royal court departed in 1364. Caravans still set out from here for Darfur and Kordofan, and a hereditary Nubian lord styled mekk kept his seat in the old citadel of a half-deserted town. In 1444 Dongola was a Muslim Nubian town on the edge of a vanished Christian world, its people farmers along one narrow strip of river, its mekk soon to be drawn into the orbit of the rising Funj.

By 1523 Amara Dunqas's Funj realm stretched north to Dongola, and the town became the seat of the sultanate's northern provinces: the mekk ruled on the spot and even bore the Arabic title of malik while sending tribute to Sennar. An Ottoman army marching up the Nile against the Funj was crushed at Hannik by the Third Cataract in 1585, which fixed the frontier with Egypt. Around 1600 the mekk Qashqash held Dongola, and when the Frenchman Poncet visited in 1699 he found a half-ruined place whose castle could still overawe the Arabs of the open country. Trade ebbed as the Shaigiya horsemen made themselves independent on the river to the south, and in 1812 the Mamluks fleeing Muhammad Ali's purges seized the town and founded a new Dongola downstream. When the Turks arrived in 1821, the old northern capital had passed into history.
zh:
栋古拉旧城（旧栋古拉）坐落于尼罗河东岸，与豪瓦尔干河口隔河相望，曾是基督教马库里亚诸王的都城。花岗岩柱大教堂与王宫中殿使它在九个世纪里稳居努比亚首城之位；此后阿拉伯人的袭击令街巷十室九空，王宫大殿于1317年改为清真寺，王室宫廷也在1364年迁离。前往达尔富尔和科尔多凡的商队仍从此出发，一位称「梅克」的世袭努比亚首领在半荒废城池的旧堡中保有座位。1444年的栋古拉是一座穆斯林努比亚城镇，伫立在已逝基督教世界的边缘，居民是尼罗河一线狭地上的农人，梅克不久便被卷入兴起的丰吉势力范围。

到1523年，阿马拉·敦卡斯的丰吉疆土已北展至栋古拉，旧城成为苏丹国北方诸省的治所：梅克在本地称尊，甚至使用阿拉伯语「马利克」（王）的称号，同时向森纳尔纳贡。1585年，沿尼罗河上犯的奥斯曼军队在第三瀑布附近的哈尼赫被击溃，第三瀑布就此成为与埃及的边界。约1600年，梅克卡什卡什据有栋古拉；1699年法国人蓬塞到访时，见到的是一座半毁之城，城中的城堡仍能震慑旷野上的阿拉伯人。随着沙伊吉亚骑兵在南方河道割据自立，商路日渐萧条。1812年，为躲避穆罕默德·阿里清洗而逃出埃及的马穆鲁克人夺取此城，在下游另建了新栋古拉。1821年土耳其军队抵达时，这座古老的北方都城已成陈迹。

en:
Berber stands on the east bank of the Nile, just above the mouth of the Atbara, where the river road of Nubia meets the desert road to Sawakin. A town since Meroitic times, by the fifteenth century it belonged to the Arabized Nubians of the Ja'al country, Muslim camel- and cattle-owners living beside Nubian-speaking villagers, its livelihood resting on the Nile traffic and the caravans that crossed the Bayuda. In 1444 it was a small market town of the northern Sudan without a strong sovereign, the nearest thing to a gateway between the Nile bend and the Red Sea.

Under the Funj sultans Berber came into its own. It became the crossing-place of pilgrimage caravans making for the Hijaz and the chief emporium where the goods of the Sudan changed hands: ivory, ostrich feathers and hides moving out through Sawakin, and cloth, silk, perfumes and spices coming back, and travellers ranked its brick-built qaysariyya market with those of Fez, Cairo and Jeddah. From the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the town was famed for its khalwa Quranic schools, which drew students from across the Sudan. It shared the fortunes of the north, governed through the Abdallabi lords of Qarri and then left to the riverine Arab chiefs as Sennar weakened, raided and overawed by the independent Shaigiya; when Burckhardt visited in 1813 it was still a busy caravan town. Eight years later the Ottoman Egyptian conquest carried the Funj age away.
zh:
柏柏尔位于尼罗河东岸，南距阿特巴拉河汇入口不远，是努比亚河路与通往萨瓦金的沙漠商道交会之处。早在麦洛埃时代这里已有城镇；到15世纪，此地属于达尔贾阿尔的阿拉伯化努比亚人——穆斯林骆驼客和牧人与说努比亚语的村民为邻，城镇的生计系于尼罗河运输和横穿百卢达的商队。1444年，它是苏丹北部一座没有强势君主的小集镇，也是尼罗河大弯与红海之间最近似门户的地方。

在丰吉苏丹治下，柏柏尔迎来全盛：它成为赴汉志朝觐商队的渡河之地，也是苏丹货物易手的总集散地——象牙、鸵鸟羽和皮革经此运往萨瓦金，布匹、丝绸、香料和香水由原路折返；行旅把当地砖砌的盖萨里亚大市场与非斯、开罗和吉达的市集相提并论。16至17世纪起，此城又以赫勒瓦古兰经经学学校闻名，学生从苏丹各地负笈而来。它与整个北境共沉浮：先由驻加里的阿卜杜拉比领主统治，森纳尔衰落后落入河畔阿拉伯酋长之手，又遭自立的沙伊吉亚人侵扰威压。1813年布尔克哈特到访时，这里仍是繁忙的商队城镇；八年后，奥斯曼埃及的征服为丰吉时代画上句号。

en:
Massawa grew up after the old Red Sea port of Adulis declined, its harbour occupying the islands of Basé and Taulud near the Dahlak Archipelago. From the eleventh century the Dahlak sultans made it the link between Muslim shipping on the Red Sea and the Christian Ethiopian highlands, where caravan routes from Ethiopia met traffic from Arabia. Beja and Tigre peoples lived along the shore, while a qadi headed the Muslim merchant town. Its allegiance was loose: the port paid tribute irregularly to the Bahr Negash and other highland governors, but remained tied to Dahlak, itself a vassal of Aden. In 1444 it was therefore the hot, arid sea outlet of Medri Bahri, where highland claims met Indian Ocean commerce.

Emperor Zara Yaqob pushed his authority to the coast in the mid-fifteenth century and fortified the Gerer peninsula, while Abyssinian troops sacked Massawa and Dahlak in 1464–65. Portuguese squadrons used the harbour early in the next century as their gateway to allied Ethiopia, but in 1557 Özdemir Pasha seized it for the Ottomans and tried to make Massawa the centre of the province of Habesh. The highlands resisted conquest, so Ottoman authority was exercised through a Balaw naib, while the local sharia qadi kept wide jurisdiction along the coast. In 1809 a Turkish governor was appointed, followed in 1813 by an Egyptian one, tightening direct rule as the Red Sea became an Ottoman-Egyptian frontier.
zh:
马萨瓦兴起于古老红海港口阿杜利斯衰落之后，港区位于达赫拉克群岛附近的巴塞岛和陶卢德岛一带。11世纪起，达赫拉克苏丹把这里作为红海穆斯林航运与埃塞俄比亚基督教高地之间的纽带，来自埃塞俄比亚的商路在该处接上阿拉伯半岛的海上交通。贝扎人与提格雷人居住在沿岸，一名卡迪主持这座穆斯林商镇。它的臣属关系松散：港口不定期向巴赫勒·尼加什等高地统治者纳贡，却仍依附达赫拉克，而达赫拉克又是亚丁的附庸。1444年，这里因此是梅德利巴赫里炎热干旱的出海口，高地权势与印度洋贸易在此相接。

15世纪中叶，皇帝扎拉·雅各布把权威推向海岸，在格雷尔半岛修筑要塞；1464至1465年，阿比西尼亚军队洗劫马萨瓦和达赫拉克。下一个世纪初，葡萄牙分舰队把该港用作进入盟邦埃塞俄比亚的门户，但1557年厄兹代米尔帕夏为奥斯曼人夺取马萨瓦，试图将其建为哈贝什省的中心。高地挡住了进一步征服，奥斯曼人便通过巴莱乌人的纳伊布行使统治，当地沙里亚法庭的卡迪则在沿海保有广泛司法权。1809年，一名土耳其总督被派到此地；1813年又改派埃及总督，红海成为奥斯曼—埃及边疆，直接统治也随之加强。

en:
Aswan, ancient Syene, lies immediately north of the Nile's first cataract, the natural break between Upper Egypt and Nubia. Its granite quarries supplied temples and obelisks, while the garrison and customs post below the cataract checked every vessel moving between Egypt and the southern caravan lands. The tenth-century Fatimid tombs show the town's continued Islamic life, and in 1444 it was the Mamluk Sultanate's southern gateway, a Sunni Egyptian river market for Nubian livestock, ivory and desert trade.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1517, Aswan remained part of the Egyptian eyalet, though Mamluk beys and Upper Egyptian Arab houses disputed real power in the south. In 1767 Humam ibn Yusuf, shaykh of the Hawwara, ruled a broad domain reaching from Minya to Aswan; his war with Ali Bey al-Kabir ended in defeat and Humam's death while fleeing toward Nubia in 1769. During the French invasion, Louis-Nicolas Davout's cavalry defeated Osman Hassan Bey's Mamluks near Syene on 12 February 1799 and then rested in Aswan. After the French withdrawal in 1801 and Muhammad Ali's rise in 1805, the town became a base for Cairo's renewed control of the southern frontier.
zh:
阿斯旺古称赛伊尼，坐落在尼罗河第一瀑布北侧；这道瀑布是上埃及与努比亚之间的天然分界。当地花岗岩石场为神庙和方尖碑供料，瀑布下方的驻军与税关则检查往来埃及和南方商路的每一艘船。10世纪的法蒂玛墓地显示这里在伊斯兰时代仍延续着城市生活。1444年，阿斯旺是马穆鲁克苏丹国的南部门户，也是逊尼派埃及人的河港市集，交易努比亚牲畜、象牙和沙漠商货。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，阿斯旺隶属埃及省，但南方实权长期由马穆鲁克贝伊和上埃及阿拉伯家族争夺。1767年，哈瓦拉部落长老胡马姆·伊本·优素福控制了从明亚到阿斯旺的广阔地区；他与阿里贝伊·卡比尔交战，最终兵败，1769年在逃往努比亚途中死去。法国入侵期间，路易-尼古拉·达武的骑兵于1799年2月12日在赛伊尼附近击败奥斯曼·哈桑贝伊的马穆鲁克军，随后进入阿斯旺休整。1801年法军撤出、1805年穆罕默德·阿里崛起后，这座城成为开罗政府重新控制南部边疆的基地。

en:
Suakin occupies a coral island beside a long Red Sea inlet, with the mainland quarter of the Geyf facing it. It was still a small Beja settlement when al-Hamdani named it in the tenth century, then grew after the southern port of Badi was abandoned. In 1264 a Mamluk expedition intervened in its disputes over merchants' goods, and in 1317 its ruler formally accepted Mamluk suzerainty and an annual payment. As Mamluk power weakened late in the fourteenth century, the Hedareb took the port and made it their capital. Indian shipping, African pilgrims bound for Mecca and, by the next century, Venetian merchants passed through its customs house. In 1444 Suakin was thus a wealthy Beja and Arab Muslim port under loose Mamluk overlordship.

A Portuguese fleet besieged Suakin in 1513 and another force briefly held it in 1541, during the struggle for the Red Sea. After the Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517 the town entered the Ottoman sphere, and from the mid-1550s Özdemir Pasha made it the residence of the pasha of Habesh. The Ottomans repaired the Shafi'i and Hanafi mosques, strengthened the coral fort and built roads and public buildings. The sea route around Africa gradually drew Indian commerce away, although caravans from the Funj sultanate of Sennar still brought trade up to the coast. Early in the nineteenth century the Swiss traveller Burckhardt found two-thirds of the houses in ruins, Suakin's great age of medieval prosperity long past.
zh:
萨瓦金坐落在红海一道长湾旁的珊瑚岛上，对岸是大陆上的盖夫街区。10世纪哈姆达尼提到它时，这里还只是贝扎人的小聚落，后来南方港口巴迪被废弃，萨瓦金才得以发展。1264年，马穆鲁克远征军因商人货物纠纷介入当地；1317年，萨瓦金统治者正式接受马穆鲁克宗主权并缴纳年款。14世纪末马穆鲁克势力衰弱，赫达雷布人夺取港口并将其定为都城。印度船只、前往麦加的非洲朝觐者，以及下一世纪的威尼斯商人，都曾经过这里的税关。1444年，萨瓦金因此是一座处在马穆鲁克松散宗主权下、富裕的贝扎与阿拉伯穆斯林港口。

红海争霸期间，葡萄牙舰队1513年围攻萨瓦金，另一支军队又于1541年短暂占领该港。1517年奥斯曼征服埃及后，萨瓦金进入奥斯曼势力范围；1550年代中期，厄兹代米尔帕夏把这里作为哈贝什帕夏的驻地。奥斯曼人修缮沙斐仪派和哈乃斐派清真寺，加固珊瑚石要塞，并修筑道路与公共建筑。绕非洲好望角的航路逐渐带走印度贸易，不过来自丰吉人森纳尔苏丹国的商队仍把货物送到海岸。19世纪初，瑞士旅行家布尔克哈特发现城中三分之二的房屋已成废墟，萨瓦金中世纪的繁荣时代早已远去。

en:
Kharga is the southernmost of Egypt's western oases, set in a long desert depression about 200 kilometres west of the Nile. Its wells made it a stage on Darb al-Arba'in, the Forty Days Road that linked Darfur and Kordofan with the Egyptian Nile. Caravans drove camels, donkeys, cattle and horses northward and carried gold, ivory, slaves, textiles and salt between Sudan and Egypt; Ibn Hawqal described the road in the tenth century. In 1444 the oasis was a remote Arabic-speaking Muslim possession on the desert edge of the Burji Mamluk state, valued for water, livestock and passage rather than for dense settlement.

The Ottoman conquest of 1517 placed Kharga under the sovereignty of Cairo's new Ottoman governors, but its fortunes continued to follow the camel caravans. In 1698 the French traveler Poncet left Kharga on his journey toward Ethiopia and later described the waterless marches where the bones of camels marked the road. William George Browne joined a caravan on the same route in 1793 and became the first Englishman to record the journey from within. Their accounts show Kharga less as an isolated refuge than as the Egyptian gate of a still active Sudanese trade road.
zh:
哈里杰是埃及西部诸绿洲中最南的一处，坐落在尼罗河以西约200公里的狭长沙漠洼地中。这里的水井使它成为「四十日路」上的驿站，这条商路把达尔富尔、科尔多凡同埃及尼罗河谷连接起来。商队把骆驼、驴、牛和马赶往北方，也在苏丹与埃及之间贩运黄金、象牙、奴隶、织物和盐；10世纪时，伊本·豪盖勒已记载过这条道路。1444年，哈里杰是布尔吉马穆鲁克国家沙漠边缘一处遥远的阿拉伯语穆斯林属地，其价值在于水源、牲畜和通行，而不是稠密人口。

1517年奥斯曼征服埃及后，哈里杰在名义上归开罗的奥斯曼总督统辖，但它的兴衰仍随骆驼商队起伏。1698年，法国旅行者蓬塞从哈里杰出发行往埃塞俄比亚，后来记述了沿途无水路段和标示道路的骆驼白骨。1793年，威廉·乔治·布朗随商队走同一条路，成为第一个亲身记录这段旅程的英国人。他们的记载表明，哈里杰并非孤立的避难绿洲，而是一条仍在使用的苏丹商路的埃及门户。

en:
Qasr Ibrim crowns a sheer cliff on the eastern bank of the Nile in Lower Nubia, some 240 kilometres south of Aswan. The Romans knew it as Primis: after Gaius Petronius's campaign against Kush in 23 BC, their engineers rebuilt it into the strongest fortress in the Nile valley. It passed to Makuria in the early eighth century and became a chief Christian centre of Lower Nubia, seat of the Eparch of Nobatia; its cathedral went up in the first half of the eighth century, and the largest hoard of Old Nubian documents ever found later came from its ruins, including the archive of the eparchs. Timothy, the last known bishop of Faras, resided here and was buried in the cathedral around 1375. In 1444 the Christian kingdom of Dotawo, the Nubian name under which Makuria lived on, still held the cliff castle commanding the Nile, even though Islam had long triumphed in Egypt to the north.

Early in the sixteenth century, after Selim I's Ottomans had conquered Egypt, a garrison of Bosnian soldiers was installed in the fortress and part of the cathedral became a mosque; the Bosnians married into the Nubian population and held the rock for nearly three centuries. The Mamluks who fled Muhammad Ali's Cairo massacre of 1811 found refuge here, drove out the descendants of the Bosnian garrison and held out against his troops until 1813, when Ibrahim Pasha dislodged them with artillery fire. They were the last occupants of the cliff, and the old fortress was left deserted above the river.
zh:
伊布里姆堡雄踞下努比亚尼罗河东岸的岩壁之上，北距阿斯旺约二百四十公里。罗马人称之为普里米斯，公元前23年盖乌斯·佩特罗尼乌斯远征库施后，由罗马工匠将其重建为当时尼罗河谷最坚固的要塞。8世纪初它并入马库里亚王国，此后成为下努比亚的基督教中心，诺巴蒂亚都督驻节于此；大教堂建于8世纪上半叶，后来从其废墟中出土的古努比亚语文献数量为各地之最，其中包括历代都督的档案。最后一位有记载的法拉斯主教蒂莫西就长住于此，约1375年葬在大教堂中。1444年，以努比亚语自称「多塔沃」的马库里亚基督教王国仍占据着这座扼守尼罗河的崖堡，尽管伊斯兰早已在北方的埃及取得胜利。

16世纪初，塞利姆一世的奥斯曼军队征服埃及后，在堡内派驻一支波斯尼亚守军，大教堂的一部分被改成清真寺；这些波斯尼亚士兵与当地努比亚人通婚，在崖上驻守了近三百年。1811年逃过穆罕默德·阿里开罗清洗的马穆鲁克退守此地，逐走波斯尼亚守军的后裔，继续抵抗其军队，直到1813年易卜拉欣帕夏以炮火将他们逐走。他们是这座崖堡最后的驻守者，此后古要塞便荒废在河水之上。

en:
Guam, Guåhan in Chamorro, is the largest and southernmost island in the Marianas. By 1444 its villages had taken shape around latte stones, the pillar-and-capstone foundations raised for houses and important buildings. Coastal matua families held the fishing grounds while mana'chang communities lived inland, with achaot serving as go-betweens; kinship and inheritance ran through women, and seamanship, pottery and weaving were highly developed. Hagåtña was already a prominent west-coast village, and the island remained a world of Chamorro chiefs, ancestors and independent settlements.

Ferdinand Magellan reached Guam on 6 March 1521 after crossing the Pacific and his fleet named the Marianas the Islands of Thieves. Miguel López de Legazpi claimed Guam for Spain in 1565, but permanent colonization began only in 1668, when the Jesuit Diego Luis de San Vitores arrived and Chief Kepuha granted land at Hagåtña for the first church. Chief Hurao besieged the new Spanish post in 1670, and Matå'pang killed San Vitores in 1672. The wars that followed ended in reducción, with people from about 180 villages concentrated into seven towns by the early 1680s. Guam then served the Acapulco-Manila galleons until that route closed in 1815, leaving a Spanish Catholic and garrison island by 1821.
zh:
关岛在查莫洛语中称Guåhan，是马里亚纳群岛最大、最南的岛屿。到1444年，岛上村落已围绕拉提石发展，这种石柱加半球形石帽的结构用于承托房屋和重要建筑。沿海的matua上层家族掌握渔场，mana'chang下层社群居住内陆，achaot中层充当中间人；亲属与继承沿母系计算，航海、制陶和纺织都十分发达。哈加特纳已是西岸重要村落，全岛仍是查莫洛酋长、祖先祭祀和各独立聚落的世界。

1521年3月6日，斐迪南·麦哲伦横渡太平洋后抵达关岛，他的船队把马里亚纳称为盗贼群岛。1565年，米格尔·洛佩斯·德莱加斯皮代表西班牙宣称占有关岛，但永久殖民迟至1668年才开始：耶稣会士迭戈·路易斯·德·圣维托雷斯到来，酋长克普哈在哈加特纳捐地修建第一座教堂。1670年，酋长胡劳围攻新设立的西班牙据点；1672年，马塔庞杀死圣维托雷斯。随后的战争以集村政策告终，到17世纪80年代初，约180个村落的人口被集中到七座城镇。此后关岛为阿卡普尔科至马尼拉的邮船提供补给，直到该航线1815年终止；到1821年，这里已成为西班牙的天主教驻军岛屿。

en:
The land around Rabaul is the northern tip of New Britain's Gazelle Peninsula, where a flooded volcanic caldera opens into Simpson Harbour. Ash from Tavurvur and Vulcan made the coastal soil unusually fertile. The Baining, likely the peninsula's earlier inhabitants, gardened taro on rotating clearings and kept much of the forested interior, while coastal villages looked across St George's Channel toward New Ireland. In 1444 no town stood on the mangrove-fringed harbour, no foreign power claimed it, and no Christian mission had reached it; kin groups, fishing, gardens, and the threat of eruption set the rhythm of life.

For centuries the harbour was known only to local seafarers. On 27 February 1700 William Dampier became the first recorded British visitor to New Britain, which he named Nova Britannia, but the voyage did not establish a post. In 1767 Philip Carteret took HMS Swallow through St George's Channel and named the Duke of York Islands between New Ireland and New Britain; he likewise made no annexation. By 1821 the caldera still had no European fort or mission, and Gazelle remained in the hands of its own villagers and elders.
zh:
拉包尔一带是新不列颠岛加泽尔半岛北端，海水侵入的火山口形成辛普森港。塔乌鲁尔与武尔坎火山喷出的火山灰使沿海土壤异常肥沃。拜宁人很可能是半岛较早的居民，他们在轮垦地上种植芋艿，并活动于林木茂密的内陆；沿海村落则隔着圣乔治海峡与新爱尔兰相望。1444年，红树林环绕的港湾旁还没有城镇，没有外来政权宣称占有，也没有基督教传教站抵达；亲属群体、渔业、园圃和火山威胁构成了生活的基本面貌。

此后数百年间，使用这片港湾的仍是本地海民。1700年2月27日，威廉·丹皮尔成为有记载的第一位到访新不列颠的英国人，并将该岛命名为新不列颠，但这次航行没有留下据点。1767年，菲利普·卡特里特指挥「燕子号」穿过圣乔治海峡，为新爱尔兰与新不列颠之间的约克公爵群岛命名，同样没有宣布吞并。到1821年，火山口旁仍没有欧洲人的要塞或传教站，加泽尔仍掌握在本地村民和长老手中。

en:
Hanuabada, the 'big village' in the Motu language, stands on piles over a sheltered harbour on the south-eastern coast of New Guinea. Behind the shore live the Koitabu, hill people who intermarried with the Motu and shared their villages, each divided into iduhu clans. The women shaped cooking pots from local clay, while the men built lakatoi — several dugout hulls lashed together with a platform and a crab-claw sail — for the annual hiri voyages. Fleets of up to twenty craft and six hundred men sailed west into the Gulf of Papua carrying as many as 20,000 pots, and brought back sago and timber. In 1444 this cluster of stilt hamlets was already the largest of the Motu settlements, living by fishing, pottery and that long, dangerous trade.

The hiri cycle ran on for the next four centuries. In 1606 the Spanish ships of Luís Vaz de Torres explored the southern coast from Milne Bay to the Gulf of Papua, yet no European landing or post followed at this harbour, and the Motu kept their own customs and their annual voyages. Through 1821 no outside power ruled here; the lakatoi fleets remained the village's only link to the wider world.
zh:
哈努阿巴达在莫图语里意为「大村」，是新几内亚岛东南海岸一座掩蔽港湾上的木桩水上村落。岸后住着科伊塔布人，他们是来自内陆山地的居民，与莫图人通婚杂居，村落按「伊杜胡」氏族划分。莫图女人用当地陶土烧制炊罐，男人则把几艘独木舟捆在一起、上架平台、挂上蟹钳形帆，造出「拉卡托伊」多体船，用于一年一度的「希里」远航。多达二十艘船、六百名水手的船队载着多至两万个陶罐向西驶入巴布亚湾，换回西米和木材。1444年时，这片连片的水上棚屋已是莫图人最大的聚落，靠捕鱼、制陶和这段漫长凶险的贸易为生。

此后四个世纪里，希里远航周而复始。1606年，路易斯·巴斯·德·托雷斯的西班牙船队考察了从米尔恩湾到巴布亚湾的南部海岸，但没有欧洲人在这个港湾登陆或设点，莫图人照旧保留着自己的习俗和年年成行的远航。直到1821年，这里不受任何外来政权统治，拉卡托伊船队仍是这座村庄通往外部世界的唯一纽带。

en:
The Solomon Islands province lies in the double island chain east of New Guinea; Guadalcanal, locally called Isatabu, is the largest land, with rain-forested mountains behind its northern coast. Poha Cave and Vatuluma Posovi show occupation by 4500–2500 BC, and Lapita potters reached the islands around 1200–800 BC. By 1444 Melanesian villagers lived from taro and yam gardens, fishing, and inter-island canoe trade; sacred shrines bound clans together across a sea of many languages. No outside power ruled the chain.

The first known European ships came from Peru. Mendaña's two vessels, captained by Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa and Pedro de Ortega, reached Santa Isabel on 7 February 1568 and spent six months surveying Malaita, Guadalcanal, Makira and neighbouring islands. The expedition gave the Spanish name Islas Salomón but founded nothing. A second voyage tried to plant a colony on Nendö in 1595; Mendaña died there on 18 October and Isabel Barreto led the survivors away. Queirós passed through in 1606, still without lasting occupation. Carteret sighted islands in 1767, Bougainville named Choiseul in 1768, and La Pérouse was wrecked at Vanikoro in 1788; whalers later called for provisions, but in 1821 no foreign flag yet ruled the Solomons.
zh:
所罗门群岛省位于新几内亚以东的双列岛链中；最大岛屿是本地称伊萨塔布的瓜达尔卡纳尔岛，雨林山地横亘北岸后方。波哈洞与瓦图卢马·波索维遗址表明，公元前4500年至前2500年已有人居住，拉皮塔陶工约在公元前1200年至前800年抵达。到1444年，美拉尼西亚村民以芋艿、薯蓣园圃和渔业为生，并靠独木舟维持岛际贸易；神圣神龛把众多语言社群中的氏族联系在一起。当时没有外来政权统治这条岛链。

最早有记载的欧洲船只来自秘鲁。门达尼亚的两艘船分别由佩德罗·甘博阿·德·萨尔米恩托与佩德罗·德·奥尔特加指挥，于1568年2月7日抵达圣伊莎贝尔岛，随后用六个月测绘马莱塔、瓜达尔卡纳尔、马基拉及邻近岛屿。远征队留下西班牙名「所罗门群岛」，却没有建立据点。1595年，第二次航行试图在恩登岛建立殖民地；门达尼亚于10月18日病死，伊莎贝尔·巴雷托带领幸存者离去。基罗斯1606年再经此地，仍未形成持久占领。卡特里特1767年望见多座岛屿，布干维尔1768年为舒瓦瑟尔岛命名，拉彼鲁兹1788年在瓦尼科罗岛失事；此后捕鲸船前来补给，但到1821年，所罗门群岛仍未受外国旗帜统治。

en:
Vanuatu is a chain of active volcanic islands, and Espiritu Santo in the north is the largest. Lapita seafarers reached the group around 1100–700 BC, bringing yams, taro, bananas, pigs and chickens; later Melanesian settlement produced more than a hundred closely related Oceanic languages. In 1444 authority belonged to autonomous village networks rather than a single kingdom. Garden land, reefs, ancestral shrines, exchange voyages and graded ceremonial titles ordered life across islands where eruptions could suddenly remake the landscape.

The European intrusion began in 1606, when Pedro Fernandes de Queirós, a Portuguese navigator sailing for Spain, reached Espiritu Santo, believed it the edge of Terra Australis, and proclaimed La Austrialia del Espíritu Santo. His New Jerusalem on Big Bay lasted barely a month after clashes with islanders and sickness; Luis Váez de Torres sailed the remaining ships west. Bougainville returned in May 1768 and called the group the Great Cyclades. James Cook charted it from July to September 1774 and named it the New Hebrides. Bligh passed the Banks Islands in 1789, and the first recorded whaleship, Rose, called in February 1804. By 1821 these ships brought provisions and news, but no foreign sovereignty.
zh:
瓦努阿图是一列活火山岛，北部的圣埃斯皮里图岛面积最大。拉皮塔航海者约在公元前1100年至前700年抵达，带来薯蓣、芋艿、香蕉、猪和鸡；后续美拉尼西亚定居者发展出一百多种彼此相近的大洋洲语。1444年，权力属于自治的村落网络，而不是统一王国。园圃土地、礁石、祖灵神龛、交换航行和等级仪式头衔维系着各岛秩序，火山喷发也可能骤然改变地貌。

欧洲人的闯入始于1606年：为西班牙效力的葡萄牙航海家佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯抵达圣埃斯皮里图岛，以为自己到了南方大陆边缘，并宣布其为La Austrialia del Espíritu Santo。他在大海湾建立的「新耶路撒冷」因与岛民冲突和疾病仅维持约一个月，路易斯·巴斯·德·托雷斯随后率领余部西航。布干维尔1768年5月重返此地，把群岛称为大基克拉泽斯；詹姆斯·库克1774年7月至9月测绘群岛，并命名为新赫布里底。布莱1789年经过班克斯群岛，有记载的第一艘捕鲸船「玫瑰号」于1804年2月到访。到1821年，这些船只带来补给与消息，却还没有带来外来主权。

en:
Hawaiʻi, the Big Island, is the largest and south-easternmost island of the Hawaiian chain, a volcanic land overshadowed by Mauna Kea and Mauna Loa, with rainy Hilo on one flank and the drier Kona coast on the other. Its ahupuaʻa land divisions ran from forested uplands to reefs, linking gardens, bird and stone resources, and fishing grounds. By 1444 villages were spread through Kona, Kohala, Hāmākua, Hilo, Puna and Kaʻū; the dense basalt of Mauna Kea had become an important adze source after 1400. Aliʻi chiefs and kahuna priests governed through heiau temples and kapu rules, while fishponds and taro gardens sustained a ranked society along the Kona shore where Kailua later arose.

James Cook entered Kealakekua Bay in Resolution and Discovery on 17 January 1779 and was killed there on 14 February in a quarrel over a stolen boat. Muskets and ships soon entered Hawaiian succession wars. Kamehameha won the first fighting on the island in 1782 and controlled Hawaiʻi by 1791; in 1795 he conquered Maui, Oʻahu, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi, made Kailua his seat, and accepted the submission of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau in 1810, completing the kingdom. George Vancouver gave him four bulls and eight cows in 1793–1794, and a kapu on hunting let the herds multiply. After Kamehameha's death in 1819, Kaʻahumanu and Keōpūolani persuaded Liholiho to end the kapu during the October ʻAi Noa; traditionalist forces were defeated that December. Christian missionaries reached Kailua in 1820, opening a new religious age for the dynasty.
zh:
夏威夷（Hawaiʻi，又称大岛）是夏威夷群岛最东南、面积最大的火山岛，冒纳凯阿与冒纳罗亚俯瞰全岛；迎风一侧的希洛雨水丰沛，另一侧的科纳海岸较为干燥。阿胡普阿土地单元从山林延伸到礁岸，把园圃、鸟类与石材资源、渔场连接起来。到1444年，科纳、科哈拉、哈马库阿、希洛、普纳和卡乌各区都已有村落；1400年后，冒纳凯阿的致密玄武岩成为制作石锛的重要原料。酋长和祭司凭借神庙与禁忌治理，鱼塘、芋田和海岸资源供养着等级森严的社会，后来凯卢阿-科纳所在的科纳海湾，正是酋长停泊独木舟和举行仪式的地方。

1779年1月17日，詹姆斯·库克在第三次太平洋航行中率「决心号」和「发现号」进入凯阿拉凯夸湾，又在2月14日因小艇失窃引发的冲突中被杀。火器和欧洲船只很快卷入夏威夷的继承战争。卡美哈梅哈在1782年赢得岛上的首场关键战事，1791年控制夏威夷岛；1795年，他征服茂伊、欧胡、莫洛凯和拉奈，以凯卢阿为统治中心，并于1810年接受考艾与尼豪归附，完成夏威夷王国的统一。1793至1794年，乔治·温哥华赠给他四头公牛和八头母牛，卡美哈梅哈下令禁止猎杀，牛群遂在山地繁殖。1819年卡美哈梅哈去世后，加休曼努和凯奥普奥拉尼促使利霍利霍在10月的「阿伊·诺亚」中废止禁忌，守旧势力又于12月被击败。1820年，基督教传教士抵达凯卢阿，王朝的宗教秩序进入新的阶段。

en: Kiritimati is the great atoll of the northern Line Islands, on the eastern edge of the islands later gathered under the name Kiribati. Its reefs and lagoon offered seabirds, turtles and safe canoe landings, but excavated camps, marae and canoe-storage sites on the windward shore show only intermittent Polynesian use from about 1250 to 1450. Visitors probably came from Tabuaeran to gather birds and turtles; in 1444 there was no permanent village. A Spanish expedition under Hernando de Grijalva sighted the atoll and charted it as Acea in 1537. James Cook reached it on Christmas Eve 1777 and gave it the name Christmas Island, yet through 1821 Kiritimati remained without permanent settlers or foreign administration.
zh: 基里蒂马蒂是北莱恩群岛的大环礁，位于后来归入基里巴斯的岛群东缘。礁屿和潟湖盛产海鸟、海龟，也可供独木舟安全停靠，但迎风岸上发掘出的营地、马拉埃和独木舟存放遗址表明，约1250—1450年间这里只有波利尼西亚人间歇性活动。来访者可能来自塔布阿埃兰，到此捕捉海鸟和海龟；1444年时岛上并无永久村落。1537年，埃尔南多·德·格里哈尔瓦率领的西班牙远征队望见这座环礁，并把它标为Acea。1777年圣诞前夜，詹姆斯·库克抵达此处，将其命名为圣诞岛；直到1821年，基里蒂马蒂仍没有常住居民或外来行政机构。

en:
Viti Levu ('Great Fiji') is the largest island in the Fijian archipelago. Volcanic mountains divide its wet eastern coast from the drier west, while the Rewa delta opens rich farming land in the south-east. Austronesian and later Melanesian settlers had long occupied its coasts and river valleys, exchanging pottery and bark cloth with neighbouring archipelagos before Tongan influence spread through Fiji from the tenth century. By 1444, Viseisei at Vuda Point and other coastal villages were led by chiefs, elders and warriors; important settlements carried ramparts and moats, drua canoes linked the islands, and whale teeth, bark cloth and yaqona shaped rank and ceremony.

European knowledge came late. Abel Tasman's Dutch expedition reached Fiji in 1643, but it did not open lasting trade with Viti Levu. James Cook sighted and visited Vatoa in the southern Lau group on 2 July 1774, the only Fijian island where he landed. In 1789 William Bligh, cast adrift after the Bounty mutiny, sailed between Viti Levu and Vanua Levu and charted the waters later named Bligh Water without landing. Fijian canoes and chiefs still dominated local exchanges when European traders and settlers began to establish Levuka on nearby Ovalau around 1820.
zh:
维提（Viti Levu，意为「大斐济」）是斐济群岛第一大岛。火山山脉隔开湿润的东海岸和较干燥的西部，东南的雷瓦河三角洲则有肥沃农田。南岛族群及后来的美拉尼西亚人早已居住在海岸与河谷，陶器和树皮布流通于邻近群岛；10世纪起，汤加势力把波利尼西亚风俗带入斐济。1444年时，武达角的维塞塞与其他沿海村落由酋长、长老和武士统辖，重要聚落设有壕沟壁垒；drua大帆船只往来于岛屿之间，抹香鲸牙、树皮布和卡瓦酒则维系着身份等级与仪式秩序。

欧洲人认识这里相当晚。1643年，阿贝尔·塔斯曼的荷兰探险队抵达斐济，但没有为维提岛带来持续贸易。1774年7月2日，詹姆斯·库克望见并登上南部劳群岛的瓦托阿，那是他唯一登陆过的斐济岛屿。1789年，在「邦蒂号」哗变后被放逐的威廉·布莱驾船穿过维提岛与瓦努阿岛之间，测绘了后来得名布莱水道的水域，却没有靠岸。到1820年前后欧洲商人和定居者开始在附近的奥瓦劳岛建立莱武卡时，维提岛的本地交换仍主要由斐济船只和酋长掌控。

en:
The Samoan islands were settled some 3,500 years ago by Lapita voyagers, whose oldest known site, at Mulifanua, dates to about 1500 BC. Savaiʻi, the westernmost and largest island, is one great shield volcano, and at its tip lies Falealupo, where the sea-swept rock of Fafā-o-Saualiʻi was held to be the gateway to Pulotu, the land of the dead. Around the year 1000 the islands came under the Tuʻi Tonga, whose governors kept court at Safotu on Savaiʻi. In the thirteenth century the brothers Savea, Tuna and Fata rose against the last Tongan ruler, Talakaifaiki, and drove him to his ships at Mulifanua; his parting praise, mālie toa, mālie tau, gave the new paramount line its title, Malietoa. In 1444 Samoa was a patchwork of village and district chiefdoms under the matai title system, joined by voyaging canoes to Tonga and Fiji, and Falealupo was the home of the war-priestess Nafanua, whose blessing chiefs sought before any campaign.

In the 1500s the four pāpā district titles passed to Nafanua's niece Salamasina, who as tafaʻifā held all four, and her reign is remembered as a golden age of Samoan custom. Europeans remained only a rumour until 1722, when the Dutchman Jacob Roggeveen became the first outsider known to sight the islands, and Louis-Antoine de Bougainville, calling in 1768, named them the Navigator Islands for the islanders' seamanship. Contact stayed fleeting for another two generations, and only in 1821 did the first American trading vessel, the Roscoe of Salem, drop anchor here, the forerunner of the whalers soon to follow.
zh:
约三千五百年前，拉皮塔航海者定居萨摩亚群岛，已知最早的遗址穆利富努阿可追溯至约公元前1500年。萨瓦伊是位置最西、面积最大的岛屿，本身就是一座巨大的盾状火山；岛的最西端是法莱卢波村，海边浪击的法法奥萨瓦利伊岩相传是冥界普洛图的入口。约公元1000年，群岛被图伊汤加帝国征服，汤加总督驻节于萨瓦伊岛上的萨福图。13世纪，萨韦亚、图纳和法塔兄弟起兵反抗末代汤加统治者塔拉凯法伊基，在穆利富努阿海边把他逼上船；他临行时赞叹「mālie toa, mālie tau」（勇士善战），新的最高酋号「马列托亚」便由此而来。1444年的萨摩亚是马塔伊酋衔体制维系下的村落与地区酋邦，靠远航独木舟与汤加、斐济往来；法莱卢波是女战神祭司娜芙阿努阿的故乡，酋长出征前都要到此求她祝福。

16世纪，四个帕帕地区酋号传给娜芙阿努阿的侄女萨拉玛西娜，她集四衔于一身，称「塔法伊法」，她的时代在萨摩亚口述传统中被视为古风的黄金时代。此后欧洲人长期只存在于传闻中：1722年荷兰人雅各布·罗赫芬成为已知最早望见群岛的外来者，1768年路易-安托万·德·布干维尔到访，因岛民高超的航海术将其命名为「航海者群岛」。此后又过了两代人，接触仍寥寥无几，直到1821年第一艘美国商船、塞勒姆的「罗斯科号」在此抛锚，捕鲸船接踵而至的年代由此开启。

en:
The Tuamotu Islands scatter low coral atolls across the ocean east of Tahiti, whose volcanic peaks form the western centre of this sea world. Polynesians settled the western atolls from the Society Islands between roughly 900 and 1200, building coral marae on Rangiroa, Manihi and Mataiva. On Tahiti, related clans held valleys and coasts under great chiefs, councils and priests. In 1444 no European ship had yet entered these waters, and authority rested with competing chiefly lines rather than a single island throne.

European contact began when Magellan's fleet crossed the Tuamotus in 1521. Queirós passed through in 1606, Schouten and Le Maire in 1616, and Roggeveen in 1722, but these sightings brought no lasting rule. Wallis reached Tahiti in 1767, followed by Bougainville in 1768 and Cook at Matavai Bay in 1769; a Spanish mission founded in 1774 was abandoned within a year. The London Missionary Society arrived on the Duff in 1797 and allied with the Pōmare chiefs. Pōmare II was driven to Moʻorea in 1808, but his victory at Te Feipī in 1815 prepared the way for a Christian kingdom on Tahiti and Moʻorea. When he died in 1821, the Tuamotus remained in the Tahitian chiefly orbit rather than under direct European government.
zh:
土阿莫土群岛由散布在塔希提以东海面的低矮珊瑚环礁组成，火山岛塔希提（大溪地）则是这片海上世界西侧的中心。约900年至1200年间，波利尼西亚人自社会群岛渡海定居西部环礁，在朗伊罗阿、马尼希和马塔伊瓦留下珊瑚石垒成的马拉埃。塔希提的亲缘氏族各据山谷与海岸，由大酋长、议事会和祭司统领。1444年时，欧洲船只尚未进入这片海域，权力分散在相互竞争的首领世系手中，而不是统一的岛屿王位。

欧洲接触始于1521年，麦哲伦的船队穿过土阿莫土群岛。1606年奎罗斯、1616年斯豪滕和勒梅尔、1722年罗赫芬先后经过，却没有建立持久统治。沃利斯1767年抵达塔希提，布干维尔1768年随后来访，库克1769年停泊马塔瓦伊湾；西班牙人1774年设立的传教站不到一年便撤销。1797年，伦敦传道会乘「达夫号」抵达，与波马雷家族结盟。波马雷二世1808年被逐至莫雷阿岛，但在1815年的特费皮战役获胜，为塔希提和莫雷阿的基督教王国打开局面。到他1821年去世时，土阿莫土群岛仍处在塔希提首领势力范围内，尚未受欧洲人直接管辖。

en:
Manokwari lies on Doreri Bay, at the northeastern corner of the Vogelkop Peninsula. The harbour that Europeans later knew as Dory was sheltered by wooded capes and Mansinam Island, with Papuan fishing and gardening villages building over the water on posts. By the fifteenth century, if not earlier, communities on this coast were trading with canoes from the Moluccas and the Malay world. In 1444 the bay had no outside ruler or permanent foreign factory; its chiefs and clans followed local ancestral cults and received visiting traders on their own terms.

Outside ships became more frequent in the second half of the eighteenth century. In January 1775 Thomas Forrest brought the Tartar into the harbour and described large timber houses raised on piles. On 25 October 1793 Captain John Hayes landed from the Duke of Clarence and Duchess, claimed Dore Bay for Britain as Restoration Bay, named the surrounding country New Albion, and built a stockade called Fort Coronation. The post was intended to tap the massoy bark and nutmeg trade, but the East India Company gave it no support and the British withdrew in 1795, leaving the shore villages to their old commerce.
zh:
马诺夸里位于鸟头半岛东北角的多雷里湾。欧洲人后来称作多里的港湾被林木覆盖的岬角和曼西纳姆岛环抱，巴布亚渔村与园艺村落沿湾而居，房屋多架在水面木桩上。至迟在15世纪，这一带的社群已同摩鹿加和马来世界的独木舟商旅往来贸易。1444年时，港湾没有外来统治者，也没有常设外国商馆；各氏族与首领奉行本地祖灵崇拜，并按自己的条件接待前来贸易的船队。

18世纪下半叶，外来船只到访得更加频繁。1775年1月，托马斯·福里斯特率「鞑靼人号」驶入港湾，记载了架在木桩上的高大木屋。1793年10月25日，约翰·海斯船长乘「克拉伦斯公爵号」和「公爵夫人号」上岸，宣布多雷湾归英国所有并命名为复辟湾，又称周围地区为新阿尔比恩，还筑起木栅据点加冕堡。这个据点打算经营马索伊树皮和肉豆蔻贸易，但英国东印度公司不予支持，英国人遂于1795年撤走，沿岸村落仍维持旧日贸易。

en:
This wet coast runs from the Hokitika and Arahura river mouths south to the glacier-cut sounds of Te Rua-o-te-Moko, or Fiordland. In 1444 the country around Arahura belonged to Ngāti Wairangi, an isolated people whose Southern Alps had few crossings to the eastern plains. Their rivers carried pounamu, the hard green stone made into adzes, ornaments and weapons and exchanged far beyond Te Tai Poutini. Farther south, Fiordland had no large permanent settlements; Māori came seasonally to hunt, fish and gather prized stone at Anita Bay near Piopiotahi.

During the 1600s and 1700s Ngāi Tahu expansion reached the West Coast through marriage, trade and war. By the late 1700s, after the battle at Lake Mahinapua, Ngāti Wairangi had been absorbed into Poutini Ngāi Tahu, while control of Arahura and its greenstone remained decisive. James Cook first sighted Fiordland in 1770 and returned in 1773 to anchor for five weeks in Tamatea, or Dusky Sound. His charts opened the coast to European curiosity, yet through 1821 it remained a place of seasonal Māori camps and only brief ship visits.
zh:
这条多雨海岸从霍基蒂卡与阿拉胡拉河口向南，延伸到特鲁阿-奥特莫科（即菲奥德兰）冰川雕出的峡湾。1444年时，阿拉胡拉一带是Ngāti Wairangi人的土地；南阿尔卑斯山几乎没有通往东部平原的山口，使他们长期与外界隔绝。河流把pounamu绿玉冲到滩上，这种坚硬绿石被制成锛子、饰物和武器，远输到特泰波蒂尼之外。更南的菲奥德兰没有大型永久聚落，毛利人只在狩猎、捕鱼季节前来，并在皮奥皮奥塔希附近的安妮塔湾采集珍贵石料。

17至18世纪，纳塔胡通过联姻、贸易和战争扩张到西岸。18世纪末的马希纳普阿湖之战后，Ngāti Wairangi人并入波蒂尼纳塔胡，控制阿拉胡拉及其绿玉始终是当地权力的关键。詹姆斯·库克1770年首次望见菲奥德兰，1773年又返回并在塔马蒂亚（达斯基湾）停泊五周。他的海图引发欧洲人对这片海岸的兴趣，但直到1821年，这里仍只有毛利人的季节性营地和短暂来访的船只。

en:
Corsica is a mountainous island just north of Sardinia. Pisan and Genoese fleets cleared its coasts of Saracens in the eleventh century, and settlers from Tuscany gave its northern valleys a Tuscan speech. After Genoa destroyed the Pisan fleet at Meloria in 1284, the island passed under its protection, a claim contested for 150 years by Aragon, the papacy, local lords and peasants' leagues led by caporali. Around 1380 the Genoese governor Leonello Lomellino raised a fort - in the local tongue a bastìa - above the fishing cove of Porto Cardo; the governors made it their residence in the next century, and Bastia became the island's principal port. In 1444 it is a turbulent Genoese possession, its wax, honey and timber scant reward for wrung-out taxes, its shores open to Barbary raiders.

In 1453 a Corsican assembly at Lago Benedetto asked Genoa's Bank of Saint George to take the island in hand; from its fortified towns the bank strung the coast with watchtowers against Barbary corsairs. In 1553 a Franco-Ottoman fleet answered the exile Sampiero Corso and seized the island until Andrea Doria restored Genoa, confirmed at Cateau-Cambrésis in 1559; Genoa planted chestnut forests and bore down on taxes. A levy in 1729 opened forty years of revolt: the German adventurer Theodor von Neuhoff was crowned king in 1736 and as quickly discarded, and in 1755 Pasquale Paoli proclaimed a republic at Corte under one of the Enlightenment's first written constitutions. Genoa sold its rights to Louis XV on 15 May 1768, and defeat at Ponte Novu on 9 May 1769 ended the republic; three months later Napoleon Bonaparte was born at Ajaccio. Paoli returned with the French Revolution and called in the British, who held an Anglo-Corsican kingdom at Bastia from 1794 until 1796. A brief British occupation in 1814 ended with the island restored to the French crown, and in 1821 Corsica was a French department.
zh:
科西嘉是撒丁岛以北仅十余公里的多山岛屿。11世纪，比萨和热那亚的舰队肃清了沿岸的萨拉森人，托斯卡纳移民随之而来，使岛北山谷的语言接近托斯卡纳方言。1284年热那亚在梅洛里亚海战歼灭比萨舰队后，科西嘉转入热那亚庇护之下；在此后一百五十年里，阿拉贡、教皇、封建领主和卡波拉利（村社首领）领导的农民联盟不断争夺此岛。1380年前后，热那亚总督莱奥内洛·洛梅利诺在渔村波尔图卡尔多旁修起一座要塞——当地语言称堡垒为bastìa，下世纪总督们以此为驻地，巴斯蒂亚由此成为全岛首要港口。1444年的科西嘉是热那亚手中一块不安分的领地：蜂蜡、蜂蜜和山间木材抵不上被征走的重税，海岸还随时向巴巴里海盗敞开。

1453年，科西嘉人召开大会，请求热那亚的圣乔治银行接管岛屿；银行在设防城镇里统治了一个世纪，并在沿海串起瞭望塔防备巴巴里海盗。1553年，一支法国-奥斯曼联合舰队应流亡者桑皮耶罗·科尔索之请占领科西嘉，直到安德烈亚·多里亚恢复热那亚统治，1559年《卡托-康布雷西和约》予以确认；此后热那亚人大规模种植栗树，同时税负压得更重。1729年一项新税点燃了长达四十年的反抗：1736年德国冒险家特奥多尔·冯·诺伊霍夫一度加冕为王又迅速被弃；1755年，帕斯夸莱·保利在科尔特宣布成立科西嘉共和国，颁行启蒙时代最早的成文宪法之一。1768年5月15日，热那亚把权利卖给路易十五；1769年5月9日法军在蓬泰诺沃取胜，共和国覆灭，三个月后拿破仑·波拿巴出生在阿雅克肖。法国大革命后保利返岛并请来英军，1794年起英属科西嘉王国以巴斯蒂亚为都，1796年法国重新夺回全岛。1814年英军短暂占领后，科西嘉被交还复辟的法国王室；1821年时它已是法国的一个省。

en:
The Maldives are a chain of twenty-six coral atolls strung across the Indian Ocean south-west of India. Buddhism was the islands' faith from the third century BCE until 1153, when the last Buddhist king, Dhovemi, adopted Islam as Sultan Muhammad al-Adil, traditionally at the preaching of the shaykh Abu al-Barakat. Ibn Battuta spent nine months here in the 1340s, serving as chief judge under Sultan Omar I, and the fleets of Zheng He called in 1411 and 1430. In 1444 a Sunni sultan ruled from Malé, the 'King's Island', and the atolls grew rich on cowrie shells, legal tender in Bengal, and salt-resistant coir fibre that rigged the dhows sailing between Arabia and China.

The Portuguese first appeared in 1507 and extorted a tribute of coir rope; in 1558 they killed Sultan Ali VI, garrisoned Malé and ruled the islands from Goa for fifteen years, trying to impose Christianity by force. In 1573 Muhammad Thakurufaanu and his two brothers drove them out and founded the Utheemu dynasty, a victory later commemorated as the Maldives' National Day. From the mid-seventeenth century the Dutch of Ceylon held an indirect hegemony and left local customs untouched, and the coral Friday Mosque in Malé was rebuilt in the 1650s. When the British seized Dutch Ceylon in 1796, the sultanate passed into the British orbit, yet its sultans went on conducting the islands' internal affairs from Malé.
zh:
马尔代夫是印度西南方、散落在印度洋上的26个珊瑚环礁群岛。佛教自公元前3世纪起就是岛上的信仰，直到1153年末代佛教国王多维米改宗伊斯兰教，称苏丹穆罕默德·阿迪勒，相传是在谢赫阿布·巴拉卡特的劝导下皈依。伊本·白图泰14世纪40年代曾在岛上居留九个月，在奥马尔一世朝担任大法官；郑和的船队也在1411年和1430年两度到访。1444年，一位逊尼派苏丹在「国王之岛」马累发号施令，环礁靠两样物产致富：在孟加拉充当法币的货贝，以及不怕海水、用来缝制往来阿拉伯与中国之间独桅帆船的椰壳纤维。

葡萄牙人1507年初次到来，强索椰索为贡；1558年，他们杀死苏丹阿里六世，在马累驻军，此后十五年从果阿统治群岛，并以死刑威逼岛民改宗基督教。1573年，穆罕默德·塔库鲁法努与两个兄弟赶走葡萄牙人，建立乌蒂姆王朝，这场胜利后来成为马尔代夫的国庆日。17世纪中叶起，锡兰的荷兰人对群岛保持间接宗主权，不干预当地风俗；马累的珊瑚石星期五清真寺也在17世纪50年代重建。1796年英国人夺取荷属锡兰，苏丹国随之转入英国势力范围，但历代苏丹仍在马累主持群岛的内部事务。

en:
Yola is the broad Benue plain below the Adamawa Plateau, but the town of Yola did not exist in 1444. Bata, Verre and other highland peoples farmed, fished, hunted and worked iron in scattered villages, while the western grasslands felt the influence of Jukun Kwararafa. Fulbe pastoralists had begun entering the plateau by the fourteenth century, asking local chiefs for pasture and water and exchanging milk, meat, butter and hides for honey, fish and grain. Most communities kept their ancestral religions and remained politically fragmented; in 1444 the upper Benue had no Muslim court comparable with Mandara or Bornu.

Fulbe clans settled more widely in the eighteenth century, usually under local protection. A dispute over cattle and a Bata prince's exactions around 1803 led Ardo Njobbo's followers to kill the prince, and the fighting reportedly cost Modibbo Adama's father his life. Usman dan Fodio began the Sokoto jihad in 1804, but Adamawa did not join until 1809, when Adama returned from Sokoto with a flag as Lamido Fombina and made Gurin his base. He united the Fulbe clans and called Bata and Verre communities to Islam; by 1810-1811 converts and refugees from Bornu had swelled his army. Later in 1810 his forces took Guidder and sacked Mandara's capital Dulo, but could not hold it. By 1821 the new Adamawa emirate was still a Gurin-centered military frontier, not a settled capital on the Benue plain.
zh:
约拉是阿达马瓦高原下方的贝努埃河宽阔平原，但1444年时还没有约拉城。巴塔人、韦雷人和其他高原民族在分散村落中农耕、渔猎和冶铁，西部草场则受到朱昆人夸拉拉法势力影响。富拉尼牧户14世纪已开始进入高原，向本地首领请求牧场和水源，用牛奶、肉类、黄油和兽皮交换蜂蜜、鱼和谷物。多数社群仍奉行祖先宗教，政治上也很分散；1444年的贝努埃河上游还没有能同曼达拉或博尔努相比的穆斯林王庭。

18世纪，富拉尼诸部在本地保护下更广泛地迁入。约1803年，阿尔多·恩乔博因牛只和一名巴塔王公的征索发生冲突，其部下杀死王公，混战中莫迪博·阿达马的父亲据说也丧命。乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥1804年发动索科托圣战，但阿达马瓦直到1809年才加入：阿达马带着旗帜从索科托返回，被任命为丰比纳的拉米多，以古林为基地。他团结富拉尼诸部，号召巴塔和韦雷社群归信伊斯兰教，到1810至1811年，新归信者和博尔努难民已扩充了他的军队。同年晚些时候，他的军队攻占吉代并洗劫曼达拉都城杜洛，却未能守住。到1821年，新的阿达马瓦埃米尔国仍是以古林为中心的军事边疆，而非贝努埃平原上的稳固都城。

en: The land called Taveta is a flat plain between the Taita hills and the eastern foot of Kilimanjaro, watered by the Lumi river off the mountain and bounded by the swamps of Lake Jipe and Lake Chala. Bantu farmers drifted into the hills from about the year 1000, and by 1444 their clans kept gardens in the clearings of the great Taveta forest, exchanged grain and goats with the Chagga on the mountain slopes above, and lived watchfully beside the pastoralists of the open plains. From the sixteenth century the people of the Lumi were known as the Taveta, divided into upper Malaboru and lower Malakaolu, speaking a Bantu tongue close to that of the Pare beyond the mountain and keeping to the old spirits of forest and spring.
zh: 塔韦塔这片地方位于泰塔丘陵与乞力马扎罗山东麓之间，是一片平坦的原野，乞力马扎罗山融水汇成的卢米河贯穿其间，边缘是吉佩湖与查拉湖的沼泽湿地。约公元1000年起，班图农民陆续迁入这片丘陵；到1444年，诸氏族已在塔韦塔大森林的林间空地上耕作，与高坡上的查加人交换谷物和山羊，对开阔平原上的牧人则时加提防。16世纪起，卢米河畔的居民被称作塔韦塔人，分为上塔韦塔的马拉博鲁与下塔韦塔的马拉卡奥卢两部，讲与山那边帕雷人相近的班图语，仍敬奉森林与泉眼的旧神。

en:
São Tomé is the largest island in its Gulf of Guinea archipelago, a mountainous volcanic land of wet forest, black soil and fast streams lying just north of the equator. In 1444 it was uninhabited; no fishing camp or African town stood on the bay that would become the city of São Tomé. Its fertility was obvious to later navigators, but the island still waited beyond the routes Portuguese caravels were opening along the African coast.

João de Santarém and Pêro Escobar reached the island on 21 December 1470. Álvaro Caminha established the first lasting settlement there in 1493, and sugarcane spread through its clearings; a water-powered mill introduced in 1515 opened the great sugar boom, and by the mid-16th century São Tomé was Africa's foremost sugar exporter, worked by enslaved Africans brought from the Niger Delta, Kongo and Angola. Fort São Sebastião was built above the harbour in 1566. On 9 July 1595 Rei Amador led the Angolares and other enslaved people in seizing the capital, although the rising was crushed in 1596. Brazilian competition had overtaken São Tomé sugar by 1600, turning the island more fully into a slave depot; the Dutch briefly took it in 1599 and again occupied the capital in 1641.
zh:
圣多美是同名几内亚湾群岛中最大的岛屿，这座多山火山岛位于赤道以北，遍布湿润森林、黑色沃土和湍急溪流。1444年时岛上无人居住；后来形成圣多美城的海湾边，还没有非洲人的渔村或城镇。它的肥沃终将被后来的航海者看见，但此时葡萄牙卡拉维尔帆船沿非洲海岸开辟的航路尚未抵达这里。

1470年12月21日，若昂·德·圣塔伦和佩罗·埃斯科巴尔抵达此岛。1493年，阿尔瓦罗·卡米尼亚建立第一个持久定居点，甘蔗随之在开垦地上扩散；1515年引入的水力磨坊开启了大规模蔗糖繁荣，到16世纪中叶，圣多美已成为非洲首屈一指的蔗糖出口地，劳力则是从尼日尔河三角洲、刚果和安哥拉掳来的非洲奴隶。1566年，圣塞巴斯蒂昂堡建在港口上方。1595年7月9日，阿马多尔王率领安哥拉尔人和其他奴隶夺取首府，但起义在1596年被镇压。到1600年，巴西的竞争已压过圣多美蔗糖，使该岛更彻底地转为奴隶贩运中转站；荷兰人1599年曾短暂夺取，1641年又占领首府。

en:
Spiš fills the basins between the High Tatras and the Slovak Ore Mountains, a northern frontier county of the Kingdom of Hungary watched over from Spiš Castle. The royal county took shape in the 12th century, and after the Mongol invasion German traders and miners joined the Slavic population. Levoča, first mentioned in 1249 and a royal town from 1317, stood on the Poland-Hungary road and exported iron, copper, furs, leather, grain and wine. In 1412 Sigismund pawned thirteen of the Spiš towns to Poland, while the remaining eleven stayed under the Hungarian county. In 1444 the Catholic borderland was thus divided between castellan and king: John Jiskra's men held Spiš Castle for young Ladislaus, and the pawned German towns paid their revenues to a Polish governor although their sovereignty remained Hungarian.

Matthias Corvinus granted Spiš Castle to the Zápolya family in 1465; John Zápolya held it against Ferdinand I until a two-week siege in 1528. The Thurzó family followed in 1531 and the Csáky family in 1638. Levoča kept its trade long enough for Master Paul to carve its great Gothic altar around 1520, but fires in 1550 and 1599 and the Reformation altered the town; a Protestant synod met beneath Spiš Castle in 1614, and a printing press opened in Levoča in 1624. The region suffered the Thököly and Rákóczi wars, including the castle's fall to Rákóczi at Christmas 1703, and the plague of 1710-1711 killed more than 20,000 people. Maria Theresa occupied the thirteen pawned towns in 1769, their recovery was confirmed by the First Partition of Poland in 1772, and the old pledge was cancelled in 1773. A separate Spiš bishopric was created in 1776, four years before fire gutted Spiš Castle in 1780.
zh:
斯皮什位于高塔特拉山与斯洛伐克矿山之间的盆地，是匈牙利王国北方边疆州，由斯皮什城堡居高控扼。王家州在12世纪成形，蒙古入侵后，德意志商人和矿工来到此地，与斯拉夫居民混居。莱沃恰最早在1249年见于记载，1317年成为王家城镇，地当波兰与匈牙利商路，输出铁、铜、毛皮、皮革、谷物和葡萄酒。1412年，西吉斯蒙德把斯皮什十三城抵押给波兰，其余十一城仍留在匈牙利州内。因此到1444年，这片天主教边疆处于分治状态：效忠年幼拉斯洛的波希米亚雇佣军把守斯皮什城堡，被抵押的德意志城镇则向波兰长官缴纳收入，不过主权仍属匈牙利。

1465年，马加什·科尔温把斯皮什城堡封给扎波尧家族；佐波尧·亚诺什后来据城抵抗斐迪南一世，直到1528年在两周围城后失守。图尔佐家族1531年接掌，恰基家族则在1638年成为城堡主人。莱沃恰的贸易繁荣延续到16世纪初，保罗大师约1520年在此雕成宏伟的哥特式祭坛；1550年和1599年的火灾以及宗教改革改变了城市面貌。1614年，新教宗教会议在斯皮什城堡下召开，1624年莱沃恰开设印刷所。此地又经历特克伊和拉科齐战争，城堡在1703年圣诞节被拉科齐军队攻占；1710年至1711年的瘟疫造成两万多人死亡。玛丽亚·特蕾西亚1769年出兵占领十三座抵押城镇，1772年第一次瓜分波兰确认收回，1773年旧抵押正式取消。1776年斯皮什设立独立教区，四年后的1780年，大火焚毁了斯皮什城堡。

en:
Upper Guelders, in Dutch Opper-Gelre or the Overkwartier van Gelre, was the southernmost of the four quarters of the Duchy of Guelders. Its chief town, Roermond, stood where the Roer enters the Maas, received town rights in 1231 and became the quarter's capital around 1350. The town was a commercial centre with its own mint and court, joined the Hanseatic League in 1441, and was counted among the four principal cities of Guelders. In 1444 the Catholic territory was ruled by Arnold of Egmond, who had held the duchy since 1423 and kept court amid the towns, monasteries and river toll stations of the Upper Quarter.

Arnold's later quarrel with his son Adolf drew in Burgundy: Charles the Bold seized Guelders after Arnold's death in 1473, and the inheritance passed through Mary of Burgundy to the Habsburgs. Charles of Egmond recovered the duchy with French support in 1492, but when his line failed, William of Cleves surrendered Guelders to Charles V in 1543. During the Dutch Revolt the three northern quarters joined the Union of Utrecht in 1579 while Upper Guelders remained Catholic and Spanish. Near Roermond the Battle of Rheindalen on 23 April 1568 opened the Eighty Years' War; in 1572 thirteen Catholic clerics were killed there before Spanish troops retook the town. Frederick Henry captured Roermond in 1632, but Spanish rule returned in 1637 and was confirmed by the Peace of Münster in 1648. The Treaty of Utrecht divided Upper Guelders among Prussia, the Dutch Republic, Jülich and Austria in 1713. Roermond passed to the Austrian Habsburgs in 1716, joined the United Belgian States in 1790, was occupied by French forces in 1794 and annexed to France in 1795, and passed to the Kingdom of the Netherlands after the 1815 settlement.
zh:
上海尔雷，荷兰语称 Opper-Gelre 或 Overkwartier van Gelre，是海尔雷公国四个分区中最南的一个。首府鲁尔蒙德位于鲁尔河注入马斯河之处，1231年获得城市权，约1350年成为这一分区的行政中心。它拥有铸币厂和法庭，是商业要地，1441年加入汉萨同盟，也被视为海尔雷四座主要城市之一。1444年，这片天主教土地由阿诺尔德·范·埃赫蒙德统治；他自1423年起领有公国，在上海尔雷的城镇、修道院和河流税关之间维持着宫廷权威。

阿诺尔德后来与儿子阿道夫相争，勃艮第势力趁机介入：大胆的查理在阿诺尔德于1473年去世后夺取海尔雷，这份遗产又经勃艮第的玛丽转入哈布斯堡家族。埃赫蒙德的查理在法国支持下于1492年恢复公国统治，但他的血脉断绝后，克莱沃的威廉于1543年把海尔雷让给查理五世。尼德兰起义期间，北方三个分区在1579年加入乌得勒支同盟，上海尔雷则留在天主教的西班牙一方。1568年4月23日，莱茵达伦战役在鲁尔蒙德附近打响，拉开八十年战争序幕；1572年，十三名天主教神职人员在城中被杀，随后西班牙军队夺回鲁尔蒙德。腓特烈·亨德里克1632年攻占该城，但1637年西班牙恢复统治，并在1648年《明斯特和约》中得到确认。1713年《乌得勒支条约》把上海尔雷分给普鲁士、尼德兰共和国、于利希和奥地利。鲁尔蒙德1716年划归奥地利哈布斯堡家族，1790年加入比利时合众国，1794年被法军占领并于1795年并入法国，1815年的安排后转入尼德兰王国。

en:
Cambrai, the Roman Camaracum on the Scheldt, replaced Bavay as the capital of the Nervii and became under the Merovingians the seat of a bishopric whose diocese once reached to Brussels and Antwerp. In 948 Otto I granted the bishop temporal power in the city, and in 1007 Henry II extended it over the whole Cambrésis, making it a prince-bishopric of the Empire; the burghers, who rose against their bishop as early as 958, wrung a large measure of self-rule from him. The rich fields of the Cambrésis yielded grain and wool, and after the old drapery declined its weavers made batiste, the fine linen that carried Cambrai's name across Europe. In 1385 the splendid double wedding of Burgundy and Wittelsbach was celebrated there, and by the fifteenth century the bishopric lay under Burgundian protection. In 1444 the composer Guillaume Du Fay was serving Philip the Good at Cambrai, and the walled, Catholic, Walloon-speaking prince-bishopric lived by its grain and linen as a wealthy buffer between France and the Burgundian Low Countries.

France seized it during the Burgundian succession crisis of 1477, but it returned to the Empire's orbit, and in 1508 Pope Julius II's League of Cambrai against Venice was concluded there; in 1529 Margaret of Austria and Louise of Savoy negotiated there the Ladies' Peace between Charles V and Francis I. In 1543 Charles V placed an imperial garrison in Cambrai, and in 1595, during the French Wars of Religion, the Spanish took it. Mazarin's siege failed in 1649, and Turenne, who captured the city in 1657, had to abandon it when Condé marched to its relief. Louis XIV came in person for the siege of 1677: the town opened its gates on 5 April and the citadel fell on the 17th, and the Peace of Nijmegen in 1678 gave Cambrai to France. The first royal-nominated archbishop was Fénelon, the 'Swan of Cambrai', who wrote his Maximes des Saints there after 1695. Batiste weaving peaked in the seventeenth century, with 58,000 pieces stamped at Cambrai in 1775. Napoleon's Saint-Quentin Canal, driven through to the Scheldt by the Riqueval tunnel, was opened with ceremony in 1810; the old cathedral, the 'wonder of the Low Countries', did not survive the Revolution, being sold for stone and collapsing in 1809.
zh:
康布雷在罗马时代称卡马拉库姆，位于埃斯科河畔，取代巴韦成为内尔维人的中心；墨洛温时代起成为主教驻地，教区一度延伸至布鲁塞尔和安特卫普。948年奥托一世把城市的世俗权力授予主教，1007年亨利二世又将其扩展到整个康布雷西，这里由此成为帝国的采邑主教区。市民早在958年就起兵反抗主教，后来逐步争得相当程度的自治。康布雷西良田广产谷物与羊毛；旧毛织业衰落后，织工改织上等细麻布batiste，这种以康布雷之名行销欧洲的织物便是英语中cambric一词的由来。1385年，勃艮第与维特尔斯巴赫两家在此举行盛大的双重婚礼；到15世纪，主教区已处于勃艮第保护之下。1444年，作曲家纪尧姆·迪费正在康布雷为勃艮第公爵好人腓力效力；这座设防的天主教城市讲瓦隆语，靠谷物与麻布致富，夹在法兰西与勃艮第治下尼德兰之间。

1477年勃艮第继承危机中法国一度夺取城市，但它后来重回帝国势力范围。1508年，教皇尤利乌斯二世针对威尼斯缔结的康布雷同盟在此成形；1529年，奥地利的玛格丽特与萨伏依的路易丝又在此谈成查理五世与弗朗索瓦一世之间的「夫人和约」。1543年查理五世在康布雷驻扎帝国守军，1595年法国宗教战争末期西班牙人占领此城。1649年马扎然的围城以失败告终；1657年蒂雷纳一度破城，却因孔代率兵来援而弃守。1677年路易十四亲临围城：城市4月5日开城，城塞17日陷落，1678年的《奈梅亨和约》把康布雷正式划归法国。首位由国王任命的大主教是费奈隆——人称「康布雷之天鹅」，1695年后在此写成《圣徒箴言录》。细麻布织造在17世纪达到鼎盛，1775年仍有五万八千匹在康布雷验印。拿破仑的圣康坦运河经里克尔瓦隧道通到埃斯科河，1810年举行了盛大的通航典礼；而有「尼德兰奇观」之称的老主教座堂未逃过革命浩劫，被当作石料出售，残塔于1809年倾塌。

en:
Antwerp grew up beside the Scheldt, where a wharf and castle served a frontier margraviate of the Holy Roman Empire. Around 1400 it was already one of the four chief cities of Brabant, with some 18,000 inhabitants, and English cloth sold at its fairs drew merchants from across Germany while its river harbour challenged Bruges. After Philip the Good inherited Brabant in 1430, the city formed the northern maritime edge of his Burgundian Netherlands. In 1444 it was a Catholic Flemish port whose future was being shaped by the silting of the Zwin and the slow shift of trade away from Bruges.

Foreign merchant houses moved to Antwerp at the end of the 15th century, and from 1495 to 1565 the city was the commercial and financial capital of European trade, handling English cloth, German metals and Portuguese spices. Its exchange opened in 1531, fifteen sugar refineries were at work by 1550, and Christoffel Plantijn founded his printing house in 1555. The Revolt of the Netherlands then shattered the boom: iconoclastic riots began in August 1566, and on 4 November 1576 mutinous Spanish troops killed about 8,000 citizens in the Spanish Fury. Antwerp became the centre of the anti-Spanish revolt until Alessandro Farnese took it in 1585 after a siege of more than a year; roughly half the population left, the United Provinces closed the Scheldt in 1587, and the Peace of Münster confirmed the closure in 1648. Rubens, Jordaens and Teniers nevertheless made the Catholic city a centre of Baroque painting. French revolutionary troops entered in 1792 and reopened the river; Napoleon developed Antwerp as a naval arsenal and built the Bonaparte dock. After 1815 the city passed to the United Kingdom of the Netherlands, its harbour trade reviving by 1821.
zh:
安特卫普兴起于斯海尔德河畔，码头与城堡拱卫着神圣罗马帝国的边境藩侯地。1400年前后，它已是布拉班特四大城之一，约有18000名居民；集市上交易的英格兰呢绒吸引德意志各地商人，河港也开始挑战布鲁日。1430年「好人」腓力三世继承布拉班特后，这座城市成为勃艮第尼德兰北部的海上门户。1444年，它是一座天主教佛兰德港口，兹温湾淤塞和贸易重心逐渐离开布鲁日，正在塑造它的未来。

15世纪末，外国商馆陆续迁至安特卫普；1495—1565年，这里是欧洲世界贸易与公共金融中心，经营英格兰呢绒、德意志金属和葡萄牙香料。交易所于1531年开张，1550年已有十五家炼糖厂，克里斯托费尔·普朗坦则在1555年创办印刷厂。尼德兰起义随即打断繁荣：1566年8月圣像破坏运动由此蔓延，1576年11月4日哗变的西班牙军队制造「西班牙狂暴」，约8000名市民遇害。安特卫普成为反西班牙起义中心，直到亚历山德罗·法尔内塞经一年多围城，在1585年将其攻下；约半数居民离去，荷兰共和国1587年封锁斯海尔德河，1648年明斯特和约又确认封锁。即便如此，鲁本斯、约尔丹斯和特尼尔斯仍使这座天主教城市成为巴洛克绘画中心。法国革命军1792年入城并重新开放河道，拿破仑把安特卫普建成军港，还修建波拿巴船坞。1815年后，城市并入尼德兰联合王国，到1821年港口贸易已在复苏。

en:
Cantabria is the wet mountain coast between the Cantabrian Sea and the Cantabrian Mountains, where forested valleys descend to sheltered harbours. Between 1163 and 1210 Castile chartered Castro Urdiales, Santander, Laredo and San Vicente de la Barquera; their ships carried wool, iron, salt, fish and timber to England and Flanders, served Ferdinand III at Seville in 1248 and joined the Brotherhood of the Marshes in 1296. Inland, councils, monasteries and noble lineages divided the valleys. In 1444 the Four Towns were Castilian royal ports valued for shipyards and naval stores, while aristocratic and church lordships dominated the interior.

The Catholic Monarchs curbed the mountain feuds and around 1496 brought the ports into the Corregimiento of the Four Towns. Santander defeated Henry IV's attempt to grant it to the Marquis of Santillana in 1466–67, though plague later checked its growth. Bourbon recovery began after the Burgos-to-Santander wool road was ordered in 1748. Santander became a diocesan capital in 1754 and a city in 1755. On 28 July 1778 delegates at Puente San Miguel formed the Province of Cantabria; the Sea and Land Consulate was created in 1783, and Santander joined the unstable provincial project in 1796.
zh:
坎塔布里亚位于坎塔布连海与坎塔布连山脉之间，湿润的森林河谷通向避风港湾。1163年至1210年间，卡斯蒂利亚先后特许卡斯特罗-乌尔迪亚莱斯、桑坦德、拉雷多和圣维森特-德拉巴尔克拉；这些港口把羊毛、铁、盐、渔获和木材运往英格兰与佛兰德，1248年派船支援费尔南多三世攻打塞维利亚，又在1296年加入沼泽兄弟会。内陆的河谷议事会、修道院和贵族家族各据一方。1444年的四港是卡斯蒂利亚王室港口，以船坞和船用物资见重，内陆则主要由贵族和教会领主支配。

天主教双王压制了山地家族间的私战，约1496年把各港口纳入四港镇辖区。桑坦德在1466—1467年挫败了恩里克四世把它封给桑蒂利亚纳侯爵的企图，但后来的瘟疫延缓了城市复苏。1748年，王室下令修建从布尔戈斯通往桑坦德的羊毛道路，波旁时期的复兴由此开始。桑坦德1754年成为教区首邑，1755年取得城市地位。1778年7月28日，各地代表在蓬特圣米格尔组建坎塔布里亚省；1783年海陆领事馆设立，桑坦德则在1796年加入这个并不稳固的省级建制。

en:
Burgos began in 884 as a fortified settlement above the Arlanzón, planted by Diego Rodríguez Porcelos on the Leonese frontier. Fernán González united the Castilian counties around it in 931, and after Ferdinand I became king in 1038 the city served as capital of Castile until Toledo was taken in 1085. Pilgrims on the French Way and merchants driving wool toward Cantabrian ports made it northern Castile's chief market, with foreign traders and a strong urban oligarchy; in 1345 Alfonso XI imposed direct royal rule through a council of sixteen regidores. In 1444 Burgos remained a bishopric, an occasional royal seat and a cloth-and-wool exchange linking the meseta with Laredo and the Bay of Biscay.

In 1494 Isabella I created the Consulate of the Sea at Burgos, whose merchants channelled merino wool to Laredo and Bilbao for Flanders and controlled the return trade in Flemish textiles. The city's comuneros rose against Constable Íñigo Fernández de Velasco on 21 January 1521, but his troops crushed the rising the next day, three months before the main Comunero army was defeated at Villalar. In 1574 Pope Gregory XIII raised Burgos to an archbishopric. The city declined in the following century as southern trade and royal power moved elsewhere. In 1812 Wellington's unsuccessful siege of the French-held castle marked a sharp check to the allied campaign; French forces blew the castle up in 1813, after wartime requisitions had scattered merino flocks and crippled much of the local wool industry.
zh:
布尔戈斯始于884年，是迭戈·罗德里格斯·波尔塞洛斯奉莱昂边疆之命在阿尔兰松河畔高地上设立的要塞。931年，费尔南·冈萨雷斯把各卡斯蒂利亚伯国统一在它周围；1038年费尔南多一世即位后，这里成为卡斯蒂利亚都城，直到1085年托莱多被攻占。圣雅各法兰西之路的朝圣者和把羊毛赶往坎塔布连港口的商人，使布尔戈斯成为卡斯蒂利亚北部首要市场，城中外国商人和寡头势力强大。1345年，阿方索十一世改由十六名市政议员组成的王室政府直接治理。1444年的布尔戈斯仍是主教驻地、国王偶尔临幸的城市，也是连接梅塞塔高原与拉雷多和比斯开湾的羊毛、布料交易中心。

1494年，伊莎贝拉一世在布尔戈斯设立海事领事公会；商人通过这里把美利奴羊毛经拉雷多和毕尔巴鄂运往佛兰德，并垄断回程的佛兰德纺织品贸易。1521年1月21日，城中的公社派起兵反对卡斯蒂利亚事务大臣伊尼戈·费尔南德斯·德·贝拉斯科，次日即被其军队镇压，三个月后公社派主力在比利亚拉尔战败。1574年，教宗格列高利十三世将布尔戈斯升格为总主教区。此后一个世纪，随着南方贸易和王权中心转移，城市逐渐衰落。1812年，威灵顿未能攻下法军据守的布尔戈斯城堡，联军攻势受到重挫；战时征发打散了美利奴羊群并严重摧垮本地毛纺业，法军又在1813年炸毁城堡。

en:
Caceres began as a Roman camp beside the Silver Road, and in 1147 the Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min refounded it as a fortress on the frontier of al-Andalus. It passed between the Portuguese, Leon and the Almohads until Alfonso IX of Leon took it on 23 April 1229. Its charter made it a royal town with no lord but its own council, the Crown reserving the surrounding pasture between the Orders of Santiago and Alcantara; government fell to a body of agricultural knights rather than a high nobility. In 1444 Caceres was a compact walled town of flocks and wool on the Silver Road, its skyline of Muslim towers and its noble houses locked in family feuds.

In 1477, during the Castilian succession war, Isabella the Catholic curbed those feuds with an ordinance making the twelve town councillors perpetual. Its Jewish quarter, with two synagogues, was dissolved in the expulsion of 1492. In the sixteenth century local men followed the Extremaduran tide to America, and returning fortunes raised the palaces of the Golfines and other lineages that crowded the lanes of the old quarter. In 1790 Charles IV seated the Royal Court of Extremadura in the town, bringing officials and bourgeoisie; French authorities briefly planned a prefecture there in 1810.
zh:
卡塞雷斯最初是银之路古道旁的一处罗马军营，1147年穆瓦希德王朝哈里发阿卜杜勒·慕敏将其重建，作为安达卢斯边境上的要塞。此后它在葡萄牙人、莱昂与穆瓦希德人之间几度易手，1229年4月23日被阿方索九世攻取。城市特许状把它定为王室直辖镇，除市镇会议外不受任何领主管辖，王室把周围牧场划在圣地亚哥骑士团与阿尔坎塔拉骑士团的地产之间；治理权因此落在一批务农骑士手中，没有形成强大的贵族阶层。1444年的卡塞雷斯是银之路上一座以羊群和羊毛为生的紧凑城寨，穆斯林时代的塔楼勾勒出天际线，各家族宅第深陷世仇。

1477年卡斯蒂利亚王位继承战争期间，天主教君主伊莎贝尔一世颁布敕令，把市镇会议的十二名委员定为终身职，以此遏制这些家族仇杀。城中原有两座犹太会堂的犹太区在1492年驱逐令后解散。16世纪，本地人随埃斯特雷马杜拉人的大潮前往美洲，带回的财富建起戈尔芬家族等门第的宫殿，密密挤满老城区的街巷。1790年，卡洛斯四世把埃斯特雷马杜拉王室法院设在此城，官员和资产者随之而来；1810年法国当局一度筹划在此设立省府。

en:
Jaén climbs the slopes of the Cerro de Santa Catalina above the Guadalbullón plain. Under Muslim rule it was Jayyān, chief town of a large kūra, but Ferdinand III's campaigns of 1225 and 1230 failed before its walls. Muhammad I of Granada finally surrendered the city on 28 February 1246, and it became the head of Castile's Kingdom of Jaén, a frontier land shared between the crown, bishopric, nobility and military orders. In 1444 it was still a guarded gateway facing the Nasrid kingdom, its castle overlooking grain fields, olive groves and hill pastures, while Baeza and Úbeda rivalled its regional influence.

Castilian forces took Huesa in 1455 and Cambil in 1485, closing the mountain frontier before Granada fell in 1492; a tribunal of the Spanish Inquisition had already been established at Jaén in 1483. During the 16th century the old Gothic cathedral was replaced by a Renaissance building whose chapter house and sacristy became masterpieces by Andrés de Vandelvira; its Baroque façade began in 1660 and chapel works continued to 1724. The Andalusian Morisco expulsion decree followed on 10 January 1610, and the 1755 Lisbon earthquake forced repairs to the cathedral. On 19 July 1808, near Bailén in the northern province, Castaños and Reding trapped Pierre Dupont's French army and forced its surrender, the first open-field defeat of a Napoleonic army.
zh:
哈恩沿圣卡塔利娜山坡而起，俯瞰瓜达尔武利翁平原。穆斯林统治时期，这里称贾扬，是大片库拉的首邑；费尔南多三世1225年和1230年两度攻城均未得手。1246年2月28日，格拉纳达的穆罕默德一世最终交出城市，哈恩成为卡斯蒂利亚哈恩王国的首邑，这片边疆土地由王室、主教区、贵族和骑士团分掌。1444年时，它仍是面向纳斯里德王国的戒备门户，城堡俯视着粮田、橄榄园和山地牧场；在区域影响力上，巴埃萨和乌韦达仍与它不相上下。

卡斯蒂利亚军队1455年夺取韦萨，1485年拿下坎比尔，在格拉纳达1492年陷落前逐步封闭山地边界；早在1483年，西班牙宗教裁判所已在哈恩设立法庭。16世纪，旧哥特教堂被文艺复兴式主教座堂取代，其教士会礼堂和圣器室成为安德烈斯·德·范德尔维拉的杰作；巴洛克立面1660年动工，各礼拜堂工程持续到1724年。1610年1月10日，安达卢西亚摩里斯科人驱逐令颁布，1755年里斯本大地震又迫使主教座堂进行修缮。1808年7月19日，在省境北部的拜伦附近，卡斯塔尼奥斯与雷丁包围并迫使皮埃尔·杜邦的法军投降，这是拿破仑军队第一次在野战中失败。

en:
Cádiz stands on a narrow island spit guarding a wide Atlantic bay and is the oldest city in western Europe: the Phoenician Gadir, a post for the silver and tin trades, served Hamilcar Barca and then Rome as Gades, whose rich merchants were said to rival those of Rome itself. It shrank under the Visigoths and under Islam, when it was called Qādis, until Alfonso X of Castile took it in 1262 and incorporated it into his crown in 1264, raising its walls and bishopric, building royal shipyards in the bay and granting the town the monopoly of trade with Africa. In 1444 Cádiz was a small fortified Castilian port under Juan II, living by its dockyards, its Genoese merchants and the African traffic, while greater Seville overshadowed it up the Guadalquivir.

The oceanic age made its fortune: Columbus sailed from the bay on his second voyage in 1493 and his fourth in 1502, and Cádiz became the home port of the treasure fleet, which also drew its enemies. In April 1587 Francis Drake burned dozens of ships in the harbour and delayed the Armada by a year, and in the summer of 1596 an Anglo-Dutch fleet under Essex and Nottingham sacked the town and set it ablaze; the English assaults of 1625 and 1702 were beaten off. As the Guadalquivir silted up, Philip V transferred the Casa de Contratación from Seville to Cádiz by decree of 12 May 1717, opening a second golden age that brought some seventy thousand inhabitants and French and Irish merchant houses; the free-trade decree of 12 October 1778 ended the monopoly. Besieged by the French from 5 February 1810 to 24 August 1812, Cádiz became Spain's wartime capital, where the Cortes proclaimed the liberal Constitution of 1812.
zh:
加的斯坐落在一座狭长的岛屿岬角上，扼守着开阔的大西洋海湾，是西欧最古老的城市：腓尼基人建立的加的尔（Gadir）本是白银与锡矿贸易的商站，曾为哈米尔卡·巴卡所用，罗马时代称加德斯，据说城中富商的富庶可与罗马本土比肩。哥特人和穆斯林统治时期城市衰落，时名卡迪斯；1262年卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索十世将其攻取，1264年正式并入王冠，随后修筑城墙、设立主教区，在海湾建起王家船坞，并授予此城对非洲贸易的垄断权。1444年，加的斯是胡安二世治下一座设防的卡斯蒂利亚小港，靠船坞、热那亚商人和对非洲贸易为生，上游更宏大的塞维利亚令它相形见绌。

大航海时代成就了它的繁荣：哥伦布1493年第二次、1502年第四次远航都从这座海湾出发，加的斯也成为珍宝船队的母港，而财富也招来了敌人。1587年4月，弗朗西斯·德雷克在港内焚毁数十艘船只，使无敌舰队的出航推迟一年；1596年夏，埃塞克斯和诺丁汉率领的英荷联军洗劫城市并纵火，1625年和1702年的英军进攻则都被击退。随着瓜达尔基维尔河淤积日甚，费利佩五世于1717年5月12日颁布法令，把西印度贸易署从塞维利亚迁至加的斯，开启了第二个黄金时代，居民增至约七万人，法国和爱尔兰商馆林立；1778年10月12日的自由贸易法令终结了它的垄断地位。1810年2月5日至1812年8月24日法军围城期间，加的斯成为西班牙的战时首都，议会在此颁布了自由主义的1812年宪法。

en:
Alicante lies beneath the rock of Benacantil and its Santa Bárbara castle, on the best harbour of the southern Valencian coast. The Muslim medina of Laqant was taken for Alfonso X of Castile in 1248, but James II of Aragon seized it in 1296, and from 1305 it belonged to the Kingdom of Valencia with a vote in its Corts. War and plague cut it low in the 14th century - Castile held it during the War of the Two Peters, and a Granadan raid struck in 1386 - but the 15th century brought steady growth: the harbour shipped the wine, dried fruit and esparto grass of the surrounding huerta, and a merchant middle class came to run it. In 1444 Alicante was a royal town of the Crown of Aragon, Catalan-speaking, with its hinterland still largely worked by a Mudéjar peasantry.

Ferdinand the Catholic raised it to the rank of city in 1490. It held aloof from the Germanías revolt of 1519-1522, and Charles V marked its loyalty in 1524 by setting the Golden Fleece into its arms. After the Morisco expulsion decree of September 1609, 30,204 people were embarked at Alicante for Oran between that month and January 1610, emptying whole inland valleys. By then the port dominated the trade of the south, overtaking Orihuela in 1647; in 1691 a French fleet under d'Estrées bombarded the town and left it near ruin. In the War of the Spanish Succession an allied garrison held it for the Habsburg claimant from 1706 until d'Asfeld's Bourbon siege of November 1708 to April 1709: a mine fired under the Santa Bárbara castle on 3 March 1709 killed its British commander, and the last defenders sailed out on 20 April. Trade recovered with a Genoese colony on Nueva Tabarca in 1770 and an independent Consulate of the Sea in 1785. In the Peninsular War the French never managed to occupy the port.
zh:
阿利坎特背靠贝纳坎蒂尔山岩和山上的圣巴巴拉城堡，扼守巴伦西亚南部海岸最好的港湾。穆斯林的拉坎特城于1248年为卡斯蒂利亚的阿方索十世攻取，1296年阿拉贡的海梅二世将其夺取，1305年起正式归入巴伦西亚王国，并在王国议会中保有席位。14世纪的战争与瘟疫使它几度衰落——两佩德罗战争期间卡斯蒂利亚曾占领此城，1386年又遭格拉纳达军队袭掠——但15世纪这里稳步发展：港口外运周边灌溉田园出产的葡萄酒、干果和细茎针茅，商人中产阶级逐渐执掌市政。1444年的阿利坎特是阿拉贡王冠治下的皇家城镇，通行加泰罗尼亚语，腹地仍主要由穆德哈尔农民耕作。

天主教徒费尔南多1490年把它升格为城市。它置身于1519至1522年的兄弟会起义之外，1524年卡洛斯一世论功行赏，把金羊毛纹徽添入市徽。1609年9月摩里斯科人驱逐令颁布后，至1610年1月共有30204人在阿利坎特登船被送往奥兰，内地整片山谷为之一空。此时的港口已主导南方贸易，1647年从奥里韦拉手中夺走南部辖区首府之位；1691年，德斯特雷率领的法国舰队炮轰全城，城市近乎毁灭。西班牙王位继承战争中，盟军卫戍部队自1706年起为哈布斯堡觊觎者守港，直到1708年11月至1709年4月波旁军队围城：1709年3月3日达斯费尔德下令引爆圣巴巴拉城堡下的地道，炸死英军司令，最后的守军于4月20日乘船撤离。此后贸易在18世纪复苏，1770年在近海建立热那亚人定居点新塔瓦尔卡，1785年设立独立的海上领事会。半岛战争期间，法军虽屡屡威胁，却始终未能占领此港。

en:
Ceuta sits on a narrow isthmus at the Strait of Gibraltar, the southern of the ancient Pillars of Hercules. Phoenicians settled the sheltered peninsula as Septem Fratres, and through Roman, Byzantine and Muslim rule the port was fought over by every power contending for the strait; the Marinids of Fez made themselves its masters in 1387. On 21 August 1415 King John I of Portugal, his sons including the young Henry the Navigator, stormed the town with 45,000 men, Portugal's first overseas conquest. The first governor, Pedro de Meneses, beat off a Marinid siege in 1419. In 1444 Ceuta was a Portuguese fortress-town supplied across the water from Andalusia, its garrison a heavy expense now that the Saharan caravans carried their gold to Tangier instead.

An attempt to take Tangier in 1437 ended in disaster and nearly bargained Ceuta away. The Portuguese crown kept its prize, recognised by Castile in the Treaty of Alcáçovas of 1479, and raised the bastioned Royal Walls from the 1540s; the poet Luís de Camões served here in 1549–1551 and lost an eye skirmishing in the hinterland. In 1580 Ceuta passed with Portugal to Philip II, and when Portugal restored its independence in 1640 the city alone stayed loyal to Madrid, which received it formally in the Treaty of Lisbon of 1 January 1668. From 23 October 1694 to 22 April 1727 the armies of Sultan Moulay Ismail maintained a thirty-three-year siege, the longest on record, without taking the Royal Walls. A Moroccan attempt of 1790–1791 also failed, and British troops garrisoned Ceuta from 1810 to 1815 during the Napoleonic wars.
zh:
休达地处直布罗陀海峡边的狭窄地峡，是古代赫拉克勒斯双柱中的南柱。腓尼基人在易守难攻的半岛上建立定居点七兄弟堡，历经罗马、拜占庭和穆斯林统治，这座港口始终是争夺海峡的各方势力交锋之地；1387年，非斯的马林王朝成为这里的主人。1415年8月21日，葡萄牙国王若昂一世偕诸子（包括年轻的航海家恩里克）率四万五千人攻克此城，这是葡萄牙的第一次海外征服。首任总督佩德罗·德·梅内塞斯在1419年击退了马林人的围攻。1444年的休达是一座葡萄牙要塞城镇，靠安达卢西亚跨海接济；撒哈拉商队改道丹吉尔转运黄金，驻军成了沉重的开支。

1437年攻取丹吉尔之役惨败，休达险些被作为交换退还。葡萄牙王室保住了这份产业，1479年的《阿尔卡索瓦什条约》获卡斯蒂利亚承认，1540年代起筑起棱堡环绕的皇家城墙；诗人路易斯·德·卡蒙斯1549至1551年在此戍守，在内地的小规模战斗中失去右眼。1580年休达随葡萄牙并入腓力二世的版图，1640年葡萄牙复国时，唯独此城继续效忠马德里，1668年1月1日的《里斯本条约》正式把它划归西班牙。1694年10月23日至1727年4月22日，穆莱·伊斯梅尔苏丹的军队围城三十三年，是有记载以来最长的围城，却始终未能攻破皇家城墙。1790至1791年摩洛哥的再次围攻同样失败；拿破仑战争期间，英军于1810至1815年进驻休达。

en:
Rzhev is the highest town on the Volga, and its wharves guarded the river's first crossing on the road from Moscow to the west. Local tradition claims a mention as early as 1019, and the chronicles first clearly note it in 1216, when Mstislav Udatny of Toropets relieved a siege there. Princes of the Smolensk line made it their appanage and split the town into the Prince-Dmitry and Prince-Feodor sides, names the two banks still bore after Rzhev became a Muscovite border stronghold. Algirdas of Lithuania took it in 1356 and again in 1359, and it changed hands repeatedly in the wars of Moscow, Tver, Novgorod and Lithuania; Vasily I rebuilt its fortifications and in 1408–1410 granted it in feeding to the Lithuanian exile prince Švitrigaila. In 1444 Rzhev, lately held by Dmitry Shemyaka during the Muscovite civil war, was still counted among Moscow's western appanage towns, a Volga fortress more accustomed to sieges than to peace.

Hard pressed by Shemyaka, Vasily II promised Rzhev to Boris of Tver, whose troops took it after a long siege in 1446 when the townspeople rose against him; Lithuania seized the town in 1448 and returned it under the peace treaty of 1449. On Boris's death Rzhev was divided between his sons, and only in 1521 did it pass for good to Moscow. During the Time of Troubles the townsmen backed the first False Dmitry and withstood a Polish siege under the boyar Fyodor Sheremetev, at heavy cost. Old Believer merchants then made its fortune: by the mid-18th century twenty-five works wove sailcloth and cables for the Baltic fleet, a hundred barges sailed each summer and up to seven thousand wagon trains left each winter, while two annual fairs filled the stone gostiny dvor of a hundred and five shops. In 1775 Rzhev became an uyezd seat of the new Tver Viceroyalty, its merchantry still overwhelmingly Old Believer.
zh:
勒热夫是伏尔加河上位置最高的城镇，它的码头扼守着伏尔加河上游通往西方大道的第一处渡口。当地传说称城市早在1019年便见诸文书，编年史首次明确记载是在1216年，当时托罗佩茨王公姆斯季斯拉夫·乌达特尼曾来解围。斯摩棱斯克系的王公将其作为封邑，并把城镇分给德米特里王公与费奥多尔王公两支，两岸长期保留着这两个名字，勒热夫也由此成为莫斯科的边防要塞。立陶宛大公阿尔吉尔达斯1356年、1359年两度攻占此城，在莫斯科、特维尔、诺夫哥罗德与立陶宛的争战中，勒热夫几经易手；瓦西里一世重修城防，1408至1410年又把它封给投奔莫斯科的立陶宛王公斯维特里盖拉「供养」。1444年的勒热夫在莫斯科内战中刚被德米特里·舍米亚卡占据，名义上仍是莫斯科的西方封邑之一，这座伏尔加河畔的要塞惯于围城，鲜享太平。

瓦西里二世被舍米亚卡所迫，把勒热夫许给特维尔王公鲍里斯；1446年市民起而反抗，特维尔军队经长期围攻才拿下该城。1448年立陶宛夺取勒热夫，1449年又依立特和约归还特维尔。鲍里斯死后，勒热夫被其二子瓜分，直到1521年才永久归入莫斯科。动荡时期，市民曾支持第一个伪德米特里，并在贵族费奥多尔·舍列梅捷夫率领下抗击波兰人的围攻，损失惨重。此后旧礼仪派商人造就了城市的繁荣：到18世纪中叶，城中有二十五家工场，为波罗的海舰队织造帆布和缆绳，夏季有上百艘驳船起航，冬季出发的车队多达七千挂，每年两场集市挤满了有一百零五间石铺的客商市场。1775年，勒热夫成为新设特维尔总督区的县城，城中商贾仍以旧礼仪派为主。

en:
Kostroma stands at the confluence of the Volga and the Kostroma river, officially founded in 1152 by Yury Dolgoruky, prince of Rostov-Suzdal. The Mongols sacked it in 1238, and it became the seat of its own small principality; Vasily Yaroslavich, a younger brother of Alexander Nevsky, ruled all Vladimir-Suzdal from Kostroma as grand prince of Vladimir after 1272 and died there in 1276. The town passed to Moscow in 1364, and as one of the northernmost strongholds of the grand principality it sheltered the court when Tokhtamysh burned Moscow in 1382, and again in 1408 and 1433. Novgorod river pirates, the ushkuiniks, plundered it in 1375, and in 1419 the wooden town was moved to higher ground, where a kremlin and its first stone church, the Dormition cathedral, were raised. In 1444 Kostroma was a fortified northern town of Vasily II's Muscovy, a refuge for the court and a staging point on the Volga route.

About 1468 Afanasy Nikitin stopped here on his journey to India. In the 16th century Kostroma grew rich on Volga trade and on English and Dutch merchants sailing in from Arkhangelsk, and Boris Godunov had the Ipatiev and Epiphany monasteries rebuilt in stone. The Time of Troubles struck hard: the Polish raider Lisowski's bands sacked the town twice, and in 1613 the national embassy reached the Ipatiev monastery to offer the crown to young Mikhail Romanov, making Kostroma the cradle of the Romanov dynasty; the peasant Ivan Susanin, who led a Polish detachment astray in the nearby snows, gave the town its martyr. By mid-century it was the third craft town of Russia after Moscow and Yaroslavl, famed for linen, leather and icons, with an English trading factory. Peter I made it a provincial town of Moscow Governorate in 1708, Catherine II granted it a coat of arms in 1767, and after the great fire of 1773 Kostroma was rebuilt on its radiating street plan.
zh:
科斯特罗马位于伏尔加河与科斯特罗马河汇流处，官方认定1152年由罗斯托夫-苏兹达尔王公尤里·多尔戈鲁基建立。1238年蒙古人洗劫了该城，此后它成为一个小封邑公国的中心；亚历山大·涅夫斯基之弟瓦西里·雅罗斯拉维奇1272年成为弗拉基米尔大公后仍留驻本城，在科斯特罗马号令东北罗斯，直到1276年去世。1364年城市并入莫斯科公国，作为大公国最北的重镇之一，1382年脱脱迷失焚毁莫斯科时，以及1408年、1433年，宫廷都曾到此避难。1375年诺夫哥罗德水盗乌什库伊尼基劫掠该城；1419年木城迁往一处高地，建起克里姆林和城内第一座石砌教堂圣母升天大教堂。1444年的科斯特罗马是瓦西里二世治下莫斯科北方的设防城镇，既是宫廷避难所，也是伏尔加河水路上的据点。

约1468年，阿法纳西·尼基京远行印度途中曾在此停留。16世纪，科斯特罗马靠伏尔加河贸易，以及与从阿尔汉格尔斯克驶来的英荷商人通商而兴盛，鲍里斯·戈东诺夫下令把伊帕季耶夫修道院和主显修道院改建为石构。混乱时代中该城两度遭波兰强人利索夫斯基的队伍洗劫；1613年，全国使团抵达伊帕季耶夫修道院，将皇位奉给年轻的米哈伊尔·罗曼诺夫，科斯特罗马由此成为罗曼诺夫王朝的摇篮；农民伊万·苏萨宁把一支波兰队伍引入附近的雪地密林而殉难，成为这座城市的英雄。到17世纪中叶，它是仅次于莫斯科和雅罗斯拉夫尔的俄罗斯第三大手工业城市，以麻布、皮革和圣像画闻名，还设有英国商馆。1708年彼得一世将其划为莫斯科省下辖城镇，1767年叶卡捷琳娜二世赐下城徽，1773年大火后城市按放射状街道格局重建。

en:
Murom takes its name from the Muroma, a Finnic people who settled the banks of the Oka in the early first millennium, and the Primary Chronicle lists it as early as 862 among the towns subject to Rurik. Around 900 it was a trading post linking Volga Bulgaria with the Baltic, and from 1010 it was the seat of its own princes, among them Gleb, slain in 1015, and Konstantin, who brought Christianity to the town; the thirteenth-century princely pair Peter and Fevronia were later venerated as patrons of married love, and the epic hero Ilya Muromets was said to be a native. Batu's Mongols sacked Murom in 1238, and after another burning it vanished from the chronicles in 1293, reappearing only in 1351. In 1392 Vasily I of Moscow obtained the patent for its throne, and in 1444 the town, its markets fed by Oka grain and fish, stood as a fortified eastern border holding of the Grand Principality of Moscow.

In the 1540s and again in 1552 Ivan the Terrible mustered his armies here for the Kazan campaigns, and Murom's first stone churches went up, among them the Nativity Cathedral built at his command. In 1565 the tsar placed the town in the zemshchina rather than the Oprichnina. Murom gave Russia the master gun-founder Andrei Chokhov, who cast the Tsar Cannon in 1586, and in the seventeenth century its leather, kalachi rolls and smiths' work carried its name across the country. In 1708 Murom was assigned to Moscow Governorate, and in 1778 it became an uyezd town of the new Vladimir Viceroyalty. Great fires in 1792 and 1805 destroyed almost all the old wooden town, which was rebuilt on the regular grid approved by Catherine II back in 1788.
zh:
穆罗姆得名于公元初几个世纪定居奥卡河畔的芬兰语部族穆罗马人，《往年纪事》早在862年就把它列为留里克治下的城镇。约900年时，这里是连接伏尔加保加利亚与波罗的海的贸易据点；1010年起成为独立王公的驻地，王公中有1015年遇害的格列布和为当地施洗的君士坦丁，13世纪的王公夫妇彼得与费夫罗尼娅后来被尊为婚姻与家庭的主保圣人，史诗中的壮士伊利亚·穆罗梅茨相传也是穆罗姆人。拔都的蒙古军1238年洗劫穆罗姆，城市再度遭焚后于1293年从编年史中消失，直到1351年才重新见载。1392年莫斯科大公瓦西里一世取得穆罗姆的封诰，到1444年，这座靠奥卡河的粮食和鱼鲜供应市集的城镇，已是莫斯科大公国东部边境上设防的据点。

16世纪40年代及1552年，伊凡雷帝两度在此集结大军远征喀山，穆罗姆最早的一批石砌教堂随之建起，其中包括奉他旨意修建的圣母圣诞大教堂。1565年沙皇划分特辖区与领主区时，穆罗姆被划入领主区。出身穆罗姆的铸炮名匠安德烈·乔霍夫于1586年铸成沙皇炮；进入17世纪，穆罗姆的皮革、环形小面包和铁器声名远播。1708年穆罗姆划归莫斯科省，1778年成为新设弗拉基米尔总督区的县城。1792年和1805年的大火烧毁了几乎全部旧木构城区，城市随后按叶卡捷琳娜二世早在1788年批准的正交网格规划重建。

en:
Ustyug, later called Veliky Ustyug, commands the point where the Sukhona and Yug meet to form the Northern Dvina. A Rostov town first recorded in 1207, with the Mikhaylo-Arkhangelsky Monastery founded in 1212, it guarded the river portages that carried furs, fish and salt from the White Sea hinterland toward central Russia. Its fortress was rebuilt after a Novgorodian attack in 1399, while Gleden was sacked during the Muscovite civil wars of 1436-1438. In 1444 Ustyug was therefore an Orthodox Muscovite frontier town: a garrison and river market on the road from Moscow to Perm, Yugra and the fur lands of the north.

Dmitry Shemyaka seized Ustyug in 1450, drowned citizens who rejected his rule in the Sukhona, and held the town for two years before Vasily II's men recovered it. Under Ivan IV it became one of the oprichnina towns and received the formal style Veliky Ustyug. On 25 January 1613 a Lisowczycy raiding band under Jakub Jacki besieged it without success. During the following decades Siberian furs flowing along the Sukhona to the White Sea made the town prosperous and drew foreign merchants; Semyon Dezhnyov, Yerofey Khabarov and Vladimir Atlasov were natives of the district. Its workshops became known for icons, niello, silver filigree, birch-bark work and glazed tiles. Peter I placed Ustyug in Archangelgorod Governorate in 1708, after which St Petersburg diverted the northern trade. It became a provincial centre in 1719, passed to Vologda Viceroyalty in 1780, and was rebuilt after severe fires at the end of the century.
zh:
乌斯秋格，后来称大乌斯秋格，控扼苏霍纳河与尤格河汇合成北德维纳河的河口。这座罗斯托夫城镇在1207年首见记载，1212年建立米哈伊洛-阿尔汉格尔斯克修道院，扼守连接白海内地与俄罗斯中部的河运连水陆路，毛皮、鱼和盐都经此转运。1399年诺夫哥罗德人来攻后，城镇重修要塞；格列坚又在1436至1438年的莫斯科内战中遭劫。因此到1444年，乌斯秋格已是莫斯科治下的东正教边城，既是要塞，也是莫斯科前往彼尔姆、尤格拉和北方毛皮之地途中的河埠。
