1450年，德米特里·舍米亚卡夺取乌斯秋格，把拒绝承认他的市民沉入苏霍纳河，并据城两年，最后被瓦西里二世的军队收复。伊凡四世时期，它被列入特辖制城市，并正式获得「大乌斯秋格」之称。1613年1月25日，雅各布·亚茨基率领的利索夫奇克武装围攻此城，却未能攻破。此后数十年，西伯利亚毛皮沿苏霍纳河输往白海，使城镇繁荣起来，也吸引了外国商人；谢苗·杰日尼奥夫、叶罗费·哈巴罗夫和弗拉基米尔·阿特拉索夫都出生在这一地区。当地作坊以圣像画、黑银工艺、银丝细工、桦树皮器物和琉璃砖闻名。1708年，彼得一世将乌斯秋格划入阿尔汉格尔斯克省；圣彼得堡兴起后，北方商路逐渐转移。1719年它成为省州治所，1780年并入沃洛格达总督区，世纪末的几场大火后又按新规划重建。

en:
The Budjak is the steppe corner between the Danube delta and the Dniester mouth, where Romanian villagers held the hills and Nogai herdsmen grazed the coast. Its key was Chilia, on the Danube's Chilia arm, the Genoese Licostomo: a Genoese notary's register of 1360–1361 records wheat, honey, wax, wine, salt and fish shipped out to Constantinople. Wallachia held it under Mircea the Elder, until in 1426 Alexandru cel Bun of Moldavia seized the citadel from the hard-pressed Dan II. In 1444 Chilia was Moldavia's busiest port on the Danube mouths, a royal garrison watching both the Ottoman fleet and the kings of Hungary.

In 1448 Prince Petru ceded Chilia to János Hunyadi, who had restored him to his throne. Stephen the Great's assault failed on 22 July 1462 and left him wounded at the ankle, but he took the citadel after a single day's siege in January 1465, and rebuilt it on the left bank in the summer of 1479, with 800 masons and 17,000 labourers at work. Sultan Bayezid II came with over 60,000 men, opened the siege on 6 July 1484 against four hundred Moldavians led by Ivanco and Maxim, and forced the fortress on 14 July; Cetatea Albă fell within weeks, and the last Black Sea ports were in Ottoman hands. Chilia became an Ottoman sanjak, its 1570 register listing 298 Muslim and 316 Christian households, with a Circassian quarter among the Muslim neighbourhoods, while the Nogai steppe behind it served as a border grazing ground and the new fortress of Izmail overshadowed the old port. Russian troops stormed Chilia in the war of 1787–1792 but handed it back in 1792; taken again in 1806, the town and the whole Budjak were ceded to Russia by the Treaty of Bucharest in 1812.
zh:
布贾克是多瑙河三角洲与德涅斯特河口之间的草原一隅，罗马尼亚人在丘陵间务农，诺盖牧人在滨海地带放牧。此地的锁钥是多瑙河基利亚汊道上的基利亚，热那亚人称之为利科斯托莫：1360至1361年热那亚公证人留下的账册记载，小麦、蜂蜜、蜂蜡、葡萄酒、盐和鱼从这里装船运往君士坦丁堡。瓦拉几亚的老米尔恰曾据有此堡，1426年摩尔达维亚的善人亚历山德鲁趁瓦拉几亚的丹二世处境艰难，将其夺取。1444年的基利亚是摩尔达维亚在多瑙河口最繁忙的港口，一支王家驻军同时戒备着奥斯曼舰队与匈牙利国王。

1448年，大公彼得把基利亚割让给助他复位的匈雅提·亚诺什。1462年7月22日，斯特凡大公攻城不克，脚踝负伤；1465年1月他只用一天就拿下城堡，又在1479年夏于多瑙河左岸重建新城，上工的有800名石匠和17000名民夫。1484年，巴耶济德二世率六万余人来攻，7月6日合围，城内只有伊万科和马克西姆带领的400名摩尔达维亚人，7月14日城堡陷落；几周后白堡（阿克曼）也告失守，黑海最后的港口尽入奥斯曼之手。基利亚成为奥斯曼的桑贾克，1570年的户籍登记有298户穆斯林和316户基督徒，穆斯邻里还包括一区切尔克斯人；城后的诺盖草原充作边境牧场，新兴的伊兹梅尔堡则使旧港日渐失色。1787至1792年的战争中，俄军强攻占领基利亚，却在1792年将其交还；1806年它再度落入俄军之手，1812年《布加勒斯特和约》把该城连同整个布贾克割让给俄国。

en:
The Upper Palatinate was the old Bavarian Nordgau, a wooded and iron-bearing country between Franconia, Bohemia and the Bavarian Danube. By the Treaty of Pavia in 1329 it passed to the Palatine branch of the Wittelsbachs; Heidelberg was far away, so a governor ruled the eastern territory from Amberg. First recorded as Ammenberg in 1034 and holding town law by 1294, Amberg became the chief market for the region's iron. Ore was smelted nearby, sent down the Vils to Regensburg, and exchanged for salt. The Electoral Castle was built in 1417, and great walls rose around a town already famed for its armourers. In 1444 this Catholic Palatine land drew its wealth from Upper Palatine iron.

The Palatine government returned to Amberg in 1543 under Elector Frederick II, and Lutheranism spread through the territory in the sixteenth century. The Amberg tin-plate trading company, founded in 1533, lasted until 1631. Frederick V's defeat at the White Mountain on 8 November 1620 ended Palatine rule: Bavarian troops occupied Amberg in 1621, Jesuits directed the return to Catholicism, and the Upper Palatinate was formally annexed in 1628. Many Protestants fled to Nuremberg and Regensburg, while war and shifted trade routes impoverished the mining country. Imperial troops took Amberg only after a siege in 1703. On 24 August 1796 Archduke Charles defeated Jourdan's French army nearby. A royal rifle factory opened in 1801, and although Amberg headed the Naab district from 1806, its regional administration moved to Regensburg in 1810.
zh:
上普法尔茨的前身是巴伐利亚的诺德高，这片森林与铁矿之乡位于法兰克尼亚、波希米亚和巴伐利亚多瑙河地区之间。1329年《帕维亚条约》将它划归维特尔斯巴赫家族的普法尔茨支系；由于海德堡路途遥远，东部领地由驻在安贝格的总督管理。安贝格1034年以阿门贝格之名首见记载，1294年已拥有城市权，后来成为这一地区最重要的铁器市场。铁矿石在附近冶炼，沿菲尔斯河运到雷根斯堡，再换回食盐。选帝侯宫建于1417年，宏伟城墙环绕着这座早已以兵器匠闻名的城市。1444年，这片信奉天主教的普法尔茨领地正以上普法尔茨的铁矿致富。

1543年，选帝侯腓特烈二世把普法尔茨在东部的政府迁回安贝格；16世纪里，路德宗在领地内传播。1533年成立的安贝格白铁皮贸易公司一直经营到1631年。1620年11月8日，腓特烈五世在白山战役战败，普法尔茨的统治随之终结：巴伐利亚军队1621年占领安贝格，耶稣会主导重新天主教化，上普法尔茨最终于1628年被正式吞并。许多新教徒逃往纽伦堡和雷根斯堡，战争与商路改道又使这片矿业之乡凋敝。1703年，帝国军队经围城才攻占安贝格。1796年8月24日，卡尔大公在城附近击败儒尔当的法军。1801年，王家步枪厂设立；安贝格虽在1806年成为纳布行政圈首府，但其地区行政机关于1810年迁往雷根斯堡。

en:
Hanover began as a ferrymen's and fishermen's settlement on a raised, flood-free bank of the Leine, its name Honovere probably meaning 'high bank'. Henry the Lion had the place enlarged in the 12th century and enfeoffed it to the counts of Roden, and in 1241 the Brunswick duke granted it town privileges. A wall with three gates rose in the 14th century, and Hanover joined the Hanseatic League, its merchants shipping linen to London, trading cloth to Flanders and bringing back furs from Novgorod, wax from Norway and herring from southern Sweden. The Great Privilege of 1371 added customs and mill rights and leave to fortify. In 1444 it was still a small, largely self-administering market town of the Welf Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg, overshadowed by nearby Brunswick.

George, duke of Calenberg, made the fortified town his residence in 1636, and the court transformed it. Duke Ernest Augustus introduced primogeniture in 1682 and in 1692 won the ninth electoral dignity of the Empire, while Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz served his house as librarian and councillor and Electress Sophia laid out the gardens of Herrenhausen. In 1714 Sophia's son mounted the British throne as George I and carried the court to London. After the defeat at Hastenbeck the French occupied Hanover on 9 August 1757, extracting a contribution of 100,000 thalers before they left in February 1758. French troops returned under General Mortier in 1803, and from 1810 the town was the chief place of the Aller department in the Kingdom of Westphalia. The Welfs returned after the Battle of Leipzig in 1813, and in 1814 Hanover became the capital of a kingdom.
zh:
汉诺威起于莱讷河一处高燥不淹的河岸，最初是摆渡人和渔民的聚落，地名Honovere可能意为「高岸」。12世纪狮子亨利扩建此地，封给罗登伯爵；1241年，不伦瑞克公爵授予它城市特权。14世纪，带三座城门的城墙筑起，汉诺威加入汉萨同盟，商人把亚麻布运往伦敦，向佛兰德贩卖呢绒，又从诺夫哥罗德贩回毛皮、从挪威贩回蜂蜡、从南瑞典贩回鲱鱼。1371年的《大特权书》又给了关税权、磨坊权和筑城权。1444年时，它还是韦尔夫家族不伦瑞克-吕讷堡公国里一座自行管理政务的小集镇，光彩为附近的不伦瑞克所掩。

1636年，卡伦贝格公爵格奥尔格把这座要塞化的城镇定为都城，宫廷随之改变了城市面貌。公爵恩斯特·奥古斯特1682年确立长子继承制，1692年为家族赢得神圣罗马帝国第九个选帝侯席位；戈特弗里德·威廉·莱布尼茨在他府中任图书馆长和枢密顾问，选帝侯夫人索菲则营建了海恩豪森花园。1714年，索菲之子以乔治一世之名登上英国王位，把宫廷带往伦敦。哈斯滕贝克战败后，法军于1757年8月9日占领汉诺威，勒索了十万塔勒的军税，至1758年2月才撤走。1803年法军在莫尔捷将军率领下再度占领，1810年起汉诺威成为威斯特伐利亚王国阿勒尔省的省会。1813年莱比锡会战之后韦尔夫家族回归，1814年汉诺威成为一个王国的首都。

en:
Potsdam commands a crossing of the Havel where the Nuthe enters the river among lakes and morainic hills. The Hevelli Slavs built a castle there in the seventh century, and on 3 July 993 Emperor Otto III granted the settlement of Poztupimi to Quedlinburg Abbey. Albert the Bear conquered it in 1157, a German stone tower rose at the crossing, and Potsdam received town rights in 1345. The town passed to the Hohenzollerns in 1416. In 1444 it was still only a small Catholic market town in the Mittelmark, controlling a useful Havel crossing beneath the growing twin city of Berlin and Kölln.

Potsdam remained modest—it had about 2,000 people in 1573—and the Thirty Years' War, together with two great fires, cost it nearly half its population. The Great Elector Frederick William bought back pledged parts of the town and from 1660 developed it as a second residence beside Berlin. His Edict of Potsdam in 1685 drew Huguenot, Dutch, Bohemian and other Protestant settlers, reviving crafts and trade. Frederick William I turned the town into a major garrison and laid out new baroque quarters, while Frederick II reshaped the old market and began Sanssouci Palace above the vineyards in 1745; the New Palace later completed his royal park. Napoleon's troops entered in 1806, and the French occupation helped push Prussia into reform. In 1815 Potsdam became capital of the new Province of Brandenburg.
zh:
波茨坦扼守哈弗尔河渡口，努特河在此注入河湖交错、冰碛丘陵起伏的水网。斯拉夫赫维利人7世纪时在此修建城堡；993年7月3日，皇帝奥托三世把名为波茨图皮米的聚落赠予奎德林堡修道院。1157年，大熊阿尔布雷希特征服此地，德意志石砌塔楼随后立在渡口，波茨坦则于1345年获得城市权。1416年，城镇转入霍亨索伦家族手中。1444年的波茨坦仍是米特尔马克一座小小的天主教集镇，守着哈弗尔河上的重要渡口，风头不及日渐壮大的柏林与克尔恩双城。

波茨坦长期不大，1573年约有两千居民；三十年战争加上两场大火，使它损失近半人口。大选帝侯腓特烈·威廉赎回被抵押的城区，自1660年起把它建设成柏林之外的第二座驻跸地。1685年，他颁布《波茨坦敕令》，吸引胡格诺教徒、荷兰人、波希米亚人和其他新教移民迁入，重振了手工业与商业。腓特烈·威廉一世把这里变成重要驻军地，开辟新的巴洛克城区；腓特烈二世重塑旧市场，又于1745年在葡萄园上方动工修建无忧宫，后来的新宫则使王家园林更为完整。1806年拿破仑军队入城，法国占领也推动普鲁士走向改革。1815年，波茨坦成为新设勃兰登堡省的省会。

en:
Koblenz takes its name from the Latin ad confluentes, 'at the confluence', where the Moselle joins the Rhine. Around 9 BC Drusus planted the castellum of Confluentes to guard the Rhine valley road, and a Roman bridge stood here from AD 49. The Franks made it a royal estate; in 842 the Carolingian heirs negotiated in the church of St Castor over the partition sealed at Verdun the following year, and Vikings sacked the town in 882. In 1018 Emperor Henry II granted Koblenz to the archbishop-elector of Trier. Across the Rhine the castle on the Ehrenbreitstein grew into a fortress holding the electorate's treasures, while Stolzenfels above the river tolled the Rhine shipping; Archbishop Baldwin of Luxembourg spanned the Moselle with the Balduin Bridge, the first fixed crossing since Roman times. In 1444 the town, held for Trier, lived by the carrying trade of Rhine and Moselle beneath the guns of Ehrenbreitstein.

During the Thirty Years' War Elector Philipp Christoph von Sötern built the Schloss Philippsburg under the fortress rock and moved his residence there from Trier; the last elector, Clemens Wenzeslaus, occupied the new electoral palace in 1786. After 1789 Koblenz became the rallying point of the French émigrés, as the king's brothers the counts of Provence and Artois ran a counter-revolutionary 'little Paris' here until General Marceau's French troops took the city in 1794; the Ehrenbreitstein held out until 1799. The Peace of Lunéville in 1801 confirmed the annexation, and Koblenz became capital of the French department of Rhin-et-Moselle. Russian troops entered in 1814, and the Congress of Vienna in 1815 gave the city to Prussia, who rebuilt it as the fortress of Koblenz, one of the strongest fortified systems in Europe.
zh:
科布伦茨的名字来自拉丁文「汇流处」（ad confluentes），因摩泽尔河在此注入莱茵河而得名。公元前9年前后，德鲁苏斯在此建起康夫卢恩特斯要塞，拱卫莱茵河谷大道，公元49年罗马人又在此架起桥梁。法兰克人把这里作为王家庄园，842年加洛林王朝的继承人们在圣卡斯特教堂谈判，次年缔结《凡尔登条约》三分帝国，882年维京人洗劫了这座城镇。1018年，皇帝亨利二世把科布伦茨封给特里尔大主教选帝侯。莱茵河对岸埃伦布赖特施泰因山上的城堡逐渐扩建成要塞，存放选帝侯国最珍贵的圣物与档案；河畔的施托尔岑费尔斯堡则向莱茵河商船征税。大主教巴尔杜因·冯·卢森堡修筑巴尔杜因桥，这是罗马时代之后摩泽尔河上第一座固定桥梁。1444年，这座隶属特里尔的城镇靠着莱茵河与摩泽尔河的转运贸易为生，头顶便是埃伦布赖特施泰因要塞的炮火。

三十年战争期间，选帝侯菲利普·克里斯托夫·冯·瑟特恩在要塞山脚下兴建菲利普斯堡，把宫廷从特里尔迁来；末代选帝侯克莱门斯·文策尔劳斯1786年迁入新建的选帝侯宫。1789年后，科布伦茨成为法国流亡贵族的汇聚之地，路易十六的两个兄弟普罗旺斯伯爵和阿图瓦伯爵在此经营着一个反革命的「小巴黎」，直到1794年马尔索将军率法军攻占城市，埃伦布赖特施泰因要塞则坚守至1799年。1801年《吕内维尔和约》正式确认吞并，科布伦茨成为法国莱茵-摩泽尔省的省会。1814年俄军入城，1815年维也纳和会把城市划归普鲁士，普方随即将其扩建为科布伦茨要塞，跻身欧洲最坚固的要塞体系之列。

en:
Worms rose on the left bank of the Rhine as Celtic Borbetomagus and Roman Wormatia. A bishopric by 614, it became a favoured city of the Salian emperors; the Concordat of Worms was concluded there in 1122, while the Romanesque cathedral rose above the bishop's quarter. Its Jewish community was one of the three ShUM communities, with a synagogue dedicated in 1034 and the Holy Sand cemetery in use from at least 1058 or 1059, though crusaders destroyed much of the community in 1096. By 1444 the council governed a privileged imperial city beside the Wonnegau vineyards, while the cathedral clergy kept extensive rights and the Electoral Palatinate's influence pressed in from the surrounding Rhineland.

The imperial diet of 1495, meeting in Worms under Maximilian I, proclaimed the Eternal Peace and established the Imperial Chamber Court. Civic revolt in 1512 and 1513 and Franz von Sickingen's feud of 1515 to 1519 weakened the city's finances before Martin Luther defended his teachings before Charles V at the Diet of 1521. Worms then became a Reformation printing centre: Peter Schöffer the Younger printed an English New Testament for William Tyndale in 1526 and the first complete German Protestant Bible in 1529. The city turned Protestant, but in 1689 Louis XIV's troops destroyed it during the Palatine Succession War and expelled its people. Worms passed under French rule in 1792 and, after 1815, to the Grand Duchy of Hesse; in the same period the white wine from the Church of Our Lady's vineyards became known as Liebfrauenmilch.
zh:
沃尔姆斯位于莱茵河左岸，前身是凯尔特人的博尔贝托马古斯和罗马时代的沃尔马提亚。这里至迟在614年已设主教区，也是萨利安皇帝重视的城市；1122年《沃尔姆斯宗教协定》在此订立，罗曼式主教座堂高耸于教士区。当地犹太社群是舒姆三社群之一，会堂于1034年落成，圣沙公墓至迟1058或1059年已在使用，但1096年十字军曾重创这一社群。1444年时，市议会治理着这座享有特权的帝国城市，周围是沃内高的葡萄园，教士仍保有大量特权，普法尔茨选侯国的势力也从莱茵兰周边不断渗入。

1495年，马克西米利安一世在沃尔姆斯召开帝国议会，颁布《永久和平法令》并设立帝国枢密法院。1512至1513年的市民暴动，以及1515年至1519年弗朗茨·冯·西金根挑起的武力纷争使城市财政困顿；1521年，马丁·路德又在沃尔姆斯帝国议会上当面向查理五世辩护。此后沃尔姆斯成为宗教改革印刷中心，小彼得·舍弗1526年为威廉·廷代尔印制英文《新约》，1529年印出第一部德语新教完整圣经。城市改宗新教后，又在1689年普法尔茨继承战争中遭路易十四军队摧毁，居民被逐。1792年沃尔姆斯转入法国统治，1815年后归属黑森大公国；同一时期，圣母教堂葡萄园出产的白葡萄酒以「圣母之乳」之名闻名。

en:
Lower Hesse covers the northern Hessian valleys of the lower Fulda, Eder and Schwalm, with Kassel as its residence and market centre. The place first appears in 913 as Chassalla, a fortified royal estate beside a Fulda crossing, and by 1189 Kassel had the standing of a town. In 1277 Henry I made it the chief residence of the new Landgraviate of Hesse. The old town, new town and Freiheit were joined in 1378, and the late medieval town still gained its Rathaus in 1408 and the Druselturm in 1415. Although the County of Ziegenhain long lay between the lower and upper Hessian lands, in 1444 the Catholic landgrave Louis I ruled an undivided Hesse from Kassel.

Philip I introduced the Reformation in 1526, and the partition of 1567 made Lower Hesse the heartland of Hesse-Kassel under William IV; under Landgrave Maurice the territory turned from Lutheranism to the Reformed confession early in the next century. Kassel escaped direct destruction in the Thirty Years' War, but famine and plague sharply reduced its people. Landgrave Charles later transformed the court with the Karlsaue and the Hercules and water gardens above the city, while after 1685 about 4,000 Huguenots settled in Kassel and its surrounding country. French troops occupied the city more than once during the Seven Years' War, and Simon Louis du Ry's late-eighteenth-century squares and palaces gave Kassel its baroque residence. In 1807 Napoleon made it capital of the Kingdom of Westphalia under Jérôme Bonaparte; Russian troops restored the elector in 1813, while the Brothers Grimm were among the scholars working in the restored city.
zh:
下黑森位于黑森北部，涵盖富尔达河下游、埃德尔河与施瓦尔姆河流域，卡塞尔是这里的邦君驻地和商业中心。卡塞尔最早在913年以「查萨拉」之名出现，当时是富尔达河渡口旁设防的王室庄园，到1189年已具有城市地位。1277年，海因里希一世把它定为新建立的黑森领地伯爵国的主要驻地。旧市、新市和自由区1378年合并，城市又在1408年建起市政厅，1415年建起德鲁泽尔塔。尽管齐根海因伯国长期横亘在下黑森与上黑森之间，1444年时天主教徒领地伯爵路德维希一世仍以卡塞尔为中心统治着尚未分裂的黑森。

菲利普一世1526年推行宗教改革；1567年黑森再度分治，下黑森成为威廉四世所领黑森—卡塞尔的核心地带，下一世纪初领地伯爵莫里茨又使此地从路德宗转向归正宗。三十年战争中卡塞尔未遭严重的军事破坏，但饥荒和瘟疫使人口大幅减少。后来领地伯爵卡尔大兴土木，在城外营造卡尔草甸、大力神雕像和山地水景园林；1685年以后，又有约4000名胡格诺教徒定居卡塞尔及周边地区。七年战争期间，法军曾多次占领这座城市；18世纪末，建筑师西蒙·路易·迪·里设计的广场和宫殿使卡塞尔成为一座巴洛克式驻地。1807年，拿破仑把这里定为热罗姆·波拿巴统治的威斯特伐利亚王国首都。1813年俄军恢复领地伯爵的统治，格林兄弟也在这座光复后的城市搜集他们的童话。

en:
Lower Lusatia grew from the heaths and streams of the Lusici, a West Slavic tribe whose people became part of the Sorbian settlement area. From the ninth century their lowland castles guarded the country around the Spree Forest, while German settlers founded towns and monasteries beside the older Sorbian villages. Cottbus, first documented in 1156, stood on the Spree and the Salt Road from Halle toward Poland; its woolen cloth was sold in Brandenburg, Bohemia and Saxony. In 1367 Elector Otto V sold the margraviate to Emperor Charles IV, who incorporated it into the Bohemian Crown. Royal power remained distant, and the estates at Lübben managed much local business. In 1444 the country was still Catholic, Sorbian-speaking in many villages, and formally Bohemian, although Cottbus itself was about to pass to Brandenburg in 1445.

The Hussite wars and successive pledges weakened the old march, and the four-curie diet meeting at Lübben became its strongest political body. Between 1520 and 1540 the Reformation spread through town and countryside, with preaching in German and Sorbian; only Neuzelle Abbey remained Catholic. In 1619 the Lower Lusatian estates joined the Bohemian Confederation against Ferdinand II. The Thirty Years' War then brought repeated occupations and plunder, and Cottbus shrank from nearly 3,500 inhabitants before the war to a few hundred by 1648. The Peace of Prague assigned the margraviate to Saxony in 1635, while Cottbus remained a Brandenburg exclave. Huguenot settlers and attempts at silkworm cultivation revived the town in the eighteenth century. The Peace of Tilsit briefly joined Cottbus to Saxony in 1807, but the Congress of Vienna gave all Lower Lusatia to Prussia in 1815 and dissolved the old margraviate.
zh:
下劳西茨起于卢西奇人生活的荒野与水网之间；这支西斯拉夫人后来成为索布聚居区的一部分。从9世纪起，他们的低地要塞守卫着施普雷瓦尔德一带，德意志移民则在较早的索布村庄旁建立城镇和修道院。科特布斯最早见于1156年，地处施普雷河畔和从哈勒通往波兰的盐路上，毛织物销往勃兰登堡、波希米亚和萨克森。1367年，选帝侯奥托五世将这片边疆伯国卖给皇帝查理四世，后者把它并入波希米亚王冠领地。王权始终遥远，吕本的等级会议处理了大量地方事务。1444年，此地仍信奉天主教，许多村庄使用索布语，名义上属于波希米亚，但科特布斯即将在1445年转入勃兰登堡之手。

胡斯战争和接连不断的抵押削弱了旧边疆伯国，在吕本集会、分为四个议席团的等级会议成为最强的政治机构。1520年至1540年间，宗教改革传遍城乡，讲道同时使用德语和索布语；只有新策勒修道院仍保持天主教。1619年，下劳西茨等级加入波希米亚同盟，对抗斐迪南二世。三十年战争随后带来反复占领和劫掠，科特布斯人口从战前近3500人降到1648年的数百人。1635年《布拉格和约》将边疆伯国划归萨克森，但科特布斯仍是勃兰登堡飞地。18世纪，胡格诺派移民和养蚕尝试使城镇恢复生气。1807年《蒂尔西特和约》一度把科特布斯并入萨克森，但1815年维也纳会议将整个下劳西茨交给普鲁士，并解散旧边疆伯国。

en:
The Burgas bay is the westernmost arm of the Black Sea, watched over by the little fortress of Pyrgos — Greek for 'tower', from which Burgas takes its name — while the lakes behind the shore yield salt. The Romans planted the veteran colony of Deultum on the Via Pontica under Vespasian in AD 70, and emperors bathed at the hot springs of Aquae Calidae, Thermopolis. Medieval Bulgarian tsars and Byzantine emperors fought over the coastal forts: at the Skafida river in 1304 Tsar Theodore Svetoslav defeated the Byzantines and took the southern shore, and soon afterwards the Catalan Company sacked the region. The Ottomans first came under Murad I in 1367–68, but the crusade of Amadeus of Savoy seized the coast towns and handed them back to Byzantium. In 1444 the gulf is therefore a forgotten corner of the dying empire: Greek and Bulgarian Orthodox fishermen and salters under a Byzantine governor, clustered around a watchtower-harbor and the half-ancient baths.

In the first weeks of 1453, just before Constantinople, the southern Black Sea coast at last submitted to Mehmed II, and Deultum was left in ruins, never to rise again. The sultans still prized the springs — Bayezid II kept an estate and a lighthouse at Poros, and Suleiman raised a new bath over the Roman pools — and after Lepanto in 1571 the harbor of Pirgos served as an Ottoman shipbuilding station. An Ottoman register of 1603 first names the iskele, the quay of Pirgos, on the site of the modern city. From the mid-seventeenth century Burgas grew as a grain port with its own official measure, the Burgas-Kile; Katib Celebi and Evliya Celebi found two harbors busy with shipping, and Mehmed IV took the waters in 1672 on his way to war in Poland. The town held only a few thousand souls, and around the turn of the nineteenth century the kircali bandits who plagued the Balkans emptied much of it, so that by 1821 the salt pans and the grain road were quieter than they had been for a century.
zh:
布尔加斯湾是黑海最西端的海湾，湾畔有瞭望小要塞皮戈斯——在希腊语中意为「塔」，布尔加斯之名即由此而来，岸后的湖滩则自古产盐。罗马皇帝韦斯巴芗于公元70年沿滨海大道设立老兵殖民城戴乌尔图姆，历代皇帝还常来阿奎埃卡利德（又称塞尔莫波利斯）的温泉沐浴。中世纪时，保加利亚沙皇与拜占庭皇帝反复争夺沿岸要塞：1304年，沙皇托多尔·斯韦托斯拉夫在斯卡菲达击败拜占庭，夺取南部海岸；此后不久加泰罗尼亚佣兵团又洗劫此地。奥斯曼人最初在穆拉德一世时的1367—1368年到来，但萨伏依伯爵阿马德乌斯的十字军夺取沿海诸城后将它们交还拜占庭。因此1444年的海湾是垂死帝国一个被遗忘的角落：拜占庭总督治下的希腊与保加利亚东正教渔民和盐户，守着一座瞭望塔港和几处半为古迹的温泉。

1453年初，就在君士坦丁堡陷落前夕，南部黑海沿岸终于向穆罕默德二世臣服，戴乌尔图姆被夷为废墟，再未复兴。苏丹们仍看重这里的温泉：巴耶济德二世在波罗斯设有庄园和灯塔，苏莱曼则在罗马浴池旧址上建起新浴室。1571年勒班陀海战后，皮戈斯港成为奥斯曼的造船据点。1603年的一份奥斯曼地籍册首次在今城址上记载了「皮戈斯码头」。17世纪中叶起，布尔加斯作为粮食港口兴起，还有官定的「布尔加斯斗」作为量器；卡蒂布·切莱比与爱维亚·切莱比都记述这里两处泊地商船往来，穆罕默德四世1672年远征波兰途中也曾来温泉沐浴。小城居民不过数千，18、19世纪之交横行巴尔干的克尔贾利盗匪使此地大半荒废，到1821年，盐田与粮道都已比一个世纪前冷清许多。

en:
Sofia occupies the Sofia Valley beneath Vitosha, where hot springs and roads between the Danube, Morava, Maritsa and Adriatic worlds sustained Roman Serdica and medieval Sredets. Khan Krum took the city for Bulgaria in 809, and after Byzantine rule it returned to the Second Bulgarian Empire in 1194. Ottoman forces captured it in 1382. During the 1443 crusade John Hunyadi's Christian army briefly entered Sofia and Bulgarian townspeople heard Mass in St Sophia, but the campaign ended in Ottoman recovery and persecution after Varna. In November 1444 Sofia was therefore an Ottoman road centre and forward base for campaigns toward central Europe, set among Bulgarian Orthodox villages beneath Vitosha.

Ottoman rule soon gave Sofia a new imperial role. Rumelian governors resided there at times from the mid-fifteenth century, and in 1530 it became the permanent capital of the Rumelia Eyalet, the chief province administering the sultan's European conquests. It remained the seat of its own sanjak and became a caravan-trade emporium handling commerce with Ragusa, as well as a forward depot for armies marching into Hungary. Churches including St Sophia and St George were turned into mosques; libraries, schools, hammams, fountains and the great bedesten reshaped the centre, while Mimar Sinan built the Banya Bashi Mosque. The same age was harsh for Bulgarian Orthodox Christians: George the New was executed there in 1515 and Nicholas of Sofia in 1555 among the city's new martyrs.

Sofia entered an economic and political decline in the seventeenth century. In 1737 an uprising planned across Sofia, Samokov and western Bulgaria was suppressed by Ottoman authorities, and by the later eighteenth century local warlords and Janissary factions were ravaging the surrounding countryside. In 1821 Sofia was still the Ottoman capital of Rumelia, but its caravans, bazaars and fortifications now sustained a diminished, war-taxed town rather than the prosperous provincial court of the sixteenth century.
zh:
索非亚位于维托沙山下的索非亚盆地，温泉与连接多瑙河、摩拉瓦河、马里查河和亚得里亚海方向的道路，曾供养罗马城市塞尔迪卡和中世纪的斯雷德茨。809年，克鲁姆汗将城市并入保加利亚；拜占庭统治之后，它在1194年重归第二保加利亚帝国。奥斯曼军1382年攻占此城。1443年十字军期间，匈雅提·亚诺什的基督教军队短暂进入索非亚，保加利亚市民在圣索菲亚教堂举行弥撒，但这场远征最终以奥斯曼恢复统治、瓦尔纳战后基督徒受迫害告终。1444年11月，索非亚因此成为奥斯曼人的道路枢纽和进军中欧的前沿基地，周围是维托沙山下的保加利亚东正教村庄。

奥斯曼统治很快给了索非亚新的帝国角色。15世纪中叶起，鲁米利亚总督已时常驻节于此；1530年，索非亚成为鲁米利亚省的常设首府，这个大省负责管理苏丹在欧洲征服的土地。它同时是索菲亚桑贾克的治所，也是与拉古萨贸易的商队商城，还为进军匈牙利的军队充当前方仓库。圣索菲亚、圣乔治等教堂被改成清真寺，图书馆、学校、土耳其浴室、喷泉和大贝德斯坦重塑了城市中心，科查·米马尔·希南则修建了班亚巴希扎米亚。同一时代对保加利亚东正教徒也十分严酷：新乔治1515年在此遇害，索菲亚的尼古拉1555年被杀，二人都属于索非亚的新殉道者。

17世纪，索非亚进入经济和政治上的衰退期。1737年，一场遍及索非亚、萨莫科夫和西保加利亚的起义被奥斯曼当局镇压；到18世纪后期，地方军阀和禁卫军派系又不断蹂躏周边乡村。1821年时，索非亚仍是奥斯曼帝国的鲁米利亚首府，但商队、巴扎和城防支撑着的已是一座萎缩而承受战争税赋的城镇，不再像16世纪那个繁荣的行省宫廷之城。

en:
Kosovo is the high basin of Kosovo Polje, with Pristina set near its eastern mines. It became a heartland of the medieval Serbian state under the Nemanjići: Gračanica was founded in 1315, the Patriarchate of Peć was established in 1346, and Saxon miners and Ragusan merchants worked silver, lead and gold at Novo Brdo and Trepča. On 28 June 1389, Lazar's Christian coalition met Sultan Murad I on the Kosovo field; both rulers died in the inconclusive slaughter and Serbia soon accepted Ottoman vassalage. Vuk Branković held much of the region until his fall in 1398. After the Ottoman occupation of 1439 and the peace of 1444, Đurađ Branković's despotate returned, while Ottoman garrisons kept key strongpoints; the mines and roads thus made Kosovo a contested borderland in 1444.

In October 1448 John Hunyadi led a 24,000-strong Hungarian army onto Kosovo Polje and lost a two-day battle against Murad II. The region finally passed under Ottoman rule in 1455, when its lands were organized around the sanjaks of Vučitrn and Prizren. Pristina grew into a mining and trading centre near Novo Brdo, its fairs dealing in goatskin, goat hair and gunpowder. Orthodox life revived after the Patriarchate of Peć was restored in 1557, while conversion to Islam spread through the towns. During the war of 1689–1690 Pjetër Bogdani helped rally Albanians to the Austrian advance; after the Ottoman victory at Kaçanik on 1 February 1690, Patriarch Arsenije III led Serbian refugees northward. The war of 1737–1739 brought another exodus, and in 1766 the Ottomans abolished the Patriarchate of Peć.
zh:
科索沃是科索沃平原所在的高地盆地，普里什蒂纳位于其东部矿区附近。尼曼雅王朝治下，这里成为中世纪塞尔维亚国家的腹地：格拉查尼察修道院建于1315年，佩奇牧首区设于1346年，萨克萨矿工和拉古萨商人在新布尔多、特雷普查开采银、铅和金。1389年6月28日，拉扎尔统率的基督教联军在科索沃平原迎战苏丹穆拉德一世；这场胜负难分的血战令两位统帅双双殒命，塞尔维亚不久也接受奥斯曼宗主权。武克·布兰科维奇据有此地大部，直至1398年失势。1439年奥斯曼占领后，1444年和议使久拉吉·布兰科维奇的专制公国恢复管辖，但奥斯曼守军仍控制若干要地；因此在1444年，矿藏和商路使科索沃成为纷争不断的边地。

1448年10月，匈雅提·亚诺什率两万四千人的匈牙利军队进抵科索沃平原，在与穆拉德二世持续两日的交战中战败。1455年，此地最终落入奥斯曼统治，被分别编入以武奇特恩和普里兹伦为中心的桑贾克。普里什蒂纳邻近新布尔多，发展为采矿与贸易中心，市集上交易山羊皮、山羊毛和火药。1557年佩奇牧首区恢复，东正教生活一度复兴，与此同时伊斯兰教也在各城镇传播。1689—1690年战争期间，皮耶特尔·博格达尼号召阿尔巴尼亚人响应奥地利军队；1690年2月1日奥斯曼军在卡查尼克获胜后，牧首阿尔塞尼耶三世率领塞尔维亚难民北迁。1737—1739年的战争又带来一波迁徙，1766年奥斯曼废除佩奇牧首区。

en:
Slavonia is the open Drava lowland around Osijek, a dry rise above the river marshes not far upstream from the Danube. A royal charter of 1196 already identified Osijek as a Drava crossing, ferry and toll place on an old road between the Balkans and the Pannonian plain. During the 14th century it passed to the powerful Kórógyi family, whose lords developed its county fair and administrative role. In 1444 the Catholic market town remained within the Hungarian-Croatian kingdom, sheltered by a small lordly castle and busy with merchants, craftsmen and river traffic while the Ottoman frontier advanced toward the Balkans.

On 14 August 1526 Osijek surrendered without battle to the Ottoman army of Ibrahim Pasha and was subsequently destroyed. Rebuilt under Ottoman rule, it became part of the Sanjak of Požega, and in 1566 Suleiman I commissioned the famous eight-kilometre bridge of boats and timber across the Drava marshes to Darda. The Holy League liberated Osijek on 29 September 1687; an Ottoman siege in 1690 devastated the town again but failed to retake it. Habsburg engineers then built the Tvrđa fortress between 1712 and 1721, around which Baroque garrison life, a Jesuit gymnasium in 1729 and a Franciscan printing house in 1735 took root. Joseph II united Tvrđa, Gornji Grad and Donji Grad on 2 December 1786, and on 28 August 1809 Osijek was raised to a free royal city.
zh:
斯拉沃尼亚这一省环绕奥西耶克，地处多瑙河上游不远处的德拉瓦河低洼平原，城市建在沼泽间一块较高的干地上。1196年的王室特许状已经提到，奥西耶克是德拉瓦河渡口、渡船和税卡，位于连接巴尔干与潘诺尼亚平原的古道上。14世纪，它转入权势显赫的科罗吉家族之手，领主们发展了县集和行政功能。1444年，这座信奉天主教的集镇仍属匈牙利—克罗地亚王国，有小型领主城堡庇护，商人、工匠与河运往来其间；此时奥斯曼边境正沿巴尔干向北推进。

1526年8月14日，奥西耶克不战而降，落入易卜拉欣帕夏的奥斯曼军队手中，随后遭摧毁。奥斯曼统治时期城市得到重建，隶属波热加桑贾克；1566年苏莱曼一世下令修建著名的8公里舟桥木桥，横跨德拉瓦沼泽直至道尔达。1687年9月29日，圣同盟军队光复奥西耶克；1690年奥斯曼军队围攻并再次严重破坏城市，却未能夺回。哈布斯堡工程师随后在1712年至1721年间修建特弗尔达要塞，巴洛克驻军生活随之发展，1729年设立耶稣会中学，1735年方济各会开办印刷所。1786年12月2日，约瑟夫二世下令合并特弗尔达、上城和下城；1809年8月28日，奥西耶克升格为自由王家城市。

en:
The Lienz basin, where the Drau meets the Isel, held the Roman municipium of Aguntum before the Slavic settlement and the Bavarian advance of the early Middle Ages. The Meinhardiner, Vögte of the patriarchs of Aquileia, made the place their residence: the market below their hill was first recorded about 1030, received city rights in 1242, and the counts finished Burg Bruck above the town about 1278. Lienz grew rich on the road leading from Friuli over the Plöcken Pass to Salzburg, its mint striking the Lienz pfennig from 1200 and its merchants forwarding Carinthian ore, hides and loden against southern cloth and wax; around 1300 the Jewish banker Isak of Lienz was the eastern Alps' foremost moneylender. When Venice swallowed the patriarchal lands of Friuli the counts moved their seat north from Gorizia, and in 1429 Henry VI reunited the whole county under his rule. In 1444 Lienz, a town of perhaps 1,500 souls, was the capital of the last independent Görz line; a great fire swept it that same year.

Ottoman raiders threatened the town towards the century's end and the counts built new walls, but on 12 April 1500 Count Leonhard, last of the Meinhardiner, died, and an inheritance contract delivered Lienz and the Puster Valley to Maximilian I, who united them with Tyrol in 1501. The Habsburgs at once sold the lordship to the Wolkenstein-Rodenegg, under whom a brass works set up about 1564 employed up to a hundred hands, until fire again gutted Lienz in 1609 and debt forced the surrender of Burg Bruck in 1642. In April 1797 French columns came up from Carinthia only to be driven out by the Tyrolean levy the same day; a second visit cost the town hostages and 24,000 gulden, and another great fire in 1798 destroyed 151 houses and both monasteries. After the Peace of Pressburg in 1805 Lienz went to Bavaria; in 1809 the Tyrolean rising freed the town and Hofer's militia threw back the Bavarian counterstroke, but General Rusca retook it in August and East Tyrol was attached to the Napoleonic Illyrian Provinces. Austrian troops returned in 1813 and Lienz was reincorporated into Tyrol.
zh:
利恩茨盆地位于德拉瓦河与伊瑟尔河汇流处，罗马时代曾是自治城阿贡图姆的所在地，中世纪早期经历了斯拉夫人定居和巴伐利亚人东进。阿奎莱亚牧首的护佑官、迈因哈德家族把这里当作府邸：山下的集市约在1030年首见记载，1242年获得城市权，伯爵们又在1278年前后在山丘上建成布吕克堡。利恩茨靠着弗留利经普洛克恩山口通往萨尔茨堡的商路致富：造币厂自1200年起铸造利恩茨芬尼，商人把克恩滕的矿石、兽皮和罗登呢转运出去，换回南方的布匹和蜂蜡；1300年前后，犹太银行家利恩茨的伊萨克是东阿尔卑斯最重要的放债人。威尼斯吞并弗留利的牧首领地后，伯爵们把府邸从戈里齐亚北迁，1429年亨利六世重新统一整个伯国。1444年，这座约有一千五百人的小城是迈因哈德家族最后一支独立世系的都城，而就在这一年，一场大火席卷了全城。

世纪末奥斯曼袭扰军逼近，伯爵们为此新筑城墙；但1500年4月12日末代伯爵莱昂哈德去世，依照继承契约，利恩茨和普斯特山谷归于马克西米利安一世，1501年与蒂罗尔合并。哈布斯堡旋即把领地卖给沃尔肯施泰因-罗德内格家族，其治下约1564年兴办的黄铜厂一度雇有上百工人；1609年大火再次焚毁全城，1642年负债累累的领主被迫交出布吕克堡。1797年4月，法军从克恩滕北上，当天就被蒂罗尔民兵逐出；法军第二次到来时勒索十万古尔登，利恩茨人只凑出二万四千，法军撤离时带走人质并大肆劫掠，1798年又一场大火烧毁151所房屋和两座修道院。1805年普雷斯堡和约后利恩茨归属巴伐利亚；1809年蒂罗尔起义解放城市，霍费尔的民兵击退巴伐利亚反攻，但吕斯卡将军于8月再度占领，东蒂罗尔随后被并入拿破仑的伊利里亚行省。1813年奥地利军队收复利恩茨，将其重新并入蒂罗尔。

en:
Görz, called Gorizia in Italian and Gorica in Slovene, grew beneath a castle guarding an Isonzo crossing on the old road from Aquileia to Laibach. The settlement was first documented in 1001, and it gave its name to the Meinhardiner County of Görz, whose lords held lands around both the Isonzo and Lienz. After Venice conquered the Aquileian mainland by 1434, Count Henry VI, who had reunited the county in 1429, manoeuvred between Venetian and Habsburg pressure. In 1444 the Catholic market beneath his castle was a meeting place of Friulian merchants, German officials and Slovene-speaking villagers, while the count himself often kept his residence at Lienz.

Henry's son Leonhard, the last Count of Görz, died in 1500. Under an inheritance contract, and with the backing of governor Virgil von Graben, Maximilian of Austria acquired the county, although Venice occupied Görz in 1508 and 1509 during the Italian wars. The town then spread below its castle and drew merchants from northern Italy. Protestant preaching reached Görz by the mid-sixteenth century, including a visit by Primož Trubar, but Dean Johann Tautscher and the Jesuits brought the town firmly back to Catholic practice. In 1747 Görz was joined with Gradisca to form the Princely County of Gorizia and Gradisca. French forces held the town from 1809 to 1813, after which Habsburg rule was restored.
zh:
戈兹在意大利语中称戈里齐亚，斯洛文尼亚语称戈里察，起源于一座扼守伊松佐河渡口的城堡下方，该处位于从阿奎莱亚通往莱巴赫的古道上。此地1001年首见记载，并成为迈因哈德家族戈里齐亚伯国的名称来源；伯爵们的领地兼跨伊松佐河流域与利恩茨一带。威尼斯到1434年已征服阿奎莱亚宗主教区的大陆领地，1429年重新统一伯国的亨利六世伯爵便在威尼斯与哈布斯堡的压力之间周旋。1444年，城堡脚下的天主教集镇汇聚了弗留利商人、德意志官员和讲斯洛文尼亚语的村民，而伯爵本人常住在利恩茨。

亨利之子、末代伯爵莱昂哈德1500年去世。凭借继承契约和总督维吉尔·冯·格拉本的支持，奥地利的马克西米利安取得伯国；不过意大利战争期间，威尼斯又在1508年至1509年占领戈里齐亚。此后城镇向城堡下方扩展，吸引了许多意大利北部商人。新教布道在16世纪中叶传到戈里齐亚，普里莫日·特鲁巴尔也曾前来讲道，但教长约翰·陶舍尔和耶稣会最终使城市坚定回归天主教。1747年，戈里齐亚与格拉迪斯卡合并为戈里齐亚和格拉迪斯卡亲王伯国。1809年至1813年，法国军队控制此地，随后哈布斯堡恢复统治。

en:
Manhartsberg is the long ridge dividing Lower Austria's forested northwest from the vineyard country to its east, and this province reaches its richest ground where the Danube passes Krems and the eastern Wachau. Krems was first documented in 995, had a parish by 1014 and a Babenberg mint between the 1130s and 1190, while neighbouring Stein was a princely toll station before 1200; the two settlements shared written town law by 1305. In the 11th and 12th centuries Krems was nearly as large as Vienna, though its Jewish community was destroyed in Duke Albrecht V's persecution of 1421. In 1444 the town belonged to the Catholic Habsburg Duchy of Austria and lived by Danube traffic, tolls and the wine of the Wachau and Kamp valley.

Krems's vintners' guild of St Paul was first recorded in 1447, the oldest such guild documented in the German-speaking lands. In 1463 Frederick III granted the town a new double-eagle arms and the privilege of building a Danube bridge. During the 16th century wealthy merchants on the Italy-to-northern-Europe route made Krems a centre of the Reformation, and by about 1600 it was almost entirely Protestant before the Counter-Reformation reimposed Catholicism. Swedish troops took the town in 1645 and imperial forces under Hans Christoph von Puchheim and Johann Wilhelm von Hunolstein retook it on 5 May 1646, with half its houses damaged or destroyed. The Baroque painter Martin Johann Schmidt, called Kremserschmidt, settled in Stein in 1756 and worked there until his death in 1801. At Dürnstein on 11 November 1805, Austro-Russian troops defeated Marshal Mortier's French corps outside Stein, a local success that could not save Austria after Austerlitz.
zh:
曼哈茨山是一道绵长山脊，隔开下奥地利西北部的森林高地与东面的葡萄种植丘陵；本省最富庶之处在南端多瑙河流经多瑙河畔克雷姆斯和瓦豪东缘的地方。克雷姆斯首见于995年记载，1014年已有教区，1130年代至1190年间设有巴本堡王朝铸币厂；邻近的施泰因在1200年前已是诸侯关税站，两地到1305年已有共同的成文城市法。11至12世纪时，克雷姆斯的规模几乎不亚于维也纳，但1421年阿尔布雷希特五世发动迫害，城中犹太社群被毁。1444年，克雷姆斯属于天主教的哈布斯堡奥地利公国，依靠多瑙河运输、关税，以及瓦豪和坎普河谷的葡萄酒为生。

克雷姆斯的圣保罗酿酒工行会首见于1447年记载，是德语地区有文献可考的最古老酿酒工行会。1463年，腓特烈三世赐给城市新的双头鹰纹章，并授予修建多瑙河桥的特权。16世纪，往来意大利与北欧商路的富商使克雷姆斯成为宗教改革中心，到1600年前后几乎全城都是新教徒，随后反宗教改革又恢复了天主教。三十年战争中，瑞典军队1645年攻占该城；1646年5月5日，汉斯·克里斯托夫·冯·普赫海姆与约翰·威廉·冯·胡诺尔施泰因率领帝国军队收复城市，但半数房屋已受损或被毁。巴洛克画家马丁·约翰·施密特（人称「克雷姆斯施密特」）1756年定居施泰因，在此创作直至1801年去世。1805年11月11日，奥俄联军在施泰因城外的迪恩施泰因击败莫蒂埃元帅的法国军团，但这场局部胜利未能挽回奥地利在奥斯特里茨之后的败局。

en:
The seat of the province is Litoměřice, where the Ohře joins the Elbe beneath the Central Bohemian Highlands. A Přemyslid stronghold crowned its cathedral hill, and the chapter founded there by Duke Spytihněv II in 1057 is the town's oldest written record; Ottokar I made it a royal city in 1219. Its staple right made every boat bound downstream for Pirna or Dresden unload and sell for three days, and in northern Bohemia its mile right was shared only with Žatec and Most. Charles IV endowed it richly, and the warm flatland round about was called the Garden of Bohemia. Tin was already worked at Krupka in the 1240s, when Matthew Paris complained that its tin was costing English metal its German markets, and forest glasshouses had sat in the Lusatian Mountains since the late 1200s. In 1426 the Hussites cut a crusader army to pieces at Ústí, and in April 1433 they stormed Krupka. In 1444 Litoměřice remains the first royal city of northern Bohemia, living on the Elbe carrying trade.

In 1537 a fire gutted part of the town, and in 1547 it backed the Bohemian estates' revolt against Ferdinand I. The Swedes used Litoměřice as a garrison and supply base in 1639–40 and again from 1643 to 1648; when the war ended, only 93 of its 597 houses were habitable. Re-Catholicisation came with the peace, and in 1655 the town became the seat of the newly founded diocese, while over the following century its records and schools turned from Czech to German. Through these same decades Bohemian cut and engraved glass led the luxury trade of Europe. Prussian troops occupied Litoměřice in 1757, and on 29–30 August 1813 the Austrian, Prussian and Russian armies defeated Vandamme's French corps at nearby Chlumec, opening the road to Leipzig.
zh:
本省的首府是利托梅日采，城在中波希米亚高地脚下、奥赫热河注入拉贝河之处。普热米斯尔王朝的要塞雄踞城中的教堂山，1057年斯皮季赫涅夫二世在此设立教士团，这是城市现存最早的文字记载；1219年奥托卡一世将其建为王家城市。它的「堆货权」规定，每一条顺流开往皮尔纳、德累斯顿的船都必须卸货并在本地市场售卖三天；而在北波希米亚，与它同享一哩专营权的城市只有扎泰茨和莫斯特。查理四世曾大量赐地给它，周围温暖的平原被称为「捷克花园」。1240年代克鲁普卡已在开采锡矿，马修·帕里斯曾抱怨那里的锡夺走了英国锡在德意志的销路；卢萨蒂亚山脉的密林里，13世纪末就已设有玻璃作坊。1426年胡斯派在乌斯季击溃一支十字军，1433年4月又攻陷克鲁普卡。1444年时，利托梅日采仍是北波希米亚首屈一指的王家城市，靠拉贝河的转运贸易为生。

1537年大火烧毁了部分城区，1547年城市又卷入波希米亚等级反抗斐迪南一世的起义。三十年战争中，瑞典人在1639至1640年、以及1643至1648年两度把利托梅日采当作驻军和补给基地；战争结束时，全城597栋房屋中仅93栋尚可居住。和议之后再天主教化随之而来，1655年城市成为新设教区的主教驻地；此后一个世纪里，城市的账簿和学校又从捷克语转为德语。也正是在这一百多年间，波希米亚的刻花玻璃在欧洲奢侈品贸易中首屈一指。1757年普鲁士军队占领该城；1813年8月29至30日，奥地利、普鲁士和俄国联军在附近的赫卢梅茨击败旺达姆的法国军团，打通了通往莱比锡的道路。

en:
Pozsony is the Danube province centred on Pressburg, the city now called Bratislava. Its castle guarded the crossing where the Morava meets the Danube, where Amber Road traffic met river commerce beneath the Little Carpathians. After becoming part of Hungary in the tenth century, Pressburg withstood Henry III's siege in 1052. Andrew III granted it town privileges in 1291, Sigismund enlarged them in 1405, and the town received its own coat of arms in 1436. In 1444 Pressburg was a Catholic free royal town of the Hungarian kingdom; German burghers dominated the walls and landing places, while Slovak villagers and Hungarian nobles lived in the surrounding grain country.

Matthias Corvinus confirmed Pressburg's liberties with a golden bull in 1464 and granted the town the sword right in 1468. Ottoman forces failed to take it after the Battle of Mohács in 1526, and in 1536 Pressburg became the capital of Royal Hungary. The Hungarian Diet met there from 1542, the archbishop of Esztergom moved his see there in 1543, and after the first coronation in 1563 the town served as Hungary's coronation city. The seventeenth century brought anti-Habsburg risings, Ottoman warfare and plague; the epidemic around 1711 killed about 3,860 people. Maria Theresa was crowned queen of Hungary there in 1741, and her reign filled the town with palaces before the walls were demolished in 1775. Joseph II moved the central offices to Buda and the crown jewels to Vienna in 1783. The Peace of Pressburg was signed in the Primate's Palace in 1805, Napoleon's troops besieged the city in 1809, and the castle burned in 1811.
zh:
波佐尼是多瑙河畔以普雷斯堡（今布拉迪斯拉发）为中心的省份。城堡扼守摩拉瓦河汇入多瑙河的渡口，小喀尔巴阡山下，琥珀之路商旅与多瑙河贸易在此相接。10世纪并入匈牙利后，普雷斯堡在1052年顶住亨利三世的围攻。1291年，安德拉什三世授予城市特权；西吉斯蒙德1405年扩大这些特权，城市又在1436年获得自己的纹章。1444年，普雷斯堡是匈牙利王国的天主教自由王城，城墙与码头内以德意志市民为主，城外谷物乡野间则住着斯洛伐克乡民和匈牙利贵族。

1464年，马加什·科尔温以金玺诏书确认普雷斯堡的自由，1468年又授予城市剑权。1526年摩哈赤之战后，奥斯曼军队未能攻下此城；1536年，普雷斯堡成为皇家匈牙利的首都。匈牙利议会自1542年在此召开，埃斯泰尔戈姆大主教1543年迁驻此地；1563年首次加冕后，这里又成为匈牙利国王的加冕城。17世纪，反哈布斯堡起事、奥斯曼战争和瘟疫反复消耗城市，约1711年的大疫造成3860人死亡。玛丽亚·特蕾西亚1741年在此加冕为匈牙利女王，她统治时期城中宫殿林立；1775年，城墙奉敕拆除。1783年，约瑟夫二世把中央机构迁往布达，并将王冠珍宝送往维也纳。1805年，《普雷斯堡和约》在总主教宫签署；1809年拿破仑军队围城，城堡则在1811年失火焚毁。

en:
Nafplio guards a rocky peninsula and one of the best harbours on the Argolic Gulf, with the Acronauplia heights above the town and the Argive plain at its back. Frankish crusaders took it in 1212 and made it part of the lordship of Argos and Nauplia; in 1388 that lordship was sold to Venice. During the following 150 years the Venetians enlarged the lower town, the port and the Acronauplia fortifications, treating Nauplia as one of their chief strongholds in the Levant. In 1444 this Greek Orthodox corner of the Morea was therefore a Venetian naval base, although the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea held much of the nearby peninsula.

The town repelled Ottoman sieges in the war of 1463-79 and again under Suleiman, but it surrendered to the Ottomans in 1540, was renamed Mora Yenişehri, and became an administrative seat. Venetian forces returned in 1686 during the Morean War and made Nafplio the capital of their Kingdom of the Morea, crowning the heights with the Palamidi fortress. An Ottoman campaign retook it in 1715, after which it again served as an administrative centre in the Morea. When the Greek revolt began in 1821, its garrison and sea-girt walls made Nafplio one of the principal Ottoman strongholds besieged by Greek forces.
zh:
纳夫普利翁扼守岩石半岛和阿尔戈利斯湾的优良港湾，城上是阿克罗纳夫普利亚高地，背后是阿尔戈斯平原。法兰克十字军于1212年夺取此地，将其并入阿尔戈斯与纳夫普利翁领地；1388年，这块领地被卖给威尼斯。此后150年间，威尼斯人扩建下城、港口和阿克罗纳夫普利亚防御工事，把纳夫普利翁视为他们在黎凡特最重要的据点之一。因此在1444年，摩里亚这个希腊东正教角落实际上是威尼斯海军基地，尽管邻近半岛的大片土地仍属拜占庭摩里亚专制国。

在1463至1479年的战争中，纳夫普利翁击退了奥斯曼围城，苏莱曼一世时期又再次守住，但最终于1540年投降。奥斯曼将其改名为摩里亚新城，并设为行政中心。1686年，威尼斯军队在摩里亚战争中卷土重来，把纳夫普利翁作为其摩里亚王国的都城，又在高地上修建帕拉米蒂城堡。1715年，奥斯曼军队再度攻占，此后这里继续充当摩里亚的行政中心。1821年希腊起义爆发时，凭借驻军和环海城墙，纳夫普利翁成为希腊军队围攻的主要奥斯曼据点之一。

en:
Treviso stands where the river Sile winds out of the Venetian plain towards the lagoon, the Roman Tarvisium, a municipium from 89 BC on the road between Opitergium and Aquileia. The Lombards made it one of their ducal seats with a busy mint, and Charlemagne made it capital of the March of Treviso. It joined the Lombard League and won its liberty at the Peace of Constance in 1183, after which Ezzelino da Romano and then the da Camino lords held the town, which even sheltered a short-lived university from 1318. The Scaliger of Verona occupied it in 1329, and in 1339 Treviso gave itself spontaneously to Venice, becoming the Republic's first notable possession on the Italian mainland. The peace of 1381 handed it to the duke of Austria and the Carraresi of Padua ruled it from 1384, but in 1388 it returned to Venice for good. In 1444 it is a loyal Venetian town ringed by walls and canals, its waterwheels grinding the grain of the March while the Republic's barges tie up at its river port.

Venetian rectors ruled the Trevigiano more closely than almost any other mainland province, and the walls were rebuilt under Fra Giocondo. The long peace broke only with the War of the League of Cambrai: in 1509 Treviso fortified afresh and became Venice's rallying point after Agnadello, and an Imperial and French siege was raised in 1511. The Serenissima then gave the city nearly three centuries of quiet prosperity, its barges and island fish market moving to the rhythm of the lagoon trade. In 1797 French troops under General Édouard Mortier took Treviso, and Napoleon later made him Duke of Treviso; the town passed to Austria in 1798 but was assigned to the Kingdom of Italy in 1806, and in 1814, with Napoleon's fall, it returned to Austria as part of the Kingdom of Lombardy–Venetia.
zh:
特雷维索坐落在西莱河从威尼托平原蜿蜒通向潟湖的水道上，罗马时代称塔尔维西乌姆，公元前89年成为自治城，地处连接奥皮泰尔吉乌姆与阿奎莱亚的大道旁。伦巴第人把它列为公爵驻地之一，设有繁忙的铸币厂，查理曼又将它定为特雷维索边区的首府。它加入伦巴第联盟，1183年凭康斯坦茨和约赢得自治，此后先后由埃泽利诺·达·罗马诺和达·卡米诺家族统治，1318年还曾短暂办过一所大学。1329年维罗纳的斯卡拉家族占领该城，1339年特雷维索主动归附威尼斯，成为共和国在意大利大陆的第一块重要领地。1381年的和约把它交给奥地利公爵，1384年起又被帕多瓦的卡拉雷西家族占据，1388年才永久回归威尼斯。1444年的特雷维索是一座忠诚的威尼斯城市，城墙与运河环绕，水轮带动磨坊碾磨边区的谷物，共和国的驳船在河港停靠。

威尼斯派来的行政长官对特雷维索一带控制之严，在大陆诸省中数一数二，城墙也由弗拉·乔孔多主持重修。长久的和平只被康布雷同盟战争打破：1509年特雷维索重新加固城防，在阿尼亚代洛惨败后成为威尼斯重整旗鼓的据点，1511年又顶住帝国与法国联军的围攻，迫使其撤围而去。此后共和国给了这座城市近三百年的平静繁荣，驳船和小岛上的鱼市随潟湖贸易的节奏运转。1797年，爱德华·莫尔蒂埃将军率法军占领特雷维索，拿破仑后来封他为特雷维索公爵；城市1798年归奥地利，1806年又被划入意大利王国，1814年随拿破仑败亡重归奥地利，成为伦巴第-威尼托王国的一部分。

en:
Holstein is the country between the Elbe and the Eider, named after the Holcetae, the Saxon 'wood-dwellers' recorded by Adam of Bremen. Its eastern corner on the Kiel Fjord was long the only Baltic outlet of the Schauenburg counts: Count Adolf IV founded Kiel there in 1233 as Holstenstadt tom Kyle, and his son John I granted it Lübeck law in 1242. Beyond the little Levensau lay Danish Schleswig, beyond the Schwentine the Slavic land of Wagria. Kiel helped found the Wendish city league in 1259 and entered the Hanse around 1283, yet its trade never approached Lübeck's, and in 1444 it was a small fortified market town serving as the capital of the County of Holstein under Count Adolf VIII of the Rendsburg line.

When Adolf VIII died without heirs in 1459, his nephew Christian I of Denmark first secured Schleswig and was then, elected by the estates at Ribe in 1460, recognised as lord of Holstein; in 1474 Emperor Frederick III raised the county to a duchy held directly of the Empire. From 1469 to 1496 Kiel itself was pledged to Lübeck, and the January fair called the Kieler Umschlag, first recorded in 1469, became the duchy's central market for goods and money. The Reformation reached the town in 1526 with Marquard Schuldorp, a Kiel burgher's son who had studied under Luther at Wittenberg, and after the ducal partition of 1544 Kiel passed to the Gottorp line, under which it lost its Hanse membership in 1554 for harbouring pirates. Duke Christian Albert founded the university in 1665, the northernmost in the Empire. In 1773 the Gottorp share of Holstein passed to the Danish crown in exchange for the County of Oldenburg, uniting the whole duchy under the king of Denmark as its duke. Swedish troops held Kiel during the 'Cossack winter' of 1813, and the Peace of Kiel was signed here in January 1814; in 1815 the duchy entered the German Confederation, still ruled in personal union by the Danish king.
zh:
荷尔斯泰因地处易北河与艾德河之间，名字得自不来梅的亚当所记载的萨克森部族霍尔克泰人，意为「林中居民」。其东端的基尔峡湾长期是绍恩堡伯爵们唯一的波罗的海出海口：1233年，阿道夫四世伯爵在此建城，当时称作「基尔的荷尔斯泰因人之城」，其子约翰一世于1242年授予它吕贝克法。莱文绍河对岸是丹麦的石勒苏益格，施文廷河对岸是斯拉夫人的瓦格里亚。基尔1259年参与创立文德城市同盟，约1283年加入汉萨同盟，但贸易始终远不及吕贝克；1444年时它只是一座设防的小集镇，作为荷尔斯泰因伯国的首府，处在伦茨堡系的阿道夫八世伯爵治下。

1459年阿道夫八世无嗣而终，他的外甥丹麦国王克里斯蒂安一世先取得石勒苏益格，又在1460年经里伯的等级会议选举被承认为荷尔斯泰因之主；1474年皇帝腓特烈三世把伯国升为直属帝国的公国。1469至1496年，基尔城本身被抵押给吕贝克；1469年首次见载的一月集市「基尔结算集市」后来成为公国货物与资金交易的中心。1526年，曾在维滕贝格师从路德的基尔市民之子马夸德·舒尔多普回乡任职，把宗教改革带到基尔；1544年公爵们瓜分领地后，基尔划归戈托普支系，1554年因窝藏海盗被汉萨同盟开除。1665年，克里斯蒂安·阿尔布雷希特公爵创办大学，这是神圣罗马帝国最靠北的大学。1773年，戈托普家族在荷尔斯泰因的份额以换取奥尔登堡伯国的方式归丹麦王室所有，整个公国统一在身兼公爵的丹麦国王治下。1813年「哥萨克之冬」，瑞典军队占领基尔，1814年1月《基尔和约》在此签订；1815年荷尔斯泰因加入德意志邦联，仍与丹麦身合。

en:
White Karelia is the northern, White Sea-facing part of Karelia, a thinly peopled country of rivers, lakes and forest reached by Orthodox Karelians moving north under Novgorod's influence; by the late fourteenth century they controlled this coast. At the mouth of the Kem River, Kem was a fishing landing and transit point for boats bound to the Solovetsky Islands. In 1444 its Karelian villagers were Orthodox subjects of Novgorod, living from fishing, trapping and the coastal exchange that would soon be organized around monastic salt works.

In 1450 Marfa Boretskaya donated Kem to Solovetsky Monastery. After Ivan III annexed Novgorod in 1478, the shore passed to Moscow while the monastery remained its local landlord. Kayan raiders devastated Kem in 1579 and 1580, and Swedes ravaged the district in 1590; the next year the crown granted the whole volost, with its peasants, salt houses and coastal trades, to Solovetsky. The monastery built a two-storey wooden fort there in 1657. Kem's wooden tent-roofed cathedral was raised in 1711–1717. Catherine II's secularization reforms brought the old monastic estate under the state in 1764, and on 16 May 1785 Kem was chartered as a district town.
zh:
白卡累利阿是卡累利阿北部面向白海的部分，河湖与森林广布，人烟稀少。信奉东正教的卡累利阿人在诺夫哥罗德影响下向北迁徙，到14世纪末已控制这片海岸。克米河注入白海处的克米是一处渔港，也是乘船前往索洛韦茨基群岛的中转地。1444年时，这里的卡累利阿村民是诺夫哥罗德的东正教属民，以捕鱼、捕猎和沿海交易为生，不久后这些营生又被修道院的盐场组织起来。

1450年，玛尔法·博列茨卡娅把克米捐赠给索洛韦茨基修道院。1478年伊凡三世吞并诺夫哥罗德后，这片海岸转入莫斯科之手，修道院仍是当地领主。1579年和1580年，卡扬袭击者两度洗劫克米，1590年瑞典人又蹂躏这一乡区；次年，沙皇将整个克米乡连同农民、盐坊和沿海营生一并赐给索洛韦茨基修道院。1657年，修道院在当地建起两层木堡。1711—1717年，克米建成木结构帐篷顶大教堂。1764年，叶卡捷琳娜二世的世俗化改革把旧修道院领地收归国家；1785年5月16日，克米被特许设为县治城镇。

en:
Kola commands the meeting of the Kola and Tuloma rivers where they enter Kola Bay. Sámi clans long lived there by fishing, hunting and reindeer herding, while from the twelfth century Pomor seafarers opened regular fishing grounds and bartered for furs. Novgorod's tribute collectors followed, and after the 1326 Treaty of Novgorod Norway gave up its claim to the peninsula, though Sámi communities sometimes paid tribute on both sides. In 1444 this was still a remote Novgorod land of tundra, river mouths and seasonal camps, valued for furs and fish rather than towns.

Novgorod lost the peninsula after Shelonsk in 1471 and its formal annexation by Moscow in 1478. Kola itself is first documented in 1565, when three households stood there; by 1573-1574 there were thirty-three. Its wooden ostrog was begun in 1583, resisted Sweden during the war of 1590-1595, and was recognized as Russian by the Treaty of Teusina in 1595. Pomors later sailed from Kola to Spitsbergen and Novaya Zemlya, and Peter I rebuilt the fortress during the Great Northern War after a Swedish squadron failed to take it. Made a district town in 1784, Kola was briefly occupied by a British landing party in 1809.
zh:
科拉位于科拉河与图洛马河汇入科拉湾的要冲。萨米氏族长期在此以捕鱼、狩猎和牧鹿为生；12世纪起，波莫尔海船开辟了固定渔场，并以货物交换毛皮。诺夫哥罗德的贡赋官随后到来。1326年《诺夫哥罗德条约》后，挪威放弃对科拉半岛的权利要求，但一些萨米社群仍同时向两边纳贡。1444年，这里仍是诺夫哥罗德治下遥远的冻原与河口地带，只有季节性营地；它的价值在毛皮和鱼类，而不在城镇。

1471年舍隆河战役后，诺夫哥罗德失去这片土地；1478年莫斯科正式吞并诺夫哥罗德。科拉本身首次见于文献是在1565年，当时只有三户人家，到1573年至1574年已有三十三户。木构要塞于1583年动工，在1590年至1595年战争中抵御了瑞典，并在1595年《特乌西纳条约》中被承认为俄罗斯所有。波莫尔人后来从科拉出航斯匹次卑尔根和新地岛；大北方战争期间，一支瑞典分舰队未能夺取此地，彼得一世随即重建要塞。1784年，科拉成为县治城市；1809年，一支英国登陆队曾短暂占领这里。

en:
Kasimov stands on the left bank of the Oka, in the forests and swamps of the Meshchyora. Yuri Dolgorukiy of Vladimir-Suzdal founded a border fortress there in 1152, Gorodets Meshchyorsky; the native Meshchyora Finns paid fur tribute and were gradually absorbed by Russian settlers and Turkic-speaking, Muslim Mishar Tatars. In 1362 the local Meshchera prince sold the town to Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow, and after it was sacked in 1376 it was rebuilt as Novy Nizovoy. In 1444 it was a small Muscovite outpost on the frontier facing the Kazan Tatars, its people a mix of Orthodox Russians and Sunni Mishars.

The grand princes soon turned it into a loyal Tatar buffer. After Vasily II was captured by the Kazan khan Ulugh Muhammad at Suzdal in 1445, and the Kazan princes Qasim and Yakub fled to Moscow, Vasily in 1452 granted Novy Nizovoy to Qasim: the Qasim Khanate, after whom the town was called Kasimov from 1471. Its khans and their guards marched with Moscow on every campaign against Kazan, including the conquest of 1552, and Shahghali was three times placed on the Kazan throne. After 1552 Russian voyevodas ran the khanate while khans still reigned; the last Kazan queen, Süyümbike, died there in exile, and the baptised khan Simeon Bekbulatovich was briefly paraded by Ivan the Terrible as a puppet grand prince. Forced Christianisation under Sayed Borhan (1627-1679) provoked a Tatar revolt in 1656. With the death of Queen Fatima Soltan in 1681 the khanate was abolished, leaving the khan's stone minaret and the royal mausolea of 1555 and 1658.
zh:
卡西莫夫位于奥卡河左岸，地处梅谢拉的森林沼泽之间。1152年，弗拉基米尔-苏兹达尔的尤里·多尔戈鲁基在此修建边境要塞戈罗杰茨梅晓尔斯基；土著的梅谢拉芬兰人以缴纳毛皮贡为生，逐渐被俄罗斯移民和操突厥语、信奉伊斯兰教的米萨鞑靼人同化。1362年，当地梅谢拉王公把这座城卖给莫斯科的德米特里·顿斯科伊，1376年城市遭劫后重建，改名新尼佐沃伊。1444年时，这里是莫斯科面向喀山鞑靼人的边境据点，东正教俄罗斯人与逊尼派米萨人杂居。

莫斯科大公很快把它变成忠诚的鞑靼缓冲。1445年瓦西里二世在苏兹达尔被喀山汗兀鲁·穆罕默德俘虏，喀山王公卡西姆与雅库布逃奔莫斯科，瓦西里二世遂于1452年把新尼佐沃伊封给卡西姆，卡西姆汗国由此建立，城市也从1471年起改称卡西莫夫。历代卡西姆汗率卫队参加莫斯科对喀山的每一次征战，包括1552年攻灭喀山之役，沙赫·阿里还曾三次被扶上喀山汗位。1552年以后汗国由俄罗斯督军治理，汗仍在位；喀山末代王后苏尤姆别卡被流放并死于此城，受洗的汗谢苗·别克布拉托维奇还被伊凡雷帝短暂抬出来充当傀儡大公。赛德·布尔罕在位时（1627—1679年）强行推行基督教化，引发1656年鞑靼人起义。1681年末代王后法蒂玛·苏丹去世，汗国被废除，只留下汗的石砌宣礼塔以及1555年和1658年的两座王陵。

en:
Komi is the great forest country of the Vychegda and Pechora basins, represented here by Yarensk on the Vychegda near the Yarenga. Komi-Zyryan hunters, fishermen and reindeer herders carried furs and hides along the old road from Novgorod toward the Urals. Stephen of Perm, sent from Moscow in 1365, created the Perm eparchy in 1383 and devised an alphabet for Komi; the chronicle first names the Yaren gorodok in 1384, when he founded a monastery there. Pagan Komi from Udora and Pinega burned and looted the house in 1389. In 1444 Yarensk was therefore a small Orthodox waystation and fur-collection point on the edge of a still largely pagan Komi wilderness.

In 1485 Ivan III confirmed the rights of local state peasants to hunting and fishing grounds around Yarensk in their dispute with the Perm bishops. The settlement remained a minor fortified station until 1606, when Vasily Shuisky sent the first voivode, Vasily Unkovsky, and made it the centre of Yarensky uyezd. A survey of 1628 records an ostrog above the Vychegda with a voivode's court, customs office, powder store and artillery. The river kept undermining the old hill, so in 1632 Michael I ordered the fort and posad moved to the Kizhmola; the transfer was carried out in 1635. Yarensk was placed in Siberian Governorate in 1708 and in Ustyug Province of Archangelgorod Governorate in 1719. When the academician Ivan Lepekhin visited in 1771, he found a poor, almost one-street town of 171 houses and three wooden churches, yet its uyezd stretched more than a thousand versts to the Pechora and Udora. By 1821 it was a remote imperial fur-road county town and place of exile.
zh:
科米是维切格达河与伯朝拉河流域的广袤林海，本省以维切格达河畔、邻近亚连加河的雅连斯克为代表。科米-济良猎人、渔民和养鹿人沿诺夫哥罗德通往乌拉尔的古道贩运毛皮。彼尔姆的斯捷凡1365年受莫斯科派遣传教，1383年促成彼尔姆教区，并为科米语创制文字；1384年，编年史首次记载雅连斯基城寨，斯捷凡同年在此建立修道院。1389年，来自乌多拉和皮涅加的异教科米人焚毁并洗劫了这座修道院。因此1444年时，雅连斯克是东正教在仍多奉本地信仰的科米荒野边缘设立的小驿站和毛皮收集点。

1485年，伊凡三世在雅连斯克周边国有农民与彼尔姆主教的争端中，确认农民对狩猎地和渔场的权利。1606年，瓦西里·舒伊斯基派遣首任督军瓦西里·温科夫斯基，雅连斯基城寨成为雅连斯克县中心，此前它只是小型设防站。1628年的调查册记载，维切格达河高地上有一座寨堡，内设督军院、海关、火药库和火炮。河水不断侵蚀旧丘，米哈伊尔一世遂在1632年下令把寨堡和城郊迁至基日莫拉河，迁移于1635年完成。1708年雅连斯克划入西伯利亚省，1719年改属阿尔汉格尔斯克省乌斯秋格专区。1771年，科学院学者伊万·列皮奥欣到访时，看到这座贫穷城镇几乎只有一条街，有171栋房屋和三座木教堂，但辖境却向伯朝拉河和乌多拉延伸一千多俄里。到1821年，它已是俄国北方毛皮商路上偏远的县城和流放地。

en:
Alasora rises on a hill in the central highlands of Madagascar, a country of marshes and rice valleys that generations of villagers drained with dikes and channels. The earlier people of the plateau were the Vazimba, and in the fifteenth century Hova clans moving up from the war-torn south-east settled among them, herding zebu and planting rice on the higher ground. In 1444 the land around the sacred hill was a patchwork of small fortified villages, their chiefs independent of one another and untouched by the Muslim trade reaching the coasts.

Tradition names Andriamanelo, who ruled at Alasora from about 1540 to 1575, as the founder of Imerina: he led the long wars that drove the Vazimba from the highlands, fortified his towns with moats and stone gates, armed his men with iron spears and set the noble andriana caste above the people. His son Ralambo (1575–1612) gave the country the name Imerina, introduced the royal talismans called sampy and the New Year feast of the fandroana, and made beef the meat of kings. Ralambo's son Andrianjaka seized the Vazimba hill of Analamanga and built the rova there that grew into Antananarivo, paying for his first firearms in cattle. The kingdom reached its early height under Andriamasinavalona (1675–1710), who raised the dikes of the Betsimitatatra rice fields and named his capital, but dividing the realm among four sons brought seventy-seven years of civil war. In 1787 Andrianampoinimerina began the work of reunion from Ambohimanga, took Antananarivo in 1793–94 and carried Merina arms down to the Betsileo country; his son Radama I, recognised as King of Madagascar by Britain in 1817, opened the highlands to European missionaries and traders.
zh:
阿拉索拉坐落在马达加斯加中部高地的一座山丘上，这一带沼泽与稻田交错，村民世代用堤渠排干洼地。高原上更早的居民是瓦津巴人；15世纪，霍瓦诸氏族从战乱的东南方迁入高地，与瓦津巴人杂处，牧养瘤牛，在高地上种稻。1444年时，这座圣山周围散布着各自设防的小村庄，首领互不统属，连抵达沿海的穆斯林贸易都不曾波及此地。

口传传统把约1540至1575年在阿拉索拉立国的安德里亚马内卢奉为伊梅里纳的奠基者：他发动长年战争把瓦津巴人逐出高地，用壕沟和石门加固村镇，让部众装备铁矛，并确立贵族安德里亚纳等级。其子拉兰博（1575–1612年在位）将国名定为伊梅里纳，引入王室护符桑皮和新年节法德罗阿纳，使牛肉成为王的肉食。拉兰博之子安德里安贾卡夺取瓦津巴人的阿纳拉曼加山，在山上建起罗瓦宫城，即后来塔那那利佛的雏形，并用牛换来第一批火器。王国在安德里亚马西纳瓦卢纳时代（1675–1710年）达到早期鼎盛：他加高贝齐米塔塔特拉稻田的堤坝，并为都城定名；但他把王国分给四个儿子，引发长达七十七年的内战。1787年，安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳从安布希曼加出发重新统一国土，1793至1794年攻占塔那那利佛，并把梅里纳兵锋南推至贝齐略之地；其子拉达马一世1817年获英国承认为马达加斯加王，向欧洲传教士和商人打开了高地。

en:
The lower Limpopo crosses a wide, hot coastal plain of swamp flats and open woodland before entering the Indian Ocean north of Delagoa Bay. Tonga clans of the Tsonga family kept cattle, fished the lagoons and planted sorghum and millet in villages along the river and its seasonal tributaries, while Hlengwe hunters of the inland thornveld tracked elephant across the great game flats. In 1444 their tusks were already carried overland to Muslim dhow traders at Inhambane and Delagoa Bay, but no European had yet entered the valley.

After the Portuguese opened a permanent factory at Inhambane in 1534, followed by the first Jesuit mission there in 1560, the lower Limpopo became one of the hunting grounds feeding its ivory trade, and Tonga chiefs and Hlengwe hunters also bartered tusks for cloth, beads and brass at Delagoa Bay. In the eighteenth century the traffic turned increasingly to slaves, bought on the coast by Portuguese and Indian merchants, and long droughts unsettled the old clans. Their world ended in the Mfecane: after Shaka broke the Ndwandwe on the Mhlatuze in 1820, Nguni war bands swept across the southern plains, and in 1821 the Ndwandwe leader Soshangane led his followers into the lower Limpopo, subduing the Tonga villages as the nucleus of the Gaza power named after his grandfather.
zh:
下林波波河穿过一片广阔炎热的沿海平原，两岸是沼泽低地和疏林，最后在德拉戈阿湾以北注入印度洋。聪加族系的通加诸部沿干流和季节性支流而居，牧牛捕鱼，种植高粱和谷子；内陆灌丛草原上的赫伦圭猎人则在广袤的猎场上追踪象群。1444年，他们猎得的象牙已被运往伊尼扬巴内和德拉戈阿湾，交给穆斯林独桅帆船的商人，而欧洲人还没有踏进这条河谷。

1534年葡萄牙人在伊尼扬巴内设立常设商馆，1560年又在那里建起第一处耶稣会传教站，下林波波河谷从此成为供给其象牙贸易的猎场之一，通加首领和赫伦圭猎人也在德拉戈阿湾以象牙交换布匹、珠子和黄铜。18世纪，这门生意越来越转向奴隶，由葡萄牙和印度商人在海边收购，连年干旱又使旧有诸部动荡不安。他们的世界终结于姆费卡内：1820年恰卡在姆拉图泽河击溃恩德旺堆后，恩古尼战团横扫南方平原，1821年，恩德旺堆首领索尚加内率部进入下林波波，征服通加村寨，这支以其祖父名号命名的加扎势力就此在河谷中扎下根基。

en: Só'taeo'o is the self-name of one of two closely related Algonquian peoples known to outsiders as Cheyenne, but in 1444 this dry western edge of the Badlands is still a Shoshone frontier. Numic bands moving east from the Great Basin hunt bison on foot, use dog travois and camp through severe winters before horses reach the northern plains. After the 1680 Pueblo Revolt horses spread through the region, and the mounted Shoshone branch moving south was called Comanche in Spanish records by 1706. The Só'taeo'o later moved west from the upper Missouri, adopted tipis, horse herds and bison hunts, and ranged into Wyoming and the Black Hills country; about 1730 the Cheyenne passed horses to Lakota bands. In 1742–43 Louis-Joseph and François de La Vérendrye crossed present Wyoming and sighted the Rockies without founding a post. By 1776 Lakota pressure had taken much of the Cheyenne Black Hills country, and in 1821 the creek crossings and bison ranges were still controlled by mounted Native camps rather than European settlers.
zh: 索塔埃奥是两支关系密切、被外界统称为夏安人的阿尔冈昆人群之一的自称；但在1444年，恶地西缘这片干旱高地仍是肖肖尼人的前沿。来自大盆地的努米克游群向东移动，徒步猎野牛、用狗拉拖橇，在严寒中扎营，此时马尚未进入北方平原。1680年普韦布洛起义后，马匹在这一地区传播，南下的骑马肖肖尼分支到1706年已被西班牙文献称作科曼奇人。索塔埃奥人后来从密苏里河上游西迁，改用梯皮、马群和野牛狩猎，活动范围进入怀俄明与布莱克山一带；约1730年，夏安人把马匹传给拉科塔游群。1742—1743年，路易-约瑟夫与弗朗索瓦·德·拉韦朗德里穿越今怀俄明并望见落基山，但没有建立据点。到1776年，拉科塔人的压力已夺取夏安人在布莱克山附近的大片土地；1821年，这些溪河渡口和野牛场仍由骑马的原住民营地控制，欧洲裔定居者尚未建立城镇。

en:
The Saskatchewan (Cree kisiskāciwani-sīpiy, 'the swift-flowing river') is formed by the meeting of its northern and southern branches and winds east for some 340 miles through forest, marsh and island-dotted lakes to Lake Winnipeg. On its lower reaches the boreal woods give way to aspen parkland, and Cree bands kept their summer fisheries at places like The Pas, taking sturgeon and whitefish, hunting moose and beaver in the forest and running buffalo on the prairie edge, while their Assiniboine allies held the open plains to the south. In 1444 no European had yet seen the river; the Cree travelled it by canoe and dog-train along a highway of their own.

Henry Kelsey of the Hudson's Bay Company set out from York Factory in June 1690 and reached Deering's Point, near The Pas, on 10 July after thirty-three portages; in 1691 he pushed south on to the prairie with Cree companions and on 20 August became the first European to see buffalo and grizzly bears there, returning to the bay in 1692. Louis-Joseph de La Vérendrye reconnoitred the lower Saskatchewan for France in 1739, and in 1741 French traders built Fort Bourbon at the mouth of the river and Fort Paskoya at The Pas. Anthony Henday descended the valley in 1755 after wintering on the plains, but the posts were abandoned after the fall of New France. In 1774 Samuel Hearne built Cumberland House, the company's first permanent inland post and later the depot for the route to the Athabasca country. Smallpox swept the river camps in 1781–82, and a North West Company post faced Cumberland House from 1793 until the two companies united in 1821.
zh:
萨斯喀彻温河在克里语中作 kisiskāciwani-sīpiy，意为「湍急之河」，由北支与南支汇合而成，向东蜿蜒约340英里，穿过森林、沼泽和岛屿密布的湖泊，注入温尼伯湖。下游一带针叶林渐变为杨树林草原：克里人各氏族夏天在帕斯等地的渔场捕捞鲟鱼和白鱼，入林猎驼鹿、捕河狸，又到草原边缘围猎野牛；南面的开阔高原则属于他们的盟友阿西尼博因人。1444年时还没有任何欧洲人见过这条河，克里人驾独木舟、带狗橇往来其上，是这条水道唯一的主人。

1690年6月，哈得孙湾公司的亨利·凯尔西从约克工厂出发，经33处水陆转运，于7月10日抵达今帕斯附近的迪灵角；1691年他随克里人南下进入草原，8月20日成为最早在那里见到野牛和灰熊的欧洲人，并于1692年返回海湾。1739年，路易-约瑟夫·德·拉韦朗德里为法国踏勘了萨斯喀彻温河下游，1741年法国商人在河口建起波旁堡，在帕斯建起帕斯科亚堡。1755年，安东尼·亨迪在草原越冬后顺河谷东归；新法兰西覆灭后这些堡垒均遭废弃。1774年，塞缪尔·赫恩修建坎伯兰豪斯，这是哈得孙湾公司在内地的第一座永久商站，后来成为通往阿萨巴斯卡地区的补给中枢。1781至1782年天花横扫沿河营地；1793年西北公司在坎伯兰豪斯对岸设立商站与之竞争，直至两家公司于1821年合并。

en:
Pathein, the old Bassein, sits on a western branch of the Irrawaddy more than a hundred kilometres from the sea, yet ocean-going ships can make their way up to its quays, making it the deepest inland seaport in Burma. The Mon knew it as Phasem and Pali inscriptions as Kusima, the Cosmim of later Portuguese charts; a Sri Lankan inscription of 1165 mentions the town, and in 1180 a fleet of Parakramabahu I of Polonnaruwa raided it during his war with Pagan. With the rise of the Mon kingdom of Hanthawaddy in the fourteenth century the swampy delta was opened to settlement and commerce, and Pathein grew into one of its principal ports, a market for the rice of the surrounding country and for ships from India and the Malay world. In 1444 it belonged to the Mon kings who ruled from Pegu.

In 1534 Tabinshwehti of Toungoo began his raids into the delta. Pegu fell in 1538, and late in that year Bayinnaung destroyed a Hanthawaddy army at Naungyo, somewhere in the delta flats; after Martaban was taken in 1541 Pathein passed under Toungoo rule. The port kept its trade: the Portuguese still marked it on their charts as Cosmim, and Arab merchants grew numerous there in the sixteenth century. In 1740 the delta became part of the Mon restoration of Hanthawaddy, but in May 1755 Alaungpaya's Konbaung armies overran the Irrawaddy delta, two years before Pegu itself fell. By the early nineteenth century Burman settlers and Karen migrants had made the old Mon town a Burman rice market, and few Mon remained.
zh:
勃生（旧称巴森）位于伊洛瓦底江一条西支的河畔，虽距大海一百多公里，海船仍可直抵码头，是缅甸最深入内陆的海港。孟人称之为帕森，巴利文碑铭称其为库西马，后来的葡萄牙海图则写作科斯明；1165年的一块斯里兰卡碑铭已提到此城，1180年，波隆纳鲁沃的波罗迦罗摩巴忽一世在对蒲甘的战争中派舰队劫掠了这里。14世纪孟人勃固王国兴起后，这片沼泽三角洲得到开垦和通商，勃生成为王国的主要港口之一，是本地稻米与来自印度、马来群岛船只的交易之所。1444年，它属于以勃固为都的孟人国王。

1534年，东吁的德彬瑞梯开始侵扰三角洲。1538年勃固陷落，同年晚些时候莽应龙在三角洲平原上的瑙约击溃勃固大军；1541年马达班陷落后，勃生归入东吁治下。港口贸易依旧：葡萄牙海图仍把它标作科斯明，16世纪在此经商的阿拉伯商人也越来越多。1740年，三角洲成为孟人复兴的勃固王国的一部分，但1755年5月雍笈牙的贡榜军队横扫伊洛瓦底三角洲，比勃固城陷落还早两年。到19世纪初，随着缅人移民和克伦人迁入，这座孟人古城已变成缅人的稻米集镇，孟人所剩无几。

en:
Beijing sits on the northern plain with mountains on three sides, commanding the Great Wall passes into the Chinese heartland. As Ji it was the capital of the state of Yan in the Warring States age, and as Youzhou a Tang frontier command from which An Lushan rose in 755. The Khitan Liao made it their southern capital Nanjing in 938, and the Jurchen Jin made it Zhongdu in 1153, until the Mongols sacked the city in 1215 and Kublai Khan built his capital Dadu on the site. Ming armies took Dadu in 1368 and renamed it Beiping, the fief of Zhu Di, Prince of Yan. As the Yongle Emperor he renamed the city Beijing in 1403 and raised the Forbidden City from 1406 to 1420, moving the court north from Nanjing in 1421. In 1444 Beijing was the Ming capital, the grain fleets of the Grand Canal feeding a city already among the largest in the world, with the steppe and the Wall just beyond its gates.

Five years later the Oirats captured the Zhengtong Emperor at Tumu, and in October 1449 Esen's army was at the walls; the minister Yu Qian organized the defense and drove it off. In 1550 Altan Khan of the Tümed forced the Gubeikou pass and raged beneath the walls after his bid for trade was refused, and in 1551 the Ming opened horse markets at Xuanfu and Datong. In 1626 the Wanggongchang gunpowder depot blew up in the south-west of the city, killing more than 20,000, and a great plague in 1643 took over 200,000 lives. On 25 April 1644 Li Zicheng's army entered Beijing and the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself on Coal Hill; forty days later Dorgon's Manchus entered unopposed and made the city the Qing capital, quartering the Eight Banners in the inner city. Jesuit astronomers served the new court, and in 1652 Catholics raised a church on the site of Matteo Ricci's chapel, while the emperors laid out the Old Summer Palace and other gardens to the north-west. In 1813 Lin Qing led two hundred Eight Trigrams sectarians through gates opened by bribed eunuchs into the Forbidden City itself before they were cut down.
zh:
北京三面环山、面朝华北平原，扼守着长城诸关通往中原的门户。战国时为燕国都城蓟城，唐代为幽州边防重镇，755年安禄山即由此起兵。938年契丹辽朝以这里为陪都南京，1153年女真金朝定都中都，1215年蒙古军破城，后来忽必烈在原址营建大都。1368年明军攻取大都，改称北平，封给燕王朱棣。朱棣经靖难之役即位后，1403年改北平为北京，1406至1420年营建紫禁城，1421年正式把朝廷从南京北迁。1444年的北京是大明京师，大运河的粮船供养着这座已是世上最大的城市之一，城门外不远便是草原与长城。

仅仅五年之后，瓦剌在土木堡俘走明英宗，1449年十月也先大军进抵北京城下，兵部尚书于谦主持京师保卫战将其击退。1550年，土默特部首领俺答汗求贡互市被拒，自古北口入塞、兵临北京城下，大掠而退，明朝次年开放宣府、大同等处马市。1626年，城西南工部王恭厂火药库发生大爆炸，死伤两万余人；1643年的大鼠疫又使二十多万人丧生。1644年4月25日李自成军进入北京，崇祯帝在煤山自缢；四十天后多尔衮率满洲大军兵不血刃入城，定北京为清朝京师，八旗分驻内城。耶稣会天文学家在新朝供职，1652年天主教在利玛窦经堂旧址建起教堂，清帝又在西郊营建圆明园等离宫园林。1813年，林清率天理教信徒二百人，由买通的宦官开门，竟攻入紫禁城内，随即被剿灭。

en:
Nan occupies a remote basin at the Nan River's mountain sources, with old tracks leading south toward Sukhothai and east toward Luang Prabang. Phaya Phu Kha founded Wora Nakhon at Mueang Pua around 1282, and the Phukha dynasty moved its capital to the present Nan valley in the 14th century. The small mueang kept more contact with Sukhothai than with the other northern states, yet its isolation allowed the local dynasty to survive. In 1444 Kaen Thao still ruled Nan after using a false report of a Vietnamese invasion to draw in Tilokaraj of Lan Na and murder the ruler of Phayao.

Tilokaraj turned on his unreliable ally and, by the Thai chronicle dating of 1450, Nan was brought into Lan Na. Burmese armies opened a longer period of overlordship in 1560, and repeated local attempts to break away ended with direct Burmese rule from 1714. From 1726 Luang Tin Mahawong ruled Nan apart from Burmese-governed Chiang Mai, but the little principality later had to acknowledge Konbaung Burma and then Siam's Thonburi court. In 1788 the ruler of Nan went to Bangkok and entered the tributary order of Rama I, leaving his dynasty to govern the valley as a semi-autonomous Siamese principality.
zh:
楠府位于难河源头群山环抱的偏远盆地，旧路南通素可泰，东通琅勃拉邦。约1282年，帕雅·普卡建立以勐普瓦为中心的沃拉那空，普卡王朝后来在14世纪把都城迁到后世难城所在的河谷。这个小勐与素可泰的往来多于北方诸邦，偏僻地势也使本地王朝得以延续。1444年，孔涛仍是楠府的统治者；此前他谎称越南来犯，借兰纳国王滴洛拉阇之手除掉了帕尧国王。

滴洛拉阇随后转而对付这个不可靠的同盟者；按泰文史料纪年，楠府于1450年并入兰纳。1560年，缅甸军队开启了更长期的宗主权，当地人多次谋求独立均告失败，1714年起更直接受缅甸统治。1726年，銮廷玛哈旺使楠府脱离缅甸控制下的清迈而自治，但这个小邦后来仍先后向贡榜缅甸和暹罗吞武里宫廷称臣。1788年，楠府统治者前往曼谷，加入拉玛一世的藩属秩序，其王朝此后作为半自治的暹罗诸侯统治这片河谷。

en:
Chikuzen lies on the Hakata Bay side of northern Kyushu, facing the Korea Strait. Its port of Hakata had served Dazaifu, the island's mainland-facing administrative center, and after the first Mongol landing burned the town in 1274, a stone rampart was raised along the bay. In the Muromachi period Hakata was largely governed by its wealthy merchants; ships traded to Ming China, Korea and the Ryukyus, bringing back raw silk and copper cash. A contemporary reckoning described about ten thousand households in two quarters, Oki no Hama under Otomo protection and Hakata Hama under the Shoni. In 1444, therefore, Chikuzen was rich from continental trade and caught among the Otomo, Shoni and Ouchi houses.

Ouchi Masahiro drove the Shoni out of Hakata in 1478, and the port became a prize in Ouchi trade with Ming China; rival Japanese missions clashed at Ningbo in 1523. After Ouchi Yoshitaka fell in the 1551 revolt of Sue Harukata, Otomo Sorin took the city, but warfare burned Hakata again in 1559, 1580 and 1586. Toyotomi Hideyoshi rebuilt it after his Kyushu campaign of 1587, appointing Ishida Mitsunari as magistrate and drawing on merchants Kamiya Sotan and Shimai Soshitsu for the Taiko street plan. After Sekigahara, Kuroda Nagamasa received Chikuzen in 1600 and built Fukuoka Castle from 1601 to 1607 across the Naka River from merchant Hakata. The Korean potter Hachizan, brought back by the Kuroda, opened the Takatori kiln around 1600; under Kuroda Tadayuki its tea vessels found favor with Kobori Enshu. As seclusion narrowed overseas commerce, Hakata continued as a coastal shipping and domain merchant town.
zh:
筑前位于九州北部、博多湾沿岸，面向朝鲜海峡，首府博多是日本通往大陆的门户。博多曾是大宰府的外港；1274年第一次元军登陆并烧毁市区后，博多湾沿岸筑起石垒。室町时代，博多大体由富商自治，商船前往明朝、朝鲜和琉球，购回生丝和铜钱。当时的记载称港内息滨约六千户、博多滨约四千户，分别受大友氏和少贰氏保护。因此到1444年，筑前靠着大陆贸易致富，也夹在大友、少贰和大内等豪强之间。

1478年，大内政弘将少贰势力逐出博多，博多成为大内氏对明贸易的要地；1523年，大内与细川的遣明船又在宁波相争。1551年大内义隆因陶晴贤谋反而败死后，大友宗麟控制博多，但战火又在1559年、1580年和1586年一再烧毁市区。1587年丰臣秀吉平定九州后复兴博多，任命石田三成为奉行，并依靠神屋宗湛、岛井宗室等商人实施太阁町割。关原之战后的1600年，黑田长政受封筑前，1601年至1607年在那珂川对岸修筑福冈城，与商人之城博多隔河相对。黑田氏带回的朝鲜陶工八山约在1600年开高取窑；到黑田忠之时，高取茶器得到小堀远州赏识。锁国之后，海外贸易收窄，博多转为回船中转港和藩内商人市镇。

en:
Tosa, or Doshū, is the southern province of Shikoku, a long Pacific coast backed by steep, thickly forested mountains whose rivers, the Shimanto among them, float timber down to the sea. The name first appears in the Nihon Shoki in 675, and its remoteness made it a land of exile from the Asuka age: Minamoto no Mareyoshi, Fujiwara no Moronaga and the Emperor Tsuchimikado were all banished here. Court and temple manors, above all the Ichijō family's great Hata estate in the west, drew what wealth the province had, while Hosokawa shugo governed through deputies and stayed in Kyoto. In 1444 real power lies with local warrior houses in their mountain valleys, owing little more than nominal service to absent governors.

The Ōnin War even brought the capital to Tosa: in 1468 the former kampaku Ichijō Norifusa withdrew from the war-torn Kinai to his Hata manor at Nakamura, and his son Fusaie laid out a little Kyoto there, with the same street names and courtly airs, ruling western Tosa from the Nakamura Palace. The east was fought over by the seven warrior houses of Tosa, until the Chōsokabe of Okō Castle overbore the Motoyama and the rest: Motochika expelled his overlord Ichijō Kanesada to Bungo in 1574, shattered his comeback at the Shimanto River in 1575, and by 1585 was master of all Shikoku. Hideyoshi's invasion that same year broke him in a single campaign and left him only Tosa; his son Morichika joined the western army at Sekigahara in 1600 and was attainted. The province then passed to Yamauchi Kazutoyo, who built Kōchi Castle and laid out its castle town, and the Yamauchi ruled Tosa to the end of the Tokugawa age, balancing their imported upper samurai against the local gōshi retainers.
zh:
土佐别称土州，地处四国南部，濒临太平洋的海岸线漫长，内陆是陡峭而密林遍布的山地，四万十川等河流把山中木材顺流送入大海。「土佐」之名最早见于《日本书纪》675年的记载，因地处偏远，自飞鸟时代起便是流放之地，源希义、藤原师长、土御门天皇都曾被遣送至此。这里的财富主要归于公家与寺院的庄园，其中以一条家在西部幡多的大庄园为最；细川氏虽任守护，却委派代理、长住京都。1444年的土佐，真正的权力落在山谷间的国人豪族手中，对远在京都的统治者不过是名义上的恭顺。

应仁之乱甚至把京城本身带到了土佐：1468年，前关白一条教房为避开战火，在大平等国人的接应下来到幡多庄园中村，其子房家照京都的街巷格局建起一座「小京都」，以中村御所号令土佐西部。东部则是土佐七雄的鏖战之地，直到以冈丰城为据点的长宗我部氏压过本山氏等群雄：元亲1574年把主君一条兼定逐往丰后，1575年又在四万十川之战击溃兼定的反扑，到1585年已号令整个四国。同年秀吉发动四国征伐，一战便将其压回土佐一国；其子盛亲1600年在关原之战中加入西军，战败后被除封。土佐随后封给山内一丰，他建起高知城与城下町；山内氏让随封而来的上士与当地乡士并用，在这种微妙的等级平衡中统治土佐，直至江户末年。

en:
Awa, or Ashū, fills the northeast of Shikoku between the Yoshino River and the Kii Channel, where the whirling Naruto strait faces the Kinai across the water, the nearest shore of Shikoku to Osaka Bay. The north of the province was once called the Millet Country for the grain of its river valley, and in 713 its name was fixed as Awa. The Sasaki and Ogasawara held the shugo post in the Kamakura age; under the Muromachi shoguns it passed to the Hosokawa, one of the three kanrei houses, whose Awa vassals the Miyoshi, based at Shōzui Castle, grew steadily stronger. In 1444 Awa is counted a 'superior country' of the old codes, its Yoshino valley rich, its lords the Hosokawa, and its future already stirring in Miyoshi ranks.

The Miyoshi overtook their masters in the Sengoku years: serving as the Hosokawa kanrei's chief men, Miyoshi Yukinaga and Motonaga reached into Kyoto, and under Nagayoshi the brothers ruled Awa, Awaji and Sanuki while he governed the Kinai as deputy kanrei. That power collapsed when the brothers and Nagayoshi's heir died in quick succession and Nagayoshi himself, a sick and broken man, died in 1564; Nobunaga destroyed the main line in 1573. Chōsokabe Motochika of Tosa then invaded and brought Awa under him in 1584, but in 1585 Hideyoshi's 100,000-strong army landed in the province and within two months confined Motochika to Tosa. Awa went to Hachisuka Iemasa, who built Tokushima Castle at the Yoshino mouth in 1586 and laid out its castle town, and the open bon dances he is said to have licensed in 1586–1587 are remembered as the origin of the Awa dance. Forced into the tonsure on Kōyasan by Ishida at Sekigahara, he was restored by Ieyasu; his son Yoshishige fought at Osaka and from 1617 held Awa with all Awaji at 257,000 koku. Indigo spread along the lower Yoshino under the Hachisuka, and the Awa indigo merchants grew rich enough to patronize the puppet theatre and music of the later Tokugawa towns.
zh:
阿波别称阿州，位于四国东北部，吉野川横贯其间，北隔鸣门激流与畿内相望，是从大阪湾进入四国的第一站。其地古时北部因盛产粟谷称「粟国」，713年正式定名为阿波。镰仓时代佐佐木氏、小笠原氏先后担任守护；室町时代这里成为三管领之一细川氏的领国，而以胜瑞城为据点的细川家臣三好氏日渐坐大。1444年的阿波在律令中位列上国，吉野川河谷丰饶，名义上仍由细川氏统治，三好氏的野心已在家臣团中悄然滋长。

战国乱世，三好氏反客为主：三好之长、元长几代人作为管领细川氏的重臣进军京都，到三好长庆一代势力达到极盛——诸弟分领阿波、淡路、讃岐，长庆本人以管领代身份在京都把持畿内大权。然而短短数年间诸弟与嫡子义兴相继死去，安宅冬康又被长庆诛杀，精神失常的长庆本人也于1564年病故，三好政权随之内乱瓦解，嫡流1573年被织田信长消灭。土佐的长宗我部元亲趁机攻入，1584年征服阿波；但1585年丰臣秀吉的十万大军在阿波登陆，两个月内便迫使元亲退回土佐一国。阿波封给蜂须贺家政，他1586年在吉野川口筑起德岛城并规划城下町，相传1586至1587年间他特许的无礼讲盆舞，便是阿波舞的起源之一。关原之战时家政被石田三成逼迫出家、幽居高野山，战后由德川家康恢复旧领；其子至镇从军大阪之阵立功，1617年起领有阿波与整个淡路，合计二十五万七千石。蜂须贺氏治下，吉野川下游广种蓝草，阿波蓝商富甲一方，资助了江户后期城镇上的人形净琉璃与三味线艺能。

en:
Nanjing, the old Jiankang on the Qinhuai River, was capital of the Six Dynasties and of the Southern Tang, and seat of empire once more when Zhu Yuanzhang took the city in 1356 and, as the Hongwu Emperor, proclaimed the Ming there in 1368. He girdled it with more than thirty kilometres of walls and raised the Ming Xiaoling mausoleum; the Longjiang shipyard below the walls built the great ships of the treasure voyages, while the glazed pagoda of the Great Bao'en Temple, seventy-eight metres high and supervised by Zheng He, rose between 1412 and 1428. In 1421 the Yongle Emperor moved his court to Beijing, and in 1441 Nanjing was settled as the secondary capital, keeping a shadow set of the six ministries. In 1444 it remained the grand metropolis of the south, its white porcelain tower visible far off on the Yangtze.

Through the middle and later Ming the city grew rich on private silk looms, fan shops and publishing houses, and the Qinhuai riverbank became the most famous pleasure quarter in the empire. Matteo Ricci and the Jesuits found a footing here until the Nanjing Incident of 1616–17 drove the missionaries out to Macao. After Beijing fell in 1644 the Prince of Fu was enthroned in Nanjing as the Hongguang Emperor of the Southern Ming, but on 6 June 1645 Prince Dodo's Qing army entered almost unopposed. Yingtian became Jiangning, seat of the Liangjiang governor-general, and from 1649 a walled banner city occupied the ruins of the Ming palace; in 1659 the great siege by Zheng Chenggong was beaten back from the gates. Under the high Qing, Jiangning held more than 30,000 satin looms, the Imperial Silk Manufactory supplied the court and served as a palace on the southern tours, and the Jiangnan examination compound already seated 7,500 candidates in 1630.
zh:
南京古称建康，雄踞秦淮河畔，曾是六朝与南唐的都城。1356年朱元璋攻取集庆、改称应天，1368年在此登基建立明朝，南京再度成为一统王朝的京师。他下令营建周长三十余公里的城墙和明孝陵，城外龙江船厂为郑和下西洋建造巨舶，1412至1428年又由郑和督造，建成高七十八米的大报恩寺琉璃塔。1421年永乐帝迁都北京，1441年正式定南京为陪都，保留一套名义上的六部机构。1444年的南京仍是南方最宏大的都会，白色琉璃塔在长江之滨熠熠生辉。

明中后期，南京的民间丝织、制扇与刻书业日益富庶，秦淮河畔成为全国最负盛名的风月之地。利玛窦等耶稣会士曾在此立足，但1616至1617年的南京教案将传教士逐往澳门。1644年北京陷落后，福王朱由崧在南京即位，建立南明弘光朝廷；1645年6月6日多铎的清军几乎兵不血刃进入南京。应天随后改名江宁，成为两江总督驻地，1649年起又在明故宫旧址筑起驻扎八旗的满城；1659年，郑成功率大军围攻江宁，被清军击退。清代盛世时的江宁有缎机三万余张，江宁织造署供应皇家缎匹，并在皇帝南巡时充当行宫；江南贡院在1630年已能容纳七千五百名生员应考。

en:
Suzhou rose beside Lake Tai as Gusu, the capital of the kingdom of Wu, where King Helü settled his court in 514 BC. The Grand Canal made it a great manufacturing and trading metropolis, and in 1356 the warlord Zhang Shicheng made the city his royal capital; Zhu Yuanzhang took it only after a ten-month siege in 1367, renamed it Suzhou Prefecture under the Southern Metropolitan Region, and loaded its old families with crushing taxes. The city was too wealthy to keep down. In 1444 it was the foremost silk town of the Ming, crowded with weavers and embroiderers, its boats and markets strung along the canals, while the Xushuguan toll station outside the walls returned the second-largest customs revenue of the empire's eight main customs houses.

When the shipwrecked Korean official Choe Bu passed through in 1488, he judged Suzhou to surpass every other city in China. In the middle Ming its silk rooms, where merchants supplied the capital and weavers their labour, marked the rise of a workshop economy, and retired officials built the private gardens that made the city famous: Wang Xianchen laid out the Humble Administrator's Garden in 1509, and the Wu-school master Wen Zhengming painted thirty-one views of it in 1533. In 1626 the townspeople rose against the Embroidered Uniform Guard arresting the respected gentleman Zhou Shunchang; thirteen men were seized and five executed, remembered at the Five Men's Tomb. Under the Qing the Jiangsu provincial administration moved to Suzhou in 1661, the city ranked among the empire's four great commercial centres, the Fengqiao quays became the largest grain market in the land, and thirty-four of the 204 zhuangyuan of the Ming and Qing came from the prefecture.
zh:
苏州濒临太湖，春秋时为吴国都城姑苏，公元前514年吴王阖闾在此筑城。大运河开通后，这里成为东南的手工业与商贸大都会。1356年，割据一方的张士诚以苏州为都城，1367年朱元璋围城十个月才将其攻灭，随后改置苏州府，隶属南直隶，并对城中故家大族课以重税。但苏州很快恢复了富庶：1444年的苏州是明朝首屈一指的丝绸之城，织工绣户栉比，市肆沿河道展开，城外的浒墅关在全国八大钞关中税收名列第二。

1488年，遭遇海难的朝鲜官员崔溥漂流来华、途经苏州，在游记中称天下城市无出其右。明中后期，城中出现「机户出资、机工出力」的机房，成为手工工场兴起的标志；致仕官员纷纷营造私家园林，御史王献臣于1509年始建拙政园，吴门画派大师文徵明据传曾参与构思，并在1533年依园中景物绘图三十一幅、各系以诗。1626年，锦衣卫到苏州逮捕触怒魏忠贤的乡绅周顺昌，市民奋起殴击官旗，事后十三人被捕、五人就义，乡人立五人墓纪念他们。入清后，江苏布政使司于1661年移驻苏州，苏州位列「天下四聚」之一，枫桥米市成为全国最大的粮食交易市场，明清两代二百零四名状元中，苏州府独占三十四名。

en:
Stung Treng—Xiang Taeng to the Lao, the 'river of reeds' in Khmer—marks the point where the Mekong, coming down from the Lao lands, cuts through the last hills into the Cambodian plain and the Sekong, Sesan and Srepok join it from the eastern forests. Under the kings of Angkor this was the northern gateway of the empire, a string of river villages growing rice on the banks while Brao and Kavet highlanders brought cardamom, wax and ivory out of the woods. As the court withdrew south after the sack of 1431, the middle Mekong fell within the orbit of Lan Xang; in 1444 its chiefs still owned allegiance to the Khmer king at Chaktomuk while sending tribute upriver as well.

For three centuries Xiang Taeng lived by the river road, its markets serving Khmer, Lao and Chinese merchants plying between Vientiane and the Khmer capitals. When Sourigna Vongsa, the last strong king of Lan Xang, died in 1694, a nephew backed by a Vietnamese army seized the throne, and the southern lands broke away: in 1713 they became the kingdom of Champasak, with Bassac, Attapeu and Stung Treng as its chief centers. Taksin of Siam broke Champasak in 1777 and made it a vassal the next year, and by 1800 the river route carried cardamom, resin, hides and forest goods from the east bank to Khorat and Bangkok. In 1821 the 'river of reeds' answered to Bangkok through the kings of Champasak, its people Khmer, Lao and highlanders, its old tie to the Khmer crown little more than memory.
zh:
上丁，老挝语称「相当」，高棉语意为「芦苇之河」。湄公河自寮国之地南下，在此穿过最后一片丘陵进入高棉平原，公河、桑河、斯雷博河也从东部林莽间汇入。吴哥诸王时代，这里是帝国的北部门户，沿河村寨种稻为业，森林里的布劳、加维山民以豆蔻、蜂蜡、象牙出山交易。1431年吴哥遭劫、朝廷南迁之后，湄公河中游落入澜沧的势力范围；1444年时，这里的酋长仍承认四臂湾高棉国王的名分，同时也向北方入贡。
