洛兰与法尔斯特由狭窄的古尔堡海峡相连，是横在朗厄兰岛与西兰岛之间两座低平肥沃的岛屿，土壤为丹麦之最，田土却几乎尽归大庄园。文德海盗曾频频袭扰这片海岸，12世纪末人们在尼克宾筑起城堡扼守海峡；1253年吕贝克军队攻破城堡、焚毁城镇，1368年至1370年的丹麦-汉萨战争中，汉萨诸城再度围攻此堡。纳克斯考由12世纪的渔村发展为两岛首镇，现存最早的城市特许状可追溯到1266年，商人与北德诸城贸易不绝。1416年，圣布里吉特会在马里博创建修道院，1419年波美拉尼亚的埃里克又在尼克宾设立方济各会修道院。1444年，洛兰与法尔斯特是丹麦治下信奉天主教的王属岛屿，财富出自谷物、牲畜和渔业，农民所受的庄园束缚已是全国最重。

1446年，洛兰地方法庭颁行《洛兰规约》（Lollands Vilkår），强化贵族权利，并首次在丹麦把佃农束缚在庄园土地上。1510年吕贝克人焚毁纳克斯考；1534年伯爵战争中，尼克宾和马里博都站在克里斯蒂安二世一边，1530年代宗教改革又使修道院相继解散。腓特烈二世的遗孀梅克伦堡的索菲自1588年起在尼克宾新建的文艺复兴式城堡统辖整个洛兰-法尔斯特，直至1631年去世。1658年，卡尔十世·古斯塔夫的军队从朗厄兰踏冰登岛；1659年瑞典军久围攻克纳克斯考，城池残破，人口折损一半。战后，纳克斯考成为丹麦最早允许犹太人定居的城镇之一；1780年代起，本地大贵族雷文特洛主持王室的农业改革，废除农民的人身依附，使佃农逐步走上购地自营之路。

en:
North Jutland lies around the Limfjord, joining Aalborg's narrow crossing with the farmlands of Vendsyssel, Thy and the old bishopric of Viborg. Aalborg held trading privileges from 1342, renewed by Eric of Pomerania in 1430 and Christopher of Bavaria in 1441; its merchant guild is recorded from 1431, and late-fourteenth-century Budolfi Church stood above a harbour busy with Norwegian and North Sea traffic. Viborg had been a bishopric from about 1060 and housed five monasteries in the Middle Ages. In 1444 the province was a Catholic world of herring catches, cattle markets and strong commercial towns.

Christian II granted Aalborg a monopoly on salting Limfjord herring in 1516, deepening a trade that reached England and the Baltic. Reformation began in Viborg while Hans Tausen preached there in 1525-1529, and the first Danish church received leave to hold Lutheran services. During the Count's Feud, Skipper Clement made Aalborg his base before Johan Rantzau stormed the town in December 1534; as many as 2,000 people died, and the monasteries were closed in 1536. Aalborg became a Lutheran bishopric in 1554, prospered until the mid-seventeenth century despite imperial occupation in 1627-1629, and suffered a serious fire in 1663. Viborg's great fire of 1726 destroyed its cathedral and eastern quarter. Aalborg grew again in the later eighteenth century, then lost much of its Norwegian trade when Denmark ceded Norway in 1814.
zh:
北日德兰环绕利姆海峡，连接奥尔堡的狭窄渡口与温叙塞尔、蒂的农地以及古都维堡教区。奥尔堡1342年获得贸易特权，又分别于1430年和1441年得到波美拉尼亚的埃里克与巴伐利亚的克里斯托弗确认；当地商人行会1431年已有记载，14世纪末的圣布多尔菲教堂俯瞰着往来挪威和北海的繁忙港埠。维堡约1060年成为主教驻地，中世纪时拥有五座修道院。1444年，这片省份是天主教世界的一部分，以鲱鱼捕捞、牛市和富庶商业城镇闻名。

1516年，克里斯蒂安二世授予奥尔堡腌制利姆海峡鲱鱼的垄断权，使这项远达英格兰和波罗的海的贸易更加深厚。1525年至1529年汉斯·陶森在维堡布道，宗教改革由此展开，当地一座教堂成为第一所获准举行路德宗礼拜的丹麦教堂。伯爵战争期间，克莱门特船长以奥尔堡为基地；1534年12月，约翰·兰曹攻破城市，多达两千人丧生，修道院也于1536年被关闭。1554年，奥尔堡成为路德宗主教驻地。尽管1627年至1629年曾遭帝国军队占领，城市仍繁荣到17世纪中叶，1663年又遭遇大火。1726年，维堡大火摧毁了大教堂和城市东区。18世纪后期奥尔堡再度发展，但1814年丹麦割让挪威后，它失去了大量对挪威贸易。

en:
Närke is a small inland province of plains and forests between Hjälmaren and Vättern. Its peasants paid grain, butter and pork, while the northern mining hundreds produced osmund iron. Örebro grew where a gravel bank made the Svartån fordable, carrying roads between Västergötland, Värmland, Bergslagen and the Mälaren basin, while Hjälmaren opened a water route to the east. The trading town held privileges by 1404. Its royal fortress on an islet in the river, probably raised under Magnus Eriksson in the mid-fourteenth century, gathered taxes and withstood repeated sieges. Engelbrekt's rebels took it in 1434, and he held Örebro as a fief from 1435 until his murder the next year. In 1444 it was Catholic Sweden's fortified bridge market on the road to the interior.

Gustav Vasa's forces retook Örebro from the Danes on 30 January 1522, and in 1529 the Örebro Synod met there as Sweden's first evangelical church assembly, stopping short of a complete break with Rome. Under Duke Charles, later Charles IX, the town gained a monopoly over the regional iron trade; its merchants exported Bergslagen iron and carried food back to the miners. Works in 1596–1605 recast the old fortress as a Renaissance residence, and an arms factory was founded around 1600. In 1653, during famine, about fifteen Närke crofters rose against conscription and heavy taxes in the Morning Star rebellion; the movement was quickly crushed and its leaders executed. On 21 August 1810 the diet at Örebro elected Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte crown prince of Sweden, and on 18 July 1812 Britain and Russia concluded their peace treaty in the town.
zh:
内尔克是耶尔马伦湖与韦特恩湖之间一片不大的内陆平原和林乡。农户缴纳谷物、黄油和猪肉，北部矿区百户区则出产奥斯蒙德铁。厄勒布鲁起于斯瓦特河上一处砾石浅滩，道路由此连接西约特兰、韦姆兰、贝里斯拉根和梅拉伦湖区，耶尔马伦湖又提供东去水路。这座商镇在1404年前已获特权。河心小岛上的王家要塞可能建于14世纪中期马格努斯·埃里克松在位时，用于征税并抵御反复围攻。恩厄尔布雷克特的起义军1434年夺取要塞，他本人从1435年起受封厄勒布鲁，次年遇刺。1444年，这里是天主教瑞典通往内地道路上一座设防的桥梁商镇。

1522年1月30日，古斯塔夫·瓦萨的军队从丹麦人手中夺回厄勒布鲁；1529年，厄勒布鲁会议在此召开，这是瑞典第一次福音派教会会议，但尚未与罗马彻底决裂。后来的卡尔九世、当时的卡尔公爵治下，商镇取得地区铁业专卖权：商人输出贝里斯拉根的铁，再把粮食运回矿区。1596—1605年，旧要塞被改建为文艺复兴式宅邸，约1600年这里又设立兵工厂。1653年荒年，约十五名内尔克佃农因征兵和重税发动晨星起义，起事很快被镇压，首领遭处决。1810年8月21日，议会在厄勒布鲁选举让-巴蒂斯特·贝尔纳多特为瑞典王储；1812年7月18日，英国与俄国又在此签订和约。

en:
New Caledonia centres on Grande Terre, the long mountainous island ringed by reefs; future Nouméa occupies a sheltered south-western peninsula above a deep lagoon roadstead. Lapita potters reached the Koné coast around 1300–200 BC, and their settlements, joined by later Melanesian currents, became the Kanak clans. In 1444 those clans fished the lagoon, cleared rotating gardens, raised yams on ridges and watered taro terraces. Society was ordered by clan and customary land rather than by one island-wide ruler, while marriage, alliance and exchange voyages linked neighbouring districts and islands.

Outside ships did not know the reef until Cook's second voyage. On 4 September 1774 James Colnett sighted Grande Terre from HMS Resolution; James Cook named it New Caledonia after Caledonia, the Latin name for Scotland, and the expedition met Kanaks at Balade the next day before following the east coast to the Isle of Pines on 23 September. In 1788 Lapérouse probably examined the west coast shortly before his disappearance. D'Entrecasteaux's search expedition passed the Isle of Pines and the southern coast in June 1792, then surveyed the west coast in April and May 1793. Contacts remained sparse for the rest of the period; in 1821 the future Nouméa roadstead was still Kanak water, with no mission, fort or trading post.
zh:
新喀里多尼亚以格朗德特尔岛为中心，这座狭长多山的大岛被礁群环绕；未来的努美阿坐落在西南半岛，俯瞰潟湖中隐蔽的深水锚地。拉皮塔陶工约在公元前1300年至前200年抵达科内海岸，他们的定居点与后来的美拉尼西亚人流汇合，形成后世的卡纳克诸氏族。1444年，这些氏族在潟湖捕鱼，开辟轮垦园圃，堆垄种植薯蓣，并引水浇灌芋艿梯田。社会按氏族和传统领地组织，没有统辖全岛的首领；婚姻、联盟和交换航行则把邻近地区与岛屿连接起来。

直到库克第二次远航，外来船只才知道这片礁群。1774年9月4日，詹姆斯·科尔内特在「决心号」上望见格朗德特尔岛；詹姆斯·库克以苏格兰的拉丁名喀里多尼亚将其命名为新喀里多尼亚。远征队次日在巴拉德与卡纳克人接触，随后沿东海岸南下，9月23日抵达松树岛。1788年，拉彼鲁兹很可能在失踪前不久察看了西海岸。当特尔卡斯托的搜救队1792年6月经过松树岛和南岸，又在1793年4月至5月测绘西海岸。此后接触仍零散；到1821年，未来努美阿的锚地仍是卡纳克人的水域，没有传教站、要塞或商馆。

en:
The Society Islands divide into the Windward and Leeward groups, linking Tahiti and Moʻorea with Raʻiātea, Huahine, Bora Bora and smaller volcanic islands. Polynesians had settled them by around 1000, and Raʻiātea's Taputapuātea marae became a chief ceremonial centre of eastern Polynesian navigation and priesthood. High chiefs traced descent from the gods, ruled through councils and supported the red-feather cult of ʻOro. In 1444 the islands were bound by language, marriage and voyaging, but divided among competing chiefdoms, with no single ruler over Tahiti, Raʻiātea or Bora Bora.

European contact began when Wallis landed on Tahiti in 1767. Bougainville followed in 1768, and Cook in 1769 named the Leeward cluster the Society Islands. Spanish expeditions from Peru established a short-lived mission on Tahiti in 1774-1775. Iron, firearms and British trade then altered the balance between rival chiefs. The London Missionary Society reached Tahiti on the Duff in 1797 and backed the Pōmare line; Pōmare II's victory at Te Feipī in 1815 made Tahiti and Moʻorea the core of a Christian kingdom. The missionary William Pascoe Crook founded Papeete on its sheltered roadstead in 1818, while Raʻiātea, Huahine and Bora Bora remained separate Polynesian powers when Pōmare II died in 1821.
zh:
社会群岛分为向风群岛和背风群岛，把塔希提、莫雷阿与赖阿特阿、胡阿希内、波拉波拉等火山岛连成一片。波利尼西亚人约在1000年已定居于此，赖阿特阿的塔普塔普阿泰马拉埃成为东波利尼西亚航海与祭司体系最重要的仪式中心。大酋长宣称神灵血统，依靠议事会施政，并扶持以红羽腰带为象征的「奥罗」崇拜。1444年的诸岛共用语言、互结婚姻并保持远洋往来，却分属相互竞争的酋长领地，塔希提、赖阿特阿和波拉波拉之上并无共主。

欧洲接触始于1767年沃利斯在塔希提登陆。布干维尔1768年随后来访，库克1769年把背风岛群命名为社会群岛。1774年至1775年，秘鲁派出的西班牙远征队在塔希提设立了短暂存在的传教站。此后，铁器、火枪和英国贸易改变了敌对酋长间的力量对比。1797年伦敦传道会乘「达夫号」抵达塔希提，支持波马雷家族；波马雷二世1815年在特费皮战役获胜，使塔希提和莫雷阿成为一个基督教王国的核心。1818年，传教士威廉·帕斯科·克鲁克在避风锚地旁建立帕皮提。波马雷二世1821年去世时，赖阿特阿、胡阿希内和波拉波拉仍是独立的波利尼西亚势力。

en:
Rapa Nui is a remote triangular volcanic island in the south-eastern Pacific. Polynesian voyagers settled it around 1200, honouring ancestors on coastal ahu platforms and carving the great moai at Rano Raraku. By the fifteenth century its lineage groups had formed two confederations: the western and northern Tuʻu, whose royal Miru line centred Anakena, and the eastern ʻOtu ʻItu. In 1444 rival clans still raised statues under the ancestor cult, while chiefs, priests and warriors ordered the affairs of this isolated island.

Around 1680 the huri moʻai period opened as images were toppled, and spiritual prestige shifted toward the tangata manu competition at Motu Nui. On 5 April 1722 Jacob Roggeveen reached the island on Easter Sunday, anchored in the long bay that became Hanga Roa, and named it Easter Island. The ʻOtu ʻItu fought the Tuʻu for control from 1724 to 1750. Felipe González de Ahedo arrived on 15 November 1770, made the first Spanish chart, named the island San Carlos and claimed it for Spain, but left no garrison. Cook visited in 1774 and La Pérouse in 1786. In 1821 Rapa Nui still had no European colonial government; its clans and bird-man ritual retained local power.
zh:
拉帕努伊是东南太平洋上一座遥远的三角形火山岛。波利尼西亚航海者约在1200年前后定居于此，在海岸的阿胡石台上供奉祖先，并从拉诺拉拉库采石场雕运巨大的摩艾石像。到15世纪，岛民按血缘组成两大联盟：西部和北部属图乌，王室米鲁世系以阿纳基纳为中心，东部则属奥图伊图。1444年，相互竞争的氏族仍在祖先崇拜下竖立石像，大酋长、祭司和武士维系着这座孤立岛屿的秩序。

约1680年，推倒石像的「胡里摩艾」时期开始，精神权威也逐渐转向在莫图努伊小岛举行的「唐加塔马努」，即鸟人竞赛。1722年4月5日复活节，雅各布·罗赫芬抵达该岛，停泊在日后成为安加罗阿的长湾，并将其命名为复活节岛。1724年至1750年，奥图伊图与图乌为控制全岛交战。1770年11月15日，费利佩·冈萨雷斯·德·阿埃多到达，绘制最早的西班牙海图，把岛屿命名为圣卡洛斯并宣布归属西班牙王室，却没有留下驻军。库克1774年、拉彼鲁兹1786年先后到访。1821年的拉帕努伊仍无欧洲殖民政府，氏族和鸟人仪式继续掌握本地权力。

en:
Muʻa stands on the eastern lagoon of Tongatapu, its villages of Lapaha and Tatakamotonga fronting the waters from which Tongan voyaging canoes sailed across the central Pacific. As the seat of the Tuʻi Tonga, it was the ceremonial heart of a maritime polity whose influence reached toward Fiji, Samoa, Uvea, Futuna and Niue; chiefly visitors brought tribute at the ʻinasi first-fruits ceremony, while the tiered coral langi tombs proclaimed the sacred ruler's ancestry. In 1444 the Tuʻi Tonga still dwelt at Lapaha, and the wealth of the islands moved through canoes, fishponds, plantations and exchange rather than through European trade.

Around 1470 Moʻungāmotuʻa founded the Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua line and took political power, leaving the Tuʻi Tonga as a sacred figure at Lapaha; the new court's followers became the low-road people, while the old court remained the inland-road people. Around the turn of the seventeenth century the Tuʻi Kanokupolu line emerged as another great chiefly power. Dutch mariners Willem Schouten and Jacob Le Maire made the first recorded European visit in April 1616, and Abel Tasman reached Tongatapu and Haʻapai in 1643. James Cook attended an ʻinasi in 1773 and named Tonga the Friendly Islands. In April 1799 Fīnau ʻUlukālala II's faction killed the Tuʻi Kanokupolu Tukuʻaho at Muʻa, opening fifty years of civil war. The ship Port-au-Prince was taken in Haʻapai in 1806, and Fīnau used its cannon against Nukuʻalofa in 1807; after his death in 1809 Haʻapai and Vavaʻu drew away from Tongatapu. In 1821 Muʻa remained a sacred capital, but Tonga was ruled in practice by rival chiefs.
zh:
姆阿位于汤加塔布岛东侧潟湖畔，拉帕哈和塔塔卡莫通加两村临水而立，汤加人的远洋独木舟正是从这片水域驶往中太平洋。作为图伊汤加的驻地，这里是一个海上政权的礼仪中心，其影响远及斐济、萨摩亚、乌韦阿、富图纳和纽埃；各地首领在「伊纳西」初果礼上进贡，层叠的珊瑚朗吉王陵则宣示神王的世系。1444年，图伊汤加仍住在拉帕哈，群岛的财富通过独木舟、鱼塘、种植园和交换流通，还没有欧洲贸易介入。

约1470年，蒙加莫图阿开创图伊哈塔卡拉瓦王朝并接掌政治权力，图伊汤加则留在拉帕哈保有神圣地位；新朝廷的追随者成为「低路人」，旧王廷则为「内陆路人」。17世纪初前后，图伊卡诺库珀鲁一系又崛起为另一股强大首领势力。1616年4月，荷兰航海者威廉·斯考滕和雅各布·勒梅尔留下欧洲人首次到访的记录；1643年，亚伯·塔斯曼抵达汤加塔布和哈阿派。1773年，詹姆斯·库克参加「伊纳西」礼，将汤加称为友谊群岛。1799年4月，菲瑙·乌卢卡拉拉二世一派在姆阿刺杀图伊卡诺库珀鲁图库阿霍，开启长达约五十年的内战。1806年，「太子港号」在哈阿派被夺，菲瑙又在1807年用船上火炮进攻努库阿洛法；他1809年死后，哈阿派和瓦瓦乌逐渐脱离汤加塔布。1821年，姆阿仍是神圣都城，但汤加实际已分由相互争战的首领统治。

en:
Tuvalu is a scattered chain of three reef islands and six atolls in the central South Pacific. Polynesian voyagers spreading from the Samoa-Tonga sphere settled eight of the islands; the name Tuvalu means 'eight standing together', while Niulakita remained outside that older pattern. Small communities drew their living from coconuts, fish and the reef, and canoe voyages linked neighbouring atolls with Samoa and Tonga. In 1444 the islands were known only within that Polynesian sea world and had not yet entered European charts.

On 16 January 1568 Álvaro de Mendaña sighted Nui and charted it as Isla de Jesús, but he did not land. During his second Pacific voyage he passed Niulakita on 29 August 1595 and named it La Solitaria. John Byron mapped part of the group as the Lagoon Islands in 1765, and Francisco Mourelle sailed past Nanumea and Niutao in 1781. In May 1819 Arent Schuyler de Peyster named Funafuti Ellice's Island, a name later extended to the whole archipelago; even then European contact remained brief and irregular.
zh:
图瓦卢是散布在南太平洋中部的三座礁岛和六个环礁。波利尼西亚航海者经萨摩亚、汤加一带向外扩展，在其中八座岛屿上定居，「图瓦卢」一名意为八座并肩而立，尼乌拉基塔则不在这一古老格局之内。各小岛社群依靠椰子、渔获和珊瑚礁为生，独木舟航路连接邻近环礁以及萨摩亚、汤加。1444年时，这些岛屿只存在于波利尼西亚人的海洋世界中，尚未出现在欧洲人的海图上。

1568年1月16日，阿尔瓦罗·德·门达尼亚望见努伊，将其标为「耶稣岛」，但没有登陆。第二次横渡太平洋时，他又在1595年8月29日经过尼乌拉基塔，命名为「孤岛」。1765年，约翰·拜伦把其中一部分环礁绘入「潟湖群岛」；1781年，弗朗西斯科·莫雷列经过纳诺梅阿和纽陶。1819年5月，阿伦特·斯凯勒·德佩斯特把富纳富提命名为埃利斯岛，这个名称后来扩及整个群岛；即便此时，欧洲人的接触仍短暂而零星。

en:
Tarawa is a coral atoll in the Tungaru or Gilbert chain, its islets strung around a broad lagoon with an unusually large ship passage. Gilbertese seafarers had settled the Gilberts by around 200 BC, sailing between atolls in locally built canoes and reading the swells and stars. On this central island, authority belonged less to permanent chiefs than to elder councils and the descent groups who held each strip of land. In 1444 Tarawa's villages subsisted on lagoon fish, coconuts, pandanus and swamp taro, bound to neighboring atolls by marriage, feud and voyaging.

On 20 June 1788 Thomas Gilbert, captain of the East India Company ship Charlotte, reached Tarawa and became the first European to describe it. He did not land, naming an islet Matthew Island and the lagoon Charlotte Bay; his sketches survive. In 1820 Adam Johann von Krusenstern gave the whole chain Gilbert's name, but no foreign administration yet touched Tarawa.
zh:
塔拉瓦是通加鲁（吉尔伯特）群岛中的一座珊瑚环礁，一串小岛环绕宽阔潟湖，并有一条异常宽大的航道可供船只出入。吉尔伯特航海者约在公元前200年已定居吉尔伯特群岛，他们驾驶本地建造的独木舟，在环礁之间依涌浪和星象航行。在这座中部岛屿上，权威更多属于长老议事会和掌握各条土地的世系群，而非固定首领。1444年，塔拉瓦各村以潟湖渔获、椰子、露兜树和沼泽芋为生，并通过婚姻、仇怨与航行同邻近环礁相连。

1788年6月20日，东印度公司商船「夏洛特号」船长托马斯·吉尔伯特抵达塔拉瓦，成为首位描述这座环礁的欧洲人。他没有登岛，只把一座小岛命名为马修岛、把潟湖命名为夏洛特湾，他的草图后来得以保存。1820年，亚当·约翰·冯·克鲁森施滕以吉尔伯特之名称呼整个群岛，但此时还没有外来行政机构触及塔拉瓦。

en: Nauru, called Naoero in its own language, is a small raised coral island set far apart from its neighbours. Long isolation produced a distinct Nauruan language and a society of twelve matrilineal clans, remembered in the island's twelve-pointed star. Families caught young milkfish and raised them in the sheltered waters of Buada Lagoon, supplementing that staple with coconuts and pandanus fruit. In 1444 the island managed its own reef, lagoon and clan lands without any outside power. In 1798 the British captain John Fearn sailed past in the Hunter and named it Pleasant Island, but through 1821 European contact remained only a distant prospect.
zh: 瑙鲁在本族语言中称诺埃罗，是一座远离邻近岛屿的隆起珊瑚岛。漫长的孤立孕育出独特的瑙鲁语，也形成十二个按母系追溯血统的氏族，岛旗上的十二角星正纪念这些氏族。居民捕捞幼虱目鱼，在受遮蔽的布阿达潟湖水中养育，再以椰子和露兜树果实补充食物。1444年时，这座岛的珊瑚礁、潟湖和氏族土地都由岛民自行管理，不受外来政权支配。1798年，英国船长约翰·费恩乘「猎手」号经过，将它命名为快乐岛，但直到1821年，欧洲人的接触仍只是遥远的可能。

en:
The Marshalls consist of twenty-nine coral atolls and hundreds of islets in the parallel Ratak, or Sunrise, and Ralik, or Sunset, chains. Majuro in Ratak is a ring of sixty-four islets around a lagoon of about 295 square kilometres; earth ovens at Laura show Marshallese use there around the first century AD. Settlers brought coconuts, breadfruit, giant swamp taro and chickens, and sailed walap canoes by stars and the way swells bent around hidden reefs, training pilots with stick charts. Chiefs called iroij held land and tribute, while paramount iroijlaplap dominated whole chains. In 1444 the wetter southern atolls supported denser taro and breadfruit villages, and the drier north lived chiefly from pandanus and coconuts.

On 21 August 1526 Alonso de Salazar, sailing in the surviving Spanish ship of the Loaísa expedition, sighted a northern atoll and named it San Bartolomé. Álvaro de Saavedra visited Ujelang and Enewetak in 1528, but later galleons generally kept to routes farther north. The British captain John Marshall explored through the islands in 1788, and the group later received his name. When Otto von Kotzebue arrived in 1817, Marshallese society still showed little European influence and remained under its own paramount chiefs.
zh:
马绍尔群岛由二十九座珊瑚环礁和数以百计的小岛组成，分属东西并行的拉塔克（日出）礁链与拉利克（日落）礁链。首府马久罗位于拉塔克链，六十四座小岛围出约二百九十五平方公里的潟湖；劳拉地方的地炉遗迹表明，马绍尔人约在公元1世纪已在此活动。定居者带来椰子、面包果、大沼泽芋和鸡，驾驶瓦拉普独木舟，凭星象以及涌浪绕开暗礁后的折转航行，并用木棒海图训练航海者。土地和贡纳掌握在称「iroij」的酋长手中，最高酋长「iroijlaplap」则统辖整条礁链。1444年，较湿润的南部环礁有更密集的沼泽芋和面包果村落，干旱的北部则主要依靠露兜树与椰子。

1526年8月21日，洛艾萨远征队中幸存西班牙船的指挥官阿隆索·德·萨拉萨尔望见一座北部环礁，将其命名为圣巴托洛缪。1528年，阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉又到访乌杰朗和埃内韦塔克；但后来的西班牙大帆船多改走更北航线。英国船长约翰·马歇尔于1788年穿过这片群岛，整个群岛后来便以他的姓氏命名。1817年奥托·冯·科策布抵达时，马绍尔社会仍很少见到欧洲影响，继续处在本地最高酋长治下。

en:
Wake is a remote coral atoll of three islets, Wake, Wilkes and Peale, set around a shallow lagoon north of the Marshalls. It has no reliable fresh water, and archaeologists have found no proof of permanent ancient settlement. Yet the Polynesian rat and Marshallese traditions of Ānen Kio, the island of the kio flower, suggest that voyagers knew the reef: parties from the southern atolls are said to have crossed there to hunt seabirds and collect albatross bones for tattooing. In 1444 Wake was therefore an uninhabited waypoint in a sea that Marshallese canoemen could still read.

The first recorded European sighting came on 2 October 1568, when Álvaro de Mendaña de Neira, sailing north after reaching the Solomon Islands, found a low, waterless island with seabirds and bushes but neither coconuts nor pandanus and named it San Francisco. Captain Samuel Wake of Prince William Henry rediscovered the atoll in 1796 and left it his name. Through 1821 no power occupied Wake or built on its reef.
zh:
威克是马绍尔群岛以北的偏远珊瑚环礁，由威克、威尔克斯和皮尔三座小岛围绕浅水潟湖而成。岛上没有可靠淡水，也未发现古人永久定居的实物证据。不过，波利尼西亚鼠的存在以及马绍尔人关于「Ānen Kio」（基奥花之岛）的传说，都表明航海者知道这座礁岛：据说南部环礁的人会渡海前来捕猎海鸟、收集信天翁骨用于纹身。1444年的威克因此无人常居，却是马绍尔独木舟航海者仍能辨识的海上落脚点。

1568年10月2日，阿尔瓦罗·德·门达尼亚·德·内拉在抵达所罗门群岛后北航，首次有文字记载地望见这座低平岛屿。他发现岛上无淡水，只有海鸟和灌木，没有椰子或露兜树，于是将其命名为圣弗朗西斯科。1796年，「威廉·亨利王子号」船长塞缪尔·威克重新发现这座环礁，并以自己的姓氏命名。直到1821年，仍没有任何政权占领威克或在礁上营建。

en:
Pohnpei is the high volcanic island at the heart of the Senyavin group in the eastern Carolines, its rainy slopes rising above a reef and lagoon. From the 8th or 9th century islanders built Nan Madol on artificial islets off the eastern shore, linking stone platforms and ceremonial enclosures with canals. By the 15th century this coast was the centre of the centralized Saudeleur order: all land was held under chiefs, five tribes were each led by two principal chiefs, and tribute, raiding and banishment sustained local power. In 1444 Pohnpei was still beyond European charts.

The Spanish navigator Álvaro de Saavedra sighted the island on 14 September 1529 while seeking a route back to New Spain, charting it as San Bartolomé. Pedro Fernandes de Queirós passed on 23 December 1595 without landing. Pohnpeian tradition places the end of Saudeleur rule around 1628, when the more decentralized nahnmwarki chiefships took shape. Ships did not establish a foreign post, and in 1821 the island remained governed by its own chiefs, canoes and tribute networks.
zh:
波纳佩是东加罗林群岛谢尼亚温群岛核心的火山岛，多雨的山地耸峙在礁盘与潟湖之上。从8或9世纪起，岛民在东岸外的人工小岛上修建南马多，以运河连接石台和祭祀围墙。到15世纪，这片海岸已是集权的绍德雷尔秩序中心：土地在名义上归首领所有，五个部落各由两名大首领统领，贡赋、袭掠和放逐维系着地方权力。1444年时，波纳佩仍未出现在欧洲人的海图上。

1529年9月14日，西班牙航海者阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉在寻找返回新西班牙的航路时望见此岛，将其标为圣巴托洛梅。1595年12月23日，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯经过附近，但没有登陆。波纳佩传统把绍德雷尔统治的终结定在1628年前后，此后形成更为分权的南姆瓦尔基首领制度。欧洲船只并未在此建立商馆或据点；到1821年，岛屿仍由本地首领、独木舟航路和贡赋网络支配。

en:
Palau's western Carolinian chain centres on Babeldaob, a high volcanic island facing the smaller, densely settled island of Koror across a narrow channel. Austronesian seafarers had settled its coasts by the last millennium BC; over the centuries they cut hillside terraces, raised basalt and coral platforms, and linked compact villages with stone paths. A village centred on its painted bai, or meeting house, while caves on southern Babeldaob and northern Koror supplied crystalline limestone to Yapese canoe expeditions. The disks they quarried became rai stones, ceremonial wealth carried back to Yap by canoe or raft. In 1444 Palau had no European administration or mission, and power rested with Palauan chiefs and villages.

The first recorded European sighting of the main islands came at the end of January 1543, when Ruy López de Villalobos's Spanish expedition charted Babeldaob, Koror and Peleliu as Los Arrecifes. After Palauan castaways reached Samar in December 1696, the map Paul Klein sent in 1697 stirred Jesuit interest, but missions attempted in 1700, 1708 and 1709 failed. Francisco Padilla reached the islands on 30 November 1710, and two priests left on Sonsorol were later killed. British shipping then brought more regular contact: after the East India Company vessel Antelope was wrecked off Ulong in 1783, Henry Wilson took Lee Boo, son of the Koror ruler Abba Thulle, to London, where the young man died of smallpox in 1784. No colonial post had been established by 1821, when Palau remained under its own chiefs.
zh:
帕劳地处加罗林群岛西端，核心是火山岛巴伯尔道布，与较小而人口集中的科罗尔岛隔狭窄水道相望。南岛语族航海者至迟在公元前一千纪已定居海岸；此后许多世纪中，他们开辟山坡梯田，用玄武岩和珊瑚石垒筑台地，并以石路连接聚居村落。村落以绘有图案的「bai」（会所）为中心，巴伯尔道布南部和科罗尔北部洞穴中的晶质石灰岩则吸引雅浦人乘独木舟前来。他们凿出的圆盘成为石币，作为礼仪财富，由独木舟或竹筏运回雅浦。1444年时，帕劳没有欧洲人的行政机构或传教站，权力仍掌握在帕劳首领和村落手中。

欧洲人对主要岛屿的最早可靠记录，是1543年1月底鲁伊·洛佩斯·德比利亚洛沃斯的西班牙船队；他们把巴伯尔道布、科罗尔和佩莱利乌标为「洛斯阿里西费斯」，意为群礁。1696年12月，漂流到萨马岛的帕劳人向传教士保罗·克莱因描述群岛方位，克莱因1697年送出的地图引发耶稣会兴趣，但1700、1708和1709年的传教尝试都告失败。1710年11月30日，弗朗西斯科·帕迪利亚抵达群岛，两名被留在松索罗尔的神父后来被杀。此后英国船只带来更经常的接触：1783年东印度公司商船「羚羊号」在乌龙附近失事，亨利·威尔逊把科罗尔统治者阿巴·图勒之子李布带到伦敦，年轻人次年死于天花。到1821年，欧洲人仍未设立殖民据点，帕劳依旧由本地首领统治。

en: Midway is a small atoll at the remote north-western end of the Hawaiian chain, where Sand, Eastern and Spit enclose a lagoon. Its Hawaiian name means the loud din of birds, but the islets had no permanent indigenous settlement. In 1444 there were no chiefs, marae, villages or fishing fleet here; Hawaiian voyaging and chiefdoms belonged to the larger islands far to the south-east, while Midway's beaches were left to albatrosses, monk seals and turtles. From 1444 to 1821 no recorded European or American vessel entered the lagoon, and the atoll remained an unoccupied anchorage without a colonial claim or resident population.
zh: 中途岛是夏威夷岛链西北端的偏远小环礁，由沙岛、东岛和斯皮特岛围出一片潟湖。它的夏威夷语名称意为「群鸟喧闹」，但几座小岛上没有永久原住民定居点。1444年时，这里没有酋长、马拉埃、村落或渔船队；夏威夷人的航海活动和酋邦社会属于东南方更远的主要岛屿，中途岛的海滩则归于信天翁、僧海豹和海龟。从1444年到1821年，没有任何有记载的欧洲或美洲船只进入这片潟湖，中途岛始终是没有殖民宣称、也无常住人口的空旷锚地。

en:
Christmas Island rises as a steep, forested volcanic island south of Java, its central plateau ending in sea cliffs. In 1444 it had no people, harbour or ruler; seabirds and red crabs occupied the beaches and monsoon forest, and seafarers knew no settled anchorage there.

On Christmas Day 1643, Captain William Mynors of the East India Company ship Royal Mary sailed past and gave the island its name. Dutch cartographer Pieter Goos marked it as Mony or Moni on a map in 1666, yet it long remained little more than a remote hazard on navigation charts. In March 1688 William Dampier, sailing aboard Cygnet, was blown off course; two of his crew landed on the west coast at the Dales in the first recorded landing, and Dampier reported the island uninhabited. Captain Daniel Beeckman of Eagle passed it on 5 April 1714 and described the voyage in a book published in 1718. Through 1821 Christmas Island still had neither settlers nor a permanent administration.
zh:
圣诞岛是爪哇以南一座林木茂密的陡峭火山岛，中部高原直落为海岸悬崖。1444年，岛上没有居民、港口或统治者；海滩和季风雨林属于海鸟与红蟹，航海者也不知道这里有可供定居的锚地。

1643年圣诞节，东印度公司船只「皇家玛丽号」船长威廉·迈纳斯经过此岛，并以圣诞节为它命名。荷兰制图师皮耶特·古斯在1666年的地图上把它标作 Mony 或 Moni，但该岛长期只是航海图上一处偏远险地。1688年3月，随「西格尼特号」航行的威廉·丹皮尔被风吹离航线，两名船员在西岸的戴尔斯登陆，这是最早有记录的登岛，丹皮尔也记载岛上无人居住。「伊格尔号」船长丹尼尔·贝克曼于1714年4月5日经过此岛，并在1718年出版的航行记中记述了这段经历。直到1821年，圣诞岛仍没有定居者，也没有常设政府。

en:
The Cocos, or Keeling, Islands are two low coral atolls in the open Indian Ocean: isolated North Keeling and the horseshoe-shaped southern atoll around a lagoon. In 1444 the 27 islets had no permanent inhabitants, no ruler and no established port. Coconut palms and seabird colonies occupied the low land, while the archipelago lay well south of the ordinary routes between Sumatra and India.

Captain William Keeling of the East India Company sighted the islands in 1609 on a return voyage from the East Indies, which gave the group its Keeling name. Recorded visits long remained rare. The Swedish captain Carl Gustaf Ekeberg sketched North Keeling in 1749, and his drawing showed coconut palms; British hydrographer Alexander Dalrymple placed the atolls on a chart in 1789. No trader or planter established a lasting post before 1821, so the islands remained without a permanent population throughout the period.
zh:
科科斯（基林）群岛由开阔印度洋上的两座低矮珊瑚环礁组成：一座是孤立的北基林岛，另一座是呈马蹄形、环绕潟湖的南基林群岛。1444年，这27座小岛没有常住居民、统治者，也没有成型港口；低地上只有椰林和海鸟群落，群岛本身也远在苏门答腊与印度之间的常用航线以南。

1609年，东印度公司船长威廉·基林从东印度返航时望见这组群岛，基林之名由此而来。此后有记录的到访长期稀少。1749年，瑞典船长卡尔·古斯塔夫·埃克贝里测绘北基林岛，图上已经画出椰树；1789年，英国水文师亚历山大·达尔林普尔又把环礁绘入海图。到1821年为止，没有商人或种植园主在此建立长久据点，群岛始终没有常住居民。

en: The Galápagos are a chain of arid volcanic islands straddling the equator far off the Peruvian coast. Giant tortoises, marine iguanas and seabirds thrived on shores that offered little fresh water, and no secure traces of permanent Indigenous settlement have been found; in 1444 the islands were uninhabited and lay beyond the regular Andean sea routes. On 10 March 1535 Tomás de Berlanga, Bishop of Panama, reached them after being blown off course while sailing to Peru. Maps by Ortelius and Mercator labelled them the Turtle Islands around 1570, and from Richard Hawkins's visit in 1593 English pirates used their coves as shelters while raiding Spanish shipping from Peru, a practice that continued until 1816. A Spanish scientific expedition under Alejandro Malaspina called there in 1790, but no lasting colony was founded in these years.
zh: 加拉帕戈斯是横亘赤道、远悬秘鲁海岸外的干旱火山群岛。大海龟、海鬣蜥和海鸟在淡水稀少的岸边繁衍，岛上没有发现原住民永久定居的确证；1444年时这里无人居住，也不在安第斯世界常走的航路之内。1535年3月10日，巴拿马主教托马斯·德·贝兰加乘船前往秘鲁时被洋流吹离航线，偶然抵达群岛。1570年前后，奥特柳斯和墨卡托的地图把这里标作「龟岛」。1593年理查德·霍金斯到访后，英国海盗常以这些海湾为藏身地，袭扰从秘鲁出航的西班牙商船，这种活动一直延续到1816年。1790年，亚历杭德罗·马拉斯皮纳率领的西班牙科学考察队曾到此，但这一时期仍未建立持久殖民地。

en:
The Ktunaxa hold the valley of the Kootenay River and the forests around Kootenay Lake, in the long trench between the Rockies and the ranges to their west. Their speech is a language isolate, unrelated to that of any neighbour. The bands moved with the seasons, taking fish with traps and weirs, paddling the waterways in a distinctive sturgeon-nosed bark canoe, and hunting deer and waterfowl; the upper bands crossed the Rockies each summer to run bison on the plains, where they clashed with the Blackfoot. In 1444 no European had yet seen these mountains.

The Ktunaxa first appear on a European map on Alexander Mackenzie's chart of about 1793, and smallpox, travelling ahead of the traders, had already thinned the bands that hunted east of the mountains. In 1807 David Thompson sent Jaco Finlay to raise Kootanae House on Columbia Lake, the North West Company's first post in the Columbia Basin, where the Ktunaxa traded their furs. Peigan war parties closed the Howse Pass route and the post was abandoned in 1812.
zh:
克图纳哈人（Ktunaxa，即库特奈人）的家园在库特内河沿岸与库特内湖周围的山林地带，地处落基山脉与西侧群山之间的落基山地沟。他们的语言是孤立语言，与四邻都不相通。各部随季节迁徙，用鱼梁和陷阱捕鱼，驾着独特的鲟鱼鼻形树皮独木舟往来河面，猎取鹿和水禽；上游的部落每年夏天翻过落基山到平原围猎野牛，常与黑脚人冲突。1444年，还没有欧洲人见过这片群山。

克图纳哈人最早出现在欧洲人的地图上，是1793年前后亚历山大·麦肯齐绘制的地图；而在商人到来之前，天花已经使翻山东猎的部落人口大减。1807年，戴维·汤普森派雅科·芬利在哥伦比亚湖畔建起库特奈商站，这是西北公司在哥伦比亚河流域的第一处商站，克图纳哈人在此交易毛皮；后来皮甘武士封锁了豪斯山口通道，商站于1812年被放弃。

en:
The Kainaa, 'Many Chiefs' in the Blackfoot tongue — their Plains Cree enemies called them the Blood — are one of the three nations of the Niitsitapi, the Blackfoot Confederacy, beside the Siksika and Piikani. In 1444 they hold the shortgrass plains watered by the Belly and Oldman rivers, where winter bands of ten to thirty lodges camped in the wooded valleys and summer gatherings united the nation for the bison hunt. No European horse had yet reached them: they moved on foot, packed their lodges on A-frame travois pulled by dogs, and drove the herds into pounds and over jumps, drying the meat into pemmican. Their range ran north to the Bow River, and at the summer camps a man rose through the warrior societies by brave deeds.

Horses reached the Niitsitapi around 1730 — they named them ponokamita, 'elk dogs' — and within a generation the mounted Kainaa and their allies were raiding south against the Shoshone; by 1787, when David Thompson travelled the country, the Blackfoot had overrun most of the Shoshone lands. In the autumn of 1754 Anthony Henday of the Hudson's Bay Company met a great Blackfoot camp in what is now central Alberta and urged its chiefs to carry their furs to Hudson Bay; they refused, fearing Cree and Assiniboine attack on the long journey. In time the trade came to them instead, as Company posts rose along the North Saskatchewan on the edge of their range, where Kainaa parties brought pemmican and bison robes rather than beaver.
zh:
凯纳（Kainaa，中文维基译盖恩纳，仇敌克里人称之为「血部落」）在黑脚语中意为「众酋长」，与西格西卡人、皮卡尼人并称尼特西塔皮（黑脚联盟）三大民族。1444年，他们游牧于贝尔河（Belly River）与奥尔德曼河（Oldman River）浇灌的短草平原：冬天，十来座到三十座帐篷组成的小队在林木河谷中扎营；夏天全族聚集，合力围猎野牛。当时欧洲人的马尚未到来，他们徒步行走，把帐篷装上狗拉的A字形雪橇，把牛群赶入围栅或逼下悬崖，再将牛肉制成肉糜饼。游猎范围北抵弓河，夏日营地里，男子凭勇武事迹升入战士会社。

约1730年，马传到尼特西塔皮人这里，他们称之为 ponokamita，意为「麋狗」。不过一两代人，骑马的黑脚各部便南下攻掠肖肖尼人；1787年戴维·汤普森行经此地时，黑脚人已夺占肖肖尼人的大部分土地。早在1754年秋，哈得孙湾公司的安东尼·亨德（Anthony Henday）在今艾伯塔中部遇到一座庞大的黑脚营地，他劝酋长们把毛皮运往哈得孙湾，却因路途遥远、惧怕途中遭克里人与阿西尼博因人袭击而被拒绝。后来贸易反而自己找上门：公司在黑脚疆域北缘的北萨斯喀彻温河畔设立商栈，凯纳人带来的不是海狸皮，而是肉糜饼和野牛皮袍。

en:
Assapasca is the name of the aspen parkland between the Touchwood Hills and the Qu'Appelle River, where aspen groves, pothole lakes and grassland mark the passage from the boreal forest into the open plains. In 1444 there were no towns or European posts here. Small bands—the people later recorded as Cree and Assiniboine, or Nakoda—moved on foot with the seasons, fishing the lakes, trapping beaver and hunting moose in the woods, and taking bison where the parkland opened to the south. Their trails and river crossings carried trade and diplomacy long before any European saw them.

Henry Kelsey reached this parkland from York Factory in 1691, after wintering near The Pas; travelling with Cree, probably near the Touchwood Hills, he met Assiniboine hunters, described vast bison herds and grizzlies on 20 August, and returned to Hudson Bay in 1692. French competition opened from the east when La Vérendrye built Fort La Reine on the Assiniboine River in 1738. By the 1740s Cree and Assiniboine bands of the Iron Confederacy were exchanging furs and provisions for muskets, kettles and beads, and by mid-century horses from the Blackfoot country had transformed the bison hunt. In 1787 the North West Company planted Fort Espérance on the lower Qu'Appelle, using it chiefly as a pemmican depot; an XY Company post followed in 1801, and a Hudson's Bay Company post competed nearby from 1813 until Nor'Westers burned it in 1816. Fort Espérance itself was abandoned in 1819 and its remains passed to the Hudson's Bay Company when the rival companies merged in 1821.
zh:
阿萨帕斯卡是图奇伍德丘陵与卡佩勒河之间杨树林草原的名字。白杨林、锅形湖和草地交错，构成北方针叶林通往开阔平原的过渡地带。1444年时，这里没有城镇，也没有欧洲商栈；后来被记载为克里人和阿西尼博因人（自称Nakoda）的小族群随季节徒步迁徙，在湖中捕鱼，在林中捕海狸、猎驼鹿，又在林缘草原向南敞开处猎捕野牛。早在欧洲人到来前，他们的小径和渡口已承担着贸易与外交往来。

1691年，亨利·凯尔西在帕斯附近过冬后，随克里同伴从约克厂深入这片林缘草原；他很可能在图奇伍德丘陵一带遇见阿西尼博因猎人，8月20日记录下大群野牛和灰熊，并于1692年返回哈得孙湾。法国人的竞争自东而来：1738年，拉韦朗德里在阿西尼博因河畔建起拉雷讷堡。到1740年代，加入铁联盟的克里人和阿西尼博因人已用毛皮和食物换取火枪、铁锅和珠子；到18世纪中叶，来自黑脚之地的马匹又改变了野牛狩猎。1787年，西北公司在卡佩勒河下游建立埃斯佩朗斯堡，主要把它当作干肉饼补给站；XY公司1801年随设商栈，哈得孙湾公司1813年也在附近竞争，后者1816年被西北公司焚毁。埃斯佩朗斯堡本堡于1819年废弃，1821年两家竞争公司合并后，残余设施归入哈得孙湾公司。

en:
Ashalaho, 'Many Lodges', was the later name of the Mountain Crow, the largest of the Apsáalooke bands. Their homeland lay along the upper Yellowstone, called Elk River in Crow, where the Absaroka and Bighorn ranges overlook cold plains and beaver streams. In 1444 the Crow were still settled village people closer to the Upper Missouri and related Hidatsa, while Shoshone and other northern Plains hunters moved through these valleys after bison, carrying their lodges on dog-drawn travois rather than horse-drawn ones.

The Crow broke from the Hidatsa and moved west in the late seventeenth century. Tradition names No Intestines as the leader who brought the Ashalaho to the upper Yellowstone, where they drove Shoshone bands westward and became mounted bison hunters. Horses spread rapidly among Plains peoples from about 1730, and the Crow became breeders and dealers whose herds drew raids from Blackfoot and Gros Ventre parties. The North West Company trader François-Antoine Larocque accompanied a Crow camp into the Yellowstone country in 1805, leaving the first detailed European account. In 1807 Fort Raymond was built near the Bighorn's mouth, traded with the Crow until about 1813, and drew the mountain valleys into the Upper Missouri fur trade.
zh:
阿沙拉霍意为「多营盘」，是后来山地克劳人的名称，也是阿普萨鲁克（Apsáalooke，克劳人自称）最大的支派。他们的家园在黄石河上游，克劳语称麋鹿河；阿布萨罗卡岭与大角山俯瞰寒冷平原和盛产河狸的溪流。1444年时，克劳人还是靠近上密苏里河、与希达沙人亲缘相近的定居民，休休尼人和其他北方平原猎手则在这些河谷间追逐野牛，用狗拉拖架运载营帐，马匹尚未成为迁营的依靠。

17世纪晚期，克劳人与希达沙人分离并向西迁移。相传首领无肠率领阿沙拉霍人抵达黄石河上游，将休休尼部落逐向西边，继而成为骑马猎牛的平原人。约1730年起，马匹在平原各族间迅速普及，克劳人成为养马者和贩马者，马群也引来黑脚人和格罗斯文特人的袭击。1805年，西北公司商人弗朗索瓦-安托万·拉罗克随一处克劳营地进入黄石地区，留下最早的详细欧洲人记录。1807年，雷蒙德堡建于大角河河口附近，与克劳人贸易至约1813年，也把这些山谷卷入上密苏里的毛皮贸易。

en:
The Sahnish, whom later French and American traders would call the Arikara or Ree, speak a Caddoan tongue and are close kin of the Pawnee; their ancestors began separating from the Skidi Pawnee around the 15th century and carried village life up the Missouri. On terraces above the river in what is now central South Dakota they raised fortified towns of earth lodges, and the Arzberger site holds the remains of more than forty-four lodges. Fields of corn, beans, squash and sunflowers fed the villages and supplied the nomadic camps that came to trade, while twice a year long parties left on the bison hunt. In 1444 the Sahnish were the settled farmers and corn merchants of the middle Missouri.

Late in the 17th century they were attacked by the migrating Omaha and Ponca, though peace and intermarriage followed. In 1743 two sons of La Vérendrye reached a Sahnish village on this stretch of the Missouri and buried a lead plate claiming the country for France. The smallpox epidemic of 1780–1782 reduced the Arikara villages along the Missouri from thirty-two to two, and Lakota raids pressed hard on the survivors. Lewis and Clark met the remnant in 1804, and a delegation sent to Washington in April 1805 ended with the chief Ankedoucharo dying in the capital, leaving the Sahnish bitterly distrustful of the Americans.
zh:
萨尼什人——后来的法国和美国商人称他们为阿里卡拉人或里人——使用卡多语，与波尼人是近亲；他们的祖先约在15世纪与斯基迪波尼人分离，把村落农耕生活带到密苏里河上游。在今南达科他中部的河畔阶地上，他们建起土屋组成的设防村镇，河畔的阿茨伯格遗址就保存着四十四座以上的屋舍遗迹。玉米、豆类、南瓜和向日葵田养活了村庄，也供应前来交易的游牧部落；每年还有两次大队人马出动的长途猎牛。1444年时，萨尼什人是密苏里河中游定居的农耕者和玉米商人。

17世纪末，迁徙中的奥马哈人和篷卡人曾进攻他们，但双方后来议和通婚。1743年，拉韦朗德里的两个儿子抵达这一段密苏里河畔的一座萨尼什村庄，埋下一块铅碑，以法兰西国王的名义宣示这片土地。1780至1782年的天花大流行使密苏里河畔的村庄从三十二座锐减到两座，拉科塔人的袭击又不断压迫幸存者。1804年，刘易斯与克拉克远征队遇到残存的萨尼什人；1805年4月前往华盛顿的使团以酋长安克杜查罗客死首都告终，萨尼什人从此对美国人深怀戒心。

en:
The Missouri cuts through the northern South Dakota grasslands, taking in the Grand and other small timbered rivers. In 1444 its terraces were the northern country of the Caddoan-speaking earth-lodge villagers, kinsmen of the Sahnish or Arikara: their fortified towns of domed lodges overlooked fields of corn, beans, squash and sunflowers, and surplus grain was traded to the bison hunters of the open plains. The short-grass sea around them belonged to those hunters and the great herds, under winters severe enough to kill anyone caught far from shelter.

Horses reached the river early in the 18th century and transformed the plains hunt. The smallpox epidemic of 1780–1782 broke the villagers' power, and in the early 1780s raiders burned a fortified village on this stretch of the Missouri, leaving seventy-one men, women and children dead among the ruins later studied as the Larson site. Lakota bands then crossed the river into the emptied country, and the Sihasapa, the 'Blackfeet' Lakota, made the Grand River valley their own. In October 1804 Lewis and Clark met the surviving Arikara at villages near the Grand's mouth, and after 1807 American fur traders led by Manuel Lisa began pushing their posts up the river.
zh:
密苏里河穿过南达科他北部的草原，沿途纳入格兰德河等林木丛生的小河。1444年，河畔阶地是卡多语系土屋村民分布的北缘，他们是萨尼什人（即阿里卡拉人）的亲族：圆顶土屋组成的设防村镇俯瞰着玉米、豆类、南瓜和向日葵田，余粮用来与开阔平原上的猎牛人交易。村镇之外的短草荒原属于猎人和庞大的野牛群，这里的严冬足以冻死任何来不及躲避的人。

18世纪初，马匹传到密苏里河，改变了平原狩猎。1780至1782年的天花大流行摧毁了村民的势力；1780年代初，袭击者焚毁了这一段密苏里河畔的一座设防村庄，废墟中后来发现七十一名男女和儿童的遗骸，即考古学上的拉森遗址。拉科塔各部随后渡河进入空虚的土地，锡哈萨帕人——意为「黑脚」的拉科塔人——把格兰德河谷变成了自己的家园。1804年10月，刘易斯与克拉克在格兰德河口附近的村庄会见残存的阿里卡拉人；1807年后，以曼努埃尔·利萨为首的美国皮货商开始把贸易站向河的上游推进。

en:
Oglala is the short-grass country west of the Missouri River's bend above later Pierre, where river terraces look toward the Black Hills. In 1444 the valley belonged to the Middle Missouri world of earth-lodge farmers and bison hunters; the Arikara were then diverging from the Skidi Pawnee. A century earlier the fortified Arzberger village below Pierre had enclosed forty-four houses behind a stockade with twenty-four bastions, one of the last traces of the older Initial Coalescent way of life in this stretch of the river.

Written contact reached the Arikara villages near Pierre in 1743, when François and Louis de La Vérendrye visited them. The Oglala were becoming a distinct Lakota division in the same period. After the Lakota acquired horses from the Cheyenne around 1730, the Oglala and Brulé moved into the James River valley and by about 1760 held the Missouri's eastern bank. The smallpox epidemic of 1780–1782 shattered the Arikara, Mandan and Hidatsa villages that had barred the crossing, allowing Lakota bands to enter the High Plains. Lewis and Clark met armed Lakota on the river in 1804, and the subsequent fur trade tied Oglala bands to European goods.
zh:
奥格拉拉位于后来皮尔以北的密苏里河河弯以西，河畔阶地从这里通向布莱克山方向的短草平原。1444年时，密苏里河谷属于中土屋农夫与野牛猎人的世界，阿利卡拉人正是在这一时期与斯基迪波尼人分化。约一个世纪前，皮尔下游设防的阿兹贝格村以木栅和二十四座棱堡围住四十四座房屋，是这一段密苏里河较古老的「初始融合文化」最后痕迹之一。

1743年，弗朗索瓦与路易·德·拉韦朗德里访问皮尔附近的阿利卡拉村庄，文字记载由此进入此地。同一时期，奥格拉拉人正形成独立的拉科塔分支。拉科塔人约1730年从夏延人那里获得马匹后，奥格拉拉人与布鲁埃人进入詹姆斯河流域，并在约1760年控制密苏里河东岸。1780—1782年的天花摧毁了阻挡他们渡河的阿利卡拉、曼丹和希达察村庄，拉科塔各群体随即进入高平原。1804年刘易斯与克拉克在河上遇到武装的拉科塔人，随后的毛皮贸易也把奥格拉拉群体与欧洲货物联系起来。

en:
Pequot country takes in the sheltered shore where the Thames, Mystic and Pawcatuck rivers enter Long Island Sound, in southeastern Connecticut. The Pequot spoke an Algonquian dialect closely related to Mohegan, and their palisaded villages, fishing stations and canoe routes tied inland hunting grounds to coastal exchange between Niantic country to the west and Narragansett country to the east. In 1444 no European ship had entered these waters; the sound's fish and shellfish and the estuary crossings remained in Pequot hands.

Adriaen Block put the coast on European maps in 1614, when he entered Long Island Sound and the Connecticut River; his voyage also gave the name New Netherland its first printed map use. A 1633 epidemic devastated the Pequot, and after John Oldham was killed in 1636 English colonies, Mohegans and Narragansetts made war upon Sassacus's people. On 26 May 1637 John Mason's force and its allies burned the palisaded village at Mystic, killing 400 to 700 Pequots. The 1638 Treaty of Hartford dissolved the nation, forbade the Pequot name, and distributed survivors among allies or into slavery, although reserves were later held at Mashantucket in 1666 and Pawcatuck in 1683. John Winthrop the Younger founded an English town at the harbor in 1646, and it was formally named New London in 1658. The harbor became a Revolutionary War privateer base; on 6 September 1781 Benedict Arnold burned much of New London and stormed Fort Griswold, where many of William Ledyard's garrison were killed after surrender.
zh:
佩科特人的土地位于康涅狄格东南，泰晤士河、米斯蒂克河与波卡塔克河注入长岛海湾的曲折海岸。佩科特人使用与莫西干语相近的阿尔冈昆方言，栅栏村落、渔场和独木舟水道把内陆猎场与海岸往来连接起来；其西是奈安蒂克人的土地，东面则是纳拉甘西特人的土地。1444年，欧洲船只尚未进入这片水域，海湾中的鱼、贝类和河口渡口仍掌握在佩科特人手中。

1614年，阿德里安·布洛克驶入长岛海湾和康涅狄格河，把这片海岸绘入欧洲地图；他的航行也使「新尼德兰」一名首次用于印刷地图。1633年的瘟疫重创佩科特人，1636年约翰·奥尔德姆被杀后，英格兰殖民地联合莫西干人与纳拉甘西特人，对萨萨库斯麾下的佩科特人开战。1637年5月26日，约翰·梅森所部及其盟友焚毁米斯蒂克的栅栏村落，400至700名佩科特人遇害。1638年的《哈特福德条约》解散佩科特人的政治实体、禁止他们再使用佩科特之名，并把幸存者分给盟友或卖为奴隶；不过佩科特人后来仍在1666年获得马尚图克特保留地，1683年获得波卡塔克河保留地。1646年，小约翰·温思罗普在河口建立英格兰城镇，1658年正式定名新伦敦。独立战争期间，这个港湾成为私掠船基地；1781年9月6日，本尼迪克特·阿诺德焚毁大半个新伦敦并强攻格里斯沃尔德堡，威廉·莱德亚德所部投降后仍有许多守军被杀。

en:
This is the Shenandoah Valley, the long corridor between the Blue Ridge and the Allegheny ridges, where the forks of the Shenandoah River run north to the Potomac. In 1444 its bottomlands belonged to the Senedo, a farming people whose language and kinship no record preserves; they planted and hunted along the north fork and left the earthen mounds later found above the river bends. The valley was also a common war road through which raiding parties passed between the northern nations and the distant Catawba country to the south.

Later settlers recorded a tradition that the Senedo had been destroyed by Catawba raiders before 1700, and the valley held no towns when John Lederer became the first European to look down into it from the Blue Ridge in 1670. Governor Alexander Spotswood's Knights of the Golden Horseshoe crossed at Swift Run Gap in 1716, and Adam Miller staked out the first farm on the south fork in 1727. Through the 1730s German and Scots-Irish families moved south along the old Indian road later called the Great Wagon Road, and Winchester grew among their settlements. The 1744 Treaty of Lancaster bought the Iroquois claim to the valley for 200 pounds in gold; the few Shawnee still there withdrew beyond the Alleghenies in 1754. During the Revolutionary War its wheat harvests and its riflemen fed and manned the Continental Army.
zh:
这一省便是谢南多亚河谷，蓝岭山脉与阿勒格尼山脊之间的一条漫长走廊，谢南多亚河的诸支汊向北流去，注入波托马克河。1444年，河谷滩地的主人是塞内多人——一个务农的部族，其语言与族属都没有记载留存；他们在北汊一带耕作渔猎，在河湾上方留下后人见到的泥土坟丘。河谷还是一条各方共用的征战通道，北方各部与远方南方卡托巴人之地的袭击队伍都由此往来。

后来的移民记下一种说法：塞内多人在1700年之前被卡托巴袭击者覆灭。1670年，约翰·莱德勒成为第一个从蓝岭俯瞰这座河谷的欧洲人，当时谷中已无村镇。1716年，总督亚历山大·斯波茨伍德的「金马掌骑士」之行从斯威夫特河山口越过蓝岭；1727年，亚当·米勒在南汊开辟第一座农庄。1730年代，德意志和苏格兰－爱尔兰裔家庭沿古老的印第安人小路（后来的「大车道」）源源南下，温彻斯特在他们的定居点之间兴起。1744年的《兰开斯特条约》以200英镑金币买下易洛魁联盟对河谷的权利；谷中仅存的肖尼人则在1754年迁往阿勒格尼山以西。独立战争期间，这里的小麦收成供给大陆军粮秣，本地的步枪手也入伍参战。

en:
Ersegonteog covered the basin of the Saint-François River, the Abenaki canoe route that runs from the southern lakes north-west to Lake Saint-Pierre. In 1444 this was Western Abenaki country without European settlements. Bands followed the river and its portages by season, fishing, hunting, and raising maize, beans and squash in summer camps, gathering in autonomous villages rather than under a single chief.

By 1660 Sokoki families were living near the lower Saint-François, and the French built Fort Crevier beside the river in 1687. The Jesuit mission of Saint-François-de-Sales, founded at the Chaudière River in 1684, was moved here by Jacques Bigot in 1700 after repeated crop failures; its village became Odanak. French engineers fortified it with a palisade and redoubts in 1704 during the War of the Spanish Succession. After Dummer's War ended in 1725, about 300 Abenaki warriors and their families from Maine missions swelled the settlement. During the Seven Years' War Robert Rogers's rangers burned Odanak on 4 October 1759. The Constitutional Act of 1791 opened the upper basin to British township surveying; Dunham, the first township, was granted in 1796, drawing Loyalists and New England farmers along the old canoe routes.
zh:
埃尔塞冈泰奥格位于圣弗朗索瓦河流域。这条阿贝纳基人的独木舟航路从南部湖群蜿蜒西北，通向圣皮埃尔湖。1444年时，这里仍是西阿贝纳基人的土地，没有欧洲人定居。各群体随季节利用河道和搬运道，捕鱼狩猎，在夏季营地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜；人们聚居于各自作主的村落，并不受一位首领统辖。

1660年前后，索科基人的家庭已在圣弗朗索瓦河下游居住；1687年，法国人在河畔修建克雷维埃堡。耶稣会的圣弗朗索瓦·德萨勒传教站1684年先设于肖迪耶尔河畔，因连年歉收，雅克·比戈在1700年把它迁到此处，形成后来的奥达纳克村。1704年西班牙王位继承战争期间，法国工程师又为村子加筑栅栏和棱堡。1725年达默战争结束后，约三百名来自缅因传教村的阿贝纳基战士及家属迁入，使村落扩大。七年战争期间，罗伯特·罗杰斯率领别动队在1759年10月4日焚毁奥达纳克。1791年《宪法法案》后，英国按乡镇制重新勘分上游盆地；第一个乡镇邓纳姆于1796年获批，效忠派和新英格兰农户随后沿着旧日独木舟水路进入此地。

en:
Allesikantekw covers the lower Kennebec, where the river broadens into the freshwater tides of Merrymeeting Bay and then runs into the Gulf of Maine. Eastern Abenaki families kept camps by the bay, fished the tidal river, planted the open grounds, and used the Kennebec as a canoe road into the interior. Sagamores led each band rather than a single central chief. In 1444 this was still Wabanaki country, its trade and marriage routes following the coast and rivers long before any European post stood on the shore.

French and English vessels explored the coast in 1604-05; George Weymouth's English voyage of 1605 seized five Wawenock men to learn the country's routes. The Plymouth Company planted the Popham Colony at the river mouth in 1607, raising Fort St George and building the pinnace Virginia of Sagadahoc before abandoning the post after fourteen months. English traders opened Cushnoc far up the Kennebec in 1628. The river then became a wartime frontier: Abenaki forces struck English settlements during King Philip's War after 1675, and in August 1724 Massachusetts militia destroyed the Kennebec mission village of Norridgewock, killing the Jesuit Sébastien Rale and many of its people. In 1775 Benedict Arnold's expedition to Quebec followed the Kennebec northward through Maine.
zh:
阿莱西坎特库位于肯纳贝克河下游，河水在此展宽为受潮汐影响的淡水湾梅里米廷湾，再注入缅因湾。东阿布纳基人的家族在湾边设立营地，在感潮河道捕鱼，于开阔地耕作，并把肯纳贝克河当作深入内陆的独木舟通道。各群体由酋长分别统领，没有唯一的最高首领。1444年时，这里仍是瓦巴纳基人的土地；欧洲人设立据点以前，海岸与河流早已串联起当地的贸易和通婚网络。

1604—1605年，法国和英国船只先后考察这段海岸；乔治·韦茅斯1605年的英国航行掳走五名瓦沃诺克人，以打探当地路径。1607年，普利茅斯公司在河口建立波帕姆殖民地，修筑圣乔治堡并建造帆船「萨加达霍克的弗吉尼亚号」，但仅十四个月后便弃守。1628年，英国商人在肯纳贝克河上游开设库什诺克贸易站。此后这条河成为战争前沿：1675年腓力国王战争爆发后，阿布纳基武装不断袭击英国定居点；1724年8月，马萨诸塞民兵摧毁肯纳贝克河畔的传教村诺里奇沃克，杀害耶稣会士塞巴斯蒂安·拉勒和许多村民。1775年，本尼迪克特·阿诺德远征魁北克时，又沿肯纳贝克河北上穿越缅因。

en:
Natchitoches was the westernmost of the three Caddo-speaking confederacies, with the Hasinai in eastern Texas and the Kadohadacho higher on the Red River. Its villages stood among the bayous and cane bottoms of northwestern Louisiana, where the people grew maize, beans and squash, made fine pottery, and exchanged river produce with neighboring Caddo towns. In 1444 the old mound-building centers had given way to dispersed farming villages, but Natchitoches remained an independent Red River power on the road between the Mississippi and Spanish Texas.

A Spanish entrada crossed Caddo country in the 1540s, and Henri de Tonti reached the Natchitoches village in February 1690. French traders were using the Red River site by 1699 and Bienville visited in 1701. Louis Juchereau de St. Denis founded Fort St. Jean Baptiste near the village in 1714, and Du Tisné garrisoned a permanent post in 1716 to face Spanish Texas. Epidemics cut the confederacy from Bienville's estimated 400–450 warriors in 1700 to about 80 warriors and fewer than 200 people by 1718. Natchitoches nevertheless became France's principal ally and supply point on the upper Red River, trading corn, game and bear oil for European goods and growing tobacco by the 1730s. In 1732 St. Denis broke a Natchez attack near Cloutierville, after which the fort was enlarged. Louisiana passed to Spain after 1763, and O'Reilly's suppression of the 1768 Creole revolt made Spanish rule effective. Returned to France and sold to the United States in 1803, Natchitoches received a federal fur factory in 1805 and was incorporated in 1819.
zh:
纳基托什是三大卡多语联盟中最西的一支，另外两支是东得克萨斯的哈西奈人和雷德河上游的卡多哈达乔人。他们的村落散布在路易斯安那西北部的牛轭湖与甘蔗丛低地间，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，制作精良陶器，并以河上物产同邻近卡多城镇交换。到1444年，古老的筑丘中心已演变为分散的农业村落，但纳基托什仍是雷德河畔一支独立势力，扼守密西西比与西属得克萨斯之间的通路。

16世纪40年代，一支西班牙远征队穿过卡多土地；1690年2月，亨利·德·通蒂到达纳基托什村落。法国商人到1699年已在雷德河这一带活动，比安维尔则于1701年前来访问。1714年，路易·朱谢罗·德·圣但尼在村落附近建立纳基托什圣让巴蒂斯特堡；1716年，迪蒂涅率军常驻，建成面对西属得克萨斯的永久据点。疫病使联盟人口骤降：1700年比安维尔估计有四百至四百五十名战士，到1718年拉阿尔普统计只剩约八十名战士、不足两百人。尽管如此，纳基托什仍成为法国在雷德河上游最重要的盟友和补给点，以玉米、猎物和熊油换取欧洲商品，并在18世纪30年代种植烟草。1732年，圣但尼在克洛蒂维尔附近击退纳奇兹人的进攻，要塞随后扩建。1763年后路易斯安那转入西班牙之手，奥赖利镇压1768年克里奥尔起义后，西班牙统治才真正稳固。该地随路易斯安那先交还法国、又于1803年售予美国；1805年美国在此设立毛皮贸易站，1819年正式设市。

en:
Lake Nipigon, Animbiigoo-zaaga'igan in Ojibwe, the lake of waters that stretch to the horizon, is a vast inland water north of Lake Superior and the largest lake lying wholly within Ontario. The swift Nipigon River carries its overflow south into Nipigon Bay, the greatest of all the rivers feeding Lake Superior. Its Ojibwe people fished the cold waters, hunted caribou in the shore forests and trapped beaver along the streams, and their canoes crossed between the great lake and the country to the north. In 1444 this was a remote but fur-rich Anishinaabe land, untouched by Europeans.

Refugees first brought the French there: in the Iroquois onslaught of 1649–50 the Nipissing fled to Lake Nipigon, and on 29 May 1667 Claude Allouez said the first mass beside the Nipigon River among them. In 1683 Daniel Greysolon du Lhut built Fort La Tourette on the lake, probably at Ombabika Bay, naming it after his brother; the crown closed it in 1696 when beaver glutted the market and the western trading permits were withdrawn. In 1744 the fur profits of Lac Alemipigon were granted to Jean de La Porte, and after the country passed to Britain in 1763 the North West Company traded there until the Hudson's Bay Company, which opened its first post on the lake in 1792, absorbed it in 1821.
zh:
尼皮贡湖在奥吉布瓦语中意为「绵延至天际的水域」，是苏必利尔湖以北的巨大内陆湖，也是全境都在安大略境内的第一大湖；湍急的尼皮贡河把湖水向南送入尼皮贡湾，是注入苏必利尔湖的最大河流。湖畔的奥吉布瓦人在冷水中捕鱼，在沿岸森林猎取驯鹿，在溪流间捕捉河狸取皮，独木舟往来于大湖与北方之地。1444年，这里是偏远却盛产毛皮的阿尼什纳贝人之地，欧洲人尚未来到。

难民最先把法国人引到此地：1649—1650年易洛魁人大举进攻时，尼皮辛人逃到尼皮贡湖避难，1667年5月29日，克洛德·阿卢埃在尼皮贡河畔、在他们中间做了第一场弥撒。1683年，达尼埃尔·格雷索隆·迪吕特在湖畔（很可能是翁巴比卡湾）建起拉图雷特堡，以其兄弟之名为之命名；1696年，因海狸皮供过于求、西部贸易特许被收回，王室下令关闭该堡。1744年，阿莱米皮贡湖的毛皮收益权被授予让·德拉波特；1763年此地归入英国后，西北公司在此贸易，直到1792年已在湖畔设立首个商站的哈德逊湾公司于1821年将其合并。

en:
Bungi, the Red River country, lies on the flat bed of ancient Lake Agassiz, with the wooded Pembina and Turtle hills rising along its western edge. In 1444 it was Nakota ground: the bands later recorded as the Assiniboine followed the bison north in summer and wintered in the sheltered parkland, hauling their lodges with dog travois, for neither horses nor guns had yet reached the northern plains. The Hidatsa word for a broken, wooded hill country was Amahami, and their Awaxawi kinsmen traced their origin to Devils Lake on the edge of this land before their villages shifted to the Missouri. Beaver pelts, bison hides and the corn of the Missouri villages already passed along native trade routes, with the Assiniboine among their brokers.

Henry Kelsey of the Hudson's Bay Company met Assiniboine hunters in the 1690s, and in 1738 La Vérendrye reached the Forks of the Red and Assiniboine, where Fort Rouge was raised as a French depot before he went on to the Mandan; it was abandoned by 1749. The trade returned: the Hudson's Bay Company kept a post on the Red by 1793, the North West Company's Chaboillez built at the Pembina River mouth in 1797, and Alexander Henry the Younger built opposite him in 1801. Assiniboine and Cree middlemen brought furs, Métis hunters made Pembina the rendezvous of the great buffalo hunts, and Saulteaux bands led by Peguis reached the Red in the 1790s, becoming known as the Bungi; the smallpox of 1782 had thinned every camp. In 1812 Selkirk's Scottish settlers built Fort Douglas and Fort Daer, the Pemmican Proclamation of January 1814 opened the Pemmican War, and on 19 June 1816 Governor Semple and twenty settlers fell at Seven Oaks. Selkirk's treaty with the Cree, Assiniboine and Ojibwa followed in 1817, and when the two rival fur companies merged in 1821 the country passed under the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
邦吉即红河地区，坐落在古阿加西湖干涸后的平坦湖床上，西缘隆起林木覆盖的彭比纳丘陵与龟山。1444年，这里是纳科塔人的土地：后来被记作阿西尼博因的诸氏族夏天随野牛群北上，冬天退入避风的林带，用狗拉拖杆搬运帐篷——此时马和火器都还没有传到北部大平原。希达察语把丘陵林木交错之地称作「阿马哈米」，与他们同源的阿瓦克萨维人传说自己就起源于这片土地边缘的魔鬼湖，后来村落才迁到密苏里河畔。河狸皮、野牛皮和密苏里村落的玉米早已沿着原住民商路流通，阿西尼博因人便是中间人之一。

哈得孙湾公司的亨利·凯尔西在1690年代最先遇见阿西尼博因猎人；1738年拉韦朗德里抵达红河与阿希尼伯恩河汇流处，建起作为法商货栈的鲁日堡，随后前往曼丹人那里，该堡到1749年已废弃。贸易还是回来了：哈得孙湾公司1793年已在红河畔设有商栈，西北公司的沙布瓦耶1797年在彭比纳河口建栈，小亚历山大·亨利1801年在对岸另立一栈。阿西尼博因人与克里人充当毛皮贸易的中间人，梅蒂猎人把彭比纳变成大规模野牛狩猎的集合地；佩吉斯率领的索尔特奥人在1790年代迁居红河，被称为邦吉人。1782年的天花曾使沿途营地人口锐减。1812年，塞尔扣克的苏格兰移民建起道格拉斯堡和达尔堡；1814年1月的《干肉饼公告》引发干肉饼战争，1816年6月19日总督森普尔和二十名移民在七橡树被杀。1817年塞尔扣克与克里、阿西尼博因和奥吉布瓦人缔约；1821年两家竞争的毛皮公司合并，这片土地归入哈得孙湾公司治下。

en:
The Matiyininiwak country is the belt of boreal forest and aspen parkland between the Peace and North Saskatchewan rivers, where Lesser Slave Lake drains through the Lesser Slave River into the Athabasca. In 1444 its moose ranges, beaver streams and fishing lakes belonged to small Athabascan-speaking hunting bands, kin of the Dane-zaa or Beaver and of the later Tsuu T'ina; they moved by birchbark canoe and snowshoe between winter camps, taking moose, woodland caribou and beaver, and trading skins and dried meat to the bison hunters of the open plains to the south.

During the 18th century Cree bands armed through the Hudson's Bay trade pushed west as middlemen, pressing the Dane-zaa toward the Peace River while the forest people who became the Tsuu T'ina broke away south for the plains. The long Cree-Beaver fighting ended only when the smallpox epidemic of 1781 devastated both sides, and a peace set the Peace River as the boundary. Traders followed the warriors: Peter Pond built the Athabasca country's first post in 1778, Fort Chipewyan rose on Lake Athabasca in 1788, and in 1802 the North West Company built a post at Buffalo Bay on Lesser Slave Lake, tying the lake country to the northern fur brigades.
zh:
马蒂厄因伊瓦克之地位于皮斯河与北萨斯喀彻温河之间的针叶林与白杨疏林草原带，小奴湖经小奴河注入阿萨巴斯卡河。1444年，这里的驼鹿猎场、海狸溪和鱼湖属于说阿萨巴斯卡语的小股游猎群，他们是戴尼扎人（即比弗人）和后来的楚蒂纳人的亲族；人们乘桦皮舟、踏雪鞋在各个冬营之间迁徙，猎取驼鹿、林地驯鹿和海狸，再把毛皮和肉干卖给南方开阔平原上的猎牛人。

18世纪，经哈得孙湾贸易获得枪械的克里人各部以中间商身份西进，把戴尼扎人逼向皮斯河，林中后来成为楚蒂纳人的人群则分离出去、南下平原。克里人与比弗人的长期战争，直到1781年天花大流行重创双方才告结束，和约以皮斯河为界。商人随军而至：彼得·庞德1778年在阿萨巴斯卡地区建起第一座贸易站，1788年阿萨巴斯卡湖畔建起奇普瓦恩堡，1802年西北公司在小奴湖的布法罗湾设立商站，把这片湖地纳入北方皮货运输队的航路。

en:
The Tsuu T'ina land is the eastern flank of the Rocky Mountains, where forested foothills run down from the Banff and Jasper ranges toward the short-grass prairie. In 1444 small Athabascan-speaking bands hunted this forest edge, kin of the Dane-zaa of the northern woods, for the Tsuu T'ina had not yet separated from them: they took moose, elk and bison in the timbered river valleys through the winter and ranged out onto the prairie after buffalo in summer. Dog trains and travois, not yet horses, moved their camps, and beyond the edge of the woods the Blackfoot world began.

Early in the 18th century the people who would be called Tsuu T'ina split from the Dane-zaa and moved south onto the plains, becoming tipi-dwelling buffalo hunters and, in time, close allies of the Blackfoot Confederacy. The smallpox epidemic of 1781 swept their camps with the rest of the northern plains. In September 1799 the North West and Hudson's Bay companies built Rocky Mountain House and Acton House on the North Saskatchewan at the edge of their winter woods, trading with the Blackfoot and with Kootenay bands crossing the mountains; from there David Thompson found Howse Pass in 1807. In the 1810s Thompson found Tsuu T'ina bands living in the Beaver Hills near modern Edmonton, side by side with the Cree.
zh:
楚蒂纳之地是落基山脉的东麓：森林覆盖的山麓从班夫、贾斯珀一带的山岭向下延伸，过渡到短草平原。1444年，小股说阿萨巴斯卡语的游猎群在这条林缘地带出没，他们是北方林中戴尼扎人的亲族，当时楚蒂纳人尚未与戴尼扎人分离：冬天在林木繁茂的河谷猎取驼鹿、马鹿和野牛，夏天则前出平原追猎野牛。移动营地靠狗队和拖橇，那时还没有马；林缘之外，便是黑脚人的世界。

18世纪初，后来被称为楚蒂纳的人群与戴尼扎人分离，南下进入平原，改住圆锥形帐篷，成为猎牛人，并最终成为黑脚联盟的亲密盟友。1781年的天花大流行，像席卷北部平原其他各部一样扫过他们的营地。1799年9月，西北公司和哈得孙湾公司在北萨斯喀彻温河、楚蒂纳人冬季林地的边缘，先后建起落基山屋和阿克顿商站，与黑脚人及翻山而来的库特尼人交易；1807年，戴维·汤普森正是从落基山屋出发，找到了豪斯山口。1810年代，汤普森发现楚蒂纳人的队伍住在今埃德蒙顿附近的比弗山一带，与克里人毗邻而居。

en:
The Nimíipuu, whose name means 'we, the people,' are the Plateau people of the lower Snake and Clearwater river canyons and their grassy uplands. For thousands of years families moved with the seasons: taking salmon at fishing stations, gathering camas and cous roots, hunting in the mountains, and wintering in sheltered stream villages. In 1444 this country was traveled on foot and by river canoe, bound to other Sahaptin-speaking villages and to trading partners across the Columbia Plateau, the northern Great Basin, and the edge of the plains. No outside ruler claimed the canyons; leadership rested with village headmen and experienced families.

Horses reached the Nimíipuu during the eighteenth century. Carefully bred herds became a measure of wealth, enabled longer bison hunts beyond the mountains, and the spotted horses later known as Appaloosas became especially associated with them. On 20 September 1805, William Clark's party met a Nimíipuu camp at Weippe Prairie after a starving crossing of the Bitterroots, and the people fed the exhausted explorers. Walammottinin, known as Twisted Hair, kept their horses while Lewis and Clark went on to the Pacific. When the expedition returned in the spring of 1806, it spent about a month among the Nimíipuu before turning east. French-Canadian trappers had already spread the name Nez Percé, but in 1821 the Snake and Clearwater country remained firmly Nimíipuu land.
zh:
尼米普人在自己的语言中意为「我们这些人」，是斯内克河下游、克利尔沃特河峡谷及周围草甸高原的居民。数千年来，各家族随季节迁徙：在渔场捕捞鲑鱼，采集卡马夏和苦根，入山狩猎，冬天回到溪流旁避风的村落。1444年时，人们仍靠步行和独木舟穿行此地，同其他说萨哈泼丁语的村落，以及哥伦比亚高原、北部大盆地和大平原边缘的贸易伙伴往来。没有外来统治者控制这些峡谷，权威属于村落首领和富有经验的家族。

十八世纪，马传入尼米普人中间。精心繁育的马群成为财富的标志，也使人们能够翻山进行更远的野牛狩猎；后来被称为阿帕卢萨马的斑点马尤其与他们联系在一起。1805年9月20日，威廉·克拉克的队伍在翻越比特鲁特山脉后，于韦普大草原遇到尼米普人的营地，饥疲交加的探险者得到了食物。绰号「缠发」的瓦拉莫蒂宁替他们照料马匹，让刘易斯和克拉克继续前往太平洋。1806年春远征队返程时，又在尼米普人中间停留约一个月，随后东归。法裔加拿大捕兽者虽已传开「内兹珀斯」这个称呼，但到1821年，斯内克河与克利尔沃特河流域仍是稳固的尼米普人之地。

en:
Banakwut is high Shoshone country on the Snake River Plain, where cold sagebrush flats and lava fields are cut by streams draining toward the Snake. Shoshoni-speaking peoples spread onto the plain between 600 and 1500. In 1444 small bands followed a seasonal round, gathering camas and other roots, reaching the river's fishing places for salmon, and taking game whose furs saw them through severe winters.

Horses reached the Snake country in the late 1600s or early 1700s, and during the eighteenth century a Northern Paiute band that became the Bannock joined the Northern Shoshone on these plains. Mounted bands ranged south into the Great Basin and east through the Rockies to hunt bison. Lewis and Clark became the first non-natives to reach the Snake watershed in 1805, and their passage through the region in 1805–1806 was followed by American and British fur trappers. By 1821 beaver parties were entering Bannock and Shoshone country, but mounted camps still controlled the interior trails.
zh:
巴纳库特是斯内克河平原上高寒的肖肖尼土地，寒冷的艾灌丛荒原和熔岩原被流向斯内克河的溪流切开。说肖肖尼语的人群在600年至1500年间扩散到这片平原。1444年时，一个个小群体按季节迁徙，采集卡马夏等根茎，到河上渔场捕捞鲑鱼，并猎取野兽，用兽皮熬过严冬。

马在17世纪末或18世纪初传入斯内克地区；18世纪，一支后来成为班诺克人的北派尤特群体来到这些平原，与北肖肖尼人共同生活。骑马的队伍向南进入大盆地，向东穿过落基山脉猎捕野牛。1805年，刘易斯与克拉克成为最早抵达斯内克河流域的非原住民；他们在1805—1806年穿越这一带后，美国和英国毛皮猎人相继到来。到1821年，捕猎河狸的队伍已经进入班诺克与肖肖尼人的土地，但骑马营地仍控制着内陆通道。

en:
The Miwok of this province are the Coast Miwok, whose lands run from the Golden Gate north to Duncans Point and along the south of Sonoma, taking in the Point Reyes peninsula, Tomales and Bodega bays and the tidal marshes of San Pablo Bay. In 1444 the Hookooeko of Marin, the Olamentko around Bodega and the Lekahtewutko of southern Sonoma lived in independent village communities without a common chief. They gathered acorns and buckeye, netted salmon in the creeks and camped on the shore in fishing season, leaving great shellmounds around the bays, and kept charmstones at Tolay Lake for ceremony and healing. No foreign sail had yet been seen from these headlands.

On 17 June 1579 Sir Francis Drake anchored the Golden Hind in the sheltered bay under Point Reyes, spent five weeks repairing her, named the country New Albion and was visited by crowds of Miwok; the ship's chaplain left the first written account of them. In 1595 the Manila galleon San Agustin, under Sebastian Cermeno, was wrecked by a storm in the same bay, and its cargo washed into Miwok hands. Spain never settled this shore: from 1783 Coast Miwoks were drawn instead to Mission San Francisco across the Golden Gate, 850 of them baptised by 1817. On 14 December 1817 Father Vicente de Sarria founded Mission San Rafael Arcangel in their homeland as a hospital outstation for sick neophytes, the northernmost and last Spanish foundation in Alta California. By then only the ocean coast from Point Reyes to Bodega still belonged to the Miwok; four years later Spanish rule gave way to Mexican independence.
zh:
本省的米沃克人是海岸米沃克人，他们的土地从金门向北延伸到邓肯斯角，包括雷伊斯角半岛、托马莱斯湾、博德加湾和圣巴勃罗湾的潮汐沼泽。1444年，马林的胡库艾科人、博德加一带的奥拉门特科人和索诺马南部的莱卡特乌特科人分成一个个互不统属的村庄，没有共同的酋长。他们采拾橡子和七叶树果，在溪中网捕鲑鱼，渔汛时到海边扎营，在海湾四周留下巨大的贝丘；托莱湖则是供奉护符石、举行仪式与疗愈的圣地。那时的海岬上还没有人见过外来的帆影。

1579年6月17日，弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士把「金鹿号」停泊在雷伊斯角背风的海湾里，花五周修好船身，将这片土地命名为新阿尔比恩；成群的米沃克人到营地造访，随船牧师留下了关于他们最早的文字记载。1595年，塞巴斯蒂安·塞尔梅尼奥率领的马尼拉大帆船「圣阿古斯丁号」在同一个海湾遇风暴沉没，船上货物流入了米沃克人手中。西班牙人始终没有在这片海岸殖民：从1783年起，海岸米沃克人被陆续带进金门对岸的圣弗朗西斯科传教所，到1817年已有八百五十人受洗。1817年12月14日，文森特·德·萨里亚神父在他们的故地建立圣拉斐尔·阿坎赫尔传教所，作为疗养患病新信徒的医疗分站，这是西班牙在上加利福尼亚建立的最北、也是最后一处据点。到那时，只有雷伊斯角到博德加的大洋沿岸仍归米沃克人所有；四年后，西班牙的统治随墨西哥独立而终结。

en:
Haida is Haida Gwaii, the archipelago beyond Hecate Strait formed around Graham and Moresby islands and exposed to Pacific swells. The Haida speak a language isolate and were among the great seafarers of the Northwest Coast. Cedar-plank houses, carved poles, Raven and Eagle clans, ocean-going canoes, halibut and salmon fishing, potlatches, and long-distance trade shaped island life; sea raids also brought captives and wealth. By 1444 more than a hundred villages occupied sheltered beaches and streams, and the islands looked outward to sea routes rather than toward the mainland.

Juan Pérez's Spanish ship Santiago traded with Haida canoes in July 1774, although currents prevented a landing. James Cook's expedition sighted the islands in 1778, and the sea-otter trade opened decisively when George Dixon arrived in 1787 and named them the Queen Charlotte Islands. Haida dealers drove hard bargains with Spanish, British, Russian, and American ships and used acquired guns and cannon in their own wars. The trade could turn violent: in 1794 Haida parties captured and sank the American ships Ino and Resolution, with only one crewman surviving from each. Through 1821 the islands remained an independent Haida stronghold at the centre of a profitable sea-otter network.
zh:
海达即赫卡特海峡外的海达瓜依群岛，以格雷厄姆岛、莫尔斯比岛和周边小岛直面太平洋涌浪。海达语是一门孤立语言，海达人也是西北海岸最出色的航海族群之一。雪松木板大屋、雕刻柱、渡鸦与鹰两大家族、远洋独木舟、大比目鱼和鲑鱼捕捞、夸富宴以及长途贸易塑造了岛屿生活；海上劫掠也带来俘虏和财富。到1444年，已有一百多座村庄分布在避风海滩与溪流旁，群岛的联系主要面向海上航路，而非东侧大陆。

1774年7月，西班牙探险家胡安·佩雷斯的「圣地亚哥号」与海达独木舟交易，但海流使其未能登陆。詹姆斯·库克的探险队于1778年望见这些岛屿；1787年乔治·迪克森抵达后，海獭贸易真正打开，他将群岛命名为夏洛特皇后群岛。海达商人与西班牙、英国、俄国和美国船只强硬议价，也把获得的火枪和火炮用于自身战争。贸易随时可能转为暴力：1794年，海达人俘获并击沉美国船「伊诺号」和「决心号」，两船各只有一名船员生还。直至1821年，群岛仍是独立的海达要塞，位于利润丰厚的海獭贸易网络中心。

en:
Between the upper Delaware and the North Branch of the Susquehanna lie the wooded ridges of the Endless Mountains, broken by the long river meadow the Munsee called xwéːwamənk, 'at the big river flat' — the Wyoming Valley. Munsee bands, the northernmost division of the Lenape, kept stockaded villages on the flats: two fortified villages stood opposite modern Wilkes-Barre in the fifteenth century. They raised maize on the floodplains (the crop appears in valley archaeology around 1300), fished the river and hunted the oak and pine ridges, while the Iroquoian Susquehannock below the mountains were rivals and occasional trading partners. In 1444 neither the Minisink trail nor the Susquehanna carried any European goods, and these highlands were entirely Munsee country.

Change arrived through dispossession to the east. After the fraudulent Walking Purchase of 1737, the Onondaga orator Canassatego in 1742 ordered the Delaware River Lenape into the Wyoming flats, joining Shawnee bands settled there since 1701; Nanticoke followed in 1748. Moravians came too — Count Zinzendorf preached on the plain that same November, and David Zeisberger worked the valley for years. In 1754 Teedyuscung led his band up from Gnadenhütten, led the frontier raids of 1755–56 and argued the Lenape case at Easton before being burned in his cabin in April 1763; the Mill Creek killings that year drove out Connecticut's first surveyors. The Susquehanna Company held a disputed Iroquois deed of 1754 and sent settlers in force from 1769, and its 'Yankees' and Pennsylvania's 'Pennamites' besieged each other's forts through 1769–1771 and skirmished again at Christmas 1775. On 3 July 1778 John Butler's Loyalist rangers with Seneca warriors overran the valley militia in the Battle of Wyoming, sending hundreds of families fleeing over the Poconos in the 'Great Runaway'; Sullivan's expedition marshalled here in 1779 before marching against the Haudenosaunee. A Continental Congress tribunal at Trenton awarded the valley to Pennsylvania in December 1782, yet a third war flared in 1784. Luzerne County was created in 1786, the Confirming Act secured the Yankee land titles in 1787, and the Compromise Act of 1799 closed the thirty-year quarrel. In 1808 Jesse Fell of Wilkes-Barre proved that the local anthracite would burn in an iron grate, opening the great coalfield beneath the flats.
zh:
在上特拉华河与萨斯奎哈纳河北支之间，横亘着林木覆盖的「无尽山脉」，群山之间夹着一道长长的河滩——蒙西人称之为 xwéːwamənk，意为「大河滩之地」，即怀俄明谷。蒙西人是特拉华三大分支中最北的一支，在滩地上设栅筑村，15世纪时今日威尔克斯-巴里对岸就有两座栅寨。他们在河漫滩上种玉米（当地考古所见玉米约始于1300年），在河里捕鱼，在橡树与松树林覆盖的山梁上狩猎；山脉以南讲易洛魁语的萨斯奎哈纳人既是对手，也是偶尔往来的贸易伙伴。1444年，无论米尼辛克小路还是萨斯奎哈纳河上都还没有欧洲货，这片高地完全是蒙西人的土地。

变局来自东方的夺地。1737年欺诈性的「步行购地」之后，1742年，奥农达加演说家卡纳萨特戈勒令特拉华河畔的特拉华人迁入怀俄明河滩，与1701年起就落脚于此的肖尼人为邻，南蒂科克人也于1748年随之而来。摩拉维亚传教士接踵而至：同年11月亲岑道夫伯爵就在这片平原上传教，大卫·蔡斯伯格更在此地活动多年。1754年，蒂迪尤斯康率部从格纳登许顿迁入，领导了1755—1756年的边疆袭扰，并在伊斯顿谈判中为特拉华人申辩；1763年4月，他在自己的棚屋里被烧死，随后的米尔溪杀戮赶走了康涅狄格的第一批测量员。萨斯奎哈纳公司凭一份1754年取得、争议重重的易洛魁地契，于1769年起大举移民，公司的「扬基」与宾州的「宾州仔」在1769—1771年间互相围攻堡垒，1775年圣诞节间再次冲突。1778年7月3日，约翰·巴特勒率领的效忠派游骑兵会同塞内卡战士击溃谷地民兵，是为怀俄明之战，数百户人家翻山逃入波科诺山区，史称「大逃亡」；1779年沙利文远征军以此为集结地，北上征讨豪德诺索尼。1782年12月，大陆会议在特伦顿的仲裁庭把怀俄明谷判给宾州，但1784年第三次战争又起。1786年宾州设立卢泽恩县，1787年《确认法》保住了扬基们的地契，1799年《妥协法》终于结束这场长达三十年的争执。1808年，威尔克斯-巴里的杰西·费尔证实本地无烟煤能在铁炉箅上燃烧，滩地下方大煤田的开发由此开启。

en:
Garoowe sits in the broad Nugaal valley, where the seasonal Nugaal river runs east to the sea at the old harbour of Eyl. The valley is wide pastoral country: Darod Somali clans, including the Marehan, grazed camels and flocks across its thorn scrub and watered them at wells where trade routes from the Bari highlands, Mudug and the interior met, which in time made Garoowe a caravan crossroads. Eyl, an ancient port at the river's mouth, linked the coast to the Indian Ocean traffic in hides, livestock and fish. From the early 15th century the rising Majeerteen sultanate on the Guardafui coast made its influence felt this far south, and in 1444 the valley's clans were Sunni Muslims and nominal subjects of the house of Aluula.

The Majeerteen re-emerged as a strong, centralized kingdom in the mid-18th century, and by the years around 1800 the Nugaal pasturelands and the Eyl roadstead were counted an integral part of its domains; their herds and coast were the sultanate's southern flank, bordering the country of rival clans. Garoowe itself remained no more than a well station and market amid the grazing grounds until colonial times.
zh:
加罗韦位于宽阔的努加尔河谷中，季节性的努加尔河由此向东，在古老的埃伊尔港入海。河谷是广阔的牧地：包括马雷汉人在内的达鲁德系索马里氏族在灌丛间放牧骆驼和羊群，在水井处饮水；巴里高地、穆杜格与内陆的商路也在此交汇，使加罗韦逐渐成为商队枢纽。河口的埃伊尔是一座古老港口，把沿岸出产的兽皮、牲畜和鱼接入印度洋贸易。15世纪初，瓜达富伊角沿岸兴起的马吉尔廷苏丹国把势力伸展到这么靠南的地方；1444年时，河谷诸氏族都是逊尼派穆斯林，名义上臣属阿卢拉的王帐。

18世纪中叶，马吉尔廷重新崛起为强大的集权王国，到1800年前后，努加尔牧场和埃伊尔锚地已被视为其版图不可分割的一部分，畜群与海岸构成苏丹国的南翼，与敌对氏族的土地接壤。加罗韦本身在殖民时代到来之前，始终不过是牧地中的一处水井驿站和集市。

en:
South Georgia is a rugged, mountainous island in the cold South Atlantic, about 1,400 kilometres east of the Falklands. Glaciers descend from its central ridge, whose highest peak is Mount Paget, while deep bays and fjords cut into the northern coast. Its harsh climate and distance from the mainland meant that no indigenous people settled there. In 1444 it lay beyond the regular routes of European shipping, its shores crowded with elephant seals, fur seals and seabirds rather than hunters or garrisons.

British accounts credit the London merchant Anthony de la Roché with a probable sighting in 1675, and early maps called it Roche Island. The Spanish account, especially in Argentine historiography, identifies the merchant ship León under Gregorio Jerez as the first recorded discoverer on 29 June 1756, St Peter's Day, hence the name Isla San Pedro. The first certain landing came on 17 January 1775, when James Cook in HMS Resolution surveyed the island, claimed it for George III and named it the Isle of Georgia. From 1786 sealers began using its harbours, but the work remained seasonal; in 1821 South Georgia still had no permanent settlement.
zh:
南乔治亚是寒冷南大西洋上一座崎岖多山的岛屿，位于福克兰群岛以东约1400公里。冰川沿中央山脊下泻，最高峰为佩吉特山，北岸则被深湾与峡湾切入。严酷气候和远离大陆的位置使这里没有原住民定居。1444年，它尚在欧洲船只的常规航线之外，岸边聚集的是象海豹、海狗和海鸟，而不是猎人或驻军。

英国说法认为，伦敦商人安东尼·德拉罗什可能在1675年望见此岛，早期地图因而称其为罗奇岛。西班牙文资料及主要的阿根廷史学叙述则认为，有记录的发现者是格雷戈里奥·赫雷斯指挥的商船「莱昂号」，日期为1756年6月29日，即圣彼得日，岛名圣佩德罗岛也由此而来。首次确定登陆发生在1775年1月17日，詹姆斯·库克率「决心号」测绘该岛，以乔治三世之名宣布占有，并命名为乔治亚岛。1786年起，海豹捕猎者开始利用这里的港湾，但活动仍限于季节往返；到1821年，南乔治亚依旧没有常住定居点。

en:
Thanjavur stands in the green Kaveri delta, the rice granary of the Tamil country. The imperial Cholas made it their capital from the ninth century, and around 1010 Rajaraja I raised the Brihadisvara temple in its heart, its granite tower rising over a city of weavers, merchants and brahman settlements. Pandya armies took it in 1279, and the raids of Malik Kafur early in the fourteenth century opened it to the Delhi sultanate and then the short-lived Ma'bar sultans. Vijayanagara's generals absorbed the delta from the 1360s, and an inscription of Deva Raya II dated 1443 shows that in 1444 the city was a provincial seat of the empire, ruled through a nayak governor while its looms and the delta's rice harvests kept its markets full.

In 1532 the viceroy Sevappa Nayak made his line hereditary and founded the Thanjavur Nayak kingdom. Even after the Vijayanagara army went down at Talikota in 1565 his successors ruled on as patrons of Telugu and Tamil poetry and temple building. In 1673 Chokkanatha Nayak of Madurai seized the city, but within a year Ekoji, a Maratha feudatory of Bijapur and half-brother of Shivaji, took it and founded the Maratha dynasty under which Thanjavur became a centre of Carnatic music and home to the painted style known as Tanjore. The Marathas held their own against the nawab of Arcot and the European companies on the coast until 1799, when the British restored Serfoji II to the throne but took the kingdom's administration into their own hands, leaving the raja his fort and his court.
zh:
坦焦尔（坦贾武尔）位于肥沃的高韦里河三角洲，是泰米尔之乡的米仓。9世纪起，称霸南印的朱罗王朝以此为都；约1010年，罗茶罗乍一世在城中心修建布里哈迪希瓦拉神庙，花岗岩高塔俯瞰着织工、商人和婆罗门聚落遍布的城市。1279年，潘地亚军队攻陷此城；14世纪初马利克·卡富尔的入侵又使它先后归入德里苏丹国和短命的马巴尔苏丹。14世纪60年代起，毗奢耶那伽罗的将领们逐步吞并三角洲；一块镌于1443年的提婆罗耶二世铭文表明，1444年的坦焦尔已是帝国的一处行省重镇，由纳亚克总督治理，织机与三角洲稻米支撑着繁荣的市集。

1532年，地方长官塞瓦帕·纳亚克将权位转为世袭，建立坦焦尔纳亚克王朝。1565年毗奢耶那伽罗大军在塔利哥达战败后，他的继承者仍继续统治，庇护泰卢固语与泰米尔语诗歌，大兴寺庙。1673年，马杜赖的乔卡纳塔·纳亚克夺取此城，但不出一年，为比贾布尔苏丹效力的马拉塔将领、希瓦吉的异母弟埃科吉便攻占坦焦尔，建立马拉塔王朝；在其治下，坦焦尔成为卡纳提克音乐的中心，也孕育了后世称作「坦焦尔画」的绘画风格。马拉塔人在阿尔科特纳瓦布和海岸上欧洲公司之间周旋求存，直到1799年，英国人扶立塞尔福吉二世复位，却把王国行政收归己手，只给这位罗阇留下城堡与宫廷。

en:
Arcot, the Tamil Arkad or 'fig forest', lies on the southern bank of the Palar river, where the road from the Coromandel coast climbs through the Javadi hills towards Mysore. In 1444 it was a fortified town of the Vijayanagara Empire, guarding a gap in the eastern ghats and gathering the grain and iron of the Palar valley for the merchants of the coastal plain. For another two centuries it remained an imperial garrison town in the Tamil south.

With Vijayanagara's collapse the Carnatic was divided between Golconda and Bijapur in the 1640s, and in 1692 Aurangzeb made Arcot the seat of Zulfiqar Khan, first Mughal subahdar of the Carnatic. Saadatullah Khan moved his court there from Gingee in the 1710s, and thereafter Arcot was the capital of the nawabs of the Carnatic. In 1740 the Marathas swept through the Damalcherry pass, killed Nawab Dost Ali Khan and took the town almost without resistance. A disputed succession drew in the European trading companies: in 1751 Robert Clive seized Arcot for Muhammad Ali Wallajah and with a tiny garrison survived a fifty-three-day siege by Chanda Sahib's French-backed forces, from 23 September to 14 November. Wallajah's long reign left the nawab deep in debt to the Company, and in 1801 the East India Company took over the Carnatic outright, leaving the nawabs a pension and their name alone.
zh:
阿尔果德，泰米尔语「阿尔卡德」，意为榕树林，坐落在帕拉尔河南岸，科罗曼德海岸通向迈索尔的道路在此穿过贾瓦迪丘陵的山口。1444年，这里是毗奢耶那伽罗帝国的一座要塞城镇，扼守东高止山的隘口，把帕拉尔河谷的粮食和铁料汇聚到沿海平原的商人手中。此后近两百年间，它始终是帝国在泰米尔南部的驻军要地。

毗奢耶那伽罗崩溃后，卡纳提克在1640年代被高康达与比贾布尔瓜分；1692年，奥朗则布任命祖勒菲卡尔汗为首任卡纳提克总督，驻节阿尔果德。1710年代，萨阿达图拉汗把宫廷从京吉迁来，此地此后成为卡纳提克诸纳瓦布的都城。1740年，马拉塔人越过达马尔切里山口，纳瓦布多斯特·阿里汗战死，阿尔果德几乎未作抵抗便告失守。随后的继承之争把欧洲商馆也卷了进来：1751年，罗伯特·克莱武替穆罕默德·阿里·瓦拉贾夺取阿尔果德，凭借一支微弱的守军顶住了钱达·萨希布背后有法国支持的军队长达五十三天的围攻（9月23日至11月14日）。瓦拉贾的长期统治使纳瓦布债台高筑、受制于东印度公司，1801年公司直接兼并卡纳提克，留给纳瓦布的只有年金和空头名号。

en:
Mahur commands wooded ridges above the Penganga valley, on the old frontier between the Deccan sultanates, Berar and Gond-held lands. The Renuka temple on Mahurgad made the hills a Hindu pilgrimage place, while the great fort guarded roads through dense forest. Gond rulers held the stronghold after its earlier medieval history, but Bahmanid power took it in 1358, lost it to a Gond king of Berar in 1398, and reconquered Mahurgad under Ahmad Shah in 1428. Thus in 1444 Mahur was a recently subdued Hindu border country governed from the Bahmanid camp, its forests supplying timber and its fort watching the northern approaches.

In 1478 or 1479 the Bahmanis divided Berar into two provinces, one centred on Gawil and the other on Mahur. When Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk founded the independent Imad Shahi sultanate of Berar in 1490, Mahur was brought into his new kingdom. Burhan Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar defeated Alauddin Imad Shah and occupied the fort in 1527, and Ahmadnagar absorbed the remainder of Berar in 1574. Mughal forces took Mahur in 1617 and later granted the district as a jagir; Savitribai Deshmukh, called Rai Bagan, served Aurangzeb in the succession war of 1658. Maratha forces under Shivaji gained the region in 1670, Mughal rule returned after 1689, and following the Battle of Balapur in 1724 Mahur passed under the Nizam of Hyderabad.
zh:
马胡尔据守彭甘加河谷上方林木茂密的山脊，处在德干诸苏丹国、贝拉尔与冈德人土地之间的古老边地。马胡尔加德的雷努卡神庙使这片丘陵成为印度教朝圣地，大山寨则扼守穿过密林的道路。中世纪早期之后，冈德统治者占据这座要塞；巴赫曼尼势力1358年将其夺取，1398年又被贝拉尔的冈德国王夺回，艾哈迈德沙阿1428年再度征服马胡尔加德。因此到1444年，马胡尔是一片新近被降服的印度教边地，由巴赫曼尼阵营统辖；山林出产木材，要塞监视北方通道。

1478年或1479年，巴赫曼尼把贝拉尔分为两个省，分别以加维尔和马胡尔为中心。1490年，法图拉·伊马德—穆勒克建立独立的贝拉尔伊马德沙阿苏丹国，马胡尔被纳入新王国。1527年，艾哈迈德讷格尔的布尔汉·尼扎姆沙阿击败阿拉乌丁·伊马德沙阿并占领要塞；1574年，艾哈迈德讷格尔吞并贝拉尔余部。莫卧儿军队1617年夺取马胡尔，后来把这一地区封作札吉尔；被称为拉伊·巴甘的萨维特里拜·德什穆赫在1658年继承战争中为奥朗则布效力。希瓦吉率领的马拉塔军队1670年取得此地，1689年后莫卧儿统治恢复；1724年巴拉普尔战役后，马胡尔转入海得拉巴尼扎姆治下。

en:
South Kanara is the southern half of Tulu Nadu, a rainy coast squeezed between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats, whose rivers Netravati and Gurupura meet the sea in the great estuary at Mangalore. The sixth-century Greek monk Cosmas counted Mangarouth among the five pepper ports of Malabar, and rice, areca, pepper and ghat timber have moved through its roadstead ever since. The native Alupa dynasty governed the country as feudatories of the Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Hoysalas from the seventh century until 1345, when Vijayanagara took control; Ibn Battuta, landing in 1342, had found Manjarur one of the busiest estuaries of the coast. In 1444 the land, divided into the Mangalore and Barkur provinces, answers to Vijayanagara, its Tulu-speaking chieftains and merchants shipping pepper and timber to Arabia.

Vasco da Gama touched the St Mary's Islands in 1498, and in 1506 Varthema saw nearly sixty rice ships in Mangalore roads; in 1526 the viceroy Lopo Vaz de Sampaio seized the town for Portugal, and the coastal trade fell under its guns. In 1554 Sadashiv Nayaka of Keladi established his authority over South Canara, and after the fall of Vijayanagara in 1565 the Keladi Nayakas ruled from Bednore, Arabs burning the town in 1695 in reprisal for Portuguese trade controls. Hyder Ali of Mysore conquered it in 1763; the British held it from 1767 until Tipu Sultan retook it in 1783 and renamed it Jalalabad, then signed the treaty of Mangalore with the Company on 11 March 1784. Tipu's fall in 1799 left the port to the British, and in 1801 Buchanan found it prosperous, its rice sailing to Muscat, Goa and Bombay, its pepper and sandalwood following.
zh:
南卡纳达是图卢纳德的南半部分，夹在阿拉伯海与西高止山之间，气候多雨，内德拉瓦蒂河与古鲁普拉河在门格洛尔的大河口入海。6世纪的希腊修士科斯马斯把门格劳特列为马拉巴尔五大胡椒港之一，此后大米、槟榔、胡椒和高止山木材一直经此外港转运。本土的阿卢帕王朝作为遮娄其、罗湿陀罗拘陀和曷萨拉的藩属，从7世纪统治此地到1345年为毗奢耶那伽罗所并；1342年伊本·白图泰登岸时，已见曼贾鲁尔是沿岸最繁忙的河口之一。1444年，这片土地分为门格洛尔和巴尔库尔两行省，奉毗奢耶那伽罗为主，说图卢语的酋长和商人把胡椒、木材运往阿拉伯。

1498年瓦斯科·达·伽马途经圣玛丽群岛，1506年瓦尔泰马在这里看到近六十艘满载大米的船只；1526年葡属印度总督洛波·瓦斯·德·桑帕约夺取城镇，沿海贸易落入葡萄牙的炮火控制。1554年，凯拉迪的萨达希夫·纳亚卡确立了对南卡纳达的统治，1565年毗奢耶那伽罗陷落后，凯拉迪纳亚卡家族从贝德努尔发号施令，1695年阿拉伯人因葡萄牙限制贸易而焚毁城镇。1763年迈索尔的海德尔·阿里征服此地，英国东印度公司1767年起占据，1783年提普苏丹将其收复并改名贾拉拉巴德，又于1784年3月11日与公司签订《门格洛尔条约》，结束第二次英国—迈索尔战争。1799年提普败亡，港口落入英国之手；1801年布坎南到此，见商路殷盛，大米远销马斯喀特、果阿和孟买，胡椒与檀香木随之出海。

en:
Goa is the island-studded mouth of the Mandovi and Zuari rivers, where the Western Ghats meet the Arabian Sea and the spice-laden Malabar coast opens on the harbours of the Konkan. The Kadamba kings made their port of Govapuri there, and after the Delhi sultan's armies overran it in 1312, Harihara I of Vijayanagara brought the islands under his rule by about 1370. In 1444 Goa was a busy imperial harbour, its wharves landing Arab horses for the Vijayanagara cavalry and shipping out the pepper and cardamom gathered in the Ghat forests; mosques stood beside Jain and Hindu temples in a town long used to foreign merchants.

The Bahmani sultan's armies seized Goa in 1469, and when that sultanate split apart the Adil Shahis of Bijapur built a new walled city on the Mandovi, their second capital. In 1510 Afonso de Albuquerque, called in by the Goan privateer Timoji, took that city, lost it within months, and retook it on 25 November. It became the capital of the Portuguese East, an archbishop's see and a city said to rival Lisbon: Francis Xavier landed there in 1542, a Jesuit press produced the first books printed in India at Saint Paul's College in 1556, and the Goa Inquisition opened in 1560. Dutch blockades, Maratha raids and repeated epidemics wore the old city down in the seventeenth century; the viceroy withdrew to Panjim in 1759, the Pinto revolt of Goan clergy and nobles against racial privilege was betrayed and crushed in 1787, and the Inquisition was at last abolished in 1812, when the once-proud eastern capital had become a city of great churches standing among ruins.
zh:
果阿是曼多维河与祖阿里河河口的群岛地带，西高止山在此直抵阿拉伯海，盛产香料的马拉巴尔海岸也在此接上孔坎诸港。卡丹巴王朝曾以这里的戈瓦普里为港；1312年德里苏丹的军队将其攻陷，1370年前后又被毗奢耶那伽罗的诃里诃罗一世收入版图。1444年的果阿是帝国一座繁忙的海港：码头上卸下供毗奢耶那伽罗骑兵使用的阿拉伯马，再把西高止山林出产的胡椒、豆蔻装船外运；这座城市见惯了外商，清真寺与耆那教、印度教寺院比邻而立。

1469年，巴赫曼尼苏丹的军队夺取果阿；苏丹国瓦解后，比贾布尔的阿迪尔沙王朝在曼多维河畔建起一座有城墙的新城，作为自己的第二都城。1510年，应果阿私掠船长提莫吉之请，阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克攻占此城，不出数月又失守，同年11月25日再度攻克。果阿此后成为葡属东方的首府、大主教驻节之地，富庶据说不输里斯本：1542年方济各·沙勿略在此登岸，1556年耶稣会在圣保罗学院印出印度最早的书籍，1560年果阿宗教裁判所成立。进入17世纪，荷兰人的封锁、马拉塔人的袭击和接连不断的瘟疫让旧城日渐凋敝；1759年总督迁往帕纳吉，1787年果阿教士与贵族反抗种族特权的平托起义被出卖并镇压，1812年宗教裁判所终告废除——此时这座昔日的东方名城，已是伟教堂矗立于废墟间的模样。

en:
Morasanadu is the old Morasu Nadu, the high plateau east of the Mysore country and homeland of the Morasu Vokkaliga peasant warriors, watered by the Arkavati. A hero stone found at Begur names the village of Bengaluru in an inscription of 890, and Vijayanagara court records knew the same place as Devarayanagara.
