A garrison lieutenant posted there in 1687 commanded a thousand bannermen; Bargu Mongols were settled there in 1692 and 131 Sibe tribesmen followed in 1699. In 1727 a deputy garrison general took his seat at Xiongyue with authority over every banner post from the Yalu to the Liaodong Peninsula, making it the military centre of the south. Gaiping itself remained the market town of a fishing and coasting shore.
zh:
盖州位于辽东半岛西北岸，滨海丘陵在此缓缓落入渤海。西汉高帝十二年（前195年）此地置平郭县；高句丽时称盖牟城，是后来「盖」字的根源，645年唐军克建安城后，渤海国在此置盖州。辽代改为辰州，金明昌六年（1195年）复名盖州。明洪武四年（1371年）废州改卫，置盖州卫，次年改筑新城；它与金州卫、复州卫、海州卫并称「南四卫」，刑名事务跨海隶属山东按察司。1444年，这里是渤海岸上一座筑城屯守的渔业海港，补给船渡海往返山东。

1621年沈阳、辽阳失守，盖州卫随辽东各卫归入后金。康熙三年（1664年），清廷取「盖州」「平郭」首字置盖平县，隶奉天府；近旁的熊岳城则在顺治元年（1644年）成为关外最早设立的九处八旗城守官驻地之一。1687年熊岳改设防守尉，额兵一千；1692年巴尔虎蒙古派驻于此，1699年又有一百三十一名锡伯兵调来。1727年，熊岳置副都统，统辖鸭绿江至辽东半岛各处驻防，成为辽南实质上的军事中心，而盖平始终是这片渔舟往来的海岸上的集镇。

en:
Ereen takes its name from the Ereen Dabsan Nuur, the “variegated salt lake” set in the Gobi steppe where the Xilingol grasslands give way to the Khalkha desert. Mongol herdsmen pastured their flocks around its brine pools, and raiders and caravans alike crossed this neck of the Gobi. In 1444 the land was the grazing ground of Mongol otogs under the Northern Yuan of Taisun Khan, whose Oirat taishi Esen five years later shattered the Ming army at Tumu and carried off the Zhengtong Emperor. The Sünid ranged here under their own lords, and the lake's salt drew flocks and traders from across the desert.

After Dayan Khan, reigning from 1480 to 1517, reunited the Mongols, these pastures were allotted to his left wing, and in time the Sünid became a tribe of the Chahar tumen. When Ligdan Khan pressed hard on the southern tribes, the Sünid chiefs Tenggis and Susai led their people north to the Khalkha and then submitted to Hong Taiji; in 1641 and 1642 the tribe was settled in two banners under the Xilingol League. Qing peace made the Gobi crossing safe, and the caravan track from Kalgan to Khüree grew busy. In 1820 the Yilin relay station was established beside the salt lake, watering the camel trains that carried goods between China and the north.
zh:
二连（额仁）得名于额仁达布散淖尔，即戈壁草原上的「斑斓盐湖」，地处锡林郭勒草原向喀尔喀戈壁过渡的咽喉地带。蒙古牧人在湖畔盐碱滩周围放牧，兵马与商队也都从这处戈壁要径穿行。1444年，这里是北元岱总汗治下蒙古鄂托克的牧场；五年之后，掌握实权的瓦剌太师也先在土木堡击溃明军，俘走明英宗。苏尼特人在自己的领主率领下游牧于此，湖盐也吸引着大漠南北的畜群与客商。

达延汗1480年至1517年重新统一蒙古后，这片牧场被封给左翼，苏尼特后来成为察哈尔万户之一部。林丹汗威逼漠南诸部时，苏尼特首领腾机思、素塞率部北避喀尔喀，随后归附皇太极；1641年和1642年，苏尼特部编为左右两旗，会盟于锡林郭勒。清代承平，戈壁南北通行无警，张家口至库伦的商道日渐繁忙，1820年湖畔设立伊林驿站，为往来中国与北方的驼队补给饮水。

en:
The headwaters of the Luan open here into high pasture between the Gobi and the Ming wall. At Shangdu on this grassland Kublai kept his summer capital from 1263 until Ming armies took it in 1369, and the ruined city stood empty after the Yuan court withdrew onto the steppe. The Chahar grew from the personal guard of the Yuan khans and drifted north during the 15th century. In 1444 this was pasture of the Northern Yuan, where Taisun Khan shared power uneasily with his Oirat strongman Esen, and the Chahar had not yet become the khan's own tumen.

Under Dayan Khan the Chahar became one of the six eastern tumens, the Great Khan's personal appanage in the left wing. Pressed by Altan Khan in the mid-16th century, Daraisung Guden Khan led them east onto the Liao. Ligdan Khan (r. 1604–1634), the last universally recognized Great Khan, tried to reforge Mongol power, but Hong Taiji's campaign of 1632 drove him west to die in flight, and his son Ejei surrendered the imperial seal in 1635 and was enfeoffed at Yizhou. In 1675 the young prince Burni rose with 3,000 riders during the Revolt of the Three Feudatories; within two months the rising was crushed, the Chahar royals were put to death after the battle of 20 April 1675, and the Qing moved the tribe to the Dolon Nor–Zhangjiakou line as the Eight Banners of Chahar, answerable to the throne alone. At Dolon Nor in 1691 Kangxi received the submission of the Khalkha khans and founded the Huizong Monastery, built from 1691 to 1712, which drew pilgrims and caravans to the town. Around 1758 Chahar companies were posted to the newly conquered Ili valley.
zh:
滦河发源于此，高原草场铺展在戈壁与明长城之间。忽必烈在这片草原上的上都度夏，1263年升为夏都，1369年被明军攻克，元廷退回草原后城址荒废。察哈尔由元朝大汗的亲军护卫演变而成，15世纪间北迁到这一带。1444年，这里是北元的牧场，脱脱不花汗与权臣也先同床异梦，察哈尔此时尚未成为大汗亲领的万户。

达延汗时，察哈尔被编入东蒙古六万户，是左翼中大汗亲领的万户。16世纪中叶，在俺答汗的压力下，达赉孙库登汗率部东迁到辽河流域。林丹汗（1604—1634年在位）是最后一位受公认的蒙古大汗，力图重振汗权；1632年皇太极远征，林丹汗西逃、1634年死于途中，其子额哲携传国玉玺于1635年归降，受封亲王、安置于义州。1675年，年轻的亲王布尔尼趁三藩之乱率三千人起兵，不到两月即败亡，王族在1675年4月20日一战后被诛；清廷将部众迁到多伦诺尔至张家口一线，编为察哈尔八旗，不设盟长，直属皇帝。1691年，康熙在多伦诺尔接受喀尔喀诸汗归附，下令营建汇宗寺（1691—1712年建成），多伦诺尔由此成为朝觐者与商队汇聚之地。1758年前后，又有察哈尔兵丁被调驻新定的伊犁河谷。

en:
The Ih Huree country is the valley of the Tuul, where the river curves beneath the forested bulk of Bogd Khan Mountain: rich summer pasture on the old road that linked Karakorum with the sacred Khentii. No town stood here in 1444. The clans grazing their herds in the valley looked to the Chinggisid khan Taisun, though the armed strength of the eastern Mongols was commanded by his Oirat taishi Esen, and the Buddhism that would one day make the place famous had not yet crossed the Gobi in strength.

In 1639 the Khalkha nobles pitched a great yurt monastery at Lake Shireet Tsagaan Nuur as the seat of Zanabazar, the four-year-old first Jebtsundamba Khutuktu. This was Örgöö, the palace camp, which moved its tents twenty-nine times along the Orkhon, Selenge and Tuul, and was even carried into Inner Mongolia before Galdan's advance in 1690. Schooled in Tibet, Zanabazar returned in 1651 and made his camp the heart of Mongol Buddhism, a school of sculpture and letters where he devised the Soyombo script in 1686. After the Treaty of Kyakhta in 1727 the Beijing–Kyakhta caravan road ran through Khüree, and Siberian furs changed hands there for Chinese cloth and tea; by the early eighteenth century it was called Ikh Khüree, the Great Enclosure, with a Chinese trade town of Maimaicheng to its east. A Qing amban was posted to the camp from 1758, and in 1778 the monastery settled for good on the Tuul beneath Bogd Khan Mountain, the same year Beijing recognised the annual ceremony on the mountain. Gandan Monastery was founded in 1809, and by 1810 some thirteen thousand monks lived in a camp that had become Outer Mongolia's religious and commercial capital.
zh:
大库伦一带是土拉河谷地，河水在林木葱郁的博克多汗山脚下蜿蜒流过；这里水草丰美，地处连接哈拉和林与神圣肯特山的古道之上。1444年此地还没有城镇，在河谷放牧的部众听命于成吉思汗后裔岱总汗，而东蒙古的兵马由卫拉特太师也先统领；日后让此地闻名于世的佛教，此时还尚未大举越过戈壁。

1639年，喀尔喀贵族在一处湖畔支起大帐寺院，作为年仅四岁的一世哲布尊丹巴活佛扎那巴扎尔的驻锡地，这便是「乌尔嘎」——宫殿之帐。此后它的帐篷沿鄂尔浑河、色楞格河和土拉河迁徙了二十九次，1690年噶尔丹东进时甚至一度避入内蒙古。扎那巴扎尔在西藏学成，1651年返回，把驻帐之地经营成蒙古佛教的中心和造像、学问之所，并于1686年创制索永布文字。1727年《恰克图条约》之后，北京通往恰克图的商路经过库伦，西伯利亚的毛皮在此换取中国的布匹和茶叶；18世纪初它已称大库伦（伊赫库伦），城东兴起汉人商贾的买卖城。清朝自1758年起向库伦派驻办事大臣；1778年，寺院在博克多汗山下的土拉河畔定居下来，同年清廷认可了每年的祭山大典。甘丹寺建于1809年，到1810年约有一万三千名僧人住在这片帐营之中，此时的大库伦已是外蒙古的宗教与商贸之都。

en:
Zasagt is the dry southern reach of the later Khalkha western wing, where Gobi pastures rise toward the Govi-Altai and the headwaters of the Zag River. In 1444 these grazing lands were inside the Oirat confederation of Esen Taishi: the herdsmen moving between desert-edge winter camps and mountain summer pastures were Khalkha speakers, while rule belonged to the western Mongols. Their Tengri cult and horse herds placed the country on the long frontier between Oirat and Khalkha power, decades before a Zasagt khanate bore this name.

After Esen's death in 1455 Khalkha princes pressed westward. When Gersenji Khongtaiji died in 1549 his descendants built the western Khalkha polity later called Zasagt Khan, and Subadai took the Zasagt Khan title in 1596. The khanate became a Dzungar target after Shar was killed by the Tüsheet Khan Chakhundorj in 1687 and Galdan invaded in 1688. Shar's brother Tsevenjab submitted to the Kangxi Emperor at Dolonnuur in 1691. Qing authorities then organized the pastures into banners, nine by 1692 and nineteen under the Qianlong Emperor, with a triennial assembly at Binderiyaa Nuur near the source of the Zag River.
zh:
札萨克图是后来喀尔喀右翼的南部干草原，戈壁牧场向戈壁阿尔泰山和札克河源抬升。1444年，这些牧场仍在也先太师的瓦剌联盟境内；在荒漠边缘冬营地与山地夏牧场之间转场的是喀尔喀人，统治权则属于西蒙古人。这里信奉腾格里、牧放马群，在此后数十年间一直处在瓦剌与喀尔喀势力消长的前沿，而札萨克图汗部此时尚未得名。

1455年也先死后，喀尔喀贵族向西进逼。1549年格哷森札札赉尔死后，其后裔建立喀尔喀右翼政权，即后来的札萨克图汗部；1596年，素巴第称札萨克图汗。1687年，札萨克图汗沙喇被土谢图汗察珲多尔济攻杀，次年噶尔丹入侵喀尔喀。沙喇之弟策旺扎布投奔清朝，并于1691年在多伦诺尔向康熙帝归附。清朝随后把这片牧场编为盟旗，1692年已有九旗，乾隆年间增至十九旗，并在札克河源的毕都尔诺尔三年会盟一次。

en:
Urzhar is the valley of a 206-kilometre river that rises in the southern Tarbagatai Mountains and ends in the bitter, salt lake Alakol. Rashid al-Din's chronicle already names Urzhar with the Emil country among Mongol camping grounds. In 1444 it lay on the western edge of Esen Taishi's Oirat confederation: mountain streams watered seasonal herds, while Alakol's saline shore made this a useful grazing and salt-producing frontier rather than a town.

After the Kazakh Khanate emerged around 1465, Kazakh authority spread through the steppe and, by the late fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, reached toward the upper Irtysh and the western approaches to the Altai. The Tarbagatai pastures then became a Kazakh-Dzungar frontier. Raiding widened into formal wars from the seventeenth century, and a new Dzungar invasion in 1723 opened the devastating conflict lasting to 1729 or 1730. When Qing armies broke the Dzungar state between 1755 and 1758, Kazakh tribes asked to use the emptied former Dzungar pastures near Tarbagatai; the valley remained a contested livestock borderland through the rest of the eighteenth century.
zh:
乌尔贾尔是一条206公里长河流的河谷，河水发源于塔尔巴哈台山南坡，最终注入苦咸的阿拉科尔湖。拉施德丁的史书中已把乌尔贾尔与额敏一带并列为蒙古营地。1444年，这里位于也先太师的瓦剌联盟西缘：山溪滋养季节性牧群，阿拉科尔湖的咸岸又提供食盐，因此此地是有用的牧地和盐业前沿，而不是城镇。

哈萨克汗国约于1465年兴起后，哈萨克势力在草原上扩展，到15世纪末至16世纪已远达额尔齐斯河上游和阿尔泰山西缘，塔尔巴哈台牧场随之成为哈萨克与准噶尔之间的前沿。17世纪起，袭掠演变为双方之间的长期战争；1723年，准噶尔再度入侵哈萨克草原，开启了持续至1729年或1730年的惨烈战争。1755年至1758年清军击灭准噶尔国家后，哈萨克部落请求进入塔尔巴哈台附近空旷的旧准噶尔牧场放牧；在18世纪余下时间里，这条河谷始终是牲畜往来、势力交错的边境牧地。

en:
Chuguchak, the Chuhuchu of Qing records, lies beneath the Tarbagatai range whose Mongol name means 'the place with marmots'. The hills were Oirat pastureland when Esen Taishi led the confederation in 1444; herders moved between mountain and steppe camps, and marmot colonies, livestock and furs counted for more than any fixed market town.

The pastures later belonged especially to the Torghuts before Dzungar power drew them into the new Oirat order. In 1640 Oirat and Khalkha lords met in the Tarbagatai country and issued the Khalkha-Oirat Legal Code, an attempt to settle Mongol law amid pressure from the Manchus. Qing conquest reached Tarbagatai in 1755. In 1764 the Qing built Zhaofeng City at Yahr and posted a Tarbagatai councillor under the General of Ili; the cold, exposed site did not suit a garrison, so Agui secured a move. In 1766 a new walled town was completed at Chuhuchu and named Suijing by the Qianlong Emperor, becoming the military centre from which the Qing watched the Tarbagatai frontier.
zh:
楚古恰克在清代史料中作楚呼楚，位于塔尔巴哈台山麓；「塔尔巴哈台」的蒙古语意思是「有旱獭的地方」。1444年也先太师统领瓦剌联盟时，这片山地是卫拉特人的牧场，牧民在山地与草原营地间迁徙，旱獭、牲畜和毛皮比任何固定商镇都更重要。

这片牧场后来尤其与土尔扈特部有关，随后又被崛起的准噶尔势力纳入新的卫拉特秩序。1640年，四卫拉特与外喀尔喀蒙古诸部在塔尔巴哈台会盟，颁布《喀尔喀—卫拉特法典》，试图在满洲压力下整束蒙古人的法度。清朝的征服在1755年抵达塔尔巴哈台。1764年，清军在雅尔修筑肇丰城，并设置受伊犁将军节制的塔尔巴哈台参赞大臣；由于雅尔寒冷荒旷、不宜驻军，阿桂奏请移治。1766年，新城在楚呼楚竣工，乾隆帝赐名绥靖城，成为清朝控扼塔尔巴哈台前沿的军事中心。

en:
The Ili River waters broad pastures below the Tianshan, and the Karluk city of Almaliq once stood in the valley. It became a Chagatai capital, and from the 1350s Tughlugh Timur ruled there and made Islam a court religion while Nestorian Christians and Catholic missionaries were still present in the town. Warfare and the nomadic Moghul order gradually emptied Almaliq after the fourteenth century. The Eastern Chagatai Khanate had formed on the Ili in 1347, and after Uwais Khan's time Ming records called the realm Yili-bali. In 1444 the Muslim Chagatayid Esen Buqa held the valley through tribal lords and mounted herdsmen; its strength lay in pasture, cavalry and the road west toward Zhetysu rather than in a restored Almaliq.

Esen Buqa ruled until 1462 and repeatedly raided the Timurids, but after his death Moghul power split and its centre drifted toward Turfan and Yarkand. In the seventeenth century the Dzungars made the Ili valley a capital country again, founding a settled seat near Ghulja with Buddhist monasteries, warehouses and irrigation works; later khans brought farmers from southern Xinjiang to grow wheat, millet, melons and fruit. Qing armies broke Dzungar power in 1755. Ming Rui became the first General of Ili in 1762, and Huiyuan Cheng was built on the river in 1763 as his headquarters. Ningyuan, also founded in 1762 for farmers and merchants from the southern oases, joined the garrison towns known as the Nine Cities of Ili, making the valley a grain-producing military and administrative centre of Qing Xinjiang in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.
zh:
伊犁河滋润着天山北麓的宽阔牧场，葛逻禄人建立的阿力麻里就曾坐落在这片河谷中。它后来成为察合台汗国都城，14世纪中期，秃忽鲁·帖木儿在此统治，把伊斯兰教推向汗廷，而城中仍有景教徒和天主教传教士活动。14世纪以后，战乱和蒙兀儿人的游牧秩序使阿力麻里逐渐荒废。东察合台汗国1347年在伊犁一带形成，歪思汗以后，明代史籍称这支政权为亦力把里。1444年，穆斯林察合台汗也先不花通过部族首领和骑马牧人控制河谷；这里的力量来自牧场、骑兵和通往西方七河地区的道路，而不是一座复兴的阿力麻里。

也先不花统治至1462年，屡次袭扰帖木儿王朝；他死后蒙兀儿势力分裂，政治重心逐渐转向吐鲁番和叶尔羌。17世纪，准噶尔人使伊犁河谷再次成为汗国重心，在固勒札附近营建带有佛寺、仓廪和灌溉设施的定居都城，后来的准噶尔汗又从南疆迁来农户，种植小麦、黍和瓜果。1755年，清军击溃准噶尔政权。1762年，明瑞成为第一任伊犁将军；1763年，惠远城在伊犁河畔建成，作为将军驻地。同样建于1762年的宁远城安置来自南疆绿洲的农户和商人，与各驻防城合称伊犁九城，使伊犁河谷在18世纪后期至19世纪初成为清朝新疆的产粮、军事和行政中心。

en:
Kuqa lies below the Tian Shan on the northern Tarim road, watered by rivers flowing from the mountains into one of the richest oases east of Aksu. It was ancient Kucha, the largest Buddhist oasis kingdom recorded in the Han histories, with markets, music and copper, iron and lead that Chinese pilgrims described in the seventh century. Uyghur settlement and later Islamic Chagatai rule transformed it. In 1444 the Sunni Turki oasis belonged to the Moghul realm of Esen Buqa II, but the Dughlat amirs who had backed his succession held Kuqa and nearby Bai, giving the local lords nearly as much weight as the khan.

Chinese records place Kuqa under the Eastern Chagatai khans in 1468 and then under the Yarkand Khanate in 1533. Its position on the road between Aksu and Turpan made it useful to the Chagatayid princes, Sufi envoys and caravan merchants moving through the northern Tarim, although the old Buddhist kingdom survived chiefly in cave monasteries outside the Muslim town. Galdan's Dzungar campaigns brought Kuqa under Dzungar control with the rest of Altishahr in 1680. Almost eighty years later the Qing destroyed Dzungar power, and in 1759 the court appointed a Kucha affairs commissioner, stationing imperial administration on this stretch of the Tarim road for the remainder of the period.
zh:
库车位于天山南麓、塔里木盆地北道，山间河流在阿克苏以东滋养出一片富庶绿洲。这里是古龟兹，《汉书》所记西域城郭诸国中的大国；7世纪的中国求法僧人曾记述这里的市集、乐舞，以及铜、铁、铅等物产。回鹘迁入和之后察合台系的伊斯兰统治改变了这座古城。1444年，这片逊尼派突厥语绿洲在也先不花二世的蒙兀儿势力范围内，但曾支持其继位的杜格拉特异密占有库车和邻近的拜城，地方领主的权势几乎不亚于汗。

中文史料记库车1468年受东察合台汗国统治，1533年隶属叶尔羌汗国。它处在阿克苏与吐鲁番之间的道路上，对往来塔里木北道的察合台王公、苏菲使者和商队都很重要；古老的佛教世界主要只残存在穆斯林城镇外的石窟寺院中。1680年，噶尔丹的准噶尔军事行动使库车与阿尔蒂沙尔其余诸城一同受准噶尔控制。近八十年后，清朝击灭准噶尔势力，并于1759年设置库车办事大臣，在这一时期余下的时间里把帝国行政机构设在塔里木北道的这处要冲。

en:
Hami, known to its Turkic inhabitants as Kumul, is the last great oasis east of the Tian Shan: the caravan road from the Gobi narrows here before it passes the Jiayu Gate into the Tarim Basin. When Yuan rule collapsed the Chagatayid prince Gunashiri made himself its lord and sent tribute to the Ming from 1380. In 1404 Engke Temür was invested by the Ming as Zhongshun Wang, the Obedient King, and in 1406 a Hami Guard was set up over the kingdom as a loose bridle office. During the 1430s Hami submitted to the Oirats, so in 1444 its Buddhist Chagatayid khan stood between the Ming court and the western Mongols, ruling Uyghur villagers, Muslim merchants and Mongol herdsmen together.

In 1446 disturbances brought a Ming army under Ren Li into Hami, and 1,230 people were carried off beyond the Jiayu Pass. After a pro-Mongol faction overthrew the khan in 1463, the Ming repeatedly restored Gunashiri's house without ever stabilizing the oasis. In 1513 Mansur Khan of Turpan captured Hami and annexed it outright in 1515, imposing Islam; the Ming court gave up the Hami Guard, and Turpan raided through the pass for decades. Hami later passed to the Dzungars, until its chief Ebeydulla submitted to the Qing in 1697 and was made a jasak, his banner enrolled the next year. The Qing raised the old Muslim town in 1717 and a Chinese town in 1727, and after the conquest of Xinjiang the oasis became Hami Subprefecture in 1759, its sweet melons by then famed across the empire as tribute fruit.
zh:
哈密，当地突厥语居民称之为昆莫勒，是天山以东最后一片大绿洲：出戈壁而来的商路在此收窄，过嘉峪关便进入塔里木盆地。元朝崩溃后，察合台后裔兀纳失里割据哈密，1380年起向明朝纳贡。1404年，安克帖木儿被明朝封为忠顺王，1406年明廷又在其地设哈密卫，行羁縻之治。1430年代哈密臣服瓦剌，因此到1444年，这位信奉佛教的察合台系汗王夹在明朝与西蒙古之间，治下兼有畏兀儿农人、回回商人和蒙古牧民。

1446年哈密生乱，明将任礼率军入城，一千二百三十人被迁往嘉峪关内。1463年亲蒙古的一派推翻汗王，明朝此后多次复立兀纳失里的后裔，却始终未能稳定哈密。1513年，吐鲁番的满速儿汗攻占哈密，1515年正式吞并，伊斯兰教随之传入；明廷最终放弃哈密卫，吐鲁番此后数十年不断经嘉峪关内犯。哈密后来转入准噶尔之手，1697年其首领额贝都拉归附清朝，受封札萨克一等达尔罕，次年编设札萨克旗。清朝1717年修筑哈密回城镇远城，1727年又修汉城；1759年平定新疆后哈密设厅，所产甜瓜也早已作为贡品闻名天下。

en:
Qakilik, the Charklik oasis at the foot of the Altyn Tagh, was once the heart of Shanshan. The Han knew the kingdom as Loulan until their envoy assassinated its king in 77 BCE and the court renamed the realm Shanshan, moving its seat of government to Wuni in the Charklik oasis. At Miran, the old Yixun, Han soldiers farmed military colonies guarding the crossroads where the road from Dunhuang split towards Korla to the north and Khotan to the west. As Lop Nur shrank, the kingdom's cities were swallowed by the Lop Desert, and in 644 the pilgrim Xuanzang passed a Charklik he called Nafubo. By 1444 only a small Turki-speaking oasis remained within the Moghul khan Esen Buqa's domains, its traffic reduced to caravans plying between Hami and the Khotan oases.

The eastern Tarim stayed with the Moghul line that ruled from Turpan: in the early sixteenth century Mansur Khan led its ghazis east against Hami and Dunhuang, raiding the Ming frontier. Later in that century the Yarkand Khanate at its height gathered Turpan, Hami and the southern oases into one realm, and Charklik shared the rule of the khojas and the coming of the Dzungars, who turned the last Moghul khans into clients after Galdan's campaign of 1680. When Qing armies crushed the Khoja brothers' rising in 1759, the roads south of the Tian Shan were reopened under Qing control, though Charklik remained no more than a minor caravan halt on the southern route.
zh:
若羌（维吾尔语称卡克里克，即古之Charklik）是阿尔金山脚下的绿洲，曾是鄯善国的腹心。汉朝最初称其为楼兰；前77年，汉使刺杀楼兰王，朝廷改国名为鄯善，王都南迁到卡克里克绿洲上的扜泥城。在米兰——即汉代的伊循城——汉军屯田戍守，看护这里的岔路口：从敦煌而来的道路在此分岔，北向库尔勒，西向和阗。后来罗布泊退缩，鄯善诸城渐次没入荒漠，644年玄奘经过时，把卡克里克一带称作纳缚波。到1444年，这里只剩一个说突厥语的小绿洲，在蒙兀儿汗也先不花二世的疆域内，商旅只在哈密与和阗诸绿洲之间往返。

东塔里木此后归属以吐鲁番为都的蒙兀儿一支：16世纪初，速檀满速儿率部向东对哈密和敦煌发动圣战，屡犯明朝边塞。该世纪后期，叶尔羌汗国鼎盛，把吐鲁番、哈密与南路诸绿洲都纳入版图，卡克里克也随之经历了和卓的统治和准噶尔人的到来——1680年噶尔丹远征之后，末代蒙兀儿诸汗沦为附庸。1759年清军平定大小和卓之乱，天山南路的商道重新畅通，只是卡克里克始终不过是南道上一处不起眼的商旅歇脚地。

en:
Yarkand is the fertile oasis watered by the Yarkand River south of the Taklamakan, on the Silk Road branch leading toward the Pamirs and Ladakh. Chinese records knew it as Suoju, but for long periods it was less prominent than neighbouring oasis towns. After the Mongol conquests most of Kashgaria became a Chagatai appanage, and Dughlat emirs came to control its cities. Marco Polo, visiting about 1273, found Muslims and some Nestorian Christians in a province rich in provisions, especially cotton. In 1444 Yarkand was a Turki Muslim oasis under Dughlat lordship, with cotton and caravan supplies moving along the southern Tarim roads.

In 1509 the Dughlats broke from Moghulistan, and in 1514 Sultan Said Khan conquered them and founded the Yarkent khanate, initially ruling from Kashgar before moving his capital to Yarkand. The city became the chief mart of the Tarim Basin. When the Jesuit Benedict Goez reached it with a Kabul caravan late in 1603, he waited about a year for a new caravan to Cathay; merchants bought the king's safe-conduct for the road, and Yarkand jade was valued above other trade goods. Rivalry between the White Mountain and Black Mountain khojas weakened the khanate. Galdan's Dzungars took Yarkand in 1680 and set up a puppet khan, and around 1700 Tsewang Rabtan ended the dynasty and imposed direct Dzungar rule. Qing armies secured the city in 1759 while suppressing the revolt of Burhan-ud-din and Khoja Jahan, and through 1821 it remained part of the Qing frontier garrison system.
zh:
叶尔羌是塔克拉玛干沙漠南缘由叶尔羌河滋养的肥沃绿洲，处在通往帕米尔和拉达克的丝路支线上。汉文古籍称这里为莎车，但在很长时期里，它的声名还不及邻近几座绿洲城。蒙古征服之后，喀什噶尔大部成为察合台系封地，杜格拉特埃米尔逐渐控制各城；马可·波罗约在1273年经过时，看到这里的居民多为穆斯林，也有一些景教徒，物产充足，尤其盛产棉花。1444年的叶尔羌是杜格拉特贵族治下的突厥语穆斯林绿洲，棉花与商队补给沿塔里木南道流通。

1509年，杜格拉特人脱离蒙兀儿斯坦；1514年，萨亦德汗征服杜格拉特，建立叶尔羌汗国，最初以喀什噶尔为都，后来把都城迁到叶尔羌。这里由此成为塔里木盆地最重要的商市。1603年底，耶稣会士鄂本笃随喀布尔商队抵达，等待约一年才重新组成前往契丹的商队；商人要向汗购买沿途通行的授权，而叶尔羌玉石被视为最值得贩运的货物。白山派与黑山派和卓的争斗削弱了汗国。1680年，噶尔丹率领准噶尔军攻占叶尔羌，另立傀儡汗；约1700年，策妄阿拉布坦不再立汗，改为准噶尔直接统治。1759年，清军平定大小和卓之乱，控制叶尔羌；到1821年，该城都在清朝边疆驻防体系之中。

en:
The Kochkor valley lies high in the inner Tian Shan, a grassy basin 1,800 to 2,500 metres up enclosed by the Kyrgyz Ala-Too, Kyzart and Jumgal ranges, its road running north to the Chu and south over the Torugart pass towards Kashgar. Saka and Wusun remains show it was grazed from antiquity; it took Islam under the Karakhanids, and the Mongol conquest of the thirteenth century folded it into the Chagatai ulus and later Moghulistan. Tughluq Timur had made Islam the Moghul khans' religion, yet the highland clans kept most of their old beliefs. In 1444 Kochkor was summer pasture of Kyrgyz tribes on Moghulistan's remote Tian Shan frontier, valued for horses, sheep and wool rather than for towns.

As Moghulistan dissolved, the Kyrgyz dealt with its heirs as free allies: in 1514 their chief Muhammad Kyrgyz helped Sultan Said seize Kashgar, but after he raided Turkestan alongside the Kazakhs he was captured at Barskoon in 1517. Through the sixteenth century Kyrgyz clans marched with the Kazakh khans against Yarkand and the Uzbeks. In 1643 a 50,000-strong Dzungar army under Batur drove them from eastern Zhetysu, and the blow was repeated in 1652; the great invasion of the 1720s scattered the highlanders into Fergana, leaving only those who submitted by Lake Issyk-Kul. After Qing armies broke the Dzungars in 1755–57 the Kyrgyz climbed back to their old jailoos, fought Abylai Khan's Kazakhs over the recovered pastures, and made peace in 1780. Early in the nineteenth century the expanding Khanate of Kokand began demanding tribute from the northern Kyrgyz tribes.
zh:
科奇科尔谷地深藏天山腹地，是海拔1800至2500米的草原盆地，为吉尔吉斯阿拉套、克扎尔特与朱姆加尔山脉所环抱，谷中道路北通楚河，南越图噜噶特山口通往喀什。萨卡人与乌孙人的遗迹表明这里自古便是牧场；喀喇汗时期传入伊斯兰教，13世纪蒙古征服后，先后归入察合台汗国与东察合台。秃黑鲁·帖木儿虽将伊斯兰教立为蒙兀儿汗的宗教，高山中的部落却大多保留旧有信仰。1444年的科奇科尔是吉尔吉斯部落在东察合台遥远天山边境上的夏牧场，所重的是马匹、绵羊和羊毛，而非城镇。

东察合台瓦解之际，吉尔吉斯人以自由盟友的身份周旋于其继承者之间：1514年，首领穆罕默德·吉尔吉斯助速檀·赛义德夺取喀什，但在随哈萨克人劫掠突厥斯坦后，于1517年在巴尔斯孔被俘。整个16世纪，吉尔吉斯诸部与哈萨克诸汗联兵，同叶尔羌和乌兹别克作战。1643年，巴图尔珲台吉率五万准噶尔大军将他们赶出七河东部，1652年战火重燃；1720年代的大入侵又把高地人驱散到费尔干纳，只有臣服者留在伊塞克湖畔。1755至1757年清军击灭准噶尔后，吉尔吉斯人重返旧日的夏牧场，又为收复的牧场同阿卜赉汗的哈萨克人交战，至1780年议和。19世纪初，扩张中的浩罕汗国开始向北方吉尔吉斯诸部索要贡赋。

en:
The valley of the Chu, where the river runs between the Kyrgyz Ala-Too and the steppe on its way to the Muyunkum, was one of the cradles of Silk Road urban life. Suyab, whose ruins lie west of Tokmok, began as a Sogdian merchant town and became the chief capital of the Western Turkic khagan; Tang China built a fortress there in 679 and long held it among the Four Garrisons of the Anxi protectorate. Suyab was overtaken by Balasagun, capital of the Muslim Karakhanids, where the poet Yusuf, author of the Kutadgu Bilig, was born and beside which stands the eleventh-century Burana minaret. The Kara-Khitai took the city in 1134 and the Mongols in 1218; in 1253 William of Rubruck found only ruins along the Chu, and by the fourteenth century Balasagun was a village beside abandoned walls. In 1444 the valley belonged to Moghulistan, its pastures roamed by Kyrgyz and Moghol nomads.

This was the birthplace of the Kazakh Khanate: the Moghul khan Esen Buqa had granted the Chu valley to the sultans Kerei and Janybek, who proclaimed their khanate there around 1465. Through the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries Kyrgyz and Kazakh clans campaigned together against Yarkand and the Oirats, until the Dzungars broke into Zhetysu in 1643 and again in the 1720s, when the valley was largely abandoned. Kyrgyz and Kazakh herdsmen flooded back after the Qing crushed the Dzungars in 1755–57, then fought each other over the empty grasslands until a truce in 1780. By the early nineteenth century the expanding Khanate of Kokand was pushing north towards the Chu and making the northern Kyrgyz tribes its tributaries.
zh:
楚河在吉尔吉斯阿拉套山与草原之间流向穆云库姆沙漠，其河谷是丝绸之路城市文明的摇篮之一。托克马克以西的碎叶本是粟特商镇，后来成为西突厥可汗的首要都城；唐朝于679年在此筑城，曾长期将其列为安西四镇之一。后来碎叶让位于穆斯林喀喇汗王朝的都城八剌沙衮——《福乐智慧》的作者诗人优素福便出生于此，城旁还立着11世纪所建的布拉纳塔。喀喇契丹1134年攻取该城，蒙古人1218年再度占据；1253年鲁布鲁克沿楚河所见已是一片废墟，到14世纪八剌沙衮更沦为废墙旁的村落。1444年的楚河谷地属东察合台，吉尔吉斯与蒙兀儿游牧人在草场上往来迁徙。

这里是哈萨克汗国的诞生地：东察合台汗也先不花将楚河谷地封给克烈与贾尼别克两位苏丹，二人于1465年前后在此称汗建国。16至17世纪，吉尔吉斯与哈萨克诸部联兵对抗叶尔羌与卫拉特，直到准噶尔人1643年攻入七河，又在1720年代大举来犯，河谷大半荒废。1755至1757年清朝击灭准噶尔后，吉尔吉斯与哈萨克牧民蜂拥而回，旋即为空旷的草原互相攻伐，至1780年议和。19世纪初，扩张中的浩罕汗国向楚河方向北进，将北方吉尔吉斯诸部逐步变为自己的藩属。

en:
Yashilkul is a freshwater lake lying 3,734 metres high in the Alichur Pamir, ringed by the wide grassy uplands that give the Roof of the World its name; the Alichur River flows in and the Gunt flows out toward the Panj. Kyrgyz herders drive their sheep and yaks up to these summer pastures from the lower valleys, and the Ming envoy Chen Cheng, crossing to the Timurid court in the Yongle era, may already have recorded the lake as Yixi-ke'er. In 1444 the high country formed the remote fringe of the eastern Chagatai Moghul khans; their descendants founded the Yarkand khanate in 1514, until the Dzungars overran Altishahr between 1678 and 1705.

In the summer of 1759, as Qing armies crushed the revolt of the khoja brothers, the general Fude pursued Burhan al-Din and Khwaja Jahan through the Alichur valley and routed their last stand on the ridges above the lake. The brothers fled into Badakhshan with only some three hundred followers, where Sultan Shah seized them, and the Qianlong emperor had a victory stele in Manchu, Chinese and Turki raised east of the lake, with a Qing garrison maintained at nearby Suman.
zh:
叶什勒池清代称伊西洱库尔淖尔，是阿尔楚尔帕米尔的一座高原淡水湖，湖面海拔3734米；阿尔楚尔河自东注入，湖水西流为贡特河，奔往喷赤河。湖周是被称作「帕米尔」的宽阔夏牧场，柯尔克孜牧人赶着羊群和牦牛从低地山谷来此度夏。明代永乐年间，出使帖木儿朝的陈诚在《竹山集》中留下「亦息渴儿」一名，可能就是此湖最早的汉文对音。1444年，这片高寒之地处在察合台系蒙兀儿汗廷遥远的边缘；其后人于1514年建立叶尔羌汗国，而1678至1705年间，准噶尔人征服了天山南路。

1759年夏，清军平定大小和卓之乱，富德一路追击波罗尼都、霍集占，在阿尔楚尔之战后又于湖畔山岭击溃和卓军最后的抵抗。大小和卓只带三百余众逃入巴达克山，被巴达克山首领素勒坦沙擒获；乾隆皇帝下令在湖东立满、汉、维三种文字的御制纪功碑，并在附近的苏满驻兵戍守。

en:
Tsaparang was the citadel-capital of Guge, the kingdom that rose in the Sutlej valley of western Tibet after the old Tibetan empire collapsed. When King Langdarma's persecutions ended the monarchy, his great-grandson Kyide Nyimagon fled to Ngari around 910, and one branch of his grandsons' inheritance became Guge, ruled by exiled Tibetan royalty. King Yeshe-Ö founded Tholing in 997, sent the translator Rinchen Zangpo to study in India, and welcomed the Indian master Atiśa in 1042, making these valleys the cradle of Buddhism's 'upper revival'; its monasteries grew rich on the ancient India–Tibet trade route and the gold of Ngari. The kings built their capital into a pyramid of rock above the river, caves and tunnels climbing past the White and Red chapels to the summer palace on the summit. Guge absorbed Purang in 1378 and for a time ruled Ladakh, and in 1444 it was again a confident Buddhist power under its ancient dynasty.

From 1499, however, Guge's kings had to acknowledge the Rinpungpa rulers of Tsang. In 1626 the Portuguese Jesuit António de Andrade reached Tsaparang, the first known European to cross the Himalayas, and the last king, Tashi Drakpa, let him build churches below the citadel and at Rudok, leaning on the missionaries against his brother, the chief lama. In 1633 the monks rose in revolt, and in 1635 a Ladakhi army called in by the rebels starved the rock-fortress into surrender; the king and his royal kin were put to death, and Ladakh held Guge for nearly half a century. In 1679–80 the 5th Dalai Lama's general Galdan Chhewang drove out the Ladakhis with a Mongol-Tibetan army and annexed Guge to Lhasa. Tsaparang never recovered: its dynasty gone, the citadel emptied into sand and ruins.
zh:
札布让是古格王国的堡寨都城，古格兴起于吐蕃崩溃后西藏西部的象泉河谷。朗达玛灭法、旧制瓦解之后，他的曾孙吉德尼玛衮约在910年西逃阿里，其孙辈分封所得的一支便是古格，由吐蕃王室后裔世袭。益西沃于997年兴建托林寺，派遣大译师仁钦桑布赴印度求法，又于1042年迎请印度高僧阿底峡入藏，使这些河谷成为藏传佛教「上路弘法」的摇篮；寺院与王宫依托古老的印藏商路和阿里的黄金富庶一时。历代国王把都城修成河畔一座高耸的土山金字塔，洞窟暗道自山脚层层而上，经白殿、红殿直达山顶的夏宫。古格1378年吞并普兰，还曾一度统治拉达克；1444年的古格在古老王朝治下，仍是一个底气十足的佛教政权。

然而从1499年起，古格王不得不承认藏地仁蚌巴政权的宗主权。1626年，葡萄牙耶稣会士安东尼奥·德尔·安德拉德抵达札布让，成为有记载最早翻越喜马拉雅山的欧洲人；末代国王赤扎西扎巴德放任他在宗堡脚下和日土各建一座教堂，想借传教士制衡出家为僧、身为宗教领袖的王弟。1633年僧侣发动叛乱，1635年，应叛党之请而来的拉达克军队围困数月，逼降这座石山要塞，国王与王室成员被杀，拉达克统治古格近半个世纪。1679至1680年，五世达赖麾下的将领噶丹泽旺率蒙藏联军赶走拉达克人，把古格并入拉萨治下。札布让再未复兴：王统既绝，堡城渐渐倾颓，没入黄沙。

en:
The forested valleys around Nyingchi form the western heart of Kongpo, where the Nyang River leaves the eastern Himalayan gorges and meets the Yarlung Tsangpo. Its river flats grow grain above steep pasture and timberland. Kongpo kept its own local kings, while Buchu Monastery, founded under Songtsen Gampo in the seventh century, was the oldest Buddhist sanctuary in the region. During the Sakya and Phagmodrupa periods the Nyingchi valleys came into the Karma Kagyu sphere. In 1444 they were still part of the Phagmodrupa realm under Drakpa Jungne, but the 1434 succession strife, only healed in 1443, had left local lords and monasteries with much of the real power.

The rivalries of the Rinpungpa and Tsangpa with the Phagmodrupa drew Kongpo into Tibet's Kagyu-Gelug struggles. After Güshi Khan's victory in 1642, the Ganden Phodrang government assigned the Nyingchi lands to noble houses including the Ngapoi, Jiangzhong and Jiala, and they were later organized into the Zela, Qomo, Xoka and Gyamda dzongs. Gelugpa monks were already established at Buchu by the seventeenth century, though its older Nyingma traditions were not formally displaced until much later. The dzong administration in Kongpo was restored during the Jiaqing reign between 1796 and 1820.
zh:
林芝周围森林密布的河谷是工布西部的核心地带，尼洋河从喜马拉雅东段峡谷流出，在此汇入雅鲁藏布江；河边阶地种植谷物，上方是陡峭牧场与林地。工布长期有本地土王，7世纪松赞干布时期创建的布久拉康则是这一带最古老的佛教道场。萨迦与帕木竹巴时期，林芝诸谷成为噶玛噶举派的势力范围。1444年，这里仍在帕木竹巴第悉札巴迥乃的政权范围内，但1434年的继承纷争到1443年才和解，地方首领和寺院掌握着许多实际权力。

仁蚌巴、藏巴汗与帕木竹巴之间的角力，把工布卷入西藏噶玛噶举派与格鲁派的竞争。1642年固始汗取胜后，甘丹颇章政权把林芝一带封给阿沛、江中、甲拉等贵族家族，随后又分设则拉、觉木、雪卡、江达等宗。17世纪时，格鲁派僧人已进入布久拉康，但寺院旧有的宁玛派传统直到很久以后才被正式取代。清朝嘉庆年间（1796—1820年），工布恢复宗制。

en:
Qamdo—Chab-mdo, the meeting of the waters—grew where the Dza and Ngom rivers join to form the Mekong, the gateway through which the caravan roads from Sichuan and Yunnan entered central Tibet. Tea, salt and wool changed hands below its cliffs, and the town guarded the eastern road to Lhasa. In 1373 the sixteen-year-old Tsongkhapa, travelling from Amdo, spent a night at the river junction and foretold a great monastery on the spot. His disciple Sherab Sangpo, born in 1395, duly founded Jampaling in 1437 (1444 by another tradition), the first Gelugpa monastery in Kham, opening the Yellow Church's spread across the eastern highlands. In 1444 the young house dominated a town still shared, like all Kham, between local chiefs and lamas, subject to no distant king.

The Pakpalha incarnation line rose within its walls: the second Pakpalha was invited to teach by the Mu chiefs of Lijiang, and in 1594 the third Pakpalha became the monastery's fourteenth abbot, after which the incarnations ruled the house. When Güshi Khan's Khoshut Mongols destroyed the Bon king of Beri in 1639–1640, the fourth Pakpalha received a patent ordering all central Kham to obey him. The fifth Pakpalha founded the monastic labrang in 1676, confirming Jampaling's theocratic rule over the district. As Qing armies entered Tibet against the Dzungars, the sixth Pakpalha aided the Kangxi Emperor's surveyors bound for the Kailash range and in 1719 received the first Qing title together with a copper seal, after which the lineage was registered among the great reincarnating hierarchies of the frontier. In 1791 the seventh Pakpalha raised a hall for the Qianlong Emperor's eightieth birthday, and the emperor's plaque named it the Zhuxi Temple. Through every change of masters the caravans kept passing, leaving the monks of Jampaling lords of Tibet's eastern gateway.
zh:
昌都，藏语意为「两江汇合处」，兴起于扎曲与昂曲汇成澜沧江之地，是四川、云南商道进入卫藏的门户。茶、盐、羊毛在崖下集市易手，城镇扼守通往拉萨的东路。1373年，十六岁的宗喀巴从安多赴拉萨学经，途经两河交汇处夜宿一晚，预言此地日后当建大寺。其弟子、生于1395年的西绕松布后来于1437年（另说1444年）创建强巴林寺，这是康区第一座格鲁派寺院，拉开了黄教在东部高原传播的序幕。1444年的昌都由这座年轻的寺院与当地头人、喇嘛分治，与整个康区一样，并不听命于远方的君王。

帕巴拉活佛世系在寺中兴起：第二世帕巴拉曾应云南丽江木氏土司之请前往讲经；1594年，第三世帕巴拉出任强巴林寺第十四任法台，此后历世帕巴拉成为寺院之主。固始汗率领的和硕特蒙古于1639至1640年攻灭崇奉苯教的白利土司后，第四世帕巴拉获得颁照，写明中部康区各地均听其号令。第五世帕巴拉于1676年设立拉让，最终确立起强巴林寺对昌都地方的政教合一统治。清军入藏进击准噶尔期间，第六世帕巴拉因配合康熙派往冈底斯山勘界的人员，于1719年受封「阐讲黄法额尔德尼那门汗」并获赐铜印，帕巴拉系统自此成为清朝在册的边疆大活佛。1791年，第七世帕巴拉为庆贺乾隆帝八旬万寿在寺内建殿，乾隆帝亲题「祝釐寺」匾额。主人几经更迭，商队往来不绝，强巴林寺的僧众由此成为藏东门户的主人。

en:
Markam—Smra-khams, the goodly land—is a country of high pastures cut by the upper Mekong, facing the Bathang country across the Jinsha River to the east and Yunnan to the south. Later Chinese gazetteers noted that its people lived entirely by their herds and tilled no fields. In the southern river gorges the salt pits of Tsakalo, the 'salt wells' of Yanjing, had been worked since the age of the Tibetan Empire: brine drawn from the wells was evaporated on terraced pools and carried through Kham by yak caravan. Backed by mountains and fronting the river, Markam was the midway point of the Sichuan–Tibet road, where the Yunnan caravan route joined it. Under the early Ming the local chiefs held tusi titles, and in 1444 Markam, like the rest of Kham, obeyed no single ruler.

In the late Ming the Naxi chiefs of Lijiang pushed up the Jinsha and held the Bathang country, the salt wells included, for some seventy years. Their hold ended with the Khoshut: after Güshi Khan's campaign of 1639–1640 broke the king of Beri, Mongol sde-pa officials were posted to Bathang and Lithang to collect taxes. In 1719 the Qing general Yue Zhongqi led two thousand men on Bathang, its sde-pa surrendered, and the frontier settlement of 1726, which delimited the Sichuan, Yunnan and Tibetan borders, fixed the Sichuan–Tibet line at the Ningjing hills east of Markam; the herders and salt-boilers west of the line remained on the Tibetan side. Markam stayed a stage on the great road between Sichuan and Lhasa, its caravans and flocks undisturbed by the drawing of boundaries.
zh:
芒康，藏语意为「善妙之地」，是澜沧江上游群山间的一片高原牧区，东隔金沙江与巴塘相望，南接云南。后来的汉文方志记载，当地居民多以牧畜为生，不事农业。南部河谷中的察卡洛盐井（汉语称盐井）自吐蕃时期便已开采：卤水自井中取出，引上层层梯田式盐池晒制，再由牦牛商队贩运康区各地。芒康负山临河，正处川藏大路中途适中之所，云南来的商道也在此交汇。明初当地首领受封土司，1444年的芒康与整个康区一样，没有一个统辖全境的君王。

明朝后期，丽江木氏土司势力越过金沙江北上，统治巴塘地方达七十一年，盐井也在其辖境之内。和硕特时代到来后，固始汗于1639至1640年攻灭白利土司，随即派第巴分驻巴塘、里塘征税。1719年，清将岳钟琪率兵两千进逼巴塘，巴塘第巴归降；1726年清廷勘定川、滇、藏边界，川藏界线定在芒康以东的宁静山，线西的牧民与盐民仍属西藏一侧。此后芒康始终是四川通往拉萨大路上的台站，界线虽划，商队和畜群依旧往来如昔。

en:
Dege is a country of steep gorges and high pastures in northern Kham, where the upper Yangtze cuts between the grasslands and the peaks. Its lords were the Gar clan, who claimed descent from Gar Tongtsen, minister of the seventh-century king Songtsen Gampo, and had held an estate here since the thirteenth century; their renown was in metalwork as well as prayer. In 1444 they ruled a small Vajrayana Buddhist kingdom of barley farmers and yak-herding nomads, answerable to no outside power. Four years later, in 1448, the lord Bota Tashi Sengge moved his seat to Gengqing and, with the wandering siddha Thang Tong Gyalpo, founded the Tanggya chapel there; Gengqing would remain the Derge capital.

In 1639 the Qoshot Mongol Güshi Khan marched into Kham against the Bon king of Beri, and with the Derge lord's help destroyed him in a year; Derge itself grew great on the victory and its rulers took the title of Dharma King around 1640. The Sakya Gongchen monastery rose as their family temple, and through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the kingdom expanded until it numbered twelve to fifteen thousand households. In 1728 the Derge king accepted a tusi title from the Qing, and in 1729 King Tenpa Tsering founded the great printing house beside the monastery, carving blocks for the Kangyur and Tengyur and the collected tantras; later rulers completed it, and by the end of the century it held more than two hundred thousand blocks. Two women wore the crown, the last of them Queen Tsewang Lhamo, who died in 1812 after printing the Nyingma tantras. In 1821 Dege was still one of the cultural capitals of Tibet, its presses famous from Lhasa to Beijing.
zh:
德格是康北一片峡谷与高山牧场交织的地方，金沙江上游在草场与雪峰之间穿行。统治此地的噶尔家族自称是7世纪松赞干布的大臣噶尔·东赞的后裔，自13世纪起便领有这片庄园；他们既以佛法闻名，也以金属工艺见长。1444年，他们统治着一个由种青稞的农民和放牧牦牛的牧民组成的金刚乘佛教小王国，不臣服于任何外力。四年后的1448年，首领博塔·扎西森根把治所迁到更庆，与云游的大成就者汤东杰布共同修建了汤甲经堂，更庆从此成为德格的都城。

1639年，和硕特蒙古的固始汗进军康区，讨伐信奉苯教的白利土司，在德格土司相助下一年将其攻灭；德格借此战崛起，约1640年起其首领自称法王。萨迦派的贡钦寺成为王家寺院，经过17、18世纪的扩张，王国鼎盛时有一万二千至一万五千户人众。1728年，德格王接受清朝的土司封号；1729年，却吉·登巴泽仁土司在寺院旁创建宏大的印经院，为《甘珠尔》《丹珠尔》和各部密续雕版，后继者续建完成，到18世纪末存版已逾二十万块。还有两位女性登上王位，最后一位是女王策旺拉姆，她主持刊印宁玛派密续，1812年去世。1821年的德格仍是藏地的文化中心之一，印经院的声名从拉萨传到北京。

en:
Rebgong, the 'golden valley' in Tibetan, is the valley of the Rongwo River in Amdo, where Tibetan tribes herd sheep, yaks and horses over the high pastures above the Yellow River. In 1301 the Sakyapa order founded a small monastery, the Zhikha Lhakhang, on the ground where Rongwo Monastery now stands; under the Yuan the valley was part of the Brikhu myriarchy, and the early Ming enrolled it loosely as the Brikhu guard. From the thirteenth century painters in the farming hamlets laid bright mineral colours on thangkas for the monasteries, a craft drawn from Tibetan painting that grew into the Regong style. In 1444 the twelve tribes of Rebgong still lived under their own chiefs and lamas, tied to the Ming by titles rather than by officials.

In 1462 Samten Rinchen rebuilt Rongwo Monastery, and his brother Lodrö Sengge, succeeding him as abbot, was invested by the Ming court with the title 'National Preceptor of Profound Cultivation and Marvellous Awakening'; its lamas henceforth ruled the valley as both prelates and lords. The monastery turned to the Gelug order in 1605 and was enlarged, and in 1622 the Tianqi emperor bestowed the plaque 'Holy Land of the Western Regions'. In 1630 Kaldan Gyatso, recognised as the reincarnation of Samten Rinchen and the first Shartsang Khutuktu, founded the dialectical college and, under the title Erdeni Nangso, governed the twelve tribes of the Rongwo valley and the Zekog pastures. The painters of Wutun and the neighbouring villages carried thangkas and appliqué hangings to monasteries across Amdo, and under the Qianlong emperor the Shartsang incarnations inherited the old preceptors' theocratic rule.
zh:
热贡，藏语意为「金色的谷地」，是安多隆务河流域的河谷，藏族部落在黄河上游的高山牧场放牧绵羊、牦牛和马。1301年，萨迦派在今隆务寺所在建起一座小寺智卡贡康；元代这一带属必里万户府，明初松散地改设为必里卫。13世纪起，农耕村落里的画师便用鲜亮的矿物颜料为寺院绘制唐卡，这门源自西藏绘画的手艺逐渐发展为热贡艺术。1444年，热贡十二部族仍由本族头人和喇嘛治理，与明朝之间只有封号相系，不派流官。

1462年，三木旦仁钦重建隆务寺，其弟罗哲森格继任法台，被明廷封为「弘修妙悟国师」，寺僧自此以教领政，统治这片河谷。1605年隆务寺改宗格鲁派并大加扩建，1622年天启帝赐「西域胜境」匾额。1630年，被认定为三木旦仁钦转世的一世夏日仓呼图克图蔼丹嘉措建立显宗学院，并以「额尔德尼昂锁」的身份统辖隆务河谷与泽库草原上的十二部族。五屯及邻近村落的画师把唐卡和堆绣送往安多各处寺院；乾隆年间，夏日仓活佛系统承袭了旧日国师的政教合一统治。

en:
Garzê (dkar mdzes) sits in the barley valleys of the upper Yalong River, in the northern Kham country called Hor. Its ruling houses traced their line to Hor Namgyal, son born to a Mongol prince of Kublai Khan's generation and a woman of the land, whose descendants had brought the neighbouring tribes under their sway. In 1444 the clans of Trehor and Dzakhok pastured their herds and raised highland barley along the upper Yalong, their castles guarding the northern caravan road, while the ancient Achak Dru clan that had long ruled the country was nearing the end of its male line.

Soon afterwards that line failed, and the Hor lord Namkha Gyaltsen married his son to the Achak Dru heiress and joined their lands from Dzakhok to Draggo and Dawu; the kingdom was then divided among six sons, giving birth to the Five Hor States—Mazur, Khangsar, Trehor, Draggo and Beri—whose castles stood above the growing town. Fiercest was Bon Beri: under Dönyö Dorjé its raiders reached Chamdo, Riwoche and Markam and menaced the Gelug monasteries, until at the call of the Fifth Dalai Lama and the Panchen Lama, Güshi Khan of the Khoshut invaded Kham in 1639 and, aided by Derge, destroyed Beri within a year and put its king to death. About 1642 the Mongols founded Kandze Monastery on the hill above the Mazur and Khangsar castles; it grew to hold fifteen hundred monks, ranking with Chamdo's Jampaling as the greatest monastery in Kham, one of the earliest Gelug houses planted across the Hor country. In 1728 Beri and the other Hor chiefs submitted to the Qing and were enrolled as tusi, and the barley valley of Garzê remained a caravan stage on the northern road into Tibet.
zh:
甘孜（藏语 dkar mdzes）位于雅砻江上游的青稞谷地，属康北称「霍尔」的地区。据藏文史籍《汉藏史集》记载，当地诸部首领的世系可追溯到霍尔南嘉——忽必烈时代一位蒙古王子与当地女子所生之子，他的后裔逐步臣服了周边各部落。1444年，朱倭、扎科的氏族在雅砻江上游放牧、种植青稞，寨堡扼守北路商道，而久主其地的古老氏族男嗣已近断绝。

此后不久旧氏绝嗣，霍尔首领南喀坚赞之子娶其独女为妻，将从扎科到炉霍、道孚的土地合为一国，随后由六子分家，形成麻书、孔撒、朱倭、章谷、白利五大霍尔土司，寨堡雄踞在日渐兴盛的甘孜镇北山之上。五部中最强悍的是信奉苯教的白利：土司顿月多吉四出攻伐，兵锋远达昌都、类乌齐、芒康，威胁格鲁派寺院。应五世达赖喇嘛和四世班禅之请，和硕特部固始汗于1639年进军康区，在德格土司相助下一年内攻灭白利，擒杀顿月多吉。约1642年，和硕特蒙古在麻书、孔撒两寨堡上方的山头兴建甘孜寺，最盛时僧众达一千五百人，与昌都强巴林寺并称康区最大的寺院，也是黄教在霍尔地区最早的大寺之一。1728年，白利与其他霍尔各部首领归附清朝，受封长官司等土司世职，青稞丰饶的甘孜谷地由此成为川藏北路上的商队要站。

en:
Xuanhua lies in the basin of the Yang River between the Inner and Outer Great Wall, the last strong place on the road from the steppe to the Juyong Pass and Beijing. Its walls began in the Tianbao reign as the Xiongwu fortress An Lushan raised in the eighth century; under the Liao it was the seat of Guihua Prefecture, and under the Jin and Yuan a garrison on the same small earthen rampart. The Ming made it a city of soldiers. In 1394 Zhu Hui, Prince of Gu, enlarged the town to a walled circuit of more than twenty-four li with seven gates; in 1422 the general Tan Guang added gate towers, corner towers and over a hundred and seventy watch-rooms, and from 1441 the censor Luo Hongxin faced the crumbling rammed-earth wall with grey brick and gave it barbicans, enceintes and a moat. In 1444 Xuanhua was the headquarters of the Xuanfu Garrison, one of the Nine Border Garrisons and a key seat of the high command that coordinated Xuanfu, Datong and Shanxi—a crowded town of troops, military households and camp traders living off the garrison and the basin's grain fields.

Five years later the garrison's hour came. In 1449 Esen's Oirats destroyed the imperial army at Tumu Post, in the Xuanfu sector, and led the Zhengtong Emperor away captive; through the panic the walled towns of the command held, and the dynasty weathered the crisis under Yu Qian's defense of Beijing. For the rest of the Ming, Xuanfu kept its martial character, its Zhenshuo and Qingyuan towers rising over the central avenue. Under the Qing the wall ceased to be a frontier: in 1693 the Kangxi Emperor converted the old garrison into a civilian prefecture, Xuanhua Fu, 'proclaiming civilization', famed as the first prefectural city west of the capital. In 1757 nearly a hundred and twenty thousand taels were spent renewing its crenellations and gun platforms, while the Ming stronghold mellowed into a quiet prefectural town looking east toward Beijing.
zh:
宣化地处洋河河谷盆地，夹在内、外两道长城之间，是草原通往居庸关与北京的大路上最后一处可守的重镇。其城始于唐天宝年间安禄山在飞狐塞修筑的雄武城，辽代为归化州治所，金、元两代继续在此屯驻，城垣却始终只是座不大的土城。明代把它变成了一座兵城：1394年，就藩于此的谷王朱橞嫌旧城狭隘、不足以屯兵，展扩城池，城墙周长超过二十四里，开有七门；1422年永宁伯谭广大饬边防，添建城楼、角楼和一百七十余间铺房；1441年起，都御史罗亨信又给容易倾颓的夯土城墙外包灰砖，并增筑瓮城、月城与城壕。1444年的宣化是九边重镇之一宣府镇的驻地，也是节制宣府、大同、山西三镇的宣大军门重地，城中挤满驻军、军户和随军商贩，靠着军镇与盆地里的粮田为生。

五年之后，这座兵城迎来生死之秋。1449年，瓦剌也先在宣府镇地界的土木堡击溃御驾亲征的明军，俘走明英宗；惊魂之秋，防区内的城寨守住了，明廷也靠于谦主持北京守备度过危局。此后有明一代，宣府始终不改尚武本色，镇朔楼、清远楼等城楼矗立在城中干道上。入清以后，长城不再是边防前线，1693年（康熙三十二年），朝廷改宣府镇为宣化府，取「宣扬教化」之意，号称「京西第一府」，军镇让位于府县；1757年又耗白银近十二万两，新修垛口、海墁与炮台。明代的九边雄镇，就这样渐渐变成一座安安静静、东望京城的府城。

en:
Daming stands on the grain-rich plain where southern Hebei meets Henan and Shandong, crossed by the Wei River course of the old Yongji Canal. Under the Tang it was Weizhou, the headquarters of the Wei-Bo military governors after the An Lushan rebellion, and the Later Han renamed its Xingtang Prefecture as Daming Prefecture. The Northern Song made the city its northern capital, Beijing, a bastion against the Liao and the greatest city in Hebei, called the lock and key of the northern frontier. The Jin kept it as a prefectural centre and the Yuan as Daming Route. In 1401 floods on the Zhang and Wei rivers buried the old Song city in silt, so the military commissioner Wu Mi built a new seat north of Aijiaokou. In 1444, therefore, Ming Daming was still a relatively new walled prefectural city in the Northern Metropolitan Region, with Yuancheng County attached to it and grain and Wei River traffic sustaining its markets.

In 1472 Prefect Xiong Xiang built towers over the four city gates, and in 1565 Prefect Yao Ruxun faced the walls with brick and stone. The early Qing made Daming the planned seat of the governor-general of Zhili, Shandong and Henan in 1648; when the Viceroyalty of Zhili was restored in 1661, Daming remained its residence until the office was abolished in 1669. In 1725 the counties of Neihuang, Xun and Hua were transferred to the Henan prefectures of Zhangde and Weihui. In 1758 Wei County was dissolved and its territory divided between Daming and Yuancheng counties.
zh:
大名位于冀南与河南、山东相接的富饶平原上，永济渠故道所经的卫河流贯此地。唐代这里称魏州，安史之乱后是魏博节度使驻地，后汉将兴唐府改名为大名府。北宋以大名府为北京，作为抵御辽朝的前沿重镇，也是当时河北最大的城市，号称「河朔重镇」「北门锁钥」。金代仍为府路中心，元代设为大名路。1401年，漳河、卫河洪水将宋代旧城淤埋，都指挥使吴宓遂在艾家口镇北另筑新城。因此到1444年，明代北直隶治下的大名还是一座较新的包砖府城，元城县附郭，平原粮食与卫河舟楫维系着城中市集。

1472年，大名知府熊祥主持修建四门城楼；1565年，知府姚如循又将城墙外包砖石。清初的1648年，朝廷设置直隶山东河南三省总督，预定以大名府为总督府驻地；1661年复置直隶总督，驻地仍在大名，至1669年裁撤。1725年，内黄县、浚县、滑县改属河南彰德府和卫辉府。1758年魏县被裁撤，辖境分入大名、元城二县。

en: This is the flat country of the northern Shandong plain, crossed by the Tuhai River and running north to the Bohai mudflats, administered under the Ming as Le'an Zhou of Jinan Prefecture. The early Ming settled new villages on land emptied by the wars, but unrest soon followed: in 1420 Tang Saier, a woman of Putai who preached the White Lotus way and styled herself the 'Buddha Mother', roamed these counties with her followers before the revolt she led was put down. Zhu Gaoxu, the Yongle Emperor's second son and a famed cavalry leader of the Jingnan campaign, held his fief at Le'an, and on 2 September 1426 he rose there against his nephew the Xuande Emperor. At Yang Rong's urging the emperor took the field himself, and the prince surrendered on the twenty-first day of the month; Le'an was thereupon renamed Wuding. In 1444 it was a quiet grain-growing sub-prefecture under Jinan. It passed to Li Zicheng and then to the Qing in 1644, was made an independent sub-prefecture in 1724, and in 1734 became Wuding Prefecture, with the new Huimin County as its seat.
zh: 武定一带是鲁北平原上的平坦乡野，徒骇河流经其境，向北一直伸到渤海湾的滩涂海岸，明代为济南府乐安州。明初官府招民垦荒，在战乱抛荒的土地上重建村落，但地方并不平静：1420年，蒲台县（今滨州）女子唐赛儿传白莲教、自称「佛母」，往来滨州、益都、安丘、莒州、即墨、寿光诸州县聚众，起事当年即被镇压。明成祖第二子、靖难之役中以骁勇闻名的汉王朱高煦居藩乐安，宣德元年八月初一（1426年9月2日）在此起兵反叛侄子明宣宗；宣宗纳杨荣之谏御驾亲征，八月二十一日朱高煦出城投降，乐安州随即改名武定州。1444年的武定是济南府治下一座安静的粮作州城。1644年它先附李自成的大顺，随后归清；1724年升为直隶州，1734年再升为武定府，以新设的惠民县为府治。

en:
The seat of Laizhou was Ye County, on the eastern shore of the Laizhou Bay, the southern bight of the Bohai Sea. A county had stood there since the early Han, when it headed the Donglai commandery; the Sui renamed the prefecture Laizhou in 585, and in 1376 the Ming raised it to Laizhou Prefecture, governing the eastern Shandong peninsula from Ye. In 1444 it was a Ming walled town of fishermen and salt-boilers: the bay was one of north China's fishing and sea-salt grounds, and its harbour carried the coasting trade between Shandong and the other ports around the Bohai.

In the winter of 1631 the Liaodong officers Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming mutinied at Wuqiao and swept east. Dengzhou fell in the first month of 1632 and the rebels laid siege to Laizhou, whose prefect Zhu Wannian held the walls with the governors Xu Congzhi and Xie Lian. Xu was struck down by rebel cannon fire in the fourth month; in the seventh, Kong feigned surrender and killed Zhu and Xie after they came out of Ye County to announce a pardon, yet the city never fell. Imperial troops crushed the revolt in 1633 and Kong fled across the Bohai to the Manchus. In 1642 Manchu raiders under Abatai plundered as far as Laizhou and Dengzhou before withdrawing, and after the Ming collapse in 1644 the prefecture passed to the Qing.
zh:
莱州的治所是掖县，地处渤海南部海湾莱州湾的东岸。西汉初年这里便已置县，为东莱郡治所；隋开皇五年（585年）改光州为莱州，明洪武九年（1376年）升为莱州府，以掖县为附郭县，管辖山东半岛东部。1444年时，这里是明朝一座以渔人和盐户为主的城邑：莱州湾是中国北方重要的渔场和海盐产区，掖县海港则承担山东与渤海沿岸各港之间的沿海贸易。

崇祯四年（1631年）冬，辽东将领孔有德、耿仲明在吴桥兵变，挥师东进。崇祯五年（1632年）正月登州府陷落，叛军进围莱州。知府朱万年会同山东巡抚徐从治、登莱巡抚谢琏据城坚守，四月徐从治被叛军红衣大炮击伤而死；七月孔有德诈降，谢琏、朱万年出掖县城宣旨时被俘，朱万年不屈就义，谢琏也于当年遇难，莱州城却始终未破。崇祯六年（1633年）明军平叛，孔有德渡海投降后金。1642年，阿巴泰率领的清军入塞掳掠，兵锋及于莱州、登州，次年退兵；1644年明朝灭亡后，莱州府归入清朝。

en:
Yanzhou, named among the Nine Provinces of the Yu Gong, had its seat at Ziyang, the old town of Xiaqiu. In 1385 the Hongwu Emperor raised it to a prefecture governing four sub-prefectures and twenty-three counties across southern Shandong — among them Qufu, home of Confucius, and Zouxian, home of Mencius — and the same year enfeoffed his tenth son Zhu Tan there as Prince of Lu. A patron of letters who wrote poetry, Zhu Tan died in 1390 after taking alchemical elixirs, earning the unflattering posthumous name Huang; his son Zhu Zhaohui held the fief for sixty-four years. Within the prefecture, Jining straddled the Grand Canal carrying the southern grain tribute to Beijing, while at Qufu the Duke Yansheng, Confucius's direct heir, kept his ancestral temple. In 1444 Yanzhou was one of Shandong's foremost princely seats, guarding the south of the province.

In 1499 lightning struck the Temple of Confucius at Qufu and burned the Great Completion Hall and more than a hundred and twenty bays of buildings; the court rebuilt it over five years at a cost of 150,000 taels. The Ming ended at Yanzhou in blood: in the fifth Manchu inroad, Abatai's army entered the pass in the tenth month of 1642 and stormed the city, killing the Prince of Lu Zhu Yipai. Three of its gates burned in a single day, the town was sacked, and two centuries of treasure heaped up in the Lu palace were carried off. The dead prince's younger brother Zhu Yihai escaped and, after the fall of Beijing, fled south to lead the Southern Ming resistance as prince-regent. Under the Qing the prefecture kept its standing: in 1684 the Kangxi Emperor came to Qufu to sacrifice to Confucius, where the sixty-fourth-generation descendant Kong Shangren, later famed for The Peach Blossom Fan, lectured before him; in 1724 lightning again fired the temple, rebuilt under the Yongzheng Emperor over six years.
zh:
兖州之名远承《禹贡》九州，府城设在古老的滋阳，旧称瑕丘。洪武十八年（1385年），明太祖升兖州为府，下辖四州二十三县，覆盖整个鲁南——孔子故里曲阜、孟子故里邹县都在境内；同年他封第十子朱檀为鲁王，就藩兖州。朱檀好文礼士、善写诗歌，却在洪武二十二年因服食丹药毒发伤目而死，得到一个不加掩饰的恶谥「荒」；其子朱肇煇嗣位，在藩长达六十四年。府境之内，济宁州横跨输送南方漕粮北上的大运河，曲阜则有孔子嫡裔衍圣公世守家庙。1444年的兖州是山东首屈一指的藩府重镇，坐镇鲁南，孔氏圣裔与运河漕路是它的两大凭依。

1499年，曲阜孔庙遭雷击起火，大成殿等一百二十余楹建筑化为灰烬，朝廷历时五年、耗银十五万两重修。明末兖州在兵燹中倾覆：1642年十月清军第五次入塞，阿巴泰所部破关南下，攻陷兖州，杀鲁王朱以派；四座城门中的南、北、东门同日烧毁，城内民居焚荡殆尽，鲁王府积蓄二百余年的财物被洗劫一空。朱以派之弟朱以海幸免于难，北京陷落后南下，以鲁王监国继续抗清。入清以后兖州仍为鲁南重镇：1684年康熙帝亲临曲阜拜谒孔庙、祭孔，孔子六十四代孙、后来以《桃花扇》闻名的孔尚任曾为皇帝讲经；1724年孔庙再毁于雷电火，雍正帝发帑重修，历时六年告成。

en:
Xuzhou, the ancient Pengcheng, guards the gap where the Shandong hills meet the North China Plain, at the old confluence of the Si and Bian rivers. It was the heartland of the Han imperial house: Liu Bang was born at Pei within its borders, and in 206 BC Xiang Yu made Pengcheng the capital of his Western Chu; the Han Princes of Chu held their court here and went to their tombs dressed in jade burial suits. Under the Northern Song the Liguo works north of the city became one of the greatest iron centres of the empire, with thirty-six private smelters and thousands of foundrymen, and in 1077 the prefect Su Shi raised the Su Embankment to hold back a Yellow River flood. The Jurchen took the city in 1129, and in 1352 the Yuan chancellor Toqto stormed it to crush the Red Turban rebel 'Sesame Li' and keep the grain route open. Under the Ming, Xuzhou became a Grand Canal town of the Southern Metropolitan Province, with a great state granary and one of the seven customs barriers, as boatmen hauled junks through the Xuzhou and Lüliang rapids below the walls. In 1444 it was a rich but flood-prone transport hub where iron and tribute grain changed hands at the wharves.

The Yellow River nevertheless proved the stronger. The river policy of 1579, which impounded clear water to scour the silted bed, raised the river against Xuzhou instead. In 1605 the new Jia Canal drew the main canal route away to the north-east to bypass the rapids, most traffic abandoned the wharves and the city's trade declined, and in 1624 a Yellow River breach buried the walled city under four metres of water and sediment. During the Ming-Qing transition Xuzhou was one of the Four Jiangbei Garrisons of the Southern Ming until Qing armies took it in mid-1645; local scholars Yan Ermei and Wan Shouqi, the 'Two Ming Loyalists of Xuzhou', refused office under the new dynasty. The Tancheng earthquake of 1668 wrecked much of the city. In 1733 the Qing raised Xuzhou from a subprefecture to a prefecture, with Tongshan county as its seat, governing the border counties of four provinces.
zh:
徐州古称彭城，扼守山东丘陵与华北平原之间的缺口，古为泗水、汴水交汇之处。这里是汉朝皇室的故乡：刘邦生于境内沛县，公元前206年项羽以彭城为西楚都城；汉代楚王世代都此，王陵中以金缕玉衣随葬。北宋时，城北的利国监是全国最大的冶铁中心之一，设有三十六处民营冶场，工匠数千；1077年知州苏轼为抵御黄河洪水主持修筑苏堤。1129年金兵攻占徐州；1352年元丞相脱脱攻破州城，镇压红巾军首领「芝麻李」，保住漕运粮道。明代徐州为南直隶徐州直隶州，倚大运河而兴，设有大型官仓和全国七处钞关之一，纤夫在城下的徐州洪、吕梁洪间挽舟过险。1444年的徐州是富庶而多水患的漕运枢纽，铁器与漕粮在码头往来不绝。

但黄河终究更为凶险。1579年推行「蓄清刷黄」之策，拦蓄清水冲刷淤高的河床，结果反使黄河在徐州一带更加高悬。1605年新开的泇河把大运河主航道引向东北以避开险滩，多数舟楫不再经过徐州，市面随之萧条；1624年黄河决口，洪水与泥沙将州城深埋四米。明清鼎革之际，徐州是南明江北四镇之一，1645年年中被清军攻取，乡绅阎尔梅、万寿祺坚不仕清，并称「徐州二遗民」。1668年郯城大地震又使城郭大半被毁。1733年，清廷升徐州为徐州府，以铜山县为府治，管辖四省交界的州县。

en:
Huai'an grew up at the junction of the Huai River and the Grand Canal, where as early as 486 BC the Hangou Canal first carried Yangtze traffic into the Huai. In 1128 a Song governor breached the Yellow River levees to check the Jin advance, and the great river then seized the Si and lower Huai channels on its way to the sea; its silt built the coastal flats east of the city and swelled Hongze Lake, leaving Huai'an with perpetual floods. In 1366 Zhu Yuanzhang made it Huai'an Prefecture, under the Southern Province, its jurisdiction reaching the sea through the salt-boiling and fishing coast of Yancheng. The Pingjiang Earl Chen Xuan, who managed grain transport for thirty years under the Yongle Emperor, dredged the old Sha River channel in 1410 as the Qingjiangpu and built four locks; the four state shipyards and the great imperial granaries made the town the throat of the grain fleets. In 1444 Huai'an is the busiest transshipment city north of the Yangtze, where southern boats changed to northern horses.

The later Ming stationed a director-general of grain transport at Huai'an, and river commissioners sat there too; the Wanli-era Pan Jixun fought the Yellow River's silt with long dikes and raised the Gaojia weir above Hongze Lake. Wu Cheng'en (1506–1582) of Shanyang wrote Journey to the West in this city. The wars of the Ming-Qing transition swept along the canal, and under the new dynasty Haizhou and the northern counties were detached from Huai'an, though both the grain-transport and Southern River director-generals kept their seats here, the Qingjiangpu shipyards and warehouses stretching for miles. When the Qinghe county seat was destroyed by flood in the 1760s, its magistrate moved into booming Qingjiangpu, by then the true pivot of canal traffic, where passengers changed between southern boats and northern horses.
zh:
淮安位于淮河与京杭大运河交汇处，早在公元前486年，吴王夫差开凿的邗沟便在末口入淮，长江的舟船从此可直达淮上。1128年，宋朝官府为阻遏金兵掘开黄河大堤，黄河此后夺泗水和淮河下游入海；泥沙在城东淤出大片滩地，也垫高了洪泽湖，使淮安世世代代与水患相伴。1366年朱元璋改淮安路为淮安府，隶南直隶，辖地向东一直到盐城一带煮海为盐、以渔为业的海滨。永乐年间，平江伯陈瑄总督漕运三十年，1410年循沙河故道挑浚成清江浦，建起新庄、福兴、清江、移风四道闸门；工部的四大漕船厂与户部的皇家仓廒云集于此，使淮安成为漕船队的咽喉。1444年的淮安是长江以北最繁忙的水陆码头，南船在此换马，北客在此登舟。

明代后来又向淮安派驻漕运总督，治河大臣也常驻于此，万历年间的潘季驯便以长堤束水、借淮刷黄，在洪泽湖一线加修高家堰。山阳县人吴承恩（1506—1582）就在这里写成了《西游记》。明末清初的战火沿运河席卷而过，入清以后，海州及北部各县被析出另设，淮安仍驻有漕运总督与南河总督，清江浦的船厂仓廒绵延数十里。1760年代，清河县城毁于洪水，县治迁入鼎盛的清江浦，这里遂成为运河上真正的交通总枢，行旅照例在此由南船换乘北马。

en:
On the middle Huai, Fengyang was the ancient Zhongli and later the seat of Haozhou, an obscure county town until it gave China a dynasty. Zhu Yuanzhang was born here in 1328 to a poor farming family; when famine and plague carried off his family in 1344 he took vows at the Huangjue Monastery before joining the rebellions that made him the Hongwu Emperor. From Nanjing he heaped honours on his home soil. In 1369 he ordered a 'Central Capital' built beside Haozhou to the standard of an imperial capital, with Li Shanchang superintending the works, and raised the Huangling Mausoleum over his parents' grave. The new prefecture and county were named Fengyang in 1374, but in 1375, shaken by resistance among the conscripted craftsmen and alarmed at the cost, he abandoned the nearly finished Zhongdu. Thousands of families were moved in from Shandong, Shanxi, Hebei, Guangdong and the Taihu country. In 1444 the grand walls enclosed a half-empty city: the chief county of the vast Fengyang Prefecture in South Zhili was in truth a mausoleum garrison, where princes had once drilled troops and Zhu Wengui, son of the dethroned Jianwen Emperor, remained confined since the Yongle reign.

The quiet of the imperial necropolis ended with the collapse of the late Ming. In 1635 the rebel armies of Gao Yingxiang, Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong marched on Fengyang to humble the dynasty and took the city in less than ten days, killing the prefect Yan Rongxuan, sixty eunuchs and four thousand garrison soldiers, then burning the Huangling Mausoleum and the Huangjue Monastery. Under the Qing the prefecture passed from Jiangnan Province to the new province of Anhui. In 1667 the county seat was moved within the old imperial city, and in 1754 Linhuai County was merged into Fengyang. The palaces of the Central Capital were never rebuilt: their walls and gate platforms were taken over by the county town or left to crumble, while the stone statues of the imperial mausoleum kept watch over the abandoned home capital of the Ming.
zh:
凤阳地处淮河中游，古为钟离，隋唐以后是濠州治所，本是个不起眼的县城，直到这里走出了一代开国之君。1328年，朱元璋出生在当地一户贫苦农家；1344年灾荒与瘟疫夺走他的家人，他一度在皇觉寺出家，后来投奔起义军，终成明太祖。定都南京后，他把无上的荣耀堆给故乡：1369年下诏在濠州以西营建规制一如京师的中都，由李善长主持工程，又在父母的墓前修建皇陵。1374年，新府、新县赐名凤阳；但1375年，迫于应役工匠的抗争、又惊于工程劳费，朱元璋在中都将成之际下诏罢建。朝廷还从山东、山西、河北、广东和太湖一带强迁大批民户来此充实。1444年的凤阳，宏伟城墙圈着一座半空的城：作为南直隶辖境辽阔的凤阳府首县，它实质是座皇陵驻军之城，皇子诸王曾在此练兵讲武，被废的建文帝之子朱文圭自永乐初年起仍幽禁在皇城之中。

皇陵之城的沉寂在明末大乱中终结。1635年，高迎祥、李自成、张献忠等路农民军为挫明朝声威直取中都凤阳，不到十天便攻破城池，杀知府颜容暄、宦官六十人和官军四千，随后纵火焚烧明皇陵，又焚毁朱元璋曾出家的皇觉寺。入清以后，凤阳府先属江南省，后划归新设的安徽省。1667年，凤阳县治移入旧皇城；1754年，临淮县并入凤阳县。中都的宫殿再未重建，城墙与城门台基或被县城沿用、或任其倾颓，唯有皇陵的神道石刻留存下来，守着这座被放弃的朱明故里之都。

en:
Where the Ying River crosses the plain to join the Huai, the Qin set up Ruyin County, and in 523 the Northern Wei made it the seat of Yingzhou, a name it kept for most of the next thousand years. Under the Northern Song it was raised to Shunchang Prefecture, and there in 1140 Liu Qi, with fewer than twenty thousand men, beat off a Jin army said to exceed a hundred thousand under Wuzhu—one of the Song dynasty's most celebrated defensive victories. The aged Ouyang Xiu had retired to Yingzhou and died there in 1072. The place's largest part in dynastic history came at the end of Yuan rule: in 1351 Liu Futong, a Yingzhou man, raised the Red Turban standard on this plain, the rising that shook Mongol China to pieces. Under the Ming, Yingzhou was a sub-prefecture of Fengyang Prefecture within South Zhili, its walled town standing on old Ruyin. In 1444 it was an unassuming farming county, its grain floated down the Ying toward the Huai.

Ming centuries passed quietly over Yingzhou. In 1735 the Yongzheng Emperor raised it to a full prefecture, Yingzhou Fu, and created Fuyang County as its seat—the first appearance of the name this province bears. The new prefecture took in the sub-prefecture of Bozhou and five counties across the whole north-western corner of Anhui, a flat, crowded country that Qing administrators rated 'busy, worn and hard to govern'. Through the Qing it stayed one of the granaries of the middle Huai, its markets and villages thick along the Ying, though plenty moved with the harvest and the river.
zh:
颍河横穿平原、向东南注入淮河，秦代已在这里置汝阴县，523年北魏又于此设颍州，此后近千年间大半沿用此名。北宋升为顺昌府，1140年，刘锜率不足两万人的八字军在此挫败金兀术麾下十余万大军，是为南宋抗金名役顺昌之战。年迈的欧阳修晚年退居颍州，1072年长逝于此。此地在王朝鼎革中分量最重的一幕出现在元末：1351年，颍州人刘福通在这片平原上举起义旗，红巾军由此起事，最终撼动了元朝在汉地的统治。明代，颍州是南直隶凤阳府下辖的散州，城垣坐落在古汝阴旧址。1444年的颍州是个朴实的农耕州县，出产的粮食顺颍河而下，运往淮河。

明代的颍州大体平静。1735年（雍正十三年），清廷升颍州为颍州府，增设附郭阜阳县为府治，「阜阳」之名由此而始。新府领亳州一州和五县，覆盖皖西北的整片平原，清代考语为「繁、疲、难」，是出名的难治之区。整个清代，这里始终是淮河中游的粮仓之一，颍河两岸村镇相望、市集相连，只是丰歉全系于收成与河水。

en:
Zhenjiang, long known as Jingkou and Runzhou, guards the south bank of the Yangzi where the river meets the Grand Canal. Sun Quan fortified the bluff above the crossing in 209, and the southern canal developed under the Sui turned the garrison into a relay between the Yangzi delta and northern China. The Song raised Runzhou to Zhenjiang Prefecture in 1113. Mongol forces took it during their 1275 advance against the Southern Song, and Xu Da seized it for Zhu Yuanzhang in 1356. Under the Ming, Zhenjiang Prefecture formed part of Nanzhili and governed Dantu, Danyang and Jintan; the guard commander Song Li rebuilt the prefectural walls in 1368. In 1444 it was a river garrison and canal port opposite Yangzhou, where tribute grain and silk moved between river craft and canal boats.

When the Southern Ming collapsed along the lower Yangzi in 1645, Zhenjiang passed to the Qing. In 1659 Zheng Chenggong and Zhang Huangyan sailed upstream, captured the city and briefly threatened Nanjing before their expedition failed. The Qing afterwards stationed a permanent garrison at Jingkou under a Vice-Commander, while the prefecture continued to watch the grain transport route. In 1730 Liyang County was transferred from Jiangning Prefecture to Zhenjiang. During the eighteenth century its wharves remained one of the chief trans-shipment points between the Grand Canal, the Yangzi crossing and the sea-going junks trading along the coast.
zh:
镇江古称京口、润州，扼守长江南岸，正处长江与大运河交汇之处。209年，孙权在渡口高地上修筑军城；隋代以后江南运河贯通，使这处江防要地成为长江三角洲与北方之间的转运枢纽。1113年，北宋升润州为镇江府。1275年元军南下攻宋时占领此地，1356年徐达又为朱元璋夺取镇江。明代，镇江府隶属南直隶，下辖丹徒、丹阳、金坛三县；1368年，镇江卫指挥宋礼主持修筑府城。1444年的镇江与扬州隔江相望，是河防驻军所在和运河港口，漕粮、丝货在此由江船转驳运河船。

1645年，南明在长江下游的防线崩溃，镇江归入清朝。1659年，郑成功与张煌言率水师入长江，攻克镇江，一度进逼南京，但北伐最终失败。此后清朝在京口常设驻防，置副都统统率驻军，镇江府则继续监护漕运通道。1730年，溧阳县由江宁府划归镇江府。整个18世纪，这里的码头始终是大运河、长江渡口与沿海海船之间最重要的转运点之一。

en:
Ningguo is the mountain country of south-eastern Nanzhili, where the streams of the Huangshan ranges gather into the Qingyi River on their way to the Yangtze. In 208 Sun Quan split the south of Wanling county into Huaian and Ningguo, and the region long answered to Xuanzhou, a posting that poets prized: at the end of the 5th century Xie Tiao governed it and sang of Jingting Hill beyond the walls, and Li Bai later climbed that hill seven times, leaving it known as the poetry hill of the south. In 1166 Xuanzhou became Ningguo prefecture with its seat at Xuancheng, and Zhu Yuanzhang's army took the circuit in April 1357; under the Ming the prefecture ruled six counties, Jingxian among them. Jingxian had made paper since the Tang, when Xuanzhou tribute paper reached the court, and its soft, moth-resistant xuan paper, said to last a thousand years, together with its writing brushes, was the stock on which painters and calligraphers relied. In 1444 the prefecture lived by these workshops and by its mountain trade with Zhejiang.

The paper workshops carried on under the Qing, and when Jiangnan was split into Jiangsu and Anhui in the Kangxi reign Ningguo passed to the new province. Its later fame was in learning rather than arms. Mei Wending (1633–1721) of Xuancheng, the foremost astronomer and mathematician of the early Qing, wrote more than eighty works that reconciled the Chinese computational tradition with the Jesuit science newly arrived from Europe. Below Jingting Hill the monk-painter Shitao, a scion of the fallen Ming house, spent more than ten years at Guangjiao Monastery, and the landscapes he made of the Ningguo hills and Huangshan became a model for Qing painters long after.
zh:
宁国是南直隶东南的山乡，黄山余脉的溪涧汇成青弋江，北入长江。208年，孙权分宛陵县南境置怀安、宁国二县，这一带长期隶属宣州，而宣州是诗人向往的名郡：5世纪末谢朓任宣城太守，写下《游敬亭山》，后来李白七登城北的敬亭山，题诗数十首，此山遂有「江南诗山」之称。1166年宣州升为宁国府，治宣城；1357年四月朱元璋攻取宁国路，仍置宁国府，入明后领宣城、南陵、泾县、宁国、旌德、太平六县。辖下泾县自唐代起造纸，宣州贡纸唐代已入宫廷，其地出产的宣纸受墨润、久藏不蠹，号称「纸寿千年」，宣笔同样名家，历代书画家多赖此挥洒。1444年的宁国府，便靠这些纸坊和通往浙江的山路商贸易为生。

入清以后，纸坊维持旧业，康熙年间江南分省，宁国府改隶新设的安徽省。此地后来以学术而非武功闻名：宣城人梅文鼎（1633—1721）被誉为清初历算第一名家，著书八十余种，把中国传统算学与欧洲传教士带来的西方天文历算融会贯通。明清易代之际，明宗室后裔、画僧石涛在敬亭山下的广教寺修行十余年，他笔下的宁国山水与黄山，后来成为清代画家共同取法的范本。

en:
Huizhou is a fastness of narrow valleys in the Huangshan range, short of farmland but rich in crafts. The Qin already set up She and Yi counties here; under the Jin it was Xin'an commandery, and in 1121 the Song renamed it Huizhou, a prefecture of six counties – Shexian, Xiuning, Wuyuan, Qimen, Yixian and Jixi – whose borders then held for eight hundred years. When Zhu Yuanzhang's forces entered the mountains in the late Yuan, Zhu Sheng (1299–1370) of Xiuning gave him the counsel to build high walls, store up grain and be slow to claim the throne. Wuyuan was the ancestral home of Zhu Xi (1130–1200), whose Neo-Confucian teaching became the creed of the prefecture's lineage schools. Its crafts were already famed: the ink master Li Tinggui, Xi Chao's son granted the imperial surname by the Southern Tang lord Li Yu, made Xin'an ink a byword under the Song. In 1444 Ming prefectural records confessed that the local harvest met barely a tenth of the prefecture's needs, and nine households in ten lived by crafts or by trading in other provinces.

The exodus came after the salt reform of 1505, when salt licenses could be bought for silver: Huizhou men crowded the yards of Lianghuai and Liangzhe, Yangzhou above all, and by the Wanli reign they stood with the Shanxi and Shaanxi merchants as masters of the commerce, until no market town was without a Huizhou man. Wang Zhi of Shexian ran an armed fleet from Hirado and was beheaded in 1560; Hu Zongxian (1512–1565) of Jixi, the supreme commander who crushed the wokou raids, was ensnared in the fall of Yan Song and died in prison. Learning kept pace with trade: Dai Zhen (1724–1777) of Xiuning, the greatest evidential scholar of the age, edited the Four Treasuries for the Qianlong emperor, while Xu Xiake twice climbed Huangshan and named it the strangest mountain under heaven. In 1790 Gao Langting led his Sanqing troupe to Beijing for the emperor's eightieth birthday, and the other three great Huizhou companies followed; their erhuang opera was later counted an ancestor of Peking opera.
zh:
徽州是黄山群峰环抱中的山府，田少而瘠，林竹、溪涧与百工之巧却饶富。秦代已在此置黟、歙二县，晋为新安郡，1121年北宋改歙州为徽州，从此领歙县、休宁、婺源、祁门、黟县、绩溪六县，辖境八百年基本不变。元末朱元璋兵入徽州，休宁人朱升（1299—1370）献上「高筑墙、广积粮、缓称王」三策，为其所纳。婺源是朱熹（1130—1200）的祖籍，程朱理学在这里化为宗族与书院的风气；匠作也早已成名：晚唐制墨名家奚超父子避乱南来，南唐后主李煜赏识其子廷珪所制之墨，赐姓李氏，李廷珪的「新安香墨」在宋代已成稀世珍品。1444年的徽州山多田少，《徽州府志》已称本地一岁所入不足开销的十分之一，民户十九靠手艺或远走他郡贩负为生。

大规模外出经商的高潮，起于弘治末年（1505年）盐法改行开中折色、商人可在运司纳银领引之后：徽州人涌向两淮、两浙的盐场，尤以扬州为根基，到万历年间已与山陕商人并执商界牛耳，世称「无徽不成镇」。东南海疆则一造一毁了两个徽州人：歙县人汪直以日本平户为据点，统领武装海商集团，1560年被处斩；绩溪人胡宗宪（1512—1565）总督东南、剿平倭寇，却因严嵩一案牵连，1565年死于狱中。学问与商路并进：休宁人戴震（1724—1777）是清代考据学的宗师，晚年入四库全书馆任纂修官，获赐同进士出身；旅行家徐霞客两度登临黄山，誉为「天下第一奇山」。1790年，高朗亭率领的扬州三庆班入京为乾隆帝贺八十大寿，四喜、春台、和春各班随后相继北上，四大徽班把二黄声腔带去京师，后世视为京剧的远祖。

en:
Shaoxin, usually recorded as Shaoxing, lies on the Hangzhou Bay shore at the edge of the Kuaiji Mountains. Early in the fifth century BC Fan Li built a triangular stronghold for King Goujian of Yue, and the place later became Shanyin and Kuaiji. The Tang knew it as Yuezhou, a regional command on the Zhejiang east coast. After the Song court fled from the Jurchen, Emperor Gaozong took refuge there; in 1131 his new Shaoxing reign title gave the city its name, and Yuezhou was raised to Shaoxing Prefecture as a Southern Song auxiliary capital. By 1444 the Ming prefecture contained eight counties, with Kuaiji and Shanyin sharing the walled canal city; rice wine, waterborne trade and examination culture supported its offices, schools and markets.

The prefecture's scholar-officials gave it unusually wide influence. Wang Shouren, born in Yuyao in 1472, became the chief philosopher of the School of Mind, commanded troops on the frontier and suppressed the Prince of Ning's revolt in 1519. On 7 September 1645, after Nanjing and Hangzhou had fallen, Zheng Zunqian and Zhang Guowei installed Zhu Yihai, Prince of Lu, as regent in Shaoxin. His court failed to coordinate with the Longwu emperor at Fuzhou, and in the sixth month of 1646 Qing forces broke through Zhejiang; Zhu escaped by sea to Zhoushan. Under Qing rule Shaoxin became identified with private legal secretaries, the Shaoxing masters, who served officials across the empire. Wang Huizu, born in Xiaoshan in 1730 and died in 1807, became a model of that profession, while rice wine and examination families sustained the old prefectural city into the early nineteenth century.
zh:
绍兴位于杭州湾南岸、会稽山北缘。公元前5世纪初，范蠡为越王勾践修筑城邑，此地后来设为山阴、会稽。唐代称越州，是浙东沿海的区域统治中心。宋廷避金军南下，宋高宗曾驻跸越州；1131年，他改元绍兴，越州因年号得名，升为绍兴府，并成为南宋陪都。1444年的绍兴府辖八县，会稽、山阴两县同在这座水网城垣中治事；黄酒、水运贸易和科举之学支撑着城中的官署、学舍与市肆。

绍兴府的士大夫在外影响尤大。1472年生于余姚的王守仁是心学集大成者，也曾在边疆统军，并于1519年平定宸濠之乱。1645年9月7日，南京、杭州相继陷清后，郑遵谦、张国维等在绍兴迎立鲁王朱以海监国。鲁王朝廷与福州隆武帝不能协同，1646年六月清军攻破浙江，朱以海由张名振等人护卫逃往舟山。入清以后，绍兴又以在各地官署供职的刑名师爷，即「绍兴师爷」闻名。1730年生于萧山的汪辉祖，至1807年去世，成为这一行业的典范；黄酒与科举世家则维持着府城到19世纪初的繁荣。

en:
Ningbo lies where the Yong River reaches the sea east of the Ningshao Plain. The Tang created Mingzhou in 738, and in 821 its administration moved to Sanjiangkou, where a walled inner city became the core of the later port. A Song maritime trade office opened in 999, and Mingzhou ships sailed to Goryeo and Japan while Zen monks carried Buddhist teachings in both directions. Trade continued under the Yuan, and the late-Yuan warlord Fang Guozhen held the area before submitting to Zhu Yuanzhang in 1367. In 1381 Mingzhou was renamed Ningbo, meaning calm waves. By 1444 its maritime office handled licensed trade with Korea and Japan and the port was the designated gateway for Japanese tally missions, even as coastal garrisons and sea bans tightened around a population of Wu-speaking sailors, fishermen and shipwrights.

In May 1523 rival Hosokawa and Ouchi missions from Japan clashed at Ningbo over their tally credentials; the fighting killed Ming officers and spilled into the surrounding countryside, prompting Beijing to close the Zhejiang and Fujian maritime trade offices. Much of the traffic then moved to Shuangyu, an island anchorage south of the Zhoushan archipelago where Chinese, Japanese, Portuguese and Southeast Asian merchants traded from 1524 until Ming forces under Zhu Wan destroyed the settlement in 1548. The wokou wars that followed brought Yu Dayou and Qi Jiguang's coastal campaigns to Ningbo. Ming officials surrendered the city to the Qing in 1645, but the Yin County native Zhang Huangyan kept up a naval resistance for nearly two decades until his execution in 1664. Qing evacuation orders and sea bans injured the port, though Ningbo merchants extended their networks inland, while Huang Zongxi and Quan Zuwang made the city a centre of the Eastern Zhejiang scholarly tradition.
zh:
宁波位于宁绍平原以东，甬江由此入海。738年唐代设立明州；821年州治迁至三江口并修筑内城，奠定了后世港城的核心。999年北宋设立明州市舶司，海船往来高丽与日本，禅宗僧侣也随航路传法。元代海外贸易继续繁盛，元末方国珍割据这一带，1367年归降朱元璋。1381年，明州取「海定则波宁」之义改称宁波。到1444年，宁波市舶司掌管对朝鲜、日本的勘合贸易，也是日本贡船入明的指定口岸；但在倭寇压力下，海防卫所与海禁同时收紧，城中多是操吴语的水手、渔民和造船工匠。

1523年5月，日本细川氏与大内氏的贸易使团在宁波为勘合符真伪发生冲突，混战中杀死明朝军官并劫掠附近地方，史称宁波之乱；明朝随后废除福建、浙江市舶司，只留广东一处。贸易转而流向舟山群岛以南的双屿港，1524年至1548年间，中国、日本、葡萄牙和东南亚商人在此交易，形成海上私市，最后被朱纨统率的明军剿平。此后倭患加剧，俞大猷、戚继光都曾在宁波沿海用兵。1645年，宁波明朝官员降清，但鄞县人张煌言率水师坚持抗清近二十年，直到1664年被俘就义。清代迁界与海禁使港口遭受重创；海禁松弛后，宁波商人继续向内地扩展商路，黄宗羲、全祖望等人也使这里成为浙东学派的中心。

en:
Jinhua, the old Wuzhou, lies in the Jin-Qu Basin of central Zhejiang, where the Dongyang and Wuyi rivers join to form the Wu River and flow on through Lanxi toward the Qiantang. In 266 the Wu state established Dongyang Commandery with its seat at Changshan, and the town became a collecting point for rice, bamboo and mountain goods moving along the water network toward the southern end of the Grand Canal. Cured hams were already made there under the Tang and were presented to the Song court. The Yuan walls of the present city date from 1352. Zhu Yuanzhang took Wuzhou in 1358, briefly renamed it Ningyue, and established Jinhua Prefecture in 1360. In 1444 its seven counties formed a bookish inland grain prefecture whose rice, timber, bamboo and hams moved downriver.

In 1471 the Ming court created Tangxi County, completing the prefecture's eight-county pattern. In 1646, after Bolo's Qing army broke through the Southern Ming line on the Qiantang River, the Grand Secretary Zhu Dadian held Jinhua rather than surrender. The city fell in the seventh month, and local accounts record a massacre in which about 50,000 people were killed. The Qing kept Jinhua as an eight-county prefecture; cured hams were again listed as tribute, while the river wharves continued to gather rice, bamboo and mountain produce for the Qiantang route. By the eighteenth century Jinhua remained the agricultural market and river-transport centre of the central Zhejiang basin.
zh:
金华古称婺州，位于浙江中部金衢盆地，东阳江与武义江在城边汇成金华江，再经兰溪汇入钱塘江水系。266年，孙吴设置东阳郡，治所长山，此后这里成为稻米、竹材和山货沿水网运往大运河南端的集散地。腌制猪腿在唐代已经出现，宋代列为贡品，即后来闻名的金华火腿。现存府城的元代城墙始于1352年。1358年朱元璋攻取婺州路，改称宁越府，1360年又改设金华府。1444年，金华府下辖七县，是文风兴盛的内陆产粮区，稻米、木材、竹材和腌腿顺江西运。

1471年，明廷析置汤溪县，金华府自此形成八县格局。1646年，清贝勒博洛攻破南明钱塘江防线后，督师大学士朱大典率金华军民据城死守。七月城陷，清军屠城，据地方文献记载约有五万人遇难。清代仍设辖有八县的金华府，金华火腿再度列为贡品，江边码头也继续集散稻米、竹材和山货，供应钱塘江水路。到18世纪，金华仍是浙中盆地的农业市集与河运中心。

en:
Poyang faces the great lake of the same name, where the Gan River gathers before passing to the Yangtze in north-eastern Jiangxi. A county stood here under the Qin, and after Zhu Yuanzhang took the region in 1361 the walled town became the seat of Raozhou prefecture, whose seven counties included Fuliang with its porcelain town of Jingdezhen. Renamed in 1004 for the Jingde reign era, Jingdezhen had run the Yuan porcelain bureau from 1278 and made its name with blue-and-white ware. From 30 August to 4 October 1363 the lake was the stage for Zhu's battle with Chen Youliang, whose tower fleet was burned out by fire ships, the last great fight before the founding of the Ming. In 1369 the Ming opened an official pottery at Jingdezhen, followed under the Xuande emperor by the imperial kiln, and in 1444 the town was already firing palace blue-and-white while its wares paid for silver from overseas.

The Ming kilns went from triumph to triumph, from the contending-colours doucai of the Chenghua reign to the five-coloured wares of Jiajing and Wanli, and Jingdezhen was counted with Foshan, Hankou and Zhuxian as one of the four great towns of the age. Its cups and dishes went down the Chang to the lake, on to the Yangtze, and south over the Meiling pass to Canton, where Portuguese and Dutch ships carried them to Europe. Under the Qing, supervisors were posted to the imperial kiln: after the blue-and-white of the Kangxi reign came soft-coloured fencai and enamel-painted wares, and under Yongzheng and Qianlong the bannerman Tang Ying (1682–1756), who had mastered every craft of the kiln, produced the 'Tang kiln' wares ranked among the finest ever fired there.
zh:
鄱阳在鄱阳湖东岸，这片大湖收纳赣江，是赣东北水网通往长江的总汇。秦代已在此立县（番县），1361年朱元璋取饶州、改路为府，鄱阳自此为饶州府治，领七县，浮梁县及其属下的景德镇皆在境内。景德镇1004年以宋真宗景德年号得名，元代1278年置浮梁瓷局，以青花瓷器闻名天下。1363年8月30日至10月4日，朱元璋与陈友谅在鄱阳湖上决战，火船焚毁陈军的楼船巨舰，这是明朝开国前最后一场大战。1369年明朝在景德镇设陶厂，宣德年间又设御窑厂；1444年的景德镇已在烧造宫廷青花，一窑烟火换来了海外的白银，饶州府由此富庶。

明代窑业登峰造极，成化斗彩、嘉靖与万历朝的五彩相继称绝，景德镇与佛山、汉口、朱仙并称天下四大名镇。瓷器顺昌江入湖、转长江，并南越梅岭抵达广州，再由葡萄牙、荷兰商船载往欧洲。清代向御窑厂专派督陶官，康熙青花之后又有粉彩与珐琅彩；雍正、乾隆年间，内务府唐英（1682—1756）躬亲窑务、洞悉胎釉火候，他督造的「唐窑」被列为历代官窑中的上品。

en:
Jianning is the old heart of northern Fujian, where mountains ring the upper valley of the Min. In AD 196 the Han warlord Sun Ce set up Jian'an county here, one of the first four Chinese counties in Fujian, and under the Wu it became the seat of a commandery ruling nearly the whole region. In 943 Wang Yanzheng made the town, then named Jianzhou, capital of his short-lived empire of Yin. Song times were its golden age: the Beiyuan tea plantations sent up the famous dragon-and-phoenix cake tea as tribute, the kilns fired black-glazed Jian tea bowls, and the woodblock editions cut at Masha and the book town of Jianyang sold all over the empire; the Neo-Confucian master Zhu Xi taught in these same hills. In 1162 Jianzhou was raised to Jianning Prefecture, the first fu in Fujian. Under the Mongols it became Jianning Route, wealthy enough for Marco Polo to describe it as Quenlinfu, a city of three long bridges and much silk. The Ming kept it a prefecture. In 1444 this was a crowded Northern Min-speaking, Confucian country of tea gardens and bookshops.

In 1455 the Ming court enfeoffed a ninth-generation descendant of Zhu Xi as hereditary Erudite of the Five Classics, raising an official mansion beside the Master's shrine and binding the city still closer to his cult. The later sixteenth century brought a new trade: the pine-smoked black tea of the Wuyi hills, the first of all black teas, was carried down to the coast, and in 1610 Dutch ships brought it to Europe, where Wuyi bohea became the taste of the age. War closed the era in 1648, when Qing armies stormed the prefectural city against the Ming prince Zhu Changhu and sacked it; of a population that had filled the twin county seats of Jian'an and Ouning, fewer than a hundred survived. Recovery came with the tea trade of the following century, as Wuyi black tea found buyers across Europe and the hill country grew prosperous again on its leaves.
zh:
建宁是闽北的古老中心，群山环抱着闽江上游的谷地。196年，孙策在此设立建安县，是福建最早的四县之一，孙吴时又成为统领几乎全闽的建安郡治所。943年，王延政以建州为都，建立了短命的大殷国。宋代是建州的黄金时代：北苑茶山为宫廷进贡著名的龙凤团茶，窑场烧造黑釉建盏，麻沙和书坊一带的建阳刻本风行天下；理学大师朱熹也在这片山中讲学。1162年，建州升为建宁府，是福建境内的第一府。元代改建宁路，其富庶让马可·波罗笔下的Quenlinfu有三座长桥、丝绸成匹。明代仍置建宁府。1444年的建宁，是闽北语通行、儒学兴盛之地，茶园连绵、书坊林立。

1455年，明朝封朱熹九世孙为世袭翰林五经博士，在朱子祠旁敕建博士府，这座城市与朱子之学的联系就此被朝廷定格。16世纪后期，新的贸易兴起：武夷山一带以松烟熏制的正山小种是红茶之祖，茶叶顺流运到沿海，1610年由荷兰商船带回欧洲，武夷茶（bohea）一时成为风尚。明清易代的战火终结了旧日繁华：1648年，清军为讨伐明宗室郧西王朱常湖攻破府城并大肆屠戮，曾挤满建安、瓯宁两座县衙的城池，幸存者不过百人。此后一个世纪，随着武夷红茶在欧洲销路日广，茶山之利重新养好了这片谷地，建宁也再度殷实起来。

en:
The mountains of western Fujian are Hakka country, and Tingzhou was the first prefectural seat built for the Hakka. After the upheavals of the fourth century drove northern families into these valleys, the Tang court created Tingzhou in 736 to settle the migrants and placed its seat at Changting on the Ting River, whose current runs south through the hills to join the Han and reach the sea at Chaozhou. The land kept a frontier edge: under the Song, bands of armed men gathered after the harvest and moved across the border prefectures of Fujian, Jiangxi and Guangdong, and local risings had to be put down again and again. The hills held a quieter wealth, for the fine white Yukou paper of Changting was already an imperial tribute in Southern Song times, while the plainer maobian paper went to printers across the south. The Mongols ruled it as Tingzhou Route, and in 1368 the Ming reorganized it as Tingzhou Prefecture over eight Hakka counties. In 1444 it was a crowded, Hakka-speaking Confucian land of bamboo groves, paper troughs and river rafts.

Ming peace filled the remaining valleys, and Changting grew into the market of a three-province borderland, its paper, bamboo and timber rafted down the Ting to Chaozhou and the sea. The end of the dynasty played out in the prefectural yamen itself: in 1646 the Longwu emperor Zhu Yujian, abandoned by his admiral Zheng Zhilong and fleeing the Qing armies, was captured at Tingzhou and put to death, and his court dissolved.
