Through the rest of the period the Jam kept his little state under Kalat's loose overlordship, paying tribute and ruling the Lasi tribes of the plain.
zh:
贝拉位于普拉利河（亚历山大史家笔下的阿拉比乌斯河）出山、穿过拉斯平原入海之处。公元前325年，亚历山大的军队在这里见到奥里塔人的城镇兰巴基亚；他认定此地大有可为，留下赫费斯提翁营建新城。阿拉伯文献称此地为阿尔马比勒，《恰奇纪事》说它是信德仅次于德巴尔的第二大港，当地佛教首领于631年归降；711年穆罕默德·本·卡西姆进军信德时途经此城。附近的欣戈尔河谷中有欣格拉杰圣地，穆斯林治下仍有印度教徒络绎前来朝觐。1444年的贝拉是一座靠椰枣和渔获为生的逊尼派小城，也是从信德进入莫克兰路上的第一处驿站。

本地政权成形于1742年：贾莫特部首领贾姆·阿里·汗建立拉斯贝拉酋长国，以贝拉为首府。后来卡拉特汗纳西尔汗一世（「大帝」）入侵拉斯贝拉，把贾姆纳入自己的部落联盟。贾姆王朝治下，平原上的松米亚尼湾港口松米亚尼成为同马斯喀特和信德贸易的热闹锚地，船只在采珠场作业，商人把坎大哈和卡拉特的货物转运出海。此后的岁月里，贾姆在卡拉特松散的宗主权下维持着这个小国，向汗廷纳贡，统辖平原上的拉西诸部。

en:
Kharan is a high sandy desert closed off from coastal Makran by the black ridges of the Siahan range, its caravan tracks joining the Rakhshan valley to the lowlands eastward. Under the name Buqan it first appears in Islamic sources in 674, usually named together with Qiqan, the future Kalat, and Kufic inscriptions of the early Islamic centuries have been found in its oases; the old gabr-band dams there are popularly credited to Zoroastrian builders. The nine domed tombs at Ladgasht in Mashkhel mark the Nausherwani, a Baluch people whose tradition traces them to Iranian Khorasan and to the Mongol Arghun chief Nikodar Oghul, who took the name Sultan Ahmad Khan on his conversion in 1282. In 1444 the wells and grazing of Kharan belonged to Sunni Baloch clans pasturing sheep and camels, a land of transit rather than of power.

In the troubled seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the Nausherwani grew rich on the caravan traffic between Kandahar, Kalat and Makran and made themselves the ruling house of Kharan. When Mir Ahmad Khan founded the Khanate of Kalat in 1666 the desert country lay on the edge of his Brahui confederacy, and Nasir Khan I, the Great, later invaded Kharan and bound its nawab to the Khanate. Its fortress town remained the seat of Nausherwani chiefs through the rest of the period, paying tribute when Kalat was strong and going its own way whenever it weakened.
zh:
卡兰是一片高耸的沙质荒漠，西亚汉山脉黑色的山脊把它与南方沿海的莫克兰隔开，商道穿过这里，连接拉赫尚河谷与东方的低地。它在伊斯兰文献中最初以布甘之名出现于674年，常与日后卡拉特的所在地齐齐干并称；绿洲中发现过伊斯兰早期数百年的库法体铭文，当地古老的加巴尔班德拦水坝在民间传为祆教徒所修。马什凯勒的拉德加什特有九座穹顶古墓，与诺希尔瓦尼人有关——这支俾路支人自称来自伊朗呼罗珊，先祖可追溯到蒙古阿尔浑部首领尼库达尔·兀鲁勒，他于1282年改宗伊斯兰教，取名苏丹·艾哈迈德汗。1444年，卡兰的水井和牧场属于放牧牛羊骆驼的逊尼派俾路支诸部，与其说是权力中心，不如说是商旅过境之地。

在17、18世纪的动荡中，诺希尔瓦尼人靠坎大哈、卡拉特和莫克兰之间的商队贸易壮大，成为卡兰的统治家族。1666年米尔·艾哈迈德汗建立卡拉特汗国时，这片荒漠还处在布拉灰联盟的边缘；后来纳西尔汗一世（「大帝」）攻入卡兰，令其纳瓦布臣服。此后的岁月里，要塞城镇一直是诺希尔瓦尼酋长的驻地：卡拉特强盛时便纳贡称臣，汗廷衰弱时就自行其是。

en:
Chabahar lies on a sheltered bay of the Makran coast, where the monsoon keeps the weather so mild that its Persian name means 'four springs'. Five kilometres to the northwest stood Tis, the ancient Tiz, in its day one of the great ports of these seas: goods from India and the lands beyond came up to its wharves and went on into Iran, Central Asia and the Caucasus, and al-Muqaddasi in the tenth century and Kermani in 1188 both wrote of its commerce; al-Biruni held that the coast of India began at Tiz. The Mongol raids of about 1223 wrecked the port, which never recovered. In 1444 Tiz was a fishing village above a ruined harbour, and the Baloch families of the bay lived by their catch.

In 1616 a Portuguese fleet seized Tiz and Chabahar and held them until 1621, fortifying the headland; their ruined walls long remained a landmark above Tis. After the Portuguese withdrawal the bay reverted to the Baloch chiefs of Makran, at first the Buledais and later the Gichkis, whose writ ran thin on this remote shore, while the governors of Bampur claimed an equally loose overlordship from the north. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Chabahar remained a cluster of fishing hamlets on a fine anchorage, supplying dried fish and dates to the coastal trade while the rich commerce of older days stayed with Muscat and the ports of India.
zh:
恰巴哈尔位于莫克兰海岸一处避风海湾，季风使这里气候温和，波斯语地名意为「四季如春」。城西北五公里处是提斯，即古港梯兹：当年它是这片海域最大的港口之一，印度乃至更远地方的货物在此上岸，再转往伊朗、中亚和高加索；10世纪的穆卡达西和1188年的克尔曼尼都记述过它的商贸，比鲁尼更认为印度的海岸即始于梯兹。约1223年的蒙古入侵摧毁了这座港口，它再未恢复旧日的规模。1444年，提斯已是废弃港池上方的渔村，海湾的俾路支人家以捕鱼为生。

1616年，一支葡萄牙舰队夺取提斯和恰巴哈尔，盘踞到1621年，并在海角上筑垒据守；残存的城墙此后长久作为提斯的标志。葡萄牙人撤走后，海湾重新归于莫克兰的俾路支首领——先是布莱迪家，后来是吉奇基家，他们对这段偏远海岸的控制十分松弛，北方班布尔的长官也只保持着同样松散的宗主权。17、18世纪里，恰巴哈尔始终只是优良锚地旁的一簇渔村，以鱼干和椰枣参与沿海贸易，而旧日繁盛的商利尽归马斯喀特和印度诸港。

en: Rafsanjan lies on a high, semi-desert plain between Kerman and Yazd, where qanats watered cotton fields and garden villages along a busy caravan road. Its old bazaar was traced in local tradition to the Muzaffarid period, and the town also knew conquest and plunder by Timur's armies and later frontier raiders. In 1444 it was a Persian-speaking Sunni Muslim market town within the Timurid Empire, valued less for size than for its position on the Kerman-Yazd road, its cotton and the copper-bearing country around it. At the collapse of Safavid power, Afghan invasion brought destruction from which Rafsanjan recovered only slowly through the 18th century. In 1787 the town submitted without fighting to Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar, and under the early Qajars it remained a modest caravan and cotton market, with the old bazaar repaired and extended.
zh: 拉夫桑贾位于克尔曼与亚兹德之间的半沙漠高原，坎儿井滋养着棉田和村落花园，也使这里成为繁忙商路上的一站。当地传统把老巴扎的历史追溯到穆扎法尔王朝时期，城镇也曾被帖木儿的军队和后来的边疆袭掠者征服、洗劫。1444年，它是帖木儿帝国境内一座说波斯语的逊尼派商业城镇，重要性不在城邑规模，而在克尔曼至亚兹德的道路位置、棉布贸易和周边产铜的山地。萨法维政权崩溃时，阿富汗入侵者给拉夫桑贾造成严重破坏，整个18世纪恢复缓慢。1787年，城镇未作抵抗便归附阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔；在卡扎尔王朝早期，它仍是一座不大的商旅与棉布集镇，老巴扎也得到修缮和扩建。

en:
Sabzevar was a Silk Road town of western Khurasan, set between the Iranian plateau and the roads to Herat. After the Mongol conquest it became the centre of the Sarbadars, a movement of villagers, dervishes and local commanders that rose at Bashtin and seized Sabzevar in the summer of 1337. Their rule gave the city a strong Twelver Shia imprint, though power shifted uneasily between religious shaikhs and military amirs. In 1381 Khwaja 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad submitted to Timur at Nishapur and was confirmed as governor at Radkan; Sabzevar kept its local administration and escaped a Timurid garrison. By 1444 the Sarbadars had faded after Timur's death, and their old capital was a provincial town within Timurid Khurasan.

In the following centuries Sabzevar shared the fate of the Khurasan frontier. The Uzbeks of Transoxiana took the district from the Safavids, but a Safavid counter-offensive around 1600 recovered it together with Herat and Farah. During the collapse of Safavid power in the early eighteenth century, Nader, commander of Tahmasp II's army, pursued the suspicious shah through this region and besieged him in the fort of Kohne Sangan. The campaign left Tahmasp a figurehead and made Nader the real power in Khurasan before his conquests of Herat and Isfahan.
zh:
萨卜泽瓦尔是呼罗珊西部丝绸之路上的城镇，扼守伊朗高原与通往赫拉特道路之间的要冲。蒙古征服之后，这里成为萨尔巴达尔运动的中心；这场由村民、德尔维希和本地将领组成的运动在巴什廷起兵，并于1337年夏夺取萨卜泽瓦尔。萨尔巴达尔政权使城市带有浓厚的十二伊玛目派什叶派色彩，权力却一直在宗教谢赫与军事埃米尔之间摇摆。1381年，霍贾·阿里·穆阿亚德在内沙布尔向帖木儿臣服，随后在拉德坎被确认为总督；萨卜泽瓦尔保留了本地行政机构，也没有驻扎帖木儿军队。到1444年，萨尔巴达尔势力已在帖木儿死后衰落，这座旧都成了帖木儿系呼罗珊境内的一座省城。

此后几个世纪，萨卜泽瓦尔的命运同呼罗珊边疆连在一起。河中地区的乌兹别克人从萨法维王朝手中夺下这片地区，但约1600年的萨法维反攻又将它与赫拉特、法拉一同收复。18世纪前期萨法维政权崩溃时，塔赫玛斯普二世麾下将领纳迪尔经这一带追击心存猜忌的沙阿，将其围困在科赫内桑甘要塞。这场远征使塔赫玛斯普沦为名义君主，纳迪尔则成为呼罗珊的实际掌权者，为其后征服赫拉特和伊斯法罕铺平道路。

en:
Bojnord lies in the Aladagh foothills, where the Khurasan highlands meet Turkmen raiding country beyond the Kopet Dag. Local tradition traces control of the pastures and springs here to the Qarai Turks after the Mongol conquest of the thirteenth century. In 1444 there was no great city on the site, but the district was a guarded Timurid frontier: nomads moved between mountain and plain, and caravans or raiders followed the gaps leading toward Mashhad, Astarabad and the Kara Kum.

The fortified town that became Bojnord took shape under the Safavids, who used loyal tribesmen to secure the border against Turkmens and Uzbeks. Ismail I began moving Kurdish families to Khurasan, and Tahmasp I continued the policy early in the sixteenth century. From 1598 to 1601 Abbas the Great settled another 45,000 Kurdish families and organized a chain of Kurdish domains from Astarabad to Chenaran. Bojnord became the seat of the Kurdish Shadiyan tribe, its walled town divided into eleven quarters with bazaars and four mosques.
zh:
博季努尔德坐落在阿拉达格山山麓，正是呼罗珊高地与科佩特山脉另一侧土库曼人活动地带相接之处。本地传统认为，13世纪蒙古征服之后，这一带的牧场和泉眼由卡拉伊突厥人控制。1444年时此地还没有大城市，但这片地区是帖木儿系势力戒备森严的边疆：游牧民在山地与平原间迁徙，商队和袭掠者则沿着通往马什哈德、阿斯塔拉巴德和卡拉库姆的山口往来。

后来成为博季努尔德的设防城镇形成于萨法维时期，萨法维君主以效忠的部落民守卫边境，抵御土库曼人和乌兹别克人。伊斯玛仪一世开始把库尔德家庭迁往呼罗珊，塔赫玛斯普一世在16世纪初继续推行这一政策。1598年至1601年，阿拔斯大帝又安置了四万五千户库尔德人，并在阿斯塔拉巴德至切纳兰之间组织起一连串库尔德领地。博季努尔德成为库尔德沙迪扬部落的驻地，城墙内分为十一个街区，设有巴扎和四座清真寺。

en:
Takrur was the kingdom of the middle Senegal River, the fertile valley later called Futa Toro. Its first dynasty, the blacksmith-kings of Dya'ogo, were said to have brought iron-working to the land; a Soninke line from Wagadu, the Manna, took power in the ninth or tenth century. In 1035 King War Jabi imposed sharia law, the first Sahelian ruler to adopt Islam outright, and his son allied the kingdom with the rising Almoravids. Takrur grew rich on the trans-Saharan trade, holding the river posts that linked the salt coast of Awlil to the goldfields of Bambuk. The thirteenth century brought civil war and conquest: Mali installed military governors around 1286, and as Mali faded the Fula dynasties of Lam Termess and Lam Taaga emerged. In the fifteenth century the Jolof emperor Tyukuli N'Diklam overran the valley and divided it among governors. Thus in 1444 Takrur, already beginning to be called Futa Toro, was a Muslim land of Fula farmers and fishermen under loose Jolof lordship.

By 1506 that lordship had collapsed into war between rival governors. Koli Tenguella, a Fula warlord out of Futa Jallon, conquered the valley in 1512 and founded the Denianke dynasty, fixing his capital at Tumbere-Jiinde; after the Jolof defeat at Danki in 1549 his successors drew tribute from Gajaaga, Bambuk and many neighbouring lands. The Denianke satigis, however, remained pagan rulers over a Muslim people, and the Char Bouba war of the 1670s plunged the dynasty into civil war. In the eighteenth century the Trarza Moors, backed by Morocco, and the French of Saint-Louis contended for the river's gum arabic trade, raising and pulling down satigis almost at will. In 1776 a Torodbe revolution led by Sulayman Bal overthrew the Denianke and created the Imamate of Futa Toro, whose first almamy, Abdul Qadir ibn Hammadi, made the valley a power of the jihad age.
zh:
特克鲁尔是塞内加尔河中游的王国，即后来被称为富塔托罗的肥沃河谷。最早的王朝是迪亚奥戈的铁匠诸王，相传把冶铁术带到此地；9或10世纪，来自瓦加杜的索宁克曼纳王朝取得政权。1035年，国王瓦尔·贾比推行沙里亚法，成为萨赫勒第一个正式皈依伊斯兰的统治者，他的儿子又使王国与兴起的穆拉比特人结盟。特克鲁尔靠跨撒哈拉贸易致富，占据的河畔据点把奥卢勒产盐的海岸与邦布克产金地连在一起。13世纪内战与外侮接踵而至：约1286年马里派来军事总督，马里衰落后，富拉尼人的拉姆·泰尔梅斯和拉姆·塔加两朝先后兴起。15世纪，沃洛夫皇帝蒂乌库利·恩迪克拉姆攻占河谷，将其分给众总督。因此1444年的特克鲁尔——此时已开始被称作富塔托罗——是一片富拉尼农夫和渔民的穆斯林土地，只在名义上臣服沃洛夫。

到1506年，这种宗主权已化为众总督间的混战。来自富塔贾隆的富拉尼军阀科利·滕格拉于1512年征服河谷，建立登尼扬克王朝，定都通贝雷-金德；1549年沃洛夫在丹基战败后，他的继承者们接受加贾加、邦布克及众多邻邦的朝贡。但登尼扬克的萨蒂吉是统治穆斯林民众的异教君主，17世纪70年代的沙尔·布巴战争使王朝陷入内战。18世纪，有摩洛哥撑腰的特拉尔扎摩尔人与圣路易的法国人争夺河畔的阿拉伯胶贸易，几乎随意废立萨蒂吉。1776年，苏莱曼·巴尔领导托罗德贝革命推翻登尼扬克，建立富塔托罗伊玛目国；首任阿尔马米阿卜杜勒·卡迪尔·本·哈马迪使这片河谷成为圣战时代的一方强权。

en:
Kantor is the upper Gambia river country, where the stream bends east towards the goldlands of Bambuk. Mandinka farmers shared its banks with Wolof, Bainuk and Jula settlers, and at Sutuco, the river's chief market since the fifteenth century, three roads met: up the Sandugu Bolong, east through Bundu to the Niger, and south-east through Tanda into the Fouta Djallon. Caravans brought Bambuk gold and ivory down to the wharves and carried coastal salt back east. In 1444 the country was a western tributary of the Mali mansa, though as Mali waned the Buurba of the Jolof was already coming to claim its homage.

The Portuguese reached it early: Diogo Gomes sailed up as far as Kantora in 1456, and in 1506 Duarte Pacheco Pereira described Sutuco as a walled town of some 4,000 people with a great fair where cloth, brass and beads bought gold, five or six thousand doubloons' worth reaching Portugal in good years. In the 1520s Mansa Jalali Wali made the north bank independent as the kingdom of Wuli and fought off an invasion from Futa Toro, while Kantora at one point became a province of Kaabu. When Richard Jobson visited in 1621 the king of Wuli held Sutuco, by then a seat of marabouts and Koranic learning as well as trade, served by its river port downstream at Fattatenda. Mungo Park passed through on both his journeys to the Niger, in 1795 and 1805, when the old market still prospered under the mansas of Wuli.
zh:
坎托尔地处冈比亚河上游，河道由此折向东方的班布克金矿区。曼丁卡农人在河畔而居，另有沃洛夫人、拜努克人和朱拉商人聚居；苏图科（今苏图科巴）自15世纪起便是这条河上首屈一指的市集，三条商路在此交汇：沿桑杜古博隆北上、向东经邦杜通往尼日尔河、向东南经坦达深入富塔贾隆。商队把班布克的黄金和象牙运到码头，再把沿海的食盐运回东方。1444年，此地是曼萨治下马里西陲的附庸；随着马里衰落，沃洛夫的布尔巴也已开始索取它的朝贡。

葡萄牙人很早就到了这里：迪奥戈·戈梅斯1456年溯河而上，最远抵达坎托拉；1506年，杜阿尔特·帕切科·佩雷拉记载苏图科是一座约有四千居民的设防城镇，市集盛大，人们用布匹、铜镯和珠子换取黄金，太平年份每年输往葡萄牙的黄金值五六千达布隆。1520年代，曼萨贾拉利·瓦利在北岸建立独立的伍利王国，击退了来自富塔托罗的入侵，而坎托拉一度成为南方卡布帝国的一个省。1621年理查德·乔布森到访时，苏图科已归伍利国王管辖，那里既是贸易重镇，也是马拉布特聚居、讲授古兰经的学术中心，下游河港法塔滕达为其吞吐货物。蒙戈·帕克1795年和1805年两度探查尼日尔河，途中都经过此地，当时这座古老市集仍在伍利诸曼萨治下保持繁荣。

en:
Siine is the Serer country on the north bank of the Saloum delta, a coast of creeks, palm groves and farming villages along Senegal's Petite Côte. Its people had drifted south over generations from the Senegal valley from the eleventh century, keeping the old rites as Islam spread around them, and the villages were governed by priest-chiefs called lamans. In the fourteenth century a Mandinka maternal clan, the Guelowar, fled defeat in Kaabu and won asylum from the laman council; their leader Maysa Wali, chosen king by the lamans, became the first Maad a Sinig about 1350 and ruled from Mbissel. In 1444 Siine was one of the Serer vassal kingdoms of the Jolof confederacy, its court still keeping the old Serer religion.

Portuguese ships reached the coast in the 1450s, and the Venetian navigator Alvise Cadamosto recorded the kingdom as Barbaçim, the name Europeans used for it thereafter. About 1495 Mbegane Ndour came to the throne; he killed Moussa Eli Bana Sall, a Takruri marabout who had made himself master of Saloum, by poison, and a marriage to a princess-priestess of Baol sealed his conquest of that kingdom. In 1520 Siine and Saloum were the first states to throw off Jolof's overlordship, almost thirty years before the Battle of Danki. When Nasr ad-Din's marabout wave swept Senegambia in the 1670s, the Buur of Saloum sent the army that helped Cayor's lingeer overthrow cleric rule, while Siine itself kept its throne and its old rites; through the eighteenth century, as Muslim reformers founded new states to the north, the Guelowar kings still ruled at Mbissel.
zh:
塞尼是谢列尔人的土地，位于萨卢姆三角洲北岸，沿小海岸分布着溪汊、棕榈林与农耕村落。自11世纪起，谢列尔人一代代从塞内加尔河谷南迁，在周围纷纷皈依伊斯兰之际仍守旧仪，各村由身兼祭司的首领——拉曼——治理。14世纪，曼丁卡人的母系氏族盖卢瓦尔在加布的内争中失败来投，获拉曼会议收容；其首领迈萨·瓦利被拉曼们推举为王，约在1350年成为第一代马阿·西尼格，以姆比塞尔为都。1444年，塞尼是卓洛夫联盟治下的谢列尔属国之一，王廷仍守谢列尔旧教。

1450年代，葡萄牙船只抵达海岸，为葡萄牙效力的威尼斯航海家卡达莫斯托把这个王国记为巴尔巴辛，此后欧洲人便以此称呼它。约1495年，姆贝甘·恩杜尔即位；他用毒药除掉了已在萨卢姆自立的塔克鲁尔族马拉布特穆萨·埃利·巴纳·萨尔，又以与巴奥勒的公主兼女祭司联姻，巩固了对萨卢姆的征服。1520年，塞尼与萨卢姆率先摆脱卓洛夫的宗主权，比丹基之战早了近三十年。1670年代纳西尔丁的马拉布特浪潮席卷塞内冈比亚时，萨卢姆的布尔出兵帮助卡约尔王太后推翻教士政权，塞尼本土则保住了王座与旧仪；整个18世纪，当穆斯林改革者在北方建立新国家时，盖卢瓦尔诸王仍在姆比塞尔实行统治。

en:
Galam, also called Gajaaga, was the Soninke kingdom of the upper Senegal, straddling the river and its Falémé tributary at the edge of the Bambuk goldfields. Its Bathily dynasty, the Bacili of Manding tradition, came up from the Inner Niger Delta between the eighth and eleventh centuries, subdued the local Gaja Soninke and cemented their rule in the thirteenth, keeping alive the old snake cult of Wagadu. 'Galam' means gold in Wolof, and the markets of the tunka passed Bambuk gold into caravans bound across the Sahara. In 1444 Galam was a tributary of Mali, still guarding the gateway to the goldfields.

In 1506 Songhai attacks broke Mali's hold on the Sahel, and by the late sixteenth century Galam paid only nominal tribute to the Denianke of Futa Toro; by the middle of the seventeenth it was perhaps the strongest power on the upper river. In 1690 the tunka granted the Torodbe cleric Malick Sy a holding that became Bundu, a neighbour that would soon gnaw at the kingdom's southern flank. The French built Fort Saint-Joseph in 1700, and for decades Galam supplied most of the slaves shipped out of Saint-Louis, while raids by the Trarza Moors and Kaarta opened a century of succession wars. The joint invasion of Kaarta and Khasso in 1750 was beaten off but laid the kingdom's weakness bare. In 1820 the French returned to the upper river and rebuilt their post at Bakel.
zh:
加兰又名加贾加，是塞内加尔河上游的索宁克王国，地跨大河与其支流法莱梅河，扼守邦布克产金地的边缘。统治这里的巴蒂利王朝——曼德传统中称作巴西利——在8至11世纪间从内尼日尔三角洲北上，征服当地的加贾索宁克人，13世纪真正巩固权力，并保留了瓦加杜古老的蛇神崇拜。「加兰」在沃洛夫语中意为黄金，通卡治下的市集把邦布克黄金装进横跨撒哈拉的商队。1444年的加兰是马里的属国，仍守着产金地的门户。

1506年，桑海的进攻打碎了马里对萨赫勒的控制，到16世纪末，加兰只在名义上向富塔托罗的登尼扬克人纳贡；17世纪中叶，它或许已是河上游最强的政权。1690年，通卡把一块封地赐给托罗德贝神职人员马利克·西，那里后来发展成邦杜——一个很快从南翼蚕食旧主的邻邦。法国人于1700年建成圣约瑟夫堡，此后数十年间，从圣路易运出的奴隶大多由加兰供应，特拉尔扎摩尔人与卡尔塔的袭掠则开启了长达一个世纪的继承战争。1750年卡尔塔与哈索联手入侵，虽被击退，却暴露了王国的虚弱。1820年，法国人重返河上游，在巴凯尔重建据点。

en:
The estuaries between the Geba and Rio Grande de Buba were Biafada country. Its fishing villages and mangrove channels belonged to three kingdoms, Biguba, Guinala and Bissege; Biguba and Guinala were subject to the Mandinka mansa of Kaabu, heir to Mali's old power in Senegambia. Guinala had a port town, an inland seat at Bruco, and a large weekly market at Bijorei. In 1444 canoes carried salt and dried fish from the coast, pepper and kola nuts from the forest, iron, and Mandinka cotton cloth; European ships were only beginning to know the shore.

Alvise Cadamosto reached the coast in 1455 and Diogo Gomes in 1456; Portugal claimed the region from the 1450s, but Biafada rulers kept the river villages. About the middle of the century Guinala defeated a Fula armed migration led by Dulo Demmba. In the sixteenth century Guinala became the leading Euro-African port here, exporting on average 3,000 enslaved people a year to the Americas. In the 1580s lançados built the fort of Porto da Cruz nearby; after Bijagos raiders struck it in 1610, they withdrew upstream to Bolola, near later Buba. The captive trade continued through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, fed by wars involving Kaabu and Futa Jallon, while Portuguese authority scarcely reached beyond scattered coastal posts.
zh:
热巴河与布巴河之间的河口湾和红树林水道，是比亚法达人的土地。沿岸渔村分属比古巴、吉纳拉和比塞盖三个王国，其中比古巴和吉纳拉臣属加布的曼丁卡曼萨，而加布继承了马里在塞内冈比亚的旧有势力。吉纳拉有港口商镇、设在内陆布鲁科的统治中心，还有比若雷的大型周市。1444年，独木舟载着沿海的盐和鱼干、森林出产的胡椒与柯拉果、铁器以及曼丁卡棉布往来；欧洲船只这时才刚开始认识这段海岸。

1455年，阿尔维塞·卡达莫斯托抵达这段海岸，迪奥戈·戈麦斯也在1456年到来。葡萄牙从15世纪50年代宣称占有此地，但比亚法达统治者仍掌握着河畔村落。约在15世纪中叶，吉纳拉击败了杜洛·登巴率领的富拉人武装迁徙队伍。16世纪，吉纳拉成为这里最重要的欧非贸易港，平均每年向美洲输出3000名奴隶。16世纪80年代，兰萨多斯商人在附近修建十字港要塞；1610年比热戈斯袭击者攻打该港后，他们退往上游、靠近后来布巴的博洛拉。17—18世纪，俘虏贸易仍在继续，加布与富塔贾隆之间的战争提供了许多俘虏，而葡萄牙人的权威几乎没有越过零散的海岸商站。

en:
The mangrove corridor between Sherbro and Cape Mesurado is broken by the granite headland of Cape Mount and the tidal lagoon behind it, later called Lake Piso. Creeks and rivers including the Mafa, Mano and Gallinas drain the Gola forests toward the sea. In 1444 Gola and other forest communities lived by fishing, farming and creek trade, exchanging salt and kola nuts with Mande-speaking travellers from the interior. Dense mangrove swamps gave the coast few large markets, and no European chart had yet fixed its names.

Pedro de Sintra charted the headland in 1461 and named it Cabo do Monte; Portuguese pilots later knew the mangrove channels as Rio das Galinhas. About 1545 Mane-Sumba invaders following the Mano and Moa rivers reached Cape Mount, breaking the older coastal order and spreading Mande military organization. Camara-clan Mandinka moving toward the sea intermarried with Gola communities and helped form the Vai, whom Dutch records first placed near Cape Mount in the first half of the seventeenth century. The Dutch built a trading post at Cape Mount in 1602 but destroyed it the next year. During the 1620s new Mande coalitions called Quoja and Karou imposed their power along the shore; Karou war bands campaigned around Cape Mount and the Mafa, Mano and Gallinas rivers, and their pressure continued into the next century. Cape Mount became a slaving anchorage, while the remoter Gallinas creeks drew heavy traffic only in the late eighteenth century. After Britain enforced its slave-trade ban in 1808, those hidden channels sheltered illegal slavers; by 1821 no European power controlled the shore.
zh:
谢尔布罗与梅苏拉多角之间的红树林走廊，被大角山的花岗岩岬角和岬后潮汐潟湖截断；这处潟湖后来称皮索湖。马法河、马诺河和加利纳斯河等水道穿过戈拉人活动的林区入海。1444年，戈拉人和其他森林社群以渔捞、农耕和河汊贸易为生，同来自内陆的曼德语旅人交换盐与柯拉果。稠密的红树林沼泽使海岸难以形成大型市场，欧洲海图也还没有固定这里的名称。

1461年，佩德罗·德·辛特拉测绘这座岬角，将其命名为山角（Cabo do Monte）；葡萄牙领航员后来把红树林水道称为母鸡河（Rio das Galinhas）。约1545年，马内-松巴入侵者沿马诺河和莫阿河抵达大角山，打破旧有海岸秩序，也传播了曼德式军事组织。向海岸迁徙的卡马拉氏族曼丁卡人与戈拉社群通婚，促成瓦伊人群体；17世纪上半叶的荷兰文献首次把瓦伊人记在大角山附近。荷兰人1602年在大角山设立贸易站，次年便将其摧毁。17世纪20年代，夸贾和卡鲁等新的曼德联盟在沿海建立霸权，卡鲁战团在大角山及马法河、马诺河、加利纳斯河一带征战，其压力延续到下一世纪。大角山成为贩奴船锚地，而更偏僻的加利纳斯河汊直到18世纪末才迎来大量贸易。英国1808年实施奴隶贸易禁令后，这些隐蔽水道为非法贩奴船提供藏身之处；到1821年，仍没有欧洲政权控制这段海岸。

en: The arid pastures of Termes centred on the wells of Awdaghust, whose ruins at Tegdaoust mark one of the early southern terminals of trans-Saharan caravans. Sanhaja Berbers held the oasis in the ninth century, exchanging salt for gold with the lands farther south; after it passed to Ghana, Abd Allah ibn Yasin's Almoravids stormed it in 1054-55. Al-Bakri described its markets, palms and henna trees, but the town never recovered, and early in the thirteenth century Walata, 360 kilometres to the east, took its caravan trade. In 1444 Muslim Soninke herders around the old wells lived on a remote edge of weakening Mali, which lost Baghena and Wagadu to the Mossi around 1470.
zh: 泰尔姆的干旱牧地以奥达古斯特的水井为中心，泰格达乌斯特的废墟，正是撒哈拉商道早期南端商站之一。9世纪时，桑哈贾柏柏尔人占据这片绿洲，用盐与南方各地交换黄金；它后来并入加纳，1054至1055年被阿卜杜拉·伊本·雅辛率领的穆拉比特军队攻破。白克里曾记载这里市集繁盛，遍布椰枣和散沫花，但城市再未恢复，13世纪初，以东360公里的瓦拉塔夺走了它的商队贸易。1444年，旧井周边的穆斯林索宁克牧人处在衰落中的马里遥远边陲；约1470年，巴格纳和瓦加杜又被莫西人夺取。

en:
The Tagant is a long sandstone plateau rising from the desert of central Mauritania, its southern cliffs looking over the dry Aoukar basin; its Berber name means 'forest', for the highland catches enough rain for acacia scrub, pasture and date-palm oases. Stone villages of the ancient Tichitt culture, among West Africa's oldest settlements, stand abandoned along the cliffs since the climate dried around 500 BC. The medieval caravan trade brought the plateau back to life: Tichit was founded in the twelfth century as a stage between Oualata and Chinguetti on the road to Sijilmasa, and Soninke of the Azer tongue and the Afro-Berber Imasna lived by its caravans and dates. In 1444 the Tagant had no prince; Sanhaja Berber clans and Fula pastoralists moved between wells and oases on the old southern fringe of the Ghana and Mali worlds.

From the mid-seventeenth century groups moving down from the Adrar plateau pushed the Toucouleur inhabitants south towards Futa Toro. Out of the upheaval of the Char Bouba war the Idaw Aish, the Idawish clan, built the Emirate of the Tagant, with Tidjikdja as its capital, and the walled ksour of Tichit, Rachid and Tidjikdja throve on dates, caravan dues and learning. The new power soon clashed with its neighbours: a Brakna army besieged the Idawish for three months at Dhahr Tagant before accepting forty horses and withdrawing. The emirate stood at its height through the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, but feuds within its ruling houses never ceased; from the second half of the 1700s succession disputes split and weakened it, the same decline that wore down every Moorish emirate of the age.
zh:
塔甘特是毛里塔尼亚中部沙漠中隆起的长条砂岩高原，南缘悬崖俯临干涸的奥卡尔盆地；其柏柏尔语名意为「森林」，因为高地所得雨水足以养育金合欢灌丛、牧场和椰枣绿洲。崖壁上留存着古老提希特文化的石砌村落，属西非最古老的定居点之一，约公元前500年因气候变干而废弃。中世纪的商队贸易让高原复苏：提希特建于12世纪，是瓦拉塔通往欣盖提、再到西吉勒马萨商路上的一站，讲阿泽尔方言的索宁克人与阿非罗-柏柏尔的伊马斯纳人靠商队和椰枣为生。1444年的塔甘特没有君主，桑哈贾柏柏尔部族和富拉尼牧人在古井与绿洲间转徙，处在古加纳与马里世界的南缘。

17世纪中叶起，从阿德拉尔高原南下的部族把原住的图库洛尔人逐往南方的富塔托罗。历经沙尔·布巴战争的动荡，伊达乌·阿伊什（即伊达维什）部族建立塔甘特埃米尔国，以提吉克贾为都，提希特、拉希德、提吉克贾等设防枣城靠椰枣、商税和学术而兴盛。这个新政权很快与邻邦交兵：卜拉克纳军队曾在塔甘特崖下围困伊达维什人三个月，最后收下四十匹马撤走。埃米尔国在整个18世纪和19世纪初保持鼎盛，但统治家族内讧不歇，自18世纪下半叶起继承之争使它日渐分裂衰弱，与当时所有摩尔人埃米尔国走上同一条下坡路。

en:
Wagadu was the Soninke name of old Ghana, but this province's market centre lay farther south, at Dia on the Diaka channel at the western edge of the Inner Niger Delta. Its settlement mounds preserve a town older than nearby Djenné, linking floodplain fisheries, rice fields and northern caravan routes. After Ghana's collapse in the thirteenth century, Sosso and then Mali dominated the region. Ibn Battuta, travelling through Mali's domains in the fourteenth century, heard of Zagha, identified with Dia, as a town whose people were 'old in Islam' but whose chief still obeyed the mansa. By 1444 Dia was effectively a self-governing clerical town called Balad Allah, 'the town of God'; the mansa's agents did not enter it, while Bozo fishing rites and Marka cults persisted beneath its Muslim identity.

In 1494 or 1495 Askia Muhammad's Songhai forces took Zaagha, drawing the old scholarly town into Songhai's westward expansion. Long after Songhai power passed, Dia remained under a local non-Muslim warrior house, the Diawara or Traore, even though its marabouts continued to call it Balad Allah. In 1818 Seku Amadu founded the Dina, the Fulani Islamic state of Macina; after Dia submitted, the new government displaced the Marka ruling family and entrusted authority to the maraboutic Koreissi, completing the town's Islamization.
zh:
瓦加杜是索宁克人对古加纳的称呼，但这一省的市集中心更靠南方，是坐落在尼日尔河内陆三角洲西缘、迪亚卡河水道上的迪亚。这里的居址土丘保存着一座比邻近杰内更古老的城镇，把洪泛区渔场、稻田和通往北方的商路连接起来。13世纪加纳崩溃后，索索继而马里先后控制此地。14世纪伊本·白图泰行经马里疆土时，听说被比定为迪亚的扎加居民「早已奉教」，但其首领仍听命于曼萨。到1444年，迪亚实际上已是自行其是的伊斯兰教学者城镇，被称为「真主之城」巴拉德安拉；曼萨的官吏不敢入城，而在穆斯林身份之下，博佐人的渔猎仪式和马尔卡人的旧祭仪仍未消失。

1494或1495年，阿斯基亚·穆罕默德的桑海军队夺取扎加，把这座古老学术城镇纳入桑海向西扩张的范围。桑海势力消退很久以后，迪亚仍由本地非穆斯林武士家族迪亚瓦拉（又称特拉奥雷）统治，城中的伊斯兰教学者则继续称此地为「真主之城」。1818年，塞库·阿马杜建立富尔贝人的伊斯兰国家马西纳迪纳；迪亚臣服后，新政权废黜马尔卡统治家族，把权力交给宗教学者家族科雷西，完成了这座城的伊斯兰化。

en:
The arid pastures of Baghena surround Koumbi, the old Ghana capital whose ruins are Koumbi Saleh. Al-Bakri described twin towns six miles apart, a stone Muslim city of merchants and a nearby royal residence, handling the salt and gold of the trans-Saharan road; in the eleventh century the capital held perhaps 30,000 people. Almoravid forces took it in 1076, and around 1240 Sundiata Keita's Mali army seized and destroyed it. By 1444 the Friday mosque and stone houses were ruins around wells used by Muslim Soninke herders and Tuareg camel nomads; after the Tuareg took Timbuktu in 1430 and Walata in 1433, Koumbi survived as a pasture frontier rather than a caravan city.

Around 1470 Mali lost Baghena and Wagadu to Mossi pressure. Under the Askia dynasty the country became a military province under a governor titled the Baghena-fari. On 12 March 1591 Judar Pasha's Saadian army destroyed Songhai power at Tondibi, and in 1591-92 the Baghena-fari Bokar ben Askia Muhammad Benkan rose against the new Moroccan order. His revolt failed, and Baghena passed into the loose frontier of the Timbuktu pashalik, its value lying in flocks rather than in the old royal markets.
zh:
巴吉诺（Baghena）的干旱牧地环绕着库姆比，古都废墟即昆比萨利赫。白克里曾记载两座相距十公里的城镇：一座是商人居住的石造穆斯林城，另一座是附近的王宫，掌控撒哈拉商道上的盐与黄金；11世纪时，这座都城约有三万居民。穆拉比特军队于1076年攻占该城，约1240年，松迪亚塔·凯塔的马里军队又将其夺取并摧毁。到1444年，聚礼清真寺和石屋已成废墟，水井周边是穆斯林索宁克牧人和图阿雷格骆驼游牧民的天地；图阿雷格人1430年夺取廷巴克图、1433年夺取瓦拉塔后，库姆比只剩牧地边疆的意义，不再是商队城市。

约1470年，马里在莫西人的压力下失去巴格纳和瓦加杜。阿斯基亚王朝时，这里成为一个军事行省，由称「巴格纳法里」的总督管辖。1591年3月12日，朱达尔帕夏的萨阿德军队在通迪比击溃桑海；1591至1592年，巴格纳法里博卡尔·本·阿斯基亚·穆罕默德·本坎起兵反抗新的摩洛哥秩序，终归失败。巴格纳随后落入廷巴克图帕夏辖区的松散边疆，其价值在于畜群，而不是旧日的王城市集。

en:
Hodh, the Arabs' El Hodh or 'the Basin', is the dry Aoukar depression ringed by the Tichitt-Walata and Tagant cliffs. Its oasis of Biru, later called Walata, belonged to Ghana and then rose early in the thirteenth century as Aoudaghost's replacement at the southern end of the trans-Saharan road; caravans from Sijilmasa reached it after the salt mines of Taghaza, making it both a market and a religious centre. It passed to Mali in the fourteenth century. Ibn Battuta stayed there for about fifty days and found Muslim Massufa Sanhaja, date palms and watermelons over groundwater, plentiful mutton, and women held in unusual respect. As Timbuktu overtook the oasis, Tuareg forces took Timbuktu in 1430 and Walata in 1433, so in 1444 the town was a smaller Muslim Tuareg-held station living from wells, flocks and dates.

War returned at the end of the century. In 1477 Nasséré, king of Yatenga, crossed the Niger and ravaged Bagana and Malian borderlands; his troops took Walata in 1480 after a month's siege and sacked it, though the inhabitants rallied, pursued the raiders and rescued many of the people carried off. When Leo Africanus visited in 1509-10, Walata was a small Songhai tributary kingdom of three large villages set among palm groves, its prince answerable to the ruler of Timbuktu. Early in the seventeenth century Hassaniya Arabs moved into the town, while the Lemhajib, three Soninke families assimilated into the Berber and Arab milieu, dominated its politics for a century and a half.
zh:
霍德在阿拉伯语中称「霍德」，意为盆地，即干旱的奥卡尔洼地，周围环绕着提希特—瓦拉塔崖壁和塔甘特崖壁。洼地里的绿洲比鲁后来改称瓦拉塔，曾臣属于加纳，13世纪初取代奥达古斯特，成为撒哈拉商道的南端终点；来自锡吉勒马萨的商队经过塔加扎盐矿后来到这里，使它兼具市集与宗教中心的地位。14世纪，瓦拉塔并入马里。伊本·白图泰曾在此停留约五十天，见到的居民多为信奉伊斯兰教的马苏法桑哈贾人；椰枣树荫下种着西瓜，地下水养育城镇，羊肉充足，女性也享有少见的尊重。随着廷巴克图后来居上，图阿雷格军队1430年夺取廷巴克图、1433年夺取瓦拉塔，因此1444年时，这里已是图阿雷格人控制的较小穆斯林驿站，靠水井、畜群和椰枣维持。

15世纪末，战火再次降临。1477年，亚滕加国王纳塞雷渡过尼日尔河，蹂躏巴加纳和马里边地；他的军队在围攻一个月后于1480年攻占并洗劫瓦拉塔，但居民重新集结，追击劫掠者，救回许多被掳走的人。利奥·阿非利加努斯1509至1510年到访时，瓦拉塔已是桑海的小附庸国，棕榈林间只有三座大村，其君主听命于廷巴克图统治者。17世纪初，讲哈桑语的阿拉伯人迁入；莱姆哈吉布则是三个索宁克家族，融入柏柏尔和阿拉伯社会环境后，主导当地政治达一个半世纪。

en:
The grassy uplands between the Sankarani and the upper Niger were the land called Dô, one of the oldest Mande countries. Arab geographers knew it early: al-Bakri heard of the land of Daw and its neighbour Malal near the goldfields, and al-Idrisi in 1154 set the two four days' journey apart in a valley of the Niger. Oral tradition remembers Dô as a kafu of twelve towns ruled by the Condé clan, and it was absorbed, with the other chiefdoms of the Manding, into the Mali empire proclaimed after Sundiata Keita's victory. The highland pastures were cattle country, and tracks linked the villages with Niani to the east and the goldfields of Bouré and Bambuk. In 1444 Dô was a Mandinka province of the mansa.

Songhai pressure reached the Manding in the next century: in 1545 a force under the kanfari Dawud sacked Niani, though it did not hold it. After Mansa Mahmud IV's defeat at Jenne in 1599 and his death about 1610, Keita power broke into chiefdoms, and when the last mansa, Mama Maghan, failed in his siege of Ségou in 1670 he withdrew to Kangaba in Dô's own river country, reduced to a local chief. In 1751 Biton Coulibaly's Bamana army took Niani and made its mansa a vassal, and the old pasturelands became a march of the Bamana powers. From the later eighteenth century the Fulbe armies of the new almamyate of Futa Jallon pressed north into the Manding, so that in 1821 Dô was a raided borderland between Ségou and the Fulbe highlands.
zh:
桑卡拉尼河与尼日尔河上游之间的草丘高地，是称作多（Dô，又称道、多杜古）的土地，曼德最古老的地方之一。阿拉伯地理学家很早就知道它：贝克里听闻过产金之地附近的「道」与邻邦马拉尔；1154年，伊德里西记载两城相距四日路程，同在尼日尔河谷中。口述传统里，多是孔戴氏族治下、统有十二座城镇的卡富，后来与曼丁其他酋邦一道，并入松迪亚塔·凯塔胜利后建立的马里帝国。高地草场是牧牛之地，小路把村落与东边的尼亚尼、布雷和班布克金矿区相连。1444年，多是曼萨治下的一个曼丁卡省份。

下个世纪，桑海的压力抵达曼丁：1545年，坎法里达乌德的军队洗劫尼亚尼，但并未久占。1599年曼萨·马哈茂德四世兵败杰内、约1610年去世后，凯塔政权瓦解为诸酋长国；末代曼萨马马·汉围攻塞古失败，于1670年退回多本地河畔的康加巴，沦为地方酋长。1751年，比通·库利巴利的班巴拉大军攻占尼亚尼，将那里的曼萨降为附庸，旧日牧场沦为班巴拉诸强的边地。18世纪后期起，新兴的富塔贾隆阿尔马米国派富拉尼军队向北进逼曼丁，到1821年，多已成塞古与富拉尼高原之间屡遭攻掠的边境。

en:
Sibiridugu is the river country at the rapids where the upper Niger drops out of the Manding hills into the middle valley, the district of Barouéli and Niamina with Bamako at its crossing. Long before the town was famous, Bozo and Somono fishermen worked the fords and fishing pools while Mandinka farmers tilled the banks, and caravans carried gold, ivory, kola nuts and salt between the southern Manden and the Sahel. The land passed from the dominion of Ghana into the Mali empire, whose mansa still ruled it in 1444.

In the sixteenth century the Niaré, a family of Soninke origin, established the kafu of Bamako at the rapids: tradition names the hunter Simballa Niaré as the man who chose the site and his son Diamoussa as its founder, who gave the city its first quarter, Niaréla. Muslim Touré and Drave families, clerics and merchants, shared the early town, whose name means 'crocodile river' in Bambara. Bamako grew as a client of the rising Bambara state at Ségou, and between 1712 and 1755 Biton Coulibaly conquered the Sibiridugu, the Niaré chiefs keeping their town as vassals. When Mungo Park passed through on his second Niger journey in 1805-06 the kafu held about 6,000 people, a busy riverside market between Ségou and the Manding. In 1821 Bamako remained a Bamana town within the Ségou empire, even as Seku Amadu's Fulbe caliphate triumphed in the delta downstream.
zh:
锡比里杜古是上尼日尔河闯过曼丁丘陵、跌向中游的急流地带，即巴鲁埃利、尼亚米纳一带，河津要地巴马卡正位于此。早在城镇闻名之前，博佐和索莫诺渔民便在渡口与鱼湖中劳作，曼丁卡农人耕耘两岸，商队驮着黄金、象牙、柯拉果和食盐往返于南曼丁与萨赫勒之间。这片土地先归加纳统辖，后入马里帝国，1444年仍在曼萨治下。

16世纪，索宁克出身的尼亚雷家族在急流边建立巴马卡卡富：传统说猎人辛巴拉·尼亚雷选定城址，其子迪亚穆萨主持建城，城里最早的街区尼亚雷拉便得名于他们。早期城中还有以教士和商人为主的图雷、德拉韦家族；在班巴拉语中，巴马卡意为「鳄鱼河」。它后来成为兴起中的塞古班巴拉国家的附庸；1712至1755年间，比通·库利巴利在缔造帝国的征战中征服锡比里杜古，尼亚雷酋长作为藩属保有城镇。1805至1806年蒙戈·帕克第二次探查尼日尔河途经此地时，这个卡富有约六千居民，是塞古与曼丁之间一处繁忙的河滨市集。1821年，巴马卡仍是塞古帝国境内的班巴拉城镇，而塞库·阿马杜的富拉尼哈里发国此时已在下游三角洲得势。

en:
South of the Bani and west of Djenné lies the Bendugu, the 'country of grass' in Bamana, an old province first of the Mali and later of the Songhai empire. Its Bozo fishing camps grew into the market of San, where a ford over the Bani linked the Inner Niger Delta with the goldfields to the south. Around 1400 a trade town dependent on the kingdom of Daa arose there, founded, as oral traditions variously say, by Marka from Dia or Dyula from Djenné. Twelve local kings, mostly of the Traore lineages, ruled its villages under a centrally appointed governor called the yaw. In 1444 the Bendugu was a farming province of the mansa, its markets fed by the river trade.

In 1542 Askia Ishaq I defeated a Malian army in the Bendugu, but the province stayed in Malian hands; Askia Daoud raided it again in the 1570s, campaigning to restore Songhai control of the periphery. After Tondibi the Bendugu slipped from all imperial rule and the twelve kings went their own way. In the eighteenth century it lay on the loose fringe of the Ségou empire, whose Biton Coulibaly had carried his arms into the San country, and petty chiefdoms proliferated. In 1739 Famaghan Ouattara of Kong intervened in a Bamana civil war and destroyed San, which was rebuilt a little to the north. Horse-breeding, mud-cloth weaving and the Bani rice trade sustained the new town, and each dry season the collective Sanké mon fishing rite drew crowds to the sacred pool. In 1818 Seku Amadu's jihad triumphed at Noukouma beyond the Bani, and by 1821 the new caliphate of Hamdullahi overshadowed the fords of the Bendugu, whose petty kings faced a Fulbe power rising at the edge of the delta.
zh:
巴尼河以南、杰内以西，是班巴拉语意为「青草之乡」的本杜古，先后为马里帝国和桑海帝国的旧省。博佐人的渔村中长出了桑镇：巴尼河上的一处渡口把内尼日尔三角洲与南方金矿区连起来，约1400年，一座臣属于达阿王国的商业城镇在此兴起；口述传说或说是迪亚来的马尔卡人、或说是杰内来的朱拉人所建。本地的十二位小王多属特拉奥雷氏族，在名为亚夫的中央任命官吏治下管辖各村。1444年，本杜古是曼萨治下的农牧省份，河上贸易养活着这里的市集。

1542年，阿斯基亚·伊沙克一世在本杜古击败一支马里军队，但此地仍归马里；1570年代阿斯基亚·达乌德又来攻掠，意在恢复桑海对边陲的控制。通迪比之战后，本杜古脱离一切帝国统辖，十二位小王各自为政。18世纪，这里处在塞古帝国松散的边缘——比通·库利巴利的兵锋已抵达桑镇一带——小酋邦林立。1739年，孔国的法马甘·瓦塔拉乘班巴拉内战攻入，摧毁桑镇，城镇后来在稍北处重建。养马、织造泥染布和巴尼河稻米贸易支撑着新桑镇，每年旱季，桑凯蒙集体渔祭都吸引人群聚集圣塘。1818年，塞库·阿马杜的圣战在巴尼河彼岸的努库马获胜；到1821年，新兴的哈姆杜拉希哈里发国已投下阴影，本杜古诸小王面对的是三角洲边缘崛起的富拉尼强权。

en:
Lobi is the country beyond the southern Black Volta, a spread of earthen compounds, farmland and hunting grounds rather than a single royal capital. In 1444 its villages were organized around elders, earth priests and war leaders, with Gan, Lohron, Kulango and other Gur-speaking communities already holding much of the country; the related peoples later grouped as Lobi still lived mainly east of the river. At Loropéni, stone enclosures held gold workings and trade routes then at their height between the fourteenth and seventeenth centuries. Elsewhere, banco compounds were built like small fortresses, with a single low entrance and shrines where villagers offered to the spirits called thila.

Around 1770, Lobi groups began crossing the Black Volta in waves from the east, settling among the Gan, Koulango and older Teese inhabitants. They kept their decentralized order and initiation rites, which made them difficult subjects for neighboring cavalry states. In 1815 Bakary Ouattara, brother of the founder of Gwiriko, raided the country and burned several villages before Lobi archers killed him with a poisoned arrow. The raid did not destroy the village confederacies, and into the early nineteenth century Lobi warriors remained known for their bows, earthworks and defense of their shrines.
zh:
洛比是黑沃尔特河上游以南的一片地方，没有单一王都，只有分散的土坯院落、农田和猎场。1444年，各村落由长老、土地祭司和战事首领维系，甘人、洛龙人、库兰戈人等古尔语族群已占据此地许多村社；后来被统称为洛比人的相关族群，当时主要还住在河以东。在洛罗佩尼，石墙围合的要塞控制着金矿开采和商路，14至17世纪正是其繁荣时期。其他地方的土坯院落也筑得像小要塞，设唯一的低矮入口，村人在神龛前向称作提拉的神灵献祭。

约1770年，洛比诸群体从东方分批渡黑沃尔特河，迁入甘人、库兰戈人和更古老的泰塞人已经居住的土地。他们保留分散的秩序和成丁仪式，因此邻接的骑兵强国难以将其变成顺民。1815年，格维里科建立者的兄弟巴卡里·瓦塔拉来袭，焚毁数座村庄，最后被洛比弓箭手用毒箭射死。这次袭击没有摧毁各村社同盟；进入19世纪初，洛比战士仍以弓箭、土工和守护神龛而闻名。

en:
Gwiriko was the later Dyula name for the remote lands around the Banifin valley and upper Mouhoun bend, meaning 'at the end of the long stage'. Its heart was Say, the Sia of local tradition and later the old core of Bobo-Dioulasso. Local French-language tradition traces it to Kibidoué, a Bobo farming village founded around 1050 and enlarged by Mande Dyula traders. By the fifteenth century Sia linked the Inner Niger Delta and Djenné with Kong, Begho and the Gold Coast, especially in horses carried south, while Bobo-Oulé farms supplied the market with grain. In 1444 it was therefore a Bobo-Dyula trading town where Muslim merchants lived among farming clans who kept their own rites, not yet a Wattara capital.

In 1714 Famagan Ouattara founded Gwiriko near Sya, though the Wattara war house secured the town only in 1737–38 during Kong's northern expansion. Sia then became the chief city of a nearly autonomous branch controlling Tiefo, Dafin and Bwamu country and protecting routes from Djenné toward Kong and the southern goldfields. After Seku Ouattara died in 1745, Famagan's heirs combined Dyula merchant houses, Bobo-Oulé grain supplies and cavalry power. Subject villages repeatedly revolted later in the eighteenth century, and the Wattara rulers answered with harsh campaigns. By the opening of the nineteenth century Gwiriko remained a Sya-centered network of markets, war leaders and tributary villages rather than a tightly centralized kingdom.
zh:
圭里科是后来朱拉语对巴尼凡河谷与穆洪河上游河湾一带边远土地的称呼，意为「长途驿站的尽头」。它的核心是萨（Sya），也就是后来博博迪乌拉索的旧城核心。法文地方传说把萨城追溯到约1050年博博农民建立的基比杜埃，其后曼德朱拉商人到来，村落逐渐扩大。到15世纪，萨城已经把内尼日尔河三角洲、杰内同孔、贝戈和黄金海岸连接起来，尤其参与向南输送马匹的贸易；博博—乌莱人的农田则向市场供应谷物。因此，1444年的萨城是博博人与朱拉人共处的商镇，穆斯林商人住在保留本地仪轨的农耕氏族中间，此时还不是瓦塔拉都城。

1714年，法马甘·瓦塔拉在萨城附近建立圭里科，但瓦塔拉军头直到1737—1738年孔向北扩张时才稳固取得萨城。此后，萨城成为一个近乎自治的瓦塔拉支系的首要城市，控制蒂埃福、达凡和布瓦穆等地，护卫从杰内通往孔和南方黄金产区的商路。1745年塞古·瓦塔拉死后，法马甘的继承者把朱拉商人家族、博博—乌莱人的谷物供应和骑兵力量结合起来。18世纪后期，臣属村落不断起事，瓦塔拉统治者以严酷征伐回应。到19世纪初，圭里科仍是一个以萨城为中心，由市场、军头和朝贡村落组成的网络，而不是高度集权的王国。

en:
Bono Manso, on the forest-savanna fringe in what is now central Ghana, was the capital of Bono, remembered as the earliest of the Akan states. Akan farmers and ironworkers had settled the region for centuries, and the town took shape around the year 1000 as a market and ritual centre. Its Dwabirem market drew Wangara and Juula caravans from Djenné and Timbuktu, who brought Saharan salt, cloth and brass to exchange for gold dust, kola nuts and ivory. In 1444 the Bonohene at Bono Manso ruled the leading power of the northern Akan lands, grown wealthy on the goldfields and the caravan trade.

The kings Ameyaw and Obunumankoma enlarged Bono in the later fifteenth century, and by the sixteenth century Bono Manso was a major centre of crafts and long-distance trade. In the seventeenth century drought, succession disputes and the rise of European trading posts on the coast drew commerce away to the southern Akan states, which grew rich on firearms. During the reign of Ameyaw Kwakye I, the Asantehene Opoku Ware I invaded in 1722-1723, and Bono Manso was stormed and destroyed. The Bono royal line re-established itself at Techiman under Asante overlordship, and its rulers paid annual tribute to Kumasi.
zh:
博诺曼索位于今加纳中部的森林与草原交界地带，是博诺王国的都城，博诺被认为是阿肯诸邦中最早的一个。阿肯农民和铁匠在此定居已有数百年，城镇约在1000年前后成形，成为市集与祭祀中心。城里的德瓦比伦市场吸引来自杰内和廷巴克图的万加拉与朱乌拉商队，他们运来撒哈拉的盐、布匹和黄铜，换取金砂、柯拉果和象牙。1444年，坐镇博诺曼索的博诺赫内是北阿肯诸地最强大的统治者，王国因金矿和商队贸易而富庶。

15世纪后期，阿梅尧和奥布努曼科马两位国王扩张了博诺的疆土；到16世纪，博诺曼索已成为手工业和长途贸易的重要中心。17世纪时，干旱、王位纷争以及欧洲人在沿海设立商站，使商业转向靠火器致富的南方阿肯诸邦。在阿梅尧·夸基一世在位期间，阿散蒂赫内奥坡库·瓦雷一世于1722至1723年大举入侵，博诺曼索被攻陷并摧毁。博诺王族后来在阿散蒂宗主权下于泰奇曼重建王统，年年向库马西纳贡。

en:
West of Bono Manso the Akan forest opens into grassland cut by the Black Volta, the corridor followed by the northern caravans. Its great market was Begho, also called Nsoko, a town founded in the eleventh century where Soninke Wangara merchants from Mali traded Saharan salt, cloth and brassware for Akan gold and kola; its quarters held Brong farmers and Mande Muslim families side by side, and three roads ran south from the town to the coast, among them the road through Dormaa to Elmina. In 1444 this was Akan country on the western fringe of the Bono state, living on the trade that passed through Begho.

In the seventeenth century Aduana Akan from Dormaa moved into the Black Volta basin, brought the Kulango, Nafana and Ligbi peoples under their rule, and made Amanvi the seat of the kingdom of Gyaman, with the old Dyula town of Bondoukou as its commercial hub. Asante expansion reached Gyaman in 1740-1741, when the Asantehene Opoku Ware I destroyed its capital and reduced it to tribute; Begho was sacked around the same years and its merchants dispersed to Bondoukou and Kong. Around 1800 Kwadwo Adinkra took power, and in 1818 he withheld tribute and rose against the Asantehene Osei Tutu Kwamina. He was killed in the war that followed, and in 1819 Asante turned Gyaman into an occupied province. The stamped and printed cloths of his reign survived him as the Adinkra symbols of the Akan.
zh:
博诺曼索以西，阿肯森林让位于黑沃尔特河穿过的草原地带，这正是北方商队往来的走廊。当地的大市场叫贝戈，又名恩索科，是11世纪兴起的城镇：来自马里的索宁克万加拉商人用撒哈拉的盐、布匹和铜器交换阿肯人的黄金和柯拉果；城里各个街区中，布龙农民与曼德穆斯林家庭比邻而居，三条商路从这里南通海岸，其中一条经多尔马抵达埃尔米纳。1444年，这里是博诺西缘的阿肯人之地，靠途经贝戈的贸易为生。

17世纪，来自多尔马的阿肯阿杜阿纳氏族迁入黑沃尔特河流域，将库兰戈人、纳法纳人和利格比人纳入治下，以阿曼维为都建立贾曼王国，古老的朱乌拉城邦邦杜库则成为其商业中心。1740至1741年，阿散蒂赫内奥坡库·瓦雷一世的扩张打到贾曼，摧毁其都城，迫使贾曼称臣纳贡；贝戈也在同一时期被洗劫，商人四散逃往邦杜库和孔城。1800年前后，夸德沃·阿丁克拉即位，1818年他停止纳贡，起兵反抗阿散蒂赫内奥塞·图图·夸米纳，在随后的战争中被杀；1819年阿散蒂将贾曼改为军管的行省。他在位时使用的戳印和模印花布流传下来，成为阿肯人的阿丁克拉符号。

en:
Dagbon is the kingdom of the Dagomba, in the open grassland of the White Volta basin. The Gbewaa dynasty united the farming villages of the indigenous Tindaamba earth-priests, and Naa Nyagsi, who reigned from 1416 to 1432, overthrew the local chiefs and set his capital at Yani Dabari, near modern Tamale, placing his own sons over the conquered towns. Grain, cattle and iron came from its plains, and Dyula caravans between the Niger bend and Hausaland already passed through its markets. In 1444 the Yaa Naa at Yani Dabari ruled the strongest power of the northern Volta basin, a people who still kept their ancestral earth cults.

In the seventeenth century the rising Gonja kingdom struck from the west and seized Daboya, with its salt trade on the road from Yendi to Bouna. After years of war Yaa Naa Luro moved the court east to Yendi, and Naa Zanjina late in the century defeated the Gonja near the new capital and killed their chief Kumpatia. As the first Muslim Yaa Naa he welcomed Dyula and Hausa scholars and traders; a Muslim community settled by the palace, and around 1700 the Moliyili house of learning made Dagbon a centre of Arabic letters. Kola and salt linked Yendi with Salaga, Kumasi and the Hausa cities, and by 1788 the town was said to be larger than Kumasi. Asante armies reached Yendi in the 1740s, and Dagbon paid tribute to Kumasi for a time.
zh:
达格邦是达贡巴人的王国，地处白沃尔特河流域开阔的草原上。格贝瓦王朝把本地土地祭司廷达姆巴所辖的农耕村落统一起来；1416至1432年在位的纳·尼亚克西推翻各地酋长，定都亚尼·达巴里（在今塔马利附近），并把诸子分封为征服城镇的统治者。平原出产谷物、牲畜和铁器，往返于尼日尔河河曲与豪萨兰之间的朱乌拉商队已经途经这里的市场。1444年，坐镇亚尼·达巴里的亚阿·纳是北沃尔特河流域最强大的君主，他的人民仍信奉祖传的土地崇拜。

17世纪，兴起的贡贾王国从西方攻入，夺取了耶恩迪通往布纳商路上的盐业重镇达博亚。多年战争后，亚阿·纳·卢罗把宫廷东迁至耶恩迪；17世纪末，纳·赞吉纳在新都附近大败贡贾人，斩杀其首领昆帕蒂亚。作为第一位信奉伊斯兰教的亚阿·纳，他礼遇朱乌拉和豪萨的学者与商人，宫门外形成穆斯林社区；约1700年创立的莫利伊利学馆使达格邦成为阿拉伯学术的中心。柯拉果和盐的贸易把耶恩迪与萨拉加、库马西及豪萨诸城连在一起，到1788年，据说耶恩迪比库马西还要大。18世纪40年代阿散蒂军队进抵耶恩迪，达格邦一度向库马西纳贡。

en:
The forest country between the Ofin and the Pra, around Dunkwa-on-Offin, was in 1444 a land of Akan village-clans. The Agona and other Akani families washed gold in the Ofin and Oda valleys and answered to the older state of Adanse, the spiritual heartland of the forest Akan; their gold moved south through Akani broker-towns toward a coast where no European fort yet stood, and north to the marts of Begho and Bono Manso. No paramount king yet ruled the district.

By the mid-seventeenth century the Agona had built the kingdom of Denkyira and made Abankeseso an imperial capital, reducing Adanse, Sefwi, Wassa, Aowin and Assin to tribute and heaping their gold into the Sikadan treasury; in 1692 Dutch, English and Brandenburg envoys travelled inland to Denkyirahene Boamponsem, whose country European factors called the richest in gold on the coast. His successor Ntim Gyakari drove the subject states to rebellion with his tribute demands, and in 1701 Osei Tutu's Asante army destroyed Denkyira at Feyiase, killing Ntim Gyakari and sacking Abankeseso. A revolt in 1706 was crushed, and for the rest of the eighteenth century Denkyira answered to Kumasi, its goldfields and trade routes feeding the Asante empire.
zh:
奥芬河与普拉河之间的林区，即奥芬河畔敦夸所在之地，1444年还只是阿肯人氏族村落的乡土。阿戈纳等阿卡尼家族在奥芬河与奥达河谷淘金，尊奉林中阿肯人的精神故土、更为古老的阿丹斯邦；他们的黄金向南经阿卡尼商人的集镇运往还没有欧洲商堡的海岸，向北则送到贝戈和博诺曼索的市集。此时这里还没有一统各部的大王。

到17世纪中叶，阿戈纳人已建立登基拉王国，把阿班克塞索经营成帝都，阿丹斯、塞夫维、瓦萨、奥温、阿辛等邦相继纳贡，黄金堆满王室的西卡丹宝库；1692年，荷兰、英国和勃兰登堡的使节深入内地觐见登基拉赫内博阿蓬塞姆，欧洲商馆管事称他的国家是海岸上最富金的国度。继任者恩蒂姆·贾卡里索贡无度，各属邦转而投向崛起的库阿曼；1701年，奥塞·图图的阿散蒂军队在费亚斯之战击灭登基拉，恩蒂姆·贾卡里阵亡，阿班克塞索被洗劫。1706年的反叛再遭镇压，此后整个18世纪登基拉都听命于库马西，它的金矿区和商路转而滋养阿散蒂帝国。

en:
The western Gold Coast runs from the Nzima country around Axim east to the headlands of the Fante, a surf-bound shore backed by gold-bearing hills. In 1444 Akan towns held the beaches and lagoons: Nzima fishermen at the mouth of the Ankobra, the old kingdom of Eguafo around the village of Mina, and Fetu further east. Gold washed in the forest rivers came south to be bartered for salt and fish, while Akani brokers carried the dust toward the northern marts, and no European had yet appeared on the coast.

The Portuguese reached it in 1471, and in 1482 Diogo de Azambuja treated with the Eguafo lord Caramansa and raised São Jorge da Mina at Elmina, the first European stronghold in sub-Saharan Africa; Fort Santo António followed at Axim in 1515 and Fort São Sebastião at Shama in 1558. A Dutch assault was beaten off at Elmina in 1625 but succeeded in 1637, and Axim passed to the Dutch in 1642. At Cabo Corso the Swedes built Carolusborg in 1653, which Robert Holmes seized for the Royal African Company in 1664 and rebuilt as Cape Coast Castle, the English headquarters on this stretch of coast. The Brandenburgers raised Groß Friedrichsburg at Pokesu in 1682 and sold it to the Dutch in 1721; the local chief John Konny held the abandoned fort against Dutch arms from 1717 to 1724. As captives overtook gold as the staple trade, Fante brokers mediated between the castles and the interior, until the Ashanti–Fante wars of 1806–1807 broke their power and by 1816 the Fante states were tributary to Kumasi.
zh:
黄金海岸西部，西起阿克西姆一带的恩济马人之地，东到芳蒂人的岬角，拍岸浪后面是盛产黄金的丘陵。1444年，阿肯人的城镇据有海滩和潟湖：安科布拉河口的恩济马渔村、米纳村周围古老的埃瓜福王国，以及更东边的费图。森林河川里淘出的黄金南运，换取食盐和咸鱼，阿卡尼掮客则把金沙转往北方的市集，此时海岸上还没有欧洲人出现。

葡萄牙人1471年抵达，1482年第奥古·德阿赞布雅与埃瓜福首领卡拉曼萨谈判，在埃尔米纳筑起圣若热·达米纳堡，这是撒哈拉以南欧洲人的第一座要塞；1515年阿克西姆建起圣安东尼奥堡，1558年沙马建起圣塞巴斯蒂安堡。荷兰人1625年攻打埃尔米纳被击退，1637年得手，阿克西姆也于1642年易手。在科博科索，瑞典人1653年建成卡尔斯堡，1664年罗伯特·霍姆斯替皇家非洲公司将其夺占，扩建为海岸角城堡，作为英国人在这段海岸的总部。勃兰登堡人1682年在波克苏筑起大腓特烈堡，1721年卖给荷兰；当地酋长约翰·康尼在1717年至1724年间据守这座被遗弃的堡垒，力抗荷兰军队。18世纪奴隶取代黄金成为主要贸易，芳蒂掮客在城堡与内地之间居间取利，直到1806至1807年的阿散蒂—芳蒂战争击垮其势力，到1816年芳蒂各邦都向库马西纳贡。

en:
Sah lies on the right bank of the Bara-Issa, the smaller Niger branch that carries the northern outflow of Lake Débo. Each flood turned the surrounding channels into fishing grounds and left silty fields for millet and rice as the water fell. Somono canoemen, Bozo fishermen, Bambara cultivators and Fulbe herders shared this moving landscape. In 1444 Sah was part of Jenné's river world: its canoes served the trade lane from Jenné to Timbuktu, carrying grain and fish north while salt came south, even though many villagers kept ancestral rites rather than the Islam of the merchant cities.

Sonni Ali built his power on Niger fleets rowed by Sorko fishermen, and after years of siege Jenné submitted in 1473, drawing Sah into the Songhai Empire. That river order lasted until March 1591, when Judar Pasha's Saadi army broke Askia Ishaq II at Tondibi. Moroccan garrisons became the local Arma; after the last reinforcement crossed the desert in 1618, the pashalik fragmented into garrison towns, and in the eighteenth century the delta passed within the orbit of the Bambara state at Ségou. Seku Amadu defeated the Bambara coalition at Noukouma in 1818, took Jenné in 1819 and founded Hamdullahi in 1820. Sah thus entered the Peul Diina of Massina, whose judges and land-masters regulated fishing, floods, fields and cattle tracks.
zh:
萨坐落在巴拉-伊萨河右岸；这条较小的尼日尔河支流向北排出代博湖的湖水。每年洪水使周围水道成为渔场，水退后露出的淤泥地可种粟和稻。索莫诺船夫、博若渔民、班巴拉农夫和富拉尼牧民共用这片随水势变化的土地。1444年，萨属于杰内的河水世界：独木舟往来杰内至廷巴克图的商路，把谷物和鱼类北运，再把食盐南运；许多村民仍守祖灵仪式，而非商城中的伊斯兰教。

桑尼·阿里依靠索尔科渔民划桨的尼日尔船队扩张；杰内在数年围城后于1473年投降，萨也被纳入桑海帝国。这一河上秩序延续到1591年3月，朱达尔帕夏的萨阿德军队在通迪比击溃阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世。摩洛哥驻军后来成为本地阿尔马人；1618年最后一批援军穿越沙漠后，帕夏领地分裂为若干军镇，三角洲在18世纪进入塞古班巴拉国家的势力范围。1818年，塞库·阿马杜在努库马击败班巴拉联军，1819年夺取杰内，1820年建立哈姆杜拉希。萨由此并入富拉尼人的马西纳迪纳，由法官与土地主人管理渔场、洪水、农田和牧道。

en:
Méma is the alluvial plain west of Lake Debo and the Inner Niger Delta, a granary watered by the annual flood. It was an old Soninke kingdom and once a province of Ghana, and the Epic of Sundiata remembers its Tunkara sheltering the young Sundiata and sending cavalry to help him overthrow Soumaoro Kante; under Mali it kept a freer standing than ordinary provinces. It broke away in 1433. In 1444 its king again ruled his own country, its millet floating by water to the markets of Timbuktu, while the Tuareg masters of that city and the Songhai of Gao both pressed for his allegiance.

Within a generation Sonni Ali's Songhai had conquered Méma. In 1496 the new town of Tindirma arose in its east, founded by Sephardic Jews expelled from Iberia, and it became the seat of the Kurmina-fari, governor of the western provinces. Askia Ishaq II sacked the town in 1588 after a revolt, and after the disaster of Tondibi the Moroccans placed one of their Niger garrisons there. As Arma power ebbed, the Bambara of Ségou filled the gap: under Bitòn Coulibaly between 1712 and 1755 they took Djenné and struck at Timbuktu, drawing the grain country of Méma into their empire.
zh:
梅玛是德博湖与内尼日尔三角洲西侧的冲积平原，靠一年一度的河水泛滥成为粮仓。这里本是古老的索宁克人小王国，曾为加纳的行省；《松迪亚塔史诗》记述，梅玛的通卡拉王收留了流亡的松迪亚塔，又派骑兵助他推翻苏毛洛·坎特，因此它在马里帝国之内享有比普通行省更自主的地位。1433年梅玛重新独立。1444年，通卡拉王再度统治自己的国家，出产的粟米顺水路运往廷巴克图的市集，而城里的图阿雷格主人与加奥的桑海人都在争取他的归附。

此后不到一代人，桑尼·阿里的桑海便征服了梅玛。1496年，新兴的廷迪尔马城在其东部建起，由被逐出伊比利亚的塞法迪犹太人建立，后来成为西部行省长官库尔米纳法里的驻所。1588年，阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世在一场叛乱之后摧毁该城；通迪比惨败之后，摩洛哥人把尼日尔河沿线戍堡之一设在这里。阿尔马人的势力衰落后，塞古的班巴拉人填补了空白：比顿·库利巴利1712—1755年在位期间，他们夺取杰内、进逼廷巴克图，把梅玛这片产粮之地纳入班巴拉帝国。

en:
Kala was the river province above the Inner Niger Delta, covering both banks of the Niger north of Bendugu. Its Mali-era governor, the Fala Faren, sat at Kokry, while Sama, Niono, Sansanding and Sibila commanded channels, fishing grounds and flood fields. Bozo and Sorko families worked the pirogues and nets, exchanging river fish for grain, cloth and salt with Jenné's merchants. In 1444, despite its nearness to Jenné, Kala was still one of the provinces answering to the mansa of Mali; many river people combined Islam with older water rites.

Sonni Ali's Songhai forces took Kala in the 1470s, and its governor became known as the Cha'a. By the mid-1500s the province marked Songhai's southwestern border, with neighbouring lands still under Mali's influence. After Tondibi in 1591 it rebelled, forcing Askia Ishaq II to campaign there in person. At Jenné in 1599 the Kala-sha Bukar sided with the Timbuktu pashalik rather than Mansa Mahmud IV, whose defeat ended Mali's last imperial bid. A Bambara revolt in 1645 destroyed the old chiefdoms, though Traoré petty kings remained. Kong raiders devastated the region early in the eighteenth century; after 1712 Biton Coulibaly's Ségou built a Somono war fleet and drew Kala into its orbit. Sansanding became a great Bamana market, where Mungo Park found 8,000 to 10,000 people in 1796 and returned in 1805. By 1821 the old provincial name was largely confined to the north bank, under Ségou's shadow, while Seku Amadu's new Massina state held the delta to the south.
zh:
卡拉曾是内尼日尔三角洲上游的河省，涵盖本杜古以北的尼日尔河两岸。马里时代的长官法拉·法兰驻在科克里，萨马、尼奥诺、桑桑丁和西比拉等城镇控制水道、渔场和洪泛地。博若与索尔科家族驾独木舟、撒渔网，用河鱼同杰内商人交换谷物、布匹和食盐。1444年，尽管邻近杰内，卡拉仍是奉曼萨号令的马里行省之一；许多河居者同时保留伊斯兰教信仰和更古老的河水仪式。

15世纪70年代，桑尼·阿里的桑海军队夺取卡拉，长官改称「恰阿」。到16世纪中叶，这里是桑海的西南边界，邻近地区仍受马里影响。1591年通迪比之战后，卡拉反叛，迫使阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世亲自出征。1599年杰内之战，卡拉-恰·布卡尔站在廷巴克图帕夏一方，没有支持曼萨·马哈茂德四世；后者战败，马里复兴帝国的最后尝试告终。1645年，班巴拉起事摧毁旧酋长领地，但特拉奥雷小王仍存。18世纪初孔格军队的入侵使此地残破；1712年后，比顿·库利巴利的塞古联合索莫诺人建造河战舰队，把卡拉纳入势力范围。桑桑丁成长为班巴拉大市场，蒙哥·帕克1796年见到当地已有八千至一万人，1805年又再度停留。到1821年，旧省名已主要限于北岸，在塞古阴影下存续，而塞库·阿马杜新建的马西纳政权控制着南方三角洲。

en:
This is the straight reach of the Niger between Timbuktu and Gao, where the river narrows past Bamba and the fishing villages of the Sorko haul their catch from waters thick with fish. The Sorko were the Songhai's oldest rivermen: they built the long kanta canoes, crewed the imperial fleet, and paid their tribute in dried fish. In 1444 the bank belonged to the Songhai kings of Gao, with Bamba and Karabara serving as their riverside stations on the road to Timbuktu, while Tuareg herds grazed the desert edge to the north.

In February 1591 Judar Pasha's musketeers crossed the Sahara and reached the village of Karabara near Bamba; the following month their firearms destroyed the Songhai army at Tondibi, and the middle Niger became the spine of the Moroccan Pashalik. Bamba received one of the new kasbah garrisons. After 1618 its soldiers, the Arma, appointed their own pashas without regard to Marrakesh, and in 1630 they made their peace with the surviving Songhai of Dendi. As Arma rule fragmented through the eighteenth century, the Tuareg took Gao around 1770, and the riverside villages answered to whichever cavalry reached the bank.
zh:
这一段是廷巴克图与加奥之间的尼日尔河干流：河水在班巴附近收窄，索尔科渔民的渔村沿岸散布，从鱼产丰足的河水中捕捞收获。索尔科人是桑海最老牌的河上人：他们造长长的坎塔木船，为帝国舰队充当水手，以干鱼缴纳贡赋。1444年，这片河岸属于加奥的桑海国王，班巴与卡拉巴拉是通往廷巴克图道路上的河畔驿站，北侧的沙漠边缘则有图阿雷格人的牧群。

1591年2月，朱达尔帕夏的火枪手越过撒哈拉，抵达班巴附近的卡拉巴拉村；次月，他们的火器在通迪比摧毁桑海大军，尼日尔河中游就此成为摩洛哥帕夏辖区的脊柱，班巴也设起一座卡斯巴戍堡。1618年之后，戍兵阿尔马人不再理会马拉喀什，自行任命帕夏，并于1630年与退守登迪的桑海残部议和。18世纪里阿尔马统治四分五裂，图阿雷格人约在1770年夺取加奥；河畔诸村从此谁的骑兵到了岸边，就向谁纳贡。

en:
The Haayre is the broken country around Douentza, east of the Inner Niger Delta. Rocky outcrops rise from a dry Sahelian plain; the hills hold water for much of the year and offered refuge, while farming on the foothills remained at the mercy of erratic rains. From roughly 700 to 1200 the area supported dense villages and iron-working on a large scale. By 1444 it had become an exposed northern march of the Mossi kingdom of Yatenga, where villagers cultivated risky fields, kept cattle and retreated to the rocks against cavalry raiders, with the Niger merchant cities lying to the west.

Sonni Ali's war with the Mossi states dragged on for six years, and his victory at Kubi, south of Lake Débo in 1483, drew the Haayre frontier into Songhai's hegemonic orbit. The Songhai collapse after Tondibi in March 1591 left the rocky march to local chiefs and raiders. From the seventeenth century Tuareg bands and Fulbe groups moving out of the Inner Delta fought over its villages, cattle and water points, and the plateaus became places of refuge. During the second decade of the nineteenth century, as Seku Amadu founded Massina in 1818 and built Hamdullahi in 1820, Fulbe chiefs in the Haayre likewise turned raiding bands into a more centralized Fulbe-led kingdom, with Douentza its leading town and conquered villages supplying labour and grain. By 1821 the Haayre stood on Massina's rocky eastern periphery.
zh:
海雷是杜安扎周围、内尼日尔三角洲以东的破碎地带。岩丘从干旱的萨赫勒平原隆起，山地一年多数时候有水，也能提供庇护，山麓农业却始终受制于无常的降水。约700年至1200年间，这里曾分布着稠密村落，并有大规模冶铁活动。到1444年，它已是莫西人雅滕加王国北缘的暴露边地，村民在风险重重的土地上耕种、牧牛，遇到骑兵袭掠便退入岩丘，西面则连接着尼日尔河商城的世界。

桑尼·阿里与莫西诸邦的战争持续了六年；1483年，他在代博湖以南的库比取胜，把海雷边地纳入桑海的势力范围。1591年3月通迪比之战后桑海崩溃，这片岩地转由本地酋长和袭掠者角逐。自17世纪起，图阿雷格队伍与从内尼日尔三角洲迁出的富拉尼群体争夺村落、牛群和水源，岩质高原成为避难所。19世纪第二个十年，塞库·阿马杜于1818年建立马西纳、1820年兴建哈姆杜拉希；受此影响，海雷的富拉尼首领也把掠袭队伍整合成更集中、由富拉尼人主导的王国，以杜安扎为首要城镇，被征服的村落提供劳力和谷物。到1821年，海雷已处在马西纳东侧的多岩边地。

en:
The Hombori is a wall of mesas rising from the Gourma steppe south of the Niger bend, crowned by Mount Hombori Tondo, the highest peak in these lands. Dogon villagers and Songhay-speaking hunters held its terraces and narrow valleys, keeping to the old cults while Islam ruled the river towns; tradition calls Hombori older than the tenth century. In 1444 the escarpment country lay on the northern marches of the Mossi kingdom of Yatenga, whose horsemen raided between the Niger and the hills, and Gao was not yet strong enough to claim it.

In 1483 Sonni Ali broke off his canal works toward Walata to hurl back a Mossi invasion, and in the fighting of 1483–84 the Hombori country passed under Songhai. When Tondibi overthrew the empire in 1591, a branch of the Askia royal house fled to these fastnesses and Songhai refugees followed, making Hombori a keep of the old empire's traditions; the Songhai successor chiefs who raided south into Mali sallied from this country, while villages hidden deeper in the crags, such as Tabi, were never subdued at all.
zh:
洪博里是尼日尔河套南侧古尔马草原上拔地而起的一道台地峭壁，主峰洪博里通多山是这一带的最高点。多贡村民和讲桑海语的猎人守着台地与狭谷生活，河滨城镇已归伊斯兰，山里人却仍奉守古老的信仰；相传洪博里在10世纪之前便已建村。1444年，这片崖地处在莫西人雅滕加王国的北疆，其骑兵在尼日尔河与群山之间纵横劫掠，而加奥尚未强大到能把它收入版图。

1483年，桑尼·阿里中断通往瓦拉塔的运河工程，回师击退莫西人的入侵；在1483—1484年的战事中，洪博里地方并入桑海。1591年通迪比之役帝国倾覆，阿斯基亚王室的一支逃入这片险地落脚，桑海难民随后相继来投，洪博里由此成为旧帝国传统的堡垒；南征马里的桑海残余势力常从这里出师，而塔比等深藏岩壑之间的村落则始终无人能够征服。

en:
Liptako is the hot, hilly pastureland north of Gourma, between the Niger bend and the upper Volta country. Its seasonal ponds, above all the water later known as Dori or Wendu, drew Gourmantché farmers, Songhai traders, Tuareg caravans, and Mossi raiders to the same grazing grounds. Before the Fula jihads, local power around the ponds rested chiefly with Gourmantché chiefs, while cattle, salt, and grain moved along tracks leading toward the Niger. In 1444 Liptako was therefore a loose frontier country rather than a walled capital, living by livestock and the bargaining of its herder camps.

Fula clans from Macina and Gourma began settling there in the seventeenth century, at first accepting Gourmantché authority and later revolting against it. Brahima Seydou Birmali sent to Usman dan Fodio for support and received a Sokoto banner; his forces defeated the Gourmantché at the Yayré pond and founded the Emirate of Liptako in 1809–1810. Dori became the capital of the new Islamic state, the westernmost extension of the Sokoto Caliphate, and its livestock market grew with caravan trade toward Say and the Niger. In 1821 a Fula Muslim elite ruled this pastoral borderland from Dori.
zh:
利普塔科是古尔马以北炎热多丘的牧地，处在尼日尔河河湾与沃尔特河上游之间。季节性水塘，尤其是后来称作多里或温杜的水域，把古尔曼切农人、桑海商人、图阿雷格商队和莫西袭击者都引向同一片草场。富尔贝圣战以前，水塘周围的地方权力主要掌握在古尔曼切首领手中，牛、盐和谷物则沿道路运往尼日尔河方向。因此，1444年的利普塔科不是设有城墙都城的严密国度，而是一片松散边地，靠畜牧和牧民营地间的交易维系。

17世纪，来自马西纳和古尔马的富尔贝氏族开始在此定居，起初接受古尔曼切人的统治，后来起兵反抗。布拉希马·赛义杜·比尔马利向乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥求援并获得索科托战旗，其部众在 Yayré 塘边击败古尔曼切人，于1809至1810年建立利普塔科埃米尔国。多里成为这个新伊斯兰政权的都城，也是索科托哈里发国最西端的延伸，牲畜市场随着通往萨伊和尼日尔河的商路而兴盛。1821年，富尔贝穆斯林精英已在多里统治这片畜牧边地。

en:
Bilanga is the open grain country east of the Mossi plateau and west of the Gourma savanna, a land of scattered villages rather than Niger-side cities. Its chief town gave its name to one of the small Gurma-Mossi polities counted among the Mossi kingdoms; its ruler bore the title bilanbedo. Horsemen from Wogodogo, Yatenga, and Gourma crossed its fields, while Songhai armies moved through the wider borderland. In 1444 Bilanga was therefore a chiefly village on a contested frontier, sustained by grain, tribute, and the ancestral earth cults of its Gurma and Mossi people.

The town's place in Songhai history was bloody. After Askia Ishaq II lost Tondibi in March 1591 and was deposed, he fled toward Gourma and sought shelter in Bilanga, a town he had previously campaigned against. In April 1592 its people stormed his lodging and killed him on his first night there. Bilanga then returned to the rivalries of the Volta chiefdoms. After the Fula jihad created the Emirate of Liptako to the northwest in 1809–1810, its old ruling house kept to the eastern savanna, and in 1821 the village remained a small Gurma-Mossi center of grain and ancestral cult.
zh:
比朗加位于莫西高原以东、古尔马草原以西，是一片开阔的谷物地带，村落分散，没有尼日尔河沿岸那样的大城市。其中心城镇为莫西诸政权中的一个古尔曼-莫西小酋邦得名，统治者称号为比兰贝多。来自沃戈多戈、雅滕加和古尔马的骑兵都会穿过这里的田野，桑海军队也在更广阔的边地往来。因此，1444年的比朗加是争夺边地上的酋长村落，靠谷物、贡赋以及古尔曼切人和莫西人的土地祖灵信仰维系。

这座城镇在桑海史中留下了血腥一页。阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世1591年3月在通迪比战败并被废后，逃往古尔马，到自己曾经征伐过的比朗加寻求庇护。1592年4月，当地居民袭击他的住所，在他入城第一夜将他杀死。此后，比朗加重回沃尔特诸酋邦的竞争之中。1809至1810年，富尔贝圣战在西北方建立利普塔科埃米尔国，旧有统治家族仍守在东部草原；到1821年，这座村庄依旧是古尔曼-莫西人的小型谷物与祖灵信仰中心。

en:
Tenkodogo, whose name means 'the old land' in Mooré, stands on the upper White Volta in south-eastern Mossi country, and tradition honours it as the eldest of all the Mossi dynasties, founded in the early twelfth century. Its villages grew millet and sorghum, Peul herders tended the cattle, and Bissa farmers, a Mande people settled along the river below the town by 1300, cultivated groundnuts; iron and pottery were worked and the market gathered every three days. In 1444 the Tenkodogo-naaba ruled his own people, joined by kinship and ritual to the other Mossi kings, while Wogodogo to the north-west under its Mogho Naaba was growing into the dominant power of the Mossi lands.

Early in the sixteenth century the Mogho Naaba Wubri of Wogodogo conquered most of the other Mossi kingdoms, and his successors carried the united lands to their greatest extent around 1540; Tenkodogo nevertheless kept its own dynasty as one of the five senior Mossi realms. Its caravans took part in the north-south trade, carrying kola north and salt south, and Muslim merchants lived in the kingdom while the court kept its ancestral sacrifices. In the early nineteenth century the Fulbe jihads of Sokoto and Masina pressed the Volta basin, yet the Mossi of Tenkodogo held to their old rites and answered to no foreign ruler.
zh:
滕科多戈在莫雷语中意为「古老的土地」，地处莫西地区东南部的白沃尔特河上游；传统上它被尊为所有莫西王朝中最古老的一个，传说建于12世纪初。四乡种植黍和高粱，颇尔牧人照看牛群，比萨农民——一支1300年前后已定居在城下方河畔的曼德人——种植花生；人们冶铁制陶，集市每三天举行一次。1444年，滕科多戈纳巴统治着自己的人民，与其他莫西诸王以血缘和祭仪相联，而西北方莫戈霍·纳巴治下的瓦加杜古正成长为莫西诸地的霸主。

16世纪初，瓦加杜古的莫戈霍·纳巴·乌布里征服了莫西诸邦中的大多数，他的后继者约在1540年把这片统一的疆土扩至极盛；但滕科多戈保住了自己的王朝，始终是莫西五大旧邦之一。它的商队参与南北贸易，把柯拉果运往北方、把盐运回南方，穆斯林商人在王国内居住，宫廷则维持着祖传的祭祀。19世纪初，索科托和马西纳的富尔贝圣战势力进逼沃尔特河流域，滕科多戈的莫西人仍守旧礼，不奉外来的统治者。

en:
Aribanda is the right-bank country of the Niger below Gao, dry grassland broken by river islands and floodplain. Its chief place, Kukiya, stands on an island some 150 kilometres downstream from Gao, hard by the modern border with Niger. It is the oldest seat of the Songhai kings: the Za rulers held court here before moving upstream to Gao by the early tenth century, and when Mali seized Gao at the end of the thirteenth, the old royal line withdrew downstream again. Arabic tombstones in the Bentia cemeteries run from the late 1200s into Songhai times, yet the chroniclers of Timbuktu still remembered Kukiya as 'the center of paganism'. Its islands commanded the river at a stopping point for trade between Borgu, Hausaland and the north. In 1444 the Aribanda bank belonged to the Songhai state of the Sonni dynasty, its villages growing grain and fishing under Muslim rulers whose people largely kept the old cults.

From 1464 Sonni Ali Ber, raised in the traditions of the downstream country by his Dendi mother, built the Songhai Empire from Gao while the old Kukiya lands remained its riverine core. In March 1591 the Saadian army destroyed the Songhai host at Tondibi, and the last Askias withdrew down the Niger through these islands on their way to Dendi. The Moroccans made Timbuktu, not Gao, their capital; the upstream cities withered and the Aribanda bank reverted to its river chiefs and the askias downstream, Kukiya's island town fading into an ordinary riverside village.
zh:
阿里班达是加奥以下尼日尔河右岸之地，干燥草原间散布着河洲与漫滩。本省首镇库基亚坐落在加奥下游约150公里、紧贴今尼日尔边境的一座河洲上，是桑海诸王最古老的驻地：扎王朝的君王在10世纪初迁到上游的加奥之前世代在此设朝；13世纪末马里夺取加奥后，旧王裔又退守下游。本提亚墓地留存的阿拉伯文墓碑从13世纪末一直延续到桑海时代，但廷巴克图的史家仍把库基亚称作「异教的中心」。河洲扼守航道，这里也是博尔古、豪萨兰与北方贸易的停泊处。1444年，阿里班达河岸属松尼王朝的桑海国家，村民以种粮捕鱼为生，统治者是穆斯林，百姓大多仍守旧俗。

1464年即位的松尼·阿里由登迪母亲按河乡旧俗抚养长大，他以加奥为都建立桑海帝国，库基亚故地仍是其河上腹地。1591年3月，萨阿德王朝的军队在通迪比击溃桑海大军，末代阿斯基亚们经这些河洲顺河南撤登迪。摩洛哥人定都廷巴克图而非加奥，上游诸城随之凋敝，阿里班达河岸重新落入本地河酋和下游登迪诸阿斯基亚之手，库基亚的岛城也渐渐沦为普通的河畔村落。

en:
Zarmaganda, the 'land of the Zarma', is the dry Sahel plateau between the Niger valley and the Azawagh, sandy pasture cut by seasonal watercourses, with its chief market at Ouallam, north of the later site of Niamey. The Zarma are kinsmen of the Songhai; their name is said to mean 'descendants of Za', after the ancient kings of Kukiya and Gao, and their traditions bring them southeast out of the Niger bend onto this plateau during the Songhai centuries. They keep cattle, sheep, goats and camels, farm the wadi bottoms, follow the Sunni Islam of the Maliki school and live in village communities under chiefs bearing the title zarmakoy. In 1444 the plateau lay on the southwestern marches of the Songhai state, its herds and wool already part of the trade of the Sahel.

Zarma horsemen served the new Askia dynasty and helped Askia Muhammad overthrow Sonni Baru in 1493, though the descendants of the old Za line never recovered their former power. From the seventeenth century onwards, pressed by Tuareg from the north and Fulani from the southeast, Zarma communities pushed south out of the plateau into the Dallol Bosso valley; around 1750 a zarmakoy named Aboubacar founded the Dosso state there, while Ouallam remained the chief town of the northern Zarma. After 1804 the Fula jihad that founded the Sokoto Caliphate overran the Hausa country to the southeast, bringing a century of frontier pressure on the Zarma chiefdoms.
zh:
扎尔马甘达意为「扎尔马人的土地」，是尼日尔河谷与阿扎瓦格之间干旱的萨赫勒高原——沙质牧场间贯穿着季节性水道，首镇瓦拉姆位于后来尼亚美城址以北。扎尔马人与桑海人同源，据说族名意为「扎的后裔」，出自库基亚和加奥的古老扎王；按其口传，他们在桑海时代从尼日尔河曲向东南迁上这片高原。他们牧养牛、绵羊、山羊和骆驼，在旱谷底部耕作，奉马立克学派的逊尼伊斯兰，以村落为单位生活在称「扎尔马科伊」的酋长治下。1444年，高原地处桑海国家的西南边地，畜群和羊毛已是萨赫勒贸易的一部分。

扎尔马骑兵为新兴的阿斯基亚王朝效力，曾于1493年助阿斯基亚·穆罕默德推翻松尼·巴鲁，但扎王朝旧裔终究未能恢复昔日的权位。17世纪以后，在北方图阿雷格人和东南方富拉尼人的挤压下，扎尔马各部陆续南出高原，进入达洛尔博索谷地；约1750年，名阿布巴卡尔的扎尔马科伊在谷中建立多索国，瓦拉姆则始终是北方扎尔马人的首镇。1804年后，建立索科托哈里发国的富拉尼圣战席卷东南方的豪萨之地，给扎尔马诸酋邦带来了长达一个世纪的边患。

en:
The Dallol country takes its name from the broad dry valleys — dallols in Songhai — that carry the wet-season rains south from the Azawagh and the Ader hills towards the Niger, becoming watercourses and garden land where they join the river. The province's river town, Say, stands at that meeting point; eastward stretches the Dallol Maouri, whose Hausa-speaking people, the Maouri, are called Arawa by their Zarma neighbours. They were the stubborn pagans of this country, sacrificing to the Doguwa spirits under a priestly authority seated at Bagaji and ruled from the twin capitals Matankari and Lougou, and the small state of Arewa kept that order alive on the edge of the Muslim world. In 1444 the Dallol valleys were the southeastern march of Songhai, their flood-retreat fields growing grain for the river trade, with Gobir and Kebbi just beyond.

When the Saadian army broke the Songhai host at Tondibi in 1591, refugees from the fallen empire sheltered along the Niger around small river towns such as Say, and the Dendi askias kept their last capital of Lulami somewhere in the country south of the town, its site now unknown. The Maouri valleys kept their old rites through the long decline of the Songhai successor states. After 1804 the Fula jihad founded the Sokoto Caliphate and overran the neighbouring Hausa kingdoms; the Maouri of Matankari and Lougou were among the peoples who resisted forced conversion, holding to their Doguwa shrines as jihad states rose all around them.
zh:
达洛尔地区得名于宽阔的旱谷——桑海语称「达洛尔」。雨季时，阿扎瓦格和阿德尔山地的降水汇成季节性河流南流，在注入尼日尔河处化为水网与园田，本省河埠赛正坐落于此。向东是达洛尔毛里谷地，讲豪萨语的毛里人住在谷中，扎尔马邻族称他们为阿拉瓦人。他们是这一带坚守旧神的人：在巴加吉的祭司权威下祭祀多瓜精灵，由马坦卡里和卢古两座都城分治，小国阿雷瓦在穆斯林世界的边缘维系着这套秩序。1444年，达洛尔诸谷是桑海的东南边地，退水后的田地出产谷物供河上贸易，再往外就是戈比尔和凯比。

1591年萨阿德军队在通迪比击溃桑海大军后，帝国遗民纷纷到赛这样的河畔小镇避难，登迪诸阿斯基亚最后的都城卢拉米就设在赛以南的乡野，今址已不可考。在桑海后继诸国漫长的衰微中，毛里诸谷始终守住了旧礼。1804年后，富拉尼圣战建立索科托哈里发国，攻灭周边豪萨诸城；马坦卡里和卢古的毛里人是拒绝被强迫改宗的民族之一，在四周圣战国家林立之时仍守护着多瓜神龛。

en:
The Azawagh is the bed of a dead river, a plain of grass and thornscrub between the Adrar des Ifoghas, the Aïr and the Hoggar, where nomads watered their herds at wells strung along the ancient wadi; its name means 'savannah' in Tamasheq. Islam had reached the western Aïr by the eighth century. In 1444 the camps of the Iwellemmeden Tuareg grazed these steppes as far as the gates of Gao, and their clansmen acknowledged the kings of Songhai only when a royal army drew near.

The Songhai collapse after Tondibi in 1591 opened the country east of Gao to the confederation. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries its western arm, the Kel Ataram with their centre at Ménaka, harried the Arma garrisons and gradually brought the Niger towns under tribute, their riders reaching the river all the way from the inland delta to Say. By the later eighteenth century the Iwellemmeden had drawn apart into the Kel Ataram of the west and the Kel Dinnik of the Azawagh proper.
zh:
阿扎瓦格是一条死河的河床，草原与灌丛铺展在古干谷两侧，夹在伊福加斯山地、阿伊尔高原与霍加尔山之间，游牧民沿着干谷上的水井放牧；其名在塔马舍克语中意为「稀树草原」。伊斯兰教8世纪已传到阿伊尔山西麓。1444年，伊韦勒梅登部图阿雷格人的营地在这片草原上一直牧到加奥城下，只有加奥的桑海国王大军临近时，各部才承认其宗主权。

1591年通迪比之役桑海崩溃，加奥以东的土地彻底向这个联盟敞开。17至18世纪间，其西支凯尔·阿塔拉姆人以梅纳卡为中心，与阿尔马戍兵长期周旋，逐步使尼日尔河沿岸城镇纳贡称臣，骑手的势力从内河三角洲一直伸展到萨伊。到18世纪末，伊韦勒梅登人已分成两支：西方的凯尔·阿塔拉姆人与阿扎瓦格本土的凯尔·丁尼克人。

en:
Azbin, or Asben, is what Tuareg and Hausa call the western reaches of the Aïr: granite hills running out into the Azawagh plain, where rainwater gathers in the salt flats. At In-Gall, oasis gardens sit beside pans whose salt has been scraped out for as long as caravans have passed. Further west the copper mines of Takedda, at Azelik, made a Tuareg kingdom famous in the fourteenth century; Ibn Battuta visited it on his way home from Mali in 1353. By 1444 the mines had passed their prime, but In-Gall's wells, salt and provisions made it a standing stage on the road between the Aïr towns and the Niger bend, under the amenukal of Agadez.

In the sixteenth century In-Gall marked the easternmost reach of Songhai power, as Askia's armies and then the warlord Kanta campaigned through the Aïr and made Agadez tributary. When Songhai collapsed after the Moroccan victory of 1591, the sultanate of Agadez stood again on its own, and In-Gall remained one of its southern stations, supplying salt and dates to caravans bound for Kano. The seventeenth century brought decline, and in 1740 the Kel Owey confederation swept down from the north, sacking Agadez and reducing the sultan to their client. Under their rule the old salt road carried on regardless, and each year after the rains the Tuareg drove their herds to the pans about In-Gall for the salt pasture.
zh:
阿兹宾（又作阿斯本）是图阿雷格人与豪萨人对阿伊尔西缘的称呼：花岗岩丘陵向西没入阿扎瓦格平原，雨水在盐滩中汇聚蒸发。因加尔的绿洲菜园旁就是盐池，自有商队经过以来，人们便在此刮取盐晶。更往西，阿泽利克的塔凯达铜矿在14世纪成就了一个图阿雷格王国，1353年伊本·白图泰从马里归国途中曾到访此地。到1444年，铜矿盛况已过，但因加尔的水井、盐和补给使它成为阿伊尔诸城与尼日尔河河曲之间商路上的固定驿站，臣属于阿加德兹的阿梅努卡尔。

16世纪，因加尔是桑海势力的东界：阿斯基亚的大军、随后是军阀坎塔先后攻入阿伊尔，迫使阿加德兹称臣。1591年摩洛哥人击灭桑海后，阿加德兹苏丹国重新独立，因加尔仍是它南方的驿站之一，为前往卡诺的商队供应盐和椰枣。17世纪此地随商路一同衰落。1740年，凯尔·奥韦联盟自北方席卷而下，洗劫阿加德兹，将苏丹变为傀儡。在他们治下，古老的盐路依旧通行；每年雨后，图阿雷格人仍把畜群赶到因加尔一带的盐滩，进行盐疗放牧。

en:
The Ader is the broken Sahelian country where the Aïr sinks into the plains of Hausaland: granite outcrops, thorn scrub and seasonal valleys that run green for a few weeks after the rains. In 1444 Hausa villagers farmed the valley floors, many of them the animist Azna of Gobir stock, while Tuareg drum-groups, the Kel Geres and Kel Itesen, drove their camels and cattle down from the massif each dry season to pasture and water here. What authority there was ran loosely through the amenukal at Agadez and the Hausa lord at Gobir.

Tahoua itself grew from two villages, Bilbis and Fakoua, and only began to fill out in the seventeenth century, when Fulani herders, Tuareg pushed south by the troubles in the Aïr and Azna families fleeing Muslim rulers all settled about its wells. The pressure grew after 1740, when the Kel Owey made themselves masters of the massif and drove the Kel Geres and Kel Itesen permanently into the Ader. When Usman dan Fodio rose against the Hausa kings in 1804, the Tuareg of these valleys joined Yunfa of Gobir; at Tsuntua that December they helped destroy a jihadist army, leaving two or three thousand dead. The victory was wasted, for Alkalawa fell in 1808 and Gobir was swallowed by the new Sokoto Caliphate, sending a stream of Hausa and Tuareg refugees through the Ader toward Maradi and Damagaram.
zh:
艾德尔是阿伊尔高原倾入豪萨平原处的破碎萨赫勒地带：花岗岩孤丘、荆棘灌丛和雨后泛青几周的季节性谷地。1444年，豪萨村民在谷底耕作，其中多为戈比尔系、信奉旧神的阿兹纳人；凯尔·格雷斯、凯尔·伊特桑等图阿雷格部族联盟则每年旱季赶着驼群和牛群下山，到此放牧饮水。这里若有什么统属，也只是松散地系于阿加德兹的阿梅努卡尔和戈比尔的豪萨君主。

塔瓦本身起于比尔比斯和法库瓦两个小村，17世纪才开始成形：富拉尼牧人、因阿伊尔动乱南迁的图阿雷格人、以及逃避穆斯林统治者的阿兹纳家族，陆续到井畔定居。1740年凯尔·奥韦成为高原之主，把凯尔·格雷斯人和凯尔·伊特桑人永久赶入艾德尔，压力愈发沉重。1804年乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥举兵反对豪萨诸王，谷地的图阿雷格人加入戈比尔君主云法一方；同年12月的聪图阿之战，他们协助歼灭一支圣战军，敌军死者两三千人。胜利未能持久，1808年阿尔卡拉瓦陷落，戈比尔被新生的索科托哈里发国吞并，大批豪萨与图阿雷格难民穿过艾德尔，逃往马拉迪和达马加兰姆。

en:
The Aïr is a wedge of mountains rising from the central Sahara, its high valleys catching enough rain to form an island of Sahelian pasture and date gardens in the desert. Tuareg kels have been its masters since at least the twelfth century, and Assodé, founded around 880 by the Isandalen clan, was long the first town of the Aïr and the early seat of its Tuareg chiefs. As trade grew between the Hausa cities and the Mediterranean, the caravan town of Agadez overtook it. Around 1405 the Tuareg factions, worn out by feuding, chose a neutral outsider, Yunus, as their amenukal; by the middle of the fifteenth century his successors had settled the sultanate in Agadez, where Katsina merchants set up the first indigo dyeworks. In 1444 Assodé and Agadez together presided over a wealthy crossroads on the road from Kano to Tripoli.

Around 1500 the Songhai of the Niger bend conquered Agadez; the Hausa captain Kanta campaigned there in Songhai's service before making himself lord of Kebbi and holding the Aïr on his own account, and only in the later sixteenth century, backed by Kano and Katsina, did Agadez break free again. It was a city of perhaps 30,000 souls at its sixteenth-century height, but the next century brought intestine wars and a steep decline in people and trade. In 1740 the Kel Owey confederation came down from the Algerian desert, destroyed Assodé and sacked Agadez, reducing the sultan to their client. Assodé was never rebuilt; under their chief the anastafidet the Kel Owey dominated the mountains and the caravan roads toward Damergu, while Agadez shrank to a fraction of its old size.
zh:
阿伊尔是撒哈拉腹地拔地而起的楔形山地，高谷截留雨水，在沙漠中托出一片萨赫勒式牧场和椰枣园。至迟从12世纪起，图阿雷格各部便是这里的主人；约880年由伊桑达伦氏族建立的阿索代，长期是阿伊尔首城和图阿雷格酋长最早的驻地。随着豪萨诸城与地中海之间贸易兴盛，商镇阿加德兹后来居上。约1405年，苦于内争的图阿雷格诸派系推选身份中立的外人尤努斯为阿梅努卡尔；到15世纪中叶，其继任者已将苏丹廷设在阿加德兹，卡齐纳商人在那里建起最早的靛蓝染坊。1444年，阿索代与阿加德兹共同扼守着卡诺通往的黎波里大道上的富庶十字路口。

约1500年，尼日尔河河曲的桑海人征服阿加德兹；豪萨籍将领坎塔先为桑海转战于此，后自立为凯比之主，凭己力控制阿伊尔；直到16世纪后期，阿加德兹才在卡诺和卡齐纳支持下重新独立。鼎盛时城中约有三万人，但随后的一个世纪内讧不断，人口与贸易双双凋敝。1740年，凯尔·奥韦联盟从阿尔及利亚方向的沙漠南下，摧毁阿索代、洗劫阿加德兹，把苏丹降为傀儡。阿索代再未复兴；在其首领阿纳斯塔菲德特统率下，凯尔·奥韦称雄群山、掌控通往达梅尔古的商路，阿加德兹则萎缩到旧日规模的零头。

en:
The Ténéré is the vast sand plain east of the Aïr Mountains, with the Erg of Bilma running toward the Kawar escarpment. Its chief refuge is Agram, better known as Fachi, an oasis beside a small rocky outcrop between Agadez and Bilma. Wells, date gardens, and salt evaporation pans made it a stage on the Taghlamt caravan, and a high ksar of banco salt blocks guarded its Kanuri and Toubou inhabitants against Tuareg and Bedouin raiders. In 1444 the Tuareg sultanate in Aïr mediated the clans to the west, while Fachi's trade also looked toward Kanem-Bornu and the Kawar oases.

Around 1516-17 the Hausa captain Muhammadu Kanta led a Songhai campaign against Agadez and then broke away to form Kebbi, leaving the Aïr trade network caught between Songhai and its successor states. Agadez regained independence after Songhai's collapse in 1591, but the seventeenth century brought decline and clan rivalry. During the eighteenth century Tuareg confederations seized the Kawar oases from Kanem-Bornu; in 1740 the Kel Owey moved south, destroyed Assodé, sacked Agadez, and reduced the sultanate to their authority. By the early nineteenth century their Taghlamt caravans passed through Fachi carrying salt and dates toward the Sahel and hides, ostrich feathers, and captives northward.
zh:
泰内雷是阿伊尔高原以东的广阔沙原，比尔马沙海朝卡瓦尔崖壁延伸。沙海中最主要的避难地是阿格拉姆（Aghram，即法奇绿洲），它坐落在阿加德兹与比尔马之间一处小型岩丘旁。水井、椰枣园和晒盐池使它成为塔格拉姆特商队的停靠站，一道用盐坯土砖砌成的高堡护卫着卡努里和图布居民，抵御图阿雷格人与贝都因人的劫掠。1444年，阿伊尔的图阿雷格苏丹国在西侧诸氏族间居间裁断，而法奇的贸易也朝向加涅姆-博尔努和卡瓦尔绿洲。

约1516—1517年，豪萨将领穆罕默杜·坎塔率桑海军队进攻阿加德兹，随后脱离桑海建立凯比，使阿伊尔商路夹在桑海与其后继政权之间。1591年桑海崩溃后，阿加德兹恢复独立，但17世纪走向衰落，氏族争斗不断。18世纪，图阿雷格联盟从加涅姆-博尔努手中夺取卡瓦尔绿洲；1740年，凯尔·奥韦人南迁，摧毁阿索代、洗劫阿加德兹，并使苏丹国臣服。到19世纪初，他们的塔格拉姆特商队经法奇往返，把盐和椰枣带往萨赫勒，再把兽皮、鸵鸟羽和人口运往北方。

en:
Itesan takes its name from the Kel Itesen, the strongest of the Tuareg drum-groups of the Aïr in the fourteenth century. Their country is the steppe between the southern edge of the mountains and the Hausa kingdom of Gobir: grass after the rains, thorn scrub and wells, ideal winter grazing for the camels and cattle of nomads who summered in the massif. When the Itesen leader failed to win recognition from the other groups, the feuding clans resolved their quarrel by creating the office of the amenukal around 1405, and the Kel Itesen became one of the chief pillars of the new sultanate. In 1444 its herdsmen still moved each year between the wells of the Aïr and the valleys of Gobir, trading livestock and salt at Agadez and the Hausa markets.

The confederacy's fortunes fell with those of the sultanate. The troubles of the seventeenth century thinned the caravans, and around 1740 the Kel Owey, descending from the north, overcame the older groups and drove the Kel Itesen and Kel Geres out of the best Aïr valleys toward the south and west. The Kel Itesen then made the Gobir borderlands their winter ground, which drew them into the wars of the jihad: in December 1804 they fought alongside Yunfa of Gobir at Tsuntua, where the Tuareg horsemen helped cut down more than two thousand of Usman dan Fodio's men. Four years later Gobir fell regardless, and the Kel Itesen were left on the open steppe between the Sokoto Caliphate and the Kel Owey mountains, subject to the demands of both.
zh:
伊特桑得名于凯尔·伊特桑——14世纪阿伊尔诸图阿雷格部族联盟（鼓群）中最强大的一支。其地是山脉南缘与豪萨人的戈比尔王国之间的草原：雨后青草遍野，遍布灌丛和水井，是夏季在高山放牧的游牧民理想的冬季驼牛牧场。伊特桑首领未能获得其他部族承认，相互仇杀的各氏族为平息争端，于约1405年创设阿梅努卡尔之位，凯尔·伊特桑由此成为新生苏丹国的主要支柱之一。1444年，其牧民仍年年往返于阿伊尔的水井与戈比尔的谷地之间，在阿加德兹和豪萨集市上买卖牲畜与盐。

联盟的国运随苏丹国一同衰落。17世纪的动荡使商队日渐稀少；约1740年，凯尔·奥韦自北方南下压倒旧有诸部，把凯尔·伊特桑人和凯尔·格雷斯人逐出阿伊尔最肥沃的谷地，压向南方和西方。凯尔·伊特桑人从此以戈比尔边地为冬牧场，也因此被卷入圣战的战火：1804年12月，他们在聪图阿与戈比尔的云法并肩作战，图阿雷格骑兵协助斩杀乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥部下两千余人。四年后戈比尔依然覆灭，凯尔·伊特桑人留在索科托哈里发国与凯尔·奥韦群山之间的开阔草原上，两头听候需索。

en:
Kawar is a chain of palm oases tucked beneath a long north-south escarpment on the eastern edge of the Ténéré. Its groundwater feeds Bilma and Dirkou, where salt and natron pans and date gardens stood on the old Bornu-to-Fezzan caravan road. In 1444 sedentary Kanuri families worked the gardens and evaporation pans while Tuareg and Toubou pastoralists supplied camels and claimed protection dues. The Muslim rulers of Kanem-Bornu and the Tuareg confederacies facing Aïr contended for the wells and tolls, with no fixed desert border.
