In 1444 the Haaninin were still east of the Upper Missouri, one people with the Arapaho in the Red River country; the Montana valley that later bore their name was crossed by dog-travois hunting camps rather than settled towns.

Ojibwe pressure pushed the related Haaninin and Arapaho toward the Upper Missouri early in the eighteenth century. The two peoples separated, possibly near Devils Lake, and the Haaninin continued into Montana, acquiring horses by the middle of the century. Their earliest known meeting with white men came around 1754 between the forks of the Saskatchewan, and smallpox soon cut deeply into their numbers. Around 1793 they burned two Hudson's Bay Company posts in Saskatchewan because the trade there supplied guns to Cree and Assiniboine raiders. After joining the Blackfoot Confederacy they ranged across north-central Montana and southern Canada. In 1805 the Lewis and Clark Expedition named the pale, clay-laden Milk River, and in 1818 the Anglo-American boundary settlement cut through its northern watershed while Haaninin hunting camps still crossed the line.
zh:
汉尼宁（Haaninin）意为「白粘土人」，后来被法国商人误称为格罗斯文特，意思是「大肚子」。他们后来的家园在熊爪山与小落基山之间寒冷的牛奶河草原；野牛群穿过半干旱平地，各部落在林木水畔过冬。1444年时，汉尼宁人仍生活在上密苏里以东，与阿拉帕霍人同属红河谷地的一个族群；后来以他们为名的这片蒙大拿河谷没有城镇，只有使用狗拉拖架的狩猎营地往来。

18世纪初，在欧及布威人的压力下，有亲缘关系的汉尼宁人与阿拉帕霍人向上密苏里迁移。两族可能在魔鬼湖附近分离，汉尼宁人继续进入蒙大拿，并在18世纪中叶获得马匹。已知他们与白人最早的接触约在1754年，地点在萨斯喀彻温河两支流之间，天花随后使人口大减。约1793年，由于贸易站向克里人和阿西尼博因袭击者提供枪械，汉尼宁人焚毁了萨斯喀彻温的两座哈德逊湾公司商站。加入黑脚联盟后，他们游猎于蒙大拿中北部与加拿大南部。1805年，刘易斯—克拉克探险队因河水挟带粘土、颜色泛白而将其命名为牛奶河；1818年英美划界切开其北部流域，而汉尼宁游猎队仍往返于界线两侧。

en:
Ashshipite is the broken, grassy country where the Yellowstone and Musselshell meet the Missouri – river valleys, eroded breaks and shortgrass plains black with buffalo. In 1444 it was the northern home of the Kiowa, the Cáuigú, whose oral tradition remembered the Yellowstone basin as the place where they became a distinct people. They had no horses yet: dog travois dragged the lodge poles and baggage, and the hunters ran buffalo on foot in great communal surrounds. Their language, kin to the Tanoan speech of the distant Rio Grande pueblos, set them apart from every neighbour on the river.

About 1650 the Kiowa moved off southeast to the Black Hills, where they dwelt at peace with the Crow; a century later the invading Cheyenne and Sioux drove them on to the southern plains. In their place came the River Crow, kinsmen who had split from the Hidatsa on the Knife after a quarrel over a buffalo stomach; the Crow called them Ashshipíte, 'the Black Lodges', the name this land now bears. From about 1730 they raised great horse herds on the Yellowstone grasslands and beat off Blackfoot, Gros Ventre and Assiniboine raiders. The new century brought the Lakota: in 1800–01 the Crow killed at least thirty of them, and the next year Lakota and Cheyenne warriors wiped out a Crow camp of thirty tipis, slaying every man. In 1820 another allied war party destroyed a camp on the Tongue River, the worst blow the River Crow ever suffered.
zh:
阿什希皮特是黄石河、马瑟尔谢尔河汇入密苏里河一带起伏破碎的草地——河谷、蚀沟与漫无边际的矮草平原上野牛成群。1444年，这里是基奥瓦人（自称Cáuigú）北方的家园，他们的口传把黄石盆地记为本民族成形之地。那时他们还没有马，狗拉的拖橇载着帐篷杆和家当迁徙，猎人们徒步大队合围野牛。他们的语言与遥远的格兰德河畔普韦布洛人的塔诺安语同源，使他们在沿河各邻族中与众不同。

1650年前后，基奥瓦人向东南迁到黑山，与克罗人和平共处；一个世纪后，西进的夏安人和苏族人又把他们继续赶向南部平原。取而代之的是河克罗人——因争夺野牛肚与奈夫河畔的希达察人反目、西迁至此的亲族；克罗语称他们为Ashshipíte，意为「黑棚屋」，这片土地的名字便来自他们。约1730年起，河克罗人在黄石草原上养起大群马匹，击退黑脚人、格罗斯文特人和阿西尼博因人的袭掠。新世纪给他们带来拉科塔人：1800至1801年，克罗人至少杀死三十名拉科塔人，第二年拉科塔人与夏安人便屠灭一个有三十座帐篷的克罗营地，杀光营中男子。1820年，又一支联军在汤河畔摧毁一处克罗营地，这是河克罗人遭受过的最沉重打击。

en:
Eelalapito, the “Kicked in the Bellies,” was the name later borne by a Crow band whose country became the Bighorn Basin. It is a dry plateau ringed by the Absaroka Range to the west and the Bighorn Mountains to the east, where the Wind River becomes the Bighorn. In 1444 this was still a pre-horse northern plains world: small bison-hunting camps moved with dog travois, spent hard winters in wooded river valleys, and dried meat and berries into pemmican. The Crow themselves had not yet split from the Hidatsa villages far to the east.

In the late seventeenth century the Crow moved west onto the Yellowstone and its tributaries, fighting Shoshone bands for the new hunting grounds. The Eelalapito made the basin their own, ranging south toward the Owl Creek, Bridger and Sweetwater country. By the 1740s horses had enlarged their camps, hunts and horse herds, which also drew Blackfoot and other raiders. In 1805 François-Antoine Larocque travelled for two and a half months with a Crow camp toward the Bighorn Mountains, leaving the first detailed European record of their movements. John Colter explored the basin itself in 1807, when Crow country was being drawn into the Missouri fur trade.
zh:
Eelalapito意为「被踢中腹部的人」，是后来克劳人一支的名称，他们的家园成为大角盆地。这片干旱高原西临阿布萨罗卡岭，东接大角山，温德河在这里改称大角河。1444年的北方平原尚未进入骑马时代：小型野牛狩猎营地靠狗拉橇迁移，在林木河谷度过严冬，把肉和浆果制成肉糜饼以备饥荒。那时克劳人还未从遥远东方的希达沙人村落中分离出来。

17世纪末，克劳人西进黄石河及其支流，为争夺新猎场与休休尼诸支交战。Eelalapito人以大角盆地为家园，活动范围南至猫头鹰溪、布里杰山和斯威特沃特一带。到1740年代，马匹扩大了营地规模、狩猎范围和马群，也引来黑脚人等部族袭掠。1805年，弗朗索瓦-安托万·拉罗克随一处克劳营地行进两个半月，抵达大角山一带，留下欧洲人对其迁徙活动最早的详细记录。1807年，约翰·科尔特勘探大角盆地；此时克劳人的土地正被卷入密苏里河皮草贸易。

en:
Tsetsehesahese renders Tsétsêhéstâhese, “those who are like this,” the name of the Cheyenne proper. Their later plains country lay between the Bighorn Mountains and the Black Hills, along the upper Powder, Tongue and Little Bighorn rivers, where cottonwood bottoms gave winter shelter and short-grass uplands supported great bison herds. In 1444 horses had not yet reached this part of the northern plains. The Tsitsistas themselves still lived far to the east, in the Minnesota woodlands, where wild rice and village hunts shaped a life not yet wholly given to the nomadic plains.

The earliest written notice of the Cheyenne came in the mid-seventeenth century, when a band visited the French Fort Crevecœur near the Illinois River. Pressure from the Assiniboine and Ojibwe helped push them westward; Cheyenne villagers reached the Missouri in 1676, although some communities remained in the Minnesota lake country until the 1760s. West of the Missouri they took up horse nomadism and moved into the Black Hills and Powder River Country. Around 1730 they helped pass the new horse culture to the Lakota, and in 1743 François and Louis de La Vérendrye probably travelled within sight of the Black Hills. Through the rest of the century the Tsitsistas camped and raided with Arapaho and Lakota allies, rivals above all to the Crow. By 1821 their horse country was bound into the Missouri fur trade.
zh:
Tsetsehesahese是Tsétsêhéstâhese的拼写，意为「如此之人」，指夏延人本体。他们后来的草原家园位于大角山与黑山之间，地处保德河、汤河和小大角河上游，三角叶杨林河谷可供冬季避寒，短草高原则养育着庞大的野牛群。1444年，马匹尚未传入北方平原这一带；Tsitsistas人仍住在遥远东方的明尼苏达林地，采集野稻、在村落周边狩猎，生活尚未完全转向草原游牧。

关于夏延人最早的文字记录出现在17世纪中叶，当时有一支夏延人访问伊利诺伊河附近的法国克雷沃克尔堡。阿西尼博因人和欧及布威人的压力推动他们西迁：夏延村民于1676年抵达密苏里河，但也有一些群体直到1760年代仍留在明尼苏达湖区。跨过密苏里河后，他们接受骑马游牧生活，进入黑山与保德河地区。约1730年，他们把新兴的马文化传给拉科塔人；1743年，弗朗索瓦和路易·德·拉韦朗德里兄弟很可能已行进到能望见黑山的地方。此后一个世纪里，Tsitsistas人与阿拉帕霍、拉科塔盟友共同扎营和袭掠，尤其与克劳人为敌。到1821年，这片骑马族群的土地已被纳入密苏里河皮草贸易网络。

en:
Kuccuntikka, also written Guchundeka or Kuchun-deka, means 'Bison Eaters.' It was the name of the Eastern Shoshone bands most at home in the Green River and Wind River valleys beneath the Wind River and Absaroka ranges, whose hunting and travel rounds reached toward Yellowstone, Jackson Lake, and the Teton passes. In winter small family camps sheltered in the valleys; spring brought bands together before they moved toward bison grounds, fished, and gathered roots through the summer, then reassembled for the autumn hunt. In 1444 no outside power held these mountains. The Shoshone, who called themselves Newe, traveled on foot and with dogs, moving between Great Basin, Plateau, and Plains worlds before their later horse-mounted expansion.

By 1500 Shoshone bands were crossing into the northwestern plains, and after horses spread among them the mounted Kuccuntikka became a power of the bison country; at the height of that horse culture in the 1700s, bison supplied roughly half their diet. The Comanche split off on the southern edge of this expansion by about 1700, while pressure from Blackfoot, Crow, Lakota, Cheyenne, and Arapaho bands later forced many Eastern Shoshone back toward the mountains; in 1787 David Thompson reported that the Blackfoot had overrun much of their former plains territory. In October 1807 John Colter left Manuel Lisa's Fort Raymond on the Yellowstone, traveled more than 500 miles through Crow and Shoshone country, crossed the winter Yellowstone and Teton region, probably via a northern Wind River pass, and returned in March or April 1808 with stories of geysers that many listeners dismissed. Beaver men were beginning to probe the mountains, but in 1821 the Green and Wind River valleys still belonged to the Eastern Shoshone, even as their old hunting grounds remained contested.
zh:
库聪蒂卡又写作古聪德卡或库春德卡，意为「食野牛者」。这是东肖肖尼人一支队群的名称，他们以温德岭和阿布萨罗卡岭下的绿河谷、温德河谷为家园，狩猎和迁徙路线远达黄石、杰克逊湖及提顿山口。冬天，小型家族营地在河谷中避风；春天各队群重新汇合，随后前往野牛场，夏季捕鱼并采集根块，秋天再集合进行集体狩猎。1444年，没有外来势力控制这些山地。自称「内韦」的肖肖尼人靠步行和狗驮运，往来于大盆地、高原和大平原世界之间，后来的骑马扩张此时尚未发生。

到1500年，肖肖尼队群已越过山地进入西北大平原；马传入后，骑马的库聪蒂卡人成为野牛之乡的一支强权。在十八世纪骑马文化鼎盛时，野牛约占他们食物的一半。科曼奇人约在1700年从这场扩张的南缘分离出去；此后黑脚、克劳、拉科他、夏延和阿拉帕霍等队群的压力又迫使许多东肖肖尼人退回山地，1787年戴维·汤普森记载，黑脚人已占领他们昔日平原领地的大部。1807年10月，约翰·科尔特离开曼努埃尔·莉萨在黄石河畔建立的雷蒙德堡，穿越克劳和肖肖尼地区五百多英里，在冬天经过黄石与提顿地区，可能取道温德岭北部山口，于1808年3月或4月返回；他讲述的间歇泉被许多听者当作无稽之谈。海狸捕兽者已开始探入群山，但1821年的绿河与温德河谷仍属于东肖肖尼人，只是旧日猎场早已争夺激烈。

en:
Baachinena, the “red willow men,” was the Southern Arapaho name for the Northern Arapaho. Their later high-country camps followed the cold shortgrass plains and willow-lined river valleys of eastern Wyoming and western Nebraska, especially along the upper North Platte and Loup waters. In 1444 this was still a pre-horse world: small bison-hunting bands moved on foot with dog travois and sought shelter from severe winters in the river bottoms. The Arapaho themselves were far to the northeast, sharing a Red River valley homeland with the people later called Gros Ventre.

Early in the eighteenth century Ojibwe pressure pushed that Algonquian people toward the upper Missouri, where Arapaho and Gros Ventre separated. The Arapaho moved south into Wyoming and Colorado, took up horse nomadism, and became close allies and traders of the Cheyenne. In 1800 their camps began to divide into northern and southern groups; Lewis and Clark's 1806 reports located people who became the Northern Arapaho around the Loup headwaters. Eleven years later Wilson Price Hunt of the Astor Expedition recorded the North Platte valley as a route across these plains. By 1821 that account had placed the Baachinena hunting grounds on the edge of the expanding Missouri fur trade.
zh:
Baachinena意为「红柳人」，是南阿拉帕霍人对北阿拉帕霍人的称呼。他们后来的高海拔营地散布在怀俄明东部和内布拉斯加西部寒冷的短草平原与柳树河谷，尤其沿北普拉特河上游和卢普河水系活动。1444年，这里仍处于前马匹时代：小型野牛狩猎队步行迁徙，用狗拉橇搬运，严冬时到河谷低地避风。那时阿拉帕霍人还远在东北方，与后来被称作格罗斯文特人的族群共享雷德河谷家园。

18世纪初，欧及布威人的压力把这支阿尔冈昆人推向密苏里河上游，阿拉帕霍人与格罗斯文特人在途中分离。阿拉帕霍人南下进入怀俄明和科罗拉多，接受骑马游牧，并成为夏延人的亲密盟友与贸易伙伴。1800年，他们的营地开始分化为南北两群；刘易斯与克拉克1806年的报告把后来成为北阿拉帕霍的人群定位在卢普河源头附近。十一年后，阿斯托利亚远征队的威尔逊·普赖斯·亨特记录了穿越这片平原的北普拉特河谷通道。到1821年，这份记述已使Baachinena人的猎场进入扩张中的密苏里河皮草贸易边缘。

en:
Skiri, the Wolf band of the Pawnee, gives its name to the Platte and Loup river country of central Nebraska. In 1444 the Skiri were still the northernmost and most distinct Caddoan Pawnee group, closer in speech to the Arikara than to the three southern bands and not yet joined to them. Their earth-lodge villages then lay mainly on the Republican River, where women raised maize, beans and squash and the whole community left on foot for communal bison hunts. Priests and hereditary chiefs governed ceremonies and camps in a society that had not yet seen horses or European firearms.

Mounted Apache raids and armed Siouan migrants pressed the Skiri after about 1670; the bands united around 1680 and gradually moved from the Republican to the upper Loup, where larger circular earth lodges formed compact, defensible villages. A French map placed the Panimaha Skiri near the Platte in 1718. In 1720 they destroyed the Spanish Villasur expedition near the Loup's mouth, killing Villasur, forty-five Spaniards and eleven Pueblo allies. Panimaha leaders joined a French peace council at a Kansa village in 1724, the Mallet brothers visited them in 1739, and in 1750 their leading chief was reported to command 900 warriors. Smallpox after 1760 reduced their eight large villages of 1725 to one by 1800. American officers visited the Pawnee towns in 1806, and the first land cession to the United States followed in 1818.
zh:
斯基伊（史料通译斯基迪）是波尼人的「狼族」，这片内布拉斯加中部地方因他们而得名，地当普拉特河与卢普河流域。1444年时，斯基迪人仍是波尼各支中位置最北、差异也最明显的卡多语群体，语言比三支南部波尼更接近阿利卡拉人，也尚未与他们合为一体。他们的土屋村当时主要分布在共和河沿岸，妇女种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，全村则徒步外出集体猎捕野牛。祭司和世袭酋长主持仪式、管理村落；这时的社会还没有马匹，也没有见过欧洲火器。

约1670年后，骑马的阿帕奇人袭掠和持有武器的苏语移民不断施压，斯基迪各群体约在1680年联合，并逐渐从共和河迁往上卢普河，用更大的圆形土屋组成密集而利于防守的村庄。1718年的法国地图已把帕尼马哈斯基迪人标在普拉特河附近。1720年，他们在卢普河口附近歼灭西班牙维拉尔苏尔远征队，杀死维拉尔苏尔、四十五名西班牙人和十一名普韦布洛盟友。1724年，帕尼马哈首领在堪萨人的村庄参加法国主持的和会；1739年马莱兄弟到访；1750年有记载称他们的大酋长能集结九百名战士。1760年后天花反复流行，到1800年，1725年时的八座大村只剩一座。1806年美国军官到访波尼村镇，1818年波尼人首次向美国割让土地。

en:
The Utsehta were the second great division of the Osage, the Wazhazhe of the Middle Waters — 'Down-Below People', whose lodges stood just below the hilltop towns of the Pahatsi. French traders, misreading their signs for 'above' and 'below', rendered the two bands as the Great and the Little Osage. Their villages and hunts lay west of the Pahatsi, in the oak woods and prairies stretching toward the Kansa. Like the Great Osage they farmed the bottomlands in summer and trailed buffalo on foot far into the plains, and in 1444 no European could yet have named either band.

Marquette and Jolliet placed the Osage on their Mississippi map in 1673, and the horse had reached the bands by 1690. By 1720 French trade goods had drawn the Utsehta away from the Pahatsi into new villages on the Missouri River terraces. Étienne de Bourgmont built Fort Orleans there in 1723, the first European post on the Missouri, and in 1725 escorted Utsehta and other Osage chiefs to France, where they were presented to Louis XV and hunted in his forest. The Little Osage grew strong on guns and horses, trading and raiding between the Missouri and the Arkansas. After France ceded Louisiana in 1763, the Spanish of St Louis dealt with them through the Chouteau brothers, until smallpox carried off perhaps 2,000 Osage in 1801–2. Lewis and Clark in 1804 found the Little Osage a short distance upstream from the Great Osage, and the treaties of 1808 and 1818 steadily handed their Missouri grounds to the United States.
zh:
乌采塔是奥塞奇（瓦扎热人，「中游之水的儿女」）的另一大分支——「下方之民」，屋舍就在帕哈齐人山顶诸镇的下方。法国商人把他们手势中的「上」「下」误读成「大」「小」，两支便被叫作大奥塞奇与小奥塞奇。他们的村落和猎场位于帕哈齐以西，林莽与草原一直铺向堪萨人的地界。和大奥塞奇人一样，他们夏天在河滩种地，徒步远入大平原追猎野牛；1444年时，还没有任何欧洲人能叫出这两支的名字。

1673年，马凯特与若利埃把奥塞奇人标上了他们的密西西比河地图；到1690年，马已传入各支。1720年前后，法国货吸引乌采塔人脱离帕哈齐，迁到密苏里河畔的阶地上另建新村。1723年，艾蒂安·德·布格蒙在那里建起密苏里河上第一座欧洲人要塞奥尔良堡；1725年，他护送乌采塔和其他奥塞奇首领前往法国，觐见路易十五，并在国王的森林中行猎。小奥塞奇靠着火枪与马匹壮大，在密苏里河与阿肯色河之间贸易、劫掠。1763年法国割让路易斯安那后，圣路易斯的西班牙人经舒托兄弟与他们交易；1801至1802年天花夺去约两千奥塞奇人的性命。1804年，刘易斯与克拉克发现小奥塞奇人住在大奥塞奇上游不远处；1808年和1818年的条约，则把他们在密苏里的土地陆续交到美国手中。

en:
Hiraaca takes its name from Hiraacá, 'People of the Willows', the name of the Hidatsa themselves, whose earth-lodge towns stood on the Knife River where it joins the Missouri, a few miles above the Mandan villages. Their ancestors had farmed this stretch of the valley since the thirteenth century, and Big Hidatsa, the greatest of their towns, rose around 1600. The women tended large gardens of corn, beans, squash and sunflowers while war parties hunted buffalo between the Knife and the Yellowstone. Surplus corn, dressed hides and crafts made the Knife River towns the emporium of the northern plains, visited by Cree, Assiniboine, Crow and Cheyenne. In 1444 the Hidatsa and Mandan held the river as neighbours and allies.

The first Europeans reached the Missouri towns in 1738, when the French party of La Vérendrye visited the Mandan, then reckoned at some 15,000 people in nine fortified villages. Horses reached the Hidatsa soon after, and by mid-century their trade network ran from Minnesota to the southern plains and the Gulf. The smallpox epidemic that swept north from Mexico in 1781–82 emptied whole villages, and the much-reduced Hidatsa closed ranks with the Mandan. Around 1790 they beat off a great Sioux siege of Big Hidatsa, killing more than a hundred of the attackers in the counter-attack. David Thompson and other North West Company traders came in the 1790s; in 1800 Hidatsa raiders carried off the Shoshone girl Sacagawea, and in the winter of 1804–05 Lewis and Clark built Fort Mandan beside the five allied villages and took her west as their guide and interpreter.
zh:
希拉卡得名于希达察人的自称Hiraacá，意为「柳树之人」。他们的土屋城镇坐落在奈夫河注入密苏里河之处，南距曼丹人的村落只有几英里。早在13世纪，奈夫河谷就有他们先人的村庄；最大的城镇大希达察约在1600年形成。妇女在大片园圃里种玉米、豆子、南瓜和向日葵，战士们则在奈夫河与黄石河之间猎捕野牛。富余的玉米、鞣皮和手工制品使奈夫河畔的城镇成为北部平原的贸易中心，克里人、阿西尼博因人、克劳人和夏安人都远道而来。1444年时，希达察人与曼丹人在河上比邻而居，互为盟邦。

1738年，拉韦朗德里率领的法国队伍抵达密苏里河畔的城镇、造访曼丹人——据估计当时曼丹人有一万五千之众，分住九个设防村落，这是欧洲人第一次来到这里。此后不久马传到希达察人手中，到18世纪中叶，他们的贸易网已从明尼苏达延伸到南方平原和墨西哥湾。1781至1782年，自墨西哥北上的天花使整村整村地死空，人口大减的希达察人遂与曼丹人合居联防。约1790年，他们击退苏族人对大希达察的大规模围攻，反击中杀敌逾百。1790年代，西北公司的戴维·汤普森等商人开始来访；1800年，希达察战队掳回肖肖尼少女萨卡加维亚，1804至1805年冬，刘易斯与克拉克在五个结盟村落旁建起曼丹堡，并带她西行担任向导和翻译。

en:
Itscheabine is the name preserved in early Assiniboine band lists, where Maximilian recorded Itscheabinè as les gens des filles and other accounts called it the Girls' band. Their country was the broken grassland of the upper Souris River and Missouri Coteau, between the Assiniboine parklands and the Mandan and Hidatsa earth-lodge towns on the Missouri. In 1444 Nakota parties still moved on foot, hauling their lodges with dog travois, hunting bison in the wooded Souris valley and taking beaver and wolves from the pothole country. They carried furs, robes and pemmican south to exchange for Mandan corn and crafts; horses, muskets and Europeans had not yet reached the coteau.

In the autumn of 1738 La Vérendrye, having just built Fort La Reine on the Assiniboine, joined a large Assiniboine band and pushed southwest across this prairie to a Mandan village in December, returning in January 1739 as the first known European party through the country. Horses and muskets then recast the Nakoda as mounted bison hunters and middlemen between Hudson Bay, the Assiniboine posts and the Missouri towns. In 1790 the North West Company built Fort Montagne à la Bosse on the high bank of the Assiniboine elbow, a stockaded post that dealt in bison robes, wolf skins and pemmican and exchanged messages with the Mandan; it was reopened in 1794, and François-Antoine Larocque left it for the Yellowstone in 1805 before it closed. The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 carried American claims up the Missouri, and the 1818 convention drew the 49th parallel across the northern edge of the old range. By 1821 no European post remained on the Souris coteau.
zh:
伊茨切阿比内是阿西尼博因早期队群谱牒保存下来的名字：马克西米利安记作Itscheabinè，法语解释为gens des filles，其他记录称其为女孩队群。这支人的土地在苏里斯河上游与密苏里高地间起伏破碎的草原上，东北接阿西尼博因林缘，西南通曼丹人与希达察人在密苏里河畔的土屋村镇。1444年，纳科塔猎队仍徒步迁徙，用狗拉拖橇搬运帐篷，在苏里斯河林木河湾猎野牛，在锅形湖沼间捕海狸和狼；他们把毛皮、皮袍和干肉饼带往南方，换取曼丹人的玉米和器物。马匹、火枪和欧洲人都还没有进入这片高地。

1738年秋，拉韦朗德里刚在阿西尼博因河畔建成拉雷讷堡，便随一大队阿西尼博因人向西南穿过这片草原，12月抵达一座曼丹村镇，次年1月返回，这是已知第一支经过此地的欧洲队伍。此后，马匹和火枪把纳科达人重塑为骑马的野牛猎手，也使他们成为连通哈得孙湾、阿西尼博因商栈与密苏里村镇的中间人。1790年，西北公司在阿西尼博因河转弯的高岸上建立蒙塔涅阿拉博斯堡，这座围栅商栈收购皮袍、狼皮和干肉饼，并与曼丹人互通消息；它1794年重开，1805年弗朗索瓦-安托万·拉罗克由此出发前往黄石河，不久后关闭。1803年路易斯安那购地使美国的主权声张沿密苏里河上延，1818年的条约又以北纬49度线划过旧猎场北缘。到1821年，苏里斯高地上已没有欧洲商栈留存。

en: The Wahpekute, whose Dakota name means 'Leaf Archers' or 'Shooters among the Trees', were one of the four Eastern Dakota bands and kept close ties with the Mdewakanton of Mille Lacs. In 1444 their camps used the woods, lakes and prairie openings between Mille Lacs and the Minnesota River, where deer coverts gave way to buffalo ground. Pierre-Charles Le Sueur traded with Wahpekute and other Dakota bands in 1700, then built Fort L'Huillier on the Blue Earth for the winter fur trade before the post was abandoned. Ojibwe warfare through the eighteenth century pressed the Wahpekute south and west, but they still held their Minnesota hunting grounds after Zebulon Pike made the first United States-Dakota treaty in 1805; in 1821 this remained a country of Dakota camps and fur trails.
zh: 瓦佩库特（Wahpekute）在达科他语中意为「叶间射手」，是东达科他四支之一，与米拉湖的达科他邻族关系密切。1444年，他们的营地往来于米拉湖与明尼苏达河之间的林地、湖群和草原疏林，在鹿群藏身的树林与野牛出没的开阔地间迁徙。1700年，皮埃尔-夏尔·勒叙厄尔先与瓦佩库特等达科他群体贸易，随后在蓝土河修建利利耶堡，作为冬季毛皮贸易站，但该站很快废弃。18世纪奥吉布瓦人的战事迫使瓦佩库特人向南、向西收缩；1805年泽布伦·派克缔结美国与达科他的第一个条约后，他们仍掌握着明尼苏达的猎场，到1821年这里依旧是达科他营地和毛皮小径纵横的土地。

en:
In 1444 the lower Des Moines valley and the portage paths around the Des Moines Rapids lay within the wide Illinois world. The Moingwena were a Miami-Illinois band closely tied to the Peoria. Their families planted corn, beans and squash in summer river villages, lived in longhouses and mat-covered wigwams, and hunted bison on the prairie before returning to the Mississippi bottoms.

Jacques Marquette heard of the Moingwena as an Illinois-speaking people in 1672, and in 1673 he and Louis Jolliet followed a path from the Mississippi to three nearby Illinois villages; a later Marquette map identifies one as Moingwena. La Salle claimed the valley for France in 1682, while the Beaver Wars had already reached the Illinois country: in 1680 Iroquois raiders destroyed the main Kaskaskia town and carried off hundreds of captives. By 1700 the Moingwena had merged into the Peoria, and Jacques Gravier could name the two groups together. Guillaume Delisle's 1718 map labelled the river 'le Moingona', and in 1721 Charlevoix saw the prairie beyond it filled with bison. After 1763 Peoria families crossed to the Spanish side of the Mississippi; American posts followed the Louisiana Purchase, with a factory at the rapids in 1804 and Fort Madison in 1808, which British-allied warriors destroyed in 1813. The Peoria ceded their Illinois lands by the Treaty of Edwardsville in 1818.
zh:
1444年，得梅因河下游与得梅因急流周围的转运小路属于广阔的伊利尼世界。莫因圭纳（中文资料亦作默因维纳）是一支与佩奥利亚人关系密切的迈阿密-伊利诺伊语群体。各家在河畔的夏季村落种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，住长屋与草席覆盖的维格沃姆棚屋，又到草原上猎捕野牛，随后回到密西西比河低地。

雅克·马凯特1672年已听说莫因圭纳是说伊利诺伊语的族群；1673年，他和路易·乔利埃特从密西西比河沿一条小路来到附近三座伊利尼村落，后来归在马凯特名下的地图把其中一座标为莫因圭纳。1682年，拉萨尔代表法国宣布整个河谷归法国所有，而海狸战争此时已经波及伊利尼地区：1680年，易洛魁袭击者摧毁卡斯卡基亚人的主要城镇并掳走数百人。到1700年，莫因圭纳人已并入佩奥利亚人，雅克·格拉维耶已可将两个群体并称。纪尧姆·德利尔1718年的地图把这条河标为「le Moingona」；1721年，沙勒瓦看到河外草原上遍布野牛。1763年后，佩奥利亚家族渡密西西比河迁往西班牙控制的一侧；路易斯安那购地后，美国人于1804年在急流设立贸易站，1808年修建麦迪逊堡，该堡又在1813年被亲英的战士摧毁。1818年，佩奥利亚人根据《爱德华兹维尔条约》割让他们在伊利诺伊的土地。

en:
The Michigamea, the 'great water' people of Algonquian speech, were the southernmost band of the Illiniwek confederacy. In the fifteenth century their village stood on the Mississippi among the lakes and bayous of the St Francis River, in what is now north-eastern Arkansas, where floodplain forest met southern woods; later French visitors found they needed an interpreter, as the Michigamea may have spoken a Siouan tongue. They farmed the rich bottoms and took fish and waterfowl from the marshes. In 1444 they held the confederacy's southern edge, closest to the Quapaw towns on the Arkansas.

Marquette and Jolliet reached the Michigamea village in 1673 on their voyage down the Mississippi, turning back only at the Quapaw beyond. By 1700 the long reach of the Iroquois wars had driven the band out of Arkansas, and they resettled near the mouth of the Kaskaskia River among the French towns of the Illinois Country. Their chief Chicagou, sent to France with five other chiefs in 1725, pledged allegiance to the young Louis XV on 25 November and danced in Paris, the visit inspiring Rameau's air Les Sauvages; Chicagou later campaigned with the French in the Chickasaw Wars. A Michigamea village occupied from about 1730 was overrun by the Sauk in 1752, most survivors being absorbed by the Kaskaskia and the Quapaw. By 1803 the Michigamea were no longer counted as a separate people.
zh:
米奇加梅人（Michigamea，阿尔冈昆语意为「大水之人」）是伊利尼韦克联盟最靠南的一支。15世纪时，他们的村落坐落在密西西比河畔圣弗朗西斯河的湖泊与水网之间，即今阿肯色州东北部，河漫滩林在此与南方林地相接；后来的法国人发现需要翻译才能与他们交谈，因为米奇加梅人说的可能是一种苏语。他们在肥沃的低地耕作，从沼泽获取鱼和水禽。1444年，他们守在联盟的南缘，与阿肯色河畔的夸帕人城镇相距最近。

1673年，马凯特与乔利埃特顺密西西比河南下，抵达米奇加梅人的村落，直到更南方的夸帕人处才折返。到1700年，易洛魁战争的波及已把这支人赶出阿肯色，他们在卡斯卡基亚河口附近重新定居，置身伊利诺伊地区的法国城镇之间。首领希卡古1725年与另外五名首领被送往法国，11月25日向年轻的路易十五宣誓效忠，并在巴黎起舞，这次访问启发拉莫写下乐曲《野蛮人》；希卡古后来还随法国人参加奇克索战争。一座约自1730年起居住的米奇加梅村落于1752年被索克人攻陷，幸存者大多并入卡斯卡基亚人与夸帕人。到1803年，米奇加梅人已不再被当作一个单独的部族。

en:
South of the Ozarks the Arkansas River is joined by the Verdigris and the Neosho in a wooded, prairie-fringed country the French would call the Three Forks. In 1444 its bottomlands belonged to Caddoan-speaking villagers who raised corn, beans and squash, fired pottery and hunted buffalo at the grassland edge, while their trade paths ran from the Red River towards the Missouri; no horse had yet entered the land. It would later take its name from the Santsukhdhin, the Arkansas band of the Osage.

Osage raiders broke into the Three Forks during the long wars of the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and by 1750 they had defeated the Caddoan villages there and made the country their southern hunting ground. Around 1800, after a quarrel among the bands, roughly half the Osage nation left the Osage River under the chief Big Track and settled on the Verdigris, becoming the Arkansas band; Lewis and Clark found them on that stream in 1804. The Chouteaus traded at their towns, but in June 1817 Western Cherokee and their allies under Spring Frog surprised Pasuga, Chief Clermont's village below Claremore Mound, while its warriors were away on the hunt, killing 38 and carrying off 104 captives. The cession called Lovely's Purchase in 1816 had already prised the Verdigris valley from them, and the Treaty of St Louis in 1818 surrendered more of the old Osage grounds.
zh:
欧扎克山以南，阿肯色河与弗迪格里斯河、尼欧肖河汇流，林木与草原相接，法国人后来称之为「三汊口」。1444年，河滩上居住着卡多语村落的农人，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，烧制陶器，到草原边缘猎杀野牛，商路从红河一直通向密苏里河；那时还没有马踏入这片土地。后来，这里因奥塞奇人的阿肯色支——萨图斯赫丁人而得名。

17世纪末至18世纪的长期战乱中，奥塞奇袭击者攻入三汊口；到1750年，他们已击败当地的卡多语村落，把这片土地变成南部猎场。1800年前后，诸支内讧，约半数奥塞奇人在首领大迹（Big Track）率领下离开奥塞奇河南迁，定居弗迪格里斯河，是为阿肯色支；1804年刘易斯与克拉克就在这条河畔找到了他们。舒托家族到他们的镇子交易，但在1817年6月，西部切罗基人及其盟友在春蛙率领下，趁克莱蒙酋长的帕苏加村——位于克莱尔芒丘下——武士外出狩猎时发动突袭，杀死38人、掳走104人。1816年名为「拉夫利购地」的割让已迫使他们交出弗迪格里斯谷地，1818年的《圣路易斯条约》又让出大片奥塞奇故地。

en:
The Adai were a Caddoan-speaking people of the pine country between the Red and Sabine rivers, where Louisiana and Texas now meet. Like their kinsmen of the Caddo confederacy, they lived in thatched lodges beside their cornfields, in villages strung along the Red from Louisiana west beyond the Sabine. In 1444 their world was the Caddo world of maize fields, river crossings and clan villages, and no European had yet entered their forests.

They were among the first peoples of the region heard of in Europe: Cabeza de Vaca noted the name 'Atayos' in 1530, and Iberville met them on the Red in 1699. When the French founded nearby Natchitoches in 1714, Spain answered in 1716 with the mission of San Miguel de los Adaes; seven Frenchmen from Natchitoches seized it in June 1719, and the Marqués de Aguayo rebuilt it in 1721 as the presidio of Los Adaes, capital of Spanish Texas until 1773. The Adai themselves kept trading with the French and never took to mission life. Imperial war, disease and drink wasted them; the missionaries were withdrawn in 1768, and by 1778 the Adai were nearly gone. Around 1792 fourteen families removed to San Antonio while the rest merged with the Caddo, and in 1820 the Rev. Jedidiah Morse counted only thirty survivors.
zh:
阿代人是说卡多语的一支，住在雷德河与萨宾河之间的松林地带，即后来路易斯安那与得克萨斯相接之地。和卡多联盟里的亲族一样，他们在玉米地旁搭建草顶木屋，村落沿雷德河排开，从路易斯安那向西一直越过萨宾河。1444年时，他们的世界就是卡多人的世界：玉米田、渡口和氏族村落，还没有一个欧洲人走进他们的森林。

他们是这一带最早被欧洲人知晓的族群之一：1530年，卡韦萨·德巴卡记下了「阿塔约人」这个名字；1699年，伊贝维尔在雷德河畔见到他们。1714年法国人在邻近建起纳基托什，西班牙随即在1716年设立圣米格尔·德洛斯阿代传教站；1719年6月，七名来自纳基托什的法国人夺取了它，1721年阿瓜约侯爵将其重建为洛斯阿代斯要塞，作为西属得克萨斯的首府一直存在到1773年。阿代人自己始终和法国人往来贸易，并不接受传教站的生活。帝国间的战争、疫病和烈酒耗尽了他们：传教士1768年被撤走，到1778年阿代人已近乎消亡。约1792年，十四户人家迁往圣安东尼奥，其余并入卡多人；1820年莫尔斯牧师清点时，幸存者只有三十人。

en:
Bdewekhantunwan was the lake country of the Bdewákhathuŋwaŋ, the Mdewakanton Dakota, whose name means the people of Mde Wákhaŋ, the Spirit Lake or Mille Lacs. The shallow waters yielded fish through the ice and in open water, while wild-rice beds, oak woods, and hunting grounds stretched around its shores. The Rum River carried canoes south from the lake to the Mississippi. In 1444 Dakota camps and mound sites dotted these shores; the Santee lived by woodland hunting, rice gathering, fishing, and the fur of beaver, otter, and deer.

French maps called the great lake Lac Buade or Lac des Issatis. Daniel Greysolon du Lhut visited the Izatys country in 1679, and a 1687 account described the large Dakota village on the southwestern shore. The lake became a meeting place for Canadian coureurs des bois and Native fur trappers. Through the eighteenth century, Ojibwe groups moving west with French and British firearms pressed the Dakota from the Lake Superior country; around Kathio, Ojibwe oral tradition remembered a battle that opened Mille Lacs to their expansion, and many Mdewakanton shifted toward the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers. In 1805 Zebulon Pike obtained a contested treaty from two Mdewakanton villages, ceding land for American military posts on the upper Mississippi. During the War of 1812 Mdewakanton warriors led by Wapasha II served with the British, and by 1821 the old Spirit Lake shore was no longer the sole center of the band.
zh:
布德韦坎通万是 Bdewákhathuŋwaŋ（姆德瓦坎顿达科他人）的湖地，族名来自 Mde Wákhaŋ，即灵湖，法语后称米尔莱克斯湖。开阔而水浅的湖面在冰封和通航季节都能提供鱼获，湖岸周围分布着野米床、橡树林和猎场。拉姆姆河把独木舟从湖南端送往密西西比河。1444年，达科他人的营地和坟丘散布湖岸；桑蒂人在林地狩猎、采集野米、捕鱼，并取得河狸、水獭和鹿的毛皮。

法国地图把这座大湖称为比阿德湖或伊萨蒂湖。达尼埃尔·格雷索隆·迪吕1679年进入伊萨蒂人的地区，1687年的记述又描绘了西南岸那座达科他大村。湖畔随后成为法裔加拿大林居者与原住民捕兽人交换毛皮的会合地。整个18世纪，携法国和英国火器西移的奥吉布瓦人从苏必利尔湖方向压迫达科他人；在卡西奥一带，奥吉布瓦口述传统记有一场为他们打开米尔莱克斯的战斗，许多姆德瓦坎顿人逐渐转向密西西比河与明尼苏达河。1805年，泽布伦·派克从两个姆德瓦坎顿村落取得一份有争议的条约，割让密西西比河上游用于美国军站的土地。1812年战争中，瓦帕沙二世率领姆德瓦坎顿战士随英国作战；到1821年，古老的灵湖湖岸已不再是这支人唯一的中心。

en:
La Pointe faces Chequamegon Bay from Mooningwanekaaning, later called Madeline Island, the largest of the Apostle Islands on Wisconsin's Lake Superior shore. Its Ojibwe name refers to the golden-shafted flicker; wild-rice marshes nearby recalled the Anishinaabe prophecy of food upon the water, while the cold lake supplied whitefish and trout and the mainland woods supplied beaver and otter. In 1444 the island was an Anishinaabe fishery, camp and canoe crossing, also used by Dakota and other lake peoples; the related Noquet country lay east toward the Bay de Noc. No French post yet stood on the shore.

Médard Chouart des Groseilliers and Pierre-Esprit Radisson built a rough trading hut on Chequamegon Bay around 1659-1660. Father René Ménard visited in 1661, Claude Allouez founded a mission in 1665, and Jacques Marquette worked there from 1669 to 1671. Pierre-Charles Le Sueur built a French fort on Madeline Island in 1693, abandoned by 1698. The French returned in 1718, when Louis Denis de la Ronde opened the post called La Pointe for furs and copper exploration; its garrison lasted until 1759. The Fox Wars of 1712-1737, whose main fighting ended in 1716 and 1733, repeatedly reshaped the Native alliances guarding routes to the south. After Britain's conquest Alexander Henry and Jean-Baptiste Cadotte made the trade permanent. Cadotte's son Michel married the Ojibwe leader's daughter Ikwesewe, and in 1808 John Jacob Astor's American Fur Company took up the island post, which Lyman and Truman Warren joined in 1818.
zh:
拉潘特位于莫宁瓦内卡宁（后称马德琳岛）西岸，隔海望向谢夸梅贡湾；该岛是威斯康星州苏必利尔岸阿波斯特尔群岛中最大的一座。岛的奥吉布瓦语名来自金胸啄木鸟，附近野米沼泽呼应阿尼什纳比人关于「食物长在水上」的迁徙预言，寒冷湖水提供白鱼和鳟鱼，大陆林地则出产河狸与水獭。1444年，这里是阿尼什纳比人的渔场、营地和独木舟渡口，达科他与其他湖区民族也会使用；与他们相近的诺奎特人之地在东面的贝德纳克湾方向。此时湖岸上还没有法国贸易站。

约1659—1660年，梅达尔·舒阿尔·德·格罗塞耶与皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松在谢夸梅贡湾搭起简陋贸易棚。1661年，勒内·梅纳尔神父到访；1665年，克洛德·阿卢埃建立传教站，雅克·马凯特则于1669—1671年在此工作。1693年，皮埃尔-夏尔·勒叙厄尔在马德琳岛修筑法国堡垒，1698年前已废弃。1718年法国人重返此地，路易·德尼·德·拉龙德开设名为拉潘特的据点，经营毛皮并探察铜矿，驻军一直维持到1759年。1712—1737年的福克斯战争虽以1716年和1733年两段主要战事告终，却反复重塑着守护南方通路的原住民联盟。英国征服后，亚历山大·亨利与让-巴蒂斯特·卡多特把贸易固定下来。卡多特之子米歇尔娶奥吉布瓦首领之女伊克韦塞韦；1808年，约翰·雅各布·阿斯特的美国毛皮公司接下岛上商站，莱曼和杜鲁门·沃伦又在1818年加入。

en:
The Kilatika were one of the bands that made up the Miami (Myaamiaki), Algonquian-speaking villagers of the tallgrass prairies southwest of Lake Michigan. Their country lay around the upper Illinois River, where the Kankakee and Des Plaines meet, and eastward toward the Wabash. Women raised maize, beans and squash in river-bottom fields while men hunted the prairie bison, a way of life rooted in the Mississippian Fisher tradition. In 1444 nothing European had reached these prairies, and the Kilatika shared the country with the Illiniwek and the other Miami bands.

French traders reached the western Miami bands in the 1650s, the first Europeans to set down their name. The Beaver Wars then scattered them before Iroquois raiders, yet in the French years the Kilatika kept their main village at the meeting of the Kankakee and Des Plaines, at the head of the Illinois River. French guns and trade let the Miami push back east by 1700, and the Kilatika settled on Indiana's Eel River; they seized Fort Miami in Pontiac's rising of 1763 and fought the United States until the Treaty of Greenville in 1795.
zh:
基拉提卡人是迈阿密人（Myaamiaki）的一支，说阿尔冈昆语系的迈阿密－伊利尼语，居住在密歇根湖西南的高草草原上。他们的乡土在伊利诺伊河上游一带——坎卡基河与德斯普兰斯河在此汇成伊利诺伊河——向东延伸至沃巴什河。妇女在河漫滩的田里种玉米、豆子和南瓜，男子到草原上猎捕野牛，这种生计承自密西西比文化的费希尔传统。1444年时，还没有任何欧洲人踏上这片草原，基拉提卡人与伊利尼维克人及迈阿密其他各支共享此地。

法国商人在1650年代抵达偏西的迈阿密各支，首次记下他们的名字。随后的海狸战争里，易洛魁武装来袭，各族流散；但在法国统治时期，基拉提卡人的主村仍设在坎卡基河与德斯普兰斯河交汇处、伊利诺伊河的起点。靠着法国人的枪支和贸易，迈阿密人在1700年前后向东重返故土，基拉提卡人最终定居在印第安纳的鳗河畔，即后来的鳗河支；他们在1763年庞蒂亚克起事时夺取迈阿密堡，此后与美国交战，直至1795年签订《格林维尔条约》。

en:
The Mengkonkia were a band of Miami-Illinois-speaking villagers on the tallgrass prairies between the Illinois River and the Mississippi. Women tended fields of maize, beans and squash down in the river bottoms, while the men hunted the vast bison herds out on the grass. In 1444 these prairies were known only to the bands who burned and crossed them, and the Mengkonkia moved, traded and feuded among the other Miami and Illiniwek villages without a single written record.

The French Jesuit Jacques Marquette heard in 1672 of the Mengakonkia as one of the Illinois tribes who all spoke the same language, and in 1673 he and Louis Jolliet visited villages of theirs on the prairie; later French records called the same band Moingwena. In 1721 Charlevoix described 'le Moingona' as an immense prairie alive with bison, and around 1700 the band merged into the Peoria. The Miami lists farther east still kept the Mengkonkia name, remembered as the band of the war chief Little Turtle, who shattered St. Clair's army in 1791 and signed the Treaty of Greenville in 1795.
zh:
蒙康基人说迈阿密－伊利尼语，村落散布在伊利诺伊河与密西西比河之间的高草草原上。妇女在河漫滩照料玉米、豆子和南瓜田，男子到旷野猎捕庞大的野牛群。1444年时，这片草原只有年年焚烧、穿行其间的各支族人知晓；蒙康基人与迈阿密、伊利尼维克人的其他村落一道迁徙、贸易、仇杀，没有留下任何文字记载。

法国耶稣会士雅克·马凯特1672年听说过Mengakonkia之名，把他们列为「彼此说着同一种语言」的伊利诺伊诸部之一；1673年，他与路易斯·若利埃走访了他们在草原上的村落，后来的法国记载又称这一支为莫因圭纳。1721年，沙勒瓦把「le Moingona」描绘成一片遍布野牛的辽阔草原；约1700年前后，这支人并入皮奥里亚人。更东边的迈阿密谱系仍保留蒙康基之名，称他们是战酋小海龟的支派——小海龟1791年击溃圣克莱尔的军队，1795年签署《格林维尔条约》。

en:
Saginawe is a form of Zaagiinaang, the Ojibwe name for where water flows out into Saginaw Bay. The province covers the bay shore and the valley in which the Tittabawassee and Shiawassee rivers join to form the short Saginaw River, a canoe route leading into Lake Huron. Marshes supplied fish, waterfowl and wild rice; the inland woods gave maple sugar, deer and beaver. Ojibwe bands later remembered as the Saginaw, Black River and Swan Creek people had lived in eastern Michigan since at least the fourteenth century, and Odawa and Potawatomi parties crossed their lands. In 1444 the river mouth was a Native fishing place and fur rendezvous without a European post.

Jacques Marquette became the first European known to visit Saginaw Bay in 1668, after founding the mission at Sault Ste. Marie. Jean Enjalran tried an Indian mission in the valley in 1686, but it failed. French and, after 1763, British traders continued to meet Ojibwe trappers at the river mouth, yet no permanent European town took root. The United States included the country in Michigan Territory in 1805, and the 1807 Treaty of Detroit fixed the nearer southeastern boundary. After the War of 1812, Louis Campau opened a trading post on the Saginaw. On 24 September 1819 Lewis Cass met Ojibwe leaders Mash Kee Yosh, Okemos and Wasso, with Ottawa and Potawatomi representatives, for the Treaty of Saginaw; they ceded more than six million acres of the central Lower Peninsula, opening the bay country to American survey and settlement.
zh:
萨吉纳韦是奥吉布瓦语 Zaagiinaang 的转写，意为河水流出之地，即今萨吉诺湾口一带。此省涵盖湾岸，以及蒂塔巴瓦西河与夏厄沃西河汇成短短萨吉诺河的谷地；这条水路借萨吉诺河通往休伦湖。沼泽出产鱼、水禽和野米，内陆林地则提供枫糖、鹿和河狸。后来被称为萨吉诺、黑河与斯旺克里克人的奥吉布瓦诸部，至少自14世纪起就住在密歇根东部，奥达瓦和波塔瓦托米队伍也会经过其地。1444年，河口是原住民渔场和毛皮会合点，还没有欧洲人据点。

1668年，雅克·马凯特在苏圣玛丽建立传教站后，成为已知最早到访萨吉诺湾的欧洲人。1686年，让·昂雅尔朗试图在谷地建立印第安传教站，但未能成功。1763年后，法国及随后的英国商人继续在河口与奥吉布瓦捕兽人交易，却始终没有形成欧洲人永久城镇。1805年，美国把这里纳入密歇根领地，1807年《底特律条约》又确定了东南侧相邻边界。1812年战争后，路易·康波在萨吉诺河畔开设贸易站。1819年9月24日，刘易斯·卡斯与马什基约什、奥基莫斯、沃索等奥吉布瓦首领及奥达瓦、波塔瓦托米代表签订《萨吉诺条约》，割让下半岛中部六百多万英亩土地，湾岸地带由此向美国测绘和定居开放。

en:
Mascouten is the old prairie country of the southern Lower Michigan interior, a land of oak openings, grassy clearings, beech-maple woods, marshes and short portages between the Saginaw country and the Potawatomi and Miami lands farther south. French missionaries later called its Algonquian-speaking people the Fire Nation, although their name more probably meant Little Prairie People, and the same accounts described them as unusually numerous. Their camps followed river crossings, deer drives, maple groves and beaver ponds. In 1444 there was no mission or European fort here, only Mascouten villages, trails and the wider Native commerce of the lakes.

Neutral and Five Nations raiders struck the Lower Peninsula during the mid-seventeenth-century Beaver Wars; by the 1660s Mascouten families were moving west of Lake Michigan with Sauk, Fox, Kickapoo, Miami and Potawatomi refugees, leaving much of the country between Lakes Huron and Michigan thinly occupied. The Mascouten later fought beside the Fox and Kickapoo in 1712 and were last named as a separate band on the Wabash in 1779, before being absorbed among the Kickapoo. French missions and posts spread through the upper lakes from the 1660s, and Cadillac's founding of Detroit in 1701 gave the old southern trails a new eastern anchor. France ceded Michigan to Britain in 1763 and the United States claimed it in 1783; by 1821 no separate Mascouten people remained in the land that bore their name.
zh:
马斯古顿是密歇根下半岛南部内陆的旧草原之地，橡树疏林、草地空场、山毛榉—枫林、沼泽和短途搬运道交错其间，北接萨吉纳韦，南连波塔瓦托米人与迈阿密人的土地。法国传教士后来把这里讲阿尔冈昆语的居民称为「火族」，但其族名更可能意为「小草原人」；同样的记述还称他们人口异常众多。他们的营地依河口渡口、围鹿场、枫树林和河狸塘移动。1444年，这里没有传教站或欧洲堡垒，只有马斯古顿人的村庄、步道和更大范围的湖区原住民贸易。

17世纪中叶的河狸战争中，中立联盟与五族易洛魁袭击下半岛；到1660年代，马斯古顿人与索克、梅斯夸基、基卡普、迈阿密和波塔瓦托米难民陆续西迁到密歇根湖以西，休伦湖与密歇根湖之间的大片土地因而人烟稀疏。马斯古顿人后来在1712年与福克斯人、基卡普人并肩作战，史料最后一次把他们作为独立群体记载，是1779年在沃巴什河畔，此后他们并入基卡普人。1660年代起，法国传教站和商站深入上游湖区；1701年卡迪亚克建立底特律，又为这些南部古道提供了新的东方支点。法国1763年把密歇根割让给英国，美国1783年提出主权要求；到1821年，这片仍以他们命名的土地上已不再有独立的马斯古顿人。

en:
Piankeshaw is the lower Wabash country of the Peeyankihšiaki, the Miami people whose name means those who split off. In 1444 their homeland centered on wooded bottoms above the Embarras River, the place later called Chippekawkay, 'place of edible roots', where Vincennes now stands. The Wabash and the old Buffalo Trace carried canoe parties and hunters between the Ohio valley, the prairies and the Wea country upstream, while cornfields and summer camps occupied the fertile flats. Closely related to the Wea, the Piankeshaw lived beyond European maps or trade routes.

On 28 October 1702 Charles Juchereau opened a French post on the lower Wabash to buy bison hides; more than 13,000 reached the traders in two years before his death abandoned the station. In 1732 François-Marie Bissot, Sieur de Vincennes, built a second post among the Piankeshaw and persuaded them to settle beside it, founding the town later named for him. He was captured and burned by the Chickasaw in 1736. After France ceded the region in 1763 the British built Fort Sackville, which Henry Hamilton retook in December 1778; George Rogers Clark marched from Kaskaskia through flooded lowlands and captured it in February 1779. The 1786 Battle of the Embarras River drove many Piankeshaw from Vincennes to the Wea at Terre Haute or to Kaskaskia. In 1818 Chief Chekommia signed away most remaining Piankeshaw land rights to the United States.
zh:
皮安克肖是佩扬基赫夏基人在下沃巴什河的土地；这个迈阿密群体的名称意为「分离出去的人」。1444年，他们的家园以埃姆巴拉斯河以上林木繁茂的河漫滩为中心，即后来称作奇佩科凯、意为「可食根茎之地」的地方，温森斯就坐落在这一带。沃巴什河与古老的野牛小道把独木舟队伍和猎人引向俄亥俄河谷、草原以及上游的韦阿人土地，肥沃低地上则分布着玉米田和夏季营地。皮安克肖人与韦阿人关系密切，那时仍处在欧洲人的地图和商路之外。

1702年10月28日，夏尔·朱什罗在下沃巴什开设法国贸易站收购野牛皮；短短两年便收购了一万三千多张，他死后据点也遭废弃。1732年，弗朗索瓦—马里·比索·德·万塞讷在皮安克肖人中修建第二个贸易站，并劝他们在站旁定居，由此形成后来以他命名的城镇。1736年，他被奇克索人俘获并处以火刑。1763年法国割让这一地区后，英国人修建萨克维尔堡；亨利·汉密尔顿于1778年12月重新占领该堡，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克则从卡斯卡斯基亚穿过洪水泛滥的低地进军，在1779年2月将其夺取。1786年埃姆巴拉斯河之战后，许多皮安克肖人离开温森斯，前往特雷霍特投奔韦阿人，或迁往卡斯卡斯基亚。1818年，酋长切科米亚签约，把大部分残存的皮安克肖土地权利让给美国。

en:
Waapi-nipi is the Miami-Illinois name for the shining white waters of the upper Wabash. Above a bed of pale limestone, the river gathered streams such as the Mississinewa and carried canoes from the Maumee portage toward the Ohio. In 1444 Miami-Illinois villagers kept the fertile bottomlands, raising maize, beans, and squash and hunting in the prairies and oak woods. The river was their road and larder long before French traders gave it the form Ouabache; no European post yet stood on this part of the Wabash.

Iroquois raids during the Beaver Wars emptied much of the valley in the later seventeenth century, but Miami-speaking bands returned to their Wabash homeland as French trade reopened the Canada-to-Mississippi route. The frontier wars of the new United States then reached the upper river: after Anthony Wayne's campaign of 1794 and the Treaty of Greenville in 1795, American movement up the Wabash increased. On 17 December 1812 John B. Campbell led about six hundred mounted men against Miami and Delaware villages on the Mississinewa, destroying several towns before some three hundred warriors counterattacked at dawn. Campbell withdrew after ten Americans and about forty Native fighters were killed. The treaties signed at Saint Marys in 1818, chiefly the treaty with the Miami, opened the New Purchase, roughly a third of Indiana, and replaced open Wabash country with reservations and American survey lines.
zh:
瓦皮尼皮是迈阿密—伊利诺伊语中对上游沃巴什河白色闪光河水的称呼。淡色石灰岩河床上，沃巴什河汇米西沙尼瓦等支流，把独木舟从莫米陆运道送往俄亥俄河。1444年，迈阿密—伊利诺伊语村民占据着肥沃的河畔低地，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，并在草原与橡树林中狩猎。早在法国商人把河名拼作 Ouabache 以前，这条河就是他们的通路和渔猎仓库；此时沃巴什这一段还没有欧洲人的据点。

17世纪后期海狸战争中的易洛魁袭击曾使河谷大片空弃，但随着法国贸易重新打通从加拿大到密西西比河的路线，迈阿密语诸部回到沃巴什故土。新生美国的边疆战争随后波及上游：1794年安东尼·韦恩的战役和1795年《格林维尔条约》之后，美国人沿沃巴什河推进。1812年12月17日，约翰·B·坎贝尔率约六百名骑兵进攻米西沙尼瓦河畔的迈阿密与特拉华村落，摧毁数座村镇；次日拂晓，约三百名战士反击。美军十人与约四十名原住民战士阵亡后，坎贝尔撤退。1818年在圣玛丽斯签订的诸条约，尤其是与迈阿密人的条约，开放了被称为「新购地」的土地，约占印第安纳三分之一；开放的沃巴什土地随之被保留地和美国人的测量线取代。

en:
Chalahgawtha was one of the five Shawnee divisions and the one traditionally charged with the nation's political leadership. Its principal chief lived in a town called Chillicothe, so whenever that town moved in war or migration, the name moved with it. In 1444 the Scioto and Paint Creek valleys lay in the southern Ohio homeland of the Shawnee, an Algonquian country of bark-covered villages, river-bottom maize fields, deer drives and beaver trails running south toward the Ohio. No European post yet stood in the valley; power rested in village councils and in the exchange of furs and native trade goods among neighbouring peoples.

Iroquois raids during the Beaver Wars scattered the Shawnee in the later seventeenth century as far as Pennsylvania, the Illinois country and the Savannah River, and large towns formed again only after bands returned to the Ohio Country in the 1730s. Lower Shawnee Town grew on the Ohio as a fur-trading centre, but in 1758 its people, joined by Shawnee from Logstown, withdrew up the Scioto near Paint Creek and founded the next Chillicothe. The town had about 300 warriors in 1762 and was the birthplace of Tecumseh in 1768. Dunmore's War brought Virginia's army to the Scioto in 1774. Under Blackfish, Chalahgawtha raiders struck Kentucky and captured Daniel Boone in 1778; after Blackfish was mortally wounded in 1779, George Rogers Clark burned the relocated Old Chillicothe in 1780. Americans attacked the Scioto town in 1787, the Treaty of Greenville opened the country in 1795, and Nathaniel Massie laid out the settler town of Chillicothe in 1796. It became capital of the reduced Northwest Territory in 1800 and served as Ohio's capital from 1803 to 1810 and again from 1812 to 1816.
zh:
查拉高萨是肖尼人的五大分支之一，按传统为全族提供政治领袖。分支大酋长所在的主村称奇利科西；每逢战乱或迁徙，村名也随人迁走。1444年，赛欧托河谷与佩恩特溪一带位于肖尼人记忆中的南俄亥俄故土，树皮屋村落、河畔玉米地、鹿群猎道和通向俄亥俄河的河狸小径构成了这片阿尔冈昆土地。当时河谷中还没有欧洲人的商站或堡垒，权力属于村落议事会，毛皮与土产交易也仍在相邻族群之间流转。

17世纪后期的河狸战争中，易洛魁人的攻掠把肖尼人驱散到宾夕法尼亚、伊利诺伊乃至萨凡纳河一带；直到18世纪30年代，各支派返回俄亥俄地区，大村镇才重新形成。下肖尼镇在俄亥俄河畔成长为毛皮贸易中心，但1758年镇民与来自洛格斯敦的肖尼人一起沿赛欧托河北上至佩恩特溪附近，建立了新的奇利科西。1762年，这座村约有三百名战士，1768年特库姆塞出生于此。1774年邓莫尔战争中，弗吉尼亚军队进抵赛欧托河。黑鱼率领查拉高萨战士袭掠肯塔基，并在1778年俘获丹尼尔·布恩；1779年黑鱼受致命伤后，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克又于1780年焚毁迁走的旧奇利科西。1787年，美军攻击赛欧托河畔的村镇；1795年《格林维尔条约》开放这一地区，纳撒尼尔·梅西1796年规划了欧洲裔定居者的奇利科西。1800年它成为缩小后的西北领地首府，并在1803年至1810年、1812年至1816年两度担任俄亥俄州首府。

en:
Shatteras takes its name from a Siouan mountain people whom early seventeenth-century maps placed in the Ouasioto, or Cumberland, ridges. These forests between the Ohio Valley and the Kentucky headwaters were crossed by trade paths and canoe portages used by Tutelo and Moneton groups, Shawnee hunters and Iroquoian-speaking middlemen. In 1444 the country had no European post and no single fixed border; it was a fur-rich hunting ground on the edge of the Shawnee world, from which the Kispoko war division later took its place in Shawnee history.

In 1671 Thomas Batts and Robert Fallam, sent out by Abraham Wood of Virginia, crossed these western waters and met Mohetan and Moneton communities near the New and Kanawha rivers. The Beaver Wars then emptied much of the region as the Haudenosaunee dispersed the Tutelo around 1670 and claimed the Ohio Valley's southern hunting grounds. Kispoko bands had already been driven toward the Creek country, though Shawnee power later returned to the Ohio. Virginia militia under Andrew Lewis defeated Cornstalk's Shawnee and Mingo warriors at Point Pleasant on 10 October 1774; the Treaty of Camp Charlotte then surrendered Shawnee hunting rights south of the Ohio. Fighting continued through the Revolutionary and Northwest Indian wars until the Treaty of Greenville in 1795, three years after Kentucky became a state.
zh:
查特里斯得名于一支山地苏语人群，17世纪早期地图把他们标在奥瓦西奥托，即坎伯兰山岭中。俄亥俄河谷与肯塔基河源之间的这片森林，布满图特洛人、莫内顿人、肖尼猎人和易洛魁语中间商使用的商路与独木舟陆路转运线。1444年时，这里没有欧洲人的商站，也没有单一固定边界，只是一片毛皮丰沛的猎场，位于肖尼世界边缘；后来的基斯波科军事分支便属于这一肖尼世界。

1671年，受弗吉尼亚的亚伯拉罕·伍德派遣，托马斯·巴茨和罗伯特·法拉姆越过这些西流河水域，在新河与卡诺瓦河附近遇到摩赫坦和莫内顿社群。随后的海狸战争使这一带人口大量离散：约1670年，霍德诺索尼人驱散图特洛人，并把俄亥俄河南岸划为猎场。基斯波科群体此前已被逐向克里克人地区，但肖尼势力后来又回到俄亥俄。1774年10月10日，安德鲁·刘易斯率领的弗吉尼亚民兵在波因特普莱森特击败康姆斯托克领导的肖尼与明戈战士；《坎普夏洛特条约》随之放弃肖尼人在俄亥俄河南岸的狩猎权。战事又贯穿独立战争和西北印第安战争，直到1795年《格林维尔条约》才告一段落，此时肯塔基已在三年前建州。

en:
Along the lower Little Tennessee and the Tennessee it joins, where the Great Smoky Mountains fall away toward Coosa, Dallas-culture villagers kept platform-mound towns: Coste at the river mouth, Tali and Satapo upstream on the maize-rich bottoms. The Tennessee was the road between the mountain chiefdoms and Coosa, and these towns stood on the edge of that chiefdom's orbit. In 1444 their mound centres still flourished, and no European had yet entered the valley.

De Soto's army came down the Tennessee in July 1540. At Tali the townspeople tried to flee by canoe before his soldiers; the chief gave the Spaniards porters and women and kept them supplied with maize gruel until they reached Coosa on 16 July. In October 1567 Juan Pardo marched from Chalahume on to Satapo, until a friendly warning of a plot against him sent the expedition hurrying back to Chiaha. Disease emptied the Muskogean towns; Cherokee settlers took their place and kept their names—Satapo lived on as Citico, Tali probably as Toqua—and the river became the chain of Overhill towns. After colonial forces burned five Overhill towns in 1776, the war chief Dragging Canoe led his people down the Tennessee in 1777 to found eleven towns on Chickamauga Creek and fought the Americans until 1794; John Sevier burned Toqua in 1788. The Cherokee ceded the valley to the United States in the Calhoun Treaty of 1819.
zh:
小田纳西河在此汇入田纳西河，大雾山余脉向库萨方向低伏展开，达拉斯文化的村民在这一带有多座带墩台的市镇：河口是科斯特，上游玉米丰饶的滩地上坐落着塔利与萨塔波。田纳西河是山地诸酋邦前往库萨的通道，这些市镇正处在库萨势力的边缘。1444年，它们的墩台中心依旧繁荣，欧洲人尚未进入这条河谷。

1540年7月，德·索托的队伍沿田纳西河而来。在塔利，镇民试图乘独木舟逃散，被士兵逼回；酋长向西班牙人献上脚夫和女子，又一路送去玉米粥，直到远征队在7月16日抵达库萨。1567年10月，胡安·帕尔多从查拉休梅进抵萨塔波，却因得到有人密谋加害的密报，匆忙退回奇亚哈。疫病使这些讲穆斯科格语的市镇人口断绝，切罗基人取而代之并沿用旧名：萨塔波演变为西蒂科，塔利很可能就是后来的托夸，沿河形成山外切罗基城镇链。1776年殖民地军队焚毁五座山外城镇后，战酋拖独木舟于次年率部顺田纳西河而下，在奇卡莫加溪建立十一座城镇，与美国人缠斗至1794年；托夸于1788年被约翰·塞维尔烧毁。1819年，切罗基人依据《卡尔霍恩条约》把小田纳西河谷割让给美国。

en:
The lower Yazoo River and the swampy delta where it meets the Mississippi were Tunican-speaking ground in 1444. Farming towns of the Plaquemine world dotted the bluffs above the floods, ringed with palisades and crowned by a chief's mound against the endemic wars of the river chiefdoms; the strongest polity on this stretch of the great river was Quizquiz. Maize, beans and squash filled the bottomland fields, and canoes carried skins and shells between its villages and the chiefdoms upstream.

In the spring of 1541 Hernando de Soto's army, ragged after its mauling by the Chickasaw, fell on Quizquiz's main town at midday and seized more than three hundred of its women; the aged chief rose from his sickbed with a battle-axe, and the Spaniards soon moved on to the river and crossed it by night. Epidemics and pressure from hostile neighbours had thinned the river towns long before French missionaries found the Yazoo and Koroa here in the 1690s. France built Fort St. Pierre on the bluffs in 1719, but on 11-12 December 1729 the Yazoo and Koroa, answering the Natchez call, killed the Jesuit Jean Rouel and wiped out the post. French and Choctaw retaliation ended the Yazoo as a people, the survivors sold into slavery or absorbed by their neighbours. Choctaw war parties then held the emptied country until Spain raised Fort Nogales on the bluffs in 1790; the United States took over in 1798, and the Choctaw cession at Fort Adams in 1801 opened the delta to cotton planters.
zh:
亚祖河下游及其汇入密西西比河处的沼泽三角洲，在1444年是图尼卡语诸族的土地。普拉克明文化传统的农耕城镇散布在洪水线之上的陡崖间，城外栅栏环绕、酋长的土丘高踞，以应对沿河酋邦之间无休无止的争战；这一段大河上最强的政权是基斯基斯。肥沃的河滩地里种满玉米、豆类和南瓜，独木舟载着兽皮与贝壳，往来于各村落与上游诸酋邦之间。

1541年春，遭奇克索人重创的德·索托队伍在正午突袭基斯基斯的主城，掳走三百多名妇女；年迈的酋长抱病持战斧起身，西班牙人不久便退往河边，趁夜渡过大河。早在欧洲传教士重返此地之前，疫病和邻族压力已使沿河村镇凋零；1690年代，法国传教士在这里见到的是亚祖人与科罗阿人（Koroa）。1719年，法国人在陡崖上建起圣皮埃尔堡；1729年12月11至12日，亚祖人与科罗阿人响应纳奇兹人的号召，杀死耶稣会士让·鲁埃尔，拔除了这座据点。法国与乔克托联军的报复使亚祖人作为一个部族不复存在，幸存者被卖为奴，或并入邻族。此后乔克托战士据有这片空旷之地，直到1790年西班牙人在崖上修建诺加莱斯堡；1798年美国人接管，1801年乔克托人依《亚当斯堡条约》割地，三角洲随之向棉花种植园主敞开。

en:
The Natchez Bluffs, where the Mississippi bends south, were the seat of the strongest chiefdom left in the lower valley. Plaquemine farmers had raised platform mounds here since at least 700, and around 1500 their lands ran from the Big Black River to the Homochitto, centred on Emerald Mound, the second-largest pre-Columbian earthwork north of Mexico. By 1444 power had gathered at the Grand Village of the Natchez, seat of the Great Sun. The paramount chief inherited through his mother's line over Suns nobles, Honored men and commoners who worked the maize fields, under rites that sent retainers to follow a dead Sun to the grave.

In 1542-43 the canoes of a powerful chiefdom on these bluffs harried the survivors of de Soto's expedition for three days on the river, an encounter many scholars read as the Natchez under the name Quigualtam; then came more than a century of silence and unseen epidemics. La Salle was welcomed here in 1682 and nearly attacked on his return upriver, and Iberville smoked the pipe of peace with the Great Sun in 1700. Four French wars followed: after the first, in 1716, Bienville built Fort Rosalie beneath the Grand Village, founding the town that became Natchez. On 28 November 1729 the Natchez burned the fort and killed more than two hundred colonists rather than surrender White Apple village to a tobacco planter; Choctaw and French retaliation crushed them, and in January 1731 the Great Sun himself was captured and sold into slavery in Saint-Domingue, while the last refugees fled to the Chickasaw. The bluffs then passed from France to Britain in 1763, to Spain in 1779, and to the United States in 1798, when Natchez became capital of the Mississippi Territory; in 1817 it became the first capital of the state of Mississippi, grown rich on cotton floated down the river.
zh:
纳奇兹陡崖是密西西比河折流向南之处，也是下游硕果仅存的最强酋邦所在。普拉克明农民至迟在公元700年便在此修筑台丘，1500年前后，其疆土北起大黑河、南至霍莫奇托河（Homochitto），中心是翡翠丘（Emerald Mound）——墨西哥以北第二大的史前土建工程。1444年时，权力已集中于纳奇兹大村庄，最高酋长称「大太阳」。大太阳按母系继承，治下有「太阳」贵族、「受敬者」与耕作玉米田的平民；按当时的礼制，一位太阳酋长去世，随从便要殉葬同行。

1542至1543年，崖上某个强大酋邦的独木舟在河上截击德·索托远征队残部长达三日；多数学者认为，这个以基瓜尔塔姆（Quigualtam）之名见于记载的酋邦就是纳奇兹人。此后是一百四十余年的隔绝与无形的疫病。1682年，拉萨尔在此受到款待，回程溯河而上时却险些遇袭；1700年，伊贝维尔与大太阳共抽和平烟斗，盟好三日。其后是四次法国战争：第一次战争后的1716年，比安维尔在大村庄下方修筑罗莎莉堡（Fort Rosalie），日后的纳奇兹城由此而起。1729年11月28日，为保住白苹果村不被烟草种植园主夺走，纳奇兹人攻陷并焚毁要塞，杀死两百余名殖民者；法国与乔克托联军随即反扑，1731年1月，连大太阳本人也被俘，卖到圣多明戈为奴，最后的残部逃入奇克索人之中。此后陡崖之地1763年归英国，1779年归西班牙，1798年归美国，纳奇兹同年成为密西西比准州首府，1817年又成为密西西比州的第一个州府，凭顺河而下的棉花富甲一方。

en:
Biloxi Bay opens behind the barrier sands of the Mississippi Sound, with Ship Island offering ships a roadstead offshore. In 1444 its shores belonged to the Tanêks, called Biloxi by later French writers, a Siouan-speaking farming people descended from Mississippian mound-building societies. Women grew maize, beans and squash, while men fished the sound and hunted deer, bear and bison; bark-roofed cabins and shell ornaments marked their coastal villages.

When Iberville arrived in 1699, the Biloxi said their once numerous nation had lately been cut down by smallpox. He began Fort Maurepas on the northeast shore on 8 April and completed it on 1 May 1699, leaving about a hundred men under Sauvolle and the young Bienville. Choctaw envoys reached the post in September 1700 seeking help against the Chickasaw, but fever killed Sauvolle in 1701 and Bienville moved the main settlement to the Mobile River in January 1702. New Biloxi and Fort Louis were built across the bay after 1717, Fort Maurepas burned in 1719, and the Louisiana capital returned to Biloxi in 1719-20 before Bienville moved it to New Orleans in 1722. Britain took the coast in 1763, Spain secured it in 1779 and received West Florida by treaty in 1783, and United States authority reached Biloxi in 1811. Surviving Biloxi drifted west; by 1806 one band lived on the Red River and another at Lake Avoyelles, eventually merging with the Tunica and neighboring peoples.
zh:
比洛克西湾在密西西比湾的障沙岛后方展开，外海的船岛为船只提供锚地。1444年，湾岸属于塔内克斯人，后来的法国文献称他们为比洛克西人；他们使用苏语族语言，是密西西比土丘社会传下的农耕人群。妇女种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，男子在海湾捕鱼，猎取鹿、熊和野牛；树皮屋顶的小屋与贝壳饰品构成他们的海岸村落。

伊贝维尔1699年到来时，比洛克西人说这个曾经人口众多的族群不久前刚遭天花重创。1699年4月8日，他在湾东北岸动工修建莫勒帕堡，5月1日完工，留下约一百人归索沃尔和年轻的边维尔指挥。1700年9月，乔克托使者来到要塞，请求法国帮助他们对抗奇克索人；但热病在1701年夺走索沃尔的生命，1702年1月边维尔把主要定居点迁往莫比尔河。1717年后，海湾对岸建起新比洛克西和圣路易堡，旧莫勒帕堡1719年焚毁，路易斯安那首府在1719—1720年间回到比洛克西，1722年边维尔又将其迁往新奥尔良。1763年英国取得海岸，1779年西班牙控制此地并在1783年依条约获得西佛罗里达，1811年美国权威延伸到比洛克西。幸存的比洛克西人逐渐西迁，到1806年已有一支住在雷德河、一支住在阿瓦耶勒湖，最终同图尼卡人及邻近族群融合。

en:
Abihka is the upper country of the Coosa and Tallapoosa, where the rivers come down out of the southern Appalachians to the coastal plain. In 1444 this was the heart of the Coosa chiefdom, the strongest power of the interior Southeast: its capital on the Coosawattee held a plaza and three platform mounds, eight subject villages lay along its river valleys, and the paramount chief's alliance ran four hundred miles from the Tennessee into central Alabama. The towns worked wide maize fields in the Mississippian manner, while a people the later Spanish chronicles call the Napochi held the western tributaries on the Black Warrior.

De Soto entered Coosa in July 1540, received its chief in state, and then chained the chief and his headmen and dragged them south as far as Talisi. In the summer of 1560 a two-hundred-man detachment from Tristan de Luna's colony reached Coosa, marched with the Coosa against their rebellious Napochi tributaries on the Black Warrior, found the towns abandoned, and accepted the Napochi leaders' submission and renewed tribute. Epidemics then emptied the old chiefdom, and its survivors gathered into the Upper Creek towns, of which Abihka became one of the four mother towns. The French built Fort Toulouse at the forks of the Coosa and Tallapoosa in 1717, the remnant of the Natchez took refuge among the Abihka after the French destroyed their towns, and by 1771 white traders were living in the village. The Upper Towns were the backbone of the Red Stick rising of 1813: Andrew Jackson's forces burned Tallushatchee and relieved Talladega in November 1813, and on 27 March 1814 crushed the Red Sticks at Horseshoe Bend on the Tallapoosa. The old French fort was rebuilt as Fort Jackson, where on 9 August 1814 the Creeks ceded 22 million acres, the whole Abihka country among it; Alabama became a state in 1819.
zh:
阿比卡是库萨河与塔拉普萨河上游之地，河水从阿巴拉契亚山南麓奔流而下，进入滨海平原。1444年，这里是库萨邦国的核心，也是东南内陆最强的势力：都城在库萨瓦提河畔，有广场和三座高台墩，八个属镇沿河谷分布，大君的同盟从田纳西一带绵亘四百英里，直到阿拉巴马中部。诸镇按密西西比式农耕开辟大片玉米田；西边黑沃里尔河支流上的一支居民，后来被西班牙史家称作纳波奇人。

1540年7月德索托进入库萨，先受到酋长的隆重接待，随即将他和头人锁拿，一路押解南行到塔利西。1560年夏，德卢纳殖民队伍的两百人分队抵达库萨，随库萨人出征黑沃里尔河畔叛离的纳波奇人，见其城镇已弃守，纳波奇首领最终屈服、恢复进贡。疫病随后掏空了旧邦国，幸存者汇聚成上克里克诸城，阿比卡便是四大母镇之一。1717年法国人在库萨河与塔拉普萨河汇流处建起图卢兹堡；纳奇兹人在城镇被法军摧毁后多投奔阿比卡，到1771年已有白人商人住在镇中。上镇正是1813年红棍起事的骨干：安德鲁·杰克逊的军队11月间焚毁塔卢沙奇、解救塔拉迪加，1814年3月27日在塔拉普萨河的蹄铁湾击溃红棍。旧法国堡垒被改建为杰克逊堡，1814年8月9日克里克人在此割让2200万英亩土地，阿比卡故土尽在其中；1819年阿拉巴马正式建州。

en:
Mabila is the lower Alabama and Tombigbee country, where the rivers leave the fall-line hills and wind through maize-rich bottoms toward Mobile Bay. In 1444 it was the southern edge of the Mississippian world: villages subject to a paramount chief whose capital was Atahachi, a newly built fortified town with a platform mound and a plaza above the Alabama River. West of the river lived Choctaw-speaking peoples, while down toward the delta the Tohome and Mobile held the lower Tombigbee and Tensaw.

In October 1540 de Soto came down from Coosa and at Atahachi took the paramount chief Tuskaloosa hostage. On 18 October the Spaniards reached Mabila, a palisaded fortress town on a cleared plain, with more than 2,500 warriors hidden inside. The fight ran eight or nine hours, the town was fired, and almost none within it survived; the chronicler Biedma puts the dead at more than 5,000, Tuskaloosa's son was found among them, and the chief himself vanished. The chiefdom never recovered, and within a century its people had been drawn into the forming Choctaw and Creek confederacies. In 1702 the French raised Fort Louis de la Louisiane on a Mobile River bluff, first capital of Louisiana; the Tohome and Mobile settled beside it about 1709, Bienville moved the town down to the bay in 1711, and the brick Fort Conde rose from 1723. Mobile passed to Britain in 1763, fell to Bernardo de Galvez's Spaniards in 1780, and was seized for the United States by James Wilkinson in 1813. That summer the Creek War reached the Tensaw: Red Sticks stormed Fort Mims on 30 August 1813 and killed perhaps 250 to 500 people, and after Horseshoe Bend the district passed with the Creek cession of 1814.
zh:
马比拉地处阿拉巴马河下游与汤比格比河流域，河水越过瀑布线丘陵，穿过盛产玉米的滩地流向莫比尔湾。1444年，这里是密西西比文化世界的南境：各村镇臣服于一位大君，都城阿塔哈奇是阿拉巴马河畔一座新建的设防城镇，筑有高台墩与广场。河以西住着操乔克托语的族群，下游三角洲一带有托霍梅人和莫比尔人，据守汤比格比河与坦索河下游。

1540年10月，德索托自库萨南下，在阿塔哈奇挟制了大君塔斯卡卢萨。10月18日，西班牙人抵达马比拉——平原上一座木栅要塞，寨外草木被砍到弩箭射程之外，2500多名战士埋伏其中。战斗持续八九个小时，城镇被焚毁，寨中几乎无人幸免；编年史家别德马称死者超过5000人，塔斯卡卢萨之子陈尸其间，他本人则不知所终。邦国再未恢复，不到一个世纪，其民众便被卷入正在形成的乔克托联盟和克里克联盟。1702年，法国人在莫比尔河畔高崖上建起路易斯堡，作为路易斯安那的第一个首府；托霍梅人和莫比尔人约1709年获准迁居堡旁，1711年边维尔把城镇迁到河口海湾，1723年起以砖石修建孔代堡。莫比尔1763年归英国，1780年被贝尔纳多·德·加尔维斯的西班牙军队攻占，1813年又被詹姆斯·威尔金逊为美国夺取。同年夏天克里克战争烧到坦索：红棍战士1813年8月30日攻破米姆斯堡，杀死约250至500人；蹄铁湾之战后，这片地区随1814年克里克人的割地而易手。

en:
Between Choctawhatchee Bay and the Apalachicola, the Chipola and Choctawhatchee rivers cut through the pine hills and fertile bottoms of western Florida. In 1444 this was Muskogean country, held by the farming people whom Spanish records would call Chacato and English writers Chatot. Their pottery and economy resembled those of Apalachee, and the two mounds and circular fortification at Waddells Mill Pond mark a late prehistoric center in their later homeland. No Spanish mission or garrison yet stood among them.

Chacato warriors and towns first appear in Spanish records in 1638, during a peace settlement with Apalachee. Franciscans founded San Carlos Borromeo and San Nicolás de Tolentino in Chacato villages in June 1674. In the summer of 1675 Juan Fernández de Diocsale and two companions conspired to kill Fray Barreda after the friar enforced mass attendance and Christian marriage rules; Barreda was wounded in an ambush but escaped, many Chacato fled to Tawasa, and Diocsale was exiled to Mexico. Chacato workers helped build Spanish Pensacola in 1698. The Carolina destruction of Apalachee in 1704 drove 200-250 Chacato through Pensacola to French Mobile, where a count of about 250 men soon fell to forty in 1725-26 and thirty in 1817. Their old country passed to Britain with West Florida in 1763 and back to Spain in 1783, while most survivors moved into Louisiana, later appearing at Rapides, the Red River, Bayou Boeuf and, in 1817, the Sabine.
zh:
在乔克塔哈奇湾与阿巴拉奇科拉河之间，奇波拉河和乔克塔哈奇河穿过西佛罗里达的松林丘陵与肥沃低地。1444年，这里是穆斯科格语人群的土地，住着后来西班牙文献称作查卡托、英文文献称作沙托的农耕者。他们的陶器和生计都与阿巴拉奇人相近，沃德尔磨坊池遗址的两座土丘与环形防御工事，正标示出他们后来祖地中的一座史前晚期中心。此时沙托人中间还没有西班牙传教站或驻军。

沙托战士与村落最早在1638年出现于西班牙记录，当时他们同阿巴拉奇人议和。1674年6月，方济各会在沙托人的村落建立圣卡洛斯·博罗梅奥和圣尼古拉斯·德·托伦蒂诺两座传教站。1675年夏，胡安·费尔南德斯·德·迪奥克萨莱与两名同伴合谋杀害巴雷达修士，起因是修士强制参加弥撒并推行基督教婚姻规则；巴雷达在伏击中受伤但逃脱，许多沙托人逃往塔瓦萨，迪奥克萨莱则被流放墨西哥。1698年，沙托劳工还参与修建西班牙人的彭萨科拉。1704年卡罗来纳势力摧毁阿巴拉奇传教区后，有二百至二百五十名沙托人经彭萨科拉逃到法属莫比尔；当地约二百五十名男子的人口，到1725—1726年只剩四十人，1817年只剩三十人。他们的祖地1763年随西佛罗里达归入英国，1783年又交还西班牙，而大多数幸存者迁往路易斯安那，后来先后见于拉皮德、雷德河、伯夫湾，并在1817年出现于萨宾河一带。

en:
In 1444 Yustaga occupied the western Suwannee Valley between the Aucilla and Suwannee rivers, the westernmost of the Timucua peoples and the immediate eastern neighbor of Apalachee. As many as eight local chiefdoms shared Suwannee Valley ceramics and a Timucuan dialect close to Potano; their villages kept maize, bean, and pumpkin stores, while Potohiriba probably held primacy over the other towns. Across the Suwannee lived the closely related Northern Utina, and marriage, trade, defense, and raiding tied the two countries together without making them one chiefdom.

Survivors of Pánfilo de Narváez's expedition may have met Chief Dulchanchellin here in 1528. In 1539 Hernando de Soto entered an evacuated Uzachile on 25 September; a chronicler counted two hundred houses and abundant maize, beans, and pumpkins. French visitors from Fort Caroline called the local chief Houstaqua in 1564 and credited him with 3,000 to 4,000 warriors. Yustaga kept Franciscans out until about 1623, when the chief of Potohiriba accepted two friars; San Pedro de Potohiriba then headed a mission province estimated to contain some 12,000 people. A missionary described its ball game in 1630, and Yustaga teams still played it in the 1680s after the Apalachee abandoned theirs. Chief Diego of Potohiriba was one of the leaders of the Timucua Rebellion in 1656, and Spanish victors executed rebel chiefs from Potohiriba and Machaba. Four missions still served 330 families in 1689, but Carolinian and Creek raids after 1704 destroyed them. Surviving Yustaga then withdrew toward St. Augustine and merged with other mission peoples.
zh:
1444年，尤斯塔加占据奥西拉河与萨旺尼河之间的西萨旺尼河谷，是蒂穆夸语人群中最西的一支，也是阿巴拉契东边的紧邻。约八个地方酋邦共同使用萨旺尼河谷风格陶器，所说的蒂穆夸方言接近波塔诺语；村落地里种植并储存玉米、豆类和南瓜，波托伊里巴（Potohiriba）可能在诸镇中地位最高。萨旺尼河对岸是关系密切的北乌蒂纳人，联姻、贸易、共同防御和袭掠把两地连在一起，却没有让它们合成同一个酋邦。

1528年，潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯远征的幸存者可能在此见到酋长杜尔昌切林。1539年9月25日，埃尔南多·德·索托进入已经撤离的乌萨奇莱；一名记述者称当地有两百座房屋，并有大量玉米、豆类和南瓜。1564年，来自卡罗琳堡的法国人称当地酋长为乌斯塔夸，说他能出动三千至四千名战士。尤斯塔加长期拒绝方济各会入境，约1623年波托伊里巴酋长才接纳两名修士；圣佩德罗·德·波托伊里巴随后成为一个传教教区的中心，据估当时教区约有一万二千人。1630年，一名传教士记述了这里的球赛；阿巴拉契人放弃球赛后，尤斯塔加球队直到1680年代仍在比赛。1656年，波托伊里巴酋长迭戈成为蒂穆夸叛乱首领之一，西班牙人取胜后处死了来自波托伊里巴和马查巴的叛乱首领。1689年，四座传教站仍统辖三百三十户人家，但1704年后卡罗来纳人与克里克人的袭掠将其摧毁。幸存的尤斯塔加人随后撤往圣奥古斯丁方向，与其他传教区人群融合。

en:
The mangrove coasts and broad estuaries of southwest Florida, from Charlotte Harbor to Marco Island, were the heart of the Calusa kingdom. Its capital, Calos, probably stood on Mound Key in Estero Bay, its houses and temples raised on shell mounds above the tides, and the king's great hall alone was said to hold two thousand people. The Calusa planted no maize: fish, oysters, turtles and waterfowl taken from the shallows fed the densest population in South Florida, perhaps 20,000 souls around 1500, supporting nobles, priests and a war captain beneath a sacred king who was expected to take his sister as queen. Dugout canoes carried their power along every shore of the peninsula, and the Mayaimi of Lake Okeechobee, the Tequesta and the Jaega paid them tribute. In 1444 this fisher-kingdom was still untouched by Europe.

Contact came in May 1513, when Juan Ponce de León careened his ships at the mouth of the Caloosahatchee and fought off twenty war canoes; returning in 1521 to plant a colony, he was wounded by a Calusa arrow and died in Cuba. Hernando de Escalante Fontaneda, shipwrecked as a boy and held among the Calusa for seventeen years, later described their realm to Spain. In 1566 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés sealed an uneasy peace by marrying King Carlos's sister, baptized Doña Antonia, and built the fort and mission of San Antón de Carlos at Calos; three years later the Spaniards had killed Carlos and his successor Felipe and withdrawn. A Franciscan mission in 1697 lasted only months, and the old religion held firm. After 1702 Creek and Yamasee slavers armed by Carolina swept south through a people already thinned by epidemics; in 1711 the Spanish ferried 270 survivors to Cuba, where nearly 200 soon died. When Spain ceded Florida in 1763, the last Calusa were carried away to Cuba, ending a kingdom that had kept Europe at arm's length for two centuries.
zh:
佛罗里达西南海岸红树林环抱的宽阔河口，从夏洛特港到马科岛，是卡卢萨王国的腹地。都城卡洛斯据信坐落在埃斯特罗湾的芒德礁上，房屋与神庙都建在贝冢堆成的高台之上以避潮水，据说仅王宫中的大殿便能容纳两千人。卡卢萨人不种玉米：浅海中网罟所获的鱼、牡蛎、海龟和水禽养活着南佛罗里达最稠密的人口——1500年前后约有两万人——并供养起贵族、祭司和军事首领，居于其上的是一位圣王，按制须以亲妹为后。独木舟把他们的武力送往半岛各处海岸，奥基乔比湖畔的马亚依米人、特克斯塔人和哈埃加人都向其纳贡。1444年，这个渔人王国仍与欧洲全然隔绝。

1513年5月，庞塞·德莱昂在卡卢萨哈奇河口修船，击退了二十艘作战独木舟；1521年他卷土重来试图殖民，被卡卢萨人的箭射伤，退回古巴死去。少年时遇海难、在卡卢萨人中生活了十七年的埃尔南多·德·埃斯卡兰特·丰特内达，后来向西班牙人详述了这个王国。1566年，佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯娶国王卡洛斯之妹（受洗名安东尼娅女士）以缔结盟约，并在卡洛斯建起圣安东·德·卡洛斯要塞与传教站；三年后，西班牙人杀死卡洛斯及其继立者费利佩，撤兵而去。1697年方济各会的传教站只维持了几个月，旧信仰始终未被动摇。1702年后，被卡罗来纳武装起来的克里克和亚马西奴隶贩子席卷南下，而此时卡卢萨人已被疫病削弱；1711年西班牙人将270名幸存者运往古巴，近200人很快病死。1763年西班牙割让佛罗里达，最后的卡卢萨人被迁往古巴，这个与欧洲周旋了两百年的王国就此终结。

en:
The Mayaimi took their name from Lake Mayaimi, the 'big water' now called Okeechobee, the vast shallow lake at the heart of the Everglades. They lived in small towns of thirty or forty households raised on earthen mounds above the flood, linked by canals dug for their shovel-ended dugout canoes, with ceremonial earthworks such as Fort Center among them. Bass, eels, turtles and alligator, together with flour grated from the coontie zamia root, fed them; in high-water season the mounds became islands and they lived on fish alone. In 1444 the lake towns were the inland subjects of the Calusa kings of the Gulf coast.

The Spaniards knew the Mayaimi chiefly through Hernando de Escalante Fontaneda, who passed through their towns during his seventeen years among the southern tribes. After 1702 Creek and Yamasee slavers raided as far as the tip of the peninsula, burning and carrying off the inhabitants for sale from Boston to Barbados. A party of 280 Florida refugees that reached Cuba in 1710 included the cacique of 'Maimi'. In 1738 the Maymi still held a fortified place on the coast south of Cape Canaveral, and in 1743 missionaries found a remnant of them, about a hundred souls with Santaluzo and Mayaca survivors, four days' march north of the Miami River. The last of the Mayaimi are believed to have been evacuated to Cuba with the Spaniards when Florida was ceded in 1763.
zh:
马亚依米人因马亚依米湖得名——「马亚依米」意为「大水」，也就是后来的奥基乔比湖，大沼泽地中央一片浩渺的浅水湖。他们住在三四十户规模的小镇里，房屋建在土筑高台之上以避洪水，台地之间挖有运河，供两头平阔如铲的独木舟往来，森特堡等仪式土垒便矗立在这些村镇之中。黑鲈、鳗、龟、短吻鳄，加上用泽米蕨根磨出的淀粉，是他们的食粮；涨水季节高台沦为孤岛，他们便只以鱼为食。1444年，湖畔诸镇是墨西哥湾沿岸卡卢萨诸王的内陆属民。

西班牙人主要通过埃尔南多·德·埃斯卡兰特·丰特内达知道马亚依米人——他在南部诸族中生活十七年，曾往来于湖畔村镇。1702年后，克里克和亚马西奴隶贩子的洗劫一直深入半岛南端，焚毁村镇，把掳来的人卖到从波士顿到巴巴多斯的市场。1710年抵达古巴的一支280名佛罗里达难民中，便有「迈米」的首领。1738年，马亚依米人在卡纳维拉尔角以南的海岸仍据有一处「堡垒」；1743年，传教士发现他们的孑遗已与圣卢索人、马亚卡人合为约一百人的群体，住在迈阿密河以北四天路程处。1763年佛罗里达割让之际，最后的马亚依米人据信随西班牙人撤往了古巴。

en:
Ichisi was a late Mississippian chiefdom on the Ocmulgee floodplain south of present Macon, with its principal town commonly identified with the Lamar mounds and village site. In 1444 its maize fields, river bottomlands and earthen platform mounds supported a hierarchical Muskogean town linked by trails to Ocute and neighboring chiefdoms. Women cooked corn cakes and roasted venison, priests and chiefs conducted ceremony at the mounds, and no European settlement yet stood on the Ocmulgee.

Hernando de Soto's Spanish expedition entered Ichisi in March 1540 and reached the main town on March 30; its chief received the strangers peacefully, supplied corn cakes, wild onions and venison, and allowed a cross to be raised on a mound. New diseases and political chaos devastated the Ocmulgee chiefdoms over the following century. In the eighteenth century Hitchiti people lived around Ocmulgee Fields near Macon within the emerging Creek world, and the Ochese Creek towns withdrew toward the Chattahoochee after the Yamasee War of 1715. The United States acquired the lands between the Oconee and Ocmulgee in 1806 and built Fort Benjamin Hawkins; the Creek cession of Ocmulgee Fields in 1821 opened coveted short-staple cotton country to American planters.
zh:
伊奇西是密西西比文化晚期的酋长领地，位于今梅肯以南的奥克马尔吉河洪泛平原，主城通常被比定为拉马尔土丘村落遗址。1444年时，玉米田、河畔低地和平顶土丘支撑着一个等级分明的马斯科吉城镇，并有小径通往奥库特和邻近酋长领地。妇女制作玉米饼、烘烤鹿肉，祭司与酋长在土丘主持仪式，奥克马尔吉河畔尚无欧洲人定居点。

1540年3月，埃尔南多·德·索托率领的西班牙远征队进入伊奇西，并在3月30日抵达主城；酋长和平接待这些陌生人，供应玉米饼、野洋葱和鹿肉，还允许他们在一座土丘上竖立十字架。随后一个世纪里，新传入的疾病和政治动荡摧毁了奥克马尔吉诸酋长领地。18世纪，希奇蒂人居住在梅肯附近的奥克马尔吉原野，属于正在形成的克里克世界；1715年亚马西战争后，奥切斯溪诸镇向查特胡奇河方向退去。1806年，美国取得奥科尼河与奥克马尔吉河之间的土地，并修建本杰明·霍金斯堡；1821年克里克人割让奥克马尔吉原野，这片令人垂涎的短绒棉土地随之向美国种植园主开放。

en:
Ocute was a Late Mississippian paramount chiefdom in the Oconee River valley, a loose alliance of mound towns whose Shoulderbone center had been founded around 1325 between Altamaha at Shinholser and Cofaqui-Patofa at Dyar. In 1444 its mico ruled over maize fields, platform mounds and subject lords, while long war with Cofitachequi to the east was turning the Savannah, Saluda and Broad river country into a raided wilderness. The province was therefore a populous but heavily armed frontier, not yet touched by European settlement.

De Soto reached Altamaha on April 3, 1540, exchanged gifts with its chief Zamuno, and visited Ocute on April 9, where he raised a cross before marching toward Cofitachequi. After St. Augustine was founded in 1565 the mound centers lost population, Altamaha became dominant, and Spanish records called the province La Tama; Fray Pedro de Chozas passed through Tama, Ocute, Talufa and Usatipa in 1597. Disease weakened the towns around 1630, and Westo slave raids in 1661-1662 drove the people from the Oconee. Spanish documents called their refugee confederation the Yamasis from 1663; after moving to South Carolina in 1685, they became British-allied raiders until defeat and dispersal in the Yamasee War of 1715-1717. The 1802 Treaty of Fort Wilkinson opened Oconee lands to the United States, Milledgeville was founded in 1803 and became Georgia's capital in 1804, and cotton commerce soon replaced the old mound province.
zh:
奥库特是奥科尼河流域晚密西西比文化的等级酋长领地，由若干土丘城镇松散联合而成。约1325年建立的肩骨中心位于欣霍尔泽的奥尔塔马霍与戴尔的科法基—帕托法之间。1444年时，它的米科首领统辖着玉米田、平顶土丘和从属首领；同东方科菲塔切基的长期战争，正把萨凡纳河、萨卢达河与布罗德河一带变成屡遭袭掠的荒野。因此这里人口不少，却是戒备森严的边疆，欧洲人尚未定居。

1540年4月3日，德索托抵达奥尔塔马霍，同首领萨穆诺交换礼物，4月9日访问奥库特，在当地竖立十字架，随后向科菲塔切基进军。1565年圣奥古斯丁建立后，土丘中心人口流失，奥尔塔马霍取得优势，西班牙记录称这一地区为拉塔马；1597年，佩德罗·德·乔萨斯修士经过塔马、奥库特、塔卢法和乌萨蒂帕。1630年前后，疫病削弱了这些城镇；1661至1662年，韦斯托人的奴隶袭掠迫使人们离开奥科尼。西班牙文献从1663年起把这些难民联盟称为亚马西人。他们1685年迁往南卡罗来纳，成为与英国结盟的袭掠者，最终在1715至1717年的亚马西战争中被击败并离散。1802年《威尔金森堡条约》使奥科尼土地向美国开放，米利奇维尔1803年建立，1804年成为佐治亚首府，棉花贸易很快取代了旧日的土丘酋邦。

en:
The tidal sounds and Sea Islands between the Altamaha River and the mouth of the St. Johns were Mocama country. Its people spoke the Mocama dialect of Timucua and made the grog-tempered San Pedro pottery found along these waterways. On the eve of European contact two powerful chiefdoms dominated the coast: the Saturiwa around Fort George Island and the mouth of the St. Johns, and the Tacatacuru on Cumberland Island. In 1444 their villages still moved by canoe through salt marsh and inland channels, trading and raiding under chiefs whose authority reached across several settlements.

French Huguenots reached the coast in 1562, and the Saturiwa helped them build Fort Caroline in their territory. Spanish forces destroyed that French foothold and gradually drew Mocama into the mission province of Spanish Florida. Franciscans founded San Pedro de Mocama on Cumberland Island around 1580, while San Juan del Puerto on Fort George Island and Santa Maria de Sena on Amelia Island became the other principal stations. A Guale raid was beaten back from San Pedro in 1597, but epidemics, slave raids and warfare shattered the chiefdoms. English-backed Westo attacks between 1675 and 1680 destroyed the mission system, and South Carolina's 1702 invasion overran the remaining refugee stations. By 1733 the survivors could not prevent James Oglethorpe from founding Georgia; in 1763 some remaining Mocama and Guale Christians were among the eighty-nine mission Indians evacuated to Cuba with Spain's garrisons.
zh:
阿尔塔马哈河与圣约翰斯河口之间的潮湾和海群岛，是莫卡马人的土地。他们使用蒂穆夸语的莫卡马方言，沿水道制作掺碎陶胎的圣佩德罗陶器。欧洲人到来前夕，沿岸有两个强大酋邦：以乔治堡岛和圣约翰斯河口一带为中心的萨图里瓦人，以及据有坎伯兰岛的塔卡塔库鲁人。1444年时，各村仍乘独木舟穿行盐沼与内河航道，在统辖多个聚落的酋长领导下贸易、征战。

1562年，法国胡格诺派到达海岸，萨图里瓦人协助他们在自己的土地上修建卡罗琳堡。西班牙军队摧毁这个法国据点后，逐渐把莫卡马纳入西属佛罗里达的传教省。方济各会约1580年在坎伯兰岛建立圣佩德罗·德·莫卡马传教站，乔治堡岛的圣胡安·德尔·普埃尔托和阿米莉亚岛的圣玛丽亚·德·塞纳则是另外两处主要站点。1597年，瓜莱人对圣佩德罗的进攻被击退，但疫病、掳奴袭击和战争瓦解了各个酋邦。1675年至1680年间，得到英国人支持的韦斯托人摧毁了传教体系；1702年南卡罗来纳的入侵又踏平残存的避难传教站。到1733年，幸存者已无力阻止詹姆斯·奥格尔索普建立佐治亚。1763年，一些残存的莫卡马和瓜莱基督徒被计入八十九名传教印第安人，随西班牙守军撤往古巴。

en:
Etowah — italwa, simply 'town', in the Muscogee language — lies on the north bank of the Etowah River, in the valley where the Piedmont meets the Appalachian ridges. Founded around 1000, it had grown by the fourteenth century into a fortified chiefdom: a semicircular palisade and a moat ten feet deep guarded its plazas, some 140 buildings and three great mounds, the tallest rising sixty-three feet above the river. Its elites went to the grave wearing embossed copper plates; traders brought conch shells from the Gulf and mica and copper from the Cumberland plateau, and its armies contended with Moundville for mastery of the Alabama basin. In 1444 the town had passed its first peak but still held the valley within the cycling paramountcy of Coosa.

Hernando de Soto crossed the valley in 1540 and recorded a town called Itaba between Coosa and Ulibahali that was almost certainly Etowah; within a generation epidemics and the collapse of the chiefdoms had emptied it. The Muscogee Creek kept the ruined mounds sacred as Italwa, their foremost ancestral town, and Coweta, leading town of the Lower Creeks and first reported to the English by Henry Woodward in the 1670s, carried that inheritance into the deerskin-trade world of the eighteenth century. Late in that century the Cherokee, retreating before European-American pressure from the east and north, took the Etowah valley from the Creek. Andrew Jackson's victory over the Creeks in 1814 forced open the surrounding country, leaving the old mound lands a borderland between the Cherokee nation and the advancing American frontier.
zh:
埃托瓦在穆斯科格语中写作italwa，意思就是「镇」。它坐落在埃托瓦河北岸、皮德蒙特与阿巴拉契亚山脉相接的河谷中。遗址约始于1000年，到14世纪已发展为设防的酋邦：半圆形木栅和深达十英尺的壕沟环护着广场、约140座建筑和三座大土丘，最高的一座高出河面63英尺。显贵入葬时身佩压花铜片，贸易把墨西哥湾的海螺壳、坎伯兰高原的云母和铜料带到这里，它的军队还与芒德维尔争夺亚拉巴马河流域的霸权。1444年的埃托瓦虽已越过第一个鼎盛期，仍作为库萨势力圈内此消彼长的酋邦据守河谷。

1540年，埃尔南多·德索托穿过这条河谷，记下库萨与乌利巴哈利之间一座叫伊塔巴的城镇，几乎可以肯定就是埃托瓦；此后不到一代人的时间，疫病和酋邦体系的崩溃便使它沦为空城。穆斯科格克里克人把这片废墟视为最重要的祖居之地Italwa，长期供奉；下克里克人的首镇考维塔——1670年代由亨利·伍德沃德首次报告给英国人——也带着这份遗产进入18世纪的鹿皮贸易世界。18世纪末，为躲避东面和北面欧美移民压力而迁徙的切罗基人从克里克人手中夺取埃托瓦河谷。1814年安德鲁·杰克逊击败克里克人，迫使周边土地开放，古老的土丘之地沦为切罗基国与步步进逼的美国边疆之间的边地。

en:
Saluda lies in the piedmont valley of the Saluda River, whose waters run about two hundred miles to join the Broad and form the Congaree on their way to the Santee and the Atlantic. At Saluda Old Town, stamped pottery, a low mound and a plaza mark a farming village of the Temple Mound period, occupied from roughly AD 950 to 1550. In 1444 the river valley was therefore part of the late Mississippian maize-country, linked by fords and trails that later became the Cherokee Path.

A people recorded as the Saluda occupied the Old Town site by the late seventeenth century, possibly a Shawnee band, but they had abandoned it and moved north by 1712. George Hunter mapped the Cherokee Path through this frontier in 1730 as Charles Town traders pushed on to Ninety Six and the Lower Cherokee towns. On 2 July 1755 Governor James Glen met the Cherokee leader Old Hop at the abandoned town; with Attakullakulla, the Little Carpenter, Old Hop acknowledged British sovereignty over Cherokee lands in South Carolina, then estimated at 360,000 square miles. The area was included in Ninety-Six District when it was created on 29 July 1769, and colonial settlers then entered the former frontier. Thomas Chappell established a ferry on the Saluda after the treaty and built a bridge there in 1792; when the bridge was lost in 1800, the river crossing returned to ferry use.
zh:
萨卢达位于萨卢达河的皮德蒙特河谷，河水奔流约二百英里，与布罗德河汇合成康加里河，再经桑蒂河注入大西洋。萨卢达旧城遗址出土的压纹陶器、低矮土丘和广场表明，这里在约950年至1550年间是庙丘时期的农业村落。1444年时，这片河谷仍属于密西西比后期玉米农业地带，河上浅滩和林间小路彼此相连，后来这些道路发展为切罗基商道。

17世纪末，一支被记作萨卢达的人占据旧城遗址，他们可能是肖尼人的一个分支，但到1712年前已放弃这里并向北迁移。1730年，乔治·亨特测绘穿过这片边疆的切罗基商道，查尔斯顿商人沿此前往九十六和切罗基下镇。1755年7月2日，詹姆斯·格伦总督在废城会见切罗基领袖老霍普；老霍普与「小木匠」阿塔库拉一同承认英国对南卡罗来纳境内切罗基土地的主权，当时这些土地估计有36万平方英里。1769年7月29日九十六司法区设立，这片地区被划入区内，殖民者随后进入旧日边疆。条约之后，托马斯·查普尔在萨卢达河上经营渡口，1792年又在当地修建桥梁；桥梁1800年被毁后，渡口重新承担渡河交通。

en:
Cusabo is the low-country coast around Charleston Harbor, where the Ashley, Cooper and Wando rivers meet the Atlantic behind a chain of sea islands. In 1444 the shores and islands belonged to the Kiawah, Etiwan, Kussoe, Stono and related villages later grouped as the Cusabo. Settlers recorded five of these peoples as sharing one language, yet it did not fit the Algonquian, Iroquoian, Muskogean or Siouan families known around them.

Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón's Spanish party visited the coast in 1526. English colonists founded Charles Town at Albemarle Point in 1670 and moved it to the defensible peninsula between the Ashley and Cooper in 1680; by the 1690s it was one of the largest towns in North America. War with the Kussoe broke out in October 1671, and Stono fighting followed in 1674, ending in land cessions and a symbolic deerskin tribute. The Cusabo later served under John Barnwell in the Tuscarora War of 1711-12. Barnwell's 1715 census listed five Cusabo villages with ninety-five men and two hundred women and children, besides a separate Itwan village; in the Yamasee War later that year the Cusabo supported Carolina, after which most survivors joined the Catawba or Muscogee. The port meanwhile drew the Atlantic slave and deerskin trades, and Blackbeard blockaded Charles Town for several days in May 1718 to obtain medicine. On 28 June 1776 William Moultrie's palmetto-log fort on Sullivan's Island repulsed the first British attack, but from 29 March to 12 May 1780 Benjamin Lincoln's garrison surrendered after the long siege that made Charles Town the British base in the South. The royal forces finally evacuated in December 1782, and on 13 August 1783 the town was incorporated as Charleston.
zh:
库萨博是查尔斯顿湾周围的低地海岸，阿什利河、库珀河和万多河在一串海岛后方汇入大西洋。1444年时，沿岸与岛礁属于基亚瓦、埃蒂万、库索、斯托诺及相关村落，后来被统称为库萨博人。殖民者记录其中五个族群使用同一种语言，但这种语言并不符合他们周边已知的阿尔冈昆、易洛魁、马斯科吉或苏语语系。
