1526年，卢卡斯·巴斯克斯·德·艾永的西班牙队伍到访这段海岸。1670年，英国殖民者在阿尔伯马尔角建立查尔斯镇，1680年迁至阿什利河与库珀河之间更易防守的半岛；到1690年代，这里已是北美最大的城镇之一。1671年10月殖民地对库索人开战，1674年又与斯托诺人交战，最终以族群割让土地、缴纳象征臣服的鹿皮贡赋告终。库萨博人后来在1711至1712年随约翰·巴恩韦尔参加图斯卡罗拉战争。巴恩韦尔1715年的人口调查列出五座库萨博村落，有九十五名男子和二百名妇女儿童，另有一座单独的埃蒂万村落；同年亚马西战争爆发，库萨博人支持卡罗来纳，战后多数幸存者投奔卡托巴人或马斯科吉人。与此同时，港口卷入大西洋奴隶贸易和鹿皮贸易，1718年5月黑胡子曾封锁查尔斯镇数日以索取药品。1776年6月28日，威廉·穆尔特里在沙利文岛用棕榈木构筑的要塞击退英军第一次进攻；但1780年3月29日至5月12日，本杰明·林肯所部在长期围城后投降，查尔斯镇成为英军在南方的基地。英军最终于1782年12月撤离，1783年8月13日城镇正式设市并改名查尔斯顿。

en:
Waccamaw is the blackwater coast where the Waccamaw and Great Pee Dee rivers approach the Sampit and Black River before their channels enter Winyah Bay. Waccamaw villages stood on both the Waccamaw and Pee Dee; maize had become the staple of their settled towns after Mississippian influences reached the coast around 1150-1200. In 1444 their canoe routes and village networks met those of the Winyah, Sampit, Sewee, Santee and Pedee, and no European settlement had yet occupied the bay.

Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón's Spanish expedition reached the coast in 1526, the first recorded European intrusion into Waccamaw waters. Eurasian diseases later thinned the people before colonial records fully described them. A Carolina census in 1715 counted 610 Waccamaw, including 210 men. In the Yamasee War that year the Cheraw urged them to fight the English, and warnings from escaped enslaved people helped bring the Waccamaw into the rising; colonists founded the Euaunee trading post in 1716 and reported a hundred warriors four years later. A brief war in 1720 ended with sixty Waccamaw men, women and children killed or captured. Elisha Screven platted Georgetown on Winyah Bay in 1729, and its river lands were turned into indigo and rice plantations worked by enslaved Africans; the Winyah Indigo Society used dues paid in indigo to open a school in 1757. In 1755 Governor James Glen told Catawba chief King Haigler that South Carolina had persuaded the Cheraw, Waccamaw and Pedee to join the Catawba. During the Revolution Francis Marion operated through the nearby swamps and rivers, while Georgetown supplied Nathanael Greene's army. Rice became the district's leading crop in the early nineteenth century.
zh:
沃卡莫是一片黑水河滨海岸，沃卡莫河与大皮迪河流向桑皮特河、布莱克河的水道，最终汇入温亚湾。沃卡莫人的村落同时分布在沃卡莫河与皮迪河畔；约1150至1200年密西西比文化影响沿海后，玉米成为定居城镇的主要作物。1444年时，他们的独木舟航路和村落网络与温亚人、桑皮特人、西维人、桑蒂人和皮迪人相接，欧洲人尚未在湾畔设立定居点。

1526年，卢卡斯·巴斯克斯·德·艾永率领的西班牙远征队抵达这段海岸，这是有记载的欧洲势力第一次进入沃卡莫水域。后来，欧亚大陆传来的疾病在殖民者完整记录他们之前便使人口大减。1715年卡罗来纳人口调查记载沃卡莫人共有610人，其中男子210人。同年亚马西战争中，切罗人劝说他们攻打英国人，逃亡奴隶带来的警报也促使沃卡莫人加入起事；1716年殖民者在尤奥尼设立贸易站，四年后记录有一百名战士。1720年的短暂战争导致六十名沃卡莫男子、妇女和儿童被杀或被俘。1729年，伊莱沙·斯克里文在温亚湾规划乔治敦，河畔土地随后变成由非洲奴隶劳作的靛蓝和水稻种植园；1757年，温亚靛蓝协会用以靛蓝缴纳的会费开办学校。1755年，詹姆斯·格伦总督告知卡托巴酋长海格勒王，南卡罗来纳已劝说切罗人、沃卡莫人和皮迪人加入卡托巴人。独立战争期间，弗朗西斯·马里昂利用附近沼泽与河汊作战，乔治敦则为纳撒内尔·格林的军队提供补给。19世纪初，水稻成为这一地区最重要的作物。

en:
The Yadkin winds more than two hundred miles through the Carolina Piedmont, through a broad valley of oak woods and cane meadows, before joining the Pee Dee; its name comes from a Siouan word perhaps meaning 'place of big trees'. In 1444 its banks held the palisaded corn towns of the Saura and other Catawban-speaking peoples, with the Tutelo and Keyauwee nearby, while the river's Trading Ford carried ancient paths from the Appalachians toward the Chesapeake. The first Europeans to draw near would be the Spaniards of Hernando de Soto and Juan Pardo, who passed through Joara to the west in 1540 and the 1560s.

In 1673 James Needham and Gabriel Arthur, sent from Virginia by Abraham Wood to reach the Tomahittans beyond the Occaneechi middlemen, crossed the Saura towns on the upper Yadkin and the Dan; Needham was murdered by an Occaneechi guide, while Arthur escaped and made his way home in 1674. Around 1710 Seneca raids drove the Saura from the Dan to the Pee Dee, and they were eventually adopted into the Catawba. Scots-Irish and German farmers then poured down the Great Wagon Road: Rowan County was formed in 1753, with Salisbury, at the old trading-path crossing, as its seat. German Moravians had bought 98,985 acres of the Granville District for their Wachovia settlement, and on 17 November 1753 twelve single brethren founded Bethabara, the 'House of Passage', which they stockaded in 1756 when Cherokee raids drove hundreds of refugees to its mill; Bethania followed in 1759 and Salem in 1766. Fort Dobbs, raised on the western frontier in 1756, beat off a Cherokee attack on 27 February 1760. Daniel Boone, whose family had settled on the Yadkin near Mocksville in 1750, married Rebecca Bryan in the valley on 14 August 1756. On 9 May 1771 Benjamin Merrill's Regulators turned back a militia force on the Yadkin that was marching to join Governor Tryon, too late to alter Tryon's victory at Alamance a week later.
zh:
亚德金河在皮德蒙特群山间蜿蜒二百多英里，穿过橡树林和芦苇荡汇成的宽阔谷地，最后注入皮迪河；河名来自苏语，一说意为「大树之地」。1444年，河畔分布着绍拉人等卡托巴语族居民设有栅栏的玉米镇，附近还住着图特罗人和基奥维人；河上的贸易浅滩是古老渡口，内陆小路由此从阿巴拉契亚山脉一直通到切萨皮克。最先逼近这片谷地的欧洲人，是1540年和1560年代取道西边乔阿拉的德·索托与胡安·帕尔多麾下的西班牙人。

1673年，弗吉尼亚人亚伯拉罕·伍德为绕开奥卡内基中间商，派詹姆斯·尼达姆和加布里埃尔·阿瑟前往托马希坦人处，两人穿过亚德金河上游和丹河一带的绍拉城镇；尼达姆被一名奥卡内基向导杀害，阿瑟脱身，于1674年辗转回到弗吉尼亚。1710年前后，塞内卡人的袭击把绍拉人从丹河逼到皮迪河，他们最终并入卡托巴人。此后，苏格兰—爱尔兰裔和德意志农户沿大篷车道源源而来：1753年设立罗安县，索尔兹伯里凭借旧日商路交会处的位置成为县治。德意志摩拉维亚弟兄会在格兰维尔区购下98,985英亩土地，开辟瓦霍维亚居留地；1753年11月17日，十二名单身弟兄建起贝塔巴拉，意为「过路之家」，1756年切罗基人袭扰时他们围起木栅，数百名难民到磨坊旁避难；其后1759年建贝萨尼，1766年建塞勒姆。1756年，西部边疆筑起多布斯堡，并在1760年2月27日击退切罗基人的进攻。布恩一家1750年已迁居莫克斯维尔附近的亚德金河畔，丹尼尔·布恩1756年8月14日在谷中娶了丽贝卡·布赖恩。1771年5月9日，本杰明·梅里尔率领的规约者在亚德金河畔截回一支正赶去与特赖恩总督会合的民兵，但一周后已挡不住总督在阿拉曼斯取胜。

en:
The Waxhaws, a rolling stretch of piedmont meadows and cane brakes on the upper Catawba, took their name from the small Siouan people who lived there—the Wysacky of some writers—kin by language and marriage to the Catawba and Wateree. Their villages stood in the rich creek bottoms along what is now the North–South Carolina border, where women worked the cornfields and hunters took deer on the oak savanna. In 1444 this was still unvisited border country; the first European to meet the Waxhaw was the Spaniard Juan Pardo, who passed the region on his marches inland in the 1560s.

In 1711 twenty-seven Waxhaw warriors under their own Captain Jack marched with John Barnwell's South Carolina army against the Tuscarora, wading through a swamp to storm Fort Narhontes; early in February 1712 the company slipped away to sell the slaves it had taken. The Waxhaw joined the Yamasee confederacy when it rose in 1715, and after the Carolinians broke the rising the Catawba made peace and turned on their kinsmen, destroying the Waxhaw as a tribe; the survivors merged with the Cheraw or followed the Yamasee south. Their empty lands drew Scots-Irish and German farmers down the Great Wagon Road, and on 15 March 1767 Andrew Jackson was born here to newly arrived Scots-Irish parents—just which side of the future state line was long disputed. On 29 May 1780 Banastre Tarleton's British Legion overtook Colonel Abraham Buford's Virginians in the Waxhaws and the killing went on after the first offers of surrender, leaving 113 dead. The cry of 'Tarleton's quarter' swept the backcountry and swelled the patriot ranks for the rest of the war.
zh:
瓦克斯霍是一片起伏的皮德蒙特丘陵地，草甸连绵、芦苇丛生，地处卡托巴河上游，地名来自住在这里的苏语小部落——有的文献称他们维萨基人，语言和姻亲都与卡托巴人、沃特里人相近。他们的村落坐落在今南北卡州界一带肥沃的溪边洼地上，妇女种玉米，猎人在橡树稀树草原上猎鹿。1444年，这里还是外人未至的边地；第一个接触到瓦克斯霍人的欧洲人，是1560年代内陆远征途中经过此地的西班牙人胡安·帕尔多。

1711年，27名瓦克斯霍战士在自己的杰克上尉率领下，随约翰·巴恩韦尔的南卡军队出征图斯卡罗拉人，涉过沼泽攻下纳洪茨堡；1712年2月初，这队人不辞而别，去卖掉掳来的奴隶。1715年雅马西联盟起兵，瓦克斯霍人加入其中；卡罗来纳人镇压起义后，卡托巴人议和并反过来攻打这支亲族，把瓦克斯霍部落彻底打散，幸存者或并入绍拉（切罗）人，或随雅马西人南迁。空置下来的土地引来沿大篷车道南下的苏格兰—爱尔兰裔和德意志农户；1767年3月15日，安德鲁·杰克逊就出生在这里的新移民家庭——他究竟生在后来的州界哪一边，长期争论不休。1780年5月29日，巴纳斯特·塔尔顿的英军军团在瓦克斯霍追上亚伯拉罕·布福德上校的弗吉尼亚部队，最初的投降请求也没让杀戮停止，共有113人丧命。「塔尔顿的饶命」一说传遍山乡，此后投身爱国者阵营的边民源源不断。

en:
The lower reaches of the Cape Fear River, opening under the treacherous Frying Pan Shoals, were known to their native people as Chicora. The small Cape Fear Indians, whose language was probably Siouan, planted riverside fields around villages such as Necoes, took fish and oysters from the estuary, and carried deerskins through the longleaf-pine forests that met the coast. In 1444 these were quiet, uncharted waters; the first European to sight the headland, Giovanni da Verrazzano sailing for France, would not make landfall until 1 March 1524.

In 1585 Richard Grenville's fleet, bound for Roanoke, was embayed behind the headland, and the crew's fear of wrecking gave Cape Fear its English name. William Hilton traded here in 1662, and Barbadian planters planted Charles Towne on the west bank in 1664, but war with the Cape Fear people over the Indian slave trade, followed by the great hurricane of 1667, emptied the settlement by year's end; the colonists' next venture became Charleston, far to the south. A census found only 206 Cape Fear Indians in 1715, and the survivors drifted up the Pee Dee before settling inland from Charleston. Brunswick Town, founded in 1726, was the first lasting settlement, while Wilmington, laid out at the river fork in 1732 and named in 1739 for the Earl of Wilmington, became the chief port for the pitch, tar and turpentine of the pine woods; by 1767 enslaved Africans made up more than three fifths of the lower Cape Fear. Stamp Act crowds made the stamp agent resign in 1765 and stopped river shipping rather than clear vessels on stamped paper, and on 27 February 1776 patriot militia scattered a loyalist Highland charge at Moore's Creek Bridge, eighteen miles above Wilmington. Brunswick Town was burned in a British raid that same year and never rebuilt.
zh:
开普菲尔河下游在凶险的煎锅浅滩旁入海，这一带在当地原住民口中叫奇科拉。人数不多的开普菲尔印第安人语言可能属苏语族，他们在尼科兹等村落旁的河畔田里耕作，在河口湾捕鱼采蚝，又穿过与海岸相连的长叶松林贩运鹿皮。1444年的河口风平浪静，也不见于任何欧洲地图；第一个望见这座岬角的欧洲人——为法兰西效力的乔瓦尼·达·韦拉扎诺——要到1524年3月1日才在此登陆。

1585年，前往罗阿诺克的理查德·格伦维尔船队被困在岬角内侧，船员惧怕沉船，海角的英文名 Cape Fear（意为「恐惧角」）由此而来。威廉·希尔顿1662年到此贸易，巴巴多斯种植园主1664年在西岸建起查尔斯城，却因英国人贩卖印第安奴隶而与开普菲尔人开战，又逢1667年大飓风，到年底定居点已无人存留；殖民者再往南尝试，建起了远处的查尔斯顿。1715年的人口调查只点到206名开普菲尔人，幸存者沿皮迪河而上，最终在查尔斯顿以北的内陆落脚。1726年建立的布伦瑞克镇是第一处存续下来的定居点；威尔明顿1732年在河汊处开辟，1739年以威尔明顿伯爵的封号得名，成为松林沥青、焦油和松节油的主要输出港，到1767年，被奴役的非洲人已占下开普菲尔人口的五分之三以上。1765年，抗议印花税的人群逼印花税官辞职，宁可让河上航运停摆，也不用贴了印花的文件为船只清关。1776年2月27日，爱国者民兵在威尔明顿以北十八英里的穆尔溪桥击溃效忠派高地人的冲锋；布伦瑞克镇同年在英军突袭中被焚毁，再未重建。

en:
Roanoke Island, set between the Albemarle and Croatan sounds behind the Outer Banks, was the heart of a Carolina Algonquian world: the Roanoke on the island, the Chowanoke and Weapemeoc on the mainland rivers. Their cedar-bark palisaded towns stood beside cornfields and fish weirs, and Wanchese on the island's south end had served as a seasonal fishing station for fifteen hundred years. Canoes linked the sounds in trade, while kinship and occasional war tied the villages to the Tuscarora of the interior. In 1444 nothing on these shores yet foreshadowed the English.

In 1584 Philip Amadas and Arthur Barlowe, sent by Walter Raleigh, landed on the island and claimed it for England as Virginia. Ralph Lane built a fort there in 1585, but short supplies and bad relations with the Roanoke led him to evacuate with Francis Drake in 1586. A second party under John White arrived in 1587; White's granddaughter Virginia Dare, born on 18 August, was the first English child born in an American English colony, and when White at last returned in 1590 the settlers had vanished, leaving only the word CROATOAN carved on a post. Virginians began taking up the Albemarle shore in the 1650s, and George Durant bought land there in 1662; in 1677 the settlers rose against the proprietors' customs officers in Culpeper's Rebellion. The Tuscarora War of 1711-13 made the sounds a battleground, where the Chowanoke and Tom Blount's northern Tuscarora sided with the English, and the treaty of 1718 settled the remaining Tuscarora on a reserve on the Roanoke River in Bertie County. The town laid out on Queen Anne's Creek in 1712 became Edenton in 1722 and served as the young province's capital until 1743; in 1774 fifty-one of its women, led by Penelope Barker, signed the tea boycott remembered as the Edenton Tea Party.
zh:
罗阿诺克岛坐落于阿尔伯马尔湾与克罗阿坦湾之间，外有外滩群岛为屏障，是卡罗来纳阿尔冈昆世界的中心：岛上住着罗阿诺克人，大陆各河畔住着乔瓦诺克人和维佩米奥克人。他们的城镇以雪松树皮盖屋、围以栅栏，旁边是玉米地和鱼梁；岛南端的万切斯作为季节性渔村已有一千五百年之久。独木舟在各海湾间往来贸易，姻亲关系与不时发生的战事又把这些村落和内陆的图斯卡罗拉人连在一起。1444年的海岸上，还没有任何英格兰人将至的迹象。

1584年，沃尔特·雷利派出的菲利普·阿马达斯和阿瑟·巴洛登上罗阿诺克岛，以英格兰的名义将其领有，称作弗吉尼亚。1585年拉尔夫·莱恩在岛上筑起要塞，但补给不足、又与罗阿诺克人交恶，1586年随弗朗西斯·德雷克撤离。第二批移民由约翰·怀特率领，1587年抵达；怀特的外孙女弗吉尼亚·戴尔于8月18日出生，是在英格兰人的美洲殖民地出生的第一个英格兰婴儿。怀特1590年终于返回时，移民已不知所终，只在一根木桩上刻着「CROATOAN」（克罗阿坦）。1650年代起，弗吉尼亚人陆续到阿尔伯马尔湾岸定居，乔治·杜兰特1662年在此购地；1677年，殖民者又起事反对业主政府的海关官员，史称卡尔佩珀暴动。1711至1713年的图斯卡罗拉战争把各海湾变成战场，乔瓦诺克人与汤姆·布朗特率领的北部图斯卡罗拉人站在英格兰一边；1718年的和约把余下的图斯卡罗拉人安置在罗阿诺克河畔伯蒂县的保留地上。1712年在安妮女王溪畔开辟的城镇1722年定名伊登顿，并作为这个年轻省份的首府直到1743年；1774年，镇上51名妇女在佩内洛普·巴克带领下签署抵制英茶的倡议书，即「伊登顿茶会」。

en:
Tutelo country is the mountain headwater land of southwest Virginia: the upper Roanoke where the Staunton and Dan rivers join, the gorges of the New River, and the Big Sandy beyond the Allegheny ridges. The Tutelo spoke an eastern Siouan tongue close to those of their Monacan and Manahoac kinsmen, built their towns on river terraces, and buried their dead in earthen mounds. In 1444 these high valleys were a crossing of mountain Indian roads, with the Monacan to the east and the closely related Saponi beside them.

In 1671 the Batts and Fallam expedition, sent out by Abraham Wood, noted 'Totero Town' on the upper Roanoke near where Salem later stood, and crossed the divide to the New River, the first Virginians to push beyond it. Within a few years Iroquois raids drove the Tutelo onto islands at the Roanoke forks above the Occaneechi, where they joined the Saponi; by 1701 they had withdrawn to the headwaters of the Yadkin in North Carolina. In 1714 they settled under Virginia's protection near Fort Christanna, and the 1722 Treaty of Albany ended the Iroquois attacks. In the 1730s they moved to Shamokin in Pennsylvania under the Oneida overseer Shickellamy, and in 1753 they were formally adopted by the Cayuga and built Coreorgonel below Cayuga Lake. The town was burned by Sullivan's expedition in 1779; the Tutelo followed the Cayuga to the Grand River in Canada, where 75 of them were counted in 1785.
zh:
图特洛人的家园是弗吉尼亚西南部的山地河源地带：斯汤顿河与丹河汇流成罗阿诺克河的上游、新河的峡谷，以及阿勒格尼山脊以西的大桑迪河流域。图特洛人操一支东苏语方言，与亲族莫纳坎人和马纳霍克人的语言相近；他们把村镇建在河流阶地上，将死者葬入土丘坟冢。1444年，这些高山河谷是山间印第安小路的交汇之地，莫纳坎人居于其东，语言相通的萨波尼人紧邻其侧。

1671年，受亚伯拉罕·伍德派遣的巴茨与法勒姆远征队在罗阿诺克河上游、后来塞勒姆兴起之处记下「托特罗镇」，并越过分水岭抵达新河，是首批跨过分水岭西进的弗吉尼亚人。几年之内，易洛魁人的袭击把图特洛人逼到罗阿诺克河汇流处的岛上，与萨波尼人同居于奥卡尼奇人之地的北缘；到1701年，他们已退至北卡罗来纳的亚德金河源头。1714年他们受弗吉尼亚保护定居在克里斯蒂安娜堡附近，1722年的《奥尔巴尼条约》结束了易洛魁人的攻击。1730年代他们迁往宾夕法尼亚的沙莫金，归附奥奈达管理人希基拉米，1753年被卡尤加人正式接纳，在卡尤加湖畔建起科雷奥戈内尔村。该村在1779年毁于沙利文远征军，图特洛人随后随卡尤加人前往加拿大的格兰德河，1785年当地册得图特洛人75名。

en:
The Moratuc, usually counted as Algonquian speakers, lived on the middle Roanoke River, which bore their name. In 1444 they farmed its bottomlands and fished its weirs, unvisited by Europeans. In March 1586 their representatives sat with the Chowanoke, Mangoak and Weapemeoc at Choanoac when Ralph Lane's armed party from Roanoke surprised the gathering and carried off the Chowanoke chief Menatonon. His son Skiko told the English of Chaunis Temoatan, a land to the west rich in copper, and Lane led forty men roughly a hundred miles up the Moratuc; but Pemisapan had warned the river villages, and they stood empty and stripped of food, so the expedition returned half-starved.

After the Tuscarora War of 1711-1715, planters pushed up the Roanoke and founded Halifax at the head of navigation in 1757. On 12 April 1776 North Carolina's provincial congress met there and adopted the Halifax Resolves, the first official call by an American colony for independence.
zh:
莫拉托克（中文维基译作「莫拉图克」）人通常被归为阿尔冈昆语族群，住在罗阿诺克河中游——这条河当时便叫莫拉托克河。1444年，他们在河畔低地种玉米、靠鱼堰捕鱼，从未见过欧洲人。1586年3月，拉尔夫·莱恩率罗阿诺克的武装队伍突袭乔阿诺阿克的集会，莫拉托克代表正与乔瓦诺克、曼戈阿克、韦阿佩梅奥克等部聚首，乔瓦诺克首领梅纳托农被掳走。其子斯基科称西方有个盛产铜的「Chaunis Temoatan」，莱恩便带四十人溯莫拉托克河而上约一百英里；但佩米萨潘已事先通报，沿岸村镇人去粮空，探险队饥困而返。

1711至1715年塔斯卡洛拉战争后，种植园主沿罗阿诺克河上迁，1757年在通航起点建立哈利法克斯。1776年4月12日，北卡罗来纳省议会在此通过《哈利法克斯决议》，这是英属北美殖民地第一份正式要求独立的文件。

en:
The peninsula between the Rappahannock and Potomac rivers was Algonquian country. The Rappahannock held thirteen villages along their river from their chief town Topahanocke, while on the upper Potomac the Doeg kept their capital Tauxenent, with a hamlet at the place later called Quantico; both peoples grew corn, fished the tidal creeks and dealt in shell beads. In 1444 these were independent villages of the coastal Algonquian world, untouched by Europeans.

Colonists began patenting the Northern Neck in the 1650s. In 1651 the dying Rappahannock weroance Accopatough deeded them land east of Totuskey Creek; his successor Taweeren was killed in a colonial brawl in 1654, the reserve set out in 1653 was narrowed in 1662, and by 1669 the tribe had withdrawn to the Mattaponi headwaters. In July 1675 a Doeg raiding party crossed the Potomac and took hogs from the planter Thomas Mathew, whom they accused of withholding payment; the colonists' pursuit killed Doeg and innocent Susquehannock alike, Mathew's son and two servants died in the reprisal, and Nathaniel Bacon's militia swept into Maryland and besieged the Susquehannock - the spark of Bacon's Rebellion in 1676. A Doguetown still sheltered Doeg near Portobago in 1720.
zh:
拉帕汉诺克河与波托马克河之间的半岛是阿尔冈昆人的土地。拉帕汉诺克人沿河拥有十三座村庄，多格人则住在波托马克河上游，在后来得名匡蒂科的地方有其村落；两族都种玉米、在潮汐溪捕鱼、以贝珠交易。1444年，这些都是沿海阿尔冈昆世界里独立自主的村庄，欧洲人尚未到来。

1650年代，殖民者开始在北内克半岛申领土地。1651年，拉帕汉诺克老首领临终前立约，把河东土地让给殖民者；继任首领1654年在与殖民者的冲突中被杀，1653年划定的保留地1662年又遭压缩，到1669年部落已退往马塔波尼河源头。1675年7月，一队多格人渡过波托马克河，从拖欠货款的种植园主托马斯·马修家赶走猪群；殖民者追击时不分青红皂白杀了多格人和无辜的萨斯奎汉诺克人，报复中马修之子和两名仆人丧命，纳撒尼尔·培根的民团随即攻入马里兰围攻萨斯奎汉诺克人，这便是1676年培根起义的导火索。迟至1720年，这一带仍有一个名为「多格镇」的多格人聚落。

en:
Calicula covers the upper Monongahela, a river whose Lenape name describes banks that slip and fall into the water. From the West Fork and Tygart Valley it runs north through forested ridges toward the forks at Pittsburgh. From about 1050 the Monongahela culture built ordered villages of up to fifty or a hundred structures, raised maize in the bottoms and traded stone, shell and other goods through neighboring networks. In 1444 its people still lived beyond direct European contact, their river linking hill villages with the wider Ohio world.

The Monongahela villages disappeared in the 1620s or 1630s, most likely under the combined pressure of epidemic disease, droughts and raids as rival nations fought for fur-country hunting grounds. The upper valley then became a march between Native warriors, French claim and Virginia expansion. After Britain's victory in 1763, Zackquill and David Morgan entered the country about 1767; Zackquill built Fort Morgan in 1772, and in 1774 frightened families crowded into refuge forts while at least a hundred blockhouses and palisades stood across the Monongahela valley. Virginia formed Monongalia County in 1776, and the assembly marked out fifty acres for Morgan's Town in October 1785. In 1817 Pennsylvania chartered the Monongahela Navigation Company, beginning the locks and dams that would carry bituminous coal downstream.
zh:
卡利库拉覆盖莫农加希拉河上游。河名来自莱纳佩语，形容河岸不断坍塌滑入水中。莫农加希拉河由西支流与泰加特谷支流汇合后，穿过林木葱郁的山脊向北流向匹兹堡河口。约1050年起，莫农加希拉文化居民在此建起布局整齐的村落，最大者有五十至一百座建筑，在河洲上种植玉米，并通过邻近网络交换石器、贝壳和其他货物。1444年时，他们仍未与欧洲人直接接触，这条河把丘陵村落与更广阔的俄亥俄世界连接起来。

莫农加希拉人的村落于1620年代或1630年代消失，最可能是疫病、干旱和战争共同压迫的结果；当时各部族为控制毛皮贸易猎场彼此攻伐。此后上游河谷成为原住民战士、法国领属主张和弗吉尼亚扩张之间的边地。英国1763年获胜后，扎奎尔·摩根与戴维·摩根约在1767年进入此地，扎奎尔于1772年修建摩根堡；1774年，受惊的家庭纷纷躲入避难要塞，仅莫农加希拉河谷就有至少一百座木屋碉堡和木栅。弗吉尼亚于1776年设立莫农加利亚县，1785年10月议会划出五十英亩土地建立摩根镇。1817年，宾夕法尼亚特许成立莫农加希拉航运公司，开始修建船闸与水坝，烟煤此后得以顺水运往下游。

en:
The Manahoac country is the northern Virginia piedmont above the falls of the Rappahannock, the wooded upland between the Fall Line and the Blue Ridge through which the Rappahannock and its Rapidan branch run. Its people were a loose confederacy of Siouan-speaking bands — Mahaskahod below the meeting of the two rivers, Hassinunga at the forks, Stegara farthest upstream — perhaps a thousand strong in all. They were leagued with their Monacan kinsmen to the south, at war with the Powhatan below the falls and with the Iroquois raiders who came from beyond the Potomac. In 1444 the falls still closed their hill country to every stranger from the coast.

In 1608 John Smith met a large Manahoac party above the Rappahannock falls and recorded their seven villages. In 1656 their bowmen, with the Nahyssan and a mountain people called the Richahhecrian, defeated Virginia militia and their Pamunkey allies at the Battle of Bloody Run, where the Pamunkey leader Totopotomoi was slain. Beaver Wars raids and disease did the rest: a count in 1669 found only fifty bowmen left, and when John Lederer crossed the emptied country in 1671 the Seneca already claimed it as their hunting ground. Survivors joined the Monacan and then the Tutelo-Saponi; a Stegaraki band appeared at Fort Christanna in 1714, and the Ontponea were last heard of in 1723. After 1728 the name Manahoac vanishes from the records.
zh:
马纳霍克人的家园在拉帕汉诺克河瀑布线以上的弗吉尼亚北部皮德蒙特，即瀑布线与蓝岭山脉之间林木覆盖的丘陵，拉帕汉诺克河与其支流拉皮丹河穿流其间。他们是若干操苏语部落组成的松散联盟——两河汇流处下方的马哈斯卡霍德、居于河口的哈西宁加、位置最靠上游的斯特加拉——总人口约有一千。他们与南方的亲族莫纳坎人结盟，一面同瀑布以下的波瓦坦人交战，一面抵御波托马克河以北来袭的易洛魁人。1444年，瀑布仍把海岸方向的一切外来者挡在这片山地之外。

1608年，约翰·史密斯在拉帕汉诺克河瀑布上方遇到一大群马纳霍克人，记下了他们的七座村镇。1656年，他们的弓箭手会同纳赫桑人和一支被称为里卡赫克里安的山地部族，在血溪之战中击败弗吉尼亚民兵及其帕蒙基盟军，帕蒙基首领托托波托莫伊战死。海狸战争的袭击和疫病完成了余下的打击：1669年的一次人口清点只找到五十名弓箭手；1671年约翰·莱德勒穿过这片已无村落的土地时，塞内卡人已把它称作自己的猎场。幸存者先后投奔莫纳坎人和图特洛－萨波尼人；一支斯特加拉基人1714年还出现在克里斯蒂安娜堡，翁特波尼亚人最后一次见载是1723年。1728年以后，「马纳霍克」之名便从记载中消失了。

en:
Patawomac is the upper Potomac highland country, where the North and South Branch valleys run between Allegheny ridges and Wills Creek opens a route toward the later site of Cumberland. River fords and trails such as the Great Indian Warpath linked these hills with the Susquehanna, Shenandoah, Monongahela, and Ohio countries. In 1444 no colonial boundary crossed the mountains; Susquehannock, Piscataway, Delaware, and other Native parties used the valleys as hunting, trading, and war paths rather than as the site of a permanent European town.

John Smith entered and mapped the Potomac in 1608, but the upper country remained a Native travel corridor for generations. Thomas Cresap established a trading post near Wills Creek a few years before 1754, and with the Delaware chief Nemacolin he improved a path across the Alleghenies to Redstone Creek on the Monongahela. Maryland militia built Fort Mount Pleasant at the creek's mouth in autumn 1754 and renamed it Fort Cumberland in 1755. The post became the westernmost British outpost in North America and the base for Edward Braddock's 1755 march against Fort Duquesne; after Braddock's defeat and death on 9 July, George Washington brought the survivors back. The fort supplied the Continental Army and held British prisoners from about 1778. The Patowmack navigation works begun in 1785 were completed in 1802 to link the Tidewater with Cumberland, and work on the Cumberland Road west toward the Ohio began in 1811.
zh:
波托马克是波托马克河上游高地，北支流与南支流的河谷穿行于阿利根尼群山之间，威尔斯溪则在后来坎伯兰所在地打开一条通道。河上徒涉点和「大印第安战道」等小径把这些山地同萨斯奎汉纳、谢南多厄、莫农加希拉和俄亥俄方向连接起来。1444年时，还没有殖民地边界越过群山；萨斯奎汉诺克人、皮斯卡塔韦人、特拉华人及其他原住民群体把这些河谷当作狩猎、贸易和征战通道，这里并非欧洲人的永久城镇所在地。

约翰·史密斯1608年进入并测绘波托马克河，但上游高地在此后许多代里仍是原住民的通行走廊。1754年前几年，托马斯·克雷萨普在威尔斯溪附近设立贸易站，并与特拉华酋长内马科林一起拓宽一条穿越阿利根尼山脉、通往莫农加希拉河雷德斯通溪的小路。1754年秋，马里兰民兵在溪口修建芒特普莱森特堡，1755年改名坎伯兰堡。该据点成为英国在北美最西端的前哨，也是爱德华·布雷多克1755年进军迪凯纳堡的基地；7月9日布雷多克战败身亡后，乔治·华盛顿率残部退回这里。约1778年起，这座堡垒为大陆军提供补给，并关押英国战俘。1785年开工的波托马克航运工程于1802年完成，用以连接潮水带与坎伯兰；通往西方俄亥俄方向的坎伯兰大道则于1811年动工。

en:
Nentego was the Nanticokes' own name, meaning 'Tidewater People'. The province covers the lower Nanticoke River and the marshy creeks of Maryland's Eastern Shore, where the tidal river runs into Tangier Sound and Chesapeake Bay. Algonquian-speaking Nanticoke chiefdoms, among them the Wicomoco, Monie, and Manokin, kept riverside villages and exchanged goods across the bay; Chicacone, on the site of later Vienna, was their largest settlement. In 1444 canoes moved between fishing weirs, hunting grounds, and shellfish shallows, with the river itself serving as the chief road through the country.

John Smith sailed up the Nanticoke in 1608, mapped the river, and visited Chicacone. Beaver pelts drew the Nanticoke into trade and alliance with the English, but Maryland's expansion soon followed. Their leader Unnacokasimon signed a peace treaty in 1668, and in 1684 the colony defined a reservation between Chicacoan Creek and the Nanticoke. Vienna was founded in 1706 and grew on river trade, shipbuilding, and tobacco. The Nanticoke bought 3,000 acres on Broad Creek in 1707; after an intertribal gathering was broken up by the British in 1742, many left Chicacone, gained Iroquois permission in 1744 to settle along the Susquehanna and Juniata, and Maryland dissolved the remaining reserve in 1768-69. During the American Revolution, British raiders struck Vienna, while Nanticoke allies of Britain moved north to Fort Niagara in 1778.
zh:
嫩特戈是楠蒂科克人的自称，意为「潮水之人」。这片地区位于马里兰东岸的楠蒂科克河下游及多沼泽的河溪地带，感潮河道由此流入坦吉尔湾和切萨皮克湾。说阿尔冈昆语的楠蒂科克各酋邦——包括威科米科、莫尼和马诺金——在河畔设立村落，并在海湾内外交换物产；最大的聚落位于后来维也纳镇所在之处。1444年时，独木舟穿行于鱼梁、猎场和盛产贝类的浅水之间，河流本身就是穿越此地的主要道路。

约翰·史密斯1608年驶入楠蒂科克河，测绘河道并访问最大聚落。海狸皮贸易把楠蒂科克人带入与英国人的贸易和同盟，但马里兰的扩张随之而来。其首领乌纳科卡西蒙1668年签订和约，殖民地又于1684年在奇卡科恩溪与楠蒂科克河之间划定保留地。维也纳镇建于1706年，依靠河运、造船和烟草发展。楠蒂科克人1707年在布罗德溪购得三千英亩土地；1742年一次跨部落集会被英国人驱散后，许多人离开最大聚落，1744年获易洛魁许可，迁往萨斯奎汉纳河与朱尼亚塔河一带，马里兰则在1768—1769年取消剩余保留地。美国独立战争期间，英国袭击者进攻维也纳；与英国结盟的楠蒂科克人也在1778年向北迁往尼亚加拉堡。

en: The forested headwaters of the Ohio above the falls, ridges and bottomlands spanning later eastern Ohio, western Pennsylvania and West Virginia, were the country remembered in French records as Oniasont or Honniasontkeronon. In 1444 its people lived within the Fort Ancient and Monongahela world of palisaded villages, maize fields, hunting paths and ridge trails; their language may have been Iroquoian, but the record is too thin to say more. European goods reached the upper valley through Native routes after 1550, before epidemics and the Beaver Wars emptied many settlements. In 1669 La Salle heard at Montreal of Honniasontkeronon and Shawnee villages above the Ohio falls. After that the name disappears, as Haudenosaunee, Lenape and Shawnee resettlement reshaped the Allegheny frontier.
zh: 俄亥俄瀑布以上的林木河源，即日后分属俄亥俄东部、宾夕法尼亚西部和西弗吉尼亚的山脊与河谷低地，在法国记录中称作奥尼亚松特或奥尼亚松特克农。1444年，这里的人处于弗特安蒂恩与莫农加希拉世界之中，有木栅村落、玉米田、猎道和山路；他们的语言可能属易洛魁语系，但史料太少，无法断定。1550年后，欧洲货物已通过原住民商路进入上游河谷，疫病和海狸战争随后使许多聚落荒废。1669年，拉萨尔在蒙特利尔听说俄亥俄瀑布以上有奥尼亚松特克农人和肖尼人的村落。此后这个名字消失，豪德诺索尼、莱纳佩和肖尼人的迁居重塑了阿勒格尼边地。

en:
Onojutta is the mountain valley of the Juniata, a shallow river that cuts through Tuscarora and Jacks Mountain before joining the Susquehanna. In 1444 the Onojutta-Haga, an Iroquoian people closely connected with the Susquehannock, lived along the river and its creeks. Their villages used the fertile bottomlands for corn and the water gaps as trails and hunting corridors. The river name later recorded as Onayutta, meaning 'Standing Stone', belonged to this country long before European traders reached it.

Little is recorded of the Onojutta-Haga before 1648, by which year they had become forced auxiliaries of the Susquehannock; when that power was broken and dispersed, the Juniata bands were probably absorbed with them. The valley was later used and settled by Lenape, until Pennsylvania land treaties opened the country east of the Allegheny Ridge to colonial farmers. In 1755 and 1756, during the French and Indian War, Lenape and Shawnee warriors based at Kittanning raided the new settlements and carried off captives. Fort Granville, near present Lewistown, was burned in 1756, and in September Lieutenant Colonel John Armstrong led Pennsylvania's retaliation that destroyed Kittanning. For a time the Juniata remained a hard military frontier rather than a secure farming valley.
zh:
奥诺朱塔是朱尼亚塔河流经的山地河谷；这条水浅的河流切过图斯卡罗拉山和杰克斯山，最后汇入萨斯奎哈纳河。1444年，与萨斯奎汉诺克人关系密切、操易洛魁语的奥诺朱塔-哈加（Onojutta-Haga）人沿河溪两岸而居。他们的村落利用肥沃低地种植玉米，并把水口当作步道和狩猎通道。后来被记作Onayutta、意为「立石」的河名，早在欧洲商人抵达前便属于这片土地。

1648年以前，奥诺朱塔-哈加人的记载很少；到1648年，他们已成为萨斯奎汉诺克人的被迫辅助者。萨斯奎汉诺克势力被击溃并离散后，朱尼亚塔诸部很可能也一同被吸收。谷地后来由莱纳佩人使用和定居，直到宾夕法尼亚的土地条约把阿勒格尼岭以东开放给殖民农民。1755年至1756年法国-印第安人战争期间，以基坦宁为基地的莱纳佩人和肖尼人战士袭击新定居点并掳走居民。1756年，今刘易斯敦附近的格兰维尔堡被焚毁；同年9月，约翰·阿姆斯特朗中校率领宾州报复部队摧毁基坦宁。此后一段时间，朱尼亚塔仍是严酷的军事边疆，而不是安全的农垦河谷。

en:
Atrakwaye was the principal town of the Akhrakouaeronon, a Susquehannock people whose villages stood on the east side of the Susquehanna just below the West Branch. In the late fifteenth century Susquehannock hamlets also extended up the North Branch; their people farmed maize, beans and squash on the river flats, hunted the surrounding ridges and palisaded their towns against raiders. In 1444 European traders had not yet entered the valley, and its grain and furs moved along Indigenous trails and canoe routes. John Smith's 1608 map later marked the place as Quadroque.

Smith's Susquehannock contacts in 1608 opened the valley to written European record. From the 1620s beaver pelts went to Virginia, New Netherland and New Sweden in exchange for metal tools, kettles and firearms. Maryland made peace with the Susquehannock in 1652, but epidemics and Haudenosaunee attacks broke their power; after the siege on Piscataway Creek in 1675, the survivors scattered or were absorbed. The old river junction became Shamokin, a Delaware, Seneca and Tutelo settlement occupied from 1727 to 1756, where the Oneida leader Shikellamy lived until his death in 1748. Pennsylvania built Fort Augusta there in 1756-1757, laid out Sunbury and created Northumberland County in 1772, and sheltered thousands of West Branch refugees there during the Great Runaway of 1778.
zh:
阿特拉夸耶是阿赫拉克瓦埃罗农人的主城。这支萨斯奎汉诺克人的村落位于萨斯奎哈纳河东岸、西支汇口稍下处。15世纪后期，萨斯奎汉诺克人的小村还沿北支延伸；人们在河畔低地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在周围山岭狩猎，并在城镇外竖立木栅抵御袭击者。1444年时，欧洲商人尚未进入这条河谷，谷物和毛皮只沿原住民小径与独木舟路线流通。约翰·史密斯1608年的地图后来把此地标为夸德罗克。

1608年，约翰·史密斯与萨斯奎汉诺克人接触，河谷开始进入欧洲文字记载。1620年代起，河狸皮被运往弗吉尼亚、新尼德兰和新瑞典，换回金属工具、铜锅和火器。马里兰1652年同萨斯奎汉诺克人议和，但疫病和易洛魁联盟的攻击摧毁了他们的力量；1675年皮斯卡塔韦溪之围后，幸存者四散或被吸收。旧河口后来成为沙莫金，1727至1756年间是特拉华人、塞内卡人和图特洛人的聚落，奥奈达领袖希克拉米在此居住，1748年去世。宾州1756至1757年在此修建奥古斯塔堡，1772年规划森伯里并设立诺森伯兰县；1778年「大逃亡」期间，数千名西支难民又到这座要塞避难。

en:
Espachomy was the Esopus country on the west bank of the Hudson, where Rondout Creek and fertile river flats supported Munsee Lenape villages, fishing places and cornfields. Trails linked the river landings with hunting grounds in the woods and hills to the northwest. In 1444 this was Esopus land rather than a European colony: its inhabitants moved between planted valleys and hunting camps, and no Dutch fort yet commanded the Hudson landing.

Henry Hudson's voyage in 1609 opened the region to Dutch traders, who built a post at the mouth of Rondout Creek in 1614 before the Esopus destroyed it. Settlers returned in 1652, were driven out, and in 1658 Peter Stuyvesant concentrated them in the stockaded village of Wiltwyck, chartered in 1661. The First Esopus War ran from 20 September 1659 to 15 July 1660 after settlers fired on Esopus workers paid with brandy. On 7 June 1663, Esopus warriors entered Wiltwyck pretending to sell produce while others destroyed Nieu Dorp, later Hurley; they burned much of Wiltwyck and carried off women and children. Reinforced from New Amsterdam and guided by Mohawk allies, Dutch forces burned the Esopus fields and took their upland stronghold in early September, killing the Esopus chief. New Netherland passed to England in September 1664; Richard Nicolls made a peace treaty with the Esopus in 1665, and Wiltwyck was renamed Kingston in 1669. The opened lands later drew French Huguenot settlers to New Paltz. In 1777 Kingston briefly served as the first capital of New York State, George Clinton was inaugurated there on 30 July, and British troops burned the town on 16 October. Kingston was incorporated as a village in 1805, its sloops carrying Hudson Valley grain toward New York.
zh:
埃斯帕丘米（即埃索普斯人的土地）位于哈德逊河西岸，龙多特溪与肥沃的河滨阶地支撑着芒西-莱纳佩人的村落、渔场和玉米地。各条步道把河畔渡口同西北林地与丘陵中的猎场连接起来。1444年，这里仍是埃索普斯人的土地，而不是欧洲殖民地；居民往来于河谷农田和猎营之间，哈德逊河畔还没有受荷兰人控制的堡垒。

1609年亨利·哈德逊的航行使这一地区向荷兰商人敞开。1614年，荷兰人在龙多特溪口设立贸易站，但很快被埃索普斯人捣毁。1652年移民重返此地，又被驱逐；1658年，彼得·斯泰弗森特把移民集中到一座栅栏设防的村落，该村于1661年获得特许状。第一次埃索普斯战争始于移民向领取白兰地作为工酬的埃索普斯工人开枪，从1659年9月20日持续到1660年7月15日。1663年6月7日，埃索普斯战士假装出售农产品进入村内，另一支部队则摧毁新村（后来的赫尔利）；他们烧毁大片村舍并掳走妇女儿童。得到新阿姆斯特丹增援和莫霍克盟友引导后，荷兰军队焚毁埃索普斯人的田地，并在9月初攻下其山地据点，杀死埃索普斯酋长。1664年9月，新尼德兰转入英国之手；理查德·尼科尔斯于1665年同埃索普斯人缔约，村落则在1669年改名金斯顿。随后开放的土地吸引法国胡格诺派移民建立新帕尔茨。1777年，金斯顿短暂成为纽约州第一个州府，乔治·克林顿于7月30日在此就职，英军又在10月16日焚毁城镇。金斯顿于1805年正式设村，单桅帆船载着哈德逊河谷的谷物驶向纽约。

en:
The forested dome of the Adirondacks rises between the Mohawk valley and Lake Champlain, threaded with cold lakes and beaver streams that the Mohawk and Oneida used as hunting grounds, while Mahican and Algonquin bands hunted the eastern slopes. At the mountains' foot the Mohawk called the narrows between Lake George and Lake Champlain tekontaró:ken, 'the junction of two waterways', after which this province is named; its short portage was the gateway of the old war-road from the St Lawrence to the Hudson. In 1444 only native canoes and war parties used it, and the rivalry over these hunting grounds was already old.

On 30 July 1609, near the narrows, Samuel de Champlain and two Frenchmen joined an Algonquin and Huron war party against some two hundred Mohawks; his first arquebus shot killed two of their three chiefs, opening a century and a half of war between France and the Iroquois. In 1642 the captive Jesuit Isaac Jogues was the first white man led through the Adirondacks. The French built Fort Carillon at the portage in 1755; on 8 July 1758 Montcalm's 4,000 defenders repulsed Abercromby's 16,000 troops, and General Amherst took the fort only in 1759, renaming it Ticonderoga. On 10 May 1775 Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys surprised its small British garrison, and Henry Knox hauled the captured cannon to Boston. Burgoyne retook the fort in 1777, but after Saratoga it was abandoned.
zh:
林木覆盖的阿迪朗达克山地隆起于莫霍克河谷与尚普兰湖之间，寒冷的湖泊与河狸溪穿行其间。莫霍克人和奥奈达人把这里作为猎场，莫希干人与阿尔冈昆人的游猎队则活动在东坡。山脚下，莫霍克人把乔治湖与尚普兰湖之间的狭窄水道称为特康塔罗肯（tekontaró:ken），意为「两条水道交汇处」，省名即由此而来；那里的短陆运道是圣劳伦斯河通往哈得孙河的古老战道门户。1444年时，只有印第安人的独木舟和战队取道于此，争夺猎场的宿怨由来已久。

1609年7月30日，在这处狭窄水道附近，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰和两名法国火枪手加入阿尔冈昆人与休伦人的战队，迎战约二百名莫霍克人；他的第一发火绳枪弹便击毙对方三名酋长中的两人，由此开启法国与易洛魁之间长达一个半世纪的战争。1642年，被俘的耶稣会士艾萨克·若格成为第一个被押解穿过阿迪朗达克山地的白人。1755年，法国人在陆运道旁修建卡里永堡；1758年7月8日，蒙卡尔姆以四千守军击退阿伯克龙比的一万六千大军，直到1759年阿默斯特才攻克要塞，改名提康德罗加堡。1775年5月10日，伊森·艾伦率领绿山兄弟突袭兵力空虚的英国守军，亨利·诺克斯随后把缴获的大炮运往波士顿。1777年伯戈因重占该堡，但萨拉托加战役后它便被废弃。

en:
Quiripi was the Eastern Algonquian language of the Quinnipiac and neighboring village clusters on the north shore of Long Island Sound; their principal village, Quinnipiac, stood at New Haven harbor and the mouth of the Quinnipiac River. In 1444 its people fished the harbor, raised maize in coastal fields, and took beaver and deer in river-valley woods. Landings and trails linked shellfish banks, cornfields and hunting grounds along a coast lying between the Pequot country to the east and the Manhattan communities nearer the Hudson.

Adriaen Block briefly visited in 1614, and Dutch traders later exchanged beaver pelts there without settling. In April 1638 John Davenport and Theophilus Eaton led 500 Puritans into the harbor; the Quinnipiac sold land in return for protection, and the newcomers laid out the nine-square town that they named New Haven by 1640. The English also set apart 1,200 acres as a supervised Quinnipiac reserve in 1638. From 1651 to 1669 Abraham Pierson preached near Branford and translated a catechism into Quiripi in 1658, but conversion made little progress. New Haven Colony was absorbed into Connecticut in 1664; the Collegiate School moved to the town in 1716 and was renamed Yale College after Elihu Yale's gift in 1718. By 1774 an estimated 38 Quinnipiac survived in their homeland, and on 5 July 1779 William Tryon's British and Loyalist force raided New Haven, sparing it from the fires set elsewhere on the coast.
zh:
奎里皮是长岛湾北岸奎尼皮亚克（中文维基作昆尼帕）及邻近村群使用的东阿尔冈昆语；他们的主要村镇奎尼皮亚克位于纽黑文港和奎尼皮亚克河口。1444年，这里的人在港湾捕鱼，在沿海田地种植玉米，并在河谷林地猎取河狸与鹿。渡口与小径把贝类滩地、玉米田和猎场连接起来；这片海岸东接佩科特人的土地，西连更靠近哈得孙河的曼哈顿族群。

1614年，阿德里安·布洛克曾短暂到访，后来荷兰商人也在此零星交换河狸皮，但没有永久定居。1638年4月，约翰·达文波特和西奥菲勒斯·伊顿率领五百名清教徒驶入港湾；奎尼皮亚克人以土地换取保护，新来者规划九街方格城镇，并在1640年前命名为纽黑文。同年，英国人还划出1200英亩受其代理人监管的奎尼皮亚克保留地。1651至1669年，亚伯拉罕·皮尔森在布兰福德附近传教，并于1658年把教理问答译成奎里皮语，但皈依成效有限。1664年，纽黑文殖民地并入康涅狄格；联合教会学校1716年迁至该城，1718年因伊莱休·耶鲁的捐款更名耶鲁学院。到1774年，留在故土的奎尼皮亚克人估计仅剩三十八人；1779年7月5日，威廉·特赖恩率领英军和效忠派部队袭掠纽黑文，但没有像攻击海岸其他城镇那样将其焚毁。

en:
The hooked arm of Cape Cod and the islands beyond it, Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket, were the country of the Wampanoag, the 'eastern people' of the southern New England shore. Their sachems ruled many villages from the bay where Plymouth now stands eastward around the cape; maize, beans and squash grew behind the shore settlements, where men took herring and shellfish and pursued whale in dugout canoes, and their speech was the Massachusett language shared with the tribes around Boston. In 1444 the Wampanoag country was a densely known and named landscape, its fishing places and planting grounds ordered by custom older than any European claim.

Giovanni da Verrazzano sailed these coasts in 1524, and in 1614 the English captain Thomas Hunt seized Patuxet men, among them Tisquantum, and sold them in Spain; when Tisquantum made his way home in 1619 his village had been emptied by the great epidemic of 1616–19. In December 1620 the Mayflower's Pilgrims settled those abandoned cornfields as Plymouth. In March 1621 Samoset and Tisquantum brought the sachem Massasoit to a treaty of peace, and the harvest feast shared that autumn became the seed of the Thanksgiving legend. The alliance held for forty years, but after Massasoit's death his son Metacom, called Philip, rose in 1675 in King Philip's War; his defeat and death in 1676 left the Wampanoag broken, many sold into slavery in Bermuda and the West Indies and the rest confined to praying towns such as Mashpee on Cape Cod, whose lands were deeded to them in 1660. Plymouth Colony was absorbed into the royal Province of Massachusetts Bay in 1691. A plague in 1763 nearly ended the Nantucket band, and after independence the state of Massachusetts ended Mashpee's self-rule in 1788 and set overseers over it.
zh:
弯钩般的科德角半岛和海外的玛莎葡萄园岛、南塔克特岛，是万帕诺亚格人的故土——他们是新英格兰南部海岸的「东方之人」。在众多酋长治理下，他们的村落从今日普利茅斯所在的海湾沿半岛向东分布；海岸村落后方是玉米、豆子和南瓜田，人们乘独木舟捕捞鲱鱼、采挖贝类、追猎鲸鱼，所说的语言与波士顿一带诸族通用的马萨诸塞语相同。1444年的万帕诺亚格土地是一片人烟稠密、处处有名号的山水，渔场和耕地由远早于欧洲人到来的古老习俗所规范。

1524年，乔瓦尼·达·韦拉扎诺沿海岸航行；1614年，英人托马斯·亨特掳走一批帕图克塞特人卖往西班牙，蒂斯匡特姆（斯昆托）即在其中。他1619年辗转返乡时，自己的村子已在1616至1619年的大瘟疫中绝了人烟。1620年12月，「五月花号」上的清教徒移民在这片荒弃的玉米地上建起普利茅斯。1621年3月，萨莫塞特和蒂斯匡特姆引见酋长马萨索伊特，双方缔和；那年秋天共享的丰收宴，就是后世感恩节传说的源头。联盟维持了约四十年。马萨索伊特死后，其子梅塔科姆（英人称菲利普）于1675年举兵，即菲利普国王战争；1676年他兵败身亡，万帕诺亚格人就此溃散，许多人被卖到百慕大和西印度群岛为奴，余生者被并入科德角上的祈祷镇——1660年立契划给他们的马什皮即是其一。1691年，普利茅斯殖民地并入王室治下的马萨诸塞湾省。1763年的一场瘟疫几乎使南塔克特岛上的支族绝灭；独立之后，马萨诸塞州又于1788年取消马什皮自治，派员监管其地。

en:
At the broad bends of the upper Merrimack, where the river leaves the New Hampshire lakes and turns south toward the sea, stood Pennacook, the principal village of the loose network of Algonquian bands that bore its name. Its people worked the rich floodplain with maize, beans and pumpkins, netted salmon, sturgeon and alewife at the rapids, and traveled by birchbark canoe as far as the coast or Lake Winnipesaukee; Pennacook is usually glossed as 'at the foot of the hill'. Their country lay between two old dangers, the Mohawk to the west and the Mi'kmaq raiders of the east. In 1444 the village was the upriver center of the Pennacook alliance, its fishery and planting grounds the heart of the Merrimack country.

The great epidemic of 1616–19, followed by smallpox in 1633, shattered that world. Passaconaway, the bashaba of the alliance, chose peace with the English and in 1660 yielded his authority to his son Wonalancet, who tried to keep his people neutral in King Philip's War; when he withdrew his followers to Pennacook in 1675, Captain Mosely's men burned the village and its winter stores. Kankamagus led the survivors back to war in 1689, but after his family was seized in 1690 he made peace and withdrew north under French and Abenaki protection, and Wonalancet himself died in 1697, maintained in his old age by Jonathan Tyng at Dunstable. The upper valley then lay long empty, until Massachusetts granted the Plantation of Penacook on 17 January 1725; Ebenezer Eastman and families from Haverhill settled it in 1725–27, it was incorporated as Rumford in 1734, and after a long boundary quarrel with Bow, Governor Benning Wentworth renamed it Concord in 1765. Blodget's canal of 1807 at Amoskeag opened the river route to Boston, and in 1808 Concord became the permanent capital of New Hampshire, its State House completed in 1819.
zh:
梅里马克河上游的宽阔河湾处，河水刚离开新罕布什尔的湖区、掉头向南奔向大海，佩纳库克古村就坐落在这里——阿尔冈昆诸族那个松散联盟即以它为名。人们在肥沃的泛滥平原上种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，在急流张网捕捞鲑鱼、鲟鱼和灰西鲱，乘桦皮船远行至海边或温尼珀索基湖；「佩纳库克」通常被解释为「山脚之地」。他们的国土夹在两重旧患之间：西边的莫霍克人和东边不时来犯的米克马克人。1444年时，这个村子是佩纳库克联盟的上游中心，渔场与玉米地正是梅里马克地区的心脏。

1616至1619年的大瘟疫和1633年的天花摧毁了这个世界。联盟大酋长帕萨科纳韦选择与英人和平相处，1660年把权位传给儿子沃纳兰塞特；后者在菲利普国王战争中力图保持中立，1675年率部众退守佩纳库克，莫西上尉的队伍却追来烧毁了村子和全部冬粮。坎卡马格斯1689年率幸存者重新开战，1690年妻儿被俘后被迫讲和，率部北投法国人与阿布纳基人；沃纳兰塞特本人于1697年在邓斯特布尔由乔纳森·廷收留、终老于此。上游河谷此后长期空旷，直到1725年1月17日马萨诸塞授予「佩纳库克种植园」；埃比尼泽·伊斯特曼等黑弗里尔人家在1725至1727年间到此定居，1734年设治为拉姆福德，后来与鲍镇长期争界，总督本宁·温特沃思于1765年将其改名康科德，取和解之意。1807年阿莫斯凯格的布洛杰特运河打通了通往波士顿的水路，1808年康科德成为新罕布什尔的永久首府，州议会大厦于1819年落成。

en:
The north-eastern arm of Lake Champlain, with Missisquoi Bay and the Missisquoi River falling into it, was the country of the Missisquoi band of the Western Abenaki, whose name survives in this province's name of Missiasik. Their principal village stood at the river mouth by a chert quarry that gave them their name of 'people of the flint'; they raised maize in the river intervals, fished the bay and the lake, and hunted the western flanks of the Green Mountains. The lake was also a war-road, and its southern shores were a long frontier of rivalry with the Mohawk. In 1444 no European had yet seen these waters.

On 9 July 1609 Samuel de Champlain landed on Isle La Motte, named the lake for himself and mapped it. In 1666 the French built Fort Sainte Anne on the same island, the first European settlement in what is now Vermont; it was abandoned by 1670, and through the colonial wars the Abenaki kept the eastern shore as allies of France. Settlement came only after the Treaty of Paris in 1763, when New Englanders poured into the New Hampshire Grants; Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys first defied New York and then the Crown. In 1777 the settlers proclaimed the independent Vermont Republic, and on 4 March 1791 Vermont entered the Union as its fourteenth state. The Missisquoi, caught in the Revolutionary War, had withdrawn north to Odanak.
zh:
尚普兰湖东北端的米西斯夸湾与注入湾中的米西斯夸河一带，是西阿布纳基人米西亚西克（Missisquoi，又译米西斯夸）部的土地，省名也由此而来。他们的主要村镇位于河口，村外有一处燧石矿，部族之名便意为「燧石之人」；他们在河滨台地种植玉米，在湾中和湖里捕鱼，在绿山西坡游猎。尚普兰湖也是一条战道，湖南岸长期是与莫霍克人相争的边界。1444年时，还没有欧洲人见过这片水面。

1609年7月9日，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰登上拉莫特岛，以自己的名字为湖命名并绘下地图。1666年，法国人在该岛修建圣安娜堡，这是今佛蒙特境内最早的欧洲人定居点，1670年前即遭废弃；此后的殖民战争年代里，阿布纳基人作为法兰西的盟友据守湖的东岸。直到1763年《巴黎条约》之后，新英格兰移民才大批涌入「新罕布什尔赠予地」；伊森·艾伦率领的绿山男孩先抗纽约、后抗英王。1777年，定居者宣布建立独立的佛蒙特共和国，1791年3月4日佛蒙特加入联邦，成为第十四个州。战火中的米西斯夸人则已向北退往奥达纳克。

en:
Sokoki was Western Abenaki country in the upper Connecticut River valley, where river meadows, woods and lakes supported seasonal camps, fishing, hunting and fields of maize, beans and squash. In 1444 no European boundary crossed the land; kinship and trails, rather than a colonial town, linked its families to the Cowasuck and Pennacook. Beaver pelts and moose hides gave the country its place in the trade that Europeans would soon enter.

Epidemics and pressure from English settlements drew many Abenaki toward French missions on the St. Francis River from around 1669, while the upper Connecticut became a wartime frontier during King Philip's War and the Abenaki wars of 1675-1725. Massachusetts granted Plantation No. 4 in 1735; settlers arrived in 1740 and raised a stockade in 1744. A French and Abenaki force besieged it for three days in 1747, but Phineas Stevens and 31 militiamen held the fort. Rechartered as Charlestown in 1753 and incorporated in 1783, the township marked the replacement of Sokoki country by New England settlement.
zh:
索科基是西阿贝纳基人的土地，位于康涅狄格河上游。河畔草甸、森林与湖泊支撑着季节性营地、渔猎，以及玉米、豆类和南瓜田。1444年时，这里还没有欧洲人的边界；把各部家庭同科瓦萨克人、佩纳库科人联系起来的是亲族和小径，而非殖民城镇。河狸皮与驼鹿皮使这片土地在欧洲人很快卷入的贸易中占有一席之地。

1669年前后，疫病和英格兰定居点的压力迫使许多阿贝纳基人迁往圣弗朗索瓦河畔的法国传教站；在1675年开始的菲利普国王战争和1675至1725年的阿贝纳基诸战争中，康涅狄格河上游成为交战边疆。马萨诸塞1735年授出「第四号种植园」，定居者1740年抵达，1744年筑起木栅要塞。1747年，法国与阿贝纳基联军围攻三日，菲尼亚斯·史蒂文斯率31名民兵守住要塞。此地1753年重新获特许状并改名查尔斯敦，1783年正式设镇，也标志着新英格兰定居点取代了索科基人的故土。

en:
Kinnipekw is the upper Kennebec country, running from the cold waters of Moosehead Lake down through rapids toward Norridgewock, called Nanrantsouak in Abenaki. The Norridgewock band kept its principal village there, and the French later knew the settlement as Kennebec. Fishing places, cornfields, hunting grounds, and portages linked the river to the Penobscot country and Canada; parties also came to Moosehead's Mount Kineo for its workable rhyolite. In 1444 no European crown ruled here, and Eastern Abenaki families moved through the lakes and rapids with the seasons.

The Jesuit Sébastien Rale settled at Nanrantsouak in 1693 and made its chapel a centre of French-backed resistance to New England's expansion. On 23 August 1724 Massachusetts militia attacked Old Point, killed Rale and as many as forty villagers, burned the settlement, and destroyed its cornfields; survivors took refuge farther north or in French Canada. In September 1775 Benedict Arnold led 1,100 Continental soldiers up the Kennebec and across the height of land toward the Chaudière. Leaking boats, swampy portages, storms, and poor maps reduced the column to about 600 starving men before it reached Quebec.
zh:
金尼佩库是肯纳贝克河上游地区，范围从寒冷的穆斯黑德湖顺流而下，穿过多处急流，通向阿布纳基语称南兰楚阿克的诺里奇沃克。诺里奇沃克人群的主要村落就在这里，法国后来也称该定居点为肯纳贝克。渔场、玉米地、猎场和水陆转运路把这条河同佩诺布斯科特人地区与加拿大连接起来；穆斯黑德湖畔的基尼奥山出产适于制作石器的流纹岩，也会吸引各方人群前来。1444年时，没有任何欧洲王权统治这里，东阿布纳基人的家族随季节穿行于湖泊与急流之间。

耶稣会士塞巴斯蒂安·拉勒1693年定居南兰楚阿克，使村中教堂成为法国支持下抵抗新英格兰扩张的中心。1724年8月23日，马萨诸塞民兵袭击旧角，杀死拉勒和多达四十名村民，焚毁村落并毁坏玉米地；幸存者向北避居或逃往法属加拿大。1775年9月，本尼迪克特·阿诺德率一千一百名大陆军士兵沿肯纳贝克河北上，越过分水高地前往肖迪耶尔河。漏船、沼泽转运路、风暴和粗糙地图使这支队伍抵达魁北克前只剩约六百名饥疲交加的士兵。

en:
The foggy, island-strewn mouth of the St. Croix and the waters of Passamaquoddy Bay, churned by the great tides of the Bay of Fundy, are the country of the Peskotomuhkatiyik — 'those of the place where pollock are plentiful', the Passamaquoddy. Each summer their bands gathered on the bay shores and islands to spear pollock and herring, take seals and dig clams, then scattered inland for the winter moose hunt, travelling the lakes by birchbark canoe; their chief camp of Qonasqamkuk stood at the head of the bay. Kinsmen of the Maliseet and Mi'kmaq, they were one of the nations of the Wabanaki league of the Dawnland, and in 1444 no European ship had yet wintered among them.

Europe arrived in June 1604, when the French nobleman Pierre Dugua de Mons, with Samuel de Champlain, put a wintering party on Sainte-Croix Island in the river mouth; scurvy killed 35 of the 79 men before spring, and the survivors moved across to Port Royal in 1605. Samuel Argall burned what remained on the island in 1613. French traders and Jesuits made the Passamaquoddy, whom they called the Etchemins, into allies and converts, and their warriors raided the New England frontier through the long Wabanaki wars of the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries. Settlers came only after the fall of New France: fishermen occupied Moose Island in 1772, and Machias, granted in 1770, became a hotbed of rebellion. In June 1775 its men captured the armed schooner Margaretta, the first British warship taken in the Revolution, and in August 1777 forty Passamaquoddy warriors under Joseph Neeala helped drive Sir George Collier's squadron back from the town. An Anglo-American commission fixed the St. Croix border in 1797–98, cutting the old homeland in two. War returned in 1814: the British seized Eastport on 11 July and occupied Machias in September, holding the bay until the Treaty of Ghent — and Eastport itself until 1818.
zh:
圣克罗伊河口雾气弥漫、岛屿散布，帕萨马科迪湾的海水受芬迪湾大潮吞吐——这里是帕萨马科迪人的故土，他们自称 Peskotomuhkatiyik，意为「狭鳕丰饶之地的人」。每年夏天，各部群聚到湾岸和岛屿，用鱼叉捕捞狭鳕与鲱鱼、猎海豹、挖蛤蜊，冬天则分散到内陆猎驼鹿，乘桦皮独木舟往来于湖沼之间；他们的主要营地科纳斯卡姆库克就位于湾顶。作为马勒西特人和米克马克人的亲族，他们是「黎明之地」瓦巴纳基联盟的成员之一；1444年时，还没有一艘欧洲船在他们中间过冬。

欧洲人在1604年6月到来：法国贵族皮埃尔·迪加·德蒙与尚普兰率一队人在河口的圣克罗伊岛设营过冬，春天之前79人中有35人死于坏血病，幸存者于1605年迁往对岸的皇家港。1613年，塞缪尔·阿盖尔烧毁了岛上残存的房屋。法国商人与耶稣会士把他们所称的「埃切明人」发展为盟友和信徒，在17世纪至18世纪初漫长的瓦巴纳基战争中，帕萨马科迪战士不断袭扰新英格兰边疆。直到新法兰西陷落之后，移民才真正到来：渔民于1772年占据穆斯岛，1770年获颁建镇的马柴厄斯成了反叛的温床。1775年6月，镇民夺取武装帆船「玛格丽塔号」，这是独立战争中缴获的第一艘英国军舰；1777年8月，约瑟夫·尼阿拉率领的四十名帕萨马科迪战士又协助击退了乔治·科利尔爵士舰队的进攻。1797—1798年，英美联合委员会划定圣克罗伊河边界，把他们古老的故土一分为二。1814年战端重启：英军7月11日夺取东港，9月占领马柴厄斯，控制整个海湾直到《根特条约》签订，东港一地更是迟至1818年才归还。

en:
Inland from Passamaquoddy Bay the land climbs into a cold, forested interior cut by the upper tributaries of the Saint John — the Aroostook, whose Wolastoqey name Wool-ahs-took means 'good river for everything', and the Tobique. The Wolastoqiyik, the 'People of the Bright River', used these waters as winter hunting grounds: families paddled and snowshoed up them after moose and caribou, trapped beaver, took salmon at the rapids and made maple sugar when the thaw came, while their palisaded, maize-growing villages stood downriver at Meductic and at the Saint John's mouth. Raids from the Haudenosaunee far to the west were an old danger. In 1444 no European had yet ascended these streams.

French ships charting the Bay of Fundy met the Wolastoqiyik at the Saint John's mouth from 1604, and both Champlain and Lescarbot describe a large village there; a century of French fur trade, Jesuit missions and military alliance followed. Wolastoqey warriors fought beside the French in every war against New England, and when the St. John River campaign of 1758 burned Meductic while the Acadian expulsion emptied the lower valley, the survivors withdrew upstream. Maliseet and Acadian refugees together made Madawaska, at the head of the river, one of the largest Wolastoqey villages of the later eighteenth century. In 1801 the colonial government, acting on the band's petition, granted a reserve of nearly 20,000 acres at the mouth of the Tobique. When this period closed in 1821, the Aroostook interior remained unceded forest, with no permanent settler town and no agreed international boundary.
zh:
从帕萨马科迪湾向内陆去，地势抬升为寒冷多林的高地，圣约翰河的上游支流纵横其间——阿鲁斯图克河与托比克河；前者的马勒西特语原名 Wool-ahs-took 意为「百物皆宜之河」。沃拉斯托奎伊克人，即「亮河之民」，把这些水道当作冬季猎场：家户划独木舟、踏雪鞋溯河而上猎驼鹿和驯鹿、诱捕海狸，在急流处捕捞鲑鱼，开春转暖后熬制枫糖；他们种植玉米、设栅据守的固定村落则位于下游的梅达克蒂克和圣约翰河口。西面远方豪德诺索尼人的袭扰，是由来已久的威胁。1444年，还没有欧洲人溯这些溪流而上。

1604年起，测绘芬迪湾的法国船只在圣约翰河口与沃拉斯托奎伊克人相遇，尚普兰和莱斯卡博都记述过当地的一座大村；此后是约一个世纪的法国毛皮贸易、耶稣会传教与军事同盟。在历次对新英格兰的战争中，沃拉斯托奎伊克战士都与法国人并肩作战。1758年的圣约翰河战役烧毁梅达克蒂克，阿卡迪亚大驱逐又使下游河谷为之一空，幸存者于是向上游转移。马勒西特难民与阿卡迪亚难民在河首的马达瓦斯卡合居，使这里在18世纪后期成为最大的沃拉斯托奎伊克村落之一。1801年，殖民政府根据部落请愿，在托比克河口划给他们一片近两万英亩的保留地。1821年本时期结束时，阿鲁斯图克内陆仍是一片未割让的森林，既没有固定的移民城镇，也没有议定的国际边界。

en:
Gespogoitnag is Kespukwitk, or 'Land's End', the southwestern arm of Nova Scotia. The great tides of the Bay of Fundy meet the Atlantic South Shore among inlets, rivers, lakes and canoe portages; the Annapolis Basin, called Nme'juaqnek for its abundant fish, was a gathering place for Mi'kmaq chiefs and a junction on routes through Kejimkujik. The district's saqamaw took part in the wider councils of Mi'kma'ki. In 1444, fishing weirs and seasonal camps, not European walls or seigneuries, marked control of this land.

Membertou, saqamaw of Kespukwitk, later claimed to have been a grown man when he met Jacques Cartier in 1534; he became a grand chief and forged the Mi'kmaq alliance with the French at Port Royal. Pierre Dugua's party founded Port Royal on the Annapolis Basin in 1605, the first enduring French settlement in what became Canada, but raiders from Virginia destroyed the habitation in 1613. Scottish settlers built Charles Fort in 1629, and France recovered the place in 1632. About four hundred people lived around Port Royal by 1671, although the basin changed sovereigns repeatedly in the Anglo-French wars. A British siege captured it in 1710 and the town was renamed Annapolis Royal; the Treaty of Utrecht confirmed the cession in 1713. It remained the capital of Nova Scotia until Halifax was founded in 1749. The British deported Port Royal's Acadians in autumn 1755; fighting flared at Bloody Creek in 1757 and American privateers attacked Fort Anne in 1781. Loyalists, including Black Loyalists, settled there after the American Revolution and reshaped the old garrison town.
zh:
格斯波戈伊特纳格是凯斯普库维特克，意为「陆地尽头」，即新斯科舍的西南半岛。芬迪湾的大潮与大西洋南岸在港湾、河流、湖泊和独木舟搬运道之间相接；安纳波利斯盆地的米克马克语名为Nme'juaqnek，意为鱼群丰饶之地，既是米克马克酋长聚会之处，也是经凯吉姆库吉克往来的水路枢纽。本地区酋长参加米克马克基的大议事会。1444年，标示这片土地归属的是鱼梁和季节性营地，而不是欧洲人的城墙或领主庄园。

凯斯普库维特克酋长梅姆伯图后来自称1534年遇见雅克·卡特尔时已是成年人；他后来成为大酋长，并在皇家港与法国人缔结盟约。1605年，皮埃尔·迪加一行在安纳波利斯盆地建立皇家港，这是后来加拿大境内最早长期维持的法国定居点，但来自弗吉尼亚的袭击者在1613年摧毁了居留地。1629年苏格兰移民修建查尔斯堡，1632年此地又归还法国。到1671年，皇家港周边约有四百人，而这片盆地在英法战争中多次易主。1710年英军围攻占领后，城镇改名安纳波利斯罗亚尔，1713年《乌得勒支和约》确认割让。直到1749年哈利法克斯建立前，这里一直是新斯科舍首府。1755年秋，英国驱逐皇家港的阿卡迪亚人；1757年战火烧至血腥溪，1781年美国私掠船又进攻安妮堡。美国独立战争后，包括黑人效忠派在内的效忠派到此定居，重塑了这座旧要塞城镇。

en:
Eskikeogag is Eskikewa'kik, the 'skin-dressing place', at the eastern end of mainland Nova Scotia around Chedabucto Bay and Canso. The district faces Cape Breton across the Strait of Canso and runs from the St. Mary's River toward Atlantic headlands. The harbour called Gamso'q, with its islands and beaches, supported Mi'kmaq seasonal fishing, hunting, hide work and meetings, while canoe routes linked the camps to other districts of Mi'kma'ki. In 1444 no European fish flakes or forts stood on these shores; the strait and its fishing grounds were controlled by Mi'kmaq canoes.

European fishing ships began using Canso in the 1500s, and La Rochelle merchants of the Company of Acadia built a fortified fishing and trading post on Chedabucto Bay; fifty fishers worked there in 1686. Cyprian Southack raided Fort St. Louis in 1690 and destroyed the remaining French station during the Squirrel Affair in September 1718, even though the bay had been assigned to Britain by the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713. New Englanders began a British post at Canso in 1720 and finished Fort William Augustus later that year. Mi'kmaq attacks on the works in August 1720 and July 1722 helped make the fishery a front of Dummer's War. In April 1745 William Pepperell's 4,070 troops assembled at Canso before moving against Louisbourg. Mi'kmaq fighters seized Joseph Gorham's party there in August 1749, and the deportation transport Duke William waited at Canso in 1758. American privateers raided the fishery in 1775; John Paul Jones destroyed fifteen vessels there in September 1776, and the fisheries were wrecked again in 1779. Loyalists founded Guysborough in 1784, Black Loyalists among them. A blockhouse guarded the old fort during the War of 1812, but only six families lived at the Wilmot town plot in 1813 and a few houses and stores were not raised until 1821.
zh:
埃斯基凯奥加格是埃斯基凯瓦基克，意为「鞣皮之地」，位于新斯科舍大陆部分东端，环绕沙达巴克托湾和坎索。地区隔坎索海峡与布雷顿角相望，从圣玛丽斯河延伸向大西洋岬角。坎索的米克马克语名为Gamso'q，港湾、岛屿和滩涂支撑着米克马克人的季节性渔猎、兽皮加工和聚会，独木舟路线又把各营地与米克马克基其他地区相连。1444年，这些海岸上还没有欧洲人的晒鱼架或堡垒，海峡和渔场由米克马克人的独木舟掌控。

16世纪，欧洲渔船开始使用坎索。阿卡迪亚公司的拉罗谢尔商人在沙达巴克托湾建起设防的渔业与贸易站，1686年时有五十名渔民在此作业。西普里安·索萨克1690年袭攻圣路易堡，又在1718年9月的「松鼠号事件」中摧毁残存的法国据点；虽然1713年《乌得勒支和约》已把海湾划归英国。新英格兰人1720年开始在坎索设立英国据点，同年晚些时候建成威廉·奥古斯都堡。米克马克人1720年8月袭击工事，1722年7月再度进攻，使渔场成为达默战争前线。1745年4月，威廉·佩珀雷尔率领四千零七十名军队在坎索集结，随后进军路易斯堡。1749年8月，米克马克战士在此俘获约瑟夫·戈勒姆所部；1758年，阿卡迪亚大驱逐中的运输船「威廉公爵号」曾在坎索停泊。美国私掠船1775年袭扰渔场，约翰·保罗·琼斯1776年9月摧毁十五艘船，1779年渔场再遭破坏。效忠派1784年建立盖斯伯勒，其中包括黑人效忠派。1812年战争期间，旧堡设有木碉堡防守，但威尔莫特镇址到1813年只有六户人家，直到1821年才出现少量房屋和店铺。

en:
The Wolastoq, the ‘shining river’ the French would name the Saint John, runs from the forests south of the St. Lawrence to a tide-reversing fall on the Bay of Fundy. The Wolastoqiyik, People of the Bright River, held its whole valley in palisaded villages, growing corn, beans and squash on the intervales and taking salmon, sturgeon and bass from the water. At the harbour they called Menahkwesk, where the river meets the bay, stood one of their largest villages, also frequented by Mi'kmaq sealing parties. The Mi'kmaq were their kinsmen to the east, the Passamaquoddy around the bay and the Penobscot to the west, while raiders from the Haudenosaunee far inland were the old enemy against whose war parties the river villages were stockaded. In 1444 no European ship had yet entered the bay.

On 24 June 1604, the feast of St John the Baptist, Samuel de Champlain landed at the harbour and named the river. In 1631 Charles de Saint-Étienne de la Tour built Fort Sainte-Marie at Portland Point, and the post became a stronghold of the Acadian civil war: in 1645, while la Tour was in Boston, his rival Charles de Menou d'Aulnay stormed it against the defense of la Tour's wife, Françoise-Marie Jacquelin, who died within weeks of the fort's fall. The Wolastoqiyik traded furs to the French and, from their upriver headquarters at Meductic, fought in all the colonial wars as allies of France. At Utrecht in 1713 France ceded Acadia to Britain without consulting them. The French Fort Menagoueche, raised at the river mouth in 1751, was burned by its own commander Boishébert in 1755 after the fall of Beauséjour; the British rebuilt it as Fort Frederick in 1758 and harried the Acadians who had fled up the valley. American privateers sacked Fort Frederick in 1775, and Major Gilfred Studholme built Fort Howe late in 1777. Loyalist fleets began landing in May 1783, over ten thousand within months, and on 18 May 1785 the settlements of Parrtown and Carleton were joined by royal charter as Saint John, the first incorporated city in what is now Canada and the chief port of the new colony of New Brunswick.
zh:
沃拉斯托克意为「闪光之河」，法国人后来称之为圣约翰河，发源于圣劳伦斯河以南的森林，在芬迪湾口形成潮水倒灌的急瀑。沃拉斯托基伊克人——「闪光河上的人」——在整条河谷居住，村落以木栅设防，在河畔滩地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在河中捕捞鲑鱼、鲟鱼和鲈鱼。河海相接处、他们称作梅纳赫奎斯克的港湾旁，有他们最大的村落之一，米克马克人的海豹捕猎队也常来此地。他们的东邻是同族的米克马克人，湾畔住着帕萨马科迪人，西邻佩诺布斯科特人；远在内陆的霍德诺索尼人则是世仇，沿河村落筑栅正是为了抵御他们的袭击。1444年，还没有任何欧洲船只驶入过这座海湾。

1604年6月24日施洗者圣约翰节，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰在港湾登陆，并以圣约翰为河流命名。1631年，夏尔·德·圣艾蒂安·德·拉图尔在波特兰角修建圣玛丽堡，这座据点后来成为阿卡迪亚内战的要冲：1645年拉图尔身在波士顿时，他的对手夏尔·德·梅努·多爾奈攻破堡垒，拉图尔之妻弗朗索瓦丝-玛丽·雅克兰率众死守，城破后数周便死去。沃拉斯托基伊克人以毛皮与法国人交易，并以中游的梅杜克蒂克为大本营，在历次殖民地战争中作为法国盟友出战。1713年《乌得勒支和约》中，法国未与他们商议便把阿卡迪亚割让给英国。1751年法国人在河口修建梅纳古埃什堡，1755年博塞茹尔陷落后，守将布瓦埃贝尔亲自将其焚毁；英国人1758年在原址改建弗雷德里克堡，并追击逃入河谷上游的阿卡迪亚人。1775年美国武装民船洗劫弗雷德里克堡，吉尔弗雷德·斯塔多姆少校于1777年年底修建豪堡。1783年5月起，效忠派船队源源登陆，数月内超过一万人；1785年5月18日，帕尔敦与卡尔顿两个居民点凭皇家特许状合并为圣约翰，成为今加拿大境内第一座获特许状建制的城市，也是新设的新不伦瑞克殖民地的首要港口。

en:
Madawaska is the cold upper valley of the Saint John River, around the mouth of the Madawaska River. In 1444 it was Maliseet country, called Wolastoqey after the river itself. Family bands followed a seasonal round through its woods and river terraces: they fished, hunted, gathered berries and nuts, and raised corn, beans, squash and tobacco. The confluence was a camping and meeting place on the canoe routes downstream, beyond which lay Mi'kmaq country to the east and Passamaquoddy and Penobscot lands to the south and west.

French fur traders entered the Saint John in the early seventeenth century, drawing Maliseet trappers into the French alliance and bringing Jesuit missions in their wake. During the Acadian expulsions of 1755-1764, Maliseet communities sheltered Acadian families moving upstream beyond British raids. In 1785 twenty Acadian families led by Joseph Daigle worked their way up from Fredericton, raised a cross at their landing and formed the first permanent European settlement on both banks. French Canadians from the lower St Lawrence soon joined them, clearing farms and working the timberlands. The Treaty of Paris in 1783 left the headwaters unsurveyed, so in 1821 Madawaska remained a French-speaking and Maliseet borderland disputed between Britain and the United States.
zh:
马达沃斯卡是圣约翰河寒冷的上游河谷，位于马达沃斯卡河汇入圣约翰河一带。1444年，这里是马勒西特人的土地；他们因圣约翰河而自称沃拉斯托奇人。各个家族群随季节在林地与河流阶地间迁徙，捕鱼狩猎、采集浆果和坚果，并种植玉米、菜豆、南瓜和烟草。两河交汇处是独木舟路线上的营地与会合点，顺河可通向下游；其东是米克马克人的地域，南面和西面则邻接帕萨马科迪人与佩诺布斯科特人的土地。

17世纪初，法兰西毛皮商人进入圣约翰河流域，把马勒西特猎手拉入法兰西同盟，耶稣会传教士也随后到来。1755年至1764年阿卡迪亚人大流放期间，马勒西特社群收容了溯河而上、躲避英军搜捕的阿卡迪亚家庭。1785年，约瑟夫·戴格尔率领二十个阿卡迪亚家庭从弗雷德里克顿溯河抵达这里，在登陆处竖起十字架，在圣约翰河两岸形成第一个永久欧式定居点。圣劳伦斯河下游的法裔加拿大人很快前来汇合，开垦农场并采伐林地。1783年《巴黎条约》没有勘定河源边界，因此到1821年，马达沃斯卡仍是法语居民与马勒西特人共处、英国和美国均提出声索的边境地带。

en:
Siknikt, ‘the drainage place’, is the Mi'kmaq name for the narrow neck of land joining the Nova Scotia peninsula to the continent, only twenty-four kilometres across where the Fundy tides of Chignecto Bay all but meet the green water of Baie Verte opening on the Gulf of St Lawrence. Its heart is the Tantramar, a vast sweep of salt marsh where Mi'kmaq families netted salmon and waterfowl and crossed by the short carry between bay and gulf, the route that made the isthmus a road between two coasts. As Signigtewa'gi it formed the south-eastern district of Mi'kma'ki, its villages governed by their own saqamaq under the Grand Council of the Wabanaki confederacy. In 1444 no European sail had yet entered the Bay of Fundy, and the marshes knew only the seasonal round.

Acadians from Port-Royal founded Beaubassin beside the Missaguash in 1671, dyking the Tantramar with aboiteaux into wheat fields and cattle ranges. Benjamin Church's New Englanders sacked it twice, in September 1696 and again on 17 July 1704, and after Utrecht in 1713 the unsettled Anglo-French frontier came to rest on the Missaguash. In May 1750 the missionary Jean-Louis Le Loutre burned Beaubassin himself rather than let Major Charles Lawrence fortify it; Lawrence returned in September to raise Fort Lawrence on the ashes, and the French answered from the next ridge with Fort Beauséjour, built in 1751–1752, and Fort Gaspareaux on Baie Verte. On 3 June 1755 Colonel Robert Monckton opened his siege with two thousand New England volunteers, and on 16 June the garrison of 460 marched out, the same day Fort Gaspareaux was abandoned; Beauséjour was renamed Fort Cumberland, and the round-ups and burnings of the Great Upheaval began on the isthmus. Acadian and Mi'kmaq bands harried the forts through 1756–1757, but from 1760 New England Planters took the vacant farms, and in 1763 the townships of Amherst, Sackville and Cumberland were surveyed, followed by a thousand Yorkshire settlers in 1772–1775. In October and November 1776 Jonathan Eddy's rebel band of Yankees, Acadians, Maliseet and Mi'kmaq besieged Fort Cumberland for the American cause, until troops sent from Halifax scattered them.
zh:
希格尼克特意为「排水之地」，是米克马克人对这条连接新斯科舍半岛与北美大陆的狭窄地峡的称呼：希格内克托湾的芬迪涌潮与通向圣劳伦斯湾的贝尔特湾几乎在此相接，最窄处仅24公里。地峡的中心是坦特拉马大盐沼，米克马克氏族在这里张网捕捞鲑鱼、猎取水鸟，并借一条短联运道往来于芬迪湾与圣劳伦斯湾之间——正是这条通道使地峡成为两大海岸间的门户。此地米克马克语称西尼克特瓦吉，是米克马克基东南一区，各村由酋长在瓦巴纳基联盟大议事会下自行治理。1444年，还没有欧洲船帆驶入芬迪湾，沼泽地带只随米克马克人的季节节律而兴衰。

1671年，来自罗亚尔港的阿卡迪亚人在米萨瓜什河畔建立博巴桑村，用水闸海塘把坦特拉马沼泽开垦成麦田和牧场。新英格兰人本杰明·丘奇的队伍曾两度洗劫此地：一次在1696年9月，另一次在1704年7月17日。1713年《乌得勒支和约》后，悬而未决的英法边界落在米萨瓜什河上。1750年5月，传教士让-路易·勒卢特尔亲手烧毁博巴桑，不让查尔斯·劳伦斯少校据此筑垒；劳伦斯9月重返，在废墟上建起劳伦斯堡，法国人则在相邻的山脊上应对：1751至1752年修筑博塞茹尔堡，并在贝尔特湾修建加斯帕罗堡。1755年6月3日，罗伯特·蒙克顿上校率两千名新英格兰志愿兵发起围攻，6月16日，460名守军出降，加斯帕罗堡也在同日弃守；博塞茹尔堡更名为坎伯兰堡，「大动荡」中的搜捕与焚烧就此在地峡展开。1756至1757年间，阿卡迪亚与米克马克游击队不断袭扰两座堡垒，但自1760年起新英格兰垦殖者接手空置的农庄，1763年又勘定阿默斯特、萨克维尔和坎伯兰三个镇区，1772至1775年迁来上千名约克郡移民。1776年10至11月，乔纳森·埃迪率领由新英格兰人、阿卡迪亚人、马勒西特人和米克马克人组成的叛军，为支援美国独立事业围攻坎伯兰堡，最终被哈利法克斯派来的援军击溃。

en:
Placentia's ice-free roadstead and broad rocky beaches made the bay one of Newfoundland's finest natural fishing stations. In 1444 its salmon rivers, seal grounds and offshore cod were still used by Beothuk bands, heirs of the island's Little Passage hunting tradition, who camped along the shore without facing a European garrison. The same beaches later let fishermen dry cod without building costly wooden stages, a fact that would draw Basque seasonal fleets across the Atlantic.

A Basque will of 1563 already called the harbour Plazençia. France formed its Terre-Neuve colony around Plaisance in 1655 and established a permanent fortified settlement in 1662, adding Fort Royal above the harbour in 1687. English raiders sacked the town in 1690, but the French rebuilt and used Plaisance as a base against English Newfoundland. In the winter of 1696–97 Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville and Governor de Brouillan struck from the bay, destroying St. John's and most of the English fishing posts before the survivors held on at Bonavista and Carbonear. The Treaty of Utrecht forced the French out in 1713; settlers, soldiers and many Mi'kmaq allies withdrew toward Louisbourg, while British troops occupied the Castle Hill works until 1811. In 1786 the future William IV spent the summer here acting as a surrogate judge, a sign that Placentia still rivalled St. John's in importance.
zh:
普拉森西亚湾解冻早、锚地隐蔽，又有宽阔岩滩，是纽芬兰条件最好的天然渔场之一。1444年，贝奥图克族群仍在此利用鲑鱼河、海豹场和外海鳕鱼；他们继承岛上的小通道狩猎传统，在岸边设营，附近还没有欧洲驻军。同样的岩滩后来使渔民不必耗费大量木材搭建晒鱼台，便能晾晒鳕鱼，这一点把巴斯克季节性船队引过了大西洋。

1563年的一份巴斯克水手遗嘱已经把这个港口称为Plazençia。法国1655年以普莱桑斯为中心建立纽芬兰殖民地，1662年设置常驻设防据点，1687年又在港口上方修建皇家堡。英国劫掠者1690年洗劫城镇，但法国人将其重建，并把普莱桑斯当作进攻英属纽芬兰的基地。1696至1697年冬，皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德伊贝维尔与布鲁扬总督从这里出击，摧毁圣约翰斯和大多数英国渔业据点，只有博纳维斯塔和卡博尼尔的幸存者守住阵地。1713年《乌得勒支条约》迫使法国人撤离；居民、士兵和许多米克马克盟友迁往路易斯堡方向，英军则占据城堡山工事直到1811年。1786年，后来的威廉四世曾在此度夏并代理审判，显示普拉森西亚当时仍足以同圣约翰斯抗衡。

en:
Sikumiut means 'people of the sea ice', a fitting name for the Labrador Inuit country of island chains, tide-split fjords and winter ice north of Hamilton Inlet. Archaeology at Okak Bay traces Labrador Inuit occupation there from about 1200. In 1444 families moved with the ice and animal migrations: they wintered in shoreline sod houses, raised skin tents in summer, and used kayaks and open umiaks to hunt seal, whale and Arctic char while inland caribou herds supplied hides and winter food. The coast had no European mission or permanent trading post, and its exchanges still ran through Inuit families and neighboring peoples rather than a colonial power.

Basque whalers encountered Labrador Inuit in the 1500s, but sustained European presence came only after Britain took the coast from France in 1763. Moravian missionaries led by Jens Haven founded Nain in 1771 and Okak in 1776, then established Hopedale at the Inuit settlement of Agvituk in 1782. The stations offered baptism, European goods and a fixed yearly rhythm, gradually drawing families into settled mission villages and the Newfoundland trade. Labrador was detached from Lower Canada and transferred to Newfoundland in 1809. In 1821 the northern coast remained a sparse chain of Inuit camps and Moravian stations, tied more closely to sea ice and mission boats than to roads.
zh:
锡库缪特意为「海冰上的人」，用来指哈密尔顿湾以北这片岛链、潮汐峡湾与冬季浮冰交错的拉布拉多因纽特土地十分贴切。奥卡克湾的考古遗存显示，拉布拉多因纽特人约1200年已在此居住。1444年，各个家庭随海冰和动物迁徙转换营地：冬天住在岸边草泥屋，夏天支起兽皮帐篷，乘皮艇和敞篷乌米亚克捕猎海豹、鲸与红点鲑，内陆驯鹿群则提供皮革和冬粮。海岸上还没有欧洲传教站或固定贸易栈，物资交换仍经由因纽特家庭与邻近族群进行，而不掌握在殖民势力手中。

16世纪，巴斯克捕鲸者已与拉布拉多因纽特人相遇，但欧洲人的持续存在要到1763年英国从法国手中取得海岸之后。摩拉维亚传教士在延斯·黑文带领下于1771年建立内恩，1776年建立奥卡克，又在1782年于因纽特居点阿格维图克设立霍普代尔。传教站带来洗礼、欧洲货物和固定的年度节奏，逐渐把各个家庭吸引到定居的传教村落，并纳入纽芬兰贸易。1809年，拉布拉多从下加拿大划出，转交纽芬兰管辖。1821年的北岸仍是一条稀疏的因纽特营地与摩拉维亚站点链，联系它们的与其说是道路，不如说是海冰和传教船。

en:
The name Naskapi, 'people beyond the horizon', was later given to the northern nomadic branch of the Innu whose country, St'aschinuw, stretched between Ungava Bay, Hudson Bay and the Torngat Mountains. This province centers on the barrens and lake crossings of southern Labrador, above all Ashuanipi; in Innu the name means 'a place to cross', and its routes led down the Moisie toward the St Lawrence North Shore or north toward Okak. In 1444 small bands moved behind caribou herds, fished lake trout and char, pitched skin tents at sheltered crossings, and traveled between Innu and Inuit neighbors. No mission, fur post or fixed capital stood in the interior.

Europeans long knew this country only from reports carried south. About 1643 the Jesuit André Richard recorded the Ounackkapiouek among the small nations north of Tadoussac, and in 1733 the name Naskapi appeared in accounts placing about forty families at Ashuanipi. In 1740 Joseph Isbister of the Hudson's Bay Company heard of people northeast of Richmond Gulf, and Moravian reports from Okak called the Indians west of that mission Nascopies in 1790. Anglo-French claims changed after 1763 and Labrador passed to Newfoundland in 1809, yet no colonial administration reached the barrens. In 1820 the Hudson's Bay Company man James Clouston descended the Caniapiscau; a year later the interior still had no permanent company trading post.
zh:
纳斯卡皮意为「地平线之外的人」，后来用以称呼因努人中偏北的游猎分支；他们的故土St'aschinuw伸展于昂加瓦湾、哈德逊湾与通戈山脉之间。本省围绕拉布拉多南部的冻原与湖上渡口，核心是阿舒阿尼皮湖。湖名在因努语中意为「可以横渡之地」，从这里可顺穆瓦西河通往圣劳伦斯河北岸，也可向北前往奥卡克。1444年，小队人群跟随驯鹿群移动，捕捞湖鳟和红点鲑，在避风渡口支起兽皮帐篷，并往来于因努与因纽特邻人之间。腹地中没有传教站、毛皮栈或固定首府。

很久之间，欧洲人只能通过南来的传闻知道这片土地。约1643年，耶稣会士安德烈·里夏尔记载了塔杜萨克以北诸小族中的Ounackkapiouek；1733年，文献首次出现Naskapi一名，并称约四十个家庭在阿舒阿尼皮湖一带有重要营地。1740年，哈德逊湾公司的约瑟夫·伊斯比斯特听说里士满湾东北方有人群活动；1790年，来自奥卡克的摩拉维亚报告把传教站以西的印第安人称作Nascopies。英法间的主权归属在1763年后改变，拉布拉多又于1809年划归纽芬兰，但没有殖民行政力量真正进入冻原。1820年，哈德逊湾公司职员詹姆斯·克拉克斯顿沿卡尼亚皮斯科河下行；一年之后，内陆仍没有固定的公司贸易站。

en:
At Mingan the river of the same name opens into the gulf beside a long chain of bare limestone islands, and the Innu called the place Ekuanitshit, 'the place where something is washed ashore' — likely the whales that stranded among the islands. It was one of their great summer camps: families who had wintered at inland caribou grounds came down to spear salmon, hunt whale and seal and meet in trade, then vanished back upriver before the ice closed in. The river-mouth and archipelago belonged to the seasonal round of Nitassinan, and in 1444 nothing European had yet been raised on the shore.

The Mingan seignory was granted in 1661, the first French holding on this stretch of coast, and a fur post took root at the river-mouth. In 1680 Louis XIV granted the Mingan Archipelago, with Anticosti, to Louis Jolliet, the explorer of the Mississippi; from his island fort he traded arms and goods to the Montagnais and Papinachois for sealskins. The Innu kept to their summer-only custom at Mingan, coming in each year to barter furs. The post was run for a time by the North West Company, and in 1807 it passed to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
在明根，同名河流注入海湾，河口外横着一长串裸露的石灰岩群岛。因努人称此地为埃夸尼楚（Ekuanitshit），意即「有东西被冲上岸的地方」，所指大概是常在群岛间搁浅的鲸。这里是他们夏日大聚的营地之一：在内陆猎驯鹿越冬的各家来到河口，叉鲑鱼、捕鲸和海豹、聚会交易，封冻前再溯河而去。河口与群岛都在尼塔希南的季节迁徙范围之内，1444年时岸上还没有任何欧洲人造物。

1661年，明根领地获得封授，这是法国人在这段海岸上的第一处产业，河口随之立起毛皮贸易站。1680年，路易十四把明根群岛连同安蒂科斯蒂岛封给探察过密西西比河的路易·若列；他在岛上的设防据点用武器杂货向蒙塔涅人和帕皮纳舒瓦人换取海豹皮。因努人仍只在夏天到明根，每年来站上以毛皮易物。贸易站一度由西北公司经营，1807年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Between the broad mouths of the Manicouagan and the Betsiamites, the coast belonged to the Montagnais bands the French called the Bersimis — the Pessamit Innu, for Pessamit means 'the place of lampreys' — with the Papinachois up the Betsiamites and the Ouchestigouetch at the head of the Manicouagan. They summered at the river-mouths taking salmon, seal and lamprey, and wintered far inland on caribou. Champlain marked them on his map of 1632 as the 'Sauvages Bersiamiste'. In 1444 this was still untouched Innu country, deep in Nitassinan, its rivers known only to the people who paddled them.

Jacques Cartier noted the Manicouagan's mouth without naming it at the end of August 1535. Once the French opened the trade at Tadoussac to the west, the Bersimis became among their earliest allies, and in June 1664 the Jesuit Henri Nouvel became the first missionary to ascend the great river the Innu called Manikouaganistikou and the French the Rivière Noire. Missionaries went on working the summer gatherings for the rest of the century, and the Innu signed the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. In 1733 Intendant Gilles Hocquart had a fur post built at Pointe-des-Bersimites. The post was later leased to the North West Company, and in 1821 it passed with that company to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
在马尼夸根河与 Betsiamites 河两个宽阔河口之间，海岸属蒙塔涅人的几支：法人称作 Bersimis 的一支，即佩萨穆因努人——Pessamit 意为「七鳃鳗之地」；Papinachois 人住在 Betsiamites 河上游，Ouchestigouetch 人住在马尼夸根河源头一带。他们夏天聚到河口捕鲑鱼、海豹和七鳃鳗，冬天深入内陆猎驯鹿。尚普兰1632年的地图已把他们标作 Sauvages Bersiamiste。1444年时，这里仍是欧洲人未曾涉足的因努土地，深藏在尼塔希南腹地，各条河流只在因努人的独木舟下有名。

1535年8月底，卡蒂亚记下马尼夸根河口，却没有为它命名。法国人开通西边的塔杜萨克贸易后，Bersimis 人成为法人最早的盟友之一。1664年6月，耶稣会士亨利·努韦尔成为第一位溯行这条因努语称作 Manikouaganistikou、法人称作黑河的大河而上的传教士。此后整个世纪，传教士继续在各夏日聚点传教；1701年，因努人签署《蒙特利尔大和约》。1733年，新法兰西行政长官吉勒·奥卡尔在 Pointe-des-Bersimites 建起毛皮贸易站。贸易站后来租给西北公司，1821年随该公司并入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
Anticosti is a long, forested island set across the mouth of the St Lawrence where the gulf narrows into the Jacques Cartier and Honguedo straits. The Innu called it Notiskuan, 'where bears are hunted', and for thousands of years mainland parties crossed to it in summer to hunt bear and take salmon from its rivers, yet they never settled it the year round. In 1444 it was an empty, fog-bound hunting ground: no European had seen it, and even the people who owned it withdrew to the mainland through the long winter.

Jacques Cartier was the first European to report the island, in 1534, and on 15 August 1535, sailing past on the feast of the Assumption, he named it Île de l'Assomption. In 1680 Louis XIV granted it with the Mingan Archipelago to Louis Jolliet, explorer of the Mississippi. Jolliet raised a fortified post against Inuit raiders and settled there in the spring of 1681 with his family and servants, trading arms and goods to the Montagnais for sealskins. In 1690 William Phips's Massachusetts troops, retreating from their failed attack on Quebec, seized the fort. Jolliet died in 1700, and after a long lawsuit the island passed among his three sons, who kept it until the Treaty of Paris in 1763. It was annexed to Newfoundland that year, returned to the Province of Quebec in 1774 and attached to Newfoundland again in 1809, a distant timber-rich seigneurie whose few inhabitants lived by fishing and the fur trade.
zh:
安蒂科斯蒂是一座狭长的森林大岛，横在圣劳伦斯河口，扼守雅克·卡蒂亚海峡与翁格多海峡。因努人称它为诺蒂斯宽（Notiskuan），意即「猎熊之地」。几千年来，大陆上的人夏天渡海而来猎熊、在岛河上捕鲑鱼，却从不在岛上常年定居。1444年时，它还是一座雾霭笼罩、空无一人的猎场：欧洲人尚未见过它，连以岛为猎地的人们在漫长冬季也撤回大陆。

1534年，卡蒂亚成为第一个记载此岛的欧洲人；1535年8月15日圣母升天节，他再次绕过该岛，将它命名为圣母升天岛。1680年，路易十四把此岛连同明根群岛封给探察过密西西比河的路易·若列。若列筑起设防据点以防因纽特人袭击，1681年春携家眷和仆人定居岛上，用武器杂货向蒙塔涅人换取海豹皮。1690年，威廉·菲普斯麾下攻打魁北克失利的马萨诸塞部队在撤退途中占领了这座堡垒。若列1700年去世，经过一场漫长官司，海岛分归他的三个儿子，若列家族一直保有到1763年《巴黎条约》。该年岛屿被划归纽芬兰，1774年交还魁北克省，1809年再度并入纽芬兰。这座遥远而林木丰茂的封地上居民寥寥，皆以捕鱼和毛皮贸易为生。

en:
Pekuakami is the Innu name of the broad, shallow lake the French would call Lac Saint-Jean, set in the Laurentian highlands and draining through the Saguenay River. Its people are the Pekuakamiulnuatsh, 'the people of Pekuakami', the Innu band the French knew as the Montagnais. They followed the shoreline and the surrounding boreal forest, hunting caribou and moose, fishing through the ice and taking beaver, and in summer families gathered at river-mouth points such as Métabetchouane to meet and trade. In 1444 no European had yet seen the lake, which lay deep in the Innu country called Nitassinan, and the year still turned to the old seasonal round.

French ships were trading at Tadoussac by 1600, and the Innu became France's first allies upriver: Champlain made his alliance with them in 1603, and Montagnais warriors went with him in 1609. On 17 July 1647 the Jesuit Jean de Quen, ascending the Saguenay, became the first European to reach Pekuakami and said mass on its shore. In 1652 Governor Jean de Lauson had a fur post raised at Métabetchouane, within the king's own domain; a Jesuit mission was added there in 1676, the same year as the Chicoutimi post, but in 1697 the post was closed and its trade moved to Chicoutimi. Iroquois raiding parties reached the lake country during that century's wars, until the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. After the British conquest the post reopened and its stone powder magazine was built between 1760 and 1778; the North West Company ran it from 1802, and in 1821 it passed, with the whole company, into Hudson's Bay Company hands.
zh:
佩夸卡米是因努语对这片宽阔浅水湖的称呼，法国人后来称它为圣让湖。湖在劳伦琴高原之间，湖水经萨格奈河流出。湖畔居民是佩夸卡米乌尔努阿特，意即「佩夸卡米人」，属因努人的一支，法国人称之为蒙塔涅人。他们循着湖岸与周围的针叶林迁徙，猎驯鹿和驼鹿、冰下捕鱼、诱捕海狸；夏天各家聚到梅塔贝楚安等河流入湖处相会交易。1444年时还没有欧洲人见过这座湖，它深藏在因努人称作尼塔希南的土地腹地，一年仍按古老的季节节律轮转。

到1600年，法国商船已在下游的塔杜萨克贸易，因努人成为法国人溯河而上最早的盟友：尚普兰1603年与他们结盟，1609年蒙塔涅战士随他出征。1647年7月17日，耶稣会士让·德康溯萨格奈河而上，成为第一个抵达佩夸卡米的欧洲人，并在湖边做了弥撒。1652年，总督让·德洛松在梅塔贝楚安建起毛皮贸易站，此地属国王直辖的王家领地；1676年站内增设耶稣会传教所，与希库蒂米贸易站同年，但1697年贸易站关闭，生意并入希库蒂米。那个世纪的易洛魁战争中，劫掠队伍一度深入湖区，直到1701年《蒙特利尔大和约》才告平息。英国征服后贸易站重开，石砌火药库建于1760至1778年间；西北公司自1802年起经营此站，1821年随该公司一并落入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Atikamekw is the upper Saint-Maurice country that its people call Nitaskinan, a boreal world of lakes, spruce forest and family hunting grounds above the later French town of Trois-Rivières. In 1444 its people gathered at riverside places such as Wemotaci in summer, then split into small winter camps to fish under the ice, hunt moose and trap beaver. Birchbark canoes and snowshoes tied the territory together, and no European power had yet reached it.

French records first mention the Atikamekw in the early seventeenth century. As the fur trade developed, beaver pelts moved down the Saint-Maurice to the St. Lawrence, while metal tools returned upstream. French seigneurial settlement after 1634 stayed close to the river mouth, leaving the upper country to Atikamekw hunters and traders rather than habitant farms. The name Wemotaci first appears in a written source in 1724. Fur traders continued to use the Saint-Maurice through the eighteenth century, and Jean-Baptiste Perrault built the first confirmed trading post there in 1806; the Hudson's Bay Company took it over in 1821.
zh:
阿蒂卡梅库是阿蒂卡梅库人称作尼塔斯基南的土地，位于圣莫里斯河上游，是后来三河城以北一片由湖泊、针叶林和家族猎场组成的北方世界。1444年，人们夏季在韦莫塔奇等河畔地点聚集，入冬后分成小群营地，在冰下捕鱼、猎取驼鹿并诱捕河狸。桦皮舟和雪鞋把这片土地连为一体，欧洲势力当时尚未到来。

法国文献在17世纪初首次提到阿蒂卡梅库人。毛皮贸易发展后，河狸皮沿圣莫里斯河运往圣劳伦斯河，金属工具则溯流而上。1634年以后，法国人的领主拓殖仍集中在河口附近，河流上游依旧是阿蒂卡梅库猎人和商人的天地，并未出现农户定居带。韦莫塔奇一名最早见于1724年的文字记载。整个18世纪，毛皮商人持续利用圣莫里斯河；1806年，让-巴蒂斯特·佩罗在韦莫塔奇建起第一座可确认的商站，1821年该站转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Timiskaming is a long, deep lake on the Ottawa River, where the water bends from its northwestern course toward Montreal. Its Algonquin name was Temi Kami, and at the narrows called Obadjiwan, 'the strait where the current flows', Algonquin families kept a summer camp, fishing the lake and taking beaver and moose in the surrounding forest. In 1444 the country was Anishinaabe land, and the lake stood near the midpoint of the canoe route that would one day join the St. Lawrence to James Bay by way of Lake Abitibi.

The route first carried Europeans in 1686, when a French expedition paddled north through the lake to surprise the English posts on James Bay. A Montreal merchants' post built on the west shore about 1679 was destroyed by the Iroquois in 1688. In 1720 French merchants founded Fort Témiscamingue at the Obadjiwan narrows, on the old Algonquin campground, and for forty years the post traded guns, brandy and ironware for furs. After the fall of New France it was reopened by independent traders, and in 1788 it passed to the North West Company, whose brigades still carried the northern furs down the Ottawa to Montreal.
zh:
蒂米斯卡明是渥太华河上一道又长又深的湖，河水在此由西北流向折而奔向蒙特利尔。湖的阿尔冈昆语名作Temi Kami；在名为奥巴吉万（Obadjiwan，意为「水流湍急的狭口」）的窄道处，阿尔冈昆家族设有夏季营地，在湖中捕鱼，到周围森林猎取河狸与驼鹿。1444年，这片土地属于阿尼希纳贝人，湖的位置接近一条独木舟路线的中点——这条路线日后经由阿比蒂比湖，把圣劳伦斯河与詹姆斯湾连接起来。

1686年，一支法国远征队为奇袭詹姆斯湾上的英国商站取道此湖北上，路线上第一次出现了欧洲人。约1679年蒙特利尔商人在湖西岸建起的商栈，1688年被易洛魁人摧毁。1720年，法国商人在奥巴吉万狭口、旧日的阿尔冈昆营地处兴建蒂米斯卡明堡，四十年来以枪支、白兰地和铁器交换毛皮。新法兰西陷落后，商栈由独立商人重新经营，1788年转入西北公司之手，北方的毛皮仍由成队独木舟沿渥太华河南运蒙特利尔。

en:
Animouski is the Algonquian name the French would write as Rimouski, a river that enters the lower St. Lawrence estuary on this forested south shore, between the Bic headland and Matane. In 1444 the Wolastoqiyik, the Maliseet bands of the Wabanaki confederacy, moved with the seasons between these river mouths and the inland lakes, taking salmon, seal and moose, while Mi'kmaq parties from the east used the same coast; the Matapédia and Témiscouata portages ran from here toward Chaleur Bay and the Saint John River. No European had yet settled, but by about 1570 Basque whalers were rendering their catch on Île aux Basques off Trois-Pistoles, where they built three stone try-furnaces.

Early in the seventeenth century La Rochelle merchants ran a fur post at Matane, trading European goods with the Mi'kmaq. The French granted more than twenty seigneuries along this coast, but settlers were few: the seigneury of Rimouski was granted in 1688 and occupied only in 1696, when René Lepage moved his family over from the Île d'Orléans. At the conquest of 1760 a few dozen families lived in just four seigneuries between Rivière-du-Loup and Matane.
