Across the seas the Sultans of Ternate were drawing the whole coast into their tribute network, while Bugis and Malay traders threaded the two waters for gold, rice and coconut. In 1444 the court of Gorontalo still kept the old ancestral cults, though its fortunes were already bound to Ternate and the spice trade.

Islam came through marriage and commerce: in 1525 Raja Amai, who reigned from 1523 to 1550, wed a princess of Palase Gomonjolo, a house linked by blood to Ternate, accepted her faith and took the title sultan; under his son Matolodulakiki Islam became the religion of the kingdom, which grew into one of the chief centres of the faith in eastern Indonesia, remembered as the 'Porch of Medina'. In 1615 the court moved downstream to Tuladenggi, and the royal town received its formal charter on 19 March 1728. The VOC's shadow lengthened after Ternate ceded its Sulawesi fiefs by a treaty of 11 May 1677: Governor Padtbrugge came to Kwandang the next year to receive Gorontalo and Limboto, a Company trading office opened in 1705, and Fort Nassare rose in 1770 to guard the gold and rice trade. Sultan Eato (1673–1679) and, in the next century, Sultan Botutihe kept their throne, but after the Company's collapse in 1799 the Dutch state inherited its treaties, and through 1821 the sultan at Biawu reigned under ever closer Batavian oversight.
zh:
哥伦打洛横在苏拉威西北支半岛的蜂腰处，北濒苏拉威西海，南临深邃的托米尼湾，是一片平原广产稻米、山中蕴藏黄金的土地。这里的王国由约1300年的谷地小邦乌兰塔朗吉发展而来；14世纪，国王伊拉胡杜把十七个小酋长邦（利努拉）联合成一国，王室又通过波哈拉血缘之盟，与林博托、苏瓦瓦、博朗戈、阿廷戈拉四个邻邦王室互通声气。海那边的特尔纳特苏丹正把整片海岸纳入贡赋网络，布吉斯和马来商人穿行于两海之间，贩运黄金、稻米和椰产。1444年的哥伦打洛宫廷仍守着古老的祖灵崇拜，但它的命运已经系于特尔纳特和香料贸易。

伊斯兰教随联姻与贸易而来：1525年，1523至1550年在位的国王阿迈迎娶帕拉塞·戈蒙佐洛的公主——该家族与特尔纳特素有血缘之盟——皈依伊斯兰教并改称苏丹；其子马托洛杜拉基基在位时，伊斯兰成为王国国教，哥伦打洛也成长为印尼东部最重要的伊斯兰中心之一，后世有「麦地那廊庑」之称。1615年，王都顺波朗戈河迁往图拉登吉；1728年3月19日，王城获得正式建制。1677年5月11日，特尔纳特依约把在苏拉威西的属地割让给荷兰东印度公司，公司的阴影随之压来：次年帕德特布鲁赫亲赴宽当，接收哥伦打洛和林博托；1705年商馆开设，1770年纳萨雷堡筑起，看守黄金与稻米贸易。苏丹埃阿托（1673—1679年）以及下一个世纪的苏丹博图图赫保住了王位，但公司1799年破产后，各项条约由荷兰国家接手；直到1821年，驻跸比亚武的苏丹仍在位上，巴达维亚的管束却已日益收紧。

en:
Palu stands at the head of a narrow, almost landlocked bay, where the long Palu River valley opens a road into the very heart of Sulawesi—the natural gateway between the Makassar Strait coast and the highland interior. It is the country of the Kaili, whose riverside and hill villages lived by fishing, farming and the forest, ruled in early days by warrior headmen (Tomalanggai) before councils and an aristocracy of madika nobles took shape in the fifteenth century. The bay was already a trading crossroads: Makassar and Bugis praus called there for coconut oil and for forest produce floated down from the interior, though the busiest anchorage remained Donggala, out at the bay's mouth. In 1444 the villages where Palu now stands were still small, pagan and unfortified, waiting on the first power strong enough to take them.

That power was Gowa: in the mid-sixteenth century Karaeng Tunipalangga, who reigned from about 1546 to 1565, carried Makassar arms along the whole west coast from Kaili to Tolitoli, and Portuguese ships were soon calling at the bay for trade and port rights. Gowa's grip loosened after its wars with the VOC ended in defeat in 1667–1669, and the Kaili shore returned to a patchwork of small kingdoms—Sigi, Bangga, Banawa, Palu and others. In 1796 four riverside villages, Besusu, Tanggabanggo, Panggovia and Boyantongo, joined in the Patanggota council to found the kingdom of Palu; its first magau, Pue Nggari (1796–1805), accepted Islam with his court from the Sumatran preacher Dato Karama. His daughter Labugulili ruled as the kingdom's first queen in 1805–1815, and Malasigi Bulupalo had sat on the throne since 1815, so that in 1821 Palu was a young Muslim kingdom whose trade still passed chiefly through Donggala, its people untouched as yet by Dutch rule.
zh:
帕卢坐落在狭长而近乎封闭的海湾顶端，长长的帕卢河谷在此打开一条通往苏拉威西腹地的道路，是望加锡海峡沿岸与内陆高地之间的天然门户。这里是凯利人的家园：河畔与山间村落以渔猎、农耕和山林物产为生，早期由尚武的首领托马朗盖统辖，到15世纪，长老议事与名为马迪卡的贵族阶层逐渐成形。海湾早就是贸易要冲：望加锡和布吉斯人的帆船在此收购椰油，以及从内陆顺河而下的山货，不过最繁忙的锚地始终是湾口的东加拉。1444年，后来帕卢城所在的几处村落仍然狭小、信奉泛灵、不设城防，只待第一个足够强大的政权来取。

这个强权便是戈瓦：16世纪中叶，卡拉昂·图尼帕朗加（约1546—1565年在位）率领望加锡军队横扫整条西海岸，势力从凯利一直伸展到托利托利，不久葡萄牙商船也来湾内停泊，求取贸易与港口权益。1667至1669年戈瓦在与荷兰东印度公司的战争中战败，控制随之松动，凯利沿岸又回到锡吉、邦加、巴纳瓦、帕卢等小王国林立的局面。1796年，贝苏苏、唐加邦戈、潘戈维亚、博扬通戈四个滨河村落组成帕坦戈塔议事会，建立帕卢王国；初代马高普·恩加里（1796—1805年）在苏门答腊传道者达托·卡拉马的劝说下率宫廷皈依伊斯兰。其女拉布古利利作为王国第一位女王执政于1805至1815年，此后马拉西吉·布卢帕洛自1815年起在位；因此1821年的帕卢已是一个年轻的伊斯兰王国，贸易仍主要经由东加拉出入，荷兰人的统治尚未降临。

en:
Palopo lies on the Gulf of Bone beneath a steep pass into the Toraja highlands. In 1444 Luwu's palace centre was nearby at Malangke, also called Amassangan, and Palopo was not yet the capital. Bugis settlers had occupied the coast around 1300, and iron ore brought through the Lemolang lands of Baebunta was smelted at Malangke into weapons and tools for the rice-growing south. By the middle of the fourteenth century Luwu was a feared overlord on the peninsula. In 1444 its datu ruled a multi-ethnic trading coalition, linking coastal Bugis with highland peoples while the court still followed ancestral spirits.

Bataraguru, Luwu's earliest named ruler, made peace with Bone in the mid-fifteenth century; Dewaraja later campaigned against Wajo and Sidenreng around 1495-1520 as southern kingdoms overtook Luwu. Palopo's coral-block Jami Mosque is dated 1604. On 4 or 5 February 1605 La Patiwareq became the first major South Sulawesi ruler to accept Islam, taking the name Sultan Muhammad Wali Mu'z'hir al-din. After the North-South war between rival princes, the court left Malangke for Palopo in the early seventeenth century. The new town had a royal square and market at Lalebbata, and its position facing the Seko-Rongkong valleys gave the diminished sultanate access to highland exchange across the pass.
zh:
帕洛波位于波尼湾畔，后方有一条陡峭山道通向托拉查高地。1444年时，鲁乌的宫廷中心还在附近的马朗凯（又称阿马桑甘），帕洛波尚未成为都城。约1300年，布吉斯定居者进入这片海岸；铁矿石经莱莫朗人的巴埃本塔运到马朗凯，熔铸成武器和农具，输往南方种植稻米的平原。到14世纪中叶，鲁乌已是半岛上令人生畏的宗主。1444年，这里的达图统治着一个多族群贸易联盟，把沿海布吉斯人与高地各族连接起来，宫廷仍信奉祖灵。

可考的最早鲁乌君主巴塔拉古鲁在15世纪中叶与波尼议和；1495年至1520年前后，德瓦拉查又进攻瓦乔和西登伦，但南方诸国已逐渐超过鲁乌。帕洛波以珊瑚石建造的贾米清真寺可追溯至1604年。1605年2月4日或5日，拉·帕蒂瓦雷克成为南苏拉威西第一位接受伊斯兰教的主要统治者，改名苏丹穆罕默德·瓦利·穆扎希尔·丁。对立王子之间的「北方—南方战争」之后，宫廷于17世纪初离开马朗凯，迁至帕洛波。新城在拉莱巴塔设有王宫广场和市场，又正对塞科—龙孔谷地，使衰弱的苏丹国仍能通过山口经营高地贸易。

en:
Buton is a large island off southeast Sulawesi, where the Wolio harbor that later became Baubau commands the Buton Strait. Four small districts, Gundu-gundu, Barangkatopa, Peropa and Baluwu, joined with neighboring chiefdoms and in 1332 installed Wa Kaa Kaa as their first ruler; the district heads, the bonto, formed the council that elected and checked later monarchs. The Nagarakretagama named Buton in 1365. In 1444 the island remained an animist kingdom whose proas linked the Sulawesi coast with the spice traffic passing toward Maluku, while its court balanced noble families and sea traders.

In 1541 Sheikh Abdul Wahid bin Sharif Sulaiman al-Fathani and Imam Fathani converted the Wolio court, and Lakilaponto, also called Halu Oleo, was enthroned as Sultan Murhum Kaimuddin Khalifatul Khamis. During the sixteenth century Buton became an important secondary center under Ternate, controlling regional trade and forwarding tribute from the spice route. Sultan La Sangaji began the coral-and-limestone Wolio fortress between 1591 and 1596, and Sultan La Elangi made it permanent. The Murtabat Tujuh law code was adopted in 1610, defining offices and the legislative siolimbona. Pressured by Gowa and Ternate, the sultanate accepted Dutch East India Company protection in the seventeenth century; Sultan La Badaru still reigned at Wolio in 1821, having ruled since 1799.
zh:
布敦（又译布顿）是苏拉威西东南方的大岛，后来发展为巴务巴务的沃利奥港湾扼守布敦海峡。贡杜—贡杜、巴朗加索帕、佩罗帕和巴卢武四个小区与邻近首领联合，于1332年推立瓦·卡卡为第一位统治者；各区首领邦托组成议事会，负责选立并约束后来的君主。1365年的《爪哇史颂》已经提到布敦。1444年，这里仍是一个泛灵信仰王国，岛民的马来快船连接苏拉威西海岸与通往摩鹿加的香料贸易，宫廷则在贵族家族和海商之间维持平衡。

1541年，谢赫·阿卜杜勒·瓦希德·本·谢里夫·苏莱曼·法塔尼与伊玛目·法塔尼使沃利奥宫廷改宗，拉基拉蓬托（又称哈卢·奥莱奥）即位为苏丹穆尔胡姆·凯穆丁·哈利法图尔·哈米斯。16世纪，布敦成为特尔纳特势力下重要的次级中心，控制区域贸易，并经香料航路转输贡赋。1591年至1596年，苏丹拉·桑加吉开始以珊瑚和石灰岩修筑沃利奥堡垒，苏丹拉·埃兰吉时将其建成永久工事。1610年，《穆尔塔巴特·图朱》法典颁行，规定各项官职和西奥林博纳议事机构。在戈瓦与特尔纳特的压力下，苏丹国于17世纪接受荷兰东印度公司保护；1821年，自1799年在位的苏丹拉·巴达鲁仍在沃利奥统治。

en:
The Sula Islands — Taliabu, Mangole and Sulabesi, ringed by many islets — lie where the Molucca, Seram and Banda seas meet, a stepping-stone between Sulawesi and Halmahera. Sula and Mangole clans lived by the sea and the forest, sailing out to trade damar resin, rattan and beeswax, while on Sulabesi the four-soa confederacy of Soa Gareha ordered local affairs by the harbor that became Sanana. In 1444 the islands kept their own councils; sailors from Makassar, the Bugis lands and Java knew these waters, but the power of Ternate had not yet reached them.

In 1511 Sultan Bayanullah of Ternate drew the Sulas into his sultanate as its outer seawall, posting a Salahakan of the Tomaito clan and a Sangadji at Sanana to gather tribute of resin, rattan and beeswax. In 1652 the Dutch East India Company raised the stone Fort De Verwachting on Sanana's shore to close the straits to Bugis, Makassarese and English smugglers and guard its spice monopoly; the garrison stored the islands' produce, watched the sea lanes, and weathered both hongi raiders and village elders who refused its levies. Sanana remained a small outpost in Ternate's shadow, passing with the Company to the Dutch crown, and in 1821 the old fort still guarded the crossroads of the three seas.
zh:
苏拉群岛由塔利阿布、曼戈莱、苏拉贝西三座大岛和环绕四周的众多小岛组成，地处马鲁古海、塞兰海与班达海交汇处，是苏拉威西与哈马黑拉之间的踏脚石。苏拉人和曼戈莱人诸部靠海和山林为生，驾船外出贸易达玛树脂、藤条和蜂蜡；在苏拉贝西岛，由四个「索阿」组成的传统联盟「索阿·加雷哈」在后来发展为萨纳纳的港湾旁处理公共事务。1444年的群岛仍由本地议事会自主治理，望加锡、布吉之地和爪哇的水手熟知这片海域，特尔纳特的权势却尚未延伸至此。

1511年，特尔纳特苏丹巴亚努拉把苏拉群岛纳入苏丹国版图，作为其海上外藩，派托迈托氏族的「萨腊坎」和驻萨纳纳的「桑阿吉」征收树脂、藤条和蜂蜡贡物。1652年，荷兰东印度公司在萨纳纳海岸修建石砌的德韦瓦赫廷要塞（意为「希望要塞」），封锁海峡、防范布吉人、望加锡人和英国走私者，以保卫香料专卖；驻军储存岛产、监视航道，既要应付洪吉武装掠船，也常面对拒缴摊派的村社长老。萨纳纳始终是特尔纳特阴影下的小小据点，后随公司一同转归荷兰国家；1821年时，古老要塞仍扼守着三海交汇之地。

en:
Fakfak is a harbour on the Onin coast, the western arm of the Bomberai Peninsula, across the Berau Strait from Seram. In 1444 its bays were held by Papuan Onin clans whose inland and shore communities followed ancestral cults. Their canoes traded with Moluccan praus, carrying nutmeg and other sea and forest products into routes linking Seram, Bacan and the clove sultanates. No European post existed there; the port's allegiance depended instead on loose ties between local leaders and rival Moluccan rulers.

The Moluccan struggle drew the coast more deeply into island politics. In 1521 Sultan al-Mansur of Tidore accepted a Spanish alliance against Ternate and Portugal, but Spanish forces withdrew from the region in 1663, while Tidore's claims over western Papua endured. Manuscripts cited for the old Patimburak mosque date the arrival of Islam on the Fakfak coast to 1606, as authority spread from Bacan to Tidore; coastal leaders embraced the new faith while inland communities kept their ancestral cults. Through the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries Fakfak remained one of Tidore's Papuan ports, although Onin clans retained much of their power beside the new mosques and Moluccan shipping lanes.
zh:
法克法克是邦巴赖半岛西部奥宁海岸上的港口，与斯兰岛隔贝劳海峡相望。1444年，沿岸各湾由巴布亚的奥宁氏族分据，内陆和滨海社群都奉行祖灵崇拜。他们的独木舟同摩鹿加商船贸易，把肉豆蔻及其他海林物产带入连接斯兰、巴占和丁香诸苏丹国的商路。当时这里没有欧洲人的据点，港口的向背主要取决于本地首领与摩鹿加争霸者之间时松时紧的盟属关系。

摩鹿加诸强的争夺把这条海岸更深地卷入岛屿政治。1521年，蒂多雷苏丹曼苏尔接纳西班牙为盟友，以对抗特尔纳特和葡萄牙；西班牙势力最终于1663年撤出，蒂多雷对西巴布亚沿岸的宗主权却延续下来。帕廷布拉克旧清真寺所引手稿称，1606年，随巴占到蒂多雷的权力扩张，伊斯兰教传入法克法克，沿岸领袖改奉新信仰，内陆社群仍守祖灵信仰。16至18世纪，法克法克一直是蒂多雷联结巴布亚世界的港口之一，而奥宁氏族在新兴清真寺和摩鹿加航道旁仍保有相当权势。

en:
The bay that Europeans would one day call Astrolabe Bay lies on New Guinea's north coast, fronted by smoking volcanic islands: Karkar a day's paddle offshore and Manam beyond it. Beach villages of Austronesian Bel-speaking peoples line the shore. The Bilibil dwelt on a cramped islet too small to feed them, built deep-hulled seagoing canoes and fired clay pots, which they carried along the coast from Karkar as far as western Morobe, taking sago, taro and timber from inland and island peoples in return. Behind the coast the rainforested ranges of the Rai Coast rise steeply, cut by fast rivers and held by a mosaic of Papuan-language villages living by gardens, fishing and the same exchange. In 1444 no lord ruled this shore; each village kept its own trade friends, its canoes and its feuds.

Europeans knew only the offshore waters. On 10 and 12 August 1545 the Spanish carrack San Juan of Iñigo Órtiz de Retez, on the voyage that gave New Guinea its name, sighted Karkar and Long islands. Willem Schouten and Jacob le Maire saw Karkar in 1616, Abel Tasman passed this way in 1643, and William Dampier visited Karkar about 1699; none of their charts marked the bay behind the islands. Through 1821 no European is known to have landed on this coast, and the potters' canoes still carried the trade between the volcanoes and the shore.
zh:
这片日后被欧洲人称作阿斯特罗莱布湾的水域位于新几内亚岛北海岸，海外矗立着喷烟的火山岛：划一天独木舟可到的卡尔卡尔岛，以及更远处的马纳姆岛。沿岸排开的是说南岛语系贝尔语族各族的滨海村落。比力比尔人住在一座小得养不活全族的岛上，造深舷远洋独木舟、烧陶罐，驾船从卡尔卡尔岛沿东南海岸一直贸易到莫罗贝省西部，用陶器向内陆和海岛居民换取西米、芋艿和木材。岸后是雨林覆盖、陡然而起的莱伊岭山地，急流穿行，山里散落着众多说巴布亚语的村落，靠园圃、渔捞和同样的交换为生。1444年的这片海岸没有共主，每个村落各有自己的贸易伙伴、独木舟和世仇。

欧洲人只知道外海的航路。1545年8月10日和12日，伊尼戈·奥尔蒂斯·德·雷特斯的西班牙大帆船「圣胡安号」——新几内亚的名字正是这次航行所取——先后望见卡尔卡尔岛和长岛。1616年威廉·斯豪滕和雅各布·勒梅尔见到卡尔卡尔岛，1643年亚伯·塔斯曼路经此地，约1699年威廉·丹皮尔还登上卡尔卡尔岛，但他们的海图没有一张标出群岛背后的海湾。直到1821年，没有任何欧洲人在这片海岸留下登陆记录，陶匠的独木舟依旧把持着火山与岸滩之间的贸易。

en:
At the head of Huon Gulf, where the Markham River comes down from the Finisterre Range and breaks into mangrove channels, lies a shore of beach ridges, swamp and lagoon. Austronesian-speaking villagers — the Ahi villages above the river mouth, among them Butibam, and the Labu among their coastal lagoons — fished the gulf, tended gardens and paddled trading canoes along the coast and up the river, exchanging the sea's produce for taro, bananas and sago with the Papuan-speaking peoples of the Markham valley. Behind them rise the forested folds of the Huon ranges, where human habitation is among the oldest in Oceania: stone tools some 40,000 years old have been found on the peninsula's raised coast terraces. In 1444 this was a world of villages and trade partnerships with no paramount chief, the gulf itself its highway.

In August 1545 the Spanish carrack San Juan sighted Long Island in the Vitiaz Strait to the west, on the voyage that gave New Guinea its name, yet no European ship entered Huon Gulf. In 1793 the French expedition of Bruni d'Entrecasteaux, searching for the lost La Pérouse, passed well offshore and gave the gulf and peninsula the name of his captain, Jean-Michel Huon de Kermadec, without making a landing. Through 1821 these waters still belonged to the canoes of the Ahi and the Labu.
zh:
休恩湾湾首是一片滩脊、沼泽与潟湖交错的海岸，发源于菲尼斯特雷岭的马卡姆河在此散成红树林水道入海。说南岛语的村落就住在这里：河口上方的阿希诸村（布提班是其中之一），以及守着海岸潟湖的拉布人。他们在湾中捕鱼、经营园圃，驾贸易独木舟往来沿岸、溯马卡姆河而上，用海产向马卡姆河谷说巴布亚语的居民换取芋艿、香蕉和西米。村落后方是休恩岭密林深叠的群山，人类在此居住的历史在大洋洲也属最古老之列——半岛抬升海岸阶地上发现过约四万年前的石器。1444年的此地是一个没有共主、由村落和贸易伙伴关系维系的世界，海湾本身便是通途。

1545年8月，西班牙大帆船「圣胡安号」在为新几内亚命名的那次航行中，望见了西边维蒂亚兹海峡里的长岛，但没有欧洲船只驶入休恩湾。1793年，布吕尼·当特勒卡斯托率法国船队搜寻失踪的拉佩鲁兹，从远离海岸的外海经过，以其麾下舰长让-米歇尔·于翁·德·凯尔马代克之名为海湾和半岛命名，全程未曾登陆。直到1821年，这片水域仍属于阿希人和拉布人的独木舟。

en:
This is the concave shore of the Gulf of Papua, where rivers off the southern scarp of the central highlands — the Purari, the Vailala and their fellows — spill into the sea through deltas, sago swamps and tidal forest. The people here speak Papuan languages, Elema and Toaripi on this eastern stretch, and live in patrilineal clan villages with no chief above the clan. Their great men's longhouses, raised on piles and hung with carved gope boards, masks and bullroarers painted in red ochre, lime and charcoal, were the setting for initiations and for the ritual headhunting raids between rival villages. Sago from the swamps and fish from the rivers fed them, and every year the lakatoi fleets of the Motu arrived from the east, unloading thousands of clay pots to carry home filled with Gulf sago and timber. In 1444 that dangerous voyage was the coast's only window on the wider world.

The hiri fleets kept arriving for the next four centuries. In 1606 the Spanish expedition of Luís Vaz de Torres charted this southern coast as far as the Gulf of Papua, yet it left no post and no recorded landing on these shores. Through 1821 the longhouses stood untouched by any outside power, and the annual coming of the Motu canoes remained the great event of the year.
zh:
这里是巴布亚湾向内凹进的海岸，发源于中央高地南坡的普鲁阿里河、瓦伊拉拉河等河流穿过三角洲、西米沼泽和潮汐林莽入海。沿岸居民说巴布亚语，东段住的是埃莱马人和托阿里皮人，按父系氏族聚居，没有凌驾于氏族之上的首领。他们建造高大的男子长屋，架在木桩上，屋内挂满雕成的「戈佩」祖灵板、面具和吼器，以红赭、石灰和炭黑绘彩，是少年入会和敌对村落之间仪式性猎头袭击的场所。沼泽里的西米、河流中的鱼养活着居民；每年莫图人的拉卡托伊船队从东方而来，卸下数以千计的陶罐，装满海湾的西米和木材返航。1444年时，这段凶险的航程是这片海岸通往外部世界的唯一窗口。

此后四个世纪，希里船队年年如约而至。1606年，路易斯·巴斯·德·托雷斯的西班牙探险队把这段南部海岸测绘到巴布亚湾，但没有留下据点，也没有在这些岸滩登陆的记录。直到1821年，这里的长屋依旧不受任何外来权力打扰，莫图独木舟一年一度的到来仍是一年中的大事。

en:
Daru is a low, elliptical island, nowhere higher than 27 metres, set in the narrow waters between the mouth of New Guinea's Fly River and the reef-strewn Torres Strait. Around it lie seagrass pastures where dugong graze and turtles come to breed, and its people lived by harpooning them from sailing outrigger canoes and by fishing the island roads. To the north their canoes traded with the Kiwai villages of the Fly delta; to the south they belonged to the strait's long exchange network, where trumpet shells, bailer shells and turtle-harpoon shafts bought Papuan canoe hulls, cassowary bone-tipped arrows and bamboo, a trade that ran on south to the Aboriginal peoples of Cape York. In 1444 Daru was a link in that island chain, its shores and reefs governed by clan custom and the tides rather than by any outside power.

On 5 September 1606 the island was sighted by the Spanish expedition of Luís Vaz de Torres, then feeling its way along New Guinea's southern coast; weeks later the ships passed through the strait that now bears his name. They made no landing on Daru and left no post, and the passage was so little used that Europe learned of it only when Alexander Dalrymple published captured Spanish accounts in 1770–71. Through 1821 no outside flag flew over Daru, and the canoe trade between the Fly delta, the strait and Cape York ran on as before.
zh:
达鲁是一座低矮的椭圆形岛屿，最高处不足27米，坐落在新几内亚岛弗莱河口与礁群密布的托雷斯海峡之间的狭窄水域中。岛周是海草丛生的浅海，儒艮在此觅食，海龟前来繁殖，岛民驾挂帆的舷外支架独木舟镖猎儒艮和海龟，在岛际水道捕鱼为生。他们的独木舟向北与弗莱河三角洲的基瓦伊村落贸易，向南则织入海峡古老的交换网络：用法螺、贝砵和捕龟镖杆换取巴布亚人的独木舟船体、鹤鸵骨镞箭和竹器，这条贸易线还一直延伸到南方约克角的原住民那里。1444年的达鲁是这条岛链上的一环，岸滩与礁群只受氏族习惯和潮汐支配，没有任何外来权力。

1606年9月5日，路易斯·巴斯·德·托雷斯的西班牙探险队在沿新几内亚南海岸摸索航行时望见达鲁岛；数周后，船队穿过了日后以他命名的海峡。西班牙人没有登陆达鲁，也没有留下据点，而这条水道极少有人再走，欧洲直到亚历山大·达尔林普尔1770—1771年公布缴获的西班牙文献才知道它的存在。直到1821年，达鲁岛上没有升起过任何外来者的旗帜，弗莱河三角洲、海峡与约克角之间的独木舟贸易照旧运转。

en:
Yos Sudarso is the large, low-lying island that Europeans later knew as Frederik Hendrik; local names include Kolepom, Dolok and Kimaam. Mangroves line its Arafura coast and the narrow muddy straits facing southern New Guinea. In 1444 Kimaam and related Kolopom clans lived in small fishing and gardening villages among the swamps, with Kimaam settlement facing the Buaya Strait and Komoran Island. Their world was centred on canoes, sago grounds and tidal channels; no Moluccan sultanate or foreign factory yet reached the island.

The first Europeans to see the coast passed without occupying it. About January 1606 Willem Jansz brought the Duyfken through the bight between the island and New Guinea while returning from the Australian coast; his chart marked the low, muddy land as Tiuri. In 1623 Jan Carstensz rounded its south-western cape and named it Valse Kaap, the False Cape. Those visits put the shore on Dutch charts but produced neither a fort nor a permanent trading post, and through the rest of the period Kimaam and Kolopom communities kept control of their mangrove channels.
zh:
约斯苏达索是一座低平大岛，欧洲人后来称它弗雷德里克·亨德里克岛，当地名称则有科洛波姆、多洛克和基马姆。岛屿南临阿拉弗拉海，朝向巴布亚南部的狭窄泥质海峡两岸遍布红树林。1444年，基马姆人和相关的科洛波姆氏族在沼泽间组成小型渔猎和园艺村落，东南的基马姆聚落隔布阿亚海峡与科莫兰岛相望。他们的世界围绕独木舟、西谷椰地和潮沟展开，摩鹿加苏丹国或外国商馆都还没有伸到这里。

最早见到这段海岸的欧洲人并未占领岛屿。约1606年1月，威廉·扬松指挥「杜伊夫根号」从澳大利亚海岸返航时，穿过此岛与巴布亚之间的海湾，他的海图把这片低平泥地标作蒂乌里。1623年，扬·卡斯滕斯绕过岛西南端的海角，将其命名为Valse Kaap，意为「假角」。这些航行只把海岸画入荷兰海图，没有留下要塞或常设商馆；此后直到本时期结束，基马姆和科洛波姆社群仍掌握着自己的红树林水道。

en:
Asmat is a tide-woven land on New Guinea's south-western coast, where Arafura Sea tides enter mangrove forest, tidal swamp, freshwater swamp and lowland rainforest. In 1444 the Asmat clans occupied this country in broadly coastal and inland groups, differing in dialect, livelihood, social structure and ritual. Woodcarvers shaped ancestral figures and spirit-canoe designs as part of ceremonies for the dead, while warfare and ancestor rites linked rival villages. Mudbanks, mangroves and shifting channels left the region without an outside ruler, mission or trading post.

European contact began only from the sea. In 1623 the Dutch expedition of Jan Carstensz made the first apparent sighting of Asmat people from the deck of a passing ship. On 3 September 1770 James Cook's party from HM Bark Endeavour became the first Europeans known to land on the Asmat coast; they met a group of Asmat warriors and, judging the encounter dangerous, quickly withdrew. No fort, mission or factory followed during the rest of the period, so the clans kept control of their rivers, woodcarving and ancestral ceremonies through 1821.
zh:
阿斯马特是新几内亚西南岸一片由潮汐织成的土地，阿拉弗拉海的潮水伸入红树林、潮汐沼泽、淡水沼泽和低地雨林。1444年，阿斯马特各氏族占据这片水网，大体分为滨海和内陆两群，方言、生计、社会组织与仪式各不相同。雕木匠把祖先形象和灵舟纹样刻入木器，作为祭奠死者仪式的一部分；战事与祖灵仪式则维系、也对立着相邻村落。泥滩、红树林和摆动不定的水道使这里没有外来统治者、传教站或商馆。

欧洲人最初只能从海上接触这片海岸。1623年，扬·卡斯滕斯率领的荷兰船队从经过的船甲板上首次明确望见阿斯马特人。1770年9月3日，詹姆斯·库克「努力号」上的一队人成为已知最早登上阿斯马特海岸的欧洲人；他们遇到一群阿斯马特战士，判断情势危险后很快撤回船上。本时期余下时间里，这里没有出现要塞、传教站或商馆，直到1821年，各氏族仍掌握着自己的河流、木雕与祖灵仪式。

en:
The Aru Islands are a scatter of some ninety-five low islands on the Sahul Shelf, between the Banda Sea and the Arafura, their fauna half Papuan and their people Austronesian. Aru was already a node of the old eastern Indonesian trade: Banda, Bugis and Makassar merchants came for pearl shell, tortoiseshell, trepang, sago and the plumes of birds of paradise, while the islanders, ordered in hospitable clans and the two ritual leagues Ursia and Urlima, kept little hierarchy and no king. In 1444 this commerce still moved entirely under native sail, and no outsider had a footing on the islands.

Portuguese ships appeared in 1522–1524, when Martim Afonso de Melo wintered among these islands; the Spaniard Álvaro de Saavedra sighted them in 1528, and the Dutch yacht Duyfken sailed these waters in 1606. The VOC made its first contract with west-coast villages in 1623 and put a trading post and small fort on Wokam in 1659, drawing pearls, birds of paradise and slaves into the Bandanese market, while a few islanders took Islam or Dutch Protestantism from the 1650s. The Company's monopoly galled, and when the Tidorese prince Nuku rose against the Dutch, Aru rose with him: in 1787 the Muslims of Ujir killed the Dutch garrison and set Nuku's brother Jou Mangofa over much of the archipelago, until a Bandanese expedition retook the islands in 1791. British operations in the Moluccas after 1795 then dissolved what remained of Dutch control, and in 1821 Aru was again left to its own traders and councils.
zh:
阿鲁群岛是散落在萨胡尔大陆架上的约九十五座低平岛屿，介于班达海与阿拉弗拉海之间，动物已带一半新几内亚色彩，岛民则属南岛人。阿鲁早就是东印度尼西亚古老商路的一环：班达、布吉斯和望加锡商人前来采办珍珠贝、玳瑁、海参、西谷米和极乐鸟羽；岛民以好客的氏族和乌尔西亚、乌尔利马两个祭祀同盟维系社会，少有等级，也没有国王。1444年时，这桩贸易仍全靠本地商船运转，没有任何外人在岛上立足。

1522至1524年葡萄牙船首次出现，马丁·阿方索·德梅洛曾在这一带过冬；1528年西班牙人萨阿韦德拉望见群岛，1606年荷兰船「杜伊夫根号」也驶过附近水域。荷兰东印度公司1623年与西岸村落签下首份契约，1659年在沃坎岛设立商站和小要塞，把珍珠、极乐鸟和奴隶卷入班达市场；1650年代起，少数岛民改宗伊斯兰教或荷兰新教。公司的垄断令人怨愤，蒂多雷王子努库起兵反荷时，阿鲁起而响应：1787年乌吉尔岛的穆斯林消灭荷兰驻军，拥努库之弟焦·曼加法统治群岛大部，直到1791年一支班达远征军重新夺回群岛。1795年后英国在摩鹿加的军事行动又瓦解了荷兰人残余的控制，到1821年，阿鲁重新交还给本地商人与村议。

en:
Malgana is Gathaagudu, the 'two waters' of Shark Bay, where an arid coast breaks into long peninsulas, tidal flats and island shelters. Wulybidi, the Peron Peninsula, reaches toward Wirruwana, now called Dirk Hartog Island. The Malgana spoke a Kartu language of the Pama–Nyungan family, and shell middens on the peninsula and islands record fish and shellfish gathered from these rich waters. In 1444 the bay's wells, landing places and seasonal camps belonged to that maritime life; no European ship had yet found the western edge of Australia.

On 25 October 1616 Dirk Hartog's Eendracht reached Wirruwana in the first recorded European landfall on the Western Australian coast. Hartog examined the coast and islands for three days, nailed a pewter record to a post and named the mainland Eendrachtsland. Willem de Vlamingh replaced the plate in 1697, and William Dampier named Shark Bay on 7 August 1699. In 1712 the Dutch East India Company ship Zuytdorp was wrecked on the cliffs to the south; Malgana tradition preserved stories of survivors building shelters and trading stores for hunting implements. A French party under Louis Aleno de Saint-Aloüarn claimed the coast for Louis XV in March 1772, Emmanuel Hamelin re-erected Vlamingh's plate in 1801, and Louis de Freycinet removed it in 1818. None of these visits founded a settlement, and the Malgana still held Gathaagudu in 1821.
zh:
马尔加纳是鲨鱼湾的加塔古杜，意为「两片水域」。干旱海岸在这里分成长半岛、潮滩和多座可作庇护的岛屿；武利比迪（佩龙半岛）伸向维鲁瓦纳，即后来的德克哈托格岛。马尔加纳人使用帕马—尼翁甘语系的卡尔图语，佩龙半岛和岛屿上的贝丘记录着他们从富饶水域获取鱼类、贝类的生活。1444年，海湾的水井、登陆处和季节性营地仍属于这种海上生计；还没有欧洲船只抵达澳大利亚的西缘。

1616年10月25日，德克·哈托格的「恩德拉赫特号」抵达维鲁瓦纳，这是欧洲人在西澳大利亚海岸有记录的最早登陆。哈托格用三天考察海岸和岛群，把刻有日期和船员名字的锡镴牌钉在柱上，并将陆地称为恩德拉赫特地。1697年，威廉·德·弗拉明换走锡牌；1699年8月7日，威廉·丹皮尔将海湾命名为鲨鱼湾。1712年，荷兰东印度公司商船「祖伊特多普号」（Zuytdorp）在南方悬崖失事，马尔加纳人的口述传统保存了幸存者搭建棚屋、用存粮交换狩猎器具的故事。1772年3月，法国航海家圣阿卢安率队在岛上正式为路易十五宣称这片海岸；1801年，埃马纽埃尔·哈梅林重新竖立弗拉明的锡牌，路易·德·弗雷西内又在1818年将其取走。这些访问都没有建成定居点；1821年，加塔古杜仍由马尔加纳人守护。

en:
Minang is the southern Noongar country around King George Sound, called Mammang-Koort in the Menang language, where Princess Royal Harbour and Oyster Harbour lie sheltered behind Breaksea and Michaelmas islands. In 1444 Minang families came in summer to Kinjarling, the Albany shore, fishing the harbours and maintaining fish traps at Emu Point and on the Kalgan River while moving between the coast and their hinterland.

European ships entered this country late. George Vancouver reached the sound in 1791 and named it for George III. Matthew Flinders lay there from 8 December 1801 to 5 January 1802, his botanists collecting more than 500 plant species while Noongar diplomacy helped the survey proceed; Nicolas Baudin's French expedition followed in February 1803, and Phillip Parker King called in 1818. In 1821 King George Sound was a known anchorage, but it still had no permanent European settlement.
zh:
米南是农雅人最南部的一支——米南人围绕乔治王湾的土地，米南语称这片海湾为马芒库特。皇家公主港和牡蛎港在布里克西岛、米迦勒节岛遮蔽下形成避风水面。1444年，米南家族夏季来到金贾林，也就是奥尔巴尼海岸，在港湾捕鱼，在伊米角和卡尔根河使用鱼梁，并随季节往返于海岸与内陆之间。

欧洲船只很晚才驶入这片土地。1791年，乔治·温哥华抵达海湾，以英王乔治三世之名命名。1801年12月8日至1802年1月5日，马修·弗林德斯在此停泊测绘，随船植物学者采集了500多种植物，考察也得到农雅人的善意配合；1803年2月，尼古拉·博丹的法国探险队继之而来，菲利普·帕克·金则于1818年到访。到1821年，乔治王湾已是欧洲人知道的锚地，但仍没有永久欧洲据点。

en:
The Tiwi, who call themselves Tunuvivi, occupy Ratuati Irara, 'the two islands', where Bathurst and Melville lie across Apsley Strait in the Timor Sea. Their language is an isolate with no apparent link to the languages of nearby Arnhem Land, and Tiwi society is ordered through matrilineal descent. Islanders moved with the monsoon through forest, mangroves, beaches and fishing grounds, taking game and sea food while song and painting formed part of their Dreaming rituals. In 1444 there were no outside forts or missions on the islands, and the Tiwi followed their own seasonal round across two closely linked sea countries.

For more than two centuries after 1444, the islands kept their separate course. Makassan and Chinese traders are thought to have reached them from around 1600, but no foreign post was planted. On 30 April 1705 Maarten van Delft brought three Dutch East India Company ships into Shark Bay on Melville Island and landed; the Tiwi skirmished with the visitors and the Dutch withdrew without founding a settlement. In 1818 Philip Parker King's British expedition became the first recorded British party to meet them, exchanging iron tools for fish, water and sago and naming Melville Island, Bathurst Island and Apsley Strait. In 1821 the Tiwi islands still had no European garrison or mission.
zh:
提维人自称图努维维，居住在拉图阿蒂·伊拉拉，即提维语中的「两座岛」：巴瑟斯特岛与梅尔维尔岛隔阿普斯利海峡相望，地处帝汶海。提维语是孤立语言，与近处阿纳姆地诸语言没有明显亲缘，社会则按母系继嗣组织。岛民随季风往来于林地、红树林、海滩和渔场，猎取陆地动物与海产，歌和绘画也是梦创仪式的一部分。1444年，岛上没有外来堡垒或教会，提维人仍按自己的季节节律，往来于两片紧密相连的海洋家园。

1444年后的两个多世纪里，群岛大体维持着自身轨迹。约自1600年起，提维人被认为已同望加锡和中国商人接触，但外人并未建立永久据点。1705年4月30日，马滕·范德尔夫特率荷兰东印度公司三艘船驶入梅尔维尔岛的鲨鱼湾并登陆；提维人与来者发生冲突，荷兰人最终撤离，没有建立定居点。1818年，菲利普·帕克·金的英国探险队成为首支有据可查、与提维人交往的英国队伍，用铁器换取鱼、水和西米粉，并命名梅尔维尔岛、巴瑟斯特岛与阿普斯利海峡。到1821年，提维群岛仍没有欧洲驻军或传教站。

en:
Yolngu, meaning 'person' in the Yolngu languages, is the collective name of clans whose estates cover north-eastern Arnhem Land, from Arafura Sea beaches and coastal dunes to paperbark wetlands such as the Arafura Swamp. Every clan belongs to Dhuwa or Yirritja, the two moieties that order kinship, ceremony and responsibility for country. Fishing, hunting, gathering, inland exchange and message-stick networks tied the coast to peoples far to the south; boomerangs, for example, reached Yolngu hands through trade from Central Australia. In 1444 these monsoonal coasts had no foreign port, and authority remained with the Yolngu clans.

The first Dutch name on this coast came in 1623, when Willem Joosten van Colster's ship Arnhem gave Cape Arnhem its name without producing a settlement. By the eighteenth century, Makassan and Sama-Bajau praus from Sulawesi sailed seasonally to Marege', their name for the northern coast, to dry and smoke trepang for Chinese markets. Yolngu granted anchorage and labour in return for cloth, knives, metal, tobacco, rice, canoes and pipes; trade words entered Yolngu life, including Balanda, their term for Europeans. Through 1821 no mission, fort or colonial station had been built in Yolngu country.
zh:
雍古（Yolŋu）在雍古诸语中意为「人」，是对多个氏族的统称；他们的土地位于阿纳姆地东北部，从阿拉弗拉海的海滩和沿岸沙丘延伸到阿拉弗拉沼泽等白千层湿地。每个氏族分属Dhuwa或Yirritja两大半族，亲属关系、仪式和对土地的责任都由这套二分秩序安排。捕鱼、狩猎、采集、内陆交换和传信木杖网络把海岸与南方远处的人群连接起来，例如回旋镖就是从中澳大利亚贸易到雍古之地。1444年，这片季风海岸还没有外来港口，权力仍在各雍古氏族手中。

1623年，威廉·约斯滕·范·科尔斯特率领荷兰船只「阿纳姆号」在此航行，阿纳姆角由此得名，但海图并没有带来定居点。到18世纪，来自苏拉威西的望加锡人和萨马-巴乔人乘帆船季候性来到他们称为Marege'的北方海岸，熏晒供应中国市场的海参。雍古人允许船队停泊并提供劳力，换取布料、刀具、金属、烟草、稻米、独木舟和烟斗；贸易词汇也进入雍古生活，例如称呼欧洲人的Balanda即由此而来。直到1821年，雍古之地仍未建立传教站、堡垒或殖民据点。

en:
Awngthim is Winduwinda country on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Carpentaria, where the Mission River drains toward Albatross Bay and monsoon woodland gives way to mangrove flats. The Thaynakwith language, also recorded as Awngthim, belonged to this western Cape York coast, whose people moved between rivers, inlets and seasonal camps to fish, gather and hunt. In 1444 no European chart marked the bay, and the shore was ordered instead by its channels, wells, landing places and the neighbouring Paman-speaking countries to the east and south.

Recorded European ships arrived more than a century and a half later. Willem Janszoon's Duyfken made the earliest documented Dutch landfall in Australia at the Pennefather River in 1606. On 8 May 1623 Jan Carstenszoon's men clashed with a party of 200 Aboriginal people near Cape Duyfken; he then named the gulf after Pieter de Carpentier and sailed south to the Staaten River. Abel Tasman surveyed the gulf in 1644, and Matthew Flinders charted the same low coast in 1802 and 1803. The visits filled European maps, but by 1821 no fort, mission or trading post had yet been planted on Albatross Bay.
zh:
阿翁提姆是温杜温达人位于卡奔塔利亚湾东岸的土地，米申河从热带季风雨林流向阿尔巴特罗斯湾，林缘接着大片红树林潮滩。这里使用的塔伊纳克维特语也被记作阿翁提姆语，居民往来于河流、海湾和季节性营地之间捕鱼、采集和狩猎。1444年，还没有欧洲海图标出这座海湾；当地人依水道、淡水井、登陆点以及东面和南面相邻的帕马语族群土地来理解这条海岸。

有记载的欧洲船只在一个半世纪后才到来。1606年，威廉·扬松的「杜伊夫肯号」在彭尼法瑟河完成澳大利亚有记录的最早荷兰人登陆。1623年5月8日，扬·卡斯特斯松的部下在杜伊夫肯角附近与二百名原住民发生冲突；他随后以彼得·德·卡彭蒂耶之名将海湾命名为卡奔塔利亚湾，并南航至斯塔滕河。阿贝尔·塔斯曼1644年考察海湾，马修·福林达斯则在1802年和1803年测绘同一条低平海岸。这些航行补全了欧洲人的地图，但到1821年，阿尔巴特罗斯湾仍未建起要塞、传教站或商栈。

en:
The mouth of Wabalumbaal, later called the Endeavour River, is Guugu Yimithirr country on the wet tropical coast of Cape York Peninsula. Its coastal clans called themselves saltwater people, while the country around modern Cooktown was known as Gangaar, the place of rock crystals; quartz used in ceremony was carried along exchange routes at least 300 kilometres to the south. In 1444 the river mouth, reef passages and nearby inland were still held and managed by Guugu Yimithirr clans, with no outside power claiming the shore.

On 11 June 1770 James Cook beached the damaged Endeavour at the river mouth for nearly seven weeks of repairs. Joseph Banks and Daniel Solander collected local plants, and Banks wrote down about fifty Guugu Yimithirr words, including gangurru, making this the first Australian Aboriginal language recorded in writing. Contact was at first cautious and then friendly, but on 19 July a dispute over sharing turtles ended in grassfires and gunshot wounds. In June 1819 Philip Parker King's surveying expedition reached the river with the botanist Allan Cunningham; King returned in 1820, recorded more words and noted large outrigger canoes. No European settlement had been planted there by 1821.
zh:
奋进河（古古伊米吉尔语称Wabalumbaal）河口位于约克角半岛湿润的热带海岸，是古古伊米吉尔人的土地。沿海氏族自称「咸水人」；后来库克敦附近的地方称Gangaar，意为水晶之地，仪式所用的石英曾沿交换路线向南流通至少300公里。1444年，河口、堡礁水道和邻近内陆仍由古古伊米吉尔各氏族拥有和管理，还没有外来势力控制这片海岸。

1770年6月11日，詹姆斯·库克把受损的「奋进号」拖上河口滩涂修理，停留近七周。约瑟夫·班克斯和丹尼尔·索兰德采集当地植物，班克斯还记下约50个古古伊米吉尔词，包括gangurru，使这种语言成为第一种被文字记录的澳洲原住民语言。双方起初谨慎接触，随后一度友好往来，但7月19日因海龟分享问题发生冲突，草地被点燃，也有人遭火枪击伤。1819年6月，菲利普·帕克·金率测量队抵达，植物学家艾伦·坎宁安随行；金1820年再来，记录更多词汇并注意到大型舷外架独木舟。到1821年，欧洲人仍未在此建立定居点。

en:
The Wulgurukaba, whose name means canoe people from wulgurru, a bark canoe, held the dry-tropical coast around Cleveland Bay and Halifax Bay. They crossed between the mainland and Yunbenun, the mountainous island later named Magnetic Island, where seasonal camps, shell middens and cave drawings marked the bays they used. Wulguru dialects linked the coastal groups with neighbouring rainforest peoples. In 1444 this was a seascape as much as a shoreline: bark canoes carried people to offshore islands and reefs, and no outside power had entered Cleveland Bay.

In June 1770 James Cook's Endeavour sailed along the coast; Cook named Magnetic Island and Cleveland Bay but did not land, while he observed people crossing the shallows in eight-foot bark canoes. The first recorded European landing in the area came in 1819, when Phillip Parker King's surveying expedition arrived with the botanist Allan Cunningham. Through 1821 no European settlement followed, and Wulgurukaba groups continued to command the passages between their mainland shores and island camps.
zh:
乌古鲁卡巴（Wulgurukaba）其名来自wulgurru（树皮独木舟），意为「独木舟人」。他们居住在克利夫兰湾与哈利法克斯湾一带的干热带海岸，往返于大陆和Yunbenun（后来的磁岛）之间；岛上多处海湾留有季节性营地、贝冢和岩画，标示出他们反复利用的地方。Wulguru语各方言把这些沿海群体与邻近雨林族群联系在一起。1444年，这里既是海岸也是海路世界，人们乘树皮独木舟前往外岛和礁区，还没有外来势力进入克利夫兰湾。

1770年6月，詹姆斯·库克的「奋进号」沿岸驶过；库克命名了磁岛和克利夫兰湾但没有上岸，同时看见有人乘8英尺长的树皮独木舟穿越浅滩。1819年，菲利普·帕克·金率测量队抵达，植物学家艾伦·坎宁安随行，这是欧洲人在当地登陆的最早记录。此后到1821年仍无欧洲定居点，乌古鲁卡巴各群体继续掌握着大陆海岸与岛屿营地之间的水道。

en:
Baiali, also written Byelle or Byellee, is the coastal country from the Fitzroy delta to the deep harbour between the Calliope and Boyne Rivers. The Fitzroy, called Toonooba by the peoples of its catchment, drains a vast basin into Keppel Bay, and the Baiali are remembered there with the Jetimarala as Darumbal-connected clans. Around the future Gladstone, Baiali people shared the shore with Gooreng Gooreng, Toolooa and Meerooni groups; their Pama–Nyungan language, Bayali, was later recorded from Rockhampton to Gladstone. In 1444 the estuaries, islands and harbour were known through Baiali speech and neighbouring coastal networks, not through any European chart.

In May 1770 James Cook's Endeavour passed the harbour entrance in darkness and did not enter. On 1 August 1802 Matthew Flinders, sailing the Investigator during his circumnavigation of Australia, sighted the inlet and named it Port Curtis after Vice-Admiral Sir Roger Curtis, who had helped repair his ship at the Cape of Good Hope the previous October. Flinders put the sheltered water on European maps, but in 1821 there was still no British settlement on the Baiali coast.
zh:
拜阿里（Baiali，也拼作Byelle或Byellee）的滨海土地，从Fitzroy河口三角洲延伸到Calliope河与Boyne河之间的深水港湾。Fitzroy河被流域各族称为Toonooba，其广阔水系注入Keppel Bay；在这一带，Baiali人与Jetimarala人都被记作与Darumbal人相连的氏族。在后来的Gladstone周围，Baiali人与Gooreng Gooreng、Toolooa和Meerooni群体共用海岸；他们的帕马—尼永甘语Bayali，后来在Rockhampton至Gladstone之间留下记录。1444年，河口、岛屿和港湾只存在于Baiali人的语言与邻近海岸网络中，欧洲海图上还没有这里。

1770年5月，詹姆斯·库克的「努力号」乘夜驶过港湾入口，没有驶入。1802年8月1日，马修·弗林德斯乘「勘察者号」环绕澳大利亚航行时望见这座水口，将其命名为Port Curtis，以纪念前一年10月在好望角协助修船的罗杰·柯蒂斯海军中将。弗林德斯把这片避风水域标上欧洲海图，但到1821年，拜阿里海岸仍未出现英国定居点。

en:
Between Batemans Bay and Cape Howe the Yuin hold a coast of rocky headlands, sea inlets and surf beaches backed by the forested scarp of the Great Dividing Range. They are many clans—Wandandian, Walbunja, Djiringanj, Thaua and others—living by fish, shellfish and the mullet runs, and putting out to sea in bark canoes. Above the shore at Tilba rises Gulaga, the mother mountain, whose sons are Najanuka at her side and Barunguba, Montague Island, far out in the ocean. Perhaps 11,000 Yuin lived along this coast on the eve of European arrival. In 1444 the only sails here were their own.

On 21 April 1770 Cook's Endeavour, passing well offshore, named Gulaga Mount Dromedary. No ship put in then, but in 1789 smallpox ran ahead of the settlers, reaching the coast through Aboriginal networks from Sydney years before most Yuin saw a European. George Bass, driving south in an open whaleboat in 1797, sheltered in Twofold Bay in February 1798 and gave the bay its name; returning that October with Matthew Flinders in the Norfolk, he surveyed it and made first contact with the Thaua. Sealing and whaling vessels followed, and the Mary was wrecked sheltering there in 1821. By then no European station yet stood on Yuin ground, though the old coastal life had already been broken by disease.
zh:
在巴特曼斯湾与豪角之间，尤因人守着一条遍布岩岬、海湾与浪滩的海岸，背后是林木覆盖的大分水岭陡坡。他们分为众多氏族——万丹迪安、瓦尔本贾、吉林甘、陶阿等——以鱼、贝类和鲻鱼渔汛为生，划树皮独木舟出海。蒂尔巴岸边矗立着母亲山古拉加，她的两个儿子是身旁的纳贾努卡和远在海中的巴伦古巴，即蒙塔古岛。欧洲人到来前夕，约有一万一千名尤因人生活在这条海岸上。1444年，海面上只有他们自己的帆影。

1770年4月21日，库克的「奋进号」在远海经过，将古拉加山命名为单峰驼山，当时并无船只靠岸。1789年，天花赶在殖民者之前，沿原住民的往来网络从悉尼传到海岸，比大多数尤因人见到欧洲人早了许多年。1797年乔治·巴斯驾无甲板捕鲸艇南下，1798年2月在图福德湾避风并为海湾命名；同年10月他与马修·弗林德斯乘「诺福克号」重返，测绘海湾并首次与陶阿人接触。随后海豹猎船和捕鲸船接踵而至，1821年「玛丽号」在湾中避风时失事。此时尤因人的土地上还没有欧洲人的定居站，但旧日的海岸生活已被疫病摧残得元气大伤。

en:
The Gunditjmara, also called Dhauwurd Wurrung, hold south-western Victoria around Portland, Port Fairy, Warrnambool and the volcanic wetlands of Budj Bim. The Kerrup Jmara clan lived around Lake Condah and the Koroitgundidj near Tower Hill. Lava flows from Budj Bim reshaped Darlot Creek into chains of swamps and pools, where the Gunditjmara built kilometres of channels, weirs, dams and holding ponds to trap and rear short-finned eels. Small stone huts clustered around these works. In 1444 the country was a settled aquaculture landscape, with particular lakes, traps and villages held under clan law.

European ships appeared only at the end of the period. In December 1800 James Grant sailed along the coast in Lady Nelson and named Portland Bay; Matthew Flinders in Investigator and Nicolas Baudin recorded more landmarks in 1802. Around 1810 whalers and sealers began using Portland Bay as a seasonal base, bringing limited trade and new diseases but establishing no permanent post. Through 1821 the eel channels, stone settlements and clan estates remained in Gunditjmara hands.
zh:
贡迪杰马拉人（也称Dhauwurd Wurrung人）是维多利亚州西南部的原住民，土地环绕波特兰、费里港、瓦南布尔和布吉必姆火山湿地。Kerrup Jmara氏族住在康达湖周围，Koroitgundidj氏族则靠近塔山。布吉必姆的熔岩流使达洛特溪一带形成串珠状沼泽与水塘，贡迪杰马拉人在此开凿数公里长的渠道，修筑堰、坝和蓄养池，用来诱捕和蓄养短鳍鳗；小石屋也围绕这些工程聚落成村。1444年时，这里已是由氏族按湖泊、鱼梁和村落管理的定居型水产养殖之地。

欧洲船只到这一时期末尾才出现。1800年12月，詹姆斯·格兰特乘「纳尔逊夫人号」沿岸航行，命名波特兰湾；1802年，马修·弗林德斯乘「考察者号」、尼古拉·博丹也先后记录更多海岸地标。约1810年起，捕鲸者和海豹猎者开始把波特兰湾当作季节性据点，带来有限贸易和新的疾病，但尚未建立永久站点。到1821年，鳗鱼渠、石屋聚落和氏族领地仍掌握在贡迪杰马拉人手中。

en:
The Nukunu hold the eastern shore of upper Spencer Gulf, their country running from north of the Broughton River mouth and Crystal Brook to the head of the gulf, and inland through Melrose, Mount Remarkable, Gladstone, Quorn and Baroota. Nukunu is a Thura–Yura language, and this meeting of coast, southern Flinders Ranges and plains shaped its camps, sacred places and male initiation law. In 1444 no European ship had entered Spencer Gulf, and Nukunu families moved freely between its tidal shores, watercourses and hill country.

Matthew Flinders made the first recorded European exploration of Spencer Gulf in February 1802, aboard Investigator, and named it Spencer's Gulph on 20 March after the Earl Spencer. Nicolas Baudin's French expedition surveyed the same waters soon afterwards. Neither voyage established a shore post or broke Nukunu control of the interior. Through 1821 the upper gulf and its nearby ranges remained Nukunu country.
zh:
努库努人住在斯潘塞湾上段东岸，传统地域从布劳顿河口以北和克里斯特尔布鲁克向北延伸到湾头，并向内陆经过梅尔罗斯、里马克布尔山、格拉德斯通、阔恩和巴鲁塔。努库努语属于图拉—尤拉语支；海岸、南弗林德斯岭与平原相接，塑造了他们的营地、圣地和男性成年礼规。1444年时还没有欧洲船只进入斯潘塞湾，努库努各家族仍自由往来于潮汐岸、水道和山地之间。

1802年2月，马修·弗林德斯乘「考察者号」首次有记录地勘探斯潘塞湾，并于3月20日以斯潘塞伯爵之名将海湾命名为斯潘塞湾。尼古拉·博丹率领的法国探险队随后也测绘了这片水域。这些航行都没有在岸上建立据点，也没有打断努库努人对内陆的控制。到1821年，上海湾及附近山岭仍是努库努人的土地。

en:
Between the forested Remutaka and Tararua ranges and the sea runs the south-eastern coast of the North Island, from the great Ahuriri lagoon in Heretaunga, later called Hawke's Bay, down to the glistening waters of Lake Wairarapa. Its people are Ngāti Kahungunu, descendants of Kahungunu of the Tākitimu canoe and of Rongomaiwahine, whom he married at Māhia. Under Taraia his followers made Heretaunga their own, displacing the earlier Whatumamoa, Rangitāne and Ngāti Awa, and a chief named Te Ahuriri cut the lagoon's outlet to the sea that still bears his name; related hapū settled south among the eel and bird grounds of Wairarapa. In 1444 Ngāti Kahungunu held the whole coast from the bay to the Wairarapa lakes.

Late in the eighteenth century Te Kahu-o-te-rangi and Te-O-Tane shattered the war parties of Te Whānau-ā-Apanui at Whāwhāpō, securing the northern approaches to Heretaunga. In October 1769 James Cook became the first European to sail this shore, naming Hawke Bay after Admiral Sir Edward Hawke and Cape Kidnappers after an attempt to seize a Tahitian boy from his ship; the potatoes introduced on Cook's voyages soon spread through Māori gardens. No European settlement followed for another two generations, and the coast remained entirely in Ngāti Kahungunu hands in 1821.
zh:
在林木茂密的雷穆塔卡山脉、塔拉鲁阿山脉与大海之间，是北岛的东南海岸：北起黑雷陶加（后称霍克湾）畔的阿胡里里大潟湖，南至波光粼粼的怀拉拉帕湖。住在这里的是雅提卡胡伍努伊人，即塔基蒂穆号独木舟上的卡胡伍努与他在马希亚娶得的朗戈迈瓦希内的后裔。在首领塔拉亚率领下，卡胡伍努的部众取得黑雷陶加，取代早先的瓦图马莫阿、朗吉塔内和恩加蒂阿瓦等部；酋长特阿胡里里为潟湖开凿出海水道，这处地方便以他得名；同族的支系则向南定居在怀拉拉帕盛产鳗鱼和水鸟的湿地间。1444年，从霍克湾到怀拉拉帕湖群的整条海岸都在雅提卡胡伍努伊人手中。

18世纪末，特卡胡奥特朗吉与特奥塔内在法法波一战大破特瓦瑙阿阿帕努伊人的战阵，稳固了黑雷陶加北面的门户。1769年10月，詹姆斯·库克成为第一个驶过这段海岸的欧洲人，以海军将领爱德华·霍克之名命名霍克湾，又因当地人试图掳走船上一名塔希提少年而命名绑架角；随其远航传入的马铃薯很快推广到毛利人的园圃中。此后又过了两代人，欧洲人仍未在此定居，到1821年，这段海岸还完全掌握在雅提卡胡伍努伊人手中。

en:
Te Tau Ihu, 'the tip of the fish's nose', is the pointed top of Te Waipounamu, the South Island: the long sandspit beyond Cape Farewell, the shallow bay of Mohua, Tasman Bay and the drowned valleys of the Marlborough Sounds. Some of the oldest settlements in the country stand here. The Waitaha, descendants of Rākaihautū's Uruaokapuarangi canoe, kept the 400 hectares of the Waimea Gardens below Pikimai, the hill above the anchorage later called Whakatū, or Nelson, and were the first people to quarry pakohe argillite on Rangitoto ki te Tonga, D'Urville Island; its dark adzes were traded through the sound of Tōtaranui as far north as Te Ika-a-Māui. In 1444 the kūmara gardens, eel weirs and rich seafood grounds of the tip belonged to the old peoples of the sounds, with Waitaha foremost among them.

Early in the 1600s Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri of the Kurahaupō canoe pushed west through the sounds and made themselves masters of the whole northwest for two centuries. In December 1642 two strange ships entered Mohua, Abel Tasman's Heemskerck and Zeehaen, the first Europeans Māori had ever seen. Waka challenged them with trumpets and ritual calls; a Dutch cockboat was rammed, four seamen were killed and one warrior was shot, and Tasman sailed away naming the place Murderers' Bay without ever landing. In 1770 James Cook sheltered in Tōtaranui, which he named Queen Charlotte Sound, and from a hill on Arapaoa Island saw the sea passage between the two islands that now bears his name; he returned in 1773 and 1777. Around 1810, after long wars over the greenstone trail, Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri were defeated in the Paparoa Ranges, their chiefs Te Pau and Te Kokihi slain, and their lands divided among Ngāi Tahu, Ngāti Apa and Ngāti Kuia.
zh:
陶伊胡意为「鱼鼻尖」，是特怀波纳穆（南岛）最北端的尖角：告别角外长长的沙嘴、水浅的莫胡阿湾、塔斯曼湾和马尔堡峡湾一片被海水淹没的山谷。新西兰最早的居民点有一些就在这里。怀塔哈人是拉凯豪图所率乌鲁阿奥卡普阿朗吉号独木舟的后裔，他们在皮基迈山下经营着四百公顷的怀梅阿园圃——皮基迈山俯瞰的港湾后来称华卡图，即尼尔森；怀塔哈人最早在朗吉托托基东加（德于维尔岛）开采巴科赫泥岩，打出的深色石斧经托塔拉努伊峡湾远销北岛。1444年，这处尖角上的库马拉园圃、鳗鱼堰和丰饶的海场属于峡湾诸部，其中以怀塔哈人为首。

17世纪初，乘库拉豪波号独木舟迁来的恩加蒂图马塔科基里人沿峡湾西进，成为整个西北部的主人，称雄近二百年。1642年12月，两艘陌生的大船驶入莫胡阿湾，那是阿贝尔·塔斯曼的「赫姆斯凯克号」与「泽哈恩号」，也是毛利人初见欧洲人。毛利人的独木舟吹起螺号、以战叫向船挑战；一艘荷兰交通艇被撞沉，四名水手被杀，一名战士中枪，塔斯曼未敢登陆便起航离去，将此地命名为「杀人犯湾」。1770年，詹姆斯·库克泊入托塔拉努伊，将其命名为夏洛特女王湾，并在阿拉帕瓦岛的一座山丘上望见分隔两岛、后来以他命名的海峡；他又于1773年和1777年两度回到这里。约1810年，在为绿玉商路长期交战之后，恩加蒂图马塔科基里人在帕帕罗瓦山脉战败，大酋长特保与特科基希被杀，土地被纳塔胡、恩加蒂阿帕和恩加蒂库伊亚三部分占。

en:
The Waikato is the wide, garden-rich basin of New Zealand's longest river, which winds north from the great lake of Taupō to the sea. Its terraces and swamps grew kūmara, taro and yams, its lakes and backwaters teemed with eels and waterfowl, and before European times it was the third most densely peopled part of the country. The Tainui, descendants of Hoturoa's Tainui waka, had been settled at Kāwhia since the fourteenth century and entered the Waikato around 1400 bringing kūmara with them. At Kirikiriroa, 'the long stretch of gravel' where Hamilton now stands, the villages of Te Parapara, Miropiko and Pukete lay among river gardens. In 1444 the river was a highway of canoes and fish catches, and Tainui hapū were still working up its reaches against the earlier peoples of the interior.

By the end of the seventeenth century they had made the upper basin theirs after the siege of Pōhatu-roa. The age's great trial came around 1807 at Hingakaka, near Ōhaupō, where the Waikato chief Te Rauangaanga led 3,000 Waikato and Ngāti Maniapoto warriors to victory over a host of 7,000 to 10,000 raised by Ngāti Toa and Ngāti Raukawa — the largest battle ever fought in New Zealand. Te Rauangaanga's son Pōtatau Te Wherowhero led the Waikato taua south on the Āmiowhenua raid in 1821, while to the north Hongi Hika's musketeers destroyed Mauinaina and stood at the Waikato's gateway; the storm soon to break over Kirikiriroa was already gathering.
zh:
怀卡托是新西兰第一长河怀卡托河冲积出的宽阔盆地，河水自陶波大湖北流入海。河阶与沼泽种着库马拉、芋头和薯蓣，湖泊河汊盛产鳗鱼与水禽，欧洲人到来之前，这里是新西兰人口第三稠密的地区。泰努伊人自认是霍图罗阿所驾「泰努伊号」独木舟移民的后裔，14世纪起定居卡菲亚，约1400年携库马拉进入怀卡托。在今哈密尔顿所在的基里基里罗阿——意为「长长的砾石滩」——蒂帕拉帕、米罗皮科、普凯蒂等村落散布在河畔园地之间。1444年的怀卡托河是独木舟与渔获往来的大道，泰努伊各部仍在沿河向上游推进，与内陆先住民争地。

到17世纪末，经波哈图罗阿围城一役，泰努伊人已把上游盆地收入囊中。约1807年，这个时代的大考验在奥豪波附近的欣加卡卡到来：怀卡托酋长特·劳安甘甘加率三千名怀卡托与恩加蒂马尼亚波托武士，击败恩加蒂托阿、恩加蒂劳卡瓦联军七千到一万之众，是新西兰有史以来规模最大的战役。特·劳安甘甘加之子波塔陶·特·维罗维罗1821年率怀卡托战团南下参加「环地」远征，而北方杭吉·希卡的火枪兵已踏破莫伊纳伊纳寨堡，陈兵怀卡托北境门户——即将袭向基里基里罗阿的风暴正在聚集。

en:
Jeju is the volcanic island dominated by Hallasan in the strait south of Korea. Its Tamna rulers traded with China, Japan, and the Korean kingdoms while keeping local rulers under Goryeo overlordship. After the Sambyeolcho resistance ended there, the Yuan used island pastures for Korean and Mongol cavalry horses; Jeju returned to Goryeo in 1295. Joseon ended the autonomy of the old seongju and wangja houses in 1404, and in 1416 Taejong divided the island into Jeju-mok, Jeongui-hyeon, and Daejeong-hyeon under Jeolla. In 1444 a magistrate governed from basalt-walled Jeju over fishing villages, fields, horse pastures, and a distant island also reserved for political exiles.

European shipping reached this isolated outpost in 1653, when Hendrick Hamel, a Dutch East India Company clerk sailing to Japan, was wrecked on Jeju. Joseon would not let the survivors leave for thirteen years; after Hamel escaped to Dejima in 1666, his journal, published in the Netherlands in 1668, gave Europe its first detailed account of Korea. In 1793 famine struck the island's three districts: more than six hundred people had starved and five government grain ships were lost. The merchant Gim Man-deok spent her fortune on mainland rice and gave it to the hungry. King Jeongjo acknowledged the rescue in 1796 and, breaking the usual restriction on Jeju islanders crossing the sea, allowed her to visit Hanyang and the mainland before her death on Jeju in 1812.
zh:
济州是朝鲜海峡中一座以汉拿山为中心的火山岛。岛上的耽罗政权曾与中国、日本和朝鲜半岛诸国贸易，并在高丽宗主权下保留本地君长。三别抄的抵抗在岛上结束后，元朝把这里的牧场用作高丽和蒙古骑兵的养马地；1295年，济州复归高丽并改用今名。1404年，朝鲜废除旧有星主、王子家族的自治权，1416年太宗又将全岛划分为全罗道下属的济州牧、旌义县和大静县。1444年，地方官从玄武岩城墙环绕的济州城治理渔村、农田和牧场；这座远海岛屿同时也是政治犯的流放地。

1653年，欧洲商船终于来到这座偏远外岛：驶往日本的荷兰东印度公司书记员亨德里克·哈梅尔在济州遇险。朝鲜不许幸存者离境，哈梅尔被留十三年，直到1666年才逃到出岛；他的游记1668年在荷兰出版，成为欧洲第一部详细记述朝鲜的亲历记录。1793年，济州三邑遭遇饥荒，六百余人饿死，五艘官府运粮船又在途中沉没。商人金万德散尽家产，从陆地购米赈济饥民。1796年，正祖表彰她的义举，并打破济州人不得随意渡海的限制，允许她前往汉阳和大陆；1812年，金万德在济州去世。

en:
Yukjin, the Six Garrisons, was the chain of Hoeryong, Jongseong, Onsong, Gyeongwon, Gyeongheung and Puryong below a bend of the Tumen River. Gyeongwon, once called Gongju, had long been contested between Goryeo and the Jurchen. Joseon established Gyeongwon-bu there in 1398, evacuated it after a Jurchen attack in 1409, restored the garrison in 1414 and moved its seat in 1428 while sending farmers north. In 1433 Kim Jong-seo fixed the frontier on the Tumen and moved 2,200 farming households from southern Hamgil to the new forts. By 1444 Gyeongwon headed a string of Korean military settlements, while Jurchen villages still held much of the river country.

The mixed border remained volatile. In 1583 Nitanggae, a Jurchen tributary chief near Hoeryong, rose against Joseon; the revolt lasted from January to July and exposed the weakness of the old garrison system. During the Japanese invasion of 1592, Katō Kiyomasa's 22,000-strong second army pushed through Hamgyeong as far as Onsong, but Jeong Mun-bu raised a Righteous Army among the Six Garrisons, suppressed local collaborators and fought the Japanese around Gyeongseong and Kilju until they withdrew early in 1593. Qing forces raided Hamgyeong in the winter war of 1636-1637, and after King Injo's surrender the Tumen garrisons belonged to a Joseon kingdom tributary to the Qing.
zh:
六镇是图们江一处河弯以南的会宁、钟城、稳城、庆源、庆兴和富宁六座军镇。庆源旧称孔州，长期处在高丽与女真人争夺的边缘。朝鲜1398年设庆源府，1409年因女真进攻而迁空，1414年恢复为庆源都护府，1428年再移治所并迁移南方百姓开垦。1433年，金宗瑞把东北边界推进并确定到图们江，又从咸吉道南部迁移2200户农家充实庆源等新镇。到1444年，庆源统领着一串年轻的朝鲜军屯，但图们江两岸仍有不少女真村落。

这条混居边防线始终并不安稳。1583年，会宁一带的藩胡首领尼汤介起兵反朝鲜，动乱从1月持续到7月才被镇压，也暴露了旧有镇管体制的弱点。1592年壬辰战争中，加藤清正率二万二千日军穿过咸镜道，最远推进到稳城；郑文孚在六镇组织义兵，诛灭当地附乱者，并在镜城、吉州一带持续作战，迫使日军于1593年初南撤。1636年至1637年的冬季战争中，清军攻掠咸镜道；仁祖投降后，图们江诸镇仍属朝鲜，只是朝鲜已成为清朝的藩属。

en:
Gyeongseong lies on the East Sea coastal plain beneath the Hamgyong Mountains. After Goguryeo and Balhae, the country was held by Jurchen communities, who knew it as Urong'i or Mokranggo; it was repeatedly disputed with Goryeo and at times placed under Yuan authority. The new Joseon dynasty named it Gyeongseong in 1398, set up a military camp in 1400, established Gyeongseong-bu in 1410 and raised it to a protectorate office in 1432. In 1444 it was therefore a garrison administration on the cold northeastern edge of the kingdom, guarding Korean outposts and fishing coast among Jurchen settlements.

In 1467 Yi Si-ae's rebellion of Hamgil gentry began at Gilju and tied down royal armies until August. After its defeat Gilju was demoted, Gyeongseong was promoted as the new northern centre, the North Military Camp was placed there, and in 1468 the province was renamed Hamgyeong from Hamheung and Gyeongseong. During the Japanese invasion, Katō Kiyomasa's army occupied the far north in 1592, but in the ninth lunar month Jeong Mun-bu raised a Righteous Army, entered Gyeongseong by turning its collaborator commander, and used the town as a base before killing him and clearing North Hamgyeong. Qing raids reached Hamgyeong in 1636-1637, after which the garrison formed the northeastern frontier of Qing-tributary Joseon.
zh:
镜城位于咸镜山脉与东海之间的沿海平原。这里先后受高句丽、渤海控制，后来成为女真诸部的土地，女真人称之为于笼耳或木郎古；高丽曾长期在此争夺，它也曾一度处于元朝势力之下。新生的朝鲜王朝1398年将此地命名为镜城，1400年设兵马节度使军营，1410年设镜城府，1432年升为镜城都护府。到1444年，这里已是朝鲜寒冷东北缘的军镇，在女真聚落之间守卫着朝鲜哨所和海岸渔村。

1467年，咸吉道豪族李施爱在吉州起兵，叛乱直到8月才被镇压。事后吉州被降级，镜城升为北方新的军政中心，北兵营设于此地；1468年，道名也取咸兴与镜城之首字，改称咸镜道。1592年日军入侵，加藤清正所部占据北方；同年农历九月，郑文孚组织义兵，先争取镜城的附乱首领入城，随后将其诛灭，并以镜城为基地肃清咸镜北部。1636年至1637年清军攻掠咸镜道，战后镜城成为向清朝称臣的朝鲜东北边疆军镇。

en:
Yeongbyeon lies in the hills along tributaries of the Ch'ongch'on River, guarding the road from Pyongyang toward the Yalu frontier. Under Goryeo the country was divided between Yeonju and Muju; in 1413 Joseon reorganized them as Yeonsan and Musan, and in 1429 King Sejong merged the two into the Yeongbyeon Grand Protectorate, with its seat at Yaksan Fortress. The Sejong sillok gazetteer counted 1,121 households and 2,906 people, including 50 guard troops, 532 wing soldiers, 24 fortress soldiers and 208 boatmen. In 1442 the military headquarters was moved to Ganggye, so in 1444 Yeongbyeon remained a walled northern stronghold but no longer housed the regional command.

The headquarters returned in 1446, was removed again in 1450, and was restored under King Danjong. During the Japanese invasion of 1592, the Jeonju copy of the Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty was briefly sheltered on Mount Myohyang, while Hyujeong of Pohyon Temple was named chief overseer of the eight provinces and sixteen sects and called monk soldiers to arms. In 1624 Yi Gwal rose in revolt at Yeongbyeon and briefly occupied Hanyang before royal troops put him down. The command moved to Anju in 1627; during the Manchu invasions of 1627 and 1636, besieging forces spent days before the steep fortress without taking it. By 1759 the protectorate comprised 12 wards, its walled center and 134 villages, with 7,354 households and 26,600 people. In the 1811 Hong Gyeong-rae rebellion, magistrate Oh Yeon-sang executed more than ten plotters led by Nam Ik-hyeon and held the walls, so Yeongbyeon joined Kusong and Uiju among the towns that did not fall.
zh:
宁边位于清川江支流间的山地，扼守平壤通往鸭绿江边境的道路。高丽时期这一带分设延州、抚州；1413年朝鲜改为延山都护府与抚山县，1429年世宗将二者合并为宁边大都护府，治所设在抚山的药山城。《世宗实录地理志》载当地有1121户、2906人，军额包括侍卫军50人、翼军532人、守城军24人、船军208人。1442年节制使营移往江界，因此1444年的宁边虽是北方城塞要地，却暂未驻有区域统军机构。

1446年节制使营迁回宁边，1450年再度撤废，到端宗时恢复。1592年壬辰倭乱时，全州史库所藏《朝鲜王朝实录》一度移存妙香山；普贤寺的休静被任为八道十六宗都总摄，号召僧兵起兵。1624年，李适在宁边发动叛乱，一度攻占汉阳，不久被官军镇压。1627年节制使营移往安州；1627年和1636年两次胡乱中，围攻的后金与清军面对险峻城塞数日不能破城。到1759年，宁边府辖有12坊、1处府内和134里，共7354户、26600人。1811年洪景来之乱时，府使吴渊常先捕杀南益显等十余名内应并加固城防，宁边与龟城、义州同为未被攻陷的城镇。

en:
Gyeongju, called Seorabeol or Geumseong, was for nearly a thousand years the royal capital of Silla. After the unification of 668 it became the political and cultural heart of the Korean peninsula: the Cheomseongdae observatory was built in the 640s, the nine-storey wooden pagoda of Hwangnyongsa rose in 645, and in the eighth century the minister Kim Daeseong founded Bulguksa and the Seokguram grotto. When Silla submitted to Goryeo in 935 the court departed, and the city, renamed Gyeongju, served briefly as Goryeo's 'Eastern Capital' from 987 until the title was withdrawn in 1012. Mongol invaders burned Hwangnyongsa's great pagoda in the thirteenth century, and in early Joseon Neo-Confucian zealots smashed Buddhist images on Namsan. In 1444 Gyeongju was a quiet prefectural town of Gyeongsang, its fields and lanes scattered with the monuments of a vanished dynasty.

During the Japanese invasion of 1592 the Gyeongju plain became a battlefield: Kim Ho's local righteous army defeated a Japanese force at Nogok in August, but the old capital fell, and in May 1593 the invaders burned Bulguksa, where close to two thousand bays of halls went up in smoke. Government troops under Pak Jin and the militia leader Gwon Eung-su retook the city later that year after two sieges, bombarding its walls with the newly devised flying-thunder bombs, and state-sponsored repairs to Bulguksa began in 1604. In 1601, while the war still raged, the Gyeongsang provincial office was moved from Gyeongju to Daegu, and the town never recovered its old rank. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries it remained a country seat of the Southerners faction and of old Silla-descended lineages, their yangban villages such as Yangdong lying among the royal tombs while traffic moved past the broken pagoda of Hwangnyongsa.
zh:
庆州古称徐罗伐、金城，近千年间一直是新罗的王都。668年新罗统一之后，这里成为朝鲜半岛的政治与文化中心：瞻星台建于640年代，皇龙寺九重木塔于645年落成，8世纪大臣金大城又主持修建佛国寺与石窟庵。935年新罗归降高丽，朝廷不复存在；改称庆州后，它在987年被高丽定为「东京」，1012年这一称号又被废止。13世纪蒙古入侵，皇龙寺大塔毁于兵火；进入朝鲜时代初期，性理学者中的排佛激进者还砸毁了南山的佛教造像。1444年的庆州是庆尚道一座安静的府城，田野街巷间散落着旧王朝的遗迹。

1592年壬辰倭乱，庆州平原沦为战场：金虎率领的本地义兵8月在露谷击败一支日军，但旧都终归陷落，1593年5月日军放火焚烧佛国寺，近两千间殿宇化为灰烬。翌年稍后，朴晋的官军与义兵首领权应铢两度围城，用新造的飞击震天雷轰开城墙，收复庆州；佛国寺的国家修复工程则于1604年启动。1601年，战火尚未平息，庆尚道监营已从庆州迁往大邱，庆州再未能恢复旧日的行政地位。17、18世纪里，它是南人派和新罗旧族后裔的乡居之地，两班村落如良洞村坐落于王陵之间，行人车马从皇龙寺残破的塔址旁经过。

en:
Vidin commands a broad Danube crossing in fertile north-western Bulgaria, where Roman Bononia guarded Upper Moesia and medieval Bdin grew into a Bulgarian stronghold. Its Baba Vida citadel took shape between the tenth and fourteenth centuries. In 1356 Ivan Stratsimir received the city and ruled the surrounding Vidin Tsardom as an effectively independent Bulgarian ruler; Hungarian crusaders held it only from 1365 to 1369. After Sultan Bayezid I's victory at Nicopolis in 1396, the Ottomans annexed Vidin and made it a sanjak. King Vladislav III besieged the town during the 1444 crusade, but by the time of Varna the Danube fortress and its fertile, wine-growing hinterland were back under an Ottoman garrison.

For three centuries Vidin lay in the Ottoman-Habsburg border belt. It remained an administrative and economic pashalik, trading wine together with furs and barrelled caviar from the Danubian region, but great wars repeatedly reached its walls. Austrian troops took Vidin in October 1689, held it for nine months and destroyed much of the town before the Ottomans returned in August 1690. Frontier disorder later raised Osman Pazvantoğlu, a former Janissary mercenary who ruled the Vidin region almost independently from 1795 until his death in 1807 and built a mosque, library and Janissary barracks there. His wars and rival Ottoman campaigns scattered villagers across the Danube flats. Between 1812 and 1820 the authorities attracted Bulgarian families returning from Wallachia to resettle abandoned estates, leaving Vidin in 1821 a fortified Ottoman river town on a slowly recovering frontier.
zh:
维丁扼守保加利亚西北部肥沃土地上的多瑙河渡口，罗马的波诺尼亚曾在此守卫上默西亚，中世纪的布丁则发展为保加利亚要塞。巴巴维达城堡在10至14世纪间逐渐成形。1356年，伊凡·斯拉齐米尔获得此城，以近乎独立的保加利亚君主身份统治周围的维丁沙皇国；匈牙利十字军只在1365至1369年间占据过这里。1396年苏丹巴耶济德一世在尼科波尔获胜后，奥斯曼吞并维丁并将其设为桑贾克。1444年十字军期间，国王瓦迪斯瓦夫三世曾围攻维丁，但到瓦尔纳战役时，这座多瑙河要塞及其肥沃产酒的腹地已重新由奥斯曼驻军掌控。

此后三个世纪，维丁处在奥斯曼与哈布斯堡的边界缓冲地带。它仍是重要的行政和经济帕夏辖区，经营葡萄酒，也输出来自多瑙河地区的毛皮和桶装鱼子酱，但大战一再波及城墙。1689年10月，奥地利军队攻占维丁，占据九个月，摧毁大片城区，直到1690年8月奥斯曼人才夺回。边疆动荡后来把前禁卫军雇佣兵奥斯曼·帕兹万特奥卢推上台面；他从1795年起近乎独立地统治维丁地区，直至1807年去世，并在城中修建清真寺、图书馆和禁卫军兵营。他的战争以及奥斯曼各派军队的争斗使多瑙河平原村民离散。1812至1820年间，当局吸引从瓦拉几亚返回的保加利亚家庭重新垦殖废弃庄园；到1821年，维丁仍是一座奥斯曼设防河城，守着缓慢恢复的边疆。

en:
Khara Narin Ula, the Black Narrow Mountain, is the range known to the Chinese as the Lang Shan, the Wolf Mountains — the westernmost spine of the Yin system guarding the north-west corner of the Yellow River's Ordos Loop. Its southern cliffs fall straight to the back-loop plain, while the gentler northern slope runs out into the stony Gobi plateau. Through a gorge in the range runs Gaoque, the High Tower pass, where the kings of Zhao carried their long wall and Han armies marched out against the Xiongnu. In 1444 no Ming garrison or magistrate remained in the back loop; the mountains and desert pastures were roamed by Tatar, Oirat and Uriankhai herdsmen under the loose lordship of the Northern Yuan.

Around 1510 Dayan Khan's victories brought the loop within his reunited Mongol realm, and the Ordos tumen made these lands their grazing ground; for a century their horsemen filed through the Lang Shan passes on their way to raid the Ming frontier. Qing rule remade the border. In 1648 the Urad chiefs were enfeoffed and their people set in three jasak banners, and in 1649 the banners moved to the north bank of the Yellow River. The eastern Wolf Mountains and the steppe stretching north toward the Gobi became Urad pasture under the Ulanqab League, a quiet frontier facing the Khalkha across the desert.
zh:
哈拉纳林乌拉，蒙古语意为「黑色的窄山」，汉人称之为狼山，是阴山山脉最西端的一道山脊，扼守黄河河套的西北角。山南峭壁直落后套平原，北坡平缓，逐渐没入砾石遍布的戈壁高原。山间峡谷中有高阙塞，赵武灵王筑长城「至高阙为塞」，汉军也由此出塞与匈奴争战。1444年，后套已无明朝的卫所与官吏，狼山及北面的荒漠牧场由鞑靼、瓦剌、兀良哈等部众游牧，名义上尊奉北元大汗。

1510年前后，达延汗连战连捷，河套并入其重新统一的蒙古，鄂尔多斯万户以此为牧场；此后百余年间，骑兵屡屡穿过狼山口南下，袭扰明朝边境。入清之后边防改易：1648年乌喇特首领受封，部众编为三个札萨克旗，1649年三旗移牧黄河北岸。狼山东段及以北通往戈壁的草原成为乌拉特牧地，会盟乌兰察布，化作与大漠以北喀尔喀相望的安静边地。

en:
Jianchang lies along the Anning River valley between the Dadu and Jinsha rivers, the corridor through which Sichuan meets Yunnan and the Daliangshan Yi country. The Tang post of Xizhou was refashioned by Nanzhao in the ninth century as Jianchang Prefecture, and Dali kept the name. The Mongols subdued the region between 1253 and 1256; in 1275 they created Jianchang Route, with its seat at Jian'an in present Xichang, under the Luolusi native command. Marco Polo, who knew the country as Jiandu, noted rods of gold and molded salt used in exchange. Ming forces took over in 1382, creating Jianchang Prefecture and Jianchang Guard; the civil prefecture was abolished in 1392, and from 1394 the guard was the seat of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission, which controlled five guards, eight battalions and four native offices. In 1444 Jianchang was therefore a garrison borderland rather than an ordinary county town.

The Ming garrison order survived the dynastic transition. In 1650 the Qing placed a Jianchang intendant in the guard to oversee grain supplies and inspect the old military administration; the office was withdrawn in 1667 and restored two years later. In 1728, as the court tightened control over the Liangshan frontier, it established Ningyuan Prefecture and Xichang County at Jianchang, giving the Anning valley a regular civilian administration. During the eighteenth century, missionaries of the Paris Foreign Missions Society also brought Roman Catholicism into Ningyuan.
zh:
建昌位于大渡河与金沙江之间的安宁河谷，是四川入云南、通往大凉山彝区的走廊。唐朝巂州在9世纪被南诏改建为建昌府，大理国沿用此名。蒙古于1253至1256年征服这一带，1275年置建昌路，治所在今西昌的建安州，归罗罗斯宣慰司管辖。马可·波罗称此地为建都，记载当地人以金条论值、用模制盐块作小额交易。1382年明军接管，设建昌府和建昌卫；建昌府于1392年废除，1394年起建昌卫成为四川行都指挥使司治所，下辖五卫、八所、四长官司。因此1444年的建昌是军镇边地，而不是普通县城。

明朝的卫所秩序经历了王朝更替。1650年，清廷派驻整饬建昌道于建昌卫，督理粮储并分巡旧行都司辖区；该道于1667年裁撤，两年后复置。1728年，随着清廷加强对凉山边地的控制，又于建昌设宁远府和西昌县，使安宁河谷有了常规文官行政。18世纪，巴黎外方传教会的传教士也把罗马天主教传入宁远。

en:
Tikhvin grew up around the Orthodox Predtechensky pogost on the Tikhvinka River, where portages and boat routes linked the Volga with Lake Ladoga and the Baltic. It is first mentioned in 1383, when a chronicle records a wooden Church of the Dormition there. Its position at that crossroads drew traders and craftsmen, and by the turn of the sixteenth century it was known well beyond Novgorod's northeastern forests. In 1444, however, it was still a Novgorodian parish and calling point on the Volga-Ladoga route, rather than the fortified monastery town it later became.

After Novgorod passed to Moscow, Vasily III paid for a stone Dormition Cathedral, built in 1507-1515 by the Italian architect Fryazin and Dmitry Syrkov for the Tikhvin icon of the Mother of God. In 1560 Ivan IV ordered the Dormition Monastery and the smaller Vvedensky Convent, with two trading settlements, raised in a single spring and summer; by the mid-seventeenth century the monastery had nine towers and log walls packed with earth and stone. In 1613 De la Gardie's Swedish troops burned the posad, but on 25 May Leonty Artsybashev led an uprising and the townspeople withstood a siege in the monastery before driving the Swedes out; the war ended in 1617. Tikhvin blacksmiths and the Tikhvin Fair prospered in the following decades. The townspeople gained their own magistrate in 1723, the town was chartered in 1773, and the Tikhvin water system opened in 1811, eventually carrying as many as 6,000 vessels a year toward St Petersburg and the Volga fairs.
zh:
季赫温起于季赫温卡河畔的东正教普列杰琴斯基教区聚落，附近的水陆联运路线把伏尔加河、拉多加湖和波罗的海连接起来。它最早见于1383年的记载，一部编年史提到当地建起木制圣母安息教堂。处在商路交会处使这里吸引了商人和工匠，到16世纪初，它的名声已传出诺夫哥罗德东北森林之外。但1444年时，这里仍是诺夫哥罗德的教区和伏尔加河至拉多加湖航路上的停靠点，尚未成为后来那座设防修道院城镇。

诺夫哥罗德归入莫斯科后，瓦西里三世出资修建石造圣母安息大教堂；1507—1515年，意大利建筑师弗里亚津与德米特里·瑟尔科夫为季赫温圣母像建成此堂。1560年，伊凡四世下令兴建圣母安息男修道院和规模较小的圣母进堂女修道院，同时建起两个工商业聚落，整个工程在一个春夏内完成；到17世纪中叶，修道院已有九座塔楼，以及内部填实土石的双层木墙。1613年，德拉加迪麾下的瑞典军队焚毁城镇聚落，但列昂季·阿尔齐巴舍夫在5月25日领导起义，市民退入修道院坚守围城，最终击退瑞典人，战争于1617年结束。此后数十年，季赫温铁匠和季赫温集市日益兴盛。1723年，居民获得自己的市政机构，1773年正式设市，1811年季赫温水系开通，每年通行船只一度多达六千艘，往来于圣彼得堡与伏尔加河流域市集之间。

en:
Plovdiv rises on the hills beside the Maritsa in the fertile Upper Thracian plain, where Roman Philippopolis guarded the junction of the Via Militaris with roads to the Danube, Aegean and Black Sea. It later passed repeatedly between Byzantium and medieval Bulgaria, was destroyed by Kaloyan in 1206 and rebuilt under successive rulers. Ottoman forces took Philippopolis in 1364 and called it Filibe. The town served as an early Ottoman seat of Rumelia until 1382, when Sofia became the province's main centre, but it remained the chief town of the Plovdiv sanjak. In November 1444, after the defeat at Varna, Filibe was therefore a securely Ottoman road and caravan centre set in productive Bulgarian Orthodox country.

During the following Ottoman centuries Filibe became one of the principal commercial towns of the inland Balkans. Traffic between Edirne and Istanbul, Sofia and Belgrade moved through its khans, while the Maritsa valley and side roads carried the grain, livestock and crafts of the Thracian plain. Ottoman patrons built mosques, madrasas, caravanserais, bazaars and hammams, yet the city also remained an important centre of Bulgarian culture and Orthodox memory. In the seventeenth century Evliya Çelebi described a large, handsome city of many mosques, minarets, lodges, khans, baths and schools, and ranked it among the notable Ottoman cities of Rumelia. In 1821, though no longer the provincial capital, Filibe was still the seat of a sanjak and a rich market on the empire's main Balkan road.
zh:
普罗夫迪夫坐落在肥沃的上色雷斯平原、马里察河畔的丘陵上。罗马时代的菲利普波利斯正位于军事大道与通往多瑙河、爱琴海和黑海道路的交会处。此后它在拜占庭与中世纪保加利亚之间多次易手，1206年被卡洛扬摧毁，又在后继统治者手中重建。1364年，奥斯曼军队攻占菲利普波利斯，改称菲利贝。这座城曾是奥斯曼人在鲁米利亚的早期治所，1382年索非亚成为该省主要中心后，它仍是普罗夫迪夫桑贾克的首城。1444年11月瓦尔纳战败之后，菲利贝已稳在奥斯曼手中，是生产丰裕的保加利亚东正教土地上的道路与商队中心。

在随后的奥斯曼世纪里，菲利贝成为巴尔干内陆最重要的商业城镇之一。埃迪尔内、伊斯坦布尔与索非亚、贝尔格莱德之间的人流货流经它的客店周转，马里察河谷和支道又运来色雷斯平原的谷物、牲畜和手工业品。奥斯曼庇护者修建清真寺、伊斯兰学校、商队旅馆、巴扎和土耳其浴室，而城市也仍是保加利亚文化和东正教记忆的重要中心。17世纪时，埃夫利亚·切莱比记载这是一座大而美观的城市，有许多清真寺、宣礼塔、道堂、客店、浴室和学校，并称其为鲁米利亚值得注意的奥斯曼城市之一。1821年，菲利贝虽不再是行省首府，却仍是桑贾克治所和帝国巴尔干干道上的富庶市场。

en:
Cuenca crowns a narrow ridge between the gorges of the Júcar and Huécar rivers. It grew around Qunka, a Muslim fortress of the Santaver district, until Alfonso VIII of Castile stormed the town on 21 September 1177 after a long siege. The Fuero of Cuenca, a bishopric created in 1183 and civic rank granted by Alfonso X in 1257 secured its place in Castilian law. Flocks and woollen cloth paid for the cathedral and drew new quarters down the river slopes. In 1444 Cuenca was therefore a Catholic Castilian wool town in the Iberian System, prosperous but still defensively tied to its rocky citadel.

Henry IV added the titles 'Very Noble and Very Loyal' in 1465. The Jewish quarter, documented since the Christian conquest, came to an end with the expulsion of 1492, and the Inquisition pursued converted families long afterwards; the last major crypto-Jewish trials in the city ran from 1718 to 1725. Woollen cloth and tapestries made Cuenca famous in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, but the trade collapsed in the seventeenth and the city lost population sharply. It recovered somewhat in the following century and, after supporting Philip V in the War of the Spanish Succession, received the titles 'Most Faithful and Heroic'. Charles IV later restricted local textile production to protect the royal tapestry works, and during the Peninsular War Cuenca was sacked more than nine times.
zh:
昆卡坐落在胡卡尔河与韦卡尔河峡谷之间的一道狭窄山脊上。它围绕穆斯林桑塔韦尔地区的昆卡要塞发展起来，1177年9月21日，卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索八世在长期围困后攻下此地。《昆卡法典》、1183年设立的主教区，以及阿方索十世1257年授予的城市地位，确立了它在卡斯蒂利亚法律中的位置。牧群和毛纺织业为大教堂提供资金，也把新的街区推向河谷坡地。1444年的昆卡已是伊比利亚山脉中一座信奉天主教的卡斯蒂利亚毛织业城镇，虽称富庶，防务仍系于岩石上的城寨。

1465年，恩里克四世授予昆卡「至贵至忠」的称号。自基督教征服后便有记载的犹太区，随着1492年驱逐犹太人而终结；宗教裁判所此后长期追查改宗家庭，当地最后一轮大规模隐秘犹太教徒审判发生在1718年至1725年。15至16世纪，毛料和挂毯让昆卡闻名，但这门产业在17世纪崩溃，城市人口也急剧减少。下个世纪昆卡略有恢复，并因在西班牙王位继承战争中支持费利佩五世而获「至信至勇」称号。卡洛斯四世后来限制当地纺织生产以保护皇家挂毯厂；半岛战争期间，昆卡又遭九次以上洗劫。

en:
Romsdal is the fjord country of western Norway where the Romsdalsfjord meets the steep valley of Romsdalen and the Rauma river runs down to the sea. Before the unification of Norway it was a petty kingdom, and in the Viking age the island of Veøya, where the inner sea lanes forked, held the district's first market town and probably the seat of Jarl Ragnvald of Møre; the little St Peter's church was raised there over a heathen site at the end of the 1100s. In 1122 King Eystein I died at Hustad on this coast while travelling towards Nidaros. In 1444 Romsdal belonged to the Norwegian crown within the Kalmar Union, a Catholic land of free fishermen and farmers under the diocese of Nidaros, with Veøya and the fishing haven of Bud as its chief settlements.

In 1604 Molde, by then a timber-and-herring harbor trading with Holland, became a loading place under Trondheim. In 1612, during the Kalmar War, some 300 Scottish mercenaries landed at Isfjorden to march to Sweden and were cut down by Norwegian peasants at Kringen. By the treaty of Roskilde in 1658 the Swedish frontier came down to the Romsdalsfjord, but the farmers refused Swedish taxes and conscription, and the treaty of Copenhagen in 1660 restored the border. Molde became the seat of the governor of Romsdal, residing at Moldegård from 1705, and on 29 June 1742 Christian VI granted it full market-town rights despite protests from Bergen and Trondheim. The district followed Norway into the union with Sweden in 1814.
zh:
鲁姆斯达尔是挪威西部的峡湾之乡，鲁姆斯达尔峡湾在此与陡峻的鲁姆斯达尔山谷及奔流入海的劳马河相接。挪威统一之前这里是一个小王国；维京时代，扼守内海航道分岔口的韦于亚岛形成了本区最早的商镇，很可能还是默勒伯爵拉格瓦尔德的驻地，12世纪末岛上又在异教圣地建起圣彼得小堂。1122年，国王厄斯泰因一世在前往尼达罗斯途中病逝于海岸边的胡斯塔。1444年的鲁姆斯达尔属卡尔马联盟中的挪威王冠，是尼达罗斯教区治下天主教自由渔民和农民的土地，韦于亚和渔港布德是其主要聚落。

1604年，当时靠木材和鲱鱼与荷兰贸易的莫尔德成为特隆赫姆管辖的装卸港。1612年卡尔马战争期间，约三百名苏格兰雇佣兵在伊斯菲尤伦登陆，打算开往瑞典，在克林根被挪威农民伏击歼灭。1658年的《罗斯基勒条约》把瑞典边界推到鲁姆斯达尔峡湾北岸，但农民拒不缴纳瑞典赋税、不服瑞典兵役，1660年的《哥本哈根条约》恢复了旧界。莫尔德成为鲁姆斯达尔长官驻地，1705年起长官住进莫尔德庄园；1742年6月29日，克里斯蒂安六世不顾卑尔根和特隆赫姆反对，授予莫尔德完整市镇权。1814年，鲁姆斯达尔随挪威并入与瑞典的联盟。

en:
Narbonne was founded by the Romans in 118 BC as the colony of Narbo Martius, capital of Gallia Narbonensis, where the Via Domitia forked toward Spain and the Atlantic. Under the Visigoths it headed the kingdom of Septimania, and after the Frankish reconquest of 759 its archbishop and viscount ruled it jointly. The twelfth century was its golden age: the viscountess Ermengarde held court for the troubadours, and its Jewish scholars were famed across Latin Christendom. Around 1300, with some 30,000 people, Narbonne was the greatest cloth-working centre in Languedoc, shipping woollens to Spain and the Levant. A flood in 1320 swept away the Aude's dam and its harbour began to silt; the Black Death, the Free Companies and the Black Prince's chevauchée of 1355 did the rest. In 1444 the city, still one of France's oldest archiepiscopal sees, was a half-empty former port whose viscounts no longer resided there.

In 1447 the Tinières family sold the viscounty to Gaston IV of Foix; his son Jean's daughter Germaine married King Ferdinand of Aragon in 1505. Cardinal Giulio de' Medici was archbishop from 1515 until his election as Pope Clement VII in 1523. The cathedral of Saints Justus and Pastor mirrors the decline: its choir vault rises 41 metres, among the highest in France, but the nave was never built, blocked by the city wall. From the sixteenth century the town dredged and rebuilt its old waterway as the Canal de la Robine, at last joined to the Canal du Midi in 1776. In 1790 the Revolution made Narbonne a district town of the new Aude department, with Carcassonne as capital, and the Concordat of 1801 suppressed the ancient archbishopric, merging it into Carcassonne. Wine, carried out on the Robine, remained the district's livelihood.
zh:
纳博讷由罗马人建于公元前118年，初名纳尔博·马提乌斯殖民地，是纳尔博南西斯行省的首府，多弥提亚大道在此分岔，通往西班牙与大西洋。西哥特时期它是塞蒂马尼亚王国的都城，759年法兰克人收复后，城市长期由大主教与子爵共同治理。12世纪是纳博讷的黄金时代：女子爵埃芒加德在宫中庇护行吟诗人，城中的犹太学者闻名于整个拉丁基督教世界。1300年前后，纳博讷约有三万居民，是朗格多克最大的呢绒织造中心，毛料远销西班牙和黎凡特。1320年一场洪水冲毁奥德河上的拦河坝，港口日渐淤塞；黑死病、自由佣兵和黑太子1355年的骑行劫掠又接踵而至。1444年的纳博讷虽仍保有法兰西最古老的总教区之一，已是一座半空的旧港，子爵一家也久居在外。

1447年，蒂尼耶尔家族将子国卖给富瓦伯爵加斯东四世，其子让的女儿热尔梅娜于1505年嫁给阿拉贡国王斐迪南。1515年至1523年，枢机主教朱利奥·德·美第奇担任纳博讷大主教，随后当选教皇，称克雷芒七世。圣茹斯特与圣帕斯托尔大教堂正是这场衰落的写照：歌坛拱顶高达41米，为法兰西最高的几座之一，正殿却受城墙所阻始终未能建起。16世纪起，市民疏浚重建旧河道，修成罗比讷运河，终于在1776年与米迪运河连通。1790年大革命将纳博讷划为新奥德省的地区治所，省会设在卡尔卡松；1801年教务专约撤销古老的总教区，并入卡尔卡松教区。沿罗比讷运出的葡萄酒，始终是这一带赖以为生的行当。

en:
La Mancha is Castile's dry southern tableland, crossed by the Guadiana and bounded by the Montes de Toledo and Sierra Morena. After the Reconquista its towns and grazing grounds were granted chiefly to the Orders of Santiago and Calatrava. Alfonso X founded Villa Real in 1255 as a royal town embedded in Calatrava's domain, and rivalry with the order shaped its early history; the Cortes met there in 1346, and John II made it Ciudad Real in 1420 after its militia supported him against the military orders. In 1444 it was still a small royal city overshadowed by Almagro, while the plains lived from grain and sheep and Calatrava's mines at Almadén produced cinnabar and quicksilver.

In the Castilian succession crisis, the Pachecos of Villena and the masters of Santiago and Calatrava supported Juana la Beltraneja and her Portuguese husband; towns around Alcaraz rose in March 1475, until the 1479 Treaty of Alcáçovas confirmed Isabella and Ferdinand. Anti-converso rioting shook it in 1474, an Inquisition tribunal sat there in 1483-85, and a royal chancellery in 1494-1505. The comunero rising of 1520 reached the region, and after its defeat the military-order estates, including Almadén, passed to the Crown in 1523. The Fuggers then administered the mercury mines; after amalgamation spread in American silver mining, Almadén quicksilver went through Seville to the Indies, and from 1566 convicts worked its toxic shafts. The mines returned to crown administration in 1645. Windmills multiplied in the sixteenth century, and Cervantes placed Don Quixote's adventures in this countryside in 1605 and 1615. La Mancha became a province in 1691, with Ciudad Real as capital except when Almagro held that role from 1750 to 1761. The Battle of Almansa helped secure Philip V, and Charles III founded Spain's first mining academy at Almadén in 1777. French forces took it in March 1809 and held it until 1813; Almadén fell in January 1810 and remained occupied until 1812.
zh:
拉曼查是卡斯蒂利亚南部干燥高原，瓜迪亚纳河流贯其间，北接托莱多山，南连莫雷纳山。再征服运动后，这里的城镇和牧场主要封给圣地亚哥骑士团与卡拉特拉瓦骑士团。1255年，阿方索十世在卡拉特拉瓦领地中建立皇家镇，作为王室直辖城镇，城镇与骑士团的对抗塑造了它的早期历史；1346年卡斯蒂利亚议会在此召开，1420年皇家镇民兵在内战中支持胡安二世，国王遂升其为城市，改称雷阿尔城。1444年，它仍是一座被阿尔马格罗盖过锋芒的小型王领城市；高原因谷物和绵羊为生，阿尔马登的卡拉特拉瓦矿山则出产辰砂和水银。

卡斯蒂利亚继承危机中，比列纳的帕切科家族及圣地亚哥、卡拉特拉瓦骑士团首领支持胡安娜·贝尔特拉内哈和她的葡萄牙丈夫。1475年3月，阿尔卡拉斯一带的城镇起事，直到1479年《阿尔卡索瓦斯条约》确认伊莎贝尔与费尔南多获胜。1474年雷阿尔城发生反对改宗者的骚乱，宗教裁判所1483年至1485年在此设庭，皇家大法官法院又于1494年至1505年驻于此地。1520年公社派起事波及这一地区；失败后，包括阿尔马登在内的骑士团地产于1523年并入王室。富格尔家族随后经营汞矿，美洲银矿采用混汞法后，阿尔马登水银经塞维利亚运往西印度；1566年起，苦役犯被送入有毒矿坑。矿山1645年恢复由王室管理。16世纪风车在高原上增多，塞万提斯在1605年和1615年出版的《堂吉诃德》中，把主人公的冒险放在这片乡野。1691年拉曼查设省，雷阿尔城为省会，仅1750年至1761年由阿尔马格罗担任。邻近的阿尔曼萨战役帮助费利佩五世巩固王位，卡洛斯三世又于1777年在阿尔马登创办西班牙第一所矿业学院。1809年3月法军攻占雷阿尔城并占领至1813年；阿尔马登于1810年1月失守，被控制到1812年。

en:
Soria sits high on the upper Douro, on the old frontier between Castile, Aragon and Navarre. The Aragonese king Alfonso the Battler conquered and resettled it between 1109 and 1114, and it passed to Castile in 1134; Alfonso VIII was born here in 1155. His fueros put the town in the hands of twelve noble lineages, the Doce Linajes. Its wealth came from wool: Soria stood at the head of several royal drovers' roads, and under the Mesta created in 1273 it organized the summer shearing of great transhumant flocks and sent the clip north through Burgos to the ports. Its Jewish quarter, some 1,000 strong in the census of 1290, handled much of that trade. In 1369, during the Castilian civil war, Bertrand du Guesclin's mercenaries stormed it, after which the Crown granted the town as a lordship to royal princes. In 1444 Soria was a prosperous wool town of noble lineages, though the frontier wars that had enriched it were already past.

The union of Castile and Aragon in 1479 cost Soria its border trade, and the expulsion of the Jews in 1492 dispersed its merchant community; the lordship reverted to the Crown only in 1539, and a long decline set in. In the War of the Spanish Succession the town took the side of Philip V. During the Peninsular War French troops captured Soria in 1808 and put it to the torch, badly damaging its medieval walls and Romanesque churches.
zh:
索里亚坐落在杜罗河上游的高原上，地处卡斯蒂利亚、阿拉贡与纳瓦拉之间的旧边界。阿拉贡国王阿方索一世（斗士）于1109至1114年间攻占并重新移民此地，1134年并入卡斯蒂利亚；1155年阿方索八世出生于此。他赐予的特许状把市政交给十二支贵族世家（「十二族」）治理。城市的财富来自羊毛：索里亚扼守数条皇家牧道的起点，依托1273年成立的梅斯塔荣誉会组织大群转场绵羊的夏季剪毛，再把羊毛经布尔戈斯运往北方各港。本地犹太社区在1290年普查中约有千人，承担了其中大部分贸易。1369年卡斯蒂利亚内战中，贝特朗·杜·盖克兰的雇佣兵强攻入城，此后城市被王室作为封邑封给王族成员。1444年的索里亚是一座由贵族世家治理的富庶羊毛城镇，只是养肥它的边境战争已成往事。

1479年卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡合一，索里亚失去了边镇之利；1492年驱逐犹太人，又散去了它的商人群体。封邑迟至1539年才归还王室，城市由此陷入长期衰落。西班牙王位继承战争中，索里亚站在腓力五世一边。半岛战争期间，法军于1808年攻占索里亚并纵火焚城，其中世纪城墙和罗曼式教堂损毁严重。

en:
The highlands of Welayta fill the broken country between the Bilate and the Omo, where the rains turn the valleys into marsh and the mountain woods run with coffee. Its Omotic-speaking people, the Wolayta, were ruled by kings bearing the title kawo, in a kingdom whose own traditions reach back to about 1251 and which some scholars identify with the medieval kingdom of Damot of the remembered Kawo Motolomi. More than fifty kings across four dynasties are said to have reigned, and in 1444 the Malla kawo still held court beyond the reach of both Christian Ethiopia and the Muslim lords of the lowlands, his people keeping their old rites among coffee forests and cattle pastures.

The wars of Ahmad Gragn reached even these marshes in the sixteenth century, when Adal's men for a time occupied the country, until its waterlogged roads drove them out, as the Adal chronicler Arab Faqih himself admitted. Far more lasting were the Oromo migrations, which stripped away the kingdom's subject lands and in the upheaval replaced the Malla dynasty with the Tigre Malla line; in the seventeenth century Kawo Gazenja struck back and won a string of victories over Oromo raiders. Through it all the highland markets kept up the trade in coffee and ivory, above all the old hill town of Bonga on the road towards Kaffa, and the Wolayta kept their crown and their old beliefs in their mountains.
zh:
瓦莱塔高地占据着比拉特河与奥莫河之间的破碎地带，雨水把谷地泡成沼泽，山林间遍布咖啡。当地的瓦莱塔人说奥莫语族语言，统治者号称「卡沃」。按本国传统，瓦莱塔王国始建于约1251年，一些学者认为它就是中世纪的达莫特王国，传说中的卡沃·莫托洛米即其君主。据说四个王朝的五十多位君王相继在位；1444年，马拉王朝的卡沃仍在这片山乡发号施令，基督教的埃塞俄比亚和低地的穆斯林领主都鞭长莫及，族人在咖啡林与牧场之间守着旧有仪轨。

16世纪，艾哈迈德·格兰的战火甚至烧进了这片沼泽，阿达尔军队一度占领此地，但正如阿达尔编年史家阿拉伯·法基赫所承认的，泥泞难行的水乡最终迫使他们撤走。影响更深远的是奥罗莫人的迁徙：王国的属地大片沦丧，动荡之中马拉王朝被蒂格雷·马拉一系取代。17世纪，卡沃·加曾贾挥军反击，对奥罗莫袭掠者连获大胜。高地集市的咖啡与象牙贸易始终未断，其中最负盛名的是通往卡法要道上的古老山城邦加；瓦莱塔人的王冠与旧信仰也在这片群山中延续下来。

en:
Kaffa lies on the wet, forested southern flank of the Ethiopian Highlands. The Gojeb River bounds it to the north and the Omo to the east; near Anderaccha the Guma flows into the Gichey. Oral tradition dates the kingdom to about 1390, when Minjo replaced the earlier Mato dynasty; Bonga became the first royal center. In 1444 the sacred king, the tato, ruled the Kefficho people from these mountain forests. Hunters, leatherworkers and blacksmiths held distinct hereditary duties, while Muslim traders and Ethiopian Christians lived in the kingdom before it became a Christian state. The fertile highland valleys could yield three harvests a year, and the shade forests were an early home of Coffea arabica.
