During the sixteenth century Emperor Sarsa Dengel's influence persuaded Kaffa's court to accept Christianity as the state religion, and the church of St George at Baha preserved a tabot bearing his name; the faith largely faded in later centuries. Under Gali Ginocho, who reigned from 1675 to 1710, Kaffa began a long expansion and annexed the Gimira lands of She, Benesho and Majango. Mecha Oromo invasions in the eighteenth century cost it all territory north of the Gojeb, but the forested mountain core held. Tato Shagi Sherocho, ruling from 1775 to 1795, brought Welayta and Konta under control and pushed the frontier to the Omo and Denchya rivers. Hoti Gaocho, ruler from 1798 to 1821, carried Kaffa's power to its greatest extent.
zh:
咖法（亦译卡法）在埃塞俄比亚高原南部湿润多林的山坡上，北以戈杰布河为界，东接奥莫河；安德拉恰附近，古马河汇入吉切河。口述传统把王国的开端定在约1390年，明乔取代更早的马托王朝，本加成为最早的王都。1444年，具有宗教权威、称「塔托」的国王在这些山地森林中治理卡菲乔人。猎户、皮匠和铁匠各有世袭职分，穆斯林商人和埃塞俄比亚基督徒也住在王国境内，尽管基督教要到后来才成为国教。肥沃的高地谷地一年可三熟，遮阴林则是阿拉比卡咖啡树的原生地之一。

16世纪，在埃塞俄比亚皇帝萨尔·登格尔的影响下，咖法宫廷接受基督教为国教，巴哈的圣乔治教堂保存着刻有他名字的塔博特；但这种信仰在以后几个世纪里又大致衰落。1675年至1710年在位的加利·吉诺乔开启长期扩张，吞并谢、贝内绍和马扬戈等吉米拉人的土地。18世纪梅查·奥罗莫人入侵，咖法丢失戈杰布河以北的全部属地，却守住密林山地核心。塔托·沙吉·谢罗乔1775年至1795年在位时控制瓦莱提和孔塔，把边界推到奥莫河与登奇亚河。1798年至1821年在位的霍蒂·高乔则把咖法的势力带到最大范围。

en:
Illubabor covers the forested Gibe uplands of western Ethiopia, the country called Ennarea in Gonga tradition. After separating from Damot in the fourteenth century, it became the strongest power in the non-Muslim south, drawing tribute from Kaffa and Bosa and sending gold, slaves and cattle to the Ethiopian emperors; a song for Yeshaq I records that tribute by the early fifteenth century. In 1444 a Hinnario court still governed farmers and retainers among the Gibe headwaters, tied to the Christian empire to the north but ruled through its own Gonga institutions.

The Borana Oromo conquered much of Gibe between 1578 and 1586 and formed the Sadacha federation. After they took Ennarea in 1588, Emperor Sarsa Dengel campaigned south of the Nile and brought Christianity to its elite. A Sadacha attack in 1594 cost Ennarea the land between the main Gibe and Gibe Ennarea. In the mid-seventeenth century a Kaffa royal clan seized power and Kaffa, with Sheka, broke away. Emperor Iyasu I reached Ennarea in 1704 during a civil war, but around 1710 the Sadacha overthrew Shisafotchi. He led survivors south across the Gojeb into Kaffa, where an exile kingdom was subdued by Kaffa in the early nineteenth century. Oromo settlers then turned from pastoralism to agriculture, and five kingdoms, including Limmu-Ennarea, took shape in the old Ennarean lands.
zh:
伊路巴博是埃塞俄比亚西部林木茂密的吉贝高地，贡加传统称之为伊那瑞亚。14世纪脱离达莫特后，它成为南方非穆斯林诸邦中最强的政权，迫使咖法和博萨纳贡，又把黄金、奴隶和牛只送往埃塞俄比亚皇帝那里；一首为耶沙克一世而作的歌在15世纪初已记载这种贡赋。1444年，辛纳里奥人的宫廷仍在吉贝河源的山地间统治农民和侍从，它同北方基督教帝国联系密切，却依照自身的贡加制度治理。

1578年至1586年，博尔纳奥罗莫人征服吉贝大部，并组成萨达查联盟。1588年他们夺取伊那瑞亚后，埃塞俄比亚皇帝萨尔·登格尔进兵青尼罗河以南，把基督教带到当地精英中间。1594年萨达查再度来攻，伊那瑞亚失去吉贝干流与吉贝·伊那瑞亚之间的土地。17世纪中叶，咖法王室夺取政权，咖法和谢卡相继独立。1704年，伊亚苏一世在一场内战中抵达伊那瑞亚，但约1710年萨达查人推翻希萨福奇。他率残部南越戈杰布河进入咖法，这个流亡王国在19世纪初被咖法臣服。奥罗莫定居者随后从游牧转向农耕，旧伊那瑞亚土地上形成五个王国，利穆-伊那瑞亚便是其中之一。

en: Gambela is the hot riverine lowland between the Openo-Baro and Akobo, where streams from the Ethiopian Highlands descend toward the Upper Nile. Between the twelfth and fifteenth centuries the ancestors of the Anuak, a Luo Nilotic people, moved south and east from the Gezira between the Blue and White Niles and settled as farmers and herdsmen along the Baro and Gilo. In 1444 their scattered river villages held the country, a frontier that highland Ethiopian rulers knew chiefly as a source of slaves rather than a directly taxed province. For the rest of the period it remained a slave-raiding borderland; in the late 1700s Baggara raids west of the Nile forced Nuer groups out of southern Kordofan and southward.
zh: 甘贝拉是奥佩诺-巴罗河与阿科博河之间炎热的河畔低地，埃塞俄比亚高地的河川由此流向尼罗上游。12至15世纪，阿努亚克人的祖先——属于尼罗特卢奥人群——从青尼罗河与白尼罗河之间的杰济拉向南、向东迁徙，在巴罗河与吉洛河沿岸定居，亦农亦牧。1444年，正是他们分散的河畔村落据有这片土地；高地埃塞俄比亚政权主要把这里视为掠取奴隶的边疆，而非直接征税的省份。此后直到本时期结束，低地仍是掠奴边界；18世纪末，巴加拉人在尼罗河以西的掠奴活动迫使努尔人退出南科尔多凡，继续向南迁徙。

en:
Hadiya is the fertile, well-watered plateau south of Shewa, its ridges around the highland heart of Angacha given over to grain fields, orchards and horse pastures above the Rift Valley lakes. Its people, Muslim like the lords of Zeila and Adal, were the Cushitic Hadiyya, Halaba and Kebena, with the Semitic-speaking Silte among them, and their ruler bore the title garad. The Arab geographer al-Umari in the fourteenth century already praised its cereals, fruit and herds and its strange iron currency, and reckoned it could raise forty thousand horsemen; since the bloody campaign of Amda Seyon against King Amano the Ethiopian emperors had held it as a tributary. In 1444 the country smarted from a fresh chastening: the Emperor Zara Yaqob had deposed the tribute-refusing Garad Mahiko in favour of his uncle Bamo, and Mahiko, slain in flight to Adal, had his head and limbs sent back to the imperial camp. The Hadiya princess Eleni, baptized and married to the emperor, would one day hold the regency itself; Badlay of Adal's attempt to avenge all this ended in his death at Gomit in 1445.

Hadiya was still a quiet, densely wooded tributary paying cattle to Lebna Dengel when the Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares passed through in the 1520s. When Ahmad Gragn invaded, its Muslim governor opened the country without a fight and marched at his side. In 1569 the Emperor Sarsa Dengel crushed the revolt of Garad Aze at the Battle of Hadiya, and before the century ended the Oromo had overrun the eastern marches, where the Arsi would in time claim Hadiya forebears. Early in the seventeenth century Garad Sidi Muhammad routed the troops of Emperor Susenyos, and Hadiya kept its independence behind its forests: the Portuguese Fernandez was briefly detained and turned back in 1613, and as late as 1751 the Czech traveller Remedius Prutky could still describe an independent Muslim kingdom south of Abyssinia, marching with the western border of Adal.
zh:
哈迪亚是绍阿以南肥沃湿润的高原，昂加查一带的高地丘陵上，谷田、果园和马场连成一片，俯瞰东非大裂谷的湖群。居民与泽伊拉、阿达尔的统治者同为穆斯林，包括说库希特语的哈迪亚人、哈拉巴人、克贝纳人，以及说闪米特语的西尔提人，君主号称「加拉德」。14世纪的阿拉伯地理学家欧麦里已盛赞此地五谷丰登、果木成林、牲畜成群，以铁片为通货，并估计其能出骑兵四万；自从阿姆达·塞约恩讨平国王阿马诺的抵抗、血洗其国之后，埃塞俄比亚皇帝便把它收为藩属。1444年，哈迪亚刚挨过新的惩戒：拒纳贡赋的加拉德·马希科被皇帝扎拉·雅各布废黜，改立其叔巴莫，马希科逃奔阿达尔途中被杀，首级和四肢被送回皇帝大营；被带入宫廷、受洗并嫁给皇帝的哈迪亚公主埃莱尼，日后还将亲掌摄政权。阿达尔苏丹巴德莱兴兵复仇，于1445年在戈米特兵败身亡。

16世纪20年代，葡萄牙神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯路过时，哈迪亚仍是一片林木茂密、向勒布纳·丹格尔皇帝贡纳牲畜的安静藩地。艾哈迈德·格兰入侵时，当地穆斯林长官不战而开放国境，并随军出征。1569年，萨尔萨·登格尔皇帝在哈迪亚战役镇压了加拉德·阿泽的叛乱；到该世纪末，奥罗莫人已席卷其东部边地，后来的阿尔西奥罗莫人便自称有哈迪亚人的血统。17世纪初，加拉德·西迪·穆罕默德击溃苏森约斯皇帝的军队，哈迪亚凭密林保住了独立：1613年葡萄牙人费尔南德斯被短暂扣留后遣返；迟至1751年，捷克旅人雷梅迪乌斯·普鲁特基仍能记述，在阿比西尼亚以南、与阿达尔西境接壤处存在着这样一个独立的穆斯林王国。

en:
The Arsi country is the chain of fertile highlands southeast of Shewa, between the Awash basin and the lakes of the Rift Valley. Before the sixteenth century it belonged, with neighbouring Dawaro, to the Muslim principality of Hadiya, whose Cushitic farmers kept great herds of horses and cattle and traded iron and highland produce through the Zeila union under a ruler called the garad. Restive under Christian overlordship, the Hadiya garad Mahiko refused tribute to Zara Yaqob, fled to Adal and was killed in the pursuit, while the emperor married a Hadiya princess, Eleni. In 1444 Arsi was still Hadiya country, Muslim and tributary, in the shadow of the wars between Adal and Abyssinia.

In the 1530s Ahmad Gran's army was welcomed in Hadiya as it marched against the Christian empire, and the land supplied the imam's campaigns. After Gran's overthrow the great Oromo expansion reached these highlands: by the end of the sixteenth century the Arsi clans had occupied the country and given it their name, absorbing or displacing the older Hadiya communities. Hadiya chiefs nevertheless defeated an army of the emperor Susenyos in the early 1600s and kept their frontier independent for centuries, and a Hadiya kingdom south of Abyssinia was still reported in 1751. The Arsi lived under their own elders and customs, pasturing cattle on the heights above Assela and sending coffee and other highland goods through the markets of Harar; no outside power subdued them before the nineteenth century.
zh:
阿尔西是绍阿东南方一串肥沃高地，夹在阿瓦什河流域与裂谷湖群之间。16世纪以前，这里与邻近的达瓦罗同属穆斯林小邦哈迪亚；操库希特语的农人牧养大群马匹和牛只，在称「加拉德」的首领治下通过泽拉联盟贩卖铁器和高地物产。哈迪亚加拉德马赫科不甘基督教宗主的统治，拒绝向扎拉·雅各布纳贡，逃奔阿达尔后在追兵手中丧命，皇帝则迎娶了哈迪亚公主埃莱妮。1444年的阿尔西仍是哈迪亚之地，居民信奉伊斯兰教、称臣纳贡，处在阿达尔与阿比西尼亚战争的阴影之下。

1530年代，艾哈迈德·格兰的军队进攻基督教帝国时在哈迪亚受到欢迎，当地为伊玛目的征战供给粮草。格兰败亡后，奥罗莫人大扩张波及这片高地：到16世纪末，阿尔西部落已占据此地并以自己的名字称呼它，同化或逐走了早先的哈迪亚居民。不过哈迪亚诸首领在17世纪初击败苏塞尼奥斯皇帝的军队，使这条边疆独立了数百年之久；迟至1751年，仍有记载称阿比西尼亚以南存在一个哈迪亚王国。阿尔西人在自己的长老和习俗下生活，在阿塞拉上方的高地牧场放牧牛群，把咖啡等高地货产经哈勒尔市集外销，直到19世纪都没有外来势力征服他们。

en:
South of the Blue Nile and west of Shewa stretch the fertile highlands of Damot, the country that would later be called Welega. Its people once spoke Omotic languages and kept a pagan kingdom of their own, until tradition brought the monk Tekle Haymanot to convert its ruler and the armies of Emperor Amda Seyon I annexed the land in 1316–17. Damot became a valued province of the Ethiopian realm: its gold was carried east to the markets of Zeila, Muslim merchants prized its slaves, and its spearmen and archers marched in the emperor's wars against Ifat and Adal. In 1444 Christian lords governed these highlands on the empire's remote south-western march, whose wealth was still measured in gold dust and cattle.

The Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares, visiting in the early sixteenth century, found Damot a large and plentiful land. In 1531 the armies of Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim of Adal overran it and installed Gasa Umar as governor; imperial rule returned only after the imam's death in 1543, when Emperor Gelawdewos retook the province. Sarsa Dengel later campaigned there and led Damot warriors against the Oromo at Waj in 1572, but the Oromo tide could not be held: under the luba Birmaje, between 1578 and 1586, the Boran and Macha Oromo engulfed the province, enslaving many and carrying off the herds. Numbers of Christians fled across the Blue Nile, taking the name Damot to the Gojjam side, while the Macha settled the vacated highlands and their growing markets became the first towns of a new Welega.
zh:
青尼罗河以南、绍阿以西，横亘着达莫特的肥沃高地，即后来的沃莱加。当地居民原说奥莫语族语言，保有自己的异教王国；相传僧侣特克莱·海马诺特使其统治者皈依基督教，阿姆达·锡安一世皇帝的大军又于1316至1317年吞并此地。达莫特由此成为埃塞俄比亚的重要省份：黄金东运至泽拉的市集，奴隶深受穆斯林商人看重，当地的长矛兵和弓箭手则随皇帝出征伊法特与阿达尔。1444年，基督教诸侯统治着帝国西南边陲的这片高地，财富仍以砂金和牲畜计算。

16世纪初葡萄牙神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯到访时，见达莫特地域辽阔、物产丰足。1531年，阿达尔伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣的大军攻陷此地，任命加萨·奥马尔为总督；直到伊玛目1543年战死，格拉德沃斯皇帝才收复该省。萨尔萨·登格尔后来多次到此巡战，1572年率达莫特士兵在瓦季迎击奥罗莫人，但迁徙大潮已无法阻挡：1578至1586年的比尔马杰轮值期，博兰与马查两部奥罗莫人席卷全省，掳人为奴、夺其牲畜。大批基督徒北渡青尼罗河，把达莫特之名带到戈贾姆一侧；马查人则在空出的高地上定居，日益繁荣的市集成为新沃莱加最早的城镇。

en:
West of Damot the highlands break into forested ravines that plunge towards the White Nile basin. This is the country later called Benishangul, home to the Gumuz and other Nilo-Saharan peoples whom the Christian highlanders knew as the Shanqella and had raided for slaves since the days of Aksum; gold panned from the mountain streams was the land's other treasure. For centuries it lay as a buffer and a no-man's-land between the Muslim sultanate of Sennar on the Nile and the Christian provinces of the Ethiopian plateau. In 1444 it marked the furthest edge of Damot's reach, a borderland valued for gold dust and for the slave caravans led away by Sudanese merchants.

During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the Berta, kinsmen of the Funj of Sennar, drifted in from the Sudan and built their villages on craggy hills to guard against slave raiders. The Emperor Susenyos led an army through the country in 1617–18, but highland rule did not hold, and in 1685 the land passed to the Funj sultanate of Sennar. From the middle of the eighteenth century Oromo groups began to filter in as Funj power ebbed, settling and mingling among the Shangul villages. When the Ottoman Egyptian armies overthrew Sennar in 1821, this ravined borderland was left in the hands of its own small hill chiefdoms.
zh:
达莫特以西，高地裂作林木密布的深谷，一路俯向白尼罗河盆地。这便是后来所称的本尚古勒，住着古穆兹等尼罗-撒哈拉语族群；高原上的基督徒称他们为香克拉，自阿克苏姆时代起便到此掳掠奴隶，而山溪中淘出的黄金是此地的另一宗财富。多个世纪里，这里始终是尼罗河上穆斯林的森纳尔苏丹国与埃塞俄比亚高原基督教行省之间的缓冲地带、无人管辖之境。1444年，它处在达莫特势力所及的最西缘，领主们看重的是砂金，以及由苏丹商人成队贩走的奴隶。

16至17世纪，与森纳尔丰吉人同源的贝尔塔人从苏丹陆续迁入，为防备掠奴者，把村舍建在峭峻的山丘上。1617至1618年，苏塞尼奥斯皇帝曾率军深入此地，但高原的统治未能维持，1685年这片土地转归森纳尔的丰吉苏丹国。18世纪中叶起，随着丰吉势力衰退，奥罗莫群体开始渗入，在尚古勒人的村落间定居杂处。1821年奥斯曼埃及的军队攻灭森纳尔时，这片沟壑纵横的边地已落入本地众多小山酋之手。

en:
Aussa is the inland delta of the Awash, whose waters lose themselves in the sands and salt lakes of the northern Afar country; its perennial pastures and gardens make the oasis a meeting ground for Afar camel-herders and caravans plying between Zeila, Harar and the Ethiopian highlands. Older Harla and Doba peoples had long mingled with the Afar here. In the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries the oasis formed the western march of the Muslim Adal sultanate, and in 1444 its clans marched with Sultan Badlay in the jihad that the Emperor Zara Yaqob broke at Gomit the following year.

In 1577, after Oromo invasions and a terrible famine had undone Harar, Imam Muhammad Gasa moved Adal's capital to the Aussa oasis, near Asaita. The amirs of Harar broke away in 1647, and the imamate, worn down by raiding, was overthrown by the local Mudaito Afar in 1672. In 1734 the Mudaito leader Data Kadafo made himself sultan and founded the dynasty that ruled Aussa into modern times; he was followed by his son and grandson, whose long reigns gave the caravan roads peace. In the last decade of the century the Debne-Wemas Afar marched on the capital with hundreds of Yemeni matchlockmen hired at Aden, slew Sultan Yusuf ibn Idjahis and sacked the town. Aussa never quite recovered its political weight, but its fair remained a perpetual market thronged with Afar and Somali caravans.
zh:
奥萨（阿法尔语称阿乌萨）是阿瓦什河的内陆三角洲，河水最终消失在阿法尔北部的沙地与盐湖之间。绿洲上常年有牧草和园地，是阿法尔驼队往来于泽伊拉、哈拉尔与埃塞俄比亚高原之间的会集之地，更早的哈拉人和多巴人也早已与当地阿法尔人融合。14、15世纪时，这片绿洲是穆斯林阿达尔苏丹国的西部边地；1444年，这里的部族随苏丹巴德莱参加对埃塞俄比亚的圣战，次年这支大军被皇帝扎拉·雅各布击败于戈米特。

1577年，在奥罗莫人入侵和大饥荒摧毁哈拉尔之后，伊玛目穆罕默德·加萨把阿达尔都城迁到奥萨绿洲，在阿萨伊塔一带立足。1647年，哈拉尔的埃米尔们分立；此后伊玛目国在各路袭扰中日渐衰弱，1672年被当地的穆代托阿法尔人攻灭。1734年，穆代托首领达塔·卡达福自立为苏丹，建立了一直延续到近代的王朝，其子其孙相继在位，长久的统治护佑了商路安宁。18世纪最后十年，德布内-韦马斯阿法尔人带着数百名在亚丁雇来的也门火绳枪手进攻都城，苏丹优素福·伊本·伊德贾希斯兵败被杀，城镇遭到洗劫。奥萨的政治分量再未完全恢复，但它的集市始终是阿法尔人与索马里人驼队长年往来的常设市场。

en: Assab is a wide, sheltered bay on the arid Danakil coast, just north of the Bab-el-Mandeb; Hellenistic sailors knew a trading post nearby as Arsinoe Epidires, but by the fifteenth century the shore held only Afar fishing camps and camel herds. In 1444 it formed the remote southern edge of the Adal sultanate's coast, far from its emirs and off the caravan routes that carried slaves and ivory westward to Zeila and Tadjoura. After the Ottomans seized Massawa in 1557 their Habesh province ended well to the north, and the bay remained in the hands of local Afar chiefs, who by the eighteenth century acknowledged the sultan of Aussa as their nominal overlord.
zh: 阿萨布是干旱的达纳基尔海岸上一处宽阔避风的海湾，就在曼德海峡以北不远处。希腊化时代的水手知道附近有个叫阿尔西诺伊·埃皮迪雷斯的商站，但到15世纪，岸边只有阿法尔人的渔村和驼群。1444年，这里是阿达尔苏丹国海岸遥远的南端，远离它的埃米尔，也不在把奴隶和象牙输往泽伊拉、塔朱拉的商路上。1557年奥斯曼人夺取马萨瓦后，其哈贝什行省的管辖仅止于北面很远的海岸，阿萨布湾始终留在当地阿法尔酋长手中；到18世纪，他们在名义上奉奥萨苏丹为宗主。

en:
The grain country around Mendefera is the historic Seraye highland, southernmost of the Christian plateau districts bound together in Medri Bahri. It had been part of the Aksumite world since antiquity: a cemetery in the area held second-century-BCE burials, pottery, and bronze bracelets, and later finds included crosses and Roman coins. In the fourteenth century followers of Ewostatewos founded Debre Mariam, which grew into an important monastery and school linked to Aksum. Under Zara Yaqob, the Bahr Negash at Debarwa was raised above the chiefs of Hamasien and Seraye, and the emperor confirmed the monastery's lands. In 1444 Mendefera's fertile plateau therefore stood on Medri Bahri's southern road, where Tigrinya-speaking Orthodox villagers, monks, and traders looked toward both Aksum and Massawa.

Seraye was swept into the Ethiopian-Adal war in 1535. After Imam Ahmad's men occupied the district, a local lord, Tasfa Le'ul, killed the Adalite governor Addole and sent his head to the emperor; Wazir Abbas then defeated the rising and was appointed Bahr Negash, though plague and famine helped force the occupiers out. The Ottoman seizure of Massawa in 1557 turned the road through Seraye into a contested military corridor, and Bahr Negash Yeshaq was killed fighting with the Turks against Sarsa Dengel at Addi Qarro in 1578. During the seventeenth century local rule settled into hereditary highland families, above all the house of Hab Sellus. As imperial power faded in the eighteenth century, rival chiefs divided Seraye and the surrounding Medri Bahri lands.
zh:
门德费拉周围的谷物之乡，是历史上的瑟拉耶高地，也是梅德里·巴赫里诸基督教高原区域中最靠南的一处。此地早自古代便属于阿克苏姆世界：当地一处墓地有公元前2世纪的墓葬、陶器和铜镯，后世还出土过十字架与罗马钱币。14世纪，埃沃斯塔特沃斯的追随者建立德布雷·马利亚姆修道院，使它发展成与阿克苏姆相连的重要修院和学府。扎拉·雅各布在位时，驻德巴尔瓦的总督地位提高，统辖哈马西恩与瑟拉耶的首领，皇帝还确认了修院地产。因此在1444年，门德费拉的肥沃高原正位于梅德里·巴赫里的南道上，操提格雷尼亚语的正教村民、修士和商人同时通往阿克苏姆与马萨瓦。

1535年，瑟拉耶被卷入埃塞俄比亚—阿达尔战争。伊玛目艾哈迈德的军队占领此地后，本地首领特斯法·莱乌勒杀死阿达尔总督阿多勒，把他的首级送给皇帝；瓦齐尔·阿巴斯随后镇压起事并被任命为总督，不过瘟疫和饥荒也迫使占领军撤出。1557年奥斯曼人夺取马萨瓦后，穿过瑟拉耶的道路成为反复争夺的军事走廊。1578年，总督伊沙克与奥斯曼人联手对抗萨尔萨·丹格尔，战死于阿迪卡罗。17世纪，地方统治逐渐落入世袭高原家族之手，其中最显赫的是哈布·塞卢斯家族。18世纪帝国权威衰退，敌对首领分割了瑟拉耶和周围的梅德里·巴赫里土地。

en:
Enderta lies on the eastern edge of the Tigray highlands, where its historic seat Antalo, also called Hintalo, occupied a plateau beneath Amba Aradam and became a natural mountain fortress. Hereditary chiefs had ruled the district after the Solomonic restoration, but their bid for independence brought Emperor Amda Seyon north in the 1320s; in 1328 his son Bahr Seged also received the maritime lands. By the fifteenth century Enderta appeared on indigenous maps of the northern Horn. Its governor held the title bäalgada and organized salt caravans linking the Danakil and Afar flats with the highlands. In 1444, under Zara Yaqob, Antalo's cliffs thus guarded a Tigrinya Orthodox province of the Ethiopian empire, living from highland grain, livestock, and taxed desert salt.

Enderta entered the Adal wars early: Ras Robel, its lord and salt-district governor, was serving as governor of Tigray when he was killed fighting Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi's army at Sambera Kware on 7 March 1529. Antalo first appears in a written account in 1648, when a Yemeni ambassador described it as a fortified town; in 1678 Lasta chiefs marching to join a southern Tigray revolt were defeated nearby, and men of Hintalo were driven over the precipices. The Enderta noble Mikael Sehul became Ras of Tigray and regent at Gondar, and on 7 May 1769 his men killed Emperor Iyoas, opening the Era of Princes. After Mikael's defeat at Sarbakusa in May 1771, Enderta's governor Kefla Iyasus challenged him for Tigray and was killed. Kefla's son Wolde Selassie, born at Antalo in 1736, became Ras in 1790, kept Hintalo as his capital, sheltered Emperor Tekle Giyorgis in 1799 and 1800, and received Henry Salt there in 1805 to discuss British friendship and trade. He remained the dominant Christian warlord of northern Ethiopia until his death on 28 May 1816.
zh:
恩德塔位于提格雷高原东缘，其历史首府安塔洛又称欣塔洛，坐落在安巴·阿拉达姆山南的台地上，是天然的山寨要塞。所罗门王朝复兴后，这里长期由世袭首领统辖；14世纪20年代，他们谋求独立，安达·塞永一世因而北上压制，1328年又令其子巴赫里·塞格德兼管滨海地区。到15世纪，恩德塔已出现在非洲之角北部的本土地图上。当地总督拥有「巴阿尔加达」头衔，负责组织往来达纳基尔与阿法尔低地的盐队。1444年，在扎拉·雅各布皇帝治下，安塔洛的崖壁守护着埃塞俄比亚帝国这个操提格雷尼亚语的正教省份，居民依靠高原谷物、牲畜和向沙漠盐路征税为生。

恩德塔很早便被卷入阿达尔战争：其首领、盐区总督罗贝尔担任提格雷长官期间，于1529年3月7日在桑贝拉夸雷与艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的军队作战身亡。1648年，安塔洛首次见于文字记载，一名也门使节称它为设防城镇。1678年，拉斯塔首领准备会合南提格雷的叛军，在附近被击败，欣塔洛人被赶下悬崖。出身恩德塔贵族的米卡埃尔·塞胡尔成为提格雷总督和贡德尔朝廷摄政，1769年5月7日，他的部下杀死伊约阿斯皇帝，开启「王侯时代」。1771年5月米卡埃尔在萨尔巴库萨战败后，恩德塔总督凯夫莱·伊亚苏斯试图争夺提格雷，兵败被杀。凯夫莱之子沃尔德·塞拉西1736年生于安塔洛，1790年成为拉斯，仍以欣塔洛为都城；他在1799年和1800年庇护特克勒·乔治斯一世，1805年又在此会见亨利·索尔特，商谈与英国的友好和贸易。直到1816年5月28日去世前，他始终是埃塞俄比亚北部最有权势的基督教军阀。

en:
Angot, whose name means 'the Neck', is the ribbon of broken highland country running south from Lake Ashenge along the rim of the Ethiopian plateau, where the mountains fall away into the Muslim Afar lowlands. It was always a borderland: Christianity had been preached here in the last age of Aksum, and medieval emperors kept churches and garrisons above the escarpment, while the Dobe'a pastoralists of Doba grazed great herds below and traded with the Adal coast. Their chief market was Manadeley, on the highland edge overlooking the desert. In 1444 Angot obeyed the Christian Emperor Zara Yaqob, but many of its people were Muslim, and its caravans and kinship tied the province to Adal, whose sultan was already gathering his jihad.

Early in his reign the Emperor Baeda Maryam (1468–1478) harried the Dobe'a for years until they submitted, accepted Christianity and turned to farming; he built a church of the Virgin and planted vines and orange groves in their country. When Francisco Álvares visited Manadeley in the 1520s he found a market 'like a city or seaport', thronged with merchants from Jeddah, Cairo, Tunis, Fez, Ormus and India. The Ethiopian–Adal war swept this away: Angot was overrun and governed for Adal by Ali Ankarsah, and on 29 August 1542 Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi stormed the Portuguese stockade at Wofla on the shore of Lake Ashenge and put Cristóvão da Gama to death. After the war the Yejju, converts of the imam, settled Angot under their sheikh Umar, while Raya and Wollo Oromo pressed in from the later sixteenth century. From this mixed frontier rose the Yejju Warra Sheik, Oromo ras lords who dominated the Gondar court during the age of the princes; in the early nineteenth century the mightiest of them, Ras Gugsa of Yejju, held the puppet emperors in his hand.
zh:
安戈意为「脖颈」，是从阿申盖湖向南、沿埃塞俄比亚高原边沿延伸的一条破碎高地，再往下便是穆斯林阿法尔人的低地。这里自古是边界之地：阿克苏姆末期基督教已传入，中世纪的皇帝们在崖畔建堂驻军，崖下多巴地区的多贝阿牧人放牧着大群牲畜，与阿达尔海岸通商，他们最大的市场是坐落在高原边缘、俯瞰荒漠的马纳德莱。1444年，安戈臣属于基督教皇帝扎拉·雅各布，但居民中穆斯林众多，商路和亲族都把这方边地与阿达尔连在一起，而阿达尔苏丹此时已经在集结他的圣战大军。

巴埃达·马里亚姆皇帝（1468—1478年在位）即位之初连年征讨多贝阿人，最终迫使其归降、皈依基督教并转为农耕；他在当地建起圣母教堂，还种下葡萄和橙子。1520年代，弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯到访马纳德莱，看到这里的集市「如同城市或海港」，挤满了来自吉达、开罗、突尼斯、非斯、霍尔木兹和印度的商人。埃塞俄比亚—阿达尔战争把这一切击碎：安戈被攻占，由阿达尔方面的阿里·安卡尔萨管辖；1542年8月29日，艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐攻破阿申盖湖畔沃夫拉的葡萄牙人营寨，将克里斯托旺·达伽马处死。战后，被这位伊玛目改宗的耶朱人在谢赫·奥马尔率领下定居安戈，拉亚和沃洛的奥罗莫人也从16世纪后期起不断涌入。正是在这片混杂的边地上，耶朱人的「谢赫家族」瓦拉·谢赫崛起，在王子纷争时代以奥罗莫「拉斯」的身份掌控贡德尔宫廷，其中权势最盛的拉斯·古格萨在19世纪初挟制傀儡皇帝。

en:
Lasta is the mountain fastness of the Agaw, set between Wag and Bete Amhara. The Zagwe dynasty kept its court at Roha after losing Aksum and ruled Ethiopia from there between about 1150 and 1270; King Lalibela, who reigned around 1181–1221, gave his capital its eleven churches cut from the living rock, laid out like a second Jerusalem after the city in Palestine had fallen to the Muslims, and after his death Roha bore his name. Yekuno Amlak's restoration of the Solomonic line in 1270 ended Zagwe rule, but the dynasty's heirs stayed in Lasta and Wag, holding the title of Wagshum and claiming Israelite descent, and still commanded respect. In 1444, under Zara Yaqob, Lasta was an ancient Christian province governed through these Zagwe lords, and its rock churches already drew pilgrims.

In the 1520s the Portuguese Francisco Álvares visited Lalibela twice and despaired of making Europe believe the churches he had seen. Between July and September 1531 the soldiers of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi wasted the district, and the Adal chronicle claims he burned one of the rock churches; yet Portuguese who came after him found the churches had defied crowbars and even gunpowder. Lasta's proudest hour came under Susenyos: from 1629 the Agaw of the Emekina mountains rose under Melka Krestos for the old Orthodox faith, defeated the emperor's armies and forced him to abandon Catholicism in 1632. The revolt outlived him — at Libo in 1637 the rebels routed Fasilides and Melka Krestos briefly seized the throne before he was killed, and in 1638 another imperial army perished in the Lasta cold. Later Gondarine emperors campaigned there for generations, for Lasta and Wag kept resisting imperial control through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries; in the 1750s a European traveller still counted Lasta among the six provinces of Ethiopia truly deserving the name of kingdom.
zh:
拉斯塔是阿高人的险峻山地，夹在瓦格与贝特阿姆哈拉之间。扎格维王朝失去阿克苏姆后以罗哈为廷，约1150至1270年间在此统治埃塞俄比亚；拉利贝拉王（约1181—1221年在位）在都城凿出十一座整岩教堂，在耶路撒冷落入穆斯林之手后按第二座耶路撒冷的形制布局，罗哈在他死后也改以他的名字为名。1270年耶库诺·阿姆拉克恢复所罗门王朝，扎格维的统治告终，但其后裔留在拉斯塔和瓦格，保有「瓦格舒姆」头衔和以色列后裔的血统宣称，仍受朝野敬重。1444年扎拉·雅各布在位时，拉斯塔是由这些扎格维领主治理的古老基督教省份，岩凿教堂已吸引着八方朝圣者。

1520年代，葡萄牙人弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯两度到访拉利贝拉，说自己无论怎样描述这些教堂，欧洲人都不会相信。1531年7月至9月，艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的军队蹂躏此地，阿达尔编年史称他焚毁了一座岩教堂，可后来的葡萄牙人发现，这些教堂在撬棍甚至火药之下都安然无恙。拉斯塔最有声色的一页在苏西约斯时代：1629年起，埃梅基纳山区的阿高人在梅尔卡·克里斯托斯率领下为捍卫旧正教起事，屡败皇军，最终迫使皇帝在1632年放弃天主教。叛乱比皇帝更长寿——1637年叛军在利博击溃法西里德斯，梅尔卡·克里斯托斯一度登上皇位，随即被杀；1638年又一支皇军葬身于拉斯塔的严寒。此后贡德尔历代皇帝一再兴兵，而拉斯塔与瓦格在17、18世纪始终抗拒朝廷；1750年代到访的欧洲旅人仍把拉斯塔列为埃塞俄比亚六个真正配称王国的省份之一。

en:
Agawmeder, the 'Land of the Agaw', fills the rolling country between Gojjam, Lake Tana and the Sudanese lowlands, where the town of Dangila would later stand. The Agaw, a Cushitic people already named in Aksumite inscriptions of the fourth century, count among the oldest inhabitants of the Ethiopian highlands, and from their stock came the Zagwe dynasty that ruled the country until 1270, Lalibela among its kings. Under the restored Solomonic line their western lands became a frontier province: long since Christian, the Agaw kept their own tongue, grew grain on the high plateaux and pastured large herds, while slaves and gold brought up from the western lowlands changed hands at their markets. In 1444 Agaw lords held the western marches for the emperor, a country the court knew as a granary and a gateway towards the Muslim lands on the Nile.

The wars of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi reached the Agaw with Gojjam's fall after the Battle of Zari in 1531, and Adal raiders harried the province for the rest of the war. From the later sixteenth century Oromo war-bands pressed on the southern flank and crossed the Blue Nile, and the frontier knew no long peace. Susenyos passed through Dangila in 1620 while making his power felt along the west from Fazogli to Suakin, but his turn to Catholicism brought civil war, and his reign ended in revolt and abdication in 1632, when his son Fasilides restored the old faith. Order returned under the Gondarine kings: after putting down the pretender Yeshaq in 1685, Iyasu I marched the following year beyond southern Gojjam against the Agaw who had backed him, and in 1688 campaigned by way of Metekel into the Shanqella country, burning Gisa and Gorsi; in 1704 he settled the Christianized Gawe Oromo along the north bank of the Abbay as a bulwark. Agawmeder was never a strong polity of its own, and in the eighteenth century the lords of Gojjam gradually absorbed it, pushing their frontier west towards the little sultanate of Gubba.
zh:
阿高默德尔意为「阿高人之地」，位于戈贾姆、塔纳湖与苏丹低地之间的起伏地带，丹吉拉后来便兴起于此。阿高人属库希特语族，4世纪的阿克苏姆铭文中已有记载，是埃塞俄比亚高原最古老的居民之一；统治埃塞俄比亚直至1270年的扎格维王朝——拉利贝拉即在其列王之中——便出自阿高人。所罗门王朝复辟后，阿高人的西部土地成为帝国的边疆行省：居民早已信奉基督教，仍保留本族语言，在高原台地上种植谷物、牧放大群牲畜，西部低地贩来的奴隶和黄金也在此地市集转手。1444年，阿高诸侯为皇帝扼守西陲，宫廷视此地为粮仓，也是通向尼罗河畔穆斯林诸地的门户。

格兰的战火随着1531年扎里战役后戈贾姆陷落而蔓延到阿高，阿达尔骑兵在战争剩余的年月里连年蹂躏此地。16世纪后期起，奥罗莫武装从南境压来、渡过青尼罗河，边疆再无长久太平。1620年，苏塞尼奥斯在西巡、将兵威伸展于法祖格利到萨瓦金一线的途中经过丹吉拉；但他改宗天主教引发内战，统治于1632年在叛乱与退位中终结，其子法西利德斯随即恢复古老信仰。贡德尔林诸帝重建了秩序：1685年伊亚苏一世平定僭称者叶沙克，次年便进军戈贾姆以南，惩讨支持叛乱的阿高人；1688年他取道梅特克尔攻入香克拉人之地，焚毁吉萨、戈尔西两镇；1704年又将已改宗基督教的加韦部奥罗莫人安置在青尼罗河北岸，充作藩屏。阿高默德尔从未形成强有力的政权，18世纪间被戈贾姆诸侯逐步吞并，后者的边疆一路向西推进，直抵小邦古拜苏丹国。

en:
Semien is a wall of tablelands and pinnacles north of Lake Tana, rising to Ras Dashen and cut by the Tekezé. A sixth-century record of an Aksumite inscription called its snowy peaks inaccessible and the mountains a place of exile. The high valleys later sheltered Beta Israel villages whose people followed Haymanot Judaism, farmed cold plots, and worked as weavers and smiths. In 1329 Amda Seyon campaigned in Semien, Wegera, Tselemt, and Tsegede, and Emperor Yeshaq's conquest of Semien and Dembiya between 1414 and 1429 broke the power of Jewish governors; his settlement tied inherited land to baptism. Thus in 1444, under Zara Yaqob, the Ethiopian crown claimed the province, but many Beta Israel kept their faith in fortified villages above Christian estates and the Dabareq pass.

In 1445 Zara Yaqob married Seyon Moges, daughter of the Beta Israel leader Gideon V. After a highland revolt in 1462 she was executed for alleged espionage and Jewish leaders imprisoned; from 1465 to 1472 General Markos's campaigns demolished synagogues, built churches, and forced baptism. During the Adal war they first joined Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi, then after Dawit II's death supported Gelawdewos. Sarsa Dengel later turned captured Ottoman cannon against Semien strongholds and put the leader Gershom to death. A 1614 revolt against Susenyos was crushed by 1625, ending Beta Israel autonomy; lands were seized and Judaism forbidden. In 1629 Susenyos made his son Fasilides governor with the title Aggafari. After Fasilides became emperor in 1632 and expelled the Jesuits, Jewish craftsmen served near Gondar, while Semien passed to royal princes: Yostos held it until 1676, followed by Iyasu I and their sister Eleni. Dabareq first appears in records as a late-seventeenth-century supply stop on Iyasu's northern campaigns. James Bruce passed its high market in 1770, and Ras Gebre ruled the mountain province from Amba Hay from 1771 until 1815. In 1814 Henry Salt mapped Dabareq and noted Semien wool carpets.
zh:
塞米恩是塔纳湖北侧一列台地与尖峰，耸立着拉斯达山，并被特克泽河切开。6世纪记录下来的一份阿克苏姆铭文称这里的雪峰难以接近，还把群山当作流放之地。后来，高山河谷庇护了许多贝塔以色列村落；居民奉行哈伊马诺特犹太教，在寒冷高地上耕作，并以织布和打铁闻名。1329年，安达·塞永一世征讨塞米恩、韦格拉、策莱姆特和策格德；1414年至1429年间，伊沙克皇帝征服塞米恩与登比亚，瓦解犹太首领的权力，并把土地继承权与受洗绑定。因此在1444年扎拉·雅各布在位时，埃塞俄比亚皇权已声称领有此地，但许多贝塔以色列人仍在设防山村中保持信仰，俯视低处的基督教地产和德巴尔格山口。

1445年，扎拉·雅各布娶贝塔以色列首领吉迪恩五世之女锡永·莫格斯为妻。1462年高地爆发叛乱后，她被控通敌而处死，许多犹太首领被囚禁；1465年至1472年，马科斯将军的征讨拆毁会堂、改建教堂并强迫受洗。阿达尔战争期间，他们起初投奔艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐，达维特二世死后又转而支持格拉德沃斯皇帝。萨尔萨·丹格尔后来把缴获的奥斯曼火炮用于塞米恩山寨，并处死首领革顺。1614年反苏斯尼约斯的起义到1625年被镇压，贝塔以色列的政治自治终结，土地被没收，犹太教也遭禁止。1629年，苏斯尼约斯封其子法西利德斯为塞米恩总督，称阿加法里。法西利德斯1632年继位并驱逐耶稣会士后，犹太工匠到贡德尔附近服役，塞米恩则成为皇族亲王的封邑：约斯托斯治理到1676年，其后由伊亚苏一世和他们的姐妹埃莱尼相继管辖。德巴尔格最早见于17世纪后期记载，是伊亚苏北征途中的补给站。1770年，詹姆斯·布鲁斯经过这里的高山市场；1771年至1815年，拉斯·格布雷以安巴海为要塞统治这个山地省份。1814年，亨利·索尔特把德巴尔格绘入地图，并记载了塞米恩的羊毛地毯。

en:
Dembiya is the low-lying country on the northern shore of Lake Tana, where the warm Foggora plain rises from the reed-fringed water towards the Begemder and Wogera heights; the lake itself was once called Dembea. Amhara farmers shared it with Beta Israel villages, the Falasha whose communities stretched from here towards Semien, and its dark soil grew cotton and grain for the lake markets, with the island monastery of Gelila Zakarias standing just offshore. In 1444, under Zara Yaqob, Dembiya was a settled province of the Christian empire, its peasant villages and Falasha hamlets living together under the emperor's peace.

The jihad of Ahmad Gran reached the lake: on 19 March 1537 his men burned the monastery of Gelila Zakarias, and on 21 February 1543 the emperor Galawdewos and his Portuguese allies killed Gran at Wayna Daga on the Dembiya lake shore and routed the Adalite army. Half a century later the province became the unlikely centre of a Catholic experiment. In 1607 Susenyos granted the Jesuits land at Gorgora, where Pedro Páez built a stone church between 1618 and 1621 and a royal palace rose beside it; Susenyos declared for Rome, and perhaps 100,000 people of Dembiya and Wegera are said to have accepted the Roman rite. Orthodox revolt forced his abdication in 1632, and his son Fasilides expelled the Jesuits, abandoned Gorgora, moved the court inland to found Gondar in 1636, and in 1665 ordered the Catholic 'books of the Franks' burned. During the Era of the Princes the dejazmachs of Dembiya held the lake plain and took tribute from Muslim Galabat on the Sudan road.
zh:
德姆比亚是塔纳湖北岸的低地，温暖的福格拉平原从芦苇丛生的湖边向北抬升到贝格姆德尔和沃格拉高地；塔纳湖本身旧名就叫德姆贝亚。阿姆哈拉农民与贝塔以色列人（法拉沙人）的村落共处，后者的社群从这一带一直延伸到瑟门；肥沃的黑土种植棉花和谷物供应湖畔集市，格利拉·扎卡利亚斯岛修道院就矗立在近岸水面上。1444年扎拉·雅各布在位时，德姆比亚是基督教帝国治下安居一省，农夫的村庄与法拉沙人的村落在皇帝的和平中相邻而居。

格兰的圣战很快波及湖区：1537年3月19日，他的部下焚毁格利拉·扎卡利亚斯修道院；1543年2月21日，皇帝格拉德沃斯与葡萄牙盟友在德姆比亚湖畔的韦伊纳达加击杀格兰，阿达尔大军就此崩溃。半个世纪后，这个省份意外成为一场天主教实验的中心：1607年苏西约斯把戈尔戈拉的土地赐给耶稣会士，佩德罗·佩斯1618至1621年在此建成石砌教堂，旁边又修起王宫；苏西约斯宣布皈依罗马，据说德姆比亚和沃格拉有十万人随之改奉罗马礼。正统教派的叛乱最终迫使他在1632年退位，其子法西里德斯驱逐耶稣会士、弃置戈尔戈拉，1636年把宫廷迁往内陆、兴建贡德尔，又在1665年下令焚毁「法兰克人的经书」。王子时代里，德姆比亚的德贾兹马奇们据守湖原，并向通往苏丹道上的穆斯林城镇加拉巴特收取贡赋。

en:
Mora is the dry belt between the Harar plateau and the Gulf of Tadjoura, a country of granite hills, dry riverbeds and wells where Issa and other Somali clans pastured their camels, and where caravans coming down from Harar with coffee, ivory and slaves made their first camps on the Zeila road. The old name of the march was that of Mora, one of the Muslim principalities of the Ifat confederation, whose lord the Makhzumi sultan defeated in 1264 and which was folded into Ifat about 1288; the armies of Amda Seyon reached it in the invasion of 1332, and in later centuries it was absorbed by Adal. Such settlements as Ali Adde grew under Ifat and Adal rule, and in 1444 the whole arid border belonged to the sultan of Adal, its wells mustering the Somali lancers who filled his armies.

The emir Usman routed the raiding columns of the Emperor Baeda Maryam on this frontier in the 1470s, and for a generation the emir Mahfuz of Zeila launched his raids through these lowlands into Christian country, until Lebna Dengel's ambush destroyed his army in Fatagar and left Mahfuz dead. The sultan Abu Bakr moved his capital from Dakkar to Harar in 1520, and Ahmad Gragn rode this same road on his conquest of Abyssinia. After the long war and the Oromo incursions of the mid-sixteenth century the Adal court withdrew to Aussa in 1577; the camel clans stayed by their wells, and the Zeila road carried its coffee and ivory as before.
zh:
莫拉是哈勒尔高原与塔朱拉湾之间的干旱地带，花岗岩丘陵、干涸河床和水井散布其间；伊萨等索马里氏族在此放牧骆驼，从哈勒尔驮着咖啡、象牙和奴隶前往泽伊拉的商队，出城后第一批营地就扎在这里。这片边地古称莫拉，原是伊法特联盟中的穆斯林小邦之一：1264年其君主被马赫祖米苏丹击败，约1288年并入伊法特；1332年阿姆达·塞约恩入侵时兵锋曾抵达此地，后来几个世纪里它又被阿达尔吸收。阿里阿德等聚落便是在伊法特和阿达尔治下发展起来的。1444年，整条干旱边地都归阿达尔苏丹所有，各水井处集结着他军队中的索马里骑兵。

15世纪70年代，埃米尔乌斯曼在这道边境击溃了巴德·玛利亚姆皇帝的讨伐纵队；此后一代人时间里，泽伊拉的埃米尔马赫福兹不断经这些低地袭掠基督教地区，最终勒布纳·丹格尔在法塔加尔设伏歼灭其军，马赫福兹本人战死。1520年，苏丹阿布·贝克尔把都城从达卡尔迁往哈勒尔，艾哈迈德·格兰后来正是沿这条道路出征阿比西尼亚。长年大战和16世纪中叶奥罗莫人的涌入之后，阿达尔宫廷于1577年西撤奥萨；骆驼氏族仍守着各自的水井，泽伊拉商路上的咖啡与象牙也照旧往来。

en:
At the mouth of the Jubba River the Somali coast breaks into a chain of low islands and reefs running south toward Pate. Somali herders watered their stock at the wells of the hinterland, while on the islands lived Bajuni fishermen, Swahili-speaking Muslims in coral hamlets who sailed the sea lanes in lateen-rigged beden boats, taking shark and trading dried fish up and down the coast. Both answered to the Ajuran sultans of the House of Garen, whose engineers dammed the Jubba and Shabelle and ringed the country with stone wells, making theirs the only hydraulic empire in Africa. River plantations sent grain and fruit through Barawa and Mogadishu to Arabia and India. In 1444 the fishing anchorage that would become Kismayo was a quiet southern outpost of that wealthy state.

Early in the sixteenth century a Portuguese fleet under Tristão da Cunha stormed and burned nearby Barawa, yet could not hold the town and dared not attack Mogadishu; in the 1580s the coastal cities joined the Ottoman corsair Mir Ali Bey, a Somali fleet sailing with him to seize Pate, Mombasa and Kilwa before a Portuguese armada retook them. In the mid-1600s the Garen sultans fought long campaigns, the Gaal Madow wars, against Oromo pressing down to the coast, converting those they captured to Islam. The empire grew oppressive as it weakened, and at the century's end a former general, Ibrahim Adeer, overthrew its local vassals and founded the Geledi state of the Gobroon dynasty, which by 1821, under Sultan Mahamud Ibrahim, held the Jubba mouth and its fishing islands.
zh:
朱巴河河口一带的索马里海岸散落着一长串低矮岛屿与礁群，向南一直延伸到帕泰。内陆，索马里牧人依托水井放牧畜群；岛上住着巴琼尼渔民，他们是讲斯瓦希里语的穆斯林，聚居在珊瑚石小村，驾驶挂斜桁帆的「贝登」船往来海上，捕捞鲨鱼、沿海南北贩卖鱼干。两者都臣服于加伦家族的阿朱兰苏丹：其工匠在朱巴河与谢贝利河上筑坝修堰、在各地开凿石井，阿朱兰也由此成为非洲唯一的水利帝国。河畔农庄出产的谷物和果实，经巴拉韦与摩加迪沙销往阿拉伯和印度。1444年，后来发展为基斯马尤的那处渔港，还是这个富庶国家南端一处宁静的据点。

16世纪初，特里斯唐·达·库尼亚率葡萄牙舰队猛攻并焚毁了邻近的巴拉韦，却无力久占，更不敢进犯摩加迪沙；1580年代，沿岸各城响应奥斯曼私掠首领米尔·阿里·贝伊，一支索马里舰队与他联手夺取帕泰、蒙巴萨和基尔瓦，直到葡萄牙大舰队反攻夺回。17世纪中叶，加伦王朝对南下压迫海岸的奥罗莫人连年用兵，史称「加尔·马多战争」，被俘虏者尽数改宗伊斯兰教。帝国在衰弱中渐趋苛暴，世纪之末，出身将领的易卜拉欣·阿代尔推翻其地方封臣，建立格布龙家族的格勒迪国家；到1821年马赫穆德·易卜拉欣苏丹在位时，朱巴河口与这片渔岛都已在格勒迪治下。

en:
Merca is an old roadstead on the Banaadir coast, southwest of Mogadishu. The first-century Periplus of the Erythraean Sea already knew a trading emporium here, Essina. By the twelfth century al-Idrisi placed the Hawiye along this shore, and Ibn Sa'id called Merca their capital, ranking it with Mogadishu and Barawa as one of the three chief Muslim cities of the East African coast. In the fifteenth century it was an administrative centre of the Ajuran Sultanate, governed by the sultan's naa'ibs, to whom local tradition credits the pillar tombs around the town. The Ming treasure fleets counted the port, recorded as Molugan, among their African calls, and it was also the birthplace of the saint Sheikh Hussein, who carried Islam into Bale. In 1444 Merca was a prosperous Ajuran haven, shipping the produce of the Shabelle lowlands to Arabia.

Tristão da Cunha's Portuguese burned Barawa in 1507, and later fleets bombarded Mogadishu, but Merca itself was never stormed, and its merchants kept the Indian Ocean trade. In the 1580s its ships joined the Somali-Ottoman counterstroke of Mir Ali Bey, which briefly cleared the Portuguese from Mombasa and Kilwa. As Ajuran power crumbled at the end of the seventeenth century, a warlord called Amir seized Merca and expelled its Ajuran lords; his following, the El Amir, ruled for thirty-four years until the Bimaal drove them out in their turn. The Bimaal made the town their stronghold and kept it independent even after the Geledi Sultanate arose inland at Afgooye.
zh:
马尔卡是贝纳迪尔海岸一座古老的锚地港口，位于摩加迪沙西南。公元1世纪的《厄立特里亚海航行记》已记载这一带有商埠埃西纳。12世纪时，伊德里西记述哈维耶人居住在这片海岸；伊本·赛义德更称马尔卡为哈维耶人的都会，把它与摩加迪沙、巴拉韦并列为东非海岸三座最重要的穆斯林城市。15世纪时，它是阿朱兰苏丹国的行政中心之一，由苏丹的总督纳伊卜治理，当地传说把城外的柱墓归于他们所建。明代郑和船队也曾抵达此港，将其记作「木鲁旰」；这里还是圣徒谢赫·侯赛因的出生地，他后来把伊斯兰教传入巴莱。1444年的马尔卡是阿朱兰治下一座殷实港口，把谢贝利河下游的物产运往阿拉伯。

1507年，特里斯唐·达·库尼亚麾下的葡萄牙人焚毁巴拉韦，后来的舰队又炮轰摩加迪沙，但马尔卡本身始终未遭攻破，商人得以继续印度洋贸易。1580年代，马尔卡的船只加入米尔·阿里·贝格领导的索马里—奥斯曼联合反攻，一度把葡萄牙人逐出蒙巴萨和基尔瓦。17世纪末阿朱兰国势瓦解，一个名叫埃米尔的首领率众夺取马尔卡，赶走了阿朱兰统治者；他的部众「埃米尔人」统治此地三十四年，最终又被比马尔人逐出。比马尔人以马尔卡为据点，即便盖莱迪苏丹国在后方的阿弗戈耶兴起之后，仍长期自主掌控这座港口。

en:
Afgooye stands on the lower Shebelle River, where roads from Mogadishu and the Benadir ports meet routes into the grain-growing interior. Its medieval core was Lama Jiidle, meaning 'two roads', the seat of the Silcis, who governed the district under Ajuran overlordship. Their officials took a daily measure of grain from Geledi households and dues from herdsmen watering stock at the river. In 1444 the riverine farms, camel caravans and subject clans around Lama Jiidle made it a useful administrative and tribute centre rather than a great stone city.

Late in the 17th century, after Ajuran power weakened, Ibrahim Adeer led the Geledi revolt against Silcis ruler Umar Abrone and founded the Gobroon dynasty. Afgooye, as the town came to be called, became the capital of the Geledi Sultanate. Gobroon authority reached across the country between the Shebelle and Jubba rivers and to parts of the Benadir coast, and its markets drew ivory, leopard skins and aloe from inland caravans in exchange for cloth, sugar, dates and firearms. By the early 19th century the walled town had five gates, mosques and palaces, with weavers, potters and jewellers serving the caravan trade.
zh:
阿夫戈耶（通行译名阿夫哥耶）坐落在谢贝利河下游，摩加迪沙和贝纳迪尔诸港通往内陆产粮区的道路在此交会。其中世纪核心是意为「两条路」的拉马吉德莱，希尔西斯人以此为中心，在阿朱兰宗主权下治理这片地区。他们的官吏向格勒迪各户逐日征收谷物，又向到河边饮水放牧的牧民收费。1444年时，河畔农田、骆驼商队和纳贡诸族使拉马吉德莱成为实用的行政与贡赋中心，而不是一座巨石筑成的大城。

17世纪末阿朱兰势力衰微，易卜拉欣·阿代尔率领格勒迪人起兵，推翻希尔西斯统治者奥马尔·阿夫罗内，建立戈布伦王朝。改称阿夫戈耶的城镇成为格勒迪苏丹国都城。戈布伦的势力跨越谢贝利河与朱巴河之间的土地，远及贝纳迪尔海岸的一部分；市场吸引内陆商队带来象牙、豹皮和芦荟，换走布匹、糖、椰枣和火器。到19世纪初，这座有城墙的城镇设有五座城门，拥有清真寺和宫殿，织工、陶匠与珠宝匠为商路贸易服务。

en:
Bardera stands on the Jubba where the river bends through high, fertile ground, its banks and farms thick with tall palms — hence its Somali name Baardheere, 'the tall palm'. In 1444 it was one of the foremost inland cities of the Ajuran Sultanate, Africa's hydraulic empire: Ajuran dams and wells commanded the Jubba, its granaries supplied the Benadir ports, and Ajuran roads carried its merchants down to Barawa and Mogadishu. Its madrasas made Bardera a seat of Islamic learning as well as a market for grain, ivory and cloth.

In the 1500s Portuguese fleets sacked the coastal cities and burned Barawa, but the Ajurans kept their hold on the river and Bardera's trade went on. At the end of the seventeenth century the Ajuran empire broke apart, and the Geledi sultans of the Gobroon dynasty inherited the Jubba; under them Bardera kept its citadel and became the chief ivory market of the southern Horn, linking interior caravans to the Benadir. In 1819 a local sheikh raised a puritanical revival, forbidding tobacco, folk dances, the ivory trade and the sight of unveiled women, and gathered a reformist community within the citadel whose fame outgrew the town before 1821.
zh:
巴尔代雷坐落在朱巴河穿过高腴之地的河段，河岸与农田长满高大的棕榈，索马里语名Baardheere即「高棕榈」之意。1444年时，它是阿朱兰苏丹国——非洲的水利帝国——最重要的内陆城市之一：阿朱兰人的水坝和水井控制着朱巴河，这里的粮仓供给贝纳迪尔诸港，阿朱兰人修筑的道路把商人送往巴拉韦和摩加迪沙。城里的经学堂使巴尔代雷既是伊斯兰学术之地，也是谷物、象牙和布匹的集市。

16世纪，葡萄牙舰队洗劫沿海诸城，焚毁巴拉韦，但阿朱兰人守住了河道，巴尔代雷的贸易得以维持。17世纪末阿朱兰帝国瓦解，戈布伦家族的盖莱迪苏丹接管朱巴河流域；在其治下，巴尔代雷保留了城堡，成为非洲之角南部首要的象牙市场，把内陆商队与贝纳迪尔海岸连在一起。1819年，当地一位谢赫发起清教式复兴，禁止烟草、民间歌舞、象牙贸易和妇女不戴面纱露面，并在城堡内聚集起一个改革派社群，到1821年前其声势已超出这座城。

en:
Werder, in Somali Wardheer, is the well-country of the eastern Ogaden: the dry Doollo plain of red and white sand between the Haud and the grazing lands of the Darod clans. Its people in the 15th century were Sunni Somalis, above all the Marehan, who counted their wealth in camels and sheep and followed their own clan chiefs rather than any city sultan. Their wells made the district a node on the tracks between the upper Shebelle and the northern markets, and in 1444 the plains lay beyond the direct reach of the Adal court on the Harar plateau, a Somali pastoral country loosely bound to the Muslim world of the interior.

When Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi summoned the Somali clans to his jihad, the Marraihan, as the chronicler Arab Faqih calls the Marehan, answered under their chief Hirabu and fought from Shimbra Kure in 1529 through the conquest of Abyssinia, until the Imam's death at Wayna Daga in 1543 returned the plains to clan rule. To the south the Ajuran Sultanate, whose power ran up the Shebelle to Qalafo, set the wider order of the interior until its decline in the 17th century. From that century onward the caravan trails across the Ogaden also carried slaves taken among the Arsi and other southern peoples toward Berbera and the Red Sea, together with the livestock and hides that remained the country's real wealth; no garrison sat over Wardheer's wells, which belonged to the clans that could hold them.
zh:
韦尔德（索马里语名Wardheer）是东欧加登的水井之地：处在豪德与达鲁德诸族牧地之间的多洛干旱平原，红白沙地之上河道常年干涸。15世纪时这里的居民是逊尼派索马里人，以马雷汉人为主，他们以骆驼和羊群计富，听从本族酋长，而非任何城里的苏丹。各处水井使这一地区成为上谢贝利河与北方市场之间商路的节点；1444年，驻在哈勒尔高原的阿达尔朝廷号令难及这片平原，它是一块索马里游牧之地，与内陆穆斯林世界只保持着松散的联系。

艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐号召索马里诸族参加圣战时，编年史家阿拉伯·法基赫笔下的「马拉伊汉」人——即马雷汉人——在酋长希拉布率领下起兵响应，从1529年的欣布拉库雷之战起转战整个征服阿比西尼亚之役，直到1543年伊玛目战死瓦伊纳达加，平原才重归氏族自治。南面的阿朱兰苏丹国势力沿谢贝利河上溯至卡拉福，在17世纪衰落之前一直主导着内陆大局。也是从17世纪起，穿过欧加登的商路除了牲畜和兽皮这两宗本地真正的财富，还把掳自阿尔西等南方民族的奴隶运往柏培拉和红海；韦尔德的水井之上不设驻军，它们属于守得住水井的氏族。

en:
Afder, in Somali Afdheer, is the southern grazing country of the Ogaden, the semi-arid plains beyond the upper Ganale Dorya River, which here separates Somali rangeland from the Oromo country to the west. Darod Somali clans—the Ogaden and the Absame families—move camels and small stock between its wells, and in the 15th century these lands lay within the wide sphere of the Habr Maqdi, a Somali confederacy of the Bartire and Yabarre whose chieftains are remembered as holding the grazing grounds from the Bakool country as far as Afder between the 14th and 18th centuries. They were Sunnis, trading livestock toward Harar and the Shebelle valley, and in 1444 the plains formed the quiet southern wing of the Muslim frontier below the embattled provinces of Bale and Dawaro.

When Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi raised his jihad the Habr Maqdi answered with the largest of the Somali contingents and stayed his most loyal followers, fighting from Shimbra Kure in 1529 until his death at Wayna Daga in 1543. In the wars' wake Oromo migrants spread over the flat plains of Bale to the north, but the Afder grazing grounds stayed in Somali hands under the Maqdi chieftainship, which endured here into the 18th century. The Bartire kept up their long-standing tie with the emirs of Harar after the emirate broke away in 1647, and Harari caravans crossed Afder buying livestock, hides and ivory for the Red Sea markets.
zh:
阿夫德（索马里语名Afdheer）是欧加登南部的牧地，即加纳莱·多里亚河上游以外的半干旱平原；这条河在此把索马里牧场同西面的奥罗莫地区分开。达鲁德系索马里氏族——欧加登人和阿布萨梅诸部——赶着骆驼和小家畜往来于各处水井之间。15世纪时，这些土地处在哈卜尔·马克迪联盟的广阔势力范围内：它由巴尔蒂雷和亚巴雷两支索马里人组成，相传14至18世纪间，其酋长的辖地从巴科勒一直延伸到阿夫德的牧场。他们是逊尼派穆斯林，赶着牲畜同哈勒尔和谢贝利河谷贸易；1444年，在战事不断的巴勒和达瓦罗两省以南，这片平原构成穆斯林边疆平静的南翼。

艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐发动圣战时，哈卜尔·马克迪以索马里诸部中最大的一支兵力响应，也是他最忠诚的追随者，从1529年的欣布拉库雷之战一直打到1543年他战死瓦伊纳达加。战乱之后，奥罗莫移民散布到北面巴勒的平坦原野，阿夫德的牧场则始终在索马里人手中，马克迪酋长的势力在此延续到18世纪。1647年哈勒尔酋长国独立后，巴尔蒂雷人保持着他们与哈勒尔埃米尔之间由来已久的联系，哈勒尔商队穿过阿夫德收购牲畜、兽皮和象牙，运往红海市场。

en:
Beledweyne is the crossing of the middle Shebelle valley in Hiran, where the river divides the town and pastoral roads from the Ogaden meet caravan routes running south toward Mogadishu. In 1444 it lay within the Ajuran Sultanate, whose wells, river controls and tribute system bound Hawiye pastoralists to the riverine farms. Livestock, hides and access to water mattered more here than the trade of a coastal city.

As Ajuran rule weakened, the Darandoolle and other Hiraab clans challenged its governors, while the Gaaljecel, Baadicade and Xawaadle united in the upper and middle Shebelle valley to drive the Ajuran out. By 1700 Hiraab power stretched from this riverine corridor toward Mudug and the Benadir coast, leaving the Beledweyne crossing to the pastoral clans and caravan traffic of the new order.
zh:
贝兰德文（通行译名贝莱德文）是希兰地区谢贝利河中游的渡口，河流将城镇分开，来自欧加登的牧道与南下摩加迪沙的商路在此相接。1444年，这里属于阿朱兰苏丹国；阿朱兰人的水井、河道控制和贡赋制度，把哈维耶游牧民与河畔农田联系在一起。此地的重要性在牲畜、兽皮和用水权，而不在海港城市那种贸易。

阿朱兰统治衰微后，达兰多莱和其他希拉布氏族起而对抗其总督，加勒杰勒、巴迪卡德和哈瓦德莱则在谢贝利河中上游联手驱逐阿朱兰人。到1700年，希拉布势力已从这条河谷走廊延伸到穆杜格和贝纳迪尔海岸，贝兰德文渡口也转入新秩序下的游牧氏族与商队交通之中。

en:
Gedo is the upper Jubba country around the Dawa confluence, with Luuq set in a horseshoe bend of the Ganane, as the upper Jubba is called here. Digil and Mirifle clans farmed and pastured stock along its rivers, while Luuq was already one of the older market settlements on the road from the Benadir coast into southern Ethiopia. In 1444 Ajuran governors kept those caravan roads open; Bender-Luuq merchants drew coffee, gold, slaves and ivory from the interior and sent goods onward toward Bardera and the coastal ports.

In the Geledi period, the Gasaaragude dynasty ruled the upper Jubba within the Geledi federation and made Luuq its military centre, where troops trained, weapons were made and prisoners were held. The town's merchants used weights, credit and written contracts, exchanging Benadir cotton cloth for cattle among Arsi and Borana Oromo, then trading the cattle to hunters for ivory. In 1811 Captain Thomas Smee reported a heavily fortified town with more than two thousand stone houses, mosques, roads, palaces and castles at its centre.
zh:
盖多是达瓦河汇流处一带的朱巴河上游地区，卢格坐落在当地所称加纳内河的马蹄形河弯中。迪吉尔与米里弗莱诸氏族沿河畔农耕牧畜，卢格则早已是贝纳迪尔海岸通往埃塞俄比亚南部道路上的古老集市之一。1444年，阿朱兰总督维持着这些商路畅通；本德尔-卢格商人从内陆取得咖啡、黄金、奴隶和象牙，再把货物运往巴尔代雷和沿海港口。

格勒迪时期，加萨拉古德王朝在格勒迪联盟内统治朱巴河上游，并以卢格为军事中心，军队在此训练、武器在此制造、囚犯也关押于此。城中商人使用度量衡、信贷和书面契约，把贝纳迪尔棉布卖给阿尔西与博兰纳的奥罗莫人换取牛只，再用牛向猎人交换象牙。1811年，托马斯·斯米船长报告称，这座设防坚固的城镇有两千多所石屋，并有清真寺、道路、宫殿和位于城中心的堡楼。

en:
Warsheikh is a coastal town about seventy kilometres north of Mogadishu. Somali tradition identifies it with Sarapion, the harbour listed in the first-century Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, though modern scholars place that ancient port somewhere between here and Mogadishu. By the later Middle Ages it was an early centre of Islam, trade and learning, and one of the chief towns of the Sultanate of Mogadishu, whose Fakhr al-Din dynasty minted its own coin and traded as far as Egypt, Arabia and China. Like the rest of the Banaadir, the town lay within the hegemony of the Ajuran Sultanate. In 1444, under the sultan in Mogadishu, Warsheikh lived by its anchorage and by the livestock driven down from its arid hinterland.

The Portuguese sacked the Swahili cities farther south and burned Barawa in 1507, but never forced themselves on Mogadishu and its ports, so Warsheikh kept its place in the city's Indian Ocean commerce. That order ended in the late seventeenth century, when Ajuran rule collapsed before the revolt of the Hiraab clans: the Yacquubi imams took Mogadishu, and Warsheikh passed to their new Hiraab Imamate, ruled locally by Abgaal chiefs. Through the eighteenth century the imams kept European shipping at arm's length from this coast, and the town remained a quiet Muslim anchorage in Hiraab hands into the new century.
zh:
瓦尔希赫是摩加迪沙以北约七十公里处的一座滨海城镇。索马里传统把它认作公元1世纪《厄立特里亚海航行记》所记的古港萨拉皮翁，但学者多把这座古港推定在瓦尔希赫与摩加迪沙之间一带。到中世纪后期，它已是伊斯兰教、商贸与学术的早期中心，也是摩加迪沙苏丹国的首要城镇之一；当时的法赫尔丁王朝自铸钱币，商路远达埃及、阿拉伯和中国。与贝纳迪尔其他地方一样，该镇处在阿朱兰苏丹国的霸权之下。1444年，瓦尔希赫归属摩加迪沙的苏丹，靠港湾贸易和干旱腹地赶来的牲畜为生。

葡萄牙人劫掠了更南方的斯瓦希里诸城，又于1507年焚毁巴拉韦，却始终未能染指摩加迪沙及其属港，瓦尔希赫因此得以保住它在摩加迪沙印度洋贸易中的位置。这一秩序在17世纪末终结：阿朱兰统治在希拉布诸部的反抗中崩溃，雅库比家族的伊玛目们夺取摩加迪沙，瓦尔希赫随之归入新建的希拉布伊玛目国，由当地的阿布加尔酋长治理。整个18世纪，伊玛目们把欧洲船只拒在这段海岸之外，这座城镇也作为穆斯林港镇，在希拉布手中平静地进入下一个世纪。

en:
Hobyo is an ancient Somali anchorage on the arid Mudug coast, founded in the 13th century as a coastal outpost of the Ajuran Sultanate. Its market drew livestock and grain from the interior into the Indian Ocean coastal trade. At the height of Ajuran power the sultanate's reach ran from Hobyo in the north to Kismayo in the south, so in 1444 the Sunni Somali port was a northern gateway of a centralized Muslim state, watched over by nearby coastal settlements such as Mareeg.

In the late 17th century the Hiraab clans rose against Ajuran rule, heavy taxation and neglect of Islamic law feeding the revolt. By 1700 their imamate controlled a wide belt from the Shabelle valley through the dry lands of Mudug to the coast around Hobyo, and it maintained independent rule for at least two centuries. The hinterland supplied sorghum, beans, camels, cattle, sheep and goats; Hobyo exported livestock, hides, aromatic woods and raisins, took in rice, foodstuffs and clothing, and provisioned ships sailing down the Somali coast.
zh:
霍比奥是干旱的穆杜格海岸上一座古老的索马里锚地，13世纪作为阿朱兰苏丹国的沿海据点建立。内陆的牲畜和谷物汇集到这里的市场，再进入印度洋沿岸贸易。阿朱兰强盛时，势力北起霍比奥、南至基斯马尤；因此在1444年，这座逊尼派索马里港口是这个集权穆斯林国家的北方门户，与马雷格等邻近沿海聚落彼此呼应。

17世纪末，希拉布诸部起兵反抗阿朱兰统治，沉重赋税和统治者对伊斯兰教法的疏失推动了叛乱。到1700年，他们的教长国已控制从谢贝利河谷穿过穆杜格旱地、直达霍比奥附近海岸的广阔地带，并维持了至少两个世纪的独立统治。内陆供应高粱、豆类、骆驼、牛、绵羊和山羊；霍比奥输出牲畜、兽皮、香木和葡萄干，输入稻米、食品和布匹，也为沿索马里海岸南下的船只补给。

en:
Galkayo is a stretch of wells and grazing grounds in the arid Mudug plains, the border country where the Darod clans pressing from the north met the Hawiye of the south, both watering camels, sheep and cattle there in the dry season and feuding over wells in bad years. There was no town yet in 1444, but the land looked toward Hobyo on the coast, an ancient harbour which the Ajuran empire had founded as one of its northern outposts in the 13th century; Ajuran governors and Somali caravan traders drew the herds and hides of Mudug into the Indian Ocean commerce. The people were Sunni Muslims, and the sultanate's hold over these dry marches was loose, resting on kinship and trade rather than garrisons.

In the late 17th century the Hiraab, a Hawiye confederation, rose against the Ajuran and built their own imamate, which through the 18th century ruled from the Shabelle valley and the Benaadir coast up to the arid lands of Mudug. Hobyo prospered under the new order: it shipped out livestock, hides, aromatic woods and raisins, took in rice, cloth and metals, and provisioned vessels sailing down the coast to Mogadishu. Around Galkayo the change of dynasties mattered less than the old rivalry of Darod and Hawiye over pasture and water, which outlasted the imamate itself. As late as 1821 the place remained a nomads' rendezvous rather than a city.
zh:
加勒卡约是干旱的穆杜格平原上一片有水井和牧场的地方，北来的达鲁德氏族与南方的哈维耶人在此交界：旱季双方都到这里饮骆驼、羊和牛，年景坏时便为水井争斗。1444年时这里还没有城镇，但这片土地在经济上朝向海边的霍比奧——那是阿朱兰帝国13世纪建立的北方港口据点之一，阿朱兰的官吏和索马里商队把穆杜格的畜群和兽皮纳入印度洋贸易。当地居民都是逊尼派穆斯林，苏丹国对这片干旱边地的控制松散，靠的是姻亲关系和贸易而非驻军。

17世纪末，哈维耶人的希拉布联盟起兵推翻阿朱兰统治，建立自己的伊玛目政权，整个18世纪其治下从谢贝利河谷、贝纳迪尔海岸一直延伸到穆杜格的干旱地带。霍比奧在新秩序下繁荣起来：输出牲畜、兽皮、香木和葡萄干，输入大米、布匹和金属，并为沿海岸南下摩加迪沙的船只补给给养。加勒卡约一带对王朝更迭感受不深，真正贯穿始终的是达鲁德与哈维耶之间争夺牧场和水源的旧怨，比伊玛目政权本身还要长久。直到1821年，这里仍是游牧者的会聚之地，而不是一座城市。

en:
El Buur, or Ceelbuur, lies in the dry inland heart of Galguduud, where tracks from Hiran, the Ogaden, Mudug and Warsheikh meet around wells and low hills. The Murusade branch of the Hawiye had settled there by at least the 13th century. In 1444 the town served the Ajuran Sultanate as a local commercial hub, and its quarries yielded soft sepiolite, or meerschaum, which craftsmen carved into dabqaad incense burners and pipes.

As Ajuran rule collapsed, the Habar Gidir and Duduble fought the Ajuran out of Galguduud and Mudug. By 1700 those lands lay within the Hiraab Imamate's inland arc, which stretched from the Shebelle valley through the arid country toward Mudug and the coast between Mogadishu and Hobyo. El Buur then remained a Murusade caravan market, linking pastoral herdsmen with the Benadir ports while its carved incense burners continued to carry the town's name along the trade roads.
zh:
埃勒布尔（索马里语名Ceelbuur）位于加勒古杜德干旱的内陆中心，希兰、欧加登、穆杜格和瓦尔谢赫方向的道路在水井与低丘间交会。哈维耶人的穆鲁萨德支系至迟在13世纪已定居于此。1444年，这座城镇是阿朱兰苏丹国的地方商业中心；当地矿坑出产质地柔软的海泡石，工匠将其雕成达布加德香炉和烟管。

阿朱兰统治崩溃时，哈巴尔·吉迪尔人与杜杜布莱人经过苦战，把阿朱兰势力逐出加勒古杜德和穆杜格。到1700年，这些土地已纳入希拉布伊玛目国的内陆势力圈，其范围从谢贝利河谷穿过干旱地带，延伸至穆杜格以及摩加迪沙与霍比奥之间的海岸。此后埃勒布尔仍是穆鲁萨德人的商队集市，连接游牧牧民与贝纳迪尔诸港；雕制香炉也继续让这座城镇的名字随商路外传。

en:
Bosaso, historically Bender Qassim, lies on the Bari coast at the mouth of the Baalade valley. The author of the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea knew this shore as Mosylon, famed for its frankincense. The present anchorage takes its name from Qasim, a trader said to have settled here in the fourteenth century; his favourite camel was called Boosaas. The Kaptallah were its first settlers, and for centuries the Dishiishe and other Harti clans of the Darod family held the coast, shipping frankincense, dates, skins and livestock to Arabian ports. In 1444 it was a chain of small Muslim fishing and trading roads under its own clan elders, within the loose orbit of Adal.

In 1520 the ships of the Portuguese embassy to Abyssinia watered along this coast between Cape Guardafui and Mount Felis, buying goats and taking aboard white gum for caulking their hulls; Francisco Álvares found a sterile land where thick cloth served as money and a local ruler reigned subject to Adel. In the following centuries the Majeerteen, another Harti clan, built up a kingdom on the Guardafui peninsula: oral tradition places its first rulers in the late fifteenth or sixteenth century, and by the late eighteenth century it was a centralised sultanate with a strong seafaring tradition. Bender Qassim remained a Dishiishe harbour within that Harti maritime world, its dhows carrying the frankincense of the interior hills to Arabian and Indian ports.
zh:
博萨索旧称班达尔·卡西姆，位于巴里海岸、巴拉代河谷入海处。《厄立特里亚海航行记》的作者把这片海岸称为莫西隆，以乳香闻名。这处锚地得名于传说中14世纪在此定居的商人卡西姆，他最心爱的骆驼名叫博萨斯，城市后来由此得名。卡普塔拉人是最早的定居者，此后数百年间，达鲁德族系下的迪希谢等哈提氏族据有这片海岸，把乳香、椰枣、兽皮和牲畜运往阿拉伯港口。1444年，这里是一连串穆斯林小渔村和贸易锚地，由本地氏族长老自行治理，处在阿达尔势力松散的辐射之下。

1520年，出使阿比西尼亚的葡萄牙船队在瓜达富伊角与费利斯山之间的海岸补充淡水，收购山羊，并把大量白色树胶装上船填补船缝；弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯发现这是一片贫瘠之地，厚布在这里充当货币，当地统治者「臣属于阿达尔」。此后数百年间，同为哈提氏族的马吉尔廷人在瓜达富伊半岛建立起王国：口述传统把其早期统治者置于15世纪末或16世纪，到18世纪晚期它已是一个组织严密、以航海见长的苏丹国。班达尔·卡西姆则始终是迪希谢人的港口，属于这个哈提航海世界的一部分，独桅船把内地山丘的乳香运往阿拉伯和印度。

en:
Hamasien is the highland basin around Asmara, the central plateau of the Eritrean highlands between the Red Sea hills and the Mereb River. After the long post-Aksumite movements of Beja and Agaw peoples, its villages were Tigrinya-speaking Christian communities in the Solomonic period, governed by local kantiba chiefs and councils of elders under the Bahr Negash. Emperor Zara Yaqob strengthened that office and placed the two kantiba of Hamasien under the Bahr Negash at Debarwa, who controlled routes carrying gold, ivory and enslaved people toward Massawa. In 1444, therefore, Hamasien was the Christian highland core of Medri Bahri, its local chiefs tied through Debarwa to Emperor Zara Yaqob's tributary empire.

In 1520 the Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares found the Bahr Negash Dori residing at Debarwa, receiving horses, textiles and carpets as tribute and exercising authority north toward Suakin. The wars of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi later killed the local governor, and after the Ottomans took Massawa in 1557 their troops raided into the highlands in 1559. Bahr Negash Yeshaq eventually joined the Ottomans and was killed at Addi Qarro in 1578; when an Ottoman force seized Debarwa in 1587, Emperor Sarsa Dengel's counterattack retook the town and by 1589 confined the Turks to the coast. In the seventeenth century the hereditary Deki Teshim governors under Hab Sellus ruled from Tsazega and unified local customary law, before their descendants split into the rival Tsazega and Hazega houses. When James Bruce visited in 1770, Medri Bahri was still a distinct highland power, frequently at war with the Abyssinian court.
zh:
哈马森是阿斯马拉周围的高原盆地，地处厄立特里亚高地中央，位于红海山地与马雷布河之间。阿克苏姆衰落后，贝扎人和阿高人先后迁徙到此；到所罗门王朝时期，这里的村落已是说提格里尼亚语的基督教社群，由本地坎蒂巴酋长和长老会议在巴赫勒·尼加什之下治理。皇帝扎拉·雅各布强化这一官职，把哈马森的两名坎蒂巴置于驻德巴尔瓦的巴赫勒·尼加什之下；通往马萨瓦的商路由其控制，黄金、象牙和奴隶经此外运。1444年，哈马森因此是梅德利巴赫里的基督教高地核心，本地首领经由德巴尔瓦臣属于扎拉·雅各布的纳贡帝国。

1520年，葡萄牙神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯见到巴赫勒·尼加什·多里驻在德巴尔瓦，接受马匹、织物和地毯作为贡物，其权威向北延伸至萨瓦金一带。后来，艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的战争杀死了当地长官；奥斯曼人1557年夺取马萨瓦后，又于1559年派军突入高地。巴赫勒·尼加什伊沙克最终与奥斯曼人结盟，1578年战死于阿迪卡罗。1587年奥斯曼军队攻占德巴尔瓦，皇帝萨尔萨·登格尔发起反攻收复该城，到1589年已把土耳其人限制在沿海。17世纪，哈布·塞卢斯之下的世袭德基·特希姆统治者以察泽加为中心统治，并统一当地习惯法；其后人后来分裂为察泽加与哈泽加两个对立支系。詹姆斯·布鲁斯1770年到访时，梅德利巴赫里仍是独立的高地政权，常与阿比西尼亚朝廷交战。

en:
Hafun stands on a low promontory tied to the mainland by a long sandspit, the easternmost inhabited point of Africa, where a sheltered bay looks onto the Guardafui Channel. It is the ancient Opone: the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, a Greek pilot's guide of the 1st century CE, calls it a market-town into which cinnamon, cloves and ivory were brought and from which great quantities of tortoiseshell and incense went out to Egypt, Persia, India and the Red Sea, and excavations in the tombs at nearby Damo have recovered pottery from the Mediterranean and the Persian Gulf. In later centuries the old emporium shrank to a Somali fishing and trading settlement, its people Sunni Muslims who drew frankincense from the hills and salt from the shore pans. By 1444 it lay within the growing orbit of the Majeerteen.

From the mid-17th century Hafun was counted among the core lands of the Majeerteen sultanate, the Migiurtinia of European maps, and was judged its most strategic place: a fortress was raised at Ras Hafun to watch the channel where the currents of the Indian Ocean crowd shipping toward the cape. The sultan's boats used the bay as a roadstead, carrying gum and frankincense, dried fish and salt north to Aden and the Red Sea ports and bringing back cloth and dates. Wrecks were frequent on the headland, and wrecked cargoes, salvage and the ransom of crews became as much a part of the coast's living as the incense trade. Hafun remained in the Majeerteen realm, still a small windswept port, in 1821.
zh:
哈丰坐落在一道由长沙嘴与大陆相连的低矮岬角上，是非洲有人居住的最东端，一处避风海湾对着瓜达富伊海峡。这里就是古代的奥波内：成书于公元1世纪的希腊航海指南《厄立特里亚海航行记》把它记作一座商埠，肉桂、丁香和象牙运入此地，大量玳瑁和熏香则销往埃及、波斯、印度和红海各港；在附近达莫的墓葬中，考古发掘出了来自地中海和波斯湾的陶器。后世这座古商埠衰落为索马里人的渔村和贸易点，居民是逊尼派穆斯林，从山间采乳香、在岸边盐池取盐。到1444年，它已落入马吉尔廷势力日益扩张的范围之内。

从17世纪中叶起，哈丰被视为马吉尔廷苏丹国（欧洲地图上的米朱提尼亚）的核心领土之一，并被认为是其最险要的地方：拉什哈丰角建起要塞，监视印度洋海流把船只挤向海角的瓜达富伊海峡。苏丹的船队以这个海湾为锚地，把树胶、乳香、鱼干和盐北运亚丁和红海港口，换回布匹和椰枣。海角附近海难频发，沉船货物、打捞救助和船员赎金，与熏香贸易一样成了沿岸生计的一部分。直到1821年，哈丰仍是马吉尔廷版图内一座常受海风侵袭的小港。

en:
Las Khorey is an old anchorage of the Maakhir coast, where the frankincense-bearing Cal Madow mountains come down to the Gulf of Aden. In the thirteenth century Dhidhin, chief of the Warsangali branch of the Darod, rose to power on this shore and took the title of Garaad, founding the line that long ruled these mountains. His people herded camels, tended dates in the coastal wadis and gathered frankincense and gum arabic for Arabian and Indian dhows; the settlement itself long remained little more than a well and a roadstead. In 1444 it belonged to the Warsangali domain, the northernmost Muslim coast, looking across the gulf to Arabia.

The town of Las Khorey dates to 1735, when Sheikh Ali Mahmud Nuh of the Warsangali dug a well, built a mosque and raised a fortress there; its merchants then opened trade with Arabia, India, the Swahili coast and Zanzibar. Under Garaad Mohamed II, who ruled from 1721 to 1764, the Warsangali capital moved to the new port, and his successor Ali II took the title of sultan in 1764. By the first years of the nineteenth century Sultan Mahmud II, who came to the throne in 1804, was repairing the coastal towers whose ruins Henry Salt mapped in 1809. Las Khorey had become the chief harbour of the Warsangali state, the busiest port of the frankincense coast.
zh:
拉斯戈赖是马希尔海岸的古老锚地，盛产乳香的阿尔马多山脉在此直逼亚丁湾。13世纪，达鲁德族系瓦尔桑盖利分支的首领迪丁在这一带兴起，采用「加拉德」（领主）称号，开创了长期统治这片山区的王统。他的部众放牧骆驼，在沿海涸谷里栽种椰枣，采集乳香和阿拉伯树胶供应阿拉伯与印度的独桅船；而这片居停长期不过是一口水井加一处锚地。1444年，它属于瓦尔桑盖利的领地——穆斯林世界最靠北的海岸，隔湾与阿拉伯相望。

拉斯戈赖作为城镇始于1735年，瓦尔桑盖利的谢赫·阿里·马哈茂德·努赫在此挖井、建清真寺、筑堡垒；商人随后开通了与阿拉伯、印度、斯瓦希里海岸和桑给巴尔的贸易。1721至1764年在位的加拉德·穆罕默德二世把瓦尔桑盖利的都城迁到这座新港，其继承人阿里二世于1764年改称苏丹。进入19世纪，1804年继位的苏丹马哈茂德二世着手修缮沿海碉楼，亨利·索尔特1809年的地图上绘下了它们的废墟。拉斯戈赖此时已是瓦尔桑盖利国家的首要港口、乳香海岸最繁忙的港湾。

en:
Sanaag is the mountain country behind the Maakhir coast, where the frankincense woods of the Cal Madow range run down to Gulf of Aden roadsteads. Its oldest harbour is Maydh, already marked in the medieval Egyptian treatise the Book of Curiosities. Tradition holds that the town was settled in the twelfth or thirteenth century by Sheikh Isaaq ibn Ahmad al-Hashimi, an Arab scholar who crossed from Arabia, and his domed tomb there made Maydh a place of pilgrimage, for the great Isaaq clan family counts him its ancestor; the navigator Ahmad ibn Majid also listed it among the notable ports of the Somali coast. In 1444 Sunni Somali herdsmen and sailors held the shore under their Warsangali garaads, and the port lay within the dominion of the sultans of Adal.

In 1520 the Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares landed at Maydh with the embassy to Abyssinia and found fifty or sixty hearths, two mosques and a Quranic school; his ships dug fresh wells and filled more than a thousand casks in three days, then burned the houses and small craft when they sailed away. At the Battle of Shimbra Kure in 1529 the Harti of Maydh, described in the Futuh al-Habash as 'a people not given to yielding', fought on the left wing of Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim's army. In later centuries the Habr Yunis gathered frankincense in the mountains behind the town, Arab and Banyan merchants called there for hides, and aged Isaaq clansmen came to spend their last years and be buried near Sheikh Isaaq, until the graveyard stretched a mile in every direction. Inland, the ruined trading town of Maduna still keeps the three-metre walls of its mosque, dated to the fifteenth to seventeenth centuries.
zh:
萨纳格是马希尔海岸背后的山乡，阿尔马多山脉的乳香林顺着山坡一直延到亚丁湾的各处锚地。这里最古老的港口是迈德，中世纪埃及地志《奇物志》的地图上已标出它的位置。相传12或13世纪，从阿拉伯渡海而来的学者谢赫·伊萨克·伊本·艾哈迈德·哈希米在此定居，他的圆顶陵墓使迈德成为朝谒之地——庞大的艾萨克氏族体系奉他为始祖；航海家艾哈迈德·伊本·马吉德也把迈德列入索马里海岸的名港。1444年，信奉逊尼派的索马里牧人与水手在瓦尔桑盖利加拉德们治下据有海岸，港口则归阿达尔苏丹统辖。

1520年，随葡萄牙使团前往阿比西尼亚的神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯在迈德登陆，见到五六十户人家、两座清真寺和一所古兰经学校；船队新挖水井，三天内注满一千多只水桶，离去时却放火烧毁了民房和小船。1529年的辛卜拉库雷之战中，迈德的哈尔蒂人在伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣的军队左翼作战，《阿比西尼亚战记》说他们「是一群不肯屈服的人」。此后数百年，哈布尔尤尼斯人在城后山中采割乳香，阿拉伯和巴尼亚商人来此收购兽皮，年迈的艾萨克人纷纷到此度过余生、葬在谢赫·伊萨克身旁，墓园由此扩展到方圆一英里。内陆的马杜纳商镇遗址仍留有三米高的清真寺残墙，考古断代在15至17世纪之间。

en:
Ankober perches on the eastern escarpment of the Ethiopian Highlands, where the cool Amhara plateau of northern Shewa drops towards the arid lowlands of the Afar. Behind it lie Menz and Tegulet, the oldest Christian Amhara country and cradle of the Solomonic restoration of 1270, while the escarpment tracks were the gateway for caravans and armies moving between the highlands and the Muslim coastlands; the grain fields and pastures fed the imperial camps. In 1444 this was royal demesne of Zara Yaqob's Christian empire on the Adal frontier, watched over by lords and monasteries.

A dozen years later Zara Yaqob built his capital at Debre Birhan, just west of the escarpment, after the celestial light of 1456; the court drifted away under his successors and the town shrank to a large village. In the wars of Ahmad Gran, Debre Birhan served first the emperor and then the imam as a mustering ground, and Gran harangued his army there in 1535. When the Oromo expansion cut Shewa off from Gondar, the Amhara of Menz held these mountains and Negasi Krestos built his power among them around 1682; in the mid-eighteenth century his descendant Amha Iyasus moved the Shewan capital to Ankober, which crowns the escarpment and commands the road to the lowlands. It remained the residence of the meridazmachs and kings of Shewa, ringed by palaces and churches, through the Era of the Princes and into the new century.
zh:
安科伯尔坐落在埃塞俄比亚高地的东缘陡崖上，凉爽的北绍阿阿姆哈拉高原从这里俯临干燥的阿法尔低地。崖后的门兹和特古莱特是最古老的阿姆哈拉基督教之乡，也是1270年所罗门王朝复辟的摇篮；崖上的通道是商队和军队往返高地与穆斯林沿海低地的门户，谷地和牧场则供应皇家营帐所需的粮食。1444年，这里是扎拉·雅各布基督教帝国面向阿达尔边疆的王室领地，由领主和修道院拱卫。

十余年后，扎拉·雅各布在陡崖以西的德卜勒伯尔汉建立都城，起因是1456年天空出现异光；后继诸君在位时朝廷渐渐离去，都城缩为一座大村庄。艾哈迈德·格兰战争期间，德卜勒伯尔汉先后被皇帝和伊玛目用作集结大军之地，1535年格兰还在那里向军队发表演说。奥罗莫扩张使绍阿与贡德尔隔绝后，门兹的阿姆哈拉人据守这些山地，内加西·克雷斯托斯约于1682年在他们之中崛起；18世纪中叶，他的后裔阿姆哈·伊亚苏斯把绍阿都城迁到雄踞陡崖、扼守低地通道的安科伯尔。此后历经「王侯时代」直到新世纪，这里一直是绍阿默里达兹马奇和诸王的居所，宫殿与教堂环绕四周。

en: Togdheer takes its name from the Tug Dayr, the wide dry riverbed that carries the rains of the interior plateau toward the Berbera coast. In 1444 it was pasture rather than a kingdom: Somali nomads of the Isaaq family drove their camels and flocks from waterhole to waterhole, raising the livestock that fed the coastal markets, while caravans climbed from Berbera into the Hawd and on toward Harar carrying cloth and dates and bringing back hides, ivory and slaves. No town existed here before the late eighteenth century, when nomads began gathering at the Ceel-Gooni well; the market that grew around it became Burao, linking the port of Berbera with the hinterland. Around the same time the Habr Yunis, breaking away from the Isaaq sultanate, set up their own line of sultans under Sugulle, son of the chieftain Ainanshe Hersi, and the wells and grazing of the Togdheer became the centre of their power.
zh: 托格代尔得名于图格达伊尔河——一条宽阔的干河床，雨季把内陆高原的雨水输向柏培拉海岸。1444年，这里是牧场而非王国：艾萨克族系的索马里游牧民赶着驼群和羊群逐井而居，为沿海市场繁育牲畜；商队从柏培拉登上高原，深入豪德草原、远抵哈勒尔，运去布匹和椰枣，带回兽皮、象牙和奴隶。18世纪晚期以前这里没有城镇，游牧民后来聚集到埃勒戈尼井旁，井边长成的集市就是布拉奥，把柏培拉港与腹地连成一线。差不多同一时期，哈布尔尤尼斯人脱离艾萨克苏丹国，在首领艾南沙·赫尔西之子苏古勒之下建立起自己的苏丹世系，托格代尔的水井与牧场由此成为他们权力的中心。

en:
Hargeisa is the well-watered valley in the Ogo highlands behind Berbera, where the Aleyadera watercourse runs between grazing hills on the old road from the coast to Harar. Long before it was a town it was a watering stop for nomads and caravans, where Somali of the Isaaq clans — Arap, Habr Yunis, Eidagale, spreading southwest from their early home at Maydh from the fifteenth century — watered their herds. In 1444 the country belonged to the Adal sultanate and shared in the prosperity of its inland cities: the caravans resting at these wells carried ivory, coffee and slaves from the Harar and Ogaden interior down to Berbera, the busiest of the Muslim ports on this coast.

The Isaaq lancers of the Habr Magadle marched with Ahmad Gragn in his conquest of Abyssinia between 1529 and 1543, and the chronicle Futuh al-Habasha remembers their part in the jihad. When Adal broke after the wars, its old interior cities fell into ruin while the Somali clans kept the wells and the caravan roads alive. In the middle of the eighteenth century the Eidagale leader Abdi Eisa defeated the Absame tribes at Lafaruug near Berbera, and in July 1750 his son Guled was crowned the first sultan of the Isaaq; under the Rer Guled line the sultanate taxed livestock, kept mounted raiders and ruled the Hargeisa grazing lands into the next century.
zh:
哈尔格萨是柏培拉后方奥戈高原上水草丰足的谷地，阿莱亚德拉干河在牧场丘陵间流过，正处在海岸通往哈勒尔的古道上。在成为城镇之前很久，这里只是游牧民和商队歇脚补水的站点；15世纪起，伊萨克氏族的阿拉普、哈布尔·尤尼斯、埃达加勒等支从早期聚居地迈德赫向西南扩散，陆续来到这一带牧放畜群。1444年，此地属于阿达尔苏丹国，分享着内陆诸城的繁荣：在这些水井边歇脚的商队，把哈勒尔和欧加登内陆的象牙、咖啡和奴隶运往海岸，柏培拉正是这一带穆斯林港口中最繁忙的一个。

1529至1543年艾哈迈德·格兰征服阿比西尼亚时，哈布尔·马加德勒各部的伊萨克长矛骑兵随他出征，《丰陀哈·哈巴沙》记下了他们在这场圣战中的角色。阿达尔在战后崩解，内陆古城纷纷沦为废墟，索马里诸氏族却守住了水井和商道。18世纪中叶，埃达加勒首领阿卜迪·伊萨在柏培拉附近的拉法鲁格击败阿布萨梅诸部，1750年7月，其子古莱德加冕为第一位伊萨克苏丹；在雷尔·古莱德一系治下，苏丹国征收牲畜贡赋、蓄养骑马袭掠者，哈尔格萨的牧场也一直在它治下进入下个世纪。

en:
Barawa stands on the Banaadir coast south of Merca, facing the Indian Ocean from a flat, briny shore. The Tunni Somali, led by their saint Aw-Ali, founded the town and made it the capital of their Tunni Sultanate, and they admitted Muslim families from Yemen and Syria as early as the tenth century. Al-Idrisi described its coral-stone houses, and Ibn Sa'id called Barawa 'an Islamic island on the Somali coast', ranking it with Mogadishu and Merca among the three chief cities of the coast. Its ulama drew students from across the Horn, while its craftsmen were famed for woven alindi cloth and the embroidered caps called kufi baraawa. Under the Ajuran sultans the town entered its golden age: the Ming treasure fleets of the early fifteenth century called there, and Fei Xin noted its salt pans, its multi-storeyed coral houses and its cargoes of frankincense, myrrh, ambergris and ivory. In 1444 Barawa was one of the richest Muslim harbours in the Ajuran realm.

In February 1507 Tristão da Cunha and Afonso de Albuquerque appeared before Barawa with sixteen ships. The town refused their summons behind a strong wall and a reported garrison of four thousand; the Portuguese stormed it, gave it over to sack and fire, and Tristão himself was wounded, but they sailed on without holding the place, and the refugees returned from the interior to rebuild. Barawa afterwards made its peace with the Portuguese and kept trading. When Ajuran power collapsed at the end of the seventeenth century, the town became the chief port of the new Geledi Sultanate, its wharves shared by Tunni townsmen and Swahili-speaking Bravanese merchants. As Geledi power waxed through the eighteenth century, so did the traffic of its harbour.
zh:
巴拉韦位于马尔卡以南的贝纳迪尔海岸，从低平多盐的滩涂上面朝印度洋。图尼族索马里人在圣徒奥-阿里带领下建城，以巴拉韦为都建立图尼苏丹国；早在10世纪，他们便接纳了来自也门和叙利亚的阿拉伯穆斯林家族。伊德里西曾描写这里的珊瑚石房屋，伊本·赛义德则称巴拉韦为「索马里海岸上的伊斯兰之岛」，把它与摩加迪沙、马尔卡并列为东非海岸三大都会。城中的乌理玛吸引着非洲之角各地的学生，工匠织造的阿林迪布和名为「库菲·巴拉瓦」的绣帽远近闻名。在阿朱兰苏丹治下，此城进入黄金时代：15世纪初郑和的船队曾到此，费信记下了当地的盐池、高达三五层的珊瑚石屋，以及乳香、没药、龙涎香和象牙等货物。1444年的巴拉韦是阿朱兰版图内最富庶的穆斯林海港之一。

1507年2月，特里斯唐·达·库尼亚与阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克率十六艘船兵临巴拉韦。城上高墙坚固，据称守军四千，拒绝了投降通牒；葡萄牙人强攻得手，大肆劫掠后纵火焚城，达·库尼亚本人也受了伤，但他们随即扬帆离去，并未占住此地，逃入内陆的居民陆续返回家园重建城市。巴拉韦后来与葡萄牙人议和，贸易依旧。17世纪末阿朱兰崩溃后，此城成为新兴的盖莱迪苏丹国的首要港口，码头上是图尼市民与讲斯瓦希里语的巴拉瓦尼商人。整个18世纪，盖莱迪国势强盛，这座港口的船来船往也随之日渐兴隆。

en:
Mareeg is a sandy anchorage on the arid coast of central Somalia, on the long shore between Warsheikh and Hobyo. Somali and Arabic sources make the town a foundation of the thirteenth century that flourished as a capital of the Ajuran Empire, whose domains ran from Hobyo in the north to Kismayo in the south and westward to Qelafo. The Garen sultans kept wells, garrisons and stone fortifications along this dry littoral, and the port had its share in the sea trade carrying Somali livestock and Banaadir goods to Arabia. In 1444 Mareeg was a fortified seat of Ajuran rule on the northern stretch of the empire's coast.

At the end of the seventeenth century the Ajuran Empire crumbled under oppressive taxation and clan revolt. The Hiraab imams who had seized Mogadishu carried their power along the coast towards Hobyo, and Mareeg passed into their Hiraab Imamate under Abgaal chiefs. Through the eighteenth century it remained a small anchorage serving the pastoral clans of its dry hinterland, its livestock trade untouched by the European rivalries farther south, and in 1821 it was still living under loose Hiraab overlordship.
zh:
梅雷格是索马里中部干旱海岸上的一处沙岸锚地，坐落在瓦尔希赫与霍比奥之间的漫长海岸线上。索马里语和阿拉伯语资料都称此城建于13世纪，曾作为阿朱兰帝国的都城而兴盛；阿朱兰版图北起霍比奥、南至基斯马尤，向西一直延伸到克拉福。加伦王朝的苏丹们在这段干旱海岸经营水井、驻军与石造工事，梅雷格也参与把索马里牲畜和贝纳迪尔货物运往阿拉伯的海上贸易。1444年，梅雷格是阿朱兰帝国北部海岸的一处设防治所。

17世纪末，阿朱兰帝国在苛政重税与诸部反抗中瓦解。夺取了摩加迪沙的希拉布伊玛目们把势力沿海岸向霍比奥方向推进，梅雷格随之并入希拉布伊玛目国，由阿布加尔酋长治理。整个18世纪，它始终是一座为干旱腹地的游牧氏族服务的小港，牲畜贸易照旧，未被更南方的欧洲列强争斗波及；直到1821年，它仍处在希拉布松散的宗主权之下。

en:
Pate is the mangrove-fringed largest island of the Lamu Archipelago, cut near Siyu by a sea channel that becomes dry ground at low tide. Farming villages there had become a Muslim Swahili trading society before the fourteenth century, when Pate town rose as the centre of a sultanate. Pate, Siyu and Faza were stone-town rivals of Lamu, frequented by Arab, Persian and Indian merchants but not founded as a foreign colony. In 1444 a Nabahani sultan at Pate dominated the island's harbour politics, while Siyu in the north was already an established Muslim settlement.

When Gaspar de Santo Bernardino visited Siyu in 1606, he described it as the largest town on the island. During the 1700s the Famao patricians there shared rule with Somali shaykhs from a new wave of settlers; that diarchy opened an Islamic revival in which Siyu became known for learning and book production. Pate town remained the seat from which the Nabahani sultanate took its name, and Fumo Madi ibn Abi Bakr reigned from 1776 to 1809 before fresh succession struggles weakened the court. Around 1812 a joint Pate and Mombasa army attacked Lamu but was broken on the dunes near Shela, allowing Omani power to overshadow the northern coast. In 1821 Pate still had a Nabahani ruler, yet its island towns no longer led Swahili commerce.
zh:
帕泰是拉穆群岛最大的岛屿，沿岸红树林环绕，西尤附近有一道海潮沟，涨潮时把岛屿分开，退潮后便成干地。14世纪以前，岛上的农业村落已发展为穆斯林斯瓦希里商业社会，帕泰城随后崛起为苏丹国中心。帕泰、西尤和法扎都是与拉穆争胜的石城，常有阿拉伯、波斯和印度商人往来，却不是外来者建立的殖民地。1444年，帕泰的纳卜汉苏丹主导岛上港湾事务，北部的西尤也已是成型的穆斯林定居点。

加斯帕尔·德·圣贝纳迪诺1606年到访西尤时，称它是岛上最大的城镇。18世纪，西尤的法茂望族与新迁入的索马里谢赫共同主政；这种双头格局开启了一场伊斯兰复兴，使西尤以学术和书籍制作闻名。帕泰城仍是纳卜汉苏丹国名号所系的都城，富莫·马迪·伊本·阿比·贝克尔于1776年至1809年在位，此后新的继承纷争削弱了宫廷。约1812年，帕泰与蒙巴萨联军进攻拉穆，却在谢拉附近的沙丘间被击溃，阿曼势力由此笼罩北部海岸。1821年时帕泰仍有纳卜汉统治者，但岛上城镇已不再主导斯瓦希里商路。

en:
Shendy sits on the east bank of the Nile, where the river road north meets the caravan track across the Butana to the Red Sea, forty-five miles northeast of the ruins of Meroe. By the later Christian age it was already one of the great markets of the Nile, where West African pilgrim caravans bound for Mecca met the grain and livestock trade going downstream to Egypt. In 1444 Nubian villagers still worked its irrigated fields while Arab tribes, the future Ja'alin, were taking over the carrying trade, and Shendy's lord gave only loose obedience to the Nubian kings of Dongola.

After the Funj victory of 1504 Shendy entered the Sennar system, ruled by the Sa'dab dynasty of the Ja'alin with the title makk, at first through the Abdallabi viceroys of Qarri and in time almost independent. Its weekly market became the greatest in Nubia: passing through in 1772, James Bruce found the town ringed with orchards and watered fields, exchanging Egyptian cotton, copper and sugar for the cattle, horses, gum arabic, honey and coffee brought from the interior through Sennar, and noted that its ruler was a woman, Sitna. In 1814 Burckhardt joined a Shendy caravan of two hundred camels and three hundred slaves bound for Suakin and Yemen by way of Quz Rajab; the town wove its own cotton cloth, and its makk Nimr, born of the Wad Ajeeb royal line, paid Sennar a yearly sum and otherwise ruled alone. In March 1821 Nimr submitted to the advancing Turco-Egyptian army of Ismail Pasha.
zh:
申迪位于尼罗河东岸，北去埃及的河路与东穿布塔纳、通往红海的商道在此交汇，东北45公里外便是麦罗埃故城遗址。基督教时代后期，它已是尼罗河上首屈一指的大市场，西非穆斯林前往麦加的朝圣商队，与顺河运往埃及的谷物、牲畜在此交易。1444年，努比亚农人仍耕种着河畔的水浇地，后来形成贾阿林人的阿拉伯部落已在把持转运贸易，申迪的首领对栋古拉的努比亚国王只维持着松散的臣属。

1504年丰吉人取胜后，申迪被纳入森纳尔体系，由贾阿林人的萨达卜王朝以「马克」之衔统治，最初臣属于驻盖里的阿卜杜拉布副王，久而久之几乎完全独立。它的周市号称努比亚第一：1772年詹姆斯·布鲁斯路过时，见到城镇四周果园与水浇地环绕，埃及来的棉布、铜器和食糖，在此交换经森纳尔从内地贩来的牲畜、马匹、阿拉伯胶、蜂蜜和咖啡，他还记下当时的统治者是一位名叫西特纳的女性。1814年，布尔克哈特在申迪加入一支拥有两百峰骆驼、三百名奴隶的商队，取道库兹拉杰布前往萨瓦金和也门；申迪本地也织造棉布，马克尼姆尔出身瓦德阿吉卜王族，每年向森纳尔缴纳一笔贡金，其余事务皆自专。1821年3月，尼姆尔向进抵此地的伊斯梅尔帕夏土埃军队投降。

en:
Soba stands on the Blue Nile some twenty kilometres upstream from the meeting of the two Niles. From the sixth century it was the capital of Alodia, or Alwa, southernmost and greatest of the three Christian Nubian kingdoms; its red-brick churches and the royal court drew traders from the Middle East, India and even China, and Nubian and Greek were written in its schools. From the twelfth century droughts, raids from the south and the shift of trade towards the Red Sea wore the kingdom down, and after the first Arab bedouin migration of 1324 the nomads steadily overran the Nile valley. In 1444 a Christian Nubian king still ruled at Soba, but his realm was reduced to the country around the capital, ringed by Muslim Arab tribes who increasingly withheld his tribute.

In 1474 the Arabs founded Arbaji on the Blue Nile, and tradition remembers a first assault on Soba in that same year. Around 1500 Abdallah Jammah united the Arab tribes and, allied with Amara Dunqas and his Funj coming from the south, stormed and razed the Christian capital, though one tradition dates the sack to 1509. Arab chroniclers claimed Soba then served the Funj kings as their seat until they founded Sennar in 1504–05, and when the Jewish traveller David Reubeni passed by in 1523 the city was in ruins, even if a 'Kingdom of Soba' still lingered on the Blue Nile. The land entered the Funj sultanate of Sennar, governed there by the Abdallab shaykhs of Qarri, while Islam and Arabic spread among the Nubians. Soba remained partly inhabited until the early seventeenth century, its bricks carried away for Sufi domed tombs, and when Ottoman Egypt founded Khartoum in 1821 the last ruins were stripped for building stone.
zh:
索巴位于青尼罗河畔，在两条尼罗河汇流处上游约二十公里。从6世纪起，它是努比亚三个基督教王国中位置最南、也最强大的阿洛迪亚（又称阿卢瓦）的都城：红砖教堂和王宫吸引着来自中东、印度乃至中国的商人，学堂里通行努比亚文和希腊文。12世纪以降，干旱、南方部族的袭扰和商路转向红海使王国日渐衰弱，1324年阿拉伯贝都因人开始迁入，随后游牧部落逐渐遍布尼罗河谷。1444年，一位信奉基督教的努比亚国王仍以索巴为都，但疆土只剩都城周围，四境尽是穆斯林阿拉伯部落，贡赋也越来越收不上来。

1474年，阿拉伯人在青尼罗河畔建立阿尔巴吉城，相传索巴也在同年首遭攻击。1500年前后，阿卜杜拉·贾马联合各阿拉伯部落，与南方阿马拉·敦卡斯率领的丰吉人结盟，攻陷并夷平了这座基督教都城，另有传说将城破之日系于1509年。据阿拉伯史家记载，索巴此后一度是丰吉国王的驻地，直到1504至1505年营建森纳尔；犹太旅人戴维·雷乌贝尼1523年途经此地时，城市已成废墟，但青尼罗河上仍残存着一个「索巴王国」。这片土地从此归入森纳尔的丰吉苏丹国，由驻在凯里的阿卜杜拉布酋长代管，伊斯兰教和阿拉伯语也在努比亚人中传播开来。索巴直到17世纪初仍有居民，砖石不断被拆去修筑苏菲圣徒的穹顶墓；1821年奥斯曼埃及营建喀土穆时，最后的遗迹也被搜刮一空充作建材。

en:
The Sennar district lies on the west bank of the Blue Nile, the southern heartland of Alodia, last of the Christian Nubian kingdoms. Its capital Soba stood downstream near the confluence of the two Niles, but royal power had long faded: by the fifteenth century the Gezira was divided among petty lords, Arab Bedouin had brought Islam and Arabic into the pastures, and the Abdallab federation of Abdallah Jammah destroyed what remained of the old kingdom. In 1444 Nubian villagers and Christian communities still lived along the river under weak local rulers.

In 1504 the Funj, pastoralists from the upper Blue Nile led by Amara Dunqas, made themselves overlords of the Abdallab and founded a new capital at Sennar, ruling as Muslim sultans. When the traveller David Reubeni passed through in 1523, he found Amara moving ceaselessly about his realm with great herds and mounted captains. Sennar grew rich on royal caravans linking the Ethiopian frontier with Egypt and the Hejaz, and on gold from Fazughli, conquered by Badi II in 1665. The Abdallab sheikh Ajib seized most of the kingdom before he was defeated and killed at Karkoj in 1612, and in 1744 Badi IV routed the invading Ethiopian army of Iyasu II on the Dinder river. In 1762 the Hamaj cavalry commander Muhammad Abu Likaylik entered Sennar and reduced the sultans to puppets; civil war followed, and when the Turks reached the city in June 1821 the last sultan, Badi VII, submitted amid the ruins of once-wealthy Sennar.
zh:
