森纳尔地区位于青尼罗河西岸，是基督教努比亚古国阿勒底亚南部的腹地。阿勒底亚的都城索巴坐落在下游、靠近两河汇流处，但王权早已衰落：到15世纪，杰济拉分据于众多小首领之手，阿拉伯贝都因人把伊斯兰教和阿拉伯语带进牧场，阿卜杜拉·詹马的阿卜杜拉布联盟摧毁了古国仅存的残余。1444年时，沿河仍住着努比亚村民和基督教社群，统治他们的是弱小的地方首领。

1504年，来自青尼罗河上游的游牧民族丰吉人在阿马拉·敦卡斯率领下压服阿卜杜拉布人，在森纳尔建立新都，以穆斯林苏丹的身份统治。1523年旅行家大卫·鲁本尼路过此地，见到阿马拉带着大群牲畜和骑兵队长在王国中不停巡行。森纳尔靠皇家商队致富——商队把埃塞俄比亚边疆同埃及和汉志连接起来，又有1665年巴迪二世征服法祖格利后运来的黄金。阿卜杜拉布谢赫阿吉卜一度占据大半个王国，最终于1612年在卡尔科季兵败被杀；1744年，巴迪四世在丁德尔河畔击溃伊亚苏二世的埃塞俄比亚入侵大军。1762年，哈马吉骑兵将领穆罕默德·阿布·利凯里克进入森纳尔，把苏丹降为傀儡，随后内战连绵。1821年6月土耳其军队兵临城下时，末代苏丹巴迪七世在一度富庶的森纳尔废墟之间投降。

en:
Waylula is the name the poet al-Harrani gave to the last capital of Alodia, the southern Christian kingdom of the Nubians: after old Soba fell to ruin, he wrote, the king's city stood on the west bank of the Nile and was 'very large'. Drought, plague and incoming Arab tribes had broken the kingdom, and by 1444 Nubian farmers worked the White Nile's western bank with a half-remembered Christianity and no priests, while Bedouin grazed their herds on the plain behind them and the king at Soba ruled little beyond his crumbling town.

Around 1500 the Arab chief Abdallah Jammah destroyed what remained of Soba, and in 1504–05 the Funj king Amara Dunqas founded the sultanate of Sennar. The river villages became part of the Blue Sultanate, where Sufi holy men spread Islam and Arabic slowly displaced Nubian, still spoken along the Nile into the nineteenth century. The west-bank crossing carried caravans and West African pilgrims on their way to Mecca. After the Hamaj seized Sennar in 1762 the realm lapsed into civil war, and in May 1821 the army of Muhammad Ali Pasha, led by his son Ismail, reached the Nile confluence; on 14 June the last sultan, Badi VII, submitted at Sennar and the west bank passed to Egypt.
zh:
瓦伊卢拉是诗人哈拉尼对努比亚人南方基督教王国阿勒底亚末代都城的称呼：他写道，旧都索巴残破之后，这座王城位于尼罗河西岸，「极其宏大」。旱灾、瘟疫和不断迁入的阿拉伯部落瓦解了这个王国。1444年，努比亚农人在白尼罗河西岸耕作，守着没有祭司、只剩模糊记忆的基督教，贝都因人在他们身后的平原放牧，索巴的国王号令不出残破的城池。

约1500年，阿拉伯首领阿卜杜拉·詹马摧毁了索巴的残迹；1504年，丰吉国王奥马尔·冬卡建立森纳尔苏丹国。河畔村落并入蓝苏丹国，苏菲圣徒传播伊斯兰教，阿拉伯语逐渐取代努比亚语——直到19世纪，尼罗河畔仍有人说努比亚语。西岸渡口往来着商队和前往麦加的西非朝圣者。1762年哈马吉人夺取森纳尔后，国家陷入内战；1821年5月，穆罕默德·阿里帕夏之子伊斯梅尔率军抵达两河汇流处，6月14日末代苏丹巴迪七世在森纳尔归降，西岸改属埃及。

en: North of Al-Fashir and east of the Kobbei caravan road, the arid Medwa country surrounds the Meidob volcanic field, where craters such as Malha hold springs and a salty lake amid the desert. Nubian-speaking Midob people herded and cultivated around the craters, while Zaghawa nomads moved camels and sheep between Darfur, Kanem and the Nile. In 1444 these wells formed a remote northern edge of the Tunjur-ruled Darfur world. Around 1600 Sulayman Solong's Keira expansion brought the Zaghawa under Darfur, after which Medowa lay on the desert flank of a sultanate whose Kobbei caravans carried slaves, ivory, ostrich feathers and gum north toward Egypt. Muhammad Tayrab's conquest of Kordofan around 1785 extended that power eastward, but the Turco-Egyptian victory near Bara in 1821 still stopped short of the craters.
zh: 在法希尔以北、科贝商路以东，干旱的梅德瓦环绕迈多布火山地；马勒哈等火山口保存着泉水和咸水湖，是沙漠中罕见的停泊点。说米多布语的米多布人在火山口周围放牧耕作，扎加瓦牧民则驱赶骆驼和绵羊往来达尔富尔、卡涅姆与尼罗河之间。1444年，这些水井构成通朱尔人统治的达尔富尔世界的遥远北缘。1600年前后，苏莱曼·索龙扩张凯拉政权，使扎加瓦人臣服达尔富尔；此后梅多瓦位于苏丹国的沙漠一侧，科贝商队把奴隶、象牙、鸵鸟羽和树胶向北运往埃及。穆罕默德·泰拉布约1785年征服科尔多凡，把这一势力推向东方；1821年土埃军队在巴拉取胜，但仍未进抵这些火山口。

en:
The ruins of Kobbe follow the Wadi Kobbei, west of Al-Fashir, at the southern end of the Darb El Arba'in, the Forty Days Road to Asyut in Egypt. Wells and stone cairns guided caravans across desert stages where water could be several days apart; the geographer Ibn Hawqal knew the road in the tenth century. In 1444, under Tunjur rule, the wadi was a northern gateway of Darfur rather than the great market it later became. Camels from the interior carried slaves, ivory, gold and salt toward Egypt, while cloth, metals and manufactured goods moved south.

From the seventeenth century the Forty Days Road became busier under the Keira sultans, linking Kobbe directly with Asyut. The sultanate drew slaves and ivory from its southern frontiers and exchanged them through Kobbe for Egyptian weapons, horses, cloth and other goods. Around 1700, during Ahmad Bukr's reign, arms obtained from Egypt helped Darfur repel a Wadai invasion that had reached Kabkabiya. The French traveller Charles-Jacques Poncet came down the road to Kobbe in 1698, and William George Browne rode with the camel caravan in 1793, the year after Sultan Abd al-Rahman established the new capital at Al-Fashir. By the early nineteenth century Kobbe was the largest town in Darfur, with as many as 8,000 people, trading slaves, ostrich feathers, camels, ivory and gum. The Turco-Egyptian conquest of Kordofan in 1821 stopped short of Darfur, leaving Kobbe's caravans in an independent sultanate at the close of this period.
zh:
科贝废墟沿科贝干河延伸，位于法希尔以西，是通往埃及艾斯尤特的「四十日路」在达尔富尔一端的终点。水井和石堆路标引导商队穿过相隔数日路程才有水的沙漠；地理学家伊本·豪盖勒10世纪已经记载这条道路。1444年通朱尔人统治时，这条干河是达尔富尔北方门户，还不是后来那样的大市场。内陆来的骆驼队把奴隶、象牙、黄金和盐运往埃及，布匹、金属和手工制品则向南流动。

17世纪起，四十日路在凯拉苏丹治下更加繁忙，把科贝与艾斯尤特直接连起。苏丹国从南部边疆取得奴隶和象牙，经科贝交换埃及武器、马匹、布匹和其他货物。约1700年艾哈迈德·巴克尔在位时，达尔富尔便靠埃及武器击退了一支进抵卡卜卡比耶的瓦达伊侵略军。法国旅人夏尔-雅克·蓬塞1698年沿这条道路抵达科贝；1792年阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼定都法希尔后的第二年，威廉·乔治·布朗又随骆驼商队同行。到19世纪初，科贝已是达尔富尔最大城镇，人口多至8000人，交易奴隶、鸵鸟羽、骆驼、象牙和树胶。1821年土埃军队征服科尔多凡，但没有进入达尔富尔；这一时期结束时，科贝商队仍属于一个独立苏丹国。

en:
The Orinoco ends in a vast labyrinth of channels, low islands, mangroves and palm swamps, where brown freshwater meets the Atlantic. In 1444 these waterlands were Warao country; their name means the boat people, and their canoes and stilt houses tied village life to fishing, hunting, gathering and the seasonal rise of the river. Warao tradition remembered the delta as a refuge entered under pressure from more warlike mainland peoples, and no European post yet commanded its Boca de Navíos or inner caños.

Christopher Columbus sighted the Paria coast in 1498 but did not enter the delta; Alonso de Ojeda recognized the Orinoco mouth in 1499, and Vicente Yáñez Pinzón explored it in 1500, calling the water Río Dulce. Diego de Ordaz ascended the Orinoco in 1531, and Spanish tradition attributed a short-lived Santo Tomás near the Caroní mouths to the following year. On 21 December 1595 Antonio de Berrío established Santo Tomás de Guayana just above the delta approaches, the fortified river port that gives the province its capital name. Carib attacks and Dutch and English raids forced the settlement to move three times; Walter Raleigh's expeditions burned and plundered it, including the raid of 1617, and its successor was finally fixed at Angostura in 1764. The first Warao mission was founded in 1682. During the eighteenth century Spanish governors and English authorities in Trinidad tried without lasting success to settle the Warao in fixed towns, and many moved toward Suriname; the Jesuit Joseph Gumilla left one of the earliest European descriptions of their river life.
zh:
奥里诺科河在尽头铺成广阔的水道迷宫：低岛、红树林、棕榈沼泽与棕色淡水一同迎向大西洋。1444年，这片水乡是瓦劳人的家园；他们的族名意为「船民」，独木舟和水上桩屋把村落生活同捕鱼、狩猎、采集及河水季节性涨落联系在一起。瓦劳人的口述传统把三角洲视为避难之地，他们是在大陆上更好战族群的压力下进入这片水网的；此时还没有欧洲据点控制纳维奥斯河口或内部河汊。

1498年，克里斯托弗·哥伦布望见帕里亚海岸，但没有进入三角洲；1499年，阿隆索·德·奥赫达辨认出奥里诺科河口；1500年，文森特·亚涅斯·平松探查此地，并把河水称为「淡水河」。1531年，迭戈·德·奥尔达斯溯奥里诺科河而上，西班牙传统认为次年在卡罗尼河口附近出现过一个短暂存在的圣托马斯。1595年12月21日，安东尼奥·德·贝里奥在三角洲通道稍上游设立圣托马斯·德·瓜亚纳，这座设防河港也就是游戏中首府名称的由来。加勒比人的攻击以及荷兰、英格兰袭掠迫使该据点三次迁移；沃尔特·雷利的远征曾焚毁和洗劫此地，1617年的袭击是其中一次，其后继据点最终在1764年固定于安戈斯图拉。第一个瓦劳传教站建立于1682年。18世纪，西班牙总督和特立尼达的英国当局都曾试图让瓦劳人定居到固定城镇，但未能持久，许多瓦劳人迁往苏里南；耶稣会士何塞·古米利亚留下了欧洲人对其水上生活最早的描述之一。

en:
Guasipati, 'beautiful land' in the local Carib tongue, lies inland from the lower Orinoco, between the Caroní and the forests that climb towards the Guayana highlands, a rolling savanna cut by streams running north to the great river. In 1444 its Carib-speaking peoples lived in villages along those creeks, planted cassava on the banks, fished and hunted, and traded by canoe with the river and the coast; no missionary or soldier had yet entered the country from Spanish Guayana.

From 1724 Catalan Capuchins, pushing up from the Caroní, gathered the Caribs into mission towns, and on 27 September 1757 they founded Guasipati as the eleventh town of the Missions of Caroní and El Dorado. Its thin soil never made it prosperous, and the other missions sent it meat and cassava, but the chain of towns around it became the granary and cattle range of Guayana Province — nineteen villages holding some 7,000 Indians by 1817, farming the best land in the province. The Capuchins opposed the revolution from 1810 and kept their towns loyal to the Crown. In January 1817 Manuel Piar was beaten at Angostura; in February he crossed the Caroní and overran the missions, taking Upata on the 6th and routing the royal governor's troops on the 17th. Hundreds of mission Indians marched with him as archers and spearmen, and on 11 April, at San Félix on the Chirica tableland, they helped break the royalist army. The victory opened the Orinoco to the republic and ended the Capuchin mission state; the friars were carried off to confinement at Caruachi.
zh:
瓜西帕蒂在当地加勒比语中意为「美丽的土地」，地处奥里诺科河下游内陆、卡罗尼河与圭亚那高原林野之间，起伏的热带草原上溪涧纵横，向北汇入大河。1444年，说加勒比语的原住民在溪畔结村而居，岸边种植木薯，兼以渔猎，并乘独木舟与大河和海岸通商；那时还没有传教士或军人从西班牙属圭亚那进入这片土地。

1724年起，加泰罗尼亚嘉布遣会修士从卡罗尼河向上游推进，把加勒比人编入传教村镇。1757年9月27日，瓜西帕蒂作为「卡罗尼与黄金国传教区」的第十一座村镇建立。这里土壤瘠薄，始终谈不上富庶，肉食和木薯要靠其他传教村接济；但周围连成一片的传教镇却是圭亚那省的粮仓和牧场，到1817年共有十九座村镇、约七千名印第安人，耕种着全省最肥沃的土地。嘉布遣会自1810年起就反对革命，让各传教镇始终效忠于王室。1817年1月曼努埃尔·皮亚尔在安戈斯图拉战败，2月便渡过卡罗尼河横扫传教区，6日拿下乌帕塔，17日击溃省督的部队。数百名传教镇印第安人带着弓箭和长矛随他出征，4月11日在奇里卡台地的圣费利克斯助他击溃保王军。此战为共和国打开了奥里诺科河，也终结了嘉布遣会的传教基业，修士们被押往卡鲁阿奇看管。

en: The bluffs where the Orinoco begins to open into its delta were the site of Uyapari, later Barrancas del Orinoco. Barrancoid and Saladoid artifacts there go back to around 1000 BCE, and the village had been continuously occupied since at least the eleventh century; in 1444 it was a long-established indigenous river settlement above the seasonal floods, placed on canoe routes between the llanos channels and the sea. In August 1531 Diego de Ordaz entered by the Caño Manamo in search of El Dorado and found more than 400 bohíos, meeting the cacique Naricagua, whose lordship was associated with the name Uyapari. Aragonese Capuchins reached the area late in the seventeenth century, and in 1790 Fray Joaquín de Morata founded the mission of San Rafael Arcángel de Barrancas with Warao help. Alexander von Humboldt visited in 1800; during the independence wars the friars withdrew, but the native settlement remained.
zh: 奥里诺科河开始展宽进入三角洲的河岸高地上，坐落着乌亚帕里，后来的巴兰卡斯德尔奥里诺科。当地巴兰科伊德与萨拉多伊德文化器物可追溯至约公元前1000年，村落至少自11世纪起便持续有人居住；1444年，这里是一座历史悠久的印第安河居，高踞于季节性洪水之上，扼守亚诺斯水道与大海之间的独木舟航路。1531年8月，寻找黄金国的迭戈·德·奥达斯经马纳莫汊河抵达，见到四百多座茅屋，并会见了与乌亚帕里之名相连的领地首领纳里卡瓜。阿拉贡嘉布遣会士17世纪末来到这一带；1790年，华金·德·莫拉塔修士在瓦劳人帮助下建立圣拉斐尔·阿尔坎赫尔·德·巴兰卡斯传教站并修建教堂。洪堡1800年到访此地；独立战争期间修士撤离，但印第安村落仍在。

en:
The Guajira Peninsula, Woumainpa'a in the Wayuu language, is the arid, wind-scoured northern tip of South America, running from the salt pans of Manaure to the Gulf of Venezuela. In 1444 it belonged to the Wayuu, Arawak-speakers organised in matrilineal clans across scattered villages, who fished the reefs, gathered salt and traded by canoe with the Antilles; Cabo de la Vela, which they called Jepirra, was the sacred cape through which the souls of the dead passed on. Kindred peoples such as the Añú lived by the gulf, and the interior desert had never seen a European army.

Alonso de Ojeda, with Juan de la Cosa and Amerigo Vespucci, first sailed these coasts in 1499, naming the gulf Coquivacoa. In 1535, during the Welsers' German lease of Venezuela, Nicolás Federmann founded Nuestra Señora de las Nieves near Cabo de la Vela, the first Spanish settlement on the peninsula; its pearl beds drew divers from ruined Cubagua, and in 1544–45 the town was moved to the mouth of the Ranchería river as Riohacha, the 'gateway of pearls'. The Wayuu were never conquered: they took to horses and Spanish firearms, traded pearls and cattle for English and Dutch guns, and rose in revolt in 1701, 1727 and again in 1769, when up to 20,000 warriors burned the settlements and penned the Spaniards inside Riohacha, after which the Crown reorganized the coast as the separate Province of Riohacha. Francis Drake sacked the pearl town in 1596. It changed sides only on 25 May 1820, when José Prudencio Padilla's patriot fleet won the battle of Laguna Salá; under Gran Colombia the peninsula's colonial age ended, though the Wayuu kept their autonomy.
zh:
瓜希拉半岛在瓦尤语中称沃温帕阿，是南美洲最北端一片干旱多风的土地，从马瑙雷盐沼一直延伸到委内瑞拉湾。1444年，这里属于瓦尤人：这支说阿拉瓦克语的民族按母系氏族分住在散布的村落里，在礁湖中捕鱼、采盐，并划独木舟与安的列斯群岛贸易；他们称贝拉角为杰皮拉，那是亡魂渡往彼岸的神圣海角。湾边还住着阿纽人等同族部落，内陆沙漠中从未出现过欧洲军队。

1499年，阿隆索·德·奥赫达与胡安·德·拉·科萨、亚美利哥·韦斯普奇首次航行到这一带海岸，把海湾命名为科基瓦科阿。1535年，在韦尔泽家族承租委内瑞拉的德意志时期，尼古劳斯·费德曼在贝拉角附近建立雪圣母镇，这是半岛上第一个西班牙人定居点；当地珠蚌床引来从凋敝的库巴瓜迁来的采珠人。1544至1545年，城镇迁到兰切里亚河口，改称里奥阿查，号称「珍珠门户」。瓦尤人始终未被征服：他们学会了养马和使用西班牙火器，用珍珠和牲畜向英、荷走私商换取枪支，先后在1701年、1727年和1769年起义；1769年，多达两万名战士焚毁定居点，把西班牙人困在里奥阿查，王室此后只得把这片海岸单列为里奥阿查省。弗朗西斯·德雷克1596年洗劫了这座珍珠之城。1820年5月25日，何塞·普鲁登西奥·帕迪利亚的爱国舰队赢得拉萨拉达湖海战，里奥阿查才告易帜；大哥伦比亚成立后，半岛的殖民时代结束，而瓦尤人仍保有自治。

en:
The eastern shore of Lake Maracaibo, low and hot behind its mangrove fringe, was the country of the Caquetío, an Arawakan fishing people who raised stilt houses over the shallows and travelled the lagoon by canoe. Their water-villages—Lagunillas de Agua, Moporo and Tomoporo among them—stood on piles with canoes moored beneath the houses, and the people traded fish and salt toward the drier lands around Coro. In 1444 these villages answered to no outside power, and the shore knew nothing of Europeans.

Local tradition, upheld by the Zulia Academy of History, dates the port of Altagracia to 8 September 1529, when Ambrosius Ehinger's Welser expedition placed a post on this shore opposite its new settlement of Neu-Nürnberg at the lake narrows. It remained a poor fishing anchorage until 1600, when it was raised to a villa and gained streets, a church and warehouses; Santa Rita and Cabimas took shape along the same coast in the colonial years. The Maracaibo province stayed royalist after 1810, but from Altagracia Ana María Campos organised resistance to royal rule; seized and publicly tortured, she refused to recant. While Maracaibo held for the Crown, Altagracia remained a patriot doorway onto the lake.
zh:
马拉开波湖东岸地势低平、气候湿热，沿岸长满红树林，本是卡克蒂奥人的家园。他们属阿拉瓦克语族，以渔为业，在浅水中架起桩屋，乘独木舟往来湖面；拉古尼利亚斯德阿瓜、莫波罗、托莫波罗等水村都建在木桩之上，屋下系着独木舟，村民以鱼、盐与朝科罗方向的干旱地带通商。1444年，这些村落不受任何外来政权统属，湖岸上还没有欧洲人的踪迹。

按苏利亚州历史学院正式采用的说法，阿尔塔格拉西亚港始于1529年9月8日：韦尔泽家族的埃因格远征队在湖口此岸设立据点，与对岸的新城新纽伦堡遥相扼守。此后它长期只是个荒凉的渔船锚地，直到1600年才正式设镇，修起街道、教堂和仓库；殖民时期，圣丽塔和卡维马斯也在这段湖岸成形。1810年后马拉开波省仍效忠西班牙王室，安娜·玛丽亚·坎波斯却在阿尔塔格拉西亚组织抵抗运动；她被捕并当众受刑，始终不肯屈服。只要马拉开波仍在王室手中，阿尔塔格拉西亚就一直是爱国军通向大湖的门户。

en:
Coro stands on a windy coastal plain beside the Paraguaná Peninsula, with its port at La Vela a few kilometres away on the Caribbean. In 1444 this land, called Curiana, belonged to the Caquetio, an Arawak people ruled by the cacique Manaure. Spaniards first coasted these shores in 1499 with Alonso de Ojeda, whose men saw villages raised on stilts above the water and, reminded of Venice, named the country Venezuela.

On 26 July 1527 Juan de Ampíes founded Santa Ana de Coro, pledging to respect Manaure's rule, but in February 1529 Ambrosius Ehinger arrived as governor for the Welsers: Charles V had granted the province to the Augsburg banking house as Klein-Venedig, and the town, renamed Neu-Augsburg, became the first German colony in the Americas and the base of expeditions that searched the Llanos for El Dorado until the grant was revoked in 1545. Coro was the first capital of Venezuela Province and from 1531 the seat of South America's first bishopric, but pirate raids and its harsh climate cost it the capital to Caracas in 1578 and the diocese in 1636; seventeenth-century European charts marked it 'destroyed' after hurricanes and sacks. The town recovered on the hinterland's trade, and on 10 May 1795 the free zambo José Leonardo Chirino raised a slave revolt in the Sierra de Coro, a forerunner of Venezuelan independence, for which he was hanged in 1796. In August 1806 Francisco de Miranda landed at La Vela and raised his tricolour there for the first time, only to find the town deserted by its royalist inhabitants; Coro held for the king after 1810 and was taken for the republic by Josefa Camejo in 1821.
zh:
科罗（圣安娜德科罗）坐落在帕拉瓜纳半岛旁多风的沿海平原，几公里外的加勒比海岸是它的外港拉维拉。1444年，这片被称为库里亚纳的土地属于卡克蒂奥人——一支受酋长马瑙雷统辖的阿拉瓦克人。1499年，西班牙人随阿隆索·德·奥赫达的船队首次沿岸航行，水手看到水上的吊脚屋村落，想起威尼斯，便把这片土地称作委内瑞拉。

1527年7月26日，胡安·马丁·德·安普埃斯建立圣安娜德科罗，许诺尊重马瑙雷的权威；但1529年2月，安布罗修斯·埃因格作为韦尔瑟家族的首任总督到来：查理五世已把委内瑞拉省特许给这家奥格斯堡的银行家族抵债，称为「小威尼斯」，城市改名新奥格斯堡，成为美洲第一个德意志殖民地，也是深入亚诺斯草原寻找「黄金国」的各支探险队的基地，特许权于1545年被收回。科罗是委内瑞拉省的第一个首府，1531年又成为南美洲第一个主教区的驻地；但海盗的反复袭击和恶劣气候使它在1578年把首府让给加拉加斯，1636年又失去主教区。17世纪的飓风和几度洗劫之后，欧洲海图把它标作「已毁」，但靠着腹地的贸易它又恢复过来。1795年5月10日，自由的桑博人何塞·莱昂纳多·奇里诺在科罗山区发动奴隶起义，被视为委内瑞拉独立的先声，他本人于1796年被绞死。1806年8月，弗朗西斯科·德·米兰达在拉维拉登陆，第一次升起他的三色旗，却发现效忠王室的居民已弃城而去；科罗在1810年后仍站在西班牙一边，直到1821年才被何塞法·卡梅霍为共和国拿下。

en:
The Llanos are a wide tropical savanna east of the Andes, broken by gallery forests and rivers that flood the low ground in the wet season. Around the Guárico River, on the future site of Calabozo, indigenous communities hunted, fished, gathered and planted small alluvial plots in 1444, ordering their lives around drought and flood rather than a Spanish-style town. No European settlement yet marked the grassland, whose trails linked river banks, seasonal camps and hunting grounds.

Andalusian Capuchins organized missions nearby in 1723, and Villa de Todos los Santos de Calabozo was formally founded on 1 February 1724. A royal decree confirmed the foundation in 1738 and the town's title in 1774, by which time cattle, mules and horses were being driven along plains routes toward Caracas. Its first council met in 1776, and Bishop Mariano Martí recorded 428 houses and 3,448 inhabitants in 1780. In 1800 Alexander von Humboldt visited and described electrical instruments built by Carlos del Pozo y Sucre, a self-taught local experimenter. The cabildo joined the independence movement on 31 July 1811, after which royalist and republican armies repeatedly contested the crossroads. José Tomás Boves made Calabozo one of his bases, while on 12 February 1818 Simón Bolívar and José Antonio Páez struck Pablo Morillo's royalist army there; Morillo withdrew two days later.
zh:
亚诺斯是安第斯山脉以东广阔的热带草原，湿季时河漫滩被水淹没，林间走廊沿水道伸展。1444年，在后来建立卡拉沃索的瓜里科河一带，原住民群落以狩猎、捕鱼、采集和在小片冲积地上耕作维生，随旱涝节奏迁徙，并不存在西班牙式城镇。此时草原上还没有欧洲人定居点，只有连接河岸、季节性营地和猎场的小路。

1723年，安达卢西亚嘉布遣会传教士在附近组织传教区；1724年2月1日，诸圣卡拉沃索镇正式建立。王室敕令先后于1738年和1774年确认其建镇与城镇地位，到18世纪后期，牛、骡和马沿草原商路被赶往加拉加斯。卡拉沃索1776年设立首个市政会，马里亚诺·马蒂主教1780年记录当地有428栋房屋、3448名居民。1800年，亚历山大·冯·洪堡到访这里，记述了自学成才的本地实验者卡洛斯·德尔·波索·伊·苏克雷制造的电学仪器。1811年7月31日，市政会加入独立运动，此后保王军与共和军反复争夺这处草原枢纽。何塞·托马斯·博韦斯曾以卡拉沃索为据点之一；1818年2月12日，西蒙·玻利瓦尔和何塞·安东尼奥·派斯在此袭击巴勃罗·莫里略的保王军，莫里略两天后撤退。

en:
Apure is the flood-country of the western Venezuelan Llanos, where the Apure, Arauca and Capanaparo gather waters from the Andes and carry them to the Orinoco. In 1444 no Spanish frontier reached these seasonally inundated plains. Arawak and Carib peoples lived along the banks and on higher ground, using the rivers as roads through grasslands that stretched for weeks of travel; the name Apure, later said to recall a shrub or a chief called Apur, belonged first to the river.

Spanish expeditions began to enter the region in the mid-1600s, and Friar Jacinto de Carvajal used the name Apure in 1648, but effective occupation came only in the following century. Ranchers from San Carlos de Austria and Andalusian Franciscans pushed in with cattle herds and missions, while most Apure towns, including Guasdualito and Achaguas, grew up after 1760. As part of the new Province of Barinas, the river port of San Fernando del Paso Real de Apure was founded on 28 February 1788 by order of Governor Fernando Miyares. Alexander von Humboldt visited it from 27 to 30 March 1800. During the independence wars, José Antonio Páez turned the plains into cavalry country, fighting around Guasdualito in 1815, Achaguas and San Fernando in 1816, and against royalist cavalry at Las Queseras del Medio on 2 April 1819. By 1821 the Apure plains were held within Gran Colombia.
zh:
阿普雷是委内瑞拉西部草原的洪水之乡，阿普雷河、阿劳卡河和卡帕纳帕罗河在此汇集安第斯山来水，再注入奥里诺科河。1444年，西班牙人的势力尚未抵达这些季节性泛滥的平原。阿拉瓦克人和加勒比人生活在河岸与高地上，借河道穿行绵延数周路程的草原；阿普雷这个名字最初属于河流，后来有人说它来自一种灌木，也有人说来自名叫阿普尔的酋长。

西班牙远征在17世纪中叶开始进入此地，修士哈辛托·德·卡瓦哈尔1648年已使用阿普雷一名，但真正的占领要到下一个世纪。来自圣卡洛斯·德·奥地利的牧场主和安达卢西亚方济各会士带着牛群与传教站推进，瓜斯杜阿利托、阿查瓜斯等多数阿普雷城镇都在1760年以后形成。作为新设巴里纳斯省的一部分，圣费尔南多·德尔帕索雷亚尔·德·阿普雷河港于1788年2月28日奉省长费尔南多·米亚雷斯之命建立。亚历山大·冯·洪堡曾在1800年3月27日至30日到访。独立战争中，何塞·安东尼奥·派斯把这片平原变成骑兵战场，1815年转战瓜斯杜阿利托，1816年转战阿查瓜斯和圣费尔南多，1819年4月2日在拉斯克塞拉斯德尔梅迪奥与保王骑兵交战。到1821年，阿普雷草原已处于大哥伦比亚境内。

en:
The Atabapo is a blackwater river winding some 130 kilometres through rainforest, forming much of the border between Venezuela and Colombia before it meets the Guainía and the Guaviare at San Fernando, where the Orinoco proper begins. In 1444 its dark, fish-rich waters belonged to Arawak-speaking peoples, the Baniva among them, who planted bitter cassava on the banks, and to Puinave villagers of the confluence, whose hamlet of Casuru stood where the town would later rise. By dugout and short portages they traded with the Orinoco below and with the Guainía flowing towards the Amazon.

The outside world reached the river only in the 1750s, when the Crown sent its Orinoco Boundary Expedition of 1754–1761 to mark the frontier with Portuguese Brazil under the Treaty of Madrid. On 31 July 1758 José Solano, an officer of that commission, raised a fort beside the Puinave village of Casuru and, with the local chief Crucero — named lieutenant and governor of the place — founded San Fernando de Atabapo, the first Spanish settlement in what is now the state of Amazonas. The town was destroyed two years later, and in 1765 the friar José A. de Xerez attempted to rebuild it, leaving only a thin chain of mission stations along the blackwater creeks. In 1800 Alexander von Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland passed that way, travelling from the Orinoco to the Casiquiare channel and the Río Negro. During the wars of independence, in 1817, the patriot officer Hipólito Cuebas seized San Fernando with a band of only eighty men.
zh:
阿塔瓦波是一条在热带雨林中蜿蜒约130公里的黑水河，大部分河道构成委内瑞拉与哥伦比亚的国界，最后在圣费尔南多附近与瓜伊尼亚河、瓜维亚雷河相会，奥里诺科河自此正名。1444年，黝黑而多鱼的河水属于说阿拉瓦克语的诸族，巴尼瓦人是其中一支，他们在岸边种植苦木薯；河口一带还住着普伊纳维人，其村落卡苏鲁就坐落在后来城镇兴起的地方。他们驾着独木舟、经短途陆运，与下游的奥里诺科河和流向亚马孙的瓜伊尼亚河通商。

直到1750年代，外界才抵达这条河：为按1750年《马德里条约》划定与葡属巴西的边界，西班牙王室派出了1754至1761年的奥里诺科勘界远征队。1758年7月31日，队中的军官何塞·索拉诺在普伊纳维村落卡苏鲁旁筑起要塞，并任命当地酋长克鲁塞罗为副长官兼地方首领，建立圣费尔南多·德·阿塔瓦波——这是今亚马孙州境内的第一座西班牙人城镇。两年后城镇被毁，1765年修士何塞·A·德·赫雷斯试图重建，最终只在黑水溪涧之间留下一串稀疏的传教站。1800年，洪堡与邦普朗途经此地，由奥里诺科河前往卡西基亚雷水道和内格罗河。独立战争期间的1817年，爱国军军官伊波利托·奎瓦斯仅率八十人就拿下了圣费尔南多。

en:
The grasslands around Pore lie where the Llanos Orientales rise toward the Eastern Cordillera. In 1444 they were not a Spanish province: Sáliva, Guahibo, Tunebo and Piapoco communities moved among the seasonally flooded savanna, rivers and gallery forests, cultivating small clearings, fishing and hunting. Expeditions from the Andes reached the Llanos early in the sixteenth century, and encomiendas soon reduced many of the people to forced labour; the town itself came much later.

Pore was formally founded on 5 November 1644 by Adriano Vargas and Francisco Enciso. Jesuit estates then turned the surrounding plains into cattle country linked by trade to Tunja and Venezuela, until the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 weakened the region. During the Comunero rising, Javier de Mendoza led revolt across Casanare in 1781, and on 17 February 1810 Carlos Salgar, José María Rosillo and Vicente Cadena briefly seized Pore. Royalists retook the town and executed Salgar and Cadena on 30 April. In 1818 Pore became a provincial capital under the independence movement, and in 1819 Bolívar's troops joined Santander's llanero forces there before marching to Boyacá.
zh:
颇雷（Pore）周围的稀树草原，位于东部亚诺斯平原向安第斯山东科迪勒拉山脉抬升的地带。1444年这里还不是西班牙人的行省，萨利瓦人、瓜希沃人、图内博人和皮亚波科人在季节性泛滥的草原、河流与走廊林之间迁徙，在小块空地上耕作，也捕鱼狩猎。16世纪初，来自安第斯山区的远征队进入亚诺斯，监护征赋制很快迫使许多原住民服劳役；城镇本身则出现得晚得多。

1644年11月5日，阿德里亚诺·巴尔加斯和弗朗西斯科·恩西索正式建立颇雷。耶稣会庄园随后把周围平原经营成牧牛地，商路连通通哈与委内瑞拉，直到1767年耶稣会被驱逐，地区经济随之受挫。1781年市民起义期间，哈维尔·德·门多萨在卡萨纳雷领导起事；1810年2月17日，卡洛斯·萨尔加、何塞·玛丽亚·罗西略和维森特·卡德纳一度占领颇雷。保王军重夺城镇后，于4月30日处死萨尔加和卡德纳。1818年，颇雷成为独立运动的省府；1819年，玻利瓦尔的部队在此与桑坦德的亚诺斯骑兵会合，随后向博亚卡进军。

en:
The Mérida region lies on the high shelves and valleys of the Venezuelan Andes, around the Chama River beneath the Sierra Nevada. In 1444 it was still indigenous country: Timoto-Cuica, Chama, Mocotíes, Mucuchíes and Tatey villagers farmed maize and roots on irrigated terraces, exchanged goods along mountain paths, and honored mountains, lakes and the sun. Their numerous, ranked settlements gave the later Spanish province both its labor and its place names.

Captain Juan Rodríguez Suárez founded Mérida on 9 October 1558, naming it for his native Mérida in Extremadura. After conflict with neighboring peoples, Juan de Maldonado refounded it as Santiago de los Caballeros on the present plateau in 1559. It became capital of the Governorship of Mérida in 1622, was joined to Maracaibo's province in 1676, and passed from New Granada to the Captaincy General of Venezuela in 1777. Tobacco taxes and Bourbon monopolies drove a comunero revolt in 1781; in 1785 the new episcopal see gave rise to the seminary that became the University of the Andes in 1811. The earthquake of 26 March 1812 killed more than 800 people and preceded royalist reconquest. Bolívar passed through the city during his Admirable Campaign in May 1813, but royalists returned in 1814 and crushed the La Patriecita rising in 1818. Bolívar's Andean campaign freed Mérida again in 1820, and in 1821 it entered Gran Colombia in the Department of Zulia.
zh:
梅里达地区位于委内瑞拉安第斯山的高台与河谷，地处内华达山脉下方的查马河流域。1444年，这里仍是印第安人的土地：蒂莫托—奎卡人、查马人、莫科蒂人、穆库奇人和塔泰人在灌溉梯田上种植玉米和块根作物，沿山路交换物产，并敬拜山岳、湖泊与太阳。他们数量众多、层级分明的聚落，后来为西班牙行省提供了劳动力，也留下了许多地名。

胡安·罗德里格斯·苏亚雷斯上尉1558年10月9日建立梅里达，以故乡埃斯特雷马杜拉的梅里达命名。因与邻近部族冲突，胡安·马尔多纳多1559年在查马河谷的高台上重建此城，定名圣地亚哥·德·洛斯·卡瓦列罗斯。1622年它成为梅里达总督辖区首府，1676年并入马拉开波省，1777年从新格拉纳达划归委内瑞拉都督辖区。1781年，烟草税和波旁垄断引发公社者起义；1785年，新设立的主教教座催生神学院，神学院又于1811年成为安第斯大学。1812年3月26日地震致死八百余人，随后保王派重新征服此地。玻利瓦尔1813年5月在其山地远征中经过梅里达，但保王派1814年卷土重来，并在1818年镇压「小祖国」起事。1820年，玻利瓦尔的安第斯战役再次解放梅里达；1821年，它并入大哥伦比亚，隶属苏利亚省。

en:
The lands named for the Meta River run from the wet Andean foothills to the open Llanos Orientales. In 1444 Guayupe, Guahibo, Huitoto and Piapoco communities were scattered through this country of seasonal savanna, gallery forest and Orinoco tributaries, moving between rivers, hunting and fishing and working planted clearings. No Spanish town yet commanded the plains; outside knowledge of the Meta came only with conquistadors drawn by rumours of gold.

Stories of El Dorado brought Diego de Ordaz to the region around 1531, and in 1539 Alfonso de Heredia led an expedition through the Llanos to the mouth of the Meta. By 1544 encomiendas had taken root, beginning with the grant held by Pedro Rodríguez de Salamanca. Jesuit and Augustinian missionaries later gathered indigenous people into reductions, learned local languages and introduced loom weaving and European instruments. The plains long remained a mission frontier attached in part to the province of Bogotá. In 1819 Francisco de Paula Santander organized patriot forces in the Casanare and Meta llanos for Bolívar's New Granada campaign.
zh:
以梅塔河得名的这片土地，从湿润的安第斯山麓一直延伸到开阔的东部亚诺斯平原。1444年，瓜尤佩人、瓜希沃人、维托托人和皮亚波科人散居在季节性草原、走廊林与奥里诺科河支流之间，沿各河迁徙，捕鱼狩猎并耕作小块开垦地。当时还没有西班牙城镇控制这片平原；外界对梅塔的认识，要等到被黄金传闻吸引来的征服者之后才开始。

1531年前后，黄金国的传说把迭戈·德·奥尔达斯引到这一地区；1539年，阿方索·德·埃雷迪亚率领远征队穿过亚诺斯，抵达梅塔河口。到1544年，监护征赋制已经在此扎根，最早的监护地属于佩德罗·罗德里格斯·德·萨拉曼卡。后来，耶稣会和奥古斯丁会传教士把原住民集中到归化村，学习当地语言，也传授织机织造和欧洲乐器。在很长时间里，这片草原都是波哥大省边缘的传教前沿。1819年，弗朗西斯科·德·保拉·桑坦德在卡萨纳雷和梅塔的草原上组织爱国军，为玻利瓦尔的新格拉纳达战役做准备。

en:
The province bearing the name Puerto Carreño covers the lowland gateway where the Meta River enters the Orinoco. In 1444 Achagua people lived across these plains between the Casanare, Meta and Apure rivers, and the river junction let them trade farm produce for weapons with Carib groups. Seasonal floods, gallery forest and broad savanna set the rhythm of village life; no Spanish mission or fort yet stood at the confluence.

In 1666 the Jesuit Alonso de Neira founded San Joaquín de Atanari for Achagua people on the south bank of the Meta, close to its mouth, but lack of supplies and pressure from local Carib groups forced the settlement's abandonment in 1669. Missionaries returned to found Santa Teresa de Jesús and the mission and stronghold of Carichana, which became self-supporting agricultural and cattle holdings. During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the Meta and Orinoco also carried a lively contraband trade, bringing goods more cheaply than the official markets of Santafé and Caracas. The independence wars weakened these mission estates and river enterprises.
zh:
名为卡雷尼奥港的省份，覆盖梅塔河注入奥里诺科河处的低地门户。1444年，阿查瓜人生活在卡萨纳雷河、梅塔河与阿普雷河之间的平原上；凭借这个河运交汇点，他们用农产品同加勒比人群交换武器。季节性洪水、走廊林和广阔草原支配着村落生活，汇流处还没有西班牙传教站或要塞。

1666年，耶稣会士阿隆索·德·内拉在梅塔河南岸、接近河口处为阿查瓜人建立圣华金·德·阿塔纳里传教站；由于补给不足，并受到当地加勒比群体的压力，该居民点于1669年废弃。传教士后来又建立圣特雷莎·德·赫苏斯以及卡里查纳传教站和堡垒，后者发展成自给自足的农业和牧牛庄园。17至18世纪，梅塔河与奥里诺科河上还有活跃的走私贸易，货物价格低于圣菲和加拉加斯的官方市场。独立战争削弱了这些传教庄园与河上贸易事业。

en: The Guaviare begins where the Guayabero and Ariari rivers meet below the eastern Andes and carries the waters of the forested piedmont toward the Orinoco. In 1444 its banks, gallery woods and neighboring savannas were held by autonomous Guayabero, Tinigua, Sikuani, Nukak, Piapoco and Puinave communities, whose canoes used the long lower channel between fishing camps and rainforest. Spanish claims later attached the basin to the province of Popayán, but settlement did not follow the claim. In 1821 Gran Colombia assigned Guaviare to the department of Boyacá, a jurisdiction that still meant little along rivers governed chiefly by their Indigenous inhabitants.
zh: 瓜维亚雷河由瓜亚韦罗河与阿里亚里河在东安第斯山麓汇合而成，把覆满雨林的山麓水流带向奥里诺科河。1444年，河畔林、邻近草原和河岸地带属于瓜亚韦罗、蒂尼瓜、西库阿尼、努卡克、皮亚波科和普伊纳韦等自治族群；他们的独木舟沿漫长下游河道往来于渔场与雨林之间。西班牙后来在名义上把这一流域划归波帕扬省，但并没有随之建立有效移民据点。1821年，大哥伦比亚将瓜维亚雷划入博亚卡省；对这些仍主要由原住民支配的河流来说，这一行政归属在当时意义甚微。

en:
The upper Magdalena opens into a hot, fertile plain between the Cordillera Central and the Cordillera Oriental, watered by the Las Ceibas and the del Oro rivers. The north of this country was the land of the Pijao, a loose confederation of peoples led by the Coyaima and Natagaima, whom no lord had ever united into a state; the Andaquí and Yalcón lived to the south, the Páez in the western hills and the Tama to the east. The rivers that ran down from the cordilleras carried gold, and the villages of the plain traded goldwork and tobacco with both slopes of the Andes. In 1444 the valley knew nothing of Europeans, and the Pijao remained its unchallenged masters.

Captain Juan de Cabrera founded the first Neiva in 1539, on the Río Neiva in Tama country. Juan de Alonso y Arias moved it around 1550 to the place later called Villavieja, where Pijao warriors destroyed the town in 1560, in the middle of the eighty years of Pijao wars. Only on 24 May 1612 did Diego de Ospina y Medinilla refound Neiva on its present site; two years earlier the Province of Páez, soon to be the Province of Neiva, had been separated from the governorship of Popayán, and the new town became its capital, ahead of La Plata, Timaná and Purificación. Cattle haciendas spread over the plain and gold was washed along the Saldaña, while Neiva stood on the road linking the Viceroyalty of Peru with Santafé and the Caribbean; from 1717 it belonged to the new Viceroyalty of New Granada. A junta seized the town in 1810 and it proclaimed itself a free state on 8 February 1814, but Morillo's reconquest retook Neiva on 17 May 1816. The upper Magdalena returned to patriot hands in 1819.
zh:
马格达莱纳河上游在中部山脉与东部山脉之间铺成一片炎热肥沃的平原，塞瓦斯河与奥罗河穿流其间。平原北部是皮哈奥人的地盘，这是一个以科亚伊马、纳塔盖马等部为首的松散联盟，从未统一为国家；南面住着安达基人和亚尔孔人，西边山里是帕埃斯人，东面是塔马人。从两山流下的河川带金，平原上的村落用金器和烟草同山脉两侧的居民贸易。1444年，欧洲人还不知道这条河谷，皮哈奥人是这里无可争议的主人。

1539年，胡安·德·卡布雷拉船长在塔马人土地上的内瓦河畔第一次建立内瓦城。约1550年，胡安·德·阿隆索·阿里亚斯把城迁到后来称比亚维哈的地方，1560年被皮哈奥战士摧毁，时值绵延约八十年的皮哈奥战争中期。直到1612年5月24日，迭戈·德·奥斯皮纳·梅迪尼利亚才在现址重建内瓦；此前两年，帕埃斯省——旋即改称内瓦省——从波帕扬都督辖区分出，新城最终成为省会，位在拉普拉塔、蒂马纳和普里菲卡西翁之上。牧牛大庄园遍布平原，萨尔达尼亚河畔淘金繁忙，内瓦又扼守连接秘鲁总督辖区与圣菲和加勒比海的陆路通道；1717年起它归属新设的新格拉纳达总督辖区。1810年，本地洪达接管城市，1814年2月8日宣布成立自由邦，但莫里略的再征服军队于1816年5月17日攻占内瓦。1819年，上马格达莱纳才重回爱国者之手。

en:
High in the cool Pubenza Valley, 1,760 metres up between the Western and Central cordilleras, stood Yauto, seat of the Pubenza confederacy, a loose league of chiefdoms that counted the Kokonuco, Guambía, Totoró and Timbío among its peoples. At El Morro del Tulcán they had raised an adobe pyramid, and the sea shells and foreign stones buried there show their trade reaching far beyond the mountains. In 1444 the valley's villages, governed by caciques and the rulers called yasgüenes, farmed the highland basins and panned gold from their rivers, still untroubled by any European.

Captain Juan de Ampudia seized the El Azafate ridge on Christmas Eve 1536, and Sebastián de Belalcázar declared Asunción de Popayán founded on 13 January 1537, the solemn charter following on 15 August. Belalcázar made the town the seat of his gobernación in 1540, and it grew rich as the clearing house for gold from the Chocó and Barbacoas mines bound for Cartagena and Spain. Cattle began to arrive through Buenaventura after 1550, and great slave-owning families raised the baroque churches of San Francisco and Santo Domingo and patronised the Payanesa goldsmiths who made the Crown of the Andes. A royal mint opened in 1748, one of only two in the Viceroyalty of New Granada, striking gold escudos down to 1820. A junta met in Popayán in 1810 and the city proclaimed independence on 24 March 1814, while the surrounding country saw the battles of La Ladera, Calibío and La Cuchilla del Tambo; two of its sons, the jurist Camilo Torres and the scientist Francisco José de Caldas, were executed in Santafé during Morillo's reconquest. After Boyacá the mint and the mines passed to the Republic of Colombia.
zh:
在西安第斯山脉与中科迪勒拉山脉之间、海拔1760米的凉爽普本萨河谷高地上，坐落着亚乌托——普本萨联盟的中心。这个松散的酋邦联盟汇聚了科科努科人、关比亚人、托托罗人和廷比奥人等族系。他们在图尔坎山岗筑起土坯金字塔，墓中出土的海贝与远方宝石说明，其贸易网络远远延伸到群山之外。1444年，河谷中的村落由卡西克和称亚斯古恩的首领们统辖，在高原盆地耕作，从河里淘取砂金，此时还没有欧洲人来惊扰他们。

1536年圣诞夜，胡安·德·安普迪亚上尉夺取埃尔阿萨特岭；1537年1月13日，塞瓦斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔宣布建立亚松森·德·波帕扬，正式建城仪式在8月15日举行。1540年贝拉尔卡萨尔把督军辖区治所设在此地，城市随之暴富：乔科和巴尔巴夸斯矿区的黄金经此集散，运往卡塔赫纳再输往西班牙。1550年后牛群经布埃纳文图拉源源输入，蓄奴豪族建起圣方济各、圣多明各等巴洛克教堂，并供养波帕扬金器学派——「安第斯之冠」即出自当地匠人之手。1748年王家铸币厂开张，是新格拉纳达总督区仅有的两家铸币厂之一，铸造金埃斯库多直到1820年。1810年波帕扬设立洪达，1814年3月24日宣布独立，城周先后打响拉德拉、卡利维奥和坦博岭诸役；城中子弟、法学家卡米洛·托雷斯与科学家弗朗西斯科·何塞·德·卡尔达斯在莫里略再征服期间于圣菲遇害。博亚卡战役之后，铸币厂与各处金矿归入哥伦比亚共和国。

en:
Forested and rain-soaked, Darién forms the eastern neck of the Isthmus of Panama between the Gulf of Urabá and the Bay of San Miguel. In 1444 its river villages belonged to peoples later called Cueva by the Spanish; they farmed forest clearings and worked gold into ornaments. Guna communities also lived around the Urabá shore, while the swamps and rainforest kept the trails beyond the canoe routes beyond the reach of any outside empire.

The Spanish Crown divided Tierra Firme between Alonso de Ojeda and Diego de Nicuesa in 1508. In September 1510 Martín Fernández de Enciso, advised by Vasco Núñez de Balboa, founded Santa María la Antigua del Darién after the defeat of Cémaco's Cueva warriors. From that town Balboa set out on 1 September 1513 with 190 Spaniards and 1,000 indigenous auxiliaries, sighted the South Sea on 25 September and claimed it for Castile four days later in the Bay of San Miguel. Pedrarias Dávila had Balboa executed at Acla in January 1519 and founded Panama City in August, moving the seat of Castilla del Oro away from Darién; Santa María was soon abandoned and burned. William Paterson's Scots landed near Golden Island on 30 October 1698, made an alliance with a local leader and raised the colony of New Caledonia. Fever and hunger forced them out in June 1699. A second expedition of about 1,300 men returned that November, but a Spanish blockade and siege left it no choice but to ask for surrender terms on 28 March 1700. The forests of Darién then remained a contested frontier between Spanish power and its indigenous neighbours.
zh:
达连雨林潮湿，构成巴拿马地峡东部的狭颈，介于乌拉瓦湾与圣米格尔湾之间。1444年，河滨村落属于后来被西班牙人统称为库埃瓦人的诸族群；他们在林间空地耕作，并把黄金打制成饰物。乌拉瓦湾沿岸也有库纳人的聚落，而沼泽和热带雨林使独木舟水路之外的小径不受任何外来帝国控制。

1508年，西班牙王室将美洲大陆沿岸的特许权分给阿隆索·德·奥赫达与迭戈·德·尼库萨。1510年9月，马丁·费尔南德斯·德·恩西索在瓦斯科·努涅斯·德·巴尔沃亚建议下，击败塞马科率领的库埃瓦战士后建立圣玛丽亚·拉·安提瓜·德尔·达连。1513年9月1日，巴尔沃亚率190名西班牙人和1000名原住民助战者从这座城镇出发，9月25日望见南海，并在四天后于圣米格尔湾为卡斯蒂利亚宣布占有这片海洋。1519年1月，佩德拉里亚斯·达维瓦在阿克拉处死巴尔沃亚，8月建立巴拿马城，把黄金卡斯蒂利亚的统治中心迁离达连；圣玛丽亚不久被废弃并焚毁。1698年10月30日，威廉·佩特森组织的苏格兰人在金岛附近登陆，与一位当地首领结盟，建立新喀里多尼亚殖民地。热病和饥饿迫使他们在1699年6月撤离。约1300人的第二支远征队在同年11月返回，但在西班牙军队封锁和围攻下，最终于1700年3月28日请求受降。此后，达连雨林仍是西班牙势力与周边原住民反复争夺的边疆。

en:
North of the Guayas the coast becomes a hot, rain-drenched land of mangrove channels and forested capes, watered by the Santiago, Cayapas and Esmeraldas rivers. It had once been the country of the La Tolita goldworkers, whose craft in gold was traded along the Pacific shore, but by the fifteenth century it was held by small and fiercely independent peoples, the Cayapas, Campaces, Malabas and Niguas, whom the highlanders lumped together as Yumbos. No Inca road crossed their forests. In 1444 they lived by fishing, river-borne trade and the washing of gold, answering to no outsider.

Europeans first came on 21 September 1526, when Bartolomé Ruiz de Estrada, Pizarro's pilot, anchored in the bay he named San Mateo; Pizarro returned in 1531. In October 1553 a slaver bound from Panama to Lima was wrecked at Portete, and the Africans who swam ashore built the freest polity the coast had known. From 1555 their leader was Alonso de Illescas, a Cape Verdean who had spent eight years in Seville and spoke Castilian; his people made marriages and alliances among the Niguas and Cayapas and warred on a rival band under Juan Mangache and his son Francisco de Arobe. A royal decree of 8 July 1577 charged Miguel Cabello Balboa with converting them and opening a road from Quito to the Pacific. Arobe and his sons swore vassalage in Quito in 1599 and Illescas's sons in 1600, leaving the two houses as crown-recognized governors, Arobe at San Mateo in the north and the Illescas at Cabo Pasado in the south, where Sebastián de Illescas died as governor in 1607. Off Atacames in July 1594 Beltrán de Castro's galleons captured the English corsair Richard Hawkins and his ship the Dainty. Runaway slaves from the Barbacoas mines swelled the zambo towns after 1640; from 1738 Pedro Vicente Maldonado opened the first mule road over the Andes and founded La Tola, and the gold rushes on the Cayapas and Santiago after 1780 brought a last wave of African-born settlers.
zh:
瓜亚斯以北，海岸变为一片湿热多雨的土地：红树林水道纵横，森林覆盖的海岬伸入太平洋，圣地亚哥河、卡亚帕斯河与埃斯梅拉达斯河在此入海。这里曾是拉托利塔金匠的故土，金器沿太平洋海岸辗转贸易；到15世纪，据有此地的是卡亚帕人、坎帕塞人、马拉瓦人和尼瓜人等小而强悍的族群，高原人笼统称他们为永博人。印加的道路从未伸入这片雨林。1444年时，他们以捕鱼、河上贸易和淘金为生，不臣服于任何外人。

最早的欧洲人于1526年9月21日到来：皮萨罗的领航员巴托洛梅·鲁伊斯·德·埃斯特拉达在一处海湾抛锚，将它命名为圣马特奥；1531年皮萨罗重返此地。1553年10月，一艘从巴拿马驶往利马的奴隶船在波特特失事，游上岸的非洲人建起这片海岸前所未有的自主政权。1555年起，他们的首领是阿隆索·德·伊列斯卡斯——他生于佛得角，在塞维利亚生活过八年，会说西班牙语；部众与尼瓜人、卡亚帕人联姻结盟，又同胡安·曼加切及其子弗朗西斯科·德·阿罗韦率领的另一支黑人势力长期争战。1577年7月8日的王室敕令命米格尔·卡韦略·巴尔沃亚向他们传教，并开辟基多通往太平洋的道路。1599年阿罗韦带两个儿子赴基多宣誓效忠，1600年伊列斯卡斯的儿子们继之，两族由此成为王室承认的地方首领：阿罗韦据北方的圣马特奥，伊列斯卡斯家据南方的卡博帕萨多，家族的塞瓦斯蒂安1607年在总督任上去世。1594年7月，贝尔特兰·德·卡斯特罗的战舰在阿塔卡梅斯近海俘获英国海盗理查德·霍金斯和他的座舰「丹蒂号」。1640年后，从巴尔瓦科阿斯矿场逃出的奴隶不断壮大这些桑博人城镇；1738年起，佩德罗·比森特·马尔多纳多主持修通第一条翻越安第斯山的骡道并建立拉托拉，1780年后卡亚帕斯河与圣地亚哥河的淘金热又带来最后一批非洲出生的移民。

en:
The lower Piura and Chira valleys lie between the Pacific and the Sechura Desert, where seasonal rivers water fields of maize, cotton and fruit while the shore supplies fish and salt. Their Tallán communities lived in parcialidades, farming, fishing and trading by barter with neighbouring valleys; older local traditions are grouped by archaeologists under the Vicús name. By 1444 these northern Peruvian valleys were being drawn into the Chimú world, but Inca armies had not yet reached the Piura coast.

Around 1470 the Inca conquest following the Chimú-Inca war brought Tallán lands under Cuzco, though Quechua ways never fully replaced local customs. Francisco Pizarro found Tumbes unsuitable as a base, moved south to the Chira valley, and on 15 August 1532 founded San Miguel de la Nueva Castilla at the Tallán settlement of Tangarará. The town moved to Piura la Vieja in October 1534 and to Paita around 1578; after Thomas Cavendish raided that port in 1587, the settlers relocated for the last time in 1588, beside the Piura River at Tacalá. Paita then served as the northern sea gateway to the Viceroyalty of Peru, and Piura shipped cordovan leather, cotton, dried meat, tallow, salted shark and salt. On 4 January 1821 Piura proclaimed its independence at the church of San Francisco.
zh:
皮乌拉河与奇拉河下游处在太平洋和塞丘拉沙漠之间，季节性河水浇灌着玉米、棉花和果园，海岸则提供鱼与盐。当地的塔拉人以社群为单位生活，务农、捕鱼，并同邻近河谷以物易物；考古学家把他们更早的地方传统归入维库斯文化。到1444年，秘鲁北部这些河谷正被纳入奇穆世界，但印加军队尚未抵达皮乌拉海岸。

约1470年，奇穆—印加战争后的印加征服把塔拉人的土地置于库斯科统治之下，不过克丘亚习俗并未完全取代本地传统。弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗认为通贝斯不宜作为据点，便南下奇拉河谷，于1532年8月15日在塔拉人的坦加拉拉定居点建立「新卡斯蒂利亚的圣米格尔」。城镇1534年10月迁到旧皮乌拉，约1578年又迁往派塔；1587年托马斯·卡文迪什劫掠派塔后，居民于1588年最后一次迁到皮乌拉河畔的塔卡拉。派塔此后成为秘鲁总督区北方海上门户，皮乌拉输出科尔多瓦皮革、棉花、肉干、油脂、咸鲨鱼肉和盐。1821年1月4日，皮乌拉在圣方济各教堂宣布独立。

en:
Túcume lies in the lower La Leche valley on the Lambayeque plain, around the rocky hill called La Raya or Purgatorio. After Batán Grande burned and was abandoned, the Sican or Lambayeque people built a new administrative and ceremonial centre here between the eleventh and fourteenth centuries: more than 540 acres holding twenty-six major adobe pyramids and mounds. In 1444 Túcume was within the Chimú kingdom, whose rulers enlarged the old Huaca Larga and placed a Chimú-style citadel on its summit.

The site passed to the Incas after the Chimú-Inca war of 1470 and remained in their hands when Spanish invaders reached the north coast in 1532. The old ceremonial centre did not long survive the conquest as a functioning settlement. When Pedro Cieza de León visited in 1547 he already described Túcume as abandoned and ruined, while the surrounding Lambayeque plain kept its canals, fields and the eroded remains of scores of mud-brick huacas.
zh:
图库梅位于兰巴耶克平原的拉莱切河下游，环绕着名为拉亚或炼狱的岩丘。巴坦格兰被焚毁并废弃后，西坎人或称兰巴耶克人在11至14世纪间于此兴建新的行政与礼仪中心：五百四十多英亩范围内分布着二十六座大型土砖金字塔和土墩。1444年的图库梅属于奇穆王国，统治者扩建了古老的长瓦卡，并在其顶部修建奇穆式城寨。

1470年奇穆—印加战争后，图库梅转入印加之手，到1532年西班牙入侵者抵达北海岸时仍由印加控制。这座古老礼仪中心在征服后没有继续作为有效聚落存在太久。佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂1547年到访时，已将图库梅描述为一片废弃废墟；周围的兰巴耶克平原则保留着沟渠、农田和许多风蚀严重的土砖瓦卡。

en:
The eight valleys of the upper Mayo, a warm and rainy cloud-forest country east of the Andes, were the land of the Muyupampas, kin of the Chachapoyas, and their circular plain gave the place its Quechua name, muyu pampa. In 1444 the Incas had not yet entered these forests: the Muyupampas kept to their own valleys, and the river jungle sheltered peoples who refused Inca rule. It was only with the northern wars of Tupac Inca Yupanqui and his son Wayna Capac that an Inca outpost rose on the red-clay plateau.

On 25 July 1540 Juan Perez de Guevara, left behind when Alonso de Alvarado turned back from his jungle expedition, founded Santiago de los Ocho Valles de Moyobamba on that Inca site, the first Spanish town in the Peruvian Amazon. It became the 'metropolis of Maynas', a mustering point on the road to Quito and the base from which Jesuit and Franciscan missionaries pushed into the jungle. An earthquake in 1746 forced the town to be rebuilt four kilometres to the east, and in 1781 Mayoruna raiders massacred its Spanish townsfolk. By royal decree of 15 July 1802 Maynas was made a General Commandancy with Moyobamba its capital. When independence reached the Mayo, Pedro Pascasio Noriega, sent by San Martin himself, was denounced and shot with his fellow plotters in the main square on 11 April 1821; on 19 August 1821 the town proclaimed its independence and joined the republic of Peru.
zh:
上马约河的八条山谷地处安第斯山脉以东，是温暖多雨的云雾林地带，为莫尤潘帕人的土地——他们与查查波亚人同源，其圆形平原赋予此地克丘亚语名字「莫约班巴」（muyu 圆，pampa 平原）。1444年时印加人尚未进入这片丛林：莫尤潘帕人安居在自己的山谷中，河畔丛林还庇护着拒不接受印加统治的部族。直到图帕克·印卡·尤潘基及其子瓦伊纳·卡帕克发动北方战争，红土高地上才建起一座印加前哨。

1540年7月25日，阿隆索·德·阿尔瓦拉多的丛林远征中途折返，留守的胡安·佩雷斯·德·格瓦拉在这座印加旧址上建立「莫约班巴八谷圣雅各镇」，这是西班牙人在秘鲁亚马逊建立的第一座城镇。它后来成为「迈纳斯都会」，是通往基多路上的必经集结地，也是耶稣会与方济各会传教士深入丛林的基地。1746年的地震迫使城镇向东4公里重建；1781年，马约鲁纳人袭击此地，屠杀了西班牙裔市民。1802年7月15日，王家敕令设立迈纳斯总司令部辖区，以莫约班巴为首府。独立运动传到马约河畔时，受圣马丁亲自派遣的佩德罗·帕斯夸西奥·诺列加事泄被捕，1821年4月11日与同谋者一起在主广场被枪决；1821年8月19日，莫约班巴宣布独立，加入秘鲁共和国。

en:
Wankapampa, recorded in Spanish sources as Huancapampa or Huancabamba, lies in a high Andean valley east of Piura and north of Cajamarca, on the river of the same name. Before Inca expansion its people venerated jaguars, farmed the mountains and made textiles in the northern Peruvian highlands. In 1444 the valley remained outside the Inca Empire, ruled by local highland lords and suited by its pastures to llama and alpaca herds.

Around 1480 the forces of Tupac Yupanqui conquered the region, imposed Inca customs, settled mitma colonists and developed Caxas and Huancapampa on the road from Quito to Cusco. In October 1532 Hernando de Soto led sixty Spanish horsemen ahead of Francisco Pizarro: at Caxas he found the great Inca highway, cut-stone buildings, irrigation channels and military storehouses, then passed through Huancapampa, the larger and more populous of the two towns. After the conquest Pizarro placed its people in encomienda under Diego Palomino, and colonial Huancabamba formed part of the Piura corregimiento. In 1821 its alcalde, José de Adrianzén, and the townspeople received news of San Martín's proclamation of Peruvian independence.
zh:
万卡班巴在西班牙文资料中作Huancapampa或Huancabamba（中文通译宛卡班巴），地处皮乌拉以东、卡哈马卡以北的安第斯高山谷地，万卡班巴河穿境而过。印加扩张以前，这里的人崇拜美洲豹，在山地耕作并从事纺织。1444年的谷地仍在印加帝国之外，由当地山地首领统治，牧场适宜放牧美洲驼和羊驼。

约1480年，图帕克·尤潘基的军队征服此地，推行印加习俗，迁入米特马垦殖者，并在基多通往库斯科的大道上建设卡萨斯和万卡班巴。1532年10月，埃尔南多·德·索托率六十名西班牙骑兵为弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗先行侦察；他在卡萨斯见到印加大道、琢石建筑、灌渠和军需仓库，随后经过两地中更大、人口更密的万卡班巴。征服后，皮萨罗把当地居民以监护征赋制交给迭戈·帕洛米诺管辖，殖民时期的万卡班巴隶属皮乌拉辖区。1821年，镇长何塞·德·阿德里安森和居民收到了圣马丁宣布秘鲁独立的消息。

en:
Pisqupampa, recorded in Spanish as Piscobamba, means 'plain of birds' in Quechua and lies in the Conchucos highlands on the eastern side of the Ancash Andes. After Chavín, Recuay and Wari influence declined, independent ethnic lordships took shape there between 1200 and 1480. The Piscopampa themselves were divided among several curacazgos and often fought over mountain land. In 1444 their valleys remained under local chiefs, beyond the reach of the Inca court at Cusco.

Around 1480 the Inca general Capac Yupanqui advanced toward the Yanamayo River in the Chinchaysuyu campaign, but warriors of the Piscopampa, Conchucos and Siguas forced him back toward Yauya; he built the high military tambo of Maraycalle at 4,260 metres before subduing the country. In April 1533 Hernando Pizarro and Miguel de Estete passed through Pisqupampa on their return from sacking Pachacamac and were received by the local curaca Tawani before continuing to Cajamarca. Pedro Cieza de León later described a broad, long stone lodging for lords here and called Conchucos a land rich in gold and silver mines. The Spanish town of San Pedro y San Pablo de Piscobamba was founded in 1574. By 24 November 1594, when Archbishop Toribio de Mogrovejo held his eighth diocesan synod there, it was capital of the Conchucos corregimiento.
zh:
皮斯科班巴的盖丘亚语原名Pisqupampa意为「鸟之平原」，西班牙文写作Piscobamba，地处安卡什山东侧的孔丘科斯高地。查文、雷夸伊和瓦里势力衰落后，1200至1480年间，这一带形成一批独立的族群领地；皮斯科班巴人也分成数个酋邦，常因山地归属交战。1444年，这些谷地仍由当地首领统治，库斯科的印加宫廷尚未控制此地。

约1480年，印加将领卡帕克·尤潘基在钦查苏尤北征中推进到亚纳米约河一带，皮斯科班巴、孔丘科斯和西瓜战士却将他逼退向尧亚；他在海拔4260米处修筑马赖卡列军用驿站，之后才逐步压服此地。1533年4月，埃尔南多·皮萨罗和米格尔·埃斯特特洗劫帕查卡马克后沿印加道路返回，经皮斯科班巴时受到当地酋长塔瓦尼接待，随后继续前往卡哈马卡。佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂后来记述，孔丘科斯一带有富饶的金银矿，皮斯科班巴则有一座又宽又长的石造贵族驿馆。1574年，圣佩德罗与圣巴勃罗·德·皮斯科班巴建立；1594年11月24日，托里比奥·德·莫格罗韦霍在此举行第八次教区会议时，皮斯科班巴已是孔丘科斯辖区的首府。

en:
Chimbote's sheltered waters form Ferrol Bay beside the Lacramarca and Santa river valleys, the coastal corridor linking the desert shore to the Ancash highlands. Moche peoples built the adobe platforms and plazas of Huaca San Pedro between the second and seventh centuries, and Wari and Chimú influence later passed over the same coast. In 1444 the bay lay near the southern edge of the Chimú world, whose ceramics and burials have been found around the future town.

After Chimor's defeat around 1470 the region entered the Inca horizon, although no distinct Inca complex has been identified at Chimbote. Spanish rule after 1532 tied the coast to the nearby villa of Santa María de la Parrilla, but Chimbote itself never received a formal colonial foundation. Its name first appears in an official record in 1774, when Cosme Bueno described it as a small fishing settlement attached to Santa. Thus, at the close of the period in 1821, Chimbote was still a cove serving the Santa valley rather than a properly laid-out town.
zh:
钦博特的隐蔽水域构成费罗尔湾，毗邻拉克拉马卡河与圣塔河谷，是连接沙漠海岸和安卡什高地的沿海通道。莫切人在2至7世纪间修建了圣佩德罗瓦卡的土砖平台与广场，瓦里和奇穆的影响后来也波及这段海岸。1444年，海湾位于奇穆世界南缘附近，未来城区一带已发现奇穆风格陶器和墓葬。

约1470年奇穆战败后，这一地区进入印加势力范围，不过钦博特尚未发现可明确辨认的印加建筑群。1532年后的西班牙统治把海岸划归附近的圣玛丽亚·德拉帕里利亚镇管辖，但钦博特本身在殖民时代并未正式建城。它的名字最早见于1774年的官方记录，科斯梅·布埃诺当时把它描述为隶属圣塔的小渔村。因此到1821年这一时期结束时，钦博特仍是服务圣塔河谷的小港湾，而不是规划成形的城镇。

en:
The Callejón de Huaylas is the long valley of the Santa River, walled between the snows of the Cordillera Blanca and the dark ridge of the Cordillera Negra, and it gave its name to the Huaylas people. Hunters had sheltered in the Guitarrero cave thousands of years before Christ, the Chavín shrine at Pumacayán hallowed the heights above the later town, and in turn the Recuay and Wari cultures ruled the valley before the Huaylas señorío arose there. In 1444 Guaraz, a name meaning 'dawn', was a chief town of that kingdom amid maize fields and llama-rich pastures, and no Inca army had yet entered the valley. A long, cruel war followed: confederated with the Conchucos and other neighbours, the Huaylas held out until the campaigns of Huayna Capac, when they surrendered at a heavy price. The wak'a of Pumacayán was thrown down, their country was made into an Inca province, and its curacas sent their daughters to Cuzco; one of them, Añas Colque, became the mother of the prince Paullu Inca.

In January 1533 Hernando Pizarro passed through Guaraz on the road to Pachacámac and left the first Spanish description of its fertile fields and prosperous villages. The Huaylas soon served the new masters: in August 1536 the lady Contarhuacho sent a great native contingent from the valley to help defend Lima against Manco Inca's siege. In 1538 Francisco Pizarro granted the valley in encomienda to Sebastián de Torres, and silver, lead and tin drew Spanish miners, so that by the 1570s hundreds of Quechua villagers laboured in the mines. On 20 January 1574 Alonso de Santoyo y Valverde gathered the native settlements into the reducción of San Sebastián de Huaraz, with fourteen quarters around the old wak'a, and in 1576 the town became the seat of the corregimiento of Huaylas. An earthquake on 6 January 1725 wrecked its churches, and in February 1780 the town rose in the alcabala tax revolt; from 1784 it belonged to the intendency of Tarma, receiving its own town council in 1789. Late in 1820 Colonel Campino entered with 250 men and proclaimed independence, and in February 1821 San Martín made Huaraz the seat of the new department of Huaylas.
zh:
瓦伊拉斯走廊是圣河冲积出的一条长谷，夹在积雪的布兰卡山脉与黝黑的内格拉山脉之间，瓦伊拉斯人便得名于此。公元前数千年，猎人已在吉他雷罗洞穴栖身；查文文化时期，瓦拉斯上方的普马卡扬圣所香火鼎盛；此后雷夸伊文化、瓦里文化先后主宰这条河谷，最后瓦伊拉斯人的政权在此兴起。1444年时，意为「黎明」的瓜拉斯是这个政权的一座重镇，周围玉米田成片，高山牧场上羊驼成群，印加军队尚未踏入谷地。随后是漫长而残酷的战争：瓦伊拉斯人与孔丘科人等邻邦结盟，一直抵抗到瓦伊纳·卡帕克出征的年代，才付出沉重代价投降。普马卡扬圣所被拆毁，故土被编为印加的一个行省，各族酋长把女儿送往库斯科；其中的阿尼亚斯·科尔克生下了王子保柳·印卡。

1533年1月，埃尔南多·皮萨罗在前往帕查卡马克途中经过瓜拉斯，留下了西班牙人对这片肥沃田野和富庶村落的第一段记述。瓦伊拉斯人很快为新主人效力：1536年8月，女首领孔塔尔瓦乔从谷地派出大批土著队伍，协助抵御曼科·印卡对利马的围攻。1538年，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗把谷地封给塞瓦斯蒂安·德·托雷斯作委托监护地，银、铅、锡矿引来西班牙矿主，到1570年代已有数百名克丘亚村民在矿上劳作。1574年1月20日，阿隆索·德·桑托约·伊·巴尔维德把各土著村落归并为归化镇圣塞瓦斯蒂安·德·瓦拉斯，绕古老圣所设十四个坊区，1576年瓦拉斯成为瓦伊拉斯辖区的治所。1725年1月6日的大地震摧毁了城中教堂；1780年2月，市民因营业税起义；1784年起划归塔尔马监政区，1789年设立市政会。1820年末，坎皮诺上校率二百五十人入城宣布独立；1821年2月，圣马丁把新设的瓦伊拉斯省首府设在瓦拉斯。

en:
The Camaná River opens into a broad, fertile valley on one of Peru's driest coasts, with the Quilca roadstead nearby and smaller desert valleys at Ocoña and Tambo. Chango communities grew maize there and fertilized their fields with seabird dung gathered from offshore islands, while fishing and coastal exchange linked the shore to the valley. They had a reputation as a stubbornly independent people, and Spanish chronicles record that they were subdued only later by Tupac Inca Yupanqui. In 1444 Camaná was therefore not a city but a coastal borderland beyond direct Inca rule, whose food and maritime resources were already known to the highlands.

On 9 November 1539 the Spanish founded Villa Hermosa in the valley, yet in 1540 its cabildo and settlers were moved to the Chili Valley, where that settlement became Arequipa. Camaná retained its importance through nearby Quilca. In 1540 Francisco Camargo landed there with merchandise bound for Charcas, Cuzco and Arequipa, and Quilca became Arequipa's principal colonial seaport. Alonso Martínez de Rivera refounded Camaná on 29 September 1557 as the Villa de San Miguel de Rivera. In 1784 the Crown made Camaná one of the partidos of the new Intendancy of Arequipa. When Lima proclaimed Peruvian independence in 1821, this valley and its port remained under royalist control.
zh:
卡马纳河在秘鲁最干旱的一段海岸上冲出宽阔肥沃的谷地，附近有基尔卡锚地，奥科尼亚和坦博等较小的荒漠谷地也在这一带。昌戈人群体在这里种植玉米，用从近海岛屿采集的海鸟粪肥田；渔业和沿海交换把岸边与谷地连接起来。他们以顽强独立著称，西班牙编年史记载他们直到后来才被图帕克·印卡·尤潘基征服。因此，1444年的卡马纳还不是城市，而是印加直接统治范围之外的一片沿海边地，但其粮食和海产已为高地所知。

1539年11月9日，西班牙人在这片谷地建立美丽镇；1540年，镇市政会和居民被迁往奇利河谷，后来在那里发展成阿雷基帕。卡马纳的重要性仍由附近的基尔卡延续。1540年，弗朗西斯科·卡马戈在此卸下运往查尔卡斯、库斯科和阿雷基帕的货物，基尔卡也成为阿雷基帕殖民时期的主要海港。1557年9月29日，阿隆索·马丁内斯·德·里韦拉第二次建立卡马纳，命名为圣米格尔·德·里韦拉镇。1784年，王室把卡马纳设为新阿雷基帕监督区下辖的一个分区。1821年利马宣布秘鲁独立时，这片谷地和港口仍受保王派控制。

en:
Ayaviri lies on the cold plains northwest of Lake Titicaca, beside the natural corridor carrying the Inca road from Cuzco into the Collao. Pucará, Tiwanaku and later Colla influences passed over these Aymara-speaking pastures. Sarmiento de Gamboa attributed the Inca conquest and resettlement to Pachacutec in 1430, and a temple of the Sun was built above the principal local huaca. In 1444, therefore, Ayaviri was a recently secured Cuzco road station, whose high grasslands and herds supplied traffic moving south from the capital.

Diego de Almagro's Chile expedition passed through Ayaviri in 1534, drawing food and stores from its tambos. Francisco Villacastín became its first encomendero in 1543, and in 1565 its Indian parish was placed under Lampa and the Bishopric of Cuzco; the church of San Francisco was later raised on the old Sun temple's foundations. Reginaldo de Lizárraga called the windy town large and rich in livestock, and encomiendas and estancias developed its herds and carrying trade. As part of Lampa, Ayaviri passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1777 and returned to Peruvian jurisdiction in 1796. Local people joined the highland rising of 1771, welcomed Túpac Amaru II on 6 December 1780, and on 10 March 1815 provided the barracks from which Angulo and Mateo Pumacahua marched to Umachiri.
zh:
阿亚维里位于的的喀喀湖西北的高寒平原，毗邻印加道路从库斯科通往科利亚奥的天然走廊。普卡拉、蒂亚瓦纳科以及后来的科利亚势力都曾影响这片说艾马拉语的牧场。萨缅托·德·甘博把印加的征服与重新安置归于1430年的帕查库特克，当地最重要的瓦卡上方还建起太阳神庙。因此在1444年，阿亚维里是库斯科新近控制的道路驿站，高山草场和畜群为从都城南下的交通提供补给。

迭戈·阿尔马格罗远征智利时于1534年经过阿亚维里，从当地坦博获取粮食和物资。弗朗西斯科·比利亚卡斯廷1543年成为首位监护主，1565年本地印第安教区被划归兰帕和库斯科主教区；圣方济各教堂后来建在古老太阳神庙的基址上。雷希纳尔多·德·利萨拉加称这座多风的城镇规模可观、牲畜富足，监护地和牧场庄园由此发展畜群与驮运贸易。作为兰帕的一部分，阿亚维里1777年划归拉普拉塔总督区，1796年又转回秘鲁管辖。当地居民参与了1771年的高原起义，1780年12月6日迎接图帕克·阿马鲁二世，1815年3月10日又为安古洛和马特奥·普马卡瓦进军乌马奇里提供兵营。

en:
Quero, more often written Q'ero, names a Quechua people and their mountain valleys in Paucartambo rather than a Spanish-style city. Their land climbs from temperate maize slopes below 1,800 metres to puna above 4,500 metres near Ausangate, with potatoes in the high fields, llamas and alpacas on the pastures, and villages sometimes separated by days of mountain trails. In 1444 Quero belonged to Antisuyu, the Inca quarter facing the Amazonian forests, and its weavers worked patterns later recognized as Inca in style.

After the Spanish conquest the Paucartambo Andes remained a remote forest frontier rather than a dense colonial district. A corregimiento was established at Paucartambo in 1565, and trade between the highlands and the lowlands continued in coca, gold and textiles; Quero's wool and woven cloth belonged to that exchange. No Spanish town displaced Jatun Q'ero, and through 1821 its communities kept Quechua speech, reciprocal labour and oral memories of the Inca world.
zh:
克罗（Q'ero）指的不是一座西班牙式城市，而是保卡坦博一带一个克丘亚人群及其山谷家园。他们的土地从海拔1800米以下适合玉米的温暖坡地，抬升到奥桑加特附近海拔4500米以上的普纳草原；高处种马铃薯，牧场放牧美洲驼和羊驼，村落之间有时要走数日山路。1444年的克罗属于面向亚马孙森林的印加安蒂苏尤，织工使用的纹样后来被认为具有印加风格。

西班牙征服后，保卡坦博安第斯山区仍是偏远的森林边疆，而不是人口稠密的殖民核心。1565年，保卡坦博设立长老辖区，高地与低地之间的贸易继续以古柯、黄金和纺织品为大宗；克罗的羊毛和织物也参与这种交换。没有西班牙城镇取代哈通克罗，直到1821年，当地社群仍保留克丘亚语、互助劳动和关于印加世界的口传记忆。

en:
The weathered gates and platforms of Tiahuanaco stand south-east of Lake Titicaca. The city arose around 110, grew into a ritual and political centre from 375 to 700, and collapsed around 1000 as drought weakened its raised fields. Its Akapana pyramid, Kalasasaya enclosure, monoliths and Gate of the Sun remained landmarks for the peoples who came after. When Tiwanaku's power dissolved, Aymara lordships divided the Collao; the Pacajes, whose capital was Caquiaviri near the Desaguadero, held these southern lands. In 1444 their farmers grew potatoes, quinoa and oca and pastured llamas and alpacas around the old stones, while the lords of Caquiaviri still kept Inca armies beyond the frontier.

The Pacajes resisted Inca expansion until the later fifteenth-century campaigns of Tupac Inca Yupanqui, when their territory was incorporated into Qullasuyu. In 1549 Pedro Cieza de León visited and recorded the ruins while searching for the southern capital of Qullasuyu, noting that they belonged to a time older than the Incas. The village of Tiahuanaco became part of Spanish Alto Perú, and in the early seventeenth century its church of San Pedro was built with dressed stone blocks taken from the adjoining ruins. The wars of independence reached the district after the patriot defeat at Huaqui; in 1811 the Pacajes rose with Omasuyos and Larecaja against Spanish rule in the intendancy of La Paz.
zh:
蒂亚瓦纳科风蚀的石门和台地矗立在的的喀喀湖东南。这座城市约110年兴起，375年至700年间成为宗教与政治中心，约1000年因干旱削弱高台式农田而崩溃。阿卡帕纳金字塔、卡拉萨亚围院、巨型石碑和太阳门，仍是后来各族眼中的重要标志。蒂亚瓦纳科政权解体后，艾马拉诸领地分割科亚奥高原；帕卡赫斯人以德萨瓜德罗河附近的卡基亚维里为首府，占据这些南方土地。1444年，他们的农民在古迹周围种植马铃薯、藜麦和奥卡薯，牧养大羊驼与羊驼，卡基亚维里的首领仍把印加军队挡在边外。

帕卡赫斯人持续抵抗印加扩张，直到15世纪后期图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的战役后，其土地才被并入科利亚苏尤。1549年，佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂在寻找科利亚苏尤南部首府时探访并记录了这片遗址，指出它们属于比印加更古老的时代。蒂亚瓦纳科村后来成为西属上秘鲁的一部分；17世纪初，圣佩德罗教堂用取自相邻遗址的琢石块建成。爱国者在瓦基战败后，独立战争波及这一地区：1811年，帕卡赫斯人与奥马苏约斯、拉雷卡哈一同起义，反抗拉巴斯监督管区的西班牙统治。

en:
San Joaquín and its later administrative centre Exaltación anchor the wet north-eastern edge of the Moxos plains, between the Mamoré and the Itenéz, the river also called the Guaporé. In 1444 its seasonally flooded savannas, riverine forests and lakes belonged to no empire. Cayubaba villages held the country near the Mamoré, while Baure communities lived toward the San Martín and Baures rivers; both belonged to the broad Maipurean, or Arawakan, linguistic world. Their people planted manioc and maize on raised ground, hunted, fished and travelled by canoe, moving with the annual rhythm of high and low water.

The Jesuit Cipriano Barace made contact with the Baure around 1690. Agustín Zapata entered Cayubaba country in 1693 and found seven substantial villages, six with about 1,800 people and one with more than 2,000. Antonio Garriga gathered the Cayubaba into the Exaltación de la Santa Cruz mission in 1704, while Antonio de Orellana and Pedro de Rado founded San Joaquín among the Baure on 21 August 1708. The missions introduced cattle, writing and church music, organized weavers and craftsmen around central plazas, and sent cotton, cacao, rice, sugar and wax to Andean markets. Portuguese bandeirantes nevertheless crossed the rivers to seize slaves, and floods and epidemics repeatedly forced villages to move. By 1740 the Baure reductions held some 16,000 people, but after the Jesuit expulsion reached Moxos in 1768 the missions declined; late in the century the local leader Gabriel Ojeari moved San Joaquín toward the Machupo River.
zh:
圣华金及其后来的行政中心Exaltación，位于莫克索斯平原湿润的东北缘，地处马莫雷河与伊特内斯河（又称瓜波雷河）之间。1444年，这里季节性泛滥的草原、河岸林和湖泊不属于任何帝国。Cayubaba人的村落占据马莫雷河附近地带，Baure人则生活在圣马丁河与包雷斯河方向；两者都属于广义的马伊普雷（阿拉瓦克）语群。人们在高地种植木薯和玉米，狩猎捕鱼，乘独木舟往来，并随每年涨水、退水的节奏迁移。

耶稣会士西普里亚诺·巴拉塞约在1690年与Baure人接触。1693年，阿古斯丁·萨帕塔进入Cayubaba人的地方，看到七个人口众多的村落：六个约有一千八百人，另一个超过两千人。1704年，安东尼奥·加里加把Cayubaba人聚集到Exaltación de la Santa Cruz传教站；1708年8月21日，安东尼奥·德·奥雷利亚纳和佩德罗·德拉多在Baure人中建立圣华金。传教站引入牛群、文字和教堂音乐，把织工与工匠组织在中央广场周围，并把棉花、可可、稻米、糖和蜡运往安第斯市场。尽管如此，葡萄牙旗队仍渡过河流掳人为奴，洪水和疫病也一再迫使村落迁徙。到1740年，Baure人的归化村镇约有一万六千人；但1768年驱逐耶稣会的命令抵达莫克索斯后，传教区走向衰落。18世纪末，本地首领加夫列尔·奥赫阿里把圣华金迁往马丘波河方向。

en:
The Madre de Dios carries the rains of the sub-Andean forests eastward to the Beni and ultimately the Madeira and Amazon. In 1444 its banks and tributaries were an indigenous river world below the Apolobamba and Paucartambo ranges. Arawak-speaking Yine, also called Piro, lived along stretches of the Madre de Dios, Urubamba and Las Piedras, while Tacana communities were scattered along the Beni, Madre de Dios and Orthon; Araona groups held forest paths nearer the Andean approaches. Inca influence reached the upper foothills, where the Spanish later heard of the Chunchos frontier, chiefly through gifts and diplomacy rather than permanent garrisons. The river itself, rather than a highland road, joined villages, fishing camps and garden clearings.

Spanish expeditions first tested this frontier through the Pelechuco and Charazani valleys. In June 1615 Pedro de Legui Urquiza left Larecaja with 165 men and three Augustinians, and on 10 August founded Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, the nucleus of Apolo, but the post served mainly as a foothold on the mountain edge. Augustinians attempted a mission among Leco speakers on the Mapiri in 1618. In 1680 the Franciscans Bartolomé Zumeta, Francisco Corso, Andrés de Castro and Pedro de la Peña entered Araona country and founded Santa Bárbara; between 1680 and 1721 Franciscan outstations extended through Ixiamas toward the Madidi and Madre de Dios. Repeated flight of neophytes and the abandonment of stations weakened the chain, so that when the wars of independence began many river communities still lived beyond effective Spanish control.
zh:
马德雷德迪奥斯河把安第斯山麓森林的雨水向东带入贝尼河，最终汇入马代拉河与亚马孙河。1444年，它的干流和支流是阿波洛班巴岭、保卡坦博岭下方的原住民河居世界。操阿拉瓦克语的Yine人（又称Piro人）生活在马德雷德迪奥斯河、乌鲁班巴河和彼德拉斯河沿岸，Tacana人的社群则散布在贝尼河、马德雷德迪奥斯河和奥尔顿河一带；Araona人占据着更靠近安第斯入口的林间通路。印加影响主要通过馈赠和外交抵达上游山麓，即西班牙人后来所称的琼乔斯边疆，而没有长期驻军。把村落、渔营和农地连接起来的不是高地道路，而是河流本身。

西班牙远征队最初从佩莱丘科和查拉萨尼山谷试探这片边疆。1615年6月，佩德罗·德·莱吉·乌尔基萨率领165人和三名奥斯定会士离开拉雷卡哈，于8月10日建立瓜达卢佩圣母镇，即Apolo的雏形，但这个据点主要只是山麓边缘的立足点。1618年，奥斯定会士试图在马皮里河的Leco语族群中建立传教站。1680年，方济各会士巴托洛梅·苏梅塔、弗朗西斯科·科尔索、安德烈斯·德·卡斯特罗和佩德罗·德拉佩尼亚进入Araona人的土地，建立圣巴巴拉；1680年至1721年间，方济各传教点经Ixiamas一直延伸到马迪迪河与马德雷德迪奥斯河方向。新信徒不断逃离，一些传教站也遭废弃，削弱了这条传教链；因此独立战争开始时，许多河边社群仍生活在西班牙实际控制之外。

en:
Santa Cruz de la Sierra is the eastern-Bolivian lowland around the Piraí and Guapay rivers. Before the town existed, Arawak-speaking Chané villagers cultivated the Grigotá plains, a name taken from the title of their leaders, and left pottery and weapons in the country between the Andean foothills, the Chaco and the Amazon. In 1444 the plains lay far beyond Inca and Spanish power; older Chané settlements still controlled the routes, though Guaraní-speaking bands from the southeast would invade the region in the following century.

Domingo Martínez de Irala explored the region in 1549. On 26 February 1561 Ñuflo de Chaves, marching from Asunción with 158 soldiers, founded Santa Cruz de la Sierra at Santa Cruz la Vieja and named it after his Extremaduran home town. Chaves was killed in Itatín in 1568. Warfare forced moves in 1590 and 1595: San Lorenzo el Real de la Frontera arose on the Guapay while the older Santa Cruz population shifted by stages toward the Piraí, and the two towns were merged on 9 November 1621. The small frontier captaincy later supplied Jesuit expeditions to Chiquitos and Moxos, helped repel Portuguese bandeirantes, lived mainly from agriculture and kept broad autonomy without the mining mita. Bourbon reforms moved much provincial administration toward Cochabamba. On 24 September 1810 Antonio Vicente Seoane led Santa Cruz's first junta; royalists returned in 1813, and the campaigns around Ignacio Warnes kept the frontier at war until 1821.
zh:
圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉位于玻利维亚东部低地，皮赖河与瓜佩河流经这片地区。城市出现以前，讲阿拉瓦克语的查内村人在格里戈塔平原耕作，格里戈塔原是他们首领的称号；在安第斯山麓、大查科与亚马孙之间的土地上，留有他们的陶器和武器。1444年，这片平原还远在印加和西班牙势力之外，古老的查内聚落仍控制着通路；不过到下个世纪，东南方讲瓜拉尼语的群体便将攻入这一地区。

1549年，多明戈·马丁内斯·德·伊拉拉探查了此地。1561年2月26日，纽夫洛·德·查维斯率一百五十八名士兵从亚松森远征而来，在圣克鲁斯拉维耶哈建立圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉，并以他在埃斯特雷马杜拉的故乡命名。1568年，查维斯在伊塔廷遇害。战乱迫使居民在1590年和1595年迁徙：瓜佩河畔建起圣洛伦索埃尔雷亚尔德拉弗龙特拉，旧圣克鲁斯人口也分批迁往皮赖河方向，两座城镇最终于1621年11月9日合并。这个小小的边疆都督辖区后来为前往奇基托斯和莫霍斯的耶稣会远征队提供基地，协助抵御葡萄牙旗兵，以农业为生，并享有广泛自治，不实行矿区的米塔制。波旁改革把许多省级行政事务移往科恰班巴。1810年9月24日，安东尼奥·维森特·塞奥内领导圣克鲁斯建立第一个洪达；保王军1813年卷土重来，伊格纳西奥·瓦尔内斯等人的战事使这条边疆一直交战到1821年。

en:
Sucre's high valley, set between the Churuquella and Sica Sica hills at nearly 2,800 metres, was the country of the Charcas, a warlike Aymara-speaking people whose hamlet of Choquechaca stood on the city's future site. In 1444 Inca power had not yet reached these southern valleys: the Charcas kept their own lords and fields and fought off Guarani-speaking Chiriguano raiders from the eastern lowlands. Before the century was out Tupac Inca Yupanqui's armies swept the land into the Inca quarter of Collasuyo as the province of Charca, with the town of Chuquisaca its capital and Quechua imposed alongside Aymara.

The Portuguese Aleixo Garcia, the first European known to cross the continent, passed this way in 1525. Gonzalo Pizarro's men came in the late 1530s and learned of the silver of Porco, and on 16 April 1540 Pedro Anzures founded the Villa de la Plata. The discovery of the silver mountain of Potosi nearby in 1545 made La Plata the judicial capital of the richest mining country on earth: a bishopric from 1552, the seat of the Royal Audiencia of Charcas from 1559, an archbishopric in 1609, and from 1624 the home of St Francis Xavier University, one of the first in the Americas, in a city of some 14,000 people by 1639. In 1776 the Audiencia passed from the Viceroyalty of Peru to the new Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata, and the Carolina Academy, founded the same year, trained the lawyers who on 25 May 1809 deposed the Audiencia's president and set up the first autonomous junta of the Spanish-American wars of independence. Royalist troops from Peru retook the city before the year ended; in the long war that followed La Plata was occupied again and again, its deputies signed independence at Tucuman in 1816, and patriot guerrillas led by Juana Azurduy kept fighting in the hills as the war entered 1821.
zh:
苏克雷所在的高谷坐落在丘鲁克利亚山与西卡西卡山之间，海拔近2800米，本是查尔卡人的故土——这个善射好战的艾马拉语族群在今日城址上建有乔克查卡村。1444年时印加的势力尚未进入这些南方河谷：查尔卡人仍保有自己的酋长和田地，抵御着东部低地讲瓜拉尼语的奇里瓜诺人袭扰。15世纪末，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的大军征服此地，将其并入印加帝国的科利亚苏尤大区，设为查尔卡省，以丘基萨卡为首府，并在艾马拉语之外推行克丘亚语。

已知最早横穿南美大陆的欧洲人、葡萄牙人阿莱霍·加西亚于1525年经过此地。1530年代末，贡萨洛·皮萨罗的部下来到这里，得知波尔科产银；1540年4月16日，佩德罗·安苏雷斯正式建立拉普拉塔镇。1545年附近的波托西银山被发现后，拉普拉塔成为这片世界最富庶银矿区的司法与行政中心：1552年设主教区，1559年成为查尔卡斯皇家检审庭所在地，1609年升为大主教区，1624年又创办新大陆最早的大学之一圣弗朗西斯科·哈维尔大学，到1639年城中已有约1.4万人。1776年，检审庭由秘鲁总督辖区划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区；同年成立的卡罗琳娜学院培养出一批法学家，他们于1809年5月25日罢免检审庭庭长，建立西属美洲独立战争中的第一个自治政权。秘鲁派来的保王军在年底前重新占领城市，此后的战争中拉普拉塔反复易手；1816年，当地代表在图库曼签署独立宣言，而胡安娜·阿苏尔杜伊率领的爱国游击队仍在山间坚持战斗，战争一直延续到1821年。

en:
In 1444 the fertile lowlands and Aconquija foothills that would become Tucumán were a meeting ground rather than a single native polity. Pazioca or Diaguita groups in the western valleys, Calchaquí, Quilmes and Tolombón among them, farmed terraces of maize, potatoes and quinoa, wove, made pottery and kept llamas, while Lule, Vilela and Tonocote communities occupied the central and eastern lands. Inca forces only reached the Aconquija frontier around 1480, so no Inca governor yet ruled these valleys.

Diego de Rojas crossed the region in 1543, but the lasting Spanish foundation came on 31 May 1565, when Diego de Villarroel established San Miguel de Tucumán at Ibatín for the new Governorate of Tucumán, Juríes and Diaguitas. Calchaquí warriors under the cacique Gualán nearly destroyed the town in October 1578, and recurrent raids helped persuade officials to move it. On 29 September 1685 Miguel de Salas y Valdez relocated San Miguel beside the Salí River at La Toma, nearer the highway linking Peru with the Río de la Plata. The town supplied cattle, textiles and timber to convoys carrying Andean silver toward Buenos Aires until the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata was created in 1776; in 1783 Tucumán was placed under the Intendancy of Salta. On 24 September 1812 Manuel Belgrano defeated a royalist army outside the town, and on 9 July 1816 the Congress of Tucumán declared independence. Governor Bernabé Aráoz proclaimed the short-lived Federal Republic of Tucumán on 22 March 1820, only for Catamarca and Santiago del Estero to withdraw the following year.
zh:
1444年，后来成为图库曼的肥沃低地与阿孔基哈山麓并非一个统一政体，而是多片人群交会之地。西部谷地的帕西奥卡人（即迪亚吉塔人，包括卡尔查基、基尔梅斯和托隆邦等支派）在梯田种植玉米、马铃薯和藜麦，纺织制陶并牧养大羊驼；卢莱人、比莱拉人和托诺科特人则居在中部和东部。印加军队约1480年才抵达阿孔基哈边界，因此此时还没有印加总督统治这些谷地。

1543年，迭戈·德·罗哈斯穿过这里；持久的西班牙建城要到1565年5月31日，迭戈·德·比利亚罗埃尔在伊瓦廷为新设的图库曼—胡里—迪亚吉塔督辖区建立圣米格尔-德图库曼。1578年10月，酋长瓜兰率领卡尔查基战士几乎摧毁此城，持续袭掠也是后来官员迁城的原因之一。1685年9月29日，米格尔·德·萨拉斯-巴尔德斯把圣米格尔迁至萨利河畔的拉托马，更靠近连接秘鲁与拉普拉塔的王道。新城向运送安第斯白银前往布宜诺斯艾利斯的车队供应牛、纺织品和木材，直到1776年拉普拉塔总督辖区成立；1783年，图库曼被置于萨尔塔监政区下。1812年9月24日，曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺在城外击败保王军；1816年7月9日，图库曼议会宣布独立。1820年3月22日，省长贝尔纳韦·阿劳斯宣布成立短暂的图库曼联邦共和国，次年卡塔马卡和圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗脱离，实验随之瓦解。

en:
Santa Catalina is the cold heart of the Jujuy puna, a treeless altiplano nearly 4,000 metres high between the Quebrada de Humahuaca and the Bolivian plateau, where Atacameno-Lipe herders and Diaguita-speaking Omaguaca clans pastured llamas and washed gold from the mountain streams. Their stubborn resistance long barred the Inca armies, and only around 1470 did Quechua and Aymara forces bring the puna into the Inca world. In 1444 the high valleys still answered to their own chiefs.

Diego de Almagro crossed this frozen plain in 1536 on his march to Chile. The first Spanish towns planted below it, Nieva in 1561 and San Francisco de Alava in 1575, were both destroyed by the Omaguacas, and the Calchaqui wars kept the frontier aflame: in 1594 Viltipoco, chief of the Purmamarcas, led thousands of warriors against Jujuy, the very town that Francisco de Arganaraz y Murguia had founded at the mouth of the quebrada on 19 April 1593 to close the ring on the rebels. Up on the puna, Santa Catalina grew around its gold-bearing river and its llama herds, and a parish church was raised there in the seventeenth century. From 1783 the district formed part of the intendancy of Salta del Tucuman. During the independence wars its high road carried royalist armies down from Upper Peru while the gaucho bands of Martin Miguel de Guemes harried them; the Guerra Gaucha was still being fought when Guemes fell on 17 June 1821.
zh:
圣卡塔利娜是胡胡伊普纳高原的寒冷腹地，这片不生树木的高地海拔近4000米，处在乌马瓦卡峡谷与玻利维亚高原之间，阿塔卡梅诺—利佩族牧人与讲迪亚吉塔语的奥马瓜卡氏族在此放牧美洲驼、从山溪中淘洗金砂。他们的顽强抵抗长期阻挡印加军队，直到1470年前后，克丘亚与艾马拉联军才把高原纳入印加世界。1444年时，这些高山谷地仍归本地酋长管辖。

1536年，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗在进军智利途中穿过这片冰封高原。此后西班牙人在高原下方建立的最早两座城镇——1561年的涅瓦和1575年的阿拉瓦圣弗朗西斯科——都被奥马瓜卡人摧毁，卡尔查基战争使边境长年燃烧：1594年，普尔马马尔卡人首领比尔蒂波科率数千战士攻打胡胡伊；这座城正是弗朗西斯科·德·阿尔加尼亚拉斯·伊·穆尔吉亚于1593年4月19日在峡谷口建立的圣萨尔瓦多德贝拉斯科，本意就是收紧对起义者的包围。高原之上，圣卡塔利娜围绕产金的河流与美洲驼群发展起来，17世纪又建起教区教堂。1783年起，这一地区隶属萨尔塔-德尔图库曼行政区。独立战争期间，取道高原的大道上既有从上秘鲁南下的保王军，也有马丁·米格尔·德·格梅斯的高乔游骑不断袭扰；1821年6月17日格梅斯战死时，这场「高乔战争」仍未平息。

en:
The warm valley of Tarija, watered by the Guadalquivir between the high Andes and the eastern jungles, was the land of the Churumatas, with the Moyos Moyos people to their north. In 1444 it lay beyond the Inca frontier: Tupac Inca Yupanqui's Collasuyu wars of the 1470s broke the Churumatas, deported many as mitma garrison-settlers to Chile and Argentina, and planted colonies of mitimaes such as the Tomatas, brought from the Norte Chico of Chile, in their stead. When Spaniards first saw the valley it was largely depopulated, its hills crossed only by old stone roads.

Pedro de Candia's expedition of 200 men camped here from September 1539 to February 1540, but permanent conquest waited on Viceroy Toledo's frontier war against the Chiriguanos. On 4 July 1574 the Sevillian captain Luis de Fuentes y Vargas, on Toledo's orders, founded the Villa de San Bernardo de la Frontera de Tarija and moved Tomata families from the San Juan del Oro valley to till its lands. The mild climate favoured wheat, olives and vines, and Franciscan vineyards made the district a supplier of wine and singani brandy to the mining cities of Charcas through the seventeenth century. In 1807 Tarija was attached to the intendancy of Salta, and from 1809 patriots and royalists fought bitterly over the frontier town. On 14 April 1817 Gregorio Araoz de Lamadrid's United Provinces troops defeated the royalists at the battle of Tarija, yet the district changed hands more than once before the wars drew to a close in 1821.
zh:
塔里哈所在的温暖谷地位于高耸的安第斯山脉与东部丛林之间，瓜达尔基维尔河穿流其间，本是楚鲁马塔人的土地，莫约斯莫约斯人住在他们以北。1444年时这里还在印加边界之外：1470年代图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的科利亚苏尤战争击垮楚鲁马塔人，把许多人作为米特马克屯戍者迁往智利和阿根廷，又从智利的北奇科迁来托马塔人等米特马克移民填补空地。等西班牙人见到谷地时，这里已大半荒芜，山丘间只剩古老的石砌道路交错。

佩德罗·德·坎迪亚率领200人的探险队曾于1539年9月至1540年2月在此驻扎，但永久征服要等到托莱多总督对奇里瓜诺人的边境战争。1574年7月4日，塞维利亚籍统领路易斯·德·富恩特斯·伊·巴尔加斯奉托莱多之命建立「塔里哈边境圣贝尔纳多镇」，并从圣胡安德尔奥罗谷地迁来托马塔人家族耕种土地。温和的气候宜于小麦、油橄榄和葡萄，方济各会的葡萄园使这一带在17世纪成为向查尔卡斯各矿业城镇供应葡萄酒和辛加尼白兰地的地方。1807年塔里哈划归萨尔塔行政区；1809年起爱国者与保王派激烈争夺这座边镇，1817年4月14日，格雷戈里奥·阿劳斯·德·拉马德里率领拉普拉塔联合省的军队在塔里哈战役中击败保王军，但直到1821年战争末期，这一地区仍不止一次易手。

en:
The Puna de Atacama is a cold, arid Andean plateau of salt flats, volcanic ridges and sheltered quebradas. Atacameño, or Likanantay, communities herded camelids and watered small fields in the valleys. Early in the fifteenth century Topa Inca Yupanqui brought the region into the Inca Collasuyu, and Catarpe, five kilometres north of San Pedro de Atacama, became its most important Inca administrative centre in what is now Chile. From there officials directed Quitor and other fortified pukaras, while Inca roads linked the Salar de Atacama with north-western Argentina. In 1444 the plateau stood on the southern edge of Tawantinsuyu, its people living under Inca lords amid older local cults and the introduced sun cult.

The first Spanish conquistadors under Diego de Almagro reached Atacama in 1536, but armed resistance continued until a peace settlement in 1557. Colonial rule then imposed the encomienda, moved indigenous families into supervised pueblos de indios and pressed Catholic baptism, while the Kunza language lost ground. In the eighteenth century the Atacameño leader Tomás Paniri carried the region's grievances into the great Andean uprisings associated with Túpac Amaru II and Túpac Katari. For Spanish authorities the high, thinly peopled despoblado remained above all a difficult corridor between the mines and valleys of the southern viceroyalties.
zh:
阿塔卡马高原是安第斯山中寒冷干旱的高地，遍布盐沼、火山脊和有遮蔽的峡谷。阿塔卡马人（Likanantay）在谷地放牧骆驼科牲畜，并引水浇灌小片田地。15世纪初，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基把这里并入印加的科利亚苏尤；位于圣佩德罗德阿塔卡马以北5公里的Catarpe，成为印加在今智利境内最重要的行政中心。官吏由此统辖基托尔等堡寨，印加道路也把阿塔卡马盐沼与阿根廷西北部连接起来。1444年，这片高原位于印加帝国南缘，居民在印加贵族统治下生活，本地旧信仰与传入的太阳崇拜并存。

1536年，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗率领的第一批西班牙征服者到达阿塔卡马，但当地武装抵抗一直持续到1557年达成和议。殖民统治随后推行委托监护制，把原住民家庭迁入受监管的印第安人村镇，强迫接受天主教洗礼，昆萨语也逐渐衰微。18世纪，阿塔卡马人首领托马斯·帕尼里把当地怨愤带入图帕克·阿马鲁二世和图帕克·卡塔里领导的大安第斯起义。对西班牙当局而言，这片高旷、人烟稀少的荒野始终更像是南方各总督辖区矿场与河谷之间一条艰险通道。

en:
Calama is the oasis where the Loa River breaks the driest stretch of the Atacama Desert; its Kunza name is commonly explained as a town amid the waters. In 1444 Lickan-antay farmers used the wet meadows for maize and alfalfa, worked copper, and kept llamas at the crossing of coastal, altiplano and Argentine valley routes. Dried fish moved inland from Cobija while highland goods came down toward the Pacific, making the oasis a shelter between Tiwanaku's old network and the approaching Inca frontier.

Around the middle of the fifteenth century the Incas incorporated Atacama into Collasuyu and made Calama the principal tambo of the Despoblado, supplying chasquis and troops with maize, alfalfa and tempered copper weapons; natives later gave Diego de Almagro's returning party copper horseshoes made with that technique. Spanish settlement remained thin in the brutal desert, but the Corregimiento of Atacama claimed the routes for the Royal Audiencia of Charcas, linking Cobija with Potosí, Salta and Tucumán. During the rising of Túpac Amaru II, Tomás Panire led the local movement and was executed. In 1793 Andrés Baleato's map still placed Calama under the Copiapó jurisdiction of the Captaincy General of Chile, an indication of how vaguely the desert frontier was ruled.
zh:
卡拉马是洛阿河在阿塔卡马沙漠最干旱地带切出的绿洲；其孔萨语地名通常被解释为「水中央的城镇」。1444年，利坎安塔伊农人在湿地上种植玉米和苜蓿、冶炼铜器、牧养羊驼。这里正处在海岸、高原与阿根廷谷地道路的交会处：鱼干从科维哈运往内陆，高原货物则顺路通向太平洋，使这座绿洲成为旧蒂亚瓦纳科贸易网络与日益逼近的印加边疆之间的歇脚地。

15世纪中叶前后，印加把阿塔卡马并入科利亚苏约，并将卡拉马设为阿塔卡马无人区最重要的坦博驿站，为查斯基信使和军队提供玉米、苜蓿以及韧铜兵器；后来迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的队伍返程经过时，当地人还送给他们用这种工艺制成的铜马掌。恶劣气候使西班牙人始终未能大规模定居，但阿塔卡马辖区代表查尔卡斯王家检审院控制这些道路，把科维哈同波托西、萨尔塔和图库曼连接起来。图帕克·阿马鲁二世起义时，托马斯·帕尼雷领导当地起事，最终被处死。1793年，安德烈斯·巴莱阿托的地图仍把卡拉马划入智利都督府的科皮亚波辖区，足见这条沙漠边疆的治理界限何等模糊。

en:
The Antofagasta coast is one of the driest faces of the Atacama Desert, broken only by fog-watered lomas and rare springs reaching the sea. In 1444 its inhabitants were Chango fishing families, for whom Paposo, Cobija, Tocopilla and Taltal were principal camps on a shore otherwise without towns. They drew fresh water from the ravines, fished the cold Pacific, and exchanged their catch across the desert with the Lickan-antay oases. The future town and bay of Antofagasta was still empty desert, and the Inca expansion that reached Atacama around mid-century touched the inland roads more firmly than this coast.

On 4 July 1674 Francisco de Cisternas y de la Fuente Villalobos, corregidor of Copiapó, received the Paposo grant and turned the watered bay into cattle pasture; from 1679 the settlement was called Nuestra Señora del Paposo under the Copiapó jurisdiction. During Ambrosio O'Higgins's governorship Copiapó militia were posted there against English privateers, and in 1789 Gregorio Almendáriz replaced the local deputy José Zuleta after abuses against the Changos. An expedition under José Joaquín Pinto y Cobos reached Junquillar in December 1793, counted 142 people between Pan de Azúcar and Agua Salada, and planned a town, parish and school, but lack of funds postponed the project. Governor Gabriel de Avilés authorized a chapel in 1797. A royal order of 1803, confirmed in 1805, transferred Paposo toward the Viceroyalty of Peru, yet the Chilean census of 1813 still listed its port district within Copiapó with 570 inhabitants.
zh:
安托法加斯塔海岸是阿塔卡马沙漠最干旱的坡面之一，只有靠雾水滋养的洛马斯草地和极少数抵达海边的泉水能打破荒凉。1444年住在这里的是昌戈渔民家庭；帕波索、科维哈、托科皮利亚和塔尔塔尔是他们在这条几无城镇的海岸上的主要营地。他们从沟谷汲取淡水，在寒冷的太平洋捕鱼，再穿过沙漠，同利坎安塔伊人的绿洲交换渔获。未来的安托法加斯塔城和海湾仍是空旷荒漠；15世纪中叶前后抵达阿塔卡马的印加扩张，更多改变的是内陆道路，而不是这条海岸。

1674年7月4日，科皮亚波辖区长官弗朗西斯科·德·西斯特纳斯·伊·德拉富恩特·比利亚洛沃斯获得帕波索封地，把这片有水的海湾辟为牧牛地；从1679年起，该地以「帕波索圣母」之名归科皮亚波管辖。安布罗西奥·奥希金斯任都督期间，科皮亚波民兵驻守此地，防范在阿塔卡马海岸出没的英国私掠者；1789年，地方代表何塞·苏莱塔因虐待昌戈人被格雷戈里奥·阿尔门达里斯接替。1793年12月，何塞·华金·平托·伊·科沃斯率队抵达洪基亚尔，在潘德阿苏卡尔至阿瓜萨拉达之间清点出142人，并计划设立城镇、堂区和学校，但因经费不足作罢。1797年，都督加夫列尔·德·阿维莱斯批准修建小堂。1803年的王室命令于1805年获确认，要把帕波索划归秘鲁总督辖区，但1813年智利人口普查仍把这个港区列入科皮亚波，记有570名居民。

en:
The wooded flats and seasonal floodlands of the Dulce River were held in 1444 chiefly by Tonocote communities, whom the first Spaniards called Juríes. They farmed the low ground watered by the river, wove, and made elaborate pottery and carved stonework; Lule peoples lived to the north and west, Vilela and Mocoví groups to the east, and Sanavirones to the south. Neither Inca rule nor Quechua had yet reached the place, and the river valley was a native crossroads opening toward the Chaco.

Diego de Rojas entered the Tucumán lands in 1542, but Spanish settlement began with Juan Núñez de Prado's El Barco in 1550. After two forced moves, its third site stood near the Dulce by 1552; Francisco de Aguirre then displaced Prado's settlers and on 25 July 1553 founded Santiago del Estero, the oldest town still surviving in Argentina.
