From 1564 it was the first capital of the Governorate of Tucumán, Juríes and Diaguitas, and expeditions sent from here founded San Miguel de Tucumán in 1565, Córdoba in 1573, Salta in 1582 and La Rioja in 1591. Its bishopric and government later moved away, and the silver road through Tucumán reduced the old mother city's importance. In 1776 Santiago passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata and in 1783 to the Intendency of Salta. It supported the 1810 May Revolution, suffered a damaging earthquake in 1817, and on 27 April 1820 proclaimed provincial autonomy under the autonomist leader Juan Felipe Ibarra.
zh:
1444年，杜尔塞河林木覆盖的平原与季节洪泛地主要属于托诺科特人，最早的西班牙人把他们称作胡里人。他们在河水浸润的低地耕作、纺织，并制作精美的陶器和石雕；卢莱人居在北方和西方，比莱拉人与莫科维人在东方，萨纳维龙人在南方。此时印加统治和克丘亚语都还未到达，河谷是通向查科的原住民交会之地。

1542年，迭戈·德·罗哈斯进入图库曼地区；西班牙人的定居则始于胡安·努涅斯·德·普拉多1550年建立的巴尔科。经过两次被迫迁移，第三个城址到1552年已位于杜尔塞附近。随后弗朗西斯科·德·阿吉雷排挤普拉多的移民，于1553年7月25日建立圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗，这是阿根廷现存最古老的城市。1564年起，它成为图库曼—胡里—迪亚吉塔督辖区的第一个首府；从这里出发的远征队于1565年建立圣米格尔-德图库曼，1573年建立科尔多瓦，1582年建立萨尔塔，1591年建立拉里奥哈。主教座堂和统治机构后来迁走，经过图库曼的白银道路也削弱了这座诸城之母的重要性。1776年，圣地亚哥划入拉普拉塔总督辖区，1783年又隶属萨尔塔监政区。它支持1810年五月革命，1817年遭严重地震破坏，1820年4月27日在自治派领袖胡安·费利佩·伊瓦拉力主下宣布省自治。

en:
La Rioja lies in a chain of arid Andean ranges, where irrigated valleys break the dry uplands. In 1444 its streams and passes were held by Diaguita, Capayan and Olongasta communities rather than by any European town; their scattered settlements linked the high country toward Chile with the plains that ran toward Córdoba.

Juan Ramírez de Velasco founded the City of All Saints of New Rioja on 20 May 1591 as a strategic Tucumán frontier seat, laying out a cabildo and grants for his soldiers while religious orders and encomiendas took root. Diaguita resistance nearly destroyed the new town in 1593, and a further rising in 1630 was crushed by Governor Felipe de Albornoz. After 1776 La Rioja passed from Peruvian administration into the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, and in 1783 it was attached to the intendancy of Córdoba. Its cabildo supported the May Revolution of 1810; amid the collapse of royal and porteño authority, Francisco Ortiz de Ocampo became its first provincial governor in 1820.
zh:
拉里奥哈位于一列干旱的安第斯山脉之间，灌溉河谷穿插在干燥高地之中。1444年，这里的溪流与山口掌握在迪亚吉塔人、卡帕扬人和奥隆加斯塔人社群手中，还没有欧洲人的城镇；他们分散的聚落把通向智利的高地与通往科尔多瓦的平原连接起来。

1591年5月20日，胡安·拉米雷斯·德·贝拉斯科建立「新拉里奥哈诸圣城」，把它作为图库曼边境的战略据点，为随军士兵划分市政会、城址和份地，修会与委托监护制也随之落地。1593年，迪亚吉塔人的抵抗几乎摧毁新城；1630年的又一次起义被省长费利佩·德·阿尔沃诺斯镇压。1776年后，拉里奥哈从秘鲁辖区转入拉普拉塔总督辖区，1783年划归科尔多瓦监督区。当地市政会支持1810年五月革命；在殖民权威与布宜诺斯艾利斯中央权威相继瓦解之际，弗朗西斯科·奥尔蒂斯·德·奥坎波于1820年成为首任省长。

en:
Chepes lies on the semi-arid southern plains of La Rioja, beneath the Sierra de los Llanos. In 1444 this was a frontier of Andean indigenous worlds: Diaguita groups used the northern Riojan valleys, while Huarpe villages and pasture grounds extended through the plains toward San Juan and San Luis.

The place appears in colonial records through Antonio Reynoso Tello's will made at Tama in 1754, which describes Nuestra Señora de la Limpia Concepción de Chepes as land held under a Tucumán grant. Reynoso Tello built a house and church there, planted vines and stocked cattle, giving the villa its ranching character. During the collapse of Spanish authority after 1810, these southern plains became recruiting ground for llanero militias; Juan Facundo Quiroga, born at San Antonio de los Llanos in 1788, rose as their commander in the struggles that made La Rioja autonomous in 1820.
zh:
切佩斯位于拉里奥哈南部半干旱平原，地处洛斯亚诺斯山麓。1444年，这里是安第斯原住民世界的交界地带：迪亚吉塔诸部使用拉里奥哈北部河谷，瓦尔佩人的村落和牧场则沿平原延伸向圣胡安与圣路易斯。

关于此地的殖民时代记载，最早见于安东尼奥·雷诺索·特略1754年在塔马立下的遗嘱，其中称「切佩斯至净受孕圣母」是依图库曼授地持有的土地。雷诺索·特略在那里建起住宅和教堂，栽种葡萄、牧放牲畜，使这座村镇带上庄园牧场的性质。1810年后西班牙权威崩溃，南部平原成为草原民兵招募人手的地方；1788年生于圣安东尼奥·德·洛斯亚诺斯的胡安·法昆多·基罗加，在1820年拉里奥哈走向自治的纷争中崛起为他们的指挥官。

en:
San Juan is a land of arid ranges and river oases beneath the Andes, where snowmelt from the San Juan River made the Tulum Valley habitable. In 1444 Huarpe farmers there watered maize, quinoa, beans and squash through their own canals and kept llamas, while Diaguita villages occupied the northern Jáchal and Iglesia districts. Inca power had not yet reached these valleys; its roads and influence arrived only late in the fifteenth century.

Juan Jufré de Loayza y Montese founded San Juan de la Frontera on 13 June 1562 by order of the Chilean captain general Francisco de Villagra, establishing a cabildo and distributing about 1,500 indigenous people in encomiendas. A flood of the San Juan River destroyed the fragile town late in 1593, and Luis Jufré y Meneses rebuilt it twenty-five blocks to the south around a new plaza. San José de Jáchal was founded in 1751. Long governed from Chile through Mendoza, San Juan passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776, the year an earthquake heavily damaged the town. José de San Martín became governor of Cuyo in 1814; San Juan's cabildo raised soldiers and taxed outward-bound wine and aguardiente to supply mules, food and transport for the 1816-17 crossing of the Andes. In 1820 San Juan separated from Cuyo as an autonomous province.
zh:
圣胡安是安第斯山下一片干旱山地与河谷绿洲交错之地，圣胡安河的融水使图卢姆谷地适宜居住。1444年，瓦尔佩农人在这里自开渠道，灌溉玉米、藜麦、菜豆和南瓜，并饲养骆马；迪亚吉塔人的村落则分布在北部的哈查尔与伊格莱西亚一带。此时印加势力尚未进入这些河谷，其道路和影响要到15世纪末才抵达。

1562年6月13日，胡安·胡弗雷·德·洛艾萨·伊·蒙特塞奉智利都督弗朗西斯科·德·比亚格拉之命建立「边疆圣胡安」，设立市政会，并把约1500名原住民分配到委托监护之下。1593年末，圣胡安河洪水摧毁了这座尚显简陋的城镇，路易斯·胡弗雷·伊·梅内塞斯在旧址以南25个街块处围绕新广场重建城市。1751年，圣何塞·德·哈查尔建立。圣胡安长期经门多萨受智利管辖，1776年转入拉普拉塔总督辖区，同年又遭地震严重破坏。何塞·德·圣马丁1814年出任库约省长；圣胡安市政会招募士兵，对销往外地的葡萄酒和阿瓜尔丁特酒征税，为1816至1817年翻越安第斯山提供骡子、粮食和运输补给。1820年，圣胡安脱离库约，成为自治省份。

en:
Quisquisacate, the meeting of waters where the Spanish foundation of Córdoba first stood, lies on the Suquía River below the Sierras Chicas. In 1444 the valley was Comechingón country, shared by the Henia and Kamiare groups whose ayllus farmed maize, beans, quinoa and squash on rain-fed plots, gathered algarrobo and chañar, and built rectangular houses partly dug into the earth against cold mountain winds. Their trails linked sierra camps with hunting grounds for guanaco and pampas deer; no Spanish road or town yet crossed the valley.

Jerónimo Luis de Cabrera's expedition reached the Suquía on 24 June 1573 and on 6 July founded Córdoba de la Nueva Andalucía at Quisquisacate, on the river's left bank. In 1577 the settlement was moved to the opposite bank, where Lorenzo Suárez de Figueroa laid out seventy blocks around the future plaza. The Jesuits arrived in 1599; their college grew into the University of Córdoba in 1613, the oldest university in Argentina, while the cathedral was built between 1580 and 1758. Córdoba became a see in 1699 and the seat of an intendency in 1785, nine years after the creation of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. It was briefly the viceroyalty's provisional capital during the British invasions of 1806. Four years later Santiago de Liniers led local royalists in opposing the May Revolution from Córdoba, while Dean Gregorio Funes supported the new junta.
zh:
奎奎萨卡特（Quisquisacate）是西班牙人建立科尔多瓦时的最早城址，这个「两水汇合」之地位于奇卡斯山麓的苏基亚河畔。1444年时，河谷是科梅钦贡人的土地，分属埃尼亚和卡米亚雷群体；他们的村社在雨养田地上种植玉米、菜豆、藜麦和南瓜，采集角豆和刺果豆的果实，并建造半埋入地下的长方形房屋，以抵御山间寒风。山间营地与原驼、潘帕斯鹿猎场之间有小径相连，此时还没有西班牙道路或城镇穿过河谷。

1573年6月24日，赫罗尼莫·路易斯·德·卡夫雷拉的探险队抵达苏基亚河，7月6日在河左岸的奎奎萨卡特建立「新安达卢西亚的科尔多瓦」。1577年，定居点迁到对岸，洛伦索·苏亚雷斯·德·菲格罗亚在未来广场周围规划了七十个街块。耶稣会士于1599年抵达，其学院在1613年发展为阿根廷最古老的科尔多瓦大学；大教堂则从1580年修建至1758年。1699年，科尔多瓦成为主教驻地，1776年拉普拉塔总督辖区设立九年后又于1785年成为行政区首府。1806年英国入侵期间，它曾短暂担任总督辖区临时首都。四年后，圣地亚哥·德·利涅尔斯在科尔多瓦率领当地保王派反对五月革命，教长格雷戈里奥·富内斯则支持新执政委员会。

en:
San Luis lies between the wooded Comechingón sierras, the Guanacache lagoons and the dry Pampas crossing called the Travesía Puntana. In 1444 Comechingón communities farmed the northeastern hills, Huanacache Huarpes lived around the lagoons, Olongasta Diaguitas reached the far north, and Taluhet Het groups moved across the eastern plains.

Luis Jufré de Loaysa y Meneses is traditionally said to have founded San Luis de Loyola Nueva Medina de Rioseco on 25 August 1594; after the settlement was abandoned, Martín García Óñez de Loyola ordered its refounding in 1596. It was moved to El Talar in 1643 and to its present site in 1689. As part of the Cuyo corregimiento the town was governed from Mendoza under Chile until 1776, when it passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. Its cabildo recognized the Buenos Aires junta in June 1810, and the revived intendancy of Cuyo in 1813 tied San Luis to Mendoza's war government. On 15 February 1820 an open cabildo deposed Lieutenant Governor Vicente Dupuy and proclaimed administrative autonomy; José Santos Ortiz became governor-intendant on 23 January 1821.
zh:
圣路易斯位于林木覆盖的科梅钦贡山地、瓜纳卡切湖群和被称为「特拉韦西亚·蓬塔纳」的潘帕斯旱途之间。1444年，科梅钦贡人社群在东北部山地务农，瓜纳卡切分支的瓦尔佩人住在湖群周围，奥隆加斯塔系迪亚吉塔人抵达最北端，塔尔乌埃特系埃特人则在东部平原迁徙活动。

传统说法认为，路易斯·胡弗雷·德·洛艾萨·伊·门塞斯于1594年8月25日建立圣路易斯·德·洛约拉·新梅迪纳·德·里奥塞科；居民点废弃后，马丁·加西亚·奥涅斯·德·洛约拉于1596年下令重建。城市1643年迁往埃尔塔拉，1689年迁至现址。作为库约裁判区的一部分，它在1776年前一直经门多萨受智利管辖，此后转入新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区。市政会于1810年6月承认布宜诺斯艾利斯洪达，1813年恢复的库约监督区又把圣路易斯纳入门多萨的战时政府。1820年2月15日，公开市政会罢黜副省长比森特·迪皮伊并宣布行政自治；何塞·桑托斯·奥尔蒂斯于1821年1月23日就任监督省长。

en:
The lagoons, marshes and slow rivers where the Salado approaches the Paraná were in 1444 a meeting ground of river peoples. Charrúa bands then had their center in the country that became Santa Fe, while Chaná-Timbú groups such as the Timbú, Calchín and Quiloaza lived along the Paraná, Coronda and Carcarañá. They fished, hunted rhea and deer with bolas and bows, planted maize, squash and beans in seasonal plots, gathered honey and lived under hereditary chiefs in communal houses; canoes linked the islands, fishing grounds and mainland camps.

Juan Díaz de Solís entered the Río de la Plata in 1516, and on 9 June 1527 Sebastián Gaboto completed Sancti Spiritus on the Carcarañá, the first Spanish settlement in this part of the Río de la Plata; native warriors destroyed it in 1529. Juan de Garay left Asunción on 14 April 1573 and on 15 November founded Santa Fe near Cayastá as a staging port and refuge on the route to the estuary. Floods, locust plagues and indigenous attacks forced the town's removal to the Vera Cruz site between 1650 and 1660. A royal order of 31 December 1662 made Santa Fe a designated port of call and stimulated river trade, until Viceroy Vértiz withdrew the privilege in 1780. The cabildo accepted the May Revolutionary junta on 12 June 1810, though resentment of Buenos Aires's centralism later drew the city toward José Gervasio Artigas and the federal cause.
zh:
1444年，萨拉多河趋近巴拉那河之处遍布潟湖、沼泽和缓流，是河畔诸族群交会之地。查鲁亚游群当时以后来成为圣菲的土地为中心，廷布、卡尔钦、基洛阿萨等查纳-廷布群体则居住在巴拉那河、科龙达河与卡尔卡拉尼亚河沿岸。他们捕鱼，用投石索和弓箭猎取美洲鸵与鹿，在季节性田地上种植玉米、南瓜和菜豆，采集蜂蜜，并在世袭首领率领下居住在公共长屋中；独木舟把岛屿、渔场和大陆营地连接起来。

1516年，胡安·迪亚斯·德·索利斯进入拉普拉塔河；1527年6月9日，塞瓦斯蒂安·加沃托在卡尔卡拉尼亚河畔建成圣埃斯皮里图斯堡，这是西班牙人在拉普拉塔河这一带最早的定居点，但原住民战士在1529年将其摧毁。1573年4月14日，胡安·德·加赖从亚松森出发，11月15日在卡亚斯塔附近建立圣菲，作为通往河口航路上的中转港和避难地。洪水、蝗灾和原住民攻击迫使城镇在1650年至1660年间迁往贝拉克鲁斯址。1662年12月31日的王家命令把圣菲定为指定停靠港，促进了河上贸易；贝蒂斯总督又于1780年撤销这项特权。1810年6月12日，市议会承认五月革命执政委员会，但对布宜诺斯艾利斯集权的不满后来使这座城市倒向何塞·赫尔瓦西奥·阿蒂加斯和联邦派事业。

en:
Rosario's stretch of the Paraná is a flat shore cut by the Ludueña, Saladillo and smaller streams. In 1444 there was no town here: Charrúa bands and Chaná-Timbú river peoples to the north used the islands and banks for fishing, crossed the grasslands after rhea and deer, and planted maize, squash and beans in seasonal plots. Their canoes linked this shore with the Paraná crossings, while inland tracks led toward the country that the Spanish would later call the Pago de los Arroyos.

In the early seventeenth century the crossing became a wagon stop on the royal road between Córdoba and the river route to Paraguay, but it never received a formal founding charter. Captain Luis Romero de Pineda established the first recorded permanent estancia near the end of the 1600s, the Jesuits bought the San Miguel del Carcarañal lands in 1719, and around 1724 Santiago Montenegro settled here, later building a mill and a chapel dedicated to Our Lady of the Rosary; in 1751 he was appointed the settlement's first local magistrate. During the independence wars Manuel Belgrano organized the Independencia and Libertad batteries on the bluff above the river, and at half past six on the morning of 27 February 1812 his soldiers swore allegiance to the new blue-and-white flag he raised for the first time.
zh:
罗萨里奥所在的巴拉那河西岸地势平坦，卢杜埃尼亚河、萨拉迪略河和多条小溪从草原切过。1444年这里还没有城镇：查鲁亚游群和北方的查纳-廷布河畔人群利用岛屿与河岸捕鱼，穿过草原追逐美洲鸵和鹿，并在季节性田地上种植玉米、南瓜和菜豆。他们的独木舟把这段河岸同巴拉那河各渡口连接起来，陆上小径则通向后来被西班牙人称为「溪流地」的地方。

17世纪初，这个渡口成为科尔多瓦与通往巴拉圭河路之间王家大道上的大车队停靠点，但始终没有正式建城文书。17世纪末，路易斯·罗梅罗·德·皮内达上尉建立了文献记载中第一座常设牧场；1719年，耶稣会买下圣米格尔·德尔·卡尔卡拉尼亚尔土地；约1724年，圣地亚哥·德·蒙特内格罗在此定居，后来修建磨坊和供奉玫瑰圣母的小堂，1751年被任命为当地第一任行政官。独立战争期间，曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺在临河高地上设置「独立」和「自由」炮台；1812年2月27日清晨6时30分，他的士兵向他首次升起的蓝白新旗宣誓。

en:
The bay of Montevideo is sheltered by the low cerro that later gave the place its name. In 1444 no walled town stood there; Guenoa-Minuane hunters, gatherers and fishers occupied the bay and the lands east of the Uruguay River, while the coast to the west was a zone of contact with Guaraní and Charrúa groups. Deep water made the anchorage valuable, but the hill looked over seasonal camps rather than a colonial port.

In January 1520 Francisco Albo, sailing with Ferdinand Magellan's expedition, recorded the promontory as Monte Vidi. The Portuguese founding of Colonia do Sacramento after 1680 then made the bay a frontier prize. Manuel de Freitas da Fonseca began a Portuguese redoubt there on 22 November 1723; Bruno Mauricio de Zabala's pressure from Buenos Aires opened the Spanish settlement process on 22 January 1724, with Fuerte San José, ten cannon and about a thousand mission Guaraní. On 24 December 1726 the town was surveyed and named San Felipe y Santiago de Montevideo, settled by Canarian families alongside Guaraní and enslaved Bantu Africans, with a council functioning by 1730. A military government was created in 1751, and after the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata was formed in 1776 Montevideo became its chief port and naval station. British troops captured it on 3 February 1807, but Oriental and Buenos Aires militias recovered it later that year. Francisco Javier de Elío made the city the viceroyalty's last capital on 19 January 1811; José Artigas's forces besieged it in 1811 and from 1812 until the Spanish garrison fell in 1814. Portugal invaded in 1816, occupied Montevideo from 1817 and annexed the Banda Oriental in 1821.
zh:
蒙得维的亚湾受一座低矮山丘庇护，这座山丘后来成为地名的由来。1444年时这里还没有城墙城镇；格诺阿—米努安人的狩猎、采集和渔猎群体占据海湾及乌拉圭河以东土地，以西沿海则是他们与瓜拉尼人、查鲁亚人接触往来的区域。深水条件使这里成为优良锚地，但山丘下所见仍是季节性营地，而不是殖民港口。

1520年1月，随斐迪南·麦哲伦远航的弗朗西斯科·阿尔沃把这座海角记作Monte Vidi。1680年后葡萄牙人建立萨克拉门托殖民地，使这个海湾成为边境争夺的要地。1723年11月22日，曼努埃尔·德·弗雷塔斯·达·丰塞卡开始在此修建葡萄牙棱堡；布鲁诺·毛里西奥·德·萨瓦拉从布宜诺斯艾利斯施压，西班牙人的定居过程于1724年1月22日展开，建起圣何塞堡，配备十门火炮，并驻有士兵和约一千名传教区瓜拉尼人。1726年12月24日，城镇完成测绘并得名圣费利佩—圣地亚哥·德·蒙得维的亚，居民有加那利家族、瓜拉尼人和被奴役的班图非洲人，到1730年市议会已开始运作。1751年这里设置军政长官，1776年拉普拉塔总督辖区成立后，蒙得维的亚成为首要港口和海军基地。英军1807年2月3日攻占城市，但东岸和布宜诺斯艾利斯民兵在同年将其收复。1811年1月19日，弗朗西斯科·哈维尔·德·埃利奥把这里作为总督辖区最后的首都；何塞·阿蒂加斯的部队1811年、以及1812年至1814年两度围城，西班牙守军最终在1814年投降。葡萄牙1816年入侵，1817年起占领蒙得维的亚，并于1821年吞并东部海岸。

en:
Colonia occupies the cape formed by the Punta de San Pedro and Punta de Santa Rita, with the San Gabriel Islands nearby and Buenos Aires lying across the Río de la Plata. In 1444 these were Charrúa hunting grounds on the open north bank, while Chaná-Timbú fishermen paddled canoes among the islands and shoals. The anchorage was useful, but no European town, customs house or treaty frontier yet divided the river.

Between 20 and 28 January 1680, Manuel Lobo founded the Nova Colônia do Santíssimo Sacramento, the first permanent European settlement in what is now Uruguay. José de Garro answered from Buenos Aires, and on 7 August 1680 Antonio de Vera y Mujica's troops stormed the post and renamed it Fuerte del Rosario. Portugal recovered it by treaty in 1681 and reoccupied it in February 1683. The rebuilt town became a Portuguese and British smuggling mart, exchanging manufactured goods and slaves for Potosí silver while cattle hides came in from the Banda Oriental. Spanish forces took it during the War of the Spanish Succession in March 1705, but Utrecht returned it to Portugal; after 1718 governors such as Antonio Pedro de Vasconcellos gave it strong sea bastions and a rich contraband trade. Pedro de Cevallos seized the colony on 11 October 1762, though it returned to Portugal in 1763. In 1777 Cevallos came with more than eighty ships and 9,000 men, and the Treaty of San Ildefonso confirmed Colonia to Spain. British forces took it on 5 March 1807, and José Artigas briefly commanded it for Spain that September. It joined the May Revolution in 1810, entered Artigas's Provincia Oriental in 1813, and was occupied by Portuguese troops in 1818, passing under Brazilian control with the annexation of 1821.
zh:
科洛尼亚坐落在圣佩德罗角与圣丽塔角围成的海角，附近有圣加夫列尔群岛，拉普拉塔河对岸便是布宜诺斯艾利斯。1444年时，河北岸开阔地是查鲁亚人的游猎场，查纳—廷布渔民则在岛屿和浅滩间划独木舟捕鱼。这里的锚地虽适于停泊，却还没有欧洲城镇、税关或条约划定的边界。

1680年1月20日至28日，曼努埃尔·洛博建立「至圣圣事新殖民地」，这是今乌拉圭境内第一个永久欧洲定居点。何塞·德·加罗从布宜诺斯艾利斯作出回应，1680年8月7日，安东尼奥·德·贝拉·穆希卡率军攻陷据点，将其改名为罗萨里奥堡。葡萄牙根据1681年条约收回该地，并于1683年2月重新占领。重建后的城镇成为葡萄牙和英国的走私市场，用制成品和奴隶换取波托西白银，东部海岸的牛皮也运到这里交易。西班牙军队在西班牙王位继承战争期间于1705年3月夺取城镇，但《乌得勒支和约》又将其交还葡萄牙；1718年后，安东尼奥·佩德罗·德·瓦斯康塞洛斯等总督为它修建坚固的海岸棱堡，走私贸易更加繁荣。佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯1762年10月11日攻占殖民地，但葡萄牙在1763年重新收回。1777年，塞瓦略斯率领八十多艘船和九千人再来，《圣伊尔德方索条约》确认科洛尼亚归属西班牙。英军1807年3月5日夺取该地，何塞·阿蒂加斯同年9月曾代表西班牙短暂统辖。科洛尼亚1810年加入五月革命，1813年并入阿蒂加斯的东岸省，1818年被葡萄牙军队占领，并随1821年的吞并转入巴西控制。

en:
At Salto the Uruguay River crosses a long bar of rock, broken into the rapids later called Salto Chico and Salto Grande; Guaraní speakers knew the falls as Ytú. In 1444 the east bank around them was Bohanes country, a people of the wider Charrúan world, with Yaro groups farther south between the Negro and San Salvador rivers. River crossings, fishing camps and hunting grounds met beneath the rapids, where boats could no longer pass freely upstream.

During the Guaraní War, José Joaquín de Viana brought four hundred soldiers north to enforce the Treaty of Madrid. His sheds at San Antonio del Salto Chico in October 1756 began the Spanish settlement, traditionally dated from 8 November 1756. In 1757 Viana and Pedro de Cevallos built Fuerte San Antonio and left a hundred men there, since Salto Grande blocked river navigation. On 16 June 1768 Francisco de Paula Bucareli occupied the post with 1,500 soldiers to carry out Charles III's expulsion of the Jesuits; the fort became an arsenal and prison for mission priests before a flood led the military works to be rebuilt across the river near Concordia. A small permanent population existed by early 1782. In December 1811 José Artigas's Exodus of the Eastern People camped for a month on this bank: the census made near Salto counted about 6,000 fighters, 4,500 civilians and 846 carts, and Artigas received his commission as lieutenant governor before the crossing at the Paso de Salto. Portuguese troops under Sebastião Barreto Pereira Pintos reached Salto Chico in 1817, and the permanent town grew beneath their camp before the annexation of 1821 placed the region under Brazil.
zh:
乌拉圭河流经萨尔托时穿过一条长长的岩脊，形成后来所称的小萨尔托和大萨尔托险滩；瓜拉尼语把这处急流叫作Ytú。1444年时，险滩东岸是博哈内斯人的土地，他们属于更大的查鲁亚群体；再往南，内格罗河与圣萨尔瓦多河之间还住着亚罗人。险滩以下汇聚着渡口、渔营和猎场，船只到了这里便无法继续顺畅上行。

瓜拉尼战争期间，何塞·华金·德·比亚纳率领四百名士兵北上，以执行《马德里条约》。1756年10月，他的部队在小萨尔托的圣安东尼奥搭起棚屋，西班牙人的定居点由此开始，传统上把1756年11月8日定为建城日。1757年，比亚纳与佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯修建圣安东尼奥堡，留下一百名士兵，因为大萨尔托险滩阻断了河运。1768年6月16日，弗朗西斯科·德·保拉·布卡雷利率一千五百名士兵占领据点，执行卡洛斯三世驱逐耶稣会士的命令；堡垒成了军火库和传教区神父的监狱，后来一场洪水使军事设施改在对岸的康科迪亚附近重建。到1782年初，这里已有少量常住居民。1811年12月，何塞·阿蒂加斯领导的「东岸人民出亡」在这处河岸扎营一个月；在萨尔托附近登记的人数约有六千名战士、四千五百名平民和846辆车，阿蒂加斯也在萨尔托渡口渡河前受任副都督。1817年，塞巴斯蒂安·巴雷托·佩雷拉·平托斯率领葡萄牙军队抵达小萨尔托，永久城镇在其军营周围成形；1821年东部海岸被吞并后，这一地区转入巴西治下。

en:
Yapeyú, 'ripe fruit' in Guarani, was also the old name of the Guaviraví, the stream that here enters the Uruguay through a line of soft green hills. In 1444 these banks were the southern march of the Guarani world: the farming villages of the Uruguay Guaraní lay between the Paraná and the Uruguay, while across the water ranged the Charrúa and the Yaro, the neighbours the Guaraní both raided and feared. The first Europeans were still beyond the horizon; Juan Díaz de Solís would not enter the Río de la Plata until 1516.

On 4 February 1627 the Jesuits Roque González de Santa Cruz, Pedro Romero and Nicolás Mastrilli Durán founded the reduction of Nuestra Señora de los Santos Reyes Magos de Yapeyú. Its people rounded up feral cattle between the two great rivers and built the Gran Estancia de Yapeyú, whose grazing frontier a royal cedula of 1657 carried south to the Río Queguay. By the early eighteenth century the town held some 10,000 souls, Guaraní together with Charrúa, Bohanes and Yaro, and it had become the seat of the Jesuit superior over all the Paraguay missions. The expulsion ordered by Charles III in February 1767 reached Yapeyú in 1768: the missions were secularized and the town became the capital of a civil department. Juan de San Martín took charge of it in 1774, reopened the Salto road that carried its mate, cotton, tobacco and hides to Buenos Aires, and in 1778 his son José was born here. Portuguese raids after 1801 stripped away the mission lands east of the Uruguay, and in 1817, during the Luso-Brazilian invasion of 1816 to 1821, Colonel Chagas's troops sacked and levelled the town after the defeats of Artigas and Andrés Guazurarí. The victors left Yapeyú in ruins.
zh:
「亚佩尤」（Yapeyú）在瓜拉尼语里意为「成熟的果实」，也曾是瓜维拉维河的旧名；这条小河在这里穿过连绵起伏的青翠丘陵，汇入乌拉圭河。1444年，这片河岸是瓜拉尼世界的南疆：巴拉那河与乌拉圭河之间，散布着乌拉圭瓜拉尼人的务农村落；对岸草原上游猎的则是查鲁亚人和亚罗人，瓜拉尼人对这两个邻族既劫掠又畏惧。欧洲人此时还远在视野之外，胡安·迪亚斯·德·索利斯要到1516年才驶入拉普拉塔河口。

1627年2月4日，耶稣会士罗克·冈萨雷斯·德·圣克鲁斯、佩德罗·罗梅罗和尼古拉斯·马斯特里利·杜兰在此创立「亚佩尤圣王三贤圣母」传教村。村民在两条大河之间围捕野牛，建起庞大的亚佩尤大牧场，1657年一道国王敕令更把牧地南界推到克瓜伊河畔。到18世纪初，镇上约有一万居民，除瓜拉尼人外还有查鲁亚人、博安人和亚罗人；亚佩尤也成为耶稣会统辖巴拉圭各传教区的会长驻地。卡洛斯三世1767年2月下令驱逐耶稣会，命令1768年传到亚佩尤：传教区被世俗化，城镇改为一个民政区的首府。1774年，胡安·德·圣马丁出任区长，重整萨尔托商道，把当地的马黛茶、棉花、烟草和皮革运往布宜诺斯艾利斯；1778年，他的儿子何塞出生在这里。1801年以后，葡萄牙人的袭扰夺走了乌拉圭河以东的传教区土地；1816至1821年葡属巴西大举入侵，阿蒂加斯和安德列斯·瓜苏拉利相继战败，1817年查加斯上校的部队洗劫并夷平了这座城镇，胜利者离开时，亚佩尤只剩一片废墟。

en:
Chaco Central is the thorn-forest belt bounded on the north by the Pilcomayo-Araguay and on the south by the old Bermejo and Teuco channel. In 1444 its camps and fishing grounds belonged to the Toba, Pilagá, Mocoví and other Guaycuru-speaking peoples, while Wichí groups lived toward the upper Bermejo and Pilcomayo. Bands followed game, fish, carob and honey through seasonal rounds, used bows and built light branch shelters; the rivers connected neighboring worlds, but no highland or riverine state commanded the interior.

Spanish expeditions from Asunción challenged that order. A campaign against the Guaycurúes entered the region in 1583, and on 14 April 1585 Alonso de Vera y Aragón founded Concepción de Nuestra Señora, later called Concepción de Buena Esperanza or Concepción del Bermejo. About 500 people lived there, while encomiendas at Matará and Guacara tried to force indigenous labor along the macomita track between Asunción and Talavera de Esteco. The town passed to the Governorate of Buenos Aires in 1617, but a coalition of tribes destroyed Matará in 1631 and killed much of the garrison; survivors fled to Corrientes and the cabildo was dissolved in 1645. Jesuits had founded Nuestra Señora María de los Reyes among Guaycuru people in 1610, while Guazutinguá was abandoned in 1626; later eighteenth-century missions passed to Franciscans after 1768. In 1821 mounted Chaco nations still barred Spanish and creole control of the interior.
zh:
中查科是北以皮科马约-阿拉瓜伊、南以贝尔梅霍河旧道与特乌科河为界的刺林地带。1444年，这里的营地和渔场属于托巴人、皮拉加人、莫科维人等瓜伊库鲁语族群，维奇诸群则活动在贝尔梅霍河与皮科马约河上游。各群体按季节追逐猎物、鱼群、角豆和蜂蜜，使用弓箭，搭建轻便的枝棚；河流连通着相邻世界，却没有哪个高原或河畔政权能控制这片内陆。

来自亚松森的西班牙远征挑战了这种秩序。1583年，一场讨伐瓜伊库鲁人的战役进入此地；1585年4月14日，阿隆索·德·贝拉-阿拉贡建立康塞普西翁-德努埃斯特拉-塞尼奥拉，后来称布埃纳埃斯佩兰萨的康塞普西翁或贝尔梅霍的康塞普西翁。城中约有五百居民，马塔拉和瓜卡拉的委托监护制则试图沿连接亚松森与塔莱韦拉-德埃斯特科的马科米塔小路征发原住民劳役。1617年，该城划归布宜诺斯艾利斯都督辖区。1631年，诸部族联军摧毁马塔拉，歼灭大部分守军；幸存者逃往科连特斯，市议会最终于1645年解散。耶稣会士已在1610年于瓜伊库鲁人中建立努埃斯特拉·塞尼奥拉·玛丽亚·德·洛斯雷耶斯传教区，瓜苏廷瓜传教区则于1626年废弃；18世纪又设立更多传教区，1768年后转由方济各会接续。到1821年，已掌握马匹的查科诸族仍阻挡着西班牙和克里奥尔势力控制内陆。

en:
Misiones is the red-earth country between the Upper Paraná and the Uruguay, a humid forest cut by a hundred rivers and ending northward at the Iguazú. Around 1444 Guarani war bands were still pressing into these woods from the north, filtering among the older Kaingang and Xokleng hunters; they cleared fields of maize and manioc around long-house villages, gathered the wild yerba mate the forest already gave, and called themselves avá, men. No European had yet seen the great falls. Sebastian Cabot, the first, was stopped by the Apipé rapids on the Paraná in December 1527, and Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca came overland from the Brazilian coast to reach Iguazú in 1541.

In 1610 the Jesuits José Cataldino and Simón Mazeta, sent from Asunción in December 1609, founded Loreto and San Ignacio in the Guayrá, the first of the thirty Guarani reductions. Bandeirantes from São Paulo began raiding for slaves in 1627 and sacked the Guayrá towns, so at the end of 1631 some 12,000 Guaraní fled downriver on seven hundred rafts under Antonio Ruiz de Montoya; barely 4,000 lived to refound Loreto and San Ignacio by the Yabebirí in March 1632, and their victory at Mbororé in 1641 broke the raids. Earlier, on 2 February 1627, Roque González de Santa Cruz had founded Candelaria on the Paraná, later seat of the Candelaria department. By the Treaty of Madrid of 1750 Spain exchanged the seven eastern towns for Colonia del Sacramento and ordered the Guaraní to withdraw west of the Uruguay; they refused, and in the Guaraní War of 1754 to 1756 Sepé Tiaraju fell and 1,511 Guaraní died at Caibaté on 10 February 1756. Charles III's expulsion of the Jesuits was enforced here in 1768, the towns passed to secular clergy and began to empty. Belgrano's army rested at Candelaria on its march to Paraguay in 1811, and in 1815 Andrés Guazurarí seized the Paraná towns for Artigas; but in January 1817 a Luso-Brazilian army under Francisco das Chagas Santos crossed the Uruguay, sacked the towns and carried off 1,800 Indians. The thirty pueblos were left in ruins.
zh:
米西奥内斯是上巴拉那河与乌拉圭河之间的红土之乡，湿润丛林被上百条河流切开，北端止于伊瓜苏河畔。1444年前后，瓜拉尼人的战团仍在从北方渗入这片林海，逐渐与更古老的卡因冈人、肖克伦猎人杂处；他们在长屋村落旁开辟玉米地和木薯地，采摘林中野生的马黛茶叶，并自称「阿瓦」，意思是人。此时还没有欧洲人见过那道大瀑布。塞瓦斯蒂安·卡博特是第一个：1527年12月，他在巴拉那河上被阿皮皮急流挡住去路；1541年，阿尔瓦尔·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡从巴西海岸陆路西行，抵达伊瓜苏瀑布。

1609年12月，耶稣会士何塞·卡塔尔迪诺和西蒙·马塞塔奉派离开亚松森，1610年在瓜伊拉地区建起洛雷托和圣伊格纳西奥，这是瓜拉尼三十座传教村的开端。1627年起，圣保罗的旗手不断深入掳人为奴，洗劫瓜伊拉诸村；1631年底，安东尼奥·鲁伊斯·德·蒙托亚率领约一万二千名瓜拉尼人乘七百只木筏顺河出逃，最终只有约四千人活下来，于1632年3月在亚贝贝里溪畔重建洛雷托和圣伊格纳西奥。1641年，他们在姆博罗雷击败追兵，袭掠才告平息。早在1627年2月2日，罗克·冈萨雷斯·德·圣克鲁斯已在巴拉那河畔建立坎德拉里亚，后来这里是坎德拉里亚行政区的首镇。1750年，西班牙以《马德里条约》把乌拉圭河以东的七座村镇换给葡萄牙，换取萨克拉门托殖民地，并勒令瓜拉尼人西迁；瓜拉尼人拒绝，1754至1756年瓜拉尼战争爆发，塞佩·蒂阿拉茹战死，1756年2月10日凯巴特一役有一千五百一十一名瓜拉尼人被杀。卡洛斯三世驱逐耶稣会的命令1768年在此执行，村镇转交世俗神职人员，人口开始流散。1811年贝尔格拉诺出征巴拉圭时曾在坎德拉里亚歇脚；1815年安德列斯·瓜苏拉利为阿蒂加斯夺取巴拉那河畔诸镇，但1817年1月弗朗西斯科·达斯·沙加斯·桑托斯率葡属巴西军队越过乌拉圭河，洗劫村镇，掳走一千八百名印第安人。盛极一时的三十座传教村，最终只剩废墟。

en:
The Highveld around the future Bloemfontein is open grassland some 1,400 metres above the sea, crossed by cold winters and sharp summer thunderstorms. Sotho-Tswana farmers and cattle keepers had separated into related clans by the fourteenth century, settling among older San hunter-forager communities; their homesteads combined sorghum fields, ironwork, cattle kraals and springs. In 1444 no dynasty ruled a single state here. Power rested with local chiefs and elder lineages, whose authority followed cattle, rainfall and the best grazing on the treeless plateau.

By at least the seventeenth century, a string of small Basotho chiefdoms covered much of the southern plateau, including the country that became the Free State. Their kraals formed loose confederations rather than one kingdom, trading cattle and iron with neighbours and shifting when drought or raiding exhausted a valley. During the eighteenth century, mounted Korana and mixed Cape frontier groups began moving along the Orange and Vaal river corridors, joining older Sotho-Tswana and Barolong networks around Mangaung, the spring-side place later called Bloemfontein. In 1821 those chiefly kraals still governed the plateau; the colonial town and fixed frontier had not yet crossed into it.
zh:
后来布隆方丹所在的高草原是海拔约1400米的开阔草地，冬季寒冷，夏季多猛烈雷阵雨。索托—茨瓦纳农民和牧人到14世纪已分化成相互关联的氏族，在更古老的桑人游猎社群之间定居；家园周围有高粱地、铁匠炉、牛栏和泉水。1444年时，没有一个王朝在这里统治单一国家。权力属于各地酋长和世系长老，其威望随牛群、雨量和无树高原上最好的牧场而升降。

至迟从17世纪起，一连串南索托小酋长辖地覆盖了南部高原的大部分地区，包括后来成为自由邦的土地。这些畜栏村寨组成松散联盟，而不是一个王国，人们与邻部交换牛只和铁器，遇到旱灾或袭扰使山谷无法维持时便迁徙。18世纪，骑马的科拉纳人和来自开普边疆的混血群体开始沿奥兰治河与法尔河走廊移动，汇入曼噶汪——也就是后来布隆方丹泉边一带——原有的索托—茨瓦纳和巴罗龙关系网。1821年，治理这片高原的仍是这些酋长畜栏村寨；殖民城镇和固定边疆尚未进入这里。

en:
Rio Grande guards the channel where the Lagoa dos Patos and Lagoa Mirim system opens toward the Atlantic, with open pampa behind the dunes. In 1444 Guarani villages used the lagoon shores, fishing and growing maize and manioc, while Charrua and Minuano bands crossed the grasslands to the south. No European fort stood on the waterway, and no cattle yet grazed the plains.

Portuguese navigators had called the passage Rio Grande de São Pedro after Martim Afonso de Sousa's early-sixteenth-century survey, but permanent occupation came with the Portuguese-Spanish contest over the River Plate. On 19 February 1737 Brigadier José da Silva Paes landed and began the Jesus-Maria-José fort; the formal colonial settlement followed that May. Azorean and Madeiran families made it the Vila of Rio Grande de São Pedro in 1751, and in 1760 it became the seat of its own captaincy. Pedro de Cevallos's Spanish army took the town in April 1763, sending refugees toward Viamão and Porto Alegre. Rafael Pinto Bandeira retook it on 1 April 1776, and the 1777 Treaty of San Ildefonso confirmed Portugal's hold on the coast. From 1780 the first charqueadas near Pelotas dried beef for northeastern Brazil, and Rio Grande shipped hides and salted meat. By 1821 the fortress port was the commercial mouth of the southern cattle country.
zh:
里奥格兰德扼守帕图斯湖、米林湖水系通向大西洋的水道，沙丘后方是开阔的潘帕草原。1444年，瓜拉尼村落利用湖岸渔猎，种植玉米和木薯；查鲁亚人和米努亚诺人群则在南方草原往来。水道上还没有欧洲人的要塞，平原上也没有牧牛。

马丁·阿方索·德·索萨在16世纪初勘察后，葡萄牙航海者把这一通道称为圣佩德罗大河，但永久占领要到葡西争夺拉普拉塔河时期才发生。1737年2月19日，准将若泽·达席尔瓦·派斯登陆并开始修建耶稣-马利亚-若瑟要塞，正式殖民点在同年5月形成。亚速尔和马德拉移民使它在1751年成为里奥格兰德-德圣佩德罗镇，1760年又成为独立都督辖区的治所。1763年4月，佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯的西班牙军队攻占城镇，难民逃往维亚芒和阿雷格里港一带。拉斐尔·平托·班德拉于1776年4月1日收复此地，1777年的《圣伊尔德方索条约》确认葡萄牙占有海岸。1780年起，佩洛塔斯附近出现最早的腌肉场，为巴西东北部生产风干牛肉，里奥格兰德则输出皮革和咸肉。到1821年，这座要塞港口已是南方牧地通向海洋的商埠。

en:
South of Asunción the Paraguay river loses itself in a watery wedge of esteros, lagoons and backwaters before meeting the Paraná: the Ñeembucú, in Guarani the long spill of water. To its east, ground rises gently between the Tebicuary and the Paraná into grass and palm savannah. In 1444 Guarani farmers and fishermen held the riverbanks and islands, their villages looking west across the Paraguay to the unmastered Chaco, and no European had yet entered these waters. Sebastian Cabot passed the confluence in 1528, and nine years later Asunción was founded upriver.

From 1676 the Asunción elite were granted cattle lands running south to the Tebicuary, while everything between that river and the Paraná belonged to the Jesuits, whose vast herds grazed as far as the northern edge of Ñeembucú. When the bandeirantes destroyed the Guayrá reductions, survivors migrated south from 1632 and rebuilt their towns in this strip: San Ignacio Guazú, Santa María de Fe, San Miguel, Santa Rosa and Santiago Apóstol, settled on its present hilltop in 1669; it had once held 3,151 people, Félix de Azara wrote, but only 1,215 remained when he visited in 1784. The expulsion of 1768 broke the mission world, and after the ordinance of 1782 the surviving towns passed to the intendency of Asunción. In the marshy west, raids from Chaco Indians were answered with a line of riverside forts and with the river port of Pilar, founded by Pedro Melo de Portugal in 1779, while Yabebyry was pushed out on the Paraná in 1790. Paraguay broke with Spain in 1811, and after Dr Francia took dictatorial power in 1814 the southern forts were strengthened, Humaitá among them. The old mission towns and the new cattle ports thus entered independence under Asunción's rule.
zh:
亚松森以南，巴拉圭河在汇入巴拉那河之前漫成一道水乡楔子：潟湖、浅滩与回水道纵横交错，瓜拉尼语称之为涅恩布库，意为「长长的溢水道」；它东侧地势缓缓抬升，特维夸里河与巴拉那河之间是草原和棕榈稀树草原。1444年，河畔与岛上住着以农耕渔猎为生的瓜拉尼人，他们的村落西望巴拉圭河对岸尚未被征服的查科；此时还没有任何欧洲人的船驶入这片水域。1528年，塞瓦斯蒂安·卡博特经过两河交汇处，九年后，亚松森在更上游的河畔建立。

从1676年起，亚松森的权贵获得南至特维夸里河的牧地授地，而该河与巴拉那河之间的土地尽属耶稣会，他们的庞大牛群一直牧放到涅恩布库北缘。旗手摧毁瓜伊拉传教村后，幸存者从1632年起南迁，在这条地带上重建村镇：圣伊格纳西奥·瓜苏、圣玛利亚·德拉费、圣米格尔、圣罗莎，以及1669年迁到今日丘陵址上的圣地亚哥使徒村。费利克斯·德·阿萨拉记载，该村一度有三千一百五十一名居民，而他1784年到访时只剩一千二百一十五人。1768年驱逐耶稣会令传教世界瓦解，1782年以后残存诸镇划归亚松森都督辖区管辖。在多沼泽的西部，为抵御查科印第安人的袭扰，西班牙人沿河修筑一连串要塞，佩德罗·梅洛·德·葡萄牙1779年在巴拉圭河畔建起河港皮拉尔，1790年又在巴拉那河畔推出前哨亚韦维里。1811年巴拉圭脱离西班牙，1814年弗朗西亚博士建立独裁统治后进一步加固南部诸堡，乌迈塔堡也在其中。传教村故地和新兴的牧牛港口，就这样在亚松森治下走进独立年代。

en:
Itapúa is the steep, red-earth right bank of the Upper Paraná, where the river bends south in a broad sweep opposite the forests of Argentine Misiones; inland, the ground climbs through yerba mate woods toward the San Rafael hills. The Guarani called the crossing-place Itá Púa, the pointed stone, after a rock standing out in the river. In 1444 Guarani farmers kept villages along the arroyos that cut these slopes, hunted the dense selva and gathered wild mate, and the Paraná carried no traffic but their canoes. No European had passed the Apipé rapids far downstream, and the Jesuit cross would not be raised here until 1615.

On 25 March 1615 Roque González de Santa Cruz founded the reduction of Nuestra Señora de la Encarnación de Itapúa, first on the eastern bank; threatened by bandeirantes, plague and local resistance, the town was carried across the river in three days to its permanent ground on the right bank, where Hernandarias visited it that December. More towns followed along the shore, among them San Cosme y Damián, founded on 25 January 1632 and moved four times before settling at its last site in 1718. There, from 1703, the Jesuit Buenaventura Suárez, helped by Guaraní craftsmen, built telescopes, quadrants and sundials and wrote his Lunario de un Siglo, predicting eclipses years ahead, to the wonder of European universities; his confrere Taddaeus Enis led the mission Guaraní against the Portuguese in the war of 1754 to 1756. At Trinidad and Jesús the great stone churches were still rising when the expulsion reached the towns in 1768; secular clergy took over and the pueblos slowly emptied. In 1810 and 1811 Belgrano's patriot army crossed through Itapúa into Paraguay, only to be beaten at Paraguarí and Tacuarí, and Paraguay became independent in 1811. The old pueblo of Itapúa entered 1821 as a quiet, half-forgotten frontier of the young republic, its mate woods and ruined churches overgrown by the selva.
zh:
伊塔普阿是上巴拉那河陡峭的红土右岸，大河在这里拐出一道宽阔的南弯，对岸是阿根廷米西奥内斯的丛林；内陆地势沿溪谷抬升，穿过马黛茶林，通向圣拉斐尔丘陵。瓜拉尼人把这个渡口称作「伊塔普阿」（Itá Púa），意为「尖石」，名字来自江中一块醒目的岩石。1444年，瓜拉尼农户在切过坡地的溪涧旁结村而居，入密林狩猎，采摘野生马黛茶叶；巴拉那河上往来的只有他们的独木舟。下游远处的阿皮皮急流挡住了欧洲人的来路，耶稣会的十字架要到1615年才在此竖起。

1615年3月25日，罗克·冈萨雷斯·德·圣克鲁斯创立「伊塔普阿道成肉身圣母」传教村，最初设在河东对岸；因旗手威胁、瘟疫和当地瓜拉尼人的反抗，全村用三天时间横渡大河，迁到右岸的永久址上，同年12月埃尔南达里亚斯到此视察。沿岸陆续建起更多村镇，圣科斯姆和圣达米安便是其中之一，1632年1月25日建立，历经四次迁徙，1718年才定于最后一处址地。1703年起，耶稣会士布埃纳文图拉·苏亚雷斯在瓜拉尼工匠帮助下造出望远镜、象限仪和日晷，所著《世纪历算》能提前多年推算日食月食，令欧洲大学惊叹；1754至1756年的战争中，他的同会修士塔德乌斯·埃尼斯率领传教区的瓜拉尼人抗击葡萄牙人。1768年驱逐令到达时，特立尼达和赫苏斯宏伟的石砌教堂还在施工；诸村转交世俗神职人员，渐渐荒落。1810至1811年，贝尔格拉诺的爱国军经伊塔普阿攻入巴拉圭，却在帕拉瓜里和塔夸里连遭败绩，巴拉圭于1811年独立。1821年的伊塔普阿故镇，是这个年轻共和国一处安静、近乎被遗忘的边疆，马黛林和残破教堂正被丛林慢慢吞没。

en:
The plains south and west of the Río de la Plata, where the tall grass ran unbroken to the Salado, were the country of the Querandí. They were the easternmost of the Didiuhet bands, one of the Het peoples; Guaraní neighbours gave them their name, 'they who carry fat', for the animal grease in their diet. In 1444 they moved these pastures in leather-tented bands, running down pampas deer, rheas and guanacos, famed as runners, and hunting with the bolas, gathering by the waterholes in winter and raiding inland in summer. To the Spaniards who would soon arrive, every nomad of the plains was simply a 'Pampa'.

The Querandí enter written history in 1528, in a letter sent home from Sebastián Cabot's expedition. When Pedro de Mendoza founded Buenos Aires in 1536, friendly trade soon turned to war, and on 15 June 1536 his brother Diego's column was destroyed on the shores of the Laguna de Rocha; the Querandí and their allies harried the town until the Spaniards themselves abandoned and burned it. Juan de Garay refounded Buenos Aires in 1580 and parcelled out native labour, but the Querandí name disappears from the records after Rodrigo Ortiz de Zárate's reprisals of 1586, the encomienda census of 1672 being its last echo. Their plains then filled with feral cattle hunted in vaquerías, while the survivors merged into the wider Pampas world; from 1740 to 1753 a Jesuit reduction on the Salado gathered the last settled bands. By 1821 the land south of the Salado was still an unconquered Indian frontier.
zh:
拉普拉塔河西南、高草一直铺到萨拉多河的这片平原，是克兰迪人的家园。他们是海特人一支迪迪乌维特人中最靠东的部落；瓜拉尼邻人因他们饮食中离不开动物油脂，称他们为克兰迪，意为「带脂人」。1444年，他们以兽皮帐篷为单位逐水草而居，靠双腿追逐潘帕斯鹿、美洲鸵和羊驼，以善跑闻名，又擅长投石索，冬季聚于水畔，夏季深入内陆游猎。在不久后来到的西班牙人嘴里，草原上所有这样的游猎者都只有一个称呼：潘帕斯人。

克兰迪人最初见于记载，是1528年塞巴斯蒂安·卡博特探险队寄回国内的一封信。1536年佩德罗·德·门多萨建立布宜诺斯艾利斯后，以物易物很快变成战争：同年6月15日，其弟迭戈的队伍在罗查湖畔被歼，克兰迪人会同诸部围攻新城，直到西班牙人自己弃城焚毁。胡安·德·加赖1580年重建布宜诺斯艾利斯并分配印第安劳役，但在罗德里戈·奥尔蒂斯·德·萨拉特1586年的征讨之后，克兰迪之名便从记载中消失，只有1672年的委托监护征册留下最后一笔。此后他们的草原上遍布野化牛群，供人围猎，幸存者则融入更广义的潘帕斯世界；1740年至1753年间，萨拉多河上的一座耶稣会归化村收容了最后定居下来的部众。到1821年，萨拉多河以南仍是一片未曾被征服的印第安边疆。

en:
West of the Salado the wet pampa dries into open steppe and caldén woodland. In 1444 its only roads were the tracks between waterholes, used by the western Het bands the Spaniards later called the Diuuhet and the Taluhet, their 'Pampas': nomadic hunters of guanaco and rhea, camped in leather toldos along the Chadileuvú and beneath the Lihué Calel rocks. They had no towns and no masters, and the nearest settled worlds lay far away, at Córdoba and Cuyo.

The founding of Mendoza in 1561, Córdoba in 1573 and San Luis in 1594 pushed displaced peoples south into these plains, and seventeenth-century smallpox tore through the bands. Horses and feral cattle made them formidable riders; Spanish parties crossed the grass only to fetch salt from the Salinas Grandes, while raiding parties struck the frontier estancias. From the mid-eighteenth century Araucanized Pehuenches from the Andean Ránquil country mixed with the local Tehuelches to form the Ranqueles, lords of the dry pampa, whose cacique Llanquitur was already raiding the Salado estancias by 1765. No Spanish army ever conquered this land: in 1796 the viceroy Pedro Melo de Portugal made peace with the Ranqueles instead, and in 1821 the steppe was still entirely Indian country.
zh:
萨拉多河以西，湿润的潘帕斯渐成开阔的干旱草原，间杂卡尔登树林。1444年，这里唯一的道路是连接各处水源的兽径，往来其上的是海特人中偏西的迪乌维特、塔卢维特等游群——西班牙人后来统称他们为潘帕斯人。这些猎捕羊驼和美洲鸵的游猎部族在查迪莱乌武河畔和利韦尔卡莱尔岩山下张设兽皮帐篷，没有城镇，也没有主人；最近的定居世界远在科尔多瓦和库约。

1561年门多萨、1573年科尔多瓦、1594年圣路易斯相继建城，被挤压的各部不断南迁进入这片草原，17世纪的天花又使诸部人口锐减。马匹和野化牛群把他们变成令人生畏的骑手：西班牙人只有为取盐才结队穿过草原，前往萨利纳斯格兰德斯盐沼，而游骑的袭击则频频降临边境牧场。18世纪中叶起，从安第斯山兰基尔一带来的马普切化佩文切人与当地特维尔切人融合，形成主宰干草原的兰克尔人；其酋长兰基图尔到1765年已在袭击萨拉多河畔的牧场。没有哪支西班牙军队征服过这片土地：1796年，拉普拉塔总督佩德罗·梅洛·德·葡萄牙选择与兰克尔人议和。到1821年，这片草原仍完全是印第安人的天下。

en:
The sheltered bay of Coquimbo opens below the Elqui valley, one of the transverse valleys cutting through Chile's semi-arid Norte Chico. The people later called Diaguitas lived in separate chiefdoms, farming irrigated valley floors, trading fish and shells from the coast to the mountains, and painting pottery in red, black and white. In 1444 the anchorage was still an Indigenous fishing landing beneath the hills, not a Spanish port; the Elqui communities were linked by exchange and ceramic traditions, not by a single state.

Late in the fifteenth century Inca armies reduced the Diaguita valleys, appointing kurakas and placing mitmas colonies; Cuzco designs entered local pottery and metalwork. Spanish conquest came with Juan Bohón, who founded Villanueva de la Serena in 1544. On the night of 11 January 1549 an Indigenous rising killed nearly all the Spaniards and burned the town. Francisco de Aguirre refounded it on 26 August as San Bartolomé de La Serena, and Charles I granted it the title of city in 1552. Bohón and Pedro de Valdivia had already judged Coquimbo Bay the natural port for the settlement. Francis Drake was repulsed at Guayacán Bay in 1579, Bartholomew Sharp attacked the poorly defended town in 1680, and Edward Davis's raiders were driven out in 1686; persistent corsair attacks finally forced fortification in 1730.
zh:
科金博的避风海湾开在埃尔基河谷下方，这里是智利半干旱小北地区的横断山谷之一。后来被称为迪亚吉塔人的族群分作若干酋邦，在灌溉谷底耕作，把鱼和贝壳从海岸交易到山地，并烧制红、黑、白三色彩陶。1444年，这片锚地仍是山丘下的原住民渔港，而非西班牙港口；埃尔基各社区由交换和制陶传统联系在一起，却没有统一国家。

15世纪后期，印加军队征服这些横断山谷，任命库拉卡并安置米特马克移民，库斯科风格随之进入当地陶器和金属工艺。西班牙征服随胡安·博翁到来，他于1544年建立塞雷纳新镇。1549年1月11日夜，原住民起义杀死几乎所有西班牙人并焚毁城镇；同年8月26日，弗朗西斯科·德·阿吉雷将其重建为圣巴托洛梅·德·拉塞雷纳，卡洛斯一世又在1552年授予城市称号。博翁和佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚都已认定科金博湾是这座定居点的天然港口。1579年，弗朗西斯·德雷克在瓜亚坎湾被击退；1680年，巴塞洛缪·夏普袭击防备空虚的拉塞雷纳；1686年，爱德华·戴维斯的突袭队入城后又被赶走。不断的海盗袭击终于促使城市在1730年修筑防御工事。

en: The willow-lined valley of the Río Negro cuts through the northern Patagonian steppe from the Limay–Neuquén junction toward the Atlantic. In 1444 its islands, fords and camping grounds were in the country of the Gününa këna bands, eastern people whom Mapuche speakers called Puelche. They lived in branch-and-hide shelters, hunted guanaco and rhea, gathered wild fruit and moved in small family groups under elder headsmen. Spanish explorers out of Buenos Aires first reached the inland river in 1604 while searching for the City of the Caesars. Mercedes de Patagones was founded at the mouth in 1779, but late-eighteenth-century epidemics and increasing Mapuche influence changed the middle valley's peoples before any permanent colonial settlement reached it.
zh: 内格罗河两岸多柳，利迈河与内乌肯河汇合后，河水穿过北巴塔哥尼亚草原流向大西洋。1444年，河上的岛屿、徒涉场和营地都在被马普切人称为普埃尔切人的诸群体活动范围内。他们以树枝和兽皮搭屋，猎捕原驼和美洲鸵，采集野果，结成小型家庭群体迁徙，由年长的首领带领。1604年，从布宜诺斯艾利斯出发的西班牙探险队为寻找恺撒城首次进入内格罗河内陆地带。1779年，梅塞德斯·德·帕塔戈内斯在河口建立，但殖民据点仍未控制中游；18世纪末的疫病和日益增强的马普切影响，先一步改变了谷地居民。

en:
Senqu is the river that later Dutch travellers called the Groote Rivier and then the Orange, known to earlier Khoe-speaking communities as the Gariep. The province covers its arid southern fringe, where Bushmanland's open plains and isolated koppies run down toward the water. The soil is poor and the groundwater often saline, so San hunter-foragers and Khoekhoe pastoralists timed their movements to the river, seasonal pans, springs and game migrations. In 1444 permanent settlement was impossible away from reliable water; power lay in knowing those scattered places.

During the eighteenth century, Cape trekboers pushed into the dry parts of Bushmanland, grazing cattle and sheep on enormous loan farms rather than laying out towns. Families moved between summer and winter pasture, living in wagons, tents or simple reed-and-clay hartbees houses, while San stock raids made the northern frontier dangerous. In 1779 Colonel Robert Jacob Gordon reached the river and named it the Orange for William V of Orange, replacing the older Groote Rivier on colonial maps. By 1821 this stretch still had no magistrate or fixed town; river camps, cattle posts and widely separated loan holdings remained the only settled marks along the Senqu.
zh:
森库是一条河的名字，后来的荷兰旅人先称它为大河，再改名为奥兰治河，而更早的科伊语社群称它为加里普河。本省涵盖它干旱的南缘，布什曼兰开阔平原和孤立岩丘一直延伸到水边。这里土壤贫瘠，地下水常带盐味，因此桑人猎民和科伊科伊牧人都依照河流、季节性盐盘、泉水和猎物迁徙来安排行动。1444年时，离开可靠水源便无法长期定居；谁熟悉这些分散的水点，谁就能在此生存。

18世纪，开普的游牧布尔人推进到布什曼兰的干旱地带，在面积广大的借地牧场上放牧牛羊，而没有建立城镇。各家各户在夏季和冬季牧场之间迁徙，住在大车、帐篷或芦苇黏土搭成的简陋小屋里；桑人盗畜也使北部边疆充满危险。1779年，罗伯特·雅各布·戈登上校抵达这条河，以奥兰治的威廉五世之名把它命名为奥兰治河，殖民地图上旧有的「大河」一名由此被取代。到1821年，这一河段仍没有法官驻地或固定城镇；河边营地、牲畜哨站和彼此远离的借地牧场，仍是森库沿岸仅有的定居痕迹。

en:
Between the southern foothills of the Tandil ranges and the Río Negro stretch the driest of the pampas, the land of the Gününa Küne. They never called themselves Puelches: that Mapudungun name, 'people of the east', was given them by the Araucanians across the Andes, and Thomas Falkner grouped them with the northern Tehuelches of his 'Het'. In 1444 small bands followed guanaco and rhea between the river valleys and brackish lakes, dressed in guanaco-hide cloaks and camped in skin toldos along the waters that ran down to the Río Negro. They had never seen a European.

Two Puelche headmen were among the Indians who came to Buenos Aires to treat with Governor Salcedo in 1739, and the treaties signed at Sierra de la Ventana in 1742 opened their country to Jesuit missions and the poncho fairs at El Cayrú and Chapaleofú. Contact brought disaster: epidemics at the end of the eighteenth century shattered the bands, and the survivors were drawn into the Araucanization spreading from the Andes, until by 1800 the name Puelche covered a mixed, Mapuche-speaking equestrian people. In 1779 the Spanish planted Fuerte del Carmen on the Río Negro, at their southern edge, and in 1782 Basilio Villarino sailed up that river into their territory. In 1821 the Puelches remained masters of the plains between the new forts and the river, though no longer quite the people their grandparents had been.
zh:
坦迪尔群山南麓与内格罗河之间，是潘帕斯最干旱的一段，古努纳克讷人的土地。他们从不自称普埃尔切——这个词是马普切语「东方之人」的意思，由安第斯山另一侧的阿劳卡诺人所起；托马斯·福克纳则把他们归入他所说「海特」人中的北特维尔切群。1444年，小股游群在河谷与咸水湖之间追逐羊驼和美洲鸵，身披羊驼皮斗篷，在内格罗河水系两岸的兽皮帐篷里栖身。他们还从未见过欧洲人。

1739年，两名普埃尔切酋长随诸部首领前往布宜诺斯艾利斯与萨尔塞多总督议和，1742年在本塔纳山签订的和约向耶稣会传教和埃尔凯鲁、查帕莱奥富的篷乔集市打开了他们的土地。接触带来的却是灾难：18世纪末的瘟疫重创诸部，幸存者被卷入自安第斯山蔓延开来的阿劳卡诺化，到1800年前后，「普埃尔切」一名已指称一个讲马普切语的混血骑马民族。1779年，西班牙人在其南缘的内格罗河畔建起卡尔门堡，1782年巴西利奥·比利亚里诺溯河驶入他们的腹地。到1821年，普埃尔切人仍是新建堡垒与大河之间草原的主人，只是已不及其祖辈时的模样。

en:
West of Tandil the Tandilia hills sink into the central plains of Buenos Aires, threaded by the Tapalqué and Chapaleofú streams. In 1444 this was sierra country, roamed by the Serrano bands the Spaniards lumped together with the Pampas. Its glens and dry-stone corrals served the great poncho fair of El Cayrú, which from at least the early seventeenth century gathered plains Indians, Patagonians and Araucanian traders at the westernmost end of the hill chain. The peoples of the plains knew these uplands as a refuge and a marketplace long before any European saw them.

In 1741 a Spanish expedition crossed this district and signed peace with the 'sierra Indians' of the Catriel line of caciques, whose authority was recognized across the hill country; the Spanish estancias, meanwhile, never passed the Salado, far to the north. El Cayrú kept its yearly trade in ponchos, hides and cattle even as Araucanization spread the Mapuche language and customs among the Tehuelche families camped in these glens. Through the viceroyalty years Spanish columns reconnoitred as far as Tandil, but no fort was raised on the western ranges. In 1821 the Tapalqué country still lay wholly within the unconquered Indian 'desert' south of the Salado.
zh:
坦迪尔以西，坦迪利亚山渐没入布宜诺斯艾利斯省中部平原，塔帕尔凯河与查帕莱奥富河蜿蜒其间。1444年，这里同样是「山民」的天地，游猎的塞拉诺诸部被西班牙人归入潘帕斯人之列。他们的山谷和干砌石畜栏旁，是盛大的埃尔凯鲁篷乔集市场地——至迟从17世纪初起，草原印第安人、巴塔哥尼亚人和阿劳卡诺商人就在这条山系的最西端会聚。远在欧洲人踏足之前，草原诸族已把这些高地当作避难所和集市。

1741年，一支西班牙探险队经过此地，与卡特里尔世系的「山印第安」酋长们缔结和约，后者对这片山区的权威得到承认；而西班牙人的牧场始终没有越过北方远处的萨拉多河。年复一年，埃尔凯鲁照常交易篷乔、兽皮和牛只，与此同时，阿劳卡诺化把马普切的语言和习俗带进了在这些山谷栖居的特维尔切人家族。拉普拉塔总督区时期，西班牙远征队的侦察最远只到坦迪尔，西部山地从未建起堡垒。1821年，塔帕尔凯一带仍完全处在萨拉多河以南未被征服的印第安「荒漠」之中。

en:
Chañar lies on the dry passage from the Cuyo uplands to the southern pampa, around the western streams that run toward the Desaguadero-Chadileuvú and Colorado rivers. In 1444 this was Diuihet country, one of the nomadic Het groupings later described by Thomas Falkner between about 35° and 38° south, east of the Pehuenche. Families followed guanaco, deer and rhea, gathered wild seeds and sweet chañar pods, and used boleadoras in open steppe and thorn scrub. Their camps shifted with water and game, and no Spanish road, fort or mission yet controlled the land.

Spanish towns grew in Cuyo without subduing this steppe. Pehuenche and Huilliche raiders crossed it on the way to San Luis in 1712, and in 1740 Cangapol's allied plains nations passed through the region during their great raid toward Buenos Aires. From the late seventeenth century, Pehuenche and Mapuche movement eastward tied local Het bands into Araucanized trading and raiding networks; Falkner recorded the Diuihet division in 1774. By the last colonial decades the surviving communities were being absorbed into the Pampa and Ranquel world. The Ranquel confederation then kept its independence between the Chadileuvú and Salinas Grandes, while the Camino de los Chilenos carried salt and stolen cattle toward the Neuquén passes and Chile. In 1821, with Spanish rule collapsing, no settled frontier government yet controlled Chañar.
zh:
查尼亚尔位于库约山地通向南方潘帕斯的干旱通道上，西部分别流向德萨瓜德罗—查迪莱乌武河与科罗拉多河的溪流纵横。1444年，这里是迪维特人的土地；迪维特是托马斯·福克纳后来记载的Het游牧支系之一，活动在南纬35度至38度之间、佩温切人以东。各家追逐原驼、鹿和美洲鸵，采集野生籽粒与甜美的查尼亚尔豆，在开阔草原和灌丛中使用投石索。营地随水源和猎物迁移，没有西班牙道路、堡垒或传教站控制这片土地。

西班牙人在库约建立城镇后，长期没有征服这片草原。1712年，佩温切人与维利切人的突袭队伍经此前往圣路易斯；1740年，坎加波尔联合草原诸部，向布宜诺斯艾利斯发动大规模突袭时也穿过这一带。从17世纪末起，佩温切人和马普切人向东移动，把本地Het群体纳入阿劳卡尼化的贸易与劫掠网络；福克纳在1774年记录下迪维特这一分支。到殖民时代末期，遗存群体正融入潘帕斯和兰克尔世界。此后，兰克尔联盟在查迪莱乌武河与大盐沼之间保持独立，「智利人之路」则把盐和掠来的牲畜运往内乌肯山口和智利。1821年西班牙统治崩溃时，仍没有定居的边疆政府控制查尼亚尔。

en:
San Antonio is the deep bay cut into the arid plateau on the northern shore of the San Matías Gulf. In 1444 mobile bands that later European observers grouped with the Het or ancient Pampas peoples and the northern Tehuelches moved along this coast, hunting guanaco and rhea, gathering wild seeds and using boleadoras in open country. The inlet offered shelter and a landmark between the Río Negro and the great gulf, but no permanent Spanish post yet stood there.

Ferdinand Magellan reached the gulf on St Matthias's day, 24 February 1520, and gave it the name it still bears. For more than two and a half centuries the bay remained chiefly a coastal reference for passing ships. After the Spanish founded Fuerte San José in January 1779 and Carmen de Patagones that April, Basilio Villarino, captain of the brig Nuestra Señora del Carmen, surveyed the area of the future Puerto de San Antonio between 25 October 1780 and 1 January 1781.
zh:
圣安东尼奥是圣马蒂亚斯湾北岸干旱高原上凹入的深水海湾。1444年，后来欧洲观察者归入海特人（古潘帕人）与北特维尔切人的游群在这一带海岸活动，在旷野中猎取原驼和美洲鸵、采集野生种子并使用投石索。这座海湾为内格罗河与圣马蒂亚斯湾之间的航路提供庇护和方位，但此时还没有西班牙人的常设据点。

1520年2月24日圣马蒂亚斯日，斐迪南·麦哲伦抵达这片海湾并为其命名，圣马蒂亚斯湾之名由此沿用下来。此后两个半世纪里，这里主要只是过往船只辨认海岸的标志。1779年1月西班牙人建立圣何塞堡，同年4月又建立卡门-德帕塔戈内斯；随后，「卡门圣母」号双桅船船长巴西利奥·比亚里诺在1780年10月25日至1781年1月1日间测绘了后来的圣安东尼奥港一带。

en:
The shores of San Julián Bay, where Florida Blanca would later be built, were Aónikenk Tehuelche country. In 1444 bands moved between the coast and the interior steppe, wintering near sheltered inlets to fish, gather shellfish and hunt seals, then following guanaco and rhea inland in summer. There was no permanent town for Europeans to seize; the bay's value lay in fresh water, anchorage and a little shelter from the Patagonian wind.

Magellan reached the anchorage on 31 March 1520 and wintered there for five months. Contact with the tall Aónikenk gave Europeans the name Patagonians, while a mutiny against Magellan ended in executions on the shore. Francis Drake arrived on 15 June 1578, found the old gallows and overwintered as well; Thomas Doughty was tried and beheaded there before Drake sailed to the Strait of Magellan in August. Spain tried to secure the coast only on 19 April 1780, when Antonio de Viedma founded Nueva Colonia y Fuerte de Floridablanca for Charles III, naming it for José Moñino, Count of Floridablanca, the crown's chief minister. Roughly 150 people were meant to support themselves by farming under an Enlightened plan of family holdings, but scurvy and hardship defeated the colony. It was abandoned and deliberately destroyed in 1784 so that no foreign power could use the bay.
zh:
后来修建佛罗里达布兰卡的圣胡利安湾海岸，本是阿奥尼肯克·特维尔切人的土地。1444年，各群体在岸边与内陆草原之间迁徙：冬季住在可避风寒的海湾附近捕鱼、拾贝、猎海豹，夏季进入内陆追踪原驼和美洲鸵。这里没有可供欧洲人夺取的常设城镇，海湾的价值在于淡水、锚地和稍能阻挡巴塔哥尼亚强风的地形。

1520年3月31日，麦哲伦到达这座锚地并在此过冬五个月。欧洲人与高大的阿奥尼肯克人相遇，由此有了「巴塔哥尼亚人」的称呼；一场反对麦哲伦的哗变也以岸边处决告终。1578年6月15日，弗朗西斯·德雷克抵达，见到旧日绞架并同样在此越冬；托马斯·道蒂受审后被斩首，德雷克随后在8月驶往麦哲伦海峡。西班牙直到1780年4月19日才试图巩固这片海岸：安东尼奥·德·别德马为卡洛斯三世建立「佛罗里达布兰卡新殖民地与要塞」，并以国王首席大臣佛罗里达布兰卡伯爵何塞·莫尼尼奥命名。约150名居民本应按照启蒙时代的家庭农场计划务农自给，但坏血病和严酷环境摧垮了殖民地。1784年，居民撤离并主动毁掉设施，以免它被外国势力利用。

en:
The dry steppe between the Río Negro and Chubut is broken by wet hollows, stony mesetas and rivers such as the Senguerr. In 1444 nomadic Tehuelche bands, later recorded by Spaniards as Patagones, moved seasonally between winter lowlands and summer uplands, following guanaco and rhea. Skin-tent camps, kinship and trade linked the interior to the Atlantic shore and the Andean valleys; no outside power yet commanded the grasslands.

Magellan's meeting with Tehuelche people at San Julián in 1520 spread the European name Patagonia, but settlement long clung to the coast. Horses, known to Tehuelche bands from about 1570, gradually extended their hunts and raids. During the eighteenth century, exchange with the Pampas and Araucanía carried Mapuche speech and customs into the steppe. Spain founded San José de la Candelaria on Península Valdés in 1779, reduced it to a fort in 1784, and Tehuelche warriors destroyed it on 7 August 1810. Around 1820 Patagones and Pehuenches fought on the Senguerr, proof that the interior remained indigenous country.
zh:
内格罗河与丘布特河之间是干旱草原，间杂湿草甸、石质台地和森格尔河等水道。1444年，逐原驼和美洲鸵而居的特维尔切诸群体在此游牧，冬季移往低地，夏季登上高原。他们住在兽皮帐篷中，凭亲属关系和交换把内陆、大西洋沿岸与安第斯谷地连接起来；此时还没有外来势力能够统治这片草原。

1520年，麦哲伦一行在圣胡利安与特维尔切人相遇，巴塔哥尼亚这个欧洲名称由此传播开来，但欧洲人的定居点长期只依附海岸。约1570年起，特维尔切群体开始使用马匹，狩猎和袭掠的范围随之扩大。18世纪，与潘帕斯和阿劳卡尼亚的贸易把马普切语言和习俗带入草原。西班牙于1779年在瓦尔德斯半岛建立圣何塞·德·拉坎德拉里亚，1784年将其降为要塞，1810年8月7日被特维尔切战士摧毁。约1820年，巴塔哥尼亚人与佩文切人又在森格尔河畔交战，可见此时内陆草原仍掌握在原住民手中。

en:
Poya is a country of cold lakes, volcanic cordillera and forested passes behind mainland Chiloé. The Poya, also called Ténesch, were a northern Tehuelche people living on both Andean slopes and around the eastern and southern shores of Nahuel Huapi. In 1444 family bands lived in skin tents, followed guanaco and choique under chosen chiefs, and gathered roots, wild fruit and llao-llao fungus. They had not yet adopted horses, and the trails from Chilean fjords toward the eastern steppe remained under their own control.

Captain Juan Fernández crossed the mountains to Nahuel Huapi in 1620 and found Puelche and Poya camps nearby. The Jesuit Diego de Rosales crossed from Chile in 1650, and Nicolás Mascardi founded the Nahuel Huapi mission in February 1670 after returning freed Poya prisoners from Chiloé. He planted the first apple trees and in 1672 followed the Limay and Negro rivers to the Atlantic, but opposing Poya killed him in 1674 and the mission was abandoned. Felipe Laguna restored it in 1703 and was poisoned in 1707. Juan José Guillelmo opened the Vuriloche Pass in 1715; Puelches then burned the station for fear it would mark a slaving road, Guillelmo was killed in 1716, and Francisco Elguea and the rebuilt houses were destroyed in 1717. Franciscan expeditions from Chiloé reached the lakes in 1792 and returned through 1795 without re-establishing a permanent mission. By then horses had transformed Poya hunting, and Mapuche-speaking neighbours knew the mountain people as Vuriloche.
zh:
波亚是奇洛埃大陆后方一片由冰寒湖泊、火山山脉和林中山口组成的土地。波亚人也称特内施人，是北巴塔哥尼亚人的一支，生活在安第斯山两坡以及纳韦尔瓦皮湖的东岸和南岸一带。1444年，家族队伍住在兽皮帐篷中，由酋长率领着追逐原驼和小美洲鸵，并采集块根、野果与利亚奥—利亚奥菌。此时他们尚未获得马匹，从智利峡湾通向东部草原的山路仍掌握在自己手中。

1620年，胡安·费尔南德斯队长越过山脉抵达纳韦尔瓦皮，在附近发现普埃尔切和波亚营地。耶稣会士迭戈·德·罗萨莱斯于1650年从智利翻山而来；1670年2月，尼古拉斯·马斯卡尔迪把从奇洛埃解救的波亚囚徒送返乡土地，并建立纳韦尔瓦皮传教站。他种下当地最早的苹果树，又在1672年沿利迈河和内格罗河抵达大西洋，但反对传教的波亚人在1674年将他杀死，传教站也遭废弃。费利佩·拉古纳1703年重建传教站，1707年被毒杀。胡安·何塞·吉列尔莫1715年开通武里洛切山口，普埃尔切人担心这会成为贩奴通道，随即焚毁站点；吉列尔莫在1716年被杀，弗朗西斯科·埃尔格亚与重建的房舍也在1717年被毁。1792年，从奇洛埃出发的方济各会探险队抵达湖区，并在1795年前多次往返，却未能重建常驻传教站。到这时，马匹已经改变波亚人的狩猎方式，说马普敦贡语的邻人则把这些山地人称为武里洛切。

en:
Chiquiyami covers the arid Andean edge south of Cuyo, where the Atuel, Diamante and Barrancas rivers cut down from the Malargüe highlands toward the eastern plains. In 1444 its mobile bands belonged to the southern Huarpe kinship world and were later included among the people whom Mapudungun speakers called Puelche. They lived by hunting and gathering and traded with Huarpe villages farther north, where maize, quinoa and beans were grown. Their camps lay between Huarpe country, the Pehuenche mountains and the Het steppe, with no Spanish town yet in the valleys.

Francisco de Villagra explored the district in December 1552 with seventy horsemen. After Pedro del Castillo founded Mendoza on 2 March 1561, Spanish estates and labour systems fixed themselves on the northern Cuyo oases rather than these southern ranges. The Pehuenche rising of 1769 carried war down the Malargüe trails toward Mendoza. In 1770 a Pehuenche band displaced by the fighting in Chile crossed to Malargüe and in December attacked the newly built Fort San Carlos; the Parliament of Negrete in February 1771 calmed the Chilean frontier, but the eastern valleys remained under indigenous leaders. In 1816 San Martín met Pehuenche chiefs at San Carlos to seek men and supplies for his crossing of the Andes. After the Battle of the Biobío on 19 January 1819, the Pincheira royalists withdrew to the eastern cordillera and, with Pehuenche and Huilliche allies, used Atuel, Varvarco and Epulafquen as refuges and cattle routes. In 1821 Mendoza was ruled by its independent government, while Chiquiyami remained a mountain land beyond the frontier.
zh:
齐奎亚米位于库约以南的干旱安第斯边缘，阿图埃尔河、迪亚曼特河和巴兰卡斯河从马拉圭山地切过，流向东部荒原。1444年，这里的游动群体属于南瓦尔佩亲属圈，后来也被归入说马普敦贡语者所称的普埃尔切人之中。他们以狩猎采集为生，并与北面种植玉米、藜麦和豆类的瓦尔佩村落交换物产。营地处在瓦尔佩土地、佩温切山地与Het草原之间，河谷中还没有西班牙城镇。

1552年12月，弗朗西斯科·德·比利亚格拉率七十名骑兵勘探这一地区。佩德罗·德尔·卡斯蒂略1561年3月2日建立门多萨后，西班牙人的地产和劳役体系集中在北面的库约绿洲，没有深入这些南部山地。1769年佩温切人大起事后，战火沿马拉圭山路蔓延到门多萨。1770年，一支被智利战事逼迫的佩温切群体翻山到马拉圭落脚，并在12月攻打当年新建的圣卡洛斯堡；1771年2月的内格雷特议会缓和了智利前线，东部山谷却仍掌握在原住民首领手中。1816年，圣马丁在圣卡洛斯与佩温切首领会谈，为翻越安第斯山争取人力和补给。1819年1月19日比奥比奥战役后，平切拉保王派退到山脉东坡，联合佩温切人和维利切人，把阿图埃尔、巴尔瓦尔科和埃普拉夫肯湖一带当作庇护所与贩牛通道。1821年，门多萨已由独立派政府统治，齐奎亚米却仍是边界之外的山地。

en:
Chiloé is the large green island at the heart of a rainy archipelago, separated from the mainland by the Chacao Channel. The Piuchén and Pirulil highlands run through it, forests and swamps cover the wetter west, and calmer eastern and northern coves open onto the Sea of Chiloé. In 1444 Chono canoe parties hunted, fished and gathered shellfish, while Huilliche and Cunco communities grew potatoes, maize and beans and kept llamas. Their dalca boats linked coves and smaller islands. The later name Chiloé comes from Huilliche and means the place of the chelles gull; the island's life already belonged more to sea routes than to mainland chiefdoms.

Alonso de Camargo sighted the coast in 1540, Francisco de Ulloa entered the Chacao Channel and explored the islands in 1553, and García Hurtado de Mendoza claimed the archipelago for the Spanish Crown in 1558. Conquest began in 1567 with the foundation of Castro, first called New Galicia. In 1600 the Dutch corsair Baltazar de Cordes and local Huilliches captured Castro, but a Spanish counterattack forced him to withdraw northward. Jesuits reached the islands at the turn of the seventeenth century and built a circuit of chapels; seventy-nine stood there by their expulsion in 1767, and Franciscans took over the mission in 1771. A Huilliche revolt against Spanish encomenderos began in early February 1712 and was crushed within a week, leaving several hundred Huilliches and several dozen Spaniards dead. During the Spanish American wars of independence Chiloé remained a remote royalist enclave: a patriot expedition failed in 1820, and in 1821 the islands still remained under the Crown.
zh:
奇洛埃是这片多雨群岛中心的苍翠大岛，北隔查考海峡与大陆相望。皮乌琴和皮鲁利尔山地纵贯全岛，湿润西部遍布森林沼泽，东面与北面较平静的小湾朝向奇洛埃海。1444年，乔诺人的独木舟队伍在此狩猎、捕鱼、采集贝类，韦利切和昆科社群则种植马铃薯、玉米和菜豆，并饲养羊驼。他们的「达尔卡」舟往来于各个海湾和小岛之间。后来的奇洛埃一名出自韦利切语，意为「切莱斯鸥之地」；这里的生活也更依赖海路，而非大陆上的酋邦。

阿隆索·德·卡马戈1540年望见海岸，弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚1553年进入查考海峡并巡弋群岛，加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨则于1558年为西班牙王冠宣布占有。1567年，卡斯特罗建立，征服由此展开，新城初名新加利西亚。1600年，荷兰私掠船长巴尔塔萨尔·德·科德斯与当地韦利切人攻占卡斯特罗，但西班牙军队随即反击，迫使他向北撤退。耶稣会士在17世纪初抵达群岛，沿巡回传教路线建立小堂；到1767年被驱逐时已有79座，方济各会士于1771年接掌传教事务。1712年2月初，韦利切人起兵反抗西班牙委托监护主，起义一周内便遭战斗与屠杀镇压，数百名韦利切人和数十名西班牙人死亡。西属美洲独立战争期间，奇洛埃仍是偏远的保王据点；1820年独立派远征失败，到1821年群岛仍在西班牙王权统治下。

en:
Aysén is the glacier-carved threshold of Chilean Patagonia. The Guaitecas and Chonos islands guard its rainy coast, channels run south toward the Taitao Peninsula and Ofqui Isthmus, and the Andes, icefields and eastern grasslands rise behind them. In 1444 the channels between about 44° and 48° south belonged to Chono groups. They moved by canoe, men fishing and hunting sea lions while women gathered seaweed and shellfish; they kept dogs, wove rough dog-hair cloth, and in places planted small potato crops. South of Taitao lived Kawésqar canoe people, later called Alacaluf by outsiders, while Aónik'enk or Tehuelche hunters followed game on the open mainland. No town or outside chiefdom controlled these crossings.

Magellan's passage through the strait in 1520 led Spanish geography to associate the broken coast with Trapananda and the Lands of December, but the first recorded encounter with the Chonos came on Francisco de Ulloa's voyage of 1553, which reached the archipelago and Taitao. Between 1557 and 1679 the Spanish launched twelve religious expeditions; Jesuits from Castro visited the Guaitecas in 1612 at a Chono leader's invitation, building chapels and preparing local assistants, while raids from Chiloé also carried canoe people into servitude. In 1710, 166 Chonos of all ages came to Calbuco seeking peace and baptism; later about 600 were gathered on Guar Island, where a Jesuit mission was formed in 1717, though timber-cutters and settled life led most back to nomadism. The wreck of HMS Wager in the Guayaneco Islands in 1741 drew new Spanish attention. Mateo Abraham Evrard went to Wager Island in 1743, and Ferdinand VI ordered Fort San Fernando de Tenquehuén on Taitao in 1749, only for the post to be dismantled. Authorities later emptied parts of the archipelago to deny corsairs native support, and in 1821 Aysén still had no permanent Spanish town, only seasonal sea-lion and sea-otter hunters and cypress cutters from Chiloé.
zh:
艾森是智利巴塔哥尼亚由冰川塑造的门户。瓜伊特卡斯群岛与乔诺斯群岛屏障般横亘在多雨海岸外，水道向南通向泰陶半岛和奥夫基地峡，后方则耸立着安第斯山、冰原与东部草原。1444年，南纬约44度至48度间的水道属于各个乔诺人群。他们乘独木舟不断迁徙，男子捕鱼、捕猎海狮，妇女采集海藻和贝类；他们养狗，用狗毛织成粗布，也会在一些地点粗放种植马铃薯。泰陶半岛以南是卡韦斯卡尔独木舟人群，后来被外人称作阿拉卡卢夫；开阔大陆上则有阿奥尼肯克人，即特维尔切猎人追逐草原猎物。没有任何城镇或外来酋邦控制这些水道。

麦哲伦1520年穿过海峡后，西班牙地理学把这片破碎海岸与「特拉帕南达」和「十二月之地」的名称联系起来，但首次有记录地接触乔诺人，是弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚1553年抵达乔诺斯群岛和泰陶半岛的航行。1557年至1679年间，西班牙人组织了十二次宗教探险；1612年，卡斯特罗的耶稣会士应一位乔诺首领邀请前往瓜伊特卡斯，修建小堂并培养本地助手，而来自奇洛埃的掳掠也把一些独木舟居民带入奴役。1710年，166名各年龄段的乔诺人来到卡尔布科，请求和平与受洗；后来约六百人被安置到瓜尔岛，耶稣会1717年在那里设立传教站，但伐木者侵扰和定居生活使多数人重新回到游牧生活。1741年，英国军舰「韦杰号」在瓜亚内科群岛失事，使西班牙重新关注此地。马特奥·亚伯拉罕·埃夫拉尔1743年前往韦格岛，费尔南多六世1749年下令在泰陶半岛修建圣费尔南多·德·滕克文堡，该据点后来却被拆除。西班牙当局随后清空部分群岛，使私掠船得不到当地人支援；1821年的艾森仍没有西班牙常设城镇，只有来自奇洛埃、季节性捕猎海狮与海獭并采伐柏树的营地。

en:
The Chubut rises in the eastern foothills of the Andes and winds east across dry Patagonian tablelands; its Tehuelche name, chupat, means transparent. In 1444 the shallow river, its floodable bottomlands and the nearby Río Chico were seasonal country for nomadic Tehuelche bands. They hunted guanaco and rhea, camped in skin tents and used the valley as a corridor between winter lowlands, summer uplands and the Atlantic coast.

Magellan's ships sighted this coast in 1520. On 24 February 1535 Simón de Alcazaba, Charles V's governor of Nueva León, founded Puerto de los Leones near Camarones. He then marched inland to the Río Chico, where Tehuelche guides led his men for ten days toward a rumoured gold city; the party found only desolate steppe. Alcazaba was killed in a mutiny in May, and the settlement was abandoned on 17 June. Missionaries later crossed parts of Chubut, while horses and Mapuche trade reshaped Tehuelche life in the eighteenth century, but the river valley remained without a permanent Spanish town through 1821.
zh:
丘布特河发源于安第斯山东麓，蜿蜒向东穿过干旱的巴塔哥尼亚台地；特维尔切语称其为「丘帕特」，意思是透明。1444年，水浅的河道、会受洪水漫润的低地与邻近的奇科河，是特维尔切游牧群体的季节性天地。他们猎捕原驼和美洲鸵，在兽皮帐篷中扎营，把河谷当作冬季低地、夏季高地与大西洋海岸之间的通道。

1520年，麦哲伦的船队望见这片海岸。1535年2月24日，查理五世任命的新莱昂总督西蒙·德·阿尔卡萨瓦在卡马罗内斯附近建立莱昂港。随后他率军深入奇科河，特维尔切向导带他们走了十天，去寻找传说中的金城，却只见到荒凉草原。阿尔卡萨瓦在5月的哗变中被杀，据点也于6月17日废弃。后来传教士曾穿过丘布特部分地区，马匹和马普切贸易则在18世纪改变了特维尔切人的生活，但直到1821年，丘布特河谷仍没有永久性的西班牙城镇。

en:
Behind the harbours of Deseado and San Julián, stony canyons and semi-arid mesas rise from the Atlantic steppe toward the Chilean cordillera. In 1444 Teush was the country of the Teushen or Tehues, foot nomads placed between the Puelche to the north and the Aónikenk Tehuelche to the south. They lived by hunting guanaco and rhea, gathering seasonal foods and moving in small camps; their language was a close relative of Tehuelche.

Magellan's winter at San Julián in 1520 opened this coast to Europeans, but the interior remained beyond Spanish control. Thomas Cavendish named Port Desire in 1586 and met arrow resistance; Flores de León crossed the region in 1621 and Nicolás Mascardi in 1671–72, without founding lasting reductions. In 1780 Spanish colonists established Floridablanca near San Julián. The Aónikenk leader Julián Grande showed them a freshwater valley, and settlers exchanged goods for guanaco meat, but Charles III ordered the costly Patagonian establishments abandoned in 1783 and Floridablanca was dismantled in 1784. In 1821 the Teushen still held the inland hunting tracks.
zh:
德塞阿多港与圣胡利安港后方，石质峡谷和半干旱台地从大西洋草原向智利方向的安第斯山抬升。1444年，托伊施是特乌申人（又称特乌斯人）的土地；这些徒步游猎者北邻普埃尔切人，南接阿奥尼肯克特维尔切人。他们以猎捕原驼和美洲鸵、采集季节性食物为生，结成小型营地不断迁徙，所用语言与特维尔切语相近。

1520年麦哲伦在圣胡利安过冬，欧洲人由此认识这片海岸，但内陆仍不受西班牙控制。1586年，托马斯·卡文迪什将此地命名为德塞阿多港，并遭到弓箭抵抗；1621年弗洛雷斯·德·莱昂、1671至1672年尼古拉斯·马斯卡尔迪先后穿行这一地区，却未能建立持久的传教居留地。1780年，西班牙殖民者在圣胡利安附近建立佛罗里达布兰卡。特维尔切首领大胡利安为他们指出一处淡水谷地，殖民者也用货物交换原驼肉，但查理三世在1783年下令放弃耗费巨大的巴塔哥尼亚据点，佛罗里达布兰卡于1784年拆除。1821年时，特乌申人仍掌握着内陆猎道。

en:
Mendoza lies on the arid eastern foot of the Andes, where snowmelt rivers create irrigated oases between the mountains and the Pampas. In 1444 Huarpe farmers of the Agrelo heritage watered maize, beans, squash and quinoa in the northern and central valleys, while Puelche hunter-gatherers moved between the Barrancas and Diamante rivers. Inca power had not yet arrived; local tradition places Túpac Yupanqui's advance near Coquimbo only around 1470.

Francisco de Villagra's Chile-bound expedition wintered at Huentota in 1551 with 185 men and 500 horses and explored as far as the Diamante. Pedro del Castillo founded Mendoza del Nuevo Valle de La Rioja on 2 March 1561, naming it for Governor García Hurtado de Mendoza; the first settlement had 47 Spanish householders, 30 encomenderos and about 2,500 indigenous tributaries. Juan Jufré moved it two arquebus shots southwest on 28 March 1562 and briefly renamed it City of the Resurrection in the Province of the Huarpes, but Mendoza remained its name. As seat of the Cuyo corregimiento under Chile, the town built San Carlos fort in 1771 and San Juan Nepomuceno in 1772 against Mapuche expansion, then passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776. River works in 1788 expanded irrigated farming. The intendancy of Cuyo was restored in 1813 with Mendoza as its capital, and José de San Martín took charge in 1814. At El Plumerillo his powder works, foundry and cloth shops equipped the Army of the Andes, some 4,000 soldiers and 1,000 auxiliaries with 10,000 mules, which crossed into Chile in January 1817. The Cuyo government was dissolved on 1 March 1820; Tomás Godoy Cruz became Mendoza's governor on 3 July.
zh:
门多萨位于安第斯山东麓的干旱地带，融水河流在山地与潘帕斯之间滋养出灌溉绿洲。1444年，具有阿格雷洛文化传统的瓦尔佩农人在北部和中部谷地开渠，种植玉米、菜豆、南瓜和藜麦；普埃尔切狩猎采集者则在巴兰卡斯河与迪亚曼特河之间活动。印加势力此时尚未到达，当地传说把图帕克·尤潘基推进到科金博附近的时间放在约1470年。

1551年，弗朗西斯科·德·比亚格拉前往智利的队伍带着185名士兵和500匹马在温托塔过冬，并探索到迪亚曼特河一带。1561年3月2日，佩德罗·德尔·卡斯蒂略建立「新拉里奥哈谷地之门多萨」，以智利都督加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨命名；最初的居民点有47户西班牙人、30名委托监护主和约2500名纳贡原住民。1562年3月28日，胡安·胡弗雷把城向西南迁移两个火绳枪射程的距离，一度改名为「瓦尔佩省复活城」，但门多萨之名最终保留下来。作为智利治下库约裁判区的首府，这座城市于1771年修建圣卡洛斯堡，1772年修建圣胡安·内波穆塞诺堡，以抵御马普切人的扩张；1776年又转入拉普拉塔总督辖区。1788年的河渠工程扩大了灌溉农业。1813年，库约监督区恢复，以门多萨为首府，何塞·德·圣马丁于1814年接掌此地。他在埃尔普卢梅里略设火药厂、铸炮厂和被服工场，为安第斯军团装备约4000名士兵、1000名辅助人员和10000匹骡子，大军于1817年1月翻山进入智利。1820年3月1日，库约政府解散；托马斯·戈多伊·克鲁斯于7月3日成为门多萨省长。

en:
Matará takes its name from the Mataraes, a people linked to the Tonocoté who occupied the dry plains south of the Bermejo River between the 61st and 63rd meridians west. In 1444 their villages shared the western Chaco frontier with Vilela bands moving between the Bermejo and Salado rivers. Thorn forest, floodlands and seasonal lagoons supplied fish, game, carob and small cultivated fields, while tracks joined the Bermejo plains to Tonocoté lands around Santiago del Estero. No outside overlord yet ruled the Mataraes.

Spanish penetration turned this indigenous place into an encomienda. In 1584 Matará and nearby Guacara were assigned to settlers from Talavera de Esteco; after Alonso de Vera y Aragón founded Concepción in 1585 he claimed both villages, about seven leagues or 50 kilometres west of his new city, and the jurisdictional quarrel was carried to the Spanish king. Matará labor sustained Concepción. A census in 1622 recorded 638 Matará and Nogosna people in the encomienda. In 1631 a coalition of tribes destroyed Matará and killed much of Concepción's garrison; the survivors withdrew toward Corrientes, and Concepción's cabildo was dissolved in 1645. Some Mataraes later settled around Santiago del Estero. By 1821 no Spanish town remained at the old encomienda, while the surrounding bush stayed in Chaco hands.
zh:
马塔拉得名于马塔拉人；他们被视为与托诺科特人有关的族群，居住在贝尔梅霍河以南、西经61度至63度之间的干燥平原。1444年，他们的村落与活动在贝尔梅霍河、萨拉多河之间的维莱拉群体共同分享西查科边疆。刺林、河泛地和季节湖提供鱼、猎物、角豆和小块农田，小路则把贝尔梅霍平原与圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗一带的托诺科特土地连接起来。此时还没有外来领主统治马塔拉人。

西班牙人深入后，这个原住民地方变成委托监护地。1584年，马塔拉和附近的瓜卡拉被交给塔莱韦拉-德埃斯特科的殖民者；阿隆索·德·贝拉-阿拉贡1585年建立康塞普西翁后，宣称这两座位于新城以西约七里格、即五十公里处的村镇归自己管辖，司法争端最后上诉到西班牙国王。马塔拉的劳役支撑着康塞普西翁。1622年的人口清点记载，该监护区有六百三十八名马塔拉人和诺戈斯人。1631年，诸部族联军摧毁马塔拉，歼灭康塞普西翁的大部分驻军；幸存者退往科连特斯，康塞普西翁市议会也于1645年解散。后来一些马塔拉人在圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗一带定居。到1821年，旧监护地已无西班牙城镇存留，周围丛林仍掌握在查科诸族手中。

en:
Santa Tecla names a stretch of rolling pampa around the Rio Negro and Piraízinho, on the old line between the Guarani mission country, the River Plate garrisons, and the overland route toward Montevideo. In 1444 these grasslands were above all Charrua and Guenoa country; bands hunted the open camps and moved between waterholes and ridgeways, while Guarani-speaking travellers from the Uruguay valley crossed the same ground. No European fort had yet been planted there.

The Jesuit reduction of Santo André dos Guenoas was established in the region in 1683, and feral cattle later made the ridges a target of Spanish and Portuguese raiders. In January 1774 Juan José de Vértiz, governor of Buenos Aires, ordered the engineer Bernardo Lecocq to build a pentagonal Fort Santa Tecla, blocking Portuguese routes toward the missions and the Banda Oriental. Rafael Pinto Bandeira's guerrillas and Rio Pardo dragoons captured and dismantled it in 1776 after a long siege. The 1777 Treaty of San Ildefonso returned the border post to Spain, but in 1801 the Spanish abandoned and destroyed it during the War of the Oranges, leaving the district under Portuguese control. A military camp at the Cerros de Bagé in July 1811 became the nucleus of Bagé, and a chapel dedicated to Saint Sebastian was built there in 1820. By 1821 this was frontier cattle country around the memory of a demolished fort.
zh:
圣特克拉指内格罗河与皮拉伊齐纽河一带起伏的潘帕草原，旧处瓜拉尼传教区、拉普拉塔驻军和通往蒙得维的亚的陆路之间。1444年，这片草地主要是查鲁亚人与格诺阿人的土地；人群在开阔原野狩猎，在水源和山脊路之间移动，乌拉圭河谷讲瓜拉尼语的旅人也会经过这里。那时欧洲人尚未在此修建要塞。

1683年，耶稣会在这一地区建立圣安德烈-杜斯格诺阿斯归化村；后来野牧牛群使这些山脊成为西班牙和葡萄牙掠牛者争夺的目标。1774年1月，布宜诺斯艾利斯总督胡安·何塞·德·贝尔蒂斯下令工程师贝尔纳多·勒科克修建五边形的圣特克拉要塞，以阻断葡萄牙人通往传教区和东岸的道路。1776年，拉斐尔·平托·班德拉的游击队与里奥帕尔多龙骑兵经长期围攻攻占并拆除要塞。1777年的《圣伊尔德方索条约》使这个边堡重归西班牙，但1801年橘子战争期间，西班牙人撤离并摧毁它，地区落入葡萄牙控制。1811年7月，巴热丘陵的一座军营成为巴热的雏形；1820年，当地建起献给圣塞巴斯蒂昂的小教堂。到1821年，这里已是一座被毁要塞记忆环绕的边境牧地。

en:
Griqualand is a later political name. The dry grassland between the Vaal and Orange rivers, around the future Kimberley, was first Khoe-San country; hunter-foragers and herders knew its pans, springs and game routes, and stone tools at nearby Wildebeest Kuil recall that presence. Setswana-speaking farmers and cattle keepers later moved into the wider region from the north, organizing villages under chiefs and councils, but the Kimberley ridge itself had no recorded permanent town. In 1444 the mixed, Afrikaans-speaking Griqua community had not yet formed, and rivers, pans and springs rather than a colonial frontier governed movement.

During the eighteenth century, mounted Baster and Oorlam groups moved beyond the Cape and along the Orange River corridor. In 1801 William Anderson and Cornelius Kramer of the London Missionary Society opened a station at Leeuwenkuil among Chaguriqua Khoe and mixed Baster families; around 1805 it was moved to a higher, equally dry spring called Klaarwater. In 1813 the missionary John Campbell promoted the name Griqua in place of Baster, and Klaarwater became Griquatown, the core of Waterboer's Land under Andries Waterboer and Adam Kok II. Robert and Mary Moffat were staying there on their way to Kuruman when their daughter Mary was born in 1821, by which time the spring station linked Cape missionaries, Griqua horsemen and Tswana lands to the north.
zh:
格里夸兰是后世才有的政治名称。法尔河与奥兰治河之间、未来金伯利周围的干旱草原，最初是科伊桑人的土地；猎民和牧人熟悉盐盘、泉水和猎物通道，附近Wildebeest Kuil发现的石器仍显示他们曾在此活动。说茨瓦纳语的农民和牧牛者后来从北方迁入更广阔的区域，以酋长和议事会组织村落，但金伯利所在的山脊本身没有留下固定城镇的记载。1444年时，操南非荷兰语的混血格里夸共同体尚未形成；决定人们如何移动的是河流、盐盘和泉水，而不是殖民边疆。

18世纪，骑马的巴斯特人和奥拉姆人越过开普边疆，沿奥兰治河走廊移动。1801年，伦敦传道会的威廉·安德森和科内利斯·克拉默在Leeuwenkuil设立传教站，周围是查古里克瓦科伊人和混血巴斯特家庭；约1805年，传教站迁至一处更高、同样缺水的泉水，命名为Klaarwater。1813年，传教士约翰·坎贝尔推动以「格里夸」取代「巴斯特」一名，Klaarwater随后成为格里夸镇，也是安德里斯·沃特布尔和亚当·科克二世治下「沃特布尔之地」的核心。1821年，罗伯特·莫法特与妻子玛丽前往库鲁曼途中暂住于此，女儿玛丽在当地出生；此时这座泉水传教站已经把开普传教士、格里夸骑兵和北方茨瓦纳土地连接起来。

en:
Corumbá lies on the right bank of the Paraguay River where the seasonally flooded Pantanal plains stretch west toward Bolivia. Its lagoons were the country of the Guató, the canoe people, who lived in small family bands aboard dugout canoes and took fish and birds with the bow, while the Paiaguá ranged the river itself. In 1444 no European had yet entered this maze of floodland; its only roads were the waterways linking the Paraguay with the camps of the Mato Grosso plateau.

The first Spanish town, Santiago de Xerez, was founded in 1593, but it and the nearby Jesuit settlements were destroyed by bandeirantes raiding upstream from São Paulo; a Portuguese post at Camapuã followed in 1650. To secure the river against Spain, the governor of Mato Grosso, Luís de Albuquerque, had Forte Coimbra built from 13 September 1775, and in 1778 Sergeant-Major Marcelino Rois Camponês founded the Vila de Nossa Senhora da Conceição de Albuquerque, the settlement that would become Corumbá, on the last deep-water reach below the Serra de Albuquerque. In 1821 it was still a small garrison port serving the river traffic of Cuiabá and Cáceres.
zh:
科伦巴位于巴拉圭河右岸，季节性泛滥的潘塔纳尔平原从这里向西一直延伸到玻利维亚。潟湖之间是瓜托人的天地，他们被称为独木舟人，以小家族为单位住在挖空树干做成的独木舟上，靠弓箭捕鱼射鸟为生；帕亚瓜人则游弋于巴拉圭河上。1444年时还没有欧洲人进入这片水网之地，唯一的道路是连通巴拉圭河与马托格罗索高原各处营地的水道。

西班牙人1593年最早在这里建立圣地亚哥-德赫雷斯城，但这座城镇和附近的耶稣会定居点都被从圣保罗溯河而上劫掠的旗队探险者摧毁；葡萄牙人1650年在卡马庞设立据点。为防范西班牙、控制河道，马托格罗索都督路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克下令自1775年9月13日起修建科英布拉堡，1778年军士长马塞利诺·罗伊斯·坎波内斯又在阿尔布克尔克山以下最后一段深水河道旁建立「圣母受孕德阿尔布克尔克镇」，即后来的科伦巴。1821年时，这里仍是一座小小的驻防河港，为库亚巴和卡塞雷斯的河运服务。

en:
The steep hills above a bay of the Paraguay River, near the southern waters of the Pantanal, had no Spanish garrison in 1444. This was Mbayá and Guaná country: river people, hunters and mobile bands knew the crossings and seasonal floods, and the bluffs later chosen for a fort offered refuge in a land without towns. For more than two and a half centuries after contact, no colonial power could turn that river gateway into a secure frontier.

On 17 October 1791 the Viceroy of the Río de la Plata ordered a post built to check Portuguese advance and Mbayá raids. José Antonio Zavala y Delgadillo founded Fuerte Borbón on 25 September 1792, inviting Mbayá chiefs to the ceremony; José de Isasi became its first commander. The garrison of about a hundred men depended on convoys from Concepción and Charcas, and mistrust soon returned. Mbayá attacks in 1796 prompted a bloody reprisal at Concepción, and during the 1801 Spanish-Portuguese war an attempt against upstream Coimbra failed. In 1810 troops from Borbón fought Manuel Belgrano's expedition; after the post was abandoned it passed briefly through Mbayá and Portuguese hands before being returned. Around 1817 Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia strengthened it with a long stone wall, keeping the northern river gate of independent Paraguay.
zh:
1444年，巴拉圭河一处河湾上方、临近潘塔纳尔南缘的陡峭丘陵还没有西班牙驻军。这里是姆巴亚人和瓜纳人的土地：河畔居民、猎人和移动群体熟悉渡口与季节洪水，日后被选为要塞的高地也为这片没有城镇的土地提供了天然依托。欧洲人到来后的两个半世纪里，没有哪个殖民强权能把这座河上门户变成安全边界。

1791年10月17日，拉普拉塔总督下令设立据点，以阻挡葡萄牙推进和姆巴亚人袭掠。1792年9月25日，何塞·安东尼奥·萨瓦拉-德尔加迪略建立波旁堡，并邀请姆巴亚酋长出席建堡仪式，何塞·德·伊萨西任首任指挥官。约一百人的驻军依赖康塞普西翁和查尔卡斯运来的补给，双方的互不信任很快重现。1796年姆巴亚人袭击康塞普西翁，引发当地血腥报复；1801年西葡战争期间，西班牙人溯流攻打科英布拉堡的行动也告失败。1810年，波旁堡军队参加了对抗曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺远征的战斗；据点弃守后一度落入姆巴亚人和葡萄牙人之手，后因葡萄牙撤退而归还。约1817年，加斯帕尔·罗德里格斯·德·弗朗西亚加修一道长石墙，把这里维持为独立巴拉圭的北方河门。

en:
The Paraguay River banks and islands northwest of Asunción were Payaguá country in 1444. These Guaycuruan people, who called themselves Evueví or people of the river, moved in large dugouts between the Pantanal and downstream waters, fishing, hunting, gathering and raiding Guarani fields on the eastern shore. Behind them stretched the dry Chaco; on the water they were the power Spanish crews would later call river pirates.

After Asunción was founded in 1537, Payaguá canoes made the Paraguay unsafe for Spanish traffic. In 1613 the colony declared a 'war of fire and blood' against them and their Mbayá allies, but seventeenth-century yerba mate traffic often moved overland to avoid river raids. Policy changed after 1730, when officials sought trade and accommodation, and southern bands settled near Asunción around 1750. In 1786 Father Juan Francisco Amancio González y Escobar founded Reducción Melodía on this bank, naming it for Governor Pedro Melo de Portugal. The priest's departure left the reduction abandoned, and the place was remembered as Amancio Cué. By 1821 this frontier had a name and a river crossing, but no town strong enough to command the Chaco.
zh:
1444年，亚松森西北方的巴拉圭河岸与岛屿是帕亚瓜人的土地。他们自称埃武埃维，意为河上人，属瓜伊库鲁族群，划着大型独木舟在潘塔纳尔与下游水道之间往来，以渔猎、采集和袭击东岸瓜拉尼人的农田为生。他们身后是干旱的查科；在水上，他们正是后来西班牙船员口中的河流海盗。

1537年亚松森建立后，帕亚瓜人的独木舟使巴拉圭河对西班牙交通充满危险。1613年，殖民地对他们和姆巴亚盟友宣布「火与血之战」，但17世纪的马黛茶贸易仍常改走陆路，以避开河上袭掠。1730年后政策转向贸易与安抚，约1750年，南部帕亚瓜人开始在亚松森附近定居。1786年，神父胡安·弗朗西斯科·阿曼西奥·冈萨雷斯·伊·埃斯科瓦尔在这一岸建立梅洛迪亚传教村，以总督佩德罗·梅洛·德·葡萄牙的姓氏命名。神父离开后，传教村遭到废弃，旧址被称为阿曼西奥库埃。到1821年，这条边疆在这里有了名字和渡口，却仍没有一座足以控制查科的城镇。

en:
The grasslands and riverine forests east of the upper Uruguay, around the future São Borja, were Guarani country in 1444. Canoes and trails linked scattered villages along the river crossings, but no Spanish town or Jesuit reduction yet stood on this bank. The Uruguay was still an indigenous highway rather than an imperial boundary, and the peoples later gathered into the Seven Peoples of the Missions moved through its open campos and gallery woods beyond the reach of Spain or Portugal.

After bandeirantes had destroyed earlier Jesuit reductions in Guaíra and Tape, Spanish Jesuits returned to the region from 1682. Francisco Garcia founded São Francisco de Borja with 195 Guarani brought from São Tomé; it was the first of the Seven Peoples and held 2,814 people by 1707. Cattle herds, stone churches and planned plaza villages made the missions prosperous, but the Treaty of Madrid of 1750 assigned their east bank to Portugal in exchange for Colônia do Sacramento and ordered the Guarani moved west. Under Sepé Tiaraju they refused, opening the Guarani War of 1753–1756. At Caiboaté on 10 February 1756, 3,000 Spanish and Portuguese troops killed 1,511 Guarani at a cost of four European dead and occupied the seven reductions. The Treaty of El Pardo annulled the transfer in 1761 and returned the district to Spain, while the Jesuit expulsions of 1759 and 1767 had emptied the mission system by 1768. In 1801 a Portuguese force of only forty men under Manuel dos Santos Pedroso and José Borges do Canto seized the Seven Peoples, and São Borja was raised to a town on 13 October 1817.
zh:
乌拉圭河上游东岸、后来圣博尔哈所在的草原与河畔林地，在1444年属于瓜拉尼人。独木舟和小路连接着渡口附近散布的村落，但此时河岸还没有西班牙城镇，也没有耶稣会传道村。乌拉圭河仍是原住民的通道，而非帝国边界；后来被集中到七传道区的人群，正活动在开阔草原与林泽之间，不受西班牙或葡萄牙管辖。
