旗兵摧毁瓜伊拉和塔佩等地较早的耶稣会传道村后，西班牙耶稣会士从1682年起重返这一地区。弗朗西斯科·加西亚带着从圣多梅迁出的一百九十五名瓜拉尼人建立圣方济各·德·博尔哈；它是七传道区中的第一个，到1707年已有二千八百一十四人。牛群、石砌教堂和按广场规划的村落使传道区繁盛起来，但1750年的《马德里条约》把乌拉圭河东岸划给葡萄牙，以交换科洛尼亚-德尔萨克拉门托，并命令瓜拉尼人西迁。他们在塞佩·蒂亚拉茹领导下拒绝，1753—1756年瓜拉尼战争爆发。1756年2月10日的凯博阿特之战中，三千名西葡军队杀死一千五百一十一名瓜拉尼人，己方仅死四人，随后占领七座传道村。1761年《埃尔帕多条约》废除这次转让，地区归还西班牙；而1759年和1767年耶稣会先后遭葡萄牙、西班牙驱逐，到1768年传道体系已经瓦解。1801年，曼努埃尔·多斯桑托斯·佩德罗索和若泽·博尔热斯·多坎托率领仅四十人的葡萄牙部队夺取七传道区；1817年10月13日，圣博尔哈升格为镇。

en:
Barra guards the meeting of the Rio Grande and São Francisco, where seasonally flooded river flats and gallery forests cut through the northeastern sertão. In 1444 the confluence was Xakriabá country; these Akwé-speaking Ge people also occupied stretches of the Tocantins valley, moving between riverine woods, hunting grounds and inland trails.

In 1670 Dias d'Ávila's Casa da Torre, one of Bahia's powerful cattle and landholding houses, opened a corral on the Rio Grande ravines. Franciscans raised a chapel in 1680, and cattle pens, ferries and boat traffic on the São Francisco turned the spot into an interior river station. In 1752 the settlement was raised to a town as Vila de São Francisco do Rio Grande.
zh:
巴拉扼守格兰德河汇入圣弗朗西斯科河之处，季节性河滩与走廊林穿过东北部内陆荒原。1444年，这个河口是舍克里厄巴人的土地；他们属于说阿克温语的热依人，也活动于托坎廷斯河谷，往来利用河畔林地、猎场和内陆小径。

1670年，迪亚斯·达维拉的卡萨达托雷在格兰德河坡地设立牧栏，这是巴伊亚最有势力的畜牧与地产家族之一。方济各会于1680年建起礼拜堂，牛栏、渡口和圣弗朗西斯科河上的船运逐渐把这里变成内陆水路驿站。1752年，定居点升格为城镇，称圣弗朗西斯科-杜里奥格兰德镇。

en:
Parnaíba takes in the only open-sea delta of the Americas, where the great river splits into the Igaraçu and a web of mangrove channels before the Atlantic. In 1444 the shores were the country of the Tremembé, who fished the shoals and crossed the river mouths in canoes; the river's Tupi name means muddy-water river. Portuguese vessels reconnoitred the coast in the sixteenth century, and Jesuits began work among the Indians in 1607, but no town yet stood among the dunes.

Cattle changed all that. As ranchers occupied the Parnaíba valley, the baptized Indian Mandu Ladino rose in 1712 and for seven years led Tupi and Cariri bands through the sertões of Piauí, Maranhão and Ceará, burning fazendas; an expedition of 1716, raised with Tabajara allies from the Serra da Ibiapaba, broke the rising, and Mandu Ladino was mortally wounded and drowned in the Parnaíba. In 1758 Domingos Dias da Silva set up a charqueada and founded Porto das Barcas, and in 1762 Governor João Pereira Caldas installed the Vila de São João da Parnaíba, which became an entrepôt for dried beef and leather and took the name Parnaíba in 1801. In 1821 its quays still handled the cattle products of the Piauí sertão.
zh:
巴纳伊巴一带坐拥美洲唯一的入海三角洲，大河在注入大西洋前汊出伊加拉苏河和一片红树林水道。1444年，两岸是特雷门贝人的地盘，他们在浅滩捕鱼，划独木舟穿行河口；大河的图皮语名字意为「浑水河」。16世纪有葡萄牙船只侦察这段海岸，耶稣会士从1607年起向印第安人传教，但沙丘之间还没有城镇。

改变一切的是牛。牧人占据巴纳伊巴河谷后，受洗的印第安人曼杜·拉迪诺于1712年起事，七年间率领图皮人和卡里里人转战皮奥伊、马拉尼翁和塞阿拉的荒原，焚毁牧场；1716年，一支在伊比亚帕巴山得到塔巴哈拉人助战的讨伐队镇压了起义，曼杜·拉迪诺受伤后溺死在巴纳伊巴河中。1758年，多明戈斯·迪亚斯·达席尔瓦开设腌肉作坊、建立巴尔卡斯港；1762年，若昂·佩雷拉·卡尔达斯都督设立圣若昂达巴纳伊巴镇，这里成为腌肉和皮革的贸易站，1801年改名巴纳伊巴。1821年时，码头上装卸的仍是皮奥伊荒原出产的牛肉制品和皮革。

en:
Santa Catarina is the long island guarding a chain of Atlantic anchorages on the southern Brazilian coast, with mainland bays and the Serra do Mar behind it. In 1444 the Carijó, a Tupi-Guarani people, knew the island as Meiembipe, the mountain beside the channel. Their villages combined maize and manioc gardens with fishing and shellfish gathering, and canoes crossed the sheltered strait later used by ships bound for the River Plate.

Portuguese navigators named the island Ilha dos Patos around 1514 and Ilha de Santa Catarina in 1526, but permanent settlement began only in 1673, when Francisco Dias Velho brought settlers to the shore; a chapel dedicated to Nossa Senhora do Desterro followed in 1678. The crown made the community a parish in 1714 and a town in 1726, then created the island captaincy by an 11 August 1738 charter and appointed José da Silva Paes its governor. From 1739 the forts of Santa Cruz de Anhatomirim, São José da Ponta Grossa and Santo Antônio de Ratones secured the northern anchorage. From 1748 onward about six thousand Azorean and Madeiran families reached the coast, expanding farms and cotton and linen production. In February 1777 Pedro de Cevallos's Spanish expedition seized the island, but the Treaty of San Ildefonso on 1 October 1777 returned it to Portugal. By 1821 Desterro was an Azorean fishing, provisioning and garrison port on the road to the River Plate.
zh:
圣卡塔琳娜是一座狭长岛屿，扼守巴西南部大西洋上的一串锚地，岛后是大陆海湾和马尔山。1444年，图皮-瓜拉尼人的一支卡里若人把此岛称为梅因比佩，意为水道旁的山。他们的村落既种玉米和木薯，也捕鱼、采集贝类；独木舟往来于遮蔽良好的海峡，后来这条水路也服务于前往拉普拉塔河的船只。

约1514年，葡萄牙航海者把此岛命名为鸭岛，1526年改称圣卡塔琳娜岛，但永久定居到1673年才开始：弗朗西斯科·迪亚斯·维略率领移民登岸，1678年又建起献给流亡圣母的小教堂。王室先后在1714年将此地设为堂区、1726年升为镇，1738年8月11日颁布敕令设立岛都督辖区，并任命若泽·达席尔瓦·派斯为总督。1739年起，阿尼亚托米林圣十字、蓬塔格罗萨圣若泽和拉托内斯圣安多尼等要塞锁住北方锚地。1748年起，约六千名亚速尔和马德拉移民抵达海岸，扩展农庄并发展棉花与麻布生产。1777年2月，佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯的西班牙远征队夺取岛屿，但1777年10月1日的《圣伊尔德方索条约》又将其归还葡萄牙。到1821年，德斯泰罗已是亚速尔渔民的补给港和驻军港，扼守通往拉普拉塔河的航路。

en:
The Cuiabá country lies around the Cuiabá and Coxipó rivers, where tropical forest gives way to scrubland and seasonal floodplains. Its Bororo name is commonly explained as the place of the ikuia, a fishing arrow; Coxiponé people lived along the riverbanks when European power was still far away. In 1444 their villages, fishing grounds and forest trails belonged to no Portuguese captaincy, while the rivers feeding the Paraguay linked the region to wider indigenous networks.

Manoel de Campos Bicudo passed through in 1673 and 1682 and founded the short-lived São Gonçalo Beira-Rio. Pascoal Moreira Cabral reached the abandoned site in 1718; after a clash with Coxiponé warriors, his party found gold, and the founding act of Cuiabá was recorded at Forquilha on 8 April 1719. A richer strike was made in October 1722 by enslaved Indians working for Miguel Sutil, drawing miners to the Prainha stream. Rodrigo César de Menezes raised the settlement to Vila Real do Senhor Bom Jesus de Cuiabá on 1 January 1727. The gold soon proved thinner than hoped. The Captaincy of Mato Grosso was created in 1748, and after Antônio Rolim de Moura arrived in 1751 he established Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade as its capital. Cuiabá remained a riverside mining and supply town until it received city rank on 17 September 1818.
zh:
库亚巴一带位于库亚巴河与科希波河沿岸，热带雨林在此过渡为灌丛草原和季节性洼地。博罗罗语常把它解释为使用「伊库亚」渔箭的地方；1444年时，欧洲人的势力还远在大西洋沿岸，科希波内人住在河畔，村落、渔场和林中小径都不属于任何葡萄牙都督辖区，汇入巴拉圭河的水路则把这里接入更广的原住民交流网络。

曼努埃尔·德·坎波斯·比库多曾在1673年和1682年经过此地，建立起短暂存在的圣贡萨洛·贝拉-里奥。1718年，帕斯科阿尔·莫雷拉·卡布拉尔抵达这个废弃地点；他的队伍与科希波内武士交战后发现黄金，1719年4月8日在福基利亚登记了库亚巴的建置文书。1722年10月，为米格尔·苏蒂尔劳作的被奴役印第安人在普赖尼亚溪找到更富的矿脉，淘金人随即涌来。1727年1月1日，罗德里戈·塞萨尔·德·梅内塞斯将定居点升格为维拉·雷亚尔·杜·塞尼奥尔·邦热苏斯·德·库亚巴。金矿不久便证明不如预期丰厚。马托格罗索都督辖区于1748年设立，安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1751年到任后，把维拉贝拉达桑蒂西马特林达德建为首府。库亚巴此后长期是河畔采矿与补给城镇，1818年9月17日才升格为市。

en:
Rio Branco covers the upper valley of the Branco, where the Uraricoera and Tacutu meet before the river runs south toward the Negro. Carib-speaking Macushi lived along its savanna streams and gallery woods, while Arawak-speaking Wapishana held country to the east. High water opened the lower Branco to canoes from the Negro, and in 1444 the valley remained in Indigenous hands, its villages linked by river travel, fishing, manioc fields and regional trade.

Carmelite missionaries began work here in 1725, and Portuguese raiders and troops pushed up the Branco in the 1730s, seeking captives and forest products while securing a frontier against Dutch, English and Spanish rivals. The Portuguese built São Joaquim Fort at the Uraricoera-Tacutu confluence in 1775-1778, then placed mission villages along the rivers. In 1789 Manuel da Gama Lôbo d'Almada introduced cattle and horses, and the São Bento, São José and São Marcos ranches followed between 1793 and 1799. An English incursion in 1810-1811 was driven back from the valley.
zh:
里奥布朗库位于布朗库河上游，乌拉里奎拉河与塔库图河在此汇合，河水随后向南流入内格罗河。说加勒比语的马库希人居住在稀树草原的水道与林泽间，说阿拉瓦克语的瓦皮沙纳人则生活在东面土地。涨水时，独木舟可从内格罗河驶入布朗库河下游。1444年，河谷仍掌握在原住民手中，村落依靠河运、渔猎、木薯田和区域贸易往来。

1725年，加尔默罗会传教士开始在此传教；1730年代，葡萄牙劫掠队和军队沿布朗库河而上，掳掠人口、搜集林产品，并把这里作为对抗荷兰、英格兰和西班牙竞争者的边疆。1775—1778年，葡萄牙人在乌拉里奎拉河与塔库图河交汇处修建圣若阿金堡垒，随后在沿河设置传教村。1789年，曼努埃尔·达·加马·洛博·德·阿尔马达引入牛和马，圣本图、圣若泽和圣马科斯牧场随后在1793—1799年间建立。1810—1811年，一支进入河谷的英格兰武装被击退。

en:
Marajó is the great fluviomarine island between the Amazon mouth, the Pará channels and the Atlantic. Its indigenous name was Marinatambal. Seasonal floods shaped life on the island: for centuries river peoples had raised villages on artificial earthen mounds called tesos, planted manioc, fished the maze of channels and made decorated Marajoara pottery. In 1444 the Aruã phase of that long mound-building tradition was still underway, and the island's fishermen and canoe-warriors controlled the approaches between river and sea.

European ships entering the Amazon estuary in the sixteenth century brought trade, raids and epidemic disease, severely weakening the island's indigenous populations. On 23 December 1665 the Portuguese crown granted the island as the captaincy of Ilha Grande de Joanes, named for the Joanes people, to António de Sousa Macedo; his proxy took possession in 1667. The grant commanded strategic channels at the Amazon mouth, while natural grasslands supported cattle and hide production for Belém and the Atlantic trade. In 1696 Luís Gonçalo de Sousa Macedo gave lands near the Arari River to Capuchin friars for missions and settlement, and religious cattle ranches became a feature of the island. The crown bought the captaincy back on 29 April 1754 and placed Marajó under Grão-Pará, tightening royal control over the Amazon entrance on the eve of the Jesuit expulsion.
zh:
马拉若是横亘在亚马逊河口、帕拉河水道与大西洋之间的巨大河海岛屿，印第安人原称马里纳坦巴尔。季节性洪水塑造了岛上生活：多个世纪以来，河畔民族把村落建在名为特索的人工土丘上，种植木薯，在迷宫般的水道中捕鱼，并制作纹饰精美的马拉若陶。1444年，这一悠久筑丘传统的阿鲁昂阶段仍在延续，岛上渔民和独木舟战士控制着河海之间的通道。

16世纪，进入亚马逊河口的欧洲船只带来贸易、袭掠和传染病，使岛上印第安人口遭受重创。1665年12月23日，葡萄牙王室把全岛封赐为大若阿内斯岛都督领，名称来自若阿内斯人，受封者是安东尼奥·德索萨·马塞多；其代理人于1667年正式接管。这片封地扼守亚马逊河口的战略水道，天然草场则为贝伦和大西洋贸易提供牛只与皮革。1696年，路易斯·贡萨洛·德索萨·马塞多把阿拉里河附近土地赠予嘉布遣会修士，用于传教和定居，教会牧场由此成为岛上一景。1754年4月29日，王室购回都督领，将马拉若并入格劳帕拉管辖，在驱逐耶稣会前夕加强了对亚马逊入口的王室控制。

en:
Santo Antônio da Manga covers a stretch of the left bank of the São Francisco, between the mouths of the Urucuia and Paracatu and the Ribeirão da Conceição. In 1444 the river, its wooded islands and the surrounding sertão were Kaiapó country; an island later called São Romão held an indigenous village whose people lived by the river before Portuguese backwoodsmen and slave-raiding bands entered the middle São Francisco.

The Portuguese arraial of Santo Antônio da Manga was founded on 23 October 1668 on that left bank, taking its name from the saint of the day. The island opposite became a battleground between fugitives, runaway slaves, remnants of earlier expeditions and colonial patrols, and tradition placed the destruction of the Kaiapó village there on a feast of Saint Romanus before 1712. In 1736 the settlement was a centre of the Motins do Sertão, when backcountry men led by Pedro Cardoso rose against colonial taxation, half a century before the Minas conspiracy. As the first river port and judicial seat on the middle São Francisco, the arraial shipped gold, coin and precious stones brought from Goiás and Mato Grosso toward the coast.
zh:
圣安东尼奥-达曼加位于圣弗朗西斯科河左岸，地当乌鲁库亚河、帕拉卡图河与孔塞桑溪之间。1444年时，大河、林木覆盖的岛屿和周围腹地都是卡亚波人的土地；后来被称为圣罗芒的岛上曾有印第安村落，居民傍水而居，直到葡萄牙腹地开拓者和捕奴队进入圣弗朗西斯科河中游。

1668年10月23日，葡萄牙人在河左岸建立圣安东尼奥-达曼加村，村名来自当日的圣徒。对岸岛屿后来成为逃犯、逃亡奴隶、旧远征队残部与殖民巡逻队交战之地；相传在1712年以前的一个圣罗芒日，卡亚波人的村落就在那里被摧毁。1736年，此地成为「腹地暴动」的中心之一，佩德罗·卡多佐率领腹地居民反抗殖民征税，比米纳斯密谋早了半个世纪。作为圣弗朗西斯科河中游最早的河港和司法驻地，这个村落把来自戈亚斯和马托格罗索的黄金、钱币与宝石运往沿海。

en:
The open plateau between the Serra da Canastra and the Rio Grande was remembered in colonial records as the country of the Araxás, whose game name here is Araxas. Their lands commanded crossings and camping grounds on the routes from São Paulo towards the Goiás and Minas interior, alternating gallery forest with high grassland. In 1444 their villages remained independent, bound by kinship and intertribal diplomacy; no Portuguese farm, parish or military road had yet fixed this far western borderland of the future Minas Gerais.

European accounts place the Araxás in the region from the late sixteenth century, but sustained colonial pressure came much later. In 1749 they asked the governor of Goiás for Jesuit missionaries and settlement under the protection of the Paulista frontier leader Antônio Pires de Campos. A new village was laid out on the Rio Claro near its mouth into the Rio das Velhas in 1750–1751; while Pires de Campos was campaigning north, Caiapó warriors attacked, killed the Araxá men and carried off the surviving women and children, so that official letters reported the group destroyed by early 1751. Bandeira warfare then opened the plateau to cattle ranches, whose owners began to settle around 1770. In 1791 the farming settlement was organized as the parish of São Domingos de Araxá, carrying the indigenous name into the Portuguese province that existed by 1821.
zh:
卡纳斯特拉山脉与格兰德河之间的开阔高原，在殖民记录中被称为阿拉斯人的土地，游戏省名也作「阿拉斯」。他们的土地控制着从圣保罗通往戈亚斯和米纳斯内陆道路上的渡口与营地，景观在林带河谷和高原草场之间交替。1444年时，阿拉斯人的村落仍保持自主，依靠亲属关系和部族间往来维系；在后来的米纳斯吉拉斯极西边地，还没有葡萄牙人的农庄、堂区或军用道路。

欧洲记载从16世纪后期起已提到这一地区的阿拉斯人，但持续的殖民压力要晚得多。1749年，他们请求戈亚斯总督派遣耶稣会士，并在圣保罗边地首领安东尼奥·皮雷斯·德·坎波斯保护下建立定居村。1750—1751年，新村落设在克拉鲁河汇入旧河处附近；皮雷斯·德·坎波斯北征期间，卡亚波战士发动袭击，杀死阿拉斯男子并掳走幸存妇孺，官员信函因此在1751年初报告这一部群已覆灭。随后远征战争把高原开放给牧牛场，牧场主约在1770年开始定居。1791年，农业聚落被编为圣多明我-迪阿拉沙堂区，使这个原住民地名延续到1821年已存在的葡萄牙行省之中。

en:
Ofaie takes its name from the Ofaié, a Macro-Jê people of the Paraná bend in what is now eastern Mato Grosso do Sul. They lived along the great river about the mouth of the Sucuriú and at the headwaters of the Ivinhema and Vacaria, in small bands that hunted and planted fields in the gallery forest; their number before the colonists came was later put at perhaps five thousand. Eastward lay the sertão of the São Paulo backlands, and the cerrado stretched on every side. In 1444 this was a world of rivers and villages untouched by Europeans.

Europeans first crossed these waters in numbers after gold was found on the Cuiabá River in 1718. From the 1720s great canoe convoys called monções left Porto Feliz at high water, descended the Tietê into the Paraná and paddled past the Sucuriú mouth on the 3,500-kilometre road to the mines; the convoy of 1726 alone carried more than 3,000 people in 305 canoes. The Ofaié watched the fleets go by year after year. In 1821 no Portuguese town or fort yet stood on the Sucuriú, and the passing convoys, already past their greatest days, were the people's only regular link with the world beyond their rivers.
zh:
奥法耶得名于奥法耶人，他们是住在巴拉那河大拐弯一带的大热依语族群，地在今南马托格罗索州东部。奥法耶人聚居在苏库里乌河口附近的大河两岸以及伊维涅马河、瓦卡里亚河的源头，以小群体游猎、在长廊林间开垦为生；据估殖民者到来之前他们约有五千人。东边是圣保罗腹地的荒原，四周绵延着塞拉多稀树草原。1444年，这里还是一片欧洲人未曾涉足的河流与村落世界。

1718年库亚巴河发现黄金后，欧洲人才成批经过这片水域。从1720年代起，名为「季风船队」的独木舟队趁水涨时从波尔图费利斯出发，沿铁特河驶入巴拉那河，经过苏库里乌河口，走上去金矿的3500公里水路；仅1726年的船队就有305艘独木舟、三千余人。奥法耶人看着船队年年经过。1821年时，苏库里乌河畔仍没有葡萄牙人的城镇或要塞，已过鼎盛期的过往船队是他们与河流之外世界唯一的固定往来。

en:
The hills and water meadows of the Rio das Mortes, the River of Deaths, were Macro-Jê country on the southern approaches to the Minas interior long before the gold rush. Its streams, crossings and tracks between the Serra do Lenheiro and Serra de São José served Indigenous villages whose occupants moved between hunting, planting and interregional exchange. In 1444 there was no Portuguese royal road or mining camp in the valley; its place in the route from Paraty to the future Ouro Preto still lay in the future.

Around 1700 the Taubaté bandeirante Tomé Portes del-Rei led a Paulista party to the Rio das Mortes and opened the first lasting camps; after his death around 1702, Antônio Garcia da Cunha and other miners developed the Arraial de Nossa Senhora do Pilar. The district was drawn into the War of the Emboabas of 1707–1709, when Paulista claimants fought newcomers for control of its gold-bearing streams. Royal administration followed quickly: in 1713 the settlements were raised into the town of São João del-Rei, named for John V of Portugal, and in 1714 it became seat of the Rio das Mortes judicial district. On the Estrada Real, the town combined gold with ranching, supply trade and African slave labour; Pilar, Carmo, Mercês and Rosário churches gave it a dense baroque skyline. Even after mining declined in the later eighteenth century, it remained an administrative and market centre, and in 1789 the Minas conspiracy reached the households and militias of its comarca.
zh:
死亡河（Rio das Mortes）的丘陵与水草甸，位于通往米纳斯内陆的南缘，早在淘金潮以前就是大热依语族人群的土地。莱涅罗山和圣若泽山之间的溪流、渡口与小路服务着原住民村落，居民在狩猎、种植和区域交换之间往来。1444年时，河谷中还没有葡萄牙皇家大道或淘金营地；它日后连接帕拉蒂与未来欧鲁普雷图的道路地位也尚未出现。

约1700年，来自陶巴特的圣保罗远征者托梅·波尔特斯·德尔雷伊率队抵达死亡河，开辟了最早的持久营地；他约于1702年死后，安东尼奥·加西亚·达·库尼亚和其他矿工发展出圣母皮拉尔营地。1707—1709年恩博阿巴斯战争期间，这一地区被卷入战事，圣保罗拓殖者与新来者为控制含金溪谷交战。王室行政很快跟进：1713年，各聚居点升格为圣若昂-德尔雷伊镇，以葡萄牙国王若昂五世命名，1714年成为死亡河司法辖区驻地。凭借皇家大道上的位置，此镇把黄金生产、牧牛、补给贸易和非洲奴隶劳动结合起来；皮拉尔、卡尔莫、梅尔塞斯和罗萨里奥诸堂构成密集的巴洛克天际线。即使18世纪后期采金衰落，它仍是行政与市场中心，1789年米纳斯密谋也牵连到这个司法辖区的家族与民兵。

en:
Castro occupies the open Campos Gerais grasslands of Paraná, where the Iapó River cuts through forested sandstone country later known for the Guartelá Canyon. In 1444 its fords and pastures were used by Guarapiaba people, a Tupi group recorded along the Iapó, while Kaingang bands moved through the surrounding forest edge. Native paths followed the dry ground between southern grasslands and the plateaus to the north, but there was as yet no Portuguese ranch, chapel or ferry toll on the river.

Paulista cattlemen reached the Campos Gerais around the turn of the eighteenth century; the Capão Alto land grant is dated to 1704. Pouso do Iapó became a watering place and overnight camp on the Caminho de Sorocaba, used by tropeiros driving cattle from Viamão to the great fair at Sorocaba. Families from Sorocaba, Santos and Itu took up ranches, a wattle-and-daub chapel was built in 1751, and Carmelite friars put up a new church in 1769. Lieutenant-Colonel Afonso Botelho de Sam Payo visited on 15 March 1771, after which the settlement became the parish of Sant'Ana do Iapó; its boundaries were confirmed in 1775. On 24 September 1788 it was separated from Curitiba and raised to a town as Vila Nova de Castro, named for the Portuguese overseas minister Martinho de Melo e Castro. In 1821 cattle, ranching and the long mule and cattle road still defined the town.
zh:
卡斯特鲁地处巴拉那的坎波斯吉拉斯草原，亚波河在这里切过林覆砂岩地带，后来以瓜尔特拉峡谷闻名。1444年时，亚波河畔的瓜拉皮亚巴人（属图皮语族群）使用这里的渡口和牧场，卡因冈游群则在周围森林边缘活动。原住民小路沿干燥地面连接南方草原与北方高原，但河畔还没有葡萄牙牧场、小教堂或渡税卡。

18世纪初，圣保罗牧人进入坎波斯吉拉斯，卡庞阿尔托授地的时间可追溯到1704年。亚波宿地随后成为索罗卡巴路上的饮水点和夜营处，牧奴和赶畜人从维亚芒驱赶牛群前往索罗卡巴大集市，索罗卡巴、桑托斯和伊图的家族也到此经营牧场。1751年，当地建起一座泥栅小教堂；1769年，加尔默罗会修士另建新教堂。1771年3月15日，中校阿方索·博特略·德·桑帕约到此巡视，聚落随后成为圣安娜-杜亚波教区，教区边界在1775年得到确认。1788年9月24日，此地从库里蒂巴划出，升格为新卡斯特罗镇，名称来自葡萄牙海外部大臣马蒂尼奥·德·梅洛·埃卡斯特罗。到1821年，牧牛、牧场和那条漫长的赶畜道路仍决定着这座城镇的面貌。

en:
Inland beyond the Serra do Mar, the plateau broke into wide natural clearings in the Atlantic forest, grassy flats the paulistas called simply campinas. Indian peoples speaking Tupi-Guarani and Jê languages farmed mandioca, maize and beans along the watercourses and hunted the woods between. In 1444 this was sertão, unknown backcountry to the Portuguese on the coast, crossed only by native trails; for more than two centuries after the first ships reached Brazil no European road ran through it.

Between 1721 and 1730 bandeirantes from the Piratininga plateau opened the Caminho dos Goiases, a trail to the new goldfields of Minas Gerais and Goiás, and the sertanista Fernão de Camargo set up a tropeiros' stopping post in a grassy clearing called Campinas do Mato Grosso. Sesmarias were granted from 1728, but the first census, in 1767, found only 38 households and 185 souls. The chapel the settlers had asked for was marked out on 22 September 1773, and on 27 May 1774 Francisco Barreto Leme do Prado was named founder of the new nucleus; on 14 July 1774 its first mass was said and the Freguesia de Nossa Senhora da Conceição das Campinas came into being. On 14 December 1797 the settlement was detached from Jundiaí as the vila of São Carlos, later called Campinas. From the 1790s the provision farms gave way to sugarcane, encouraged by the roads built under the governor Morgado de Mateus, and Campinas became one corner of the paulista 'sugar quadrilateral' with Sorocaba, Piracicaba, Mogi-Guaçu and Jundiaí.
zh:
越过马尔山深入内陆，高原上的大西洋森林间展开大片天然草甸，圣保罗人径直称之为「坎皮纳斯」，意即草原。操图皮-瓜拉尼语和热语的印第安族群沿水道种植木薯、玉米和豆类，在林间狩猎。1444年，对海岸上的葡萄牙人来说，这里还是名为「塞唐」的未知腹地，只有土著小道穿行；首批船只抵达巴西之后的两百多年里，没有一条欧洲人开辟的道路经过此地。

1721至1730年间，皮拉蒂宁加高原的旗队开辟了通往米纳斯吉拉斯和戈亚斯新金矿区的「戈亚斯之路」，内陆开拓者费尔南·德·卡马戈在一处名叫「马托格罗索草原」的草甸上设了赶骡人歇脚点。1728年起王室开始在此分封授地，但1767年第一次人口普查只找到38户、185人。1773年9月22日，居民请愿修建的小堂划定地界；1774年5月27日，弗朗西斯科·巴雷托·莱梅·杜·普拉多被任命为新聚落的创立者，同年7月14日首场弥撒举行，「坎皮纳斯圣母无染原罪堂区」正式成立。1797年12月14日，聚落脱离容迪亚伊设镇，定名圣卡洛斯，后改称坎皮纳斯。1790年代起，在莫尔加多·德·马特乌斯总督修筑的道路网带动下，自给农庄逐渐让位于甘蔗种植，坎皮纳斯与索罗卡巴、皮拉西卡巴、莫日瓜苏和容迪亚伊一道，成为圣保罗「蔗糖四边形」的一角。

en:
Araraquara covers the open Campos de Aracoara on the central São Paulo tablelands, a country of grasslands, low hills and gallery forest. In 1444 it belonged to the Guaianás, a Macro-Jê people whose southern farming groups are counted among the ancestors of the Kaingang. They kept gardens while also hunting, fishing and gathering across the campos, and knew the sunlit ridge and plateau as Aracoara, the dwelling place of daylight. No Portuguese ranch or chapel yet stood between the Guaianá villages and the Tietê valley.

Portuguese occupation came late. Pedro José Neto, born in 1760, moved to Itu in 1787 and, after being sentenced to exile by the Itu justices, fled with his sons into the Campos de Araraquara. They built a small chapel dedicated to Saint Benedict and established cattle claims across the surrounding grasslands. On 22 August 1817 the parish of São Bento de Araraquara was created under Piracicaba, and on 30 October the settlement was raised to a district. Its early estates planted sugarcane, maize, tobacco and cotton, and raised pigs and cattle. In 1821 Araraquara was therefore only four years old as a settled parish, where São Paulo ranching expansion met the old Guaianá country.
zh:
阿拉拉夸拉位于圣保罗中部高原的阿拉科阿拉草原，四周是草地、低丘和河岸林。1444年时，这里属于瓜亚纳人；他们是大热语系族群，其中南方农耕支系被视为卡因冈人的祖先之一。瓜亚纳人既经营田园，也在草原上狩猎、捕鱼和采集，并把日照下的山脊与高原称作阿拉科阿拉，意为「日光栖居之处」。那时在瓜亚纳村落与铁特河谷之间，还没有葡萄牙牧场或小教堂。

葡萄牙人的占据来得很晚。佩德罗·若泽·内图1760年出生，1787年迁居伊图，后来被伊图法庭判处流放，便带着儿子逃入阿拉拉夸拉草原。他们建起一座供奉圣本托的小教堂，并在周围草原上取得多处牧地。1817年8月22日，隶属皮拉西卡巴的圣本托-迪阿拉拉夸拉教区设立；10月30日，聚落又被升为辖区。早期庄园种植甘蔗、玉米、烟草和棉花，也饲养猪和牛。因此到1821年，作为定居教区的阿拉拉夸拉只有四年历史，是圣保罗牧牛扩张与瓜亚纳故土相接的边地。

en:
Serro occupies a cold, broken section of the Serra do Espinhaço near the headwaters of the Jequitinhonha. The Tupi-Guarani name Ivituruí described a windy, cold hill, and in 1444 these ridges, creeks and upland camps belonged to indigenous peoples rather than to any Portuguese captaincy. No mines, roads or colonial town yet marked the country later called Serro Frio.

An expedition led by Antônio Soares Ferreira reached the area in 1701 and found gold along the Quatro Vinténs and Lucas streams. The camp was formally recorded in 1702 as Arraial do Ribeirão das Minas de Santo Antônio do Bom Retiro do Serro do Frio, and in 1714 Governor Brás Baltasar da Silveira raised it to a town as Vila do Príncipe. In 1720 it became seat of the great Serro Frio comarca, governing the north and northeast of Minas, including the future diamond camp at Tejuco. A crown foundry was ordered in 1725, forcing regional gold through official controls, while diamonds discovered around Milho Verde, São Gonçalo do Rio das Pedras and Tejuco encouraged still stricter surveillance and smuggling. By the early nineteenth century mining had declined in favour of cattle and subsistence farming; when Auguste de Saint-Hilaire visited in 1817, Vila do Príncipe had about 700 houses and 2,500 to 3,000 people, with churches rising above its amphitheatre of slopes.
zh:
塞鲁位于埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉一段寒冷崎岖的山地，靠近热基蒂尼奥尼亚河源头。图皮-瓜拉尼语称这里为伊维图鲁伊，意为多风的寒冷山丘。1444年时，这些山脊、溪流和高地营地属于印第安人，而不属于任何葡萄牙都督辖区；后来被称为塞鲁弗里乌的地方还没有矿山、道路或殖民城镇。

1701年，安东尼奥·苏亚雷斯·费雷拉率领远征队抵达此地，在夸特罗温滕斯溪和卢卡斯溪一带发现黄金。1702年，矿区被正式登记为「圣安多尼邦雷蒂鲁杜塞鲁弗里乌矿溪村」；1714年，总督布拉斯·巴尔塔萨·达西尔韦拉将其升格为镇，命名为太子镇。1720年，这里成为塞鲁弗里乌大辖区的治所，管辖米纳斯北部和东北部，包括后来的特茹科钻石营地。1725年，王室下令设立熔铸厂，把地区黄金纳入官方管制；米尔霍韦尔德、圣贡萨洛杜里奥达什佩德拉斯和特茹科一带发现钻石后，监视进一步加强，走私也随之盛行。19世纪初矿业衰落，养牛和自给农业取而代之。1817年奥古斯特·德·圣伊莱尔到访时，太子镇约有700栋房屋、2500至3000人，几座教堂耸立在层叠山坡上。

en:
The future Vila Rica, now Ouro Preto, began as steep Macro-Jê country beneath Itacolomi Peak in the Serra do Espinhaço. Indigenous villagers used the Tripuí and other mountain streams long before prospectors learned that their dark, iron-stained gravel contained exceptionally rich gold. In 1444 there was no royal road, smelter or mining arraial in these valleys; the ridges, campsites and watercourses belonged to peoples who had never encountered Portuguese tax collectors or Paulista bandeirantes.

Gold was found in the mountain streams in 1695–1696 by parties including Antônio Dias de Oliveira, Father João de Faria Fialho and Tomás Lopes de Camargo, and the rush quickly overran the valleys. The War of the Emboabas of 1707–1709 pitted Paulista pioneers against outsiders, after which the crown tightened its hold: the camps were united as Vila Rica in 1711, and the town became a judicial seat in 1714. In 1720 protests against the new foundry-house monopoly, the ban on circulating gold dust and the royal fifth brought on the Vila Rica Revolt of 28 June–19 July; the Count of Assumar crushed it and executed Filipe dos Santos, while Minas Gerais became a separate captaincy with Vila Rica as its capital. Officially recorded exports alone reached about 800 tons of gold during the eighteenth century, supporting roughly 40,000 people by 1730 and about 80,000 by mid-century. Wealth raised baroque churches and the Casa da Ópera, opened on 6 June 1770, and drew artists and poets such as Aleijadinho, Manoel da Costa Ataíde, Cláudio Manuel da Costa and Tomás António Gonzaga. As gold output declined, the derrama tax crisis fed the Inconfidência Mineira of 1788–1789; Tiradentes was arrested in 1789 and hanged on 21 April 1792. In 1821 Vila Rica remained the mountain capital of Minas Gerais.
zh:
后来的里卡镇（Vila Rica，即今欧鲁普雷图），原是埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉中伊塔科洛米峰下的大热依语族人群山地。特里普伊等山溪早为原住民村落所用，要到很久以后，探矿者才发现溪中发黑、裹着氧化铁的砾石含有极富的黄金。1444年时，这些山谷里还没有皇家大道、熔铸厂或淘金营地；山脊、营地与水道属于从未遇见葡萄牙税吏或圣保罗远征队的人群。

1695—1696年，安东尼奥·迪亚斯·德·奥利维拉、神父若昂·德·法里亚·菲亚略和托马斯·洛佩斯·德·卡马戈等人的队伍在山溪中发现黄金，淘金潮随即涌入山谷。1707—1709年的恩博阿巴斯战争使圣保罗拓殖者与外来者兵戎相见，战后王室加强控制：各营地于1711年合并为里卡镇，1714年成为司法辖区驻地。1720年，新设熔铸厂垄断、禁止金砂流通和征收五分之一金税引发6月28日至7月19日的里卡镇暴动；阿苏马尔伯爵将其镇压并处决费利佩·多斯桑托斯，米纳斯吉拉斯也在同年分设为独立都督辖区，以里卡镇为首府。仅官方登记的18世纪黄金出口就约达800吨，支撑起1730年约4万人、18世纪中叶约8万人的城市。财富带来大量巴洛克教堂和1770年6月6日开幕的歌剧院，也吸引阿列哈迪尼奥、曼努埃尔·达·科斯塔·阿塔伊德、克劳迪奥·曼努埃尔·达科斯塔、托马斯·安东尼奥·贡萨加等艺术家与诗人。随着黄金产量下降，「德拉马」摊派税危机催生1788—1789年的米纳斯密谋；蒂拉登特斯1789年被捕，1792年4月21日被处以绞刑。1821年时，里卡镇仍是米纳斯吉拉斯的山中首府。

en:
The Guaporé, called Iténez on its Spanish bank, rises in the Parecis plateau and flows west through flooded savanna and gallery forest to join the Mamoré. On its lower course, Chapacuran villagers—Chapacura, Itenes, Torá and others—cleared gardens above the annual floods, while Jê-related groups occupied the Branco, Mequens and Corumbiara valleys. They grew maize and peanuts, fished with arrows and fish poisons, and travelled the river by canoe. In 1444 the Guaporé was a native road rather than an imperial frontier: its villages controlled the crossings, fishing grounds and routes linking the river with the Mamoré and Madeira.

Spanish Jesuit missions and Portuguese gold seekers later turned the waterway into a contested border. Portugal created the captaincy of Mato Grosso in 1748, and Antônio Rolim de Moura founded Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade on the upper Guaporé in 1752. A small post, the Presídio de Nossa Senhora da Conceição, was built on the lower river in 1769 but proved too weak to secure it. Luís de Albuquerque therefore began the stone Real Forte Príncipe da Beira in April 1775; its foundation stone was laid on 20 June 1776, and work continued to 1783. Built largely with Indigenous and enslaved African labour, the fortress guarded the Guaporé-Mamoré-Madeira route and faced Spanish claims after the treaties of Madrid in 1750 and San Ildefonso in 1777. By 1821 it was a remote, fever-ridden garrison on the edge of the Portuguese Amazon.
zh:
瓜波雷河在西班牙语一侧称伊特内斯河，发源于帕雷西斯高原，向西穿过泛滥热带草原与河岸林，汇入马莫雷河。下游沿岸有查帕库拉人、伊特内斯人、托拉人等查帕库兰语族群；布兰库河、梅肯斯河和科伦比阿拉河流域则住着与热语族群相近的人群。他们在洪水线以上开辟田园，种植玉米和花生，用箭和鱼药捕鱼，并以独木舟往来河面。1444年时，瓜波雷还不是帝国边界，而是原住民自己的水路；沿岸村落掌握着渡口、渔场和通往马莫雷河、马代拉河的航路。

后来，西班牙耶稣会传教站和寻找黄金的葡萄牙人把这条水道变成相争的边地。葡萄牙于1748年设立马托格罗索都督辖区，安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1752年在上瓜波雷建立维拉贝拉-达桑蒂西马特林达迪。1769年，葡萄牙人在下瓜波雷修筑圣母受孕哨所，却不足以稳固航道。路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克遂于1775年4月动工兴建石砌的贝拉亲王皇家堡垒，1776年6月20日安放基石，工程持续到1783年。堡垒主要由原住民和非洲奴工劳动建成，守护瓜波雷—马莫雷—马代拉航路，与1750年《马德里条约》和1777年《圣伊尔德方索条约》后仍反复争执的西班牙势力隔河相望。到1821年，这里已是葡萄牙亚马孙边缘一处偏远、瘴疠流行的驻军地。

en:
Cerejeiras lies about 45 kilometres north of the Guaporé, on rolling ground in southern Rondônia where the Corumbiara, Mequens and neighbouring streams drain south toward the border river. In 1444 its gardens and hunting grounds belonged to Jê-related peoples of those tributary valleys, while Chapacuran villagers lived closer to the Guaporé itself. They planted maize and peanuts, gathered Brazil nuts in season, fished with arrows and poisons, and used canoes on the main rivers. No European post yet stood between their villages and the river crossings.

The Spaniard Ñuflo de Chávez crossed the Guaporé valley in 1541-42, and Portuguese bandeirantes entered the region around 1650. After gold was found on the river's right bank, the Portuguese Crown created the captaincy of Mato Grosso in 1748. Local history records a camp made by Antônio Rolim de Moura on this stretch of the Guaporé in 1750; fugitive slaves from Vila Bela later occupied it, and the place served traffic descending toward the lower river. Work on the stone Príncipe da Beira fortress downstream began in 1775 and continued to 1783, securing the main waterway rather than turning Cerejeiras's inland country into a town. In 1821 it remained a thinly travelled corridor between the Mato Grosso mines and the Madeira route.
zh:
塞雷热拉斯位于瓜波雷河以北约45公里，地处龙多尼亚南缘缓丘，科伦比亚拉河、梅肯斯河及邻近溪流由此南注界河。1444年，这里的田园和猎场属于这些支流河谷中与热语族群相近的人群，靠近瓜波雷干流处则住着查帕库兰语村民。他们种植玉米和花生，按季采集巴西坚果，用箭和鱼药捕鱼，并在主要河道上使用独木舟。那时在他们的村落与各渡口之间，还没有欧洲人的常设据点。

西班牙人努夫洛·德·查韦斯于1541年至1542年穿过瓜波雷河谷，葡萄牙旗队约在1650年进入这一带。瓜波雷右岸发现黄金后，葡萄牙王室于1748年设立马托格罗索都督辖区。当地史记载，安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1750年曾在这段瓜波雷河畔扎营；后来从维拉贝拉逃出的奴工占据此地，使它成为顺河下航者的补给点。下游石砌的贝拉亲王堡1775年开工、1783年仍在营建，锁住的是干流航道，并未把塞雷热拉斯的内陆林地变成城镇。1821年时，这里仍是马托格罗索金矿区与马代拉航路之间一条人烟稀少的走廊。

en:
Vila Bela lies on the upper Guaporé, where streams from the Parecis plateau gather before the river runs west toward the Bolivian plains. Gallery forest, cerrado and the ridges of the Serra de Ricardo Franco divide the country. In 1444 this was Nambikwara land: mobile Sararé, Kabixi and other bands moved between the Guaporé and Juruena headwaters, hunting, gathering and shifting camp through forest and savanna, while Chiquitano peoples held the plains and hills farther west. The river supplied fish and crossings, but no Portuguese tax house, town or permanent garrison yet controlled the valley.

Gold seekers reached the upper Guaporé in 1733-34, and in 1742 Manuel Félix de Lima descended the Guaporé, Madeira and Amazon to Belém, opening a long supply route. Diamonds were found in Mato Grosso in 1747, and the Portuguese Crown created the Captaincy of Mato Grosso on 9 May 1748. Its first governor, Antônio Rolim de Moura, arrived in 1751 and installed Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade as his capital on 19 March 1752. A mining-tax office followed, while Rolim expelled Spanish missionaries, made Indigenous alliances, opened roads toward Maranhão and Bahia, and promoted sugar cultivation. The treaties of Madrid in 1750 and San Ildefonso in 1777 framed the rivalry with Spain. On 28 February 1821 Mato Grosso became a province; after Governor Magessi was deposed on 20 August, Vila Bela raised its own junta alongside the junta in Cuiabá.
zh:
维拉贝拉位于上瓜波雷：帕雷西斯高原的溪流在此汇合，瓜波雷河随后西向玻利维亚平原。河岸林、热带稀树草原与里卡多·佛朗哥山的山脊把这片土地分隔开来。1444年时，这里是南比夸拉人的土地，萨拉拉、卡比希等游群在瓜波雷河与茹鲁埃纳河源头之间迁徙，在森林和草原间狩猎、采集、移营；更西的平原和丘陵则属于奇基托斯人。河流提供鱼获与渡口，但谷中还没有葡萄牙税务所、城镇或常设驻军。

1733年至1734年，寻金者进入上瓜波雷；1742年，曼努埃尔·费利克斯·德·利马顺瓜波雷河、马代拉河和亚马孙河下航至贝伦，开辟了一条漫长补给线。1747年马托格罗索发现钻石，葡萄牙王室遂于1748年5月9日设立马托格罗索都督辖区。首任都督安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1751年到任，1752年3月19日把维拉贝拉-达桑蒂西马特林达迪定为辖区首府。此地随后设立矿税机构，罗林驱逐西班牙传教士、与原住民结盟、开辟通往马拉尼昂和巴伊亚的道路，并推动甘蔗种植；1750年《马德里条约》和1777年《圣伊尔德方索条约》则界定着葡萄牙与西班牙的争夺框架。1821年2月28日，马托格罗索改为省；8月20日都督马热西被推翻后，维拉贝拉与库亚巴各自成立政务会。

en:
The future Cáceres lies on the upper Paraguay at the edge of the Pantanal, where seasonal floods turn grassland and riverine woods into a maze of channels. Guató people moved through these waters as canoe builders, fishermen and archers, living mainly in small family groups rather than large villages. In 1444 the Paraguay was their road between fishing grounds and temporary camps, and no Portuguese or Spanish frontier post yet stood on the bank.

On 6 October 1778 the dragoon officer Antônio Pinto Rego e Carvalho founded Vila Maria do Paraguai by order of Luís de Albuquerque de Melo Pereira e Cáceres, governor of Mato Grosso. The post was meant to check Spanish and indigenous raids, protect river navigation, and connect Vila Bela and Cuiabá with São Paulo by way of the Paraguay. Its first settlers included scattered couples and sixty Indians brought from the Castilian mission of Chiquitos; houses, a church and a council-and-prison building were laid out near a chapel dedicated to Saint Louis. By 1809 Vila Maria held a Royal Warehouse of arms, tools, food and boat equipment, serving the captaincy as a small military river port.
zh:
后来的卡塞雷斯位于巴拉圭河上游、潘塔纳尔沼泽边缘；季节性洪水会把草原与河畔林地变成纵横水网。瓜托人擅长造船、捕鱼和射箭，多以小型家族群体活动，而不是聚居成大型村落。1444年时，巴拉圭河是他们往来渔场和临时营地的通路，河岸上还没有葡萄牙或西班牙的边防据点。

1778年10月6日，龙骑兵军官安东尼奥·平托·雷戈·埃·卡瓦略奉马托格罗索总督路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克·德·梅洛·佩雷拉·埃·卡塞雷斯之命，建立巴拉圭河畔玛丽亚镇。这个据点用来抵御西班牙人和原住民的袭扰、保护河运，并经巴拉圭河把维拉贝拉、库亚巴与圣保罗联系起来。最早的居民包括分散的夫妇，以及从西班牙人管辖的奇基托斯传教区招来的六十名印第安人；住宅区、教堂、议会兼监狱围绕圣路易小堂规划。到1809年，玛丽亚镇设有皇家仓库，储存武器、工具、粮食和船只装备，是都督辖区的一座小型军用河港。

en:
Diamantino lies on the broken southern foothills of the Parecis plateau, where the Diamantino and Ouro streams descend toward the Paraguay while other valleys feed the Arinos and the Amazon. Pareci, or Haliti, Arino and neighbouring peoples moved through this cerrado and riverine-forest country, using the waterways to hunt, fish and keep distant communities in contact. In 1444 the gravel of the Ouro had not yet drawn Portuguese miners, and the plateau remained an indigenous borderland between the Amazon and Paraguay worlds.

On 18 September 1728 Gabriel Antunes Maciel found gold in the Ribeirão do Ouro and reported the strike to Cuiabá, creating the Arraial do Ouro, later called Félix. Precious stones then drew the Portuguese crown's attention: it imposed a strict monopoly, closed workings and stationed the Destacamento Diamantino do Paraguai against clandestine prospectors. The settlement nevertheless endured as a supply centre, with paranista boatmen carrying local trade north to Pará along the Arinos. On 9 August 1811 the parish of Our Lady of the Conception of Alto Paraguai Diamantino was created, its mistaken name reflecting the explorers' belief that they were near the Paraguay's headwaters. A royal charter raised Diamantino to vila status on 23 November 1820.
zh:
迪亚曼蒂努位于帕雷西斯高原崎岖的南缘，迪亚曼蒂努河与金溪的水流朝巴拉圭河方向下行，另一些谷地则汇入阿里努斯河并通向亚马孙流域。帕雷西人（自称哈利蒂人）、阿里努人及邻近族群穿行在这片塞拉多草原与河畔林地之间，借水道狩猎、捕鱼，并维系分散社群的联系。1444年时，金溪的砂砾还没有引来葡萄牙淘金者，高原仍是亚马孙世界与巴拉圭世界之间的原住民边地。

1728年9月18日，加布里埃尔·安图内斯·马西埃尔在金溪发现黄金并向库亚巴议会报告，金溪营地由此形成，后来又称费利克斯。宝石随后引起葡萄牙王室注意：王室实行严格专卖、封闭矿场，并设置迪亚曼蒂努·杜·巴拉圭支队缉拿私采者。尽管如此，定居点仍作为补给中心延续下来，「巴拉尼斯塔」船工沿阿里努斯河把本地贸易向北送往帕拉。1811年8月9日，上巴拉圭·迪亚曼蒂努圣母受孕教区设立；这个名字来自探险者的地理误判，他们以为自己已靠近巴拉圭河源头。1820年11月23日，王室特许状将迪亚曼蒂努升格为镇。

en:
The Rio das Mortes, also called the Manso, rises in the Serra de São Lourenço and runs roughly 1,200 kilometres through the Mato Grosso cerrado before joining the Araguaia. In 1444 its valley formed the northern edge of the wide Bororo world, whose villages and hunting grounds reached from the Paraguay eastward toward the Araguaia. The river gave fish, crossing places and seasonal camps, while its banks were known to Bororo travellers and neighbouring peoples; no Portuguese miner or slaver had yet mapped them.

Around 1660 slaving bandeiras led by Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva and Antônio Pires de Campos began crossing this country. In 1673 the two men, then still young, claimed to have seen the gold-rich land of Araés and the Serra dos Martírios while accompanying their fathers; forty years later the story sent expeditions into the interior. Bartolomeu marched out in July 1722 with 300 men and returned on 21 October 1725 with only sixteen, finding Goiás gold rather than the legendary place. In 1745 Amaro Leite Moreira's party struck gold in northern Mato Grosso and raised a small camp named Araés, soon renamed Santo Antônio do Amarante. Poor communications with Cuiabá, failing deposits and indigenous attacks forced its abandonment in 1789. Other placer camps along the Rio das Mortes were also deserted after the easy gold ended, leaving the valley without a Portuguese town in 1821.
zh:
莫尔蒂斯河又称曼苏河，发源于圣洛伦索山，穿过马托格罗索的塞拉多草原约1200千米后注入阿拉瓜亚河。1444年时，河谷构成广阔博罗罗人地域的北缘；他们的村落与猎场西起巴拉圭河一带，东抵阿拉瓜亚河。河流提供鱼产、渡口和季节性营地，河岸只通行于博罗罗旅行者与邻近族群的地理知识中，葡萄牙淘金者或奴隶贩子还不曾测绘这里。

1660年前后，巴托洛梅乌·布埃诺·达·席尔瓦和安东尼奥·皮雷斯·德·坎波斯率领的捕奴旗队开始进入这片地方。1673年，尚在年少的二人随父亲的远征队出行，声称见到盛产黄金的阿赖埃斯和马蒂里奥斯山；四十年后，这段说法把多支探险队引向内陆。1722年7月，巴托洛梅乌率三百人出发，1725年10月21日只剩十六人归来；他们没有找到传说之地，却在戈亚斯发现黄金。1745年，阿马罗·莱特·莫雷拉的队伍在马托格罗索北部找到金矿，建起名为阿赖埃斯的小营地，不久改称圣安东尼奥·杜·阿马兰蒂。由于与库亚巴交通困难、矿脉衰竭且不断遭到原住民攻击，村民在1789年弃村。莫尔蒂斯河沿岸其他砂金营地也在易采黄金耗尽后荒废，到1821年，河谷中仍没有葡萄牙人城镇。

en:
Iporá is the western Goiás cerrado, the headwater country of the Rio Claro and the Caiapó, whose streams run south to the Paranaíba; Iporá itself is a later Tupi name meaning 'clear waters'. In 1444 this was Xavante land, held by Jê-speaking hunters and gardeners whose villages lay between the Araguaia and the Tocantins, with the Ofaié beyond the southern rivers. No mule road or mining camp had yet entered it.

The frontier arrived in the 1730s, when the São Paulo entrepreneurs Joaquim and Felisberto Caldeira Brant worked gold strikes across western Goiás. In 1748 a troop of dragoons was posted on the right bank of the Rio Claro at the Arraial de Pilões, guarding the brothers' diamond workings; the garrison raised a barracks, the parish church of Senhor Jesus do Bom Fim and the ranchos of the garimpeiros. Diamonds proved thin, and Pilões lived on as the trading post on the overland road between Vila Boa and Cuiabá. The surrounding sertão stayed in Xavante hands through the colonial wars, until Tristão da Cunha's 'pacification' campaigns of 1794-1798 broke the villages; the site of the future Iporá remained a roadstead and a guardhouse rather than a town.
zh:
伊波拉是戈亚斯西部的塞拉多，克拉鲁河与卡亚波河发源于此，溪水南流汇入巴拉那伊巴河；「伊波拉」是后来的图皮语地名，意为「清水」。1444年，这里是沙万特人的土地：这些说热依语的猎手和农人把村落散建在阿拉瓜亚河与托坎廷斯河之间，河南更远则是奥法耶人的地盘。此时还没有一条骡道或采矿营地进入此地。

边疆在1730年代到来：圣保罗商人若阿金·卡尔德拉·布兰特与费利斯贝托·卡尔德拉·布兰特兄弟在西戈亚斯各地开采金矿。1748年，一队龙骑兵驻守克拉鲁河右岸的皮隆伊斯营地，护卫兄弟二人的钻石开采；驻军建起营房、善终耶稣教区教堂和矿工棚屋。钻石储量微薄，皮隆伊斯便靠博阿镇与库亚巴之间陆上通道的商站维持。周围腹地在殖民冲突中始终留在沙万特人手中，直到1794至1798年特里斯坦·达库尼亚的「绥靖」征讨打散了各村落；未来伊波拉所在之处，直到此时仍只是一处道口和一间哨房，没有成为城镇。

en:
Vila Boa huddles in the Serra Dourada, on the Rio Vermelho, a headwater running west to the Araguaia. The cerrado around it was the country of the Goiá, a Jê-speaking nation whose name the whole inland region came to bear. They planted maize and manioc in forest gardens and hunted the savanna, their streams already yielding the alluvial gold the bandeirantes would one day seize. In 1444 the nearest Portuguese settlements lay weeks away on the São Paulo plateau, and the Serra Dourada held nothing but Goiá villages.

Gold gave the town its birth. Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva, the second Anhanguera — 'old devil' in Tupi — had first crossed the sertão with his father in 1682; setting out again from São Paulo in 1722, he searched for nearly three years and struck rich gravels in the Rio Vermelho in 1725. Named captain-major of the mines in 1726, he laid out the Arraial de Sant'Anna in 1727, which became Vila Boa de Goiás in 1736. The Captaincy of Goiás was created on 9 May 1748, with Vila Boa its capital; its early government built the Casa de Fundição, the royal gold foundry, in 1750 and the Palácio Conde dos Arcos in 1751, while the first governor, Dom Marcos de Noronha, reached his seat only in 1753. The Casa de Câmara e Cadeia rose in 1761. As gold ran out late in the century, Governor Luís da Cunha Meneses, in office from 1778 to 1783, planted avenues and aligned the streets, leaving the shrinking town the quiet grid of adobe houses and baroque churches that suited its turn to ranching. On 28 February 1821 the captaincy became a province, with Vila Boa still its seat.
zh:
博阿镇（Vila Boa de Goiás，今戈亚斯城）深藏在多拉达山中，傍着西流注入阿拉瓜亚河的红河。四周的塞拉多本是热依语族群戈亚人的家园，后来整个内陆地区都因他们得名。戈亚人在林地里种玉米和木薯，在草原上狩猎，河溪里的沙金后来正是旗手们要夺取之物。1444年，葡萄牙人最近的据点还在数周路程之外的圣保罗高原，多拉达山中只有戈亚人的村落。

黄金催生了这座城镇。第二位「阿年古埃拉」（图皮语意为「老魔鬼」）巴托洛梅乌·布埃诺·达席尔瓦1682年就随父亲穿过这片腹地；1722年他再从圣保罗出发，寻觅近三年，于1725年在红河挖到富矿。1726年他被任命为矿区总兵，1727年辟建圣安娜营地，1736年营地升格为戈亚斯的博阿镇。1748年5月9日戈亚斯都督府设立，博阿镇即为首府；都督府初年于1750年建成王家铸金局、1751年建成阿科斯伯爵宫，首任都督多姆·马科斯·德·诺罗尼亚却迟至1753年才到任。市政暨监狱大厦建于1761年。18世纪末金沙渐尽，1778至1783年在任的都督路易斯·达库尼亚·梅内塞斯沿街植树、裁齐道路，让这座收缩中的小城变成土屋与巴洛克教堂组成的宁静棋盘，与它转向畜牧的命运相称。1821年2月28日都督府改为行省，博阿镇仍为省会。

en:
Arraial dos Couros is the high cerrado on the eastern rim of the Goiás plateau, around the Lagoa Feia, whose streams feed the Paranã and where the Itiquira river leaps off the plateau edge. In 1444 this was Jê country: Caiapó and Xavante bands moved through the gallery woods and grasslands between the Paranã headwaters and the São Francisco, and no Portuguese road had yet climbed onto the plateau.

It became a road before it became a town. In February 1736 the crown planted a toll and customs post, the Registro da Lagoa Feia, to tax the gold moving from the Goiás mines toward Bahia and Minas Gerais. Settlers soon drifted up from the Arraial de Santo Antônio do Itiquira, a Paranã-valley camp thinned by killing fevers; with muleteers who camped in leather shelters on the cool upland they formed the Arraial dos Couros in 1749, the 'leather camp', named for the wild hides dressed and traded there. Attached to the comarca of Santa Luzia, it became the chief station on the Bahia road, where tropeiros traded leather and cattle for mining tools and salt. Through 1821 it remained a rough waystation on the long haul between the mines and the coast.
zh:
阿拉亚尔-杜斯科鲁斯（Arraial dos Couros，意为「皮革营地」，即今福莫萨）坐落在戈亚斯高原东缘的高地，费亚湖一带的溪流汇入帕拉南河，伊蒂基拉河在高原边缘纵身跌落。1444年，这里是热依语族群的土地：卡亚波人与沙万特人的队伍穿行于帕拉南河源与圣弗朗西斯科河之间的林带和草原，葡萄牙人的道路还没有登上高原。

这里先成通衢，后有村镇。1736年2月，葡萄牙王室设立费亚湖税卡（Registro da Lagoa Feia），对从戈亚斯金矿区运往巴伊亚和米纳斯吉拉斯的黄金抽税。不久，帕拉南河谷中被热病掏空的圣安东尼奥-杜伊蒂基拉营地居民陆续迁来，与在凉爽高地支起皮帐歇脚的骡夫汇合，于1749年聚成阿拉亚尔-杜斯科鲁斯——「皮革营地」，得名于当地熟制、贩卖的野皮。它在行政上隶属圣卢齐亚区，逐渐成为巴伊亚商路上的首要驿站，骡队在这里用皮革和牲畜换取矿具与食盐。直到1821年，它始终是矿区与海岸之间漫长驮路上一座粗粝的驿站。

en:
Conceição lies in the high cerrado of the Tocantins-Araguaia basin, above the valley later called São João da Palma. In 1444 this was Jê country: small communities opened gardens in woodland clearings, hunted the grasslands, and shifted camp with the seasons, while the rivers and ridges kept Portuguese expeditions still far to the south and east.

Gold-seekers moving north from Goiás reached the district in the mid-eighteenth century. In 1741 Manoel Paes Andrade settled near a placer mine, built a house and a church dedicated to Our Lady of the Conception, and put enslaved workers to quarrying stone and working the diggings. The Contagem de Conceição became a fiscal post for traffic to the northern mines, and in 1755 the settlement was raised to a parish. Gold washing, cattle ranching, and the slow rhythm of a remote mining parish marked its life until 1821.
zh:
康塞桑位于托坎廷斯-阿拉瓜亚流域的高位塞拉多，俯临后来被称为圣若昂-达帕尔马的河谷。1444年，这里是热依族群的土地：小型社群在林中空地开辟园圃，在草原狩猎，并随季节迁移营地；河流与山脊使葡萄牙远征队仍远在南方和东方之外。

18世纪中叶，从戈亚斯北上的淘金者进入这一地区。1741年，曼努埃尔·派斯·安德拉德在一处砂金矿附近定居，修建住宅和献给无玷始胎圣母的教堂，并驱使被奴役者采石、挖矿。康塞桑税务站成为往来北方矿区的征税点，1755年定居点升格为堂区。直到1821年，砂金淘洗、牧牛和偏远采矿堂区的缓慢节奏，构成了这里的生活。

en:
Pontal takes its name from a point of land on the left bank of the Tocantins, in country later drawn into the mining frontier of northern Goiás. In 1444 the river and surrounding cerrado were Jê land. The Akwẽ-Xerente and related Central Jê peoples kept villages along the Tocantins, hunting, fishing, planting seasonal gardens, and moving across ground that no Portuguese expedition had yet secured.

The gold rush from Goiás reached this stretch after Natividade was founded in 1734. In 1738 Antônio Sanches established the Arraial de Bom Jesus do Pontal, a mining camp whose stone ruins later covered about ninety thousand square metres. The Presídio da Matança watched nearby trails and river traffic, while gold moved by canoe and pack train. By the late eighteenth century the placers were thinning, cattle and crops mattered more, and the Porto Real crossing drew trade away. In 1821 the old arraial remained a small settlement beside the rising river port.
zh:
蓬塔尔得名于托坎廷斯河左岸的一块尖角地，后来被卷入北戈亚斯的淘金边疆。1444年，托坎廷斯河与周围的塞拉多仍是热依人的土地。谢伦特人（Akwẽ）及相近的中央热依族群在河畔建立村落，狩猎、捕鱼、开辟季节园圃，并在尚未被葡萄牙远征队控制的土地上往来。

纳蒂维达于1734年建立后，戈亚斯的淘金潮推进到这一河段。1738年，安东尼奥·桑切斯建立邦热苏斯-杜蓬塔尔淘金营地，其石构遗迹后来广达约九万平方米。马唐萨要塞监视附近道路与河上交通，黄金则靠独木舟和驮队运出。18世纪末，砂金日渐稀少，牧牛和农耕变得更加重要，波尔图雷亚尔渡口又吸走贸易。到1821年，旧营地仍是崛起河港旁的一座小聚落。

en:
Natividade lies beneath the Serra da Natividade, in the southeastern Tocantins cerrado where highland streams drain toward the Tocantins basin. In 1444 it was Xavante country. Central Jê villagers kept seasonal gardens and hunting grounds and controlled the trails between ridges and river valleys, long before the Goiás gold frontier entered their lands.

That frontier advanced between 1724 and 1734. In the latter year Antônio Ferraz de Araújo founded the Arraial de São Luiz at the foot of the serra, naming it for Governor Dom Luís de Mascarenhas; devotion to Our Lady of the Nativity later gave the town its present name. Enslaved workers washed gold from its streams, mule caravans carried the metal toward Salvador, and Natividade became one of Goiás's largest mining camps, surpassed only by Pirenópolis. Later in the eighteenth century enslaved builders began the soapstone church of Nossa Senhora do Rosário dos Pretos, still unfinished when Pohl saw it in 1819. A royal charter in 1809 made the camp provisional seat of the new Comarca do Norte. By 1821 cattle were replacing the exhausted placers.
zh:
纳蒂维达位于纳蒂维达山脚下，地处托坎廷斯东南部的塞拉多，山地溪流汇入托坎廷斯流域。1444年，这里是沙万特人的土地。中央热依村民经营季节园圃和猎场，控制着山脊与河谷之间的小路；那时戈亚斯淘金边疆尚未进入他们的土地。

1724年至1734年间，这条淘金边疆向前推进。1734年，安东尼奥·费拉斯·德·阿劳若在山脚下建立圣路易斯营地，以总督唐·路易斯·德·马斯卡伦哈斯命名；后来对圣诞圣母的敬奉使城镇改用今名。被奴役者在溪流中淘金，骡队把黄金运往萨尔瓦多，纳蒂维达也成为戈亚斯最大的采矿营地之一，仅次于皮雷诺波利斯。18世纪后期，被奴役的工匠开始建造皂石教堂黑人玫瑰圣母堂；1819年波尔见到它时，工程仍未完工。1809年的王室敕令设立北方司法区，营地成为临时驻地。到1821年，牧牛正取代枯竭的砂金矿。

en:
In 1444 the land between the lower São Francisco and the Sergipe river was held by Tupinambá tribes, whose coastal villages grew manioc and gathered crabs in the mangroves — the river's Old Tupi name Siriîype means 'river of crabs'. By the early sixteenth century French brazilwood smugglers were already bartering with its people. The Portuguese Crown counted the coast as part of the Captaincy of Bahia, but the Tupinambá kept settlers out for decades, rising against slaving expeditions until the campaigns of the 1580s broke their resistance.

Conquest came only in 1590, when Cristóvão de Barros defeated the river tribes and founded São Cristóvão on New Year's Day, seat of the new Captaincy of Sergipe d'El-Rey. Sugar mills worked by enslaved Africans spread through the Cotinguiba valley, while cattle ranches and leather works occupied the drier interior, and French buccaneers raided the coast for its prized hardwood. Dutch troops sacked and burned São Cristóvão in 1637, and the land remained under Dutch Brazil until the Portuguese recovered it in 1645. Sergipe became a separate captaincy in 1696, was reannexed to Bahia in 1763, and on 8 July 1820 João VI restored its autonomy, with São Cristóvão the seat of the reborn captaincy.
zh:
1444年，圣弗朗西斯科河下游与塞尔希培河之间的土地属于图皮南巴诸部落，他们的滨海村落种植木薯、在红树林中捕蟹——塞尔希培河的古图皮语名「西里伊佩」意为「蟹河」。到16世纪初，走私巴西木的法国商人已来此与土著以物易物。葡萄牙王室把这片海岸算作巴伊亚都督辖区的一部分，但图皮南巴人数十年间将殖民者拒之门外，并起兵反抗掳奴远征，直到1580年代的历次战役才被压服。

征服迟至1590年才到来：克里斯托旺·德·巴罗斯击败沿河诸部，于元旦建立圣克里斯托旺，作为新设「王家塞尔希培」都督辖区的首府。使用非洲奴隶劳作的糖坊遍布科廷吉巴河谷，干旱内陆则兴起牧场和皮革业，法国海盗还为掠夺珍贵硬木频频袭扰海岸。1637年，荷兰军队洗劫并焚毁圣克里斯托旺，此后这片土地处于荷兰巴西治下，直到1645年被葡萄牙收复。塞尔希培1696年成为独立都督辖区，1763年被重新并入巴伊亚，1820年7月8日若昂六世恢复其自治，圣克里斯托旺仍是重生都督辖区的首府。

en:
Jeremoabo lies in the dry sertão of northern Bahia, where caatinga scrub and the stony Raso da Catarina are crossed by the Vaza-Barris River. In 1444 this was Tupinambá country; its later recorded Tupi name, Yuru'mún-yba, referred to a pumpkin plant and belonged to the language of the villagers who kept clearings, hunting grounds and trails through the backlands.

Cattle ranches tied to Garcia d'Ávila's Casa da Torre entered the region in the seventeenth century. In the 1660s the priests Jacob Roland and João de Barros founded the Geremoabo mission to catechize and protect the local people, but the estate, seeking captive labour, burned the mission village in 1669; the colonial government and Church forced its reconstruction. By 1698 Geremoabo had the standing of a julgado, and a royal charter of 11 April 1718 raised it to the parish of São João Batista de Geremoabo do Sertão de Cima under Vila de Itapicuru.
zh:
热雷莫阿布位于巴伊亚北部干旱的内陆荒原，卡廷加灌丛和多石的卡塔里纳裸地被瓦扎巴里斯河切过。1444年，这里是图皮南巴人的土地；后来记载下来的图皮语名Yuru'mún-yba意为南瓜植株，来自这片腹地中经营垦地、猎场和小径的村民所说的语言。

17世纪，与加西亚·达维拉的卡萨达托雷相连的牧场进入这一地区。1660年代，神父雅各布·罗兰和若昂·德巴罗斯建立热雷莫阿布传教站，向当地人传教并提供保护，但谋求奴役劳动力的庄园于1669年焚毁传教村；殖民政府和教会随后迫使庄园将其重建。到1698年，热雷莫阿布已具备司法辖区地位，1718年4月11日的王室敕令又把它升为圣若昂巴蒂斯塔-德热雷莫阿布-杜塞唐迪西马教区，隶属于伊塔皮库鲁镇。

en:
Inhambupe lies inland of the Bay of All Saints, among the rolling agreste woods that separate the sugar coast from the dry sertão. The river threading the district bears a Tupi name, 'among the waters of the inhambu', a forest tinamou, but in 1444 its valleys belong to Tapuia bands, the non-Tupi, Jê-speaking hunters and gatherers whom the coastal peoples lumped together as Tapuia, 'strangers'. They moved between riverside camps, taking game and wild fruits, with no European yet within a thousand leagues.

From the late 1500s cattle herds moved up these valleys: the Casa da Torre, the ranching empire founded near Salvador by Garcia d'Ávila, drove cattle along the royal road into the sertão to supply beef and leather to the coastal sugar mills, and its vaqueiros mixed with, or enslaved, the Tapuia as they went. Jesuits had already settled at Água Fria in 1562, and the whole district long depended on that town for justice and worship. A hermitage of the Holy Spirit formed the nucleus of Inhambupe, and in 1718 the parish of Divino Espírito Santo do Inhambupe de Cima was created; by 1757 it ran three filial chapels, and in the 1780s tobacco spread alongside the cattle lands. The governor of Bahia, Fernando José de Portugal, authorized a town in 1798, and the Vila do Inhambupe was installed in 1801.
zh:
伊尼扬布皮位于万圣湾内陆，地处沿海蔗区与干旱腹地之间的阿格雷斯特疏林丘陵间。贯穿此地的河流有一个图皮语名字，意为「在伊尼扬布鸟——一种林栖䳍鸟——出没的水畔」；1444年时，河谷属于塔普亚诸部，即沿海民族笼统称为「塔普亚」（意为外族人）的非图皮、操热语的狩猎采集者。他们在河畔营地间迁徙，猎取野味、采集野果，此时欧洲人远在千里之外。

16世纪末起，牛群沿这些河谷上行：加西亚·德阿维拉在萨尔瓦多附近建立的牧业世家「塔楼庄园」沿王家大道把牛赶入腹地，为沿海糖坊供应牛肉和皮革，牧人一路与塔普亚人通婚，或将其掠为奴隶。早在1562年，耶稣会已在阿瓜弗里亚落脚，整个地区的司法与宗教事务长期隶属该镇。一座圣灵小圣堂成为伊尼扬布皮的核心，1718年「上伊尼扬布皮圣灵教区」正式设立，到1757年已下辖三座附属小教堂，1780年代烟草种植随牧场一同扩张。1798年，巴伊亚总督费尔南多·若泽·德·葡萄牙批准设镇，伊尼扬布皮镇于1801年正式建立。

en:
Pambu names a stretch of the northern Bahian sertão, where caatinga backlands reach the islands and banks of the lower-middle São Francisco. In 1444 this country was held by the various Indigenous groups the Portuguese later called Tapuia; its camps, hunting grounds and river crossings would also be remembered through the Tumbalalá, a people historically connected with the Kariri and Procá and with the old aldeia of Pambu.

The first recorded Portuguese entrada took place in 1562, when the priest Luís da Grã travelled through on a catechizing mission. The bandeira of Belchior Dias later founded the settlement of Pambu as an Indigenous aldeia, and in the seventeenth century cattle ranges and river missions drew the Rodelas sertão into Bahia's colonial frontier. In 1809 a new ranch chapel, Bom Jesus da Boa Morte, became another nucleus in the same thinly peopled borderland.
zh:
帕姆布指巴伊亚北部内陆荒原的一片土地，卡廷加旱地在这里延伸至圣弗朗西斯科河中下游的岛洲与河岸。1444年，这片地方由后来被葡萄牙人统称为塔普亚人的多个原住民族群占据；他们的营地、猎场和渡口，也通过通巴拉拉人留存于记忆中——通巴拉拉人在历史上与卡里里人、普罗卡人及旧帕姆布传教村联系在一起。

1562年，葡萄牙人首次有记载地进入这里，路易斯·达格兰神父沿途传教。贝尔希奥尔·迪亚斯的远征队后来建立帕姆布定居点，把它作为原住民传教村；17世纪，牧牛场和河畔传教站使罗德拉斯腹地被纳入巴伊亚殖民边疆。1809年，新的邦热苏斯-达博阿莫尔特牧场礼拜堂形成，成为这个人烟稀少的边地中的又一个定居核心。

en:
Rio de Contas takes its name from the upper valleys of the Contas Pequeno, the old name of the Brumado, where the cool ridges of the Chapada Diamantina rise above the Bahian sertão. In 1444 only Indians know these mountains. Pataxó bands, peoples of the Macro-Jê family, ranged between the Contas and the Pardo, hunting the gallery forests and camping above the valley mists, while the Portuguese held no more than a few beachheads on the distant coast.

Cattle came first: in the seventeenth century the Bahian sertanista Antônio Guedes de Brito drove herds into these high valleys, and around mid-century freed and runaway Africans founded a quilombo, Pouso dos Crioulos, on the Brumado. An expedition from the coast reached it in 1690, when it was already a halting place on the trail from Minas Gerais to Salvador. Then in 1710 the São Paulo bandeirante Sebastião Pinheiro Raposo struck alluvial gold in the Brumado and its streams, and a rush of Portuguese, Paulistas and Pernambucans threw up the camps of Mato Grosso and Livramento; Mato Grosso became the first parish of the alto sertão in 1718. A royal charter of 27 November 1723 created the Vila de Nossa Senhora do Livramento das Minas do Rio de Contas, installed in 1724 by Pedro Barbosa Leal; a royal road to Jacobina followed in 1725 and a crown foundry to collect the royal fifth in 1726. Fever in the riverside seat moved the viceroy to order its transfer in 1745, and in July 1746 the planned Vila Nova was laid out at Pouso dos Crioulos. Enslaved miners worked its gold until the washings petered out early in the next century, when the town fell back on stock-raising, crops and the traffic of the royal road.
zh:
里奥孔塔斯得名于孔塔斯河上游谷地——该河旧称小孔塔斯河，即今布鲁马杜河——迪亚曼蒂纳高原的清凉山脊在此耸立于巴伊亚腹地之上。1444年时，只有印第安人熟悉这片群山：属大热语族的帕塔肖诸部游猎于孔塔斯河与帕尔多河之间的长廊林中，在谷雾之上扎营，而葡萄牙人在遥远的海岸上不过占着几处滩头。

先来的是牛群：17世纪，巴伊亚腹地开拓者安东尼奥·格德斯·德·布里托把牧群赶进这些高山谷地；约在17世纪中叶，获得自由的黑奴与逃亡者在布鲁马杜河畔建起一处逃亡者聚落，名叫「克里奥尔人驿站」。1690年，一支沿海远征队抵达该地，当时它已是米纳斯吉拉斯通往萨尔瓦多商路上的宿营地。1710年，圣保罗旗兵塞巴斯蒂昂·皮涅罗·拉波索在布鲁马杜河及其支流淘得沙金，葡萄牙人、圣保罗人和伯南布哥人蜂拥而至，建起马托格罗索与利夫拉门托两处淘金营地；马托格罗索于1718年成为巴伊亚高地的第一个教区。1723年11月27日的王旨敕设「孔塔斯河金矿圣母利夫拉门托镇」，1724年由佩德罗·巴尔博扎·莱阿尔主持建镇，1725年修通通往雅科比纳的王家大道，1726年又设王室熔金所以征收五一税。因河畔镇址热病流行，副王于1745年下令迁治，1746年7月按规划在克里奥尔人驿站建成新镇。黑奴矿工在此淘采黄金，直到19世纪初砂金渐竭，城镇转而依靠畜牧、农耕和王家大道上的往来商旅。

en:
Paratinga occupies a crossing on the middle São Francisco, where the river cuts through caatinga and gives access to overland trails through western Bahia. In 1444 the banks were Indigenous country; Tuxá people are thought to have predominated around Paratinga, while other peoples of the middle river used its islands, fishing grounds and inland trails. No permanent Portuguese settlement yet existed.

Portuguese expeditions passed through between 1543 and 1550, when Duarte Coelho Pereira visited the region, and the bandeirante Belchior Dias Moreia crossed it in 1602. Permanent colonization followed in the seventeenth century after Antônio Guedes de Brito received vast sesmarias and formed the Casa da Ponte, the second-largest latifundium in colonial Brazil; its expansion destroyed much of the middle-river Indigenous population and enslaved survivors. On the Santo Antônio do Urubu de Cima ranch, a chapel of Saint Anthony built in 1680 became the nucleus of Urubu, whose inhabitants included Luso-Brazilians, Indigenous people and Africans. By 1714 it had 362 households and 3,425 people, and on 11 April 1718 it became a parish. Cattle herds rested there between Bahia and Minas Gerais; John V ordered a town in 1746, and Vila de Santo Antônio do Urubu was installed on 27 September 1749. In the later eighteenth century it was the second-largest slave market in the Jacobina comarca, receiving 601 enslaved people, and in 1819 the Casa da Ponte lands were registered and divided into six districts.
zh:
帕拉廷加位于圣弗朗西斯科河中游一处渡口，河流穿过卡廷加旱地，并连通穿越巴伊亚西部的陆路。1444年，两岸仍是原住民的土地；一般认为帕拉廷加一带以Tuxá人为主，中游的其他族群也使用河岛、渔场和内陆小径，葡萄牙人的永久定居尚未出现。

1543至1550年间，佩南布科受赠船长杜阿尔特·科埃略·佩雷拉曾到这一地区探险，远征者贝尔希奥尔·迪亚斯·莫雷亚又于1602年经过。17世纪，安东尼奥·格德斯·德布里托获得大片授地，组成殖民巴西第二大地产蓬特庄园，永久殖民才真正展开；庄园的扩张摧毁了圣弗朗西斯科河中游的大部分原住民社群，幸存者则被奴役。在圣安东尼奥-杜乌鲁布德西马牧场，1680年所建的圣安东尼小堂成为乌鲁布村的核心，居民包括葡裔巴西人、原住民和非洲人。1714年，这里有362户、3425人，1718年4月11日升为教区。往返巴伊亚与米纳斯吉拉斯的牛群在此歇脚；若昂五世1746年下令设镇，圣安东尼奥-杜乌鲁布镇于1749年9月27日正式建立。18世纪后期，它是雅科比纳司法区第二大奴隶市场，登记接收601名被奴役者；1819年，蓬特庄园的土地被登记并划分为六个行政区。

en:
Campo Largo was the old name of a broad ranching country on the Rio Grande in the far west of Bahia. In 1444 its grasslands and gallery woods were Acroá country, part of the Macro-Jê linguistic world; Acroá was later also recorded around the headwaters of the Parnaíba and Paranaíba. No Portuguese town yet stood on the river plains.

The Rio Grande lands were later included in the Casa da Ponte land grant. In the first half of the eighteenth century, adventurers from Pernambuco settled on the riverbank and raised cattle and crops. A great flood drove them to the Alto do Umbuxeiro, where the church of Nossa Senhora Santana do Campo became the nucleus of the Campo Largo settlement. On 3 June 1820 a royal charter of John VI created the Comarca do Rio de São Francisco, seated at Vila da Barra and explicitly including Campo Largo; the municipality was created under that name in the same year.
zh:
坎普拉古是巴伊亚极西部格兰德河畔一片广阔牧地的旧称。1444年，这里的草原和走廊林属于阿克罗阿人，是大热依语世界的一部分；阿克罗阿语后来也在帕纳伊巴河与巴拉那伊巴河源头一带有记录。此时河畔平原还没有葡萄牙人的城镇。

格兰德河沿岸土地后来被划入蓬特庄园的授地。18世纪上半叶，来自伯南布哥的冒险者在河畔定居，经营畜牧和农业。一场大洪水迫使他们迁往温布谢罗高地，圣安娜-杜坎波教堂在那里成为坎普拉古居民点的核心。1820年6月3日，若昂六世颁布王室敕令，设立圣弗朗西斯科河司法区，治所设在巴拉镇，并明确把坎普拉古纳入辖区；同年，坎普拉古以这个名称设为市镇。

en:
Luziânia is the south-eastern Goiás plateau, the campo around the Rio São Bartolomeu where the cerrado begins its long fall toward the Paranaíba and the mines of Minas. In 1444 it held no towns at all: Caiapó and Xavante bands of the Jê family moved through its grasslands and gallery forest, and the creek beds soon to be turned over for gold ran untouched.

Gold found the place late and fast. On 13 December 1746 the Paulista bandeirante Antônio Bueno de Azevedo, pushing northwest from Paracatu, spotted nuggets in a creek and raised a cross the next morning, dedicating the diggings to Saint Lucy. The Arraial de Santa Luzia drew more than ten thousand people within a year, and the first mass was said there in 1746 by Father Luiz da Gama Mendonça before some six thousand miners. In April 1758 thousands of enslaved Africans began the Saia Velha cut, a 42-kilometre canal finished in two years to carry water to the washings, and on 6 December 1758 the arraial became an ecclesiastical comarca. By the end of the century the gold was spent, its people drifting out to cattle ranches and farms, leaving the eighteenth-century church of Nossa Senhora do Rosário above a quiet pastoral town on the Minas road.
zh:
卢齐亚纳（中文维基作「卢齐阿尼亚」，殖民时期称圣卢齐亚）位于戈亚斯高原东南、圣巴托洛梅乌河一带的原野上，塞拉多由此向巴拉那伊巴河和米纳斯金矿区缓缓倾斜。1444年，这里没有一座城镇：热依语族的卡亚波人与沙万特人游猎于草原和林带之间，不久后要被翻遍淘金的河床，当时还无人扰动。

黄金来得晚，却来得猛。1746年12月13日，圣保罗旗手安东尼奥·布埃诺·德阿泽维多从帕拉卡图向西北探矿，在一处溪床中发现金块，次日清晨竖起十字架，把矿区献给圣卢齐亚。圣卢齐亚营地在一年内聚起上万人；同年，路易斯·达伽马·门多萨神父主礼首场弥撒，在场矿工约六千人。1758年4月，数千名非洲黑奴开工开凿「旧裙」水渠，这条42公里长的水道历时两年修成，引水淘矿；同年12月6日，营地升为教务区。18世纪末金沙耗尽，人口散向牧场和农庄，只留下18世纪的玫瑰圣母教堂，守着米纳斯大道旁一座安静的牧歌小镇。

en:
Coxim stands at the meeting of the Coxim and Taquari rivers, where the wooded cerrado breaks into the flooded plains of the Pantanal. Its first lords were Caiapó and Bororó bands; in the Bororó tongue cojim means fish, and the rivers teemed with them. In 1444 this was still Caiapó and Bororó country, known only to its own hunters and fishermen.

The place entered colonial history in 1719, when the Lemes brothers fled São Paulo and reached the new gold diggings on the Cuiabá by way of Coxim. Sesmarias were granted along the Taquari in 1727, and in 1729 Domingos Gomes Biliago and his companions founded the Arraial do Biliago on the river bank to succour the monções, the great canoe convoys from Porto Feliz: after a thirteen-kilometre portage at Camapuã they launched into the Coxim and Taquari and entered the Pantanal. Those waters were Paiaguá country, and the canoe warriors all but annihilated convoy after convoy, killing 400 men in 1730 and leaving but four survivors in 1733, until a punitive expedition destroyed one of their towns in 1734. The arraial never prospered, and in 1821 Coxim was a mere riverside waystation on a route already past its prime.
zh:
科欣位于科欣河与塔夸里河交汇处，塞拉多稀树草原在此化作潘塔纳尔的泛滥平原。这里最早的主人是卡亚波人和博罗罗人；博罗罗语中「cojim」意为鱼，而河中正盛产鱼。1444年，这里还是卡亚波人与博罗罗人的土地，只有他们自己的猎人和渔民往来其间。

1719年，莱梅斯兄弟逃离圣保罗，经科欣抵达库亚巴河畔新发现的金矿，此地由此进入殖民史。1727年，塔夸里河沿岸的土地被分赐为份地；1729年，多明戈斯·戈麦斯·比利亚戈和同伴在河畔建立比利亚戈村，接济季风船队——这些从波尔图费利斯出发的独木舟大船队在卡马庞经过13公里陆上搬运后，转入科欣河和塔夸里河进入潘塔纳尔。那一带水域是帕亚瓜人的天下，这些独木舟战士几乎接连歼灭船队：1730年杀死四百人，1733年一队仅四人生还，直到1734年讨伐队摧毁了他们的一座城镇。村庄始终没有兴旺起来，1821年时，科欣只是河畔一处小小的中途站，所在的航路也已过了鼎盛期。

en:
Alagoas takes its name from the string of coastal lagoons between Pernambuco and the lower São Francisco. In 1444 their shores were held by the Caeté, a Tupi-Guarani people who fished the lagoons and grew manioc, while older Jê groups had been pushed inland toward the sertão. Amerigo Vespucci's voyage mapped this coast in 1501, naming the São Francisco on 4 October, and French brazilwood traders were soon anchoring at the Porto do Francês. The land then formed the southern fringe of the Captaincy of Pernambuco.

Penedo arose at the wide São Francisco estuary as settlement pushed south with the sugar frontier. After the Caetés killed the shipwrecked bishop Pero Sardinha in 1556, a punitive expedition nearly destroyed them, and in 1570 Cristóvão Lins founded Porto Calvo with five engenhos. Dutch raiders burned the towns from 1630; Domingos Fernandes Calabar, the mameluco who guided them, was hanged at Porto Calvo in 1635, and the Portuguese drove the Dutch out in September 1645. In the palm forests behind the coast, runaway slaves had built the quilombo of Palmares, an African-style kingdom ruled by Ganga Zumba and then his nephew Zumbi; in January 1694 three columns of paulistas and local troops led by Domingos Jorge Velho overran its last stronghold, and Zumbi was killed on 20 November 1695. The comarca of Alagoas was created in 1710 and held nearly fifty sugar mills by 1730; cotton spread from the 1770s, and on 16 September 1817 João VI raised Alagoas to an independent captaincy, with Penedo and Porto Calvo its chief towns.
zh:
阿拉戈斯得名于伯南布哥与圣弗朗西斯科河下游之间成串的海岸潟湖。1444年，潟湖沿岸是图皮-瓜拉尼人的一支卡埃特人的地盘，他们在潟湖捕鱼、种植木薯，更早的热依诸族则被逐往内陆旱源。1501年，阿梅里戈·韦斯普奇的远航测绘这段海岸，于10月4日命名圣弗朗西斯科河；不久，走私巴西木的法国商人便在「法国人港」停泊。当时这片土地还是伯南布哥都督辖区的南部边缘。

随着蔗糖拓殖向南推进，佩内杜在宽阔的圣弗朗西斯科河口兴起。1556年，卡埃特人杀死遇海难的主教佩罗·萨尔迪尼亚，惩罚性远征几将他们灭族；1570年，克里斯托旺·林斯建立波尔图卡尔沃和五座糖坊。荷兰袭掠者从1630年起焚毁城镇，为其引路的马梅卢科人多明戈斯·费尔南德斯·卡拉巴尔1635年在波尔图卡尔沃被处绞，葡萄牙人1645年9月将荷兰人逐出。在海岸后方的棕榈林中，逃亡奴隶建起帕尔马雷斯逃奴堡——按非洲模式组织的王国，先后由冈加·尊巴和其侄祖比统治。1694年1月，多明戈斯·若热·韦柳率领圣保罗旗兵与当地联军三路并进，踏平其最后据点，祖比于1695年11月20日战死。1710年设立阿拉戈斯司法区，到1730年已有近五十座糖坊；棉花自1770年代推广；1817年9月16日，若昂六世将阿拉戈斯升为独立都督辖区，佩内杜与波尔图卡尔沃是其首要城镇。

en:
The Borborema is the broad plateau that parts the coastal forests of Paraíba and Pernambuco from the dry sertão: its eastern escarpment catches the Atlantic rains and gives birth to more than a hundred rivers, among them the Paraíba do Norte and the Pajeú, while the westward slope fades into drought-prone caatinga. In 1444 these highlands belonged to the non-Tupi peoples the Portuguese later called tapuias — Cariri, Tarairiú and Ariú bands who farmed the moist mountain hollows and hunted the scrub, and whom the coastal Tupi held for ancient enemies.

Cattle were the first European wedge into the highlands: vaqueiros drove herds up from the coast during the seventeenth century, and missions followed the ranches. The French Capuchin Martin of Nantes worked among the Cariri from 1672, and around 1676 João Duarte do Sacramento founded the Mission of Our Lady of the Mountains among the Ararobá; the Xukuru joined it in the 1690s, and it grew into Cimbres, chartered as a town on 3 April 1762. Native resistance ran on far longer: the cycle of raids and punitive columns remembered as the Barbarians' War stretched from the mid-seventeenth century into the eighteenth, as Cariri, Tarairiú and Janduí war bands fought the cattle grants eating into the sertão. In 1697 Captain Teodósio de Oliveira Ledo settled Ariú families at Campina Grande, which with Cimbres became one of the market towns of the agreste, living on cattle and, from the later eighteenth century, on cotton.
zh:
博尔博雷马是一片宽阔高原，隔开帕拉伊巴、伯南布哥的沿海林地与干旱旱源：东麓截住大西洋雨水，帕拉伊巴河北河、帕热乌河等一百多条河流发源于此，西坡则渐入易旱的卡廷加灌丛。1444年，这片高地属于后来被葡萄牙人泛称为塔普亚人的非图皮族群——卡里里、塔莱里乌和阿里乌等部落在湿润的山谷耕作、在灌丛中狩猎，沿海图皮人视他们为世仇。

牛群是欧洲人插入高地的第一个楔子：17世纪，牧牛人从沿海把畜群赶入高原，传教士也随牧场而来。法国嘉布遣会士南特的马丁1672年起在卡里里人中间传教；约1676年，若昂·杜阿尔特·多萨克拉门托在阿拉罗巴人中间建立「山中圣母」传教站，舒库鲁人1690年代并入，传教站后来发展为辛布雷斯，1762年4月3日正式设镇。土著的抵抗延续了更久：袭扰与讨伐交相循环的「野蛮人战争」从17世纪中叶一直拖到18世纪，卡里里、塔莱里乌和扬杜伊战士抗击不断蚕食旱源的牧地封授。1697年，特奥多西奥·德·奥利维拉·莱多上尉率阿里乌人在大坎皮纳定居；大坎皮纳与辛布雷斯后来同为阿格雷斯特过渡带的集镇，以畜牧为生，18世纪后期又以棉花为业。

en:
Pastos Bons lies on the chapadas of the upper Itapecuru, the dry southeastern edge of Maranhão where cerrado grasslands meet caatinga scrub. In 1444 it was Timbira country: Jê-speaking villages of the southern Maranhão interior, with Sakamekra groups nearby, moved through gallery woods, savannah and seasonal lagoons. The Europeans struggling for São Luís and the coast were far away, and the good pastures later praised by ranchers had not yet been measured into colonial land grants.

Piauí cattlemen entering from the southeast founded Pastos Bons in 1744. The trail-and-ranch frontier supplied Maranhão's coastal towns with cattle and hides. In 1755 Portuguese law declared Indians free, while the General Trading Company of Grão-Pará and Maranhão brought thousands of enslaved Africans into the wider colony to sustain cotton, rice and other exports. By 1770 ranchers from the sertões of Pastos Bons were confirming rural grants along the upper streams, and around 1820 families from the settlement pushed on toward the Itapecuru plateau, planting sugar and cotton beside their herds.
zh:
帕斯图斯邦斯位于伊塔佩库鲁河上游台地，是马拉尼昂东南的干燥边缘，塞拉多草原与卡廷加灌丛在此相接。1444年，这里是廷比拉人的土地：马拉尼昂南部内陆的热依语村群与邻近的萨卡梅克拉人，在林缘林地、稀树草原和季节性湖泊之间迁徙。争夺圣路易斯和海岸的欧洲人尚在远方，后来受牧牛人称赞的优良牧场也还没有被划成殖民授地。

1744年，从东南进入的皮奥伊牧牛人建立帕斯图斯邦斯。这条由小径和牧场组成的边疆向马拉尼昂沿海城镇供应牛只和皮革。1755年，葡萄牙法律宣布印第安人自由；同年，大帕拉与马拉尼昂总贸易公司成立，却向整个殖民地运入数以千计的非洲奴隶，以维持棉花、水稻等出口。到1770年，帕斯图斯邦斯腹地的牧场主已在上游溪流旁确认乡郊授地；约1820年，又有居民从这里继续前往伊塔佩库鲁河高原，在牧群旁种植甘蔗和棉花。

en:
Timon occupies the Maranhão bank of the middle Parnaíba, opposite the lands that became Piauí. In 1444 the river, seasonal floodplain woods and overland trails belonged to Timbira and Gamela Indians, native groups of the eastern Maranhão interior's Jê-speaking world. There was no Portuguese town or customs point: canoes and fords linked village networks, while the cattle roads and royal highway that would fix the site still lay in the future.

After the Portuguese took São Luís from France in 1615, expeditions pushed toward the Itapecuru and enslaved or displaced nearby Timbira and Gamela communities. Cattle raising, deliberately pushed inland by Portuguese land grants so that the coast could keep producing sugar, reached the Parnaíba sertão in the seventeenth century; the Fazenda Cabrobó settlement that became Oeiras took shape in the 1670s and became Vila da Mocha in 1712. When Piauí became a separate captaincy in 1718, the crossing facing Timon gained new importance. During the eighteenth century a royal road linked Vila da Mocha with Aldeias Altas, later Caxias, and Passagem de Santo Antônio, thirteen kilometres above the future town, remained the only settlement until 1779. By 1821 Timon was still a ferry hamlet on the Maranhão shore rather than a chartered town.
zh:
蒂蒙位于帕纳伊巴河中游的马拉尼昂一岸，对岸就是后来成为皮奥伊的土地。1444年，河流、季节性洪泛林地和陆上小径都属于廷比拉人与加梅拉人，他们是马拉尼昂东部内陆热依语世界的原住民。这里还没有葡萄牙人的城镇或税卡：独木舟和浅滩连接着村社网络，后来真正固定这处地点的牧牛道与王家大道尚未出现。

1615年葡萄牙从法国手中夺取圣路易斯后，探险队向伊塔佩库鲁河推进，把附近的廷比拉和加梅拉村社掳为奴隶，或逐离故土。葡萄牙授地制度刻意把养牛业推向内陆，好让沿海继续种蔗，牧牛边疆遂在17世纪抵达帕纳伊巴河腹地；后来发展为奥埃拉斯的卡布罗博牧场在1670年代成形，1712年成为莫沙镇。1718年皮奥伊成为独立辖区后，蒂蒙对岸的渡口更显重要。18世纪，一条王家大道连接莫沙镇与后来改称卡希亚斯的阿尔德亚斯阿尔塔斯；位于未来城镇上游十三公里的圣安东尼渡口，到1779年仍是唯一聚落。到1821年，蒂蒙仍只是马拉尼昂岸边的渡口村落，还不是特许城镇。

en:
Parnaguá lies in the southern Piauí cerrado beside the Lagoa de Parnaguá, the largest lake in the state; its Tupi name joins paranã, a great river, and kûá, a cove. In 1444 the camps and fields about the lagoon belonged to Pimenteira, Xerente and Acroá bands of the Ge stock, far from any European frontier.

From 1676 the governor of Pernambuco, Pedro de Almeida, granted the country as sesmarias, and the cattle fazendas that sprang up were long harried by Macoá and Rodelleiro raiders; it was these attacks that brought the founding of a fortified settlement at Parnaguá in 1698. The povoação already stood on the western shore of the lagoon in 1751, became a freguesia in 1755, and was created a vila by royal charter of 19 June 1761, installed on 3 June 1762 in the presence of the ouvidor-geral Luís José Duarte Freire. Its independence was short: on 25 June 1816 a provincial law suppressed the vila and attached its territory to Corrente, so that in 1821 Parnaguá was no more than a district of its neighbour.
zh:
帕纳瓜位于皮奥伊南部的塞拉多草原，傍着全州最大的帕纳瓜湖；其名来自图皮语，由paranã（大河）和kûá（河湾）拼成。1444年，湖周的营地和田地属于热依语群的皮门泰拉人、谢伦特人和阿克罗阿人，离任何欧洲人的边境都很遥远。

从1676年起，伯南布哥总督佩德罗·德·阿尔梅达把这片土地分赐为份地，建起的牧牛场长期遭到马夸人和「持盾人」罗德莱罗人袭扰；正是这些袭击促成1698年在帕纳瓜设防建镇。1751年湖西岸已有聚落，1755年设堂区，1761年6月19日王室诏令升为市镇，1762年6月3日在都督辖区总督察官路易斯·若泽·杜阿尔特·弗莱雷主持下正式开镇。它的独立为时不长：1816年6月25日省法令撤销该市镇，辖区并入科伦蒂，因此1821年时帕纳瓜不过是邻镇治下的一个区。

en:
Grajaú lies in south-central Maranhão on the river of the same name, a Tupi name explained as 'river of the Carajás'. In 1444 its gallery woods and crossing places belonged to Timbira and Piocobjé Indians, Jê-speaking peoples of the southern Maranhão interior. The east-bank chapada later called Porto da Chapada held no Portuguese town or land grant; canoes and overland trails served native villages rather than colonial ranches.

Permanent Portuguese occupation came only on 11 March 1811, when Ensign Antônio Francisco dos Reis founded a settlement at Manoel Valentim Fernandes's Fazenda Chapada, also called Porto da Chapada, on the east bank. Cattle and horse ranches had pushed into the region, and the river linked the new post to markets in Maranhão and neighbouring sertões. The west bank remained Timbira and Piocobjé country, and in 1814 those Indians destroyed the settlement, then numbering forty people; only six survived because they were away. Survivors returned in 1816 and named the place São Paulo do Norte, keeping a small military detachment. In 1817 the governor established the nearby Colônia Leopoldina at Estrião Grande, placing forty line soldiers under Francisco José Pinto Magalhães to guard the frontier. By 1821 Grajaú remained a fortified river-trade outpost rather than a chartered vila.
zh:
格拉雅乌位于马拉尼昂中南部的格拉雅乌河畔；这个图皮语地名被解释为「卡拉雅人之河」。1444年，河畔林地与渡口属于廷比拉人和皮奥科贝人，他们是马拉尼昂南部内陆的热依语族群。东岸后来称为沙帕达港的台地上还没有葡萄牙城镇或授地，独木舟与陆上小径服务于原住民村社，而不是殖民牧场。

葡萄牙人的永久占据迟至1811年3月11日才开始：少尉安东尼奥·弗朗西斯科·多斯·雷斯在东岸曼努埃尔·瓦伦丁·费尔南德斯的沙帕达牧场（又称沙帕达港）建立聚落。牧牛和养马边疆已经推进到此，河流也把新据点与马拉尼昂市场及周围腹地连接起来。西岸仍是廷比拉人和皮奥科贝人的土地；1814年，这些印第安人摧毁了这座已有四十人的聚落，只有六人因外出而幸存。1816年，幸存者重返此地，命名为北圣保罗，并保留一支小型驻军。1817年，总督在附近的埃斯特里昂格兰德设立莱奥波尔迪纳殖民点，由弗朗西斯科·若泽·平托·马加良斯率领四十名线列步兵守卫边疆。到1821年，格拉雅乌仍是一座有军队护卫的河贸据点，还不是特许镇。

en:
Alcântara faces São Luís across the Bay of São Marcos, its mangrove shores and tidal channels lying between the mouths of the Mearim, Pindaré and Turiaçu. In 1444 the land held a cluster of Tupinambá villages, the principal one called Tapuitapera. Canoes moved between the bay and river mouths, while mangroves and flooded channels shaped the villages' coastal world, and no European power yet contested the shore that later became the Captaincy of Cumã.

Daniel de La Touche's French expedition made contact with these villages after founding Saint-Louis in 1612 and built the first chapel at Tapuitapera. Portuguese occupation followed between 1616 and 1618, after French rule in Maranhão collapsed, and Tapuitapera became seat of the Captaincy of Cumã, first granted to Antônio Coelho de Carvalho and his grandson Francisco. The Dutch invasion of 1641 forced the Portuguese out and the settlement was abandoned, but after the reconquest it was raised in 1648 to the Vila de Santo Antônio de Alcântara, with a town hall, pillory and parish church; sugar mills and cotton cultivation returned. The Crown reincorporated the donated captaincy by royal charter around 1754. In the late eighteenth century cotton exports and enslaved African labour made Alcântara one of Maranhão's richest plantation towns, its planters and merchants facing São Luís across the bay.
zh:
阿尔坎塔拉隔着圣马科斯湾与圣路易斯相望，红树林海岸和潮汐水道位于梅阿林河、平达雷河与图里亚苏河河口之间。1444年，这里分布着一串图皮南巴村落，主村名为塔普伊塔佩拉。独木舟在海湾与河口之间往来，红树林和潮水沟渠构成村社的海岸世界，欧洲势力还未争夺这片后来成为库芒辖区的土地。

1612年，达尼埃尔·德·拉图什率领的法国远征队在建立圣路易后与这些村落接触，并在塔普伊塔佩拉建起第一座小教堂。法国在马拉尼昂的统治崩溃后，葡萄牙人于1616年至1618年间占领此地；塔普伊塔佩拉成为库芒辖区治所，最初封给安东尼奥·科埃略·德·卡瓦略及其孙子弗朗西斯科。1641年荷兰入侵迫使葡萄牙人撤离，聚落也遭废弃；收复后，它于1648年升格为圣安多尼·德·阿尔坎塔拉镇，设有市政厅、鞭刑柱和教区教堂，糖坊与棉花种植也重新恢复。约1754年，王室通过特许状收回这座赠领辖区。18世纪末，棉花出口和被奴役非洲劳工使阿尔坎塔拉成为马拉尼昂最富庶的种植园城镇之一，种植园主和商人隔湾与圣路易斯相望。

en:
Tucuruí lies on the lower Tocantins, above the river's final approach to the Pará and Amazon delta. In Tupi the name joins tukura, a grasshopper, with oby, green, and in 1444 the forests, rapids and river crossings were used by Asurini do Tocantins, Paracanã and Gavião peoples. Their camps and trails linked the lower and middle Tocantins long before Portuguese troops tried to secure the river.

French and Portuguese expeditions probed the waterway from the sixteenth century, but permanent occupation came only in the eighteenth. In 1779 Governor Telo de Meneses founded the military settlement of Vila de São Bernardo da Pederneira, responding to the growth of the Itapocu confederation; it was renamed Alcobaça in 1780. Construction of the Fort of Nossa Senhora da Fachina, later Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, followed in 1782 with indigenous and enslaved labour. The post watched Tocantins traffic, checked gold smuggled from Goiás and Mato Grosso, and served as a base against the region's quilombos; expeditions against runaway slaves and for indigenous captives also left from Baião and Cametá. Between 1809 and 1814 Alcobaça was nominally attached to the short-lived captaincy of São João das Duas Barras during the dispute over control of Tocantins navigation.
zh:
图库鲁伊位于托坎廷斯河下游，扼守河道进入帕拉河和亚马逊三角洲前的水段。其名在图皮语中由意为蚱蜢的tukura和意为绿色的oby组成。1444年时，托坎廷斯阿苏里尼人、帕拉卡南人和加维翁人在森林、急流和渡口间活动；早在葡萄牙军队试图控制托坎廷斯河以前，他们的营地和小路就已连接着河流下游与中游。

16世纪起，法国和葡萄牙远征队先后探查这条水道，但永久性占据要到18世纪才出现。1779年，总督特卢·德梅内塞斯针对伊塔波库联盟的壮大建立军镇圣贝尔纳多-达佩德内拉，1780年改名为阿尔科巴萨。1782年，当局使用印第安人和奴隶劳力修建法希纳圣母堡，后改称拿撒勒圣母堡。据点负责监视托坎廷斯河航运，查禁从戈亚斯和马托格罗索顺河走私的黄金，并作为镇压当地逃奴堡的基地；讨伐逃亡奴隶和抓捕印第安人的远征也从这里及巴扬、卡梅塔出发。1809年至1814年，在争夺托坎廷斯河航行权期间，阿尔科巴萨名义上被划入短暂存在的双河圣若昂都督领。

en:
Para takes its name from the broad tidal Pará channel south of Marajó, and its capital Portel lies in the same forested world of islands, igarapés and seasonal floodwaters. In 1444 Tupinambá and other indigenous canoe peoples used the riverbanks and rainforest clearings for fishing, planting, travel and trade between the Amazon and Tocantins systems. No Portuguese mission or military post yet marked the route later controlled from Portel.

Portel's recorded history began in the mid-seventeenth century with Arucará, a Jesuit aldeia founded by Father António Vieira for Nhengaíba people brought from the Ilha Grande de Joanes. The settlement fitted the Portuguese strategy of occupying Amazon channels also claimed by Spain and turning river navigation into effective possession. On 24 January 1758 Mendonça Furtado, president of the captaincy of Grão-Pará, installed the municipal senate and elevated the old mission settlement to Vila de Portel during the crown's reorganization of Amazonian government. In 1786 Munduruku resistance reached the town and killed several Luso-Brazilian residents, a sharp reminder that Portuguese control still depended on contested river lanes.
zh:
帕拉因马拉若岛南侧宽阔的感潮水道帕拉河得名，首府波特尔正位于这片由岛屿、溪流和季节性洪水林组成的森林水网中。1444年时，图皮南巴人和其他以独木舟为生的印第安族群在河岸与雨林开垦地捕鱼、种植、往来，并在亚马逊水系和托坎廷斯水系之间贸易；当时还没有葡萄牙传教站或军事据点标记这条后来由波特尔控制的航路。

波特尔有记载的历史始于17世纪中叶：安东尼奥·维埃拉神父建立阿鲁卡拉耶稣会传教村，安置从大若阿内斯岛迁来的年加伊巴人。这个聚落符合葡萄牙王室的战略，即占据同样被西班牙声索的亚马逊水道，把航行控制转化为实际占有。1758年1月24日，格劳帕拉都督府主席门东萨·富尔塔多设立市参议会，在王室重整亚马逊行政的过程中把旧传教村升格为波特尔镇。1786年，蒙杜鲁库人的抵抗波及该镇，杀死若干葡裔巴西居民，也清楚表明葡萄牙人的控制仍依赖那些充满争夺的河道。

en:
Santarém occupies the bluffs at the Tapajós mouth, where the clear tributary meets the sediment-laden Amazon. From about the tenth century, the Santarém or Tapajonic culture raised riverside agricultural towns here; its Tupi-related Tapajó people kept populous villages, maize fields and ceramics at the crossroads of river routes. In 1444 the confluence had no European post. Canoes linked its fishing and farming communities with upstream and downriver peoples, and the Tapajós gateway remained under Indigenous authority.

Francisco de Orellana's Spanish party entered this stretch in mid-1542 and was met by Tapajó war canoes led by Chief Chipayo. Pedro Teixeira called at the Tupuliçus settlement near the mouth in 1626 and opened trade. On 22 June 1661 the Jesuit João Filipe Bettendorff founded Aldeia dos Tapajós and built the Chapel of Our Lady of Conception. Work on the Tapajós fortress began in 1693 and ended in 1697, giving the Portuguese mission a fortified nucleus on the lower Amazon. The last Tapajó and Urucucú at the mouth were forcibly moved to the Cumaru mission in 1698, and in 1758 the settlement was raised to a town and renamed Santarém.
zh:
圣塔伦位于塔帕若斯河河口的高岸上，清澈的支流在此与挟带泥沙的亚马孙河交汇。约从10世纪起，圣塔伦文化（又称塔帕若尼卡文化）在此发展出滨河农业城镇；与图皮语有关的塔帕若斯人在河运要冲拥有人口稠密的村落、玉米田和陶器。1444年，河口还没有欧洲人的据点。独木舟把渔耕社区与上下游各族群连接起来，塔帕若斯门户仍掌握在原住民手中。

1542年中，弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷利亚纳的西班牙队伍进入这段河道，遭到酋长奇帕约率领的塔帕若斯作战独木舟拦截。1626年，佩德罗·特谢拉在河口附近的图普利苏斯聚落停靠并开启贸易。1661年6月22日，耶稣会士若昂·菲利佩·贝滕多夫建立塔帕若斯村，并修建圣母受孕小堂。塔帕若斯堡垒1693年动工、1697年完工，使这座葡萄牙传教站成为下亚马孙设有防御的核心。1698年，河口最后的塔帕若斯人和乌鲁库库人被强行迁往库马鲁传教站；1758年，该聚落升格为镇并得名圣塔伦。

en:
Pirara lies in the Rupununi, the open savanna enclosed by forest at the head of the Essequibo. In the rains its rivers spill over the flat grassland and linger as shallow lakes, and a short carry across the Pirara watershed joins the Essequibo to the Takutu and, beyond it, the Amazon. In 1444 this was the country of the Macushi, Carib-speakers who hunted the grassland, fished the floodwaters and grew cassava on the ridges, with the Arawak-speaking Wapishana their neighbours to the south. The Rupununi, or Raponani, took its name from the whistling duck of its lagoons, and the canoe-and-portage road through Pirara was the highway between two great river systems.

It was this road that fed the dream of El Dorado. In 1595 Walter Raleigh, ascending the Orinoco no farther than Angostura, heard that the golden city of Manoa stood on a vast inland lake, and in 1596 his lieutenant Lawrence Kemys learned from Carib guides that twenty days up the Essequibo and a day's portage led to a great water the Caribs called Parime — the Rupununi savanna drowned by the rains. In 1598 Jodocus Hondius engraved the lake and city on his map of Guiana, and for two centuries Europeans sought them there. From 1616 the Dutch fort at Kyk-Over-Al drew the interior's trade down the Essequibo, while on the far side of the watershed the Portuguese built up the Rio Branco; in 1789 Manuel da Gama Lobo d'Almada brought cattle and horses into those grasslands, and ranching edged up towards the divide. Yet no fort or mission ever stood on the savanna itself, and in 1821 Pirara was still Macushi country, crossed by trade paths and by the remembered road to a lake that no one ever found.
zh:
