When Radama I's Merina armies at last entered the region, the Tsimihety had no state to defend them, and the valleys passed under the rule of Antananarivo.
zh:
齐米赫蒂之地是马达加斯加中北部崎岖的山区，夹在梅里纳高地与萨卡拉瓦平原之间，雾中的河谷向索非亚河方向倾斜。齐米赫蒂人在山坡上耕种稻田、牧放瘤牛，以互不统属的村落氏族为生，头上没有国王；即使到1444年，沿海已逐渐形成穆斯林贸易城邦，这些偏远的山谷仍不臣服于任何外来统治者。

他们的族名意为「不剪头发的人」，正铭记着这份独立：当西方的萨卡拉瓦王国宣称对他们的宗主权、要求他们在国王去世时剪发服丧时，他们拒绝了。整个18世纪，他们始终是尚武而无王的族群，抵抗安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳及其儿子的统一大军。拉达马一世的梅里纳军队最终开进此地时，没有国家组织可凭的齐米赫蒂诸谷遂落入塔那那利佛的统治。

en:
Maroantsetra stands where the Antainambalana River empties into the Bay of Antongil, Madagascar's largest bay, ringed by the wettest rainforests on the island. In 1444 its Betsimisaraka ancestors lived in small Malagasy villages of fishermen and rice farmers, each under a filohany who ruled little more than a village or two; the chiefs about Antongil Bay nevertheless kept regalia that set them above their neighbours, and their slores traded rice, slaves and tortoiseshell with the dhows of the northern coast.

In August 1500 Diogo Dias, blown off course from Cabral's India fleet, became the first European to sight Madagascar, and Portuguese ships soon learned the shelter of Antongil. By the 1680s the bay and nearby Nosy Boraha were pirate anchorages where Thomas Tew, Henry Every and William Kidd watered and sold their plunder. Their children by Malagasy women became the zana-malata, and one of them, Ratsimilaho, son of the English pirate Thomas and Queen Rahena, began at Maroantsetra the union of the coast clans: from about 1710 his fifty-year rule created the Betsimisaraka confederation that stretched 400 miles to Toamasina. The union loosened after his death in 1750, and in February 1774 the Hungarian adventurer Maurice Benyovszky landed here to found the French colony of Louisbourg, with a hospital and a quarantine post on Nosy Mangabe island; the outpost did not long outlast his departure. In 1817 the armies of Radama I of Imerina subdued the whole coast, and Maroantsetra entered the Merina empire.
zh:
马鲁安采特拉位于安泰南巴兰纳河注入安通吉尔湾处。安通吉尔湾是马达加斯加最大的海湾，环抱着全岛最湿润的雨林。1444年，贝齐米萨拉卡人的先民在一个个马尔加什小村里捕鱼种稻，各由一位菲卢哈尼统辖，权力通常不出一两座村落；不过安通吉尔湾一带的酋长保留着标识其地位的仪仗，他们的单桅帆船与北方海岸通商，输出稻米、奴隶和玳瑁壳。

1500年8月，随卡布拉尔赴印度舰队失散的迪奥戈·迪亚斯成为第一个望见马达加斯加的欧洲人，葡萄牙船只很快也晓得了安通吉尔湾的避风良港。到1680年代，海湾和附近的布拉哈岛已成为海盗锚地，托马斯·图、亨利·埃弗里和威廉·基德都在此补水、销赃。他们与马尔加什女子的后代称作扎纳-马拉塔，其中拉齐米拉胡——英国海盗托马斯与女王拉海娜之子——以马鲁安采特拉为起点联合沿岸诸氏族：约从1710年起，他以五十年统治缔造了贝齐米萨拉卡联盟，海岸绵延四百英里直至图阿马西纳。他1750年死后联盟渐松，1774年2月，匈牙利冒险家莫里斯·贝尼奥夫斯基在此登陆，建立法国殖民地路易堡，设有医院，并在近海的诺西曼加贝岛上设立检疫站，但这个据点在他离开后不久便荒废。1817年，伊梅里纳的拉达马一世大军征服整个东岸，马鲁安采特拉并入梅里纳帝国。

en:
Vatomandry, on Madagascar's rain-drenched eastern shore, takes its name from two dark rocks at the water's edge and means 'Sleeping Rocks'. In the fifteenth century it was one of many small chiefdoms on this coast: Malagasy clans lived by wet-rice fields and zebu herds under filohany headmen ruling a village or two and honouring ancestors and tromba spirits; no European had yet reached the island, and trade moved only between coastal villages in canoes.

The Portuguese captain Diogo Dias first sighted Madagascar off this coast on 10 August 1500, blown off course for India. From the 1680s British and American pirates settled the eastern bays and married chiefs' daughters, fathering the mixed zana-malata, while rice, cattle and captives sailed from Foulpointe and Tamatave to the French Mascarene Islands. In 1710 Ramanano, chief of Vatomandry, was elected head of the southern Tsikoa and led its militia against the northern ports, until Ratsimilaho, a young zana-malata of Foulpointe and son of the pirate Thomas Tew, broke the Tsikoa at Fenerive in 1712 and united the shore as the Betsimisaraka confederation, ruling until his death in 1750. His weak successors let French traders and slavers dominate the coast, until in 1817 the Merina king Radama I marched 25,000 men on Tamatave and garrisoned the east; Vatomandry became a Hova centre with an active port, and by 1821 the shore lay under Merina rule.
zh:
瓦图曼德里位于马达加斯加雨水丰沛的东岸，地名得自海边两块黑色巨石，意为「安睡的岩石」。15世纪时，它只是沿岸众多小酋邦中的一个：马尔加什诸氏族耕种水田、牧养瘤牛，菲卢哈尼酋长通常只统辖一两个村落，人们敬奉祖先与通巴神灵。当时还没有欧洲人到过这座岛屿，贸易只靠独木舟在沿岸村落之间往来。

1500年8月10日，驶往印度途中被风暴吹偏航线的葡萄牙船长迪奥戈·迪亚斯最先在这一带海面望见马达加斯加。17世纪80年代起，英、美海盗在东部港湾落脚，与酋长的女儿通婚，形成混血的扎纳马拉塔人；稻米、牛和俘虏则从富尔潘特、塔马塔夫运往法国的马斯克林群岛。1710年，瓦图曼德里酋长拉马纳诺被推举为南方齐科亚联盟的首领，率民军北上攻打各港，直到富尔潘特的扎纳马拉塔青年、海盗托马斯·图之子拉齐米拉霍于1712年在费内里夫击溃齐科亚，把整条海岸联合为贝齐米萨拉卡联盟，统治到1750年去世。他的后继者软弱，法国商人和奴隶贩子逐步把持海岸；1817年梅里纳国王拉达马一世率军两万五千攻打塔马塔夫，在东部驻扎守军，瓦图曼德里成为霍瓦人治下的繁忙港口，到1821年东岸已处于梅里纳统治之下。

en:
Vohipeno lies on the low, rain-soaked Matitanana coast, the country later called Imoro, home of the Antemoro, “people of the shore.” Its villagers fished the Indian Ocean, grew rice in the coastal plains, and traded with vessels crossing the Mozambique Channel. In 1444 this was still a world of competing Malagasy clans, including the high-status Zafiraminia, while Muslim seaborne families such as the Anteony and Antalaotra were taking root through marriage and settlement. Their Arabic learning, astrology, and Sorabe script gave them influence long before a single Antemoro kingdom dominated the shore.

During the 15th and 16th centuries those newcomers merged with the local population and made Matitana the centre of Antemoro power. Around the middle of the 1500s the Zafikasimambo noble family overthrew the Zafiraminia and established a strong kingdom, using ritual sacrifice, scribal knowledge, and the authority of the ombiasy wise men to rule. Antemoro astrologers travelled to courts across Madagascar, while the coast itself became an exporter of rice and slaves by the early 1700s. Long wars with the Ikongo-Tanala later brought invasion to the plain, and in the late 18th century Antemoro leaders sought an alliance with Andrianampoinimerina of Imerina; by Radama I’s reign, Antemoro scholars served the expanding highland court.
zh:
武希佩努坐落在雨水丰沛的马塔蒂塔纳河下游海滨，这片后来称作伊莫罗的土地，是安泰莫罗人——「海岸之民」——的家园。当地人在印度洋捕鱼，于沿海平原种植稻米，也同横渡莫桑比克海峡的船只贸易。1444年时，这里仍由彼此竞争的马尔加什氏族分据，地位崇高的扎菲拉米尼亚人是其中重要势力；安泰奥尼、安塔劳特拉等来自海上的穆斯林家族则正通过联姻和定居扎根。他们掌握的阿拉伯学术、星象学与苏拉贝文字带来了巨大声望，尽管此时海岸上还没有一个统一的安泰莫罗王国。

15至16世纪，这些新来者逐渐与本地人口融合，马塔蒂塔纳成为安泰莫罗权力的中心。约在16世纪中叶，扎菲卡西姆博贵族家族推翻扎菲拉米尼亚人，建立起强固的王国，凭借祭祀、书写知识和「翁比亚西」智者的权威进行统治。安泰莫罗星象家游走于马达加斯加各地王廷；到18世纪初，这片海岸也开始输出稻米和奴隶。此后同伊孔古—塔纳拉人的长期战争把战火烧入沿海平原，18世纪末，安泰莫罗领袖谋求与伊麦里纳的安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳结盟；到拉达马一世时代，安泰莫罗学者已在扩张中的高地王廷效力。

en:
The Betsileo country is the southern half of Madagascar's central highlands, from the Mania river in the north to the granite walls of the Andringitra massif in the south, shut in by the Bongolava hills and the eastern rainforest. Its people became the island's most patient farmers, terracing the wet valleys and carrying water to flooded rice fields, with herds of zebu on the higher ground. In 1444 the land was a scatter of small clan chiefdoms, too divided to be a kingdom, its riches mostly hidden from the trade of the coasts.

In the seventeenth century the chiefdoms hardened into kingdoms — Isandra, Lalangina, Fandriana, Fisakana and others. Tradition traces their name, 'the many invincible ones', to a King Besilau who threw back an invasion by the Sakalava of Menabe in the 1670s. Isandra grew strongest, its rulers absorbing Lalangina and Vohibato and growing wealthy on trade that crossed the island to the port of Toliara. The kingdoms kept their independence through the wars of the eighteenth century, but Andrianampoinimerina's Merina armies opened the way south, and his son Radama I completed the conquest and reorganised the country as a province of Imerina; many Betsileo were enslaved, and early in the nineteenth century the Merina built Fianarantsoa as the new administrative capital over the southern highlands.
zh:
贝齐略之地位于马达加斯加中部高地南半段，北起马尼亚河，南抵安德林吉特拉山地的花岗岩绝壁，西屏邦古拉瓦丘陵，东界热带雨林。贝齐略人是岛上最勤勉的农夫：他们把湿润的山谷修成层层梯田，引水浇灌稻田，在高处牧放瘤牛。1444年，这里只是一片零散的氏族小酋邦，分裂得不足以成为王国，其富庶也大体不为沿海贸易所知。

17世纪，诸酋邦演变为伊桑德拉、拉兰吉纳、凡德里亚纳、菲萨卡纳等王国。按口传传统，他们的族名「众多不可战胜者」得自贝齐劳王——他在1670年代击退了梅纳伯萨卡拉瓦人的入侵。伊桑德拉最为强大，其君主兼并拉兰吉纳和沃希巴图，并靠穿越全岛、通往图利亚拉港的贸易致富。这些王国在18世纪的战乱中保持独立，但安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳的梅里纳大军打开了南进之路，其子拉达马一世最终完成征服，把这片土地改组为伊梅里纳的行省；许多贝齐略人沦为奴隶，19世纪初，梅里纳人修建菲亚纳兰楚阿，作为统治南部高地的新行政首府。

en:
Mahafaly is the dry limestone and sand country of southwestern Madagascar, lying between the Menarandra and Onilahy rivers around Betioky, Ejeda, and Ampanihy. Cattle, sheep, and goats shaped both wealth and chiefly power, while cassava and grain were grown in the thinner coastal plains. In 1444 the land was divided among local ruling families known as andriantsileliky, whose authority was tied to cattle, ombiasy advisers, and the great decorated tombs through which communities honored dead chiefs and ancestors.

In the 1500s the Maroserana noble Olembetsitoto defeated or displaced those older families and founded the dynasty from which the Mahafaly took their political identity; tradition held that his seclusion made the land “holy.” In June 1649 twelve Mahafaly envoys travelled to the French settlement at Fort Dauphin and hired musketeers against the Masikoro after cattle raids. The polity soon split: Sakatovo and Menarandra emerged around 1650, Linta followed about twenty years later, and Onilahy took shape around 1750. Rivalry with the Antandroy and frequent changes of rulers marked these small kingdoms, but throughout the Merina expansion of the later 18th and early 19th centuries Mahafaly remained outside highland control.
zh:
马哈法利位于马达加斯加西南部，是门纳兰德拉河与奥尼拉希河之间干旱的石灰岩和沙土地带，贝蒂乌基、埃热达和安帕尼希等城镇坐落其间。牛、绵羊和山羊既是财富，也是酋长权力的基础；居民还在较贫瘠的沿海平原种植木薯和谷物。1444年时，这片土地由称作「安德里安齐莱利基」的地方统治家族分据，他们的权威同牛群、翁比亚西顾问以及装饰宏大的坟墓紧密相连，人们借这些坟墓尊崇已故酋长和祖先。

16世纪，马拉塞拉纳贵族奥伦贝齐托托击败或取代旧有家族，建立王朝，马哈法利人的政治认同也由此形成；传说他退居隐修后，使这片土地成为「神圣之地」。1649年6月，十二名马哈法利使者前往法国人的多凡堡殖民地，在牛群遭马西科罗人劫掠后雇用火枪兵作战。这个政权随后分裂：萨卡托沃和梅纳兰德拉约于1650年形成，林塔约二十年后分立，奥尼拉希则在1750年左右成形。这些小王国交织着同安坦德鲁伊人的竞争和频繁的统治者更替；在18世纪末至19世纪初伊麦里纳扩张期间，马哈法利始终未落入高地王国控制。

en:
Anosy is the green southeastern tip of Madagascar, centred on Tolagnaro and the Efaho valley between the Masianaka and Mandrare rivers. Its people were fishermen and sailors as well as rice growers, cattle herders, blacksmiths, and carpenters. Ironworking and Indian Ocean imports reached the region by the 13th century, and in the 1400s fortified chiefdoms dominated the rice-growing valleys, exporting cattle and receiving Chinese ceramics. In 1444 the Zafiraminia elite, connected by kinship, Islamic trade contacts, and Sorabe learning with the Antemoro coast to the north, ruled a stratified and warlike society rather than a single settled kingdom.

Portuguese ships visited early in the 1500s, and in 1613 King Andriantsiambany met a Portuguese landing at Manafiafy with hundreds of warriors. The decisive foreign arrival came in 1643, when Jacques de Pronis founded Fort-Dauphin on the Antanosy village of Taolankarana. Étienne de Flacourt later governed the post, studied Malagasy customs, and wrote his History of the Great Isle of Madagascar, but French raids, enslavement, cattle theft, and involvement in local wars destroyed trust. After the Antanosy killed much of the garrison, the French evacuated in 1674. Cattle and slaves continued to leave the coast, while the Zafiraminia capital at Fanjahira and other local kingdoms remained beyond Merina control in 1821.
zh:
安塔诺西位于马达加斯加湿润的东南端，以陶拉纳鲁和马西亚纳卡河、曼德拉雷河之间的埃法霍谷地为中心。这里的人既是渔民和水手，也种植水稻、牧养牛群，并出铁匠与木匠。13世纪时，冶铁和印度洋输入品已经抵达此地；到15世纪，设防的酋长政权控制了种植水稻的谷地，输出牛群并输入中国瓷器。1444年，扎菲拉米尼亚精英统治着一个等级分明、崇尚战事的社会；他们同北方安泰莫罗海岸通过亲缘、伊斯兰贸易联系和苏拉贝学术相连，但这里还不是一个稳固的单一王国。

16世纪初，葡萄牙船只已到访这一带；1613年，国王安德里安齐安巴尼率数百名战士在马纳菲亚菲会见葡萄牙登陆者。决定性的外来者出现在1643年，雅克·德·普罗尼斯在安塔诺西村庄陶兰卡拉纳建立多凡堡。艾蒂安·德·弗拉古后来主持该据点，研究马尔加什风俗并写成《大马达加斯加岛史》，但法国人的劫掠、蓄奴、夺牛以及介入本地战争摧毁了互信。安塔诺西人歼灭大量驻军后，法国人于1674年撤离。牛和奴隶仍从这片海岸输出，而扎菲拉米尼亚人的都城凡贾希拉及其他本地王国，到1821年仍未落入伊麦里纳控制。

en:
Ibara, the Bara country, covers the grassy southern central plateaus between the Zomandao River, the Tanala forests, the Onilahy, and the Analavelona massif, with Ihosy its historic centre. Zebu herds gave the land its identity: cattle represented wealth, marriage payment, legal bargaining power, and a young man's reputation through sanctioned rustling. Fields of grain and cassava supplemented pastoral life, but never overshadowed the herds. In 1444 there was no united Bara monarchy; lineage groups and weak chiefly families moved across the plains, and the highland power of Imerina did not yet rule them.

That changed in the 17th century, when a Mahafaly noble invaded around 1640 and installed the Zafimanely ruling line. After his death in 1653 rival Zafimanely nobles fought for mastery of Ibara until about 1680, supporting themselves through cattle raids and fines rather than a regular tribute system. The late 18th century brought wider unity, and around 1800 King Raikitroka issued regulations that calmed the feuding clans. His death was followed by renewed division into competing kingdoms, yet growing regional trade in cattle and captives made Bara raiders economically stronger. In 1821 they remained fragmented but independent of the expanding Merina court.
zh:
伊巴拉即巴拉人的土地，占据中部高原南部的草原，北起佐曼道河，东至塔纳拉森林，西南接奥尼拉希河，西抵阿纳拉韦洛纳山地，历史中心是伊胡西。瘤牛群塑造了这片土地的身份：牛既是财富、聘礼和法律交涉中的筹码，年轻人也通过被社会认可的盗牛行动赢得声望。谷地中的谷物和木薯种植补充着牧业生活，却从未压倒牛群的重要性。1444年时，这里没有统一的巴拉王权；各血缘群体和势力有限的酋长家族在草原间迁徙，高地的伊麦里纳权力也尚未统治他们。

17世纪，局势发生变化。约1640年，一名马哈法利贵族入侵，建立扎菲马内利统治世系。他于1653年死后，扎菲马内利贵族们为争夺伊巴拉的主宰权混战到约1680年；他们没有固定贡赋体系，主要依靠盗牛和罚金维持力量。18世纪末，巴拉人出现较大范围的统一；约1800年，国王赖基特罗卡颁布规章，缓和了氏族仇杀。他死后，各地再度分裂为彼此竞争的王国，而地区性牛只和俘虏贸易的增长，使巴拉袭掠者在经济上更加强大。到1821年，他们虽然政治分散，却仍独立于扩张中的伊麦里纳王廷之外。

en:
Between the Manambolo and the Tsiribihina rivers the dry western plain climbs eastward into the grey limestone crags and dry forest of the Bemaraha. Sakalava tradition places the earliest home of the proto-Sakalava at Sadia, by the Manambolo's mouth. In 1444 fishing villages stood behind the shore; clans herded zebu, farmed rice in the river valleys and sold tortoiseshell and cattle to dhows making for the Muslim marts of the north. No king yet ruled here, and the Menabe kingdom was only taking shape to the south, around Morondava.

Tradition names Andriamandazoala, who reigned in the mid-sixteenth century, the founder of Menabe, and Andriandahifotsy (r. 1610-1685) armed his following with muskets bought with slaves and made the coasting trade his monopoly. At his death his sons quarrelled: about 1685 Andriamanetriarivo kept Menabe while Andriamandisoarivo marched north to found Iboina, and Menabe remained the senior Sakalava power through the eighteenth century. In 1820 and 1821 the British-trained armies of Radama I of Imerina invaded, and King Ramitraho, hard pressed, gave his daughter Rasalimo to the Merina court. The Bemaraha country did not submit in those years: in 1821 Sakalava lords still held Antsalova and the Manambolo valley.
zh:
在马南布卢河与齐里比希纳河之间，西部干旱平原向东抬升，化作贝马拉哈灰色的石灰岩刃脊与旱生林。萨卡拉瓦人的传说把最早的家园放在马南布卢河口附近的萨迪亚。1444年时，渔村散布在海岸后方，诸氏族牧放瘤牛、在河谷种植稻米，把玳瑁和牛只卖给驶往北方穆斯林商埠的独桅帆船。此时还没有国王统治此地，梅纳贝王国尚在南方穆龙达瓦一带成形。

传说把16世纪中叶在位的安德里亚曼达祖阿拉称为梅纳贝的建立者；安德里安达希富齐（1610—1685年在位）则用奴隶换得火枪，武装部众，把沿海贸易变成自己的禁脔。他死后诸子争立：约1685年，安德里亚马内特里阿里武保住梅纳贝，安德里亚曼迪苏阿里武则北上建立伊博伊纳；整个18世纪，梅纳贝始终是萨卡拉瓦诸邦中的长者。1820年和1821年，梅里纳国王拉达马一世两度派英军训练的军队来攻，国王拉米特拉胡在重压之下把女儿拉萨利莫送入梅里纳宫廷。那些年里贝马拉哈山区并未屈服：1821年时，安察卢瓦和马南布卢河谷仍在萨卡拉瓦领主手中。

en:
The Fiherenana is a short river cutting through the arid southwestern plain to a coast of reefs, sandbars and spiny bush. In 1444 Vezo fishermen — 'the people who fish' — beached their outrigger canoes along the shore, while Masikoro clans inland grazed zebu and raised maize and rice, bartering cattle and dried fish to dhows sailing between the Muslim ports of the northwest and the southern bays. The valley had no king then; its people answered to clan elders alone.

Early in the seventeenth century the Andrevola dynasty founded the kingdom of Fiherenana, the 'Masikoro kingdom', ruling the coastlands between the Mangoky and the Onilahy rivers and growing rich on cattle, rice, maize and captives sold to other Malagasy rulers and to European ships. Sakalava tradition looks back to Fiherenana as the first home of the Maroserana princes who built the Sakalava kingdoms, and in the seventeenth century the port of Toliara grew up in the valley under Andrevola suzerainty, open to European shipping. Vezo seafarers carried the coastal trade, while the Sakalava powers to the north made themselves overlords. The Merina conquests of Radama I after 1817 broke the Sakalava monarchies to the north but did not reach the Fiherenana, and in 1821 the Andrevola still ruled their dry river kingdom, though the highland armies were drawing nearer.
zh:
费希拉那河（Fiherenana）不长，切开西南部干旱平原，注入一片遍布礁岩、沙洲与多刺灌丛的海岸。1444年时，意为「打鱼之人」的维佐渔民把独木舟停靠在岸边，内陆的马西科罗诸氏族牧放瘤牛、种植玉米和稻米，用牛只和鱼干同往返于西北穆斯林港埠与南方海湾之间的独桅帆船交易。河谷里还没有国王，人们只听命于氏族长老。

17世纪初，安德雷武拉王朝建立费希拉那王国，又称「马西科罗王国」，统辖曼戈基河与乌尼拉希河之间的沿海地带，靠向马尔加什诸统治者和欧洲船只出售牛只、稻米、玉米和俘虏致富。萨卡拉瓦人的传说把费希拉那视为马罗塞拉纳诸王最早的故土，而萨卡拉瓦诸王国正是他们建立的；17世纪，图利亚拉港在河谷中兴起，向安德雷武拉王朝称臣，对欧洲商船开放。维佐水手承担了沿海贸易，北方的萨卡拉瓦强权则成为宗主。1817年后拉达马一世的梅里纳征服战争打垮了北方的萨卡拉瓦诸王国，却没有波及费希拉那；1821年时，安德雷武拉王朝仍统治着这个干旱的河畔王国，只是高原军队已经越来越近。

en:
The Qadarif country is the southern Butana, the rolling plain between the Blue Nile, the Atbara and the Ethiopian hills. It was once the eastern march of the Christian kingdom of Alodia, but by 1444 Nubian-speaking villagers planting sorghum along the rainy-season wadis lived alongside Beja herders and Arab camel nomads, all slipping loose from the weak successors of Soba. Ivory from the Ethiopian foothills passed through the local markets on its way to the Nile.

After the Funj conquest of 1504 the Butana became a grazing and grain province of the Sultanate of Sennar, its markets drawing camels, cattle and slaves. In the seventeenth century the camel-owning Shukriya made themselves the leading tribe of the southern Butana, ruling from the tribal market of Suq Abu Sinn that grew into the town of Qadarif. Armies crossed these marches in the Funj-Ethiopian wars, under Susenyos in 1618-1619 and again when Iyasu II marched through to defeat on the Dinder in 1744. When James Bruce passed in 1772, the local sheikh Fidele held the town as a vassal of Sennar. The Egyptian army of Muhammad Ali ended that allegiance in 1821, and Qadarif became a fortified garrison post.
zh:
加达里夫一带是布塔纳平原的南部，这片起伏的平原夹在青尼罗河、阿特巴拉河与埃塞俄比亚山地之间。这里曾是基督教阿勒底亚王国的东部边陲；到1444年，在季节性河谷边种植高粱的努比亚语村民，与贝贾牧人、阿拉伯骆驼游牧民杂处其间，索巴的衰弱继承者已无力约束他们。埃塞俄比亚山麓出产的象牙经当地市集运往尼罗河。

1504年丰吉人征服后，布塔纳成为森纳尔苏丹国的畜牧和谷物之地，市集上汇聚着骆驼、牛只和奴隶。17世纪，牧驼的舒克里亚人成为南布塔纳最强大的部族，在部落市集「阿布·辛恩市场」发号施令，这座市集后来发展为加达里夫城。丰吉与埃塞俄比亚的战争中，军队不止一次穿过这片边地：1618—1619年苏塞尼奥斯在位时如此，1744年伊亚苏二世的大军经此开赴丁德尔河畔的败局亦然。1772年詹姆斯·布鲁斯路过时，当地谢赫菲德莱作为森纳尔的封臣据守此城。1821年，穆罕默德·阿里的埃及军队结束了这层臣属关系，加达里夫成为设防的驻军据点。

en:
The Makua are a Bantu people who had made the lands between the coast and Lake Malawi their own by the first millennium, and their oral tradition names Mount Namuli as their first home. They lived in villages under local chiefs advised by councils, tracing descent through the mother's line, and farmed, hunted and smelted iron in shared wood-fired furnaces, forging axes, hoes and spearheads. Ivory, grain and ironwork went out along bush tracks to the Swahili towns of Angoche and Mozambique, where Gujarati and Arab merchants paid in cloth and salt. In 1444 the Makua kept to their own spirits and ancestors and answered to no outside king.

Vasco da Gama's ships passed the coast in 1498, and for two centuries the Portuguese dealt with the Makua chiefly as traders, relations staying mostly peaceful into the mid-1700s. The eighteenth century brought an ivory boom that emptied the bush of elephants, and then slave raiders: Yao caravans from the north carried Makua captives to the markets of Zanzibar, and French planters on Reunion and the Isle de France added their own demand. From 1749 the Makua fought a long war of raids and attrition against the coastal sultans, the Portuguese and their African allies, and by the early 1800s some of their own chiefs had taken to selling captives in their turn.
zh:
马库阿人是一支班图人，公元第一个千年时已在海岸与马拉维湖之间的土地上定居，口传传统把纳穆利山视为最初的家园。他们的村庄由本地首领在议事会辅佐下治理，按母系计算世系；人们农耕、狩猎，在共用的柴火炉中冶铁，打制斧头、锄头和矛头。象牙、谷物和铁器沿林间小路运到安戈谢、莫桑比克等斯瓦希里城镇，与古吉拉特和阿拉伯商人换取布匹和食盐。1444年的马库阿人仍敬奉自己的神灵与祖先，不奉任何外来的国王。

1498年，达·伽马的船队驶过这片海岸；此后两个世纪里，葡萄牙人主要以商人身份与马库阿人往来，直到18世纪中叶关系大体和平。18世纪象牙贸易暴盛，丛林中的大象被大量猎杀，随之而来的是奴隶劫掠：北方的尧族商队把马库阿俘虏运往桑给巴尔市场，留尼汪和法兰西岛的法国种植园也争相购买。1749年起，马库阿人对沿海苏丹、葡萄牙人及其非洲盟友展开长期的袭扰与消耗战；到19世纪初，一些马库阿首领自己也转而贩卖俘虏。

en: Ngindo is the inland country of the Ngindo, a Bantu-speaking people scattered through the dry woods and plateaus around Liwale, between the roads to Kilwa and Lindi and the lands of the Makua and Yao. Their villages had no centralized kingship, and local headmen managed farming, hunting and access to water. In 1444 the coast near Kilwa was still the great market for interior ivory and other forest goods, even though Portuguese troops burned and looted the city in July 1505. Ngindo and Mwera traditions place their own movement into this country in a later period; the Ngindo kept their stateless settlement pattern as Kilwa passed under increasing Omani influence toward the end of the seventeenth century and the ivory trade expanded again in the eighteenth.
zh: 恩金多是Ngindo人的内陆家园。这个操班图语的族群散居在利瓦莱周围干燥林地和高原上，地处通往基尔瓦、林迪的道路与马库阿人、尧人土地之间。他们的村社没有集权王权，由地方头领管理农耕、狩猎和用水。1444年，附近的基尔瓦海岸仍是内陆象牙和其他林产品的重要市场，但1505年7月葡萄牙军队洗劫并焚毁了这座城市。Ngindo人与Mwera人的传统把自身进入这片土地的时间放在更晚时期；17世纪末基尔瓦日益受到阿曼影响，18世纪象牙贸易再度扩张，而恩金多仍保持着没有统一国家的散居形态。

en:
The wooded Ruvuma country lies between the southern Tanganyikan coast and the Niassa interior, along the routes that later joined Lake Nyasa with Lindi and Kilwa. In the mid-fifteenth century its villages belonged to the wider Makua world: Bantu farmers, hunters and ironworkers governed by local headmen and councils, exchanging food, ivory and metal goods for cloth and salt. The Yao, or WaYao, for whom the province is named, then lived mainly toward the Lugenda River and Niassa, and were still predominantly villagers rather than Muslim caravan chiefs.

Portuguese ships entered the Mozambique Channel at the end of the fifteenth century, and early sixteenth-century traders soon encountered Makua merchants; Portuguese power long remained strongest on the coast. In the eighteenth century, surging Indian Ocean demand for ivory enlarged the old inland paths, and Yao caravans carried ivory and grain from Niassa to Arab and Swahili merchants, receiving cloth and firearms in return. As Omani and French plantation demand turned the commerce toward slaves, Yao raiders seized Makua and Lomwe villagers; from 1749 Makua communities fought a long war of attrition against coastal sultans, the Portuguese and allied African traders. In 1821 most people around Wayao still followed ancestral rites and village headmen, with mass conversion to Islam still in the future, but guns and raiding had already entered the Ruvuma caravan country.
zh:
林木覆盖的鲁伍马地区位于坦噶尼喀南部沿海与尼亚萨内陆之间，处在后来连接尼亚萨湖与林迪、基尔瓦的商路上。15世纪中期，这里的村落属于更广的马库阿世界：班图农民、猎人和冶铁者由地方首领及议事会管理，用粮食、象牙和铁器交换布匹与食盐。省名所指的瓦窑（WaYao，尧人）当时主要生活在卢任达河与尼亚萨方向，仍以村社农耕为主，还不是后来的穆斯林商队首领。

15世纪末，葡萄牙船只进入莫桑比克海峡，16世纪初的商人很快接触到马库阿交易者，但葡萄牙势力长期集中在沿海。18世纪，印度洋对象牙的需求激增，旧有内陆商路扩大；瓦窑商队把尼亚萨的象牙和粮食运给阿拉伯与斯瓦希里商人，换回布匹和火器。随着阿曼与法国种植园需求把贸易推向奴隶，瓦窑劫掠者开始掳走马库阿和隆韦村民。1749年起，马库阿诸社对沿海苏丹、葡萄牙人及与其结盟的非洲商人展开长期消耗战。1821年的瓦窑一带，多数人仍遵循祖灵仪礼和村社首领，大规模改宗伊斯兰教还是后来的事，但枪支与劫掠已经进入鲁伍马商路地区。

en:
Katsekera covers the lowlands at the south-eastern end of Lake Malawi, where the lake drains into the Shire River and Nyanja fishermen keep canoes on the sandbars. Its people belong to the Maravi cluster, the Chewa-speaking peoples whose Kalonga rules south of the lake from Mankhamba and Manthimba. In 1444 the country answers to the Kalonga's kinsmen, its villages paying tribute in ivory, while beyond the hills to the east the Yao keep their own villages and trade ivory and grain with the Muslim merchants of the coast.

The Maravi order reached its height in the following two centuries. In 1616 the Portuguese trader Gaspar Bocarro crossed the lake country on his way overland from Tete to Kilwa, the first European to leave an account of it, and was entertained by Kalonga Muzura, under whom trade flourished until his death in the 1640s. During the 1700s the confederacy's succession broke down and the Kalonga lost his grip on outlying lands; territorial chiefs sold ivory directly to coastal caravans. Yao traders from the Chiconono hills in Niassa then opened routes westward to the lake, exchanging cloth, beads and weapons for ivory and grain, so that by 1821 the old Maravi overlordship had given way to a network of Yao caravan roads.
zh:
卡泽克拉位于马拉维湖东南端的湖岸低地，湖水在此经希雷河南下，尼亚萨渔民的独木舟停泊在沙洲上。这里的居民属于马拉维族群——讲奇切瓦语的各族尊居于湖南岸曼坎巴和曼蒂姆巴的卡隆加为共主。1444年，此地由卡隆加的亲族管辖，各村以象牙纳贡；东面山地之外是尧人的村寨，他们把象牙和粮食贩运给海岸的穆斯林商人。

此后两个世纪是马拉维秩序的鼎盛期。1616年，葡萄牙商人加斯帕尔·博卡罗从太特走陆路前往基尔瓦，途中穿过湖区，成为最早留下文字记载的欧洲人，并受到卡隆加·穆祖拉的款待；穆祖拉治下商路繁盛，直至他于1640年代去世。18世纪，马拉维的继承制度瓦解，卡隆加对边缘之地失去控制，各地酋长直接向沿海商队出售象牙。来自尼亚萨省西北部希科诺诺一带山地的尧人随即向西开辟通往湖区的商路，以布匹、珠子和武器换取象牙与粮食；到1821年，旧的马拉维宗主权已让位于纵横交错的尧人商路。

en:
Lolo is the inland plateau between the Shire valley and the Portuguese town of Quelimane, rolling miombo country watered by the Licungo and its sister rivers. Its people, the Lolo, are the southern branch of the Makua: hoe farmers and smelters of iron who worked the ore in charcoal hearths and forged axes and spear-blades. In 1444 their headmen rule scattered villages, selling ivory, grain and ironware to Muslim merchants on the Nampula coast, and the first Portuguese coming up from Quelimane will find them around Tete on the Zambezi.

That first Portuguese account, of the 1569 expedition up the Zambezi, places the Lolo around Tete; by 1590 they had been pushed eastward into the country they have occupied ever since. The pressure came from the Maravi chief Lundu on the Shire, whose Zimba warriors overran Sena and Tete, defeated the Portuguese in 1592 and 1593 and made Lolo headmen pay tribute, until Lundu made peace in 1599. Through the 1600s and mid-1700s the Makua kept the peace with Quelimane, and an eighteenth-century ivory boom sent tusks out through its port. From 1749 a Makua war of attrition against the coastal Muslim sultanates and the Portuguese disrupted the trade roads, while Yao raiders began pressing south; by 1821 the Lolo country lived under the shadow of the growing slave trade.
zh:
洛洛是希雷河谷与葡萄牙城镇克利马内之间的内陆高原，一片连绵的林地草原，利昆戈河及其支流穿行其间。这里的洛洛人是马库阿人的南支：他们锄耕为业，又在炭窑中冶铁，打制斧头和矛头。1444年，各地头人管辖着星散的村落，把象牙、粮食和铁器卖给楠普拉海岸的穆斯林商人；后来从克利马内北上的葡萄牙人，最早将在赞比西河畔的太特见到他们。

1569年远征赞比西河的葡萄牙人留下第一份记载，当时洛洛人还住在太特一带；到1590年，他们已被东逐到此后一直居住的土地。压力来自希雷河畔的马拉维酋长隆杜：他的津巴武士攻陷塞纳和太特，于1592年和1593年两度击败葡萄牙人，迫使洛洛头人称臣纳贡，隆杜最终于1599年议和。整个17世纪和18世纪中叶，马库阿人与克利马内相安无事，18世纪的象牙热潮使大批象牙经该港出口。1749年起，马库阿人对沿海穆斯林苏丹国和葡萄牙人展开长期消耗战，商路时断；与此同时尧人开始自北向南袭扰；到1821年，洛洛之地已笼罩在日益兴盛的奴隶贸易阴影之下。

en:
Lundu rules the Lower Shire valley, hot and fertile floodplain where the Shire winds south through Nsanje to the Zambezi. Its people are the Mang'anja of the Maravi cluster, hoe farmers who wove cotton cloth and dried fish on the riverbanks. Their chiefs draw power not only from the ivory trade to the coast but from the Mbona rain shrine at Nsanje, where the prophetess speaks for the slain rain spirit. The first Lundu, a kinsman of the Kalonga who broke away in a succession quarrel, set his seat at Mbewe near Chiromo; in 1444 his successor rules the valley as a Maravi paramount, its headmen sending ivory down the Shire.

In the later 1500s Lundu grew into a warrior power with the Zimba, a mercenary host said to have come north across the Zambezi. Zimba arms swallowed the Lolo and Makua country to the east, and in 1592 and 1593 they destroyed two Portuguese armies before Sena and Tete, holding a double-palisaded fort against artillery; in 1599 Lundu offered peace and it was accepted. The title Lundu first appears in a written record with Gaspar Bocarro in 1616, and in 1622 Kalonga Muzura, backed by the Portuguese, crushed Lundu's revolt and made the valley part of his empire. Through the 1700s the Maravi paramountcy withered, and by the century's end Portuguese slave traders raided up the Shire. About 1800 a chief named Mankhokwe seized the Middle Shire and claimed the Lundu title, while Tengani held the lower river; famine in the 1820s left the old Lundu a name without power by 1821.
zh:
隆杜统治着希雷河下游谷地——一片炎热肥沃的冲积平原，希雷河经恩桑杰南流汇入赞比西河。这里的居民是马拉维集群南支的曼甘贾人，他们锄耕、织棉布，在河岸边晒鱼干。酋长的权势既来自通往海岸的象牙贸易，也来自恩桑杰的姆博纳祈雨圣所：女先知在那里为遇害的雨神传谕。第一代隆杜本是卡隆加的亲族，在一场继承之争中率部出走，定都奇罗莫附近的姆贝韦；1444年，其继承者作为马拉维人的大君统治谷地，各头人沿希雷河上呈象牙。

16世纪后期，隆杜借助津巴武士成为军事强权——这支雇佣兵据说从赞比西河南岸北来。津巴兵锋东向，吞并洛洛与马库阿之地，又于1592年和1593年在塞纳、太特连歼两支葡萄牙军队，凭双重木栅据寨抵住火炮；1599年隆杜主动议和，为葡萄牙人接受。「隆杜」称号最早见于1616年加斯帕尔·博卡罗的行记；1622年，卡隆加·穆祖拉在葡萄牙人支持下镇压了隆杜的反叛，将谷地纳入其帝国。18世纪，马拉维的宗主权日趋瓦解，到世纪末葡萄牙奴隶贩子已溯希雷河劫掠。约1800年，酋长曼霍克韦夺取希雷河中游并僭称隆杜，滕加尼则据守下游；1820年代大饥馑之后，到1821年，旧日的隆杜只剩名号，再无实权。

en:
The Kalonga's lands lie in the Chewa heartland south of Lake Malawi, in the rolling hills between the lake and the Shire valley. Chewa farmers who had migrated from Katanga settled here from the 12th century; the later Phiri clan brought kingship, and its ruler took the title Kalonga, fixing his capital of Manthimba – the archaeological site known as Mankhamba – near the ancient rain-shrine hill of Kaphirintiwa. By the early 15th century the Kalonga headed a confederacy of kinsmen and subject chiefs who sent ivory to the capital, while smiths sent iron tools and cloth down the trade routes to the coast in exchange for glass beads and copper. In 1444 his court, balanced by the Makewana priestess and her rain cult, was already one of the great inland powers east of the Zambezi.

During the 16th century the Kalonga's kinsman Lundu broke away to the lower Shire, grew rich on the Zambezi trade and allied with the warrior Zimba, who defeated the Portuguese in 1592 and 1593. The Portuguese settled on the Zambezi then met the Kalonga's power directly: in 1616 Gaspar Bocarro, the first European to leave an account of the Maravi, was hosted at the southern court of Muzura. Muzura had aided the Portuguese against the enemies of Mwenemutapa Gatsi Rusere in 1608, and with Portuguese help he overthrew Lundu in 1622 to become the undisputed Maravi overlord. In 1629 he turned against his former allies and joined Mwenemutapa Kapararidze in an attempt to sweep them from Zambezia, but his assault on Quelimane failed. After Muzura's death in the 1640s the empire grew rich no longer: succession disputes split the court, chiefs sold ivory directly to coastal merchants, and gun-armed Yao traders opened new routes and began raiding Chewa villages for slaves. Manthimba was abandoned in the late 18th or early 19th century, and by 1821 the Kalonga's writ scarcely ran beyond his own settlement.
zh:
卡隆加之地位于马拉维湖南岸的切瓦人腹地，是湖泊与希雷河谷之间的起伏丘陵。12世纪起，自加丹加迁徙而来的切瓦农民在此定居；较晚到来的菲里氏族带来了王权，其首领号称卡隆加，并在古老的祈雨圣山卡菲林蒂瓦附近定都曼廷巴，即考古所见的曼坎巴遗址。到15世纪初，卡隆加已统辖一个由亲族和附庸酋长组成的联盟，各地把象牙送往都城，铁匠打出的铁器和布匹沿商道输往海岸，换回玻璃珠与铜。1444年时，他的宫廷与掌握祈雨崇拜的马克瓦纳女祭司相互制衡，已是赞比西河以东的内陆强权之一。

16世纪，卡隆加的亲族隆杜在下希雷河自立，靠赞比西河贸易致富，并与尚武的津巴人结盟，后者于1592年和1593年两度击败葡萄牙人。定居赞比西河的葡萄牙人随即直接领教了卡隆加的力量：1616年，最早留下马拉维记载的欧洲人加斯帕尔·博卡罗，在穆祖拉的南方宫廷受到接待。穆祖拉曾在1608年协助葡萄牙人攻打穆韦内穆塔帕·加齐·鲁塞雷的敌人，1622年又借葡萄牙之力推翻隆杜，成为马拉维无可争议的共主；1629年他反戈相向，与穆韦内穆塔帕·卡帕拉里泽联手，企图把葡萄牙人逐出赞比西亚，但对克利马内的进攻以失败告终。穆祖拉于1640年代去世后，帝国盛况不再：继承之争撕裂宫廷，酋长们直接向海岸商人出售象牙，持枪的尧人商人另辟商路，开始掳掠切瓦村庄为奴。曼廷巴在18世纪末或19世纪初被废弃，到1821年，卡隆加的号令已几乎不出自己的村寨。

en: The Kinga, or Wakinga, are Bantu highlanders of the Kipengere Range, called the Livingstone Mountains where it rises above the northeastern shore of Lake Nyasa. Montane grasslands, forested stream valleys and steep escarpment paths separated their clan settlements; the Sanga clan was the largest and historically dominant lineage. Beside the clans, priests of the Lwembe shrine claimed a ritual line older than chiefly authority. In 1444 this was a decentralized farming and ironworking country: Kinga smelters made hoes and spear points for Nyakyusa and Ngonde neighbours, receiving food, cattle and salt in return. During the following centuries that lake-region traffic continued in iron, cloth, pottery and salt, while Ngonde ivory also entered routes toward the coast. By 1821 the Kinga clans and Lwembe rites still belonged to the steep mountain world above the lake plain rather than to a Swahili coastal state.
zh: 金加人（Wakinga）是基彭盖雷岭的班图语高地居民；山岭在尼亚萨湖东北岸一带又称利文斯通山。山地草场、溪谷森林和陡峭崖路把各氏族村落分隔开来，桑加氏族是其中最大、历史上居于统治地位的支系。除氏族首领外，侍奉卢恩贝神祠的祭司自称承接着比首领权威更古老的仪礼谱系。1444年，这里是分散的农耕与冶铁社会：金加匠人打造锄头和矛镞，同湖滨的尼亚库萨人、恩贡德人交换粮食、牲畜和盐。此后几个世纪，铁、布匹、陶器和盐继续在湖区与高原间流动，恩贡德象牙也进入通向沿海的商路。到1821年，金加氏族和卢恩贝祭仪仍深属于湖滨平原上方的险峻山地，而不属于任何斯瓦希里海岸政权。

en:
Makonde is the thicket-covered plateau west of Lindi, bounded by the Lukuledi River to the north and the steep Ruvuma escarpment to the south. In 1444 its scattered Bantu hamlets lay on the Makua and Yao linguistic borderland. Kin groups farmed the high ground, honoured ancestor spirits, and kept wooden sculpture tied to initiation rites. There was no single king or chief: the clans later called Makonde lived in autonomous villages across the Newala and Mueda heights, and their men were already skilled carvers of the dense blackwood called mpingo.

During the eighteenth century the revival of Kilwa's ivory and slave trade sent caravans and raiders toward the plateau. Makonde clans moved upward from the Ndonde lowlands of northern Mozambique into the Mueda and Newala heights, seeking healthier ground and refuge from slavers; by 1800 Portuguese observers noted that the Mueda Plateau was being populated by Makonde. Dense bush and steep paths protected their scattered settlements. Villages were coordinated by litawa kin groups and mwenyekaya elders rather than chiefs, while mapiko mask dances and blackwood carving marked initiations and ancestral observances. Makonde oral and written accounts alike describe stubborn resistance to African, Arab and European slavers. By 1821 Portuguese power on the coast had not penetrated the escarpments, and the highland villages still governed themselves.
zh:
马孔德是林迪以西、灌木覆盖的高原，北缘有卢库莱迪河，南缘是鲁伍马河陡崖。1444年，散布在溪谷间的班图农社处在马库阿与尧语族群的交界地带。各血族在高地耕作、祭祀祖灵，并把木雕与成年仪式结合在一起。这里没有单一国王或酋长：后来被称作马孔德的氏族分居新瓦拉和穆埃达高地，组成自治村落；男子善用名为姆平戈的致密黑木雕刻。

18世纪，基尔瓦的象牙与奴隶贸易再度兴盛，商队和劫掠者向高原逼近。马孔德诸氏族从莫桑比克北部的恩东代低地迁入穆埃达、新瓦拉等高地，既为躲避疫病，也为躲避奴隶贩子；到1800年，葡萄牙观察者已注意到穆埃达高原正在被马孔德人占据。密林和陡崖保护了分散村落，社会由「利塔瓦」血族和「姆文耶卡亚」长老协调，而不是由酋长统治；「马皮科」面具舞和黑木雕刻贯穿成年礼与祖灵仪式。英文和葡文资料都记载，马孔德人长期抵御非洲人、阿拉伯人和欧洲奴隶贩子。到1821年，葡萄牙人的沿海势力仍未穿越陡崖，高地村社依旧自治。

en: The Phangwa, or Wapangwa, are Bantu highlanders of the eastern Livingstone escarpment above Lake Nyasa, concentrated around Ludewa, Mlangali and Mawengi. In 1444 these steep ridges were clan country rather than the seat of a king: Pangwa households farmed the high valleys, with Kinga neighbours to the north, Kisi and Manda communities near the lakeshore, and Yao and Makonde country opening to the east. Local accounts describe clans drawing together in Ludewa after wars in the Malawi and Mozambique direction. Through the following centuries the high valleys remained a stateless society of mountain kin groups, set between lakeshore fishing villages and the Ruvuma caravan world. By 1821 no coastal governor or great chiefly court had been established in Phangwa, and its ridges were still governed through elders and lineage communities.
zh: 庞瓦（Phangwa/Wapangwa）是尼亚萨湖东岸利文斯通崖地上的班图语山民，聚居在卢代瓦、姆兰加利和马文吉一带。1444年，这些陡峭山脊是氏族之地而非王权所在：庞瓦农户在高谷耕作，北邻金加人，湖滨分布着基西人和曼达人，东面则通向瓦窑与马孔德人的地区。地方记载称，一些氏族因马拉维、莫桑比克方向的战争迁来，在卢代瓦一带汇聚。此后几个世纪，高谷仍保持无国家的山地血族社会，夹在湖滨渔村与鲁伍马商路世界之间。到1821年，庞瓦仍没有沿海总督或大酋长宫廷设治，山脊事务依旧由长老和血缘村社处理。

en:
Ngonde lies at the north-western end of Lake Malawi, between the Songwe River in the north and the North Rukuru, a warm lakeshore plain cut by rivers and marshes. In the fifteenth century it was held by scattered Bantu farming villages; digs at Mbande Hill show a settled community there between 1410 and 1480. Its people grew millet and bananas, kept a few cattle, and fished and hunted elephant along the lake, living under local headmen with no paramount power over them. In 1444 these homesteads were still a quiet backwater, scarcely touched by the caravan trade that ran between the great lakes and the Indian Ocean.

Around 1600 the Ngonde, an offshoot of the Nyakyusa peoples who lived north of the Songwe, crossed the river and densely settled the Karonga plain, mingling with and absorbing the villagers already there. Their mixed farming of bananas, millet and cattle throve on the lakeshore soils, and homesteads spread steadily south and west. Strong local chiefs ruled under a paramount, the Kyungu, chosen from one of two princely lineages and enthroned at Mbande Hill, whose authority was chiefly ritual and religious rather than direct command. For two centuries the plain grew populous behind its swamps and rivers, and although ivory was taken from its elephant herds, no coastal traders reached the Ngonde before the nineteenth century.
zh:
恩贡德位于马拉维湖西北端，北起松圭河、南至北鲁库鲁河，是一片湿热的湖岸平原，河汊与沼泽交错、土地肥沃。15世纪时，这里散居着班图语农耕村落；姆班德山的考古发掘显示，1410至1480年间山上已有定居聚落。居民种植粟和香蕉，畜养少量牛，在湖边捕鱼、猎象，由各自的头人管辖，没有更高的共主。1444年的湖岸仍是一处安静的边地，大湖与印度洋之间的商队贸易几乎未曾波及这里。

约在1600年，原本住在松圭河以北的尼亚库萨人的一支——恩贡德人渡过河南下，在卡龙加平原密集定居，与当地原有村民杂处并逐渐融为一体。他们经营香蕉、粟和养牛相结合的混合农业，在湖岸沃土上繁盛起来，聚落不断向南、向西扩展。恩贡德各酋长势力强大，之上设有共主「昆古」，从两支王族世系中选出，驻地在姆班德山；昆古的权威主要在祭祀与宗教层面，对地方酋长并无多少直接号令之权。此后两个世纪，平原凭沼泽与河流为屏，人烟日盛；林中有象群、出产象牙，但直到19世纪之前，始终没有海岸商人到来。

en:
The Tumbuka plateau rolls between the Luangwa valley and the western shore of Lake Malawi, grassland broken by the Henga valley and the Nkhamanga plains. Tumbuka clans entered it from the country of the Luba in the early fifteenth century, drifting eastward with their goats and sheep, and by 1444 they were the people of the land: Henga in the northern valleys, Kamanga around Nkhamanga, Phoka below the Nyika plateau, Tonga by the lake. They were peaceful villagers growing millet in scattered homesteads, ruled by their own clan heads, with no king above them and no tribute beyond the occasional gift of a leopard or lion skin. Elephant herds roamed everywhere, yet ivory had little value to them until strangers came to buy it.

For three centuries the clans multiplied and spread, south to the Bua and west into what is now Zambia, still without a single ruler. From the mid-eighteenth century long-distance traders from Unyamwezi, dressed in Arab fashion and called Balowoka, 'the people who crossed over', were buying ivory as far inland as the Luangwa, paying with cloth, beads, cowries and iron hoes. Around 1780 one of their leaders, Mulowoka, crossed Lake Malawi and landed at Chilumba, then made his way inland to Nkhamanga; his free-handed gifts of hoes and cloth and his marriages into the leading Luhanga and Kumwenda clans made him a chief. Around 1805 his son became the first holder of the kingship title Chikulamayembe, Swahili for 'pick up the hoes', ruling at Bolero over a loose federation that reached from the Songwe to the Dwangwa. By 1821 the trade-built kingship of Nkhamanga stood at the height of its power.
zh:
通布卡高原地处卢安瓜河谷与马拉维湖西岸之间，草原连绵，间有亨加河谷与恩卡马加平原。15世纪初，通布卡诸氏族从卢巴故地东迁，赶着山羊和绵羊涉河东来，到1444年已成为这片土地的主人：亨加人居于北部河谷，卡曼加人在恩卡马加一带，福卡人住在尼伊卡高原南麓，通加人在湖岸。他们是安土重迁的农人，在分散的田庄里种粟，由各自的氏族头人治理，上面没有国王，也没有常赋，至多献上一张豹皮或狮皮。境内象群出没，但在外来买家出现之前，象牙在他们眼中并无多大价值。

此后三个世纪，诸氏族生齿日繁，向南散布到布阿河、向西进入今赞比亚境内，始终没有共主。从18世纪中叶起，来自乌尼亚姆韦齐的长途商人出现了，他们装束如阿拉伯人，被称作巴洛沃卡，意为「渡水而来的人」，一路深入卢安瓜河谷收购象牙，以布匹、串珠、海贝和铁锄作价。约1780年，他们的首领穆洛沃卡渡过马拉维湖，在奇伦巴上岸，循陆路进入恩卡马加；他四处散送锄头和布匹，又与当地最有权势的卢汉加、库姆温达两氏族联姻，被拥戴为酋长。约1805年，他的儿子成为王号「奇库拉马延贝」（斯瓦希里语，意为「拿起锄头」）的第一任持有者，驻于博莱罗，统辖着一个松散的联盟，疆域北起松圭河、南至德万瓜河。到1821年，这个建立在象牙贸易上的恩卡马加王权正处于鼎盛之时。

en: Lala is the well-watered plateau around Serenje, where streams cut through fertile woodland and drop at the Kundalila and Chipota falls. Its people speak Ilala, a Bantu language close to Bisa and Bemba; Lala oral history traces their clans to the Luba-Lunda world farther north before they settled this part of the upper Zambezi basin. In 1444 the country was held in dispersed farming, hunting and fishing villages rather than a royal capital. Chiefs, district headmen called chilolos and village sulutani kept the chiefdoms' boundaries, while the senior ruler bore the title Kankomba-we-Lala and the royal house was Bena Nyendwa; the Insaka ye Lala council advised the chiefs and settled disputes between them. Families cleared woodland by the chitemene method for finger millet, sorghum, cassava and groundnuts, and through the following centuries their harvests, traps, spears, fish weirs and hunting grounds remained the substance of these small highland chiefdoms.
zh: 拉拉是塞伦杰周围水草丰沛的高原，溪涧穿过肥沃林地，在昆达利拉和奇波塔形成瀑布。居民使用伊拉拉语，这是一种与比萨语、本巴语相近的班图语；拉拉口传历史称，诸氏族来自更北方的卢巴-隆达世界，后来在上赞比西盆地这一带定居。1444年，此地并非围绕王城组织，而是由分散的农耕、狩猎和渔业村落构成。酋长、称作「奇洛洛」的地区头人以及称作「苏卢塔尼」的村头维系各酋邦边界；最高首领称号为「坎孔巴-韦-拉拉」，王室称「本纳·延杜瓦」，「因萨卡·耶·拉拉」议事会为酋长出谋划策并调解酋邦争端。人们用奇泰梅内方式伐林烧灰，种植手指粟、高粱、木薯和花生；在此后数世纪里，收成、陷阱、长矛、鱼梁和猎场始终是这些高原小酋邦赖以生存的根基。

en:
Nsenga is the broad Luangwa valley, where the river curls south between wooded escarpments to meet the Zambezi, and the plateau above it. Its Nsenga people keep cattle, goats and sheep and grow millet, sorghum and groundnuts; their name is said to mean 'the journey', for the long trek that brought their clans out of the Luba country to the north. They had no kings, only clan heads called tumvi, and in 1444 their autonomous villages scatter the valley, while the Maravi kingdoms of the Shire country are still far away.

In the 1600s the Maravi chief Undi, ruling from Mano on the Tete side, pushed his authority west to the Luangwa, and the eastern Nsenga may have paid him tribute, though their own traditions remember no conquest. Early in the 1700s the Portuguese opened the feira of Zumbo at the Luangwa's mouth on the Zambezi, and its traders canoed up-river to buy ivory, drawing the Nsenga villages into the Zambezi trade. By the turn of the nineteenth century the Nsenga had broken from Undi. In 1804 the chief Mburuma fell on Zumbo and drove the Portuguese out, closing the fair; it was only reopened in 1820, on the eve of the valley's nineteenth-century troubles.
zh:
恩森加是卢安瓜河的宽阔河谷——河流在林木覆盖的崖壁间蜿蜒南去，汇入赞比西河——以及河畔的高原。恩森加人牧养牛、山羊和绵羊，种植粟、高粱和花生；据说族名意为「旅途」，纪念诸氏族从北方卢巴之地远道迁来的漫长行程。他们没有王，只有称「通比」的氏族长老；1444年，自治的村寨星散于河谷之中，希雷河一带的马拉维诸王国此时还远在南方。

17世纪，以太特一侧的马诺为都的马拉维酋长温迪把势力向西推进到卢安瓜河，东部恩森加人可能曾向他纳贡，但他们自己的口述传统里没有被征服的记忆。18世纪初，葡萄牙人在卢安瓜河汇入赞比西河处开设宗博集市，商人乘独木舟溯河收购象牙，恩森加村寨由此卷入赞比西贸易。到19世纪初，恩森加人已脱离温迪。1804年，酋长姆布鲁马袭击宗博，逐走葡萄牙人，集市就此关闭；直到1820年才重新开市，此时河谷19世纪的动荡已迫在眉睫。

en:
The Lomwe speak eLomwe, a tongue close to Makua, and hold the well-watered highland belt that rises between the Shire valley and the coastal plains of northern Mozambique. They farmed the hillsides, smelted iron and gathered ivory, living in village clusters under their own headmen. In the fifteenth century the Maravi confederation grew up around Lake Malawi under its Kalonga kings, whose kinsmen founded tributary chiefships far to the east. By 1444 the Lomwe lands lay on this eastern edge of the Maravi world, sending ivory toward the lake and receiving beads and cloth in return.

Portuguese traders pushing up from the Zambezi reached the Maravi courts around the end of the sixteenth century, and in 1616 Gaspar Bocarro crossed the country, the first European to leave an account of it. Under Kalonga Muzura, who aided the Portuguese against the Mwenemutapa in 1608 and subdued the rival Lundu in 1622, Maravi power stood at its height, though Muzura's attack on Quelimane in 1629 failed. From the mid-1700s the royal succession broke down, outlying chiefs struck their own bargains with coastal merchants, and Yao caravans from the north turned the old ivory paths into slave routes. By 1800 the Lomwe headmen answered to no Kalonga and lived amid the raiding.
zh:
隆韦人讲与马库阿语相近的隆韦语，居住在希雷河谷与莫桑比克北部沿海平原之间湿润的高地带上。他们在山坡上耕种、冶铁、获取象牙，在各村首领治理下聚寨而居。15世纪，奉卡龙加为王的马拉维联盟在马拉维湖一带兴起，王族子弟四出建立纳贡的酋长国。到1444年，隆韦之地已处在马拉维世界的东缘，象牙输往湖区，换回珠子和布匹。

16世纪末，沿赞比西河北上的葡萄牙商人接触到马拉维诸廷；1616年，加斯帕尔·博卡罗穿越此地，是留下文字记载的第一个欧洲人。卡龙加·穆祖拉在位时，1608年助葡萄牙人攻打姆韦尼·马塔帕，1622年征服对手伦杜，马拉维国势达到顶峰，但他1629年攻打克利马内失败。18世纪中叶起，王位继承制度崩坏，边远酋长径自与沿海商人交易，北方尧族的商队把旧日的象牙之路变成贩奴路线。到1800年前后，隆韦首领已不再听命于任何卡龙加，在四境的劫掠中各自求存。

en:
The Quirimbas are a chain of coral islands stepping up the coast toward Cape Delgado, first fished from Makonde canoes and then settled through the medieval centuries by Swahili Muslim traders. Ibo, sheltered behind reefs and mangrove channels a few miles from the mainland, grew into one of the chief of these little stone towns, its dhows shipping ivory, tortoiseshell and ambergris to Kilwa and bringing back Indian cloth and beads. In 1444 the sheikh of Ibo and the sheikhs of the sister islands looked to Kilwa, and the archipelago did a busy trade beyond the reach of any customs house.

Vasco da Gama is said to have rested at Ibo in 1502, and within a generation Portuguese raiders were burning the Muslim towns: one expedition sacked Ibo, killed some sixty merchants and carried off its ivory, and by 1609 the Portuguese had built a fort on the island. Merchants who would not submit withdrew to other islands and kept trading, while Ibo served the captains of Mozambique as a northern outpost and a stepping-stone for ivory and slaves. Malagasy raiders harried the archipelago through the 1700s, and late in the century the Portuguese answered with the star-shaped Fort São João Baptista, completed in 1791. By then Ibo was the second busiest slave port in the colony after Mozambique Island, its dhows feeding the Mascarene plantations; the town's silversmiths throve on the traffic when it stood at its height in 1821.
zh:
基林巴是一串珊瑚岛，沿海岸一直铺到德尔加杜角；最早是马孔德人独木舟的渔场，中世纪的几个世纪里，斯瓦希里穆斯林商人陆续来岛上定居。伊博藏在礁群与红树林水道之后，距大陆仅数公里，渐渐成为这些小石城中最重要的一个，独桅船把象牙、玳瑁和龙涎香运往基尔瓦，带回印度的布匹和珠子。1444年，伊博的谢赫与姊妹岛上的谢赫们都向基尔瓦称臣，整个群岛在任何海关都管不到的地方繁忙地贸易。

据说达·伽马1502年曾在伊博落脚；不出一代人，葡萄牙袭掠者便开始焚毁这些穆斯林城镇——一次远征洗劫伊博，杀死约六十名商人，抢走积存的象牙——到1609年，葡萄牙人已在岛上建起要塞。不肯屈服的商人退到群岛别处继续做生意，葡萄牙人则把伊博当作莫桑比克统领的北方前哨、一个象牙和奴隶贸易的跳板。18世纪，马达加斯加袭掠者不断骚扰群岛；世纪末，葡萄牙人建起星形的圣若昂·巴普蒂斯塔堡，1791年完工。此时伊博已是殖民地仅次于莫桑比克岛的第二大奴隶港，独桅船为马斯克林群岛的种植园供货；1821年这门生意正值顶峰，城中银匠也靠它兴旺起来。

en:
Luangwa is the lower valley and confluence country where the Luangwa River pours into the Zambezi. Its seasonal floods, fishing channels and steep escarpment gave villagers both food and a highway into the interior. Nsenga oral history tells of a migration from the Luba world in about the fourteenth century; in 1444 Nsenga and related Bantu clans farmed millet, sorghum and groundnuts, kept cattle, hunted elephant and moved between river villages under clan heads, long before any European fair stood at the mouth of the river.

Portuguese traders coming up the Zambezi from Mozambique founded Zumbo on the opposite bank in the early eighteenth century, and by 1720 some had crossed the Luangwa to settle at Feira, the town later renamed Luangwa. Zumbo became the dominant fair of the middle Zambezi: its traders pushed up the lower Luangwa and bartered for ivory brought from as far inland as Lake Bangweulu. African hunters, boatmen and the Chikunda communities around Feira mediated this traffic, so that by the late eighteenth century the confluence was a remote but genuine gateway between Mozambique, the Luangwa valley and the lands beyond.
zh:
卢安瓜是卢安瓜河下游及其注入赞比西河的汇流地带。季节性洪水、捕鱼水道和陡峭崖坡既为村落提供食物，也打开了通往内陆的水路。恩森加口传历史称，他们约在14世纪从卢巴世界迁徙而来；1444年，恩森加及亲缘班图氏族在河口还没有欧洲集市之前，已在氏族首领带领下种植粟、高粱和花生，饲养牛只、猎捕大象，并往来于各河畔村落。

18世纪初，从莫桑比克沿赞比西河上溯的葡萄牙商人在对岸建立宗博商站；到1720年，部分商人已渡过卢安瓜河，在后来更名卢安瓜的费拉定居。宗博成为中赞比西最重要的集市：商人沿卢安瓜河下游深入内陆，用货物交换远至班韦乌卢湖一带运来的象牙。非洲猎人、船工和费拉周围的奇昆达人居间转运，使这个汇流处在18世纪后期成为莫桑比克、卢安瓜河谷及更远地区之间偏远而真实的门户。

en: Ewaso Ngiro takes its name from the Ewaso Ng'iro, the river of 'brown or muddy water' in Maasai. Rising near Mount Kenya, it crosses semi-arid plains and spreads into the Lorian Swamp; in flood its lower course, the intermittent Lagh Dera, carries water on toward the Jubba. In 1444 Muslim Somali pastoral clans moved their camel herds between the riverbeds, wells and coastal caravan tracks, while the Ajuran state levied tribute on inland herdsmen from its strongholds in the wider Jubba and Shabelle country. During the Gaal Madow Wars of the mid-seventeenth century Ajuran forces met expanding Oromo groups, but by the early eighteenth century Ajuran power had vanished from Banaadir and the grazing lands were governed chiefly through clan rights to wells and waterholes.
zh: 埃瓦索恩吉罗得名于埃瓦索恩吉罗河，河名在马赛语中意为「褐色或浑浊的水河」。它发源于肯尼亚山附近，穿过半干旱平原后漫入洛里安沼泽；洪水期时，下游的拉格代拉季节河会把水继续送往朱巴河方向。1444年，信奉伊斯兰教的索马里游牧氏族赶着驼群，在河床、井泉和通往海岸的商路之间迁徙；更广阔的朱巴河与谢贝利河流域则处在阿朱兰政权的势力范围中，其统治者向内陆牧民征收贡赋。17世纪中叶的加拉马多战争中，阿朱兰军队迎击扩张的奥罗莫人；到18世纪初，阿朱兰势力已退出贝纳迪尔，这片牧场主要依靠各氏族对井泉和水源的权利来维系。

en: Dawa is the arid river country along the lower Dawa, which flows southeast from the Ethiopian highlands, marks the later borders of Ethiopia with Kenya and Somalia, and joins the Ganale to form the Jubba. In 1444 its seasonal pools and wells supported Muslim Somali pastoral clans, especially the Garre, whose grazing grounds and dialects were spread through the Dawa and Ganale basins. Their holdings in this country predated the southward pressure of Borana and Warday Oromo groups, and for generations wells, river crossings and pasture were the prizes disputed between clans. In the eighteenth century Garre traders controlled much of the route from Luuq into Borana country and commonly used Oromo as a trade language, tying the Dawa crossings to Jubba valley caravans.
zh: 达瓦是达瓦河下游一带的干旱河谷地区。达瓦河从埃塞俄比亚高地向东南流去，后来构成埃塞俄比亚与肯尼亚、索马里的边界，最终与格纳莱河汇合形成朱巴河。1444年，沿河的季节性水洼和井泉供养着信奉伊斯兰教的索马里游牧氏族，尤其是Garre人；他们的牧场和方言分布在达瓦河与格纳莱河流域。Garre人进入这一地区早于向南施压的博尔纳和瓦尔代奥罗莫群体，此后数代人之间，井泉、渡口和牧场始终是各氏族争夺的目标。18世纪，Garre商人控制了从卢格通往博尔纳地区的大片商路，并普遍以奥罗莫语作为贸易语言，使达瓦河各渡口与朱巴河谷商队连接起来。

en:
Turkana is the sun-scorched basin beside the great jade-green lake that its people call Anam Ka'alakol, 'the sea of many fish': an alkaline, landlocked water of the Rift Valley, fed from the Ethiopian highlands by the Omo and from the south by the Turkwel and Kerio, with no outlet but the sun, its shores broken by black volcanic rock, dunes and the vapour-venting crater of Central Island. In 1444 the lake fisheries and the dry plains around them belonged to older fishing and herding peoples, while from the north a Nilotic section of the Ateker confederation was moving into the basin with its zebu herds. These newcomers, the Turkana, were already at war with the kinsmen they had split from, and would prove the stronger.

Over the following generations the Turkana pushed southwards, defeating the peoples they met with better tactics, weapons and organization and taking the young of conquered groups into their own ranks; by the 1600s they and their allies held the whole basin. Wealth was counted in the grey zebu bulls from which the Turkana take their proud name for themselves, and power was guided by the diviners, the ngimurok. On the margins of their hard country they fought sporadic actions against Arab, Swahili and Abyssinian slave-raiders and ivory traders. Thus in 1821 the Turkana remained the unchallenged masters of the lake and its plains, in a land no European had yet seen.
zh:
图尔卡纳是骄阳炙烤的盆地，旁倚一汪碧绿色的大湖——当地人称之为阿纳姆·卡阿拉科尔，意为「多鱼之海」。这是东非大裂谷中一座没有出口的碱性内流湖，湖水靠北方奥莫河从埃塞俄比亚高地、南方特克韦尔河与凯里奥河补给，只能借蒸发排去水量；湖岸散布着黑色火山岩与沙丘，中央岛上的火山口还吐着蒸汽。1444年时，湖上的渔场和周围干旱平原的主人还是更早的渔猎与游牧部族，而一支属于阿特克尔联盟的尼罗特人正赶着瘤牛群从北方进入盆地。这些新来者就是图尔卡纳人，他们已与分裂出去的同族交战，并将成为胜者。

此后几代人之间，图尔卡纳人凭更出色的战术、武器和编组向南推进，击败所到之处的各部，又把被征服者中的年轻人纳入自己的队伍；到17世纪，他们和盟友已据有整个盆地。财富以灰色的瘤牛公牛来衡量，图尔卡纳人也以「灰牛之民」自居；权柄则听命于占卜师恩吉姆罗克。在这片严酷土地的边缘，他们不时与阿拉伯、斯瓦希里和阿比西尼亚的捕奴者、象牙商人交战。到1821年，图尔卡纳人仍是湖泊与平原无可争议的主人，他们的土地也仍未有欧洲人踏足。

en: Kuria land is the rolling grass country east of Lake Victoria, from the Migori river in the east to the Mara river and its estuary in the west, where modern Kenya and Tanzania meet. By 1444 its Bantu people, the AbaKuria, grazed cattle on the plains and tilled the wetter valleys in many independent clans, speaking a tongue close to that of their kinsmen the Gusii highlanders; between them and the lake ran a narrow Luo corridor, and their other neighbours were the Suba and Ikoma, while the grasslands far to the south-east belonged to Maa-speaking herdsmen. Cattle were the measure of all wealth, paid over as bride-price and slain in the sacrifices of the old religion, and young men were bound into warrior age-sets to guard the herds. In the early nineteenth century raiders out of the expanding Maasai country pressed these borders ever harder, and the Kuria met them with the spear rather than submission.
zh: 库里亚之地是维多利亚湖以东起伏的草原，东起米戈里河，西抵马拉河及其河口，正落在今日肯尼亚与坦桑尼亚相接之处。到1444年，住在这里的阿巴库里亚人是一支班图人，在平原牧牛、在较湿润的谷地耕作，分成众多互不统属的氏族，讲与近亲古西山地人相近的语言；他们与大湖之间隔着一条卢奥人的走廊，其他邻人是苏巴人和伊科马人，东南远方的草原则属于讲马阿语的牧人。牛是衡量一切财富的尺度，既用作聘礼，也在传统信仰的祭祀中宰杀；年轻男子按年龄结为武士团守护牛群。19世纪初，来自不断扩张的马赛之地的袭扰者日益紧逼这条边界，库里亚人以长矛而非屈服相迎。

en:
The Shamba of the Usambara Mountains call their wet highland home Shambaai, 'where bananas thrive', in contrast to the dry nyika plains below. By 1444 Shambaa clans lived in separate hill villages, clearing forest and watering banana groves through irrigation channels. They exchanged local iron tools, salt from the plains and shell ornaments reaching them from the coast. Elders settled disputes and marriage alliances linked neighbouring hills, but no single ruler governed the whole range.

Maasai raids and the arrival of refugee pastoralists in the early eighteenth century made common defence more urgent. In the first half of that century Mbegha, a hunter from the Ngulu hills, helped Vugha against dangerous game, married into leading clans, and bound the mountain villages into the Kilindi dynasty through kinship and diplomacy. His grandson Kinyashi Muanga Ike strengthened its military authority. Around 1815 Kimweri ye Nyumbai became ruler at Vugha, and in 1821 the mountain kingdom remained a growing power whose influence was reaching toward the Pangani valley and the coastal towns.
zh:
乌桑巴拉山区的珊巴人把湿润高地称为尚巴伊，意思是「香蕉繁盛之地」，与山下干旱的尼伊卡平原相对。1444年时，珊巴各氏族分居在不同山村，开垦森林，用灌溉渠滋养香蕉林。他们以本地铁器、平原出产的盐和来自海岸的贝饰互通有无。争端由长者调解，婚姻联盟把相邻山丘联系起来，但整个山区还没有统一的统治者。

18世纪初，马赛人的袭扰和避难牧人的到来使共同防御变得迫切。18世纪上半叶，来自恩古鲁山地的猎人姆贝加帮助武加除去危害人畜的野兽，又与主要氏族联姻，凭借亲属关系和外交把各山村纳入基林迪王朝。他的孙子基尼亚希·穆安加·伊凯强化了王朝的军事权威。约1815年，金韦里·耶·尼乌姆巴伊在武加继位；1821年时，这个山地王国仍在扩张，势力正向潘加尼河谷和沿海城镇延伸。

en: Gogo is the dry Ugogo plateau, the uncertain-rain country between the coastal hinterland and Tanzania's western plateau. In 1444 scattered Bantu-speaking homesteads combined cultivation and hunting with cattle keeping where pasture and waterholes permitted, their affairs resting with local elders and headmen. The road from Bagamoyo to Tabora later crossed this country. After the long-distance ivory trade expanded in the early nineteenth century, Nyamwezi caravans passed through Ugogo toward the coast, and Dodoma began as a small Gogo settlement of tembe houses. By 1821 Gogo communities stood on one of East Africa's rising inland routes, where provisions, cattle and local permission to pass had become matters no caravan could ignore.
zh: 戈戈地处干旱的乌戈戈高原，雨量无常，夹在沿海腹地与坦桑尼亚西部高原之间。1444年时，说班图语的居民以分散家户生活，在牧场和水坑允许的地方兼营农耕、狩猎与养牛，事务由当地长者和头人主持。后来，从巴加莫约通往塔波拉的道路穿过这片土地。19世纪初长途象牙贸易扩大后，尼亚姆韦齐商队经乌戈戈前往海岸，多多马也在这些年作为戈戈人的滕贝屋小聚落兴起。到1821年，戈戈诸社群已位于东非一条正在兴起的内陆商路上，商队不能不考虑这里的补给、牛群和通行许可。

en: Nyatura is the Singida plateau country of the Arimi, whose name means farmers and whose Bantu speech is Kinyaturu. In 1444 Airwana, Vahi and Anyinganyi clans farmed the plateau, kept cattle where pasture allowed, and managed their affairs through village and lineage elders rather than a single king. Kinyaturu's Cushitic influence and the people's joking partnerships with the Nyiramba and Iraqw show long contact between farmers and pastoral neighbours. In the early nineteenth century the long-distance caravan road from the coast toward Tabora and Lake Tanganyika began stopping at Kilimatinde, in southern Singida. By 1821 ivory, enslaved people and firearms were moving along that edge of Nyaturu country, drawing its decentralized villages into the commerce reaching inland from Zanzibar.
zh: 尼亚图拉是阿里米人的辛吉达高原之乡；「阿里米」意为农人，他们的班图语称基尼亚图鲁语。1444年时，艾尔瓦纳、瓦希和安宁加尼等氏族在高原耕作，在牧场允许的地方养牛，由村落和世系长者而不是单一国王处理事务。基尼亚图鲁语中的库希特语影响，以及他们与尼伊拉姆巴人、伊拉库人的戏谑伙伴关系，显示农耕者与邻近牧人早有长期往来。19世纪初，从海岸通往塔波拉和坦噶尼喀湖的长途商路开始在辛吉达南部的基利马廷德停驻。到1821年，象牙、奴隶和火器正沿尼亚图拉地带的这一南缘流动，把分散的氏族村落卷入从桑给巴尔伸向内陆的商业网络。

en:
Zigua is the hinterland country of the Zigua people, lying behind the Swahili coast between the Pangani and Ruvu rivers. By 1444 its Bantu-speaking farming clans lived in palisaded villages and, on the Ruvu, in island settlements reached by light bridges. Their matriclans held the land, while elders settled disputes through gifts and bloodwealth. Near the shore, Kaole and the small markets around Bagamoyo and Pangani linked hinterland produce with Indian Ocean exchange, but no Zigua king ruled all the villages.

For centuries authority remained local, measured by a leader's raids, gifts and ability to protect his people. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Bagamoyo grew from a small fishing and farming market into a caravan stopping place, and Muslim families settling there in the late eighteenth century traded salt and taxed traffic with the hinterland. Maasai and Baraguyu cattle raids intensified in the early nineteenth century, while Zigua leaders exchanged ivory, animals and slaves for coastal imports. By 1821 Uzigua was a country of fortified villages and ambitious zumbe, as Zanzibar's caravan commerce and competition over weapons recast power in the Pangani corridor.
zh:
兹古阿是兹古阿人的腹地家园，位于斯瓦希里海岸后方、潘加尼河与鲁伏河之间。1444年时，说班图语的农耕氏族住在栅栏围护的村落里，鲁伏河上还有靠轻便木桥出入的岛上聚落。土地归母系氏族所有，长者通过赠礼和偿命财调解争端。近海的考莱以及巴加莫约、潘加尼周围的小市场把腹地物产带入印度洋交换，但没有一个兹古阿国王统治全部村落。

此后数百年间，权威仍限于地方，取决于首领能否组织袭掠、分配礼物并保护部众。17至18世纪，巴加莫约从渔农小市场发展为商队停驻地；18世纪末定居当地的穆斯林家族经营食盐贸易，并对通往腹地的往来征税。19世纪初，马赛人和巴拉古尤人的夺牛袭扰加剧，兹古阿首领则以象牙、牲畜和奴隶交换海岸输入品。到1821年，乌济瓜已遍布设防村落和雄心勃勃的「尊贝」首领，桑给巴尔商路与武器竞争正在重塑潘加尼走廊的权力格局。

en:
Shaga is an older name for the mountain country documented as Uchaga, Dschagga or Chagga on Kilimanjaro's southern slopes. Bantu farmers had been settling there since about the eleventh century, terracing wet ridges, watering banana groves with mountain channels and keeping cattle above the hot plains. In 1444 the land was still divided among autonomous clan villages and highland mitaa, rather than the later Umangi kingdoms. Families venerated ancestors and Ruwa, the sun deity whose shrines stood in the high forest, while food, pottery and iron linked the mountain with Taveta, Taita and Pare.

The small Chagga kingdoms hardened during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Late in the eighteenth century Mangi Horombo, called Orombo in English sources, ruled from Keni, raided east into Mwika and raised large stone-walled enclosures; his power overshadowed Vunjo even while Queen Mashina preserved the small but wealthy state of Mamba. Around the same time trade from the coast began to reach up the Pangani basin. After 1810 Rengua of Machame used an iron spear to overawe rival clans in the Kikafu valley and became the first Mangi of Machame; his killing of Kibosho initiates at Kimbushi opened a long feud. As rival rulers sought weapons after 1800, Pare, Taveta and Taita smiths supplied increasing quantities of iron, tying spears, cattle and caravan goods to mountain politics.
zh:
沙嘎（查加，Uchaga/Dschagga/Chagga）是乞力马扎罗山南坡山地之国的旧称。约从11世纪起，班图农民陆续在此定居，在湿润山脊修筑梯田，引山水浇灌香蕉林，并在炎热平原上方牧牛。1444年时，这里仍由自治的氏族村落和高地社区分治，尚未形成后来的「乌曼吉」诸王国。各户敬奉祖先与太阳神鲁瓦，高山森林中设有神龛；粮食、陶器和铁器则把山地与塔韦塔、泰塔、帕雷联系起来。

17至18世纪，查加人的小王国逐渐成形。18世纪末，凯尼的曼吉·霍龙博（英文资料作奥龙博）据地称强，向东袭掠姆维卡，建起大型石墙围寨，权势压过温乔；女王玛希娜虽然保住了狭小而富庶的曼巴邦，也必须顾及他的力量。大约同一时期，海岸贸易开始沿潘加尼河盆地深入山地。1810年后，马查姆的伦瓜凭借铁矛震慑基卡富河谷的敌对氏族，成为第一位马查姆曼吉；他在金布希杀害基博绍成年礼成员，开启了长期世仇。1800年以后，诸首领争相寻求武器，帕雷、塔韦塔和泰塔铁匠供应更多铁器，使长矛、牲畜与商队货物都卷入山地政治。

en:
The Kikuyu country is the cool, fertile highland between the snowy pyramid of Mount Kenya, which they call Kirinyaga, and the long wall of the Aberdares, reaching towards the Ngong hills and Ol Donyo Sabuk. Bantu farmers of the Thagicu branch reached the northern slopes of the mountain around the third century, and by the thirteenth century their descendants had formed a settled core at Murang'a, mingling with the older hunter-gatherers of the forests. By 1444 the Agĩkũyũ were a nation of nine clans without a king, ruled by councils of elders: they tilled millet and the njahi bean in valleys that gave two harvests a year, kept the rites of Ngai at the sacred fig trees with their faces turned to Kirinyaga, and named the years by initiation sets, companies of youths circumcised together who were formed into regiments and handed power to a new ruling generation roughly every thirty-five years.

The centuries that followed were an age of steady growth: by purchase, blood-brotherhood, intermarriage and adoption the Kikuyu drew forest hunter-gatherers into their clans and opened new ridges, and in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries a great southward movement carried them from Murang'a into the Kiambu country. With the Maasai of the southern and northern plains they both traded and fought, while Kamba caravans brought the goods of the dry country to their markets. Arab and Swahili slavers moving up from the coast touched only the southern edge of the nation and were killed if they pushed farther; the Kikuyu kept no slaves and answered to no outside power. At the close of our period the ruling generation was the Ndemi, whose age-set began in 1792, and the whole highland still lay in Kikuyu hands.
zh:
基库尤之地是凉爽肥沃的高地，夹在雪锥般的肯尼亚山——他们称之为基里尼亚加——与阿伯德尔山脉的长墙之间，一直延伸到恩贡丘陵和奥尔东约奥萨布克山。属塔吉库分支的班图农民约在3世纪抵达肯尼亚山北坡，到13世纪，他们的后裔已在穆兰卡形成定居核心，并与林中更古老的采集狩猎者融合。1444年时，阿基库尤是一个没有国王、由九大氏族组成的族群，靠长老议事会治理：他们在谷地种植粟和恩贾希豆，一年两熟；在神圣的榕树下祭祀天神恩盖，脸朝基里尼亚加；他们还以成年礼年龄组纪年——一同割礼的青年编成连队，约每三十五年把统治权移交给新一代。

此后几个世纪是稳步扩张的时代：基库尤人靠购买土地、结血盟、通婚和收养，把林中的采集狩猎者纳入自己的氏族，开辟出新的山脊；18至19世纪，一场大南迁把他们从穆兰卡带到基安布地方。对南北两线平原上的马赛人，他们既通商也交战；坎巴人的商队把干旱地区的货物带进他们的市集。从海岸北上的阿拉伯与斯瓦希里捕奴商队只能擦着族群的南缘行走，再深入便会被处死；基库尤人不蓄奴隶，也不服从任何外来强权。本时期之末，当政的是恩代米一代，其年龄组始于1792年，而整片高地仍完全掌握在基库尤人手中。

en: Buzinza is the land of the Zinza, a Bantu people of the south-western corner of Lake Victoria. They fish the lake, farm bananas and grain on the shore and the offshore islands, and graze cattle on the grasslands behind. Hereditary smith-clans smelted local iron in charcoal furnaces, forging hoes, spears and knives, and weaving supplied a second trade good; Zinza iron, dried fish and cloth went to the Haya chiefdoms to the north and into Karagwe to the west. Their language ties them most closely to peoples on the northern, Ugandan side of the lake. In 1444 these shorelands lay within the sphere of the Hinda kingdom of Karagwe, then taking shape under rulers who claimed descent from the Chwezi hero Ruhinda.
zh: 布津扎是津扎人的土地。津扎人是生活在维多利亚湖西南角的班图人，在湖中捕鱼，在湖岸和近岸岛屿上种植香蕉与谷物，在岸后草原放牧。世袭的铁匠氏族用木炭炉冶炼当地铁矿，打造锄头、长矛和刀，纺织是另一项营生；津扎的铁器、鱼干和布匹销往北方的哈亚诸酋长国，也输入西边的卡拉圭。津扎语表明他们与湖北岸乌干达一侧的各族关系最近。1444年，这片湖岸地带处在欣达族卡拉圭王国的势力范围内，当时该王国正由自称齐韦兹英雄鲁欣达后裔的统治者建立成形。

en:
Busoga is the green, water-girt country east of the Victoria Nile, with Lake Kyoga to the north, the Mpologoma to the east and the broad reach of Lake Victoria to the south; fishing villages such as Bukaleba lined its shore. Its Soga people farmed bananas and millet, herded cattle on the ridges and drew much of their living from the lakes, smoking fish for the inland trade. They had no single king: clan chiefs with their own totems ruled their separate hills and answered to no overlord, though Bunyoro beyond the Nile was honoured as the wellspring of royalty. In 1444 the chiefdoms were still wholly independent.

The 16th century brought new dynasties. Mukama Namutukula, a prince of Bunyoro's Bito house, crossed Lake Kyoga with his following, and his sons founded the northern chiefdoms: Bulamogi dated to about 1550 under Zibondo Lamogi, Bukono existed before 1656 and Bugabula was founded around 1730. Bito principalities thus stood beside older clan chiefdoms. In the 17th and 18th centuries the rising kabakas of Buganda, Kimbugwe, Katerega and Mutebi, conquered stretches of Busoga, and the chiefs of the southern shore became Ganda clients. Rival Soga factions called in Bunyoro or Buganda by turns, paying cattle, goats and sometimes slaves to the stronger court, where succession disputes were arbitrated; in 1821 the eleven chiefdoms still had no common ruler.
zh:
布索加是一片被水环绕的青翠之地，位于维多利亚尼罗河以东：北临基奥加湖，东界姆波洛戈马河，南接浩瀚的维多利亚湖，湖畔分布着布卡莱巴这样的渔村。索加人种植香蕉和黍子，在山脊放牧，生计很大程度上仰仗湖泊，把鱼熏干后输往内陆。他们没有共主：各有图腾的氏族酋长统治各自的丘陵，不奉任何宗主，只把尼罗河对岸的布尼奥罗奉为王权之源。1444年时，这些酋邦仍然完全独立。

16世纪，新的王朝到来。布尼奥罗比托王室的王子姆卡马·纳穆图库拉率部众渡过基奥加湖，他的子孙在北方建立了多个酋邦：齐邦多·拉莫吉约在1550年建立布拉莫吉，布科诺在1656年以前已经存在，布加布拉则建于1730年前后，比托系公国与更古老的氏族酋邦并立。17至18世纪，日益强盛的布干达卡巴卡金布圭、卡特雷加和穆特比征服了布索加的大片土地，南湖沿岸的酋长沦为布干达的附庸。敌对的索加派系轮番向布尼奥罗或布干达求援，向更强的一方进贡牛、羊乃至奴隶，酋长继承之争也要到强国王廷上裁断；到1821年，这十一个酋邦仍没有共同的统治者。

en:
Karagwe, also called Bunyambo after its people the Abanyambo, is the high grassland between Rwanda and Lake Victoria. Its kings, titled Omugabe, belonged to the Hinda clan and claimed descent from Ruhinda, son of Wamara, the Chwezi ruler of Kitara; tradition places the founding of the line around 1450, and Bweranyange became the royal capital. Hima cattle-owning families stood above the farming clans, lending out stock to bind cultivators as clients, and the kings fought a long struggle to bring the mediums of the Kubandwa cult under court control. The land's other renown was iron: closed hereditary smith-clans smelted the ore with charcoal, and their hoes and weapons sold across the lake region. In 1444 the Hinda kingdom was newly settled on its hills, a stratified cattle-and-iron state on the western edge of Lake Victoria.

In the following generations Karagwe took its place in the chain of interlacustrine kingdoms, each clan serving the court at Bweranyange in its appointed role. Long overshadowed by Bunyoro, it turned against its northern overlord late in the eighteenth century: the Omugabe Ntare VI, who reigned from about 1775 to 1795, destroyed the Nyoro host and was remembered as Kitabanyoro, the Nyoro-slayer. Ruhinda VI ruled across the turn of the century, and about 1820 Ndagara I came to the throne. Himself a master blacksmith, Ndagara built a royal treasury of forged iron — standards, weapons, pillar anvils and horned cattle figures — and under him Karagwe's trade in iron, ivory and cattle with the wider lake region, and increasingly with caravans bound for the coast, entered its greatest age.
zh:
卡拉圭又称布尼扬博，得名于境内的尼扬博人，是卢旺达与维多利亚湖之间的高原草地。这里的国王称奥穆加贝，出自欣达氏族，自称是基塔拉的齐韦兹统治者瓦马拉之子鲁欣达的后裔；传说王统开创于1450年前后，都城设在布韦拉尼扬盖。拥有牛群的希马牧人家族高居于农耕氏族之上，以出借牲畜把农人束缚为依附者，历代国王又经过长期经营，把主宰本地宗教的库班德瓦神媒置于宫廷控制之下。卡拉圭的另一项名声是铁：封闭的世袭铁匠氏族以木炭炼铁，打出的锄头和武器销往大湖各处。1444年的欣达王国刚刚在这片丘陵上立足，是维多利亚湖西缘一个等级森严、以牛群和铁器立国的政权。

此后的几代人里，卡拉圭跻身环大湖诸王国之列，各氏族按分工在布韦拉尼扬盖的宫廷当差。它长期受布尼奥罗压制，18世纪末转而进攻北方的宗主：约1775至1795年在位的奥穆加贝恩塔雷六世击溃尼奥罗军队，被称作基塔巴尼奥罗，意为「屠戮尼奥罗人者」。鲁欣达六世在世纪之交执政，约1820年恩达加拉一世即位。恩达加拉本人是打铁大师，建起一座王室铁作宝库——铁制权标、兵器、柱形铁砧和弯角铁牛；在他治下，卡拉圭以铁、象牙和牛群与大湖各地、并越来越多地与通往海岸的商队贸易，进入全盛时代。

en:
Buganda covers the green hills and swamps north of Lake Victoria, the Ganda name for which is Nalubaale. Bantu farmers making Urewe pottery had settled there by the sixth century, and the kingdom probably took shape between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries around the small counties of Kyadondo, Busiro and Mawokota. In 1444 the fifth kabaka, Kiggala, ruled from Kitala Hill, the capital he had established about 1434. His power still depended on powerful clan heads and hill chiefs, whose villages drew tribute from productive banana gardens and dressed court and household in beaten barkcloth.

A Bunyoro invasion in the sixteenth century killed Kabaka Nakinge, but Buganda kept its independence and then expanded as Bunyoro weakened. Under Kimbugwe, Katerega and Mutebi in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, its armies took Buddu and parts of Busoga and Karagwe, made Kooki tributary and replaced conquered rulers with royal appointees. Blue beads served as state currency under Kyabaggu from about 1750 to 1780, and ivory discs circulated under Junju around 1790 to 1800. The office of katikkiro, or chief minister, took shape around 1800. In that same year Kamanya sent a hundred canoes to Jinja, had them carried overland through Busoga and reassembled, and struck the Lango from an unexpected quarter while another army moved by land. By 1821 appointed chiefs, dry-season campaigns and war-canoe logistics had made Buganda one of the most formidable powers on the Great Lakes.
zh:
布干达位于维多利亚湖以北的青翠丘陵与沼泽之间，干达人称该湖为纳卢巴莱。早在6世纪，制作乌雷韦陶器的班图农民已在此定居；王国大约在12至14世纪成形，最初只统有Kyadondo、Busiro和Mawokota等小郡。1444年，第五任卡巴卡Kiggala以Kitala山为王都，这座都邑是他约1434年建立的。他的权力仍依赖强势的氏族首领和山丘酋长；村社靠丰饶的香蕉园征收贡赋，宫廷与家户则穿着捶制的树皮布。

16世纪，布尼奥罗的入侵杀死卡巴卡Nakinge，但布干达保住了独立，并趁布尼奥罗衰落开始扩张。17至18世纪，在Kimbugwe、Katerega和Mutebi统治下，军队夺取Buddu以及Busoga、Karagwe的部分土地，迫使Kooki纳贡，并以国王任命的官员取代被征服者的首领。约1750年至1780年Kyabaggu在位时，蓝珠成为国家通货；约1790年至1800年Junju在位时，象牙圆片也进入流通。首席大臣「卡蒂基罗」之职约在1800年成形。同年，Kamanya把一百艘独木舟运到金贾，再经Busoga陆运、重新组装，从意想不到的方向攻击兰戈人，另一支军队则由陆路推进。到1821年，任命制酋长、旱季征战和战船运输体系已使布干达成为大湖地区最可畏的强权之一。

en:
This is the southern Bunyoro country around Mugenyi, whose name preserves Bigo bya Mugenyi, the great earthwork on the Katonga River. Around 1444 its outer ditch and bank ran for more than six kilometres, joining the Katonga to the Kakinga swamps and enclosing over 300 hectares around four central enclosures. Excavations have found roulette-decorated pottery, iron arrowheads and a grain knife, showing an Iron Age elite able to organize labour, hold cattle, and redistribute goods while Kibiro salt moved through Bunyoro's exchange networks.

After the Babiito kings founded the later Kingdom of Bunyoro in the late sixteenth century, their princes carried royal influence toward Busoga, Kiziba, Buzinza, and the lands beyond the Rwenzoris. Duhaga ruled Bunyoro from about 1731 to 1782, but by the end of the century internal division and Buganda's seizure of Kooki and Buddu had weakened the monarchy. Nyamutukura Kyebambe III came to the throne in 1786 and still ruled in 1821; his realm remained rich from salt, iron, and ivory, but its southern earthworks lay on a frontier increasingly pressed by Buganda.
zh:
这是穆根伊周围的布尼奥罗南部地区，穆根伊之名保存着卡通加河畔大型土垒遗址比戈·比亚·穆根伊的记忆。1444年前后，这里的外壕与土堤长逾六公里，把卡通加河与卡金卡沼泽连接起来，围住三百多公顷土地和四座中央围场。考古发现了绳纹陶、铁箭镞和收割谷物用的铁刀，说明当时已有能够组织劳役、畜养牛群、再分配货物的铁器时代精英；基比罗盐也在布尼奥罗的交换网络中流通。

16世纪末，巴比托诸王建立后来的布尼奥罗王国后，王族王子把王权影响带向布索加、基济巴、布津扎和鲁文佐里山以外地区。杜哈加约1731—1782年统治布尼奥罗；到18世纪末，内部分裂以及布干达夺取科基和布杜，削弱了王权。尼亚穆图库拉·基埃班贝三世1786年即位，1821年仍在位；他的王国仍靠盐、铁和象牙致富，但南部土垒已处在日益受布干达压力的边境上。

en:
Nkore, called Ankole only after the colonial conquest, is the rolling grass country east of Lake Edward between Buganda, Bunyoro, Karagwe and Rwanda. Its pastures were so rich that cattle could be watered almost all year round, and the land was known as Kaaro Karungi, 'the good land': Bahima herdsmen tended the long-horned Ankole cattle and stood above the Bairu millet-farmers, while the mugabe ruled through cattle-clientage, war-bands called emitwe and the sacred royal drum Bagyendanwa. Tradition made Ruhinda, founder of the Hinda dynasty, a king within living memory, and his son Nkuba firmed up the new kingship from its core at Isingiro. In 1444 Nkore was still a small kingdom in the shadow of Bunyoro.

For two and a half centuries it stayed a minor power, at times owning Bunyoro's overlordship. Ntare IV, who reigned from 1699 to 1727, turned the tables: invaded by the Bunyoro army of Cwamali, he took shelter in the Nyamistindo caves and on Kantsyore Island in the Kagera, then counter-attacked, killed Cwamali and earned the name Kiitabanyoro, 'slayer of the Banyoro', pushing his border north to the Katonga and seizing Kabula. Macwa, who followed him, kept the peace from 1727 to 1755, but his death threw the throne into disputed succession. Wars with Rwanda and cattle-raids on every frontier filled the later reigns, and in 1821 the Hinda kings still held their pastures as their own.
zh:
安科莱（殖民征服之后才叫 Ankole，旧称恩科莱）是爱德华湖以东、夹在布干达、布尼奥罗、卡拉圭与卢旺达之间的起伏草原之国。这里牧场肥美，牛群几乎一年到头都能饮水，土地因此得名「卡鲁昆吉」，意为「好地方」：巴希马牧人放牧长角安科莱牛，地位高于种黍子的巴伊鲁农人；姆加贝国王以牛群封臣、名为埃米特韦的战团和神圣王鼓巴吉丹瓦维治国。按口述传统，欣达王朝的开国君鲁欣达距当时不过一代人之久，他的儿子恩库巴在伊辛吉罗的核心之地巩固了新生王权。1444年时，恩科莱还是布尼奥罗阴影下的一个小王国。

此后两个半世纪里，它始终是个二流强国，有时还向布尼奥罗称臣。1699至1727年在位的恩塔雷四世扭转了局面：布尼奥罗的茨瓦马利率军来犯，他先避入尼亚米斯廷多洞穴和卡盖拉河中的坎乔雷岛，随后反攻，杀死茨瓦马利，赢得「基塔巴尼奥罗」（意为诛杀尼奥罗人者）的称号，并把北界推进到卡通加河、夺取卡布拉。继他之后的马克瓦在1727至1755年间维持了和平，他一死，王位便陷入继承纷争。其后诸王的岁月充斥着与卢旺达的战事和各条边境上的掠牛之争；到1821年，欣达诸王仍然独立自主地守着自己的牧场。

en:
Nduga is the hilly country of central Rwanda around the old Gitarama, reaching south toward Nyanza, a land of banana groves and cattle pastures watered by the Nyabarongo. It was once the kingdom of the Ababanda clan, whose king ruled from the hill of Rwesero with the royal drum Nyabahinda as his emblem, while Twa hunters and Hutu farmers shared the hills with incoming cattle-keeping clans. In 1444 Nduga was still its own master: the Nyiginya kingdom to its north-east was then little more than the 'Rwanda of Gasabo' around Lake Muhazi, one chiefdom among several.

Nduga kept its freedom through the first Rwandan wars of expansion. The Ababanda king Mashira retook his realm with shelter from Bugesera, and the mwami Mibambwe Mutabazi had to accept the restoration. Mibambwe then gave Mashira his daughter Nyirantobwa in marriage and, travelling through Nduga as a guest, was feasted at Nyamagana near Nyanza; in the middle of the festivities he seized his host and put Mashira and all his sons to death, and the Ababanda army was destroyed to the last man. With its royal line extinguished, Nduga was annexed in the Rwandan expansion of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and its hills became part of the kingdom's central provinces.
zh:
恩杜加地处卢旺达中部丘陵，即旧吉塔拉马一带，向南延伸到尼安扎附近，尼亚巴隆戈河滋养着这里的香蕉园和牧牛场。它曾是阿班达氏族的王国，国王在鲁韦塞罗山发号施令，以圣鼓尼亚巴欣达为权力象征；山丘上住着特瓦猎人、胡图农民，还有陆续迁入的牧牛氏族。1444年的恩杜加仍是自主之邦，东北方的尼金亚王国还只是以穆哈齐湖周边的「加萨博卢旺达」为中心的一个酋长国，与恩杜加、布格塞拉等小国并立。

恩杜加一度顶住了卢旺达扩张的最初攻势：阿班达国王马希拉在布格塞拉避难后收复故国，姆瓦米·米班布韦·穆塔巴齐不得不承认阿班达王朝复辟。后来米班布韦把女儿尼兰托布瓦嫁给马希拉，又以过客身份做客恩杜加，在尼安扎附近的尼亚马加纳赴宴；宴席之间他突然拿下主人，将马希拉和他所有的儿子处死，阿班达军队也被全歼。王统既绝，恩杜加在16至17世纪卢旺达的扩张中被兼并，这片丘陵此后成为王国中部疆土的一部分。

en:
Bafuriru is the highland country above the northern end of Lake Tanganyika, where the mountains of Uvira drop to the Ruzizi plain on the border with Rwanda and Burundi. Clans tracing their origin to the Lwindi country, at the mouth of the Ulindi on the Lualaba, settled the valleys of Mulenge, Luvungi and Lemera between the tenth and fourteenth centuries; they kept cattle, worked the fields, and won a name for pottery and basketwork. By 1444 the Bahamba clan was building these settlements into the Hamba kingdom, a small highland state more centralised than most of its neighbours, while the Ruzizi plain below served mainly as pasture and hunting ground.

In the seventeenth century the related Vira people arrived through Maniema and the Itombwe mountains and spread along the lakeside slopes from Mount Munanira above Uvira, dividing the highlands with the Bafuliru. Tradition names the mwami Kahamba Kalingishi as the founder who united the Bafuliru clans in Lemera and established their royal line, though oral accounts differ widely on his dates. From the 1600s Bafuliru hunters and herders also began to descend into the Ruzizi plain, the frontier march with the kingdoms of Rwanda and Burundi.
zh:
巴夫里鲁位于坦噶尼喀湖北端的高地，乌维拉山区在此俯临与卢旺达、布隆迪交界的鲁济济平原。当地诸氏族自称源自卢阿拉巴河上乌林迪河口的卢温迪，于10至14世纪间陆续定居穆伦盖、卢温吉和莱梅拉的河谷；他们牧牛耕种，并以制陶和编篮闻名。到1444年，巴汉巴氏族正把这些聚落组建成汉巴王国，一个比多数邻邦都集权的山地小国，而山下的鲁济济平原主要还是牧场和猎场。

17世纪，与他们相近的维拉人经马涅马和伊通布韦山区迁来，以乌维拉上方的穆纳尼拉山为中心散布到沿湖山坡，与巴夫里鲁人分据高地。相传姆瓦米·卡汉巴·卡林吉希是在莱梅拉统一各氏族、开创巴夫里鲁王统的建国者，但口述传统对他的年代说法不一。从17世纪起，巴夫里鲁的猎人和牧人也开始下山进入鲁济济平原，那里正是与卢旺达、布隆迪两王国相邻的边陲。

en: Bushubi is the highland country of the Washubi around Ngara, in the hills of north-western Tanzania between Rwanda, Burundi and the Zinza lands to the east. The Shubi lived by hunting before turning mainly to farming, growing grain and keeping cattle on the well-watered ridges. In 1444 it was still a country of autonomous hill villages, bound to the neighbouring Buha and Buhaya worlds by a Bantu language close to Kinyarwanda and Kirundi. From the late 1600s the highland communities coalesced into chiefdoms whose rulers took tribute in grain, cattle and beer; the Shubi kings, titled mwami, are remembered by the royal names Magina, Kibogora, Nsoro and Kinanaira, repeated down the remembered line of reigns.
zh: 布苏毕是瓦苏比人的山地，位于坦桑尼亚西北部恩加拉一带，处在卢旺达、布隆迪与东方津扎之地之间。苏比人原先以狩猎为生，后来主要转为农耕，在水源充足的山梁上种植谷物、牧养牛群。1444年，这里还是自治山村并立的地方，居民的班图语接近卢旺达语和布隆迪语，与相邻的布哈、布哈亚世界声息相通。17世纪末起，高地社群逐渐合并为酋长国，统治者收取谷物、牛和啤酒作为贡赋；苏比人的国王称姆瓦米，留下了马吉纳、基博戈拉、恩索罗、基纳奈拉等王名，在历代君王中循环沿用。

en:
Nkoma is the ridge country of the Nkoma massif, overlooking the Kumoso plain in what is now Rutana Province, southeastern Burundi. In 1444 it was not a royal capital. Bantu farmers, Twa hunter-foragers, and cattle-keeping families lived in scattered hill homesteads under local leaders, their farms, herds, and forges tying the ridge to both the Buha and Burundian worlds.

Later oral tradition made Nkoma the first royal stage in the rise of Ntare Rushatsi, the founder remembered in the southern Burundian cycle that also connected his following to Buha. As the Burundian kingdom coalesced during the seventeenth century, its mwami drew neighbouring hill communities into a loose monarchy. From about 1795 the wars of Ntare IV carried Burundian power back toward the smaller polities of Buha, so that in 1821 Nkoma stood on an eastern frontier being drawn toward the royal court.
zh:
恩科马是恩科马山地的山脊地带，俯瞰今布隆迪东南部鲁塔纳省境内的库莫索平原。1444年时，这里并不是王都。班图农民、特瓦族狩猎采集者和牧牛家族散居在各处山梁庄园中，受本地首领管辖；农田、牛群和锻炉把这座山脊同布哈与布隆迪两边的世界联系起来。

后来的口述传统把恩科马视为恩塔雷·鲁沙齐崛起过程中的第一个王权舞台；布隆迪南部传统谱系记住了这位开国者，也把他的追随者同布哈联系在一起。17世纪布隆迪王国逐渐聚合，姆瓦米把相邻的山地共同体纳入一个松散王权。约1795年起，恩塔雷四世的战争再次把布隆迪势力推向布哈诸小邦；到1821年，恩科马已处在东部边境上，日益被吸向王室权力中心。

en:
Buyogoma is the high eastern plateau between the Ruvubu valley and the Moso plains, on the western edge of Buha. In 1444 its Ha farmers, the Abaha, lived in dispersed homesteads and spoke Kiha, a Bantu language close to Kirundi. Sorghum and millet fields, goats and cattle sustained the villages and the tribute owed to local rulers, while ancestor spirits and the high god Imana shaped religious life.

The plateau remained a western march of Buha's small kingships rather than a town-centered state. By 1796 Ntare Rugamba's Burundian armies had opened a period of royal expansion, and Buyogoma was then held by the Buha mwami Ruhaga. Rugamba coveted its grain and open pasture and went to war with Buha. In 1821 the plateau still stood on Ruhaga's side of a hardening frontier, caught between the old Ha court and the growing power of Burundi.
zh:
布约戈马是鲁武布河谷与莫索平原之间的东部高原，位于布哈西缘。1444年，这里的Ha农民（阿巴哈人）散居在各家庄园里，使用与基隆迪语相近的班图语基哈语。高粱和粟米田、山羊和牛群维持着村落生计，也供应本地统治者索取的贡赋；祖先神灵和至高神伊马纳则支配着人们的宗教生活。

这片高原长期是布哈诸小王国的西部边地，而不是以城镇为中心的国家。到1796年，恩塔雷·鲁加姆巴的布隆迪军队已经开启王室扩张阶段，而布约戈马当时仍由布哈姆瓦米鲁哈加掌握。鲁加姆巴觊觎这里的谷物和开阔牧场，向布哈开战。1821年时，高原仍处在鲁哈加一侧日益紧绷的边境上，夹在旧布哈王庭与崛起的布隆迪强权之间。

en:
Ruguru, also called Luguru or Nkanda-Luguru, was one of the small Ha polities of Buha, covering the country around later Basanza, Murufyiti, and Makere in what is now Kasulu District. In 1444 Kiha-speaking clans lived in scattered homesteads on fertile grassland and open woodland under elders called muteko. Women cultivated millet and other food crops, men hunted and gathered honey, and Ha smelters forged hoes, knives, and arrows that could be exchanged for cattle, skins, and Uvinza salt.

The spread of shifting cultivation in the seventeenth century strengthened these village economies, but around 1800 cattle-keeping dynasties reshaped Buha during its succession wars. Their ubugabire patron-client system raised a mwami and watwale officials above the old clan heads, who retained duties over land and ritual while tribute in grain, salt, milk, honey, and cattle flowed toward the new courts. Nkanda-Luguru thus entered 1821 as one of Buha's six chiefdoms, its older Ha clan order being folded into a cattle aristocracy.
zh:
卢古鲁又称卢古鲁或恩坎达-卢古鲁，是布哈的Ha人小政权之一，地域包括今卡苏卢县境内后来的巴桑扎、穆鲁菲蒂和马凯雷一带。1444年，说基哈语的氏族散居在肥沃草地与开阔疏林中，由称muteko的长老统领。妇女种植粟米等粮食，男子狩猎并采集蜂蜜；Ha铁匠锻打锄头、刀和箭，用这些器物交换牛、兽皮和乌温扎盐。

17世纪轮作农业扩展，巩固了这些村落经济；约1800年，牧牛王朝趁布哈继承战争重塑了当地秩序。他们带来的乌布加比雷保护—依附关系把姆瓦米和称watwale的官员抬到旧氏族首领之上，旧首领仍保留土地分配和仪式职责，而谷物、盐、奶、蜂蜜和牛等贡赋流向新王庭。恩坎达-卢古鲁因此作为布哈六个酋邦之一进入1821年，旧的Ha氏族秩序正被纳入一个牧牛贵族体系。

en: Hehe is the high southern plateau later called Uhehe, around Iringa and the grazing lands above the Great Ruaha. In 1444 it was not a single kingdom. Bantu farming communities kept cattle and goats where pasture allowed, and local traditions name the Hafiwa, iron-working Vanyategeta, Vanyakilwa, Vasavila and Vadongwe among the groups settled in its hills and valleys. Small chiefs raided one another for cattle, made marriage alliances and broke them when advantage shifted. Over the following generations the Muyinga lineage built up the Nguruhe chiefdom, but chiefly power never crossed the whole plateau.
