Already a rich grain town, it was taken by the Seljuk Turks in 1074 and became known as Sultanönü; in 1097 it saw the crusader victory of Dorylaeum over Kilij Arslan I. South of the town, at Seyitgazi, a tomb and mosque built in 1207-1208 over the warrior-saint Battal Gazi became a hostel for pilgrims and caravans. In 1289 the Seljuks ceded Eskişehir to Osman Gazi, and though it fell to the Karamanids under Orhan, Murad I won it back. In 1444 it was a quiet market town in the governorate of Ankara, its grain fields watered by the Porsuk.

In 1451, when Kütahya became the seat of a governor-general, Sultanönü passed from Ankara's jurisdiction to that of Kütahya. The troubles of the Celali rising reached it in 1601, when the rebel Deli Hasan and his bands held the town for a time while crossing Anatolia. The district's quieter fame was its meerschaum: the soft white stone of its hills, the only workable meerschaum in Ottoman lands, was carved into pipes that merchants carried to Istanbul and Europe. Grain, livestock and the passing caravan and army traffic along the great eastern road kept the town modestly busy through the following centuries.
zh:
苏丹诺努省得名于其首府埃斯基谢希尔的古突厥语旧名。埃斯基谢希尔即拜占庭时代的多里莱乌姆，位于波尔苏克河畔、布尔萨通往高原东部的大道上，当时已是富庶的粮城。它于1074年被塞尔柱突厥人夺取，得名苏丹诺努；1097年，第一次十字军在此赢得多里莱乌姆之战，击败基利杰·阿尔斯兰一世。城以南的塞伊特加齐，1207—1208年在武圣巴塔勒·加齐墓地上建起的圣祠与清真寺，后来成为朝圣者和商队的客栈。1289年，塞尔柱人把埃斯基谢希尔割让给奥斯曼·加齐；奥尔汗时期它一度落入卡拉曼侯国之手，穆拉德一世将其收复。1444年，它是安卡拉总督辖区内一座安静的集镇，波尔苏克河灌溉着周围的粮田。

1451年屈塔希亚成为总督驻地后，苏丹诺努从安卡拉辖区划归屈塔希亚管辖。杰拉里叛乱的兵锋在1601年波及此地：叛乱者德利·哈桑率众横穿安纳托利亚时，一度占据埃斯基谢希尔。这片地方更温和的名气来自海泡石——周边丘陵出产奥斯曼土地上唯一可供雕刻的白色软石，当地匠人把它雕成烟斗，由商人运往伊斯坦布尔和欧洲。在其后的岁月里，粮食、畜牧以及东方大道上往来的商队与军队，维系着这座小城不大不小的景气。

en:
Kangırı, ancient Gangra, is a fortress town on the northern edge of the central Anatolian plateau, where the Acıçay and Tatlıçay streams meet on their way to the Kızılırmak. Once a residence of the kings of Paphlagonia and a great bishopric of the Byzantine world, it was taken by the Danishmend Turks after Manzikert; the crusaders of 1101 could not storm its castle, and the emperor John II Komnenos, who fought his way in in 1134, lost the town again as soon as he withdrew. Kangırı entered the Ottoman lands under Murad I. After the disaster of 1402 Timur handed it back to its old lords, and only in 1439 was it brought once more under Ottoman rule. In 1444, five years recovered, it was the seat of a district governor of the Anatolian province, with flocks pastured on the surrounding steppe.

The Ottoman centuries were quiet ones. As the centre of a sanjak, Kangırı lived by the wool of the flocks herded around it, and Suleiman the Magnificent's reign gave it its chief monument, the Great Mosque built by the architect Sadık Kalfa in the age of Sinan; a smaller stone foundation, the Ali Bey mosque, carries an inscription dated 1609. Beyond these works the old Paphlagonian fortress passed the rest of the period as a small garrison and wool town gathered beneath its ancient citadel, seldom named in the empire's wars.
zh:
堪基利古称甘格拉，是安纳托利亚高原北缘的一座要塞城镇，地处阿哲恰伊河与塔特勒恰伊河汇合处，两河在此合流后汇入克孜勒河。这里曾是帕夫拉戈尼亚国王的驻跸之地、拜占庭世界的重要主教区；曼齐刻特战役后被达尼什曼德突厥人攻取，1101年的十字军攻不破它的城堡，1134年约翰二世皇帝虽经激战拿下此城，大军一撤走便再度失守。穆拉德一世时期，堪基利并入奥斯曼版图。1402年大败之后，帖木儿把堪基利交还给旧日的领主，直到1439年它才重新归入奥斯曼统治。1444年，收复五年的堪基利是安纳托利亚省下的一个县治驻地，畜群放牧在周围的草原上。

奥斯曼时代的堪基利岁月平静。作为一个桑贾克的中心，这座小城靠周围畜群的羊毛为生。苏莱曼大帝在位时，建筑师萨德克·卡尔法以希南时代的风格主持修建了大清真寺，成为城中首屈一指的古迹；规模较小的石砌建筑阿里贝伊清真寺则留下了1609年的铭文。除此之外，这座帕夫拉戈尼亚古要塞在本时期余下的时间里，始终是古堡山下一座小小的驻军与羊毛集镇，鲜有在帝国的战事中被提及。

en: Kırşehir, the Byzantine Mocissus, is a steppe town where central Anatolian roads from Konya and Ankara turn toward Tokat and Sivas. Seljuk Turks took it in the 1070s and named it Kır Şehri, 'steppe city'. Caca Bey, the local Seljuk emir, built his medrese in 1272, and the Turkish Sufi poet Aşık Pasha died here in 1332; Ahi craftsmen's lodges tied the small market to leatherworking and caravan trade. Bayezid I's campaign of 1398 brought the Kırşehir–Sivas country under Ottoman rule, so in 1444 it was a modest Turkish Muslim town rather than the old Byzantine fortress of Mocissus. Caravans crossing the Kızılırmak used Kesikköprü, built in 1248 on the Kırşehir–Konya road. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries highwaymen so dominated its approaches that the crossing became known as Kesikköprü, the Cut Bridge.
zh: 克尔谢希尔古称莫西苏斯，是安纳托利亚草原上的城镇，科尼亚、安卡拉通往托卡特和锡瓦斯的道路在此转向。塞尔柱突厥人在1070年代夺取此地，命名为克尔谢希尔，意为「草原之城」。当地塞尔柱埃米尔卡卡贝于1272年修建了以他命名的伊斯兰学校，土耳其语苏菲诗人阿什克·帕夏则于1332年在此去世；阿赫工匠兄弟会的会馆把这座小市场同制革业和商队贸易连在一起。1398年，巴耶济德一世的远征将克尔谢希尔至锡瓦斯一带纳入奥斯曼版图，因此1444年的这里已是一座不大的土耳其穆斯林城镇，不再是旧日拜占庭要塞莫西苏斯。往来商旅经由克尔谢希尔至科尼亚道路上的克西克桥渡过克孜勒河，该桥建于1248年。17至18世纪，路匪长期控制桥梁附近道路，使这座渡口以克西克桥，即「断桥」闻名。

en:
Tokat stands where the Tokat Suyu joins the Yeşilırmak, at the junction of roads from the Black Sea coast into central and eastern Anatolia. The Danishmend Gazi took its citadel in 1074, the Rum Seljuks absorbed the town in 1175, and Eretna and Kadı Burhaneddin held it in turn. After Kadı Burhaneddin's death in 1398, Bayezid I entered Tokat at the townspeople's invitation. Timur besieged the fortress in 1402 but could not take it, and the city remained in Mehmed I's hands through the Ottoman Interregnum. It became the first capital of the province of Rum. A severe earthquake in 1418–1419 damaged Tokat, yet in 1444 its fortress, caravan market and copper workshops were still those of the chief administrative town on the empire's north-eastern road.

The 1455 register counted 46 quarters and 3,079 households. In August 1472 Aq Qoyunlu troops under Bektaşoğlu Ömer Bey forced their way in, sacked and burned the town; only 1,781 households were recorded in 1485. Tokat resisted a Safavid siege in 1505, although Nur Ali Halife's partisans later briefly opened it to Shah Ismail's cause. Bayezid II added the Hatuniye complex, and by 1574 the household count had recovered to 2,568. The Celali disorders and the Great Flight then impoverished the surrounding countryside, and rebels under Abaza Mehmed Pasha held the city briefly in 1623. In 1659 Tokat became the seat of a new revenue voivodeship, but the North Anatolian earthquake of 17 August 1668 shattered part of the citadel and walls, and a great fire in 1679–1680 destroyed much of the city.
zh:
托卡特位于托卡特河汇入耶希勒河之处，是黑海沿岸通往安纳托利亚中部和东部道路的交会点。达尼什曼德·加齐1074年夺取此地城堡，罗姆塞尔柱人1175年吞并托卡特，其后埃雷特纳和卡迪·布尔汉丁相继统治。1398年卡迪·布尔汉丁死后，巴耶济德一世应市民邀请入城。1402年帖木儿围攻城堡却未能攻克，整个奥斯曼大空位期里，托卡特都掌握在穆罕默德一世手中，并成为鲁姆行省最初的首府。1418—1419年的大地震使托卡特受损，但到1444年，这里的要塞、商队市场和铜器作坊仍支撑着它作为帝国东北道路上首要行政城镇的地位。

1455年的地籍调查记载全城有46个街区、3079户。1472年8月，贝克塔什奥卢·厄梅尔贝伊率领白羊王朝军队攻入城中，洗劫并焚毁托卡特，因此1485年登记只剩1781户。1505年，托卡特顶住了萨法维军队的围攻，不过努尔·阿里·哈利法的支持者后来一度献城，使城中为伊斯玛仪沙的事业诵读呼图白。巴耶济德二世在此增建哈通尼耶建筑群，到1574年户数恢复至2568户。此后杰拉里动乱和「大逃亡」使周边乡村凋敝，1623年阿巴扎·穆罕默德帕夏的叛军又短暂占据托卡特。1659年，这里成为新设立的包税长官辖区驻地；但1668年8月17日的北安纳托利亚大地震震毁部分城堡和城墙，1679—1680年的大火又摧毁了城市大片区域。

en:
Al-Sharqiyya, the eastern province, covers the Nile Delta's flank toward Sinai and the Levant. Its old fortress and caravan station at Bilbeis guarded the road from Cairo to the desert, and Fatimid administrators grouped the surrounding kura districts into an eastern province. Al-Kamil founded Mansura on the Damietta branch in 1219; after the Ayyubid repulse of the Fifth Crusade it received its name, 'the Victorious.' In 1250 Louis IX of France was captured in the same watery country after the Mansura campaign, and in 1260 Sultan Qutuz was assassinated at Salihiyya while returning from Ain Jalut. In 1444 Mamluk lords thus held a province of grain villages, river crossings and eastern marches, watchful for bedouin unrest and armies coming from Syria.

The Ottoman conquest of 1517 placed Sharqiyya under Cairo's new governors, but Mamluk households gradually recovered local power. Ali Bey al-Kabir, the Mamluk strongman who ruled Ottoman Egypt from 1767, stopped the tribute to Istanbul in 1769 and sent armies into the Hejaz and Syria before his fall in 1772. When the French invaded in 1798, Napoleon had the old works at Bilbeis repaired, and on 11 August the desert edge at Salihiyya saw the battle that opened the route toward Syria. French rule lasted only until 1801, when Ottoman and British intervention forced the evacuation; the returning Ottoman order then had to contend with years of Mamluk rivalry and the rising authority of Muhammad Ali in Cairo.
zh:
东部省位于尼罗河三角洲朝向西奈和黎凡特的一侧。古城贝勒比斯是要塞与商队驿站，扼守从开罗通往沙漠的道路；法蒂玛王朝的官员把周边的库拉行政区整合为东部大区。1219年，卡米勒在杜姆亚特河畔建立曼苏拉；艾优卜王朝击退第五次十字军后，这座城得到「胜利之城」的名字。1250年，法王路易九世在曼苏拉战役后的水网地带被俘；1260年，苏丹古图兹在艾因贾鲁特返程途中于萨利希耶遇刺。因此到1444年，马穆鲁克贵族掌握的是一片遍布粮村、渡口与东边通道的土地，既要防范贝都因人骚动，也要警戒从叙利亚方向来的军队。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，东部省归开罗新任总督管辖，但马穆鲁克家族逐渐夺回地方权力。1767年起主政奥斯曼埃及的马穆鲁克强人阿里贝伊·卡比尔于1769年停止向伊斯坦布尔纳贡，并派军进攻汉志和叙利亚，最终在1772年倒台。1798年法国入侵时，拿破仑下令修缮贝勒比斯旧工事；8月11日，沙漠边缘的萨利希耶爆发战役，打开了通往叙利亚的道路。法国统治只维持到1801年，奥斯曼与英国的干预迫使其撤军；恢复后的奥斯曼秩序随后又要应付连年的马穆鲁克内争，以及开罗的穆罕默德·阿里不断上升的权势。

en:
Al-Buhayra means 'the lake district,' a fitting name for the wetlands and farmlands of the western Nile Delta between Alexandria and Cairo. Its capital Damanhur, whose Coptic and pharaonic name meant 'town of Horus,' stood on the old Butic Canal and became a provincial seat under the Fatimids in the eleventh century. During the Middle Ages it prospered as a caravan town on the post road linking Cairo with Alexandria. An earthquake badly damaged it in 1302, and the Mamluk sultan Barquq later restored its fortifications as protection against Bedouin raids. In 1444 grain, river traffic and overland trade therefore moved through a marshy frontier province watched from Damanhur.

Egypt became an Ottoman province after the conquest of 1517, yet Mamluk emirs kept many offices and tax districts, and Buhayra's road between Cairo and Alexandria lost none of its importance. On 13 July 1798 that road and river line brought fighting to Shubra Khit: marching on Cairo, Napoleon formed infantry squares against Murad Bey's Mamluk cavalry while French and Ottoman flotillas clashed on the Nile. The Mamluks were unable to break the squares. Damanhur rose against the French in 1799; the revolt was crushed with great severity, with about 1,500 people killed. Anglo-Ottoman forces expelled the French in 1801, and in 1805 Muhammad Ali seized power in Cairo, opening a new era of central rule over the Delta.
zh:
布海拉意为「湖泊之地」，正适合形容尼罗河三角洲西部、亚历山大与开罗之间的湿地和农田。首府达曼胡尔的科普特与法老时代名称意为「荷鲁斯之城」，古城坐落于古布提克运河畔，11世纪法蒂玛王朝时成为行省治所。中世纪时，它作为开罗至亚历山大驿道上的商队城镇而繁荣。1302年的地震使城市损失惨重，马穆鲁克苏丹贝尔古格后来修复防御工事，以抵御贝都因人袭扰。1444年，粮食、河运和陆路贸易都要穿过这片沼泽纵横的边地，达曼胡尔则监视着四方通道。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，埃及成为帝国行省，但马穆鲁克埃米尔仍保留许多官职和税区，布海拉境内连接开罗与亚历山大的道路依旧重要。1798年7月13日，战火烧到舒卜拉希特的道路与河道：拿破仑向开罗进军时列出步兵方阵，抵挡穆拉德贝伊的马穆鲁克骑兵，法国与奥斯曼的小型舰队也在尼罗河上交战，马穆鲁克人无法冲破方阵。1799年，达曼胡尔起兵反抗法国，起义遭到严酷镇压，约一千五百人被杀。1801年，英国与奥斯曼军队将法国人逐出埃及；1805年，穆罕默德·阿里在开罗掌权，三角洲随之进入新的集权统治时代。

en: Atfih stands on the Nile's east bank, on the road and river route from Cairo into Upper Egypt. The Greeks knew the old town as Aphroditopolis, and its Ptolemaic tombs held the sacred cows of the goddess Hesat. In Mamluk records the surrounding district was called al-A'mal al-Itfihiyya, with its seat at al-Atfihiyya; floods and Bedouin raids had begun to weaken that town. In 1444 it was still a Mamluk administrative post south of Cairo. Ottoman conquest followed in 1517 and French occupation in 1798, but local Mamluk power lasted until the reforms of Muhammad Ali after 1805, when Giza became the seat of an independent district and Atfih was attached to it.
zh: 艾特菲赫位于尼罗河东岸，扼守从开罗通往上埃及的道路与河路。古希腊人称旧城为阿芙洛狄忒波利斯，当地托勒密时期墓葬曾安葬女神赫萨特的神牛。马穆鲁克文献称这一行政区为「伊塔菲哈辖区」，治所在艾特菲希亚；洪水与贝都因袭扰已使这座城镇趋于衰弱。1444年，它仍是开罗以南的马穆鲁克行政据点。1517年这里随埃及被奥斯曼征服，1798年又遭法国占领，但地方马穆鲁克势力一直延续到1805年后穆罕默德·阿里推行改革；当时吉萨成为独立行政区的治所，艾特菲赫改隶其下。

en:
Esna, ancient Latopolis, lies on the Nile's west bank about 55 kilometres south of Luxor. The Ptolemaic and Roman temple of Khnum stood in the town centre, gradually buried by centuries of river silt, while the river crossing and markets made Esna a gathering point for villagers and desert traders. Badr al-Jamali founded the first Fatimid congregational mosque in 1081-1084, and its minaret, raised in 1081, still marked the Islamic town. In 1444 the Mamluk sultan governed a Sunni Egyptian river market whose livestock, crops and craft goods moved north by Nile boat and south toward the desert roads.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1517, imperial governors ruled in name while Mamluk beys long kept provincial power. In the 18th century Hassan Bey al-Jiddawi built Wekalet al-Jiddawi, an Esna caravanserai with about forty shops and upper chambers lodging merchants from Upper Egypt and the Sudan; gum arabic, ostrich feathers, textiles, oils, animals and crafts changed hands there. French troops campaigning in the Sa'id cleared part of the buried Khnum temple, while Hassan Bey resisted them at Bir Anbar on 2 April 1799. Following the French withdrawal in 1801 and Muhammad Ali's rise in 1805, Esna was brought back under a stronger Cairo administration.
zh:
伊斯纳古称拉托波利斯，位于卢克索以南约55公里的尼罗河西岸。托勒密和罗马时期的库努姆神庙坐落于城中心，后来在数百年河泥堆积中逐渐被埋；河渡与市集则使伊斯纳成为周边村民和沙漠商人的汇集地。拜德尔·贾马利于1081—1084年兴建法蒂玛时代第一座聚礼清真寺，1081年建成的宣礼塔长期标示着这座伊斯兰城镇。1444年，马穆鲁克苏丹统治着这座逊尼派埃及河港，牲畜、谷物和手工制品或由尼罗河北运，或沿沙漠商路南行。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，总督名义上治理此地，马穆鲁克贝伊却长期掌握地方实权。18世纪，哈桑贝伊·吉达维在伊斯纳修建杰达维商馆，约有四十间店铺，楼上房舍供来自上埃及和苏丹的商人住宿；阿拉伯胶、鸵鸟羽、纺织品、油、牲畜和手工制品都在此交易。法军征战赛义德期间，士兵清理了被埋的库努姆神庙的一部分，哈桑贝伊则于1799年4月2日在比尔安巴尔抵抗法军。1801年法军撤出、1805年穆罕默德·阿里崛起后，伊斯纳重新被更强有力的开罗政府管辖。

en:
Girga stands on the west bank of the Nile in one of Upper Egypt's broad floodplains. As Qus lost trade after the late fourteenth century, Girga rose to become the leading town of the Sa'id, with Mamluk officials, river merchants and Coptic communities sharing its markets and churches. In 1444 it was therefore a substantial provincial centre rather than a mere village: taxes and grain from the surrounding Nile villages were gathered there, and the town's Coptic see gave it an enduring place in southern Egyptian Christian life.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1517, Jirja became one of Egypt's sub-provinces, and Ottoman registers named it among the governorates through which Cairo ruled the south. In 1791 the Coptic scholar and theologian Yousab El Abah was appointed bishop of Girga and Akhmim and defended the Non-Chalcedonian position against Roman overtures. On 29 December 1798 General Desaix's French army reached Girga, then called the capital of Upper Egypt, and waited twenty days for an ammunition flotilla while Murad Bey sought help from the Hijaz, Nubia and the Red Sea coast. Local resistance continued, and Arabic records place the Battle of Girga on 7 April 1799. French rule ended in 1801, and after Muhammad Ali took power in 1805 the old southern governorate was drawn into his reformed Egyptian state.
zh:
吉尔贾位于尼罗河西岸一片开阔的冲积平原上。14世纪末古斯商路衰落后，吉尔贾崛起为赛义德的首要城镇，马穆鲁克官员、河运商人与科普特社群共用这里的市集和教堂。因此到1444年，它已是相当重要的地方中心，而不只是普通村落：周边尼罗河村庄缴纳的税赋和谷物汇集于此，当地的科普特主教区也使它在南部埃及基督教生活中长期占有一席之地。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，吉尔贾成为埃及的次级行政区之一，奥斯曼册籍也把它列为开罗统治南方的辖区。1791年，科普特学者、神学家优萨卜·艾卜哈被任命为吉尔贾和艾赫米姆主教，并在罗马教廷寻求教会合一时为非迦克墩立场辩护。1798年12月29日，德塞将军率领法军抵达当时被称为上埃及首府的吉尔贾，在此等候弹药船队二十天；穆拉德贝伊则向汉志、努比亚和红海沿岸求援。当地抵抗持续不断，阿拉伯文资料把吉尔贾战役记于1799年4月7日。1801年法国统治结束，1805年穆罕默德·阿里掌权后，这个古老南部辖区被纳入他改革后的埃及国家。

en: Farafra is the smallest and most isolated of Egypt's western oases, lying in a 980-square-kilometre depression midway between Bahariya and Dakhla. Its ancient Egyptian name meant 'land of cattle', while medieval Arabs called the springs there al-Farfarun. In Ptolemaic times the oasis was administered from Oxyrhynchus, and the mud-brick fort of Qasr al-Farafra was built to protect desert caravans. In 1444 Farafra was a scant watering place on the Mamluks' distant desert frontier, useful mainly for herds and traffic between oases. It shared the formal fate of the Western Desert when Ottoman conquest ended Mamluk rule in 1517, but Cairo's governors left few recorded marks on its isolated springs.
zh: 费拉菲拉是埃及西部诸绿洲中人口最少、也最孤立的一处，位于拜哈里耶和达赫莱之间、面积980平方公里的洼地。它的古埃及语名称意为「牛之地」，中世纪阿拉伯人则称当地泉群为费尔费伦。托勒密时期，这片绿洲由俄克喜林库斯管辖；盖斯尔·费拉菲拉的土坯堡垒最初是为保护沙漠商队而建。1444年，费拉菲拉只是马穆鲁克遥远沙漠边疆上一处稀少水源，价值主要在于牧放牲畜和维系绿洲间交通。1517年奥斯曼征服结束马穆鲁克统治后，它随整个西部沙漠改换宗主权，但开罗总督在这些偏远泉眼旁留下的记载很少。

en:
The district of Ghurian lies on the Hari Rud west of Herat, irrigated fields strung along the road to Mashhad. Medieval geographers knew its town as Pushang, held to be the oldest place in Khorasan and said to have been founded by Shapur I; in the tenth century Ibn Hawqal found a walled city half the size of Herat, with three gates and famous grapes. The Mongols wrecked it, the Karts rebuilt it, and Timur destroyed it again in 1381 before the town was restored under his heirs. In 1444 Ghurian was the western gate and granary of Shah Rukh's Herat: the congregational mosque raised in the Timurid age stood in the town, and its grapes and melons went to the bazaars of Herat.

Because the road from Iran to Herat runs through these fields, Ghurian was the first prize of every invasion. In the summer of 1458 Jahan Shah's Qara Qoyunlu army passed this way towards Herat before turning back, and in 1507 the Uzbeks of Muhammad Shaybani seized the district; Shah Isma'il retook it in 1510, it fell again after his death, and Shah Tahmasp recovered it in 1528. The long Safavid-Uzbek frontier wars ruined Pushang, which was rebuilt and in time became known by its present name of Ghurian. In 1716 the Abdalis of Herat rose and ruled here as sultans until Nader Shah retook the province in 1732; in 1747 it passed to Ahmad Shah Durrani. Once Herat became an independent principality, Ghurian was tossed between border chieftains: Eshaq Khan Qara'i of Torbat-e Heydarieh took it in 1804, Firuz al-Din of Herat held it briefly in 1813–14, the Hazara chief Banyad Khan and Firuz al-Din fought over it in 1816, and after the Iranians seized it in 1818 it passed to Mohammad Khan Qara'i, who still held it in 1821.
zh:
古里扬位于哈烈以西的哈里河畔，沿通往马什哈德的大道展开，是一片受河水灌溉的富庶乡野。中世纪地理学家称此地的城镇为普尚格（Pushang），目为呼罗珊最古老的城市，相传为沙普尔一世所建；10世纪伊本·豪卡勒见到的普尚格有城墙环护，规模相当于半个哈烈，三门并峙，以葡萄闻名。蒙古人将其摧毁，卡尔特王朝加以重建，帖木儿1381年再度毁城，其继承者又把它恢复起来。1444年，古里扬是沙哈鲁治下哈烈的西部门户和粮仓：帖木儿时期修建的聚礼清真寺矗立城中，葡萄与甜瓜源源运往哈烈的巴扎。

由于伊朗通往哈烈的大路正穿过这片原野，古里扬每遇战事总是首当其冲。1458年夏，贾汉沙率黑羊王朝军队经此进逼哈烈，随后回师；1507年穆罕默德·昔班尼的乌兹别克人夺取此地，伊斯玛仪一世1510年将其收复，他死后再度失守，1528年塔赫玛斯普一世又予克复。萨法维与乌兹别克长期的边境战争毁了普尚格，城被重建后逐渐改用今名古里扬。1716年哈烈的阿布达里人起事，在此自立为苏丹，直到1732年纳迪尔沙收复该省，1747年它转入艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼之手。哈烈沦为割据公国后，古里扬在边境豪强之间几度易主：1804年托尔巴特海达里耶的伊萨克汗·卡雷夺城，1813至1814年哈烈的菲鲁兹丁短暂据有，1816年哈扎拉首领巴尼亚德汗与菲鲁兹丁又在此争夺，1818年伊朗军队取城后，该地落入穆罕默德汗·卡雷之手，1821年仍由他占据。

en: Sarakhs is the last oasis of the Hari Rud before the Karakum Desert, the midway halt between Merv and Mashhad. In Samanid and Seljuk times its libraries and madrasas made it a learned city: the Hanafi jurist Abu Bakr al-Sarakhsi taught here, a famous school of architects flourished, and the Yarty Gumbez mausoleum was raised eight kilometres to the south in 1089. The Mongols sacked the city in 1221, and although it was rebuilt under the Ilkhans and the Timurids it never regained its old size. In 1444 Sarakhs was a Timurid caravan town guarding the road to Merv. Jahan Shah's Qara Qoyunlu ravaged the oasis on their march in 1458, and in March 1459 Abu Sa'id Mirza of Samarkand defeated the Timurid princes of Khurasan and Merv in the battle fought between Merv and Sarakhs. The Uzbeks took it in 1507, and Shah Isma'il recovered it after his victory at Merv in 1510; thereafter it remained a small Safavid border station between Khorasan and the Turkmen desert.
zh: 萨拉赫斯是哈里河进入卡拉库姆沙漠前的最后一片绿洲，也是梅尔夫与马什哈德之间的中途驿站。萨曼王朝和塞尔柱时期，城中图书馆与伊斯兰学校林立，是学术名城：哈乃斐派法学家艾布·伯克尔·萨拉赫西曾在此讲学，著名的建筑师学派盛极一时，亚尔蒂·贡贝兹陵1089年建于城南八公里处。1221年蒙古人洗劫此城，伊儿汗国和帖木儿时期虽予重建，却再未恢复旧观。1444年，萨拉赫斯是帖木儿治下戍守梅尔夫大道的商队城镇。1458年贾汉沙的黑羊王朝军队进军途中蹂躏这片绿洲，1459年3月，撒马尔罕的阿布·萨义德在梅尔夫与萨拉赫斯之间击败呼罗珊和梅尔夫的帖木儿诸宗王。1507年乌兹别克人取城，1510年伊斯玛仪一世在梅尔夫获胜后将其收复；此后它一直是呼罗珊与土库曼沙漠之间一座偏远的萨法维边境驿站。

en:
Founded in the third century by the Sasanian king Shapur I, Nishapur became capital of the province of Abarshahr and, with Merv, Herat and Balkh, one of the four great cities of Khorasan. It served the Tahirids as their capital and in 1037 became the first Seljuk capital, drawing Silk Road caravans and fame for the turquoise mined in the nearby hills. Tolui's Mongols sacked it over ten days in 1221, but it revived under the Ilkhans on a site northwest of the old ruins. Ibn Battuta in the fourteenth century found orchards and busy markets and called it 'Little Damascus'; Hamdallah Mustawfi, visiting in 1339, counted forty mills working without pause on the Mirabad river. Timur took the city without a fight in the spring of 1381, Castile's envoy Clavijo passed through in July 1404, and an earthquake shook the city the following year. In 1444 Nishapur, Sunni and Persian-speaking, was a provincial market town of Shah Rukh's Timurid empire, much smaller than in its heyday but still living by turquoise and silk.

On 20 April 1447, only weeks after Shah Rukh's death, rival Timurid princes fought over the city in the succession war. Under Sultan Husayn Bayqara of Herat, the last Timurid of consequence in Khorasan, Nishapur knew peace again; its Friday mosque went up in 1493, the oldest building in the city to survive from those times. In 1507 Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks overran Khorasan, until the Safavid shah Ismail destroyed their army at Merv in December 1510 and slew Shaybani. The citadel was besieged during the Safavid factional wars of 1581, and in 1592 Shah Abbas retook Nishapur from the Uzbeks: a royal caravanserai was built there, and in 1612 the shah's edicts cutting the city's taxes were inscribed on the Friday mosque. After Nader Shah's death in 1747 the Bayat chieftains made Nishapur an independent khanate, until Ahmad Shah Durrani took it with heavy artillery in the spring of 1751 and set Shah Rukh Afshar over western Khorasan. The Qajars added the city to their realm in 1800.
zh:
尼沙布尔3世纪由萨珊国王沙普尔一世所建，后为阿巴尔沙赫尔省首府，与木鹿、赫拉特、巴里赫并称呼罗珊四大城。它曾是塔希尔王朝的都城，1037年又成为塞尔柱人的第一个都城，丝绸之路上商队往来不绝，附近山中出产的绿松石更使其闻名天下。1221年，拖雷麾下的蒙古军连攻十日将城洗劫一空，但伊儿汗国时期，城市在旧城遗址西北重新兴起。14世纪时伊本·白图泰见到的尼沙布尔果园连片、市集繁忙，称之为「小大马士革」；哈木杜拉·穆斯图菲1339年到访时，记下米拉卜河畔四十座日夜不停的水磨。1381年春帖木儿兵不血刃拿下此城，1404年7月卡斯蒂利亚使节克拉维约途经这里，次年又有一场地震撼动全城。1444年的尼沙布尔是沙哈鲁帖木儿帝国治下一座逊尼派、说波斯语的地方商城，规模远不及鼎盛年代，却仍以绿松石和丝绸为生。

1447年4月20日，沙哈鲁驾崩不过数周，争夺大位的帖木儿宗王便在此城兵戎相见。在赫拉特统治者、呼罗珊末代有为之主忽辛·拜哈拉治下，尼沙布尔重享太平，1493年建起聚礼清真寺，是城内保存最久的建筑。1507年，穆罕默德·昔班尼的乌兹别克人席卷呼罗珊；1510年12月，萨法维沙阿伊斯玛仪在木鹿大破其军、阵斩昔班尼。1581年萨法维内讧，城市城堡遭围攻；1592年阿巴斯沙阿从乌兹别克人手中收复尼沙布尔，此后在此建起皇家商队客栈，1612年又把减免赋税的敕令刻在聚礼清真寺上。1747年纳德尔沙阿死后，巴亚特部首领以尼沙布尔自立为汗国；1751年春，艾哈迈德沙阿·杜兰尼以重炮攻下此城，立阿夫沙尔王族沙哈鲁为西呼罗珊之主。1800年，尼沙布尔并入恺加王朝版图。

en:
Jask is a small peninsula harbour on the Makran coast, where the Strait of Hormuz opens into the Gulf of Oman. Medieval geographers knew it as Jashk or Ras al-Jask, one of the anchorages on the sea road between the Persian Gulf and India, and a local ruler, Tahmtan ibn Turanshah, titled Sultan Qutb al-Din, governed it after 1330. The arid country behind the port belonged to the amirs of Makran, Baloch chiefs who answered to no distant power whenever the central government was weak, while the Jagin river brought fresh water down from the Bashagird hills. In 1444 Jask was a Sunni fishing and trading harbour on the edge of the Timurid world, where coasting craft plying between the Gulf and India took water and shelter.

By the turn of the sixteenth century the Makran amirs had made the sea road unsafe, and in 1515 Shah Ismail I made a treaty with Albuquerque's Portuguese at Hormuz for help against them; Portuguese sources themselves place the amir's reach as far as Jask. Shah Abbas I brought the coast firmly under Safavid rule only after crushing Malik Shams al-Din's revolts of 1608 and 1613. The English chose Jask as their port in 1614: their first cargo ship from India anchored in 1616, and in 1619 the East India Company opened its first Iranian factory here, through which English goods moved up to central Iran until Bandar Abbas took the trade. In late 1620 Dutch ships barred two Company vessels from entering the harbour, and in the sharp battle that followed the Dutch were defeated and driven off. Jask later lost its place as the English headquarters in the Gulf to Bandar Abbas.
zh:
贾斯克是莫克兰海岸一座小半岛港湾，扼守霍尔木兹海峡通入阿曼湾的出口。中世纪地理学家称它为贾什克或贾斯角，是波斯湾通往印度航路上的停泊地之一；一位名叫塔赫姆坦·本·图兰沙、称苏丹·库特卜丁的地方统治者，在1330年之后统治此地。港后干旱的原野属莫克兰诸埃米尔——俾路支首领的地盘，中央政权衰弱时他们便不奉远命，贾金河则从巴沙格尔德山中为港湾带来淡水。1444年的贾斯克，是帖木儿世界边缘一座逊尼派的渔业与贸易港湾，往来波斯湾与印度的沿岸船只在此取水避风。

16世纪初，莫克兰埃米尔使海上商路不得安宁。1515年，伊斯玛仪一世与盘踞霍尔木兹的阿尔布克尔克葡萄牙人订约，请其出兵相助；葡萄牙史料也证实莫克兰埃米尔的势力已抵达贾斯克一带。阿拔斯沙阿在平定马利克·沙姆斯丁1608年和1613年的两次叛乱后，才把海岸牢牢纳入萨法维治下。英国人1614年选定贾斯克为商港：第一艘货船1616年自印度驶来停泊，1619年东印度公司在此设立在波斯的第一处商馆，英国货经此运往波斯腹地，直到贸易改归阿巴斯港。1620年末，荷兰舰队阻拦公司的两艘船只入港，随后的激战以荷兰人战败被逐告终。贾斯克作为英国人在海湾总部的地位，后来也让给了阿巴斯港。

en:
Fasa sits in the wide plain of south-eastern Fars on the caravan road from Shiraz to Kerman, with Jahrom to its south. Settled since Achaemenid times at the mound of Tall-e Zahhak, it made terms with the Arab army in 644. Tenth-century geographers knew it as one of the greatest towns of Fars, almost the equal of Shiraz: its markets sold multicoloured, sometimes brocaded silks, fine carpets and safflower, and its brick Friday mosque was larger than the one in Shiraz. A Buyid civil war wrecked the town in 989-90, and a night raid by Alp Arslan in 1050 carried off three million dinars' worth of plunder and three thousand captives; rebuilt after Shabankara tribesmen sacked it, Fasa never regained its old size. In 1444 it was a quiet Sunni Persian town under the Timurid governor of Fars in Shiraz, living on its orchards, grain and the silk caravans passing through.

When Shah Rukh died in 1447 the Timurid hold on Fars loosened: in 1452-53 Jahan Shah of the Qara Qoyunlu seized Shiraz and made his son Pir Budaq governor, and in 1467-68 Uzun Hasan's Aq Qoyunlu overthrew them. Shah Ismail's Safavids took Shiraz in 1504, and under Safavid rule Fasa gained its grand bazaar, congregational mosque and baths as its people turned to Shi'ism. In 1762-63 Karim Khan Zand, who had made Shiraz his capital, settled the Chahar Lang Bakhtiari with farmland near the town. Early in the nineteenth century Zayn al-Abedin Shirvani found a pleasant township of some two thousand houses, its people Tajiks and Shi'ites, ringed by thirty villages; in the Qajar years famine, plague and disorder wore it down. Around Jahrom to the south, palm groves planted in Safavid and Zand times made its dates famous, and Qajar governors laid out its bazaar and caravanserais.
zh:
法萨位于法尔斯东南部的广阔平原上，地处设拉子通往克尔曼的商路，南面是贾赫罗姆。早在阿契美尼德时期，扎哈克丘一带便有人定居；644年，法萨与阿拉伯军队议和归降。10世纪的地理学家把它列为法尔斯数一数二的大城，规模几乎与设拉子相当：市集上出售色彩绚丽、间或织锦的丝绸、精美地毯和红花，砖砌的聚礼清真寺比设拉子的那座还要大。989至990年白益王朝内战将城池摧残，1050年阿尔普·阿尔斯兰趁夜劫袭，掠走价值三百万第纳尔的财物和三千俘虏；沙班卡拉部族洗劫之后虽经阿塔贝格·乔夫利重建，法萨再未恢复旧观。1444年，它是设拉子的法尔斯帖木儿长官治下一座安静的逊尼派波斯城镇，靠果园、麦作和过境丝绸商队为生。

1447年沙哈鲁死后，帖木儿对法尔斯的掌控松动：1452至1453年，黑羊王朝的贾汉·沙夺取设拉子，以其子皮尔·布达格为总督；1467至1468年，乌尊·哈桑的白羊王朝又将其攻灭。1504年，伊斯玛仪一世的萨非军队攻占设拉子，萨非时期法萨建起大巴扎、聚礼清真寺和公共浴场，居民也改宗什叶派。1762至1763年，以设拉子为都的赞德王朝卡里姆汗把巴赫蒂亚里人的四朗部安置在法萨附近，拨给田地。19世纪初，扎因·阿比丁·希尔瓦尼见到的是一座约有两千户人家的宜人小镇，居民多为塔吉克什叶派，周围环绕着三十个村庄；卡扎尔时期，饥荒、瘟疫和动荡使它日益凋敝。南边贾赫罗姆的椰枣林在萨非和赞德时期成片栽种，椰枣自此闻名，卡扎尔的统治者又为它修建了巴扎和商队客栈。

en:
Darab, the ancient Darabgerd, lies in the warm south-eastern corner of Fars on the road towards Kerman, with Neyriz and the salt lake of Bakhtegan to its north. Before founding the Sasanian dynasty, Ardashir I made himself master of the town, and the rock relief of Shapur I nearby, carved after the capture of the Roman emperor Valerian in 260, marks its Sasanian heyday. It surrendered to the Arab army together with Fasa in 644 and remained the chief town of a large district, trading textiles, jasmine oil and a mineral balm called mumiya. Seljuk raids in the eleventh century drove its people first to the stronghold of Rombeh and then to the present site, and Ilkhanid and Timurid armies damaged the town again. In 1444 Darab was a weathered district town under the Timurid governors in Shiraz; nearby Neyriz still kept its formidable castle and the Friday mosque dedicated in 951.

The storms that crossed Fars reached Darab too: the Qara Qoyunlu took the province in 1452-53, the Aq Qoyunlu in 1467-68, and the Safavids of Shah Ismail in 1504. Under Safavid rule the district became crown land and throve again, counted among the five vizier's seats of Fars, and it stayed an important province through the Zand eighteenth century. Qajar times brought strife instead, as Turkic and Arab tribes pressed in around the town and government campaigns against them battered the countryside, leaving Darab to lag far behind Shiraz.
zh:
达拉卜古称达拉卜吉德，坐落在法尔斯东南端通往克尔曼的道路旁，北面是内里兹和巴赫泰甘盐湖。阿尔达希尔一世建立萨珊王朝之前，正是在此城起家；附近的沙普尔一世摩崖浮雕完成于260年俘获罗马皇帝瓦勒良之后，见证了它在萨珊时期的鼎盛。644年，达拉卜与法萨一同向阿拉伯军队归降，此后一直是一个大区的首城，出产织物、茉莉油和一种叫莫米雅的矿物香膏。11世纪塞尔柱人的入侵迫使居民先退守龙贝要塞，再迁至达拉卜今址，伊尔汗国和帖木儿的军队又使城池一再受创。1444年，达拉卜是设拉子帖木儿长官治下一座饱经风霜的区城；邻近的内里兹仍保有坚固要塞和951年落成的聚礼清真寺。

此后席卷法尔斯的变局同样波及达拉卜：黑羊王朝1452至1453年夺取本省，白羊王朝1467至1468年继之，1504年落入伊斯玛仪一世的萨非王朝之手。萨非时期，此地被划为王室直领，再度繁荣，位列法尔斯五个维齐尔驻地之一，整个赞德王朝的18世纪里始终是法尔斯的重要州郡。卡扎尔时期带来的却是战乱：突厥和阿拉伯部落进逼城周，官府对部落连年用兵，乡野残破，达拉卜就此远远落在设拉子之后。

en:
Kazerun guards the fertile plain between Shiraz and the Persian Gulf ports, on the road down to Bushehr. Above the plain stand the ruins of Bishapur, the round Sasanian city that Shapur I built in 266 with Roman captives taken with the emperor Valerian; as Bishapur wasted under Arab rule its people drifted to Kazerun, which kept its old faith until the tenth century. Then Shaykh Abu Ishaq Kazeruni founded the Sufi order named after the town, whose merchant-brothers carried its teaching and trade to India, China and the Ottoman lands, collecting seafarers' vows from every ship that weathered the China Sea, as Ibn Battuta witnessed; Shah Rukh himself prayed at the founder's tomb. Shabankara tribesmen burned Bishapur in 1101 until the atabeg Chawoli curbed them in 1108 and rebuilt Kazerun, and the Mongols sacked the town in 1263. In 1444 Kazerun was a wealthy Sunni market town, living on the gulf caravans and the fame of its shrines.

Shah Ismail saw the order as a rival, marched on Kazerun in person, slew its Sufi elders and installed an Afshar tribal family as governors, beginning with Khwaja Pir Budaq, and the town served as a Safavid minting centre. In 1733 Nader Shah arrived in pursuit of the rebel Mohammad Khan Baloch and afterwards made Khwaja Ali Qoli Khan governor; he settled and rebuilt the town and laid out the Bagh-e Nazar garden. His riflemen helped Karim Khan Zand defeat Azad Khan Afghan at Khesht in 1753 and at Kamarej in 1754, but the family later sided with Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar: in 1790 they tried to trap Lotf Ali Khan Zand, who escaped over the Qebleh hills to Dashtestan, then returned to storm Kazerun and blind their ruler Reza Qoli Khan.
zh:
卡泽伦扼守设拉子与波斯湾港口之间的肥沃平原，地处通往布什尔的大道上。平原上方耸立着比沙普尔城址：这座圆形的萨珊城市是沙普尔一世266年用随皇帝瓦勒良一同被俘的罗马工匠修建的；阿拉伯统治时期比沙普尔日渐荒废，居民陆续迁往卡泽伦，而卡泽伦直到10世纪仍信奉旧教。后来谢赫阿布·伊沙克·卡泽鲁尼在此创立以城名命名的卡泽鲁尼耶苏菲教团，教团的商人兄弟把教义和生意带到印度、中国和奥斯曼，凡平安渡过中国海的船只都要缴纳许愿的布施，伊本·白图泰曾亲见其事，沙哈鲁也曾到创始人墓前礼拜。沙班卡拉部落1101年焚毁比沙普尔，直到1108年阿塔贝格·乔夫利将其制服并重建卡泽伦；1263年蒙古人又洗劫了此城。1444年的卡泽伦是一座富庶的逊尼派商业城镇，靠往来海湾的商队和圣陵的声名过活。

伊斯玛仪一世把教团视为敌手，亲自进兵卡泽伦，诛杀苏菲长老，改以阿夫沙尔部落的家族为总督，首任是赫瓦贾·皮尔·布达格，卡泽伦在整个萨非时期都是铸币中心之一。1733年，纳迪尔沙为追剿叛酋穆罕默德汗·俾路支抵达此地，事后任命赫瓦贾·阿里·库里汗为总督；他招抚流民、修缮城池，还修建了纳扎尔花园。他手下的火枪队曾在1753年的赫什特和1754年的卡马雷季之战中助卡里姆汗·赞德击败阿扎德汗·阿富汗，但这个家族后来倒向阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔：1790年他们设计围捕卢特夫·阿里汗·赞德，后者弃马越过基卜勒山逃到达什特斯坦，随后回师攻破卡泽伦，刺瞎了他们的统治者礼萨·库里汗。

en: Siraf, also rendered Shilaw, occupies a narrow coastal strip pressed between the mountains and the Persian Gulf. In the 9th and 10th centuries it was the richest port on the Iranian shore: Sirafi ships sailed to India, East Africa and China, and its wharves handled spices, ivory, sandalwood, camphor, ambergris, pearls and precious stones. An earthquake in 977 badly damaged the wealthy city, and by the 13th century Yaqut al-Hamawi found only a small, ruined place whose name had shifted to Shilaw. Even so, a modest anchorage survived into the 15th and 16th centuries, carrying traffic from Fars toward Qatif and Arabia. In 1444 it was a minor Fars port on a much-diminished spice route. António Tenreiro visited 'Chilaão' in 1528 and Gasparo Balbi 'Silaú' in 1590; later travellers found only a small harbor at Taheri, whose ruins James Morier described in 1812.
zh: 希拉夫（又译西拉夫）位于高山与波斯湾之间的狭窄海岸地带。9至10世纪时，它是伊朗沿岸最富庶的港口：希拉夫商船远航印度、东非和中国，码头转运香料、象牙、檀香、樟脑、龙涎香、珍珠和宝石。977年的大地震严重毁坏这座富庶城市；到13世纪，雅古特·哈马维见到的只是一个名称已讹变为希劳的残破小地方。尽管如此，一处规模不大的锚地仍延续到15、16世纪，承担法尔斯前往卡提夫和阿拉伯半岛的航运。1444年时，它只是法尔斯治下一座小港，昔日香料商路已大为衰落。安东尼奥·特内雷罗1528年到过「希劳」，加斯帕罗·巴尔比1590年称其为「西劳」；后世旅行者只在塔赫里找到一座小港，詹姆斯·莫里尔则在1812年记述了当地的遗址。

en:
Tabas is the chief oasis at the western edge of the Great Salt Desert, where roads from Yazd, Qumis, Kerman and Quhistan converge. Al-Baladhuri called it 'the Gate of Khurasan'. In early Islamic times it was Tabas al-Tamr, 'Tabas of the Dates', for its palm groves, and tenth- and eleventh-century geographers described a walled town supplied by underground wells and surrounded by lemon and orange plantations. In the late eleventh century it became part of the Nizari Ismaili state and endured a Seljuk siege under Ahmad Sanjar in 1102. The Mongols spared Tabas, leaving its local rulers to govern Tabas, Tun and Gonabad. In 1444 it was a small Sunni Timurid frontier oasis, valuable chiefly because its water and gardens made the desert crossing possible.

Uzbek tribes occupied Khorasan in 1507. After Nader Shah's assassination in 1747, the Zangu'i Arabs ruled Tabas and nearby Tun as an independent local state. In May 1754 Ahmad Shah Durrani advanced from Herat; Ali Murad Khan, governor of Tabas, met him in a bloody battle, was killed, and the two oases fell between June and July. After the siege of Nishapur in 1755, Durrani troops returned and sacked Tun and Tabas. During Ahmad Shah's final Khorasan campaign of 1769–1770, Ali Mardan Khan of Tabas led reinforcements toward Mashhad, only to be defeated and slain near Gonabad.
zh:
塔巴斯是大盐漠西缘的主要绿洲，亚兹德、库米斯、克尔曼和古希斯坦的道路在此交汇。拜拉祖里称它为「呼罗珊之门」。伊斯兰时代早期，这里因椰枣林称塔巴斯·塔米尔，意为「椰枣的塔巴斯」；10至11世纪的地理学家记述此地城垣坚固，地下水井供水充足，周围有柠檬和柑橘园。11世纪末，塔巴斯成为尼扎里伊斯玛仪国的一部分，1102年遭艾哈迈德·桑贾尔率领的塞尔柱军队围攻。蒙古人进攻伊朗时放过塔巴斯，使当地统治者得以继续管辖塔巴斯、图恩和古纳巴德。1444年，它是帖木儿帝国一座小型逊尼派边地绿洲，价值主要在于水源和园圃使穿越沙漠成为可能。

1507年，乌兹别克诸部占领呼罗珊。纳迪尔沙1747年遇刺后，赞古伊阿拉伯人以塔巴斯和附近的图恩为中心建立独立的地方政权。1754年5月，艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼从赫拉特进军；塔巴斯长官阿里·穆拉德汗率军迎战，在一场血战中被杀，两座绿洲于6月至7月间陷落。1755年内沙布尔围城战后，杜兰尼军队又回师洗劫图恩和塔巴斯。1769—1770年艾哈迈德沙最后一次呼罗珊战役期间，塔巴斯的阿里·马尔丹汗率援军前往马什哈德，却在古纳巴德附近被击败并杀死。

en:
Kashan lies on the western edge of the Dasht-e Kavir, beneath the Karkas mountains, on the road from Qom to Isfahan. Settlement at nearby Tepe Sialk reaches back to the sixth millennium BC, but the walled town of history grew under the Buyids and Seljuks between the ninth and twelfth centuries, its houses of sun-dried brick and its fields watered by canals and qanats. It gave its name to the glazed tilework called kashi, and Yaqut al-Hamawi recorded its fine green-glazed bowls being exported to other lands and its people as all Twelver Shia, which earned the town the name Dar al-Muminin, 'abode of the faithful'. A Khwarazmshah army stormed it in 1197, and when Hulagu's Mongols reached it in the 1250s Kashan was partly spared, by one account through the intercession of Nasir al-Din al-Tusi. Ulugh Beg patronized it under the Timurids, and in 1444 Kashan was a quietly prosperous Shia weaving town, with silk already its fame, as Timurid power loosened around it.

After Timurid rule collapsed, Kashan passed through Qara Qoyunlu and Aq Qoyunlu hands before the Safavids took it soon after 1500. The sixteenth and seventeenth centuries were its golden age: Ismail I and Tahmasp I granted the town tax exemptions, and Abbas I made it a semi-royal residence, laid out the garden-palace of Fin and opened an official mint, while its gold-brocaded silks and velvet were exported to Europe and European travellers ranked its bazaars with those of London. As Shia orthodoxy tightened, the heterodox Nuqtavi circles were harshly suppressed. The Hotak Afghans overran the town in their 1722 invasion, and the eighteenth century brought Nader Shah's wars and Zand faction-fighting; the earthquake of 1778 levelled Kashan, Abbas I's buildings among them, and killed some 8,000 people. Rebuilt under the Zands and Qajars, with a fresh building boom under Fath Ali Shah, Kashan remained a textile centre well into the nineteenth century, though cheap European cloth was already eroding its workshops.
zh:
卡尚西临卡维尔盐漠、背靠卡尔卡斯山，地处库姆通往伊斯法罕的大道上。邻近的锡亚尔克台地公元前六千纪便有人类居住，但历史上城垣环绕的卡尚是9至12世纪白益王朝和塞尔柱时期发展起来的，土坯为屋，坎儿井与明渠浇灌田园。波斯语中的琉璃砖「卡希」便得名于卡尚，雅古特·哈马维也记载当地精美的绿釉碗外销各地、全城居民皆为十二伊玛目派什叶派，卡尚因此得到「信士之城」（Dar al-Muminin）的旧称。1197年，花剌子模的军队攻破此城；13世纪50年代旭烈兀的蒙古大军压境时，卡尚得以免遭大劫，一说有赖纳西尔丁·图西居间说情。帖木儿时期兀鲁伯曾予眷顾。1444年的卡尚是一座安静富庶的什叶派织城，丝绸已为它带来声名，而帖木儿的控制力正在四周瓦解。

帖木儿统治崩溃后，卡尚先后落入黑羊王朝与白羊王朝之手，1500年后不久并入萨法维版图。16至17世纪是它的黄金时代：伊斯玛仪一世和塔赫玛斯普一世赐予免税特权，阿拔斯一世把它建成半正式的驻跸之地，营造菲恩花园行宫，又开设官营铸币厂；金线锦缎、丝绸和天鹅绒远销欧洲，欧洲旅人把卡尚的巴扎与伦敦的市场相提并论。什叶派正统收紧之时，异端的努克塔维派遭到残酷镇压。1722年，阿富汗霍塔克人的入侵攻破此城，18世纪又经历纳迪尔沙阿的征战和赞德时期的党争；1778年的大地震将卡尚夷为平地，阿拔斯时代的建筑尽毁，约八千人罹难。城市在赞德和卡扎尔时期重建，法塔赫·阿里沙阿时掀起新的营建热潮。卡尚的纺织业一直维持到19世纪，只是廉价的欧洲布匹已在侵蚀这里的作坊。

en:
Tun was one of the two chief cities of medieval Quhistan, paired with Qa'en, on the desert road between central Iran and Mashhad. Its old walled city had five gates. Nasir Khusraw described Toon as a large city in the eleventh century, and Marco Polo joined it with Qa'en when naming the south Khorasan district. Mongol troops plundered and destroyed Tun in 1239, but the town recovered its place among Quhistan's main markets. In 1444 it was a Sunni Muslim city of the Timurid Empire, guarding the arid caravan route running from Yazd and Tabas toward Nishapur and Mashhad.

Uzbek tribes overran Khorasan in 1507, and after Nader Shah died in 1747 Tun was drawn into the Zangu'i Arab state based at Tabas. The town first fell to Ahmad Shah Durrani in early 1751 during his invasion of Afsharid Khorasan. In June or July 1754, after Ali Murad Khan's army was destroyed at Kakhk, Tun and Tabas submitted again. The following year, once Nishapur had fallen, Durrani troops turned back and sacked both oases.
zh:
图恩是中世纪古希斯坦两座首要城市之一，与加延并称，位于伊朗中部通往马什哈德的沙漠道路上。古城环有城墙，开有五座城门。11世纪，纳赛尔·霍斯鲁称图恩为大城；马可·波罗记载南呼罗珊时，也把图恩与加延并称。1239年蒙古军队洗劫并摧毁图恩，但此城后来恢复，仍是古希斯坦的主要市场之一。1444年，它是帖木儿帝国的逊尼派城市，扼守从亚兹德、塔巴斯通往内沙布尔和马什哈德的干旱商路。

1507年，乌兹别克诸部席卷呼罗珊。纳迪尔沙1747年死后，图恩被纳入以塔巴斯为基地的赞古伊阿拉伯人政权。1751年初，艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼入侵阿夫沙尔王朝治下的呼罗珊，图恩首次被其攻占。1754年6月至7月间，阿里·穆拉德汗的军队在卡赫克被歼后，图恩与塔巴斯再度投降。次年，内沙布尔陷落后，杜兰尼军队回师洗劫这两座绿洲。

en:
Saveh, the town shown here as Savah and often rendered Sava in Chinese sources, is an oasis settlement in Jibal, or Iraq-e Ajam, where roads from Ray divide toward Hamadan, Qazvin, Qom, Isfahan and Kashan. Under the Seljuks it was a prosperous walled town of Sunni Shafi'is, a winter station for rulers and atabegs; its Friday mosque preserves a brick minaret inscribed in 1110 or 1111. The Mongols burned its libraries and damaged its walls, Ilkhanid officials restored the walls and suburbs, and around 1320 the mosque received a great iwan. Timurid forces sacked the town again. In 1444 Saveh was a Sunni, Persian-speaking road town on the western edge of Shah Rukh's northern Iranian domains, administered around Ray by Sultan Muhammad ibn Baysunghur, valued for water, fields and highways rather than for a court.

After Shah Rukh died in 1447, Qara Qoyunlu, Aq Qoyunlu and Timurid armies overawed or disputed the crossroads for half a century. Safavid rule brought renewed patronage: in 1516 or 1517 the Friday mosque's old dome received a new tiled outer shell, and in 1539 or 1540 a builder from Qom completed the qibla iwan as Saveh was integrated into Twelver Shia Iran. In the summer of 1725 Afghan forces fought Tahmasp Mirza outside the city, then besieged and captured Saveh. Nader's defeat of the Hotaks later reopened the road to Isfahan, but the Qajar choice of Tehran as capital shifted political weight northward. By 1821 Saveh remained a well-watered road and market town, without the courtly importance it had known in Seljuk times.
zh:
萨瓦（中文资料常译萨韦）是吉巴勒、即阿贾姆伊拉克的一座绿洲城，雷伊来的道路在此分向哈马丹、加兹温、库姆、伊斯法罕和卡尚。塞尔柱时期，这里是沙斐仪派逊尼教徒居住的富庶城邑，也是统治者和阿塔贝格的冬季驻地；聚礼清真寺保存着刻于1110或1111年的砖造宣礼塔。蒙古人焚毁城中藏书并破坏城墙，伊儿汗时期官员修复城垣和城郊，约1320年清真寺又增建宏伟拱门。帖木儿军队后来再次洗劫城市。1444年的萨瓦是沙哈鲁北伊朗领地西缘一座逊尼派、说波斯语的道路城镇，由以雷伊为中心的苏丹·穆罕默德·伊本·拜宋豁儿统辖，其价值在水井、田野和大道，而不在宫廷。

1447年沙哈鲁死后，黑羊王朝、白羊王朝和帖木儿军队在此后半个世纪里不断威慑或争夺这些交叉道路。萨法维统治带来新的营建：1516或1517年，聚礼清真寺的旧穹顶加上饰有瓷砖的新外壳；1539或1540年，一位库米匠师又完成礼拜方向的拱门，萨瓦也被纳入十二伊玛目派的什叶派伊朗。1725年夏，阿富汗军队在城外与塔赫玛斯普·米尔扎交战，随后围攻并占领萨瓦。纳迪尔击败霍塔克王朝后，通往伊斯法罕的道路重新开放，但卡扎尔王朝选择德黑兰为都，使政治重心北移。到1821年前，萨瓦仍是水源充足的道路集镇，却已不再具有塞尔柱时代的宫廷重镇地位。

en:
Soltaniyeh stands on a high cold plain east of Zanjan, beside the older town of Abhar, on the road that joins Tabriz to central Iran. The Ilkhan Arghun used the meadow as a summer camp, and his son Öljaitü founded the city from 1302 and named it Soltaniyeh, celebrating its completion in 1313. He raised a wall 30,000 paces round and an octagonal mausoleum for himself, its brick dome nearly 25 metres across and about 50 metres high, meant to receive the bodies of Ali and Husayn until the ulama dissuaded him. Allama al-Hilli taught Shia doctrine in its Ghiyathiyya madrasa, while the city's silk, pearls and Indian goods traded as far as Venice. Decline set in after Abu Sa'id's death in 1335, and Timur's storm and Miran Shah's wrecking left it much reduced; Clavijo in 1404 found a populous city without walls and Öljaitü's tomb being demolished on Miran Shah's orders. In 1444 Soltaniyeh still belonged, nominally, to Shah Rukh's Timurid realm; three years later Jahan Shah of the Qara Qoyunlu seized it as the first prize of his conquest of Iran.

Venetian envoys of the late fifteenth century found only 6,000 or 7,000 people and little trade. Under the Safavids it lived on as a stage between Tabriz and the shahs' summer pastures, visited by Chardin among others, but the Ottoman–Safavid wars of Shah Abbas's age battered it further, and Nader Shah and the Zands had no use for the old capital. The Qajars brought it back to notice: it lay on the Tehran–Tabriz highway, where Tabriz was the seat of the crown prince, and Fath-Ali Shah spent sixteen summers there, reviewing troops and receiving envoys; in 1812 he began the Sepahr-e Barin palace on a mound north of town, built from stones of the ruined Ilkhanid city, as his headquarters in the war with Russia. The great dome itself, stripped and weathered, still stood over the empty plain.
zh:
苏丹尼耶位于赞詹以东高寒的平原上，毗邻更古老的阿卜哈尔城，地处大不里士通往伊朗中部的大道旁。伊儿汗阿鲁浑把这片草原辟为夏营地；其子完者都1302年起营建新城，取名「苏丹尼耶」，1313年大庆竣工。他筑起周长3万步的城墙，又为自己修建八角形陵墓，砖结构穹顶直径近25米、高约50米；他本想把阿里和侯赛因的遗骸迁来安葬，因宗教学者反对而作罢。阿拉玛·希里在城中的吉亚西耶经学院讲授什叶派教义，城市的丝绸、珍珠和印度货贸易远及威尼斯。1335年不赛因死后城市衰落，又经帖木儿攻破和米兰沙的拆毁；1404年克拉维约路过时，城市仍有人烟却已无城墙，完者都的陵墓正奉米兰沙之命遭人破坏。1444年的苏丹尼耶名义上仍属沙哈鲁的帖木儿帝国，三年后黑羊王朝的贾汉沙将它攻占，作为他征服伊朗的第一块战利品。

15世纪末的威尼斯使节见到居民只剩六七千人，商业萧条。萨法维时期它仍是大不里士通往国王夏牧场路上的重要停驻地，夏尔丹等人曾到访；阿拔斯时代的奥斯曼—萨法维战争进一步摧残了城市，纳迪尔沙和桑德王朝也无意经营这座旧都。卡扎尔时期它重新受到重视：它在德黑兰至大不里士的大道上，而大不里士是王储驻地，法塔赫-阿里沙有十六个夏天在此度过，阅兵、接见使节；1812年他下令在城北的高地上动工修建斯佩赫尔·巴林宫，石料取自伊儿汗故城的残垣，作为对俄战争的大本营。唯有那座剥蚀的巨大穹顶，依旧矗立在空旷的平原上。

en:
Rasht sits on the damp Caspian plain between the Goharrud and Zarjoub rivers, a day's ride from the lagoon port of Anzali. Arab records already call it Dar al-Marz, the 'abode of the border', in 682; the Hudud al-'Alam in 982 and Hamdallah Mustawfi in the fourteenth century describe a large village set in rain-forest, enriched by the raw silk of the mulberry country around it. West of the Sefid Rud the rain-soaked half of Gilan, Bia-pas, was ruled by the Eshaqvand, Shafi'i Sunni sayyids who held their court at Fuman and claimed descent from the Sasanians or from Isaac. Timur's cavalry never mastered these marshes. In 1444 the sayyids still governed Bia-pas in their own fashion, and Rasht on the plain was its market town, where Gilani merchants gathered the silk that went out by Anzali.

The Safavids first made Gilan their vassal, and Tahmasp I united its two halves under the Lahijan ruler Khan Ahmad Khan, but Shah Abbas ended the local dynasties outright in 1592; in 1595 he made Rasht the capital of Gilan and the seat of the raw-silk trade, where Persian, Armenian, Russian and Greek merchants flocked in, the open ditches were covered and the bazaar paved. Disaster crowded the next century: the Cossack Stenka Razin sacked the town in 1669, an earthquake levelled it in 1714, and Peter the Great's troops seized it in 1722, holding it until the Treaty of Resht returned it to Iran in 1732. Rasht was built again, and under the Qajars its caravan-loads of silk cocoons passed through Anzali to Russia; in 1808 it held some 3,000 households, six days' travel from Tehran.
zh:
拉什特坐落在潮湿的里海平原上，夹在戈哈拉德河与扎尔朱卜河之间，距潟湖港口安扎利只有一天路程。阿拉伯文献在682年已称它为「达尔·马尔兹」（边境之地）；982年的《世界境域志》和14世纪的哈姆杜拉·穆斯塔菲，都把它记为雨林中的一座大村庄，靠四乡桑园出产的生丝致富。萨菲德河以西湿润的半壁吉兰称「比阿普斯」，由奉逊尼派沙斐仪教法的伊沙克万德圣裔统治，他们在富曼建都，自称萨珊人或以撒的后裔，帖木儿的骑兵始终未能征服这片沼泽。1444年，圣裔们仍按自己的方式治理着比阿普斯，平原上的拉什特是它的市镇，吉兰商人在这里集散经安扎利外销的生丝。

萨法维王朝先使吉兰称臣，塔赫玛斯普一世又把东西两半交给拉希詹的统治者汗·艾哈迈德；阿拔斯一世最终在1592年彻底终结地方王朝，1595年将拉什特定为吉兰省会和生丝贸易中心，波斯、亚美尼亚、俄罗斯和希腊商人纷至沓来，露天沟渠被覆盖，市集铺了路面。灾祸挤满了下个世纪：哥萨克首领斯坚卡·拉辛1669年洗劫此城，1714年地震将它夷平，1722年彼得大帝的军队占领拉什特，直到1732年《拉什特条约》才把它归还伊朗。城市再度重建，卡扎尔时期，一驮驮蚕茧经安扎利运往俄罗斯；1808年全城约有3000户人家，到德黑兰要走六天路程。

en:
Astara lies where the Talysh mountains meet the Caspian, on the coastal road linking Gilan with Baku and the Caucasus. It is first named as Astarab in the Hudud al-'Alam of 982, and in the fourteenth century it became the seat of the Ispahbads of Gilan, a small Talysh principality whose old stronghold of Shandan stood north of the Astara river. The poet Qasim al-Anvar, writing in the early fifteenth century, called Astara the throne of the sipahbad Jalal al-Din Husayn, and in 1444 the local dynasty still held this wet, forested frontier between Ardabil and Shirvan.

From the sixteenth to the eighteenth century the Talysh khans of Astara ruled this coast, autonomous or nominally subject to the governors of Gilan and Ardabil. Stenka Razin's Cossack flotilla swept these waters in 1668–69, looting the ports between Baku and Rasht. The Talysh khanate that emerged after Nader Shah's death in 1747 first kept its capital at Astara, until Gara Khan moved his seat north to Lankaran. The khanate became a Russian protectorate in 1802, but Persian troops retook Lankaran in 1809; General Kotlyarevsky stormed its citadel on 1 January 1813, and the Treaty of Gulistan later that year fixed the new border on the Astara river, leaving the southern bank to Persia and splitting the town in two.
zh:
阿斯塔拉位于塔雷什山与里海相接之处，扼守吉兰通往巴库和高加索的沿海道路。982年成书的《世界境域志》已以「阿斯塔拉布」之名提到它；14世纪时，这里成为塔雷什人小王朝吉兰伊斯帕赫巴德的驻地，其旧堡尚丹就在阿斯塔拉河以北。15世纪初的诗人卡西姆·安瓦尔曾在诗中称阿斯塔拉为长官贾拉鲁丁·侯赛因的王座，1444年时，这个本地王朝仍在阿尔达比勒与希尔凡之间这片潮湿多林的边地上维持统治。

16到18世纪，阿斯塔拉的塔雷什诸汗统治这段海岸，或自行其政，或名义上臣服于吉兰、阿尔达比勒的长官。1668—1669年，斯捷潘·拉辛的哥萨克船队席卷这一带海域，洗劫巴库到拉什特之间的港口。1747年纳迪尔沙死后形成的塔雷什汗国最初以阿斯塔拉为都，加拉汗随即将都城北迁连科兰。汗国1802年成为俄罗斯的保护国，波斯军队1809年一度夺回连科兰；1813年1月1日科特利亚列夫斯基强攻拿下连科兰要塞，同年《古利斯坦条约》把新疆界划在阿斯塔拉河上，南岸留归波斯，城镇就此分成两半。

en:
Sari lies on the humid Caspian plain, where the northern forests run down from the Alborz to the sea. Near here stood Zadracarta, greatest city of Hyrcania, which some geographers place at Sari itself; its lemon and orange groves gave it the name Saru, the 'yellow city'. Rebuilt in the seventh century by the Dabuyid king Farrukhan the Great and named for his son Saruyeh, it became the capital of Tabaristan, a mountain land the Arab armies never subdued, where Alid sayyids took shelter from the caliphs and turned the people to Twelver Shiism. In 1359 the sayyid Mir-i Buzurg founded the Marashi dynasty, ruling from Sari, Amol and Vatashan, and Timur stormed the city in his campaign of 1392-93; the Zafar-nama says he burned it flat. In 1444 Sari was again one of the seats of the Shia Marashi sayyids, a town of fragrant gardens and busy bazaars on the road that climbed the Alborz to Rey.

The Marashis kept their mountain kingdom under Safavid suzerainty until 1596, when Shah Abbas I, half-Mazandarani through his mother from Behshahr, incorporated Mazandaran directly into his realm and exiled the sayyids to Shiraz, Kerman and India. He built Farahabad near Sari as a northern capital of palaces and gardens and planted Georgian, Circassian and Armenian colonies in the countryside, through which Pietro della Valle travelled in those years. Russian troops briefly held the coast in 1723 and handed it back in 1735, and after Nader Shah's death the province was torn by the wars of rival khans. On 21 March 1782 Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar, whose tribe had grown strong in these coastal forests, proclaimed Sari the capital of his new monarchy and had the city's goldsmiths fashion a crown, before moving his court to Tehran in 1786. Under Fath-Ali Shah it became a quiet provincial town and royal summer retreat on the verdant Caspian shore.
zh:
萨里坐落在湿润的里海平原上，北方的雨林从厄尔布尔士山直铺到海边。希腊人所说的希尔卡尼亚大城扎德拉卡尔塔就在这一带，有地理学家认为它就是萨里；柠檬和柑橘林使它得名萨鲁，意为「黄色之城」。7世纪，达布亚王朝的法鲁汉大帝重建此城，以儿子萨鲁耶之名命名，它由此成为塔巴里斯坦的都城——这片山地连阿拉伯大军都未曾征服，阿里派圣裔在此躲避哈里发，并把当地人引入十二伊玛目什叶派。1359年，圣裔米尔·布祖尔格建立马拉什王朝，以萨里、阿莫勒和瓦塔善三地为都；1392至1393年帖木儿东征时攻陷萨里，《帖木儿武功记》说他把全城烧成一片平地。1444年，萨里重又成为什叶派马拉什圣裔的治所之一，花园飘香、巴扎繁忙，城边就是翻越厄尔布尔士山通往雷伊的大道。

马拉什人在萨法维王朝宗主权下保住了山林王国，直到1596年——因母亲是贝赫沙赫尔人而算半个马赞德兰人的沙阿·阿拔斯一世——将马赞德兰直接并入版图，把马拉什圣裔流放至设拉子、克尔曼和印度。他在萨里附近营建法拉哈巴德，作为北方的离宫都城，又在乡间安置格鲁吉亚、切尔克斯和亚美尼亚移民，彼得罗·德拉·瓦莱那些年也曾游历此地。1723年俄国军队一度占据海岸，1735年将其归还波斯；纳迪尔沙死后，全省被各路汗王的混战撕扯。1782年3月21日，部族在这片沿海林地壮大的阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔宣布萨里为新王朝的首都，命城中金匠打造王冠，1786年才把宫廷迁往德黑兰。法特赫-阿里沙阿时代，它成为一座安静的省城，也是王室在青翠里海岸边的避暑之地。

en:
Malamir sits in a high basin of the Bakhtiari Zagros, three days’ climb through the mountains from Shushtar. Elamite kings and the later Elymaean princes cut their rock reliefs at Kul-e Farah and Eshkaft-e Salman above the valley, and the Islamic geographers knew the town as Idaj, the seat of the Hazaraspid atabegs of Greater Lur, whose citadel crowned the town and gave it its Luri name Mal al-Amir, ‘the amir’s estate’. When Ibn Battuta passed through in the fourteenth century it was still a royal city in the mountains. In 1444 it lay under the loose lordship of the Lur rulers of the Zagros, overshadowed by the Bakhtiari clans, the Astarki, Janaki and their kin, whose first arrival in the valleys is recorded in 1413. Local memory held that when atabak rule ended in 1453 the townspeople abandoned the crumbling houses for tents and flocks.

The Safavids made Greater Lur into Bakhtiari country: in 1566 Shah Tahmasp named the Astarki chief Tajmir first ilkhan of the Bakhtiyari, and his successor Jahangir Khan divided the tribes into the Haft Lang and Chahar Lang, the two confederations that shaped all their later history. The plain of ruined Malamir became winter pasture, its wool worked into Bakhtiari carpets and felt, and chieftains were buried at Shahsavar beneath carved stone lions. Nader Shah marched repeatedly against the rebel Ali Murad Khan, executed him and deported Chahar Lang clansmen to Khorasan; they distinguished themselves before Kandahar and returned to the Zagros after his murder in 1747. In 1750-52 Ali Mardan Khan Bakhtiari contended with Karim Khan Zand for the mastery of western Iran, and when Karim Khan prevailed in 1764 he disarmed the tribes and transplanted thousands of Haft Lang families to Qom and Varamin. Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar harried them again in 1785, yet the Qajar government never fully subdued the Bakhtiari pastures around Malamir.
zh:
马拉米尔位于巴赫蒂亚尔扎格罗斯群山中的一处高盆，从舒什塔尔出发要在大山里攀行三天。古代埃兰国王和后来的埃利迈斯王公曾在谷口的库勒法拉赫与埃什卡夫特萨勒曼凿下岩刻；伊斯兰地理学家把这座城称作伊达季，它是大洛雷斯坦哈扎尔阿思普阿塔贝格的都城，城堡高踞城上，卢尔语名字「马拉米尔」意为「埃米尔的庄园」。14世纪伊本·白图泰路过时，它仍是群山之中的王都。1444年，它只在扎格罗斯卢尔诸王的松散治下，声势已被1413年起陆续迁入的阿斯塔基、贾纳基等巴赫蒂亚尔氏族盖过。当地人记得，1453年阿塔贝格统治彻底终结后，居民抛下倾颓的屋舍，住进帐篷、放牧畜群。

萨法维王朝把大洛雷斯坦变成了巴赫蒂亚尔人的土地：1566年塔赫玛斯普一世任命阿斯塔基部首领塔季米尔为巴赫蒂亚尔第一位伊尔汗，继任者贾汉吉尔汗把诸部编为哈夫特朗与查哈朗两大联盟，此后数百年的部落史都围绕它们展开。马拉米尔荒城周围的平原成了冬牧场，出产的羊毛织成巴赫蒂亚尔地毯和毛毡，首领们葬在沙赫萨瓦尔，墓前立着雕凿的石狮。纳迪尔沙屡次征讨反叛的阿里穆拉德汗，将其处死，把查哈朗部众流放呼罗珊；他们在坎大哈攻城战中立功，直到1747年纳迪尔沙遇刺后才重返扎格罗斯。1750至1752年，巴赫蒂亚尔首领阿里马尔丹汗与卡利姆汗·桑德争夺西伊朗的霸权；1764年卡利姆汗取胜，解除部落武装，把数千户哈夫特朗人迁往库姆和瓦拉明。1785年阿迦·穆罕默德·卡扎尔再度攻掠，但终卡扎尔一朝，马拉米尔周围的巴赫蒂亚尔牧场也没有真正归顺。

en:
Termez commands one of the chief crossings of the Amu Darya, on the road between Bukhara, Samarkand, Balkh and northern India. The old city had been a Buddhist and then an Islamic scholarly centre, home to the tradition of al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, but Mongol troops destroyed it in 1220; the fourteenth-century town rose a short distance from the river, with canals, bazaars, grapes, quinces, meat and milk. Under Timur and Shah Rukh its sayyid families and river crossing made it one of the four leading cities of Mawarannahr listed by Hafiz-i Abru. In 1444 it belonged to the Timurids, and the shrine of al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi was being enlarged under Timurid patronage.

In 1449 Ulugh Beg gathered troops near Termez before marching on Balkh against his rebel son Abd al-Latif. After the death of Abu Sa'id the city passed to Sultan Mahmud's appanage, governed through the local sayyid Husayn Akbar. Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks took Termez in 1506 and appointed Sayyid Muhammad Sultan as governor. In the 1530s it was attached to the Balkh appanage, where Tursun Muhammad Sultan later allied himself with the Mughal ruler Humayun. Abdullah Khan II besieged and captured the city in 1571-72 after Padishah Muhammad Sultan refused to submit, then installed Mahmud Sultan. Termez remained a regional centre under the Ashtarkhanids and produced the seventeenth-century historian Khoja Samandar Termezi, though by the later eighteenth century the ancient site had shrunk to the villages of Salavat and Pattakesar.
zh:
铁尔梅兹扼守阿姆河要渡，位于布哈拉、撒马尔罕、巴尔赫与北印度道路之间。古城曾是佛教中心，后来成为伊斯兰学术名城，哈基姆·提尔米兹的学术传统便出于此；1220年蒙古军摧毁城市，14世纪的新城在离河不远处重建，水渠纵横、市肆相连，盛产葡萄、榅桲、肉食和乳品。在帖木儿与沙哈鲁时代，本地赛义德家族和河渡使它成为哈菲兹·阿布鲁所列河中四大名城之一。1444年，铁尔梅兹属于帖木儿帝国，哈基姆·提尔米兹圣陵也在帖木儿王朝资助下扩建。

1449年，乌鲁伯格在铁尔梅兹附近集结军队，随后进军巴尔赫，讨伐反叛的儿子阿卜杜勒·拉蒂夫。阿布·赛义德死后，这里成为苏丹·马哈茂德封地的一部分，由本地赛义德·侯赛因·阿克巴尔治理。穆罕默德·昔班尼的乌兹别克军队1506年夺取铁尔梅兹，任命赛义德·穆罕默德苏丹为长官。1530年代，它被划入巴尔赫封地，图尔松·穆罕默德苏丹后来与莫卧儿君主胡马雍结盟。1571—1572年，帕迪沙·穆罕默德苏丹拒绝臣服，阿卜杜拉汗二世围城攻取，随后任命马哈茂德苏丹镇守。阿斯特拉罕王朝时期，铁尔梅兹仍是区域中心，17世纪史学家和卓·萨曼达尔·捷尔梅兹便出生于此；但到18世纪后期，古城已经衰落，只剩萨拉瓦特和帕塔凯萨尔等村落环绕着遗址。

en:
Kish is the medieval Kesh, the Kashkadarya valley district whose chief town became Shahrisabz. From the late thirteenth century the pastures and walled towns belonged to the Barlas tribe, and Timur was born in 1336 at Khoja-Ilgar on the city's outskirts. After choosing Samarkand as his capital, he made his birthplace a favoured second residence: work on the tiled Ak-Saray palace began in 1380 and continued for twenty-four years. In 1437-38 Ulugh Beg added the Kok Gumbaz mosque and the adjoining House of Meditation. In 1444 Kish remained in the Timurid realm ruled from Samarkand, its Barlas amirs, flocks and wool trade overshadowed but not displaced by the capital.

The succession struggles that followed Shah Rukh's later years weakened the Timurid hold on the southern districts. Abdullah Khan II of Bukhara took Kish in 1556 and attached it to the new Karshi province; by that time the town was again girdled with strong walls and served as the centre of the Shahrisabz district within the Bukharan khanate. In the mid-eighteenth century the Uzbek Kenagas tribe turned the district into a semi-independent beylik. The Manghit dynasty took power in Bukhara in 1785, but the highland lords around Shahrisabz and Kitab kept much of their autonomy, governing from walled towns, caravanserais and the eighteenth-century bazaar beneath the surviving pylons of Ak-Saray.
zh:
基希即中世纪的谒石，是卡什卡河谷地的一部分，其重镇后来称沙赫里萨布兹。13世纪后期起，这里的牧场和城邑归巴鲁剌思部控制，帖木儿1336年出生在城郊的霍贾伊尔加尔。帖木儿选定撒马尔罕为都后，仍把出生地作为重要的第二居所：贴有彩釉瓷砖的阿克萨赖宫1380年动工，营建持续了二十四年。1437—1438年，乌鲁伯格又增建库克贡巴兹清真寺和相邻的「沉思之屋」。1444年，基希仍属以撒马尔罕为中心的帖木儿王朝；巴鲁剌思异密、羊群和羊毛贸易虽被都城的光芒盖过，却依旧支撑着此地。

沙哈鲁晚年之后的继承战争削弱了帖木儿王朝对南部地区的控制。布哈拉的阿卜杜拉汗二世1556年攻取基希，把它并入新设的卡尔希省；当时城市再次筑起坚固城墙，也是布哈拉汗国沙赫里萨布兹地区的中心。18世纪中叶，乌兹别克克纳加斯部把这一地区变成半独立的伯克领地。曼吉特王朝1785年取得布哈拉政权后，沙赫里萨布兹和基塔布一带的山地首领仍保有很大自治权；他们凭借城寨、商队驿站和18世纪的巴扎治理地方，阿克萨赖宫残存的巨柱则俯瞰着这一切。

en: Saidabad, the later name of Sirjan, lies on a high plain west of Kerman where the Kerman-Shiraz road meets tracks toward the Persian Gulf. Early Islamic geographers knew Sirgan as one of the chief cities of Kerman, watered by qanats and enclosed by walls with eight gates and two bazaars; they also noted its sugar, fruit, wealthy houses and busy trade. The old stronghold of Sang Castle went back to Sasanian times, and an inscription there dated 789 AH, or 1387, names the Muzaffarid ruler Imad al-Din Ahmad only a few years before the Timurids absorbed Kerman. In 1444 the district was therefore a Persian-speaking Timurid frontier land, its flocks, wool and caravan traffic linking the Kerman plateau with Fars and the Gulf. The medieval town later shifted sites three times, and Qajar-period settlement at Saidabad became the nucleus of modern Sirjan, where a new bazaar served the revived road trade.
zh: 赛伊达巴德是锡尔詹的旧称，位于克尔曼以西的高原，克尔曼通往设拉子的道路与通向波斯湾的小道在此相接。早期伊斯兰地理学家把锡尔甘视为克尔曼最重要的城市之一：坎儿井供水，城墙环绕，有八座城门和两座巴扎，还出产蔗糖和水果，富商宅邸与贸易往来闻名。古老的石堡可追溯到萨珊时期；堡中一方纪年为回历789年、即1387年的铭文提到穆扎法尔王朝统治者伊马德丁·艾哈迈德，几年后克尔曼便被帖木儿王朝吞并。1444年，这片地区是帖木儿王朝治下说波斯语的边疆地带，羊群、羊毛和商旅交通把克尔曼高原同法尔斯和波斯湾连接起来。中世纪城址后来三次迁移；卡扎尔时期，赛伊达巴德的定居点成为后来锡尔詹城的核心，一座新的巴扎也为复兴的道路贸易服务。

en:
Ifugao is the steep heart of the Cordillera, where rivers cut south through folded mountains toward the Magat and lowlanders rarely ventured. Its name means 'people of the hill', and from about 1200 the Ifugao farmed these slopes around villages such as Kiyyangan, growing taro, trading gold and beeswax down to the plains, and following wealthy kadangyan clans rather than kings; they set wooden bulol guardians in their granaries and chanted the hudhud epics at their feasts. In 1444 no foreign power had entered these mountains, and the Ifugao answered to no state.

The Spaniards who subjugated the coasts of Luzon found the Cordillera a harder country. Expeditions pushed up the Magat valley between 1591 and 1594 and brought back the first descriptions of the Ygolote highlanders, and the fall of the lowlands drove the Ifugao deeper into the range: between 1600 and 1700 they abandoned taro for wet rice and carved the great terraced mountainsides that still bear their name, fortifying both their fields and their independence. Punitive columns in the 1770s and 1790s tried to force highlanders into reduccion villages while forts watched the Magat below, yet in 1821 the terraces and the people who built them remained unconquered.
zh:
伊富高是中科迪勒拉山最险峻的腹地，河谷向南穿过层叠群山通向马加特河，低地人极少涉足。族名意为「山上之民」。约自1200年起，伊富高人在基扬甘等村落周围的坡地上种植芋薯，把黄金和蜂蜡运到平原交易；他们没有国王，由富有的卡丹阳氏族统领，谷仓里供着木雕的布洛尔守护神，宴会上传唱胡德胡德史诗。1444年，还没有外来政权进入这些大山，伊富高人不属于任何国家。

征服吕宋海岸的西班牙人发现，中科迪勒拉是一块更难啃的土地。1591至1594年间，远征队沿马加特河谷上行，首次留下了对「伊戈洛特」山民的记载；低地的失陷反而把伊富高人更深地赶入山区——1600至1700年间，他们弃芋种稻，在山坡上凿出后来以他们之名闻名的大片梯田，既守住了稻田，也守住了独立。1770和1790年代，西班牙又派出讨伐队，企图把山民强行迁入归并村，并在下游的马加特河畔筑堡监视，但直到1821年，这些梯田和修筑它们的人仍未被征服。

en:
The shores of Laguna de Bay, the great freshwater lake southeast of Manila Bay, were Tagalog rice country dotted with barangays — Bay, Pila and Lumbang, said to have lain within the domain of the chief Gat Pangil. The Laguna Copperplate of 900, the oldest surviving document in the Philippines, records a debtor acquitted before Jayadewa, Lord of Pailah, in this same district. Boats carrying rice crossed the lake and went down the Pasig to the markets of Tondo. In 1444 the lakeshore datus stood within the orbit of the lakan of Tondo.

Juan de Salcedo overran the district in 1571 with a hundred soldiers, and Martín de Goiti received its people as one of the largest early encomiendas, some 8,000 tribute-payers. Franciscans led by Juan de Plasencia began the baptizing in 1578, and from 1580 Bay, Majayjay, Pila, Lumban and Pagsanjan were laid out as parish towns, with Bay the first provincial capital. Chinese rebels of the 1603 Sangley rising were run to ground in the San Pablo highlands, and a second Chinese revolt held the hills above Cavinti and Lumban in 1639 before surrendering at Pagsanjan the next year. Bay kept the provincial seat until 1688, when it moved to Pagsanjan. During the British occupation of Manila, Thomas Backhouse's raiders sacked Pagsanjan hunting for galleon silver, but Francisco de San Juan carried the treasure to Simón de Anda in Pampanga.
zh:
内湖湾是马尼拉湾东南的大淡水湖，沿岸是他加禄人的稻米之乡，巴彦、皮拉、隆邦等巴朗盖散布其间，相传都在首领加特·邦吉尔的势力范围内。900年的「拉古纳铜版铭文」是菲律宾现存最古的文字，记载一名债务人在当地领主阇耶提婆面前偿清债务，地点就在这一带。载米的小船穿过湖泊、沿巴石河下行，运往汤都的市场。1444年，湖岸诸达图都处在汤都拉干的势力圈内。

1571年，胡安·德·萨尔塞多率百名士兵征服此地，马丁·德·戈伊蒂获封当地，约八千名纳贡者，是早期最大的监护征赋区之一。1578年，胡安·德·普拉森西亚率领方济各会士开始传教，1580年起巴彦、马海海、皮拉、隆班、百胜滩相继建成堂区城镇，巴彦为首任府治。1603年华人生理人起事，暴动者被追剿至圣巴勃罗山区；1639年又一次华人起事，在卡文蒂和隆班一带的高地据守，次年在百胜滩投降。巴彦的府治地位保持到1688年，之后迁往百胜滩。英军占领马尼拉期间，托马斯·巴克豪斯的部队洗劫百胜滩、搜求大帆船白银，弗朗西斯科·德·圣胡安却把财宝安全送往邦板牙的西蒙·德·安达军中。

en:
Mindoro was the Mait or Ma-i of Chinese records, named in the Song annals in 972 and described in Zhao Rugua's Zhu Fan Zhi of 1225 as a land whose people traded beeswax, cotton, pearls and tortoiseshell for porcelain and iron; Chinese accounts even credited its rulers with Buddhism. Mangyan clans farmed the interior, while the southern anchorages of Mangarin and Caminawit drew junks and Malay traders. By 1444 Muslim settlers linked to Brunei and Maynila held stretches of its coasts, the island of Lubang to the north paid tribute to Rajah Sulayman, and the Mangyan kept to the highlands.

Spaniards first explored the island in 1570 and, finding gold, named it Mina de Oro, later compressed into Mindoro; in 1572 Juan de Salcedo sailed its west coast and burned the Moro village on Lubang. Legazpi and Felipe de Salcedo took the coastal villages as encomiendas, but war and slaving emptied much of the island, refugees fleeing to Batangas. In 1602 Moro fleets sacked its Spanish towns and built a fort at Mamburao. Iranun raiders returned in force in 1757 with 74 prahus and carried islanders off to the slave market of Jolo, until a Spanish expedition of 1,200 men destroyed the Mamburao fort in 1766. Caminawit became the seat of the southern presidencia later in the century.
zh:
民都洛在中国载籍中称麻逸（Mait），《宋史》在972年已记其国，1225年赵汝适的《诸蕃志》详述其民以蜂蜡、棉布、珍珠、玳瑁交换瓷器和铁器，中国记载还认为其地可能崇奉佛教。芒扬人诸部在内地农耕，南部的曼加林、卡米纳维特锚地则吸引着中国帆船和马来商人。到1444年，与文莱和马尼拉有联系的穆斯林居民已占据沿海多处，北方的卢邦岛向拉惹·苏莱曼纳贡，芒扬人则退居山地。

1570年西班牙人首次探查此岛，因发现黄金而称之为Mina de Oro（金矿），后缩读为民都洛；1572年胡安·德·萨尔塞多沿西岸航行，焚毁卢邦岛上的摩洛聚落。莱加斯皮与费利佩·德·萨尔塞多把沿岸村落封作监护征赋区，但战乱与掳掠使岛上大半人口流失，难民纷纷逃往八打雁。1602年，摩洛舰队洗劫西班牙人城镇，并在曼布劳修筑堡垒。1757年伊拉农人集结七十四艘快船大举重来，把岛民掳往霍洛的奴隶市场，直到1766年一支一千二百人的西班牙远征军摧毁了曼布劳堡垒。该世纪后期，卡米纳维特成为南部行政长官的驻所。

en:
Buglas was the old Hiligaynon name of Negros, the long island across the Tañon Strait from Cebu. Ata foragers ranged its interior mountains, while Visayan fishing villages — Binalbagan, Ilog and the anchorage that became Silay — lined its coasts; the western shore stood under the nominal sway of the Kedatuan of Madja-as in Panay, and the east looked to the rajahs of Cebu. In 1444 the islanders sailed the Visayan seas in big outrigger boats and kept their old Visayan rites.

Legazpi's men reached the island in April 1565 and, seeing the dark-skinned Ata, named it Negros. The Carobcob settlement that became Silay was granted as an encomienda in January 1571, and Binalbagan and Ilog became towns in 1573 and 1584. Negros was governed from Oton in Panay until 1734, when it became a military district with Ilog as its capital, later moved to Himamaylan. Moro slave-raiders harried the coasts from the late 1500s, and in 1760 the people of Silay abandoned their shore village and rebuilt it behind a palisade between the Matagoy and Panaogao rivers. By 1818 the island counted 200 Spanish-Filipino families, and Silay alone was a flourishing town of more than 200 houses.
zh:
布格拉斯是米沙鄢语对内格罗斯岛的旧称，这座长形大岛与宿务隔着塔尼翁海峡相望。阿塔人在中部山地游猎，比纳巴干、伊洛格以及日后成为锡莱的锚地等米沙鄢渔村沿海岸散布；西岸在名义上臣属班乃岛的马加斯（Madja-as），东岸则受宿务诸位拉惹影响。1444年，岛民驾着大型舷外支架船往来于米沙鄢诸海之间，奉行米沙鄢旧俗。

1565年4月，莱加斯皮的部下抵达此岛，因见到肤色黝黑的阿塔人而称之为内格罗斯。日后发展为锡莱的卡罗布科布聚落于1571年1月被封作监护征赋区，比纳巴干和伊洛格则先后于1573年和1584年设镇。内格罗斯长期由班乃的奥通管辖，1734年成为军区，以伊洛格为首府，后来迁往希马马兰。16世纪末叶起，摩洛掳奴船队不断袭扰海岸，1760年锡莱居民放弃海边旧村，在马塔戈伊河与帕纳奥高河之间筑起木栅重建家园。到1818年，全岛已有二百个西班牙—菲裔家庭，锡莱一镇便是二百余栋房屋的繁华聚落。

en:
Cebu, Sugbu to its Visayan people, is a long narrow island at the centre of the archipelago, whose east coast in the 1440s held a straggling seaside port of some three hundred houses grouped around the rajah's palace and an open square. Chinese junks had traded there since the Zhufan Zhi of 1225 recorded the kingdom as Suwu, and merchants from Java, Sumatra, Siam and China bartered porcelain and silk for gold, tortoiseshell, beeswax, cotton and sea produce; Sugbu's harbour was already known as 'the place for trading'. Its rulers bore Sanskrit titles and held their seat at Singhapala, 'lion city', and Visayan legend traced the dynasty to Sri Lumay, a half-Tamil prince from Sumatra. In 1444 the island remained an Indianized rajahnate of datus and rival chiefs grown rich on its harbour.

Magellan's ships entered the port on 7 April 1521; Rajah Humabon welcomed them and was baptized, but on 27 April the explorer was killed fighting Lapulapu on Mactan, and the fleet sailed on. On 27 April 1565 Legazpi returned in force, scattered the native proas with his guns and landed, and on 8 May raised the fort that became Fort San Pedro; in a burning house a soldier found the Sto. Nino image Magellan had given Humabon's queen in 1521, and a church was later built over the spot. Rajah Tupas made his peace, and the Spanish town of San Miguel, the first permanent Spanish settlement in the islands, became the seat of their new colony; on 1 January 1571 Legazpi renamed it Villa del Santisimo Nombre de Jesus, shortly before the government followed him north to Manila. Cebu remained the chief Spanish town of the Visayas, its Chinese Parian and the diocese erected there making it the centre of the southern islands.
zh:
宿务，米沙鄢人称作苏格布（Sugbu），是群岛中央一座狭长的岛屿；1440年代，其东岸有一座沿海绵延数公里的港市，约三百户人家围绕拉者的宫殿和广场而居。早在1225年的《诸蕃志》中，中国商船就把这个王国记作束务，来自爪哇、苏门答腊、暹罗和中国的商人以瓷器、丝绸换取黄金、玳瑁、蜂蜡、棉布和海产，苏格布港当时已有「交易之地」之称。统治者使用梵语头衔，王都设在辛格帕拉（Singhapala，意为「狮城」）；米沙鄢传说把王朝始祖认作来自苏门答腊的半泰米尔王子斯里·卢迈（Sri Lumay）。1444年的宿务仍是一个印度化的拉让国，诸达图与各部首领靠着这座港口致富争雄。

1521年4月7日，麦哲伦的船队驶入宿务港，拉者·胡玛邦出面欢迎并接受洗礼，但4月27日麦哲伦就在马克坦岛与拉普拉普的交战中被杀，船队继续西行。1565年4月27日，莱加斯皮率大军重返，用火炮驱散土著战船后登陆，5月8日建起要塞，即后来的圣佩德罗堡；一名士兵在一间着火的房屋里发现了1521年麦哲伦赠予胡玛邦王后的圣婴像，后来在发现之地建起了圣婴教堂。拉者·图帕斯与西班牙人议和，圣米格尔成为群岛上第一个永久西班牙人定居点和新殖民地的首府；1571年1月1日，莱加斯皮将其改名为「圣名耶稣镇」（Villa del Santisimo Nombre de Jesus），不久政权便随他北迁马尼拉。此后宿务仍是西班牙人在米沙鄢的首要城镇，当地的华人街区「涧内」和在此设立的主教区，使它成为南方诸岛的中心。

en:
Leyte lies between Samar and Mindanao, its eastern shore opening on Leyte Gulf and its western valleys shelving to the Camotes Sea. The Spaniards who came in the 1500s found the island called Tandaya, its Warays and other Visayans living in datu settlements such as Carigara and Mairete, once ruled by lords like Datu Ete, and sharing the anito rites of the rest of the Visayas: farmers of rice and millet on the coastal flats, fishermen, boat-builders and traders along its sheltered gulfs. In 1444 there was no kingdom on Leyte and no foreign flag, only rival datus, their balangay crews, and the island traffic south to Mindanao and north to Luzon.

It was off little Limasawa, south of Leyte, that Magellan's fleet made its real Philippine landfall: on 28 March 1521 its men met Rajah Kolambu, and on Easter Sunday, 31 March, Father Valderrama said the first mass in the islands at Mazaua, after which Kolambu piloted them to Cebu. In 1543 Ruy López de Villalobos gave Leyte and Samar the name Las Islas Filipinas, in honour of the prince who became Philip II. In 1565 the datu Bankaw welcomed Legazpi at Carigara with a blood pact and baptism, but in 1621 the old convert turned again to the old gods, raising a diwata temple and six towns with his son Pagali, a babaylan priest; Juan de Alcarazo sailed from Cebu with forty ships, burned the temple and stamped out the revolt in 1622, setting Bankaw's head on a stake. Jesuits had opened a mission at Carigara in 1595, with Palo, Ormoc and Alangalang following, yet Spanish rule stayed light: in 1735 Leyte and Samar were detached from Cebu as a single province with Carigara as capital, and after the two split in 1768, the 1818 census counted only fifty-six Spanish families among more than sixteen thousand native households.
zh:
莱特位于萨马与棉兰老之间，东岸敞开为莱特湾，西部山谷缓斜入卡莫特斯海。16世纪到来的西班牙人发现这里叫坦达亚，瓦瑞人和其他米沙鄢人住在卡里加拉、迈雷特等达图聚落中，曾由埃特这样的首领统治，奉行整个米沙鄢共同的阿尼托祭祀：沿海平原种稻粟，避风海湾里是渔民、船匠和往来商人。1444年的莱特上既无王国，也无外邦旗帜，只有相互争雄的达图、他们的巴朗盖船队，以及南往棉兰老、北通吕宋的岛际航路。

麦哲伦船队真正在菲律宾落脚的地点，是莱特南边的小岛利马萨瓦：1521年3月28日，船员在此会见拉惹科兰布，3月31日复活节，巴尔德拉马神父在马萨瓦主持菲律宾第一场弥撒，随后由科兰布领航前往宿务。1543年，鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·维拉洛沃斯把莱特和萨马命名为「菲律宾群岛」，以纪念后来成为腓力二世的王子。1565年，达图班考在卡里加拉歃血欢迎黎牙实比并受洗；但到1621年，这位老基督徒重奉旧神，与任巫师的儿子帕加利筑起迪瓦塔神庙，煽动六座城镇起事。胡安·德·阿尔卡拉索率四十艘船从宿务赶来，烧毁神庙，于1622年平定叛乱，班考的头颅被悬于竹竿示众。耶稣会早在1595年就在卡里加拉开教，帕洛、奥尔莫克、阿兰加兰相继设堂，但西班牙人的统治始终稀薄：1735年莱特与萨马从宿务分出合为一省，以卡里加拉为首府；1768年两省分置后，1818年的普查在一万六千余户本地人之外，只数出五十六户西班牙裔家庭。

en:
Zamboanga guards the western tip of Mindanao, where the peninsula ends in a fine roadstead facing Basilan and the Sulu Sea. Its Sinama name, Samboangan, means a mooring place, and it was the country of the Subanen, who had farmed its river valleys since the twelfth century and kept to their ancient spirits, while Sama and Yakan boat-people held the islands offshore. By the 1400s the Islamised Tausug of Sulu, soon to found their sultanate, were the rising sea power of these straits and claimed suzerainty over the coast; in 1444 Zamboanga was still more anchorage than town, a place where raiders and traders from Mindanao, Sulu and Borneo took wood and water.

Spaniards first used the roadstead at La Caldera in 1569, but the post was withdrawn to Cebu in 1599. On 23 June 1635, at the Jesuits' urging, Captain Juan de Chaves landed with three hundred Spaniards and a thousand Visayans, and Father Melchor de Vera laid the cornerstone of Fort San José, marking the founding of the city; Mexican reinforcements followed in 1636 and 1654, and out of the camp's mixed tongues grew the Spanish creole Chavacano. The Dutch attacked the fort in 1646, and in 1662 the garrison was recalled to Manila against Koxinga, leaving only the Jesuits, who rebuilt the ruined fort in 1669. The crown returned in force in 1718–1719, when Juan Sicarra raised the present Fort Pilar, named for Our Lady of the Pillar, and in 1720 King Dalasi of Bulig stormed it with three thousand Moro raiders and was beaten off. A British bombardment in January 1798 was likewise repulsed, and the census of 1818 counted 8,640 people in the province; in 1821 the fortress was commanded for a year by Juan Fermín de San Martín, the Uruguayan elder brother of the liberator José de San Martín.
zh:
三宝颜扼守棉兰老西端，半岛尽头是一座正对巴西兰和苏禄海的优良锚地。其萨马语原名Samboangan意为「抛锚之地」，这里本是苏巴农人的乡土：他们自12世纪起在河谷耕作，恪守古老的祖灵信仰；雅坎等萨马系船民则居于外海岛屿。到15世纪，已经伊斯兰化的苏禄陶苏格人成为这片海峡正在崛起的海上强权，行将建国，并向三宝颜海岸索取宗主权。1444年的三宝颜还只是个锚地而非城镇，棉兰老、苏禄和婆罗洲的劫掠者与商人在此取水采木。

1569年西班牙人首次在拉卡尔德拉启用这处锚地，但1599年据点撤回宿务。1635年6月23日，应耶稣会之请，胡安·德·查韦斯上尉率三百名西班牙人和一千名米沙鄢人登陆，梅尔乔·德·贝拉神父为圣何塞堡奠基，三宝颜城就此诞生；1636和1654年两批墨西哥援军抵达，营中诸语混杂，逐渐生出西班牙克里奥尔语——查瓦卡诺语。荷兰人1646年来攻，1662年驻军为对付国姓爷被召回马尼拉，只留下耶稣会士，他们于1669年把被毁的要塞重新筑好。1718至1719年王室大举返回，胡安·西卡拉建起今日的皮拉尔堡，奉皮拉尔圣母为名；1720年，布利格王达拉西率三千摩洛劫掠者猛攻不克。1798年1月英国舰队的炮击同样被击退；1818年普查全省有8,640人；1821年，这座要塞由乌拉圭人胡安·费尔明·德·圣马丁——解放者何塞·德·圣马丁之兄——出任了一年司令官。

en:
Caraga is the rain-drenched eastern shoulder of Mindanao, a coast of river mouths and offshore islands facing the Pacific. Its people were the Kalagan, 'the spirited ones' in their own tongue, animists of the anito cult who lived in datu-led villages called banwa, fishing the shore and farming rice, abaca and coconut. In 1444 their chiefs ruled unchallenged, though the coast was already drawn into the commerce and wars of nearby Butuan, whose balangay fleets and goldsmiths traded with China and Champa and whose wealth drew raiding fleets from Ternate in the Moluccas.

In 1521 Antonio Pigafetta, sailing with Magellan, met the tattooed and gold-adorned Rajah Siawi of the Surigaonon and recorded these shores as 'Calagan'. Ruy López de Villalobos sailed against Surigao in 1543 but was fought off, and Spanish arms made no impression until an expedition took Tandag in 1609 and organised the district of Caraga. Recollect friars opened the permanent mission at Tandag in 1622 and named the land provincia de gente animosa, the province of spirited folk. Companies of soldiers sent from Mexico in 1635, 1670 and 1672 secured the coast, and the census of 1818 counted 2,475 native families and 25 Spanish households in Surigao.
zh:
卡拉加是棉兰老岛雨水丰沛的东翼，海岸河口纵横、岛礁散布，面向太平洋。住在这里的是卡拉甘人——族名在本族语言里意为「有胆气的人」。他们信奉阿尼托（anito）泛灵信仰，住在达图统领的村社（banwa）里，沿海捕鱼，在内地种植稻、蕉麻和椰子。1444年，酋长们仍是这片海岸无可争议的主人，但此地已被卷入西邻武端的商路与战事：武端的巴兰盖（balangay）船队和金匠与中国、占城通商，它的富庶也招来摩鹿加特尔纳特的渡海袭掠。

1521年，随麦哲伦航行的皮加费塔见到文身披金的苏里高人拉惹·西亚威，把这一带记作「卡拉甘」。1543年鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·比利亚洛沃斯来攻苏里高，被当地人击退；西班牙人的武力长期无所作为，直到1609年远征军拿下坦达格，设立卡拉加区。1622年重整奥斯定会传教士在坦达格开设常驻传教站，并把这里命名为 provincia de gente animosa，意为「勇者之地」。1635、1670和1672年，墨西哥派来的成批士兵驻防海岸；1818年的户口册载，苏里高有2,475户本地家庭和25户西班牙家庭。

en:
Taytay guards the northern neck of Palawan, where Malampaya Sound opens between the South China and Sulu seas. Chinese records of the thirteenth century counted these islands among Sandao, the vassals of the trading polity of Ma-i on Mindoro. Before the Spaniards came Taytay was the seat of a small kingdom whose king, the Italian chronicler Antonio Pigafetta later heard, was attended wherever he went by ten scribes. Its people fished the sound, farmed along its shores, and kept the animist rites of anito; in 1444 they answered to their own king.

In 1521 the survivors of Ferdinand Magellan's expedition, fleeing his death at Mactan, put in at Taytay and held the king and his queen for ransom of food before sailing on to the Moluccas. Spanish rule came a century later, when the town was formally founded in 1623 and entrusted to Augustinian Recollect missionaries. They began the stone fortress of Fuerza de Santa Isabel in 1667, but its walls were completed only in 1738; its guns covered the anchorage against the fleets of Moro raiders from the Sulu archipelago, who repeatedly struck the settlements of northern Palawan. In 1818 Taytay became capital of the province of Calamianes, covering all of Paragua, as the Spaniards then called Palawan.
zh:
泰泰扼守巴拉望岛北端，马拉帕亚湾在此连通南海与苏禄海。13世纪的中国载籍把这一带岛屿记作麻逸属国三屿的一部分。西班牙人到来之前，泰泰是一个小王国的都城；据意大利编年史家安东尼奥·皮加费塔后来记述，那里的国王无论走到何处都有十名书吏随行。岛民在海湾捕鱼、沿岸耕种，奉行泛灵的阿尼托信仰；1444年时，他们仍听命于自己的国王。

1521年，斐迪南·麦哲伦在麦克坦丧命后，其残部逃到泰泰，扣押国王与王后勒索粮食，随后继续驶往摩鹿加。一个世纪后西班牙人才建立统治：城镇于1623年正式设立，交由重整奥斯定会传教士主持。他们1667年动工修建圣伊莎贝尔石堡，城墙直到1738年才完工；要塞炮火镇守锚地，抵御从苏禄群岛前来、屡次袭扰巴拉望北部聚落的摩洛掠奴船队。1818年，泰泰成为卡拉棉省省会，该省管辖西班牙人当时称作拉帕瓜的整个巴拉望。

en:
Ise faces the deep bight of Ise Bay, its shore a string of fishing harbours and salt fields, while the Tokaido highway crosses the north of the province between Kyoto and the east. Inland, in the cedar country south of the Kushida River, stands the Ise Grand Shrine, holiest place of the imperial cult, whose twenty-year rebuilding drew offerings from every province. During the Southern Court wars the courtier Kitabatake Akiyoshi came south as provincial governor, and his family became masters of the five southern districts, ruling them from Kiriyama Castle above the Taki valley. In 1444 his descendant Kitabatake Noritomo held Kiriyama as governor-lord of southern Ise, having lately shown his loyalty to the Muromachi shogun: when the fugitive Akamatsu Noriyasu, one of the Kakitsu rebels, sought shelter with him in 1441, Noritomo refused it and let him die.

The house reached its height under Harutomo and his son Tomonori, a swordsman trained by Tsukahara Bokuden, whose power reached into Shima and the neighbouring marches. In 1568 Oda Nobunaga's armies entered northern Ise and its lords submitted, his brother Nobukane adopted into the Kudo house of Anotsu; in the eighth month of 1569 Nobunaga himself besieged Tomonori in Okawachi Castle, until the shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki mediated a peace giving Nobunaga's second son Nobukatsu to the Kitabatake as heir. Nobukatsu took the succession in 1575, and in the eleventh month of 1576 his soldiers struck down Tomonori and his sons in their retreats, the Mitsuse bloodbath that extinguished the governor's house. Under the Tokugawa, Ise was divided among several domains, the greatest the Tsu domain granted in 1608 to Todo Takatora, the castle-builder who had raised Edo Castle, rated in time at 323,000 koku. Pilgrims to the Grand Shrine multiplied on the highways, their mass okage pilgrimages crowding the shrine town of Yamada and the Tokaido post stations of the north.
zh:
伊势面向水深湾阔的伊势湾，沿岸渔村、盐田相连，东海道自北境穿过，连接京都与东国。内陆的栉田川以南杉林幽深，伊势神宫便坐落于此——它是朝廷祭祀最神圣的所在，每隔二十年的式年迁宫要从各国收取奉纳。南北朝争乱时，公卿北畠显能以国司身份南下，北畠家从此成为南伊势五郡的主人，居城是多气山谷上方的雾山城。1444年，其后人北畠教具在雾山城以国司兼领主的身份统治南伊势；1441年嘉吉之乱的败将赤松教康逃来求庇，教具拒不接纳、逼其自害，以此向室町幕府表明恭顺。

北畠家在晴具、具教父子两代达到鼎盛，势力伸入志摩及周边边境；具教曾随剑客冢原卜传习剑，本身也是闻名的剑士。1568年织田信长的大军攻入北伊势，当地豪族纷纷臣服，信长之弟信包被安浓津的长野工藤氏收为养子；1569年8月，信长亲围具教于大河内城，10月由将军足利义昭斡旋议和，条件是信长次子信雄做北畠家的养子。信雄1575年继承家督，1576年11月便派兵在三濑御所袭杀隐居的具教及其诸子，是为三濑之变，国司名门就此灭绝。德川时代伊势被分为数藩，最大的是1608年封给筑城名家藤堂高虎的津藩，石高后来达三十二万三千石。前往神宫的参拜客在各条大道上络绎不绝，大规模的御荫参挤满了门前町山田和北伊势的东海道宿场。

en:
Mikawa, or Sanshū, was the Tōkaidō province east of Owari, fronting the Pacific where Mikawa and Atsumi bays indent the coast while the Yahagi river crosses its rice plains. Ranked a 'superior' and 'near' country under the Engishiki, it long kept an informal east-west division around the Yasaku river. Heian-period shōen gave way to Kamakura vassals and then to the Ashikaga, and for most of the Muromachi age the Isshiki clan held the shugo post. In 1440 Shōgun Yoshinori had Isshiki Yoshitsura murdered and gave the office to Hosokawa Mochikiyo, throwing Mikawa into civil war, and in 1444 the province was a tangle of rival shugo, ikki bands and rising local houses — among them the Matsudaira, small landholders in the Kamo hills pushing south under their head Matsudaira Nobumitsu.

The Matsudaira climbed from this chaos. Kiyoyasu, who took Okazaki in 1531, had nearly united Mikawa when a retainer assassinated him in his Owari camp in 1535, and his young son Hirotada became a client of the Imagawa of Suruga. Hirotada's heir Takechiyo, the future Tokugawa Ieyasu, was born at Okazaki in January 1543 (the twelfth month of Tenbun 11 by the Japanese calendar) and carried off as an Imagawa hostage, but after Yoshimoto fell at Okehazama in 1560 he reclaimed the castle and made himself independent, crushed the armed True Pure Land leagues of the Mikawa Ikkō-ikki of 1563–64, and in 1566 won imperial leave to take the name Tokugawa. He moved his headquarters east to Hamamatsu in 1570, and when he entered the Kantō in 1590 Okazaki passed to Tanaka Yoshimasa, who bent the Tōkaidō through its castle town. Restored under the new shogunate, Okazaki was enfeoffed in 1602 to Honda Yasushige, first of a line of fudai lords, while Yoshida, Nishio, Kariya and Tahara became other fudai seats amid broad shogunal demesne. The highway stations carried daimyō retinues past the Yahagi bridge, the shogunate concentrated its gunpowder-making in Mikawa, and from the mid-seventeenth century the Hatchō breweries west of Okazaki were ageing the dark soybean miso that fed Edo's retainer houses.
zh:
三河（简称三州，又作参州）是尾张以东的东海道令制国，南临太平洋，海岸凹入形成三河湾与渥美湾，矢作川等河流灌溉着平原。《延喜式》中它被列为上国、近国，并长期以矢作川一线分为东三河、西三河。平安时代这里遍布庄园，镰仓以后归于足利氏，整个室町时代大半时间由一色氏担任守护。1440年，将军足利义教刺杀三河守护一色义贯，把守护之职交给细川持常，三河顿时陷入内战；到1444年，国内是新旧守护、国人一揆与在地豪族相互攻伐的乱局，其中便有起于加茂郡松平乡的松平氏，在当主松平信光手中向南扩张。

松平氏正是从这片乱局中崛起。1531年夺取冈崎的清康几乎统一三河，却在1535年于尾张阵中被家臣暗杀，史称森山崩；年幼的广忠沦为骏河今川氏的附庸。广忠之子竹千代——后来的德川家康——于1543年1月（日本纪年为天文十一年十二月）生于冈崎城，随后被送往今川处为质。1560年义元在桶狭间战死后，他夺回冈崎、宣告独立，又在1563至1564年的三河一向一揆中压服武力强大的真宗门徒，1566年获朝廷敕许改姓德川。1570年他把大本营东移滨松，1590年入主关东后，冈崎交给田中吉政，由他把东海道弯折引入冈崎城下町。幕府建立后，本多康重于1602年以五万石入城，此后冈崎世代由谱代大名执掌，吉田、西尾、刈谷、田原等也都是谱代藩，藩领之间夹杂着大片幕府直辖地。东海道上的宿场迎送着往来的大名行列，全国的火药制造被集中到三河，17世纪中叶起，冈崎城西的八丁村开始陈酿深色豆味噌，供应江户的各家武家。

en:
Roxburghshire is the middle march of Scotland, where the Teviot joins the Tweed beneath Roxburgh Castle. David I made Roxburgh a southern royal centre and planted the great abbeys of the border: Kelso in 1128 and Jedburgh in 1147, with Melrose close by. The castle was almost as often English as Scottish: ceded in 1174, stormed by James Douglas in 1314 and demolished on Bruce's orders, it was retaken by Edward III in 1334 and held by England almost without a break after 1346; Scottish sieges failed in 1417 and 1436. In 1444 an English garrison still kept its flag over the Tweed, while Jedburgh, with its abbey and horse and cattle markets, lived by march trade and raiding under the Douglas wardens.

In 1460 James II was killed before Roxburgh when one of his own bombards burst; his queen, Mary of Guelders, pressed the storm, and the captured castle and town were pulled to the ground. Roxburgh was never rebuilt, and Jedburgh became the county town.
