Spain bombarded Salé in May 1628 and a French fleet under Isaac de Razilly in July 1629, yet the 'Salé Rovers' remained the dread of Atlantic shipping. The Dila'iya brotherhood made the city its vassal in 1641, and in June 1668 Sultan Moulay al-Rashid ended the republic for the Alaouite dynasty.
zh:
塞拉位于大西洋畔的阿布·赖格赖格河口，与拉巴特要塞隔河相望。罗马人把上游更古老的聚落称作萨拉殖民地，塞拉城本身则是11世纪由巴努·阿沙拉等安达卢西亚家族建立的。穆瓦希德王朝哈里发雅各布·曼苏尔1196年敕建了塞拉大清真寺。1260年9月，阿方索十世派出的卡斯蒂利亚舰队趁开斋节突袭劫掠，掳走大量居民；马林苏丹阿布·优素福·叶尔孤白经十四天围城收复城市、重修城墙，海上城门迈里萨门即建于此时。1444年的塞拉是马林王朝治下非斯王国首要的大西洋商港，阿布·哈桑经学院坐落城中，商旅与法学家往来辐辏。

西班牙驱逐摩里斯科人彻底改变了这座城市。1609年起，数千名难民来到河口定居，其中约三千人是来自埃斯特雷马杜拉的奥尔纳乔斯富户，他们据有对岸的城堡，以海上劫掠为生；荷兰叛教者扬·扬松（穆拉德·雷斯）1624年起出任他们的舰队大统领。1627年4月，奥尔纳乔斯人驱逐萨阿德王朝总督，宣布建立独立的阿布·赖格赖格共和国，由每年改选的迪万议事会治理。西班牙1628年5月炮轰塞拉，1629年7月艾萨克·德·拉齐利率法国舰队再度来攻，都没能消灭「塞拉海盗」，他们始终是大西洋航路上最令人畏惧的名字。1641年迪拉兄弟会迫使此城臣服，1668年6月穆莱·拉希德苏丹为阿拉维王朝终结了这个共和国。

en:
Anfa stood on a rise of the Chaouia coast, the Atlantic harbour that al-Idrisi counted among the chief ports of the Maghreb al-Aqsa, enriched by its trade with al-Andalus. It grew up under the Barghawata, and when the Almohads broke that Berber kingdom they settled Hilalian Arabs across the Tamesna, turning it into the Arabised Chaouia. Marinid sultans kept the town prosperous: Abu Inan Faris founded a madrasa there between 1348 and 1358, and Ibn al-Khatib visited from Granada. By 1444, with the Marinid state collapsing, Anfa ran its own affairs, a wealthy merchant town whose corsairs raided as far as the mouth of the Tagus.

Its pirates drew Portuguese revenge: in 1468 a fleet sent by Afonso V and commanded by the Infante Ferdinand stormed the city and left it in ruins, and for three generations only Salé corsairs and local tribes used its anchorage. Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah rebuilt it from 1760, girdling the new town with walls and a fortified sqala, placing it under a pasha and naming it Dar al-Bayda, the White House, Casa Branca to the Portuguese. Under the later Alaouites it stayed a small grain port of the Chaouia, overshadowed by Mazagan and Mogador.
zh:
安法坐落在沙维耶海岸的一处高地上，伊德里西曾把这座大西洋港口列为马格里布最西端的主要港口之一，它因与安达卢西亚通商而富庶。安法兴起于巴尔加瓦塔王国时代；穆瓦希德王朝攻灭这个柏柏尔王国后，把希拉勒系阿拉伯部落迁入塔马斯纳一带，此地逐渐阿拉伯化，改称沙维耶。马林王朝时期城市保持繁荣，阿布·伊南·法里斯在1348至1358年间于此兴建伊斯兰学校，格拉纳达的伊本·哈提卜也曾到访。1444年马林国家土崩瓦解，安法人自行其是，既是富商云集之城，也是海盗巢穴，寇掠范围远至塔霍河口。

海盗招来了葡萄牙的报复：1468年，阿方索五世派出、由费尔南多亲王统率的舰队攻破安法，将城市夷为废墟。此后近一个世纪，只有萨累的海盗和当地部落间或使用这片锚地。穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉苏丹于1760年起重建新城，环筑城墙与炮台斯卡拉，派帕夏治理，并取名达尔贝达，意为「白房子」，葡语作卡萨布兰卡。在其后的阿拉维王朝治下，它始终是沙维耶平原一座小小的谷物港，声势不及马扎甘和摩加多尔。

en:
Tenerife is the largest Canary Island, dominated by the snow-veiled volcano of Teide. Its Guanches had lived there for perhaps two thousand years, herding goats and sheep, farming coastal plots, fishing and gathering shellfish. By the fifteenth century the island was divided into chiefdoms called menceyatos, each under a mencey; Taoro, in the fertile north, was the strongest. European ships knew the island and raided its coasts, but no foreign fortress or sugar settlement had taken root. In 1444 Tenerife remained entirely in Guanche hands, its rulers, pastures and mountain sanctuaries untouched by the Castilian conquest already transforming the smaller Canaries.

Castilian pressure began in 1464, when Diego García de Herrera took symbolic possession and built a short-lived tower in Anaga. After a failed raid in 1492, Alonso Fernández de Lugo landed near the future Santa Cruz in April 1494 with about 2,000 foot soldiers and 200 cavalry. The Guanches defeated him at the First Battle of Acentejo, but disease, firearms and divisions among the chiefdoms told against them; defeats at Aguere and the Second Battle of Acentejo ended resistance in September 1496. Lugo then founded San Cristóbal de La Laguna, which became the island's first capital. Sugar cane spread in the early sixteenth century, followed by Malmsey wine, cochineal and bananas; Robert Blake raided the island in 1656, the 1706 Trevejo eruption buried the port of Garachico, and Horatio Nelson lost his right arm in the failed assault on Santa Cruz in 1797.
zh:
特内里费是加那利群岛中最大的岛屿，岛上矗立着积雪覆顶的泰德峰。关切人已在此生活约两千年，牧放山羊和绵羊，在沿海地块耕作，也从事捕鱼和采贝。到15世纪，岛屿分为若干称为门塞亚托的酋邦，各由门塞统治；北部沃土上的塔奥罗最为强大。欧洲船只已经知道这座岛并袭扰海岸，但没有任何外来要塞或糖料定居点真正扎根。1444年的特内里费仍完全掌握在关切人手中，各首领、牧场和山间圣所尚未受到已改变较小加那利岛屿的卡斯蒂利亚征服波及。

卡斯蒂利亚的压力始于1464年，迭戈·加西亚·德·埃雷拉在该年进行象征性占领，并在阿纳加修建一座短命塔楼。1492年一次袭击失败后，阿隆索·费尔南德斯·德·卢戈于1494年4月率约两千步兵和两百骑兵，在后来的圣克鲁斯附近登陆。关切人在第一次阿森特霍战役中将其击败，但疫病、火器和酋邦之间的分裂逐渐压倒抵抗；阿格雷战役与第二次阿森特霍战役后，抵抗于1496年9月结束。卢戈随后建立圣克里斯托瓦尔-德拉拉古纳，这里成为岛上第一个首府。16世纪初甘蔗种植扩展，随后又有玛尔维萨葡萄酒、胭脂虫和香蕉；罗伯特·布莱克1656年袭扰本岛，1706年特雷韦霍火山喷发掩埋加拉奇科港，1797年霍雷肖·纳尔逊进攻圣克鲁斯失败，并失去右臂。

en:
Kairouan rises in the inland plains, fifty kilometres west of Susa, where the Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi pitched his camp around 670 and raised the Great Mosque that bears his name. Under the Aghlabids it was the capital of Ifriqiya, rich enough to be set beside Basra and Kufa: jurists such as Sahnun taught Maliki law in the mosque's university, and the great Aghlabid cisterns were built beyond the walls. The Fatimids withdrew to Mahdia, the Zirids brought a second bloom, and when the Hilali bedouin sacked the city in 1057 it sank into two centuries of ruin and its scholars drifted to Tunis. The Hafsids began its revival in the thirteenth century, repairing the Great Mosque in 1248 and again in 1293–1294. In 1444 Kairouan was a city of pilgrims and grain merchants rising slowly from its ruins under the Hafsid sultans, the first holy city of the Maghreb; its historian Ibn Naji had died only a few years before.

The Muradid beys took up the work early: the Great Mosque was repaired in 1618, and outside the walls Hammuda Pasha rebuilt the zawiya of Sidi Sahab around 1662, madrasa and minaret included, over the tomb of Abu Zama'a al-Balawi, companion and barber of the Prophet; his grandson Mohamed Bey remade the mausoleum dome in 1681–1685, and pilgrim caravans from across the Maghreb gathered there before setting out for Mecca. Hussein ibn Ali, founder of the Husainid line, restored the city walls and founded a madrasa, but Kairouan became his last refuge: defeated by his nephew Ali Pasha at Smendja on 4 September 1735, he was besieged here, taken beneath the ramparts and beheaded on 13 May 1740. Under his dynasty the old holy city at last recovered a respected place in the life of Tunisia.
zh:
凯鲁万矗立在内陆平原上，东距苏萨五十公里。约670年，阿拉伯名将欧格白·伊本·纳菲在此扎营建城，筑起以他之名命名的大清真寺。阿格拉布王朝时期，它是伊夫里奇亚的都城，富庶可比巴士拉与库法：塞赫农等法学家在寺中大学讲授马立克学派教法，城外还修起宏大的阿格拉布蓄水池。法蒂玛王朝迁都马赫迪叶，齐尔王朝带来二度繁荣；1057年希拉尔贝都因人洗劫全城，凯鲁万就此荒废两个世纪，学者纷纷转往突尼斯城。13世纪哈夫斯王朝开启复兴，1248年、1293至1294年两度重修大清真寺。1444年，在哈夫斯苏丹治下，凯鲁万是一座缓慢走出废墟的圣城，朝圣者与粮商云集，位列马格里布第一圣城，为它修史的伊本·纳吉几年前刚刚去世。

穆拉德王朝的贝伊们早早接过修缮之役：1618年整建大清真寺；城外，哈穆达帕夏贝伊约1662年重修西迪·萨哈布道堂，连经学院带宣礼塔一并兴建，堂下安葬着先知的伙伴兼理发师阿布·宰迈阿·拜莱维；其孙穆罕默德贝伊又于1681至1685年重建圣墓穹顶，全马格里布的朝觐商队都在此会集，再启程前往麦加。侯赛因王朝开创者侯赛因·伊本·阿里修复城墙、创办经学院，凯鲁万却成了他最后的避难所：1735年9月4日，他在斯门贾被侄子阿里帕夏击败，退守此城，最终于1740年5月13日在城墙下被俘斩首。在他的王朝治下，这座古老圣城终于在突尼斯的生活中重获尊崇的地位。

en:
Sabha is the great oasis of central Fezzan, set on the desert road that runs from the Tripolitanian coast through Hun and Waddan to Murzuk and the lands of Bornu. Springs feed its palms and the villages of the Wadi al-Bawanis, and the mound above the town holds the remains of a fortress first raised in Garamantian times, more than 2,500 years ago. Al-Bakri, writing in the eleventh century, already marked Sabha as a station five days' march south of Hun, where caravans changed guides and laid in dates before the long crossing. Kanem and Bornu successively claimed the oases between the thirteenth and fifteenth centuries, and Arab tribes pastured their flocks around them. In 1444 Sabha was a caravan town under the lords of Fezzan, its wealth counted in slaves and ivory carried north and in the horses and cloth carried south.

The Awlad Muhammad made it a town of their sultanate, and the Ottoman march south soon reached it. Mahmut Bey, the officer who led Ottoman expeditions through Fezzan as far as Kawar and Lake Chad, fell in 1583 suppressing a Bornu-backed revolt, but Ottoman control stayed as loose here as at Murzuk, asserted only by occasional expeditions in 1679–1682, 1690 and 1718. In 1622–1626 Ahmad ibn Huwaydi al-Kharmani, a local chief who claimed Garamantian descent, rebuilt the old fortress on its hill, the castle later known as Fort Elena. When the pashas of Tripoli finally made themselves masters of the sultanate in 1813, Sabha's caravans and fortress passed to them.
zh:
塞卜哈是费赞中部的大绿洲，位于从的黎波里塔尼亚海岸经洪、瓦丹通往穆尔祖克和博尔努的沙漠大道上。泉水滋养着椰枣林和布瓦尼斯河谷的村庄，城边的山冈上留存着一座要塞的遗迹，最早建于2500多年前的加拉曼特时代。11世纪的白克里已把塞卜哈记作洪以南五日路程的驿站，商队在此更换向导、备足椰枣，然后踏上漫长的穿越之旅。13至15世纪，卡涅姆和博尔努先后宣称领有这些绿洲，阿拉伯部落则在四周放牧。1444年，塞卜哈是费赞首领治下的商队之城，财富以源源北上的奴隶、象牙和南下的马匹、布匹计。

奥拉德·穆罕默德王朝把塞卜哈纳入自己的苏丹国，奥斯曼人的南征也很快波及于此。军官马哈茂德贝伊率远征军穿过费赞，远达卡瓦尔和乍得湖一带，1583年在镇压一场博尔努支持的叛乱时阵亡；但奥斯曼在此的控制和穆尔祖克一样松散，只靠1679至1682年、1690年和1718年的数次远征维持。1622至1626年，自称加拉曼特人后裔的本地首领艾哈迈德·本·胡韦迪·海尔马尼在山冈上重建古堡，即后来的埃莱娜堡。1813年的黎波里帕夏最终成为苏丹国的主人，塞卜哈的商队和堡垒一并归于他们。

en: Demnate is a Berber market town in the fertile Tassaout valley on the northern foot of the High Atlas, about 100 kilometres east of Marrakesh. Local tradition places its foundation around 998, when the Inoultan and Infedouak clans made it a meeting place for trade and common defense; in Tachelhit its name means fertile lands. A Jewish community settled there in the early twelfth century and became known for wine, leatherwork and crafts. In 1444 Demnate was a market town of the Moroccan realm, where Atlas and southern caravans exchanged wool, hides, dates, olive oil, leather and grain. Through the Saadian and Alawid periods it remained a provisioning stop on the tracks leading from Marrakesh toward the Draa and Tafilalt.
zh: 代姆纳特是大阿特拉斯山北麓、塔萨沃特河谷肥土地上的柏柏尔集镇，位于马拉喀什以东约100公里。当地传统称城镇约建于998年，由伊努尔坦和因费杜瓦克氏族辟为交易与共同防御的集会地；其名在塔切拉特语中意为肥沃之地。12世纪初，一个犹太社区在此定居，以酿酒、皮革制作和手工业闻名。1444年，代姆纳特是摩洛哥政权治下的集镇，阿特拉斯山民与南方商队在此交换羊毛、兽皮、椰枣、橄榄油、皮革和谷物。萨阿德与阿拉维王朝时期，它始终是从马拉喀什通往德拉和塔菲拉勒特道路上的补给市场。

en:
Texcoco, the Acolhua capital on the eastern shore of Lake Texcoco, became the second city of the Aztec world after the Triple Alliance was formed with Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan in 1428. Its ruler Nezahualcoyotl had returned from exile to defeat the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco, and by 1444 his court drew poets, priests and scholars. The city held royal archives and music rooms, took two-fifths of the alliance's tribute, and its aqueducts and gardens climbed toward the sacred hill of Texcotzingo.

Nezahualcoyotl ruled until 1472 and was succeeded by his son Nezahualpilli. When Hernán Cortés reached the lake in 1519, Cacamatzin ruled Texcoco; the city then became the Spanish base for the siege of Tenochtitlan, and the brigantines used on the lake were launched there in 1521. After the conquest the Franciscans Juan de Tecto, Juan de Ayora and Pedro de Gante began Christian instruction. Gante learned Nahuatl, wrote a Nahuatl catechism and opened a school where Latin, Spanish, carpentry, sewing and weaving were taught. Charles V recognized Texcoco as a city in 1551, but over the colonial centuries it was overshadowed by nearby Mexico City and lived increasingly from fishing, agriculture and lake-shore estates.
zh:
特斯科科是特斯科科湖东岸的阿科瓦人都城。1428年，它与特诺奇蒂特兰和特拉科潘结成三方同盟，随后成为阿兹特克世界的第二大城。统治者内萨瓦尔科约特尔曾流亡在外，归国后击败阿斯卡波特萨尔科的特帕内克人；到1444年，他的宫廷已吸引诗人、祭司和学者。城中设有王室档案库和乐厅，按盟约分得五分之二贡物，水渠与园林还沿特斯科钦科圣山层层而上。

内萨瓦尔科约特尔统治到1472年，其子内萨瓦尔皮利继位。埃尔南·科尔特斯1519年抵达湖畔时，特斯科科的统治者是卡卡马辛；这座城市随后成为西班牙人围攻特诺奇蒂特兰的基地，用于湖上作战的双桅船也于1521年在此下水。征服后，方济各会士胡安·德·托克托、胡安·德·阿约拉和佩德罗·德·甘特开始传教。甘特学会纳瓦语，编写纳瓦语教义问答，并开办学校，教授拉丁语、西班牙语、木工、缝纫和编织。查理五世1551年正式承认特斯科科为城市，但在整个殖民时期，它日渐被邻近的墨西哥城掩盖，主要依靠渔业、农业和湖畔庄园维持。

en:
Tlacopan, later called Tacuba, was a Tepanec city-state on the fertile western shore of Lake Texcoco. It had once been subject to Azcapotzalco, but in 1428 it joined Tenochtitlan and Texcoco in the Triple Alliance after Azcapotzalco's overthrow. In 1444 it was the alliance's junior partner, receiving only one-fifth of the tribute from joint campaigns while the Mexico-Tacuba causeway tied it directly to the island capital of Tenochtitlan.

On 30 June 1520, Cortés and his retreating men fled along that causeway toward Tlacopan during La Noche Triste; when the Spanish returned in 1521, the siege of Tenochtitlan ended the Triple Alliance. The last native ruler, Tetlepanquetzal, was tortured under suspicion of hiding treasure, and in 1526 a Spanish decree made Isabel Moctezuma, daughter of Moctezuma II, titular ruler of an encomienda whose households paid fowl, eggs, maize, tortillas and cacao. Franciscans built the church of San Gabriel over the old ceremonial centre, the Carmelites founded San Joaquín in 1689, and by 1632 sixty haciendas had spread through the district, supplying Mexico City with food, lumber and sandstone.
zh:
特拉科潘后来又称塔库巴，是特斯科科湖肥沃西岸的特帕内克城邦。它原臣属于阿斯卡波特萨尔科，但在1428年与特诺奇蒂特兰、特斯科科联合推翻旧主，加入三方同盟。1444年，它是同盟中较弱的一方，只分得联合作战所获贡物的五分之一；墨西哥城—塔库巴堤道则把它与岛上都城特诺奇蒂特兰直接相连。

1520年6月30日「悲痛之夜」，科尔特斯及其残部沿这条堤道逃向特拉科潘；1521年西班牙人卷土重来，特诺奇蒂特兰围城战终结了三方同盟。最后一位本土统治者特特莱潘克察尔因被怀疑藏匿财宝而受刑。1526年，一道西班牙敕令立蒙特祖马二世之女伊莎贝尔·蒙特祖马为恩孔米恩达的名义统治者，辖下民户缴纳禽鸟、禽蛋、玉米、薄饼和可可豆。方济各会在旧祭祀中心上建起圣加百列教堂，加尔默罗会1689年创立圣华金修院；到1632年，这一地区已有六十处庄园，为墨西哥城供应食物、木材和砂岩。

en:
Malinalco lies in the rugged hills south of Toluca, on routes between the high plateau and the warmer country toward Cuernavaca and Guerrero. Culhua, Matlatzinca, Ocuilteco and Otomi communities settled its valleys, and by 1444 Matlatzinca elites dominated a populous city-state with an old ceremonial centre on the Cerro de los Ídolos. It fought wars with Cuauhnahuac and kept commercial ties with the Basin of Mexico and Puebla-Tlaxcala, while still remaining outside the Mexica Empire.

Axayácatl conquered Malinalco in 1476, turning it into a tributary province that supplied maguey mantles, grain and stone. Around 1486-1490 Ahuízotl sent stonecarvers from Tenochtitlan and forced local labour to build the Cuauhcalli, a sanctuary for Eagle and Jaguar warriors cut into the Cerro de los Ídolos; it was still unfinished when the Spanish arrived. After La Noche Triste the people of Malinalco rose against the newcomers, and Andrés de Tapia subdued them together with Ocuilán. The encomienda first passed to Cristóbal Rodríguez de Ávalos and then to the Crown. Franciscans and Dominicans began evangelization before the Augustinians were assigned the town in 1533; they built the monastery of the Divino Salvador with stone from the unfinished sanctuary. The Jalmolonga hacienda, later worked by the Jesuits to support their Mexico City college, passed after the Jesuit expulsion to Manuel Romero de Terreros, Count of Regla. On 8 January 1813 José María Morelos passed through and signed orders concerning native agricultural customs and church funds raised for the war in Spain.
zh:
马利纳尔科位于托卢卡以南的崎岖山地，处在中部高原通往夸尔纳瓦卡和格雷罗暖地的道路上。库尔瓦、马特拉钦卡、奥奎尔特克和奥托米社群先后定居于这片谷地；到1444年，马特拉钦卡上层统治着一座人口稠密的城邦，并在偶像山上保有古老祭祀中心。它曾与夸尔纳瓦克交战，也同墨西哥盆地及普埃布拉—特拉斯卡拉谷地保持商业联系，当时尚未并入墨西哥帝国。

阿萨亚卡特尔1476年征服马利纳尔科，把它变为缴纳龙舌兰布、粮食和石材的贡赋行省。约1486—1490年，阿维索特尔从特诺奇蒂特兰派来石匠，并征调当地劳役，在偶像山岩体内开凿「鹰屋」，作为鹰战士与豹战士的圣所；西班牙人到来时工程仍未完成。「悲痛之夜」后，马利纳尔科人起兵抵抗，安德烈斯·德·塔皮亚将他们与奥基兰人一同平定。恩孔米恩达先授予克里斯托瓦尔·罗德里格斯·德·阿瓦洛斯，后收归王室。方济各会和多明我会最先传教，奥斯定会1533年受命接管，并利用未完工圣所的石料修建圣救主修院。哈尔莫隆加庄园后来由耶稣会经营，用以资助其在墨西哥城的学院；耶稣会被驱逐后，庄园落入雷格拉伯爵曼努埃尔·罗梅罗·德·特雷罗斯之手。1813年1月8日，何塞·马里亚·莫雷洛斯经过此地，签署了涉及原住民农业惯例和教会为西班牙战事筹款的命令。

en:
Acámbaro stands on the Lerma at the northeastern edge of the Purépecha state. Chupícuaro farming villages had occupied the country long before; in the fifteenth century Otomi lineages allied with the Uacúsecha were settled here to guard the frontier, and Purépecha lords then posted their own officials over the region. The Purépecha name Ak'amparhu recalled both the sacred maguey and a woman named Ak'amba, while the Otomi knew the place as Mauadá. In 1444 Otomi farmers and frontier warriors lived among maguey and maize lands by the Lerma, holding the road from Tzintzuntzan toward the Bajío.

On 19 September 1526 the cacique Nicolás de San Luis Montañés formally founded San Francisco de Acámbaro, the first Spanish-ordered town in what is now Guanajuato. Franciscans began evangelization and built the Hospital Temple; their Mudéjar aqueduct, begun in 1527 under Antonio de Bermul, carried water from Tócuaro, and the stone bridge over the Lerma followed in 1750. The native head town became an important republic of Indians, while the province was administered with Yuririapúndaro under the mayor of Celaya. On 22 October 1810 Miguel Hidalgo declared Acámbaro the military quarters of the Grand Army of America and was named Generalísimo of the Americas; more than 80,000 insurgents paraded that day, whereas only 800 had answered the Grito de Dolores a month earlier.
zh:
阿坎巴罗位于莱尔马河畔，地处普雷佩查国家东北缘。丘皮库阿罗农民的村落早已在此生息；15世纪，与瓦库塞查结盟的奥托米氏族被安置到这里守卫边境，普雷佩查贵族随后又派来官员控制这一地区。普雷佩查语地名 Ak'amparhu 既关联神圣的龙舌兰，也纪念一位名叫 Ak'amba 的女性；奥托米语则称此地为 Mauadá。1444年，奥托米农民和边境战士生活在莱尔马河畔的龙舌兰与玉米地之间，为钦聪灿扼守通向巴希奥的道路。

1526年9月19日，酋长尼古拉斯·德·圣路易斯·蒙塔涅斯正式建立圣方济各·德·阿坎巴罗，这是今瓜纳华托境内第一座按西班牙殖民秩序建立的城镇。方济各会开始传教并修建医院教堂；安东尼奥·德·贝尔穆尔主持的穆德哈尔风格输水道于1527年动工，把托夸罗的泉水引来，莱尔马河上的石桥则在1750年建成。土著首镇后来成为重要的印第安人共和国，阿坎巴罗省与尤里里亚彭达罗一同归塞拉亚长官管辖。1810年10月22日，米格尔·伊达尔戈在此宣布阿坎巴罗为「美洲大军」的军营，并受任「美洲大元帅」；当天有超过8万名起义者列队受阅，而一个月前在多洛雷斯响应呼声起事的还只有800人。

en: Ihuatzio, the Purépecha 'place of coyotes', lies on the southeastern shore of Lake Pátzcuaro below Cerro Tariaqueri. Nahua speakers occupied it from 900 to 1200 and called it Coyoacán; during the Purépecha florescence after 1200, it became one of three royal lordships, with Hiripan holding Ihuatzio while Pátzcuaro and Tzintzuntzan had their own lords. In 1444 power was already shifting to Tzintzuntzan, yet Ihuatzio remained a walled ceremonial center of raised roads, three yácatas, temples to Curicaueri and Xaratanga, and a circular observatory overlooking lake farms and fishing villages. The conquest ended its court life after 1530, but Ihuatzio survived as an indigenous community; in 1593 it was still counted among the principal subject towns governed through native Tzintzuntzan.
zh: 伊瓦齐奥在普雷佩查语中意为「郊狼之地」，位于帕茨夸罗湖东南岸、塔里亚克里山下方。900年至1200年间，纳瓦语族群居住于此，称它为科约阿坎；1200年以后普雷佩查文化进入鼎盛期，伊瓦齐奥与帕茨夸罗、钦聪灿并列为三个王家庄园，伊里潘在此镇守，另外两处则各有领主。1444年，王权虽已开始转向钦聪灿，伊瓦齐奥仍是有围墙的礼仪中心，高台道路、三座亚卡塔金字塔、库里考埃里与沙拉坦加神庙和圆形观象台俯临湖滨农田与渔村。征服在1530年后终结了这里的王廷生活，但伊瓦齐奥作为土著村社存续；1593年，它仍是通过土著钦聪灿政府管辖的主要附属村镇之一。

en:
Puruarán lies in the hot southern lowlands of Michoacán, well-watered country that slopes toward the Balsas River; its Purépecha name means 'place of the steaming springs'. It was the granary of the Purépecha kingdom: according to the Relación de Michoacán, the cazonci granted the lands running from Puruarán south to Guerrero to the lord of Tacámbaro, and the maize grown here supplied the royal heartland around Lake Pátzcuaro. In 1444 the district was governed through that local lord on the Purépecha southern frontier, the country beyond the Balsas still held by peoples the cazonci could not subdue.

Cristóbal de Olid's Spaniards reached Tzintzuntzan in 1522 and the last cazonci, Tangáxuan II, submitted. When Nuño de Guzmán marched west in 1530 the king was tortured and burned alive, and the hot country was parcelled into encomiendas and later into sugar-cane haciendas. Friars made the parish of San José a base for carrying the Gospel through the Tierra Caliente, and the cult of the Señor del Huerto venerated there had its feast confirmed by papal bull in 1721. During the independence wars the Rayón brothers made Puruarán their headquarters in 1810. On 5 January 1814 Agustín de Iturbide's royalists routed Morelos's rearguard at the bridge of Puruarán and captured Mariano Matamoros, who was executed a month later; in July 1815 Morelos's itinerant Congress took refuge at the hacienda here.
zh:
普鲁阿兰位于米却肯南部炎热的低地，泉水众多，地势向巴尔萨斯河倾斜，其普雷佩查语地名意为「沸腾泉水之地」。这里曾是普雷佩查王国的粮仓：据《米却肯纪事》记载，钦聪灿的卡松西把从普鲁阿兰向南直至格雷罗的土地封给塔坎巴罗的首领，此地出产的玉米供应帕茨库罗湖一带的王畿。1444年，这片地方由那位地方首领管辖，处在普雷佩查的南部边境，巴尔萨斯河对岸仍是卡松西无法征服的族群。

1522年，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德率领西班牙人抵达钦聪灿，末代卡松西唐加西安二世投降。1530年努尼奥·德·古斯曼西征时将他酷刑后烧死，炎热低地随后被划为委托监护地，日后又辟为甘蔗庄园。修士们以圣何塞堂区为据点，向整个铁拉卡连特传教；1721年教廷颁布诏书，确立当地「菜园基督」圣像的节庆。独立战争中，拉永兄弟1810年以普鲁阿兰为兵营。1814年1月5日，阿古斯丁·德·伊图尔维德的保王军在普鲁阿兰桥击溃莫雷洛斯的后卫，俘获马里亚诺·马塔莫罗斯，后者一个月后被处死；1815年7月，莫雷洛斯辗转各地的国会曾在当地庄园驻留。

en:
Amaxocotlan, later called Mascota, was a Tecos chief's town in the pine-covered western Sierra of Jalisco. Its Nahuatl name describes a place of deer and snakes, and its hunters and farmers lived between high mountain valleys and the Pacific slope. In 1444 the cacicazgo centered here reached over Talpa, El Tuito and coastal Chacala, giving the hill town influence beyond the mountains toward the sea.

Francisco Cortés de San Buenaventura reached Amaxacotlán Mazacotla early in 1525, sent north from Colima by Hernán Cortés; the Spaniards also called the country Valle de los Venados or Valle de Banderas. In 1530 Nuño de Guzmán subjected Mascota during his harsh western campaign, after the district had been granted in encomienda to Pedro Gómez and Martín Monje. Most of the land later passed under Augustinian administration, with the religious steward living near Mal Paso.
zh:
阿马索科特兰后称马斯科塔，是哈利斯科西部松树林山地中特科斯人酋长大镇。其纳瓦特尔语名称意为「鹿与蛇之地」，猎人和农人在高山谷地与太平洋坡地之间生活。1444年，以此地为中心的酋邦统辖塔尔帕、埃尔图伊托和滨海的查卡拉，使这座山镇的影响力越过群山通向海洋。

1525年初，弗朗西斯科·科尔特斯·德·圣布埃纳文图拉受埃尔南·科尔特斯派遣，从科利马北上，抵达阿马萨克特兰·马萨克特拉；西班牙人还把这一带称为「鹿谷」或「巴耶德班德拉斯」。1530年，努尼奥·德·古斯曼在残酷的西征中征服马斯科塔，此前该地区已被委托给佩德罗·戈麦斯和马丁·蒙赫。后来大部分土地归入奥斯定会管理，宗教事务管家住在马尔帕索附近。

en:
Tohono means 'desert people', and the western O'odham bands reached from the Gila and Colorado rivers toward the Gulf of California. The coastal people of this province were the Hia C-eḍ or Areneños, whose camps lay around the volcanic Pinacate hills and the Gran Desierto de Altar. They moved with scarce rainwater and springs, hunted and gathered in the dunes, fished along the gulf, and carried shell and other desert goods to the Cocopah and other Yuman peoples near the Colorado Delta. In 1444 this was still a roadless nomadic frontier, loosely linked to the wider Piman world to the east.

Spanish knowledge of the dune country came through Eusebio Kino, who explored the Pinacate region in 1698 and returned in later years. Missions and presidios took root farther east in the Pimería Alta, where revolt flared in 1695 and again in 1751; Charles III's expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 then removed the order that had done most to open the frontier. Those upheavals touched Sonoyta and the river valleys more than the sand sea, and the coastal Tohono bands remained largely beyond mission control when Mexican independence reached Sonora in 1821.
zh:
「托霍诺」意为沙漠之人，西部奥奥德姆群体的活动范围从希拉河、科罗拉多河延伸到加利福尼亚湾。本省沿海居民是希亚塞德·奥奥德姆人，西班牙人又称阿雷尼奥人或皮纳卡特人，营地散布在火山地貌的皮纳卡特山地与阿尔塔大沙漠周围。他们随着稀少的雨水和泉眼迁徙，在沙丘间狩猎采集，在海湾捕鱼，并把贝壳和其他沙漠物产带到科罗拉多河三角洲，与科科帕人及其他尤曼人群体交易。1444年时，这里仍是没有道路的游居边陲，只与东方更广阔的皮马人群世界保持松散联系。

西班牙人对这片沙丘地带的了解主要来自耶稣会士基诺：他在1698年探查皮纳卡特地区，此后数年间又曾重返。传教站和要塞真正扎根于更东边的皮梅里亚阿尔塔，1695年和1751年两度爆发起事；卡洛斯三世1767年驱逐耶稣会，又使最主要开拓这边疆的修会撤出。这些变动更多影响索诺伊塔和河谷地带，而非沙海本身。因此到1821年墨西哥独立的消息传至索诺拉时，沿海的托霍诺群体大体仍在传教控制之外。

en:
Tzapotzingo was one of three Totorame-speaking lordships on the Nayarit coastal plain, alongside Aztatlán and Senticpac. Its subject towns included Tepehuacan, Guaristemba, Mecatlan and Xalxocotan; Mecatlan stood near the shoreline later chosen for San Blas. Farming families grew maize, beans and chile, while fishing, shrimping and salt-making linked the coast with the Cora and Huichol mountains. By the fifteenth century the old Aztatlán network had given way to rival chiefdoms. In 1444 Tzapotzingo was still independent, bordering the inland sphere of Xalisco but not ruled from Tenochtitlan.

Francisco Cortés de San Buenaventura reached Nayarit in 1526 and received peaceful submissions, but Nuño de Guzmán began the definitive conquest in 1530; on 18 November 1531 he founded Villa del Espíritu Santo, the Spanish nucleus that became Tepic. During the Mixtón War of 1540-1542, Francisco Pantecatl, cacique of Tzapotzingo, recounted the Huasamota valley ceremony where prophets called on the peoples of Nueva Galicia to expel the Spaniards, before Viceroy Antonio de Mendoza crushed the rising. In 1768 José de Gálvez made San Blas a royal naval port and shipyard for Sonora and California, and Juan Pérez sailed north from there in 1774. The insurgent priest José María Mercado took Tepic and San Blas in 1810 and died in the royalist counterattack the following January. San Blas adhered to the Plan de Iguala on 25 July 1821.
zh:
察波钦戈是纳亚里特沿海平原上三个讲托托拉姆语的酋邦之一，与阿斯特兰和森蒂克帕克并列。它的属村包括特佩瓦坎、瓜里斯滕巴、梅卡特兰和哈尔尔索科坦；梅卡特兰靠近后来选定圣布拉斯港的海岸。农家种植玉米、豆类和辣椒，渔业、捕虾和制盐又把海岸同科拉人、惠乔尔人的山地连接起来。到15世纪，旧阿斯特兰网络已经分裂为彼此竞争的酋邦。1444年，察波钦戈仍然独立，毗邻内陆的哈利斯科势力范围，但并不受特诺奇蒂特兰统治。

1526年，弗朗西斯科·科尔特斯·德·圣布埃纳文图拉抵达纳亚里特并接受一些酋邦和平归降；努尼奥·德·古斯曼则在1530年开始决定性征服，并于1531年11月18日建立圣灵镇，这个西班牙据点后来发展为特皮克。1540至1542年米克特战争期间，察波钦戈酋长弗朗西斯科·潘特卡特记述了瓦萨莫塔谷的仪式：先知在那里号召新加利西亚各族驱逐西班牙人，随后安东尼奥·德·门多萨总督镇压了起义。1768年，何塞·德·加尔韦斯把圣布拉斯建成皇家军港和船厂，作为前往索诺拉和加利福尼亚的基地，胡安·佩雷斯于1774年由此北航。1810年，起义神父何塞·马里亚·梅尔卡多夺取特皮克和圣布拉斯，次年1月在保王派反攻中身亡。1821年7月25日，圣布拉斯宣布加入伊瓜拉计划。

en:
Sayula lies in a broad inland basin south of Lake Chapala, where shallow briny lagoons yield salt. Its people were the Tecos, Nahuatl speakers who called their town Tzaulan, 'the place where flies abound'. In 1444 it was a chiefdom within the Tecos kingdom of Colimán, and its salt and saltpeter drew traders along the western Mexican routes. The salt beds were a prize rich enough to lure the Purépecha cazonci's armies before the century was out, yet the Tecos kept their independence.

Between 1480 and 1510 the Tecos under Colímotl defeated the Purépecha in the Saltpeter War, fighting them at Zacoalco, and the caciques of Sayula, Zapotlán and Amula paid him tribute. Alonso de Ávalos, a cousin of Cortés, reached Tzaulan in 1523 and made the town the seat of his encomienda and capital of the Provincia de Ávalos under the Viceroyalty of New Spain. Franciscans founded the Convent of San Francisco in 1573 and an Indian hospital in 1578, and the Saturday market made Sayula one of the twelve towns entitled to deputies before the merchants' tribunal of the Guadalajara consulado, handling salt, soap, cloth and knives. In 1742 clay pipes carried spring water to the central stone fountain. News of Hidalgo's rising reached the town in October 1810; the Spanish merchants fled, and José Antonio Torres entered on 28 October with 5,000 men. The local priest José Guadalupe Montenegro, whose conspiracy had been uncovered back in 1793, rode out to join the insurgents.
zh:
萨尤拉位于查帕拉湖以南一片开阔的内陆盆地，水浅味咸的潟湖出产食盐。住在这里的是说纳瓦特尔语的特科斯人，他们把自己的镇子叫作察乌兰（Tzaulan），意为「苍蝇成群之地」。1444年，萨尤拉是特科斯科利曼王国治下的一个酋邦，所产食盐和硝石吸引商队往来于西墨西哥的商路。这些盐滩富庶得足以在本世纪末引来普雷佩查卡松西的大军，但特科斯人守住了独立。

1480至1510年间，特科斯人在科利莫特尔率领下打赢硝石战争，在萨科阿尔科与普雷佩查人交战并将其击败，萨尤拉、萨波特兰和阿穆拉的酋长都向他纳贡。科尔特斯的表亲阿隆索·德·阿瓦洛斯1523年抵达察乌兰，把镇子设为自己委托监护地的治所和新西班牙阿瓦洛斯省的省会。方济各会1573年建立圣方济各修道院，1578年又开设印第安人医院；每周六的集市使萨尤拉成为获准向瓜达拉哈拉商会商事法庭选派代表的十二座城镇之一，经营食盐、肥皂、布匹和刀具。1742年，陶土管道把泉水引入市中心的石砌喷泉。1810年10月，伊达尔戈起义的消息传到镇上，西班牙商人争相出逃，何塞·安东尼奥·托雷斯于10月28日率五千人入城；早在1793年密谋就已败露的本地神父何塞·瓜达卢佩·蒙特内格罗，也策马投奔起义军。

en:
Tecomán lies on the hot coastal plain of Colima, where the mountains drop to lagoons and the Pacific; its Tecos people, Nahuatl speakers, made the valley the heartland of their kingdom, with the ruler's seat at Caxitlán. In 1444 Colimán was the strongest power on the western coast. Its fishermen worked the coastal lagoons and its salt pans sent salt inland, while across the eastern hills the Purépecha cazonci cast a jealous eye on the same shore. Within a generation his armies would march on these saltpeter beds, only to be thrown back.

The Tecos under Colímotl defeated the Purépecha in the Saltpeter War of 1480–1510 and made Colima the leading power of the region. They also fended off the first Spanish expeditions: Juan Rodríguez de Villafuerte was ambushed at Trojes, Juan Álvarez Chico fell in a mountain defile, and Cristóbal de Olid was beaten at the Paso de Alima near Tecomán, until Gonzalo de Sandoval feigned a retreat and broke them at Alima in 1523. On 25 July 1523 Sandoval founded the Villa de Colima at Caxitlán, the first Spanish town council in western New Spain, and the Indian town of Santiago de Tecomán was laid two leagues away, with a hospital of Saint James recorded from about 1550. The Spanish town was moved to its present inland site on 20 January 1527, and Caxitlán slowly declined until a fire in October 1800 destroyed its parish church. In 1812 the insurgent captains Pedro and Manuel Regalado took Tecomán and Caxitlán and sacked the royal salt works of San Pantaleón.
zh:
特科曼位于科利马炎热的沿海平原，群山在此俯临潟湖与太平洋；居住于此的特科斯人说纳瓦特尔语，他们把这片河谷经营成王国的腹地，首领的驻地设在卡希特兰。1444年，科利曼是西部海岸最强大的势力：渔民在沿岸潟湖中捕捞，盐田所产的食盐输往内陆，而东山之外的普雷佩查卡松西正觊觎着同一段海岸。不出一代人的时间，他的军队就会为这些硝石滩杀来，却被击退。

1480至1510年的硝石战争中，科利莫特尔率领特科斯人击败普雷佩查，使科利马成为这一地区的首强。他们还接连击退最早的几支西班牙远征军：胡安·罗德里格斯·德·比亚富埃尔特在特罗赫斯中伏，胡安·阿尔瓦雷斯·奇科战死山隘，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德在特科曼附近的阿利马山口落败，直到贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔佯退设伏，于1523年在阿利马将其击溃。1523年7月25日，桑多瓦尔在卡希特兰建立科利马镇，这是新西班牙西部第一个西班牙市镇议会；两里格外另设印第安人城镇圣地亚哥·德·特科曼，约1550年起已有供奉圣地亚哥的医院。1527年1月20日，西班牙人的城镇迁往今日内陆城址，卡希特兰日渐衰败，1800年10月的一场大火又烧毁了它的堂区教堂。1812年，起义军首领佩德罗·雷加拉多与曼努埃尔·雷加拉多兄弟攻占特科曼和卡希特兰，洗劫了王家的圣潘塔莱昂盐场。

en:
Yohualtepec was the Nahuatl name for a mountain frontier where Guerrero's La Montaña meets the Mixteca and the edge of Puebla. Along the Tlapanec River valley, Tlapanec communities had traded with Mixtec groups since Huamuxtitlán was settled around 1200; Mixtec and Nahua communities also shared the broken country, and some accounts tied Huamuxtitlán to the Mixtec head town of Alcozauca. In 1444 its paths linked Coixtlahuaca and Tlapa, but the Triple Alliance had not yet turned them into an imperial tribute road.

In the second half of the fifteenth century, Triple Alliance armies under Nezahualcoyotl subdued the Tlapanec settlements and made Huamuxtitlán a strongpoint. The surrounding district became part of the tribute province of Yohualtepec, mostly in Oaxaca but reaching into Puebla and Guerrero; the Codex Mendoza records forty gold disks, each the size of a communion wafer. After the Spanish conquest Bernardino Vázquez de Tapia received Huamuxtitlán as an encomienda in 1531. Augustinians founded the convent of Santa María de la Asunción in 1534, using stone from the old temple, and the mountain parishes remained within New Spain until 1821.
zh:
约瓦尔特佩克是纳瓦特尔语对一片山地边区的称呼，位于格雷罗拉蒙塔尼亚、米斯特卡和普埃布拉边缘交会之处。特拉帕内克河沿岸，特拉帕内克人约从1200年起在瓦穆斯特特兰定居，并同米斯特克人贸易；崎岖山地中还混居着米斯特克人和纳瓦人，也有记载把瓦穆斯特特兰与米斯特克首领城镇阿尔科绍卡联系起来。1444年，这里的山路连接科伊斯特拉瓦坎和特拉帕，但三方同盟尚未把它变成帝国贡道。

15世纪后半叶，内萨瓦尔科约特尔麾下的三方同盟军队征服特拉帕内克聚落，把瓦穆斯特特兰建成堡垒。周边地区后来成为约瓦尔特佩克贡赋省的一部分，其大部在瓦哈卡，另有小片土地伸入普埃布拉和格雷罗；《门多萨手抄本》记载该省缴纳四十个圣饼大小的金盘。西班牙征服后，贝尔纳迪诺·巴斯克斯·德·塔皮亚于1531年获得瓦穆斯特特兰监护权。1534年，奥斯定会修士建立圣母升天修道院，并拆用旧神庙石料；这些山区教区此后一直属于新西班牙，直到1821年。

en:
Teotitlan, 'between the houses of the gods' in Nahuatl, guarded the mouth of the Oaxacan Canada, the steep corridor joining the Puebla highlands to the tropical lowlands. The town itself was Nahua, home of the Nonoalca, set amid Mazatec and Cuicatec villagers, and towns such as Huautla and Nanahuatipam stood subject to it. Three priest-lords governed, the chief called Teuctlamacaz, serving Cihuacoatl and a local form of Xipe Totec, and its workshops wove cloth carried as far as Guatemala. A report drawn up in 1581 remembered Teotitlan as an independent republic, allied to Moctezuma but paying no tribute, and in 1444 it still held that frontier rank between the Aztec world and the chiefdoms of the south.

Late in the fifteenth century, under Axayacatl, the town rebelled against Tenochtitlan and was stormed; its old Cuicatec inhabitants were killed or driven out and Mexica colonists took their place, which is why the Spaniards later found a Nahuatl-speaking town there. Under the viceroys it became Teotitlan del Camino, named for the royal road that ran from Tehuacan and Puebla down to Antequera, the gateway post through which travellers entered the Canada. A district seat under the Intendancy of Oaxaca, it entered independent Mexico in 1821.
zh:
特奥蒂特兰在纳瓦语中意为「众神之屋之间」，扼守瓦哈卡卡尼亚达峡谷的入口，这条险峻通道连接普埃布拉高原与热带低地。城本身是纳瓦人诺诺阿尔卡人的居所，周围是马萨特克人与奎卡特克人的村寨，瓦乌特兰、纳纳瓦蒂潘等镇都受它统属。三位祭司首领治理此城，为首者称特乌克拉马卡斯，供奉西瓦科亚特尔和当地化身的希佩托特克；织坊出产的布匹远销至危地马拉。1581年的一份记述回忆，特奥蒂特兰是独立的共和国，与蒙特苏马结盟而不纳贡；1444年它仍保有这种边疆地位，处在阿兹特克世界与南方诸酋邦之间。

15世纪末，在阿萨亚卡特尔在位时期，特奥蒂特兰起兵反叛特诺奇蒂特兰，城陷后旧有的奎卡特克居民或遭屠戮或被驱逐，墨西加殖民者取而代之，这也是西班牙人后来在此见到一座纳瓦语城镇的原因。总督时期，它得名特奥蒂特兰-德尔卡米诺，即「大道上的特奥蒂特兰」，成为从特瓦坎、普埃布拉通往安特克拉的王家大道上的门户驿站，旅人由此进入卡尼亚达峡谷。它作为瓦哈卡行政区下的区治，于1821年并入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
The mountains around Xocotla, on the rainy eastern slope of Citlaltepetl, were the country of the Cuauhtochca Totonacs, who had come down from the Puebla sierra and grouped their villages, among them the old Tetlalpa, into the chiefdom of Cuauhtochco. They burned incense before their gods with offerings of flowers and birds, and their priests taught the village children, while the snows of the great volcano looked over maize lands and cloud-forest hamlets on the road between the central plateau and the Gulf coast. In 1444 these valleys still answered to their own lords, though the armies of Moctezuma I were already closing on the region.

About 1454 a son of Netzahualcoyotl, leading the forces of the Triple Alliance, conquered the Cuauhtochco country and bound it under heavy tribute. In 1520 the mountain towns rose and killed more than a hundred passing Spaniards, and in November 1521, after the fall of Tenochtitlan, Gonzalo de Sandoval marched through and subdued them; under the encomienda the survivors paid tribute in cotton and cacao. In 1597 fifteen Spanish families were settled here as San Juan Coscomatepec, and some of their kin later helped to found the nearby city of Cordoba. In October 1813, during the insurgency, Nicolas Bravo and six hundred men broke a royalist siege of the town that had lasted thirty-three days. It joined independent Mexico in 1821.
zh:
索科特拉群山位于奥里萨巴山多雨的东坡，是夸赫托奇科托托纳克人的故土。他们从普埃布拉山地迁来，把特拉拉尔帕等旧村落并入名为夸赫托奇科的酋长国；他们焚香祭神，以鲜花和飞鸟为供，祭司兼任村塾的教师。大火山的雪线俯视着玉米地和云雾林中的村寨，一条连接中央高原与墨西哥湾沿岸的道路穿境而过。1444年，这些山谷仍听命于本地首领，而蒙特苏马一世的军队已在步步逼近。

约1454年，内萨瓦尔科约特尔之子率领三国同盟的军队征服夸赫托奇科之地，科以沉重贡赋。1520年，山区诸镇起事，杀死一百多名路过的西班牙人；1521年11月特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔进军此地将其平定，在委托监护制下改以棉花和可可纳贡。1597年，十五户西班牙家庭在此定居，建立圣胡安·科斯科马特佩克，后来其中几户人家还参与了邻近科尔多瓦城的创建。1813年10月独立战争期间，尼古拉斯·布拉沃率六百名起义军打破了王党军对该镇长达三十三天的围困。1821年，此地并入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
Mitla guards the upper Tlacolula valley, the eastern arm of the central valleys of Oaxaca. The Zapotecs knew it as Lyobaa, the 'place of rest', and as Monte Albán lost power it grew into the chief religious centre of the Zapotec world, a gateway between the living and the dead. Mixtec rulers took the town around 1000, but its Zapotec priests kept their authority, and in 1444 it is a largely autonomous holy city under the kings of Zaachila, its palace walls faced with precise stone mosaic fretwork found nowhere else in Mexico.

The high priest Uija-tào still held the sanctuary when the Spaniards reached the valley in 1521, and the friar Motolinía described its temples within a generation. Later in the sixteenth century Bishop Bernardo de Albuquerque had the ancient palaces dismantled, determined to break their hold on the faithful; the church of San Pablo was raised on one of the sacred quadrangles, its monolithic lintels and dressed stone taken from Zapotec halls. Diego García de Palacio described the ruins in 1576. The new pueblo of San Pablo Villa de Mitla grew up around the church on the road from Antequera to Tehuantepec, while the greca mosaics of the abandoned palaces survived as the most famous work of Zapotec stonemasons.
zh:
米特拉扼守着瓦哈卡中央谷地东支特拉科卢拉谷的上游。萨波特克人称它为略奥瓦，意为「安息之地」；阿尔班山失势后，这里成为萨波特克世界最重要的宗教中心，被视为生者与死者之间的门户。约1000年，米斯特克君主夺取此城，萨波特克祭司却仍保有权威。1444年，它是萨奇拉诸王治下一座高度自治的圣城，宫殿墙面镶嵌着墨西哥其他地方见不到的、精密拼合的石刻回纹。

1521年西班牙人进入谷地时，大祭司乌伊哈-塔奥仍主持着圣所，修士莫托利尼亚在一代人之后就记述了这里的庙宇。16世纪后期，主教贝尔纳多·德·阿尔武尔克尔克下令拆毁古宫殿，决意斩断旧信仰对信徒的维系；圣巴勃罗教堂建在一处神圣庭院之上，整块巨石的横梁和修凿的石料都取自萨波特克殿堂。迭戈·加西亚·德·帕拉西奥1576年留下了对废墟的记载。新的圣巴勃罗·米特拉村在教堂周围形成，坐落于安特克拉通往特万特佩克的大道旁；废弃宫殿里的回纹镶嵌石幸存下来，成为萨波特克石匠最负盛名的杰作。

en:
The Tzotzil, whose name means the 'people of the bat', occupy the cold pine-clad ridges and valleys of Los Altos, the highlands of Chiapas. Their ancestors had settled there by the early centuries of the first millennium, and on the eve of the conquest their country was divided among at least seven small lordships: Zinacantán was the strongest, with Chamula, Huixtán and others beside it, each lord enthroned in a fortified hilltop town. They wove cotton, worked amber, drew salt from wells near Ixtapa and sent quetzal feathers and amber north to Tenochtitlan. In 1444 the highland towns were free, quarrelsome and rich by the measure of the sierra.

In December 1522 Cuzcácuatl, lord of Zinacantán, travelled to the Spanish town of Espíritu Santo on the Gulf coast to offer an alliance, and at Easter 1524 Luis Marín's expedition, guided and fed by Zinacantec warriors, subdued the rival lordships; the people of Chamula and Huixtán abandoned their towns and fled into the mountains rather than serve. Encomiendas soon parcelled the survivors out, and on 31 March 1528 Diego de Mazariegos founded Villa Real de Chiapa, raised in 1536 to Ciudad Real de Chiapa, the seat of Spanish power over the highland towns; in 1543 Bartolomé de las Casas arrived there as first bishop of Chiapa. Heavy tribute and a new Indian cult at Cancuc brought thirty-two Tzeltal, Tzotzil and Ch'ol towns out in revolt in June 1712, the rebels calling themselves 'soldiers of the Virgin'; royal troops retook Cancuc on 21 November and crushed the rising with great severity.
zh:
索西人的族名原意是「蝙蝠人」，世居恰帕斯中部高寒的松林山脊与谷地之间。他们的祖先早在公元后最初几个世纪已到此定居；西班牙征服前夕，这片土地分裂为至少七个小邦，齐纳坎坦最强，另有查穆拉、维斯坦等，各邦君主坐镇筑垒的山头城镇。他们织棉布、制琥珀，从伊斯塔帕附近的盐井取盐，又把格查尔鸟羽毛和琥珀北销特诺奇蒂特兰。1444年，这些高原城镇自由、好斗，以山地的标准算得上富庶。

1522年12月，齐纳坎坦首领库斯卡夸特尔远赴墨西哥湾沿岸的西班牙人城镇圣灵镇求盟；1524年复活节，路易斯·马林的远征队靠齐纳坎坦战士引路供粮，征服了敌对各邦，查穆拉和维斯坦的居民则弃城逃入深山，不愿臣服。幸存者很快被编进监护征赋制分给征服者。1528年3月31日，迭戈·德·马萨列戈斯建立恰帕皇家镇，1536年升格为恰帕王城，成为西班牙人统辖高原诸城的中心；1543年，巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯到此就任恰帕首任主教。沉重的贡赋与坎库克兴起的印第安人新崇拜，终于在1712年6月激起三十二个特塞尔塔尔、索西和乔尔人城镇起事，起义者自称「圣母的士兵」；王家军队于11月21日攻陷坎库克，残酷镇压了暴动。

en:
On the high north-western shelf of the Cuchumatanes, above the river frontier with Chiapas, lies the Jacaltenango plateau, the Huista country of the Jakaltek Maya, who call themselves Popti'. Their chief town Xajlaj — Jacaltenango, 'the place of the great white rock slabs' — stood where trails from the Petén lowlands met the paths climbing from the Pacific coast, and its market drew the scattered villages around. The natural wall of the sierra kept the highland empires at arm's length, though local tradition remembers K'iche' war parties pushing this far during the reign of K'iq'ab the Great (1425–1475). In 1444 the Jakaltek towns kept their own lords and their own Q'anjob'alan tongue.

The conquest was quick but the new rule stayed distant: in 1529 Jacaltenango, together with San Mateo Ixtatán and Santa Eulalia, was granted in encomienda to Gonzalo de Ovalle, one of Alvarado's companions, and a town of some two thousand Indians became his estate. Dominicans carried out the first reducción there in 1549; the Mercedarians later traded their lowland doctrines for the Cuchumatanes, formed their Guatemalan province in 1565 and raised the convent of Nuestra Señora de la Purificación in 1567. Beyond the doctrines the forest frontier remained dangerous, as independent Lacandones raided all through the seventeenth century and forced the Spanish to garrison the northern towns. By about 1690 the chronicler Fuentes y Guzmán found Jacaltenango shrunk to eight hundred people, 'an ancient and principal place, the court of some cacique'; in 1754 the Bourbon reforms took the doctrine from the Mercedarians and handed it to the secular clergy.
zh:
哈卡尔特克人自称波普蒂人，居住在库丘马塔内斯山西北缘的高台地上，脚下就是与恰帕斯分界的河谷。他们的首镇哈伊拉赫——即西班牙人所称的哈卡尔特南戈，意为「巨大白石板之地」——正处在佩滕低地山道与太平洋沿岸上山路的交汇处，集市吸引着周围分散的村落。群山这道天然屏障把高原帝国挡在远处，不过当地相传，在基卡布大王（1425—1475年在位）的时代，基切人的战阵也曾推进到这里。1444年，哈卡尔特克诸城仍奉自己的首领、说自己的坎霍瓦尔兰语。

征服来得很快，统治却很疏阔：1529年，哈卡尔特南戈连同圣马特奥-伊斯塔坦、圣欧拉利娅一起被作为监护地封给阿尔瓦拉多的部将贡萨洛·德·奥瓦列，这座约有两千印第安人的城镇成了他的私产。1549年，多明我会在此完成第一次集村归化；后来仁慈圣母会用低地教区换得库丘马塔内斯的教区，1565年其危地马拉会省成立，1567年建起净礼圣母修道院。教区之外，林缘始终不太平：整个17世纪，独立的拉坎东人不断入袭，西班牙人被迫在北部诸城驻军。到1690年前后，编年史家富恩特斯-古斯曼见到的哈卡尔特南戈已缩至八百人，是「古老而首要之地，曾为某位酋长的宫廷」；1754年，波旁改革把这一教区从仁慈圣母会手中收归世俗教士。

en:
Q'umarkaj, called Utatlán in Nahuatl, was founded around 1400 on a defensible plateau beside the older K'iche' center of Pismachi'. Temples to Tohil, Awilix, Jakawitz and Q'uq'umatz stood around its main plaza, with the palaces of the Kaweq, Nijaib and other ruling lineages nearby. By 1444 K'iq'ab ruled there at the head of the K'iche'-Kaqchikel alliance. His highland wars had brought Rabinal, Cobán and Quetzaltenango under Q'umarkaj, while Kaqchikel support helped carry K'iche' power east to the Motagua River and south toward the Pacific cacao lands around Escuintla. The capital was then near the height of its power, drawing tribute and military service from subject peoples and allied clans.

The long expansion ended in 1470, when two sons of K'iq'ab rose during a great assembly, killed Kaqchikel warriors and Kaweq nobles, and forced the king to surrender power to rebel lords. The new government turned on the Kaqchikel, who withdrew to Iximché; after K'iq'ab died in 1475, a K'iche' attack under Tepepul ended in disaster, and Tekum was later killed fighting the Tz'utujil by Lake Atitlán. In March 1524, after Pedro de Alvarado defeated a K'iche' army in the Quetzaltenango valley and Tecún Umán fell there, the city's lords invited the Spanish to Q'umarkaj. Alvarado suspected a trap, seized the two principal rulers in his camp, burned them alive and destroyed the city. The Spanish then founded nearby Santa Cruz del Quiché, where Dominicans reused ruined stones in churches and a cathedral while former Q'umarkaj lords were reduced to peasant status. In 1638 Santa Cruz formed part of the Dominican doctrine based at Sacapulas, until the Bourbon reform of 1754 transferred the Indian parishes to secular clergy; the district remained in Spanish Guatemala until independence in 1821.
zh:
库马尔卡赫在纳瓦特尔语中称乌塔特兰，约1400年建在一座易守难攻的高原上，紧邻更古老的基切中心皮斯马奇。主广场周围矗立着托希尔、阿维利什、贾卡维茨和库库马茨的神庙，卡韦克、尼哈伊布等统治氏族的宫殿就在近旁。到1444年，基克阿布已在此以基切—卡克奇克尔同盟首领的身份统治。他的高地战争使拉比纳尔、科万和克萨尔特南戈臣服于库马尔卡赫；在卡克奇克尔人支持下，基切势力东抵莫塔瓜河，向南延伸到埃斯昆特拉一带的太平洋可可产地。此时的库马尔卡赫正接近权力顶峰，向被征服民族和同盟氏族征取贡赋与兵役。

长期扩张在1470年告终：基克阿布的两个儿子在一次大集会期间举事，杀死许多卡克奇克尔战士和卡韦克贵族，迫使国王向叛党首领让权。新掌权者转而敌视卡克奇克尔人，后者退往伊希姆契；1475年基克阿布死后，特佩普尔率军进攻伊希姆契却惨败，后来特库姆又在阿蒂特兰湖畔与楚图希尔人作战时身亡。1524年3月，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多在克萨尔特南戈谷地击败基切军队，特昆·乌曼也在该役战死后，库马尔卡赫的首领邀请西班牙人入城。阿尔瓦拉多担心中计，在营中擒获两名最高首领，将他们活活烧死并摧毁城市。西班牙人随后在附近建立圣克鲁斯-德尔基切，多明我会拆用遗址石材修建教堂和大教堂，昔日库马尔卡赫贵族则被降为农民。1638年，圣克鲁斯属于以萨卡普拉斯为中心的多明我会传教区；1754年波旁改革将印第安教区转交世俗教士。这一地区此后仍属西属危地马拉，直到1821年独立。

en:
The Kobox, or Kob'ox and also written Couoh, were a Maya people related to the Itzá, set across the broad forested karst corridor between the Yucatán plain and the Petén lakes. Spanish accounts also called the northern people of this route Kejache. Kindred Maya groups had moved south from Mayapán around 1300. In 1444, as the northern league broke apart, the woods here held fortified villages and refugee kin groups linked by overland and canoe trade between the Yucatec chiefdoms and the independent Itzá power around Lake Petén Itzá.

Hernán Cortés crossed this country in 1525 on his way to Honduras and found Kejache towns built on defensible ground, some with palisades, walls, and moats. Alonso Dávila crossed the northern part in 1531. By about 1600 the Kejache numbered perhaps 7,000 in ten to twenty settlements, receiving Yucatec refugees and acting as middlemen between Spanish Yucatán and the still-independent Petén Maya. Missions were established at Ichbalche and Tzuktok along a road pushed south from Campeche. Martín de Ursúa y Arizmendi's expedition then used the Yucatán route to capture Nojpetén in 1697, ending the independent Itzá and Kob'ox world; many survivors withdrew deeper into the Lacandón forest.
zh:
科博赫人即文献中的Kob'ox，又写作Couoh，是与伊察人有亲缘关系的玛雅群体，活动在尤卡坦平原与佩滕湖群之间广阔的石灰岩森林走廊。西班牙记载也把这条通道北部的居民称为克哈切人。约1300年起，与他们相近的玛雅群体陆续从马亚潘南迁。1444年，北方联盟正走向瓦解，这片森林中分布着设防村社和避难亲族，陆路与独木舟贸易把尤卡坦诸政权同佩滕伊察湖畔仍保持独立的伊察势力连接起来。

1525年，埃尔南·科尔特斯前往洪都拉斯时穿过此地，发现克哈切人的城镇建在易守难攻之处，有些还设有木栅、城墙和壕沟。1531年，阿隆索·达维拉穿过其北部。到1600年前后，克哈切人约有七千，分布在十至二十个定居点中；他们接纳尤卡坦难民，并在西班牙统治下的尤卡坦与仍独立的佩滕玛雅人之间充当中介。沿从坎佩切向南开辟的道路，西班牙人在伊奇巴尔切和楚克托克建立传教站。1697年，马丁·德·乌尔苏亚·阿里斯门迪的远征军沿尤卡坦路线攻占诺赫佩滕，独立的伊察与科博赫世界终结，许多幸存者退入拉坎东森林深处。

en:
Moran names the wet Caribbean slope between Chetumal, the Petén lakes and the Polochic-Izabal lowlands. Rivers such as the New, Belize, Sibun and Macal cut through forest and the Maya Mountains, carrying canoes between the coast, Lamanai and Tipu. Tipu became the chief town of Dzuluinicob, a Postclassic Maya province whose material culture was closer to Petén than to northern Yucatán and which may have grown after Mayapan's fall. In 1444 its Putún-connected Maya towns kept cacao orchards and river trade on the frontier between Chactemal and the Itza, untouched by Spanish conquest.

Cortés crossed the Mopan and Manche lowlands in 1525. The Pacheco entrada of 1543–1544 defeated Dzuluinicob with unusual brutality and attached it to the new Bacalar district, where Franciscans made Lamanai and Tipu mission towns. After decades of tribute demands, famine and flight, Tipu rose in 1638; within a few years Spanish power collapsed across Dzuluinicob, and Bacalar lost most of its Maya population. Tipu stayed autonomous until 1695, served Spanish operations against the Itza in 1696, and after Nojpetén fell in 1697 its people were forcibly removed to Lake Petén Itzá in 1707. English Baymen meanwhile turned the Belize River into a logwood and mahogany frontier; treaties of 1783 and 1786 regularised their holdings, and their victory off St George's Caye on 10 September 1798 ended the last Spanish effort to dislodge them.
zh:
莫兰指查克特马尔、佩滕湖区与波洛奇克—伊萨瓦尔低地之间这片加勒比湿润坡地。纽河、伯利兹河、西本河、马卡尔河等河流穿过雨林和玛雅山，独木舟沿水路往来于海岸、拉马奈与蒂普之间。蒂普是后古典期马雅政区Dzuluinicob的首要城镇，该政区的物质文化更接近佩滕而非北尤卡坦，可能是在马亚潘瓦解后兴起。1444年，这里与普屯人有关的马雅村镇经营可可园和河上贸易，处在查克特马尔与伊察之间的边地上，尚未遭到西班牙征服。

1525年，科尔特斯穿过莫潘与曼切低地。1543—1544年，帕切科家族的远征以异常残酷的方式击败Dzuluinicob，将其并入新设的巴卡拉尔辖区，方济各会随后把拉马奈和蒂普变成传教城镇。在数十年贡赋、饥荒和逃亡之后，蒂普于1638年起事；数年间，西班牙权力在整个Dzuluinicob崩溃，巴卡拉尔也失去大部分马雅人口。蒂普一直保持自治到1695年，1696年被西班牙用作进攻伊察人的前沿据点；1697年诺赫佩滕陷落后，蒂普居民于1707年被强行迁往佩滕湖畔。与此同时，英国「湾民」把伯利兹河变成染木和桃花心木边疆；1783年和1786年的条约确认了他们的采伐权，1798年9月10日，他们在圣乔治岛外海取胜，终结了西班牙驱逐他们的最后尝试。

en:
The Xiu province had its capital at Maní, a town founded by the Xiu lineage between 1224 and 1247 as their power shifted from Uxmal. The family had once held first place in the League of Mayapan, but by 1300 the Cocom and their Canul guards controlled the city, and many Xiu were expelled around 1400. From 1441 to 1461 Ah Xupan Xiu led the war that destroyed Mayapan and overthrew the Cocom royal house. In 1444 Maní was therefore becoming the center of the strongest western Yucatec polity, with Na, Ku, Dzul, Tun and other lineages settled within the Xiu province.

The old feud with the Cocom shaped the Spanish conquest. In 1535 a Xiu party that had received Cocom permission to sacrifice at the sacred cenote of Chichén Itzá was deceived and ambushed. During Montejo's final campaign of 1541-42, the Xiu lord of Maní submitted and converted to Catholicism, and his example encouraged the western provinces to accept Spanish rule. On 12 July 1562, after a clandestine shrine was uncovered, the Franciscan Diego de Landa held an auto de fe beside the monastery of San Miguel Arcángel in Maní, burning many Maya codices and cult images; torture and coercion speeded mass conversion. Landa was recalled to face investigation, was absolved, and returned as bishop of Yucatán in 1572, while Maní remained a colonial head town under its Franciscan monastery.
zh:
休人辖区以马尼为首府。1224年至1247年间，休家族在势力从乌斯马尔转移的过程中建立此城。该家族曾在玛雅潘联盟中居于首位，但到1300年前后，玛雅潘已由科科姆人和他们的卡努尔戍卫控制，约1400年又有大批休人被逐。1441年至1461年，阿·苏潘·休领导战争摧毁玛雅潘，推翻科科姆王室。因此到1444年，马尼正成为西尤卡坦最强大政权的中心，纳、库、祖尔、通等家族也居住在休人辖区内。

与科科姆人的旧怨深刻影响了西班牙征服。1535年，一队休人获科科姆人允许，前往奇琴伊察圣井举行祭祀，却遭到诱骗和伏击。1541—1542年蒙特霍最后一次征伐期间，马尼的休人首领归附并改宗天主教，他的先例促使西部各辖区接受西班牙统治。1562年7月12日，一处秘密祭坛被发现后，方济各会士迭戈·德·兰达在马尼的圣米格尔修道院旁举行信仰判决，焚毁大量玛雅抄本和神像；酷刑与胁迫加速了集体改宗。兰达后来被召回受审，获释后于1572年以尤卡坦主教身份返回，马尼则在方济各会修道院旁继续作为殖民时期的首镇。

en:
Chikinchel, also called Chauacá after its principal town, was the salt country of northeastern Yucatán: lagoons, marshes, hunting grounds, and a long northern shore between Ah Kin Chel, Cupul, Tases, and Ekab. As Mayapán collapsed between 1441 and 1461, this coast became one of the Maya kuchkabalob, though it was never a tightly united province. In 1444 the rival towns of Chauaca, Sinsimato, and Dzonotaké guarded the peninsula's richest salt workings from outsiders, while leading men kept to healthier villages along the coast.

In 1517 Francisco Hernández de Córdoba's expedition reached the estuary later called Río Lagartos while searching for fresh water. On 28 May 1543 the Montejo conquest government founded Valladolid at Chauac-Há in Chikinchel, laid out the Spanish town, and granted encomiendas to forty-five conquistadors. Mosquitoes, humidity, and marsh fever made the site unbearable, and on 24 March 1545 the villa was moved to Zací, a Cupul town farther inland. The Spanish settlement stayed in Chikinchel for less than two years, but the encomiendas assigned at its founding tied Chauacá's salt beds and hunting lands to colonial eastern Yucatán.
zh:
奇金切尔又称乔阿卡，后者是其主要城镇的名字。这里是尤卡坦东北部的盐乡，潟湖、沼泽、猎场和漫长北岸夹在阿金切尔、库普尔、塔塞斯和埃卡布之间。1441年至1461年马亚潘崩溃时，这片海岸成为玛雅库奇卡巴尔辖区之一，但从未形成紧密统一的政权。1444年，乔阿卡、辛西马托和佐诺塔凯等彼此竞争的城镇把守着半岛最富饶的盐场，不许外来者染指；首领们则多住在海岸一带较宜居住的村落里。

1517年，弗朗西斯科·埃尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦的探险队为寻找淡水，抵达后来被称为里奥拉加托斯的河口。1543年5月28日，蒙特霍征服政权在奇金切尔的乔阿克-阿建立巴利亚多利德，规划西班牙城镇，并向四十五名征服者分配监护征赋权。蚊虫、湿热和沼泽热病使这里难以居住，1545年3月24日，这座城镇迁往更内陆的库普尔城镇萨西。西班牙人在奇金切尔设城不到两年，但建城时分封的监护征赋权已把乔阿卡的盐场和猎地纳入殖民时期尤卡坦东部的秩序。

en:
In 1444 Ulva was the river country of the Ulwa, the southern Sumu people. Settlements followed the Río Grande de Matagalpa and Río Escondido, including the Tuma, Siquia and Mico tributaries that run from the central highlands toward Caribbean lagoons. Ulwa families fished, hunted, cleared riverside fields and travelled by dugout canoe, their territory forming a network of basins rather than a fixed frontier. Miskito communities lived to the north, Matagalpa-speaking highlanders to the west, and Kukra and Rama groups nearer the southern bays; no European post yet interrupted that river world.

Christopher Columbus's fourth voyage passed the Mosquito Shore in 1502, but outside power reached these rivers only indirectly. In the early seventeenth century Dutch and English privateers began using the Escondido and Bluefields anchorages, while British contacts after the 1630s gave Miskito allies firearms. Miskito raiders penetrated the interior to seize Ulwa and Mayangna captives, selling men toward Jamaica and incorporating many women, a trade that pulled Ulwa communities toward more isolated headwaters. Spanish missionaries and colonial officials reached the western basins in the eighteenth century, yet alliances shifted from village to village. Yarrince, an Ulwa leader from Olama, first cooperated with the British and then accepted Spanish rank as a captain-governor; he was imprisoned in 1780 and died the same year in Guatemala. The 1786 Convention of London removed British settlers without making Spanish rule firm, and after Miskito forces drove the Spanish out in 1800, the Ulwa river basins were still effectively their own in 1821.
zh:
1444年的乌尔瓦是乌尔瓦人的河网之地。乌尔瓦人是南部苏穆语人群，村落沿马塔加尔帕大河与埃斯孔迪多河展开，也分布在图马河、西基亚河和米科河等从中部高地流向加勒比潟湖的支流。乌尔瓦家庭捕鱼、狩猎、清理河畔田地，并乘独木舟往来；他们的疆域不是固定边界，而是一串相连的河流盆地。北方是米斯基托社群，西方是说马塔加尔帕语的高地人，南部港湾附近则有库克拉人和拉马人；当时还没有欧洲据点切入这个河上世界。

1502年，哥伦布第四次航行经过莫斯基托海岸，但外部势力并未直接深入这些河川。17世纪初，荷兰和英格兰私掠者开始利用埃斯孔迪多河与布卢菲尔兹锚地；1630年代以后同英国人的接触使米斯基托同盟者获得火器。米斯基托袭掠者深入内陆捉拿乌尔瓦人和马扬格纳人，把男子卖向牙买加，又把许多女子并入本社群，这种奴隶贸易迫使乌尔瓦社群向更偏远的河源退却。18世纪，西班牙传教士和殖民官吏进入西部河流盆地，但各村庄的同盟反复变化。奥拉马的乌尔瓦首领亚林塞先同英国人合作，后来又接受西班牙授予的军政长官职衔；他在1780年入狱，同年死于危地马拉。1786年《伦敦公约》撤走英国移民，却没有稳固西班牙统治；1800年米斯基托军队驱逐西班牙人后，到1821年，乌尔瓦各河流盆地实际上仍掌握在本地人手中。

en:
Xicaque is the Spanish exonym for the Tolupan country on the central Honduran coast. Its beaches, lagoons and river mouths ran from the Ulúa toward Puerto Castilla, with the forested ridges of Yoro and the Sulaco headwaters rising inland. In 1444 Tolupan-speaking villages and mobile bands cultivated bitter manioc and maize, hunted and fished, and used dugout canoes to carry maize and the cochineal cactus between Tela Bay, the rivers and the interior. Local headmen led their own settlements; there was no single capital, and no European fleet had yet anchored off the shore.

On 3 May 1524 Cristóbal de Olid established one of the earliest Spanish settlements in Honduras beside the native town of Tehuacán in Tela Bay, whose local leader the Spanish called Cucumba. The date was the feast of the Cross, and a nearby promontory became known as Triunfo de la Cruz; within months the small municipality was dissolved and the district placed under Trujillo. Spanish control remained light, and independent Tolupan groups still formed part of the forest frontier later called Taguzgalpa. At the end of the sixteenth century buccaneers haunted Tela Bay, hunting Spanish schooners carrying precious metals from Trujillo and Puerto Caballos; Franciscan reducciones began early in the next century, and in 1609 some Tolupans had settled as far inland as the Guayape and Guayambre valleys. After the British deported Black Caribs to Roatán in 1797, Garifuna families spread along the coast and founded Triunfo de la Cruz and San Juan near Tela in 1808. In 1821 the shore remained a mixed Tolupan, Garifuna and thinly settled Spanish frontier.
zh:
希卡克是西班牙人对托卢潘人土地的他称，位于洪都拉斯中北部海岸。海滩、潟湖和河口从乌卢阿河一带延伸向卡斯蒂利亚港，内陆则是约罗的林脊和苏拉克河源头。1444年，说托卢潘语的村社和流动群体种植苦木薯与玉米，兼营狩猎和渔捞，并乘独木舟把玉米和胭脂虫仙人掌运到特拉湾、各河流与内陆之间。各地由本地首领分别管辖，没有统一都城，也还没有欧洲船队在海岸外停泊。

1524年5月3日，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德在特拉湾的原住民城镇特瓦坎旁建立洪都拉斯最早的西班牙据点之一；西班牙人把当地首领称作库库姆巴。这一天是十字架节日，附近海岬后来得名特里温福·德拉鲁斯。仅数月后，这个小小的市政建制便被撤销，地区划归特鲁希略管辖。西班牙人的控制始终薄弱，独立的托卢潘群体仍属于后来被称作塔古斯加尔帕的森林前沿。16世纪末，巴克尼尔海盗出没特拉湾，猎捕从特鲁希略和卡瓦略斯港运载贵金属的西班牙纵帆船；下一世纪初方济各会开始建立集居传教区，1609年已有部分托卢潘人深入瓜亚佩河与瓜亚姆布雷河谷居住。1797年英国把黑加勒比人流放到罗阿坦岛后，加里富纳家庭沿海岸扩散，并于1808年在特拉附近建立特里温福·德拉鲁斯和圣胡安社区。1821年时，这片海岸仍是托卢潘人、加里富纳人和稀疏西班牙移民共处的边疆。

en:
Tzul covers the rainforest and foothills between Lake Petén Itzá, the Lacandón forest and the Guatemalan highlands, the country Spanish records called Tute. Its rivers linked the Itza lake world with Cahabón, Cobán and the Sierra de los Cuchumatanes; maize fields stood beside cacao, vanilla, achiote and cotton groves. The Tute and Lakandon Ch'ol were forest nations in Kan Ek's outer orbit, sometimes tributary, often dangerous to highland travellers and missionaries. In 1444 they were still entirely beyond Spanish rule, a heathen mountain wall between Nojpetén and the Christian provinces being formed in Verapaz.

Cortés crossed neighbouring Manche Ch'ol country in 1525, and Pedro Ramírez de Quiñones led the first Spanish expedition against the Lakandon in 1559. The Ch'ol later withdrew from Lakam-Tun to the hidden town of Sac Balam around 1586 and kept their independence there into the 1690s. Franciscans Antonio Margil and Melchor López were expelled in 1694, and the great Guatemalan campaign of 1695 opened the forest, baptised more than six hundred families around new Dolores settlements and occupied Sac Balam. After Nojpetén fell on 13 March 1697, the Tute fled before the troops and joined the postwar rising; Spanish prisoners named them among the killers of soldiers and looters of missionary goods. When Kan Ek' was carried to Guatemala in 1699, the Tute were counted among five fugitive Petén kingdoms, led by men named Chachulté, Chaues, Buenavista, Chatoco and Ixmucuyl. In 1712 the surviving Lakandon Ch'ol were forcibly removed toward Huehuetenango; the Tute then vanished from colonial records as a separate people.
zh:
楚尔（Tzul）位于佩滕湖、拉坎东丛林与危地马拉高地之间，是一片雨林与山麓交错地带，西班牙文献称之为图特。各条河川把伊察人的湖区世界同卡瓦翁、科万和库丘马塔内斯山脉连接起来；玉米地旁分布着可可、香荚兰、胭脂树和棉花种植园。图特人与拉坎东乔尔人是卡内克势力外圈的森林族群，有时纳贡，也常令高地商旅和传教士视为畏途。1444年时，他们仍完全不受西班牙统治，如同诺赫佩滕与正在韦拉帕斯形成的基督教辖区之间一道异教山林屏障。

1525年，科尔特斯穿过相邻的曼切乔尔地区；1559年，佩德罗·拉米雷斯·德·基尼奥内斯率领第一支征讨拉坎东人的西班牙远征队。1586年前后，乔尔人放弃拉坎-通，退入隐秘新城萨克巴兰，并在那里把独立维持到1690年代。1694年，方济各会士安东尼奥·马希尔和梅尔乔·洛佩斯被驱逐；1695年，危地马拉发动大规模进军，打开森林，在新建的多洛雷斯聚居点为六百多个家庭施洗，并占领萨克巴兰。1697年3月13日诺赫佩滕陷落后，图特人在军队逼近时逃散，并加入战后的起事；西班牙俘虏指称他们参与杀害士兵、劫掠传教士器物。1699年卡内克被押往危地马拉，图特人被列为五个继续逃亡的佩滕小王国之一，其首领名为查丘尔特、查韦斯、布埃纳维斯塔、查托科和伊什穆奎尔。1712年，幸存的拉坎东乔尔人被强行迁往韦韦特南戈一带；图特人随后也不再作为独立群体见于殖民记录。

en:
The land called Guaymi takes in the island-studded waters of Almirante Bay and Chiriquí Lagoon, backed by wet rain-forest highlands. In 1444 the Atlantic Ngäbe lived here in dispersed villages led by chiefs and powerful families; their wider country crossed the isthmus, but they had no single empire or capital. They called themselves Ngäbe, meaning 'people' in Ngäbere, while Guaymí was a later outsider name derived from Buglere.

Christopher Columbus reached these waters on 6 October 1502 while searching for a passage to the Pacific, and a leader named or titled Quibían helped drive the expedition off. Spanish footholds remained fragile: Urracá forced Captain Diego de Albites to make peace in 1522, escaped after being seized and sent to Nombre de Dios, and died a free man in 1531. Castillo de Austria, planted on Almirante Bay in 1560, was abandoned within a year, as was Artieda del Nuevo Reino de Navarra on the Cricamola in 1577–1578. During the following centuries English pirates and Miskito raiders used the lagoons. Pablo Presbere's 1709 rising reached Colón Island, and Spanish records report that a Miskito attack in 1758 destroyed the Tojar community, killing or enslaving about two thousand people. Afro-Caribbean traders settled on Bastimentos in 1817. When the isthmus left Spanish rule in 1821, the Ngäbe remained in their mountains rather than submitting to Gran Colombia.
zh:
称为瓜伊米的土地，包括岛礁散布的阿尔米兰特湾和奇里基潟湖，后方是潮湿的雨林山地。1444年，靠大西洋的恩戈贝人住在分散村落中，由酋长和望族统领；他们的活动范围横越地峡，却没有统一帝国或都城。他们自称恩戈贝，在恩戈贝雷语中意为「人」；瓜伊米则是后来外来者根据布格雷语取的名字。

1502年10月6日，哥伦布在寻找通往太平洋的水道时抵达这片海域，名为或称号为基维安的首领将远征者击退。西班牙人的据点始终脆弱：乌拉卡在1522年迫使迭戈·德·阿尔比特斯队长议和，后来他被押往农布雷-德迪奥斯又逃脱，1531年以自由之身去世。1560年设在阿尔米兰特湾的奥地利堡不足一年即遭放弃，1577年在克里卡莫拉河畔建立的新纳瓦拉王国阿尔铁达也于次年废弃。此后两个世纪，英国海盗和米斯基托袭掠者利用潟湖活动。巴勃罗·普雷斯贝雷1709年的起义波及科隆岛；西班牙记载称，1758年米斯基托人摧毁托哈尔社群，约有两千人被杀或沦为奴隶。1817年，非裔加勒比商人到巴斯蒂门托斯岛定居。1821年地峡脱离西班牙统治时，恩戈贝人仍留在山中，没有向大哥伦比亚屈服。

en:
The green shores of the Gulf of Urabá, where the muddy Atrato pours into the southern Caribbean, were Guna land in 1444. Calling themselves Dule, 'the people', these Chibchan-speakers lived in autonomous villages along the gulf and the lower Atrato, farming maize and yuca, fishing the mangrove lagoons and hunting in the rainforest behind. Their country lay at the neck of the continent, where the Darién isthmus begins, and dugouts carried them between river and sea. No paramount chief ruled them, and no European sail had yet been seen in those waters.

Rodrigo de Bastidas explored the gulf in 1501, the first Spaniard to do so, and on 20 January 1510 Alonso de Ojeda founded San Sebastián de Urabá on its eastern shore near the later town of Necoclí, the first attempted Spanish settlement on the American mainland. The Guna met it with poisoned arrows and wounded Ojeda himself; famine and siege did the rest. When Ojeda sailed away, only 42 of his 300 settlers remained, and he left the young Francisco Pizarro in command. Before the year ended the survivors crossed to the western shore to found Santa María del Darién, and San Sebastián vanished from the maps. No lasting Spanish town ever took root on the gulf: through the rest of the colonial period its coasts remained a neglected frontier of scattered Indian villages, while Guna bands, pressed by Spaniards and warring neighbours, gradually moved off westward towards the San Blas shore.
zh:
1444年，乌拉瓦湾翠绿的海岸是库纳人的土地——浑浊的阿特拉托河在此注入加勒比海的南缘。他们自称杜雷，意为「人」，说奇布查语，在海湾沿岸与阿特拉托河下游的自治村落里种植玉米、木薯，在红树林潟湖中捕鱼，到后方的雨林狩猎。此地正当大陆的咽喉、达连地峡的起点，独木舟载着他们往来于河海之间。他们没有至高的首领，那片水域上也还没有出现过欧洲人的帆影。

1501年，罗德里戈·德·巴斯蒂达斯最先勘察这个海湾；1510年1月20日，阿隆索·德·奥赫达在东岸、后来内科克利所在之处建立圣塞瓦斯蒂安·德·乌拉瓦，这是欧洲人在美洲大陆的第一个定居尝试。库纳人以毒箭相迎，连奥赫达本人也受了伤，饥馑与围攻完成了余下的事。奥赫达乘船离去时，三百名定居者只剩四十二人，他把残局交给年轻的弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗。未到年底，幸存者渡海前往西岸另建圣玛利亚·拉安提瓜·德尔达连，圣塞瓦斯蒂安从地图上消失。整个殖民时代，海湾始终没有长出稳固的西班牙城镇，沿岸长期是一条只有印第安村落零星散布的荒僻边地；在西班牙人和敌对邻族的逼迫下，一部分库纳人陆续西迁，朝圣布拉斯海岸而去。

en:
Talamanca is the rainy Caribbean slope below the Talamanca mountains, running south from Tariaca toward the Changuinola and Sixaola rivers. In 1444 Bribri and Cabécar communities shared these forests with Térraba, Viceita, Terbi and other Viceitic-speaking peoples. Autonomous villages and chiefdoms, not a single empire, governed the country; the Cabécar polity was strongest on Costa Rica's Atlantic side. Mountain terrain and dispersed nations later made the Spaniards call the region rebellious Talamanca.

Christopher Columbus reached Cariay on 25 September 1502, anchoring off Quiribrí, now Isla Uvita, during his fourth voyage, but the wet mountains long prevented occupation. Cabécar leaders Guaycorá and Sumamará burned Santiago de Talamanca in 1610. From 1660 Cartago sent expeditions into the region; some communities submitted two years later for help against English pirates and Miskito raiders, then rebelled against attacks on polygamy and shamanic practice. Slave raiding followed under Juan López de la Flor in 1665, and in 1666 Juan de Vida Martell burned villages and crops and seized more than a hundred people. Franciscans made converts after 1670, but on 29 September 1709 Pablo Presbere led peoples from Chirripó to Almirante Bay in revolt and fourteen mission churches burned. The rising was crushed and Presbere died in 1710, yet Spanish forces withdrew, leaving Talamanca an indigenous refuge; fresh attempts after 1740 had little clear result. When Spanish rule ended in 1821, Bribri and Cabécar lords still held most of the mountains.
zh:
塔拉曼卡位于塔拉曼卡山脉下方的潮湿加勒比坡地，北起塔里亚卡，南至昌吉诺拉河与锡克绍拉河一带。1444年，布里布里人和卡韦卡尔人，与特拉瓦人、维塞塔人、特尔维人及其他维塞伊语族群共居山林。这里没有统一帝国，而是由自治村落和酋长领地分治；卡韦卡尔人的政体是哥斯达黎加大西洋岸最强大的势力。山地地形和分散的诸族群，后来使西班牙人把这里称为反叛的塔拉曼卡。

1502年9月25日，哥伦布第四次航行时抵达卡里亚伊，停泊在基里布里岛（今乌维塔岛）外，但潮湿山地长期阻碍西班牙人占领。1610年，卡韦卡尔首领瓜伊科拉和苏马马拉焚毁圣地亚哥·德·塔拉曼卡。1660年起，卡塔戈不断派远征队进入这一地区；1662年，一些部落为抵御英国海盗和米斯基托袭掠者而接受臣服，却因传教士禁止多偶制和萨满习俗再起反抗。1665年，胡安·洛佩斯·德·拉·弗洛尔转而捕人为奴；1666年，胡安·德·维达·马特尔烧毁村落和庄稼，掳走一百多人。1670年后，方济各会传教士取得一些皈依者，但1709年9月29日，巴勃罗·普雷斯贝雷率领从奇里波到阿尔米兰特湾的诸族群起义，焚毁十四座传教教堂。起义次年遭镇压，普雷斯贝雷丧生，西班牙人却撤出军队，使塔拉曼卡成为原住民避难地；1740年后新的传教和军事行动仍成效不定。1821年西班牙统治终结时，布里布里和卡韦卡尔首领仍控制着大部分山地。

en:
Cuauhtochco was a small lordship in the broken country above Veracruz's Gulf plain, guarding routes between the coast, Puebla and the Mexican highlands. Its land had once formed part of Totonacapan, but a Teochichimeca group with Tlaxcalan connections founded the señorío in 1327. Its chief places were Cuauhtochco itself, later Santiago Huatusco near modern Carrillo Puerto, Otlaquiquixtla on the site of present Huatusco de Chicuéllar, and Tototlán. In 1444 the lordship was still independent, with fewer than five thousand people but a strategic hold on traffic moving inland from the Gulf.

Moctezuma Ilhuicamina conquered Cuauhtochco in 1457, and the town became a Nahuatl-speaking Mexica garrison. After Tenochtitlan fell, Gonzalo de Sandoval stormed the garrison in November 1521. Under Spanish rule it became the corregimiento of Santiago Cuauhtochco; severe depopulation allowed its old pyramid to stand almost forgotten. In the Atoyac lowlands, Indian and African labour on estates and sugar trapiches mixed with Spanish settlement, while the administrative centre shifted toward San Antonio Otlaquiquixtla, called San Antonio Huatusco from 1670. In 1778 the district was placed in the province of Córdoba within the Veracruz intendancy. During the independence war, enslaved people and sugar workers around Atoyac rose after Hidalgo's call, and in 1812 Mariano Mota established an insurgent centre on Cerro del Chiquihuite. In 1813 the Congress of Chilpancingo named Huatusco the insurgent capital of Veracruz.
zh:
夸赫托奇科是韦拉克鲁斯湾平原上方崎岖山地中的一个小领主国，扼守着海岸、普埃布拉与墨西哥高地之间的道路。这里原属托托纳克潘的一部分，但1327年，一支与特拉斯卡拉有关联的特奥奇奇梅卡人群建立了这个领主国。主要据点包括夸赫托奇科本地（即后来今卡里略港附近的圣地亚哥·瓦图斯科）、位于今瓦图斯科—德奇库埃利亚尔的奥特拉基基斯特兰，以及托托特兰。1444年时，该领主国仍然独立，人口不足五千，却控制着从海湾进入内陆的交通要冲。

1457年，蒙特苏马·伊尔维卡米纳征服夸赫托奇科，此地后来成为说纳瓦特尔语的墨西加驻军要塞。特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔于1521年11月攻占这座要塞。西班牙统治时期，这里成为圣地亚哥·夸赫托奇科科雷希米恩托；人口急剧减少，使古老金字塔几乎被遗忘。阿托亚克低地的庄园和蔗糖作坊役使原住民与非洲劳力，并形成印第安人、非洲人和西班牙人混居的社会；行政中心后来转向圣安东尼奥·奥特拉基基斯特兰，1670年起称圣安东尼奥·瓦图斯科。1778年，该地区被划入韦拉克鲁斯都督区下的科尔多瓦省。独立战争期间，阿托亚克一带的奴隶和蔗糖工人响应伊达尔戈号召起事；1812年，马里亚诺·莫塔在奇基维特山建立起义中心。1813年，奇尔潘辛戈议会将瓦图斯科命名为韦拉克鲁斯的起义首都。

en:
The Sinú river runs from forested highlands to the Caribbean beside the wetlands of the San Jorge, and in 1444 its valley was Zenú country. Zenú farmers grew maize and cotton on raised fields laced with drainage canals dug over centuries, while their craftsmen made pottery and hammered the gold dust the river washed down from the hills; Spanish chroniclers later described Finzenú, seat of the great female chief and capital of the Zenú lands, Yapel the potters' town and Mexión the weavers' town. Around the Gulf of Morrosquillo people fished and traded salt, and the burial mounds of their ancestors held the gold that would soon undo them.

Disease and slaving raids from newly founded Cartagena broke the chiefdoms between 1510 and 1535, and Pedro de Heredia's men marched up the Sinú to dig gold from the royal tombs. Survivors were gathered into encomienda pueblos such as San Andrés de Mexión, refounded in 1600, whose people rowed timber, maize and manatee oil downriver to Cartagena until direct Crown rule replaced the encomienda in 1720. In 1773 the King set aside 83,000 hectares at San Andrés de Sotavento as a Zenú reserve, and in 1777 Antonio de la Torre y Miranda founded Montería, which became the market town of the cattle ranches spreading along the river. After Bolívar's victory at Boyacá in 1819 the Sinú lands entered the republic of Gran Colombia, while the reserve kept Zenú communities alive.
zh:
锡努河（省名「西努」即由此而来）从林木茂密的高地流入加勒比海，与圣豪尔赫河的湿地相连，1444年时它的河谷是塞努人的家园。塞努农人在台地上种植玉米和棉花，田间是数百年来开挖的排灌渠网；工匠制陶、锻金，金砂就由河水从山中带下来。后来的西班牙编年史家记下了芬塞努——女大酋长的居所、塞努诸邦的都城，以及制陶之城亚佩尔和纺织之城梅希翁。莫罗斯基约湾一带的居民捕鱼、贩盐，而祖先墓丘中埋藏的黄金不久便给他们招来大祸。

1510至1535年间，疾病和从新建的卡塔赫纳派出的捕奴队摧毁了这些酋邦，佩德罗·德·埃雷迪亚的部下沿锡努河而上，掘开王陵取金。幸存者被并入监护征赋制下的村镇，1600年重建的圣安德烈斯-德梅希翁便是其中之一；村民把木材、玉米和海牛脂运往卡塔赫纳，直到1720年王室直接管辖取代监护制。1773年，国王在圣安德烈斯-德索塔文托划出8.3万公顷土地作为塞努人保留地；1777年，安东尼奥·德拉托雷·米兰达建立蒙特里亚，后来成为沿河散布的牧牛场的集镇。玻利瓦尔1819年赢得博亚卡战役后，锡努河流域并入大哥伦比亚共和国，而保留地让塞努人的社群延续下来。

en:
Here the Cauca and the San Jorge pour into the Magdalena through a maze of ciénagas and caños, the wettest country of the lower river. Its people were the Maguey, a Chimila people whose tongue was kin to Carib but who had the name of being peaceable: they grew cassava and maize on the levees, fished the lagoons and hunted the flooded forest, in villages long blended with the Zenú of the lower Cauca and with the Malibú. Maguey, Yati, Tacaloa and Guazo were the river chiefdoms of this water world when, in 1444, no European had yet entered the Magdalena.

Diego de Carvajal founded the Spanish town of Magangué in 1610, but it long remained a quiet riverside settlement, and on 28 October 1776 Antonio de la Torre y Miranda refounded it as Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria de Magangué, peopling the surrounding caños with new villages. The wars of independence reached these waterways in 1815, when royalists took the town; five years later José María Córdova captured Magangué and made it the headquarters of his general staff on the lower Magdalena.
zh:
考卡河与圣豪尔赫河在这里经由一片湖沼与河汊组成的水网注入马格达莱纳河，是下游地势最湿润的地方。住在这里的是马圭人——奇米拉人的一支，语言与加勒比语相近，却以性情温顺闻名。他们在天然堤岸上种植木薯和玉米，在潟湖里捕鱼、在水淹林中狩猎，村落很早就与下考卡的塞努人以及马利布人通婚融合。1444年欧洲人尚未进入马格达莱纳河时，马圭、亚蒂、塔卡洛阿、瓜索便是这片水乡的诸个酋邦。

1610年，迭戈·德·卡瓦哈尔建立西班牙城镇马甘格，但它长期只是个安静的河畔聚落。1776年10月28日，安东尼奥·德·拉托雷·米兰达将其重建，定名坎德拉里亚圣母马甘格，并在周围河汊设立新的村落。独立战争在1815年波及这片水道，保王派攻占了镇子；五年后，何塞·马里亚·科尔多瓦夺取马甘格，把它作为自己在下马格达莱纳的总司令部。

en:
Between the snow-capped Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the forested Serranía del Perijá lies the hot valley of the Cesar river, cut off from the sea and watered by the Ariguaní and the Guatapurí – 'cold water' in the Chimila tongue. In 1444 it belonged to the Chimila, a Chibcha people whose lands ran west to the Ciénaga de Zapatosa and the Magdalena, while the Yukpa of the Perijá hills belonged to their confederation. Their two districts, Upar and Pocabuy, obeyed a supreme sacred chief; the people of Upar farmed the riverbanks, kept bees, made pottery and played flutes at their festivals.

Raiders from Santa Marta forced their way into the valley in the 1530s, and on 6 January 1550 Hernando de Santana and Juan de Castellanos founded the Ciudad de los Santos Reyes del Valle de Upar, the future Valledupar, on the Guatapurí. Encomiendas parcelled out the Chimila, and many fled death, disease and enslavement into the mountains as the valley turned into cattle ranges. Through the eighteenth century Spanish haciendas kept pressing on their villages, and during the wars of independence the Chimila abandoned the reduction towns and slipped back into the forests of the Ariguaní; meanwhile, on 4 February 1813, Valledupar became one of the first towns in the Americas to rise against the Spanish Crown.
zh:
圣玛尔塔内华达山脉与林木茂密的佩里哈山脉之间，是炎热的塞萨尔河谷。它与海洋相隔，阿利瓜尼河与瓜塔普里河穿行其间——「瓜塔普里」在奇米拉语中意为「冷水」。1444年，这里属于奇米拉人：这支奇布查语民族的土地向西直到萨帕托萨沼泽和马格达莱纳河，佩里哈山中的尤克帕人也属于他们的部落联盟。全境分为乌帕尔和波卡布伊两大区，尊一位具有神圣地位的大酋长；乌帕尔人在河畔耕作、养蜂、制陶，在节庆上吹奏长笛。

1530年代，从圣玛尔塔出发的征服者强行进入谷地。1550年1月6日，埃尔南多·德·桑塔纳与胡安·德·卡斯特利亚诺斯在瓜塔普里河畔建立「乌帕尔谷地圣王城」，即后来的巴耶杜帕尔。监护征赋制把奇米拉人层层瓜分，许多人为躲避死亡、疾病和奴役逃入深山，谷地随之变成牧牛场。整个18世纪，西班牙大庄园不断侵占他们的村落；独立战争期间，奇米拉人离开归化集镇，退回阿利瓜尼河丛林。与此同时，1813年2月4日，巴耶杜帕尔成为美洲最早起兵反抗西班牙王权的城镇之一。

en:
The rain-soaked forests of the Catatumbo basin were the country of the Barí, whom Spanish-speakers later called Motilones. In 1444 their autonomous communities occupied the river lands between the eastern Andes and the Maracaibo lowlands, speaking a Chibchan language and combining forest fields with hunting and fishing. Large roundhouses gathered each community, and the name imposed by Europeans had not yet reached the rivers.

In 1530 Barí warriors ambushed the gold-bearing expedition of Ambrosius Ehinger, the Welser agent, in the Bobalí highlands and scattered its treasure. Spanish expeditions and Capuchin missionaries met prolonged resistance from 1530 to 1730; the friars then learned Barí, began catechism, and drew some families into mission villages. From 1772 the government of Maracaibo established peaceful relations with at least twenty-one communities, and metal tools, cacao planting and trade routes encouraged settlement around the missions. During the wars of independence the Capuchins supported the Spanish king; after patriots defeated them in 1813, most Barí abandoned the villages and returned to the forest. The bishop of Mérida removed Capuchin jurisdiction over the five remaining settlements in 1817, leaving the region thinly controlled when independence arrived in 1821.
zh:
多雨的卡塔通博河流域丛林是巴雷人的土地，说西班牙语的人后来称他们为莫蒂隆人。1444年，他们的自治社群占据东安第斯山脉与马拉开波低地之间的河间地带，使用一种奇布查语系语言，以林地农作、狩猎和捕鱼为生。各社群聚居在大型圆形长屋中，欧洲人后来强加的名字此时还未传到这些河畔。

1530年，巴雷战士在博巴利高地伏击韦尔塞家族代理人安布罗修斯·埃因格携带黄金的远征队，夺走并散失了其财宝。1530年至1730年间，西班牙远征队和嘉布遣会传教士持续遭到顽强抵抗；此后修士学习巴雷语、开始传教，并把一些家庭引入传教村。1772年起，马拉开波政府同至少21个社群建立和平关系，金属工具、可可种植和商路促使人们在传教点附近定居。独立战争期间，嘉布遣会支持西班牙国王；1813年爱国者击败他们后，大多数巴雷人放弃村庄回到丛林。1817年，梅里达主教撤销嘉布遣会对仅剩五处定居点的管辖权，因此到1821年独立到来时，这片地区仍只受到薄弱控制。

en: Moniquirá, recorded in the sixteenth century as Ubaza, lies on the wooded Eastern Cordillera slopes drained by the Moniquirá, Pómeca and Suárez rivers. Before the conquest it was a Muisca community under the cacique Susa, set on the north-western edge of the Altiplano Cundiboyacense; in 1444 its Chibcha-speaking people farmed maize and other crops in temperate and cold lands linked to highland trade in salt and cloth. Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada passed through Ubaza on 16 March 1537. In 1755 the visitador Andrés Verdugo y Oquendo sold the indigenous town, and its people were attached to Chitaraque; a parish was founded there in 1788.
zh: 莫尼基拉在16世纪的文献中称乌瓦萨，坐落在东部山脉被莫尼基拉河、波梅卡河和苏亚雷斯河穿过的林坡上。征服时代以前，这里是臣服于酋长苏萨的穆伊斯卡社群，位于昆迪博亚卡高原西北缘；1444年，说奇布查语的居民在温带和寒冷地带种植玉米等作物，并与高原上的盐和织物贸易相连。1537年3月16日，贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达途经乌瓦萨。1755年，巡视官安德烈斯·贝尔杜戈·伊·奥肯多出售这座印第安村镇，居民被并入奇塔拉克；1788年，这里建立堂区。

en:
From the cloud-forested Pacific littoral, where the Telembí and Patía run out through mangrove swamps, the land climbs to the cold Atriz Valley at the foot of the Galeras volcano, home of the Quillacingas, while the wider highland region took its name from the Pastos. Related Barbacoas and Awá bands lived along the coastal rivers. These peoples farmed maize and potatoes in scattered villages and panned gold, answering to no empire: in 1444 the Inca frontier still lay far to the south, and only on the eve of the Spanish arrival did Inca armies reach and subdue these mountains.

Sebastián de Belalcázar first founded a town here in 1537, and Lorenzo de Aldana moved it into the Atriz Valley in 1539 as San Juan de Pasto, which received its coat of arms from the crown in 1559 and became the administrative and religious centre of the southern highlands. Down on the coastal rivers Francisco de la Parada founded a settlement in 1600, and Pedro Martín Navarro formalised it in 1612 as Santa María del Puerto de los Barbacoas; its goldfields, worked by African slaves, belonged to Popayán families and made Barbacoas the richest mining town of the region. No place in New Granada defended the king more stubbornly. In September 1811 troops of the short-lived Quito junta entered Pasto, but royalists retook it in 1812–13, and in 1814 Antonio Nariño's patriot army was defeated outside the town. Even after Boyacá, Pasto fought on under Agustín Agualongo; at the close of 1821 it was still unconquered, the last great royalist stronghold of southern New Granada.
zh:
从云雾笼罩的太平洋沿岸——特莱姆比河与帕蒂亚河穿过红树林沼泽入海——地势一路抬升到加莱拉斯火山脚下寒冷的阿特里斯河谷，那里是基利亚辛加人的家园，而整个高原地区因帕斯托斯人得名。与他们亲缘相近的巴尔巴夸斯人、阿瓦人则住在沿海各条河流上。这些族群在分散的村落里种植玉米和马铃薯，从河里淘金，不臣服于任何帝国：1444年，印加的边界还远在南方，直到西班牙人到来的前夜，印加军队才推进并征服这片群山。

塞瓦斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔1537年首先在此建城，1539年洛伦索·德·阿尔达纳把城镇迁入阿特里斯河谷，定名圣胡安·德·帕斯托；王室1559年颁赐城徽，这里遂成为南部高原的行政与宗教中心。在沿海河流地带，弗朗西斯科·德·拉·帕拉达1600年建立定居点，佩德罗·马丁·纳瓦罗1612年将其正式定名为圣玛利亚·德尔普埃尔托·德·洛斯·巴尔巴夸斯；当地金矿区由黑奴开采，矿权归于波帕扬的豪族，使巴尔巴夸斯成为全区最富庶的矿业城镇。在整个新格拉纳达，没有哪个地方比这里更顽固地捍卫国王：1811年9月，短命的基多洪达的军队一度进入帕斯托，但保王派在1812至1813年间夺回该地，1814年安东尼奥·纳里尼奥的爱国军又在城外被击败。即便在博亚卡战役之后，帕斯托仍在阿古斯丁·阿瓜隆戈率领下继续作战；直到1821年末，它依旧未被攻克，是新格拉纳达南部最后一座保王堡垒。

en:
The Putumayo rises in the Nudo de los Pastos and cuts through forested gorges toward the Amazon. In 1444 its upper basin was divided among autonomous peoples: Cofán communities in the southwest, Kamëntšá in the northwest, Siona and other Tucano-speaking groups along the central and southern waters, and Witoto-speaking peoples toward the east. Long navigable stretches carried canoes and trade between these riverside communities, while Inca armies had not yet crossed the Andean foothills.

In 1492 the Inca Huayna Cápac crossed Cofán territory, subdued part of the Kamëntšá lands and placed a Quechua-speaking population in the Sibundoy valley, the community later known as the Inga. Inca power collapsed after 1533, Spanish expeditions entered Putumayo from 1542, and from 1547 successive Catholic missions administered much of this fragile frontier. Popayán remained its link to Spanish government, but distance, forest and the great river left the Cofán, Kamëntšá, Siona and Witoto communities with room to preserve their own authority. By 1821 the former mission country remained tied to Popayán rather than formed into a compact, closely governed province.
zh:
普图马约河发源于帕斯托斯山结，穿过森林峡谷奔向亚马逊河。1444年，其上游流域分属各个自治族群：西南部是科凡人，西北部是卡门查人，中部和南部水道居住着西奥纳人和其他图卡诺语族群，东部则是维托托语族群。漫长的可通航河段让独木舟和贸易往来于河畔社群之间，而印加军队此时尚未越过安第斯山麓。

1492年，印加君主瓦伊纳·卡帕克穿过科方土地，征服卡门查人的部分领地，并在锡本多伊谷地安置一支说克丘亚语的居民，即后来所称的因加人。1533年后印加政权崩溃，西班牙远征队从1542年起进入普图马约，1547年起又由接连而来的天主教传教团管理这条脆弱边疆的大部分事务。波帕扬始终是它与西班牙政府之间的联系节点，但遥远距离、雨林和大河使科方、卡门查、西奥纳和维托托社群仍有空间维持自身权威。到1821年，这片旧日传教地仍依附波帕扬，并未形成一个紧密而受严密治理的行省。

en:
The Chichitames were a desert band of the Bolsón de Mapimí, the closed basin between the sierras of Nueva Vizcaya where the Nazas and the lower Conchos lose their waters. They were one of the kindred nomad peoples the Spanish grouped together as Tobosos, hereditary enemies of the lake-dwelling Irritila to their south. They had no fields or towns: they hunted with sling and lance, gathered mesquite and mescal, moved their rancherías between waterholes and raided the richer valleys to the south and west. In 1444 no road entered the bolsón: no Spaniard existed in their world, the silver at Mapimí lay untouched, and the desert answered to no lord.

Antonio de Espejo's expedition crossed the country in 1583 and the Chichitames' Toboso kin simply vanished into the desert. Silver brought the Spaniards in force: on 25 July 1598 Antón Martín de Zapata and the Jesuit Juan Agustín de Espinoza founded Santiago de Mapimí at the foot of the Sierra de la India, whose mines became one of the richest districts of New Spain. Slave-raiding drove the desert bands to war, and they had taken to horses within a generation; Mapimí was swept by risings in 1616-17, 1654-61, 1683-87, 1703-11 and 1715, answered by a presidio and campaigns of extermination. Where twelve bands had been counted in the 1680s, by 1693 only four remained: the Osatayogliglas, Guazapayogliglas, Sisimbles and Chichitames. By 1800 the survivors had dissolved into the mestizo frontier population, and in 1811 the last echo of their long war passed through Mapimí in the person of the chained Hidalgo, carried north to Chihuahua to be shot; news of independence reached the mining camps ten years later.
zh:
奇奇塔梅斯人是马皮米盆地的一个沙漠游群——这个封闭盆地位于新比斯开的群山之间，纳萨斯河与孔乔斯河下游都在此耗尽河水。他们与几个亲缘游牧族群同被西班牙人归为托博索人，世代与南方湖畔而居的伊里蒂拉人为敌。他们没有田地和城镇：以投石器和长矛狩猎，采集豆灌木和龙舌兰，在水源地之间迁徙营地，不时向南、向西劫掠更富庶的山谷。1444年时没有一条道路通向盆地内部：他们的世界里没有西班牙人，马皮米的银矿还埋在地下，荒漠不奉任何君主。

1583年安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍的探险队穿过此地，奇奇塔梅斯人的托博索同族直接遁入沙漠。是银子把西班牙人成批引来：1598年7月25日，安顿·马丁·德·萨帕塔与耶稣会士胡安·阿古斯丁·德·埃斯皮诺萨在印度山脚下建立圣地亚哥·德·马皮米，这里的矿区后来成为新西班牙最富庶的矿区之一。奴隶猎捕把荒漠各族群逼上战争之路，他们只用一代人的时间就学会了骑马；起义在1616—1617年、1654—1661年、1683—1687年、1703—1711年和1715年反复席卷马皮米，西班牙人则以要塞和剿灭战役回应。1680年代这里还能数出十二个游群，到1693年只剩四个：奥萨塔约格利格拉斯、瓜萨帕约格利格拉斯、西辛布雷斯和奇奇塔梅斯。到1800年，幸存者已融入边境上的混血社会；1811年，这场漫长战争的最后回声以镣铐加身的伊达尔戈的形式经过马皮米——他正被押往奇瓦瓦处决，十年后独立的消息才传到这些矿营。

en:
Between the snowy volcanoes of the Cordillera Central and the hot valley of the upper Magdalena lay the country of the Pijao, a constellation of chiefdoms rather than a state: the Coyaima and Natagaima on the river plains, the mountain communities higher up, all joined in loose federations. They grew the tobacco they called tenú, rolled it into cigars and carried its trade far down the Magdalena, and they had the name of fierce raiders among all their neighbours. In 1444 the Spaniards were still only a rumour from the coast, and the valleys of the Saldaña, the Amoya and the Coello belonged entirely to the Pijao.

The conquistadors who pushed in from Mariquita and Neiva met eighty years of guerrilla war. Diego Bocanegra built his Fuerte de Palenque and Santiago de la Frontera in the Amoya country in 1572 and won the alliance of the chief Tala, but he was driven out before long; the Pijao commander Chequera answered every new settlement with raids, and Medina de las Torres, founded at Chaparral in 1586, was destroyed in its turn. The war ended only under Juan de Borja y Armendia, president of the Audiencia of Santafé, who played on the rivalries among the Pijao peoples and, after hard fighting near Chaparral, founded Natagaima on 8 September around 1608 and Nuestra Señora del Carmen de Coyaima the same year, calling the latter 'the complement of the pacification'. The survivors were gathered into resguardos; Coyaima, its foundation formally recorded in 1621, became a market where the produce of the cold highlands met that of the warm valley, and the village was moved to the Saldaña bank in 1778. Natagaima, repeatedly swept by Magdalena floods, was relocated to its final site in 1801.
zh:
在中部山脉的雪峰与马格达莱纳河上游的炎热河谷之间，是皮哈奥人的土地。这不是一个国家，而是一串酋邦：平原上有科亚伊马、纳塔盖马等部，更高的山里则是山地诸部，彼此结成松散的联盟。他们种植称作「特努」的烟草，卷成雪茄，把生意一直做到马格达莱纳河下游，在四邻眼中是出名的凶悍劫掠者。1444年，西班牙人还只是沿海传来的传闻，萨尔达尼亚河、阿莫亚河和科埃约河的河谷完全属于皮哈奥人。

从马里基塔和内瓦深入的征服者撞上的是一场长达八十年的游击战争。1572年，迭戈·博卡内格拉在阿莫亚一带修建帕伦克堡和圣地亚哥-德拉弗龙特拉堡，争取到酋长塔拉的联盟，后来仍被赶走；皮哈奥统帅切克拉对每一处新据点还以袭击，1586年建于查帕拉尔的梅迪纳-德拉斯托雷斯也被摧毁。战争直到圣菲王家检审庭主席胡安·德·博尔哈·阿门迪亚任内才结束：他利用皮哈奥各部之间的仇隙，在查帕拉尔附近苦战之后，于1608年9月8日前后建立纳塔盖马，同年又建立卡门圣母科亚伊马，称之为「绥靖的收尾」。幸存者被编入保留地；科亚伊马于1621年正式登记定名，成为寒冷高原物产与炎热河谷物产交易的市集，1778年村落迁至萨尔达尼亚河畔。纳塔盖马则屡遭马格达莱纳河洪水冲毁，1801年才迁到今日的位置。

en:
Achaguas takes its name from the Achagua, the most numerous indigenous people of the Orinoco llanos.
