Until the eighteenth century their villages spread through the Casanare, Meta and Apure basins, forming a trade network in which strings of quiripa shells served as money; later accounts put their population at more than 30,000 on the eve of European contact. In 1444 the wet savannas and river woods around the future town were Achagua country, with no mission or Spanish settlement.

The site first appeared on a 1707 map by Lorenzo Palacios. On 4 December 1774 the Capuchin friar Alonso de Castro founded Santa Bárbara de la Isla de los Achaguas, gathering Achagua, Taparita and Otomaco people with three wealthy Spanish families. During the Venezuelan independence wars, these plains saw the clash of Las Queseras del Medio on 2 April 1819, when José Antonio Páez's llanero cavalry met royalist horse. Páez's feigned retreat, sudden countercharge and the cry '¡Vuelvan, caras!' made the action famous in the memory of the llanero war.
zh:
阿查瓜斯得名于阿查瓜人——奥里诺科亚诺斯草原上人数最多的原住民。直到18世纪，他们的村落仍分布在卡萨纳雷河、梅塔河与阿普雷河流域，组成贸易网络，并用成串的基里帕贝壳充当货币；后世记载称，欧洲人到来前夕他们的人口超过三万。1444年，未来城镇周围的湿草原与河边林地属于阿查瓜人的土地，还没有传教站或西班牙人居民点。

1707年，洛伦索·帕拉西奥斯绘制的地图首次标出这一地点。1774年12月4日，嘉布遣会修士阿隆索·德·卡斯特罗建立圣巴巴拉·德·拉·伊斯拉·德·洛斯·阿查瓜斯，把阿查瓜人、塔帕里塔人、奥托马科人和三户富裕的西班牙家庭聚居于一处。委内瑞拉独立战争期间，1819年4月2日，何塞·安东尼奥·派斯的亚诺斯骑兵在拉斯克塞拉斯德尔梅迪奥与保王派骑兵交战。派斯佯装撤退后突然反身冲锋，那声「转身！」使这次战斗成为草原战争中的著名记忆。

en:
The valley of the Turbio was known to its villagers as Variquicimeto, the 'ash-coloured river'. In 1444 its maize lands and hunting grounds belonged to the Caquetío and their neighbours the Gayón, Ayamán and Jirajara, Arawakan-speaking peoples who kept up a lively traffic in cotton, salt and dye along the routes from the Caribbean coast to the inland plains. No strangers yet ruled the valley.

Gold at Buría drew the captain Juan de Villegas from El Tocuyo, and in 1552 he founded Nueva Segovia de Buría on the edge of the valley. Unhealthy ground and indigenous attacks drove the settlers in 1556 to a new site at El Carabalí, named Nueva Segovia de Barquisimeto. This was the town the rebel conquistador Lope de Aguirre burned on his march through Venezuela in 1561, and at Barquisimeto his own men turned on him and killed him on 27 October that year. Rebuilt at the meeting of the Turbio and Claro, the town was moved once more to escape harsh winds and settled for good in 1563 on the plateau north of the Turbio, its native name Variquicimeto worn down by Spanish tongues to Barquisimeto. Through the colonial years it served as an agricultural market and road junction between central and western Venezuela. Barquisimeto joined the independence rising of 1811, and its deputy José Ángel Álamo signed the Independence Act on 5 July; patriot and royalist armies fought the battle of Los Horcones nearby in 1813.
zh:
图尔维奥河谷的土著地名叫巴里基西梅托，意为「灰色的河」。1444年，这里的玉米地和猎场属于卡克蒂奥人及其邻族加永人、阿亚曼人和希拉哈拉人，他们都说阿拉瓦克语，沿连接加勒比海岸与内陆平原的道路买卖棉花、盐和染料，往来兴旺。此时还没有外来者统治这片谷地。

布里亚的金矿把西班牙队长胡安·德·维列加斯从埃尔托库约引来，1552年他在谷地边缘建起「布里亚的新塞戈维亚」。水土恶劣加上土著袭击，迫使殖民者1556年迁到埃尔卡拉瓦利新址，改名「巴里基西梅托的新塞戈维亚」。1561年，起兵反叛西班牙国王的征服者洛普·德·阿基尔在转战委内瑞拉途中烧毁此城，同年10月27日，他在巴基西梅托被自己的部下杀死。城镇在图尔维奥河与克拉罗河汇流处重建，又因风害再次迁址，1563年终于在图尔维奥河北岸的台地定居下来，土著地名巴里基西梅托也在西班牙人口中讹变为巴基西梅托。整个殖民时期，这里是连接委内瑞拉中部与西部的农业集镇和道路枢纽。1811年巴基西梅托加入独立起义，代表何塞·安赫尔·阿拉莫在7月5日签署独立法案；1813年爱国军与保王军又在城外接战，是为洛斯奥尔科内斯之战。

en:
The forested folds of the Serranía del Perijá, whose eastern streams run down to the Catatumbo and Lake Maracaibo, were the land of the Yukpa, a Carib-speaking people who lived in autonomous clan villages high above the hot plains, clearing maize and manioc fields on the mountain flanks and hunting in the cloud forest. Spanish settlers later called them Motilones, 'the shaved heads', a name they shared loosely with the Barí beyond the ridges. In 1444 no road or tribute reached these valleys: the Yukpa held their mountains on their own terms.

That independence held for nearly three centuries. Spanish expeditions probed the mountains for gold and captives but won no lasting foothold, and the first Spanish town below the sierra, Concepción, founded at the Palmar's mouth in 1717, was destroyed by its indigenous neighbours three years later. Juan de Chourio, a Navarrese holding a royal licence of 1722, brought Canary Islander and Maracaibo settler families into the foothills and from 1724 built La Villa de Perijá on the Palmar, moving it in 1729 to the healthier site it still occupies. The Yukpa burned Concepción again in 1752, and it was rebuilt for the last time that same year. Capuchin missionaries and cattle ranches then crept up the valleys, but even in 1821 the high sierra remained Yukpa country.
zh:
佩里哈山林木幽深，东坡的溪流向东汇入卡塔通博河与马拉开波湖，这里是尤克帕人的家园。他们说加勒比语，在炎热平原之上的高山中以氏族聚村而居，在山坡上刀耕火种玉米和木薯，在云雾林里狩猎。后来的西班牙移民称他们为莫蒂隆人，意为「剃光头的人」，山那边的巴里人也被笼统地叫这个名字。1444年，没有道路和赋税能伸进这些山谷：尤克帕人完全按自己的方式据守着大山。

这份独立维持了近三百年。西班牙远征队为寻找黄金、掳掠人口多次进山，却始终没能站住脚；山脚下第一座西班牙城镇康塞普西翁1717年建于帕尔马河口，三年后便被邻近的土著摧毁。1722年，纳瓦拉人胡安·德·乔里奥取得王室特许，带着加那利群岛和马拉开波的移民家庭进入山麓，1724年起在帕尔马河畔建起佩里哈镇，1729年又迁至更宜居住的现址。1752年尤克帕人再次焚毁康塞普西翁，该镇同年最后一次重建。此后嘉布遣会传教士和牧牛场才慢慢沿山谷推进，但直到1821年，高山之上仍是尤克帕人的地盘。

en:
The driest corner of the Caribbean coast, the Guajira peninsula and the arid plains running from it toward Lake Maracaibo, was Wayuu country. Speakers of an Arawakan tongue, they lived by hunting, fishing and gathering and by horticulture where the southern valleys allowed it, dwelling in communal longhouses and moving between rancherías as the waterholes dictated. Clan loyalties and the desert made the land unconquerable for outsiders. In 1444 the Wayuu knew nothing of the ships that would soon come for the pearls of their coasts.

Alonso de Ojeda's ships first sailed this coast in 1499, and Spanish settlement and pearl fishing at Cabo de la Vela in 1535 opened a border war that never really ended. The Wayuu took to the horse and, almost alone among the peoples of the Spanish Main, to firearms bought from Dutch and English smugglers with pearls and brazilwood: a Capuchin mission went up in flames in 1701, more than two thousand warriors attacked the Spanish in 1727, and further risings followed in 1741, 1757, 1761 and 1768. The greatest came on 2 May 1769, when the seizure of twenty-two Wayuu for the fortifications of Cartagena provoked the burning of El Rincón near Riohacha and the killing of its commander José Antonio de Sierra; the revolt fielded some 20,000 men at its height and swept almost every settlement in the region, until Spanish reinforcements and feuding among the clans broke it. By 1812 the authorities reckoned the unconquered Guajiros between Maracaibo and Riohacha at 40,000 people, 1,500 of them lances, and the wars of independence left the desert still Wayuu.
zh:
加勒比海岸最干旱的一角——瓜希拉半岛及由此向马拉开波湖延伸的干旱平原——是瓦尤人的地盘。他们说阿拉瓦克语，靠狩猎、捕鱼、采集为生，在南方水源较好的谷地兼营园艺，住在全族共居的长屋里，随水井在村落间迁徙。血缘氏族和沙漠让外人难以征服这片土地。1444年的瓦尤人还不曾料到，很快就会有船只为他们海岸的珍珠而来。

1499年，奥赫达的船队首次驶过这段海岸；1535年，西班牙人在贝拉角定居并采珠，开启了一场几乎从未真正停歇的边境战争。瓦尤人学会了骑马，而且在西班牙属美洲大陆的各族群中近乎独一地掌握了火器——他们用珍珠和巴西红木向荷兰、英国走私商换取枪支。1701年，一座嘉布遣会传教站被烧毁；1727年两千多名战士进攻西班牙人，1741、1757、1761和1768年又接连起义。最大的一次发生在1769年5月2日：二十二名瓦尤人被抓去修建卡塔赫纳城防，义军随即焚毁里奥阿查附近的埃尔林孔，杀死指挥官何塞·安东尼奥·德·谢拉；起义高潮时约有两万人参战，几乎席卷当地所有西班牙人定居点，最后靠西班牙援军赶到、加上瓦尤氏族反目内斗才被平息。到1812年，当局估计马拉开波与里奥阿查之间未被征服的瓜希罗人有四万之众，其中一千五百人是持矛战士；独立战争结束时，沙漠仍在瓦尤人手中。

en:
At the heart of north-central Venezuela lies the broad basin of Lake Tacarigua, later Lake Valencia, ringed by the coastal cordillera and the hot lowlands that run down to the Llanos. In 1444 its shores were farmed by the Tacarigua and other Arawak peoples, who grew maize and cotton, fished the reed-fringed water and built their villages on artificial mounds against the lake's floods; no European had yet reached the valley.

Spanish settlers had first established themselves at the nearby cove of Borburata, but repeated corsair sacks drove them inland, and on 25 March 1555 Captain Alonso Díaz Moreno founded Nueva Valencia del Rey on the lakeshore. The encomienda brought the lake villages under Spanish control, and the region supplied wheat, cattle and cotton to the coast. In 1561 the rebel conquistador Lope de Aguirre descended on the young town in his flight from Peru, and in 1677 French raiders burned its cabildo and the early records of the province. When Alexander von Humboldt reached the lake in 1800 he found Valencia a town of six or seven thousand people and recorded how the clearing of its shores was lowering the water. Valencia stood at the centre of the independence wars: the revolutionary congress met there in 1812 before royalist troops retook the province, and in 1814 the royalists of José Tomás Boves took and sacked the town after a long siege. On 24 June 1821 Bolívar won the Battle of Carabobo on the plain west of the lake, sealing Venezuela's independence.
zh:
委内瑞拉中北部腹地是塔卡里瓜湖（后称巴伦西亚湖）的宽阔湖盆，四周环绕着海岸山脉和伸向亚诺斯草原的炎热低地。1444年，湖畔的土地由塔卡里瓜人和其他阿拉瓦克部族耕作：他们种植玉米和棉花，在芦苇丛生的湖面捕鱼，把房屋建在人工土台上以避湖水泛滥；这时还没有欧洲人进入谷地。

西班牙移民最初落脚在附近的博尔布拉塔海湾，但海盗的反复洗劫迫使他们内迁。1555年3月25日，阿隆索·迪亚斯·莫雷诺上尉在湖畔建起新巴伦西亚德尔雷伊。委托监护制把湖畔的村落置于西班牙移民的控制之下，这一带向沿海输送小麦、牲畜和棉花。1561年，反叛的征服者洛佩·德·阿吉雷在逃离秘鲁途中闯入这座年轻的城镇；1677年，法国海盗烧毁了市政厅和全省的早期档案。1800年亚历山大·冯·洪堡来到湖边时，巴伦西亚已有六七千居民，他记录了湖畔伐林如何使湖面下降。独立战争中巴伦西亚处在旋涡中心：1812年革命议会曾在此开会，保王军旋即重新夺占全省；1814年，何塞·托马斯·博韦斯的保王部队经长期围困攻陷并洗劫了这座城市。1821年6月24日，玻利瓦尔在湖西平原赢得卡拉博博战役，奠定了委内瑞拉的独立。

en:
The Guanaguanare country lies where the south-western Llanos meet the Andean piedmont, between the Portuguesa and Guanare rivers. In 1444, Cuiba, Caquetío and Guamo communities farmed, fished and gathered across the savanna; their mounds and causeways probably served as flood refuges, drainage works or burial places. The Cospes later held the wooded country north of the future town, and the indigenous name Guanaguanare was explained as 'place of seagulls' or 'land between rivers'. No Spanish town yet occupied the valley.

Nikolaus Federmann and Georg von Speyer crossed these plains for the Welser company in 1534, and Philipp von Hutten was wounded here by Omagua defenders in 1542. On 3 November 1591 the Portuguese captain Juan Fernández de León founded Espíritu Santo del Valle de Guanaguanare, later shortened to Guanare, and cattle ranches and farms spread around the new town. Local tradition placed appearances of the Virgin to the Cospes chief Coromoto in the nearby woods in 1651 and 1652, and Catholic missionaries began work around Guanare and Acarigua in 1657. During the Second Republic, Simón Bolívar concentrated his troops nearby and at the Battle of Araure on 5 December 1813 defeated José Ceballos's larger royalist army, taking four standards and numerous guns while more than five hundred royalist cavalrymen were killed.
zh:
瓜纳瓜纳雷位于西南草原与安第斯山麓交会处，地处波图格萨河与瓜纳雷河之间。1444年，奎瓦人、卡克蒂奥人和瓜莫人等族群在稀树草原农耕、渔猎和采集；他们留下的土墩与堤道可能用于洪水期避难、排水或安葬。后来城镇北侧的林地由科斯佩人控制，印第安语地名瓜纳瓜纳雷被解释为「海鸥之地」或「两河之间的土地」。当时山谷中还没有西班牙城镇。

1534年，尼古劳斯·费德曼和格奥尔格·冯·施派尔代表韦尔塞公司穿过这片平原；1542年，菲利普·冯·胡滕在此遭奥马瓜人阻击并受伤。1591年11月3日，葡萄牙船长胡安·费尔南德斯·德·莱昂建立埃斯皮里图·桑托·德尔巴列·德·瓜纳瓜纳雷，后来简称瓜纳雷，牧牛场和农田随即在城镇周围扩展。当地传统称，圣母在1651年和1652年向附近林地中的科斯佩酋长科罗莫托显现；1657年，天主教传教士开始到瓜纳雷和阿卡里瓜一带传教。第二共和国期间，西蒙·玻利瓦尔在附近集结军队，于1813年12月5日的阿劳雷战役击败何塞·塞瓦略斯兵力更强的保王军，缴获四面军旗和多门火炮，击毙五百余名保王骑兵。

en:
Tuneo is the mountain gateway from the Llanos to the Sierra Nevada del Cocuy, where cloud forests and the valleys of the Cobaría and Arauca rise from the eastern plains. In 1444 the Tunebo, who call themselves U'wa and speak a Chibchan language, held these ridges and forested slopes, moving between highland farms, hunting grounds and river crossings. Their kinship and trade networks linked the Cocuy massif with the plains, while the steep country kept the richer Muisca lands around Tunja at a distance.

Nicolás Federmann and Georg von Speyer crossed the eastern cordillera into Arauca in 1536. Later gold-seeking expeditions under Hernán Pérez de Quesada pushed toward Güicán, and many Tunebo and related Güicán families withdrew behind the Sierra Nevada rather than submit. Jesuit missionaries reached Guahibo, Airico, Chiricoa and Tunebo lands in 1659, and in 1756 the Jesuit Miguel Blasco founded the reduction of Güicán on the western side of the massif; it had 310 people in 1764. After the Jesuit expulsion of 1767, Augustinian Recollects took over the plains missions and founded San Fernando de Arauca. The Comunero movement found support at Tame in 1781, and Güicán declared independence from Spain on 24 February 1814. Bolívar entered Arauca on 4 June 1819, reached Tame on 11 June, and after Santander's forces joined the march crossed the Andes by way of the Pantano de Vargas to victory at Boyacá.
zh:
图内奥是从东部草原登上科库伊雪山的山口地带，科瓦里亚河与阿劳卡河的河谷从云雾林升入安第斯山。1444年，自称乌瓦人的图内博人占据这些山脊和林坡；他们使用奇布查语，在高地农田、猎场和渡口之间往来，亲属与贸易网络连接科库伊山地和东部平原，险峻地形也使他们同通哈一带富庶的穆伊斯卡土地保持距离。

1536年，尼古劳斯·费德曼和格奥尔格·冯·施派尔越过东科迪勒拉山进入阿劳卡。后来埃尔南·佩雷斯·德·克萨达为寻找黄金进军圭坎，许多图内博人和亲缘相近的圭坎人退到雪山另一侧，拒绝臣服。1659年，耶稣会传教士进入瓜希博人、艾里科人、奇里科阿人和图内博人的土地；1756年，耶稣会士米格尔·布拉斯科在山地西侧建立圭坎归化村，1764年村中有310人。1767年耶稣会被逐后，重整奥斯定会会士接替草原传教，并建立阿劳卡的圣费尔南多。1781年公社者运动在塔梅得到响应；1814年2月24日，圭坎宣布脱离西班牙独立。1819年6月4日玻利瓦尔进入阿劳卡，6月11日抵达塔梅，随后同弗朗西斯科·德·保拉·桑坦德尔的部队会师，经巴尔加斯沼泽翻越安第斯，在博亚卡取胜。

en: Guanipa covers part of the great tableland south of the Unare plains, where the Guanipa River begins a roughly 340-kilometre course through dense swamps to the Gulf of Paria beside the Orinoco delta. In 1444 the open mesas, streams and gallery groves were Kali'na country; later local memory named the land after Guanipa, a Carib-speaking cacique said to have led his people on the mesas above the Orinoco. Christopher Columbus's third voyage documented the nearby river mouth on 1 August 1498, after which Spanish and other European expeditions entered the Orinoco waterline while the Guanipa interior remained indigenous hunting, planting and travelling country.
zh: 瓜尼帕位于乌纳雷平原以南的广阔台原上，瓜尼帕河从这里发源，流经约340公里的密林沼泽，在奥里诺科三角洲旁注入帕里亚湾。1444年，开阔台原、河道与林带属于卡利纳人的活动范围；后来的地方记忆以瓜尼帕命名这片土地，据说他是一位讲加勒比语的酋长，统领奥里诺科河上方台原的族人。1498年8月1日，克里斯托弗·哥伦布第三次航行记录了附近的奥里诺科河口，此后西班牙及其他欧洲探险队进入奥里诺科水道，而瓜尼帕腹地仍是原住民狩猎、耕作和往来通行之地。

en:
The hot coastal plain between the Unare River and the Guanipa plateau, backed by the low country that runs to the Orinoco, belonged in 1444 to a mosaic of Cariban peoples: the Cumanagoto held the Neverí valley and the shore, while the Píritu, Chacopata and Palenque lived among the Unare lagoons, farming and fishing and growing maize and cotton. Their first sight of Europeans came in 1499, when pearl-seekers from Cubagua began landing below the Maracapana hill to provision their boats.

The first Spanish town, San Cristóbal de la Nueva Écija, was founded in 1586 after Captain Cristóbal Cobos defeated the cacique Cayaurima, yet the Cumanagoto fought on for more than sixty years. Joan Orpí, charged with their conquest, founded Nueva Barcelona del Cerro Santo in 1638, and in 1671 Governor Sancho Fernández de Angulo moved the settlement two kilometres south and refounded it as Barcelona. Cattle ranches, cotton and sugar spread through its district, served by the missions founded at Clarines in 1594 and Píritu in 1656. Barcelona's junta proclaimed the province independent on 27 April 1810. The cause nearly died here: on 17 August 1814 royalist forces with 8,000 men routed Bolívar's 3,000 republicans at Aragua de Barcelona, and on 7 April 1817 they stormed the Casa Fuerte, the old Franciscan convent where the garrison and townspeople had taken shelter, putting its defenders and refugees to the sword.
zh:
在乌纳雷河与瓜尼帕台地之间，炎热的沿海平原背后是通向奥里诺科河的低地。1444年，这里是一片加勒比语族部族的拼图：库马纳戈托人据有内韦里河谷和海岸，皮里图人、查科帕塔人和帕伦克人则散居在乌纳雷河的潟湖之间，以耕作捕鱼为生，种植玉米和棉花。他们第一次见到欧洲人是在1499年，从库瓦瓜岛来的采珠人开始在马拉卡帕纳山下登岸，为船队补给。

1586年，克里斯托瓦尔·科沃斯上尉击败酋长卡尧里马之后建立了第一座西班牙城镇圣克里斯托瓦尔-德拉新埃西哈，但库马纳戈托人的抵抗又持续了六十多年。受命征服此地的霍安·奥尔皮于1638年建立圣山新巴塞罗那；1671年，省长桑乔·费尔南德斯·德·安古洛把居民点南移两公里，重建为巴塞罗那。辖区内牧牛场、棉花和甘蔗次第铺开，克拉里内斯和皮里图的传教站分别于1594年和1656年设立。1810年4月27日，巴塞罗那的执政委员会宣布本省独立。但独立事业在这里几近覆灭：1814年8月17日，八千人的保王军在阿拉瓜-德巴塞罗那击溃玻利瓦尔仅三千人的共和军；1817年4月7日，保王军又攻破卡萨富埃特——那座被守军和市民当作避难所的旧方济各会修道院，屠戮了里面的守军与难民。

en:
Guaju is the deep forest between the upper Orinoco and the Rio Branco, a country of blackwater rivers and the flat-topped Duida and Parima heights. Its wonder is the Casiquiare, a natural arm that breaks from the upper Orinoco below the Duida and winds more than 300 kilometres south into the Rio Negro, carrying Orinoco water into the Amazon — the only waterway on earth joining two river systems on this scale. In 1444 Arawak-speaking peoples, the Baré and Baniva among them, farmed and fished along the Casiquiare and the Guainía, while Ye'kuana villages held the Ventuari and its rapids; their canoes had long used the canal and the Pimichín portage to pass between the two river worlds. No European had yet seen any of it.

Word of the canal reached Europe through the Jesuit Manuel Román: in 1744, at La Esmeralda, he met Portuguese slavers who had come up from the Rio Negro and accompanied them through the waterway, the first recorded passage, and La Condamine carried the report to the Académie française. The Royal Orinoco Expedition confirmed it in 1755, and Spain set out to hold the country. In 1758 Sergeant Francisco Fernández de Bobadilla found cacao groves on the Ocamo and Padamo, and the next year work began on the fort of Buena Guardia at the Casiquiare's mouth. From 1760 Ensign Apolinar Díez de la Fuente and the friar José Antonio Jerez de los Caballeros gathered Ye'kuana families into a new town, officially founded in 1767 as San Francisco de la Esmeralda, named for an emerald supposedly found beneath Cerro Duida; that same year they pushed up the Orinoco to its source, still searching for Lake Parime and the golden city of Manoa. A native rising in 1776 wrecked the planned road from La Esmeralda to Angostura. In 1800 Humboldt and Bonpland navigated the Casiquiare and fixed its geography, yet Spanish power never reached beyond a handful of forest posts, and in 1821 the interior remained the rivers and villages of its native peoples.
zh:
瓜胡地处上奥里诺科河与里奥布朗库河之间的密林深处，到处是黑水河与杜伊达、帕里马等平顶山。这里的奇观是卡西基亚雷河：它从上奥里诺科河分出一支天然汊流，在杜伊达峰脚下蜿蜒三百多公里向南注入内格罗河，把奥里诺科河的水送入亚马孙河——世界上唯一以此规模连通两大水系的天然河道。1444年，说阿拉瓦克语的巴雷人、巴尼瓦人在卡西基亚雷河与瓜伊尼亚河沿岸耕渔为生，叶库纳人的村落据守着本图阿里河及其急流；他们的独木舟早就借由这条水道和皮米钦陆运道，往来于两个大河世界之间。这时还没有任何欧洲人到过此地。

水道的消息由耶稣会士曼努埃尔·罗曼带到外界：1744年，他在拉埃斯梅拉达遇到从内格罗河上来的葡萄牙奴隶贩子，并随他们穿过卡西基亚雷河，这是有记载的首次欧洲人通行，拉孔达明随后把报告带到法兰西科学院。1755年，皇家奥里诺科远征队正式证实了这条水道，西班牙随即着手控制这片土地。1758年，弗朗西斯科·费尔南德斯·德·博瓦迪利亚军士在奥卡莫河与帕达莫河一带发现可可林，次年又在卡西基亚雷河口动工修建布埃纳瓜迪亚要塞。1760年起，少尉阿波利纳尔·迭斯·德拉富恩特与修士何塞·安东尼奥·赫雷斯·德洛斯卡瓦列罗斯把叶库纳人迁入一座新城，1767年正式定名为圣弗朗西斯科·德拉埃斯梅拉达，名字取自据说在杜伊达山下发现的一颗祖母绿；同年，他们还溯奥里诺科河直抵源头，仍在寻找帕里梅湖和金城马诺阿。1776年的一次原住民起事使拉埃斯梅拉达通往安戈斯图拉的道路工程功亏一篑。1800年，洪堡与邦普朗航行穿越卡西基亚雷河，勘定了它的地理，但西班牙的势力始终只及密林里的寥寥几处据点，直到1821年，内陆仍属于原住民的河流与村落。

en:
The bay and river mouths that later became Jacmel were Yaquimo, a Taíno coastal district on the eastern side of Hispaniola's Tiburon Peninsula. The Caribbean shore and steep hinterland supported fishing villages, cassava fields and canoe traffic, and Spanish accounts later placed the district in Jaragua, the chiefdom ruled at contact by Bohechío; they remembered Zui and Yáquimo as Jaragua's two constituent parts. In 1444 local caciques still governed the land around the bay, untouched by European conquest.

Spanish settlers founded a town at Yaquimo in 1504, but after the Devastations of Osorio in 1605 Spain broke up the old western settlements and the coast was largely emptied. The Compagnie de Saint-Domingue established a small French town at the river mouth in 1698; metropolitan authorities designated it a colonial town in 1720, and coffee introduction in 1770 brought new trade. Sugar and coffee enriched the planters through enslaved labour. In 1791 and 1792 Romaine-la-Prophétesse led some 13,000 rebels who occupied and burned Jacmel, raided plantations from Marigot to Bainet and freed enslaved people. During the War of the South, Alexandre Pétion defended the port until Toussaint Louverture's forces took it in 1800. On 12 March 1806 Francisco de Miranda unfurled at Jacmel the first flag of Venezuela, later the model for Gran Colombia's colours.
zh:
后来成为雅克梅勒的海湾和河口地带，原是泰诺人的沿海地区亚基莫，位于伊斯帕尼奥拉岛蒂伯朗半岛东侧。加勒比海岸与陡峭腹地分布着渔村、木薯地和独木舟往来路线。后来的西班牙记载把这一地区归入欧洲人到来时由博埃奇奥统治的哈拉瓜酋长国，并称祖伊和亚基莫是哈拉瓜的两个组成部分。1444年，地方酋长仍统治着海湾周围的土地，欧洲征服尚未到来。

1504年，西班牙殖民者在亚基莫建立城镇；但1605年奥索里奥荒毁政策后，西班牙拆散西部旧居民点，这片海岸大体空虚。1698年，圣多明各公司在河口建立一座法国小镇，1720年法国本土当局将其定为殖民城镇，1770年引入咖啡后贸易有所发展。蔗糖和咖啡依靠被奴役劳工为种植园主创造财富。1791年至1792年，罗曼·拉·普罗费特斯率领约一万三千名起义者占领并焚毁雅克梅勒，袭击从马里戈特到拜内的种植园，解放被奴役者。南方战争期间，亚历山大·佩蒂翁防守这座港口，直到杜桑·卢维杜尔的军队在1800年攻占它。1806年3月12日，弗朗西斯科·德·米兰达在雅克梅勒升起委内瑞拉第一面旗帜，其配色后来成为大哥伦比亚旗帜的原型。

en:
Marien was the north-westernmost of the five Taíno chiefdoms of Hispaniola, facing the Atlantic and the Windward Passage, with Tortuga offshore and borders with Maguá, Maguana and Jaragua. Its chief town, El Guarico, stood near the later Cap-Français, and fourteen nitaínos administered its villages and northern plains. In 1444 Taíno caciques still controlled these shores, river valleys and farmlands; the ruler encountered at Columbus's arrival, Guacanagaríx, belonged to this same northern chiefly seat.

At Christmas 1492 the Santa María was wrecked off this coast; Guacanagaríx allowed Columbus to build La Navidad from the ship's timbers, but the fort had been destroyed by a rival force before Columbus returned. Spain founded Puerto Real nearby in 1503, moved the settlement to Bayajá in 1578, and evacuated the northern towns during the Osorio devastations after 1605, opening the coast to buccaneers. French settlers under Bertrand d'Ogeron founded Cap-Français in 1670; formally established in 1711, it served as capital of Saint-Domingue until 1770 and by 1790 held 15,000 people, two-thirds of them enslaved. On 14 August 1791 enslaved delegates gathered at Bois Caïman, and the great rising swept the northern plantations days later. On 18 November 1803 Jean-Jacques Dessalines defeated Rochambeau at Vertières below Cap-Français, and Haiti proclaimed independence on 1 January 1804. Henri Christophe made the north a separate state in 1807 and a kingdom in 1811, renaming the city Cap-Henri and raising the Citadelle Laferrière above Milot; his death in 1820 ended the northern monarchy.
zh:
马里安（Marién，也译马列恩）是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛五大泰诺酋长国之一，位于岛屿西北，北临大西洋，西隔向风海峡与托尔图加相望，东接马瓜和马瓜纳，南连哈拉瓜。首府埃尔瓜里科位于后来的法兰西角附近，酋邦分为十四个小区。1444年，泰诺酋长仍统治着这些海岸、河谷和农田；哥伦布到来时遇到的统治者瓜卡纳加里克斯，便出自这一北方酋邦。

1492年圣诞节，圣玛利亚号在附近海岸失事；瓜卡纳加里克斯允许哥伦布用船木修建纳维达德堡，但哥伦布返回前，堡垒已被敌对势力摧毁。1503年，西班牙人在这一带建立雷亚尔港，1578年又将居民点迁往巴亚哈；1605年后的奥索里奥荒毁政策撤空北岸城镇，给了布坎尼尔海盗可乘之机。1670年，贝特朗·多热龙率领的法国移民建立法兰西角，1711年正式设城；1770年前这里是法属圣多明各首府，到1790年已有一万五千人，其中三分之二是奴隶。1791年8月14日，奴隶代表在凯门森林集会，北部种植园数日后爆发大起义。1803年11月18日，让-雅克·德萨林在法兰西角以南的韦尔蒂埃尔击败罗尚博，海地随后于1804年1月1日宣布独立。亨利·克里斯托夫1807年在北方建立分立政权，1811年将其改为王国，把法兰西角改名亨利角，并在米洛上方修建拉费里埃城堡；他1820年去世后，北方君主制告终。

en:
The wooded Samaná Peninsula, the coast around Nagua and the mouth of the Yuna were the country of the Ciguayos. They spoke a language distinct from Taíno, carried bows and arrows, and are described as hunter-gatherers who made no pottery. Taíno expansion had pushed them into this northeastern corner and brought them within the chiefdom of Maguá, but in 1444 their villages still controlled the hills and shores around Samaná Bay.

On 13 January 1493 Columbus's landing party met Ciguayo archers on the shore later called Rincón Beach. When the islanders refused to trade their weapons, a clash left two of them wounded, and Columbus named the anchorage the Gulf of Arrows. The Spanish made little permanent use of the bay for generations, which left it open to runaways and privateers. When Guarionex fled from Maguá to the Ciguayos, their chief Mayobanex refused Bartholomew Columbus's demand to surrender him and was captured together with the fugitive cacique. Permanent Spanish settlement came only in 1756, when Governor Francisco Rubio y Peñaranda sent Canary Islander families to found Santa Bárbara de Samaná and Sabana de la Mar. The colony passed to France under the Peace of Basel, and in 1807 a British naval raid seized Samaná and turned it over to Spanish creoles fighting the French.
zh:
林木覆盖的萨马纳半岛、纳瓜一带海岸和尤纳河口，是锡瓜约人的土地。他们使用与泰诺语不同的语言，携带弓箭，被记载为不制作陶器的狩猎采集者。泰诺人的扩张把他们挤压到岛的东北一隅，并使他们落入马瓜酋长领地的势力范围；但在1444年，他们的村落仍控制着萨马纳湾周围的山丘与海岸。

1493年1月13日，哥伦布的登陆队在后来称林孔海滩的岸边遇到锡瓜约弓箭手。岛民拒绝交出武器，随后冲突中有两人受伤，哥伦布便把这片锚地命名为箭头湾。此后数代西班牙人都没有在此长期定居，使这里成为逃亡者和私掠船出没之地。瓜里奥内克斯从马瓜逃到锡瓜约人那里时，其首领马约瓦内克斯拒绝巴尔托洛梅·哥伦布交人的要求，最终和这位逃亡首领一同被俘。永久性的西班牙殖民点直到1756年才出现：弗朗西斯科·鲁维奥-佩纳兰达总督派加那利群岛移民家庭建立圣巴巴拉-德萨马纳和滨海萨瓦纳。根据《巴塞尔和约》，殖民地转入法国之手；1807年，一支英国海军舰队袭取萨马纳，并把它交给对抗法国的西班牙裔克里奥尔人。

en:
Higüey was the easternmost Taíno chiefdom of Hispaniola, its 21 nitaínos stretching from the Haina River toward Cape Engaño, Saona Island and the Mona Passage. Its principal village stood on the Yuma River, where the Spanish town of Salvaleón de Higüey later developed. Sources from the contact period name the caciques Cayacoa and Cotubanamá and the female ruler Higuanamá, but in 1444 these eastern plains, forests and canoe crossings still formed an independent Taíno world on the island's sunrise edge.

War began after dogs from a Spanish hunting party killed a local chief on Saona and Cotubanamá's followers killed eight Spaniards in reprisal. In 1503 Governor Nicolás de Ovando sent Juan de Esquivel with hundreds of soldiers, including Bartolomé de las Casas. Cotubanamá made peace and exchanged names with Esquivel in the Taíno guatiao ceremony, but he later attacked the Spanish fort; only one of its nine garrison soldiers survived. In the eight or nine months of war that followed, Juan López tracked Cotubanamá to a cave on Saona and captured him, and the cacique was taken in chains to Santo Domingo and hanged in 1504. The defeated Taínos were forced into plantation labor, and African slaves were imported as their population collapsed. Higüey received a royal privilege and coat of arms on 7 December 1508; its Spanish settlement grew around Juan Ponce de León's holding at Yuma and may have moved to its later site around 1522. Sugar cane, ginger, cacao and cattle became its colonial mainstays. The 1795 Peace of Basel transferred Santo Domingo to France, Toussaint Louverture occupied the east in 1801, Spanish rule returned in 1809, and in 1821 Higüey was drawn into the short-lived Republic of Spanish Haiti.
zh:
伊圭是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛最东端的泰诺酋长领地，下辖21个尼塔伊诺辖区，疆域从艾纳河延伸至恩加尼奥角、绍纳岛和莫纳海峡。主要村落位于尤马河畔，后来的西班牙城镇萨尔瓦莱昂-德伊圭便在此发展。接触时代的资料提到卡亚科阿、科图瓦纳马等首领以及女统治者伊瓜纳马；但在1444年，东部平原、森林和独木舟航道仍是岛的日出之端一个独立的泰诺世界。

战争起因于一支西班牙狩猎队的猎犬在绍纳咬死一名当地首领，科图瓦纳马的追随者随后报复，杀死八名西班牙人。1503年，总督尼古拉斯·德·奥万多派胡安·德·埃斯基维尔率领数百名士兵前来，巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯也在军中。科图瓦纳马起初议和，并按泰诺人的瓜蒂奥仪式与埃斯基维尔交换名字；但他后来进攻西班牙要塞，九名守军中只有一人生还。随后的战争持续八九个月，胡安·洛佩斯在绍纳岛的一个洞穴中追获科图瓦纳马，将他锁送圣多明各，并于1504年处以绞刑。战败的泰诺人被迫从事种植园劳役，随着人口锐减，非洲奴隶被输入岛上。1508年12月7日，伊圭获得王室特权和纹章；西班牙人的定居点围绕胡安·庞塞·德·莱昂在尤马的地产发展，约1522年可能迁至后来的城址。甘蔗、生姜、可可和牛只成为殖民时代的主要物产。1795年《巴塞尔和约》将圣多明各移交法国，杜桑·卢维杜尔1801年占领东部，1809年西班牙恢复统治；1821年，伊圭被卷入短命的西班牙海地共和国。

en:
East of Havana the Bay of Matanzas bites deep into Cuba's north coast, where the Yumurí, San Juan and Canímar rivers come down to the sea. Fishing peoples had camped at the mouth of the Canímar since the most ancient times, and in 1444 Taíno villages farmed the river valleys and paddled the wide, quiet bay in canoes.

Columbus sighted the southern coast of this district on his second voyage in 1494, and Sebastián de Ocampo surveyed these shores during his circumnavigation of Cuba in 1508. In 1510, before the conquest of the island had begun, a party of Spaniards persuaded native fishermen to ferry them across a river without boats; midstream the fishermen overturned the canoes, and the armored Spaniards drowned, giving the place its name of Matanzas, the slaughter, one of the first acts of indigenous resistance in Cuba. Between 1514 and 1518 the Spanish established the Indian pueblo of Canímar on the eastern edge of the bay. Long without a Spanish town, the anchorage became a haunt of smugglers and corsairs until a royal order of 25 September 1690 brought thirty families from the Canary Islands; San Carlos y San Severino de Matanzas was founded in October 1693, guarded by the Castillo de San Severino, with its cabildo meeting from 1695. Sugar then transformed the district: by 1792 the town held some 1,900 slaves, nearly a third of its people, and by 1817 more than 10,000, close to half the population, making Matanzas one of the richest sugar regions of Cuba.
zh:
哈瓦那以东，马坦萨斯湾深深切入古巴北海岸，尤穆里河、圣胡安河和卡尼马尔河在这里入海。远古时代便有渔猎部族在卡尼马尔河口栖居；1444年，泰诺人的村落耕种河谷，划着独木舟往来于宽阔平静的海湾。

哥伦布1494年第二次航行时曾望见这一地区的南岸，1508年塞瓦斯蒂安·奥坎波环航古巴时首次勘察了这里的海岸。1510年，征服古巴的战事尚未开始，一队无船可用的西班牙人让当地渔民渡他们过河，行至中流渔民掀翻独木舟，身披重甲的西班牙人溺水而亡，此地由此得名「马坦萨斯」，意为杀戮，这也是古巴最早的原住民反抗行动之一。1514至1518年间，西班牙人在海湾东岸设立了原住民村镇卡尼马尔。此后海湾旁长期没有西班牙城镇，锚地成了走私者和海盗的出没之地，直到1690年9月25日王室下令从加那利群岛迁来三十户人家；1693年10月，圣卡洛斯和圣塞韦里诺·德·马坦萨斯建城，由圣塞韦里诺城堡戍卫，市政会自1695年起运作。蔗糖随即改变了这片地区：到1792年，城中约有一千九百名奴隶、接近人口的三分之一；到1817年奴隶已超过一万人、将近居民半数，马坦萨斯由此成为古巴最富庶的蔗糖产区之一。

en:
The Escambray, called Guamuhaya in the Taíno tongue, is the mountain knot of central Cuba, forested ridges rising from the south coast to the 1,140-metre Pico San Juan. In 1444 Taíno villages kept conucos in the foothills and fished the coves of Jagua Bay, a wide sound joined to the Caribbean by a narrow mouth; the valleys belonged entirely to them, and no European had yet seen the range.

Early in 1514 Diego Velázquez founded the Villa de la Santísima Trinidad at the foot of the mountains, the third Spanish town in Cuba. Hernán Cortés recruited men there and sailed from its harbor in 1518 on his way to Mexico, and in 1527 Pánfilo de Narváez's Florida expedition lost two ships to a hurricane off the town. For two centuries Trinidad lived on cattle and small farms while Jagua Bay became a pirates' refuge and smuggling anchorage; the Castillo de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles de Jagua was raised to close its mouth and was finished in 1742. From the late eighteenth century sugar spread through the valleys below the sierra, the future Valle de los Ingenios, worked by a fast-growing slave population. On 22 April 1819 French settlers led by Luis de Clouet founded Fernandina de Jagua on the great bay, the town later renamed Cienfuegos, and it was as prosperous sugar country that the Escambray region entered the year 1821.
zh:
埃斯坎夫雷山，泰诺语称瓜穆哈亚，是古巴中部的山岳枢纽，林木覆盖的山岭从南海岸隆起，最高峰圣胡安峰海拔1140米。1444年，泰诺人的村落在山麓经营田园，在哈瓜湾的小湾里捕鱼——哈瓜湾是一道由狭窄水口通向加勒比海的宽阔潟湖；这些山谷完全属于他们，欧洲人还不曾见过这片群山。

1514年初，迭戈·贝拉斯克斯在山脚下建立至圣特里尼达镇，这是西班牙人在古巴的第三座城镇。1518年，埃尔南·科尔特斯在此招募人手并从港中出航，踏上远征墨西哥之路；1527年，潘菲洛·德·纳尔瓦埃斯的佛罗里达探险队在城外遭遇飓风，损失两艘船。此后两个世纪，特立尼达靠畜牧和小农为生，哈瓜湾却成了海盗的避风港与走私锚地；为封锁湾口，天使圣母哈瓜城堡动工兴建，于1742年建成。18世纪末起，甘蔗沿着山麓谷地扩散，那便是后来的因赫尼奥斯谷，在迅速增长的奴隶劳作下成为富庶之地。1819年4月22日，路易斯·德·克卢埃率领法兰西移民在大海湾畔建立费尔南迪纳德哈瓜，即后来更名的西恩富戈斯。1821年时，埃斯坎夫雷已是一片繁荣的蔗糖之乡。

en:
Guane is the far west of Cuba, the rolling country beyond the Sierra de los Órganos that runs out to Cape San Antonio. In 1444 it was the land of the Guanahatabey, a people older than the Taíno: hunter-gatherers who moved in small bands rather than villages, made no pottery and worshipped no cemís, living on fish and shellfish. Even the Taíno knew the western tip as the country of a different people.

In April 1494 Columbus reached this end of the island on his second voyage, and his Taíno interpreters could not understand a word the locals said, for they spoke another language. Diego Velázquez mentioned them again in 1514 and Bartolomé de las Casas in 1516, but after the conquest the Guanahatabey disappear from the record amid the collapse of Cuba's indigenous world. The Spanish town of Guane was founded in 1602, one of the few settlements in a district largely left to itself, and Canary Islanders arriving from the later sixteenth century turned the riverside vegas into tobacco country. When the crown imposed a tobacco estanco in 1717, fixing the price and the amount every grower must sell, growers revolted in 1717, 1720 and 1723; the last rising ended with twelve men shot and their bodies hung from trees along the road. In the later eighteenth century the far west was organized as the Pinar del Río tobacco district, supplying the royal factories in Havana, and in 1821 Guane remained a small town ringed by tobacco vegas.
zh:
瓜内地处古巴最西端，是奥尔加诺斯山脉之外、一直延伸到圣安东尼奥角的起伏原野。1444年，这里是瓜纳哈塔贝伊人的土地——一个比泰诺人更古老的族群：他们以小群体游徙为生而不建村落，不制陶器，也不拜塞米神像，靠鱼和贝类过活。在泰诺人看来，岛屿西端本就是另一族人的地方。

1494年4月，哥伦布第二次航行抵达这一岛端，随队的泰诺译员却听不懂当地人的话——他们说的是另一种语言。迭戈·贝拉斯克斯1514年、巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯1516年又分别提到过他们，但征服之后，随着古巴原住民世界的崩溃，瓜纳哈塔贝伊人从记载中消失。1602年，西班牙人建立瓜内镇，是这片大体被放任自流的地区少有的定居点；16世纪末起陆续迁来的加那利移民，把河畔的低地沃土建成为烟草田园。1717年王室推行烟草专卖，规定每个烟农的售价和出售数量，烟农遂于1717、1720和1723年接连起事；最后一次反抗被镇压，十二人被枪决，尸体挂在路边的树上示众。18世纪后期，远西地区被组织为比那尔德里奥烟草辖区，向哈瓦那的王家烟厂供货；到1821年，瓜内仍是一座烟草田园环绕的小镇。

en:
The Mayaca lived among the lakes and marshes of the upper St. Johns River, south of Lake George, a wet country of seasonal floods where villages stood on high ground and canoes threaded the waterways of the St. Johns culture. They hunted, fished and gathered like the Ais, whose language theirs resembled, but did not farm like the Timucua of the richer lands to the north. A paramount chief at the village of Mayaca spoke for several towns, some of them as far away as the Atlantic coast. In 1444 these lakes knew nothing of Europe, and rivalry with the Freshwater Timucua chiefs to the north shaped local politics.

The European wars of the 1560s reached the lakes as French Fort Caroline and Spanish St. Augustine fought for the Florida coast, and the Spaniards first met the Mayaca in 1566 while ransoming French captives. Franciscans came at the end of the century: the chief was baptized by 1597 and the mission of San Salvador de Mayaca was later founded. By the 1690s the Mayaca province had several missions, although Yamasee refugees had become most of its people, and unrest in 1696 and 1697 cost a friar his life. Raids by Carolina-backed Indians in 1708 broke the people apart: some Mayaca fled to St. Augustine, others south to the eastern shore of Lake Okeechobee, where in 1738 and 1739 they and their Jororo and Bomto allies fought the Calusa and their allies in battles that killed some 300 people. A last handful, mingled with Mayaimi and Santaluzo survivors, was found by missionaries in 1743; that remnant band is presumed to have sailed for Cuba with the Spaniards in 1763.
zh:
马亚卡人住在圣约翰斯河上游、乔治湖以南的湖沼地带。这里地势低洼、湖水季节性泛滥，村镇建在高地之上，独木舟穿行在圣约翰斯文化的水网之间。他们和语言相近的艾斯人一样以渔猎采集为生，不像北方沃土上的蒂穆夸人那样务农；马亚卡镇的大酋统辖数个村镇，其中一些远在大西洋岸边。1444年，这片湖乡还不知欧洲为何物，与北方「淡水蒂穆夸」诸酋的争斗左右着当地的格局。

16世纪60年代，法国的卡洛琳堡与西班牙的圣奥古斯丁争夺佛罗里达海岸，战祸波及湖乡；1566年，西班牙人在赎回法国俘虏时首次接触马亚卡人。方济各会修士在16世纪末到来，大酋到1597年已受洗入教，圣萨尔瓦多·德·马亚卡传教站随后设立。到17世纪90年代，马亚卡地区已有数座传教站，但居民已以逃难而来的亚马西人为主体；1696至1697年的骚乱中，一名修士被杀。1708年，卡罗来纳支持的印第安武装的袭击击散了马亚卡人：一部分逃往圣奥古斯丁，一部分南下到奥基乔比湖东岸。1738至1739年，他们与霍罗罗人、博姆托人结盟，同卡卢萨人及其盟友交战，约300人死于混战。传教士1743年见到的最后一小群马亚卡人已与马亚依米人、圣卢索人的孑遗混居，这群人据信于1763年随西班牙人登船前往古巴。

en:
The Potano were Timucua-speaking farmers of the Alachua savanna, the rolling prairie and oak-hammock country of north-central Florida where the Alachua culture had raised villages and burial mounds since about 700. The chief town Potano was one of a string of settlements that included Itaraholata, Utinamochana and Mala-paz. Maize, beans and squash grew in the rich upland soils, and the Spaniards who later knew them remembered the Potano as one of the strongest of the Timucua chiefdoms. In 1444 their world held only rival Timucua chiefs; no European had yet entered the interior.

Pánfilo de Narváez passed west of the Potano towns in 1528, and Hernando de Soto's army tramped through in 1539, stripping the villages of their stored maize. In the 1560s the Potano fought the Utina, who were backed first by the French of Fort Caroline and then by the Spaniards of St. Augustine; in 1584, after the Potano killed a Spanish captain leading an invasion, a punitive expedition slaughtered many and drove the rest from the chief town, which was rebuilt on a new site. Franciscans had baptized more than a thousand adult Potano by 1607, and the mission of San Francisco de Potano, founded in 1609, became the first resident mission west of the St. Johns; Spanish cattle ranches later spread across the people's former fields. The Potano joined the Timucuan rebellion of 1656, after which their towns and missions lay burned, and an epidemic in 1672 cut so deep that only 160 people remained at the two missions by 1675. From 1685 Creek and Yamasee slavers out of Carolina harried the prairie, and after the northern mission system collapsed in 1704 the surviving Potano drifted to St. Augustine as refugees and vanished as a tribe.
zh:
波塔诺人是说蒂穆夸语的农人，住在北佛罗里达中部的阿拉楚阿稀树草原——一片起伏的草甸与橡树林地，阿拉楚阿文化约自700年起便在此营建村落与墓葬土垒。酋镇波塔诺是一连串村镇之一，其余还有伊塔拉霍拉塔、乌蒂纳莫查纳和马拉帕斯。肥沃的高地上种着玉米、豆类和南瓜，后来结识他们的西班牙人把波塔诺视为蒂穆夸诸酋邦中最强的一支。1444年，波塔诺人的世界里只有彼此争雄的蒂穆夸诸酋，欧洲人尚未踏入这片内陆。

1528年，潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯的远征队从波塔诺诸镇以西经过；1539年，埃尔南多·德·索托的大军穿越其地，把各村储存的玉米劫掠一空。16世纪60年代，波塔诺人与乌蒂纳部交战，后者先有卡洛琳堡的法国人撑腰，后来又得到圣奥古斯丁的西班牙人支持。1584年，波塔诺人杀死一名带兵入侵的西班牙队长，讨伐军随即血洗其地，幸存者被逐出酋镇，村镇易地重建。方济各会修士到1607年已为一千多名成年波塔诺人施洗；1609年设立的圣弗朗西斯科·德·波塔诺传教站，是圣约翰斯河以西第一座常驻教士的传教站，后来西班牙牧牛场在波塔诺人昔日的田地上铺开。1656年，波塔诺人参加蒂穆夸大起义，战后村镇与传教站多被焚毁；1672年的一场疫病又重创其民，到1675年两座传教站中只剩160人。1685年起，卡罗来纳指使的克里克和亚马西奴隶贩子不断蹂躏草原；1704年北方传教体系崩溃后，幸存的波塔诺人作为难民流落圣奥古斯丁，作为一个部族就此消亡。

en:
The wooded lowlands bearing the name Tanu lie between the Brazos and Neches rivers, centered on Bedias Creek and the Trinity. In 1444 this was Bidai country; the people called themselves Quasmigdo, while the Caddo name Bidai referred to the brushwood of their Big Thicket homeland. Their villages farmed the river bottoms and hunting parties moved through the pine and oak woods. Galveston Bay and the Akokisa lay to the south, with Hasinai towns beyond the Neches to the east.

The first Spanish mention came in 1691, when explorers placed the Bidai near the Hasinai. François Simars de Bellisle found them farming and allied with the Akokisa in 1718–1720. French trade on the Trinity soon challenged Spanish claims: after Blancpain's trading post was broken up in 1754, Spain built Presidio San Agustín de Ahumada at El Orcoquisac in 1756 and opened the Franciscan Mission Nuestra Señora de la Luz to gather Akokisa and Bidai families there. The mission was moved in 1759, but after Louisiana passed to Spain and the Marqués de Rubí's frontier inspection, the post was abandoned in 1771. Epidemics in 1776–1777 halved the surviving Bidai, whose families then sought refuge among the Akokisa and Koasati; by 1821 the old Tanu country was no longer centered on a separate Bidai polity.
zh:
得名塔努的林地低地位于布拉索斯河与内奇斯河之间，以贝迪亚斯溪和特里尼蒂河为中心。1444年，这里是比代人的土地；他们自称夸斯米格多，而卡多语中的「比代」意指其大丛林家园中的灌柴。村落在河畔低地耕作，狩猎队伍穿行于松树与橡树林间。南面是加尔维斯顿湾和阿科基萨人，东面越过内奇斯河则是哈西奈人的城镇。

1691年，西班牙探险者首次留下记载，把比代人的位置标在哈西奈人附近。1718—1720年，弗朗索瓦·西马尔·德·贝利斯勒看到他们从事农业，并与阿科基萨人结盟。特里尼蒂河上的法国贸易很快挑战了西班牙的主权主张：布朗潘的贸易站在1754年被捣毁后，西班牙于1756年在奥科基萨克建立圣阿古斯丁·德·阿乌马达要塞，并开设方济各会的光明圣母传教站，试图把阿科基萨和比代家庭聚集到那里。传教站于1759年迁移，但在路易斯安那转归西班牙、鲁维侯爵巡边之后，整个据点于1771年废弃。1776—1777年的瘟疫使幸存的比代人减少一半，幸存者随后投奔阿科基萨人和科阿萨蒂人；到1821年，旧日的塔努之地已不再以一个独立的比代政体为中心。

en:
Nitahendé reproduces the Mescalero name Nit'ahéndé or Niit'ahénde, 'people who live against the mountains'. Their seasonal country took in the Sacramento Mountains of southern New Mexico and the Guadalupe Mountains above the west Texas desert, with canyons reaching toward the Pecos. In 1444 these Ndé hunters and gatherers moved between high pine forest, pinyon-juniper slopes, desert basins and buffalo plains. Mescal agave was roasted in pit ovens, deer and bighorn were hunted in the ranges, and buffalo hunts carried parties east toward the Pecos and Llano Estacado. Springs, caves and mountain passes made this a refuge as well as a highway.

Spaniards first entered the Guadalupe country in the sixteenth century but made no settlement there, and Spanish horses gradually gave Apache hunters greater range. After Juan de Oñate occupied New Mexico in 1598, Apache bands along the frontier alternately traded and raided Spanish herds while colonial parties retaliated and took captives. Between 1700 and 1750 Comanche expansion pushed many Mescalero groups back into the Sacramento, Guadalupe and Trans-Pecos mountains. Spanish authorities later negotiated limited peace settlements with Apache rancherías, with agreements in 1790 and 1793, but the Mexican independence struggle after 1810 drained frontier garrisons and raiding resumed. When Spanish rule ended in 1821, the Nitahendé mountains remained an unconquered Mescalero stronghold on the edge of independent Mexico.
zh:
尼塔恩德对应梅斯卡莱罗名称 Nit'ahéndé 或 Niit'ahénde，意为「住在山边的人」。他们的季节性故土包括新墨西哥南部的萨克拉门托山和耸立在得克萨斯西部沙漠上的瓜达卢佩山，峡谷向佩科斯河方向延伸。1444年，这些恩代猎人和采集者在高山松林、矮松刺柏坡、沙漠盆地和野牛草原之间迁移。梅斯卡尔龙舌兰在坑炉中烘烤，山间可猎鹿和大角羊，野牛狩猎则把队伍带向东方的佩科斯河与斯塔克平原。泉水、洞穴和山口既是避难所，也是通行要道。

16世纪，西班牙人最早进入瓜达卢佩山区，但没有在那里定居；西班牙人的马逐渐扩大了阿帕切猎人的活动范围。胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年据有新墨西哥后，边境阿帕切群体时而贸易，时而劫掠西班牙畜群，殖民队伍则以报复和掳掠人口回应。1700至1750年间，科曼奇人的扩张把许多梅斯卡莱罗群体逼回萨克拉门托山、瓜达卢佩山和佩科斯以西山地。后来西班牙当局与阿帕切牧场群落达成有限和平，1790年和1793年先后签订协议；但1810年后墨西哥独立战争削弱边境驻军，劫掠再起。1821年西班牙统治结束时，尼塔恩德群山仍是独立墨西哥边缘一处未被征服的梅斯卡莱罗据点。

en:
Ndawe Qoha is the lower Pecos borderland where the river turns southeast out of the Trans-Pecos mountains and cuts arid canyons on its way to the Rio Grande. Around its waterholes, arroyos and sparse grasslands, the cedar breaks of the Edwards Plateau meet the Chihuahuan Desert. In 1444 this was Ndé hunting country: Lipan families moved with bison and white-tailed deer, roasted agave, gathered mesquite beans, and used the fords to meet Jumano travelers whose trails ran west toward Toyah Creek and La Junta. No Spanish town or mission yet anchored the lower river, whose value lay in water, crossings and access to Coahuila.

Antonio de Espejo followed this river in 1582–1583, naming it Río de las Vacas for the buffalo herds; Jumano guides showed the way from the Pecos by Toyah Creek to La Junta. The Lipan had acquired Spanish horses by 1608, and mounted rancherías turned the lower fords into links between west Texas, Coahuila and the southern plains. By 1700 they were established across southern Texas and northern Coahuila, farming corn, beans, pumpkins and watermelons in seasonal clearings while retaining long hunting rounds. In 1778 Juan de Ugalde, governor of Coahuila, located a Lipan ranchería of about forty people led by Zapato Bordado on the Rio Grande, together with a Mescalero camp, and opened the campaigns of the following year. When Mexico became independent in 1821, the sparse frontier presidios had not pinned the lower Pecos Lipan into a settled colonial district.
zh:
恩达韦科哈是佩科斯河下游边地，河水从佩科斯以西山地折向东南，切过干旱峡谷，奔向里奥格兰德。这里的水洼、旱谷和稀疏草原，正处在爱德华兹高原的雪松峡谷与奇瓦瓦沙漠相接之处。1444年，这里是恩代猎场：利潘群体随野牛和白尾鹿迁移，烘烤龙舌兰、采集牧豆，利用各处渡口同胡马诺旅人往来，胡马诺商路向西通往托亚溪和拉洪塔。此时下游河畔还没有西班牙城镇或传教站，这片土地的价值在于水源、渡口和通往科阿韦拉的道路。

1582至1583年，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍沿这条河返程，因野牛群众多而称其为「母牛河」；胡马诺向导指引他从佩科斯河经托亚溪前往拉洪塔。利潘人到1608年已获得西班牙马，骑马的营地群落把下游渡口变成连接得克萨斯西部、科阿韦拉和南部平原的纽带。到1700年，他们已分布在得克萨斯南部和科阿韦拉北部，在季节性空地上种植玉米、豆类、南瓜和西瓜，同时保留长距离狩猎。1778年，科阿韦拉总督胡安·德·乌加尔德在里奥格兰德河畔发现一处约四十人的利潘营地，首领是萨帕托·博达多（意为「绣花鞋」），旁边还有一处梅斯卡莱罗营地；次年他由此发起讨伐。1821年墨西哥独立时，稀疏的边境要塞仍未能把佩科斯河下游的利潘人约束在固定的殖民辖区内。

en:
Natahéndé is the Pecos River corridor of the Naa'dahéńdé, the Mescal People whom Spanish records rendered as Natagés. The Pecos rises on the eastern slope of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and runs south-east through arid grasslands toward the Rio Grande. In 1444 Apache bands used its valley and side arroyos for skin-lodge camps, mescal gathering, seasonal planting and hunts for deer and bison; horses had not yet reached these camps, and no Spanish mission or presidio guarded the river.

Antonio de Espejo followed the Pecos on his return in 1582-1583, naming it Río de las Vacas after six days of travel through country thick with bison. Mounted raiding and slaving later tied the Natagés to the Texas frontier. In 1731 they joined Lipan, Teya and Jumano allies in war on San Antonio; on 9 December 1732 Governor Juan Antonio Bustillo y Ceballos attacked about four hundred tipis on the San Sabá River after a five-hour battle, but Apache raids continued. Natagé and Lipan leaders made peace with Spain at San Antonio in 1749. Comanche pressure nevertheless drove more Lipan survivors toward the Rio Grande and Coahuila in 1767, where they joined Natagé groups, and around 1780 the latter entered the Lipiyán coalition led by Picax-Ande-Ins-Tinsle. When Mexico became independent in 1821, the Pecos corridor remained an Apache route rather than a conquered colonial heartland.
zh:
纳塔恩德是Naa'dahéńdé人所居的佩科斯河通道；这个称呼意为「梅斯卡尔人」，西班牙文献转写为Natagés。佩科斯河发源于桑格雷·德克里斯托山东坡，向东南穿过干旱草原，最终汇入格兰德河。1444年时，阿帕奇群体沿河谷和支谷设立兽皮帐篷营地，采集梅斯卡尔龙舌兰，进行季节性种植，并猎捕鹿和野牛；马匹尚未传到这些营地，河畔也没有西班牙传教站或要塞。

1582—1583年，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍返程时沿佩科斯河行进，因连续六日穿行在野牛众多的地带而将其命名为「母牛河」。后来，骑马袭掠和奴隶贸易把纳塔赫斯人与得州边疆联系在一起。1731年，他们与利潘人、特亚人和胡马诺人结盟，对圣安东尼奥开战；1732年12月9日，胡安·安东尼奥·布斯蒂略·伊·塞瓦略斯总督进攻圣萨瓦河畔约四百座帐篷，战斗持续五小时，但阿帕奇人的袭掠并未停止。1749年，纳塔赫斯和利潘首领在圣安东尼奥与西班牙议和。尽管如此，科曼奇人的压力仍在1767年把更多利潘幸存者逼向格兰德河与科阿韦拉，他们在那里加入纳塔赫斯群体；约1780年，纳塔赫斯人又加入皮卡克斯-安德-因斯-廷斯勒领导的利皮亚内斯联盟。1821年墨西哥独立时，佩科斯河通道仍是阿帕奇人的往来之路，而非被征服的殖民腹地。

en:
Naflat is the Rio Grande country around Cochiti, one of the eastern Keres pueblos. Its people traced their ancestry to Ancestral Puebloan farmers who built cliff dwellings in the canyons of the Pajarito Plateau; some groups lived at Potrero Viejo and Hanut Cochiti before the historic pueblo took shape. River water, maize and cotton bound the villages together, while the finger mesas offered refuge in war. In 1444 Cochiti was an independent Keres town, linked by language, marriage and trade to the other Pueblo peoples along the river.

Juan de Oñate's expedition reached Cochiti in 1598, opening trade before Spanish rule hardened into tribute in crops, cotton and labour. Franciscans attacked traditional rites and raised the San Buenaventura mission. Cochiti joined the coordinated rising of 1680 that killed about 400 Spaniards and forced some 2,000 survivors to abandon Santa Fe de Nuevo México. When Antonio de Otermín's counterattack reached the river, Cochiti withdrew with San Felipe and Kewa to Potrero Viejo. The refugees held that mesa refuge until 1693, when Diego de Vargas's reconquest drove them from it.
zh:
纳夫拉特是科奇蒂周围的里奥格兰德河谷地带，科奇蒂是东部凯雷斯语诸普韦布洛之一。其先民是古代普韦布洛农民，曾在帕哈里托高原的峡谷中营建崖居；一些群体先住在波特雷罗维耶霍和哈努特科奇蒂，后来形成历史时期的科奇蒂。河水、玉米和棉花把村落联系在一起，指状台地则在战乱时提供庇护。1444年，科奇蒂仍是独立的凯雷斯人城镇，通过语言、通婚和贸易与沿河其他普韦布洛人往来。

胡安·德·奥尼亚特远征队1598年抵达科奇蒂，最初开放贸易；随后西班牙统治转为征收作物、棉花和劳役。方济各会打击本土仪式，建起圣布埃纳文图拉传教站。科奇蒂参加1680年的联合起义，约四百名西班牙人被杀，约两千名幸存者被迫放弃圣菲新墨西哥省。安东尼奥·德·奥特尔明反攻到河畔时，科奇蒂人与圣费利佩、克瓦人退往波特雷罗维耶霍。他们据守这座台地避难所至1693年，最终被迭戈·德·巴尔加斯的再征服军逐走。

en:
Tsi'ya is the Jemez River valley home of the Zia, an Eastern Keres Pueblo people. Their Ancestral Puebloan forebears moved into the valley in the thirteenth century and built the adobe pueblo beside irrigated maize fields; pottery and trade with neighbouring Keres and Jemez towns shaped its economy. In 1444 Tsi'ya governed its own fields and ceremonies, still untouched by the Spanish expeditions that would later enter New Mexico.

Antonio de Espejo first recorded Tsi'ya in 1583. After Juan de Oñate's arrival in 1598, Fray Alonso de Lugo founded the San Pedro y San Pablo mission, and Zia labourers had raised a church and convent by 1613. Spanish rule outlawed traditional ceremonies, and in 1680 the Zia joined Popé's Pueblo Revolt, forcing the colonists south and putting Spanish horses in Pueblo hands for the plains trade. Governor Domingo Jironza Petriz de Cruzate stormed the pueblo in 1689, killing 600 Zia and taking 70 captives. Inter-Pueblo disputes later favoured Diego de Vargas's reconquest, and the Zia leader Antonio Malacate brought the survivors home; about 120 people remained in 1692. The mission was rebuilt and entrusted to Fray Juan Alpuente in 1694, then renovated in 1707 as Nuestra Señora de la Asunción.
zh:
齐亚是齐亚人在赫梅斯河谷的家园，齐亚人是说东部凯雷斯语的普韦布洛族群。13世纪，他们的古代普韦布洛祖先迁入河谷，在灌溉玉米田旁建起土坯普韦布洛，制陶和与邻近凯雷斯、赫梅斯村镇的贸易构成生活基础。1444年，齐亚仍自行管理田地与仪式，尚未受到后来进入新墨西哥的西班牙远征波及。

安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍1583年首先记录齐亚。胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年到来后，修士阿隆索·德·卢戈建立圣佩德罗与圣巴勃罗传教站；到1613年，齐亚劳工已建起教堂和修道院。西班牙统治禁止传统仪式，齐亚遂在1680年参加波佩领导的普韦布洛起义，迫使殖民者南逃，西班牙马匹也经普韦布洛人之手进入大平原贸易。总督多明戈·希龙萨·佩特里斯·德·克鲁萨特1689年攻陷普韦布洛，六百名齐亚人被杀，七十人被俘。普韦布洛诸部之间的争端随后有利于迭戈·德·巴尔加斯再征服，齐亚首领安东尼奥·马拉卡特率幸存者返乡；1692年当地约只剩一百二十人。传教站1694年重建并交由修士胡安·阿尔普恩特主持，1707年整修后改名圣母升天传教站。

en:
The Sobaipuri were an O'odham people who farmed the well-watered valleys of the San Pedro and Santa Cruz rivers in the Pimería Alta, their compact, carefully planned villages set on river terraces where they grew maize, beans and squash with floodwater ditches. The settlements later recorded as Tumacácori and Guevavi had occupied the two valleys for generations before Europeans entered the Southwest. The Sobaipuri traded and intermarried, and at times raided, with the Apache, Jocome and Jano on their eastern flank, and they spoke the same Piman tongue as the Akimel and Tohono O'odham around them. In 1444 no friar or soldier had yet entered their valleys.

Fray Marcos de Niza may have passed Sobaipuri rancherías on the San Pedro in 1539, and Coronado's men entered the region soon after, but the expedition won no submission and the Sobaipuri valleys saw no Spaniard again for roughly 150 years. In 1691 Sobaipuri headmen traveled south to Sáric to invite the Jesuit Eusebio Francisco Kino; he visited Tumacácori and Guevavi, introduced cattle and wheat, and in 1701 raised a church at Guevavi. On Easter Day 1698 the Sobaipuri leader Coro defeated a much larger Apache, Jocome and Jano force that fell on his village of Gaybanipitea on the San Pedro, after which his people became Spain's steadfast allies and the buffer of the Sonora frontier. The Pima revolt of 1751 and the presidio founded at Tubac in 1752 pulled the mission villages toward the garrison, and the new village of Calabazas was gathered in 1756. As Apache raids worsened the Sobaipuri abandoned the San Pedro valley around 1762, and after the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 the Franciscans moved the mission headquarters from Guevavi to Tumacácori in 1771; Guevavi stood empty by 1775, the year a presidio was planted at Tucson. When New Spain's rule ended in 1821, the surviving Sobaipuri had folded into the O'odham communities at San Xavier del Bac and Tumacácori.
zh:
索巴伊普里人是奥奥德姆人的一支，在皮梅里亚阿尔塔境内圣佩德罗河与圣克鲁斯河水源充足的河谷务农。他们布局齐整的密集村落坐落在河流阶地上，用引洪水的沟渠种植玉米、豆类和南瓜。后来被记作图马卡科里和格瓦维的那些村落，在欧洲人进入西南之前的许多世代里就已居住在这两条河谷。索巴伊普里人与东侧的阿帕奇人、霍科梅人和哈诺人通婚、贸易，有时也一同外出劫掠，所说的皮曼语与周围的阿基梅尔人和托霍诺·奥奥德姆人相同。1444年时，还没有修士或士兵进入过他们的河谷。

1539年，修士马科斯·德·尼萨可能在圣佩德罗河畔经过索巴伊普里人的村落，科罗纳多的部下不久也进入这一带，但远征队没有压服任何人，此后约一百五十年间再没有西班牙人来。1691年，索巴伊普里诸首领南行至萨里克，邀请耶稣会士尤塞维奥·弗朗西斯科·基诺北上；基诺走访了图马卡科里和格瓦维，带去牛和小麦，并于1701年在格瓦维主持建起教堂。1698年复活节，阿帕奇、霍科梅和哈诺人的大军乘夜袭击首领科罗在圣佩德罗河畔的盖巴尼皮特亚村，科罗率众以少胜多；此后他的部族成为西班牙坚定的盟友，也是索诺拉边疆的屏障。1751年皮马人起义，1752年西班牙在图巴克设立要塞，各传教村落向守军靠拢，1756年又聚成新的卡拉巴萨斯村。随着阿帕奇袭扰加剧，索巴伊普里人约在1762年放弃圣佩德罗河谷；1767年耶稣会被逐后，方济各会于1771年把传教中心从格瓦维迁往图马卡科里，格瓦维到1775年已无人居住，同年图森设立要塞。1821年新西班牙统治结束时，幸存的索巴伊普里人已融入圣哈维尔·德尔·巴克和图马卡科里的奥奥德姆社群。

en:
The Pinaleño Mountains are the pine-bearing sky island at the heart of this countryside, rising above Sonoran and Chihuahuan desert valleys toward Mount Graham in the upper Gila country. Western Apache called the range Dził Nnilchí' Diyiléé, while the Tsékʼáádn, or Metate People, were the San Carlos and Pinaleño bands who gathered pine nuts, hunted, and farmed beside mountain streams. In 1444 their Ndee family groups moved between these ridges and Gila watercourses, close to older Mogollon and Hohokam farming lands and to Yavapai and O'odham neighbors.

Spanish knowledge entered the Gila watershed soon after the conquest of Mexico: Juan de la Asunción may have reached the river in 1538, and Hernando de Alarcón sailed to its Colorado confluence in 1540. The waterway was long called Río Grande de los Apóstoles or Río del Nombre de Jesús before Spanish writers fixed the name Gila early in the 1700s. Horses transformed Apache raiding by the late 1600s, and raids and reprisals through the next century kept the upper Gila frontier without fixed colonial settlement. Missions and presidios never enclosed the Tsékʼáádn mountains; in 1821 the Ndee still held them.
zh:
皮纳莱尼奥山脉是这片地方核心的松林天空岛，耸立于索诺兰沙漠与奇瓦瓦沙漠的谷地之间，最高峰格雷厄姆山俯瞰希拉河上游。西阿帕奇人称这片山脉为齐尔尼尔奇伊·迪伊莱埃；采卡登人（Tsékʼáádn，意为石磨盘人）属圣卡洛斯与皮纳莱尼奥诸群体，采集松果、狩猎，并在山溪旁耕作。1444年，他们的恩迪家族群体往来于这些山脊和希拉河水道之间，邻近莫戈永、霍霍坎人的古老农地，也与亚瓦派人和奥奥德姆人为邻。

征服墨西哥后不久，西班牙人的地理知识进入希拉河流域：胡安·德·拉·亚松森可能在1538年抵达这条河，埃尔南多·德·阿拉尔孔1540年航行到希拉河与科罗拉多河交汇处。这条水道在16—17世纪长期被称为阿波斯托莱斯大河或耶稣之名河，西班牙文书到18世纪初才固定使用希拉一名。到17世纪末，马匹改变了阿帕奇人的袭掠方式；此后一个世纪，袭掠与报复往复不断，希拉河上游边地始终没有形成固定的殖民定居点。传教站和要塞始终未能围住采卡登人的山地，1821年时恩迪人仍据守群山。

en:
The Taaqtam, later called Serranos by Spaniards, were Takic-speaking people of the San Bernardino Mountains and western Mojave. In 1444 the Yuhaaviatam, or People of the Pines, occupied mountain villages and oak groves, while Desert Serrano groups, including the Vanyume, lived along the intermittent Mojave River leading from the Cajon Pass toward Soda Lake. The stream mostly ran underground, surfacing at gorges and oases such as the village of Wá'peat, where mesquite, yucca, pine nuts, acorns, deer, and bighorn sheep sustained the people. The Mojave trail linked the Colorado River to the coast through this country, carrying coastal shell beads and asphaltum east and Southwestern ceramics and textiles west.

Mission San Gabriel Arcángel was founded on 8 September 1771 and soon claimed Serrano lands and labor. Pedro Fages entered Serrano territory in 1772, and Francisco Garcés followed the Mojave River in March 1776, naming it Arroyo de los Mártires before later Spaniards called it the Río de las Ánimas. In 1812 the Serrano joined the Cahuilla and Quechan in revolt against mission reductions. In 1819 San Gabriel opened the San Bernardino de Sena Estancia, Serrano people were relocated there and dug the Mill Creek Zanja, and the Spanish-language record also states that Mojave warriors killed many Serrano that year. At Mexican independence in 1821, the estancia remained only an edge of Spanish settlement while Taaqtam communities kept the mountains and desert roads.
zh:
塔克塔姆人后被西班牙人称为塞拉诺人，是说塔基克语的圣贝纳迪诺山脉与西莫哈韦居民。1444年，「松林之人」尤哈维亚塔姆群体住在山地村落和橡树林中；包括瓦尼乌姆人在内的沙漠塞拉诺群体，则沿时断时续的莫哈韦河生活，这条水道从卡洪山口通向苏打湖。河水大多在地下流淌，只在峡谷和绿洲露出地面，瓦佩阿特等村落借此获取牧豆、丝兰、松子、橡实、鹿和大角羊。莫哈韦商路从科罗拉多河经此地通往海岸，把沿海的贝壳珠和沥青带向东方，也把西南地区的陶器和织物带向西方。

圣加百列大天使传教站于1771年9月8日建立，很快宣称对塞拉诺土地和劳力的管辖权。佩德罗·法赫斯1772年进入塞拉诺领地，弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯1776年3月沿莫哈韦河探查，将它命名为殉道者溪，后来的西班牙人改称灵魂河。1812年，塞拉诺人联合卡维拉人和克昌人（尤马人）反抗传教站的集居管制。1819年，圣加百列传教站开设圣贝纳迪诺·德·塞纳牧场站，塞拉诺人被迁往那里并挖掘米尔溪灌溉渠；西语资料还记载，莫哈韦战士在这一年杀死许多塞拉诺人。1821年墨西哥独立时，这座牧场站仍只是西班牙人定居区的边缘，塔克塔姆诸群体仍掌握着山地与沙漠道路。

en: The Choinumni were a Kings River people among the many autonomous Yokuts tribes of the San Joaquin Valley. In 1444 their villages stood along a stretch of the upper Kings River, where oak groves supplied acorns, marshes and sloughs yielded fish, waterfowl and roots, and tule rushes roofed pit houses and made rafts. Trails over the Sierra Nevada carried trade with the Mono and other Paiute peoples. Pedro Fages entered the southern valley in 1772, but the Kings River remained beyond the mission frontier until Gabriel Moraga's Spanish expedition arrived in 1805 and named it Río de los Santos Reyes. A friar in the party thought the populous, well-watered valley suitable for a mission and presidio, yet no mission was built there. When New Spain became Mexico in 1821, the Choinumni still occupied their river villages without a colonial settlement among them.
zh: 乔伊努姆尼人是金斯河居民，也是圣华金谷众多自治约库特部族之一。1444年，他们的村落分布在金斯河上游一段河畔：橡树林提供橡实，湿地和河汊出产鱼、水禽与根茎，香蒲则可作半地穴房屋的屋顶并扎成木筏。穿越内华达山脉的小路把他们同莫诺人及其他派尤特人连接起来。1772年，佩德罗·法赫斯进入圣华金谷南部，但金斯河仍在传教边疆之外；1805年，加夫列尔·莫拉加的西班牙远征队到达这里，将河命名为Río de los Santos Reyes（三王河）。随行修士认为这片水源充足、人口稠密的河谷适合建立传教站和要塞，但最终没有任何传教站在此落成。1821年新西班牙变为墨西哥时，乔伊努姆尼人仍居住在河畔村落中，殖民居民点尚未进入他们之间。

en:
Ohlone is the country around the great inland sea of San Francisco Bay, whose narrow gate had let even Cabrillo's ships sail past. In 1444 more than fifty autonomous tribelets lived between the bay's marshes and Monterey in the south, among them the Ramaytush at the peninsula tip, where the village of Chutchui stood, and the Tamyen of the Santa Clara valley. They spoke related Utian languages, followed the Kuksu cult and raised enormous shellmounds beside their waterside villages. Tule rafts carried them across the bay to trade and feud, and salmon, acorns and the waterfowl clouds made this one of the most thickly peopled lands north of Mexico.

On 4 November 1769 Gaspar de Portola, marching up the coast, climbed Sweeney Ridge and became the first European to see the bay. Juan de Ayala sailed the San Carlos through the Golden Gate on 5 August 1775, and his pilot Canizares drew its first chart. Juan Bautista de Anza chose the settlement sites in March 1776: Father Francisco Palou said the first mass at Mission San Francisco de Asis, soon called Dolores, on 29 June, and Jose Joaquin Moraga raised the Royal Presidio on 17 September. Mission Santa Clara and the pueblo of San Jose followed in 1777, and Mission San Jose in 1797. Hundreds of Ohlone entered the missions in 1794 and 1795, just as a deadly epidemic swept the bay. In 1807 and again in 1810-11 Russian-led Aleut otter hunters raided the bay in kayaks and carried thousands of skins off to Canton. By the 1810s Dolores held some 1,100 neophytes, yet more than 5,000 had died there by the time Mexico took the province in 1821.
zh:
奥洛内是旧金山湾这片巨大内海四周的土地，海湾狭窄的入口曾让卡布里略的船也驶了过去。1444年，五十多个互不统属的部落小群住在湾边沼泽到南方蒙特雷之间：半岛尖端是拉马伊图什人，楚特奎伊村就坐落在此；圣克拉拉谷里住着塔米恩人。他们操亲属相近的乌蒂安语系语言，奉行库克苏信仰，在水畔村庄旁堆起巨大的贝丘。人们乘香蒲筏渡湾去贸易和械斗，鲑鱼、橡子和遮天蔽日的水鸟，使这里成为墨西哥以北人口最稠密的地区之一。

1769年11月4日，沿海岸北上的加斯帕尔·德·波尔托拉登上斯威尼岭，成为第一个望见这片海湾的欧洲人。1775年8月5日，胡安·德·阿亚拉驾「圣卡洛斯号」穿过金门，领航员卡尼萨雷斯绘下海湾的第一张地图。1776年3月，胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·安萨选定建址：6月29日，弗朗西斯科·帕洛乌神父在圣弗朗西斯科·德·阿西斯传教所（不久即以「多洛雷斯」闻名）举行第一场弥撒；9月17日，何塞·华金·莫拉加建起王家要塞。圣克拉拉传教所和圣何塞镇随后于1777年建立，圣何塞传教所则建于1797年。1794至1795年，数百名奥洛内人进入传教所，恰在此时一场致命疫病席卷湾区。1807年以及1810至1811年，为俄国人效力的阿留申海獭猎手两度乘皮艇闯入湾中，把数千张海獭皮运往广州。到1810年代，多洛雷斯约有一千一百名新信徒，而到1821年墨西哥接掌这片土地时，已有五千多人死在那里。

en: West of the Sacramento, from Mount Shasta to San Francisco Bay, lived the Wintun, in one of California's richest valleys. They were three peoples: the Wintu on the upper river and McCloud, the Nomlaki on its central tributaries, and the Patwin of the lower valley, perhaps 12,000 strong in 1770. Domed earth lodges lined the streams; the year turned on salmon runs, acorn meal, manzanita cider and woven baskets. The Patwin kept the Kuksu religion of the 'big head' dances, shared with the Maidu and Pomo. In 1808 the Spaniard Gabriel Moraga entered the southern valley and named the river the Rio de los Sacramentos; the southern Patwin were already being pressed toward the missions, but upriver no European had come by 1821.
zh: 萨克拉门托河以西，从沙斯塔山到旧金山湾，温图诸族住在加利福尼亚最富庶的河谷之一。他们分三支：北支住在河上游与麦克劳德河，中支据有中部各支流，南支是下游的帕特温人，1770年人口约一万二千。圆顶的土屋沿河排开；鲑鱼汛、橡子粉、熊果酒和编织篮筐构成一年的生计。帕特温人奉行「大头舞」的库克苏崇拜，迈杜人和波莫人同有此俗。1808年，西班牙军人加布里埃尔·莫拉加进入南部河谷，将河命名为「圣事之河」，萨克拉门托河的名字便由此而来；南方的帕特温人已被逼向传教团，而直到1821年，河的上游仍未有欧洲人到来。

en:
The Paipai, also called Akwa'ala or Yakakwal, held a broad stretch of northern Baja California between the Kiliwa to the south and the Kumeyaay and Cocopa to the north. Their trails ran from San Vicente on the Pacific almost to the Colorado River delta, linking better-watered Pacific hills with the drier Gulf side. Like their Yuman neighbors, they lived by hunting, gathering, fishing, and seasonal movement rather than by towns or cultivation. In 1444 autonomous Paipai bands occupied this corridor between neighboring Yuman peoples.

Sebastián Vizcaíno's ships mapped the coast in 1602, but sustained European contact did not begin until Gaspar de Portolà and Junípero Serra led the California expedition through western Paipai country in 1769. Dominican missionaries Miguel Hidalgo and Joaquín Valero founded San Vicente on 2 August 1780. With fertile soil, abundant water, and a position on the mission road, it became both a major Dominican center and a military post watching the peoples of the lower Colorado. José Loriente and Tomás Valdellón opened the inland Santa Catarina mission on 12 November 1797, near the Paipai-Kumeyaay border. Its dams watered wheat, maize, barley, and vegetables and it kept cattle, horses, mules, and sheep, but poor land and difficult supply lines kept the settlement weak while introduced diseases reduced the people it congregated. By Mexican independence in 1821, the Paipai mission frontier remained fragile.
zh:
派派人又称阿克瓦阿拉或亚卡克瓦尔，据有下加利福尼亚北部的广阔地带，南接基利瓦人，北邻库梅亚伊人与科科帕人。他们的活动路线西起太平洋畔的圣维森特，几乎东达科罗拉多河三角洲，把水源较多的太平洋山地与较干燥的加利福尼亚湾一侧连接起来。和邻近的尤曼诸族一样，他们以狩猎、采集、捕鱼和季节性迁徙为生，没有城镇或农业。1444年，自治的派派小队占据着这条夹在相邻尤曼族群之间的走廊。

1602年，塞瓦斯蒂安·比斯开诺的船队测绘了这段海岸，但持续的欧洲接触要到1769年加斯帕尔·德·波尔塔拉和胡尼佩罗·塞拉率领加利福尼亚远征队穿过派派西部才开始。1780年8月2日，多明我会士米格尔·伊达尔戈与华金·巴莱罗建立圣维森特传教站。这里土壤肥沃、水源充足，又位于传教干道上，既是多明我会的重要中心，也是监视科罗拉多河下游诸族的军事据点。1797年11月12日，何塞·洛里恩特和托马斯·巴尔德利翁在派派与库梅亚伊边界附近开设内陆的圣卡塔琳娜传教站。水坝灌溉小麦、玉米、大麦和蔬菜，传教站也饲养牛、马、骡和羊，但土地贫瘠、补给困难使聚落始终衰弱，传入的疾病更削减了被集居的人口。到1821年墨西哥独立时，派派地区的传教边疆仍然脆弱。

en:
Tecpatitlan was the older spelling of the Tepatitlán district and lay in the Tecuexe highlands of Jalisco, on the routes between Tonala and the drier Guamare frontier. The Tecuexes were Uto-Aztecan speakers divided among independent lordships; Tecpatitlan, Acatic, Xalostotitlan and Yahualican were among their seats. Tonala, whose Nahuatl name meant the place through which the sun rises, was one of the principal chiefdoms of central Jalisco. In 1444 these small realms bordered the Caxcanes and Guachichiles to the north, the Guamares to the east and the Purépecha Empire to the south.

The Purépecha wars for Lake Chapala's saltpeter opened in 1480 and lasted until 1510. An army marched on Tonala, but the ruler Cihualpilli allied with the kingdom of Colliman, and her captain Coyotl helped defeat the invaders at Tlajomulco. In 1530 Pedro Almíndez Chirino passed through Tecpatitlan on Nuño de Guzmán's campaign, while Franciscans baptized the settlement as San Francisco de Tecpatitlan; Tonala submitted after a clash and was incorporated into Nueva Galicia, its ruler baptized Juana Bautista. After Guadalajara's foundation in 1535, Tonala lost its old primacy. The Mixtón War of 1541–1542, epidemics and the later Chichimeca War broke Tecuexe power, and colonial estates and parish churches, including San Francisco at Tecpatitlan from 1742, took shape across the highlands.
zh:
特克帕蒂特兰是特帕蒂特兰地区的旧名，位于哈利斯科的特库埃克塞高地，处在托纳拉与更干旱的瓜马尔边地之间的通道上。特库埃克塞人使用犹他—阿兹特克语系语言，分成若干彼此独立的领主政权；特克帕蒂特兰、阿卡特克、哈洛斯托蒂特兰和亚瓦利坎都是其据点。托纳拉的纳瓦特尔语含义是太阳升起之地，也是哈利斯科中部最重要的酋长领地之一。1444年，这些小政权北接卡斯坎人和瓜奇奇尔人，东邻瓜马尔人，南面则与普雷佩查帝国接壤。

1480年，为争夺查帕拉湖畔硝石而起的普雷佩查战争爆发，一直持续到1510年。普雷佩查军队向托纳拉推进，统治者西瓦皮尔皮与科利曼王国结盟，她的将领科约特尔率军在特拉霍穆尔科击败入侵者。1530年，佩德罗·阿尔门德斯·奇里诺随努尼奥·德·古斯曼的征战经过特克帕蒂特兰，方济各会修士把定居地命名为圣弗朗西斯科·德·特克帕蒂特兰并进行传教；托纳拉在一场冲突后归附，被纳入新加利西亚，女统治者受洗取名胡安娜·包蒂斯塔。1535年瓜达拉哈拉建立后，托纳拉失去旧日的首要地位。1541—1542年的米克斯顿战争、疫病以及后来的奇奇梅克战争瓦解了特库埃克塞人的力量，殖民庄园和教区教堂逐渐遍布高地，特克帕蒂特兰的圣弗朗西斯科教堂即于1742年动工。

en:
Xilotepec, whose Nahuatl name means the hill of young maize, rises in the wooded hills north of the Valley of Mexico. It was the centre of an Otomi lordship with subject towns such as Soyaniquilpan, Huichapan and Nopala, linked by trade and kinship to the Huasteca, Michoacan and the Guanajuato frontier. Acamapichtli of Tenochtitlan conquered the district in 1379, but its people later recovered their autonomy. In 1444 Xilotepec was therefore still an Otomi realm, its villages growing maize and making pottery and cloth while Chichimeca peoples held the dry country farther north.

Mexica power returned under Ahuitzotl: in 1487 a campaign against the Otomi of Xilotepec destroyed Chiapa and confirmed Tenochtitlan's rule. After the Spanish conquest colonization began in 1526, Franciscans established a doctrine, and Juan Jaramillo and later Bishop Juan de Zumárraga held encomienda interests in its farmland. When silver was discovered at Zacatecas and Guanajuato, Xilotepec became a station on the royal road carrying miners, cattle and supplies into the Bajío; Otomi warriors and settlers in turn helped the Spanish pacify that frontier and found Querétaro and Apaseo. Guamare raiders reached Xilotepec in 1569. In 1810 Otomi villagers from the province joined Miguel Hidalgo and Ignacio Allende on the insurgent road south.
zh:
希洛特佩克的纳瓦特尔语含义是嫩玉米山，位于墨西哥谷北方的林木丘陵中。它是奥托米人领主政权的中心，管辖索亚尼基尔潘、维查潘、诺帕拉等城镇，商路和亲属联系通向瓦斯特卡、米却肯和瓜纳华托边地。特诺奇蒂特兰的阿卡马皮奇特利曾于1379年征服此地，但居民后来恢复自治。因此在1444年，希洛特佩克仍是奥托米人的政权；村落种植玉米、制作陶器和织物，更北面的干旱地带则分布着奇奇梅卡诸族。

阿维索特尔在位时，墨西卡势力卷土重来：1487年，墨西卡向希洛特佩克的奥托米人开战，摧毁恰帕，并巩固了特诺奇蒂特兰的统治。西班牙征服后，殖民活动于1526年展开，方济各会在此设立传教区，胡安·哈拉米略以及后来的主教胡安·德·苏马拉加都曾在这片农地上享有委托监护权益。萨卡特卡斯和瓜纳华托发现银矿后，希洛特佩克成为王家大道上的驿站，矿工、牲畜和补给经此进入巴希奥；奥托米战士和定居者也协助西班牙人安抚这条边地，并参与建立克雷塔罗和阿帕塞奥。1569年，瓜马尔袭击者曾进抵希洛特佩克。1810年，当地奥托米村民加入米格尔·伊达尔戈和伊格纳西奥·阿连德向南推进的起义队伍。

en:
The Pame, who call themselves Xi'ui, held the rugged ranges and valleys east of the Bajío: the Rio Verde country, the Sierra Gorda and the routes toward Tamaulipas and the Huasteca. In 1444 they lived from hunting, gathering, trade and seasonal maize farming, moving between rancherías and speaking an Oto-Pamean tongue. Closer to Mesoamerica than the desert nations to the north, they traded and sometimes lived beside Nahua, Otomi and Purépecha frontier villages. Spanish colonists later called this broad country Pamería.

Pressure from Spanish ranches and allied Otomi settlements reached the Bajío edge in the 1530s. After silver was found at Zacatecas, the Chichimeca War of 1550–1600 drew Pame bands into frontier raiding; Spanish records first called them the most peaceful Chichimeca nation, but by the 1570s reported kidnappings and killings. Cattlemen entered Rio Verde after 1600, and Fray Juan Bautista de Mollinedo founded the El Palmar mission in 1617. The mountains held out until José de Escandón's 1740 campaign culminated at Media Luna, breaking Jonaz and Ximpece resistance and opening the Guanajuato–Zacatecas routes; soldiers then burned Pame villages to concentrate their people around missions. The five Franciscan churches at Jalpan, Landa, Tancoyol, Concá and Tilaco were built from 1750 to 1760 under Junípero Serra, then secularized in 1770. Pame communities rose with the independence movement in 1810, Zenón Fernández raised insurgent colours in the Rio Verde valley, and royalists sacked Jalpan in 1819. When independence came in 1821, the Pamería remained restive.
zh:
帕梅人自称希乌伊人（Xi'ui），据有巴希奥东侧崎岖的山地和谷地，包括里奥韦尔德、谢拉戈尔达以及通往塔毛利帕斯和瓦斯特卡的道路。1444年，他们以狩猎、采集、贸易和季节性玉米种植为生，在各个小村落间迁移，使用奥托-帕梅语族的语言。与北方沙漠族群相比，他们和中美洲定居社会联系更紧，会同边境上的纳瓦人、奥托米人和普雷佩查人贸易，有时还毗邻而居。西班牙殖民者后来把这片广阔土地称为帕梅里亚。

1530年代，西班牙牧场和结盟的奥托米人定居点把压力带到巴希奥边缘。萨卡特卡斯发现银矿后，1550年至1600年的奇奇梅克战争使帕梅群体卷入边境袭掠；西班牙记载起初称他们是奇奇梅克诸族中最平和的一支，但到1570年代已有绑架和杀害西班牙人的报告。1600年后，牧牛人进入里奥韦尔德，胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·莫利内多修士1617年建立埃尔帕尔马传教所。山地则坚守更久，直到何塞·德·埃斯坎东1740年的远征在梅迪亚卢纳达到高潮，击破霍纳斯人和欣佩塞人的抵抗，打通瓜纳华托至萨卡特卡斯的道路；军队随后焚毁帕梅村落，把人口集中到传教所附近。1750年至1760年，胡尼佩罗·塞拉主持修建了哈尔潘、兰达、坦科约尔、孔卡和蒂拉科五座方济各会教堂，传教所1770年世俗化。1810年，帕梅社区随独立运动起事，塞农·费尔南德斯在里奥韦尔德谷地举起起义旗帜，保王军1819年洗劫哈尔潘。1821年独立到来时，帕梅里亚仍未真正安定。

en:
The high valleys of southern Zacatecas, around Nochistlán and Apulco and running south to the lakes of Pechichitán, were the señorío of Xicconecan. Its people, the Xiconaques, were Caxcan-speaking farmers whom the Nahuas called the Iztachichimecah, the 'white Chichimecas', for their pale skin or the whitish earth of their land. They planted seasonal maize in the valleys, hunted deer and hare, and lived in circular houses of zacate grass; their rulers Panen and Xahualotl held Teocaltiche as a tributary and warred with the neighbouring Cuxtaques, while around 1400 their tribes joined the Guamare confederacy raised against the Aztec and Purépecha empires. In 1444 Xiconecan remained free, its warriors recently hardened by the Zacateco pressure that was driving fresh Caxcan bands south from the Juchipila.

Nuño de Guzmán's army came through Tecpatitlan in 1531 and broke the señorío, and on 5 January 1532 he founded the first Guadalajara near Nochistlán, soon abandoned. In the Mixtón War of 1541–42 Xahualotl's son Francisco Tenamaztle led the Caxcanes, besieging Guadalajara and holding the peñol of Mixtón until the Spanish took Nochistlán and stormed the rock; Tenamaztle was captured and shipped to Spain. Raiding went on through the Chichimeca War — in 1551 the Xiconaques destroyed Diego de Ibarra's stock ranch — until Hernando Martel defeated them and, with the surviving Xiconaque and Cuxtaque families, founded the Villa de Santa María de los Lagos on 31 March 1563. Cattle and sheep haciendas then spread over the plains, with twenty thousand head by 1600, and the Real Comanja silver mine opened in 1561. The lawyer Francisco Primo de Verdad, born at Lagos, was among the first criollos to claim self-rule and died in a Mexico City dungeon in 1808; another native son, Pedro Moreno, led insurgent guerrillas until he was killed in 1817.
zh:
萨卡特卡斯南部的高地山谷，以诺奇斯特兰和阿普尔科为中心，向南一直到佩奇奇坦的湖群，是西科内坎酋邦之地。其居民希科纳克人是说卡克斯坎语的农人，纳瓦人把他们叫作伊斯特塔奇奇梅卡，即「白奇奇梅克人」，得名于他们较浅的肤色或当地泛白的碱性土地。他们在谷地种靠天吃饭的玉米，猎鹿和野兔，住圆锥形的茅草屋；君长帕年、萨瓦洛特尔父子让特奥卡尔蒂切纳贡，又与邻邦库克斯坦交战；约1400年，他们的部落加入为对抗阿兹特克和普雷佩查两大帝国而结成的瓜马尔联盟。1444年时西科内坎仍保持自由，萨卡特科人不断南侵、把新的卡克斯坎人群从胡奇皮拉河方向压向南方，也使这里的战士久经战阵。

1531年，努尼奥·德·古斯曼的大军经特克帕蒂特兰而来，击灭这个酋邦；1532年1月5日，他在诺奇斯特兰附近建立第一座瓜达拉哈拉，不久即废弃。1541至1542年的米斯特翁战争中，萨瓦洛特尔之子弗朗西斯科·特纳马斯特莱率领卡克斯坎人围攻瓜达拉哈拉，据守米斯特翁山崖；西班牙人攻下诺奇斯特兰并强攻山崖，特纳马斯特莱被俘后押往西班牙。袭击在奇奇梅克战争期间持续不断——1551年希科纳克人摧毁了迭戈·德·伊瓦拉的牧场——直到埃尔南多·马特尔将其击败，并于1563年3月31日同幸存的希科纳克、库克斯塔克家族一起建立圣马里亚·德洛斯拉戈斯镇。此后牛羊庄园遍布平原，到1600年牲畜已有两万头，雷亚尔科曼哈银矿也于1561年开采。生于拉戈斯的律师弗朗西斯科·普里莫·德·贝尔达是最早主张克里奥尔人自治的人物之一，1808年死于墨西哥城的地牢；另一位本地子弟佩德罗·莫雷诺率领起义游击队作战，1817年战死。

en:
Northwestern Chihuahua, around the future district of Janos, was Jocome country. The Jocomes were probably a sub-tribe or close relatives of the Suma, and like the Janos they moved through arid mountains and basins as hunter-gatherers without fixed settlements. In 1444 autonomous bands travelled between waterholes and hunting grounds, close to Suma, Jano, Sobaipuri, Opata and Apache groups; they traded with their neighbours and sometimes joined them in raids or marriage alliances.

In 1640 Franciscans founded Nuestra Señora de la Soledad de los Janos as a mission for the Janos, Suma and related peoples. A native uprising destroyed it in the 1680s, by which time the Jocomes were prominent near Janos. In 1684 Suma, Janos and Jocome bands still hostile to Spain found refuge in the Chiricahua Mountains and drew closer to the Apache. In 1686 Juan Fernández de la Fuente established the Presidio de San Felipe y Santiago de Janos. The Apache were first recorded on this frontier of New Spain in 1692, and although the Franciscan mission was re-established among Janos and Jocomes in 1717, the Jocome name gradually disappeared from Spanish records, its bearers probably absorbed into Apache bands.
zh:
奇瓦瓦西北部、后来雅诺斯一带，是霍科梅人的土地。霍科梅人可能是苏马人的分支或近亲，和雅诺人一样在干旱山地与盆地中狩猎采集，没有固定居所。1444年，若干自主游群往来于水源和猎场之间，邻近苏马、雅诺、索瓦伊普里、奥帕塔和阿帕奇诸部；他们与邻部贸易，也有时共同袭掠或互通婚姻。

1640年，方济各会为雅诺人、苏马人及相关部族建立孤独圣母·德·洛斯·哈诺斯传教站。1680年代，原住民起义摧毁了传教站，此时霍科梅人已在雅诺斯附近十分活跃。1684年，仍与西班牙为敌的苏马、雅诺和霍科梅游群退守奇里卡瓦山，并与阿帕奇人日益接近。1686年，胡安·费尔南德斯·德·拉·富恩特建立圣费利佩—圣地亚哥·德·雅诺斯要塞。1692年，阿帕奇人首次在新西班牙的这道边疆留下记录；尽管传教站1717年又在雅诺人和霍科梅人中间重建，霍科梅之名仍逐渐从西班牙文书中消失，其部众大概被阿帕奇诸部吸收。

en:
Between the Sierra de Morones and the Sierra de Nochistlán, the deep Juchipila river canyon was the señorío of Xochipillan, 'the place of fair flowers'. Around 1170 Caxcan warriors of Nahuatl speech came up the canyon, drove out the earlier Tecuexe villagers and made the fortified peñol of Tlaltan their capital, its citadel reachable only by a single steep stairway. Xochipillan grew into a cacicazgo of real weight, drawing tribute from Apotzolco, Xalpan, Tepechitlán and the other towns of the canyon; its farmers grew maize and cotton on the warm river terraces while its raiders harried the Zacateco and Guachichil lands to the north and east. In 1444 its lord, like the rulers of Nochistlán and Xalpa, answered to no outside power.

Cristóbal de Oñate took Tlaltan in 1530–31 and Xochipillan was granted in encomienda to Hernán Flores; Franciscans raised the canyon's first monastery around 1532. When the encomenderos' exactions grew unbearable, the last Caxcan lord, Xiuhtecuhtli, conspired with Tenamaxtle of Nochistlán and Pentacatl of Xalpa, and in 1541 the canyon rose: on 24 June the Caxcanes destroyed Pedro de Alvarado's army near Nochistlán, and the conquistador died of his wounds on 4 July. Viceroy Mendoza came in person with more than fifty thousand men and stormed the Peñón del Mixtón on 16 December 1541; Fray Antonio de Segovia then persuaded over six thousand survivors to come down peacefully, and Apozol and Juchipila were refounded. The Franciscan convent and hospital of 1542 were followed by the parish church of San Francisco in 1627, and from 1548 Juchipila governed a vast alcaldía mayor; in 1804 Charles IV transferred it from the Intendancy of Guadalajara to that of Zacatecas. When the insurgency came in 1810, the Caxcan and mestizo families of the canyon joined it and held to the cause until 1821.
zh:
在莫罗内斯山与诺奇斯特兰山之间，幽深的胡奇皮拉河谷是索奇皮尔兰酋邦之地，名字意为「名花之乡」。约1170年，操纳瓦特尔语的卡克斯坎武士沿河谷而上，逐走早先的特克塞村民，把设防的特拉尔坦山崖作为都城——崖顶城堡只有一条陡峭的阶梯可通。索奇皮尔兰发展成举足轻重的酋邦，向阿波特索尔科、哈尔潘、特佩奇特兰及河谷诸镇征收贡赋；农人在温暖的河阶上种玉米和棉花，战士则北上东征，袭扰萨卡特科人和瓜奇奇尔人的土地。1444年时，它的君长与诺奇斯特兰、哈尔帕的统治者一样，不受任何外来势力统属。

1530至1531年，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥尼亚特攻下特拉尔坦，索奇皮尔兰被作为委托监护地封给埃尔南·弗洛雷斯；方济各会士约在1532年建起河谷里的第一座修道院。由于监护主的盘剥不堪忍受，末代卡克斯坎君长休伊特莱库特利与诺奇斯特兰的特纳马斯特莱、哈尔帕的彭塔卡特尔密谋，1541年河谷举事：6月24日卡克斯坎人在诺奇斯特兰附近歼灭佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多的军队，这位征服者7月4日伤重而死。总督门多萨亲率五万多大军前来，1541年12月16日强攻米斯特翁山崖；随后修士安东尼奥·德·塞戈维亚说服六千多名幸存者和平下山，阿波索尔和胡奇皮拉得以重建。1542年方济各会修道院和医院设立，1627年又建成圣方济各堂区教堂；自1548年起，胡奇皮拉统辖一片幅员辽阔的大市政官区，1804年卡洛斯四世把它从瓜达拉哈拉都督区划归萨卡特卡斯都督区。1810年独立起义爆发后，河谷的卡克斯坎和混血家族纷纷投身起义，一直坚持到1821年。

en:
The Rarámuri—whom the Spanish would call Tarahumara—held the pine-clad ridges and gorges of the Sierra Madre Occidental, a maze of high mesas and deep canyons in western Chihuahua. They spoke a Uto-Aztecan tongue and farmed maize and beans on the canyon floors and benches, moving with their goats between highland and lowland pastures and gathering at corn-beer feasts called tesgüinadas. Scattered homesteads of logs or stone, sometimes caves, answered to no lord beyond their own elders, and in 1444 the sierra, its forests and its deep barrancas belonged entirely to them.

Jesuits made the first contact in 1606, and Juan Fonte opened the mission of San Pablo Balleza on the southern edge of their country; Fonte died with seven fellow Jesuits in the Tepehuán rising of 1616, and the mission stood empty for more than a decade. The great silver strike at Parral in 1631 pulled slavers, ranchers and missionaries into the eastern valleys, and missions soon multiplied at Satevó, Huejotitán, San Felipe and Las Bocas. In 1648 the Rarámuri burned San Francisco de Borja. Teporaca, a war captain who had once helped build the Spanish Villa de Aguilar, then led a still greater rising across the Papigochi valley in 1652; royal troops under Diego Guajardo Fajardo crushed it, and on 4 March 1653 Teporaca was hanged from the tallest pine at Tomochi. Mountain bands drove out priests and settlers until the Jesuits returned in the 1670s and baptised thousands, and further wars in 1696–1698 ended in defeat, yet the high sierra was never truly conquered. When the Jesuits were expelled in 1767 the Franciscans could not sustain their missions, and the Rarámuri withdrew deeper into the barrancas, keeping their language and their ways. The independence wars of the 1810s scarcely reached those heights, and in 1821 their mountains became part of Mexico.
zh:
拉拉穆里人——西班牙人后来称他们为塔拉乌马拉人——据有西马德雷山脉松涛覆盖的山脊与沟壑，那是西奇瓦瓦一片由高山台地和深峡构成的迷宫。他们操犹他—阿兹特克语族的语言，在谷底和台地上种植玉米、菜豆，赶着山羊在高山与低地牧场间转场，并在名为特斯吉纳达的玉米酒宴上聚会。散布各处的原木或石砌小屋（有时就是洞穴）只听命于本族长老，不认任何外来君长；1444年，整片群山、森林和深谷都完全属于他们。

耶稣会士1606年首次与他们接触，胡安·丰特在其南缘建起圣巴勃罗·巴列萨传教站；丰特在1616年的特佩瓦起义中与七名同会修士一同遇难，传教站空废了十几年。1631年帕拉尔发现大银矿，奴隶贩子、牧场主和传教士随之涌入东部谷地，萨特沃、韦霍蒂坦、圣费利佩和拉斯博卡斯很快建起传教站。1648年，拉拉穆里人焚毁圣弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈传教站。曾协助西班牙人修建阿吉拉尔镇的军事首领特波拉卡，于1652年在整个帕皮戈奇谷领导了规模更大的起义；迭戈·瓜哈尔多·法哈多率领王室军队将其镇压，1653年3月4日，特波拉卡被绞死在托莫奇最高的松树上。高山上的族人把神父和移民赶走，直到1670年代耶稣会士才得以返回，为数千人施洗；1696至1698年的又一次战争仍告失败，但高高的群山从未被真正征服。1767年耶稣会被驱逐后，方济各会无力维持各传教站，拉拉穆里人退入更深的峡谷，保住了自己的语言和生活方式。1810年代的独立战争几乎没有波及这些高山，1821年他们的群山成为墨西哥的一部分。

en:
The Náayeri—known to the Spanish as the Cora—held the knotted canyons and high mesas of the Sierra del Nayar, a rugged mountain fastness between the Pacific plain and the central plateau. In their scattered ranchos they grew maize, beans and amaranth and answered to no outside lord; the Muutzisti, Teacuacitzti and Ateacari lived by their own ancient laws, a pagan world at the very edge of Mesoamerica. In 1444 their steep gorges had never seen a Spaniard, and the traders' roads kept to the lowlands below.

Tradition dates the uniting of the three tribes into the kingdom of Huacica, also called Xécora, to 1493, when Na'ayarij fixed his capital at Sacaymuta. When Nuño de Guzmán's conquistadores pushed into Nueva Galicia in the early 1530s, Na'ayarij defeated them in several fights, and in 1536 he sealed an alliance with the Huichol king Goaxicar; he himself accepted baptism in 1531, but the mountain kingdom kept its freedom. For nearly two hundred years the Cora remained a pagan island in a sea of Christian Indians—no mine, hacienda or mission took root, while the kings Huaynoli, Yocuari, Urysty and Tonati held the high sierra and raided Acaponeta, Aztatlán and Sentispac on the frontier below. A Spanish expedition failed in 1716, and in 1720 Tonati met the viceroy Baltasar de Zúñiga in person and refused to lay down his arms even for the promised right to buy salt at Mexcaltitán. The Spaniards returned in force in 1722: at the Mesa del Nayar the Cora and Huichol army under Tlahuitole was broken and its captain executed, while Tonati was carried off to Guadalajara and died in its prison in 1725. Friars and missions entered the sierra at last, though the old rites lived on beneath the new faith. After the independence wars of 1810–1821 the mountains of Xécora passed with New Spain into independent Mexico.
zh:
纳亚里人——西班牙人称之为科拉人——据有奈亚尔山区交错的峡谷与高台地，那是横亘在太平洋沿岸平原与中央高原之间的一片险峻山地。他们在分散的村落里种植玉米、菜豆和苋米，不认任何外来君长；穆齐斯蒂、特阿夸齐斯特和阿特阿卡利三个部落按古老的规矩生活，是美索亚美利加最边缘的一个异教世界。1444年，他们陡峭的峡谷还未见过西班牙人，商路也只在山下低地间绕行。

按民间口传传统，三个部落在1493年由纳亚里统一为瓦西卡王国，又称塞科拉，定都萨凯穆塔。1530年代初，努尼奥·德·古斯曼的征服者队伍攻入新加利西亚，纳亚里数度将其击败，又于1536年与维乔尔人的国王戈阿西卡尔结盟；他本人在1531年接受了洗礼，山中的王国却保住了自由。此后近两百年间，科拉人始终是「基督教印第安人汪洋中的一座异教孤岛」——矿场、庄园和传教站无一能在此扎根，瓦伊诺利、约夸里、乌里斯蒂、托纳蒂诸王相继据守高山，不时下山袭扰边境地带的阿卡波内塔、阿斯特兰和森蒂斯帕克。1716年一支西班牙远征队无功而返；1720年，托纳蒂亲自会见总督巴尔塔萨尔·德·苏尼加，拒绝了以放下武器换取在梅斯卡尔蒂坦购盐之权的条件。1722年西班牙人大举重来，在奈亚尔台地击溃了由特拉维托莱率领的科拉—维乔尔联军，特拉维托莱被处死，托纳蒂则被押往瓜达拉哈拉，1725年死于狱中。修士和传教站终于进入山区，但古老的仪式在新信仰的掩盖下延续。经过1810至1821年的独立战争，塞科拉的群山随新西班牙并入独立的墨西哥。

en:
The Acaxee held the gorges and pine ridges east of Culiacán, a mountain fastness the Spaniards would call Topia, running some two hundred kilometres through what is now eastern Sinaloa and western Durango. Sedentary farmers of maize, beans, squash, chile and cotton, they also hunted and fished where the steep slopes gave poor harvests, living in autonomous extended-family villages that followed elders in peace and chose war leaders only in danger. A warlike people, they kept a constant frontier with the Xixime to the south and the Tepehuán beyond the eastern ranges, and Spanish chroniclers would later accuse them of eating foes taken in battle—a charge never proven. In 1444 their canyons knew no foreign rule.

The first Spanish foothold was the mining town of Topia, founded in 1564; the rich silver veins struck in the 1580s drew encomenderos, slaves and forced Acaxee labour, while epidemics in 1576–1577, 1590 and 1596–1597 reduced the people to a few thousand. In 1600 the Jesuit Hernando de Santarén toured the sierra with Captain Diego de Ávila, resettling the Acaxee into mission towns, burning their idols and cutting their hair. In December 1601 the messianic leader Perico rose, blending Christian and native promises of deliverance: within weeks some fifty Spaniards lay dead, the mining camps and forty churches were burned, and forty settlers were besieged in the church at San Andrés until relief arrived from Durango. The mines stood still for two years, until a Spanish army with Indian allies broke the rising in 1603; Perico and forty-eight war leaders were executed and the surviving rebels sold into slavery. A smallpox epidemic in 1607, arriving with Halley's Comet, extinguished what remained of the Acaxee cause, though a few fought on in the Tepehuán revolt of 1616. As a people the Acaxee then vanish from the records, their mountains left to missions, haciendas and the silver mines of Nueva Vizcaya; the Jesuits departed with the expulsion of 1767, and after 1821 the old Topia sierra became part of independent Mexico.
zh:
阿卡塞人据有库利亚坎以东的峡谷与松脊，这片西班牙人日后称作托皮亚的山地纵长约两百公里，纵贯今锡那罗亚东部与杜兰戈西部。他们是定居农人，种植玉米、菜豆、南瓜、辣椒和棉花，但陡坡上收成不足，也靠渔猎贴补生计；各家族村落各自为政，平时听从长老，遇有战事才共举军事首领。这是个好战的族群，与南边的希希梅人和东山岭外的特佩瓦人长年交战，西班牙编年史家后来还声称他们食用战场上的敌尸——此说始终没有证据。1444年，他们的峡谷尚不知外来统治为何物。
