坤甸地处婆罗洲内河大动脉卡普阿斯河入海口的沼泽三角洲，正压在赤道线上。1444年，河口一带只有几个马来渔村，处在喃吧哇和婆罗洲西南部更古老的丹戎布拉势力圈的松散影响之下。兰达河、东万律河一带的达雅克人淘洗沙金，连同在后方森林里采来的藤条、蜂蜡和樟脑，顺流运到海口。

18世纪中叶起，黄金引来大批华工，他们由三发的统治者招募而来，自治的采矿结社「公司」（kongsi）很快掌控了上游各矿区。1771年，离开喃吧哇的阿拉伯圣裔沙里夫·阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼在卡普阿斯小河与兰达河交汇处辟地建埠，创立坤甸苏丹国；荷兰人于1778年承认他的苏丹称号，又在1779年立约，在其卡德里亚赫王宫对岸设立商馆。此前的1777年，东万律上游的客家矿工已推举罗芳伯建立兰芳共和国，这个公司之邦与新生的坤甸苏丹国结盟、向清朝称臣，自养民兵、自设公堂。到1821年，三角洲已是马来宫廷、华人矿镇与荷兰商人三足鼎立的世界。

en:
Meliau lies inland on the middle Kapuas, among the first broad rice plains met after pushing up from the Borneo coast. Its riverbanks were Dayak country, with Malay traders settled among the villages, and the river carried their dealings downstream to the Sukadana coast, where the old Malay kingdom of Tanjungpura had stood since the eighth century. Local tradition remembers the upriver lands as appanages of princes of Majapahit blood who left warring Tanjungpura for the interior. In 1444 Meliau was a scatter of river villages, shipping rice, resin and forest produce down the Kapuas and keeping the old Hindu and ancestral customs of the inland courts.

Islam reached Sukadana in 1550 and crept up the Kapuas only gradually. The Kerajaan Meliau enters the records in 1762, when a prince claiming Majapahit descent set up a Malay-style river kingdom here; in time its rulers bore the Muslim title of panembahan over Dayak subjects who kept their own ways. Meliau stayed a small upriver polity, marrying and warring with its neighbours Tayan and Sanggau, and as late as 1821 it remained a self-ruling little court while Dutch power gathered along the West Borneo coast.
zh:
默利奥深居卡普阿斯河中游内陆，是从婆罗洲海岸溯河而上最先遇到的开阔稻作平原之一。河两岸是达雅克人的土地，马来商人定居在村寨之间，贸易顺流而下，通往古老马来王国丹戎布拉所在的苏卡丹纳海岸——该王国自公元8世纪即已立国。当地传说把上游各地视为满者伯夷血统王公的封地，他们因丹戎布拉征战不断而避往内陆。1444年的默利奥是一串沿河村寨，把稻米、树脂和林产运下卡普阿斯河，保留着内陆宫廷古老的印度教与祖先崇拜习俗。

伊斯兰教1550年传到苏卡丹纳，沿卡普阿斯河而上却十分缓慢。默利奥王国见于记载始于1762年，一位自称满者伯夷后裔的王子在此建立马来式的河上王国；后来的统治者使用穆斯林的「潘嫩巴汉」称号，治下的达雅克人则保留自己的风俗。默利奥始终是个小小的上游政权，与邻国戴燕、上侯时战时婚；迟至1821年，它仍是一座自治的小河宫廷，而荷兰人的势力已在西婆罗洲沿海集结。

en:
Kuching is the country of the Sarawak River, a muddy coast of mangroves and fishing villages beneath the forested ridges of south-western Borneo. At its mouth Santubong was already a trading port where Chinese junks called between the eighth and thirteenth centuries, and the ceramics they left are still dug from its earth. The coast passed under Brunei as that sultanate spread from the reign of its first ruler, Muhammad Shah. In 1444 it was a Sunni Muslim frontier of the Bruneian empire, run through local Malay datus and Land Dayak chiefs, who sent beeswax, camphor, rattan and inland gold downriver to exchange for Chinese goods and salt.

In 1578, during the Castilian War, a Spanish fleet out of Manila stormed Brunei's own capital, Kota Batu, and held it seventy-two days before disease drove it out; Sarawak itself never fell. After Brunei subdued the old Santubong kingdom, its new sultan Abdul Jalilul Akbar in 1599 posted his rival younger brother Pengiran Muda Tengah to rule Sarawak as Sultan Ibrahim Ali Omar Shah, the first and only sultan of Sarawak. He fortified Santubong, married a princess of Sukadana, and saw his son Radin Sulaiman carry Islam to the throne of Sambas. He was assassinated at Batu Buaya in 1641, and Sarawak reverted to governors appointed from Brunei. The Bruneian civil war of 1661–1673 drained the empire, and by 1821 the Sarawak River was a quiet backwater under local datus and Bruneian nobles, its small trading villages not yet grown into the town later called Kuching.
zh:
古晋是砂拉越河流域之地，乃婆罗洲西南角一片泥泞海岸，渔村散布于红树林间，背后是覆满森林的丘陵。河口的山都望早为贸易港口，8至13世纪间中国帆船常来停泊，留下的瓷片后世仍不断从土中出土。随着文莱苏丹国自初代苏丹穆罕默德·沙阿时代向外扩张，这片海岸归入文莱。1444年的砂拉越是文莱帝国的逊尼派穆斯林边疆，由当地马来拿督与陆上达雅克酋长分头治理，蜂蜡、樟脑、藤条和内陆黄金顺河而下，换取中国货物和食盐。

1578年卡斯蒂利亚战争期间，一支来自马尼拉的西班牙舰队猛攻文莱本国都城哥打巴鲁，占领七十二天后因疫病撤走；砂拉越本身并未陷落。文莱攻灭古老的山都望王国后，新苏丹阿卜杜勒·贾利鲁·阿巴尔于1599年把与自己争位的弟弟彭吉兰·穆达·登加分封至砂拉越，称苏丹易卜拉欣·阿里·奥马尔·沙阿，是砂拉越第一位也是唯一一位苏丹。他在山都望筑堡，娶苏卡丹纳公主，其子拉登·苏莱曼后来把伊斯兰教带上三发的王位。1641年他在峇都布阿亚（Batu Buaya）遇刺身亡，砂拉越重新由文莱任命的总督治理。1661至1673年的文莱继位内战耗尽了帝国国力，到1821年，砂拉越河已成安静的偏僻角落，由当地拿督和文莱贵族统辖；那些小小的贸易村落，此时还未长成日后名为古晋的城市。

en:
Bintulu lies where the Kemena River meets the South China Sea, on the open coast between Brunei Bay and the Rajang delta. Its name is said to come from the Melanau words Mentu Ulau, 'picking heads' — a memory of the headtaking that once shadowed this shore. Chinese geographical works of the Song and Yuan eras list Wen Du Ling (Bintulu) together with Igan among the lands of Fo-ni, the Bornean polity known to the Chinese; the Melanau fishing and sago villages here had their own headmen before being absorbed into the expanding Bruneian sultanate in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries. In 1444 Bintulu was a small Melanau village of stilt houses along the Kemena, part of Sultan Sulaiman's Brunei, its catch and sago moving through the coastal trade.

Like the rest of provincial Brunei, Bintulu felt the Castilian expedition of 1578 only as a distant shock: a Spanish fleet seized Kota Batu in April and abandoned it within 72 days, but Brunei never recovered its old naval reach. In 1609 Dutch intelligence already counted the Melano coast among the tribes restive against the sultan, and through the long decline of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the Kemena was left to its Melanau headmen and to Bruneian traders who came for sago, damar resin and sea produce. Raiding was the constant terror of those years, as Iranun war-fleets cruised the Borneo shore for captives to sell in the slave marts; the Melanau therefore kept their main villages up the Kemena and came down to the river mouth only with caution. No fort, bazaar or foreign settlement marked Bintulu in 1821 — only a fishing and sago village on a coast the weakened sultanate claimed but barely ruled.
zh:
民都鲁地处格盟纳河注入南海之处，位于文莱湾与拉让江三角洲之间的开阔海岸。其地名据说来自马兰诺语 Mentu Ulau，意为「割取人头」，留存着这片海岸曾被猎头习俗笼罩的记忆。宋元时期的地理书把温都灵（民都鲁）与伊干并列为浡泥属地；这里的马兰诺渔村和西谷聚落原本自有头人，14至15世纪才被扩张中的文莱苏丹国吞并。1444年的民都鲁只是格盟纳河畔一个高脚屋林立的马兰诺小渔村，属苏丹苏莱曼治下的文莱，渔获和西谷经由沿海贸易运出。

和文莱治下的边远地区一样，1578年的卡斯蒂利亚战争对民都鲁只是远方的震荡：西班牙舰队4月攻占哥打巴都，72天内便弃城而去，但文莱从此再未恢复旧日的海上势力。1609年的荷兰情报已把马兰诺海岸列为诸部不服苏丹的地区；在17至18世纪漫长的衰落中，格盟纳河交给了本地马兰诺头人，以及前来收购西谷、达玛脂和海产的文莱商人。袭掠是那些年头挥之不去的恐惧：伊拉农战船巡航婆罗洲海岸，掳人贩卖为奴，马兰诺人因此把主要村落建在格盟纳河上游，只在小心提防时才下到河口。1821年的民都鲁没有堡垒、没有市集，也没有外人定居点，只是一个出产渔获和西谷的小村，落在衰微的苏丹国名义声称、实际已无力管辖的海岸上。

en:
Kapit is the forested heart of the middle Rajang, 140 kilometres upriver from the sea, where the Balleh and other tributaries gather above the Pelagus Rapids. No sultan's road reached it; the river was the only road, and the land belonged to longhouse peoples — Kajang-speaking Kejaman, Sekapan, Tanjung and Kanowit communities, Punan families in the side streams, and Kayan war parties — who grew hill rice by shifting cultivation and took heads in ritual warfare. Chinese and Malay records knew Borneo's interior chiefly by its camphor; Brunei claimed the whole basin, and its traders came up the Rajang for camphor, beeswax and other jungle produce, though the sultan's writ scarcely passed the lowest reaches. In 1444 Kapit was country beyond Brunei's reach, governed by its own chiefs.

Over the following centuries the upriver balance was remade by migration and war. The Kayan pressed in from the eastern highlands, while from the mid-sixteenth century the Iban began their long movement out of the Kapuas country to the south, first into the Batang Lupar and the Saribas, then, by the early 1800s, into the Rejang itself, parties working up the Katibas and other southern tributaries. Their longhouse columns fought the older Kajang and Kayan communities for land, heads and captives in feuds that ran on for generations. Brunei's civil war of the 1660s and the slow collapse of its river commerce left the interior entirely to these struggles. In 1821 no town or fort yet stood at Kapit, and the middle-river peoples still held the upper Rajang against the advancing Iban war-boats.
zh:
加帛位于拉让江中游的密林腹地，溯江而上距海一百四十公里，巴拉河等支流在彼拉古斯急滩上游汇入大江。没有任何苏丹的道路能通到这里，河流是唯一的通道，土地属于长屋诸族——说卡章语的格察曼、色卡班、丹戎和加拿逸社群，散居各支流的普南人，以及善战的加央人；他们以轮耕种植旱稻，在仪式性的战争中猎取人头。中国和马来载籍对婆罗洲内陆的认识主要是樟脑；文莱名义上领有整个流域，其商人沿拉让江上行收购樟脑、蜂蜡和其他山货，苏丹的号令却几乎传不到下游河口以上。1444年的加帛是文莱势力之外的世界，由各族头人自行治理。

此后几个世纪，上游的格局在迁徙与战争中重塑。加央人从东部高地一带压入；16世纪中叶起，伊班人开始了离开南方卡普阿斯河流域的漫长迁徙，先入巴当鲁巴河与沙里拔河，到19世纪初又进入拉让江本身，成群结队沿卡提巴斯河等南部支流上溯。他们的长屋纵队为土地、人头和俘虏，与更早定居的卡章、加央诸族交战，世仇延续数代。1660年代的文莱内战及河上贸易的缓慢崩解，使内陆完全听凭这些纷争摆布。1821年的加帛还没有城镇或堡垒，中游各族仍在抵抗节节上溯的伊班战船。

en:
Langkat is the low-lying coast and river plain where northern Sumatra meets the Strait of Malacca, around the lower Batang Serangan River and later Tanjung Pura. In the fifteenth century it lay on the maritime frontier of Aru, a Malay power whose ports drew Chinese, Thai and Arab trade. Camphor, benzoin, rattan, honey and gold came down from the interior, while rice and fish supplied the coastal settlements. The 1416 Chinese account of Ma Huan describes Aru's Muslim court, though many inland people still followed older cults. In 1444 Pasai claimed the shore, but Aru's chiefs and fleets made it a contested borderland rather than a quiet province.

Aceh's expansion broke Aru during the sixteenth century. In 1568 Dewa Shahdan, an Aru commander, fled an Acehnese attack and founded the polity that became Langkat; his successor Dewa Sakti was killed in another Acehnese assault in 1612. The dynasty survived under Raja Kahar and then the bendahara rajas, preserving control of the river mouth and the traffic in forest produce. Raja Kejuruan Hitam ruled from 1750 to 1818 through repeated conflicts with neighbouring states, leaving Langkat an autonomous Malay kingdom on Aceh's southeastern flank at the end of the period.
zh:
冷吉是苏门答腊北部临近马六甲海峡的低地海岸与河原，位于巴唐塞兰甘河下游，后来的丹戎布拉也在这一带。15世纪时，这里处在马来强国阿鲁的海上边疆，其港口吸引中国、暹罗和阿拉伯贸易。樟脑、安息香、藤条、蜂蜜和黄金从内陆运出，稻米与鱼产则供应沿海聚落。马欢1416年的记载称阿鲁宫廷已经信奉伊斯兰教，但许多内陆居民仍保留旧有信仰。1444年，八昔对这片海岸拥有宗主权，但阿鲁首领和船队使这里成为争斗不断的边地，而非平静的行省。

16世纪亚齐扩张，击溃了阿鲁。1568年，阿鲁将领德瓦·沙赫丹在亚齐攻势中出逃，建立了后来冷吉苏丹国的雏形；他的继承者德瓦·萨克蒂于1612年在另一次亚齐进攻中被杀。王朝在拉惹·卡哈尔和随后的盘陀诃罗拉阇们治下延续，控制河口与山林物产贸易。拉惹·基朱兰·希坦于1750年至1818年在位，期间不断与周边政权冲突；到这一时代末期，冷吉仍是亚齐东南侧一个自治的马来王国。

en:
The low coast around the Deli River and Belawan, facing the northern entrance to the Strait of Malacca, was the fifteenth-century heartland of Aru. Its capital lay near Medan and Deli Serdang, and the site of Kota Rentang has yielded Chinese ceramics, Arabic coins and Muslim gravestones. Ma Huan, writing after the Ming voyages of 1412 and 1430, described Muslim rulers, rice farmers and fishermen; camphor, benzoin, gold and aromatic woods moved through Aru's ports. In 1444 Aru was a Muslim Malay maritime power whose prestige rivalled Pasai and Malacca.

Aceh's rise ended that balance. Kota Rentang probably fell under Acehnese pressure in 1539 and the court withdrew inland; Aceh opened its east Sumatran campaigns in 1612, and Aru submitted early in 1613. In 1632 Sultan Iskandar Muda granted the former Aru lands to his commander Gocah Pahlawan, who married into the Karo ruling family of Sunggal and founded Deli as an Acehnese vice-regency. His successor broke with Aceh in 1669, made Labuhan his capital and opened contacts with Dutch Malacca. A succession quarrel in 1720 produced the separate Sultanate of Serdang. Deli then passed between Aceh and Siak, and Siak conquered it in 1814.
zh:
碟里（Deli，当地汉籍常称日里）一带的低海岸临马六甲海峡北口，15世纪时是哑鲁王国的核心。其都城靠近后来的棉兰和日里雪冷，哥打伦唐遗址出土过中国瓷器、阿拉伯钱币和穆斯林墓碑。马欢随1412年与1430年的明朝使团到此，记载国王与居民信奉伊斯兰教，人民耕种稻米、兼事渔业；樟脑、安息香、黄金和香木从港口输出。1444年，哑鲁仍是穆斯林马来人的海上强国，声势可与帕赛和马六甲相比。

亚齐的崛起打破了均势。哥打伦唐约在1539年陷入亚齐的压力，王廷退入内陆；1612年亚齐发动苏门答腊东岸战事，哑鲁于1613年初投降。1632年，苏丹伊斯干达·穆达把旧哑鲁土地封给将领Gocah Pahlawan；他与Sunggal的卡罗族统治家族联姻，建立作为亚齐摄政领地的碟里。其继承人于1669年脱离亚齐，以拉布汉为都，并与荷兰人控制的马六甲往来。1720年的继承争端又分出Serdang苏丹国。此后碟里在亚齐与锡亚之间反复易手，1814年被锡亚征服。

en:
Barus, also called Fansur or Pansur, was the ancient emporium of Sumatra's western coast, set between the Indian Ocean and the forested Batak highlands. Its fame rested on kapur barus, the camphor carried down from inland trees and sold to Arab, Persian, Indian and Chinese merchants. The merchant Sulaiman already described superior Fansur camphor in 851, and a Tamil inscription at Lobu Tua records the port's foreign community in 1088. Settlements shifted along the coast as harbours silted up, and early Muslim tombstones at Bukit Hasang show an Islamic presence by 1370. In 1444 Barus remained a rich trading kingdom drawing gold and aromatics from the Batak interior, with a cosmopolitan harbour behind its Hindu-Batak court.

In the early sixteenth century Tomé Pires called Baros, or Pansur, a very rich kingdom known to many nations. Its most famous literary son may have been Hamzah Fansuri, the Sufi poet who helped create Malay syair; he may have been born or raised there, and Fansur later served as an Islamic educational centre under Acehnese rule. Around the middle of the century Aceh absorbed the port and stationed a panglima to command its trade. In 1668 the Dutch East India Company ousted that Acehnese governor, but Barus never recovered its old position as the leading camphor emporium, and regional commerce shifted increasingly toward other west Sumatran ports.
zh:
巴鲁斯又称凡苏尔或班苏尔，是苏门答腊西岸古老的商业港口，位于印度洋与森林密布的巴塔克高地之间。它的声名来自巴鲁斯樟脑——内陆山民采集后运来的樟脑，被卖给阿拉伯、波斯、印度和中国商人。商人苏莱曼早在851年就记载凡苏尔出产上等樟脑；1088年，洛布图阿的泰米尔碑文也记录了港中的外商社群。港口聚落会随港湾淤塞在海岸间迁移，武吉哈桑发现的早期穆斯林墓碑证明1370年时已有伊斯兰信徒。1444年，巴鲁斯仍是一座富庶的贸易王国，从巴塔克内陆获取黄金和香料，港口居民繁杂，而宫廷与内陆仍保有印度教—巴塔克信仰。

16世纪初，托梅·皮莱资称巴鲁斯（又称班苏尔）是许多民族都知道的非常富庶的王国。当地最著名的文人可能是苏菲诗人哈姆扎·凡苏里，他推动了马来沙依尔诗体的形成，相传出生于巴鲁斯或幼年在此长大；在亚齐统治时期，凡苏尔也是伊斯兰教学术中心。约16世纪中叶，亚齐吞并该港并派驻庞利马控制贸易。1668年，荷兰东印度公司赶走亚齐长官，但巴鲁斯未能恢复昔日樟脑大港的地位，地区贸易也越来越多地转向苏门答腊西岸其他港口。

en:
Gerik lies in the forested trough between the Bintang and Titiwangsa ranges, where upper tributaries of the Perak River gather beneath the old Belum rainforest. The deep woods belonged to the Semang, who hunted and gathered there as their people had for millennia, while Malay villagers kept to the river valleys, planting hill rice and fishing. In 1444 this was the remote southern hinterland of the Patani sultanate, joined to its capital by jungle tracks and boat routes, and a barely marked marcher border with Perak.

Early in the 16th century Tun Saban, treasurer of fallen Malacca, led his followers through upper Patani to Belum and became head of the upriver settlements there. The hills stayed a quiet borderland until 1785, when Siam reconquered Patani and refugees poured onto the Kroh plateau; the mineral country around Klian Intan and Kroh was absorbed into the domains of the Patani noble Tuan Mansor in 1790. Set over the local mines, he led his people to break with Patani in 1808, and in 1810 Siam's reordering of Patani into seven semi-autonomous chiefdoms made him king of Reman, the largest of them, reaching south as far as Lenggong and taking in all of Gerik. In 1818 John Bannerman, Governor of Penang, concluded an agreement with Tuan Mansor at Kroh, the first such treaty between the forest kingdom and a European power.
zh:
宜力坐落在宾当山脉与蒂蒂旺沙山脉之间的林谷，霹雳河上游的支流在古老的柏隆雨林间汇集。密林深处是塞芒人千百年来游猎采集的天地，马来村民则栖身河谷，种旱稻、捕鱼为业。1444年，这里是北大年苏丹国僻远的南部内陆，靠林中小径与水路和北方相通，也是与霹雳之间没有明确界线的边陲。

16世纪初，马六甲的财务大臣敦沙班在国破后率众人经上北大年辗转到柏隆落脚，成为这些上游聚落的首领。这片山地长期是寂静的边境，直到1785年暹罗重新征服北大年，难民涌入高乌高原；1790年，吉连旦、高乌一带富藏锡砂的地区并入北大年贵族端·曼梳的辖地。端·曼梳本受命管理当地矿场，1808年率众脱离北大年；1810年暹罗把北大年改组为七个半自治土邦，封他为拉曼（Reman）之王。拉曼是七邦中最大的一个，疆域南至玲珑，宜力全境都在其治下。1818年，槟榔屿总督约翰·班纳曼在高乌与端·曼梳立约，这是这个森林王国与欧洲势力签订的第一项条约。

en:
Across a narrow strait from the Kedah rice coast lies a hilly island the Malays call Pulau Pinang, the areca-nut isle, fringed with good anchorage and springs of fresh water; the Ming sailing charts used by Zheng He's fleets already mark it as Binglang Yu. Semang foragers and a handful of Malay fishing families lived on it, and the chiefs across the water counted it part of Kedah. In 1444, as for centuries before, traders plying between Kedah and Malacca put into its coves for water, while the mainland shore opposite was quiet rice country under the Sultan of Kedah.

An English ship first watered there in 1592, but the island's fate changed when Francis Light, acting for the East India Company, landed on 17 July 1786 and took formal possession on 11 August, renaming it Prince of Wales Island and founding George Town as a free port. Sultan Abdullah of Kedah, who had ceded the island against a promise of military aid, tried to take it back in 1791; his attack was beaten off and a treaty settled the rent at 6,000 Spanish dollars a year. Light himself died of malaria on 21 October 1794, yet settlers had already flocked in, Chinese, Indians, Bugis and Malays among them, and the population neared ten thousand by 1792. In 1800 the Company acquired a strip of the opposite mainland, named Province Wellesley, and raised the annual payment to 10,000 dollars; in 1805 Penang became the fourth presidency of British India, and by 1821 George Town was a thriving free port on the flank of Dutch Malacca.
zh:
与吉打稻米海岸隔一道窄峡相望的，是一座丘陵起伏的岛屿，马来人称之为槟榔屿，因岛上遍生槟榔树而得名，沿岸锚地良好，又有甘泉；明代郑和船队所用的航海图上，它已被标作「槟榔屿」。岛上住着塞芒游猎者和寥寥几户马来渔家，对岸的吉打酋长把它视作吉打的一部分。1444年时，和此前数百年一样，往来于吉打与马六甲之间的商船常驶入岛上的海湾补水歇脚，对岸大陆则是吉打苏丹治下宁静的稻作乡野。

1592年，第一艘英国船曾在此取水，但岛屿的命运到1786年才改变：这一年7月17日，代表英国东印度公司的法兰西斯·莱特率人登岛，8月11日正式占领，将岛屿改名威尔士亲王岛，并辟建自由港乔治市。吉打苏丹阿都拉本是以岛换取军事援助，公司食言后，他于1791年试图夺回岛屿，攻势被击退，条约规定英国年付租金6000西班牙元。莱特本人在1794年10月21日死于疟疾，但华人、印度人、武吉斯人和马来人已纷纷涌入，1792年人口已近一万。1800年，公司又取得对岸一条狭长地带，命名为威斯利省，年租增至10000元；1805年槟榔屿成为英属印度的第四个辖区，到1821年，乔治市已是荷属马六甲侧翼一座繁荣的自由贸易港。

en: Semantan is the forested interior of the Pahang basin, where the Semantan River and other hill streams join the upper Pahang River at the Temerloh confluence. The Tembeling valley was the old northern highway between the coast and the Siamese interior, and ancient gold workings along its rivers date from the early Iron Age. The Jakun and other Orang Asli gathered camphor, aromatic woods and rattan here, the same forest goods that Wang Dayuan in the fourteenth century found shipping out through the Pahang estuary. In 1444 these upriver lands kept older Hindu-Buddhist and indigenous beliefs and were ruled loosely from Pekan by Dewa Sura's local chiefs. A Ligor army marched this river route against Malacca, and Tun Perak's conquest of Pahang in 1454 opened the valleys to Malaccan rule; when Aceh overran the coast in 1615 the Pahang sultan fled upriver into these forests. The upriver chiefs later answered to Pahang's bendaharas, autonomous under Tun Abdul Majid after 1770.
zh: 士曼丹是彭亨河流域的森林内陆，士曼丹河等山溪在淡马鲁一带汇入彭亨河上游。淡美岭河谷是连接海岸与暹罗方向内陆的古老北方通道，沿河的淘金遗迹可追溯到早期铁器时代。贾昆人和其他原住民在此采办龙脑、香木和藤条，14世纪汪大渊记载从彭亨河口出海的，正是这些山林物产。1444年，上游地区仍保持印度教-佛教与本土旧信仰，由提婆素罗任命的本地酋长松散管辖。洛坤攻打马六甲的军队曾沿这条河南下，1454年敦霹雳征服彭亨后，诸河谷纳入马六甲治下；1615年亚齐攻陷沿海，彭亨苏丹溯河逃入这片丛林。后来上游酋长听命于彭亨的宰相，1770年以后归自治的敦阿都·马吉德管辖。

en:
Singapore, then called Temasek, is a low island off the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, separated from Johor by a narrow tidal strait. The Chinese mariner Wang Dayuan found a trading port here when he visited about 1330: he described the Long Ya Men passage at Keppel and a town that a Sukhothai fleet of more than seventy ships had failed to storm after a month's siege, and Siam and Majapahit long disputed its allegiance. Around 1400 its ruler Parameswara withdrew north to found Malacca, and the old hill settlement on Fort Canning was abandoned. In 1444 a small Sunni Malay fishing and trading village remains at the mouth of the Singapore River, a quiet backwater of the Malacca Sultanate whose Orang Laut fishermen know every shoal in the strait.

After Malacca fell in 1511 Singapore passed to the new Johor Sultanate, but in 1613 Portuguese raiders burned the Malay outpost at the river mouth, and for two centuries the island lay almost deserted, a haunt of Orang Laut and passing pirates while its strait traffic came under Dutch control. On 29 January 1819 Stamford Raffles landed in search of a British port beyond Dutch reach. The Temenggong Abdul Rahman governed the island for Johor, whose reigning sultan leaned on the Dutch and the Bugis; Raffles therefore brought back the exiled elder prince Tengku Hussein from Penyengat and, on 6 February 1819, signed a treaty recognising him as sultan in exchange for leave to build a factory. Declared a free port, Singapore at once drew Malay, Bugis, Chinese and Indian shipping, and pepper and gambier plantations spread inland. In 1821, barely two years later, the fishing village has become the straits' fastest-growing emporium, flying the East India Company's flag at the gateway to the South China Sea.
zh:
新加坡在14世纪称淡马锡，是马来半岛南端外海一座低平岛屿，与柔佛仅隔一条狭窄的潮汐海峡。中国航海家汪大渊约1330年到访时，这里已是商埠：他记下了岌巴港的「龙牙门」水道，还记下素可泰七十余艘兵船来攻、围城一月不下；当时暹罗与满者伯夷长期争夺该岛。1400年前后，岛上君主拜里米苏拉北撤另立马六甲，福康宁山上的旧城随之废弃。1444年的新加坡河口只剩一座小小的逊尼派马来人渔村兼商埠，是马六甲苏丹国治下安静的角落，唯有海人渔民熟悉海峡中的每一处浅滩。

1511年马六甲灭亡后，新加坡归入新兴的柔佛苏丹国；1613年葡萄牙人袭毁河口的马来据点，此后两百年间岛屿几乎荒废，只有海人和过路海盗出没，海峡贸易尽入荷兰人之手。1819年1月29日，莱佛士为寻找不受荷兰控制的港口在此登陆。实际治岛的是柔佛天猛公阿都拉曼，而在位苏丹阿都拉曼受荷兰与武吉斯人挟制；莱佛士遂把流亡在喷延格特岛的长王子东姑·胡欣接回，于1819年2月6日订约，承认其苏丹身份，换取设立商馆的许可。新加坡被辟为自由港，立刻引来马来人、武吉斯人、华人和印度人的船只，内陆也种起胡椒与甘蜜。到1821年，不过两年光景，这座渔村已成为海峡间成长最快的商埠，在南海门户升起东印度公司的旗帜。

en:
Rengat is a middle-reach settlement on the Indragiri, where the upper Batang Kuantan bends through forested country on its way toward the Sumatran coast. Before it became a capital, its riverbank was a landing and exchange point for Malay boats, while Talang Mamak communities held much of the hinterland. In 1444 the district formed part of Raja Merlang II's Indragiri kingdom, but the court still lay far downstream; Rengat itself remained a scattering of river villages under local chiefs.

By the sixteenth century Kota Lama, on Rengat's western edge, had a fortified royal precinct with walls enclosing a square roughly 400 metres on each side and rising seven metres; its cemetery held Narasinga II and other Indragiri kings. The court later moved from downstream Pekan Tua to Mudoyan for safety from Portuguese raids and piracy, then to Japura in 1765. Sultan Ibrahim fought the Dutch at Teluk Ketapang on 18 June 1784 and founded Rengat in 1786. On 5 January 1815 he moved the capital there beside the royal lake, Danau Raja, and was later buried at the nineteenth-century Great Mosque. While Dutch interference placed a Sultan Muda upriver at Peranap, Sultan Mun Bungsu kept the new Rengat court through 1821.
zh:
冷岳（Rengat）是因德拉吉里河中游的聚落，上游库安坦河在此穿过林地带，奔向苏门答腊海岸。在成为都城以前，这里的河岸只是马来船只停靠和交易的地点，后方腹地则多为塔朗·马马克人的地域。1444年，这一带属于拉惹·默朗二世的因德拉吉里王国，但宫廷仍远在下游，冷岳本身只是由本地酋长管辖的一串河畔村落。

到16世纪，冷岳西侧的哥打拉马已有设防王城区，围墙围成约400米见方、高7米的方形城塞，墓区葬有纳拉辛哈二世和其他因德拉吉里君主。后来宫廷为躲避葡萄牙袭击与海盗，从下游的北干图阿迁至穆多扬，又于1765年迁往查普拉。苏丹易卜拉欣1784年6月18日在克塔邦湾与荷兰人作战，1786年兴建冷岳。1815年1月5日，他把都城迁到王宫湖（Danau Raja）旁的冷岳，身后葬于19世纪的大清真寺。荷兰人进行干预后，副苏丹被设在上游的佩拉纳普，而苏丹蒙·邦苏在1821年仍维持着冷岳的新城宫廷。

en:
Padang occupies a broad river-mouth on Sumatra's west coast, where the Batang Arau meets the Indian Ocean below the Minangkabau highlands. Migrants from the inland valleys opened the ground as one of their rantau settlements, fishing villages grouped under the eight clans of the Padang nagari. Their boats carried downriver the highland gold, rice and forest produce that first gave the place more than local worth. In 1444 Padang still belonged to the coastal world of the Pagaruyung kings, then ordered in the old pre-Islamic manner, and its harbour was only just approaching the pepper boom that the fall of Malacca would soon bring to the whole coast.

In the 1500s Padang grew into a pepper roadstead, trading with Indian, Portuguese and later Dutch and English shipping, until Aceh brought the coast under its governors early in the next century. English seamen were already calling there in 1649. The VOC arrived in 1663, and after the Minangkabau coast rose against Aceh its agents had the Acehnese expelled by 1668; on 7 August 1669 the men of Pauh and Koto Tangah stormed the Dutch lodge at the river-mouth, an outbreak the Company soon suppressed but which Padang now remembers as its founding. A fortified post went up in 1680, and highland gold remained the staple export until about 1780, when coffee, salt and textiles took its place. The British seized Padang in 1781 during the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War and held it until 1784; a French privateer operating from Mauritius, François Thomas Le Même, sacked it in 1793, and from 1795 the British held it again until the Dutch returned in 1819. An earthquake and tsunami in 1797 wrecked Air Manis and left ships stranded far up the Arau. Back in Dutch hands, Padang became the base from which, in 1821, the Dutch intervened in the Padri War.
zh:
巴东位于苏门答腊西岸一个宽阔的河口，巴坦阿劳河在此注入印度洋，背后就是米南加保高地。高地谷地的米南加保移民把这里开辟为「朗道」定居点，渔村按巴东乡的八个氏族编组；他们的船只沿河运下高地的黄金、稻米和山货，使这地方最初便超出了普通聚落的分量。1444年的巴东仍属于帕迦鲁荣诸王的沿海天地，尚行伊斯兰化之前的旧秩序；它的港口刚刚要迎来胡椒景气——满剌加的陷落很快会把这场景气带到整条西海岸。

16世纪，巴东成长为胡椒锚地，与印度、葡萄牙以及后来的荷兰、英国商船交易，到17世纪初沿海被亚齐派官统治。1649年已有英国海员到访。荷兰东印度公司1663年来此，米南加保海岸起兵反抗亚齐后，公司人员于1668年把亚齐势力逐出；1669年8月7日，帕乌和科托坦加的民众猛攻河口的荷兰商馆，起事虽很快被公司镇压，这一天却被巴东定为建城之日。1680年筑起设防据点，高地黄金长期是头号出口货，到1780年前后才由咖啡、盐和纺织品取代。第四次英荷战争中，英国1781年攻占巴东，据守到1784年；1793年，以毛里求斯为基地的法国私掠船长弗朗索瓦·托马·勒梅姆洗劫此城；1795年起英国再度占据，直到1819年荷兰人收回。1797年的地震和海啸摧毁了埃尔马尼斯村，把船只搁浅在阿劳河上游深处。荷兰人重返后，以巴东为基地于1821年出兵介入帕德里战争。

en:
Inderapura, the Minangkabau Ujung Pagaruyung or 'Edge of Pagaruyung', lay on the swampy southern stretch of Sumatra's west coast, the southernmost of the eight gateways of the Pagaruyung realm. Rice grew on its coastal plain and gold washed down from the hills behind, while its river-mouths faced the open trade of the Indian Ocean. Its was a Minangkabau court, formally vassal to the Raja of Pagaruyung but long used to managing its own affairs. In 1444, as the highland power ebbed, Inderapura thus held the southern shore of the Minangkabau world in the old pre-Islamic fashion - the quiet before the pepper boom that would make its sway run from Padang down to Sungai Hurai.

Everything changed with the fall of Malacca to the Portuguese in 1511: traffic from the East swung through the Sunda Strait and along this coast, and pepper gardens spread as far south as Silebar. By the later 1500s Inderapura's rulers bore the title of sultan, married into the courts of Banten and Aceh, and twice helped place their own candidates on the throne of Aceh. Dutch visitors in 1616 found a prosperous kingdom under Raja Itam, with perhaps 30,000 people growing rice and pepper; his successors granted the Company duty-free harbours and sent pepper out through southern Silebar to escape Aceh's grip on the northern ports. Aceh answered with a fleet in 1633: the cargoes were seized, the defiant Raja Puti was put to death, and an Acehnese client was enthroned. As Aceh's power faded the Dutch moved in, and when the matrilineal chief Raja Adil rose at Manjuto in 1662 the hard-pressed sultan called in the VOC. The treaty of 1663, signed at Batavia by Sultan Mansur Syah, gave the Company the pepper monopoly and rights to the gold mines, and that October Inderapura was restored to its ruler under Dutch supervision, with Raja Adil confirmed as deputy at Manjuto.
zh:
因陀罗补罗，米南加保语称「乌戎帕迦鲁荣」，意为「帕迦鲁荣之端」，地处苏门答腊西岸低洼湿润的南段，是帕迦鲁荣版图八大门户中最南的一座。沿海平原种植稻米，背后山地的沙金顺水而下，各河口则面向开阔的印度洋商路。统治此地的是米南加保人的宫廷，名义上臣服帕迦鲁荣的罗阇，实际却久已自行其是。1444年，随着高地王权衰落，因陀罗补罗便这样以伊斯兰化之前的旧俗，据守着米南加保世界的南岸；此时尚是沉寂年月，后来的胡椒景气将使它的势力北起巴东、南抵乌拉伊水。

1511年满剌加被葡萄牙人攻占后，一切改观：东方来的商船改走巽他海峡和这条海岸，胡椒园一直向南推广到锡莱巴尔。到16世纪后期，因陀罗补罗的统治者已使用苏丹称号，与万丹和亚齐的宫廷联姻，并两度协助把自家拥立的人送上亚齐王位。1616年，荷兰来访者见到罗阇·伊坦治下的富庶国度，约有三万人以种稻和植椒为生；其后继者给予荷兰东印度公司免税港口，并让胡椒经南方的锡莱巴尔出口，以避开亚齐对北方港口的把持。亚齐以一支舰队作答：1633年货物被没收，抗命的罗阇·普蒂被处死，一名亚齐傀儡被扶上王位。亚齐势力衰落后荷兰人乘虚而入；1662年，奉行母系继承的首领罗阇·阿迪尔在曼朱托起兵，走投无路的苏丹向荷兰东印度公司求援。1663年，苏丹·曼苏尔·夏在巴达维亚签订条约，把胡椒专卖权和金矿开采权让给公司；同年10月，因陀罗补罗在荷兰监督下交还其君主统治，罗阇·阿迪尔则被确认为驻曼朱托的副王。

en:
The forested border mountains and island-studded coast now called Quảng Ninh were known to the fifteenth-century Vietnamese court as An Bang. Limestone peaks run into the Gulf of Tonkin, where the Vân Đồn islands guard the sea road towards China. In 1149 Lý Anh Tông established Vân Đồn as Đại Việt's first formal trading port; Chinese, Japanese, Siamese and island Southeast Asian merchants exchanged aromatics, ceramics and forest products there. The Trần kings kept ancestral lands and tombs around Đông Triều, while Yên Tử mountain remained the seat of the Trúc Lâm Buddhist tradition. In 1444 the new Later Lê dynasty held An Bang as a northeastern frontier of rice valleys, border passes and busy sea lanes.

In 1468 Lê Thánh Tông visited the limestone height later named Bài Thơ and had a poem carved into its southern cliff. During the reign of Lê Anh Tông, between 1556 and 1573, An Bang was renamed An Quảng to avoid a royal taboo. Under the Mạc in the later sixteenth century, Vân Đồn declined and was gradually forgotten as a trading harbour. The mountain received another court inscription from Trịnh Cương in 1729. Under the Tây Sơn, Kinh Môn and its seven districts, including Đông Triều, were attached to An Quảng. When Gia Long founded the Nguyễn dynasty in 1802, he kept the enlarged northeastern territory as an outer march.
zh:
今广宁这片森林密布的边境山地与群岛海岸，在15世纪的越南朝廷称为安邦。石灰岩峰峦伸入北部湾，云屯群岛扼守通往中国的海道。1149年，李英宗设立云屯，使之成为大越第一个正式商港，中国、日本、暹罗及南洋群岛商人在此交易香料、陶瓷和山林物产。陈朝诸王在东潮一带有祖地和陵寝，安子山则是竹林禅法的中心。1444年，新生的后黎朝掌握安邦，使这里成为东北方兼具稻田河谷、边境隘口与繁忙海路的边疆。

1468年，黎圣宗登临后来得名诗山的石灰岩峰，命人把诗作镌刻在南壁。黎英宗在位的1556年至1573年间，朝廷为避其名讳，将安邦改称安广。16世纪后期莫氏统治时，云屯港衰落并逐渐被人遗忘。1729年，郑棡又在诗山留下宫廷题刻。西山朝时，荆门府及包括东潮在内的七县并入安广，使其成为大镇。1802年嘉隆帝建立阮朝后，仍把这片扩大的东北疆土保留为外镇。

en:
Hưng Hóa is the broken country where the Red River plain rises toward the Đà River highlands. Under the Trần dynasty it was the Đà Giang march, formed from Quy Hóa on the upper Red River and Gia Hưng in the Đà and Mã river valleys. The White Tai leader Đèo Cát Hãn ruled Mường Lễ in Ninh Viễn and submitted to Lê Lợi in 1427, then rebelled and occupied Quy Hóa and Gia Hưng. In 1431 Lê Lợi led an army up the Red and Đà rivers, defeated him and reportedly captured 30,000 followers. Đèo surrendered early in 1432, and Ninh Viễn was renamed Phục Lễ. By 1444 his son held the chiefship, and Hưng Hóa, a regional name already used since 1419, was a recently subdued march of Tai mường under the Lê court.

In 1466 Lê Thánh Tông made Hưng Hóa one of thirteen provincial-level marches; three years later it was organized into three prefectures, four districts and seventeen châu. It became a xứ in 1490 and a military trấn during the reign of Lê Tương Dực in 1509–1516. In the mid-Later Lê period, Thuận Châu was split to form Tuần Giáo, Mai Sơn and Sơn La. The upland order broke during the great northern peasant rising led by Hoàng Công Chất. He retreated to Mường Thanh in Ninh Biên in 1751, built the Bản Phủ stronghold, distributed land and drew ten highland châu to his side. Trịnh Sâm sent armies against him after 1767; Hoàng Công Chất died in 1769, his son was driven out soon afterward, and in 1775 Mường Thanh was added to Gia Hưng prefecture.
zh:
兴化是红河平原向沱江高地抬升的破碎山地。陈朝时这里为沱江道，由红河中上游的归化与沱江、马江流域的嘉兴组成。白泰首领刁吉罕据守宁远州芒礼，1427年归附黎利，随后又反叛，占据归化、嘉兴。1431年，黎利亲率大军沿红河、沱江水陆并进，将其击败，据说俘获部属和百姓三万人。1432年初刁吉罕投降，宁远州改名复礼州。到1444年，其子已继任土官；而自1419年已经见诸记载的兴化，是后黎朝廷治下刚刚平定、由泰人诸芒组成的边镇。

1466年，黎圣宗把兴化列为十三个承宣道之一；三年后，当地被整编成三府、四县、十七州。1490年，兴化承宣改为兴化处；1509年至1516年黎襄翼在位期间，又成为兴化镇。后黎中期，顺州被分出，另设遵教、梅山、山罗三州。18世纪北方农民大起义期间，黄公质在1751年退守宁边的芒清，修筑本府城，向贫民分田，并争取到十个山地州归附。1767年后，郑森派军进剿；黄公质1769年病死，其子不久被逐，芒清终于在1775年并入嘉兴府。

en:
Nghe An is the broad rice plain of the Lam River on the coastal road from Thanh Hoa toward Hue, with highlands running west to the Lao frontier. Called Hoan Chau before the Ly dynasty and Nghe An under the Ly and Tran, it was already a southern granary of Dai Viet when the Ming overran the country in 1407. In 1424 Le Loi took Nguyen Chich's advice and marched south, making Nghe An the springboard of the Lam Son rebellion, and in 1426 his forces were besieging its Ming citadel. After the Ming withdrawal of 1427 the province became a pillar of the Later Le order. In 1444 it is a crowded frontier land of rice fields and soldier-settlers, feeding and manning the southern frontier.

After the Mac seized the throne in 1527, Nghe An and Thanh Hoa became the bases of the Le restoration under Nguyen Kim in the 1530s. In the long Trinh–Nguyen wars it stood just behind the Trinh front: in 1655 the Nguyen generals Nguyen Huu Tien and Nguyen Huu Dat swept north and overran its seven southern districts, and five years of fighting around An Truong ended only in 1660, when the Trinh retook them at Thien Loc. Hoang Ngu Phuc's army marched through in 1774 on its way to storm Phu Xuan, and the Tay Son armies swept the province in the 1780s. Under the reunited Nguyen dynasty after 1802, the Lam River plain remained one of the great grain lands of Vietnam.
zh:
乂安是蓝江下游的广阔米粮平原，处在清化通往顺化的沿海官道上，西部山地一直延伸到老挝边地。这里在李朝以前称驩州，李、陈两朝称乂安，1407年明朝吞并大虞时，已是大越南方的粮仓之一。1424年黎利纳阮隻之计南下，以乂安为蓝山义军的反攻跳板，1426年义军已围攻境内明军城垒。1427年明军撤出后，乂安成为后黎朝的支柱之一。1444年时，这里稻田相望、军屯密布，既供给南陲军粮，也出戍边士卒。

1527年莫氏篡位后，乂安与清化在1530年代成为阮淦领导的后黎复辟派根基。郑阮纷争期间，它紧贴郑氏前线：1655年阮将阮有进、阮有镒北上，连下乂安南方七县，双方在安场一带拉锯五年，1660年郑氏才于天禄收复失地。1774年黄五福大军经此南下，直取富春；1780年代西山军又席卷全省。1802年后在重新统一的阮朝治下，蓝江平原始终是越南数一数二的谷仓。

en:
Amaravati, Sanskrit for 'abode of the gods', was the northernmost of the principalities of Champa; Chinese records called it the 'Old Châu' to distinguish it from the later southern capitals. Its citadel was Châu Sa on the coast of present Quảng Ngãi, home country of the Dừa or Coconut clan, one of the two great clans whose rivalries and marriages shaped Cham politics. A seafaring land like the rest of the federation, it shipped aloewood and coastal goods north to China and west across the South China Sea. In 1402 the southern war of the Hồ dynasty wrested Cổ Lũy from King Indravarman VI and organised it as the Tư and Nghĩa prefectures, present Bình Sơn, Sơn Tịnh, Tư Nghĩa, Mộ Đức and Đức Phổ, but the Cham recovered the territory in 1407 amid the Ming conquest of Đại Việt. In 1444 Amaravati was the northern march of King Maha Vijaya's realm on the Hóa Châu frontier, and the fall of Vijaya itself to Vietnamese forces in 1446 showed how exposed that march was.

The storm returned under Lê Thánh Tông. In the 1471 campaign his admirals closed the Sa Kỳ sea gate at present Bình Sơn to seal the Cham retreat, and Vijaya fell on 2 March after four days of fighting. Amaravati and Vijaya were merged into the new Quảng Nam province with a Thăng Hoa garrison, Vietnamese soldier-farmers were settled on the coastal plain, and the old Cham land became an administered frontier of Đại Việt. After Nguyễn Hoàng took charge of Quảng Nam in 1559, his Nguyễn lords extended prefectures and military colonies over the same southward roads. The great rising of 1771 began just beyond the southern border at Quy Nhơn; the Tây Sơn seized Phú Yên in 1773, and for the rest of the civil war the Quảng Ngãi coast lay between the rebel centre at Quy Nhơn and the Nguyễn armies campaigning from the south, war passing repeatedly over its roads while the old Cham citadels crumbled. With the Nguyễn victory of 1802 the land of Amaravati entered the reunified empire as the Quảng Ngãi country.
zh:
阿摩罗伐底在梵语中意为「诸神所居」，是占婆诸邦中地处最北的一个；中国史籍称之为旧州，以别于后来南方的新都。其重镇朱沙城在今广义省沿海，是占婆两大族之一椰子部的故土，占婆的政局便常在椰子、槟榔两部的争斗与联姻之间起伏。与联邦其他地区一样，这里以航海为业，沉香和海产北销中国、西渡南海。1402年胡朝南征，从因陀罗跋摩六世手中割走古垒，置思、义二州，即今平山、山静、思义、慕德、德普各县；1407年明朝灭胡，占婆乘乱收复故土。1444年，阿摩罗伐底是摩诃贲该王治下毗邻化州的北边要地，1446年阇盘一度落入越军之手，北疆门户洞开的危势暴露无遗。

黎圣宗时风暴再起：1471年之役，越南水师封锁今平山的沙圻海口以断占军退路，阇盘在四日围攻后于3月2日陷落。阿摩罗伐底与阇盘合置为新设的广南承宣，留戍升华卫，越南军户被安置到沿海平原屯垦，旧占邦就此成为大越的经制边地。1559年阮潢兼领广南后，阮主沿这条通道继续向南推设府县和屯田。1771年大起义就在南界之外的归仁爆发；1773年西山军夺取富安，此后漫长内战中，广义海岸夹在归仁的西山中枢与南向作战的阮军之间，兵火连年，占人故城日渐倾颓。1802年阮氏取胜，阿摩罗伐底故地以广义之地归入一统的新王朝。

en:
West of Vijaya, the Jarai plateau stretches from the An Khê passes toward Pleiku and the Ayun and Ba valleys. Jarai people spoke a Chamic Austronesian language and lived in autonomous villages, trading elephants and forest products with the coast while keeping their own spirits and chiefly rituals. Early in the fifteenth century a highland ruler near An Khê bore the Sanskrit-style title Śrī Gajarāja, 'King of the Elephants', and was recorded as a vassal of the Cham king Indravarman VI. In 1444 Jarai lands were not a province of Vijaya: ties to Champa ran through kinship, language and exchange, while local headmen controlled the mountain routes.

Vietnamese records called the later Jarai chiefdoms Thủy Xá and Hỏa Xá, the Water and Fire Holds, led by ritual masters rather than territorial kings. After Vijaya fell in 1471 they remained beyond ordinary lowland administration. From the seventeenth century, Nguyễn missions from Phú Yên travelled up the Ba valley every five years, carrying brocade, bronze pots and porcelain and receiving agarwood, beeswax, deer velvet, bear bile and elephants. The two chiefdoms sent tribute to Nguyễn Phúc Khoát in 1751, submitted to Gia Long in 1803, and in 1821 the Water Hold sought to open formal tribute to Minh Mạng.
zh:
毗阇耶以西，嘉莱高原从安溪山口一直延展到波来古以及阿云、巴江上游谷地。嘉莱人使用南岛语系的占语支语言，居住在自治村寨中，与沿海交换大象和林产，同时保留本族神灵信仰与酋长仪式。15世纪初，安溪附近一位高地统治者拥有梵式称号「Śrī Gajarāja」，意为「象王」，史籍记载他是占婆国王因陀罗跋摩六世的附庸。1444年的嘉莱并非毗阇耶治下的一个省份：它与占婆的联系主要通过亲缘、语言和贸易，山路则掌握在本地头人手中。

越南史籍把后来的嘉莱酋邦称为水舍和火舍，其首领是水与火的仪式权威，而不是统治固定疆土的国王。毗阇耶1471年陷落后，它们仍处在低地常规行政之外。17世纪起，阮主从富安派出的使团每五年沿巴江河谷上行，带去锦缎、铜锅和瓷器，换回沉香、蜂蜡、鹿茸、熊胆和大象。水舍、火舍于1751年向阮福阔入贡，1803年向嘉隆称臣；1821年，水舍又请求向明命正式通贡。

en:
The Đắk Lắk plateau is Rade country, a land of red-earth ridges and Krông rivers between the coast of Kauthara and the Jarai uplands. The Rade spoke a Chamic Austronesian language, traced descent through women, and autonomous longhouse families held paddy land, cattle, gongs and jars under senior women. Cham power had reached Ea Súp by the late thirteenth century, when Jaya Simhavarman III built the brick Yang Prong tower, the only Cham temple known in the Central Highlands. By 1444 that link was one of trade and shared Chamic culture rather than provincial rule; Rade headmen controlled the routes leading inland from Kauthara.

After Vijaya fell in 1471, the coastal Cham world contracted while Rade villages kept their autonomy. Hbia Drah Hjan, daughter of an Adham Rade headman from the Cư M'gar country, entered the declining Cham court and became a queen during her short life from 1630 to 1654. From the mid-eighteenth century, pressure from the Jarai Water and Fire chiefs led many Adham Rade southwest toward Buôn Ma Thuột. Around the same period the female leader Yă Wam, called Mtao Yă, led a wide network from Krông Năng and Buôn Hồ to Ea Súp and Buôn Đôn, where Rade traders met Lao, Siamese and Khmer caravans. Through 1821 this highland network remained outside Vietnamese provincial administration.
zh:
多乐高原是埃地人的土地，红土山脊与克容诸河位于古笪沿海和嘉莱高地之间。埃地人使用南岛语系的占语支语言，按母系追溯世系；自治长屋家族中的年长女性掌管稻田、牛、铜锣和瓮罐。13世纪末，占婆势力已抵达亚苏普，制旻（Jaya Simhavarman III）在那里修建砖塔Yang Prong，这是西原已知唯一一座占婆寺庙。到1444年，这种联系体现为贸易和共同的占语文化，而不是省制统治；从古笪通往内陆的山路掌握在埃地头人手中。

1471年毗阇耶陷落后，沿海占婆世界收缩，埃地村寨仍保持自治。格姆加尔一带的Adham埃地头人之女Hbia Drah Hjan，在1630—1654年的短暂一生中进入衰落的占婆宫廷并成为王后。18世纪中叶起，受嘉莱水王与火王势力逼迫，许多Adham埃地人向西南迁往邦美蜀一带。约在同一时期，被称为Mtao Yă的女首领Yă Wam建立起从克容能、奔胡到亚苏普、奔敦的广阔网络，埃地商人在奔敦与老挝、暹罗、高棉商队交易。到1821年，这个高地网络仍在越南行省体系之外。

en:
Pursat lies where the Pursat River runs out of the Cardamom Mountains into the Tonlé Sap, a corridor of forested highlands, lakeside marshes and rice fields; its Khmer name means 'drifting banyan'. Beside the road north stands Wat Bakan, one of Cambodia's oldest Buddhist monasteries, kept alive without a break for some eight centuries. After the Siamese sack of Angkor in 1431 the refugee Khmer court found a foothold in this district, and local Khmer and Chinese tradition remembers the court of Ponhea Yat sojourning here in the 1430s. In 1444 Pursat was a royal holding in the west of the diminished kingdom — a Theravada Buddhist land of rice farmers, lake fishermen and foresters, on the road toward Siam.

The future Ang Chan I ruled from his fortified camp of Banteay Mean Chey at Pursat until 1529, when he carried the court downstream to the new capital of Lovek. Pursat then became a quiet lakeside province whose rice, fish and forest produce moved with the river trade through Lovek and Oudong. After Siam took Battambang in 1795, Pursat found itself the kingdom's western border province, facing Siamese Phra Tabong. The succession war of 1811–1813 was fought on its doorstep: Prince Ang Snguon's Siamese-backed rising drove King Ang Chan II to Saigon, and a Vietnamese army restored him through this same corridor in 1813. In 1821 Pursat was a Khmer border province within a kingdom under Vietnamese protection, while the roads to its west were watched from Bangkok.
zh:
菩萨位于菩萨河穿出豆蔻山、注入洞里萨湖之处，是山林、湖滨沼泽与稻田相间的走廊；高棉语省名意为「漂浮的菩提树」。北上的大路旁坐落着巴甘寺，它是柬埔寨最古老的佛寺之一，香火延续约八百年而不辍。1431年暹罗攻破吴哥后，南逃的高棉朝廷在这一带立足；高棉与中文的本地记述都提到，奔哈·亚的流亡宫廷在1430年代驻跸菩萨。1444年的菩萨是版图日蹙的王国西部的一处王家居地——种稻、捕鱼、采办山货的人们笃信上座部佛教，大路的尽头就是暹罗。

后来的安赞一世正是从菩萨的班迭棉吉营垒发号施令，直到1529年才率宫廷顺流而下，定都新城洛韦。此后菩萨成为王国沿湖的一处安静省份，稻米、鱼产和山货随着河运经洛韦、乌栋转贩他方。1795年暹罗取得马德望后，菩萨成了王国的西陲边省，与暹罗治下的帕达邦正面相望。1811至1813年的王位战争就打到它的门前：王子安斯农在暹罗支持下起兵，国王安赞二世逃往西贡，1813年越南军队又沿这条走廊送他复位。1821年的菩萨是一个受越南保护的王国里的高棉边省，而通往西边的道路则处在曼谷的监视之下。

en:
Kampot lies where the Praek Tuek Chhu River comes out of the Elephant Mountains and runs five kilometres through mangroves to the Gulf of Thailand. Its pepper gardens were already famous in the 13th century, when the Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan described the pepper grown in these parts, and salt pans and fishing fleets shared the coast. In 1444 Kampot was the southern maritime fringe of the Khmer kingdom, a quiet river roadstead — one of the few anchorages on this shore — where traders from China and the Malay world could take on pepper and forest produce while the king reigned far inland at Chaktomuk.

In the 1690s the Cambodian king granted the Chinese émigré Mạc Cửu authority to open up the coast; between 1687 and 1695 he planted Chinese and Vietnamese settlers in seven settlements, among them Hà Tiên and Kampot itself, called Cần Bột in Vietnamese. After Hà Tiên submitted to the Nguyễn lords in 1708 and passed out of Cambodian rule by 1714, Kampot was left as the kingdom's own chief doorway to the sea, its pepper carried abroad by Chinese junks and Malay traders. It enters the Cambodian chronicles as a military stage: in 1771 King Taksin of Siam destroyed Hà Tiên and marched on Oudong against Outey II, and the claimant Ang Non gathered his Siamese soldiers at Kampot and held it as his base until he seized the throne in 1775. The wars of the suzerains returned in 1811–1813, when Siamese and Vietnamese armies fought over the crown at Oudong; Kampot was spared the fighting but traded on beneath a court caught between Bangkok and Hué. In 1821, ringed by pepper gardens, it was the busiest seaport left to a Khmer king who ruled under Vietnamese protection.
zh:
贡布位于磅头克河流出象山山脉之处，河水穿过红树林蜿蜒五公里注入暹罗湾。这里的胡椒园早已闻名：13世纪中国使节周达观记述真腊物产时，这一带出产的胡椒便已见诸记载；沿岸还分布着盐田和渔船。1444年的贡布是高棉王国的南部海疆，河边的碇泊所是这段海岸上少有的避风良港，中国与马来世界的商人在此装运胡椒和山货，而国王远在内陆的四臂湾治国。

1690年代，柬埔寨国王授予华人移民鄚玖开发海岸的权柄；1687至1695年间，他招来华人和越南移民，建起七处村社，河仙与贡布（越南语称 Cần Bột）都在其中。河仙1708年归附阮主、1714年正式脱离高棉后，贡布便成了王国自己最重要的出海口，胡椒由中国帆船和马来商船远销海外。它首次载入柬埔寨编年史却是作为用兵之地：1771年暹罗国王达信摧毁河仙、进兵乌栋讨伐乌迭二世，王位觊觎者安农在贡布集结暹罗军队，以此为据点，直到1775年夺位成功。1811至1813年，两大宗主国又为乌栋的王冠大动干戈；贡布虽免于兵燹，却只能在曼谷与顺化之间的朝廷治下继续通商。1821年的贡布胡椒园环绕、帆樯云集，是这位在越南保护之下治国的高棉国王手中最繁忙的海港。

en:
Kampong Thom, the 'great port' on the Stung Sen, stretches between the Tonlé Sap and the sandstone hills of the north. Its old royal city was Isanapura, modern Sambor Prei Kuk, which King Isanavarman I laid out around the 620s as the capital of Chenla; the brick towers of its Siva cult still stand in the forests east of the river. Under Angkor the province guarded the lake road between Yasodharapura and the eastern strongholds, its rice lands and river harbor making it one of the richer inner provinces. After the sack of 1431 the kings settled first at Basan and then at Chaktomuk, and Kampong Thom became one of the nearest of the old royal lands to the new courts. In 1444 it was quiet rice country on the edge of a shrunken kingdom, its ancient Hindu shrines overseen by Buddhist monks around the holy hill of Phnom Santuk.

Around 1496 King Thommo Reachea I had Buddha relics carried from Angkor to a new shrine near Phnom Santuk, a sign that the crown still cared for the old heartland. It became a battleground soon after: when the commoner Sdach Korn seized the throne in 1512, King Srey Sokonthor fled to Kompong Svay while Korn made his camp at Phnom Santuk, and the fleeing king was caught and killed on the road to Pursat. The exile prince Chan Reachea came back from Ayutthaya with Siamese support in 1516, and after years of war trapped Korn in a three-month siege and beheaded him in 1525; four years later the newly crowned Ang Chan I made Longvek his capital. The region felt the wars of the next three centuries mostly through levies and passing armies, until the dynastic conflict of 1811–1813 brought Siamese troops into neighboring Pursat and the burning of Oudong in 1813. In 1821 Kampong Thom was Khmer rice land still, under a king protected by Vietnam.
zh:
磅同，高棉语意为「大港口」，位于森河之畔，处在洞里萨湖与北方砂岩丘陵之间。这里最早的王都叫伊奢那补罗，即今三博波雷古，约620年代由伊奢那跋摩一世营建为真腊都城，森河以东的林中仍立着供奉湿婆的砖塔。吴哥时代，此地扼守耶输陀罗补罗通往东部诸城的湖上要道，稻田与河港使它成为最富庶的内郡之一。1431年吴哥遭劫后，高棉国王先后定都巴山和四臂湾，磅同遂成为距新朝廷最近的旧畿之地。1444年时，这里是收缩的王国边缘一片安静的米乡，古老的印度教神龛由圣山蓬南图克一带的佛寺僧人照料。

约1496年，托摩罗阇一世把佛舍利从吴哥迎奉到蓬南图克附近的新塔安置，可见王室仍眷顾这片旧腹地。但这里不久就成了战场：1512年平民出身的斯登干篡位，国王斯雷·索贡托逃往磅斯外，斯登干在蓬南图克扎营，出逃的国王最终在前往菩萨的路上被擒杀。流亡王子安赞1516年借阿瑜陀耶之兵返国，多年征战后于1525年围城三个月，擒斩斯登干；四年后，即位的安赞一世定都洛韦。此后三百年的战乱，这里多半只以输粮纳赋和军队过境的方式体会，直到1811至1813年的王室内乱，暹罗军队进入相邻的菩萨，乌栋也于1813年被焚毁。1821年时，磅同依旧是高棉人的米乡，而它的国王受越南庇护。

en:
Preah Vihear, the 'sacred sanctuary,' takes its name from the Hindu temple crowning a 525-metre cliff of the Dangrek escarpment that forms Cambodia's northern rim. Begun early in the ninth century, rebuilt in the Koh Ker style and enlarged chiefly under Suryavarman I and Suryavarman II, it climbs along a rare north–south axis of gateways toward a shrine of Siva as god of the mountain. South of the range, Koh Ker—ancient Lingapura—was the capital of the whole empire from 928 to 944 under Jayavarman IV, who raised its seven-tiered pyramid and colossal lingas. Farther east, Preah Khan Kompong Svay, the largest walled complex of the Angkorian age, served as a royal residence under Suryavarman II and as Jayavarman VII's base in the Cham wars, and Kuy smelters worked the iron of nearby Phnom Dek to arm the empire. That complex was abandoned between the late fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, and in 1444 this was a thinly peopled march of forest and old shrines, Khmer rice villages and Kuy forges, while the king ruled far south at Chaktomuk and Ayutthaya lay just beyond the passes.

The Dangrek passes were the road by which Siamese armies entered Cambodia: the first Ayutthayan invasion of 1591 came through the Phra Charuk passage, and in 1593 one of Naresuan's four columns made for Siem Reap and Kampong Svay before Longvek fell on 3 January 1594. Through these centuries the cliff temple, converted to Buddhist use, drew Khmer and Siamese pilgrims and hermits rather than kings. In 1795 the new Bangkok dynasty brought the northwest Cambodian provinces beyond the range under direct rule, and the Dangrek became the hard frontier between Siam and the Khmer crown; the Siamese armies of the civil war of 1811–1813 marched out of bases on its western side. By 1821 the great sanctuary stood at the edge of a vassal Cambodia, its stairways looking out over Siamese-held marches.
zh:
柏威夏，高棉语意为「圣所」，省名得自矗立在扁担山525米悬崖上的印度教寺庙。柏威夏寺9世纪初开建，10世纪初按贡开风格重建，主体扩建于苏利耶跋摩一世（1006—1050年）和苏利耶跋摩二世（1113—1150年）两朝，沿少见的南北中轴层层升高，通向供奉山神湿婆的主殿。山脉以南的贡开，古称林伽补罗，928至944年曾是整个帝国的都城，阇耶跋摩四世在此建起七层金字塔式国庙和两丈高的林伽。更往东的磅斯外圣剑寺是吴哥时代占地最广的围墙建筑群，曾是苏利耶跋摩二世的行宫、阇耶跋摩七世对占婆作战的军寨；库伊铁匠在近旁的铁山冶铁，为帝国打造兵器。这座大寺在14世纪末至15世纪间被废弃，到1444年，这里已是人烟稀少的边郡：林间散落旧神龛，高棉村寨种稻，库伊人开炉冶铁，国王远在南方的四臂湾，而山隘那一边就是阿瑜陀耶。

扁担山的山口历来是暹罗军队进入高棉的通道：1591年阿瑜陀耶第一次大举入侵便取道帕差鲁隘口；1593年纳黎萱四路伐高棉，第一路直指暹粒和磅斯外，1594年1月3日洛韦陷落。此后几个世纪里，改作佛寺的柏威夏寺只吸引高棉和暹罗的朝圣者、隐修者，再没有国王登临。1795年，曼谷新王朝把山外的高棉西北诸省纳入直接管辖，扁担山从此成为暹罗与高棉王廷之间实打实的边防线；1811至1813年内乱时，暹罗军队就是从山脉西侧的基地出征的。到1821年，这座大圣所立在一个藩属柬埔寨的边缘，长长的石阶之下，望见的尽是暹罗把持的边地。

en:
Between the Mekong and the blue spine of the Central Highlands stretches a wooded march of red earth and open forest, where Khmer rice villages meet the swidden clearings of the S'Tiêng and paths that lead east into Champa. After Ayutthaya sacked Angkor in 1431, the Khmer kings carried their court south to Chaktomuk, the future Phnom Penh; this eastern borderland, facing a Champa that still held Vijaya, was then left largely to its own headmen. In 1444 it was a poor and thinly peopled province of the Khmer crown, on the forest road between the new capital and the Cham country.

The Vietnamese took Vijaya in 1471 and reduced Champa to Panduranga on this province's flank, and in the 1690s the march became the last theatre of the Nguyễn lords' southern conquests. The Cham king Po Saut rose in 1692, and the general Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh captured him in 1693; but a rising raised by the Chinese adventurer A Ban and the Cham lord Óc Nha Thát ran on into 1694, the rebels falling back through the upper woods bordering on Chân Lạp before they were crushed. When the Cambodian king Chey Chettha IV built ramparts across the approaches to Phnom Penh in 1699, Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh stormed them and in 1700 received his surrender, dying of illness on his way down the Mekong. In the Siamese-Cambodian rising of 1811 King Ang Chan was driven to Saigon by his rebel brother and a Siamese army; in 1813 more than 13,000 Vietnamese troops under Lê Văn Duyệt restored him, and the Khmer kingdom, this march with it, passed under Vietnamese protection.
zh:
湄公河与中央高地青色山脊之间，横亘着一片红土疏林的边地：高棉人的稻寨与斯丁人的刀耕火种地相接，向东的小路通往占城。1431年阿瑜陀耶攻陷吴哥后，高棉国王把朝廷南迁到四臂湾，即后来的金边；这片东境面对仍据有佛逝的占城，此后大体交给各地头人自理。1444年，它是高棉王冠下一个贫穷而人烟稀疏的省份，处在新都与占城之间的林道上。

1471年越南攻破佛逝，占城被压缩到本省侧旁的宾童龙；到1690年代，这片边地成了阮主南略的最后战场。占城王婆争1692年起兵，大将阮有镜1693年将他生擒；但华人冒险家阿班与占城贵胄屋牙挞发动的起事一直延续到1694年，败军退入与真腊接界的上游林地，才被剿平。1699年，柬埔寨国王吉·哲塔四世在金边外围筑垒拦路，阮有镜连破其垒，1700年受其归降，自己却在沿湄公河南下途中染病身亡。1811年暹罗-柬埔寨之乱中，安赞二世被叛乱的弟弟和暹罗军逼逃嘉定；1813年，黎文悦率一万三千多名越军送他复位，高棉王国连同这片边地从此处在越南保护之下。

en:
Rayong lies on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Siam, on a coastal plain of rice fields and orchards where short rivers from the hills on the Khmer frontier run down to the sea. Its name comes from Chong, the Mon-Khmer speech of the region's older inhabitants, and a town stood here from Khmer times. By the fifteenth century it counted among Ayutthaya's eastern coastal towns: in 1444 it was a small port and garrison of Borommarachathirat II's kingdom, and in 1455 the military registers of Borommatrailokkanat ranked it a third-class provincial town.

In 1570, in the reign of Maha Thammaracha, a Khmer army from Longvek swept the eastern seaboard; it failed to take Rayong but carried off many of its people. In January 1767, while Ayutthaya was still under Burmese siege, Phraya Tak – the governor who became King Taksin – cut his way out with some five hundred followers and reached the town, where he rested his men for over a week and gathered a fleet before marching on Chanthaburi and Trat. The poet Sunthorn Phu, whose father came from Klaeng, later visited his father's family there and made the journey the subject of one of his best-known travel poems, Nirat Mueang Klaeng.
zh:
罗勇在暹罗湾东岸，稻田与果园铺展在滨海平原上，泰柬边境丘陵发源的小河在此入海。罗勇一名来自当地原住民崇族（Chong）的语言，属孟—高棉语系，高棉时代已有城镇。到15世纪，它已是阿瑜陀耶东部沿海诸镇之一：1444年，它是波隆摩罗阇二世王国的一座小港口兼驻军镇；1455年，波隆摩·戴莱洛迦纳的军务文书把它列为三等府。

1570年摩诃·昙摩罗阇在位时，一支从洛韦出发的高棉军队横扫东部沿海，未能攻下罗勇，却掳走了不少居民。1767年1月，阿瑜陀耶尚在缅甸军围困之中，达府太守披耶达——也就是后来的郑信——率约五百人突围抵达罗勇，在此休整人马八九天、召集船队，而后才进兵尖竹汶和桐艾。诗人顺通铺的父亲是格灵（Klaeng）人，他后来前往探望父族，把这段旅程写成名篇《格灵城纪行诗》（Nirat Mueang Klaeng）。

en:
Bangkok and Thonburi face each other across the lower Chao Phraya, twenty miles upriver from the sandbar at Pak Nam where the river meets the sea. By the early fifteenth century the place was Ayutthaya's chief customs outpost: incoming ships declared their cargo and passenger count, paid duty and surrendered their cannon before sailing on to the capital, and the title of its officer, Nai Phra Khanon Thonburi, is recorded from the reign of Borommarachathirat II (1424–1448). The royal chronicles name the town Thonburi Si Mahasamut, while Dutch and English traders called it Bangkok; an East India Company ship, the Globe, was received there in August 1612. In the reign of King Chairachathirat a shortcut canal was cut through the great loop of the river, shortening the voyage to Ayutthaya and turning the west-bank settlement into an island.

Maritime trade peaked under King Narai. In 1685–1687 the French engineer de la Mare raised a Western-style fort on the east bank, the Chevalier de Forbin held the place as governor with a garrison of roughly a thousand Siamese, Portuguese and French, and a second French embassy under Desfarges billeted troops there in 1687. The revolution of 1688 swept it away: with Narai dying at Lopburi, tens of thousands of Phetracha's men besieged the French fort for four months until it surrendered and was demolished. Taksin made the fortified town his capital after the fall of Ayutthaya and was crowned there on 28 December 1767. His successor Rama I crossed to the east bank, erected the city pillar on 21 April 1782 and founded Rattanakosin, building the Grand Palace and resettling the Chinese merchants at Sampheng.
zh:
曼谷与吞武里隔湄南河下游相望，从河口北榄的沙洲上溯约二十英里即至。15世纪初，这里已是阿瑜陀耶最重要的税关：进港商船必须申报货物与乘员人数、缴纳关税、卸下大炮封存，才获准继续上溯京城；税官「乃帕卡农吞武里」（Nai Phra Khanon Thonburi）的头衔在波隆摩罗阇二世（1424—1448年在位）朝的文书中已有记载。王室编年史称此城为吞武里·斯里玛哈萨穆，荷兰与英国商人则叫它曼谷，1612年8月英国东印度公司商船「地球号」已在此停泊受检。帕拉猜王在位时，朝廷在湄南河大弯处开凿取直运河，缩短了前往阿瑜陀耶的航程，也使河西聚落变成一座岛。

海上贸易在那莱王时达到极盛。1685至1687年，法国工程师德·拉马尔在河东建起西式棱堡，福尔班骑士任城守，统辖约一千名暹罗、葡萄牙和法国守军；1687年德法尔热率领的第二个法国使团又在此驻军。1688年的革命将这一切一扫而空：那莱王在华富里病逝前后，帕碧罗阇的数万大军围攻法军棱堡四个月，法军最终投降撤离，堡垒被拆毁。阿瑜陀耶1767年陷落后，郑信以这座设防城镇为都，于1767年12月28日在此加冕。继位的拉玛一世跨到河东，1782年4月21日立下城柱，建立拉达那哥欣（曼谷新城），营建大皇宫，并把华人商户迁至三聘一带。

en:
Lavo – the Lavapura of the chronicles, later known as Lopburi – stands on a river of the central plain where the routes north to the Northern Cities and east on to the Khorat plateau begin. It was one of the largest moated towns of the Mon Dvaravati world, the regional centre with more subordinate settlements than any other on the central plain, and was drawn into the Khmer empire under Suryavarman I; the Bayon-style prang of Phra Prang Sam Yod still marks its old centre. As Angkor weakened Lavo went its own way, and under Ayutthaya it became a fortified stronghold of the kings, guarding the capital's northern approaches. In 1444 it was a royal garrison city of Borommarachathirat II's realm.

King Narai made its fortune. In 1666 he ordered a new palace built on the site of King Ramesuan's old residence, kept court there eight or nine months of the year and in 1685 received the French embassy of the Chevalier de Chaumont in its halls. It was in Lopburi that his reign ended: the Greek minister Phaulkon was beheaded for treason on 5 June 1688, the dying Narai was held in the palace and died there on 11 July, and Phetracha was crowned on 1 August. Court and government returned to Ayutthaya, and the town and its palace were abandoned for the rest of our period.
zh:
罗涡，古名罗婆补罗（Lavapura），即今华富里，坐落在中央平原的一条河畔，是北上北方诸城、东登呵叻高原的门户。它本是孟人陀罗钵地文化圈最大的环城之一，下辖聚落之多居中央平原之首，后在苏利耶跋摩一世时并入高棉帝国，旧城中心还立着巴戎风格的三峰塔。吴哥衰落后罗涡自立，阿瑜陀耶时代成为国王直辖的设防重镇，扼守京城北路。1444年，它是波隆摩罗阇二世王国的一座王家驻军城。

让罗涡显赫一时的是那莱王。1666年，他下令在拉梅萱王旧宫基址上营建新宫，每年有八九个月在此理政，1685年肖蒙骑士率领的法国使团就是在这座宫殿觐见。那莱朝也终结于华富里：1688年6月5日，希腊籍宠臣康斯坦丁·法尔孔以叛国罪被斩首，病危的那莱被幽禁宫中，7月11日去世，帕碧罗阇于8月1日加冕。宫廷与政府随后迁回阿瑜陀耶，罗涡城与王宫就此荒废，在本时期余下的岁月里再未恢复。

en:
Phetchabun lies in a long grain-growing valley on the upper Pa Sak River, between the hills facing Khorat and the routes to Phitsanulok and Lavo. Its old name Phuenchapura meant a town rich in crops, and Sukhothai Inscription 8 already places the Pa Sak valley among the lands held by Li Thai. Prince Damrong later read the old town as a frontier post built first in the Sukhothai or Phitsanulok period and again under Ayutthaya. In 1444 it was a fertile but exposed Ayutthayan march, a granary on the roads toward the Sukhothai lands and Lan Xang.

During the Ayutthaya centuries, Lan Xang armies moving from the Mekong slopes repeatedly came down the Pa Sak toward Lopburi and the capital. The fortified settlement was rebuilt in King Narai's reign, again placed to watch enemies from the north, while the valley's rice continued to move downstream by river.
zh:
碧差汶位于巴塞河上游的狭长产粮谷地，东面是通向呵叻的山地，西北和西南则连接彭世洛与华富里。旧名Phuenchapura意为五谷丰登之城；素可泰八号铭文已把巴塞河谷列为立泰统辖的地区。丹隆亲王后来考证，这座古城最初在素可泰或彭世洛为都时期作为边镇营建，阿瑜陀耶时期又曾重建。1444年，这里是阿瑜陀耶一处肥沃却暴露的边地，既是粮仓，也扼守通往素可泰故土和澜沧方向的山路。

阿瑜陀耶时代，澜沧军队从湄公河流域出兵时，多次沿巴塞河谷进逼华富里和都城。那莱王在位期间，这座要塞城镇再次得到营建，用以监视北方之敌，谷地里的稻米也继续顺河南运。

en:
Suphanburi, the 'city of gold', lies on the Tha Chin River in one of central Siam's richest rice plains. Its moated Dvaravati settlement was known as Mueang Thawarawadi Si Suphannaphumi; nearby U Thong has yielded Chinese and Persian Gulf imports from the eighth to tenth centuries and was later linked to Ramathibodi I, founder of Ayutthaya. In the mid-fourteenth century the settlement was refounded on the Tha Chin and renamed Suphanburi by Khunluang Pha Ngua, the governor who became King Borommarachathirat I in 1370. By 1444 it was an Ayutthayan border town and royal granary on the roads toward the western passes.

The rice plain fed Ayutthaya, while the country west of the town repeatedly became a battlefield against Burma. After Ayutthaya's fall in 1569, Toungoo overlordship was reimposed. In 1593, during the campaign commemorated on Suphanburi's seal, Naresuan killed the Burmese heir Mingyi Swa in elephant combat on the province's traditional battlefield; the victory ended the 1584-1593 war and confirmed Siamese independence. Later Burmese-Siamese wars still swept the district, leaving the old town and its monuments in ruins. The Bangkok-period settlement was rebuilt on the eastern bank of the Tha Chin.
zh:
素攀武里意为「黄金之城」，位于他金河畔，地处暹罗中部最肥沃的稻米平原之一。陀罗钵地时期，这里已有带护城河的聚落，称Thawarawadi Si Suphannaphumi；附近的乌通在8—10世纪已有中国和波斯湾器物出土，后来又与阿瑜陀耶开创者乌通王联系在一起。14世纪中叶，聚落在他金河畔重建，由城主拍乌命名为素攀武里；他后来在1370年成为波隆摩罗阇一世。到1444年，这里已是阿瑜陀耶的边镇和王家粮仓，扼守通往西部山口的道路。

这片稻米平原供应阿瑜陀耶，城西郊野却屡次成为对缅战场。1569年阿瑜陀耶陷落后，东吁王朝的宗主权再度加身。1593年，在素攀武里府徽所纪念的战役中，纳黎萱于府内传统认定的战场与缅甸王储展开象战并将其斩杀；这场胜利结束1584—1593年战争，巩固了暹罗独立。后来的缅暹战争仍多次席卷这一带，旧城与古迹多成残垣。曼谷时代的素攀武里城，则在他金河东岸重建。

en:
Kanchanaburi lies in the Mae Klong valley at the foot of the Tenasserim Hills, where the Three Pagodas Pass offers the chief road between Burma and the Chao Phraya plain. Its antiquities run deep: fourth-century trading settlements, Dvaravati Buddhist monuments and the Bayon-style Khmer temple of Mueang Sing, raised when the Khmer empire held these marches. In Sukhothai times the locality was a dependency of Suphan Buri, and under Ayutthaya it became a fortified western march with its stockade at Lat Ya. In 1444 Kanchanaburi was a Siamese, Theravada Buddhist frontier district whose people lived by the trade and the alarms of the Burma road.

The alarms proved real. In 1548 Tabinshwehti's army poured through the Three Pagodas Pass during the Burmese–Siamese war of 1547–1549, the first Burmese invasion to take that road; for the next two centuries the pass was the highway by which Burmese armies marched on Ayutthaya and Siamese armies counter-marched toward the Tenasserim coast. After Ayutthaya fell in 1767, King Rama I planted a permanent garrison town at Lat Ya, and Mueang Sing was refortified to guard it, the western shield of the new Bangkok kingdom in its wars with Burma.
zh:
干乍那武里位于夜功河河谷、丹那沙林山脉脚下，山间的三塔山口是缅甸通往湄南河平原最主要的通道。这里古史积淀深厚：有4世纪的贸易聚落、堕罗钵底佛教遗迹，还有高棉帝国据守这片边地时修建的巴戎风格石宫孟辛（Mueang Sing）。素可泰时代，这一带是素攀武里的属地；阿瑜陀耶时期，它成为设防的西部边镇，寨城设在拉亚（Lat Ya）。1444年的干乍那武里是一片暹罗人的上座部佛教边地，居民的生计与缅甸通道上的贸易和边警紧密相连。

边警终成现实。1548年，在1547—1549年的缅暹战争中，德彬瑞梯的大军穿过三塔山口涌入，这是缅军第一次取道此路；此后两百年间，这个山口始终是缅军进军阿瑜陀耶、暹军反攻丹那沙林海岸的大道。1767年阿瑜陀耶陷落后，拉玛一世在拉亚常设军镇，孟辛也重新筑城作为护卫，成为曼谷新王朝在历次对缅战争中的西部门户。

en:
Si Thep lies in the Pa Sak valley where the land begins to climb toward the Khorat Plateau. Here stood one of the great cities of the Dvaravati world, a moated town of inner and outer cities covering 4.7 square kilometres: settled from the 6th century, it raised standing images of Vishnu and carved Buddhist wheels of the law, and guarded the regional roads together with Sema and Lavo. At its height in the 8th to 10th centuries it founded the river port of Tha Rong twenty kilometres up the Pa Sak, and Khmer rule later added the brick prangs of Si Thep and Song Phi Nong. Plague and the redirection of trade thinned the city, and by the 14th century it was abandoned as power passed to Sukhothai and Ayutthaya. In 1444 its walls stood overgrown, and the valley's rice lands, Ayutthaya's remote north-eastern march, looked to the old river port of Tha Rong.

The ruins vanished into the jungle then called Dong Phaya Fai, the Lord of Fire's forest, remembered only in legend, while Tha Rong lived on as a small rice town on the road from Lavo to Khorat. In 1768 Taksin's armies marched up this corridor against Prince Thepphiphit's faction at Phimai, stormed their camp at Cho Ho beyond the pass and went on to retake Khorat. Through the early Bangkok years the valley remained a quiet march, its villagers farming rice along the Pa Sak beneath the empty Khmer prangs.
zh:
西贴位于巴塞河谷，正是地势开始升向呵叻高原之处。这里曾有陀罗钵地世界最大的城市之一：一座有壕沟围护、内外两重、广达4.7平方公里的都城，6世纪起有人定居，城中立着毗湿奴石像，刻有佛教法轮，并与色玛、罗斛（Lavo）共扼这一带的商路。8至10世纪全盛时，它在巴塞河上游20公里处设立了河港他龙（Tha Rong）；高棉时期又加建西贴、双兄弟（Song Phi Nong）砖塔。后来瘟疫流行、商路改易，人口流散，到14世纪城市已遭废弃，权力转入素可泰和阿瑜陀耶之手。1444年，城墙已被丛林吞没，这片阿瑜陀耶东北边远领地的稻田，皆以古老河港他龙为中心。

古城湮没在时称「火王林」（Dong Phaya Fai）的丛林中，仅存于传说；他龙则作为罗斛通往呵叻路上的稻米小镇延续下来。1768年，郑昭的大军沿这条河谷北上，讨伐以披迈为据点的贴披披势力，出关攻破其在卓霍（Cho Ho）的营地，进而收复呵叻。曼谷王朝前期，这片河谷始终是安静的边地，乡民在巴塞河畔种稻，身旁就是空寂的高棉砖塔。

en:
Muang Ngoi is a river landing on the upper Nam Ou, where the Nam Ngoi comes down from the hills to join it, one of a chain of Tai muang strung along that river since the 12th century. Long boats carried hill ivory, benzoin and cardamom downstream to Luang Prabang, and rice and salt back up. Fa Ngum's army came down this river on the march that took Muang Sua and founded Lan Xang in 1353, and the town itself took shape in the following century as an old district seat of the northern frontier. In 1444 it was a small Lao muang of the upriver country, whose people kept the Buddhism of the capital side by side with the older spirit cults of forest and river, answering to the king at Xieng Thong.

The Nam Ou was a road for armies as well as trade: the Burmese campaigns against Lan Xang in the later 1500s reached into these valleys, and the upriver muang followed Luang Prabang's fortunes through those wars. In 1713, after Kingkitsarat's death, his brother Inthasom marched on the capital and halted at Muang Ngoi; there he came to terms with the newly crowned Ong Kham and accepted the title of oupahat, viceroy, before taking the throne himself in 1723. His long reign kept the northern marches quiet, and tribute missions from Luang Prabang went to the Qing court in 1723 and 1734. Thereafter Muang Ngoi shared the fate of the Luang Prabang kingdom — Burmese occupation in the 1760s and Siamese suzerainty from 1778 — and in 1821 it remained a quiet timber-and-ivory river station of a kingdom tributary to Bangkok.
zh:
孟威是南乌河上游的一处河埠，南威河从山中流来在此汇入南乌河；自12世纪起，南乌河上便串着一连串泰族的勐，孟威是其中之一。长船把山地的象牙、安息香和豆蔻运往琅勃拉邦，又把稻米和食盐逆流拉回上游。1353年法昂攻取勐苏瓦、建立澜沧时，大军正是沿这条河南下；这座城镇于15世纪成形，是北方边境一座古老的县治所在。1444年，这里是南乌河上游一个小小的佬族勐，百姓信奉都城的佛教，同时保留着对河与山林的古老精灵崇拜，向川铜的国王称臣。

南乌河既是商路，也是兵道：16世纪后期缅甸征讨澜沧的战事深入这些河谷，上游各勐也随琅勃拉邦一同沉浮。1713年景吉萨去世，其弟因塔松进军王都，在孟威停军，与刚刚即位的翁坎达成和议，接受「乌巴腊」即副王的封号，最终于1723年亲自登上王位。他在位长久，北方边境安靖，琅勃拉邦并于1723年和1734年向清朝遣使朝贡。此后孟威与琅勃拉邦王国共命运——1760年代遭缅甸占领，1778年起臣属暹罗；1821年时，它仍是这个向曼谷称臣的王国里一座安静的河埠，做着木材与象牙的生意。

en:
The Roi Et country is the flat middle reach of the Chi River on the Khorat plateau, a spread of seasonal grassland and salt flats. Dvaravati and then Khmer settlers once built shrines and villages here – a sixth- or seventh-century Pallava inscription has been found at Don Khum Ngoen – but with Angkor's decline in the thirteenth century its towns were abandoned. By 1444 the plateau was an almost empty hunting ground of wild elephant herds, loosely claimed by Lan Xang but ruled from no town. Its later memory was of Saket Nakhon, a city said to have eleven gates and eleven vassal muang: sip et, 'eleven', was later misread as roi et, 'one hundred and one'.

Lao settlers returned only in 1718, when an official of King Nokasad of Champasak led some 3,000 people up the Chi to found Muang Suwannaphum, the first Lao muang in the plateau's interior. In 1775 Chao Suthonmanee brought families out from Suwannaphum to resettle the old site as Roi Et, and King Taksin soon confirmed the new muang under Bangkok; the eleven gates gave it both its name and its claim to eleven dependent towns. Taksin's armies swept through Champasak and Vientiane in 1777–1778, and the Lao lords of the Chi henceforth ruled as Siamese tributaries.
zh:
黎逸这片地方是呵叻高原栖河中游的平坦原野，遍布季节性草场和盐碱地。堕罗钵底时期及后来的高棉人曾在此建寺定居——敦坤因（Don Khum Ngoen）出土过6或7世纪的跋罗婆文碑铭——但随着13世纪吴哥衰落，城镇相继荒废。到1444年，这片高原几乎空无一人，是野象群出没的猎场，澜沧只保有松散的名义，并无城镇统辖此地。后世只记得旧城名Saket Nakhon，传说那是一座有十一座城门、十一个属勐的大城：「十一」（sip et）后来被误读成「一百零一」（roi et），黎逸（Roi Et）由此得名。

佬人迟至1718年才重返此地：占巴塞王诺卡沙手下的一名官员率约三千百姓溯栖河而上，建立苏旺那蓬（Suwannaphum），这是高原内陆第一个佬人勐。1775年，昭苏敦马尼率部众从苏旺那蓬迁出，在旧城址上重建黎逸，达信王很快确认了这个新勐对曼谷的臣属；十一座城门既给了它名字，也承载着统辖十一座属城的旧说。1777—1778年达信的军队席卷占巴塞与万象，栖河流域的佬人首领自此以暹罗藩属身份统治。

en:
Above the Mekong at the foot of Phou Khao mountain stands Vat Phou, the oldest stone temple in Laos: a sanctuary of Shiva raised around the sixth century, when nearby Shrestapura was a capital of early Chenla with ties to Champa, rebuilt under the Angkor kings and later left to Buddhist worshippers. Below the ruins spreads the Bassac plain, the last reach of the river before the Khone falls and the Four Thousand Islands, where cargoes moving between the upper Mekong and Cambodia had to change hands. Fa Ngum's armies folded the country into Lan Xang in the fourteenth century. In 1444 it was a thickly forested southern march of the million-elephant kingdom, whose Lao muang lived on rice, ivory and cardamom from the trade carried overland around the falls, while animist hill peoples held the high valleys.

Southern wars passed through Bassac under Lan Xang: Setthathirat's army marched this way on his campaigns against Cambodia in 1571–1572 and the king vanished near Attapeu, and in 1579 a revolt raised in his daughter's name came up from the south along the river road. When Lan Xang broke apart, the lord Nokasad founded the Kingdom of Champasak in 1713, ruling from a capital below Vat Phou with Attapeu and Stung Treng as his dependent principalities; in 1718 his officials planted the first Lao settlement on the empty Khorat plateau at Suwannaphum. In November 1778 a Siamese army under Surasi took Champasak and carried King Sayakumane off to Bangkok, whence he returned in 1780 to reign as a tributary. Around 1800 the Bassac route prospered, carrying cardamom, wax, resin, hides, horns and slaves to Ubon, Khorat and Bangkok. In 1815 a 'holy man' rebellion drove King Ma Noi from his capital, and in 1819 Anouvong of Vientiane intervened to place his own son Chao Yo on the Champasak throne.
zh:
湄公河畔普高山脚下的瓦普寺，是老挝最古老的石庙：约6世纪时为供奉湿婆而建，当时附近的室利陀罗补罗（Shrestapura）是与占婆往来的早期真腊都城，后经吴哥诸王重修，最终转为佛教徒的道场。遗址下方是巴塞平原——湄公河在孔瀑布和四千美岛之前的最后一段，上游与柬埔寨往来的货物都在此换手中转。14世纪法昂的军队把这片土地并入澜沧。1444年，这里是澜沧森林密布的南部边陲：佬人诸勐靠稻米、象牙、豆蔻为生，商货绕开瀑布走陆路转运，高山河谷里则住着泛灵信仰的山地族群。

澜沧治下，南方的战事多次经过巴塞：1571—1572年赛塔提拉的军队取道此处出征柬埔寨，他本人最终在阿速坡附近失踪；1579年以其女之名发动的起义也沿湄公河自南方北上。澜沧分裂后，领主诺加萨（Nokasad）于1713年建立占巴塞王国，在瓦普寺下方建都，阿速坡与上丁是他的附属亲王国；1718年，他的官员在苏旺那蓬（Suwannaphum）建立了空旷呵叻高原上的第一个佬人定居点。1778年11月，昭披耶索拉西率军攻占占巴塞，国王赛亚古曼（Sayakumane）被掳往曼谷，1780年才以藩属身份归国复位。19世纪初，巴塞商路繁盛，豆蔻、蜂蜡、松香、皮革、兽角和奴隶经此运往乌汶、呵叻和曼谷。1815年，一场「圣人」叛乱把国王昭马内（Chao Ma Noi）赶出都城；1819年万象王阿努出兵干预，把自己的儿子昭约扶上了占巴塞王位。

en: The Xe Kong rises in the Annamite crest and runs south through a broken, forested country of rapids and high plateaux before joining the Mekong at Stung Treng. Its valley held no Lao muang: the villagers were Mon-Khmer peoples – Katu, Talieng and Katang – who kept to ancestral and spirit worship and floated ivory, cardamom, horn and wax down the navigable lower river, while the old Khmer country of Muang Mang answered only loosely to distant lowland rulers. Fa Ngum brought the valley into Lan Xang in 1353, and in 1444 it was the kingdom's most thinly peopled southeastern march. When Lan Xang split the land passed to the Champasak mandala, and after the Siamese conquest of 1779 its hill chiefs sent their forest tribute through Champasak to Bangkok.
zh: 塞公河发源于长山山脉，向南穿过丘陵破碎、森林密布、急流与高原交错之地，在上丁汇入湄公河。河谷里没有佬人的勐：居民是卡杜、达连、卡当等孟高棉语族群，信奉祖先与万物有灵，把象牙、豆蔻、角材和蜂蜡沿可通航的下游河段送出；旧称勐芒（Muang Mang）的这片高棉故地，对远方低地统治者只有松散的臣属关系。1353年法昂将河谷并入澜沧，1444年时它是澜沧人口最稀、控制最弱的东南边陲。澜沧分裂后，这片土地归入占巴塞的曼荼罗体系；1779年暹罗征服之后，山地头人的森林贡赋经占巴塞送往曼谷。

en:
Lamphun lies in the narrow Ping River grain basin only a short march south of Chiang Mai. The old walled city was Haripuñjaya, the northernmost and last surviving Mon kingdom of the Dvaravati world, whose Wat Phra That Haripuñjai housed a Buddha relic from 897 and drew pilgrims long before the Tai conquest. Mangrai's agents undermined its last court, and in 1292 he absorbed the wealthy city into Lan Na. Mon sculpture, scripture and temple practice then shaped the culture of Mangrai's new kingdom. In 1444 Lamphun was therefore both an ancient Mon ceremonial centre and a closely guarded northern Thai city of Tilokaraj's Lan Na.

The wars of Lan Na carried Lamphun into the Burmese sphere when Bayinnaung's forces made the northern kingdom a vassal in 1558. Burmese overlordship lasted, with breaks and local risings, for roughly two centuries and left the old city badly exposed during the Burmese-Siamese struggles. After Kawila of Lampang took Chiang Mai with Siamese help in January 1775, Lamphun passed into Bangkok's tributary system; Thai records describe it as deserted when Kawila's Chiang Mai dynasty consolidated the region. In 1814 Rama II appointed Phraya Khamfan, a younger brother of Kawila, to rebuild Lamphun as its first new lord, beginning the slow restoration of the temples, rice lands and walled city.
zh:
南奔位于宾河狭窄的稻米盆地，北距清迈仅数日路程。这座古城就是哈利奔猜，陀罗钵地世界中位置最北、也存留到最后的孟人王国；南奔金塔寺供奉着897年入塔的佛舍利，早在泰人征服前已久负盛名。孟莱派人渗透并削弱其末代王廷，1292年吞并这座富庶城市，将其纳入兰纳。孟人的雕塑、经典和寺院传统随后深刻影响了孟莱新王国的文化。因此在1444年，南奔既是古老的孟人礼仪中心，也是滴洛拉阇治下兰纳的北疆泰人重镇。

1558年，勃印曩的军队使兰纳成为属邦，南奔也随兰纳进入缅甸势力范围。缅甸宗主权虽有中断和本地起义，仍延续约两个世纪；在缅暹战争中，这座古城屡遭冲击。1775年1月，南邦的咖威拉在暹罗协助下夺取清迈，南奔随之进入曼谷的藩属体系。泰文史料记载，咖威拉的清迈王朝巩固各地时，南奔已是一座荒城。1814年，拉玛二世册封咖威拉的幼弟帕雅·坎范为南奔新统治者，命他重建城邦，寺院、稻田和城墙内的城市由此慢慢恢复。

en:
Lampang holds the broad rice plain of the Wang River, southeast of Chiang Mai and on the southern roads toward Sukhothai. Known as Khelang Nakhon and Wiang Lakon, the mueang entered Mangrai's Lan Na, and Thai chronicles date a new walled settlement, with moats and gates, to 1302. Its position made it a southern frontier fortress and a stopping place for routes between the Ping valley, the Lao hills and Sukhothai. In 1444 Wiang Lakon guarded Tilokaraj's southern border, while the Emerald Buddha, whose carrying elephant had turned from the road to Chiang Mai, was enshrined at Wat Phra Kaeo Don Tao.

Tilokaraj had the image moved to Chiang Mai in 1468. Wiang Lakon remained a battlefield in Lan Na's wars with Ayutthaya, which took and depopulated the town in 1510–1515, and Bayinnaung's Burmese conquest of 1558 opened more than two centuries of Burmese overlordship. In 1732 the hunter Thipchang killed the Lamphun ruler Thao Mahayot at Wat Phra That Lampang Luang after he had seized Lampang; the townsmen raised Thipchang as their lord and Ava recognized him in 1735. His grandson Kawila became lord of Lampang in 1774, joined Taksin's Siamese army, and helped take Chiang Mai on 15 January 1775. Lampang then became the base of the Seven Princes; its court rebuilt the walls and moats in 1794 and built a new ruler's hall around 1808, while Kawila's kinsmen governed Chiang Mai, Lampang and Lamphun under Siamese suzerainty.
zh:
南邦控扼清迈东南的旺河稻米平原，南通素可泰。其地古称Khelang Nakhon与Wiang Lakon；并入孟莱的兰纳后，泰文编年史记载新城于1302年修筑，城墙、护城河与城门渐备。这里既是兰纳南疆要塞，也是宾河流域、老挝山地和素可泰之间商队的落脚地。1444年，威扬功为滴洛拉阇守卫南境；驮运玉佛的大象不肯前往清迈而转至南邦，当时玉佛正供奉在敦涛玉佛寺。

滴洛拉阇1468年将玉佛迎往清迈。威扬功仍是兰纳与阿瑜陀耶交战的战场，1510—1515年被阿瑜陀耶攻占并迁走人口；1558年勃印曩征服兰纳，开启两百余年的缅甸宗主权。1732年，南奔首领玛哈约占领南邦并驻于南邦金塔寺，猎人Thipchang在此将他击杀，市民遂拥立Thipchang为主，阿瓦朝廷1735年承认他为帕雅·猜颂堪。其孙咖威拉1774年成为南邦首领，随后加入郑信的暹罗军队，1775年1月15日协助攻占清迈。南邦由此成为七王子家族的基地；当地朝廷1794年重修城墙、疏浚护城河，约1808年又兴建首领厅堂，咖威拉的族人则在暹罗宗主权下分治清迈、南邦和南奔。

en:
Mamuju opens on the Makassar Strait along a coast of short, rushing rivers, the northern shore of the Mandar lands. Before the great kingdoms its people—Mandar fishermen, planters and seafarers—dwelt in small river-mouth negeri under their own lords and customary councils, putting out in the slender outriggers called sandeq to fish, trade and raid along the strait, while Gowa and Bone grew to the south and the Kaili country stretched away to the north. Bugis and Makassar praus already called at these roadsteads, which carried the commerce of the whole west coast, yet in 1444 no paramount ruled the shore: every river mouth kept its own lords and its own ancestral cults.

That changed in the next century. In 1511 I Manyambungi founded Balanipa from four small negeri, and in 1540 the realm of Mamuju itself was formed by the union of several local chiefdoms. Raja Tomepayung of Balanipa then bound the seven estuary kingdoms—Balanipa, Sendana, Binuang, Tapalang, Banggae, Pamboang and Mamuju—in the Pitu Ba'ba'na Binanga confederacy, and by the stone oath at Luyo the seven were joined with the seven upstream kingdoms of the hills, making Mandar a maritime power whose fleets were famous, and feared, in the seventeenth-century wars of Gowa and Bone. Tied to the Sultans of Gowa and Bima by religion and alliance, the coastal courts were by then Muslim. The Mandar fleet sailed with Gowa against Buton in 1667, when that island sheltered the fugitive King of Bone, and was broken by Butonese ships and Cornelis Speelman's VOC squadron; after the Treaty of Bungaya, Dutch and Bone forces campaigned through the coast until the kingdoms acknowledged the Company in 1674. The submission was never more than nominal, however, and in 1821 the Mandar rajas still ruled their river mouths much as before.
zh:
马穆朱面向望加锡海峡，海岸短促多河，一座座河口城邦散布其间，是曼达尔人之地的北缘。在诸大国兴起之前，曼达尔的渔民、农夫和航海者住在一个个河口小邦里，由各自的首领和习俗议事会统辖，划着修长的桑德克独木舟出海捕鱼、贸易、劫掠；南方是日渐强盛的戈瓦和波尼，北方连着凯利人的地面。布吉斯和望加锡的帆船已在这些锚地往来，承运着整个西海岸的贸易，但1444年还没有谁号令这片海岸：每个河口各有其主，各守自己的祖灵崇拜。

局面在下个世纪改观。1511年，伊·曼扬布尼联合纳波、萨马松杜、莫索、托当托当四个小邦建立巴兰尼帕；1540年，马穆朱本身也由数个地方酋长邦合并立国。后来巴兰尼帕的拉贾·托梅帕永以塔马贾拉之盟，把巴兰尼帕、森达纳、比努昂、塔帕朗、邦盖、潘博昂、马穆朱七个河口王国结为「七河口之盟」，又在卢约的石誓之上与山区的七个上游王国合为一体，曼达尔由此成为令人畏惧的海上强权，其舰队在17世纪戈瓦与波尼的战争中声名远扬。由于同戈瓦苏丹和比马苏丹在宗教与同盟上的纽带，这时的河口宫廷都已是穆斯林。1667年，曼达尔舰队随戈瓦进攻庇护波尼国王的布顿岛，被布顿人与斯佩尔曼率领的荷兰东印度公司舰队击败；《邦加亚条约》之后，荷兰与波尼联军横扫海岸，诸王国于1674年承认公司的权威。但这份臣服始终只是名义上的；1821年时，曼达尔的拉贾们依旧按老样子统治着各自的河口。

en:
The tidal flats, mangroves and floodplains around the Adelaide River and Cape Hotham are Wulna country, also called Djerimanga. Their Wulna language belonged to the non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia, and the seasonal round followed the monsoon: fish, crabs, turtles' eggs and waterbirds were taken from the coast and billabongs while wet-season rains spread across the plains. To the west lived the Larrakia saltwater people, who traded with the Wulna, shared ceremonies and songlines and intermarried with them. In 1444 these northern waterways were governed by kinship and seasonal movement rather than by any foreign port or fort.

Abel Tasman's Dutch voyage of 1644 helped put northern Australia on European charts, but no landing among the Wulna is recorded. From the 1640s, Makassan praus also began sailing with the north-west monsoon to northern Australia, first fishing trepang in the Kimberley and then, decades later, working the Arnhem Land coast to the east. Matthew Flinders met a Makassan fleet led by Pobasso there in February 1803. The Wulna themselves seem to have had little or no direct contact with either Dutch ships or Makassan crews, though Larrakia exchange routes tied them to the wider northern coast. In 1821 the Adelaide River country remained without a European settlement or outpost.
zh:
阿德莱德河与霍瑟姆角周围的潮滩、红树林和洪泛平原，是伍尔纳人（又称杰里芒加，Djerimanga）的土地。他们的伍尔纳语属于澳大利亚北部的非帕马—尼荣根语言；生活随季风轮转，人们在海岸和死水潭获取鱼、蟹、龟蛋与水鸟，雨季洪水则漫过平原。西方住在以海为生的拉拉基亚人，他们同伍尔纳人贸易、共享仪式和歌路，并互通婚姻。1444年，这些北部水道由亲属关系和季节迁徙维系，还没有任何外来港口或要塞。

阿贝尔·塔斯曼1644年的荷兰航程把澳大利亚北部带进欧洲海图，但没有他在伍尔纳人中间登陆的记载。自1640年代起，望加锡人的帆船也乘西北季风来到澳大利亚北部，先在金伯利一带捕捞海参，数十年后又到东方的阿纳姆地海岸作业。1803年2月，马修·弗林德斯便在那里遇到波巴索率领的望加锡船队。伍尔纳人本身似乎很少或没有直接接触荷兰船只和望加锡船员，但拉拉基亚人的交换网络把他们同更广阔的北海岸联系起来。1821年，阿德莱德河土地上仍没有欧洲人的定居点或前哨。

en:
The Yunawa are the Yanyuwa, also spelled Yanuwa, a saltwater people of the south-western Gulf of Carpentaria. Their country covers the mainland coast opposite and within the Sir Edward Pellew Group and the approaches to the McArthur River; Vanderlin is the largest island in the adjacent group. Their language, Yanyuwa, has sixteen noun classes, while fishing, tidal gathering and movement among mangroves, river mouths and island camps shaped life on the shallow coast. In 1444 the monsoon, rather than an outside port or ruler, set the rhythm of Yanyuwa country.

Abel Tasman sighted the Pellew islands in 1644 but mistook them for mainland, naming Cape Vanderlin. From the 1720s, Makassan trepanging praus entered the gulf, sailing south on the December north-westerlies and returning with the April south-easterlies. Yanyuwa trade relations with the visitors were strong; some Yanyuwa stayed for months at Makassar, and Makassar served as a lingua franca among gulf peoples. In 1802 Matthew Flinders became the first British explorer to pass the islands, naming the group after Sir Edward Pellew and noting traces of earlier foreign visitors. Through 1821 no European station had been founded there.
zh:
尤纳瓦人即扬尤瓦人，也拼作亚努瓦，是卡奔塔利亚湾西南岸的「咸水人」。他们的土地包括爱德华·佩柳爵士群岛及对岸大陆海岸，也通向麦克阿瑟河河口；附近群岛中最大的是范德林岛。扬尤瓦语有16种名词类，渔业、潮间带采集以及往来红树林、河口和海岛营地的生活，构成了这片浅水海岸的节奏。1444年，支配扬尤瓦之地节律的是季风，而不是外来港口或统治者。

1644年，阿贝尔·塔斯曼望见佩柳群岛，却把它们当作大陆的一部分，并命名范德林角。1720年代起，望加锡海参帆船进入卡奔塔利亚湾：它们乘12月的西北风南下，再借4月的东南风返航。扬尤瓦人与这些访客贸易关系密切，一些扬尤瓦人还随船到望加锡居留数月，望加锡语也成为海湾各族的通用语。1802年，马修·弗林德斯成为首位经过这些岛屿的英国探险家，将群岛以爱德华·佩柳爵士命名，并注意到更早外来者留下的痕迹。到1821年，欧洲人仍未在此设立据点。

en:
The Mingin, also recorded as the Mingginda, held the mangrove shore and grassy plains of the southern Gulf of Carpentaria, from east of Moonlight Creek to the country west of the Leichhardt River. Their estates took in the tidal flats around the later site of Burketown and the Albert River, while their Minkin language was closely associated with the gulf's Tankic languages. In 1444 the wet-season watercourses, dry-season plains and coastal shallows remained Mingin country, bordered by Yukulta and Ganggalidda neighbours, and no European ship had yet entered the gulf.

In 1606 Willem Janszoon's Duyfken became the first recorded European vessel in the Gulf of Carpentaria. Jan Carstenszoon surveyed the same waters in 1623 and named the gulf after Pieter de Carpentier, Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies. Abel Tasman returned to chart gulf coasts in 1644, and Matthew Flinders carried out a more systematic British survey in 1802 and 1803. These expeditions remained passing maritime surveys; through 1821 no European settlement had been planted on Mingin land.
zh:
明金人（亦记作Mingginda）居住在卡奔塔利亚湾南缘的红树林海岸与草原地带，地域在Moonlight Creek以东、莱卡特河以西。他们的土地包括后来伯克敦所在的阿尔伯特河潮滩一带，使用的明金语与海湾诸坦基语关系密切。1444年，雨季水道、旱季草原和海岸浅滩仍是明金人的土地，邻近尤库尔塔人和甘加利达人，欧洲船只也尚未进入海湾。

1606年，威廉·扬松的「杜伊夫根号」成为有记录以来第一艘驶入卡奔塔利亚湾的欧洲船。1623年，扬·卡斯滕斯佐恩测绘同一水域，并以荷属东印度总督彼得·德·卡彭蒂耶的名字为海湾命名。1644年，阿贝尔·塔斯曼再来测绘湾岸；1802至1803年，马修·福林达斯率英国测量队进行了更系统的测绘。这些远航都只是途经的海上调查，到1821年仍没有欧洲人在明金人的土地上设立定居点。

en:
The Kurtjar, also recorded as the Kunggara or Kuritjara, held the southern Cape York Peninsula country around the Staaten River, where it drains north-west into the Gulf of Carpentaria. Their estates extended south toward the Smithburne River and inland around Stirling and Lotus Vale, while the Maikulan and Maijabi lived beyond their borders. Gurdjar, their Paman language, had Gunggara and Rip dialects. In 1444 the seasonal rivers, savanna woodland and tidal shore remained entirely in the keeping of Kurtjar clans.

Willem Janszoon's Duyfken entered the Gulf of Carpentaria in 1606, the first recorded European voyage to the Australian coast. In 1623 Jan Carstenszoon named the Staaten River after the States General of the Netherlands. Abel Tasman charted more of the gulf coasts in 1644, and Matthew Flinders carried out his British survey in 1802 and 1803.
